abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity may increase the technical complexity of robotic mitral valve (MV) repair, but comparative outcomes with sternotomy remain poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic vs sternotomy MV repair in patients with class I obesity.
METHODS: A total of 880 patients with class I obesity (body mass index 30-34.9 kg/m2) underwent MV repair at our clinic between 2008 and 2025. After excluding those with mitral stenosis, active endocarditis, prior sternotomy, or concomitant procedures, 429 patients remained. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 132 patients in each group who underwent either robotic or conventional sternotomy MV repair.
RESULTS: Median age was 59 years (IQR: 52-66), and 81% were male. Cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were longer in the robotic group than in the sternotomy group (86 vs 65 minutes and 60 vs 48 minutes, respectively; P < 0.001). Robotic MV repair was associated with shorter hospitalization (3.5 vs 5 days; P < 0.001) and a lower postoperative transfusion rate (1.5% vs 10.6%; P = 0.002). There were no operative deaths in either group. No sternal wound infections occurred. Thirty-day readmission was numerically higher after robotic repair (12.8% vs 4.3%; P = 0.064). Ten-year survival was 92% (95% CI: 87% to 97%) with no significant difference between groups (P = 0.83).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with class I obesity, the robotic approach in comparison to sternotomy was associated with lower transfusion rates, shorter hospitalization, and comparable operative mortality and long-term survival relative to sternotomy. Although 30-day readmission was numerically higher among robotic patients, most events were minor and managed without intervention.
title: Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Class I Obesity: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
How Pulmonary Embolism Burden Shapes Left Ventricular Strain and Recovery After Thrombectomy.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effectiveness of Healthcare Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (HFMEA) in optimizing the emergency management workflow for Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) and to assess its impact on emergency efficiency, clinical outcomes, and patient satisfaction.
METHODS: AMI patients treated at our hospital during different periods were enrolled and divided into two groups: a control group receiving conventional emergency procedures and a post-optimization group managed with an HFMEA-optimized emergency workflow. The HFMEA implementation involved forming a multidisciplinary team, constructing an integrated prehospital-to-in-hospital treatment process map, identifying high-risk failure modes based on the Risk Priority Number (RPN), developing targeted improvement measures, and establishing an information-based quality monitoring system. Outcome measures included key emergency time intervals, clinical outcomes, and healthcare quality indicators.
RESULTS: Following HFMEA implementation, the post-optimization group showed significant reductions in all key emergency time metrics compared with the control group, including triage time, time to first electrocardiogram, Door-to-Catheterization (D-to-C) time, and Door-to-Balloon (D-to-B) time (all P < 0.001), and the effect sizes for all major time-related indicators between the two groups reached the large-effect level (Cohen's d ≥ 0.8, r ≥ 0.5). The total incidence of adverse events was significantly lower in the post-optimization group (P < 0.05), while rescue success rates did not differ significantly between groups (P > 0.05). Regarding healthcare quality, patients in the post-optimization group had shorter hospital stays and higher satisfaction scores as measured by a dedicated survey instrument (both P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: HFMEA effectively identifies high-risk steps within the AMI emergency workflow. Targeted process optimization can significantly enhance emergency efficiency, reduce adverse events, improve healthcare quality, and optimize patient experience.
keywords: Healthcare failure mode and effect analysis
title: Application of healthcare failure mode and effect analysis in optimizing the emergency management process for acute myocardial infarction: An observational study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: ARIES-HM3 (Antiplatelet Removal and Hemocompatibility Events With the HeartMate 3 Pump) demonstrated that aspirin can be safely omitted after HeartMate 3 (HM3) implantation when vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation is continued, resulting in reduced nonsurgical bleeding without an increased risk of thromboembolic events. The pace, extent, and pattern of adoption in clinical practice, and whether real-world outcomes after adoption are consistent with the trial, remain uncertain.
METHODS: Using the Truveta electronic health record network (30 US health systems), we identified adults undergoing de novo durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation with documented warfarin therapy from January 2016 through March 2026. Recorded early aspirin use was defined as an aspirin administration, dispense, or active order on postoperative days 2-7. Temporal trends were examined relative to ARIES-HM3 publication (November 2023) and the US Food and Drug Administration labeling revision (August 2024). Among HM3 recipients implanted after ARIES-HM3 publication and event-free at a postoperative day 14 landmark, the 12-month composite of death or first major nonsurgical hemocompatibility-related adverse event was compared using Kaplan-Meier methods and sequentially adjusted Cox regression.
RESULTS: In the overall LVAD cohort (n = 3365), recorded aspirin use declined from 90.2% in 2023 to 55.7% in 2024 and 52.7% in 2025. Of 739 post-ARIES HM3 recipients, 404 (54.7%) had recorded early aspirin use. Aspirin was continued in 67.1% of patients with prior percutaneous coronary intervention, coronary artery bypass grafting, stroke, or peripheral vascular disease vs 43.4% of those without. The 12-month composite end point occurred in 29.3% of patients with and 21.7% without recorded aspirin (unadjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.70, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-0.94); after multivariable adjustment, no significant association remained (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.61-1.22). Major nonsurgical bleeding occurred in 22.0% and 15.0% of patients, respectively (unadjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.45-0.94; adjusted HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.54-1.26). Stroke (4.7% vs 2.7%) and peripheral arterial thromboembolism (4.3% vs 2.6%) were not more frequent without aspirin; pump thrombosis was rare (2 events vs 3 events).
CONCLUSIONS: After ARIES-HM3 publication and the US Food and Drug Administration labeling revision, aspirin use in HM3 LVAD implantation declined substantially but persisted in approximately one-half of recipients, most often in those with established vascular disease, the population in which ARIES-HM3 showed preserved safety and a numerically greater bleeding reduction with aspirin avoidance. In this observational analysis, aspirin avoidance was not associated with a higher adjusted risk of the composite outcome, and no excess of stroke or arterial thromboembolism was observed.
keywords: Antiplatelet Removal and Hemocompatibility Events with the HeartMate 3 Pump (ARIES-HM3)
title: Real-World Adoption and Associated Outcomes of Aspirin Avoidance After HeartMate 3 Implantation: The PRAISE HM3 Study.

abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a stress-induced left ventricular (LV) cardiomyopathy with an unclear genetic predisposition. We investigated whether single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with other cardiomyopathies or LV physiological traits contribute to TTS susceptibility. We conducted a case-control study based on the French multicentre TAKOGENE study (NCT01520610), including 261 unrelated TTS patients and 259 sex- and age-matched controls presenting with acute coronary syndrome. All participants were of European ancestry. A total of 325 SNPs were selected from large-scale genome-wide association studies of cardiomyopathies (n=202) and LV structural/functional traits (n=123), derived from polygenic risk scores. Genotyping was performed using the Infinium OmniExpressExome-8 array. Associations were assessed by logistic regression under an additive model, adjusted for age and sex, with group-specific Bonferroni correction. A sensitivity analysis compared the 261 TTS cases with 973 French population controls from the EPP3 cohort. After quality control and statistical analysis, seventeen SNPs (nine related to cardiomyopathies and eight to LV traits) showed nominal associations (P < 0.05), but none remained significant after group-specific Bonferroni correction. The strongest signal was observed for rs6885658 in the CPEB4 gene (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.23-2.15; P = 5.8 × 10-4) related to cardiomyopathy traits. The EPP3 population-control sensitivity analysis was consistent with the primary analysis, with no association remaining significant after correction. In conclusion, common genetic variants previously associated with cardiomyopathies or LV traits do not appear to have a major effect on TTS risk. These findings support a disease-specific polygenic architecture of TTS, distinct from that underlying chronic cardiomyopathies and baseline LV traits. Future studies should explore alternative approaches, such as pathway-based analyses focusing on stress-response mechanisms.
title: Genetic susceptibility in Takotsubo syndrome: a candidate gene association analysis in the French TAKOGENE cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO.
METHODS: The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed.
RESULTS: Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P < 0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (4.9% vs 2.0% vs 1.3%; P < 0.001), and in-hospital cardiac arrest (6.1% vs 2.7% vs 1.6%; P < 0.001). Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001). Using a definition of ACO including TIMI flow grade 0 or 1, NSTEMI-ACO accounted for 216,054 presentations (24.4% of NSTEMI). In-hospital outcomes were similarly worse compared with NSTEMI-no-ACO and better compared with STEMI.
CONCLUSIONS: ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcomes only, and occlusion is defined from angiography after the event.
appraisal.one_line: A national registry analysis finds acute coronary occlusion in a sizeable share of NSTEMI patients undergoing PCI, with worse in-hospital outcomes than NSTEMI without occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It quantifies the population targeted by occlusion-based triage proposals.

title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.
The Unlucky Occlusion Patients Missed by the STEMI/NSTEMI Paradigm May Be Found by OMI/NOMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE.
METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO.
RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield.
CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 trial; 4,398 patients without diagnostic ST-elevation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Outcomes are process measures (timing of invasive management and ACO identification) rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: A substudy of a cluster-randomised trial comparing occlusion-focused triage with very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria for identifying acute coronary occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001); adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs the proposed shift from STEMI/NSTEMI to occlusion-based triage that would alter who receives immediate angiography.

title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.
Occlusion Myocardial Infarction: Ready for Prime Time?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial.
METHODS: Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients.
CONCLUSIONS: OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

title: Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
Occlusion Myocardial Infarction: Beyond STEMI and NSTEMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI.
METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207).
RESULTS: After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I2 = 0%; τ2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Frequentist pairwise meta-analysis of RCTs; 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The authors note few deaths and statistical fragility, and the prediction interval includes no difference.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of four randomised trials suggests higher 1-year mortality with immediate than with staged complete revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The timing of non-culprit intervention is a common decision in STEMI and the signal runs against immediate treatment.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
Timing of Nonculprit PCI for STEMI and Multivessel Disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI.
METHODS: Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified.
RESULTS: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA.
CONCLUSIONS: IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR.
METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed.
RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR.
METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months.
RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines advocate for intervention in primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) based on detection of severe MR using standardised thresholds. We sought to quantify sex-related differences in transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived MR severity and long-term mortality after PMR intervention.
METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing PMR intervention with validated vena contracta (VC) measurements were included. Proximal isovelocity surface area radius (PISAr), effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) and regurgitant volume (RVol) were also measured in a subset of patients. Using Cox models adjusted for PMR mortality risk factors, VC was modelled as a restricted cubic spline with an interaction term for sex. Sex-stratified receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to identify potential differences in risk calibration.
RESULTS: Within 420 patients, females (n=168, 40%) displayed significantly lower absolute values of VC (median (interquartile range): 0.60 (0.55–0.80) vs 0.70 (0.60–0.80) cm, p=0.003), PISAr (0.85 (0.70–1.00) vs 1.10 (0.90–1.30) cm, n=96, p<0.001), EROA (0.35 (0.22–0.50) vs 0.60 (0.40–0.80) cm2, n=58, p=0.018) and RVol (51 (43–83) vs 88 (67–108) mL, n=53, p=0.013) compared with males. In multivariable regression, sex-related differences in long-term all-cause mortality were moderated by VC (Pinteraction=0.013). In ROC curve analysis, VC had similar discriminatory ability in both sexes (p=0.768), although the optimum cut-off was lower in females (females: 0.67 cm vs males: 0.74 cm).
CONCLUSIONS: The present study demonstrates significant sex differences in TTE-measured MR severity and subsequent prognosis following intervention for PMR, which may merit sex-specific individualised thresholds.
title: Prognostic implications of sex-related disparities in severity assessment of primary mitral regurgitation following intervention.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) reduces adverse events in complex coronary lesions remains debated. Although optical coherence tomography (OCT) improves stent optimisation, its effect on the physiological result of PCI has not been tested in a dedicated randomised trial. The PREcise percutaneous coronary intervention for stent OptimizatION in treatment of COMPLEX lesion (PRECISION-COMPLEX) trial aims to determine whether algorithm-driven OCT-guided stent optimisation improves the physiological result of PCI, assessed by post-optimisation fractional flow reserve (FFR), compared with angiography-guided PCI.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PRECISION-COMPLEX is an investigator-initiated, multicentre, open-label, superiority randomised controlled trial at four Korean academic hospitals. Patients with stable or unstable angina and at least one prespecified complex lesion are randomised 1:1 to OCT-guided or angiography-guided PCI with current-generation drug-eluting stents. In the OCT arm, stent sizing follows a prespecified algorithm, and post-PCI OCT must confirm adequate expansion, apposition and absence of major edge dissection. Post-PCI FFR is mandated in both arms. The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients with a suboptimal post-optimisation FFR (<0.85); secondary endpoints at 2 years include target-vessel failure and its components, any revascularisation and stent thrombosis. A total of 320 patients gives 90% power to detect a reduction in the primary endpoint from 30% to 15%. Enrolment ran from 15 November 2022 to 4 December 2024; follow-up is ongoing, with main results expected in early 2027.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The trial protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Chonnam National University Hospital (CNUH-2022-283), the Institutional Review Board of Samsung Medical Center (SMC2022-11-012), the Institutional Review Board of Seoul National University Hospital (H2303-104-1414) and the Institutional Review Board of Chung-Ang University Gwangmyeong Hospital (2212–048-077). It conforms to the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice. All participants provide written informed consent. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and presentation at scientific meetings. PRECISION-COMPLEX will define the incremental impact of OCT-based optimisation on the physiological result of PCI and indicate whether anatomy-integrated and physiology-integrated guidance improves outcomes in complex coronary lesions.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05493904.
title: OCT-guided versus angiography-guided stent optimisation for post-interventional FFR in patients with complex coronary artery lesions: protocol for a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial (PRECISION-COMPLEX).

Development and internal validation of an oxygen saturation-based prehospital cardiac risk assessment index (P-CRAI) for predicting 30-day mortality in acute myocardial infarction: a multicentre registry study from the Mie ACS Registry, Japan.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung transplant (LTx) candidates often have multiple risk factors for coronary artery disease (CAD), which was previously considered a contraindication to transplantation. Improvements in revascularisation techniques have broadened transplant eligibility; however, because available evidence is based on small and heterogeneous cohorts, the optimal revascularisation strategy remains unclear.
METHOD: We conducted a literature review and describe our centre's experience with current approaches to revascularisation in LTx candidates with obstructive CAD.
RESULTS: The literature review identified 174 studies in the initial search, of which 29 studies were considered relevant. However, only six retrospective studies directly compared percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), comprising 376 revascularised patients. In some cohorts, CABG was associated with longer ventilation time and longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay and overall hospital stay, although this finding was not consistent across all studies. At our centre, 20 patients underwent concomitant CABG, and 11 underwent PCI within 12 months before transplant listing, after obstructive CAD was diagnosed during transplant assessment. Procedure time in patients undergoing concomitant CABG was significantly longer (1.2 hours; p<0.05); however, all patients in this group underwent bilateral transplantation. Three patients in the PCI group experienced postoperative coronary events, and overall mortality was higher in this group. There were no differences in other outcomes, including ICU and overall length of stay.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the heterogeneity and complexity of this patient cohort. Although no patients who underwent CABG experienced postoperative coronary events, the limited published evidence does not support a single preferred revascularisation strategy for patients being considered for lung transplantation. Case-by-case management guided by a multidisciplinary team is therefore warranted.
title: Coronary Revascularisation Strategies for Patients with Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Requiring Lung Transplantation: A Narrative Review and Single-Centre Experience.

abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high mortality and poor neurological outcomes. Dynamic assessment of metabolic recovery, reflected by lactate normalization, may offer additional prognostic value compared with static severity indices. We retrospectively analyzed 662 consecutive patients from the multicenter RESCUE II registry who remained on venoarterial ECMO for at least 48 hours. Patients were stratified by 48 hour lactate level: 48 hour lactate normalization group (< 2.0 mmol/L, n = 371) and persistent lactate elevation group (≥ 2.0 mmol/L, n = 291). The primary outcome was favorable neurologic discharge (FND), defined as discharge with a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2. The persistent lactate elevation group had a higher SOFA score (9.8 ± 3.2 vs. 8.5 ± 3.4, p < 0.001) and initial serum lactate (7.9 ± 4.8 mmol/L vs. 6.0 ± 4.3 mmol/L, p < 0.001). Lactate normalization was associated with a higher rate of FND (71.4% vs. 41.9%, p < 0.001), remained an independent predictor of FND (odds ratio [OR]: 3.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.21-4.41, p < 0.001), and was associated with lower risks of all-cause death (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.38-0.64, p < 0.001) at 12 months. In conclusion, lactate normalization within 48 hours of ECMO initiation is associated with favorable neurologic status and 12 month survival.
journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
title: Forty-Eight Hour Lactate Normalization Predicts Favorable Neurologic Recovery and Survival in Venoarterial ECMO for Cardiogenic Shock.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inadvertent perioperative hypothermia is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but adequately powered trials using high-sensitivity troponin endpoints is lacking. The SAGE trial evaluates whether an intelligent, closed-loop thermoregulation strategy reduces myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) in high-risk elderly patients.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial conducted at seven tertiary hospitals in China. Participants aged ≥65 years scheduled for elective gastrointestinal tumor resection under general anesthesia are randomly assigned (1:1) to intelligent closed-loop warming (target 36.8 °C, upper limit 37.0 °C) or routine thermal management (active warming only if core temperature ≤35.5 °C). The primary outcome is the incidence of MINS within the first 2 postoperative days , adjudicated using high-sensitivity troponin thresholds per AHA criteria. Secondary outcomes include surgical site infection, transfusion requirement, hypothermia burden, emergence delirium, delayed emergence, and postoperative shivering. With 695 participants per group (total 1,390, accounting for 10% dropout), the trial has 80% power at a one-sided significance level of 0.05 to detect a 6 absolute percentage point reduction in MINS (12% to 6%) with a superiority margin of -2 percentage points.
DISCUSSION: The SAGE trial is designed to generate new evidence on the relationship between intraoperative hypothermia exposure and postoperative cardiovascular complications. It will evaluate whether closed-loop targeted normothermia reduces myocardial injury and will explore hypothermia exposure thresholds that may inform individualized perioperative management for geriatric surgical patients.
TRIAL ACRONYM: Intelligent Thermoregulation Strategy for Advanced-Age Elders undergoing gastrointestinal tumor resection (SAGE).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), identifier: ChiCTR2600117264. Registered on January 21, 2026 (http://www.chictr.org.cn).
title: Intelligent thermoregulation strategy versus routine thermal management on myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery during gastrointestinal tumor resection in elderly patients (SAGE): a multicenter, parallel-group, superiority trial.

abstract: This single-center retrospective case series assessed early ulnar artery patency by Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) after coronary angiography via distal ulnar access (DUA), described flow evolution in patients with follow-up, and reported access-related complications. Thirty-eight consecutive patients with a day-3 DUS after coronary angiography via DUA between September 2023 and March 2024 were included. All procedures were performed by 1 operator using a short 6F sheath and 5000 IU intra-arterial heparin. Flow was categorized as thrombosis/no flow, monophasic, or triphasic; the primary endpoint was day-3 non-triphasic flow, and month-1 and month-3 DUS were selective. Mean age was 58.8 ± 10.1 years and 47.4% were male; 21.1% underwent same-session percutaneous coronary intervention. On day 3, thrombosis/no flow occurred in 18.4% (7/38), monophasic flow in 5.3% (2/38), and triphasic flow in 76.3% (29/38); non-triphasic flow was 23.7% (9/38). Month-1 DUS (n = 35) showed no thrombosis/no flow and 94.3% triphasic flow; month-3 DUS (n = 4) was triphasic in all. No clinically relevant hematoma, neuropathy, hand ischemia, or functional impairment was documented. After coronary angiography via DUA, day-3 non-triphasic flow occurred in 23.7%; selective follow-up suggested recanalization without major clinical complications, but limits generalizability.
title: Early Ulnar Artery Occlusion and Recanalization After Coronary Angiography via Distal Ulnar Access: A Doppler-Followed Case Series.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronary artery calcification (CAC) is associated with adverse events after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), traditionally attributed to inadequate stent expansion. Whether severe CAC confers residual risk despite optimal acute mechanical results remains unknown.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 709 patients who underwent pre-procedural intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) before PCI. Patients were classified as no calcification (n = 417), mild CAC (arc ≤180° or length ≤5 mm, n = 168), or severe CAC (arc >180° and length >5 mm, n = 124). The primary endpoint was clinically driven target vessel revascularization (TVR); the secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Post-PCI minimum stent area (MSA) and expansion index were compared across groups. Multivariable Cox regression using three prespecified adjustment models was performed.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 18.6 months, 57 patients (8.0%) experienced TVR and 122 (17.2%) experienced MACE. Post-PCI MSA (5.9 vs. 5.6 vs. 5.8 mm2; P = 0.286) and expansion index (0.89 vs. 0.88 vs. 0.88; P = 0.485) were comparable across groups, indicating acceptable acute stent expansion in severely calcified lesions. Nevertheless, severe CAC remained independently associated with increased TVR risk in the primary analysis (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.51, 95% CI 1.33-4.74, P = 0.005), persisting after extended adjustment (aHR 2.61, P = 0.007) and after excluding rotational atherectomy (RA) cases (aHR 2.29, P = 0.018). The association between severe CAC and MACE was more modest (aHR 1.77, P = 0.014) and attenuated after extended adjustment (aHR 1.49, P = 0.119). Calcified nodules, present in 64.5% of severe CAC lesions, independently predicted TVR (aHR 3.04, P < 0.001). Mild CAC showed no significant risk elevation.
CONCLUSION: Severe CAC identifies a subgroup at persistently elevated risk for repeat revascularization despite achieving stent expansion comparable to non-calcified lesions, challenging the conventional paradigm linking calcification to adverse events solely through underexpansion.
title: Residual risk persists in severely calcified lesions despite optimal stent expansion: a paradoxical finding from an IVUS-guided PCI cohort.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of classical prescriptions from Shang han Lun (Treatise on Febrile Diseases) and Jin gui Yao lue (Synopsis of the Golden Chamber) combined with conventional biomedicine in the treatment of angina pectoris of coronary heart disease.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eight commonly used Chinese and English databases were searched for relevant clinical studies published before 25 December 2024. Revman 5.4 and Stata14.0 software were used for data analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 131 studies involving 11,292 participants (5,660 in intervention groups and 5,632 in control groups) were included. Most classical prescriptions combined with conventional biomedical therapy showed favorable associations with improvements in angina pectoris efficiency, electrocardiogram (ECG) efficiency, and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome outcomes compared with conventional treatment alone. Subgroup analyses showed partially different patterns of relative efficacy among prescriptions, with LGZG demonstrating more consistent performance in stable angina pectoris, while other prescriptions showed variable rankings in unstable angina pectoris. For lipid-related and inflammatory outcomes, results were inconsistent across studies, and current evidence remains insufficient to support robust comparative conclusions among classical prescriptions. Regarding safety outcomes, GZFL combined with conventional biomedical therapy showed a relatively favorable safety profile, while other classical prescriptions demonstrated comparable rates of adverse events to conventional therapy.
CONCLUSION: Classical prescriptions combined with conventional biomedical therapy may be associated with improvements in clinical outcomes of angina pectoris, with an overall acceptable safety profile observed across most intervention. However, due to limitations in study quality, heterogeneity, and indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Further high-quality, multicenter randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these observations.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251029216.
title: Comparative efficacy of Traditional Chinese Medicine classical prescriptions for angina pectoris: a network meta-analysis.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) are novel biomarkers reflecting hemodynamic load and systemic inflammatory immune status, respectively. This study aimed to explore the prognostic value of combined ePVS and NLR for cardiovascular mortality in patients with heart failure (HF) complicating acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study consecutively enrolled patients diagnosed with AMI complicated by HF at Putian University Affiliated Hospital from January 2020 to June 2024. Admission hemoglobin and hematocrit levels were used to calculate ePVS, while routine blood test parameters were applied to determine NLR. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular mortality within two years after AMI. Cox proportional hazards regression models were constructed to analyze the associations of ePVS and NLR with clinical endpoints. The predictive efficacy of single and combined ePVS and NLR was comprehensively evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: A total of 2046 patients were ultimately included. During a mean follow-up of 819 days, endpoint events occurred in 14.90% of the study population. Univariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS served as a strong risk factor for cardiovascular mortality (HR = 1.571, 95% CI: 1.502-1.642, P < 0.001). After adjusting for age, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and NLR, both ePVS (HR = 1.436, 95% CI: 1.370-1.505, P < 0.001) and NLR (HR = 1.330, 95% CI: 1.258-1.406, P < 0.001) remained independent predictors of cardiovascular mortality. The combined predictive model integrating ePVS and NLR exhibited significantly superior predictive performance compared with either biomarker alone (AUC: 0.794 for ePVS vs. 0.891 for ePVS + NLR, P < 0.001). Both NRI and IDI analyses further verified the significant improvement in predictive accuracy of the combined model (all P < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: ePVS and NLR represent valuable prognostic biomarkers for cardiovascular mortality in AMI patients. The combination of ePVS and NLR significantly improves predictive performance and facilitates precise risk stratification.
title: Predictive value of combined estimated plasma volume status and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for cardiovascular mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction with heart failure.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular access is an important component of CHIP planning that influences procedural feasibility, safety, and completeness. It affects bleeding and vascular complications, guide-catheter support, compatibility with intravascular imaging and calcium-modification devices, chronic total occlusion techniques, closure and bailout options, and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) planning. Contemporary CHIP populations are increasingly older or frail and more often have chronic kidney disease, peripheral artery disease, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, prior bypass surgery, calcification, or CTO; access choice should extend beyond radial vs. femoral.
SUMMARY: This review appraises proximal and distal radial, femoral, ulnar, and brachial access; sheathless, slender, and RailTracking strategies; large-bore femoral workflows; and access planning when MCS is considered. We discuss preprocedural arterial assessment, ultrasound and micropuncture, prior access footprint, closure feasibility, hostile femoral anatomy, alternative access, and complication prevention and rescue. The available literature supports a non-dogmatic approach in which access architecture is matched to patient vulnerability, arterial anatomy, lesion complexity, guide and device requirements, support needs, haemostasis feasibility, and bailout planning. Recent randomised evidence further reinforces selective rather than routine prophylactic MCS in nonemergent high-risk PCI.
CONCLUSIONS: Forearm access should remain central whenever it permits procedural success without compromising device delivery, imaging, guide support, or bailout flexibility. Femoral access remains indispensable when large-bore support, maximal guide stability, complex device delivery, or rapid escalation are anticipated. Within a comprehensive CHIP plan, the preferred access architecture is the smallest one that enables the intended revascularisation, safe haemostasis, and timely rescue.
title: Vascular access options for complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary interventions: contemporary strategies, trade-offs, and practical algorithms.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) introduces substantial artifacts in coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Although calcification is classically associated with overestimation of stenosis severity, underestimation may be even more clinically hazardous because underestimation can lead to inappropriate deferral of revascularization. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the association between CAC burden and CCTA underestimation, with emphasis on vessel-specific anatomical heterogeneity.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 673 patients without known coronary artery disease who underwent both CCTA and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) within 90 days, yielding 2692 vessel observations. Underestimation was defined strictly at the vessel level as a CCTA stenosis grade lower than the corresponding ICA grade. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to characterize the nonlinear association between CAC burden and the risk of underestimation. Within-patient clustering across the left main (LM), left anterior descending (LAD), left circumflex (LCX), and right coronary artery (RCA) was accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEEs).
RESULTS: Any-vessel underestimation occurred in 389 patients (57.8%). Vessel-specific susceptibility varied markedly: LM, 3.0%; LAD, 27.9%; LCX, 29.3%; and RCA, 22.4%. RCS analysis demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between total CAC score and patient-level underestimation in the fully adjusted model (p-overall = 0.014; p-nonlinear = 0.004), with an upward risk trajectory observed as calcification increased relative to the median reference of 301. GEE modeling confirmed that patient-level CAC burden independently predicted vessel-level underestimation (CAC ≥400 vs. 0: odds ratio, 2.01; 95% confidence interval, 1.20-3.36; p = 0.008), with a significant interaction between CAC and vessel territory (p < 0.001). A sensitivity analysis restricted to patients without any CCTA overestimation (n = 155) confirmed a robust nonlinear association between total CAC score and pure underestimation risk (p-overall = 0.012; p-nonlinear = 0.005), suggesting that concurrent overestimation noise partially obscures this dynamic risk trajectory in the full cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: The association between calcification burden and CCTA underestimation is nonlinear and strongly dependent on coronary territory. Since the RCS-derived odds ratio (OR) = 1, crossings depend on the median reference value (CAC = 301) and should be interpreted as markers of risk trajectory rather than absolute diagnostic cutoffs. Integrating total calcium burden with vessel-specific susceptibility may help mitigate the risk of missed severe stenosis on CCTA.
title: Nonlinear and Vessel-Specific Association Between Coronary Artery Calcium Burden and Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography Underestimation of Coronary Stenosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) and percutaneous closure of the left atrial appendage are increasingly used in patients with atrial fibrillation. An interaction between this form of energy and metallic structures in the heart is an emerging problem. We first report a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC)-limiting PFA using a novel dual energy ablation catheter, solved by switching to the classic radiofrequency ablation.
CASE SUMMARY: An 85-year-old woman with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (status post pulmonary vein isolation in 2019, with a 25 mm Abbott Amulet LAAC implanted in 2023) presented with recurrent atrial tachycardia. During redo ablation, mapping revealed a macroreentrant circuit through an anterior left atrial low-voltage area. While extending a linear PFA lesion towards the LAAC, the generator repeatedly aborted applications due to invalid impedance values near the device-despite the device having been in place for 3 years. Switching to radiofrequency energy on the same catheter allowed the line to be completed successfully, achieving bidirectional block and tachycardia non-inducibility.
DISCUSSION: The interaction between PFA and metallic cardiac devices may limit catheter ablation, a problem that can be solved by technologies that allow for the switch to radiofrequency sources. Dual energy technologies may be therefore preferred in patients with LAAC devices.
title: LAA occluder device impeding pulsed field ablation of an anterior mitral line: a case report about the role of a dual energy source.
Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Perspective on the PRO-TAVI Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fulminant myocarditis (FM) progresses rapidly and carries high all-cause in-hospital mortality. Patients in the early phase often develop cardiogenic shock and malignant ventricular arrhythmias, with widely varying mortality rates reported across studies. Existing single-center cohorts yield conflicting prognostic findings with marked cross-cohort heterogeneity, and no standardized meta-analysis with GRADE certainty grading has been published to guide risk stratification. This meta-analysis pooled prognostic associations of all-cause in-hospital mortality in FM to inform acute risk evaluation and personalized care.
METHODS: Eleven Chinese and English electronic databases were searched from database establishment through June 2025. Eligible studies were observational cohorts reporting prognostic associations of all-cause in-hospital mortality among FM patients. Two independent reviewers completed screening, data extraction and quality assessment separately. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and AHRQ checklist were adopted to evaluate methodological quality. Pooled analyses were performed via the statsmodels package in Python, and the GRADE framework was applied to rate the certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: 26 retrospective cohort studies with 4,890 FM patients were enrolled. Ten potential factors were meta-analyzed, of which six showed statistically significant associations with in-hospital mortality (P < 0.05), including age (OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.02-1.04), cardiac arrest or CPR (OR = 2.57, 95% CI: 1.49-4.44), lactate (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.00-1.16), cTnI (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07), LVEF (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.90-0.97), and intravenous immunoglobulin therapy (OR = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.02-0.86). CK-MB, serum creatinine, total bilirubin, and VT/VF showed no statistically significant association (all P > 0.05). GRADE evidence ratings indicated low-certainty evidence for age and cTnI, and very-low-certainty evidence for the remaining significant factors. Sensitivity analyses indicated unstable pooled estimates for lactate and intravenous immunoglobulin therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Four factors showed positive associations with elevated all-cause in-hospital mortality. LVEF was inversely associated with mortality, whereas the inverse association for IVIG represents a fragile treatment-related signal. These findings may inform acute risk screening, but most associations were supported by low or very low certainty evidence and should not be interpreted as causal. All included data were derived from retrospective cohorts. Standardized multicenter prospective studies are required to verify these prognostic associations.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399446, identifier CRD420261399446.
title: Associated factors for in-hospital mortality in patients with fulminant myocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a paucity of information concerning automatic mitral valve apparatus (MVA) analysis of patients with mitral valve prolapse (MVP). We aimed to study with an automatic three-dimensional (3D) transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-dedicated software, patients with moderate and severe mitral regurgitation when compared to patients with no structural cardiac chamber alterations [patients with patent foramen ovale (PFO) who underwent TEE].
METHODS: We employed TEE software dedicated to automatic analysis of 34 parameters of the MVA, comparing MVP patients with moderate and severe mitral regurgitation and patients with PFO without cardiac chamber structural alterations. Mitral valve effective regurgitant orifice (ERO) and regurgitant volume were correlated to automatic MVP parameters.
RESULTS: Fifty-nine MVP patients and 43 PFO patients were analyzed. All MVP patients presented P2 MVP, 15 (25.4%) with both posterior and anterior prolapse. Twenty-seven automatic parameters (79%) were different concerning MVP and PFO patients (P<0.05): diameters, area, perimeter, height, angle, coaptation width, length, closure line length, and annulus. ERO was 0.43±0.11 cm2, and regurgitant volume was 62.9±14.9 mL/beat. Automatic analysis correlated to 75th percentile ERO MVP patients (ERO >0.48 cm2): posterior leaflet area (r=0.74, P=0.03); posterior leaflet length (r=0.73, P=0.03); tenting area (r=0.41, P=0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: Automatic mitral valve parameters differed significantly between patients with MVP and those without structural cardiac chamber remodeling. In exploratory analysis, patients in the upper range of ERO values (≥75th percentile) showed patterns involving posterior leaflet geometry that were consistent with the associations observed in continuous-variable analysis. These findings support the potential role of automated 3D assessment in the anatomical characterization of MVP.
title: Automatic transesophageal echocardiographic evaluation of patients with mitral valve prolapse: comparison with patients without structural cardiac chamber remodeling (an exploratory study).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study wasto evaluate the clinical effects of preoperative antiplatelet therapy (APT) discontinuation timing on major bleeding and adverse cardiac events in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from Fuwai Cardiac Surgery Database (FCSD), specifically from 41,689 patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing isolated CABG (2009-2019). A comparison was conducted between 10,739 patients treated with continuation APT (AP group; discontinued ≤7 days preoperation; including aspirin alone, clopidogrel alone, or aspirin + clopidogrel) and 30,950 patients with discontinuation therapy (NAP group; >7 days preoperation). Major bleeding events were defined according to the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium-CABG criteria. Composite adverse events (30-day all-cause mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, and acute renal failure) were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was applied to estimate effects.
RESULTS: Adverse cardiac events occurred in 7.8% of patients in the AP group and 9.1% in the NAP group (P<0.001), but there was no difference in the incidence of major bleeding events. Multivariable analysis showed that continuation therapy significantly decreased the risk of adverse cardiac events [odds ratio (OR) 0.832; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.754-0.918; P<0.001] without increasing the risk of major bleeding events (OR 1.006; 95% CI: 0.926-1.093; P=0.88). Subgroup analysis identified certain strategies for reducing adverse events without bleeding.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative continued APT significantly reduces the risk of 30-day adverse cardiac events post-CABG without increasing the risk of major bleeding. Optimal strategies include clopidogrel alone (discontinued <3 days preoperatively) and dual-antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel discontinued 5-7 days preoperatively).
title: Preoperative antiplatelet strategies and coronary artery bypass graft outcomes: bleeding and cardiovascular events in 41,696 patients with acute coronary syndrome.

abstract: Acute pancreatitis can present with ST-segment elevation and marked troponin elevation, mimicking acute coronary syndrome. In resource-limited settings where coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and serial high-sensitivity troponin testing are unavailable, distinguishing acute myocardial injury associated with pancreatitis from Type 1 myocardial infarction can be challenging.

title: Acute Pancreatitis Presenting With ST-Segment Elevation and Marked Troponin Elevation: A Diagnostic Dilemma in a Resource-Limited Setting-A Case Report.

abstract: Reperfusion therapies have revolutionized the treatment of acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but target-artery recanalization, downstream angiographic reperfusion, microvascular tissue reperfusion, and functional recovery are distinct endpoints. Patients may have persistent occlusion or early reocclusion, incomplete modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) reperfusion, microvascular no-reflow despite high-grade mTICI/eTICI reperfusion, hemorrhagic transformation (HT), or poor 90-day functional outcome. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) form a mechanistic link between thrombus structure, innate immune activation, endothelial injury, and antithrombotic responses. NETs provide a DNA-histone scaffold that stabilizes fibrin-rich thrombi, recruits platelets and coagulation factors, and exposes the neurovascular unit to cytotoxic granular proteins. The biological characteristics of NETs nevertheless vary among patients. Differences in neutrophil priming, platelet activation, monocyte-endothelial signaling, thrombus composition, collateral status, concurrent inflammation, and reperfusion injury create distinct thrombo-immune microenvironments. This article reviews how NET-driven immunothrombosis affects arterial recanalization, angiographic and tissue reperfusion, HT, and emerging antithrombotic strategies. It also proposes an operational immune-phenotyping framework with candidate biomarkers, assay-dependent research thresholds, sampling time points, and trial-level decision rules.
title: NETs and the thrombo-immune microenvironment: immune heterogeneity in recanalization, reperfusion, hemorrhagic transformation, and antithrombotic strategies.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is an important cause of morbidity, hospitalisation, disability, and mortality, but evidence from Somalia remains fragmented and largely confined to individual hospital-based studies. This scoping review mapped the available evidence on the epidemiology, aetiologies, clinical and diagnostic characteristics, management, outcomes, and research gaps relating to heart failure in Somalia.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to 27 July 2026. Backward citation searching was conducted on 3 August 2026. Original studies reporting heart-failure-specific findings from Somalia, including Somaliland and Puntland, were eligible. Screening was conducted independently by two reviewers. Data were charted using a structured form and verified by a second reviewer. Findings were synthesised descriptively without meta-analysis because of substantial heterogeneity and possible participant overlap.
RESULTS: The searches identified 111 records, of which 56 were duplicates. Fifty-five records underwent title and abstract screening, 13 reports were assessed in full text, and 12 studies published between 2011 and 2025 were included. Eleven studies were associated with a single tertiary hospital in Mogadishu, and no study provided nationally representative or multicentre evidence. Reported aetiologies and associated conditions included hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, anaemia, thyroid dysfunction, renal disease, and thiamine-deficiency wet beriberi. Echocardiography was the principal diagnostic method, but heart-failure definitions and ejection-fraction thresholds varied substantially. Management data were limited mainly to selected populations with thyroid dysfunction, left ventricular thrombus, or wet beriberi. Outcome reporting was sparse and included in-hospital mortality, first-year outcomes in a thrombus cohort, length of stay, stroke, thrombus resolution, and exploratory prognostic indices.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence on heart failure in Somalia is emerging but remains geographically concentrated, methodologically heterogeneous, and insufficient to estimate national burden, treatment coverage, or long-term outcomes. Prospective multicentre studies and a staged heart-failure registry using standardised diagnostic definitions, clear denominators, treatment indicators, and longitudinal follow-up are needed.
title: Heart failure in Somalia: a scoping review of the epidemiology, etiology, clinical characteristics, management, outcomes, and evidence gaps.

abstract: Blood transfusion continues to be a vital part of contemporary healthcare, especially in treating severe anemia, bleeding, trauma, obstetric crises, and critical conditions. In Africa, where transfusion-dependent conditions are prevalent and blood supplies often limited, establishing the best transfusion threshold is crucial for enhancing patient outcomes while maximizing the use of scarce resources. Restrictive transfusion practices that typically use lower hemoglobin thresholds (7-8 g/dL) are now widely accepted globally as they minimize unnecessary transfusions while maintaining safety across various clinical environments. In contrast, liberal approaches, defined by elevated transfusion thresholds (9-10 g/dL), might still be suitable for specific patient groups, such as individuals with acute coronary syndromes, persistent significant bleeding, or serious symptomatic anemia. This review analyzes the existing evidence regarding restrictive vs. liberal blood transfusion strategies in the African context, focusing on clinical outcomes, resource management in healthcare, and prospective avenues for practice and investigation. Research from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and global guidelines consistently shows that restrictive transfusion strategies correlate with similar mortality, morbidity, hospital stay duration, and functional recovery in most stable hospitalized patients, while minimizing transfusion-related complications and preserving limited blood resources. Nevertheless, the direct relevance of evidence produced mainly in high-income countries needs thorough evaluation due to Africa's distinct epidemiological characteristics, healthcare system constraints, and blood service deficiencies. Enhancing patient blood management initiatives, increasing voluntary blood donations, improving transfusion oversight, and producing robust African clinical evidence are essential priorities.
title: Restrictive vs. liberal blood transfusion strategies in Africa: clinical outcomes, resource stewardship, and future directions.

abstract: This paper explores the regionalization of care, organizational components, and critical care transport medicine for cardiogenic shock patients. It discusses the establishment of cardiogenic shock centers, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the necessary infrastructure to ensure optimal patient outcomes. Emphasizing the importance of a regionalized treatment algorithm and transfer strategy, the paper builds on the foundational understanding of managing cardiogenic shock, aiming to provide a comprehensive framework for advanced management and regional transfer strategies essential for high-risk patients.
title: Cardiogenic Shock Systems of Care Best Practices, Part 3: Regionalization of Care, Organizational Components, and Critical Care Transport Medicine.

abstract: This paper describes the contemporary inpatient management of cardiogenic shock, including critical care management and the use of mechanical circulatory support as part of a cardiogenic shock system of care. It highlights the importance of multidisciplinary shock teams for improving patient outcomes through advanced mechanical circulatory support systems and critical care management strategies. Drawing on successful models in trauma care, the paper discusses the evolution of specialized teams, the reduction of care variability, and the enhancement of survival rates through standardized best practices. A case study illustrates the effective implementation of these principles, resulting in improved short-term survival and long-term recovery for patients.
title: Cardiogenic Shock Systems of Care Best Practices. Part 2: The Shock Team and Inpatient Management.

abstract: This paper explores best practices for the prehospital and emergency department evaluation and management of cardiogenic shock, a critical condition marked by high mortality rates, within a contemporary cardiogenic shock system of care. It highlights the significance of early identification and immediate intervention to prevent irreversible cardiac and non-cardiac organ damage. Emphasizing multidisciplinary team-based care and data-driven insights, the paper details optimal strategies for managing cardiogenic shock from initial contact, noting challenges in prehospital identification and treatment due to patient and disease heterogeneity and the variability in response capabilities of prehospital teams.
title: Cardiogenic Shock Systems of Care Best Practices. Part 1: Prehospital and Emergency Department Evaluation and Management.

abstract: MI with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) represents a complex, heterogeneous syndrome with variable underlying mechanisms and substantial morbidity. The role of multimodality cardiovascular imaging in clarifying etiology and guiding therapy continues to evolve. Multimodality imaging offers insights into the pathophysiology of MINOCA. Coronary angiography remains the first-line diagnostic tool to exclude obstructive coronary disease, while adjunctive functional testing can identify epicardial or microvascular vasospasm. Echocardiography evaluates ventricular function, wall motion abnormalities, and embolic sources, whereas cardiac MRI differentiates ischemic from non-ischemic injury, detects myocardial edema, and assesses scar burden. Intravascular imaging can detect plaque rupture, erosion, or thrombus. Nuclear imaging modalities provide a quantitative assessment of microvascular perfusion and coronary flow reserve. Coronary CT angiography may further characterize non-obstructive plaque or coronary anomalies. This review summarizes the comprehensive evaluation of MINOCA. Integrating modalities can improve diagnostic accuracy, identify the underlying etiology, guide targeted therapy, and inform prognosis, underscoring the importance of a multimodal imaging approach.
title: Multimodal Imaging in MI with Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries: Unraveling Pathophysiology and Guiding Management.

abstract: A middle-aged man presented with myalgia, fever, hematemesis, and melena. He was found to have acute kidney injury, acute coronary syndrome, thrombocytopenia, and Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia, raising concern for thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). While awaiting confirmatory testing, empirical plasma exchange was initiated. Initially, minimal red blood cell fragmentation was observed, which later progressed to florid fragmentation. Despite supportive care, his clinical status deteriorated requiring hemodialysis. The presence of TMA, along with ADAMTS13 metalloprotease activity above the diagnostic threshold, worsening kidney function, and negative stool Shiga toxin testing suggested complement-mediated TMA (C-TMA). Stool PCR testing revealed rotavirus. Eculizumab was initiated, resulting in rapid normalization of hematological parameters and eventual renal recovery. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous PLG c.1735G > A (p.Gly579Arg) variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). The importance of serial review of peripheral blood smears and the diagnostic challenge of differentiating TTP, STEC-HUS, and C-TMA are the key learning points.

title: Excellent Response to Eculizumab in a Patient With Complement-Mediated Thrombotic Microangiopathy and a Novel Plasminogen Gene Variant.

abstract:
AIMS: This meta-analysis assessed the long-term impact of beta-blocker therapy on all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who continued beta-blocker use for a minimum of 1 year after hospital discharge.
METHODS: Electronic databases were searched through September 2024 to identify studies comparing long-term outcomes in patients treated with beta-blockers versus those untreated. A random-effects model was used to estimate Hazard Ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 21 studies involving 270 566 patients were included. In pooled analyses, extended beta-blocker was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in STEMI patients [HR: 0.74 (0.66, 0.83); P < 0.0001] and showing non-significant trend toward reducing cardiac death [HR: 0.77 (0.56, 1.04); P = 0.09], an effect observed predominantly in observational studies. However, in randomized controlled trials (N = 3), no significant benefit was demonstrated (all-cause mortality: P = 0.67; cardiac death: P = 0.62). No meaningful differences were found for major adverse cardiovascular events [HR: 0.90 (0.76, 1.07); P = 0.22], myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, or revascularization.
CONCLUSION: Long-term beta-blocker use is associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality among STEMI patients, though this benefit was not seen in RCTs. Effects on other cardiovascular outcomes remain uncertain, highlighting the need for further large-scale trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis; 21 studies involving 270 566 patients, of which 3 were RCTs.
appraisal.main_limitation: The apparent benefit comes predominantly from observational studies, which are open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis suggests that long-term beta-blocker use after STEMI was associated with lower mortality in observational studies but not in randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In pooled analyses, extended beta-blocker was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in STEMI patients [HR: 0.74 (0.66, 0.83); P < 0.0001]; in randomized controlled trials (N = 3), no significant benefit was demonstrated (all-cause mortality: P = 0.67; cardiac death: P = 0.62).
