abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe sex differences in cardiovascular risk factors and reperfusion delays and explore in-hospital outcomes in adults aged 18-50 years with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHOD: This retrospective single-center cohort included 497 consecutive patients (71 [14.3%] women) treated during 2023-2024. Hard major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) comprised all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or stroke. A nonstandard expanded clinical deterioration composite additionally included incident cardiogenic shock and, among patients admitted in Killip class I, incident heart failure. Sex comparisons and Firth penalized logistic models were exploratory.
RESULTS: Mean age was 40.7 +- 5.3 years. Current smoking was more frequent in men (69.0% vs 39.4%; P < 0.001), whereas obesity was more frequent in women (54.9% vs 26.8%; P < 0.001). Age-adjusted median symptom-to-first-medical-contact, first-medical-contact-to-device, and total ischemic times were 46, 10, and 48 minutes longer in women, respectively (all P < 0.001). Hard MACCE occurred in 21 patients (4.2%), incident heart failure occurred in 13 of 390 eligible patients (3.3%), and the expanded composite occurred in 46 patients (9.3%). The expanded composite occurred in 12 of 71 women and 34 of 426 men (16.9% vs 8.0%; unadjusted P = 0.025), and incident cardiogenic shock occurred in 7 women and 13 men (9.9% vs 3.1%; unadjusted P = 0.015). In the parsimonious baseline model, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for female sex was 2.61 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-5.42), attenuating to 1.90 (95% CI, 0.83-4.18) after adding admission Killip class ≥II.
CONCLUSION: Women had a different risk-factor distribution and longer documented ischemic delays. The association between sex and the expanded composite was sensitive to adjustment for baseline clinical severity. Sex-specific outcome estimates are hypothesis-generating given the small female subgroup and event counts. The retrospective single-center design, absence of post-discharge follow-up, and unavailable care- and referral-pathway variables limit causal interpretation.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated whether admission complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices were associated with angiographic high thrombus burden (HTB) in premature myocardial infarction (MI).
METHOD: Consecutive patients aged <45 years with type 1 MI and an identifiable culprit lesion who underwent coronary angiography between 2020 and 2024 were included in this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional analysis. Thrombus burden was assessed using the Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) thrombus grading scale, with occluded vessels reclassified after restoration of coronary flow; HTB was defined as grades 4-5. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) were evaluated using clinically defined multivariable logistic regression models, with and without adjustment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) presentation.
RESULTS: Among 137 patients (77 with STEMI and 60 with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction [NSTEMI]), 81 had an occluded culprit vessel; after restoration of coronary flow, only two lesions remained classified as grade 5. HTB was identified in 79 patients (57.7%) and was associated with STEMI presentation (67.1% vs. 41.4%, P = 0.003) and culprit vessel occlusion (69.6% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.004). Neither NLR (P = 0.54) nor SIRI (P = 0.20) differed significantly between thrombus burden categories, and neither was associated with HTB after adjustment for pre-event characteristics (odds ratio [OR] 1.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.94-1.17 and OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.95-1.35, respectively) or additional adjustment for STEMI presentation (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.92-1.14 and OR 1.08, 95% CI 0.90-1.30, respectively), whereas STEMI presentation remained significantly associated with HTB (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.33-5.68, P = 0.006). The findings were consistent across all sensitivity analyses, and discriminatory performance was negligible (areas under the curve of 0.531 and 0.564). No significant differences in in-hospital outcomes were detected; however, these comparisons were underpowered.
CONCLUSION: In young patients with angiographically confirmed type 1 MI, HTB was associated with STEMI presentation and initial coronary occlusion but not with admission inflammatory indices.

abstract: A 34-year-old woman, 2 days post-partum, was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for management of hypertensive crisis and respiratory failure. An 18-cm left adrenal mass was found on computed tomography (CT), suspicious for a pheochromocytoma. After cardiac arrest, the patient was placed on veno-arteriovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-AV ECMO) given recurrent destabilizing arrhythmias. After successful ECMO decannulation, the patient underwent an uncomplicated resection of her adrenal mass. Although VA-ECMO has been used to support patients with pheochromocytoma, this appears to be the first published case describing the use of a V-AV configuration in the management of a complex cardiac arrest.
title: Case Report: Veno-Arteriovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Management of Pheochromocytoma-Induced Cardiac Arrest in a Post-Partum Patient.

abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers neuroinflammation that can drive CNS injury-induced immunodepression syndrome (CIDS), a peripheral immunosuppressive state associated with increased infection risk. The endocannabinoid system, particularly cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2), represents a promising immunomodulatory target because of its anti-inflammatory actions and limited psychoactive liability. In this study, we investigated whether CB2 receptor activation confers neuroprotection and preserves systemic immune responsiveness in a murine photothrombotic stroke (PTS) model. Male C57BL/6 mice underwent PTS or sham surgery and were treated before stroke induction with the non-selective CB1/CB2 agonist WIN-55212, receptor antagonists, the selective CB2 agonist HU-308, or vehicle. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, cerebral inflammatory gene expression, and intestinal leukocyte-endothelial interactions following lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge were assessed using Neuroscore, TTC staining, RT-qPCR, and intravital microscopy. SIM-A9 microglia were used to evaluate the effects of HU-308 on viability and cytokine release under inflammatory conditions. PTS induced a CIDS-like phenotype characterized by reduced baseline leukocyte rolling and a markedly blunted leukocyte adhesion response following LPS challenge. Non-selective cannabinoid receptor activation improved neurological scores and reduced infarct size, while CB2 blockade abolished this protection. Selective CB2 activation with HU-308 reduced infarct volume, improved neurological outcome, and suppressed stroke-associated TNF and IL-6 expression in the ischemic hemisphere. In vitro, HU-308 reduced TNF release from LPS-stimulated microglia, while IL-4 enhanced microglial viability and IL-10 production. Importantly, HU-308 preserved leukocyte adhesion after LPS challenge following stroke, suggesting maintained peripheral immune responsiveness. These findings identify CB2 receptor activation as a promising neuroimmune strategy that limits acute stroke injury while attenuating the development of CIDS.
title: Selective CB2 receptor activation attenuates neuroinflammation and preserves immune responsiveness after photothrombotic stroke.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between beta-blocker use following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and clinical outcomes remain uncertain in the contemporary era of near-universal early revascularization and drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly for patients with preserved left ventricular function. We sought to determine whether associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied across Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) risk strata.
METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of 11,866 STEMI survivors from two prospective nationwide Korean registries who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with second-generation DES. Patients were categorized by beta-blocker prescription at discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at one year; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability treatment weighting were employed to mitigate confounding. Variation in associations was examined across the continuous GRACE risk spectrum, categorized into low-risk (GRACE <85), intermediate-risk (GRACE 85-179), and high-risk (GRACE ≥180) strata.
RESULTS: Beta-blockers were prescribed to 83.8% of the cohort. After propensity matching, beta-blocker use was associated with lower one-year all-cause mortality (2.7% vs. 4.2%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.91) and MACE (6.0% vs. 8.3%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.55-0.92). These associations attenuated by three years. The GRACE 2.0 score exhibited robust discrimination for mortality (AUC = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.76-0.82). Continuous interaction analyses showed small model-estimated absolute risk differences in low-risk patients (GRACE <85), whereas the largest model-estimated absolute risk difference was observed in intermediate-risk individuals (GRACE 85-179).
CONCLUSIONS: Among STEMI survivors treated with contemporary PCI, associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied according to baseline GRACE risk. No statistically significant association was observed in low-risk individuals (GRACE <85), whereas the association with lower mortality was most evident in the intermediate-risk group (GRACE 85-179). These hypothesis-generating findings warrant evaluation in randomized trials before being used to guide treatment decisions.

abstract: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by severely elevated low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) leading to premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Reducing LDL-C in FH patients is critical to prevent acute coronary syndrome (ACS) events. However, traditional lipid lowering pharmacotherapies therapies have historically been contraindicated in pregnancy. While lipid apheresis has been explored as a safe and efficacious treatment for patients with FH, there is a lack of data and literature supporting its use during pregnancy. Here, we report a case of a 40 year old pregnant patient with FH and recent myocardial infarction (MI) that was treated with lipid apheresis during pregnancy. Apheresis provided substantial LDL-C reduction and ultimately a safe pregnancy without further atherosclerotic complications. Given the limited lipid lowering options for pregnant patients, this case adds to the support of lipid apheresis during pregnancy in high-risk patients.

title: Familial hypercholesterolemia in pregnancy: A case of acute myocardial infarction treated with lipid apheresis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: M1-like and M2-like macrophages are found in acute myocardial infarction, but their activation during and after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) in humans is unclear.
METHODS: Circulating cytokines were measured in 50 patients sampled on day 1 (STEMI) and day 5 (post-STEMI), and healthy subjects (n = 22). Moreover, monocyte-derived M1-like and M2-like macrophages from the three groups were polarized and activated to analyze their phenotype and function (n = 14/group).
RESULTS: STEMI and post-STEMI patients showed elevated levels of CD80, CD86 and inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α in M1-like macrophages, whereas the levels of CD36, CD206, and anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-10 were elevated in M2-like macrophages. Additionally, compared with the conditioned medium of M2-like macrophages, that of M1-like macrophages induced the expression of molecules such as CD54 and CD31 on HUVECs in STEMI and post-STEMI patients. Finally, the levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and MMP-9 in M1-like and M2-like macrophages were similar in the plasma of STEMI and post-STEMI patients, whereas the plasma level of IL-6 was decreased in post-STEMI patients.
CONCLUSIONS: M1-like and M2-like macrophages may participate simultaneously in STEMI and post-STEMI by secreting cytokines and metalloproteinases and through endothelial activation. Furthermore, these cells may contribute to the circulating cytokine microenvironment in these patients.
title: Polarization of monocyte-derived M1-like and M2-like macrophages in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.

abstract: Plaque erosion is increasingly recognized as a critical pathological mechanism in acute coronary syndrome. In this study, we found that microRNA-145 (miR-145) levels were significantly reduced in plaques with grade III-IV stenosis compared with controls. Using an apoE-/- mouse model fed a high-cholesterol diet, we demonstrated that inhibition of miR-145 with antagomiR-145 increased plaque volume and elevated LC3-II expression, a marker of autophagy. Transmission electron microscopy further confirmed a greater abundance of autophagosomes in carotid atherosclerotic plaques from antagomiR-145-treated mice. Mechanistically, miR-145 suppressed both transforming growth factor-β receptor type II (TGFβR-II) expression and autophagy in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Silencing TGFβR-II with specific siRNA recapitulated the effects of antagomiR-145 in cultured VSMCs and in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that miR-145 may protect against carotid plaque progression by downregulating TGFβR-II and limiting autophagy.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
title: MicroRNA-145 hinders carotid plaque growth via suppression of tumor growth factor-β receptor type II and autophagy.

abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in advanced melanoma, but they may accelerate atherosclerosis, particularly in patients with immune-related adverse events (irAEs). A 64-year-old man with stage IV BRAF-wild-type primary thoracic melanoma achieved complete remission after nivolumab plus ipilimumab, but he later developed grade 3 immune-related hepatitis, requiring treatment discontinuation. Three and a half years later, symptomatic peripheral artery disease required revascularization, followed by severe coronary artery disease requiring percutaneous coronary intervention one year later. This case suggests that severe irAEs may be associated with accelerated systemic atherosclerosis, highlighting the importance of long-term cardiovascular surveillance following ICI therapy.
title: Accelerated Systemic Atherosclerosis Following Immune-Related Adverse Events in a Patient with Primary Thoracic Melanoma: A Case of Sequential Coronary and Peripheral Revascularization.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the early predictive efficacy of serum microRNA-376b-5p (miR-376b-5p) combined with immuno-inflammatory markers for all-cause mortality during hospitalization in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted. A total of 316 patients with AMI admitted to the Department of Cardiovascular Medicine of Hengshui People's Hospital from June 2023 to June 2025 were enrolled. Peripheral venous blood was collected immediately before percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI, within 24 hours after admission) to detect serum miR-376b-5p, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR), Systemic Immune Inflammation Index (SII), platelet/lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels. All patients underwent emergency or elective PCI. The outcome event was all-cause mortality during hospitalization, and patients were divided into a death group (52 cases) and a survival group (264 cases). The clinical data and the levels of the aforementioned indicators were compared between the two groups. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify the influencing factors of in-hospital mortality; receiver operator characteristic curves (ROC curves) were plotted to evaluate the predictive value of serum miR-376b-5p and immune inflammation indicators for in-hospital mortality risk in AMI patients, and the area under the curve (AUC) was calculated.
RESULTS: The proportion of patients with Killip class III in the death group and the levels of serum miR-376b-5p, NLR, SII, PLR, and hs-CRP were all higher than those in the survival group (all P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that elevated levels of NLR [odds ratio (OR)=2.097, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.453-3.027], SII (OR=2.011, 95%CI was 1.286-3.144), PLR (OR=1.067, 95%CI was 1.034-1.101), and miR-376b-5p (OR=1.831, 95%CI was 1.282-2.616) were independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI (all P<0.05). The ROC curve indicated that NLR, SII, and PLR all had predictive value for in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI, and the combined prediction of NLR+SII+PLR had a higher predictive value than each individual marker (AUC=0.859), with sensitivity and specificity of 82.69% and 76.89%, respectively. The AUC of serum miR-376b-5p for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI was 0.812, with sensitivity and specificity of 75.00% and 75.38%, respectively. The AUC of serum miR-376b-5p combined with NLR+SII+PLR increased to 0.903, which was higher than that of each individual marker (both P<0.05), with sensitivity and specificity of 88.46% and 82.58%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated serum miR-376b-5p, NLR, SII and PLR levels immediately before PCI are independent risk factors for in-hospital death in AMI patients. Serum miR-376b-5p combined with NLR+SII+PLR has a higher predictive value for in-hospital death in AMI patients.

abstract: Thyroid crisis is caused by an excess of thyroid hormones in the body, leading to a hypermetabolic state and a series of pathological and physiological changes. Clinical manifestations are often non-specific, and in severe cases, it can manifest as multiple organ dysfunction. Acute myocardial infarction combined with thyroid crisis is dangerous and has a high mortality rate. Timely identification and combination of mechanical circulatory support and antithyroid drug treatment are key to improving prognosis. On January 28, 2021, a 49-year-old female patient was admitted to Yanbian University Affiliated Hospital due to "altered mental status for 4 hours, cardiopulmonary during this period". After cardiopulmonary resuscitation, her vital signs were extremely unstable, and electrocardiogram and myocardial enzymes showed acute non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction with severe heart function decline (ejection fraction 26%). On the third day of admission, she underwent veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support, and on the sixth day, she underwent percutaneous coronary stent implantation. After surgery, the patient continued to experience recurrent persistent hyperpyrexia and profuse diaphoresis. Screening revealed a significant increase in thyroid hormones and inhibition of thyroid-stimulating hormone. Combined with thyroid ultrasound and Burch-Wartofsky score>45 points, the diagnosis was confirmed to be hyperthyroidism and thyroid crisis. Subsequently, treatment was given with propylthiouracil, propranolol, and hydrocortisone. On the 9th day of admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) was successfully withdrawn, cardiac function recovered (ejection fraction of 60%), consciousness improved, and finally the patient was weaned off the ventilator and transferred to a primary hospital for rehabilitation. After 3 months of follow-up, normal life and work were resumed. This case study suggests that early application of ECMO combined with antithyroid therapy can significantly improve the prognosis of patients with refractory cardiogenic shock and thyroid crisis. Even without a clear history of hyperthyroidism, acute coronary events may trigger crisis, and clinical vigilance should be maintained.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal myocardial perfusion remains impaired in up to half of patients after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), partly through the distal embolization of thrombus and plaque debris. Reduction of thrombus burden prior to PCI in STEMI has been associated with improved markers of perfusion. However, traditional manual syringe aspiration thrombectomy has demonstrated inconsistent efficacy of thrombus extraction in prior studies. Sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy may achieve more reliable coronary thrombus extraction, with promising early results in non-randomized analyses thus far.
OBJECTIVES: CAPTURE AMI (ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT07687576) will test whether sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy reduces pre-stent thrombus burden compared with standalone PCI in patients with highly thrombotic STEMI.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, single-center randomized controlled trial, 60 patients undergoing primary PCI with TIMI thrombus grade ≥ 4 will be randomized 1:1 to optical coherence tomography (OCT) guided PCI alone, or to sustained mechanical aspiration using the CAT-RX (Penumbra) Aspiration System followed by OCT-guided PCI. The primary endpoint is the absolute change in thrombus burden between two paired pre-PCI OCT runs, measured offline by blinded readers. Exploratory endpoints include pre-PCI thrombus volume, thrombus area and flow area, post-PCI in-stent thromboatheroma and flow volumes, final stent expansion and apposition on OCT, indices of coronary microvascular physiology and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events over 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: CAPTURE AMI will provide randomized, imaging- and physiology-based evidence on the thrombus-modifying efficacy of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in STEMI.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Rationale and design of a randomized controlled trial to evaluate thrombus modification efficacy of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in patients with ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction: The CAPTURE AMI study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving stable anchoring and effective sealing remains the principal limitation of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR). A short-frame, fully recapturable self-expanding valve may expand the procedural margin by enabling iterative repositioning and implantation depth optimisation in non-calcified anatomy.
METHODS: We analysed 13 consecutive patients with symptomatic moderate-to-severe or severe PNAR who underwent transfemoral TAVR with the ScienCrown® (Lepu Medical, Beijing, China) system. The primary endpoint was technical success at exit from the procedure room according to VARC-3 criteria. Secondary endpoints included device success and early safety at 30 days.
RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all patients (13/13, 100%), and device success at 30 days was also achieved in all patients (13/13, 100%). The 30-day early safety endpoint was met in 12 patients (92.3%). The mean prosthesis size was 27.62 ± 1.26 mm, with a mean prosthesis diameter oversizing relative to the average annular diameter of 12.90 ± 3.54%; no balloon predilatation was performed. The mean number of deployment attempts was 1.62 ± 0.77. All procedures were completed without valve embolisation/migration, coronary obstruction, second-valve implantation, or emergency surgery. One patient (7.69%) developed complete atrioventricular block on postoperative day 3 and underwent permanent pacemaker implantation; no additional pacemaker implantations occurred through 30 days. Predischarge diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated no new acute cerebral infarction. At 30 days, there were no deaths, strokes or transient ischaemic attacks, myocardial infarction, life-threatening/major bleeding, major vascular complications, endocarditis, or valve-related reinterventions. Mean transvalvular gradients were 7.67 ± 5.20 mmHg, and all patients had improved or stable NYHA functional class with no moderate or severe residual aortic regurgitation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single-centre series, transfemoral TAVR using a short-frame, fully recapturable self-expanding valve achieved 100% technical success and favourable early safety and haemodynamic performance in selected patients with PNAR. Prospective multicentre studies with longer follow-up and appropriate comparator groups are warranted.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Short-frame, self-expanding, fully recapturable transcatheter aortic valve replacement device in pure aortic regurgitation: Procedural performance and 30-day outcomes.

abstract: In acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, capillary no-reflow denotes that capillary blood flow is still blocked despite successful arterial reperfusion. This is associated with substantially increased mortality and reinfarction risk; nevertheless, no targeted therapy exists so far1,2. Because capillary no-reflow is driven by smooth muscle myosin-mediated hypercontraction of capillary pericytes, we developed R(+)2501, a myosin-specific and capillary-selective vasodilator. In reperfused animal models of acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, direct in vivo imaging showed that R(+)2501 rapidly restored capillary flow, an effect sustained even after rapid drug clearance. Ex vivo experiments confirmed reversal of pericyte constriction directly. Restoration of capillary blood flow, together with clearance of trapped neutrophils, linked resolution of capillary no-reflow to attenuation of an early driver of reperfusion injury. R(+)2501 enhanced capillary perfusion while preserving coronary autoregulation and systemic haemodynamics, and markedly improved survival during acute reperfusion. We further found that acute myocardial infarction induced renal capillary no-reflow, which was reversed by R(+)2501, suggesting that capillary no-reflow contributes to the pathophysiology of cardiorenal syndrome type I. These findings establish pericyte-targeted smooth muscle myosin inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to restore microvascular perfusion and halt the ischaemic cascade across organs, while defining a specific physiological role for capillaries and pericytes in circulatory regulation.
title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-infarction ventricular septal rupture (VSR) remains a life-threatening mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction. We evaluated the feasibility of an Impella-bridge strategy for scheduled VSR repair.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 10 consecutive patients with post-infarction VSR who were transferred to our institution and managed with Impella support. Outcomes included achievement of scheduled repair and serial changes in hemodynamic parameters and organ dysfunction during the bridging period.
RESULTS: The median age was 74 years. All patients received Impella 2.5 or CP support after transfer; veno-arterial extracorporeal life support was added in four patients, and Impella support was upgraded in one patient. The median duration from Impella initiation to VSR repair was 8 (7, 10) days. Scheduled repair was achieved in nine patients (90%). Mean pulmonary artery pressure, central venous pressure, plasma B-type natriuretic peptide levels, and lactate decreased over time before repair, whereas non-CNS SOFA scores increased during bridging.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with post-infarction VSR, an Impella-bridge strategy may help achieve scheduled VSR repair with improved hemodynamic stabilization; however, SOFA-defined abnormalities, organ support requirements, and device-related complications were observed during the bridging period. Further studies are needed to define patient selection, management strategies, and the optimal timing of repair for this strategy.
title: Physiological Effects and Clinical Limitations of Impella-Bridge Strategy for Post-Infarction Ventricular Septal Rupture.

abstract: Although Achilles tendon thickening (ATT) is associated with adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whether its prognostic impact differs over time between acute (ACS) and chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 1,362 patients who underwent successful PCI and assessment of ATT using soft X-ray radiography. ATT was defined as Achilles tendon thickness ≥8.0 in men and ≥7.5 mm in women. MACE, including death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, stroke, and target vessel revascularization, were investigated for up to 3 years. To evaluate temporal differences, we conducted the Kaplan-Meier method with landmark analysis and time-segmented Cox proportional hazards analyses dividing follow-up into ≤ 1 year and 1-3 years after PCI. ATT was observed in 228 patients (16.7%), who had a significantly higher incidence of MACE compared to patients without ATT. In ACS patients (n = 387), ATT was independently associated with an increased risk of MACE within 1 year, but not beyond 1 year. Conversely, in CCS patients (n = 975), ATT was not associated with early events, but was significantly associated with increased MACE risk during 1-3 years after PCI. Similar trends were observed after excluding familial hypercholesterolemia. These findings suggest different temporal patterns in the association between ATT and MACE after PCI in patients with ACS and CCS, which may provide additional insights into risk stratification during follow-up.
title: Temporal patterns of the association between Achilles tendon thickening and clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention in acute and chronic coronary syndromes.

abstract: The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following drug-eluting stent implantation remains uncertain. We evaluated extended DAPT versus aspirin monotherapy in patients who completed approximately 12 months of uneventful DAPT after percutaneous coronary intervention. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing these strategies. The primary outcome was myocardial infarction (MI); secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, stroke, and clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2-5). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model. Certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and trial sequential analysis was performed for MI. Six trials involving 28,601 patients were included. Extended DAPT significantly reduced MI compared with aspirin monotherapy (RR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85; P = 0.001; I2 = 37%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, or stroke. Clinically relevant bleeding was also not significantly different (RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.66-2.15; P = 0.56), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 87%) and certainty was low. GRADE certainty was high for MI, cardiac death, and repeat revascularization; moderate for all-cause mortality; and low for stent thrombosis and bleeding. Trial sequential analysis for MI crossed the conventional significance boundary but not the trial sequential monitoring boundary or required information size. Extended DAPT may reduce MI, but individualized assessment of ischemic and bleeding risk remains important, and further adequately powered trials are warranted.

title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Aspirin Monotherapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With GRADE Evaluation and Trial Sequential Analysis.

abstract: Imaging remains the foundation of prosthetic valve surveillance because it identifies valve morphology, lesion mechanism, and hemodynamic severity. However, acoustic shadowing, eccentric or multiple regurgitant jets, loading conditions, and reader variability can complicate assessment, particularly for paravalvular regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High shear stress unfolds von Willebrand factor (VWF), promotes proteolysis of its high-molecular-weight multimers, and produces a measurable defect in primary hemostasis. Multimer analysis, closure time with adenosine diphosphate (CT-ADP), and the VWF activity-to-antigen ratio therefore provide a biologic signal of abnormal flow rather than an anatomic image. Prospective studies show that VWF abnormalities track residual paravalvular regurgitation during transcatheter aortic valve replacement, occur with dysfunctional prostheses, change after mitral paravalvular-leak repair, and are associated with bleeding. The evidence nevertheless remains observational; most diagnostic cohorts are small and single-center, thresholds lack independent validation, assays are vulnerable to hematologic and preanalytic confounding, and no completed randomized trial has shown that VWF-guided management improves outcomes. VWF testing is best viewed as an investigational adjunct when imaging and the clinical picture are discordant or when prosthetic dysfunction coexists with otherwise unexplained bleeding. It should not replace guideline-directed echocardiography or be used for routine surveillance outside research protocols.
title: Von Willebrand Factor Biomarkers in Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction: An Adjunct to Imaging and Hemodynamic Assessment.

abstract: To estimate the cumulative incidence of short-term complications across different transcatheter heart valve (THV) prostheses used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol. Observational studies published from 2002 through May 2024 that included patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing predominantly transfemoral TAVR and reported prosthesis-specific complications were eligible. Although the original protocol intended to evaluate both short- and long-term complications, long-term outcomes were too sparse and inconsistently reported for robust pooled analyses; therefore, the present analysis focuses on short-term complications. Pooled cumulative incidences were calculated using random-effects models. We included 242 studies comprising 181,187 patients. SAPIEN 3 had the lowest incidence of moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak (PVL) (1.04%, 95% CI 0.69-1.55) and stroke (1.87%, 95% CI 1.64-2.14), whereas ACURATE neo2 had the lowest incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) (7.7%, 95% CI 5.82-10.11). Evolut PRO and SAPIEN 3 showed among the lowest rates of major vascular complications (3.56%, 95% CI 2.77-4.57 and 3.87%, 95% CI 3.22-4.66, respectively) and major or life-threatening bleeding (2.96%, 95% CI 2.09-4.17 and 4.8%, 95% CI 4.04-5.69, respectively). Short-term complications have decreased with newer-generation THV prostheses. PVL remains more frequent with self-expanding valves, whereas PPI is the most frequent complication and is generally less frequent with balloon-expandable valves and ACURATE neo2. Stroke rates have changed little across newer generations, and annular rupture, coronary artery obstruction, and valve embolization remain rare (< 1%).
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Short-Term Complications of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PROLONG-TAVR).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis. Among patients with left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, recovery of LV function after TAVI is heterogeneous, and reliable tools for pre-procedural risk stratification and patient counseling remain limited.
AIMS: We sought to identify simple pre-procedural predictors of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI and to develop a clinically applicable risk score to support patient counseling and post-procedural management.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with severe aortic stenosis and baseline LV ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40% enrolled in a large multicenter registry in Japan. The primary outcome was complete LVEF normalization (LVEF > 50%) at 1 year after TAVI. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression in a derivation cohort, and an exploratory weighted score was constructed. The score was preliminarily assessed in a separate single-center cohort.
RESULTS: The derivation cohort comprised 177 patients (median age 84 years; 44% women), of whom 94 (53%) achieved LVEF normalization. Lower body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-0.95; p = 0.004), higher aortic valve peak velocity (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.40-4.29; p = 0.002), and smaller LV end-diastolic diameter (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p = 0.020) were independently associated with LVEF normalization. The derived score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability groups (15%, 45%, and 71%, respectively; p < 0.001), with consistent discrimination in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: A simple exploratory score incorporating body mass index, transvalvular peak velocity, and LV size was associated with the probability of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI. This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Pre-Procedural Prediction of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Normalization After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comparative evidence for M-TEER performed at centers with versus without on-site cardiac surgery is lacking. We compared early outcomes at two centers that shared the same interventional operator team but differed in the availability of on-site cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected registry data from 64 consecutive patients with severe (4+) MR treated at a center without on-site cardiac surgery (no-CCH, n = 21) and a center with on-site cardiac surgery (CCH, n = 43). The same interventional operator team performed every procedure. At the no-CCH center, surgical expertise was provided through a shared Heart Team and a formal emergency transfer pathway. The cohorts were treated in sequential calendar periods. Principal comparative endpoints were MVARC device and procedural success at 30 days. Exploratory non-inferiority analyses used margins of -12.5% and -10%.
RESULTS: MVARC technical success was 100% versus 97.7%. Device and procedural success were each 81.0% versus 72.1% (risk difference [RD] +8.9%, 95% CI -14.9 to +27.5; p = 0.547). Freedom from major MVARC serious adverse events was 95.2% versus 95.3%. Twelve of 16 device-success failures involved a mean transmitral gradient ≥ 5 mmHg. Surgical conversion and in-hospital death were 0% in both centers.
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary same-team comparison, 30-day MVARC device and procedural success rates were 81.0% at the no-CCH center and 72.1% at the CCH center. Confidence intervals were wide and non-inferiority was not established. These findings support prospective evaluation of network-based M-TEER programs with shared interventional expertise and formal surgical backup.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair at Centers With and Without On-Site Cardiac Surgery: A Comparative Registry With a Shared Interventional Team.

abstract: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system. All had baseline office systolic BP (SBP) > 155 mmHg and diastolic BP > 90 mmHg despite at least three antihypertensive drugs at the maximum tolerated doses. Clinical response required both an office SBP reduction ≥ 10 mm Hg and a mean 24-h ambulatory SBP reduction ≥ 5 mm Hg. Outcomes were assessed within 72 h and at 1 month. All procedures were technically successful. At 72 h, 15 patients (83.3%) met both response criteria; all had an office SBP reduction ≥ 20 mm Hg. At 1 month, 16 (88.9%) were responders and 2 (11.1%) were nonresponders. Among responders, five discontinued one drug and continued dual therapy, whereas 11 continued three drugs at reduced doses. Procedural events included one iatrogenic renal artery dissection, one femoral artery dissection with perforation, one guidewire fracture successfully retrieved with an endovascular snare, and two femoral hematomas. Renal function did not deteriorate. In conclusion, radiofrequency RDN was technically feasible and was followed by an early clinical response in most patients. The small sample, short follow-up, and absence of a control group preclude definitive efficacy conclusions.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Percutaneous Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension in a High-Risk Real-World Population: Preliminary Results From a Prospective Single-Center Experience.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite intensive lipid-lowering therapy, early attainment of the guideline-recommended LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) target after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains suboptimal. Baseline factors associated with early LDL-C target attainment remain incompletely characterized, particularly the role of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]. We aimed to assess early LDL-C target attainment after a first ACS and identify baseline factors associated with target attainment, with a particular focus on Lp(a).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive hospitalized adults with a first ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2025 and April 2026. The primary endpoint was attainment of the guideline-recommended LDL-C target at early follow-up, defined as LDL-C < 55 mg/dL and a ≥ 50% reduction from baseline. Associations between clinical variables and LDL-C target attainment were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Eighty-two patients were included; 70.7% were male and 37.2% had elevated Lp(a) levels. At a median follow-up of 5 weeks (IQR, 4-6), 31.7% attained the LDL-C target despite prescription of high-intensity statin therapy at discharge. In the multivariable model, low Lp(a) (OR 8.72; 95% CI 2.04-37.33), current smoking (OR 5.29; 95% CI 1.42-19.69), and ezetimibe use in addition to high-intensity statin therapy at discharge (OR 5.28; 95% CI 1.31-21.32) were associated with LDL-C target attainment.
CONCLUSIONS: Early LDL-C target attainment after a first ACS remained limited despite routine prescription of high-intensity statin therapy. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a lower likelihood of attaining the LDL-C target. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.
title: Lipoprotein(a) and early LDL-cholesterol target attainment after a first acute coronary syndrome: a real-world cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is a common heart disease worldwide, and the morbidity and mortality rates among Chinese residents continue to rise. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can improve survival rates, but long-term management is required after the procedure. Traditional interventions have shortcomings such as dependence on medical institutions and the lack of personalized treatment plans. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Artificial Intelligence-based Health Education Precision Linkage System (AI-HEALS) in improving self-health management among young and middle-aged patients after PCI.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-center, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group controlled trial. Eligible patients aged 18-59 years from Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, will be randomly allocated at a 1:1 ratio to receive either standard care plus the AI-HEALS intervention (intervention group) or standard care alone (control group). The primary outcome is the change in self-management ability from baseline to the 3-month intervention endpoint, assessed using the Coronary Heart Disease Self-Management Behavior Scale (CSMS). Secondary outcomes include medication adherence, dietary behavior, exercise frequency, and psychological indicators. Assuming an effect size of d = 0.69, 80% statistical power, and a two-sided significance level of α = 0.05, with an anticipated 20% dropout rate, the required sample size was calculated as 86 participants (43 per group). Primary analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. Generalized linear mixed models will be used for repeated measures outcomes, and multiple imputation by chained equations will handle missing data. Quantitative findings will be integrated with qualitative data from structured interviews conducted among intervention group participants.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University (Approval No.[2024] 409-002). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conferences.Clinical Trial Registration: http://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2500100519.
title: Effect of an artificial intelligence health education accurately linking system on self-management in young and middle-aged patients after percutaneous coronary intervention: a protocol.

abstract: Distinguishing a left ventricular thrombus from a cardiac tumor is challenging when a large mass arises at an atypical non-apical site, particularly in a patient with cancer. We describe a 37-year-old man with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutant non-small cell lung cancer receiving almonertinib who developed a broad-based posterior wall left ventricular mass while cancer imaging remained stable. At detection, the reported left ventricular ejection fraction estimate was 55%, and no regional wall motion abnormality was documented. Cardiac CT showed no calcification or appreciable arterial- or delayed-phase enhancement, and Doppler echocardiography showed no internal flow. Low-mechanical-index contrast-enhanced echocardiography showed no appreciable internal perfusion in the contemporaneous examination report; later archived images also showed persistent absence of perfusion, although early-phase cine loops were not retained for retrospective reassessment. These concordant avascular features supported the presence of a thrombus but were not diagnostic. Cardiac magnetic resonance was recommended but declined because of financial concerns, and histopathology was unavailable. After approximately 9 months of prescribed edoxaban 60 mg once daily with reported adherence, the maximum linear dimension increased from 39.7 to 51.0 mm. A posterior wall regional wall motion abnormality was first documented 5 months after mass detection and therefore could not explain the lesion already present at detection. Edoxaban levels and edoxaban-calibrated anti-factor Xa activity were not measured, and human interaction data for almonertinib and edoxaban were unavailable. This case highlights the need to keep the diagnosis qualified and to reassess alternative pathology and anticoagulant exposure when an imaging-supported left ventricular thrombus follows an unexpected course.
title: Case Report: An enlarging left ventricular mass during anticoagulation in a patient receiving almonertinib after thoracic radiotherapy: diagnostic uncertainty and individualized management.

abstract: Primary cardiac intimal sarcoma is a rare malignant mesenchymal neoplasm whose intracavitary appearance may mimic other cardiac masses. We report a woman in her early 60s with recurrent palpitations and occasional exertional dyspnea. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) demonstrated a giant, highly mobile, irregular multilobulated mass occupying most of the left ventricular cavity, with slit-like interlobular clefts and a probable broad-based attachment near the apical interventricular septum. Low-velocity color Doppler demonstrated residual flow around and between lobules, while continuous-wave Doppler showed a peak left ventricular outflow tract velocity of 3.09 m/s and a peak instantaneous gradient of 38 mmHg. Cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed a large relatively hypoattenuating left ventricular mass with heterogeneous enhancement: some portions showed no obvious enhancement, whereas others showed mild enhancement; the interface with the ventricular wall was locally indistinct, so myocardial involvement could not be excluded. After induction of general anesthesia, intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) showed the mass nearly filling the left ventricular cavity, but the attachment and fine multilobulated architecture were less clearly seen than on preoperative TTE. The patient underwent tumor resection with concomitant mitral valve repair. Histology showed mildly atypical spindle cells with fascicular and focal perivascular growth, readily identified mitotic figures, and mild myxoid stromal change. Immunohistochemistry showed MDM2 positivity, and fluorescence in situ hybridization demonstrated MDM2 and CDK4 amplification, supporting the diagnosis of intimal sarcoma. At approximately 2 weeks after surgery, follow-up TTE showed no residual or recurrent left ventricular mass, preserved left ventricular systolic function, minimal residual mitral regurgitation, and a peak outflow tract velocity of 0.92 m/s without residual obstruction. Postoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT performed at approximately the same time identified no definite extracardiac primary tumor or obvious distant metastatic lesions. The case illustrates how multimodality imaging can define the anatomy and hemodynamic effects of a rare left ventricular intimal sarcoma, while histopathologic and molecular findings remain essential for definitive diagnosis.
title: Primary left ventricular intimal sarcoma: a case report of multimodality imaging and molecular confirmation.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to assess the comprehensive national trends in deaths related to pneumonia and AMI in the US from 1999 to 2023.
METHODS: CDC wonder multiple cause of death database was used to extract data of elderly (≥65 years) with pneumonia and AMI as main or contributing cause of death. Age-Adjusted Mortality Rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated. Trends were stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, state, urban-rural classification, census region, ten-year age group, and place of death.
RESULTS: A total of 186,411 deaths associated with pneumonia and AMI during 1999-2023 were identified. The cumulative AAMR was 17.76 during 1999-2020, and 14.2 during 2021-2023. A significant decline in AAMR was found through the study period (AAPC:-4.26, 95% CI -6.71 to -1.74). The AAMR of men was higher than women, and the decrease of AAMR was steeper in women (AAPC:-4.38, 95% CI -6.78 to -1.92 among women vs. -4.07, 95% CI -5.68 to -2.43 among men). NH American Indian or Alaska Native has the highest AAMR, while NH Asian or Pacific Islander had the lowest AAPC (-5.03, 95% CI -7.95 to -2.02). Non-metropolitan had higher AAMR (22.93 vs. 16.59) and AAPC (-1.69 vs. -3.51) than metropolitan. South region showed the highest AAMR and AAPC compared to other census regions.
CONCLUSIONS: The AAMR per 100,000 of pneumonia and AMI decreased among older adults in the US during 1999-2023, with higher mortality burden among men, NH American Indian or Alaska Native, rural area, and South region.
title: Trends in mortality due to acute myocardial infarction and pneumonia among older adults in the U.S.: a CDC wonder analysis (1999-2023).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) poses unique challenges. We report a case in which an apparently benign anatomy resulted in failure of conventional delivery strategies and required a novel balloon-assisted bailout technique.
CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old man with a background history of liver cirrhosis presented with severe aortic stenosis due to type 1 BAV. The patient was in Child-Pugh class A with model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) score of 14; hence, he was planned for TAVI in view of high surgical risk. Pre-procedural computed tomography showed a favourable left ventricular (LV)-aortic angle, but the fused non-coronary and right-coronary cusp behaved like functional horizontal anatomy. Various previously described wire and balloon-assisted techniques failed to deliver the valve. A novel balloon-assisted modified 'shoe-horn' technique, by inflating a 16 mm balloon in non-coronary sinus, altered the delivery trajectory and enabled successful valve delivery.
DISCUSSION: BAV with right non-coronary cusps fusion may behave like horizontal anatomy, despite favourable LV-aortic angle. A modified balloon-assisted shoe-horn technique can facilitate valve delivery when conventional methods fail. This case highlights an under-recognized mechanism of valve delivery failure in BAV and emphasizes the importance of preparedness for advanced bailout strategies.
title: Modified balloon-assisted shoehorn technique for transcatheter aortic valve implantation in functionally horizontal anatomy: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a critical syndrome with a very high fatality rate, and in-hospital mortality ranges from 27% to 51%. Among the various prognostic approaches, serum biomarkers have attracted considerable attention because they are easy to measure, inexpensive, and can be monitored dynamically. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) is a novel composite marker that integrates red blood cell heterogeneity (reflecting inflammation and oxidative stress) with albumin levels (indicating nutritional and anti-inflammatory capacity). It has shown initial promise for risk stratification in critically ill patients. However, the independent prognostic value of RAR specifically in CS remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to systematically evaluate the ability of RAR to predict 28-day mortality in these patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study used a two-cohort retrospective design. The internal training cohort was derived from CS patients in the MIMIC-IV v2.2 database, and the external validation cohort came from the medical record system of the Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University. To explore the association between RAR and short-term poor outcomes in severe CS, we applied multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression, subgroup analysis, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. To develop a simple prediction model, the internal cohort was randomly split into a training set and a test set in a 7:3 ratio. In the training set, we used five methods-Boruta algorithm, LASSO-Cox regression, random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GBDT), and support vector machine (SVM)-to select key features associated with poor CS prognosis, covering laboratory indicators, comorbidities, demographic characteristics, and vital signs. Based on the selected feature variables, we built prognostic prediction models using multivariable Cox regression in each of the three cohorts. The discriminative ability of the model was compared with that of traditional disease severity scores using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, with the area under the curve (AUC) as the measure of predictive performance.
RESULT: A total of 1,314 CS patients were included in this study. In the fully adjusted model (Model 3), both continuous RAR and RAR quartiles were independently associated with 28-day adverse outcomes. For 28-day ICU mortality, each unit increase in RAR was associated with a 13.4% higher risk (HR 1.134, 95% CI 1.076-1.197, p < 0.001); compared with the lowest quartile (Q1), the highest quartile (Q4) had a significantly increased risk of 51.7% (HR 1.517, 95% CI 1.123-2.049, p = 0.007). For 28-day in-hospital mortality, the HR for continuous RAR was 1.085 (95% CI 1.031-1.141, p = 0.002), and the HR for Q4 vs. Q1 was 1.576 (95% CI 1.196-2.076, p = 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis further confirmed a significant positive dose-response relationship between RAR and mortality (overall p < 0.05). In the external validation cohort, the predictive value of RAR for 28-day ICU mortality remained consistent and was even stronger (HR for continuous RAR: 1.359, 95% CI 1.177-1.568, p < 0.001). the RAR-based risk prediction model showed moderate but consistent discriminative performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.71, 0.70, and 0.75 in the training, test, and external validation sets, respectively, all of which were higher than those of traditional severity scores (all DeLong tests p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated in both cohorts that RAR is an independent associated with 28-day mortality risk in CS patients. The prediction model built on RAR and five other clinical features exhibited good clinical performance. With further prospective validation, this model may become a valuable exploratory tool for risk stratification in CS patients.
keywords: red cell distribution width-to- albumin ratio (RAR)
title: The red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio and 28-day mortality in patients with severe cardiogenic shock: a retrospective cohort study based on MIMIC-IV with single-center external validation.

abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is increasingly used for refractory cardiac arrest, although evidence for a survival benefit remains heterogeneous and appears highly dependent on patient selection and systems of care. We report the case of a previously healthy 36-year-old woman who presented with acute fulminant myocarditis and cardiogenic shock. Following an in-hospital cardiac arrest unresponsive to conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation, bedside ECPR was initiated using peripheral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) as a bridge to longer-term mechanical circulatory support with a biventricular assist device (BiVAD). After conversion to central BiVAD support, the patient was listed super-urgently and subsequently underwent successful donation-after-circulatory-death heart transplantation. She was discharged home neurologically intact and remains well five months after discharge. This case demonstrates that when deterioration is imminent and standard therapies have failed, ECPR may provide life-saving support while preparing for definitive mechanical circulatory support, even when most members of the clinical team lack ECPR experience. Timely leadership and coordinated multidisciplinary expertise were the key to achieving a successful outcome in this case.
title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation as a Bridge to Cardiac Transplantation in Refractory Cardiac Arrest Due to Fulminant Myocarditis: A Case Report.

abstract: A young, physically active patient with no cardiac symptoms presented with abdominal pain and was found, through incidental findings of elevated BNP, cardiomegaly, and new ECG changes, to have severe HFrEF with a left ventricular apical thrombus. Early cardiac evaluation changed management and led to complete thrombus resolution.
keywords: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
title: Abdominal Pain as the First Presentation of Severe Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction and Left Ventricular Thrombus in a Young Asymptomatic Patient: A Diagnostic Interception.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with excess cardiovascular risk, but within-patient changes in complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices at the onset of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are not well described. We compared pre-event and acute-phase values in the same patients and contextualized pre-event values against a healthy cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, within-patient paired study reviewed hospital records from July 1, 2018, to December 30, 2025 (approximately 90 months). Among 3,960 hospitalized patients with RA, 89 had clinician-confirmed ACS and qualifying paired CBC measurements. Acute-phase CBCs were obtained within 24 hours after symptom onset, and pre-event CBCs were the most recent routine measurements obtained more than 14 days before the event. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated and natural log-transformed. Pre-event values were also compared with a healthy cohort (n = 110), with age- and sex-adjusted analyses used because residual demographic imbalance was present.
RESULTS: Pre-event log(NLR), log(SII), and log(SIRI) were higher in the RA cohort than in healthy controls and remained higher after adjustment for age and sex (all P< 0.001). Within-patient analyses showed increases during ACS, with mean Δlog values of 0.466 for NLR, 0.508 for SII, and 0.381 for SIRI (all Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q< 0.001). Neutrophilia increased from 11.2% before the event to 41.6% during ACS (McNemar P< 0.001). Exploratory subgroup estimates were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across several small strata; changes did not differ materially between remission/low and moderate/high RA activity groups.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with RA who developed ACS, CBC-derived inflammatory indices were higher than in a healthy comparison cohort before the event and increased further within the first 24 hours of ACS. The paired design quantifies change relative to each patient's own pre-event value. Without a non-RA ACS comparator, however, the study cannot establish RA-specific inflammatory priming or a causal chronic-to-acute mechanism. Prospective studies with serial sampling and clinical outcomes are needed.
title: Dynamic changes in CBC-derived inflammatory indices before and during acute coronary syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a within-patient paired study.

abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an important alternative strategy for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), particularly when long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) is contraindicated or poorly tolerated. Initially developed as a surgical technique based on ligation or excision of the left atrial appendage, LAAC has progressively shifted toward refined, minimally invasive transcatheter approaches. Randomized and observational data have established non-inferiority to warfarin, and non-inferiority compared with direct oral anticoagulants has also been suggested in selected high-risk cohorts and is currently under prospective evaluation in pivotal trials. At the same time, indications for LAAC are expanding beyond the classical high-bleeding-risk population, now encompassing patients undergoing atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and those with only moderate thromboembolic risk but intolerance to OAC. Parallel advances in device design aimed at improving anatomical conformability, sealing performance, and surface biocompatibility seek to reduce peri-device leak (PDL), device-related thrombus (DRT), and bleeding and may allow for simplified or shortened post-procedural antithrombotic regimens. This narrative review summarizes the historical evolution of LAAC from surgical to contemporary transcatheter solutions, outlines key clinical evidence versus medical therapy, and discusses emerging implant-based and implant-free technologies. As evidence accumulates from ongoing randomized controlled trials, LAAC may transition from a niche intervention to a more widely adopted, guideline-supported component of AF management. However, broader implementation will depend on robust demonstration of long-term safety and efficacy, including clarification of PDL-, DRT-, and bleeding-related trade-offs, to define when LAAC can serve not only as an alternative to OAC but also as a tailored option for selected NVAF patients.
journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management
title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Past, Present, and Future.

abstract: Hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis is usually managed as one local variant of central venous stenosis, yet its mechanical environment is distinctive. The vein follows a long, multi-axially curved retrosternal course through a narrow window between the manubrium and the aortic arch, bounded by two separate junctions, the lateral venous angle and the medial brachiocephalic-caval confluence. An implanted stent is therefore exposed to focal unidirectional compression, cyclic bending and torsion, short landing zones, and branch-coverage risk, conditions not reproduced by circumferential radial testing. The sternum-aortic corridor reported in affected patients, about 4.6 mm, is narrower than the nominal diameter of stents deployed there, placing the implied compression at or beyond the lowest level characterized in published bench comparisons; pulsatile durability testing covers only cardiac-frequency diametric cycling, and pooled cohorts seldom report the segment separately. This Review synthesizes published anatomical, clinical, engineering, and computational evidence and reframes the problem as a site-specific biomechanical and device-validation question with three validation priority stages (P1-P3). P1 (required) evaluates base-platform mechanics, structure, fatigue, and deployment: focal crush resistance and recovery, radial resistive versus chronic outward force, bending and torsion durability, foreshortening, deployment accuracy, branch preservation and, for covered constructs, covering fatigue. P2 (required) evaluates anatomy-specific hemodynamics of the same platform by patient-specific computational modeling and experimental flow testing, reporting shear, residence, gradient, edge-recirculation, branch-flow, and pressure-loss metrics against matched comparators. P3 (optional) covers an added drug, coating, or surface; baseline thrombogenicity, hemocompatibility, tissue compatibility, and structural integrity remain required base-platform attributes. We state two falsifiable hypotheses with the bench, computational, imaging, and clinical evidence that would support or refute them: H1 (mechanical), that resistance to focal unidirectional crush may govern stent deformation, durability, and in-stent restenosis localization more strongly than circumferential radial resistive force alone; and H2 (hemodynamic), that stent architecture and edge configuration may generate spatially reproducible disturbed-flow regions adding incremental prediction of later in-stent restenosis distribution beyond anatomical and procedural covariates. Direct prospective evidence remains sparse: the framework is a problem definition and validation roadmap, not a clinical algorithm, device ranking, or evidence of superior performance.
title: Stent biomechanics in hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis: from site-specific loading to a staged device-validation framework.

abstract: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect (SVASD) is frequently associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return and may be missed on routine transthoracic echocardiography because of its superior and posterior location. We report a 68-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation who presented with dyspnea and marked right-sided chamber enlargement. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging identified a 33 × 21-mm superior SVASD, anomalous drainage of the right upper and middle pulmonary veins, and a persistent left superior vena cava. The Qp/Qs was 3.7 by cardiac magnetic resonance and 3.2 by right heart catheterization, with a low indexed pulmonary vascular resistance of 1.7 Wood units·m², supporting surgical repair. Three and a half months after successful repair, the patient presented with transient loss of consciousness. Cardiac evaluation showed no residual interatrial shunt, no intracardiac thrombus, and no significant arrhythmia, although right ventricular dysfunction persisted. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated asymmetric cortical and deep gray matter abnormalities. Cerebrospinal fluid showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, mildly elevated protein, preserved glucose, and positive enterovirus polymerase chain reaction. These findings supported enteroviral central nervous system infection. Because atrial fibrillation and postoperative cardiac abnormalities provided competing explanations for the neurologic presentation, the exact mechanism of the transient loss of consciousness remained uncertain. This case illustrates the importance of avoiding diagnostic anchoring when new neurologic symptoms develop after congenital cardiac surgery.
title: Late-Detected Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect and Subsequent Enteroviral Central Nervous System Infection: A Case Report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a two-lead ECG (wECG), acquired using a self-applicable, wrist-worn device, provides diagnostic value in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) detection.
METHODS: Seventy-one patients with AMI, 26 with other cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), and 54 healthy controls were enrolled in the study. To acquire lead I, one electrode of the wrist-worn device was touched with the index finger of the opposite hand, while another lead was acquired by touching the electrode on the strap to a specific part of the body. The diagnostic value of the wECG is evaluated either directly or through synthesis of the standard 12-lead ECG using an echo state network.
RESULTS: Using the standard ECG, an AMI detector based on a convolutional neural network yields a sensitivity of 0.86 and a specificity of 0.71; the corresponding figures for blinded cardiologist diagnosis are 0.77/0.88. Using the synthesized ECG, the V3 electrode touch site yields the best performance, with a sensitivity/specificity of 0.84/0.71 for AMI detection and 0.67/0.86 for cardiologist diagnosis. Compared to the synthesized ECG across all touch sites, use of the wECG results in a substantially lower sensitivity, reduced by 0.12-0.13, while the specificity is comparable or slightly higher. Implementation of a two-stage approach, consisting of detector-based screening followed by cardiologist review of positive cases, results in correct decisions in 63% of the AMI cases using either the synthesized ECG or the wECG.
CONCLUSION: The two-lead ECG acquired with a wrist-worn device offers diagnostic value and enables screening for AMI.
