abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: A recently developed cardiac troponin T (cTnT) assay measuring intact or mildly fragmented cTnT (long cTnT) has shown promise in improving the accuracy of myocardial infarction (MI) detection compared to the commercial high sensitivity cTnT (hs-cTnT) assay. However, data on patients with kidney dysfunction are limited. We compared the performance of long and hs-cTnT in MI diagnostics across the full spectrum of kidney function.
METHODS: In this prospective study, consecutive patients presenting at the emergency department with an elevated (≥14 ng/L) hs-cTnT were recruited. Long and hs-cTnT were measured on admission and kidney function was determined with plasma creatinine (Crea), cystatin C (CysC) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using contemporary equations with Crea, CysC or both (Crea-CysC) together. The association of eGFR with hs-cTnT and long cTnT concentrations and the discriminative ability of hs-cTnT and long cTnT for type 1 MI and any MI were evaluated.
RESULTS: In total, 1811 patients were included, 205 (11.3%) had a MI and 204 (11.3%) had a history of chronic kidney disease. The overall median (interquartile range) Crea-eGFR, CysC-eGFR and Crea-CysC-eGFR were 71 (51-87), 52 (36-69) and 63 (44-79) ml/min/1.73m2. In patients without MI, long cTnT showed no consistent association with kidney function (β=0.0008, P = 0.050; β=0.0005, P = 0.222; β=0.0006, P = 0.182 for Crea-eGFR, CysC-eGFR and Crea-CysC-eGFR, respectively), whereas hs-cTnT was inversely associated with kidney function (β=-0.0032, -0.0035 and - 0.0035; all P < 0.001). Long cTnT demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared with hs-cTnT for the detection of MI (P < 0.001), with the advantage becoming progressively more pronounced with lower eGFR irrespective of equation used.
CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to hs-cTnT, long cTnT is unaffected by kidney function and outperforms hs-cTnT in the detection of MI, with the greatest diagnostic advantage observed in patients with lower eGFR.
journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
title: Long forms of cardiac troponin T are independent of kidney function and improve the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term device durability and phenotype-specific safety outcomes after interatrial shunting require further characterization.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the procedural success, device durability, and heart failure (HF) phenotype-specific safety outcomes of an interatrial shunt in the RELIEVE-HF trial.
METHODS: Randomized patients were assigned 1:1 to shunt or sham control with prespecified stratification by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (LVEF ≤40%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF >40%). Procedural performance, device durability, serious adverse events (SAEs), major adverse cardiovascular or neurological events (MACNE), major bleeding, and renal outcomes were assessed through 2 years.
RESULTS: Among 605 enrolled patients (508 randomized; 97 roll-in), shunt implantation was attempted in 370 and was successful in 369 (99.7%). Among implanted patients with follow-up (n = 348), no device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). Prespecified LVEF-stratified analyses demonstrated divergent safety profiles. In HFrEF, shunt therapy was not associated with excess all-cause MACNE, major bleeding, or renal decline and was associated with lower SAE burden. In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline.
CONCLUSIONS: Interatrial shunt implantation was mechanically reliable and durable through 2 years. Safety outcomes differed by HF phenotype, with no evidence of excess clinical safety events in HFrEF but increased adverse events in HFpEF. These findings support phenotype-specific evaluation of interatrial shunt therapy. (REducing Lung congestion symptoms using the v-wavE shunt in adVancEd Heart Failure [RELIEVE-HF]; NCT03499236).

In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abbreviated dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy is increasingly used after percutaneous coronary intervention, but whether its effects are consistent across age is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: The authors examined age-related differences in outcomes with P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy vs 12-month DAPT after percutaneous coronary intervention.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the Short-Term DAPT After Deployment of Bioabsorbable Polymer Everolimus-Eluting Stent randomized trial stratified 1,387 patients at age 75 years. The primary endpoint was net adverse clinical events (NACE)-major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5) plus major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events-through 12 months.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 365 days (Q1-Q3: 353-365); 210 patients (15.1%) were ≥75 years. NACE occurred in 25 of 1,177 patients <75 years (2.4%; 95% CI: 1.4-3.3) and 7 of 210 aged ≥75 years (3.7%; 95% CI: 1.0-6.4). NACE did not differ between monotherapy and 12-month DAPT in patients <75 years (8 of 587 [1.6%; 95% CI: 0.5-2.8] vs 17 of 590 [3.1%; 95% CI: 1.6-4.6]; HR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.20-1.09) or ≥75 years (3 of 107 [3.3%; 95% CI: 0.0-6.9] vs 4 of 103 [4.2%; 95% CI: 0.1-8.1]; HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.16-3.17), with no treatment-age interaction (P = 0.637 dichotomized; P = 0.173 continuous). Major bleeding increased with age, whereas major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after 3-month DAPT was associated with similar net clinical outcomes to 12-month DAPT in both younger and older patients, with no significant treatment-age heterogeneity. These findings support consideration of abbreviated DAPT as a reasonable treatment option in selected older adults, although larger studies are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT03447379.
title: P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs Dual Antiplatelet Therapy by Age After PCI: A SHARE Substudy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) are at high-risk, and retrograde CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is often avoided because of hemodynamic and safety concerns.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated CTO-PCI strategy selection and outcomes according to LVEF, focusing on patients selected for a primary retrograde approach.
METHODS: We analyzed 11,458 patients from the Japanese CTO-PCI Expert Registry (2014-2022), including 1,692 with LVEF <40% and 9,766 with LVEF ≥40%. Core laboratory-adjudicated angiographic findings, procedural strategies, and in-hospital outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Patients with LVEF <40% had more complex coronary anatomy. A primary retrograde approach was selected in 489 of 1,692 procedures (28.9%) in the LVEF <40% group and 2,500 of 9,766 procedures (25.6%) in the LVEF ≥40% group (OR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.33; P = 0.005). Overall technical and procedural success rates were comparable between groups. In the primary retrograde cohort, technical success was achieved in 450 of 489 procedures (92.0%) with LVEF <40% and 2,186 of 2,494 procedures (87.7%) with LVEF ≥40% (OR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.14-2.37; P = 0.005). In-hospital mortality, stroke, contrast-induced nephropathy, and preprocedural mechanical circulatory support were more frequent in patients with LVEF <40%, whereas other in-hospital adverse events were generally similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced LVEF was associated with more frequent selection of a primary retrograde approach. Among selected patients undergoing primary retrograde CTO-PCI, technical success remained high despite greater anatomical complexity.
title: Strategy and Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion With Reduced Ejection Fraction.

abstract:
ANATOMY: Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies that may lead to myocardial ischemia through a coronary steal phenomenon, particularly when associated with coronary artery disease.
PATHOLOGY: We describe a case of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) diagnosis of multiple coronary-pulmonary artery fistulas associated with chronic occlusion of the right coronary artery, in a 66-year-old man presenting with unstable angina.
IMAGING CORRELATION: CCTA and echocardiography were used for evaluation of procedural planning in an acute setting.
TREATMENT: The fistulas were effectively treated with surgical exclusion combined with coronary artery bypass grafting, yielding an optimal result on the postoperative computed tomography scan.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Coronary fistulas are rare but important causes of myocardial ischemia. This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.
title: Cardiac CT Planning of Surgical Treatment of Multiple Coronary-Pulmonary Fistulas With Chronic Coronary Occlusion.

abstract:
TOPIC OF CONTROVERSY: Whether valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is preferred for structural valve degeneration of a Freestyle stentless aortic root in a young adult, and whether a Ross procedure at index surgery would have better served lifetime management.
CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with a failed stentless aortic root (implanted at age 20 for bicuspid aortic valve regurgitation) presented with severe bioprosthetic regurgitation and ventricular dilatation. Transfemoral ViV TAVI with a 29-mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 Ultra Resilia was performed successfully.
PRO VIEWPOINT: ViV TAVI avoids redo sternotomy, preserves future options, and aligns with patient preference to avoid anticoagulation.
CON VIEWPOINT: Redo SAVR with a mechanical valve-and a Ross procedure at the index operation-may offer superior lifetime sequencing, avoiding constraints of successive transcatheter implants.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Lifetime planning must begin at the index operation; both ViV TAVI and redo SAVR require heart team deliberation with explicit consideration of all future interventions.
title: Valve-in-Root TAVI vs Redo Surgery in a Young Adult With Failed Bioprosthesis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe bioprosthetic valve dysfunction presents a diagnostic challenge because distinguishing reversible leaflet thrombosis from structural valve degeneration may not be possible using echocardiography alone.
CASE SUMMARY: A patient with end-stage renal disease, previous bioprosthetic mitral and aortic valve replacement, and prior valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement presented with heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Multimodality imaging demonstrated severe bioprosthetic mitral valve dysfunction with restricted leaflet motion, raising suspicion for leaflet thrombosis. Empiric intravenous unfractionated heparin was commenced while cardiac computed tomography was arranged. Computed tomography excluded hypoattenuated leaflet thickening and demonstrated severe leaflet calcification, confirming structural valve degeneration. After heart team discussion, transseptal valve-in-valve mitral replacement resulted in rapid hemodynamic and clinical recovery.
DISCUSSION: Serial multimodality imaging guided escalation from anticoagulation to definitive valve intervention.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent prosthetic valve dysfunction after anticoagulation should prompt reassessment for structural valve degeneration. Transseptal valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement is an effective treatment for selected high-surgical-risk patients.
title: Severe Bioprosthetic Mitral Valve Dysfunction: Multimodality Imaging Identifies Structural Valve Degeneration and Guides Valve-in-Valve TMVR.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report a case of acute pericarditis caused by an occult penetrating foreign body manifesting as an ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction mimic.
CASE SUMMARY: The patient initially presented with chest pain, increased cardiac troponin I, and ST-segment elevation. Following emergency intravenous thrombolysis and urgent coronary angiography, an alternative etiology was suspected. Subsequent verification of the medical history and imaging examinations ultimately identified the culprit: a nail. The patient received prompt treatment, and the pericardial foreign body was successfully extracted.
DISCUSSION: Acute pericarditis and acute myocardial infarction are common causes of acute chest pain. Diagnostic confusion and treatment delays may arise due to overlapping symptoms, elevation of cardiac biomarkers, ST-segment elevation, cognitive bias, and incomplete history taking.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: This case highlights the value of bedside echocardiography combined with chest radiography. In patients with suspected ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, it is crucial to differentiate acute coronary occlusion from other causes, especially foreign body-induced pericarditis.
title: Occult Penetrating Trauma: A STEMI Mimic Hiding in Plain Sight.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction and mitral regurgitation are underrepresented in pivotal transcatheter edge-to-edge repair trials and are often ineligible for transplantation or LV assist devices, leaving limited options when guideline-directed medical therapy fails.
CASE SUMMARY: We describe 6 patients aged 38 to 82 years with LV ejection fraction 10% to 20% and severe (4+) to torrential (5+) mitral regurgitation, 4 patients presenting in or near cardiogenic shock requiring inotropic, vasopressor, or intra-aortic balloon pump support. All underwent transcatheter edge-to-edge repair as our multidisciplinary heart team strategy evolved.
DISCUSSION: With increasing experience, the heart team incorporated individualized pharmacologic or temporary mechanical support, preprocedural hemodynamic optimization, and anatomy-driven device selection. One patient initially referred for palliative care was subsequently reassessed and treated. This series illustrates how iterative multidisciplinary learning may expand transcatheter edge-to-edge repair candidacy in carefully selected, high-risk patients with advanced heart failure and profound ventricular dysfunction and limited therapeutic alternatives.
keywords: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Advanced Heart Failure and Ventricular Dysfunction: An Evolving Heart Team Strategy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Native mitral leaflet interference is a rare cause of acute intraprosthetic regurgitation after transcatheter mitral valve-in-ring replacement (TMViR).
CASE SUMMARY: An 83-year-old woman with previous surgical mitral annuloplasty underwent transseptal TMViR for severe regurgitation from anterior mitral leaflet flail. After implantation of a 32-mm Myval Octapro valve, severe intraprosthetic regurgitation developed. High atrial positioning and prosthesis tilting allowed the flail anterior leaflet to overhang the ventricular valve edge and impair prosthetic leaflet coaptation. Balloon postdilation failed and increased instability. A contralateral gooseneck snare enabled controlled recrossing and deeper valve-in-valve-in-ring implantation, with complete regurgitation resolution and no left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
DISCUSSION: Native leaflet interference should be considered after TMViR when acute intraprosthetic regurgitation occurs.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Snare-assisted recrossing may provide selective bailout when marked tilt or instability prevents safe conventional recrossing.
title: Native Leaflet Interference After Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Ring: Snare-Assisted Valve-in-Valve-in-Ring Bailout.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe argatroban anticoagulation in a patient with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia undergoing transcarotid transcatheter aortic valve replacement under conscious sedation.
KEY STEPS: Vitamin K antagonist therapy was discontinued and intravenous argatroban initiated, with anti-factor IIa monitoring. Procedural anticoagulation consisted of an argatroban bolus followed by continuous infusion guided by activated clotting time. An ultrasound-guided intermediate cervical plexus block with remifentanil sedation maintained consciousness for neurological assessment. Argatroban was resumed postoperatively before transition to vitamin K antagonist therapy.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Surgical carotid access under argatroban requires careful balancing of thrombotic and bleeding risks. Maintaining consciousness for neurological monitoring adds an anesthetic challenge, requiring adequate anesthesia for carotid exposure while avoiding excessive sedation; an intermediate cervical plexus block may cause dysphagia.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Integrating argatroban anticoagulation with locoregional anesthesia may address the competing requirements of surgical carotid access and continuous neurological monitoring in patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia undergoing transcarotid transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
title: Argatroban Anticoagulation for Transcarotid TAVR Under Conscious Sedation in a Patient With Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late clinical decline after heart transplantation is commonly attributed to rejection, cardiac allograft vasculopathy, or ventricular dysfunction. Progressive structural valvular disease is less frequently emphasized when graft systolic function is preserved.
CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old woman underwent orthotopic heart transplantation at age 13 for familial restrictive cardiomyopathy. Nearly 10 years later, she developed progressive exertional fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and dizziness despite preserved graft systolic function and no significant cardiac allograft vasculopathy. Serial imaging demonstrated severe mitral regurgitation, moderate to severe aortic regurgitation, and moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation. She underwent redo sternotomy with bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement and tricuspid repair, with preserved ventricular function and clinical recovery at early follow-up.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights progressive multivalvular disease as an important valve-level cause of late clinical decline after heart transplantation.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider structural valvular disease in symptomatic long-term heart transplant recipients with preserved graft function.
title: Late Progressive Multivalvular Regurgitation After Heart Transplantation With Preserved Graft Function.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction concurrent with endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm is an extremely rare and life-threatening emergency, currently lacking unified clinical guidelines for reference.
CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old male patient underwent endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and experienced persistent hypotension during the procedure. Postprocedural electrocardiogram and cardiac enzyme tests confirmed acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. The patient underwent emergency coronary angiography, which revealed severe stenosis, followed by successful balloon angioplasty. The patient recovered and was discharged following multidisciplinary postoperative care.
DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates the management principles for multiple life-threatening complications, where the clinical challenge formed by the huge retroperitoneal hematoma (bleeding risk) and the requirement for antiplatelet therapy after urgent revascularization (ischemic risk) was properly addressed. Through accurate identification, precise intervention, and multidisciplinary team collaboration, the patient was successfully rescued. This case provides a referable practical path for clinical decision-making in similar rare scenarios, highlighting the critical value of individualized treatment strategies.
title: Intraoperative ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicating Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both renal sympathetic nerves and perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) drive hypertension. However, evidence regarding renal denervation (RDN) in end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains limited.
FIRST-IN-HUMAN SUMMARY: A 74-year-old man with diabetic chronic kidney disease stage 5 presented with refractory hypertension despite treatment with 4 antihypertensive agents and intravenous nitroprusside. He underwent bilateral laparoscopic-assisted RDN combined with PRAT debulking without complications. At 5-month follow-up, office and ambulatory blood pressures were substantially reduced, while renal function and medications remained stable.
DISCUSSION: Our case provides preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility of a combined laparoscopic RDN and PRAT debulking strategy in a patient with ESRD and refractory hypertension.
NOVELTY: To our knowledge, this is the first report of RDN combined with PRAT debulking using the laparoscopic system in ESRD.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This combined intervention offers a promising new therapeutic option for refractory hypertension in patients with advanced kidney disease.
title: Laparoscopic Renal Denervation and Perirenal Adipose Tissue Debulking for Refractory Hypertension in End-Stage Renal Disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right atrial appendage atrial tachycardia (AT) during pregnancy is rare and can progress to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy and shock.
CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old woman at 36 weeks and 5 days of gestation presented with fatigue, dyspnea, and narrow-complex tachycardia at 190-210 beats/min. Echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 18%. After failed medical therapy, cardioversion, and esophageal pacing, she underwent emergency cesarean delivery and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Mapping localized the AT to the base of the right atrial appendage; endocardial radiofrequency (RF) and pulsed field ablation produced only transient sinus rhythm. Thoracoscopic bipolar RF ablation with surgical clamping restored durable sinus rhythm.
CONCLUSIONS: Appendage-origin AT in pregnancy can progress rapidly to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy, and timely venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support improves the prognosis. RF and pulsed field ablation may be insufficient for deep or possibly epicardial substrates; surgical ablation should be considered when catheter ablation fails.
title: Pregnancy-Related Right Atrial Appendage Tachycardia Requiring ECMO and Hybrid Ablation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is the main minimally invasive therapy for severe mitral regurgitation (MR) in patients at high surgical risk. Roughly 10% of patients develop recurrent MR within 1 year postoperatively. Postprocedural mitral anatomical distortion complicates reintervention, rendering recurrent MR management a common clinical challenge.
CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old man with multivalvular heart disease, chronic heart failure, multiple implantable devices and dialysis-dependent end-stage renal disease presented with symptomatic severe recurrent MR secondary to delayed anterior mitral leaflet perforation after TEER. Under combined fluoroscopic and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, our multidisciplinary team performed transcatheter closure of the perforation using a vascular plug. MR was markedly alleviated, heart failure symptoms resolved, and the patient recovered uneventfully before discharge.
DISCUSSION: TEER-related leaflet perforation caused severe recurrent MR. Percutaneous plug closure successfully downgraded MR to trivial, confirming the feasibility of this approach for mitral leaflet perforation.
title: Vascular Plug Closure of Delayed Leaflet Perforation Post-TEER in Patient With Multiple Implantable Devices.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise intolerance may persist in patients with chronic coronary syndrome despite successful percutaneous coronary intervention. Evidence regarding low-frequency whole-body vibration training (LF-WBVT) remains limited.
CASE SUMMARY: A 62-year-old woman underwent cardiac rehabilitation for reduced exercise capacity 1 year after percutaneous coronary intervention. Baseline peak oxygen uptake was 14.3 mL/kg/min. She completed an 8-week program consisting of moderate-intensity continuous aerobic training, LF-WBVT (3-9 Hz), and isometric lower-extremity resistance exercise. Peak oxygen uptake increased to 22.2 mL/kg/min, and oxygen pulse increased from 8.7 to 9.6 mL/beat. No major adverse cardiovascular events occurred.
DISCUSSION: This combined strategy improved both cardiorespiratory fitness and metabolic health. The triglyceride-glucose index reduction is a novel finding, suggesting lower future cardiovascular risk.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: LF-WBVT with isometric exercise is safe in selected patients with chronic coronary syndrome. Triglyceride-glucose index may serve as a metabolic biomarker for rehabilitation outcomes.
title: Low-Frequency Whole-Body Vibration and Isometric Exercise in Cardiac Rehabilitation: Improved Capacity and Triglyceride-Glucose Index.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The study objective was to describe an optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided strategy for stepwise calcium modification in a large protruding calcified nodule with circumferential calcium.
KEY STEPS: Rotational atherectomy was used to establish device crossability and modify superficial calcium. Serial OCT was performed to assess residual calcified nodule protrusion, circumferential calcium, lumen gain, and calcium fracture. When crossability was restored but substantial mechanical constraint persisted, the strategy was escalated to intravascular lithotripsy, followed by cutting-balloon dilation. Final OCT was used to confirm stent expansion and apposition.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Restoration of device crossability does not necessarily indicate adequate lesion preparation, whereas excessive burr escalation may increase procedural risk. Serial OCT should be used to assess the response to each modification step and guide timely strategy escalation.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: OCT assessment may guide precise calcium modification and prevent stent underexpansion in complex calcified lesions.
title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Calcium Modification for a Complex Calcified Nodule With Circumferential Calcium: From Debulking to Fracturing.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are conventionally implanted transfemorally, with transjugular and subclavian routes reported as alternatives. Axillary access has not previously been reported.
FIH SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman with chronic sacral wounds became temporary-pacing dependent following an inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. An LP was selected given infection risk. Because of a right femoral deep venous thrombosis, an abscess at the left femoral site, and restricted neck mobility limiting internal jugular access, she underwent left axillary vein implantation of an LP.
DISCUSSION: Axillary access served as a feasible alternative route. A septal position was achieved by rotating the delivery system counterclockwise, opposite the transfemoral direction, while a perpendicular sterile table supported the extracorporeal catheter length.
NOVELTY: This is the first reported axillary vein implantation of an LP.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Axillary venous access is a feasible bailout route for LP implantation when femoral and internal jugular access are unavailable.
title: First-in-Human Axillary Vein Implantation of a Leadless Pacemaker: Breaking the Access Barrier.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent in-stent restenosis (ISR) driven by accelerated neoatherosclerosis and high residual inflammatory risk remains a formidable clinical challenge.
CASE SUMMARY: A 50-year-old noncompliant, obese, diabetic woman presented with recurrent multivessel ISR. Intravascular ultrasound confirmed intrastent thin-cap fibroatheromas. Despite multiple drug-coated balloon interventions, intensive lipid-lowering via inclisiran, and glycemic control with tirzepatide, she suffered relentless ISR driven by highly elevated interleukin-6. She received advanced anti-inflammatory therapies and was referred for bypass surgery.
DISCUSSION: Literature highlights that targeting upstream inflammation is critical when standard therapies fail to halt malignant neoatherosclerosis. This case interests readers by demonstrating compliance optimization via long-acting agents and navigating advanced anti-inflammatory pathways (colchicine escalation, canakinumab) for refractory ISR.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Biomarkers like interleukin-6 must be evaluated in refractory ISR; persistent residual inflammation warrants advanced anti-inflammatory therapies or early surgical revascularization.
title: Recurrent In-Stent Restenosis and Accelerated Neoatherosclerosis in a Middle-Aged Woman With High Inflammatory Burden.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is usually displayed in 2-dimensional planes with few fixed 3-dimensional (3D) views, which may limit appreciation of the spatial relationship between plaques and vessel. We describe initial clinical experience with CorVIS, an artificial intelligence-based coronary visualization system, in complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 cases-2 chronic total occlusions and 1 heavily calcified lesion-in which CorVIS provided freely rotatable 3D reconstructions with plaque characterization. In each case, the CorVIS corresponded to specific procedural decisions, including the chosen crossing approach and calcium-modification strategy. All 3 procedures were completed successfully.
DISCUSSION: These cases suggest that artificial intelligence-based 3D CCTA reconstruction may complement conventional imaging for preprocedural planning of complex PCI. The efficacy of CorVIS in facilitating complex PCI remains to be verified in further prospective studies.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In this initial case series, CorVIS delivered freely rotatable 3D CCTA reconstructions and plaque characterization, informing key procedural decisions for complex PCI.
title: Coronary Visual Intelligence System (CorVIS) Guided Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Excessive aorto-ostial stent protrusion requires appropriate adjustment to achieve an optimal landing zone. We report a successful resolution using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided tip detection (TD) and the stent push technique under distal anchor balloon support.
KEY STEPS: A drug-eluting stent deployed at the right coronary artery ostium protruded excessively into the aorta, causing guiding catheter dislodgment. Using the IVUS-guided TD method, a guidewire was successfully advanced into the stent lumen. Under distal anchor balloon support, the stent push technique was performed to correct the protruding stent to an optimal position.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: IVUS-guided TD enables real-time visualization of the proximal stent edge and wire tip, facilitating accurate rewiring. Distal anchor balloon support provides sufficient backup for effective longitudinal stent deformation.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: The IVUS-guided TD method combined with a distal anchor balloon-supported stent push technique is an effective strategy for managing excessive aorto-ostial stent protrusion.
title: IVUS-Guided Tip Detection and Distal Anchor Assisted Stent Push for a Protruding Ostial Stent.

abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is increasingly used in patients with cardiogenic shock, advanced heart failure, and severe respiratory failure; however, anticoagulation management remains challenging due to the competing risks of thrombosis, bleeding, hemolysis, and device dysfunction. In this review, we synthesize contemporary evidence on anticoagulant selection, monitoring strategies, and device-specific management across major MCS platforms, including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, temporary ventricular assist devices, Impella devices, and durable left ventricular assist devices. Unfractionated heparin remains the cornerstone anticoagulant across most MCS platforms, while anti-factor Xa-guided monitoring is increasingly incorporated into clinical practice in many centers alongside activated partial thromboplastin time and other monitoring modalities. Direct thrombin inhibitors represent important alternatives, particularly for patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or heparin resistance. Recent advances include bicarbonate-based purge strategies for Impella support and evolving antithrombotic approaches in HeartMate 3 recipients, introduced by the ARIES-HM3 trial. Emerging investigational strategies, including direct oral anticoagulants, factor XI/XII inhibition, and precision anticoagulation approaches, show promise for improving hemocompatibility; however, current evidence remains limited, and further prospective studies are required before these strategies can be routinely adopted. Overall, contemporary evidence supports an individualized approach to anticoagulation based on device characteristics, patient-specific risk profiles, and current guideline recommendations, while highlighting important knowledge gaps that warrant further high-quality prospective investigation.
title: Anticoagulation in Mechanical Circulatory Support: Contemporary Challenges and Future Directions in Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether routine immune-inflammatory biomarkers predict no-reflow (NR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients, quantify their incremental predictive value over clinical variables, and build an interpretable peri-procedural prediction model.
METHODS: This prospective cohort recruited 382 AMI patients undergoing PCI. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates; confounder-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed nonlinear associations. LASSO regression selected core predictors with variance inflation factor (VIF) assessing multicollinearity. Four machine-learning models underwent 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation and SHAP interpretation. Incremental value was tested via ΔAUC (DeLong test), continuous NRI, and IDI. Stratified regression and interaction tests evaluated AMI-subtype effect modification.
RESULTS: NR occurred in 91 patients (23.8%). Multiple neutrophil-centred indices independently correlated with NR after adjustment. Seven predictors constituted the final model (all VIF < 2.5). LightGBM yielded optimal discrimination and modest net clinical benefit (AUC 0.799, 95% CI 0.699-0.899); AMI subtype and neutrophil-related markers dominated SHAP outputs. Neutrophil count, NAR, NHR, SII, and PIV significantly improved discrimination. Seven of the 16 tested markers yielded significant continuous NRI, and ten demonstrated significant IDI gains. In stratified analyses, neutrophil count, NLR, and MHR were associated with NR in STEMI but not NSTEMI patients; interaction tests found no significant AMI-subtype effect modification.
CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural neutrophil-centred inflammatory biomarkers are independent correlates of post-PCI NR and offer incremental predictive value over conventional clinical variables. The interpretable LightGBM model supports peri-procedural NR risk stratification, though external validation and recalibration are mandatory before clinical application.
title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of immune-inflammatory biomarkers for predicting no-reflow in patients with acute myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.
title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis.

abstract:
AIMS: Atrial enlargement is a complex maladaptive process related to pressure and volume overload. Left atrial reverse remodeling (LARR) has been described as a result of medical and interventional therapies. We sought to explore LARR prevalence and its prognostic implications following mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER).
METHODS AND RESULTS: Four-hundred and twenty-five patients from the MERIT-TEER (Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing M-TEER) who received a successful procedure from 2012 to 2024 with available left atrial volume (LAV) have been analyzed. LARR was defined as a reduction in LAV of at least 15%. LARR prevalence and its association with the risk of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality at 4 years' follow-up were evaluated in the overall population and according to mitral regurgitation etiology.At short-term follow-up, LARR was observed in 124 patients (29.20%). LARR was more prevalent among primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) patients compared with those with ventricular secondary (vSMR) and atrial secondary mitral regurgitation (aSMR) (37.23, 27.19, and 18.33%; P = 0.017). At long-term follow-up, the composite outcome occurred in 153 patients (36.2%). LARR was independently associated with lower risk of events in the overall population [adjusted hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.85, P = 0.005] and among vSMR patients (adjusted hazard ratio 0.43, 95% CI 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), but not in aSMR or PMR.
CONCLUSION: LARR was observed in less than one-third of patients undergoing M-TEER (29.2%), occurring more frequently in PMR. LARR was independently associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization in the overall population and particularly in patients with vSMR.
title: Prevalence and prognostic role of left atrial reverse remodeling in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: insights from the Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.

abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic significance of systematically screened extra-coronary vascular disease in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains incompletely understood. We investigated the prevalence and prognostic impact of polyvascular disease (PVD) identified using a routine vascular screening strategy in patients with AMI.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center observational study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement and carotid ultrasonography were routinely performed during index hospitalization. PVD was defined as the presence of peripheral artery disease (ABI ≤ 0.90) and/or carotid artery disease, defined as carotid plaque according to the Mannheim consensus (maximal wall thickness ≥ 1.5 mm) or ≥50% carotid stenosis. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and unplanned coronary revascularization after discharge.
RESULTS: Among 233 eligible patients, PVD was identified in 73 patients (31.3%), including 55 (23.6%) with single-territory PVD and 18 (7.7%) with multiterritory PVD. During a median follow-up of 419 days, the primary endpoint occurred in 43 patients. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a graded decrease in event-free survival according to increasing PVD burden (log-rank P = 0.014; P for trend = 0.007). In Cox proportional hazards analysis, the presence of PVD was significantly associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, and renal dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: PVD is common in patients with AMI and is associated with poor long-term clinical outcomes. Routine systematic assessment of extra-coronary vascular disease may improve cardiovascular risk stratification.
title: Polyvascular disease by systematic vascular screening and adverse outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
Letter to the Editor regarding: 'Conscious sedation versus general anesthesia for transesophageal echocardiography guidance of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion'.
Response to the letter to the editor regarding 'Conscious sedation versus general anesthesia for transesophageal echocardiography guidance of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion'.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.
METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.
RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).
CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide population-based cohort study; 5259 eligible patients, 292 propensity score-matched patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small matched sample and residual confounding in an observational design.
appraisal.one_line: Danish cohort study of GLP-1 receptor agonist use and outcomes after aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Generates a hypothesis for incretin-based therapy after valve replacement, a population excluded from the major cardiovascular outcome trials.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral venoarterial (VA)-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, and therefore the risk of LV distension, pulmonary edema, and cardiac stasis. Balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) provides atrial-level unloading, but the durability of LV venting remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of BAS for LV venting in patients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock (CS).
METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective study of consecutive adults with CS supported with peripheral VA-ECMO who underwent BAS for LV unloading at an academic center (2019-2024). The primary endpoint was LV venting failure, a composite of pulmonary edema, LV distension, spontaneous echocardiographic contrast, LV or aortic root thrombus, stroke due to ECMO, or escalation to additional mechanical support.
RESULTS: A total of 28 patients were included in the study. BAS resulted in a significant reduction in mean left atrial pressure (20.5-13.5 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Durable LV venting was achieved in a subset of patients; however, LV venting failure occurred in 53.6%, driven primarily by pulmonary edema. Pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting-failure status (interaction P = 0.018). Model-estimated pulse pressure was higher at 48 hours (P = 0.010) and 72 hours (P = 0.031) among patients who ultimately did not experience venting failure.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for CS, BAS achieves atrial-level decompression and may provide durable LV venting in select patients, although venting failure remains common. Observed arterial pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting failure status.
title: Atrial Septostomy and Left Ventricular Venting During Peripheral VA-ECMO.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of patients undergoing coronary angiography have angina with no obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Among ANOCA patients, 2 distinct groups exist: patients with and without a history of prior obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate associations between history of prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI and coronary microvascular and vasomotor dysfunction endotypes in ANOCA patients.
METHODS: A prospective Coronary Microvascular and Vasomotor Dysfunction Registry of consecutive ANOCA patients undergoing invasive coronary functional testing (ICFT).
RESULTS: Among 624 ANOCA patients undergoing ICFT, 11% had prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI. ANOCA patients with prior obstructive CAD had a higher prevalence of males, were older, and had higher rates of cardiovascular risk factors. Prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI was associated with an 11-point lower Seattle Angina Questionnaire 7 summary score in unadjusted (β -11.0; 95% CI: -17.0 to -4.4; P = 0.001) and adjusted models. Patients with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had a higher prevalence of epicardial spasm by angiographic criteria (70% vs 34%; P < 0.001) and 4.55-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm in unadjusted (OR: 4.55; 95% CI: 2.65-8.07; P < 0.001) and adjusted models, with similar odds of coronary microvascular dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: Among ANOCA patients, those with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had over a 4-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive ICFT in ANOCA patients with prior PCI.
title: ANOCA Patients With Prior Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease and PCI Have Higher Odds of Epicardial Spasm.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicates 5-10% of acute myocardial infarctions (AMI) and remains associated with in-hospital mortality of approximately 40-50%. The clinical predictors established do not fully explain why patients with comparable infarct severity have divergent outcomes, raising the hypothesis that host genetic factors modulate susceptibility to CS. Therefore, we conducted this systematic review to synthesize published evidence describing genetic variants associated with the development of CS complicating AMI.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through Jun 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidance. Eligible studies included any study type enrolling adults with AMI and reporting association of any specific genetic variants with CS.
RESULTS: Of 480 records identified, 9 studies met inclusion criteria. Reported variants clustered into five biological pathways: inflammatory/cytokine signaling (TNF-α -308G>A, IFN-γ +874T>A, RANTES/CCL5 -403G>A), lipid metabolism (APOE ε2/ε3/ε4), thrombosis and fibrinolysis (PAI-1/SERPINE1 4G/4 G, MTHFR C677T/A1298C), clonal myeloproliferative disease (JAK2 V617F), and hypercoagulable/antioxidant pathways (protein C/S-related thrombophilia, PON1 Q192R). The APOE ε3/4 genotype and the TNF-2 allele showed the most direct associations with CS incidence and survival, respectively; JAK2 V617F and combined PAI-1/MTHFR variants were reported in severe, thrombus-driven case presentations of CS. RANTES and PON1 genotypes were not associated with CS occurrence, although circulating RANTES levels correlated with CS severity.
CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence is limited, but the variants reported to date span inflammatory, lipid, thrombotic, and myeloproliferative pathways, suggesting that genetic susceptibility to CS complicating AMI is polygenic and mechanistically heterogeneous, requiring prospective genetic association studies.
title: Genetic predisposition to cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications.
OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes.
METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events.
RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157).
CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.
title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcarotid access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is the most commonly used alternate access in the United States. Real-world evidence on transcarotid access using the Evolut self-expanding valve based on larger numbers of patients may help inform treatment optimization towards better outcomes.
METHODS: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry™ was queried for patients undergoing native TAVR using transcarotid access with an Evolut (January 2015-December 2024). In-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year outcomes are reported.
RESULTS: We identified 2,105 patients (mean age 78.3±7.9 years) with mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted risk of mortality 6.4±5.3. Most were high/extreme surgical risk (60.0%) with New York Heart Association class III/IV heart failure symptoms (66.8%) and mean baseline Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) Score 45.3±25.4. Implant success was 99.6% primarily using general anesthesia (95.8%) with median procedure time of 88.0 (Q1=68.0, Q3=115.0) minutes. Median length of stay was 2.0 (Q1=1.0, Q3=3.0) days; 89.0% were discharged to home. In-hospital, 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality was 2.1%, 3.8% and 16.5%; stroke occurred in 3.1%, 3.8% and 5.1% of patients, respectively. At 30 days, major vascular complications (1.9%), valve related (0.4%) and non-valve related (10.9%) readmissions were low. The mean change in KCCQ score from baseline to 1-year was +30.5±27.1 points.
CONCLUSIONS: Transcarotid TAVR with the Evolut TAV is an effective, safe approach for patients with unfavorable iliofemoral anatomy. Heart teams should become facile with this technique to provide optimal care across the anatomy spectrum.
title: Transcarotid Access for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With the Evolut Self-Expanding Valve: Outcomes from a Real-World Registry.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of music on the management of anxiety and stress in patients awaiting coronary transluminal angioplasty.
METHOD: A double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted according to the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) guidelines. The study was carried out at the hemodynamics unit of the Onofre Lopes University Hospital from August to December 2024, with 52 participants equally divided into an intervention and a control group. Both groups were fitted with headphones before the procedure, but only patients in the intervention group were exposed to music. Data were collected using a sociodemographic and clinical data form, the Beck Anxiety Inventory, and Lipp's Stress Symptoms Inventory for Adults.
RESULTS: Although there were no significant reductions in the intergroup analysis, the intragroup analysis showed that music influenced a reduction in anxiety and heart rate in the intervention group. However, there was no evidence of an effect of music on stress.
CONCLUSION: No significant reductions were identified in the levels of anxiety and stress of the participants in this research. It is also suggested that the use of headphones without music may have a relaxing effect by muffling external sounds, which possibly masked relevant statistical differences.
TRIAL AND PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry: RBR-5jy7kzj (https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-5jy7kzj).
title: Effect of music on the management of anxiety and stress in patients in the preoperative period of Coronary Transluminal Angioplasty: A randomized clinical trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) mediated by short-coupled premature ventricular complexes in patients with recent myocardial infarction is termed 'Angry Purkinje Syndrome'. These arrhythmias are typically refractory to conventional antiarrhythmic therapy but may respond to quinidine.
METHODS & RESULTS: We present a case series of patients with short-coupled polymorphic VT occurring 2-8 days after acute myocardial infarction and coronary revascularisation. All three patients had recurrent polymorphic VT episodes that were consistently initiated by ventricular ectopy with a short coupling interval of 360 milliseconds. All three patients experienced arrhythmic storms requiring multiple cardioversions and were refractory to amiodarone, procainamide, lignocaine, and isoprenaline. Quinidine led to sustained suppression of ventricular arrhythmias, with marked reduction in premature ventricular contraction burden within 24 hours. Two patients were successfully extubated 4 days after arrest, and the third was decannulated from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation 4 days after quinidine initiation.
CONCLUSIONS: 'Angry Purkinje Syndrome' is an uncommon but important cause of polymorphic VT in patients with coronary disease not related to acute myocardial ischaemia. Quinidine appears to provide effective suppression of Purkinje-mediated polymorphic VT and may represent an important therapeutic option in this setting.
title: Angry Purkinje Syndrome: A Review of Short-Coupled Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia with Quinidine Treatment.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is associated with abnormal coronary flow, thrombus formation, and impaired reperfusion, but its prognostic significance after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate clinical outcomes among patients with versus without CAE presenting with ACS.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched from inception to April 2026 for studies comparing ACS patients with versus without CAE. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Subgroup, leave-one-out, and Bayesian random-effects analyses were performed to assess robustness.
RESULTS: Twelve observational studies comprising 13,540 patients were analyzed, including 1177 with CAE and 12,363 without CAE. Follow-up ranged from in-hospital assessment to 120 months. CAE was associated with a higher risk of recurrent myocardial infarction (RR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.16-3.32; P = 0.022; I2 = 61.1%), corresponding to an estimated absolute excess of 58.6 events per 1000 patients and a descriptive number needed to harm of 17. For stroke, the prespecified Hartung-Knapp analysis yielded an RR of 2.40 (95% CI, 1.59-3.61), whereas conventional random-effects inference, used as the basis of interpretation, yielded an RR of 2.40 (95% CI, 1.08-5.31; P = 0.031). This estimate was based on 3 studies and was model-sensitive. CAE was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality, in-hospital mortality, cardiac death, repeat revascularization, or MACE. Stent thrombosis was not pooled because only 2 studies provided estimable stent-exposed comparisons. Bayesian analyses supported the recurrent myocardial infarction finding.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients presenting with ACS, CAE identifies a higher-risk ischemic phenotype, with the most consistent association observed for recurrent myocardial infarction. Prospective studies are needed to define CAE-specific risk stratification and treatment strategies.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Prognostic impact of coronary artery ectasia after acute coronary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
AIM: To explore, including from a gender perspective, how people who have suffered a myocardial infarction describe the changes they need to adopt during the recovery phase following hospital discharge.
DESIGN: Qualitative interpretive phenomenological study.
METHOD: Purposive theoretical sampling strategy with maximum variation. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with subsequent thematic analysis of semantic content, with deductive coding based on relevant aspects identified in the scientific literature and inductive coding on emerging codes in interviewees' discourse.
DATA SOURCES: The interviews were conducted between March 2022 and December 2023.
RESULTS: The participants had an average age of 61 years. A total of nine participants were interviewed. Four of these were women. No one identified as non-binary. Three themes were identified: initiation of one's own resources, engagement with one's own emotions, and follow-up by the health team.
CONCLUSION: In this sample, both men and women initially described motivation to assume responsibility for their self-care and lifestyle changes. Women reported greater difficulties in returning to work and maintaining physical activity, which may contribute to increased vulnerability during recovery. These findings may help inform nurse-led cardiac rehabilitation programmes that respond to patients' real needs.
title: Users' Experiences During Cardiac Recovery Following Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Qualitative Study With a Gender Perspective.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the prognostic value of urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) normalized to creatinine in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), focusing on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 144 patients emergently admitted for ACS, with urinary NGAL measured 4-48 h postadmission. Primary and secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), respectively. Optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoffs were determined using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Associations between urinary NGAL/creatinine and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: During a median 734.5-day follow-up, 8 deaths and 44 MACCE occurred. The optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoff for predicting MACCE was 20.85 ng/mg creatinine. All deaths occurred in the high NGAL/creatinine group (≥20.85), but mortality analyses were limited by statistical separation. High NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with MACCE (hazard ratio = 3.47, 95% confidence interval = 1.61-7.47) and remained associated with a higher event hazard after adjustment for age, brain natriuretic peptide, LVEF, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (adjusted hazard ratio = 2.75; P = 0.017). In subgroup analyses, the area under the curve for MACCE was numerically higher in patients with LVEF <50% than in those with LVEF ≥50% (0.753 vs. 0.581). Formal interaction testing in the Cox model, however, did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF category (P for interaction = 0.100).
CONCLUSION: Urinary NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with long-term MACCE in patients with ACS. Although subgroup analyses showed numerically different associations according to LVEF, formal interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF.
title: Urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and clinical outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a focus on patients with impaired ejection fraction.

abstract: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor is standard for patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet real-world comparisons of ticagrelor and prasugrel remain limited. We evaluated their relative effectiveness and safety using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (2010-2024). Adult ACS patients receiving prasugrel or ticagrelor within 24 h post-PCI were included. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and cerebral infarction; secondary endpoints included individual components, major bleeding, and repeat revascularization. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses assessing robustness. Among 14,895 matched pairs (n = 29,790) from 126,273 patients, prasugrel was associated with lower risk of the composite endpoint (HR 0.641; 95% CI 0.613-0.671), all-cause mortality (HR 0.557; 95% CI 0.487-0.637), and MI (HR 0.648; 95% CI 0.616-0.680), without increased bleeding (HR 0.945; 95% CI 0.824-1.084). Repeat revascularization was higher with prasugrel (HR 1.791; 95% CI 1.639-1.957). Effects were consistent across subgroups. In this real-world setting, prasugrel demonstrated superior effectiveness over ticagrelor in reducing mortality and ischemic events without increasing the risk of bleeding, although higher rates of repeat revascularization warrant further study. These findings support prasugrel as a potentially preferred P2Y12 inhibitor in selected ACS patients undergoing PCI.
title: Prasugrel Outperforms Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Real-World Analysis.

abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in liver transplantation (LT) candidates and may require coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Risk stratification is challenging in cirrhosis because histology alone does not reliably predict clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Endoscopic ultrasound-guided portal pressure gradient (EUS-PPG) provides minimally invasive, real-time hemodynamic assessment. The aim of this study was to evaluate the role of EUS-PPG in perioperative risk stratification among LT candidates requiring CABG.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 3 LT candidates with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as the indication for transplant (2021-2023). All had obstructive multivessel CAD not amenable to percutaneous coronary intervention and were evaluated for CABG using EUS-PPG when feasible.
RESULTS: Two patients with biopsy-proven cirrhosis had PPG <6 mm Hg, excluding CSPH; both underwent CABG and successful LT. In 1 patient, PPG could not be obtained because of anatomical distortion; CABG proceeded urgently, but the patient died postoperatively from stroke and aspiration pneumonia, which were unrelated to portal hypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: EUS-PPG may be safe and clinically informative, complementing the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease-based risk stratification and histology to refine perioperative risk assessment in LT candidates with HCC and CAD, although additional cases and further study are needed.
title: Thinking outside the box: leveraging endoscopic ultrasound-guided portal pressure gradient for comprehensive risk stratification in liver transplantation candidates.

abstract:
UNLABELLED: We report the case of a woman in her 40s with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who remained symptomatic despite optimal medical therapy. A prior attempt of alcohol septal ablation was not performed due to unsuitable septal branch anatomy. Echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve (MV), and moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation. Biomarkers indicated significant hemodynamic stress, and magnetic resonance imaging revealed myocardial fibrosis. Treatment with the cardiac myosin inhibitor mavacamten was initiated and despite stepwise escalation to 15 mg/day, LVOT gradients and symptoms persisted, classifying her as a treatment non-responder. Genetic testing detected a MYH7 variant of uncertain significance, potentially associated with reduced drug effectiveness. Given refractory obstruction, the multidisciplinary heart team recommended surgical septal myectomy. Intraoperative inspection of the mitral valve revealed not only SAM-related mitral regurgitation, but degenerative MV pathology requiring MV replacement. Postoperatively, LVOT obstruction resolved, and the patient became asymptomatic.
LEARNING OBJECTIVE: This case underscores the clinical importance of recognition of non-response to mavacamten therapy. It highlights the need for careful evaluation of concomitant mitral valve pathology, which may significantly contribute to persistent symptoms beside left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. In selected patients, timely consideration of surgical intervention remains essential to achieve optimal hemodynamic improvement and symptomatic relief when pharmacological treatment alone is insufficient.
title: Managing a mavacamten non-responder in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A case report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether retinal arterial wall reflectivity is associated with future cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a large community-based Japanese cohort.
DESIGN: Community-based cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 6264 adults from the Nagahama Study (baseline 2012-2016) without a history of CVD.
METHODS: Retinal arterial wall reflectivity was measured on peripapillary OCT images at baseline. Participants were followed for approximately 7 years, and incident CVD events, including stroke and coronary artery disease (CAD), were identified through medical records. Associations were evaluated using Fine-Gray competing risk models and expressed as subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs). Retinal arterial caliber was included in multivariable analyses.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident CVD events, including stroke and CAD.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 6.7 years, 125 incident CVD events occurred. In the full cohort, retinal arterial wall reflectivity was not independently associated with CVD (SHR per 10 arbitrary units, 1.026; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.920-1.145). A continuous age-by-reflectivity interaction was observed (P = 0.029). In post hoc exploratory analyses among participants younger than 70 years, parsimonious models suggested possible associations with CVD (SHR, 1.173; 95% CI, 1.031-1.334) and stroke (SHR, 1.280; 95% CI, 1.088-1.506).
CONCLUSIONS: Retinal arterial wall reflectivity was not independently associated with incident CVD in the full cohort. Post hoc exploratory analyses among participants younger than 70 years suggested possible modest associations with CVD, particularly stroke-related outcomes. These findings suggest that retinal arterial wall reflectivity may reflect subclinical vascular alterations, but require external validation.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.
title: Retinal Arterial Wall Reflectivity and Incident Cardiovascular Disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-based renal denervation (RDN) is an interventional therapy for patients with resistant or uncontrolled arterial hypertension after the exclusion of secondary causes. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the SPYRAL™ catheter system on systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in a real-world clinical setting. Additionally, we explored whether the number of ablation points was associated with the magnitude of blood pressure (BP) reduction.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including patients aged ≥18 years with predominantly resistant hypertension with preserved renal function (eGFR ≥40 mL/min/1.73 m2) and no evidence of secondary hypertension. Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) and renal function were assessed at baseline and three months after RDN. Patients were stratified into subgroups based on the number of ablation points (≤20 vs. >20). A two-tailed p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Data from eleven patients (mean age 64.4 ± 8.1, 45.5% were male) were analyzed. At three months, eGFR remained stable (mean decrease -4.6 mL/min/1.73 m2, CI 95% -15.8-6.6, p = 0.37). Mean ambulatory SBP and DBP decreased significantly following RDN (Δ -19.4mmHg, CI 95% -9.2 to -29.7, p = 0.002; Δ -8.6 mmHg, CI 95% -3.9 to -13.3, p = 0.002; for SBP and DBP respectively). Subgroup analysis revealed that patients with more ablation points experienced a greater reduction in SBP (Δ -17.7 mmHg, CI 95% 0.1-35.3, p = 0.04) and a numerically greater reduction in DBP (Δ -4.8 mmHg, CI 95% 4.5-12, p = 0.27) than those with fewer abation points.
CONCLUSION: In this small retrospective cohort, reductions in SBP and DBP were observed following RDN using the SPYRAL™ multi-electrode system, with no excess of adverse renal events. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered patient cohorts before firm conclusions can be established.
title: Early blood pressure outcomes after SPYRAL™ renal denervation: an exploratory small cohort analysis.

abstract:
UNLABELLED: Aorto-right ventricular fistula (ARVF) is a rare complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with limited evidence to guide its treatment. Five months following TAVR, an 82-year-old woman complained of edema and dyspnea. ARVF was confirmed by echocardiography, which revealed a shunt flow originating at the site of the prosthetic valve to the right ventricle. Unlike continuous shunt flow published in the literature, in this case the flow was observed distinctly during diastole. This situation was attributed to the prosthetic valve opening during systole, interrupting the shunt flow. After refusing invasive treatment, she was treated conservatively. As TAVR becomes more common, we will encounter this rare consequence more often. To determine the best management techniques for this rare condition, more research is required.
LEARNING OBJECTIVE: Aorto-right ventricular fistula (ARVF), a rare complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), can manifest with varying localizations and hemodynamic characteristics. An ARVF with flow controlled by the aortic cusp is reported here for the first time. Patients post-TAVR should undergo long-term echocardiographic follow-up for ARVF as well.
title: Aorto-right ventricular fistula with a prominent diastolic shunt flow after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: A unique case of a valve-cusp-regulated shunt flow.
