title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) face multiple disease- and treatment-related self-management demands after discharge. Accurate assessment of discharge readiness is essential for identifying areas in which patients may require additional discharge education and transitional care support. The widely used Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale (RHDS) assesses overall discharge readiness across four domains: personal status, knowledge, coping ability and expected support. As a generic instrument, however, its broadly framed items may not adequately capture PCI-specific aspects of readiness, including treatment adherence, puncture-site healing, recognition of warning symptoms and preparedness for cardiac rehabilitation.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and initially validate a nurse-assessed Discharge Readiness Scale for Patients with CHD Following PCI (DRS-CHD-PCI).
METHODS: A multistage instrument development and validation study was conducted. Candidate items were generated using transition theory, a targeted review of relevant literature, clinical guidelines and existing discharge-readiness instruments, and semistructured interviews with patients with CHD following PCI and with healthcare professionals. Items were refined through two rounds of Delphi expert consultations and a pilot test with 20 patients. During psychometric validation, nurses assessed 444 patients on the planned discharge day; assessments took approximately 10-15 min. The sample was randomly split into two subsamples for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Psychometric evaluation included item analysis, content validity, structural validity, convergent and discriminant validity, internal consistency and split-half reliability.
RESULTS: The final scale comprised 17 items across five dimensions. Exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor structure that explained 75.84% of the total variance. Both the first- and second-order confirmatory factor analysis models showed acceptable fit. Cronbach's α was 0.945 for the total scale and ranged from 0.813 to 0.894 across the five dimensions.
CONCLUSIONS: The DRS-CHD-PCI is a 17-item, five-dimensional scale with initial evidence supporting its content validity, structural validity and internal consistency. Further multicentre longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate its predictive validity and clinical utility and to determine how its scores can be meaningfully interpreted in clinical practice.
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT: The DRS-CHD-PCI may assist nursing managers and cardiovascular nursing teams by providing a structured, assessment of discharge readiness before discharge and informing nurse-led transitional care planning following PCI. Lower total or dimension scores may highlight areas in which patients require further clinical assessment, additional education, or follow-up.
title: Development and Initial Psychometric Validation of a Nurse-Assessed Discharge Readiness Scale for Patients With Coronary Heart Disease Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an established revascularization strategy for selected patients with left main coronary artery (LMCA) disease. However, data regarding outcomes in unselected real-world populations and the impact of intravascular imaging remain limited. We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes following LMCA PCI according to clinical presentation and to assess the prognostic impact of intravascular imaging guidance.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre study including consecutive patients undergoing LMCA PCI between 2019 and 2022. Patients were classified as having chronic (CCS) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were assessed during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression and stabilised inverse probability of treatment weighting (SIPTW) analyses were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 107 patients were included (19 CCS and 88 ACS; mean age 68.6 ± 11.3 years; 80.4% male). During a mean follow-up of 1121 ± 574 days, ACS patients experienced higher rates of MACCE (40.9% vs. 15.8%; p = 0.039) and all-cause mortality (29.5% vs. 5.3%; p = 0.027) compared with CCS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with a significantly lower risk of MACCE in multivariable analysis (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.75; p = 0.009). In a SIPTW-adjusted analysis, the association remained directionally favourable, although statistical significance was not maintained (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.26-1.29; p = 0.178).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical presentation significantly influences outcomes after LMCA PCI, with worse long-term prognosis among ACS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with lower rates of MACCE and remained directionally favourable after weighting analyses, supporting its role in optimising LMCA interventions.
title: Intravascular imaging improves outcomes in left main PCI: insights from acute and chronic presentations.

abstract: ObjectivesTo describe a rapid, widely available, noncontrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for first-line morphologic assessment of suspected iliac and left renal vein compression in patients with symptoms potentially related to pelvic venous disorders.MethodsWe use a two-stack axial two-dimensional balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) acquisition extending from the renal hila through the iliac bifurcation. The sequence is available on major MRI platforms as TrueFISP (Siemens), FIESTA (GE), or bTFE (Philips). Typical 1.5-T parameters are TR/TE 3.0-3.8/1.5-1.9 ms, flip angle 60-80°, 5-mm slice thickness, and 1.3-1.6-mm in-plane resolution. Localized shimming is performed for each stack.ResultsThe abbreviated examination requires approximately 10 minutes of scanner time, including planning and breath-hold acquisitions. It depicts the site and degree of iliac or left renal vein compression and demonstrates collateral pathways that may support physiologic relevance. Morphologic abnormalities are interpreted in the clinical context and are not considered diagnostic of a symptomatic syndrome in isolation.ConclusionsA short bSSFP protocol can provide a practical, radiation-free gateway examination when comprehensive MR venography is unavailable or undesirable. It may facilitate appropriate referral and procedural planning, while invasive assessment, including intravascular ultrasound when stenting is contemplated, remains necessary in selected patients.
title: Rapid noncontrast MRI screening for iliac and left renal vein compression: A practical bSSFP technique.

abstract: Right heart thrombus-in-transit with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but potentially lethal clinical finding. Optimal management remains controversial, particularly when major contraindications or risk factors coexist. We present a 72-year-old male admitted to the emergency room with leading diagnosis acute coronary syndrome who was later diagnosed with acute PE and a massive, mobile right heart thrombus along with a concomitant ascending aortic aneurysm. Due to high surgical risk, systemic fibrinolysis was performed under close monitoring. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the intracardiac thrombus, rapid right ventricular recovery, and an intact thoracic aorta. This case highlights the importance of echocardiography in initial evaluation of patients with acute cardiovascular symptoms and also systemic thrombolysis as a viable, life-saving strategy for right heart thrombosis even in complex clinical scenarios.
journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
title: Successful systemic fibrinolysis in pulmonary embolism with a thrombus-in-transit.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support, the mortality rate for patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) remains high. Current shock frameworks rely on hemodynamic parameters and fail to capture ongoing biological injury. Our study aimed to investigate cytokine trajectories during support and their association with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed 113 patients with CS in SCAI stage ≥ C who were treated with microaxial flow pump (mAFP). Serial cytokine levels were measured from the time of mAFP implantation until day 7 afterwards. Time-point-specific multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 30-day mortality. The incremental prognostic value of cytokine levels was evaluated in relation to age, lactate, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), with interaction analyses conducted in relation to hemodynamic severity and blood culture positivity.
RESULTS: The overall 30-day mortality rate in the study cohort was 26.5%. IL-6 trajectories diverged progressively between survivors and non-survivors during mAFP support, with the greatest separation at 72 h. At this time point, log-transformed IL-6 was independently associated with 30-day mortality. ROC analysis at 72 h showed moderate discriminatory performance (AUC 0.745) and identified an optimal cut-off of 164.5 pg/mL (sensitivity 68.0%; specificity 82.1%). Patients with IL-6 levels ≥ 164.5 pg/mL presented with lower 30-day survival in exploratory landmark-type Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p < 0.001). This association was not modified by blood culture positivity, although infection, culture-negative inflammatory complications, and vasoplegic/distributive physiology cannot be excluded as contributors to IL-6 elevation.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by mAFP, persistent IL-6 elevation at 72 h was associated with increased 30-day mortality and provided additional prognostic information alongside established clinical severity markers. These findings suggest that ongoing inflammatory activity may provide additional prognostic information and support further evaluation of serial IL-6 measurements for risk stratification.
journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
title: Temporal cytokine trajectories during microaxial flow pump support identify a high-risk inflammatory phenotype in cardiogenic shock.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe real-world treatment allocation and observed long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years with failed surgical aortic bioprostheses who underwent reintervention through valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV-TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo-SAVR) in the Netherlands.
METHODS: Patients aged 50 to < 75 years who underwent ViV-TAVI or redo-SAVR for a failing surgical bioprosthesis between 2015 and 2020 were identified from the Netherlands Heart Registration. Baseline characteristics and Dutch surgical-risk categories were compared by treatment strategy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with ViV-TAVI selection. Kaplan-Meier analysis described survival, and treatment-specific Cox models explored factors associated with all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Of 345 patients, 41% underwent ViV-TAVI and 59% redo-SAVR. Patients selected for ViV-TAVI were older (median 71 vs. 67 years, p < 0.001), had higher surgical risk (EuroSCORE II: 6.2% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.014), and had a greater comorbidity burden than redo-SAVR patients. Despite these baseline risk differences, estimated survival within the ViV-TAVI cohort was 94.2% at 30 days, 89.6% at 2 years, and 74.4% at 4 years; corresponding redo-SAVR estimates were 96.1%, 89.8%, and 88.4%. Left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30% and chronic lung disease were associated both with ViV-TAVI selection (OR: 8.04, 95% CI: 2.16-29.92 and OR: 3.25, 95% CI: 1.53-6.92, respectively) and with all-cause mortality after redo-SAVR (HR: 15.70, 95% CI: 2.49-67.14 and HR: 4.23, 95% CI: 1.53-13.14, respectively).
CONCLUSION: In this Dutch observational registry, ViV-TAVI was predominantly selected for patients with a higher-risk clinical phenotype, while redo-SAVR was more often used in lower-risk reintervention candidates and showed higher observed long-term survival. These data describe contemporary treatment selection and prognosis but do not establish comparative superiority of either strategy.
authors: THI and Cardiothoracic Surgery Registration Committees of the Netherlands Heart Registration
journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
title: Treatment selection and long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years undergoing valve reintervention for failed surgical aortic bioprostheses: insights from the Netherlands Heart Registration.

abstract: The accurate echocardiographic assessment of the left ventricular (LV) contractile state remains challenging in aortic stenosis, as ejection fraction and even global longitudinal strain are markedly load-dependent. The novel pressure-strain loop-derived myocardial work were developed to overcome this limitation; however, incorporation of instantaneous LV volume may further improve this method. We aimed to quantify myocardial work using pressure-strain-volume (PSV) loops and to evaluate its prognostic value in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We enrolled 300 patients scheduled for TAVI (age 78.7 ± 6.3 years, 41% female). The endpoint was all-cause mortality, reached by 62 patients over a median follow-up of 25 months. Echocardiography and non-invasive blood pressure measurements were performed one day before TAVI. LV pressure was estimated noninvasively, while strain curves were derived from speckle-tracking analysis. Pressure-strain relations were adjusted to instantaneous LV volumes to construct PSV loops, yielding volume-adjusted indices (GWIVi and GCWVi). GWIVi showed similar extent of LV dysfunction in classical and paradoxical low-flow low-gradient AS phenotypes compared to the normal flow-high gradient patients (46.98 ± 20.71 vs. 51.99 ± 18.43 vs. 63.74 ± 22.26 mmHg%L/m2, p < 0.001), while other LV function parameters did not. In multivariable Cox-regression, GWIVi was an independent predictor of mortality (Hazard ratio: 0.955 [confidence interval: 0.773-0.993], p < 0.05) alongside clinically relevant other markers such as hemoglobin and atrial fibrillation. PSV loop-derived myocardial work detected LV mechanical differences between AS phenotypes and provided independent prognostic value in TAVI candidates, potentially offering a more physiologically accurate assessment of LV function in this population.
title: Integrating volumes into myocardial work: the prognostic role of non-invasive pressure-strain-volume analysis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation.

journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
title: Inflammation in cardiogenic shock: a marker of outcome, not yet a treatment target.
The Future in the Room: TAVR, Surgery, and the Tyranny of the Now.

abstract: BackgroundVentricular septal rupture (VSR) is a rare but devastating complication of acute myocardial infarction, historically associated with extremely high mortality rates. The optimal timing of surgical repair-balancing the risks of operating on friable, acute necrosis against the dangers of progressive cardiogenic shock during a waiting period-remains a central clinical dilemma.MethodsA systematic narrative review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from 2000 to 2024 for studies comparing early (≤7 days) versus delayed (>7 days) surgical repair of post-MI VSR. Data were extracted on patient characteristics, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use, surgical techniques, and clinical outcomes, including operative mortality, reoperation rates, and long-term survival.ResultsEvidence from contemporary observational studies confirms that delayed surgical repair is associated with significantly lower operative mortality compared to early repair, primarily due to superior tissue integrity and lower rates of residual shunt. However, this mortality gap has substantially narrowed in the contemporary era with routine use of advanced MCS, particularly veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and Impella devices. These technologies enable hemodynamic stabilization, transforming early repair from a salvage procedure to a more controlled intervention. Modern management has evolved from a rigid temporal dichotomy to a patient-tailored strategy emphasizing immediate stabilization, risk stratification, and selective MCS bridging to the optimal surgical window.ConclusionWhile delayed repair remains preferred for hemodynamically stable patients, early repair supported by advanced MCS represents a viable and often necessary strategy for patients with refractory shock. The decision paradigm has shifted toward "stabilize, support, then repair," requiring multidisciplinary heart team collaboration. Future directions include standardized MCS protocols, validated risk scores, and exploration of hybrid percutaneous-surgical approaches to further improve outcomes for this high-risk population.
title: Optimal timing of surgical intervention for post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal rupture: A comprehensive evidence review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major cardiac arrhythmias after NSTEMI are associated with increased mortality and adverse clinical outcomes. However, evidence comparing the ability of established acute coronary syndrome risk scores to predict in-hospital arrhythmic events remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive NSTEMI patients who underwent coronary angiography at Taipei Medical University Hospital between January 2017 and August 2022. Major cardiac arrhythmias were defined as ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, new-onset atrial fibrillation, and high-degree atrioventricular block occurring during hospitalization. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, electrocardiographic features, and angiographic data were analyzed. The discriminatory performance of TIMI, HEART, GRACE 2.0, T-MACS, and an integrated multivariable model was evaluated using ROC analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 485 patients were included, among whom 55 (11.3%) developed major cardiac arrhythmias during hospitalization. Patients with arrhythmias had significantly higher rates of prior heart failure, AKI, and RBBB. Multivariable logistic regression identified heart failure (OR 3.663, p < 0.001), RBBB (OR 2.611, p = 0.030), AKI (OR 2.102, p = 0.045), and higher serum sodium levels (OR 1.079, p = 0.012) as independent predictors of arrhythmic events. The integrated prediction model demonstrated higher observed discrimination for major cardiac arrhythmias (AUC 0.733, p < 0.001) compared with conventional ACS scoring systems. In contrast, the GRACE 2.0 score showed the most consistent performance for predicting in-hospital mortality.
CONCLUSION: In NSTEMI patients, an exploratory model incorporating heart failure, AKI, RBBB, and serum sodium showed discriminatory ability for major cardiac arrhythmias. Meanwhile, the GRACE 2.0 score remained the most reliable tool for mortality prediction, supporting its continued role in global prognostic assessment of NSTEMI patients.
title: Identifying the electrically unstable NSTEMI patient: Comparative performance of four scores for short-term risk stratification of major cardiac arrhythmias.

abstract: Purpose of Review Imaging-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) is rapidly evolving beyond conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based pipelines toward machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and physics-informed approaches that enable fast, wire-free, and scalable functional assessment of coronary artery stenosis. This review synthesizes recent advances in computed tomography (CT)-and angiography-based FFR measurement, with particular emphasis on emerging physics-informed neural networks and neural operators (PINNs and PINOs), as well as key considerations for their clinical translation.Recent Findings ML/DL approaches have markedly improved automation and computational speed, enabling prediction of pressure and FFR from anatomical descriptors or angiographic contrast dynamics. However, their real-world performance and generalizability can remain variable and sensitive to domain shift, due to multi-center heterogeneity, interpretability challenges, and differences in acquisition protocols and image quality. Physics-informed learning introduces conservation structure and boundary-condition consistency into model training, improving generalizability and reducing dependence on dense supervision while maintaining rapid inference. Recent evaluation trends increasingly highlight deployment-oriented metrics, including calibration, uncertainty quantification, and quality-control gatekeeping, as essential for safe clinical use.SummaryThe field is converging toward imaging-derived FFR methods that are faster, more automated, and more reliable. While ML/DL offers substantial efficiency gains, physics-informed frameworks such as PINNs and PINOs may provide a more robust balance between speed and physical consistency. Prospective multi-center validation and standardized evaluation will be critical to support broad and safe clinical adoption.
title: Imaging-derived coronary fractional flow reserve: advances in physics-based, machine learning, and physics-informed methods.

abstract: Advances in device design, imaging and vascular-closure technology have driven a progressive shift from surgical femoral exposure to totally percutaneous strategies for endovascular aortic repair. This narrative review summarises contemporary evidence and practical considerations for percutaneous access across the spectrum of aortic disease, from infrarenal endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) to thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), fenestrated/branched repair and endovascular treatment of the aortic arch. Percutaneous femoral access is now supported by randomized evidence, large registries and administrative cohorts showing high technical success, fewer wound complications, shorter operative times and shorter hospital stay compared with routine surgical cutdown, and real-time ultrasound-guided puncture has become a guideline-endorsed standard of care. Major contemporary developments include computed tomography-based access planning centred on calcification burden and sheath-to-artery ratio; an individualised, anatomy-driven choice between suture- and plug-based closure devices; endovascular preparation of hostile iliofemoral anatomy with pave-and-crack, endoconduits and intravascular lithotripsy; low-profile endografts that have widened transfemoral eligibility; and percutaneous axillary and carotid routes that enable complex TEVAR, fenestrated/branched and selected arch repairs in experienced centres, although evidence for these latter applications remains largely observational. Looking ahead, further reductions in delivery-system profile, dedicated large-bore closure technologies, image-fusion guidance and off-the-shelf branched devices are expected to extend fully percutaneous repair to increasingly complex anatomy, while prospective, aortic-specific and device-level comparisons with standardized anatomical metrics and long-term follow-up are needed to refine patient selection and confirm durable limb and target-vessel patency.
title: Percutaneous approach to aortic disease: EVAR, TEVAR and newer techniques for more proximal disease.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are two preferred methods for treating aortic stenosis. This study compared the in-hospital mortality rates associated with SAVR and TAVR.
METHODS: In accordance with the STROBE guidelines, we conducted an analytical cross-sectional study utilizing data from the National Readmission Database (NRD) spanning from 2016 to 2020. Patients who underwent TAVR or SAVR were identified using specific ICD-10 procedure codes. We employed adjusted multivariate logistic regression analysis to determine the odds ratio (OR) of death associated with SAVR compared to TAVR. Patients were followed for a year and OR with 95% CI were calculated. AI based XGBoost model were used to find the predictors of mortality.
RESULTS: Our study included a total of 361,875 patients. Among these, 182,443 underwent TAVR, while 179,432 underwent SAVR. In the TAVR group, 2,563 patients (1.4%) died during hospitalization, whereas 6,671 patients (3.7%) died in the SAVR group. The multivariate logistic regression analysis indicated that SAVR is associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR = 2.66, 95% CI 2.51-2.81, p < 0.001) compared to TAVR. Follow up data at 30 days, three months, six months, did not find any difference in mortality between TAVR and SAVR. Notably, liver failure, HLD, renal failure, SAVR, female, CHF, and atrial fibrillation are amongst the top predictor of mortality in patients undergoing (TAVR or SAVR). While in cardiac rehospitalization, risk factors like female gender, CHF, Afib, HLD, DM have higher predictability than procedure.
CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates that SAVR is associated with a higher likelihood of in-hospital mortality compared to TAVR, with organ dysfunction (liver failure, kidney dysfunction) as a predictor of mortality.
title: In-Hospital Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement Surgical Versus Transcatheter: A Nationwide Study with Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical adoption of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for risk stratification in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is often limited by long scan times and the requirement for breath-holding and contrast agents.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to validate a non-contrast, free-breathing 3D whole-heart T1/T2 CMR method (iT2prep-IR BOOST) for rapid assessment of myocardial injury in STEMI patients, hypothesizing that this technique provides promising diagnostic accuracy and quantitative assessment to conventional contrast-enhanced CMR.
METHODS: A free-breathing 3D isotropic whole-heart iT2prep-IR BOOST sequence was performed with a scan time of <8minutes. Sixty-four STEMI patients underwent CMR, including iT2prep-IR BOOST, clinical T2-STIR, late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and T1/T2 mapping. The diagnostic performance of iT2prep-IR BOOST was evaluated against LGE and T2-STIR to assess myocardial infarction (MI), microvascular obstruction (MVO), and edema. Subgroup analyses further investigated the association between MVO detected by iT2prep-IR BOOST and left ventricular (LV) remodeling at 1-year follow-up.
RESULTS: In 60 STEMI patients, the acquisition was completed in 7.2 ± 0.6min as a single free-breathing 3D whole-heart scan. Patient-level analysis showed high sensitivity and specificity for MVO (100.0% / 87.5%) and segmental MVO detection (95.8% / 97.8%). T2prep-IR BOOST yielded robust image contrast for MI comparable to LGE, while offering comparable edema visualization to T2-STIR. Volumetric and transmurality quantifications of MVO, MI, and edema showed excellent agreement with reference standards (all r > 0.90, p < 0.001), supported by significant biophysical correlations with native T1/T2 values (p < 0.001). Furthermore, in a 1-year follow-up cohort (n=51), baseline T2prep-IR BOOST-derived MVO volume was associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, showing significant correlations with both ΔLVEDVI (r = 0.305, p = 0.029) and ΔLVESVI (r = 0.293, p = 0.037).
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary single-center study, iT2prep-IR BOOST showed promising diagnostic performance and close quantitative agreement with conventional LGE and T2-STIR in stable STEMI patients. Further prospective validation in larger, independent, and more heterogeneous cohorts, including patients unable to undergo contrast-enhanced CMR, is required before this technique can be considered an alternative to standard LGE and T2-weighted sequences.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
title: Visualization of post-STEMI myocardial infarction and microvascular obstruction with non-contrast, free-breathing whole- heart iT2prep-IR BOOST.
Beyond a single measurement: the role of cumulative LDL-C exposure after percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) has progressed from a non-invasive test primarily used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease into a comprehensive cardiovascular imaging platform for coronary artery disease, myocardial disease, valvular heart disease, and structural heart disease. Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is now endorsed as a first-line test in appropriately selected patients with stable chest pain or suspected chronic coronary syndromes because it can exclude obstructive disease, depict coronary atherosclerotic burden, support preventive treatment, and inform referral for invasive coronary angiography. At the same time, contemporary cardiac CT is moving beyond luminal stenosis. CT-derived fractional flow reserve and myocardial CT perfusion add a functional assessment of ischemia, whereas late iodine enhancement, CT-derived extracellular volume fraction, myocardial strain, and pericoronary fat attenuation index provide information on fibrosis, ventricular mechanics, vascular inflammation, and prognosis. Cardiac CT also has an established role in transcatheter valve therapy, left atrial appendage occlusion, and prosthetic valve assessment by providing a three-dimensional roadmap for device selection, access planning, and complication prediction. Photon-counting detector CT and artificial intelligence are further expanding the capabilities of cardiac CT through higher spatial resolution, spectral quantification, automated segmentation, quantitative plaque analysis, image reconstruction, and structured reporting. This review summarizes the evidence, technical foundations, clinical applications, and implementation challenges of contemporary cardiac CT, with an emphasis on its transition toward a decision-making platform for personalized cardiovascular care.
title: The evolving role of cardiac CT: Emerging technologies and clinical impact.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).
OBJECTIVES: To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.
METHODS: We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.
RESULTS: Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).
CONCLUSIONS: In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.
title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.
RESULTS: In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.
title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.

abstract: Among patients with cardiogenic shock receiving Impella-based mechanical circulatory support, pulmonary vascular load and right ventricular dysfunction may affect left ventricular preload and device flow. Prospective data on the acute hemodynamic effects of inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) in this setting are limited. We evaluated short-term hemodynamic changes after iNO initiation in patients receiving Impella or Impella combined with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECPELLA) support. We conducted a prospective single-center pilot study of adult patients receiving Impella or ECPELLA support who were treated with iNO. iNO was initiated at 20 ppm after initial circulatory resuscitation once pulmonary artery pulse pressure could be reliably assessed. Hemodynamic variables were recorded immediately before iNO initiation (T0) and 30 min (T1) and 24 h (T2) after initiation. The primary endpoint was the change in mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) from T0 to T1. We enrolled 11 patients, and 10 were analyzed. mPAP decreased from 19.0 (14.8-20.3) mmHg at T0 to 16.5 (12.8-19.3) mmHg at T1 (P = 0.004). The T0-T2 difference was not significant. Lactate levels decreased, but this temporal change could not be attributed directly to iNO without a control group. Methemoglobin levels increased slightly at T2 without clinical methemoglobinemia. iNO was temporally associated with an early reduction in mPAP in patients receiving Impella-based support, without clear improvement in systemic hemodynamic indices. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger controlled studies.
title: Effects of inhaled nitric oxide during mechanical circulatory support: a prospective pilot study.

abstract: During percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), the contact force between the guidewire and the vessel wall is a key mechanical factor in vessel injury, yet it cannot be measured directly with conventional imaging. Although sensor-based methods measure the contact force directly, they increase both the complexity and the cost of the instrumentation. A sensorless guidewire contact force estimation method is therefore proposed, in which multi-scale feature extraction is combined with region mask mean pooling to learn an end-to-end mapping from conventional planar images to the contact force in each of the four predefined contact regions. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of 343 samples acquired on a 3D-printed vessel phantom, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.861 g and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.036 g. Ablation experiments show that the region mask reduces the MAE by 79% relative to the identical architecture without the region mask. Requiring neither additional sensing hardware nor complex physical modeling, the method estimates the contact force from visual information alone. These results support the feasibility of vision-based sensorless contact force estimation and suggest a possible route toward force feedback in interventional procedures.
title: Visual estimation of guidewire contact forces by integrating multi-scale features and region mask.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peri- and epicardial adipose tissue (PEAT) is a metabolically active fat depot surrounding the heart and coronary arteries that may contribute to vascular dysfunction and inflammation in type 2 diabetes (T2D). We examined associations between PEAT volume, coronary calcification (CACS), myocardial flow reserve (MFR), and systemic inflammation (hsCRP).
METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of adults with T2D without overt CVD recruited 2020-2023. PEAT was quantified on non-contrast CT; CACS was calculated by the Agatston method; MFR was measured by rubidium-82 PET/CT; hsCRP assessed systemic inflammation. Associations were tested using multivariable regression adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: Among 887 participants (mean age 65 years; 70% male; mean BMI 30 kg/m2; median PEAT 199 mL [IQR 133-283]), higher PEAT (per 100 mL) was associated with lower MFR (β - 0.04; 95% CI - 0.09 to 0.00; p = 0.041) and higher hsCRP, corresponding to a 38% increase (95% CI 28% to 48%; p < 0.001) in age- and sex-adjusted models, but not with CACS > 300 (OR 1.01; 95% CI 0.89-1.15). After further adjustment for diabetes duration, BMI, LDL cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, HbA1c, kidney function, smoking, and albuminuria, only the association with hsCRP remained significant at 14% (95%; CI 4% to 25%; p = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: In individuals with T2D without overt CVD, PEAT volume was not independently associated with CACS or MFR after multivariable adjustment. Higher PEAT volume was associated with higher hsCRP, suggesting a relationship with systemic inflammation; however, this exploratory finding should be interpreted in the context of established links between adiposity and inflammatory burden.
title: Associations between cardiac adipose tissue volume, measures of coronary calcification, myocardial microvascular function and systemic inflammation in individuals with type 2 diabetes free of overt cardiovascular disease.

abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading, modifiable risk factor for ischaemic stroke, with 20-30% of stroke patients harbouring underlying AF. Management of AF, however, differs substantially depending on clinical context. In ischaemic stroke patients with pre-known AF, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the cornerstone of secondary prevention, with initiation timing guided by infarct severity following a risk-adapted approach. In patients with no history of AF, prolonged cardiac rhythm monitoring after stroke or transient ischaemic attack improves AF detection rates. However, it remains uncertain whether this translates into a reduced risk of recurrent stroke, with randomised trials such as Find-AF 2 ongoing. Subclinical AF, detected via implantable devices, is associated with an increased stroke risk correlating with arrhythmia burden; recent trials (ARTESiA, NOAH-AFNET 6) suggest that anticoagulation may reduce ischaemic stroke risk in this population, but at the cost of increased bleeding, necessitating individualised decision-making. Particularly challenging are anticoagulation decisions with concomitant cerebral amyloid angiopathy or prior intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) due to competing risks of thromboembolism and haemorrhage. Recent meta-analyses indicate that resuming DOACs after ICH reduces ischaemic events but significantly raises the risk of recurrent haemorrhage, without clear improvement in net clinical benefit. New treatment options, such as left atrial appendage closure, carotid artery filter systems, factor XIa inhibitors or rhythm control, must demonstrate in adequately powered randomised controlled trials that they can optimise treatment outcomes in this complex and growing patient group. This article summarises some common interdisciplinary neurological and cardiological questions and discusses the most recent evidence on AF-related stroke prevention across various patient groups, highlighting the importance of individualised, multidisciplinary, and imaging-informed decision-making.
title: Atrial fibrillation in stroke patients: facts, numbers and current challenges.

abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide, despite substantial advances in reperfusion strategies and guideline-directed therapies. Increasing evidence highlights the pivotal role of inflammation. Therefore, identifying reliable and accessible inflammatory biomarkers may provide valuable prognostic information for patients with AMI. Cell-based inflammatory indices derived from routine complete blood count parameters have emerged as promising biomarkers due to their simplicity, low cost, and widespread availability. Unlike single inflammatory markers, these indices reflect the complex interactions among different immune cell populations involved in cardiovascular inflammation. Recent studies have demonstrated associations between elevated cell-based inflammatory indices and adverse outcomes following AMI. Inflammation represents a central mechanism linking coronary plaque instability, myocardial injury, and adverse outcomes after AMI. Cell-based inflammatory indices provide a practical and cost-effective approach for evaluating systemic inflammatory activity and may improve prognostic assessment in patients with AMI. Further prospective studies are required to determine their optimal clinical application, standardized cutoff values, and integration into routine cardiovascular risk models.
title: Cell-Based Inflammatory Indices for Risk Stratification in Acute Myocardial Infarction: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.

abstract: Acute coronary syndrome requires effective antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while contemporary patients often present with overlapping ischemic and bleeding risks. This clinical complexity has shifted post-PCI management from fixed-duration dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) toward individualized strategies based on DAPT duration, single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) selection, and aspirin withdrawal. Aspirin is traditionally the default maintenance agent after DAPT, although long-term aspirin use is limited by gastrointestinal intolerance, mucosal injury, and bleeding risk. P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy represents an important aspirin-free strategy, with clinical application influenced by drug potency, genetic variability, tolerability, cost, and adherence. Indobufen, a reversible cyclooxygenase-targeting antiplatelet agent, has reemerged as a potential aspirin alternative by suppressing thromboxane A2 generation through a mechanism distinct from that of aspirin. Current evidence suggests that indobufen-based DAPT may provide comparable ischemic protection with fewer bleeding or gastrointestinal adverse events in selected PCI patients, particularly those with aspirin intolerance, gastrointestinal vulnerability, or high bleeding risk. These patients often present with multiple high-risk features that simultaneously elevate both ischemic and bleeding risks, underscoring the need for careful risk stratification. Most available studies have evaluated indobufen as an aspirin substitute within DAPT rather than as SAPT after DAPT discontinuation. From a pharmacoeconomic perspective, indobufen is more expensive than aspirin, although this must be weighed against potential benefits in bleeding reduction. Future randomized trials are needed to define the optimal DAPT-to-SAPT strategy and clarify the clinical position of indobufen in acute coronary syndrome-PCI.
title: Individualized Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Acute Coronary Syndrome: Current SAPT Strategies and the Potential Role of Indobufen.

abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI), a major manifestation of coronary artery disease, remains a global health challenge despite significant advances in research and therapy. This review highlights current developments in diagnostic criteria, pathophysiology, treatment strategies, and emerging therapeutic targets. Type 1 MI, driven by atherosclerotic plaque rupture and thrombosis, continues to dominate, but growing recognition of type 2 MI and MINOCA (myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries) underscores the need for refined diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. High-sensitivity cardiac troponins and advanced imaging have improved early detection, classification, and risk stratification. The management now emphasizes personalized, evidence-based care, including percutaneous coronary intervention or thrombosis, dual antiplatelet therapy, lipid-lowering agents, and cardioprotective drugs. Despite improved outcomes, challenges, such as late presentation, treatment disparities, recurrent events, and progression to heart failure, persist. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using electronic databases, such as Web of Science, Google Scholar, PubMed, SciFinder, Reaxys, and the Cochrane Library. By identifying persistent gaps, this work aimed to inform clinicians, researchers, and policymakers on innovative strategies for prevention, early detection, and optimal MI management.
title: A Contemporary Review of Myocardial Infarction with Emphasis on Clinical Trials and Therapeutic Approaches.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transfemoral access is the default approach for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC). Although ultrasound (US)-guided femoral puncture improves first-pass success and reduces vascular complications in randomized trials, real-world data in contemporary structural heart interventions, including both arterial and venous large-sheath access, remain limited. The authors aimed to compare US-guided vs. conventional transfemoral access in patients undergoing TAVI and LAAC.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients undergoing transfemoral structural procedures between January 2022 and December 2024 (93: TAVI; 72: LAAC). Ultrasound guidance was used in 57 procedures (34.5%). Arterial and venous cohorts were analyzed separately. Primary outcomes were absolute hemoglobin decrease (ΔHb) and access-site vascular complications (hematoma, pseudoaneurysm, and arteriovenous fistula). In the arterial cohort, 1 : 1 propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.
RESULTS: Hemoglobin decline was significantly smaller with US guidance in both venous (0.80 ± 0.95 vs. 1.50 ± 1.11 g/dL; P = .009) and arterial procedures (0.58 ± 0.97 vs. 1.29 ± 1.00 g/dL; P = .002). In the venous cohort, complication rates were numerically lower but not statistically different (3.8% vs. 17.4%; P = .143). In contrast, arterial complications were significantly reduced with US guidance. After propensity matching (31 patients per group), complications occurred in 3.2% vs. 29.0% [Absolute Risk Reduction(ARR) = 25.8%, Number Need to Treat (NNT) = 4, P = .013].
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided transfemoral access was associated with reduced hemoglobin decline and fewer vascular complications, particularly in large-bore arterial procedures, supporting routine integration of real-time US guidance in structural interventions.
title: Ultrasound-Guided versus Fluoroscopy-Guided Femoral Access for Structural Heart Procedures: Outcomes From Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure.

abstract: A 36-year-old woman with severe dilated cardiomyopathy (LVEF 14%, NYHA IV) underwent heart transplantation. Postoperatively, she developed subarachnoid hemorrhage and septic shock. The ECG revealed a spiked helmet sign (SHS) pattern, with repolarization abnormalities and QT prolongation. Despite transient clinical improvement and resolution of the ECG changes after intensive support, the patient died due to infectious complications. This case highlights the occurrence of SHS in the early posttransplant period in a structurally normal donor heart, a previously unreported presentation, reinforcing its extracardiac origin and association with critical illness and poor prognosis.

title: Spiked Helmet Sign in the Early Post-Heart Transplantation Period: A Dramatic STEMI Mimic in a Structurally Normal Donor Heart.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to analyze the clinical characteristics and short-term prognostic factors of young patients with acute myocardial infarction.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included young patients (aged 18 to 45 years) who visited our center for AMI from January 1, 2014, to October 31, 2023. Baseline and outcome data were collected through the medical records system, with the primary endpoint being in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Patients were divided into MACE and non-MACE groups based on the occurrence of in-hospital MACE. Coronary angiography was performed in 154/158 patients, all achieving post-procedural TIMI 3 flow. Multivariable logistic regression using Firth penalized likelihood with a priori-selected variables (LVEF, serum uric acid, age) was used to identify independent predictors of MACE.
RESULTS: Of 166 young patients initially screened, 158 were included in the final analysis after excluding 8 due to incomplete data. Among these, 27 (17.1%) experienced in-hospital MACE. Patients in the MACE group had a lower prevalence of diabetes (0.00% vs. 19.08%, P = 0.008), lower admission blood pressure and worse left ventricular dysfunction [lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), larger left ventricular end diastolic diameter (LVEDD)]. Single-vessel disease was the most common (38.96%), with 83.77% of patients having involvement of the left anterior descending artery. The proportion of left main disease was higher in the MACE group (15.38% vs. 3.91%, P = 0.045). In the Firth model, lower LVEF was the sole independent predictor of MACE (OR 0.859, 95% CI 0.794-0.917, P < 0.001), while serum uric acid and age were not significant.
CONCLUSION: The clinical characteristics and coronary artery lesion features of young AMI patients are unique. Reduced LVEF is the sole independent predictor of in-hospital MACE in our cohort, underscoring the value of ventricular function assessment for short-term risk stratification.
title: Clinical characteristics and in-hospital prognostic factors in young patients with myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity statins are the cornerstone of post-ACS management. Real-world data frequently indicate suboptimal adherence and low attainment of guideline-recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the early efficacy of oral lipid-lowering therapy in achieving LDL-C targets following ACS in a recent cohort of Indian patients.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 511 statin-naive ACS patients. High-intensity statin monotherapy (atorvastatin 80 mg daily or rosuvastatin 40 mg daily) was initiated following diagnosis. Lipid profile, including total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, and VLDL-C, were assessed at baseline, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28. Primary endpoints included the proportion of patients achieving LDL-C goals at Day 28.
RESULTS: 50.5% of patients achieved the 2019 ESC/EAS LDL-C target (<55 mg/dL) at day 28. Similarly, 68.9% achieved the 2018 ACC/AHA target (<70 mg/dL), and 44.6% achieved the 2020 Lipid Association of India (LAI) target (<50 mg/dL) at day 28. The mean LDL-C reduced from 73.43 ± 13.99 mg/dL at Day 0 to 61.26 ± 27.00 mg/dL at Day 28, corresponding to a 16.6% reduction from baseline. On multivariate analysis, baseline LDL-C, type 2 diabetes mellitus and multivessel coronary disease were found to be independent negative predictors for achieving LDL-C goal <50 mg/dL at day 28.
CONCLUSION: LDL-C target attainment following ACS remains suboptimal despite high-intensity statin therapy, highlighting the need for earlier and more intensive lipid-lowering strategies in high-risk Indian patients.
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
title: Early efficacy of oral lipid lowering therapy in achieving LDL-C targets following acute coronary syndrome: A real-world observational study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual inflammation and dysregulated lipid metabolism are closely associated with the extent of severe multivessel coronary disease (MVD) in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). The fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio (FPR) and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 (ApoB/ApoA1) ratio reflect these two residual risk pathways, respectively, whereas the clinical value of their combined assessment for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD remains to be evaluated.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incremental value of combining FPR with the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI and to develop an adjunctive risk-stratification model.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 580 patients with NSTEMI who underwent coronary angiography. Correlation analyses, logistic regression, and restricted cubic spline models were used to assess the associations between the two biomarkers and MVD. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to evaluate the incremental value of the biomarkers. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to assess net clinical benefit, and subgroup analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: FPR remained independently and positively associated with severe MVD, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship; the association of the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio was attenuated after full adjustment, although it showed complementary value in patients with a very high coronary lesion burden. With the combined model, the AUC increased from 0.683 to 0.719, while the continuous NRI and IDI were 0.488 and 0.037, respectively; adding the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio to the model containing FPR did not significantly improve the AUC (P = 0.266) but yielded further improvements in NRI and IDI. Potential effect modification by diabetes status was observed (P for interaction = 0.025).
CONCLUSION: FPR is an important adjunctive biomarker for the pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI, whereas the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio provides complementary reclassification information. The nomogram incorporating both biomarkers may facilitate pre-angiographic risk stratification.
title: Combined assessment of fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio and ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic risk stratification of severe multivessel coronary disease in NSTEMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: An estimated 25%-34% of patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) are diagnosed with an occluded culprit artery during catheterization. Whether early serial troponin kinetics discriminate angiographically defined occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) in catheterized patients with NSTE-ACS remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 481 patients with NSTE-ACS who underwent coronary catheterization between 2017 and 2023. OMI was defined by a purely angiographic criterion: >90% culprit-vessel stenosis with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction flow grade 0, 1, or 2. Seven contemporary sensitivity troponin I metrics (absolute values at 0, 3, and 6 h; deltas; and ratios) were evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Operating characteristics are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and likelihood ratios.
RESULTS: Ninety-eight patients (20.4%) met the angiographic definition of OMI. These patients were younger (median, 65.5 vs. 70.0 years; p = 0.025), had fewer comorbidities, and more often presented with chest pain (92.9% vs. 82.8%; p = 0.013). The left circumflex artery was the most common culprit in OMI (36.7%). Twenty-nine patients with OMI (29.6%) had a presentation ECG classified as normal (no ST-T change or bundle branch block. No troponin metric reliably discriminated OMI from non-occlusion MI. The prespecified primary predictor, the 0-6-h change in troponin concentration, had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.623 (95% CI, 0.544-0.703) and the best single metric, the 6-h value, of 0.654 (0.580-0.727); all seven unadjusted troponin-metric AUCs were under 0.66. At its Youden cutoff (≥0.379 ng/mL), the 6-h troponin had a sensitivity of 69.4%, a specificity of 57.7%, a positive predictive value of 27.2%, and a negative predictive value of 89.3%. The highest positive predictive value of any metric was 41.3%, the first troponin (at 0 h) identified fewer than 40% of patients with OMI at its optimal threshold, and likelihood ratios produced only limited shifts in post-test probability.
CONCLUSION: Among analyzable patients with NSTE-ACS undergoing catheterization, approximately one in five met the study-defined angiographic criteria for OMI. Early serial troponin kinetics showed only modest discrimination, and upper confidence bounds fell below levels expected of a standalone triage biomarker. Complementary strategies for identifying these patients, including expert ECG interpretation, warrant further study.
title: Angiographic prevalence of occlusion myocardial infarction and the limited value of serial troponin in patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC). However, its safety and efficacy boundaries remain incompletely defined in dedicated comparisons against direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).
OBJECTIVE: This study applied a pragmatic framework to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of LAAO versus OAC in a DOAC-predominant setting.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAO with OAC, restricted to a DOAC-predominant comparator. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated via a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model.
RESULTS: Four trials comprising 5890 patients were included (96.4% of controls assigned to DOACs). Overall stroke (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.87-1.60; p = 0.28), systemic embolism (RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.29-4.08; p = 0.89), major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.81-1.19; p = 0.85), hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.45-1.51; p = 0.53), and all-cause mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85-1.17; p = 0.99) did not differ significantly. Ischemic stroke presented numerical asymmetry favoring OAC that approached statistical significance (RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.89; p = 0.06). Conversely, within available protocol-defined datasets, LAAO significantly reduced nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.43-0.60; p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: In a pragmatic analysis of the DOAC era, randomized data show no statistically significant differences for hard individual endpoints, though broad confidence intervals reflect precision limits. A numerical asymmetry for ischemic stroke favored OAC, while LAAO reduced nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding. Current evidence remains non-definitive, warranting shared clinical decision-making to balance individual thromboembolic risks against long-term bleeding susceptibility.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; four trials comprising 5890 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with wide confidence intervals; Mantel-Haenszel pooling with a 'pragmatic' framework and some outcomes drawn from protocol-defined datasets.
appraisal.one_line: Pragmatic meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing LAAO with oral anticoagulation in a DOAC-predominant setting found no significant difference in hard endpoints.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall stroke (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.87-1.60; p = 0.28), major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.81-1.19; p = 0.85) and all-cause mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85-1.17; p = 0.99) did not differ significantly; ischemic stroke was RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.89; p = 0.06.
appraisal.why_it_matters: LAAO versus DOAC remains contested, and the ischaemic stroke signal bears on D9 practice and on the case for further trials.
