abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile and its association with spirometry and two-dimensional (2D) echocardiographic findings in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
METHODOLOGY: A cross-sectional study was carried out at LLRM Medical College, Meerut, which included 144 COPD patients over 40 years of age, selected after informed consent and ethical approval. Patients with other respiratory or cardiac diseases, immunocompromised status, or poor echocardiographic imaging were excluded. Each participant underwent clinical evaluation, which included a history of respiratory symptoms and comorbidities, along with comprehensive investigations such as blood tests, spirometry, chest X-ray, sputum analysis, electrocardiography (ECG), arterial blood gases, and 2D echocardiography. Data analysis was conducted using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 29. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The data reveal that most COPD patients fall into Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) stage 3 (severe), with a significant number also in stage 2 (moderate), indicating a high prevalence of advanced disease. COPD predominantly affects individuals over 50, with peak occurrence in the 60-69 age-group. Disease duration increases with severity, ranging from 2.38 years in stage 1 to 16.74 years in stage 4, showing a clear link between duration and progression. ECG abnormalities such as P-pulmonale, right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH), arrhythmias, and low QRS voltage were more frequent in severe stages, especially stage 3, highlighting the cardiovascular burden in advanced COPD. Echocardiographic findings, including pulmonary hypertension, right atrial enlargement, right ventricular dysfunction, and tricuspid regurgitation, showed significant association with disease severity (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates a strong link between COPD severity and cardiovascular complications, especially right heart involvement. Significant associations between GOLD stages and 2D echocardiographic findings highlight the importance of routine cardiac screening in COPD patients. Pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction, and tricuspid regurgitation were the most common complications, underscoring the need for close monitoring and targeted treatment. Early intervention and integrated cardiac evaluation in COPD management can help prevent right heart failure and improve patient outcomes.
journal: The Journal of the Association of Physicians of India
title: Echocardiographic Manifestations in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Patients with a History of Chronic Smoking: A Cross-sectional Study.

abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.
title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.

abstract: Background: Renal denervation (RDN) safely reduces blood pressure (BP) in patients with uncontrolled hypertension. A potential long-term concern is the development of de novo renal artery stenosis (RAS) secondary to vascular injury. This study assesses the long-term vascular safety and incidence of RAS in patients treated with radiofrequency RDN from the SPYRAL HTN-OFF MED and -ON MED trials. Patients and methods: All patients underwent renal angiograms for assessment of the renal anatomy prior to randomization. Patients with RAS >50% were excluded from enrollment. At long-term follow-up (439+/-288 days), patients underwent duplex ultrasound imaging (DUS), computerized tomography angiography (CTA), and/or magnetic resonance angiography (MRA). Independent core labs evaluated all images. Clinically significant RAS was predefined as a stenosis ≥70%, confirmed by angiography. Results: A total of 610 patients were treated with RDN in the SPYRAL trials. At least one imaging modality was performed in 557 of the 610 patients (91%): 329 patients underwent DUS imaging, 230 underwent CTA, 148 underwent MRA, and 15 underwent renal angiography. With one possible exception, no clinically significant RAS was detected. No patients had renal artery reintervention. The proportion of images fulfilling pre-specified criteria for technical adequacy by the core lab was 100% (angiography), 87.5% (DUS), 80.6% (CTA), and 32.4% MRA. Conclusions: RF RDN appears to be safe, without confirmed vascular injury or RAS among 557 patients who had long-term imaging. Diagnostic utility of imaging modalities determined by specific criteria for technical adequacy for core lab evaluation was lowest with MRA and highest with DUS.
title: Renal artery imaging through long-term follow-up after radiofrequency renal denervation: Results from the SPYRAL Clinical Program.

abstract: Elevated troponin is frequently interpreted as acute coronary syndrome, yet it may reflect non-ischemic myocardial injury. We report a 79-year-old woman presenting with acute dyspnea and chest pain following forced inspiration, found to have a spontaneous sternal fracture and marked troponin elevation without ischemic ECG changes or significant ventricular dysfunction. The case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing non-STEMI from secondary troponin elevation in the setting of chest wall trauma and emphasises the need for careful clinical assessment in elderly patients.
title: [Sternum fracture and troponinism after forced inspiration].

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-directed therapies for acute pulmonary embolism (PE) are being adopted rapidly, yet real-world safety data remain limited.
AIMS: To characterize adverse events, device failure patterns, and mortality signals for three FDA-cleared catheter-directed PE platforms (EKOSONIC, INDIGO, and FlowTriever) using the FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database.
METHODS: Medical device reports (MDRs) were downloaded from each device's PE clearance (2008, 2015, and 2018, respectively) through March 2026 and filtered by text to retain PE-specific reports. Reports were classified by manufacturer, event type (death, injury, malfunction), device problem, and patient problem, and trends were assessed by calendar year.
RESULTS: Of 2528 reports, 389 were PE-specific (INDIGO 228 [58.6%], EKOSONIC 149 [38.3%], FlowTriever 12 [3.1%]), spanning 2009 to January 2026. There were 76 deaths (19.5%), 133 injuries (34.2%), and 180 malfunctions (46.3%). Annual death reports rose from 2023 (15 in 2023, 13 in 2024, 8 in 2025, and 3 in January 2026). Among 47 INDIGO deaths, 28 (59.6%) involved Lightning/Flash large-bore catheters, and 36 (76.6%) carried a perforation-, hemoptysis-, tamponade-, or extravasation-related patient problem code. Separator wire break/fracture was the leading INDIGO device failure. EKOSONIC reports showed thrombolytic-related bleeding, including intracranial or cerebral hemorrhage in 12 reports (8.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: MAUDE reports reveal distinct device-specific safety signals: pulmonary artery perforation with large-bore INDIGO aspiration catheters, and intracranial hemorrhage with EKOSONIC. Death reports increased from 2023 as mechanical thrombectomy use expanded. Absent procedural denominators, rates and causality cannot be inferred; findings support operator awareness, careful patient selection, and continued post-market surveillance.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Catheter-Directed Interventional Devices for Pulmonary Embolism: A Maude Database Analysis of Adverse Events.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is highly prevalent among elderly patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes and impaired health-related quality of life. However, different frailty assessment tools vary in their conceptual frameworks, assessment domains, and predictive performance, and their applicability in elderly PCI populations remains unclear.
AIMS: To compare four commonly used frailty assessment tools, including the Frailty Phenotype (FP), FRAIL scale, Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI), and Frailty Index (FI), and to investigate their associations with quality of life in elderly patients with CHD undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 elderly patients with CHD undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital in Shanghai from August to December 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Frailty Phenotype (FP), FRAIL scale, Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI), and Frailty Index (FI), and quality of life using the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12). Agreement was evaluated using the Kappa statistic. Associations with physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS) scores were assessed using correlation and multivariable linear regression, while discriminatory performance was examined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and Bayesian discriminant analyses.
RESULTS: Mean PCS and MCS scores were 40.08 ± 11.23 and 52.30 ± 7.82, respectively. Frailty prevalence was 40.6% by FP, 8.6% by FRAIL, 28.3% by TFI, and 22.1% by FI. Agreement was fair to moderate (Kappa = 0.242-0.496). Higher frailty scores were independently associated with lower PCS and MCS after adjustment for age, sex, education, smoking, and comorbidity burden. FP and FI showed comparable discrimination for PCS, whereas TFI had the highest AUC for MCS. Classification accuracy was highest for FP in PCS and TFI in MCS (both 79.51%).
CONCLUSION: Frailty was consistently associated with poorer quality of life. FP and FI performed similarly for physical health, whereas TFI showed the most favorable performance for mental health.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Application of Four Frailty Assessment Tools in Elderly Patients With Coronary Heart Disease PCI and Its Relationship With Quality of Life.

abstract: Severe coronary calcification is a challenge to optimal percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Adequate lesion preparation is essential to achieve appropriate stent expansion and improve long-term outcomes. Recently, orbital atherectomy (OA) has emerged as an important tool for calcium modification, offering a unique mechanism of action based on centrifugal sanding and differential cutting. This review summarizes the contemporary evidence supporting OA in heavily calcified coronary disease, compares it to other established calcium modification strategies, and highlights practical scenarios where OA offers distinctive advantages. Several calcium algorithms exist, detailing start points according to balloon crossability and stepwise escalation guided by intravascular imaging. Orbital atherectomy has recently become available across centers in Europe and the United Kingdom, providing an alternative calcium‑debulking toolkit that is of particular use in some indications, with advantages over other techniques. In this review, we look at the emerging role of OA in calcified lesions, with a critical appraisal of the data and highlighting its utility drawing examples from the published literature and our center's experience.
title: The emerging role of orbital atherectomy in the management of heavily calcified lesions in percutaneous coronary intervention.
Editorial: Exploring the impact of inflammatory processes on the course of acute myocardial infarction: pathways and therapies.

abstract: Large-vessel recanalization is essential in acute ischemic stroke, but it does not guarantee microvascular reperfusion. Endothelial responses may contribute to persistent tissue hypoperfusion through leukocyte trafficking and immunothrombosis. Many of these responses may begin during ischemia and may continue or intensify when blood flow returns. We therefore use postischemic or ischemia/reperfusion-associated terminology unless experiments isolate the contribution of reperfusion. We propose that endothelial immune reprogramming requires a coordinated molecular program, localization to a defined vascular segment and time, and a corresponding change in immune-regulatory function. An isolated increase in an adhesion molecule or circulating biomarker indicates activation or injury but cannot identify such a state. Barrier/stress, adhesive/chemotactic, and prothrombotic responses overlap. Experimental studies implicate endothelial signaling, leukocyte arrest, and platelet interactions with neutrophil extracellular traps, but have not established a common sequence of endothelial states. Human evidence comes mainly from circulating biomarkers, thrombectomy thrombi, post-mortem tissue, and perfusion imaging. The available findings have yet to link a defined cerebral endothelial state to downstream perfusion and clinical outcome in the same patients. Prospective studies should combine serial vascular biomarkers, repeated perfusion imaging, and longitudinal follow-up, with endothelial-enriched molecular profiling when tissue is available. Therapeutic studies should test whether modifying a reversible endothelial program relieves no-reflow while preserving later immune resolution and vascular repair. These approaches remain investigational.
title: Postischemic endothelial immune reprogramming in stroke.

abstract: Mitral regurgitation is a highly prevalent valvular heart disease and, when hemodynamically significant, is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite advances in surgical techniques and catheter-based edge-to-edge repair, a large number of patients remain untreated due to high surgical risk or anatomical limitations. Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) has emerged as a promising therapeutic option for these patients. Over the past 15 years, the TMVR field has substantially progressed, with multiple devices advancing to human clinical evaluation. This review aims to provide an overview of the key milestones in TMVR development, patient selection pathways, and the transition from transapical to transseptal delivery. We further summarize the available clinical outcomes across different platforms and discuss remaining knowledge gaps, as well as future directions for this evolving field.
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement: Clinical Challenges, Evolving Indications, and Future Directions.

abstract: Femoral artery pseudoaneurysm is a serious vascular complication after venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) decannulation, and optimal management remains challenging. We report the case of a 74-year-old man with acute pulmonary embolism who developed a common femoral artery pseudoaneurysm after VA-ECMO removal. Ultrasound-guided compression was unsuccessful, and surgical repair was considered but deferred because of the patient's clinical condition and operating room unavailability. Balloon-assisted percutaneous thrombin injection achieved complete thrombosis without distal embolization or other complications. This technique may represent a feasible, minimally invasive alternative to surgical repair for femoral artery pseudoaneurysms following VA-ECMO decannulation, particularly in high-risk surgical patients.

title: Successful balloon-assisted percutaneous thrombin injection for common femoral artery pseudoaneurysm after venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation decannulation.

abstract: The use of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for patients with cardiopulmonary compromise is on the rise. While these tMCS systems provide life-saving interventions, they also pose a significant risk of nosocomial infections, which are associated with higher mortality rates. Patients receiving tMCS are critically ill and require intensive care, increasing their vulnerability to infections. Common nosocomial infections include bloodstream infections (BSI) and ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in patients with ECMO and wound-related complications in patients with microaxial temporary ventricular assist devices (tVADs). Key preventative measures include the incorporation of sound ICU practices such as chlorhexidine washes, minimizing disconnections, instituting VAP bundles, and promoting enteral nutrition. The practice of continuing prophylactic antibiotics while patients are on ECMO is not routinely recommended. While treatment strategies hinge primarily on antibiotics, ensuring adequate therapeutic levels of antibiotics is challenging and may contribute to suboptimal response to systemic antibiotics in these patients. A strategy of early liberation of patients from ECMO and conversion to temporary ventricular support (temporary LVAD, RVAD, or both) may promote early extubation and patient mobilization. Whether this strategy independently reduces infectious complications remains unknown. This review examines the epidemiology and etiology of nosocomial infections in patients receiving tMCS, summarizes current prevention and treatment strategies, and discusses the impact of infection on clinical outcomes.
title: Limiting collateral damage: Nosocomial infections in patients with temporary mechanical circulatory support.

abstract: We present a case of platypnea-orthodeoxia syndrome (POS) associated with patent foramen ovale (PFO). In the upright position, right atrial compression resulting from a dilated ascending aorta and thoracic kyphosis modifies the spatial alignment of the PFO, orienting it toward inferior vena cava (IVC) inflow and increasing its tendency to remain patent. Further, a prominent Eustachian valve redirected blood returning from the IVC toward the PFO and thereby promoting right-to-left shunting. The patient subsequently underwent percutaneous transcatheter PFO closure. Even 10 months after the procedure, oxygen saturation measured on room air remained stable at 99% in both supine and upright positions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency medical service (EMS) use reduces time to treatment and improves outcomes in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), yet it is unknown whether all Australians have equitable access to EMS. This systematic review examined whether equity-related factors are associated with disparities in EMS use for patients with ACS in Australia.
METHODS: The review was pre-registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023466951). Six databases (MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Cochrane and Scopus) were searched in June 2025 for articles published from inception until May 2025. Eligible studies involved adults presenting to Australian hospitals or emergency departments with ACS or acute non-traumatic chest pain and reported EMS use by at least one PROGRESS-Plus equity-related factor. Risk of bias was assessed using JBI checklists. Findings were synthesized using tabular analysis and a vote-counting summary.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were identified, with twelve rated high quality. EMS utilization ranged from 36% to 79% and increased over time. Disparities were evident across multiple equity-related factors. Adults aged under 49 years had up to 68% lower odds of EMS use than those 65 years or older. Men had up to 11% lower odds than women. People born outside Australia had up to 15% lower odds, and those preferring non-English languages had 6-20% lower odds. Residents of remote areas had up to 25% lower odds than major city residents, while individuals living alone had up to 48% higher odds than those living with others. Findings for socioeconomic status measures were mixed.
CONCLUSION: EMS use for ACS in Australia is consistently lower among younger adults, men, people born overseas, those preferring non-English languages, and residents of remote areas. These findings can inform targeted interventions to improve EMS accessibility. Future research should examine the mechanisms underlying these access barriers, particularly for populations experiencing multiple forms of disadvantage.
title: Equity-Related Factors in Emergency Medical Service Use for Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Systematic Review.

abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a heterogeneous clinical entity that may mimic acute coronary syndromes despite the absence of significant epicardial coronary artery disease. Inflammatory myocardial conditions, such as myocarditis and perimyocarditis, represent important non-ischemic causes of MINOCA and may present with life-threatening complications, including malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. We report a case of a 37-year-old previously healthy male who presented with chest discomfort, syncope, and sudden cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation. Post-cardiac arrest electrocardiography revealed extensive anterior ST-segment elevation, with markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers and transient severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Coronary angiography demonstrated non-obstructive epicardial coronary arteries, leading to the diagnosis of MINOCA. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed late gadolinium enhancement in a pattern consistent with perimyocarditis. The patient required advanced life support and intensive care management for cardiogenic shock, followed by progressive clinical improvement with complete recovery of left ventricular function. This case highlights perimyocarditis as a rare but critical cause of MINOCA presenting with sudden cardiac arrest and malignant ventricular arrhythmias in a young patient. It underscores the importance of a systematic diagnostic approach and emphasizes cardiac magnetic resonance as a key tool for etiological diagnosis, guiding appropriate management and enabling full functional recovery.
title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest in a Previously Healthy Young Male: Perimyocarditis Presenting as Myocardial Infarction With Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is highly prevalent in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), even in the presence of preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Structural, functional, and electrical atrial remodeling may differentially influence outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), although their integrated prognostic role remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To assess whether multimodal markers of AtCM identify distinct risk phenotypes associated with adverse outcomes after TAVI in patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 122 consecutive patients with severe AS, preserved LVEF, and sinus rhythm undergoing TAVI. Structural/functional AtCM (Echo-AtCM Risk) was assessed using indexed left atrial volume (LAVI) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr), whereas electrical AtCM (ECG-AtCM Risk) was defined according to P-wave duration and morphology. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and new-onset AF. Prognostic associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Mean age was 82.3±5.6 years. High Echo-Risk was present in 54.1% of patients and High ECG-Risk in 19.7%. During a median follow-up of 13.6 months, the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization occurred in 39 patients (32.0%), while new-onset AF developed in 17 (13.9%). High Echo-Risk independently predicted death/HF hospitalization (HR 4.17, p=0.008), whereas High ECG-Risk independently predicted incident AF (HR 3.07, p=0.034). Combined profiling identified distinct phenotypes: High Echo/Low ECG predicted HF/death (HR 4.86, p=0.008), Low Echo/High ECG predicted AF (HR 8.99, p=0.004), and combined High Echo/High ECG conferred the worst prognosis (HR 6.23, p=0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Structural, functional, and electrical AtCM represent complementary domains with distinct prognostic implications in AS patients undergoing TAVI. Their integration may refine post-TAVI risk stratification; these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical management can be guided by AtCM phenotype.Keywords: Atrial cardiomyopathy; Aortic stenosis; TAVI; Left atrial strain; Heart failure; Atrial fibrillation.
title: Multimodal Atrial Cardiomyopathy Phenotypes for Risk Stratification in Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVI.

abstract: Hypothermia is recognised as a reversible cause of cardiac arrest along with hypoxia, hypovolaemia and hypo or hyperkalaemia. However, hypothermia is the rarer one of these 'four Hs'. Because cardiac arrest caused primarily by hypothermia is a rare occurrence, resuscitation teams may lack real-world experience of it. This article sets out essential information for emergency department staff to understand this presentation and its management. It provides background information on hypothermia, describes the usual pattern of deterioration leading to cardiac arrest, and explains the key interventions required to give patients the best chance of survival, whether or not extracorporeal life support is accessible. It details the guideline recommendations that differ from standard advanced life support procedures and are specific to the management of hypothermic patients in cardiac arrest.
journal: Emergency nurse : the journal of the RCN Accident and Emergency Nursing Association
title: Hospital resuscitation in patients with primary hypothermic cardiac arrest.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.
METHODS: The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.
title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.

abstract: Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.
title: Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has been associated with better clinical outcomes, but predictors of recovery remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify echocardiographic parameters associated with post-TAVR LVEF improvement in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) and reduced LVEF.
METHODS: Among 1,133 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR between December 2013 and June 2024, 128 with baseline LVEF < 50% and follow-up echocardiography within 3 months were analyzed. LVEF improvement was defined as an absolute increase ≥ 10%. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Post-procedural outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: LVEF improvement occurred in 64 patients (50%). Multivariable analysis identified higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, P = 0.01) and higher E/e' (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.18, P < 0.01) as independent predictors of improvement, whereas larger left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (OR 0.98, P = 0.01) and larger AVA (OR 0.67 per 0.1 cm², P < 0.01) were inversely associated. Patients with LVEF improvement had significantly lower 1-year all-cause mortality (98.2% vs. 87.0%, P = 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic parameters reflecting pressure overload and diastolic dysfunction predict LVEF recovery after TAVR. Postoperative LVEF improvement was associated with better 1-year survival, underscoring its prognostic value.
title: Echocardiographic predictors of left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intervention-related complications negatively affect healthcare quality and costs. Complication registration and reporting play an important role in the improvement of healthcare outcomes but are time-consuming and hampered by under-reporting.
METHODS: We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-aided tool that extracts specific complications, including bleeding, tamponade, CVA and phrenic paralysis, from electronic healthcare records of patients undergoing pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Both structured and unstructured data were used, along with additional signals identified through machine learning. The model was optimized to achieve high sensitivity.
RESULTS: Electronic records of 6,564 patients undergoing PVI, PTCA, and TAVI, performed at our hospital from 2017-2022, were used. The final model detected the various complications with a sensitivity between 94.4 and 100%, while specificity ranged from 99.4-100%. This resulted in positive predictive values ranging from 47.5-81%, with F‑scores varying between 0.64-0.87.
CONCLUSION: We developed an AI-driven tool capable of automatically detecting complications following cardiac interventions from patient healthcare records, achieving a very high sensitivity. Our tool enables registration of complications while significantly reducing administrative burden on the healthcare providers and data managers. It provides valuable and high-quality input for improvement cycles, thereby enhancing patient safety and healthcare quality.
journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
title: Development of an artificial intelligence algorithm for automated detection of cardiovascular intervention-related complications.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aims of this study are to assess clinical and patient-centered outcomes following admission for HF as stratified by ADRD status.
METHODS: We identified patients 65 years or older in the OneFlorida+ data trust with first admission for HF between October 1, 2015 and December 31, 2022. ICD-10 diagnoses codes were used to identify HF, ADRD, and relevant comorbidities. Exclusion criteria were admission with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or shock. The primary clinical outcome was all-cause 1-year mortality, and the secondary clinical outcome was 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes were length of stay and discharge home.
RESULTS: 22,342 patients with first HF hospitalization during the study period were identified. Of these, 5,261 (23.5%) patients carried a diagnosis of ADRD. Patients with ADRD were more likely to be women (57.7% vs. 53.1%, p<0.05) and Black (21.1% vs. 14.6%, p<0.05). 1-year mortality was higher in patients with ADRD (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.10-1.36, p < 0.005) as was 90-day readmissions (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.18-1.28, p <0.005). Patients with ADRD demonstrated longer lengths of stays (5.7 vs. 5.4 days, p <0.005) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR .81, 95% CI 0.77-0.84, p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Patients with ADRD hospitalized for HF demonstrate higher 1-year mortality and 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes are also worse in patients with ADRD, with longer lengths of stay and are less discharge home. These findings should be used to identify research priorities and to facilitate advanced care planning in patients with ADRD and HF.
title: Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias is Associated with Worse Clinical and Patient-centered Outcomes in Patient Admitted for Heart Failure.

abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) are increasingly discussed as complementary strategies in atrial fibrillation (AF) care, addressing rhythm control and long-term thromboembolic risk. The rationale is attractive, but the current evidence base is uneven. Randomized evidence for LAAC around AF ablation is strongest for thermal-ablation-era workflows, particularly the OPTION trial, which showed lower non-procedure-related major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding with LAAC than with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and non-inferiority for death, stroke, or systemic embolism. Dedicated PFA-specific evidence remains limited to feasibility studies and early observational experience, and no trial has demonstrated that combined ablation-LAAC procedures are clinically superior when the ablation component is performed with PFA rather than radiofrequency or cryoballoon ablation. In parallel, OAC-withdrawal trials after apparently successful ablation, including OCEAN and ALONE-AF, have reported low thromboembolic event rates in selected lower-risk populations, whereas CLOSURE-AF cautions against simple extrapolation of LAAC benefit to older, frailer patients at high stroke and bleeding risk. This review therefore positions combined PFA-LAAC as a potential option for carefully selected patients rather than an established routine strategy. We summarize procedural workflow, patient selection, trial populations, device-platform considerations, reimbursement and organizational issues, and the main uncertainties that should guide future prospective studies.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Although non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant (NOAC) monotherapy is generally recommended beyond 1 year after drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), the temporal evolution of ischemic and bleeding risks remains inadequately characterized. This study assessed whether the effects of NOAC monotherapy versus combination therapy differ by stent age in patients with AF who underwent DES implantation ≥ 1 year earlier.
METHODS: This prespecified analysis of the Appropriate Duration of Anti-Platelet and Thrombotic Strategy After 12 Months in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Treated with Drug-Eluting Stents (ADAPT AF-DES) trial compared NOAC monotherapy with combination therapy (NOAC plus clopidogrel) by stent age. Patients were classified into the remote percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) group (stent age > 2 years; n = 577) and the intermediate PCI group (stent age 1-2 years; n = 383). The primary endpoint was 1-year net adverse clinical events (NACE).
RESULTS: No significant interaction between antithrombotic strategy and stent age was found for NACE. NOAC monotherapy was associated with less major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than combination therapy in both subgroups without interaction. Although a significant interaction was observed for composite ischemic outcomes in the prespecified analysis, it was no longer observed when stent age was modeled as a continuous variable or after adjustment in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with AF ≥ 1 year post-DES, no consistent interactions by stent age were observed for clinical outcomes, supporting the safety and effectiveness of NOAC monotherapy across the spectrum of stent age.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of the ADAPT AF-DES trial; remote PCI group (stent age > 2 years; n = 577) and intermediate PCI group (stent age 1-2 years; n = 383).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; the ischaemic outcome interaction was inconsistent across modelling approaches.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified analysis of ADAPT AF-DES testing whether stent age modifies the effect of NOAC monotherapy versus NOAC plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant interaction between antithrombotic strategy and stent age was found for NACE. NOAC monotherapy was associated with less major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than combination therapy in both subgroups without interaction.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In patients undergoing surgical repair of posterior mitral valve prolapse, we compared outcomes in high- and low-volume mitral surgery hospitals to those predicted by the AATS Adult Quality Gateway (AQG) and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (STS-ACSD).
METHODS: Five hospitals performed 1,517 mitral valve operations, 1,471 repairs (97%) and 46 replacements (3.0%), in the AQG training set of 55,246 adult patients. Mitral repair techniques included leaflet resection (80%), creating artificial chordae (20%), and anuloplasty (99%); surgical approach was sternotomy or partial sternotomy in 945 (64%) and anterior thoracotomy or robotic in 525 (36%). The remaining 14 hospitals performed 159 mitral valve operations, 145 repairs (91%) and 14 (8.8%) replacements.
RESULTS: In high-volume hospitals, predicted mortality by AQG was 0.87% and by STS-ACSD 0.77%; however, observed mortality was 1 patient (0.070%). For major morbidity and mortality, AQG predicted 8.1% and STS-ACSD 6.5%, but observed was 4.0%. Patients undergoing valve replacement were more likely to be older and more symptomatic and had more tricuspid regurgitation and mitral anular calcification. All repair outcomes were worse (e.g., operative mortality was 3/145 [2.1%]) in low-volume hospitals.
CONCLUSIONS: Requiring limited data entry and employing novel statistical methodology (e.g. virtual twins), AQG provided predictions similar to those of STS-ACSD, both confirming and augmenting understanding of the volume-outcome relationship in surgical management of posterior mitral valve prolapse.

abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed.
RESULTS: MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75).
CONCLUSIONS: The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.
title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting regional left ventricular (LV) functional recovery is essential for optimizing patient selection for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in chronic total occlusion (CTO), yet direct comparisons of imaging modalities remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), alone and in combination, for regional LV wall motion recovery after PCI for CTO.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We prospectively examined 66 patients with CTO undergoing successful PCI. Multimodality imaging was performed within 3 months prior to PCI. Wall motion recovery was defined as an improvement of ≥1 grade in segmental wall motion score assessed by resting echocardiography at 6 to 8 months post-PCI. Among 153 dysfunctional segments within the CTO territory, recovery was observed in 115 (75%). DSE at 20 μg/kg/min demonstrated high sensitivity (96.5%), CMR demonstrated high specificity (68.4%), and SPECT showed moderate sensitivity (76.5%) and specificity (52.6%). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of CMR and DSE (0.819) was comparable to that of all three modalities combined (0.825) and significantly exceeded that of any single modality (CMR: 0.738, DSE: 0.733; both P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CTO undergoing PCI, multimodality imaging provides complementary information for predicting regional LV wall motion recovery. An imaging strategy in which modalities are selected and combined according to the clinical context may help optimize decision-making for revascularization.

Combining dobutamine stress echo and cardiac MRI matched 3-modality performance, aiding CTO revascularization decisions. #CTO #CardioTwitter.
title: Multimodality imaging for predicting regional wall motion recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balancing thrombotic and bleeding risk in patients requiring direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains challenging. This study evaluated the safety of dual antithrombotic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel in patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndrome or with high thrombotic risk.
METHODS: The ReDUAL PCI Real Life study was a Dutch, open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomized controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), aiming to enrol 850 patients. Patients requiring DOAC were randomized 1:1 to DOAC plus ticagrelor or DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI. The primary endpoint was any bleeding (BARC ≥2) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and net adverse clinical events (NACE: MACCE plus major bleeding). Outcomes were compared with a non-randomized ZON-HR cohort eligible for inclusion.
RESULTS: The study was terminated prematurely due to slow recruitment, with 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel). Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance. In 397 eligible non-randomized clopidogrel-treated patients, major bleeding rate was 3.4%, MACCE occurred in 12.5% and NACE in 14.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing PCI requiring oral anticoagulation, DOAC plus ticagrelor showed similar overall bleeding but numerical increase in major bleeding without apparent ischemic benefit compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel. This prematurely terminated study was underpowered, limiting abilities to draw definitive conclusions.

abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute, usually reversible left ventricular dysfunction mimicking acute coronary syndrome without a culprit epicardial lesion. Once considered benign, it carries in-hospital mortality comparable to ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is frequently observed during the acute phase, but its relationship to TTS remains uncertain: it may be a predisposing substrate, a mediator of catecholamine-induced injury, or a consequence of edema, extravascular compression, altered loading conditions, and ventricular dysfunction, and human evidence shows association rather than mechanism. The index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) is an established invasive measure of hyperemic microvascular resistance. In TTS, IMR is frequently elevated during the acute phase, and microvascular function appears to improve as left ventricular function recovers, although often incompletely. In a pooled analysis of individual patient data from 166 patients, acute-phase IMR was the only invasive index that remained associated with mortality after adjustment. The cutoff of 54 used in that analysis is an exploratory, hypothesis-generating prognostic threshold: derived within the same dataset, it requires external validation and should be distinguished from the diagnostic threshold of ≥25 used in CMD algorithms that have not been validated in acute conditions such as TTS. Wire-based IMR remains the gold standard; angiography-derived IMR is promising, but available software platforms remain investigational. This review examines proposed mechanisms, measurement methods and their validation, prognostic evidence, and management, and outlines a workflow for future research. We conclude that the clinical utility and optimal timing of invasive coronary function testing in TTS remain uncertain.
title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in takotsubo syndrome: An interventional perspective on pathophysiology, diagnostic workflow and prognosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise systolic blood pressure (SBP) indexed to fitness, expressed as SBP divided by peak metabolic equivalents (SBP/METpeak), is associated with cardiovascular events in patients undergoing exercise testing. We aimed to characterise the cardiac phenotype and outcomes of patients with elevated exercise SBP indexed to fitness.
METHODS: We analysed 530 participants with suspected angina from the CE-MARC trial who had complete exercise treadmill testing, invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging. High SBP/METpeak was defined as ≥18 mm Hg/METs. Obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) was defined by quantitative ICA as ≥70% stenosis in a major epicardial artery. Inducible ischaemia and myocardial scar were assessed by stress perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement CMR, respectively. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were defined as all-cause death and acute coronary syndrome.
RESULTS: High SBP/METpeak was present in 310 participants (58.5%) and prevalence increased progressively with the number of diseased vessels, presence of ischaemia and myocardial scar (p<0.01 for all). During a median follow-up of 15.9 years, high SBP/METpeak was associated with MACE after adjustment for age, sex, obstructive CAD, ischaemia and myocardial scar (adjusted HR per 1-unit increase, 1.02 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.03), p=0.012). Higher SBP/METpeak identified a worse prognosis in subgroups with and without obstructive CAD and in those with and without ischaemia or infarction (log-rank, p<0.005 for all).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with suspected angina, high SBP/METpeak was associated with myocardial ischaemia and scar and adverse long-term outcomes. However, this association appeared to be driven predominantly by lower exercise capacity rather than peak SBP. SBP/METpeak may therefore represent an exploratory integrated exercise marker requiring external validation.
title: Association of exercise blood pressure relative to fitness with coronary artery disease.

abstract: Hypertension prevention, diagnosis, and management are central to modifying the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although the nephrology community has long recognized CKD as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease, CKD has not historically been incorporated in cardiovascular risk prediction models. The new 2025 American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults addresses this gap by formally adopting the PREVENT calculator, which combines cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic health parameters to guide risk assessment and clinical decision making. The AHA/ACC guideline reinforces the broad blood pressure target of <130/80 mm Hg as well as makes recommendations for complex and resistant hypertension. Given the impact of these recommendations on persons living with kidney disease, the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) convened an expert work group to review and comment on the guideline. This KDOQI commentary focuses on recommendations from the AHA/ACC guideline that are pertinent to individuals at risk of CKD or with non-dialysis-dependent CKD (stages 1-5), hence excluding commentary on hypertension management in patients receiving maintenance dialysis. In areas where the AHA/ACC guideline does not offer formal recommendations (eg, medication interactions, electrolyte imbalances, and kidney injury), the work group provides expert commentary about implications for people with CKD. Overall, the work group supports the majority of the AHA/ACC recommendations and identifies areas where evidence remains limited or management in CKD warrants additional consideration.
journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
title: KDOQI Commentary on the 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.

abstract: This article is a review of the 2024 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Guideline for Perioperative Cardiovascular Management for Noncardiac Surgery, an update of previous guidelines published in 2014. The current epidemiology of cardiovascular disease in the US surgical population is discussed followed by sections exploring risk factors for the occurrence of major adverse cardiac and cerebral events (MACCE), specific recommendations for preoperative evaluation, perioperative management, and postoperative surveillance for MACCE and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery.
title: What's New in Cardiac Risk Assessment and Mitigation-The 2024 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Guidelines for Perioperative Cardiovascular Management for Noncardiac Surgery.

abstract: Objective: To investigate the incidence of in-hospital heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) and 1-year mortality in patients with first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to compare the 1-year mortality risk among different types of HF. Methods: Data were derived from the Henan STEMI registry, which was a multicentre, prospective, observational study in central China. After excluding patients with a history of MI or HF, patients with first STEMI were divided into the HF and non-HF groups according to the occurrence of in-hospital HF. Based on the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measured on the last echocardiogram during hospitalization, patients with HF were classified into HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF≥50%), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF, LVEF 41%-49%), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF≤40%), and HF with missing LVEF. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and differences between groups were assessed with the log-rank test. Multivariate Cox frailty models were used to analyze the associations of HF status (present vs. absent) and different LVEF subgroups with 1-year mortality, using the non-HF group as the reference. Results: A total of 4 737 patients with first STEMI were included in the final analysis, with a median age of 62.8 (52.4, 70.8) years, of whom 1 158 (24.4%) were female. During hospitalization, 1 978 cases (41.8%) developed HF following MI, including 268 (13.5%) with HFrEF, 309 (15.6%) with HFmrEF, 707 (35.7%) with HFpEF, and 694 (35.1%) with missing LVEF. A total of 3 967 (83.7%) patients completed the 1-year follow-up. The 1-year mortality was significantly higher among STEMI patients complicated by HF than in those without (23.3% (391/1 680) vs. 5.8% (132/2 287), log-rank P<0.001). Specifically, the rates were 29.6% (67/226) for HFrEF, 20.8% (53/255) for HFmrEF, 11.7% (72/615) for HFpEF and 34.1% (199/584) for HF with missing LVEF. Multivariate Cox frailty models identified in-hospital HF following MI as a risk factor for 1-year mortality (HR=2.13, 95%CI: 1.70-2.67). Notably, HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk of 1-year mortality (HR=1.59, 95%CI: 1.16-2.17), while the HF group with missing LVEF carried the highest risk (HR=2.49, 95%CI: 1.91-3.26). Conclusions: The incidence of HF following first STEMI during hospitalization was 41.8%, with a corresponding 1-year mortality of 23.3%. In-hospital HF following MI is a risk factor for 1-year mortality in patients with STEMI. Prognosis differed notably across HF subgroups: HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk, whereas patients with missing LVEF had the worst outcome.

abstract: Objective: To investigate the association of baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and its clinical prognostic value in patients with coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and receiving clopidogrel. Methods: This was a single-center prospective cohort study. Consecutive patients with coronary artery disease who underwent PCI at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January and December 2013 were enrolled; those receiving dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel were included. Baseline data were collected, and platelet reactivity was assessed using thromboelastography. Patients were followed up for 5 years, with cardiac death as the endpoint. Baseline eosinophil count was analyzed as a continuous variable and was also categorized into quartiles (Q1-Q4). Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze the association between eosinophil count and high on-treatment platelet reactivity. Multivariable restricted cubic spline models were used to analyze the dose-response relationship. Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed according to age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to assess the predictive value of eosinophil count for cardiac death. Results: A total of 6 524 patients were included. The mean age was (58.21±10.26) years, and 5 059 (77.54%) were male. Among them, 6 050 patients completed the 5-year follow-up, and 140 cardiac deaths (2.31%) occurred. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was negatively associated with the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (OR=0.94, 95%CI: 0.90-0.98, P=0.003). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the lowest quartile group (Q1), the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity was lower in patients in the highest quartile group (Q4) (OR=0.77, 95%CI: 0.65-0.91, P=0.003). Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis showed a linear negative correlation between eosinophil count and the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (P for overall=0.012, P for nonlinearity=0.362). Further subgroup analysis showed that the above association remained consistent across clinical subgroups stratified by age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels (all P for interaction>0.05). Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was positively associated with the risk of cardiac death (HR=1.14, 95%CI: 1.07-1.21, P<0.001). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the Q1 group, the risk of cardiac death was higher in patients in the Q4 group (HR=2.12, 95%CI: 1.25-3.59, P<0.001). Conclusions: In patients with coronary artery disease undergoing PCI and receiving clopidogrel, baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count showed a dual association with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death. A lower count was associated with an increased risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, whereas an elevated count was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiac death.

abstract: Objective: To construct a machine-learning-based prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: A total of 5829 patients with STEMI who underwent emergency PCI at the Emergency Critical Care Center of Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University, from January 1, 2015, to July 1, 2025, were enrolled. Patients were divided into the MACE group (524 cases) and the non-MACE group (5 305 cases) according to the occurrence of in-hospital MACE and were further divided into the training set (4 080 cases) and test set (1 749 cases) at a ratio of 7∶3. MACE included cardiogenic shock, severe heart failure, severe arrhythmia, acute stent thrombosis or recurrent acute myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and cardiogenic death. Demographic data, lifestyle-related factors, past medical history, admission vital signs, laboratory test results within 24 hours after admission, echocardiographic parameters, Killip classification, and coronary interventional data were collected. Univariate analysis and Lasso regression were performed to select variables for model construction. Five machine-learning algorithms, including support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression, random forest, naive Bayes, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were used to construct prediction models for in-hospital MACE. The optimal model was selected based on the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis were used to assess the probability calibration and clinical net benefit of the model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the contribution of each feature. Results: The patients were aged (58.1±12.3) years, and 4 875 (83.63%) were male. Fourteen variables were selected for model construction, including B-type natriuretic peptide, myoglobin, left ventricular ejection fraction, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-sensitivity troponin I, triglycerides, triglyceride-glucose index, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, glycated hemoglobin, creatine kinase-MB, smoking history, heart rate, Killip classification, and age. The XGBoost model yielded the best predictive performance, with an AUC-ROC of 0.992 and an AUPRC of 0.947, and exhibited favorable probability calibration and clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis demonstrated that the top five variables with the greatest contribution to model prediction were B-type natriuretic peptide, creatine kinase-MB, myoglobin, left ventricular ejection fraction, and triglyceride-glucose index. Conclusions: Machine-learning prediction models for in-hospital MACE after emergency PCI in patients with STEMI were successfully constructed and internally validated. The XGBoost model demonstrated good discriminative ability, probability calibration, and clinical net benefit and may serve as a reference for early in-hospital risk stratification and clinical decision-making in STEMI patients undergoing emergency PCI.

abstract: Objective: To preliminarily evaluate the efficacy and safety of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the mitral valve (MV-TEER) guided solely by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Methods: A total of 46 patients with mitral regurgitation who underwent MV-TEER guided solely by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at Central China Fuwai Hospital of Zhengzhou University from January 2023 to January 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up was performed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after the procedure, including echocardiography, 6-minute walk test, New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification, and grading of mitral regurgitation severity. Hospitalization for heart failure, repeat mitral valve intervention, and all-cause mortality were recorded. The cumulative incidence of rehospitalization for heart failure was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results: The median age of the enrolled patients was 67.5 (59.0, 73.0) years, and 29 patients (63%) were male. MV-TEER was successfully performed under sole TEE guidance in all 46 patients. The median follow-up duration was 15.80 (12.63, 20.64) months. The 1-year rehospitalization rate for heart failure was 20%, and 1 patient died of malignant arrhythmia. There was no repeat mitral valve intervention. At 1 year after the procedure, the left ventricular end-systolic diameter decreased significantly from (47.17±11.31) mm to (39.71±7.44) mm (P<0.05). The left ventricular end-systolic volume decreased from (87.02±20.63) ml to (72.18±17.30) ml (P<0.05), and the left ventricular ejection fraction improved from (44.98±11.78)% to (51.84±10.03)% (P<0.05). Five patients had mitral regurgitation grade 3+, while the remaining patients had grade less than 3+. Three patients were in NYHA functional class Ⅲ, 23 in class Ⅱ, and 19 in class Ⅰ. The 6-minute walk distance improved significantly from (298±78) m to (375±70) m (P<0.05). Conclusion: It is preliminarily demonstrated that MV-TEER guided solely by TEE is safe and effective, and patients have favorable midterm outcomes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the randomized CRABBIS trial, a proximal optimization technique (POT)-kissing-POT (PKP) sequence gave a better optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined stent geometry than POT-Side-POT (PSP) in large bifurcations. Whether a suboptimal PSP result can be corrected during the same procedure is unknown.
METHODS: In this pre-specified OCT sub-analysis, a suboptimal post-PSP result (minimal stent area < 90% of reference and/or malapposition) was corrected with kissing-balloon inflation and final POT. Stent geometry before and after correction was compared across four segments and with the randomized single-stent PKP arm.
RESULTS: The result was suboptimal in 22 of 30 patients (73.3%); 16 had paired OCT. After correction, minimal stent area increased in the proximal (12.5 to 14.6 mm2) and distal main vessel (7.4 to 9.1 mm2), both significant after Holm correction, and distal underexpansion fell from 13/16 (81%) to 5/16 (31%). Proximal-edge and bifurcation-core gains and the reduction in malapposition did not survive correction; eccentricity did not change significantly. No significant difference from the single-stent PKP arm was found, but the study had 80% power only for differences of 2.1 to 3.3 mm2. Of eight results judged optimal, six still showed distal underexpansion.
CONCLUSIONS: A suboptimal PSP result can be improved in the same procedure by corrective kissing-balloon inflation and final POT, mainly through larger main-vessel stent area and expansion. It did not differ significantly from an upfront PKP, but equivalence cannot be established. A PSP result judged optimal during the procedure is not necessarily optimal at offline OCT analysis.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Corrective kissing balloon inflation for a suboptimal optical coherence tomography result after POT-side-POT: An OCT sub-analysis of the randomized CRABBIS trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The interplay between inflammation and atherosclerosis is well acknowledged. However, the role of the complement system in lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association of serum-complement levels with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: Adult hospitalized patients with ACS received rosuvastatin 40 mg with an LDL-C target of <55 mg/dL and a reduction of >50% of baseline. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein, complement C3c, C4, C5a levels, LDL-C, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and apolipoprotein B levels were measured before treatment initiation, 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months afterward. Patients were followed up for 12 months for major adverse cardiovascular events (nonfatal stroke, nonfatal myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death).
RESULTS: Among 130 patients (91.5% male; mean age 56 ± 9 years), 42 (32.3%) achieved the target at 6 weeks, 61 (46.9%) at 6 months, and 63 (48.5%) at 12 months. Serum C3c levels were lower at baseline in 6-week target achievers (median [Q1-Q3], 98.9 [86.9-107.3]) vs nonachievers (126.0 [112.0-136.0]; P < .001). Similarly, C4 levels were 21.4 (18.2-26.4) mg/dL in achievers vs nonachievers (26.8 [22.1-31.6] mg/dL; P < .001); C5a levels did not differ between groups. C3c predicted failure of target attainment at 6 weeks (area under the curve, 95% CI: 0.94, 0.90-0.98; P < .001). A cut-off value of 112.5 mg/dL demonstrated sensitivity 77.3%, specificity 92.3%, and independently predicted failure (adjusted odds ratio 52.54; 95% CI, 12.49-221.0).
CONCLUSION: In patients with ACS treated with rosuvastatin 40 mg, serum C3c levels are associated with failure of LDL-C target attainment. Further research is needed to determine if they may be used to guide LLT.
title: Association of serum complement levels with failure of low-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol target attainment in patients after acute coronary syndrome: A prospective, observational study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) is often prolonged, underscoring the need for timely strategy selection. Although several preprocedural scoring systems exist, they offer limited guidance regarding intraprocedural dynamics. This study aimed to develop a framework that updates success probabilities to support optimal strategy transitions during the procedure.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Two endpoints were defined: (1) successful crossing using antegrade wire escalation (AWE); and (2) time-constrained success using either AWE (<15 min) or advanced techniques (<60 min, intravascular ultrasound [IVUS] guided or retrograde). Preprocedural complexity scores (J-CTO, PROGRESS-CTO, CT-RECTOR) and procedural responses were sequentially incorporated into a Bayesian model to update real-time success probabilities. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation compared the procedural efficiency of advanced techniques. With an initial success probability of 50%, previous failure reduced the likelihood of AWE success to 26.5% and the time-based endpoint to 40.8%. Failure with intermediate-tip-load wires (~3 g) further decreased success probabilities to 6.1% for AWE and 30.5% for the time-based endpoint. When advanced strategies were required, IVUS-guided approaches showed a trend towards higher estimated procedural efficiency (76.6%) under feasibility-constrained conditions (mean difference: 3.0%; 95% credible interval: -5.6%, 11.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: A real-time Bayesian framework enables dynamic adaptation during CTO PCI and may help identify scenarios where earlier transition to advanced techniques is warranted based on evolving procedural information.
journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
title: Bayesian Real-Time Decision Support for Strategy Optimization in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct stenting (DS) is a simplified strategy for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, its role in the era of advanced intravascular imaging remains incompletely defined. We aimed to identify determinants of DS use and its impact on procedural efficiency and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined stent implantation quality in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The ATLAS-OCT trial was a prospective multicenter nationwide study mandating OCT guidance in Japan. In this subanalysis, clinical characteristics, angiographic and OCT findings, procedural metrics, and clinical outcomes were compared between patients undergoing DS and those treated with balloon predilatation. Among 436 patients, DS was performed in 32.1% (n=140), with marked interinstitutional variability (0-68.3%; P<0.01), suggesting a strong influence of operator preference. DS use was not associated with angiographic features or OCT-defined culprit plaque morphology. DS significantly reduced contrast volume and procedure time. Post-PCI OCT showed a trend towards a larger minimum stent area and greater stent expansion index with DS. These benefits were not associated with in-hospital or 1-year outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary OCT-guided primary PCI for STEMI, DS appears to be driven primarily by operator preference rather than lesion characteristics. In this study, DS was associated with improved procedural efficiency without significantly compromising OCT-assessed stent implantation quality or mid-term clinical safety.
journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
title: Determinants and Clinical Impact of Direct Stenting in Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction - An ATLAS-OCT Substudy.

abstract: Rapid population aging has increased the number of patients with severe acute cardiovascular diseases requiring intensive care. Contemporary cardiovascular intensive care has evolved beyond traditional management of acute coronary syndromes to encompass hemodynamic instability, multiple organ dysfunction, and advanced life-support technologies. Accordingly, cardiovascular intensive care units (CICUs) must provide comprehensive, tailored critical care for increasingly complex clinical conditions. In Japan, cardiovascular intensive care remains heterogeneous, with critically ill patients managed in various critical care settings. Structured care systems and specialist training remain underdeveloped. To clarify the current status, we reviewed nationwide survey data from the JROAD-DPC database. Substantial variability in institutional care systems, limited availability of dedicated cardiac care units/CICUs, and marked regional disparities in infrastructure and human resources were identified. Intensive care unit admission was associated with lower in-hospital mortality in cardiovascular emergencies, although these observational findings should be interpreted with caution because of potential residual confounding, differences in patient characteristics, and end-of-life care pathways. These findings support the need for appropriate triage and resource allocation according to patient acuity and institutional capability, rather than the uniform establishment of dedicated CICUs. Addressing these challenges will require optimized resource allocation, strengthened regional coordination, and structured training programs to establish sustainable cardiovascular intensive care systems in Japan.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of diabetes status on outcomes after physiology-guided revascularization remains unclear. This study evaluated clinical outcomes in patients with insulin-treated diabetes (ITD), non-ITD (NITD), and without diabetes after physiology-guided revascularization.
METHODS AND RESULTS: From the J-PRIDE registry, 3,140 patients were categorized into non-diabetes (n=1,797), NITD (n=1,133), and ITD (n=210) groups. The primary endpoint was the 1-year incidence of target vessel failure (TVF), a composite of cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target vessel revascularization. The 1-year TVF rate was significantly higher in the ITD and NITD groups than in the non-diabetes group (6.1% and 4.1% vs. 2.0%, respectively), with adjusted hazard ratios for the ITD and NTD groups of 2.14 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-4.19; P=0.027) and 1.63 (95 CI 1.02-2.61; P=0.041), respectively. The non-hyperemic pressure ratio cut-off predicting fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≤0.80 was lower in the ITD than NITD and non-diabetes groups (0.87 vs. 0.89 and 0.90, respectively). The ITD group had the highest risk of TVF across all FFR values, followed by the NITD and non-diabetes groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ITD and NITD exhibit worse clinical outcomes than those without diabetes. Notably, patients with ITD remained at elevated risk across the entire FFR spectrum, suggesting that physiological severity alone may not fully capture their residual cardiovascular risk.
