abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes, yet the underlying right atrial (RA) molecular remodeling remains poorly understood. We aimed to define TR-associated RA remodeling using metabolomic and lipidomic profiling of human RA tissue.
METHODS: RA appendage tissue was obtained intraoperatively from 24 adults undergoing cardiac surgery (11 with ≥severe TR; 13 controls). Gas chromatography mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used for targeted small-molecule metabolomics, and liquid chromatography quadrupole time of flight mass spectrometry (LC-qTOF-MS) for untargeted lipidomics. Mann Whitney U testing, principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), and variable importance in projection (VIP) scoring were used to identify discriminatory multi-omics patterns between groups.
RESULTS: Patients with TR demonstrated a distinct metabolic phenotype characterized by reduced glycolysis-related intermediates (glucose-6-phosphate, β-alanine, α-glucosamine-1-phosphate; all p < 0.05) and metabolites consistent with oxidative stress and amino acid catabolism markers (6-hydroxycaproic acid, porphine, phosphoric acid; all p < 0.05). Lipidomic analysis revealed broad phospholipid remodeling and signals consistent with mitochondrial-associated alterations, including a decreased phosphatidylcholine/phosphatidylethanolamine (PC/PE) ratio and reductions in selected diacylglycerol and ceramide species. PCA and PLS-DA demonstrated clear group separation with consistent VIP signals, indicating consistent multi-omics discrimination.
CONCLUSIONS: TR is associated with coordinated metabolic and lipidomic reprogramming in the RA, a pattern compatible with, though not direct evidence of, mitochondrial stress, impaired bioenergetics, and membrane destabilization. These findings support a model in which RA remodeling is tightly linked to TR pathophysiology, highlighting candidate molecular features for future validation. Multi-omics biomarkers may enhance risk stratification, inform the timing of intervention, and guide the development of future point-of-care molecular diagnostics.
title: Multi-omics analysis of human right atrial tissue ıdentifies molecular signatures of remodeling in tricuspid regurgitation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-obstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD) represents an increasing proportion of patients presenting with angina, yet these patients face significant cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to explore distinct classes in NOCAD patients based on demographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities, and inflammatory biomarkers, and to investigate their associations with prognosis.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients diagnosed with NOCAD by coronary angiography for angina between January 1, 2023, and December 1, 2024, with follow-up until August 1, 2025. Latent Class Analysis (LCA) was employed to identify distinct classes based on demographic features, inflammatory markers, including 8 composite inflammatory indices. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations between different classes and individual inflammatory markers with clinical outcomes after multivariate adjustment. Prognostic discrimination compared with traditional risk factors was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.
RESULTS: Among 342 NOCAD patients, LCA identified three distinct classes: low-inflammation with few comorbidities (n = 156, 45.6%), elderly with multiple comorbidities (n = 126, 36.8%), and high-inflammation subgroup (n = 60, 17.5%). Over a median follow-up of 363 days (interquartile range, 193-613 days), 89 patients (26.0%) experienced MACEs. In fully adjusted models, the high-inflammation class was the strongest predictor of MACEs (HR 3.090, 95% CI: 1.614-5.919), followed by the elderly with multiple comorbidities class (HR 2.181, 95% CI: 1.224-3.886). Among 8 composite inflammatory indices evaluated, three demonstrated significant associations with MACEs: the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index (per unit increase in Z-score, HR 0.402, 95% CI: 0.230-0.703), neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR) index (per unit increase in Z-score, HR 1.234, 95% CI: 1.002-1.522), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) index (Z-score > 0, HR 1.635, 95% CI: 1.007-2.655). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated significant differences in MACE-free survival across the three classes (log-rank p = 0.001), with CALLY, NAR, and AISI also showing significant prognostic discrimination. Component analysis revealed the high-inflammation phenotype was independently associated with a 2.44-fold increased risk of hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure (HR = 2.44, 95% CI 1.230-4.846), accounting for 60.67% of total MACEs. These findings were consistently reproduced in a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients without a history of myocardial infarction.
CONCLUSION: Inflammatory and clinical phenotyping identifies distinct risk subgroups in NOCAD. While the high-inflammation phenotype is associated with the highest overall MACEs risk, this prognostic signal is predominantly driven by hospitalizations for unstable angina or heart failure. These findings suggest that inflammation-based phenotyping could serve as an exploratory complementary tool for risk stratification, requiring further external validation before any routine clinical application.
title: Inflammation-based phenotyping and prognostic implications in patients with non-obstructive coronary artery disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: After mitral valve replacement with preservation of the subvalvular apparatus, prosthetic dysfunction resulting from retained native structures is extremely rare. When it occurs, it may directly threaten the patient's life. We report an unusual case of severe regurgitation resulting from preserved chordal rupture. The key distinction of this case is the presentation of late, severe continuous prosthetic regurgitation and reversibility.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man had undergone double mechanical valve replacement for severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with mild regurgitation and concomitant aortic regurgitation three years earlier. During surgery, the posterior mitral leaflet and its entire subvalvular apparatus were preserved. Current transesophageal echocardiography revealed a mobile, cord-like structure between the lateral occluder and the prosthetic sewing ring, interfering with leaflet excursion and preventing full closure. This was accompanied by severe prosthetic mitral continuous regurgitation. Surgical findings revealed a ruptured chordae tendineae at the papillary muscle attachment, with the remnant preventing leaflet coaptation. Surgical excision of the ruptured chordal remnant successfully restored normal leaflet function, with complete resolution of the regurgitation confirmed on intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography.
CONCLUSIONS: When obstruction or regurgitation develops after valve replacement with subvalvular preservation, uncommon causes-such as residual subvalvular tissue or ruptured chordal entrapment-should be considered after excluding more common etiologies. This case illustrates the critical role of transesophageal echocardiography in the diagnosis of chordal entrapment after mitral valve replacement and potentially in preventing complications. The potential benefit of preserving the subvalvular apparatus warrants thoughtful deliberation. Surgical removal of the offending tissue or valve replacement remains the definitive treatment.
keywords: Mitral valve replacement with preserved subvalvular apparatus
title: Severe continuous prosthetic mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture after valve-sparing replacement: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to elucidate research trends, collaborative networks, and the thematic evolution of predictors for coronary slow flow (CSF).
METHODS: Relevant literature published between 1977 and 2026 was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database. Bibliometric analysis was conducted utilizing VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R 4.3.3.
RESULTS: A total of 366 articles were included, indicating an upward trend in research output. China (118 articles), Turkey (65), and the USA (35) emerged as the leading countries. Prominent institutions included China Medical University (29 articles), Capital Medical University (20), and Tabriz University of Medical Sciences (14). Influential journals were Circulation (impact factor 41.3, JCR Q1), Circulation Journal (5.8, Q1), and American Journal of Physiology-Heart and Circulatory Physiology (3.9, Q1). The most prolific author was Wang Yong, with 12 publications and an H-index of 10. Keyword clustering identified three research themes: pathogenesis of CSF, prediction for CSF following percutaneous coronary intervention, and its prognostic implications. Emerging keywords highlighted increasing attention to "endothelial function", "prevalence", "CSF phenomenon", "myocardial infarction" and "reserve".
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a bibliometric overview of key trends and future directions in the field of CSF predictors, emphasizing the growing focus on this area. Future research is anticipated to concentrate on risk stratification and mechanism-targeted intervention strategies.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
title: Uncovering research themes in coronary slow flow predictors: a bibliometric and cluster analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This review aims to provide a concise summary of hemodynamic considerations and the pharmacology and current evidence of vasoactive support, including inotropes and vasopressors, during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support.
MAIN TEXT: Patients requiring ECMO for cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest have a high mortality rate. Despite advancements in medical and mechanical therapies, optimal use of vasoactive in patients receiving venoarterial ECMO is not well defined. Venoarterial ECMO introduces unique hemodynamic disturbances and considerations for the provision of vasoactive medications. Many different pharmacotherapies with varying inotropic, vasoconstrictive, and vasodilating effects are available and include catecholamine and non-catecholamine agents. Mechanisms and level of evidence vary based on agent, yet distinct characteristics may make certain agents more attractive than others depending on the clinical situation faced during ECMO.
CONCLUSIONS: A nuanced understanding of receptor pharmacology and ECMO specific considerations is essential to tailor the vasoactive strategy in this unique population.
journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
title: Pharmacology of vasopressors and inotropes during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare serum levels of Transforming Growth Factor-Beta (TGF-β) and Platelet-Derived Growth Factor-BB (PDGF-BB) among patients with normal coronary arteries (NCA) and those with coronary artery disease (CAD) subclasses [stable CAD and acute coronary syndrome (ACS)], and to evaluate their potential diagnostic value and discriminatory power, particularly in identifying stable CAD.
METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study included 176 patients who underwent coronary angiography. Participants were classified into normal coronary artery (NCA; symptomatic control), stable CAD, and ACS groups. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical data were recorded. Blood samples were collected for the analysis of TGF-β1 and PDGF-BB levels using ELISA kits.
RESULTS: Hypertension and diabetes mellitus were significantly more prevalent in the stable CAD group compared to others (p < 0.001). Both TGF-β and PDGF-BB levels were significantly elevated in patients with stable CAD compared to individuals with normal coronary arteries and those with ACS (p < 0.001). Multivariate regression analysis identified hypertension, diabetes, TGF-β, and PDGF-BB as independent predictors of stable CAD (p < 0.01 for all). ROC curve analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance for TGF-β and PDGF-BB individually (AUC = 0.847, 0.798, respectively), with combined assessment further improving accuracy (AUC = 0.924).
CONCLUSION: Serum TGF-β and PDGF-BB levels are significantly increased in stable CAD patients relative to those with ACS and normal coronary anatomy. The combined evaluation of these biomarkers provides high diagnostic accuracy in distinguishing stable CAD, underscoring their potential role in the non-invasive assessment of chronic atherosclerotic disease. These findings support the use of TGF-β and PDGF-BB as complementary biomarkers for early identification and risk stratification in stable CAD.
title: Comparative evaluation of serum TGF-β1 and PDGF-BB levels across patients with normal coronary arteries, stable coronary artery disease, and acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the standard for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but bleeding, non-persistence and thromboembolism despite treatment create important unmet needs. Catheter ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) address distinct mechanisms and do not reproduce systemic anticoagulation.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review covers randomized anticoagulation-withdrawal studies after ablation, trials and pooled evidence on LAAO, patients unable to sustain anticoagulation, procedural imaging and healing, post-implant antithrombotic therapy, and future trial design. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were supplemented by citation screening and review of contemporary congress reports, for evidence spanning 2005-10 October 2026.
EXPERT OPINION: The completed randomized LAAO programme mainly tests substitution where OAC remains feasible. Precision source control should be investigated as rescue when OAC cannot be sustained and as a potential dose-sparing complement in selected patients, while addressing residual ischemic risk and verifying durable closure.
title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: recent evidence, catheter ablation, and future trials.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has revolutionized the management of aortic stenosis (AS), particularly for high-risk and inoperable populations. Nevertheless, patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who require TAVR present a unique clinical challenge. These patients tend to have a high burden of comorbidities, as well as chronic uremia, that purportedly predispose them to a higher risk of more frequent and rapid structural valve deterioration (SVD). This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the mechanisms, incidence, and clinical outcomes of TAVR SVD in the ESRD population. In doing so, we summarize the pathophysiology for SVD in this patient population, contextualize the reported rates of TAVR SVD, and summarize the limited literature describing the clinical outcomes for these patients. We posit that clinical management for ESRD patients must focus on proactive, multidisciplinary surveillance and the integration of predictive modeling to optimize the timing of rescue interventions. Finally, we underscore the importance of better understanding the underlying mechanisms that accelerate TAVR SVD in uremic conditions.
title: Structural Valve Deterioration in End-Stage Renal Disease Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world data after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are limited.
AIMS: We compared 1-year clinical outcomes after PCI with paclitaxel DCBs between the ACS and non-ACS patients.
METHODS: The ALLIANCE is a prospective, multicenter registry of PCI using paclitaxel DCBs. Primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality at 1 year. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences between the ACS and non-ACS patients.
RESULTS: From July 2023 to February 2024, 1794 patients with de novo lesions (ACS 513 [28.6%] and non-ACS 1281 [71.4%]) were enrolled at 57 medical institutions in Japan. Mean age was 71 years, and 76% were male. Among ACS patients, 34.7% had ST-segment elevation MI, 33.9% non-ST-segment elevation MI, and 31.4% unstable angina. Intracoronary imaging was used in 88.5% of lesions. Bailout stenting after DCB angioplasty was required in only 1.1% of 1984 lesions. Technical success, defined as post-procedural residual stenosis < 40% and absence of flow-limiting coronary dissection, was significantly lower in patients with ACS than those with non-ACS. At 1 year, TLF occurred in 7.0% of ACS and 3.8% of non-ACS patients (adjusted HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.06-3.17, p = 0.03). All-cause mortality was 6.4% and 3.3%, respectively (adjusted HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.13-3.75, p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: One-year TLF and all-cause mortality were significantly higher in ACS than non-ACS patients treated with paclitaxel DCBs in real-world clinical settings.
REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp); unique identifier: jRCT1032230218.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: One-Year Clinical Outcomes of Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Patients With and Without Acute Coronary Syndrome: The ALLIANCE Registry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive systolic blood pressure (SBP) lowering to <130 mm Hg is recommended in contemporary secondary stroke prevention guidelines; however, it did not significantly reduce overall recurrent ischemic stroke in the Secondary Prevention of Small Subcortical Strokes (SPS3) trial. In this post hoc secondary analysis of participant-level SPS3 trial data, we sought to identify baseline predictors of recurrent ischemic stroke among patients with lacunar stroke assigned to the lower SBP target in SPS3.
METHODS: This post hoc secondary analysis included SPS3 participants randomized to the lower SBP target (<130 mm Hg). The primary outcome was centrally adjudicated recurrent ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Candidate predictors were evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 1501 participants (41.1% aged ≥ 65 years; 60.8% were men), 120 (8.0%) experienced recurrent ischemic stroke over a median follow-up of 3.49 years (interquartile range, 1.80-5.08), corresponding to an incidence rate of 2.43 events per 100 person-years. In unadjusted comparisons, recurrent ischemic stroke was associated with diabetes mellitus (44.2% vs 34.2%; p = .036), coronary artery bypass grafting/coronary stent (9.2% vs 4.1%; p = .018), Black race (24.2% vs 14.4%; p = .007), elevated serum creatinine (14.2% vs 7.7%; p = .022), aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (44.2% vs 28.5%; p < .001), large-vessel atherosclerosis (29.3% vs 17.9%; p = .004), and lower prevalence of a subcortical qualifying stroke (21.7% vs 46.1%; p < .001). In multivariable analysis, aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.14-2.50; p = .009) and large-vessel atherosclerosis (HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.08-2.413; p = .020) were independently associated with recurrence. Randomization to aspirin plus clopidogrel was not associated with recurrent ischemic stroke (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.75-1.57; p = .661).
CONCLUSIONS: In SPS3 participants assigned to intensive SBP control, 8.0% experienced recurrent ischemic stroke. Aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke and large-vessel atherosclerosis remained independent predictors of recurrence. These findings may help identify patients who require preventive strategies beyond intensive SBP lowering.
title: Predictors of recurrent stroke among patients with lacunar stroke receiving intensive blood pressure control: a secondary analysis of the secondary prevention of small subcortical strokes trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality risk stratification in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains challenging with heterogeneous temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) use. We developed and temporally validated the admission-based AMICS-ADMIT model and bedside score and benchmarked them against established scores.
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study, reported according to TRIPOD+AI, included 479 consecutive patients with AMI-CS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between January 2017 and July 2025. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. AMICS-ADMIT was developed using multivariable logistic regression in the 2017-2022 cohort, internally evaluated by bootstrap resampling, and temporally validated in the 2023-2025 cohort. Missing data were multiply imputed. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and Brier scores. Benchmarking against CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, and GRACE was restricted to temporal validation; tMCS-stratified performance was exploratory.
RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 42.6% (204/479). The final model included age, left ventricular ejection fraction, prior cardiopulmonary resuscitation, estimated glomerular filtration rate, vasoactive-inotropic score, and ST-segment elevation status. The continuous model achieved AUCs of 0.809 (95% CI 0.764-0.855) in development and 0.834 (95% CI 0.769-0.899) in temporal validation, with Brier scores of 0.176 and 0.167 and favourable calibration. The bedside score achieved AUCs of 0.777 (95% CI 0.728-0.826) and 0.775 (95% CI 0.699-0.851), respectively, with stepwise mortality separation across predefined risk categories. Discrimination did not differ significantly from CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, or GRACE.
CONCLUSIONS: AMICS-ADMIT showed stable temporal performance and clinically interpretable early risk stratification in contemporary PCI-treated AMI-CS. External multicentre validation is required before clinical implementation.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
title: Mortality risk stratification in contemporary myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock: development of AMICS-ADMIT prediction model and benchmarking of established scores.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is increasingly recognized as an arrhythmogenic condition, with a subset of patients exhibiting ventricular arrhythmias beyond the hemodynamic effects of mitral regurgitation (MR). Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been proposed as a structural marker associated with arrhythmic risk, but its relationship with postoperative ventricular arrhythmias after mitral valve repair remains incompletely understood. We aimed to evaluate changes in ventricular arrhythmic burden following mitral valve repair and to investigate the association between preoperative MAD and postoperative ventricular ectopy.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 77 patients with MVP who underwent surgical mitral valve repair for severe MR and had both preoperative and postoperative 24-h Holter recordings. Premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden and ventricular arrhythmias were assessed before and after surgery. MAD was evaluated retrospectively using transthoracic echocardiography. Multivariable linear regression, sensitivity analyses, and sequential model comparison were performed to evaluate the independent and incremental association of MAD with postoperative PVC burden.
RESULTS: Overall PVC burden decreased significantly after mitral valve repair. Patients with preoperative MAD had a substantially higher PVC burden both before surgery [7,800 (7,000-9,575) vs. 4,200 (3,200-6,200) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] and after surgery [5,700 (5,175-6,425) vs. 2,200 (1,800-3,500) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] than those without MAD. The relative reduction in PVC burden was comparable between groups (-35.4 ± 20.6% vs. -39.5 ± 29.5%, p = 0.113). In multivariable analysis, preoperative MAD remained independently associated with higher postoperative PVC burden after adjustment for clinical covariates, prolapse phenotype, residual mitral regurgitation, and baseline PVC burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Mitral valve repair was associated with a significant reduction in ventricular ectopic burden in patients with MVP. However, preoperative MAD identified patients with a higher postoperative ventricular ectopic burden despite a similar proportional reduction in PVCs. These findings support the potential value of postoperative rhythm surveillance in patients with preoperative MAD.
title: Ventricular arrhythmic burden before and after mitral valve repair in mitral valve prolapse: the role of mitral annular disjunction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or optical coherence tomography (OCT), improves clinical outcomes. Contemporary data on US adoption trends, demographic, and hospital disparities remain limited.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 5,220,590 PCI admissions from the National Inpatient Sample (2012-2022). IVI use was defined by concurrent procedural codes for IVUS or OCT. Outcomes included temporal trends, in-hospital mortality, resource utilization, and disparities. Given the large sample size, standardized mean differences (SMDs) were reported to quantify between-group differences, with an absolute SMD of >0.10 indicating a meaningful imbalance. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics. To further address potential confounding by indication, propensity score matching was performed. Patients were matched 1:1 using nearest-neighbor matching without replacement, with a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the propensity score and exact matching on calendar year. Covariate balance before and after matching was assessed using absolute SMDs, with an absolute SMD <0.10 indicating an adequate balance. IVI-guided PCI increased from 7.1% (2012) to 21.3% (2022) (p trend < 0.001). Minimal demographic disparities existed, but significant hospital-level variations were observed; hospitals in the Northeast had the highest adoption (27.6% in 2022 vs. 16.3% in Western hospitals). In-hospital mortality occurred in 2.32% of IVI hospitalizations compared with 2.88% of hospitalizations without IVI guidance. After adjusting for demographic characteristics, acute clinical presentation and severity-including STEMI, NSTEMI, cardiogenic shock, and cardiac arrest-comorbidities, payer, hospital characteristics, and calendar year, IVI remained significantly associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.783, 95% CI 0.742-0.827; P < 0.001), higher routine discharge rates (84.1% vs. 83.7%; p < 0.001), longer median length-of-stay (3 days [interquartile range (IQR) 2-5] vs. 2 days [IQR 2-4]; p < 0.001), and increased costs [$25,144 (IQR $18,749-$36,439) vs. $20,165 (IQR $15,293-$28,381); p < 0.001].
CONCLUSION: While IVI-guided PCI adoption increased significantly, pronounced hospital-level disparities exist. Targeted efforts to enhance adoption-particularly in rural, non-teaching hospitals and low-utilization regions-are needed.

title: Adoption of intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention in the United States (2012-2022): temporal trends, disparities, and mortality association.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load associated with implementation of a standardized extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) activation protocol.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter observational study included 103 consecutive patients with in-hospital cardiac arrest who underwent ECPR at three tertiary hospitals in Guangdong Province, China. The control group included 30 patients treated from September 2019 to December 2023, and the post-implementation group included 73 patients treated from January 2024 to December 2025. Outcomes included resuscitation-process measures, clinical outcomes, and perceived nursing workload assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), a multidimensional measure of perceived workload.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the post-implementation group had shorter ECPR preparation time (2.87 ± 2.32 vs. 8.60 ± 1.34 min), ECMO priming time (14.83 ± 2.88 vs. 19.07 ± 1.18 min), and ECMO initiation time (35.01 ± 2.36 vs. 54.12 ± 3.55 min), and a higher one-time readiness rate of disposable supplies (100% vs. 50.0%; all P < 0.001). The total NASA-TLX score was lower after implementation (415 ± 26 vs. 452 ± 25, P < 0.001). Thirty-day survival was numerically higher in the post-implementation group but did not differ statistically (42.5% vs. 23.3%; crude OR 2.43, 95% CI 0.92-6.37; P = 0.069). Favorable neurological outcome at discharge was more frequent after implementation (30.1% vs. 10.0%; crude OR 3.88, 95% CI 1.07-14.15; P = 0.036), and the association persisted after adjustment for SAVE score and time-to-ECPR-decision (adjusted OR 3.79, 95% CI 1.02-14.08; P = 0.047).
CONCLUSION: Implementation of the standardized ECPR activation protocol was associated with shorter ECPR preparation, priming, and initiation times, lower perceived nursing workload, and higher odds of favorable neurological outcome at discharge. Thirty-day survival was numerically higher but did not differ statistically. Given the retrospective pre-post design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.
title: A standardized ECPR activation protocol and resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load: a retrospective multicenter study.

abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality in individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), despite advances in glycemic management and cardiovascular prevention. Conventional cardiovascular risk assessment may underestimate risk in T1DM, particularly among younger asymptomatic individuals, highlighting the need for markers of early vascular injury. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of T1DM, is increasingly recognized as a marker of systemic vascular dysfunction rather than an isolated ocular disorder. Non-invasive retinal visualization may provide insight into vascular and atherosclerotic disease. This mini-review summarizes evidence linking DR with subclinical coronary artery disease (CAD) and cardiovascular outcomes in T1DM, focusing on coronary artery calcium (CAC) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Observational and longitudinal studies consistently link DR severity with CAC burden, coronary plaque burden, silent CAD, and cardiovascular outcomes, independent of traditional risk factors. Albuminuria and diabetic kidney disease may provide complementary evidence of a broader microvascular phenotype associated with cardiovascular risk. Advances in retinal imaging, including optical coherence tomography angiography and artificial intelligence-based oculomics, support the role of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular risk prediction. CAC scoring remains valuable for detecting subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, while CCTA characterizes calcified and non-calcified plaque. Emerging evidence suggests that integrating retinal and microvascular markers with coronary imaging may improve identification of asymptomatic individuals at increased cardiovascular risk and support intervention. Although data are observational and prospective validation is required, multimodal strategies combining clinical risk factors, retinal biomarkers, albuminuria, CAC, and CCTA may enhance cardiovascular risk stratification in T1DM.
title: Retinal and coronary imaging in type 1 diabetes: links between retinopathy and subclinical cardiovascular disease.

abstract: Depressive symptoms are common after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and are associated with poorer recovery, lower adherence to secondary prevention, reduced participation in cardiac rehabilitation, and a higher risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence also suggests that depression after PCI is not experienced, detected, or managed in the same way across sex and gender groups. Women are more often reported to have higher early symptom scores, greater anxiety comorbidity, more somatic symptom overlap, and lower access to some forms of guideline-based cardiovascular care. Men may be less likely to disclose affective symptoms and may present psychological distress through externalizing behaviors, treatment disengagement, smoking, alcohol use, anger, or delayed help-seeking. These patterns should not be interpreted as fixed male-female traits. Rather, they probably reflect interactions among biological sex-related factors, social gender norms, comorbidity, age, socioeconomic position, and healthcare access. Unlike previous reviews that pool depression across coronary syndromes, this review is organized around patients after PCI, explicitly distinguishes conclusions directly supported by post-PCI data from those extrapolated from broader coronary populations, and identifies the remaining extrapolations as research priorities. This narrative review summarizes clinical patterns of depression after PCI, discusses plausible biological and psychosocial mechanisms, and proposes a sex- and gender-informed care pathway for screening, referral, cardiac rehabilitation, and follow-up. The available literature supports a more cautious and individualized approach than a simple binary model: screening tools should be interpreted alongside clinical interview and behavioral indicators; rehabilitation should address practical barriers, stigma, caregiving burden, and functional goals; and future studies should report sex-disaggregated data while also measuring gender-related exposures.
title: Sex and gender in depression after percutaneous coronary intervention: clinical patterns, mechanistic hypotheses, and care pathways.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute nicotine intoxication can cause cardiac arrest. We report a case of cardiac arrest managed with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) alongside serial serum nicotine monitoring.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 36-year-old woman collapsed after ingesting an unknown amount of liquid nicotine, up to 20 g. Emergency medical services found her in cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity (PEA). On arrival, she remained in cardiac arrest with PEA/asystole and severe acidosis, and VA-ECMO was established 82 min after ingestion. Cardiac function gradually improved, and VA-ECMO was discontinued on Day 3. However, she died on Day 28 from post-cardiac arrest brain injury. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC/MS) revealed an admission serum nicotine concentration of 6.44 μg/mL, declining to 0.057 μg/mL within 18 h. This decline paralleled hemodynamic recovery.
CONCLUSION: Although neurological outcome was unfavorable, VA-ECMO may provide temporary circulatory support during the toxic phase of massive nicotine intoxication.

title: Serial Serum Nicotine Concentration During VA-ECMO for Nicotine-Induced Cardiac Arrest: A Case Report.

abstract: Hepatic abnormalities in non-Fontan heart failure result from congestive hepatopathy and hypoperfusion-related ischemic injury, compounded by neurohormonal activation and systemic inflammation. Assessment of liver disease severity is challenging because standard liver biochemistries, serum fibrosis markers, severity score models, elastography, and imaging modalities have limited diagnostic accuracy in congestive hepatopathy, and hepatic fibrosis is often heterogeneous on histology in this population. Management focuses on optimization of cardiac function through medical therapy or mechanical circulatory support. Although liver biochemical abnormalities frequently improve with restoration of cardiac function, histologic reversibility is variable and not consistently observed. In patients with advanced heart failure needing heart transplantation, histologic cirrhosis and/or fibrosis accompanied by portal hypertension may merit consideration of combined heart-liver transplantation, but correlation between fibrosis and clinical outcomes varies. There remains an unmet need for tests that can reliably assess liver disease severity and predict liver outcomes in non-Fontan congestive hepatopathy.
title: Assessment and Reversibility of Hepatic Abnormalities in Heart Failure: Liver in Heart Failure.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcified coronary lesions remain among the most challenging subsets in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) because of their morphological complexity. Restoring physiological vasomotion and vascular remodeling is an emerging goal in PCI.
CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with severely calcified coronary lesions treated with PCI. Lesion preparation included rotational atherectomy was performed in 2 of 3 cases, followed by implantation of a bioadaptor-a sirolimus-eluting cobalt-chromium hybrid stent system. In 1 case, a super high-pressure OPN balloon was used for postdilatation. Six-month follow-up angiography showed favorable outcomes with sustained vessel patency in all cases.
DISCUSSION: This is the first case series reporting bioadaptor use in heavily calcified coronary lesions. Adequate lesion preparation is essential for procedural success and clinical outcomes.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In this case series, bioadaptor implantation in severely calcified coronary lesions was feasible, with favorable short-term outcomes at 6 months. In calcified lesions, more aggressive lesion preparation than for conventional drug-eluting stents may be required, as adequate calcium modification is a prerequisite for full device expansion and for realizing the bioadaptor's long-term functional benefits after uncaging.
title: Bioadaptor Implantation in Complex Calcified Coronary Lesions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid access is an alternative for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with prohibitive transfemoral anatomy, but it may cause cerebral hypoperfusion with impaired intracranial collateral circulation.
CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis, extensive comorbidities, and unsuitable transfemoral access underwent TAVR. Neuroimaging demonstrated moyamoya-pattern intracranial vasculopathy with limited collateral reserve. During left carotid exposure, test occlusion caused a >50% decline in cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy despite blood pressure augmentation. A femoral-to-carotid arterial shunt was established to maintain cerebral perfusion. A 26-mm self-expanding Evolut FX+ valve was successfully implanted via left carotid access, with excellent hemodynamics and no neurologic complications.
DISCUSSION: This approach demonstrates a novel cerebral protection strategy for selected patients with compromised cerebrovascular reserve.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Carotid-access TAVR in moyamoya-pattern vasculopathy carries hypoperfusion risk. Real-time near-infrared spectroscopy may detect intolerance to carotid clamping, while femoral-to-carotid shunting may offer cerebral protection.
title: Femoral-to-Carotid Shunting During Carotid-Access TAVR in Moyamoya-Pattern Vasculopathy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute severe mitral regurgitation (MR) can cause rapidly progressive asymmetric pulmonary edema that mimics pneumonia.
CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old man presented with fever, dyspnea, and a new pansystolic murmur. Within hours, he developed hypoxemic respiratory failure. Serial chest imaging captured rapid progression from subtle right hilar vascular prominence to extensive right-predominant airspace opacification. Echocardiography showed posterior leaflet chordal rupture with a flail P2 segment and a severe eccentric MR jet directed toward the right pulmonary venous inflow, with systolic flow reversal in a sampled right pulmonary vein. Mitral valve repair produced marked clinical and radiographic improvement.
DISCUSSION: Concordance among the MR jet trajectory, pulmonary venous abnormalities, and edema distribution supported preferential right pulmonary venous loading. Recognition of this pattern helped distinguish asymmetric cardiogenic pulmonary edema from pneumonia.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Rapidly evolving focal pulmonary opacification with a new systolic murmur should prompt urgent echocardiography.
title: Acute Mitral Regurgitation With Unilateral Pulmonary Edema: Preferential Pulmonary Venous Loading From an Eccentric Jet.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe hemodynamic guidance during valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation using simultaneous aortic and left ventricular pressure monitoring.
KEY STEPS: A 90-year-old woman with a failed 19-mm surgical bioprosthesis and severe transvalvular regurgitation underwent valve-in-valve implantation with a self-expanding valve guided by a SavvyWire. During the first deployment, the aortic waveform remained completely flat after pacing was discontinued, whereas left ventricular pulsatility persisted; the valve was recaptured. During the second deployment, aortic pulsatility recovered after pacing cessation; final release was performed. Postdilatation reduced the invasive mean transvalvular gradient from 23 to 11 mm Hg.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: A flat aortic waveform with preserved left ventricular pulsatility is a warning sign warranting system confirmation and multimodality reassessment, not a specific diagnosis of leaflet dysfunction.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Simultaneous pressure monitoring can complement fluoroscopy when valve function is uncertain during deployment and may support timely recapture when abnormal hemodynamics persist.
title: Real-Time Hemodynamic Guidance During Valve-in-Valve TAVI.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a reproducible 2-port, 3-dimensional totally endoscopic technique for left atrial myxoma resection under ventricular fibrillation without aortic cross-clamping.
KEY STEPS: Peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass is established through femoral cannulation. After 2 right thoracic ports are positioned, ventricular fibrillation is induced, the left atrium is opened, and a left atrial vent is inserted. The tumor is removed en bloc with an adequate septal margin. Continuous carbon dioxide insufflation, titrated venting, a gently blood-filled left atrium, and transesophageal echocardiography-guided de-airing provide embolic protection.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Aortic regurgitation, interatrial shunting, inappropriate venting, tumor fragmentation, and prolonged fibrillatory arrest can compromise safety.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In carefully selected patients, a short fibrillatory interval can simplify 2-port myxoma resection by avoiding aortic clamping, root cannulation, and cardioplegia. Meticulous left-heart decompression and de-airing are essential.
title: Two-Port Endoscopic Left Atrial Myxoma Resection Under Ventricular Fibrillation Without Aortic Cross-Clamping.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information.
CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.
title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent aortic valve injury following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a rare but catastrophic complication that can cause acute severe aortic regurgitation (AR) and heart failure.
CASE SUMMARY: A 49-year-old man developed recurrent acute pulmonary edema after a failed staged PCI for chronic total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe eccentric AR caused by a 7-mm injury to the noncoronary cusp and left cusp confirming iatrogenic cusp laceration. He underwent successful surgical repair with pericardial patch reconstruction and coronary artery bypass grafting, with excellent recovery.
DISCUSSION: Literature on catheter-induced aortic valve injury is sparse. This case highlights a rare cause of post-PCI shock where prompt echocardiography guided lifesaving surgical intervention.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Not all post-PCI cardiac decompensation is ischemic. Severe AR from iatrogenic aortic cusp injury, though rare, should be promptly excluded.
title: Intractable Pulmonary Edema After PCI: An Extremely Rare Iatrogenic Mechanical Cause.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary embolism (CE) is an uncommon but clinically relevant nonatherosclerotic cause of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Adult patients with congenital heart disease may be particularly vulnerable when residual intracardiac shunts, atrial enlargement, and atrial arrhythmias coexist.
CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man with partially repaired tetralogy of Fallot, residual ventricular septal defect with bidirectional shunting, and new-onset atrial fibrillation presented with inferior STEMI. Coronary angiography revealed distal right coronary artery occlusion with a large thrombus burden, in the absence of significant atherosclerotic disease. Sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy was successfully performed, with clinical and electrocardiographic improvement.
DISCUSSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy for STEMI due to CE in an adult patient with congenital heart disease with residual intracardiac shunt.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In adult patients with congenital heart disease with STEMI, CE should be suspected when intracardiac shunts and embolic risk factors coexist.
title: An Unexpected Cause of STEMI in Partially Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
Beyond Vascular Feasibility: Cerebral Reserve in Transcarotid Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
Overcoming Treatment Inertia for Mitral Transcatheter Edge-To-Edge Repair: Wait No Longer.

abstract: Valvular heart disease is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As the prevalence of most valvular heart diseases increases with age, population ageing has led to a substantial increase in disease burden. Due to advanced age or significant comorbidities, many patients are considered unsuitable for conventional surgery. Whereas medical therapy was therefore often the only treatment option in the past, the rapid evolution of transcatheter interventions has fundamentally transformed the management of valvular heart disease over the past two decades. Today, effective catheter-based treatment options are available for virtually all valvular pathologies. For patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, the prognostic benefit of transcatheter aortic valve replacement is firmly established. Large randomized trials have demonstrated non-inferiority of transcatheter aortic valve replacement compared with surgical aortic valve replacement across most patient populations, leading to an expanding use of this approach in younger and lower-risk patients. Similarly, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral and tricuspid regurgitation has been shown to improve symptoms, quality of life, and heart failure-related hospitalizations. In carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, this strategy also confers a survival benefit. In addition, dedicated transcatheter devices have recently emerged as promising treatment options for native aortic regurgitation. Given the rapid evolution of transcatheter therapies, current efforts are increasingly focused on selecting the optimal treatment strategy for the individual patient and determining the optimal timing of intervention.
title: [Evidence-based treatment of valvular heart disease].

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. Disulfide-bond oxidized HMGB1 (ds-HMGB1) functions as a core damage-associated molecular pattern that mediates acute myocardial injury. Nevertheless, commercially available HMGB1 reagents exhibit mixed proteoforms, unstable biological activity and low receptor affinity, which greatly hinder mechanistic investigations in this field. This study generated a novel mutant full-length murine ds-HMGB1, systematically dissected its molecular mechanisms underlying aggravated ischemic myocardial injury, and sought to provide a standardized protein reagent and theoretical framework for HMGB1-targeted therapies against myocardial damage. A K184S/K185S mutant HMGB1 plasmid was constructed, and protein purified by three-step chromatography. Structural modeling, mass spectrometry, SPR and PLA were used to analyze conformation, modification and receptor binding kinetics. Hypoxic cardiomyocyte co-culture and mouse myocardial infarction models were established. Flow cytometry, echocardiography, histological staining, qPCR, Western blot and RNA-seq were applied to detect molecular phenotypes and signaling pathways. The K184S/K185S mutation preserved the native overall conformation and functional disulfide bond of HMGB1, while markedly enhancing HMGB1 binding to RAGE and promoting TLR4-MD2 complex assembly. In vitro experiments revealed that mutant ds-HMGB1 either acted directly on cardiomyocytes or synergized hypoxia through endothelial-cardiomyocyte paracrine signaling to induce robust intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. In vivo administration expanded myocardial infarct size, impaired cardiac systolic performance and exacerbated inflammatory infiltration in cardiac tissue. Transcriptomic profiling identified 53 core injury genes specifically upregulated by ds-HMGB1 under ischemic stress. The mutant ds-HMGB1 developed in this study addresses the intrinsic drawbacks of commercial HMGB1 preparations. We further identified 53 key myocardial injury genes modulated by ds-HMGB1. This work delivers a standardized experimental reagent and multi-layered mechanistic evidence supporting HMGB1 as a therapeutic target for acute myocardial infarction.
journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
mesh: Receptor for Advanced Glycation End Products
title: Disulfide-oxidized HMGB1 mutant construction and its mechanism in AMI-induced myocardial injury.

title: COVID-19-associated left main coronary vasculitis: from inflammatory assessment to coronary artery bypass grafting.

abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and acute myocarditis (AM) often present with overlapping clinical features and biomarker profiles, making early differential diagnosis challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference modality for etiological assessment through functional evaluation and multiparametric tissue characterization. The aim of this study was to compare clinical and CMR characteristics of patients with MINOCA and suspected AM, and to identify imaging features enabling accurate differentiation. We retrospectively analyzed 127 consecutive patients undergoing CMR (February 2021-October 2024): 62 with suspected MINOCA and 65 with suspected AM. Clinical data, laboratory findings, ECG, and CMR parameters (cine imaging, T1/T2 mapping, extracellular volume [ECV], and late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) were assessed. MINOCA patients were older (median 59 years) and predominantly female (64.5%), whereas AM patients were younger (median 29 years) and mainly male (81.5%). AM was associated with higher troponin and inflammatory markers. Among patients initially referred with suspected MINOCA, LGE was present in 50.0%, compared with 93.8% of those referred with suspected acute myocarditis (p < 0.001). MINOCA showed predominantly ischemic LGE patterns, while AM exhibited non-ischemic subepicardial or mid-wall LGE with myocardial edema. CMR confirmed myocardial infarction in 48.4% of patients and identified alternative diagnoses in 41.9%, while 9.7% had normal CMR findings. Multiparametric CMR reliably distinguishes ischemic from inflammatory myocardial injury in patients with chest pain, elevated troponin, and non-obstructive coronaries. Early CMR integration improves diagnostic accuracy and supports tailored management.
journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA and Acute Myocarditis: A Comparative Multiparametric Evaluation.

abstract: To explore the predictive value of hibernating myocardium detected by single photon emission computed tomography (SEPCT)/positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging for the adverse cardiovascular events in unrevascularized chronic coronary total occlusion (CTO) patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Additionally, we explore whether hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory can independently predictive outcomes. Patients with at least one unrevascularized CTO on coronary angiography and LV dysfunction and who underwent rest 99mTc-MIBI SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging as well as 18F-FDG PET myocardial metabolic imaging were enrolled. All patients were followed up through telephone interviews and review of medical records. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, the extents of hibernating myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories, the extent of total scarred myocardium, and the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were calculated according to the segmental perfusion/metabolism score and the segmental assignment of coronary dominance and the results of coronary angiography. The Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between the extent of hibernating or scarred myocardium and adverse cardiovascular events. Seventy eight patients were included in the final analysis. The median follow-up duration was 70.2 (27.7, 80.3) months. The extent of total hibernating myocardium and the extent of hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory were both independent predictors for cardiac death [hazards ratio (HR) = 1.289, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.083-1.533, P = 0.004; HR = 1.262, 95% CI 1.022-1.557, P = 0.030] and the composite endpoint events (HR = 1.190, 95% CI 1.032-1.372, P = 0.016; HR = 1.273, 95% CI 1.025-1.581, P = 0.029). The extent of hibernating myocardium in the non-CTO territory, the extent of total scarred myocardium, the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were all not associated with the outcome. 99mTc-MIBI /18F-FDG SPECT/PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging has an important predictive value for prognosis in unrevascularized CTO patients with LV dysfunction. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, especially hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory, was an independent predictor for adverse cardiovascular events.
journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
title: The predictive value of 99mTc-MIBI SPECT/18F-FDG PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging in patients with unrevascularized coronary chronic total occlusion and left ventricular dysfunction.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Primary mitral regurgitation (MR) resulting from chordal rupture leads to acute volume overload and elevated left atrial pressure. Transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (TMVr) devices can effectively reduce MR, but their impact on global cardiac mechanics and diastolic filling remains difficult to predict. This study develops a whole-heart FSI framework for TMVr by extending a previously developed whole-heart model to represent chordal rupture and edge-to-edge repair and to quantify their structural and hemodynamic consequences.
METHODS: A three-dimensional FSI model of the heart derived from cardiac CT imaging was used to simulate three conditions: healthy baseline, chordal rupture-induced MR, and post-TMVr. The immersed finite element-difference method enables fully coupled simulation of blood flow, valve dynamics, and myocardial contraction. Hemodynamic metrics, including regurgitant fraction (RF), left atrial pressure (LAP), stroke volume (SV), stroke work (SW), and pressure-volume relationships, were compared with clinical reference data.
RESULTS: Chordal rupture produced moderate-to-severe MR (RF = 38%) and doubled left atrial V-wave amplitude, consistent with clinical observations. After TMVr, the central regurgitant jet produced by chordal rupture was eliminated, RF decreased to 21%, and LAP returned to near-baseline levels. However, the double-orifice valve configuration generated dual high-velocity inflow jets and reduced diastolic filling.
CONCLUSION: The repair effectively reduces regurgitation and atrial pressure while also influencing diastolic filling and ventricular output. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both regurgitation reduction and inflow characteristics when assessing TMVr outcomes and demonstrate the potential of patient-specific computational modeling for procedural planning and optimization.
title: A Whole-Heart Fluid-Structure Interaction Model for Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair in Primary Mitral Regurgitation.

abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recently approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration, 18F-flurpiridaz for positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) enables high-quality assessment of myocardial blood flow (MBF). Its half-life of approximately 110 min supports regional distribution and allows unit-dose delivery. These features make this probe well suited for MBF quantitation and expand access to quantitative cardiac PET at smaller centers.
RECENT FINDINGS: During pharmacologic stress, absolute MBF and myocardial flow reserve provide incremental diagnostic information beyond relative perfusion imaging. These measures have been validated across multiple methods and software platforms. Further study of this tracer under peak exercise may provide clinically relevant assessment of myocardial demand-induced changes in flow. Potential investigational approaches include artificial intelligence (AI)-derived virtual MBF, exercise-adjusted standardized uptake value (SUV) ratio-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) surrogate, and direct kinetic modeling during in-scanner ergometry. While conceptually promising, limitations inherent to exercise-based approaches in stress MBF and/or MFR estimation highlight the need for pragmatic research strategies before potential clinical applicability.
title: Evaluation of Myocardial Blood Flow Using 18F-flurpiridaz PET: Established Applications with Pharmacologic Stress and Roadmap for Exercise Stress Implementation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) continue to impose a substantial clinical and economic burden in Saudi Arabia. Since publication of the 2022 Saudi Heart Association (SHA) CCS guidelines, important advances have emerged in diagnosis, pharmacotherapy, cardiometabolic risk reduction, antiplatelet management, and revascularization. This 2026 focused update selectively revises and clarifies key recommendations to reflect these advances within the Saudi context.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary SHA expert panel conducted a structured review of randomized trials, meta-analyses, and relevant international guidance published since 2022. Updates were restricted to areas with substantive new evidence or evolving clinical practice. Recommendations were formulated through expert consensus in accordance with SHA methodological standards. This document complements the 2022 guideline and does not replace it.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: This focused update advances a more personalized, risk-driven approach to CCS management. Diagnostic algorithms now explicitly integrate pre-test probability, reinforce coronary computed tomography angiography as the preferred initial modality in low-to-intermediate probability, and refine the positioning of functional stress imaging. Residual risk assessment and preventive strategies are also strengthened. Importantly, this update introduces a dedicated diagnostic and management framework for angina and ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA/INOCA), emphasizing endotype-specific evaluation and targeted therapy for this historically under-recognized population. Anti-anginal therapy positions beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers as equivalent first-line agents, upgrades long-acting nitrates, and integrates ranolazine, ivabradine, and trimetazidine as evidence-based add-on options. Antiplatelet guidance emphasizes individualized dual antiplatelet therapy duration after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), early de-escalation strategies, and selective use of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. Lipid management and cardiovascular risk reduction options are now expanded and revascularization recommendations are restructured. Collectively, these updates strengthen the delivery of contemporary, evidence-based, and patient-centered CCS care and provide a clear framework for implementation across diverse healthcare settings.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus-based guideline update by a multidisciplinary expert panel; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations rest on expert consensus and are regional, so they add little to international evidence.
appraisal.one_line: National focused update of chronic coronary syndrome guidance from a Saudi expert panel, with new sections on ANOCA/INOCA and antiplatelet de-escalation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows how the shift to individualised DAPT duration and P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy is being adopted in national guidance.

journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association
title: 2026 Focused Update of the Saudi Heart Association Guidelines on Best Practices in the Management of Chronic Coronary Syndromes.

abstract: Thrombus-in-transit (TIT) across a patent foramen ovale (PFO) is a rare but life-threatening phenomenon that can result in paradoxical systemic embolism. Simultaneous deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism (PE), and an intracardiac shunt create a critical scenario requiring rapid recognition. We report an 83-year-old woman with recurrent venous thromboembolism who presented with progressive dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and lower-extremity swelling. Laboratory evaluation revealed leukocytosis of 13.6 ×10⁹/L, thrombocytopenia of 67 ×10⁹/L, creatinine of 1.42 mg/dL, lactate of 2.57 mmol/L, and D-dimer of 32.53 µg/mL. Arterial blood gas analysis showed a pH of 7.47, pCO₂ of 23 mmHg, and pO₂ of 57.8 mmHg. CT pulmonary angiography demonstrated extensive bilateral pulmonary emboli with a left atrial filling defect, while echocardiography revealed a large mobile thrombus crossing a PFO with severe right ventricular dysfunction. The patient underwent emergent pulmonary embolectomy with PFO closure and left atrial appendage ligation but developed refractory cardiogenic shock and multiorgan failure despite venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support and died 48 hours later. This case emphasizes the critical role of multimodality imaging in rapidly identifying TIT across a PFO and guiding time-sensitive multidisciplinary management.
title: Thrombus-in-Transit Across a Patent Foramen Ovale: Echocardiographic Recognition and Multimodality Management of a Fatal Paradoxical Event.

abstract: Coronary artery fistulas (CAFs) are rare vascular anomalies, and fistulas originating from the left main coronary artery (LMCA) are particularly uncommon. A 63-year-old woman with hypertension and obesity presented with acute anterior myocardial infarction and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Coronary angiography incidentally identified a tortuous vascular tract arising from the proximal LMCA, but couldn't define its drainage site. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated a 3.9 cm fistulous tract with an origin and maximal diameter of 6 mm, coursing anteriorly and to the right of the pulmonary trunk before draining into it. No focal aneurysmal dilatation, mural thrombus, calcification, or secondary branches were identified. The pulmonary trunk measured 29 mm, the right-sided cardiac chambers were not dilated, and transthoracic echocardiography showed no noninvasive evidence of a large hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt or right-sided volume overload. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed for the culprit left anterior descending lesion, after which the symptoms resolved. The clinical course favored the LAD lesion as the dominant cause of ischemia, although a contributory fistula-related steal phenomenon was not formally assessed. Following discussion among several cardiovascular experts, conservative clinical and echocardiographic surveillance was selected. This case highlights the complementary roles of coronary angiography and CCTA in defining fistula anatomy and supporting individualized management and follow-up planning.
title: Left main coronary artery-Pulmonary trunk fistula incidentally detected during acute coronary infarction: Complementary roles of coronary angiography and CCTA.

abstract: Introduction Balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and self-expanding valves (SEVs) have different frame architectures, leaflet positions and distinct deployment mechanics that may influence prosthetic haemodynamics. We compared early echocardiographic gradients after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) between SAPIEN BEV and Evolut SEV platforms in a routine-practice cohort spanning several device generations. Materials and methods We retrospectively analysed 665 TAVI procedures: 250 BEV procedures using SAPIEN 3 variants and 415 SEV procedures using Evolut variants. The primary endpoint was the early post-TAVI echocardiographic mean transvalvular gradient obtained within three months of TAVI. Secondary endpoints were absolute and relative gradient reductions, achievement of a post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg, and a residual mean gradient ≥20 mmHg. Because the continuous variables were skewed, they were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Results were reported as medians with interquartile ranges, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for differences in medians. Categorical variables were compared using Pearson chi-square tests without continuity correction when expected counts were adequate and Fisher's exact tests when cell counts were small. Paired pre- and post-TAVI measurements were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Multivariable ordinary least-squares regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors was used to adjust the post-TAVI gradient for the baseline gradient and available prespecified covariates. Results Complete pre- and post-TAVI gradients were available for 664 procedures (249 BEV and 415 SEV). The median post-TAVI gradient was 8.4 (5.85-11.63) mmHg with SEV and 10.0 (7.93-13.90) mmHg with BEV (median difference, -1.60 mmHg; bootstrap 95% CI: -2.97 to -1.00; Mann-Whitney U test: p < 0.001). The median absolute gradient reduction was also greater with SEVs (36.0 vs 32.0 mmHg; median difference, 4.0 mmHg; p < 0.001), as was the relative gradient reduction (81.52% vs 76.19%; median difference, 5.33 percentage points; p < 0.001), although SEVs had a higher pre-procedural baseline transvalvular gradient. A post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg was recorded in 61.2% of SEV procedures compared with 43.4% of BEV procedures (risk ratio 1.41; p < 0.001). Residual gradients of ≥20 mmHg were uncommon and did not differ between the two groups (6.0% in SEV procedures vs 5.6% in BEV procedures; p = 0.831). After adjustment, in 575 completed cases, SEV use remained associated with a 1.48 mmHg lower post-TAVI mean gradient (95% CI: -2.42 to -0.55; p = 0.0019). Conclusions In this cohort, Evolut SEV procedures were associated with a modestly lower early post-TAVI mean gradient than SAPIEN BEV procedures. The magnitude of this association, and its interpretation alongside baseline gradient, anatomy, and other device-selection factors, can inform further comparative evaluation. No clinical outcomes or valve-durability measures were assessed.
title: Early Post-transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) Haemodynamics With SAPIEN Balloon-Expandable and Evolut Self-Expanding Valve Platforms: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study.

abstract: Coronary embolism is an underrecognized nonatherosclerotic cause of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), most commonly associated with atrial fibrillation. We report a 76-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation who presented with acute substernal chest pain and inferolateral STEMI. Coronary angiography demonstrated a 100% thrombotic occlusion of the distal right posterolateral ventricular branch with otherwise nonobstructive coronary artery disease. In the setting of an abrupt distal coronary occlusion, minimal underlying atherosclerotic disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and fulfillment of the Shibata diagnostic criteria, coronary embolism was considered the most likely mechanism. Long-term anticoagulation was continued, and the patient remained asymptomatic at 1-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of suspected coronary embolism in patients presenting with STEMI, atrial fibrillation, and minimal underlying coronary artery disease.
title: Inferolateral ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Secondary to Suspected Coronary Embolism in a Patient with Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: A Case Report.

abstract: Hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) is increasingly recognized after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement; however, its clinical significance and optimal detection strategy in routine practice remain uncertain. We report the case of a 79-year-old woman who underwent minimally invasive aortic valve replacement using a Perceval S sutureless bioprosthesis for severe aortic stenosis. Early postoperative transthoracic echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography demonstrated normal prosthetic valve function without evidence of HALT. Oral anticoagulation was discontinued three months after surgery, and the patient remained asymptomatic. At the one-year follow-up visit, a newly detected systolic heart murmur prompted further evaluation despite stable N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels. Echocardiography revealed increased transvalvular gradients and mild-to-moderate transvalvular regurgitation, while cardiac computed tomography demonstrated HALT involving the right and noncoronary cusps. The combination of hemodynamically significant prosthetic valve dysfunction and CT-confirmed HALT was considered consistent with clinically overt bioprosthetic valve thrombosis. Oral anticoagulation was restarted, followed by complete resolution of HALT and improvement in prosthetic valve hemodynamics. This case demonstrates that clinically overt bioprosthetic valve thrombosis associated with HALT may develop in an asymptomatic patient and that a newly detected cardiac murmur may serve as a clinical trigger for further echocardiographic and CT evaluation. Careful routine clinical follow-up may facilitate recognition of hemodynamically relevant prosthetic valve dysfunction and appropriate therapeutic intervention.
title: Late-Onset Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction Associated With Hypoattenuated Leaflet Thickening Detected After a New Heart Murmur: A Case Report.

abstract: The interaction between malignancy and cardiovascular disease is increasingly recognized in cardio-oncology. While cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction is well established, a potential bidirectional relationship between heart failure (HF) and cancer progression remains underexplored. We present the cases of two patients without known cardiovascular disease who developed new-onset HF in temporal association with rapidly progressive metastatic malignancies. A 65-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma developed severe left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30%, apical akinesis, and suspected LV thrombus after a previously normal cardiac evaluation. A 44-year-old man with metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma developed severe LV systolic dysfunction (LVEF 25-30%) with global hypokinesia, also following a normal baseline cardiac assessment. In both cases, baseline electrocardiography, troponin levels, and echocardiography were normal, whereas B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels became elevated during rapid tumor progression. Both patients experienced rapid clinical deterioration and died within weeks of diagnosis. These cases highlight a potential interaction between aggressive malignancy and cardiac dysfunction, possibly mediated by inflammatory, metabolic, and neurohormonal mechanisms. Conversely, HF may adversely affect oncologic outcomes by reducing physiological reserve and limiting therapeutic options. Although causality cannot be established from these observations, new-onset HF occurring alongside rapidly progressive malignancy may represent an underrecognized clinical phenomenon with important prognostic implications.
title: A Potential Bidirectional Interaction Between Heart Failure and Cancer Progression: Insights From Two Rapidly Fatal Cases.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal secondary stroke prevention remains uncertain for patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and atrial fibrillation (AF). Anticoagulation reduces ischemic stroke in AF but increases hemorrhage. Left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion is emerging as an alternative to anticoagulation, but few data exist on its safety in patients with ICH. Amid this uncertainty, little is known about US practice patterns in this scenario.
METHODS: We performed a study using linked electronic health record, pharmacy, and insurance claims data on >11 million patients at 29 US healthcare organizations, each with multiple hospital sites, in the TriNetX Linked platform. Validated International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes were used to identify adults with AF hospitalized for ICH during 2016 to 2024. To identify antiplatelet and anticoagulant prescriptions, we used RxNorm codes, a standardized drug naming system from the National Library of Medicine. LAA occlusion was defined using validated Current Procedural Terminology codes. Kaplan-Meier statistics were used to calculate cumulative rates of therapy utilization from discharge through 5 years. We created 3 mutually exclusive treatment groups with censoring at LAA occlusion for analyses of antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy and at anticoagulation for analyses of antiplatelet therapy.
RESULTS: We identified 2276 patients with AF hospitalized with ICH. Their mean age was 65.4 (±12.8) years, 40.6% were female, median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 5 (interquartile range, 5-6), 19.6% had Medicare, 26.9% received an anticoagulant prescription within 90 days before ICH, and half were discharged home or to an acute rehabilitation facility. Cumulative 5-year rates were 59.8% (95% CI, 55.5%-64.2%) for anticoagulation, 39.9% (95% CI, 34.1%-46.3%) for antiplatelet therapy, and 4.5% (95% CI, 2.6%-7.6%) for LAA occlusion. LAA occlusion rates did not differ by index ICH date (P=0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: In a contemporary, multicenter US cohort of patients with ICH and AF, 60% were prescribed anticoagulation after discharge, and the remainder were mostly treated with antiplatelet therapy only. These findings suggest widespread use of different secondary stroke prevention strategies in patients with AF and ICH.
title: Contemporary US Practice Patterns Regarding Anticoagulation and LAA Closure in ICH Survivors With Atrial Fibrillation.
