abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical relevance of chronic total occlusion (CTO) revascularization in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and multivessel disease (MVD) remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 632 patients with NSTEMI, MVD, and CTO were included. Patients were categorized into a complete revascularization group involving successful CTO recanalization (CR-CTO, n = 119) and an incomplete revascularization group without successful CTO recanalization (ICR-CTO, n = 513). The primary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 528 ± 201 days, the incidences of MACCE (11.8% vs. 28.5%) and MACE (7.6% vs. 24.2%) were significantly lower in the CR-CTO group than in the ICR-CTO group (both p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analyses, CR-CTO was independently associated with lower risks of MACCE (hazard ratio [HR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20-0.61) and MACE (HR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.13-0.51). Among patients without successful CTO recanalization, additional revascularization of non-CTO lesions was not associated with improved outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with NSTEMI, MVD, and CTO, complete revascularization involving successful CTO recanalization was associated with improved mid-term clinical outcomes. In contrast, additional revascularization of non-CTO lesions alone was not associated with a prognostic benefit when CTO lesions remained unrevascularized. These findings suggest that CTO revascularization status may warrant specific consideration when revascularization strategies are evaluated in this patient population.
title: Mid-Term Clinical Outcomes According to CTO Revascularization Status in Patients With NSTEMI and Multivessel Disease.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is frequently associated with severe venous congestion, increasingly recognized as a key factor in the development of cardiorenal syndrome. While transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) has shown to be effective in TR reduction, their impact on visceral venous congestion remains unknown. The aim of our study was to investigate visceral venous congestion in patients with severe TR undergoing TTVI.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 30 patients undergoing TTVI for severe TR. Renal venous blood flow was assessed by Doppler ultrasound examination at baseline and 1 to 3 months after the procedure. A 5-grade rating scale was developed to categorize venous flow from continuous (Grade I°) through discontinuous to a pendulous venous flow (Grade V°) within the kidneys.
RESULTS: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER, n = 24) was performed in 24 patients; 6 patients underwent heterotopic caval valve implantation. At baseline, severe renal congestion was present in most participants, with 20 patients showing venous flow profiles IV or V. Venous flow profiles strongly correlated with invasively measured right atrial mean pressure and V wave (p < 0.01). At follow-up, venous renal blood flow profiles improved significantly (p = 0.003), reducing patients with profiles IV or V from 20 to 9. Portal vein flow showed comparable decongestive changes. In TEER patients, reduction of TR ≥ 2 grades was associated with improved renal vein profile at follow-up (p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Successful TTVI leads to visceral decongestion. Renal venous flow currently represents a physiological marker of congestion that may complement conventional echocardiographic parameters; its role in guiding patient selection or timing of intervention remains to be determined in larger studies.
title: Transcatheter Intervention Is Associated With Visceral Decongestion in Patients With Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data are available on the association between early longitudinal changes in platelet count and mortality.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the early longitudinal changes in platelet count between survivors and non-survivors.
METHODS: This was a retrospective multi-center cohort study using data from the eICU Collaborative Research Database. A total of 6,769 patients diagnosed with AMI were included in the study. The analysis employed a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) and a Generalized Additive Mixed Model (GAMM) to compare longitudinal changes in platelet count between survivors and non-survivors.
RESULTS: The ICU 28-day and ICU 7-day all-cause mortality were 6.1% and 4.6%, respectively. During the first 5 days of ICU admission, GAM showed that non-survivors exhibited a significantly greater decline in platelet count than survivors. Specifically, the GAMM results showed that the difference in platelet count between ICU 28-day non-survivors and ICU 28-day survivors increased by an average of 15.4 × 109/L daily (95% Confidence Interval [CI], 14.1 to 16.7; p < 0.001). Similarly, the difference in platelet count between ICU 7-day non-survivors and ICU 7-day survivors increased by an average of 18.0 × 109/L daily (95% CI, 16.1-19.8; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: An early longitudinal decline in platelet count was associated with a poor prognosis in patients with AMI. However, this study is observational, and causality cannot be inferred.
title: An Early Longitudinal Decrease in Platelet Count Is Associated With Poor Prognosis in Acute Myocardial Infarction Patients: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary occlusion (ACO) occurs in approximately one-quarter of patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for ACO.
METHODS: Consecutive patients admitted with NSTEMI between January 2016 and June 2023 who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Demographic, electrocardiographic, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected. Patients admitted during 2016-2020 were assigned to the training cohort (n = 670), and those admitted during 2021-2023 were assigned to the validation cohort (n = 334). Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and a nomogram was constructed based on multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Among 1,004 patients, 262 (26.1%) had ACO. Seven predictors, including smoking history, ST-segment depression ≥ 1 mm, regional wall motion abnormality, left ventricular ejection fraction, admission cardiac troponin I, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, were incorporated into the model. The area under the ROC curve was 0.731 (95% CI, 0.688-0.773) in the training cohort and 0.715 (95% CI, 0.654-0.776) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA demonstrated favorable clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and validated a multidimensional prediction model for ACO in patients with NSTEMI. The model showed acceptable performance and may aid early identification before coronary angiography, although reliance on IL-6, which is not routinely available in all centers, may limit its generalizability.
title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal hypoperfusion, driven by reduced mean arterial pressure or increased venous congestion, contributes to acute kidney injury in cardiogenic shock. Assessing cardiovascular support strategies for patients with cardiogenic shock requires controlled platforms such as mock circulatory loops (MCLs). However, most MCLs lack renal autoregulation or do not account for venous pressure, risking inaccurate renal flow estimation. Here, we describe how to implement a perfusion pressure-based autoregulated renal circulation within an MCL.
METHODS: A renal circulation was integrated into an existing biventricular MCL. Renal vascular resistance was dynamically adjusted according to a perfusion pressure-renal flow relationship. Autoregulation performance was quantified by mean square error between measured and theoretical renal flow. Left, right, and biventricular cardiogenic shock were simulated. Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) support and fluid doses were used as clinically relevant interventions to modify the arterial and venous determinants of perfusion pressure.
RESULTS: Renal autoregulation closely reproduced the target relationship, with mean square error 0.001 (L/min)2. Increasing ECMO flow increased perfusion pressure through higher mean arterial pressure (MAP) and lower mean right atrial pressure (MRAP) across all ventricular failure phenotypes. Conversely, fluid doses increased both MAP and MRAP, with the magnitude of MRAP elevation varying by ventricular failure phenotype and partially offsetting the increase in MAP, resulting in smaller increases in perfusion pressure. Renal flow responses reflected perfusion pressure rather than arterial pressure alone.
CONCLUSION: Renal flow-perfusion pressure autoregulation can be accurately implemented in an MCL. Incorporating such renal autoregulation improves physiological fidelity of MCLs and evaluation of cardiovascular devices.
title: Mock Circulatory Loop With Autoregulated Renal Circulation Based on Perfusion Pressure for Circulatory Support Devices Evaluation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac amyloidosis is increasingly recognized in older patients with severe aortic stenosis, yet advanced pressure-overload remodeling can produce overlapping imaging features that confound noninvasive diagnosis.
CASE SUMMARY: A 70-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed extremely severe calcific aortic stenosis, increased left ventricular wall thickness, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated elevated native T1 and extracellular volume with late gadolinium enhancement, and cardiac amyloid radionuclide imaging showed Perugini grade 1 uptake. Despite clinical suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis, noninvasive findings remained inconclusive. The patient underwent surgical aortic valve replacement with intraoperative myocardial biopsy, which demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis without amyloid deposition, consistent with advanced pressure-overload remodeling rather than infiltrative disease.
DISCUSSION: Extremely severe aortic stenosis can mimic cardiac amyloidosis across multiple imaging modalities. Histologic confirmation remains essential when noninvasive findings are discordant or inconclusive.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Severe aortic stenosis may closely mimic cardiac amyloidosis on multimodality imaging. Histological confirmation can be decisive in resolving diagnostic uncertainty.
title: Extremely Severe Aortic Stenosis Mimicking Cardiac Amyloidosis on Multimodality Imaging.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.
METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.
RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) in the review, four in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476).
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with a study-defined composite endpoint, and the network ranking rests on sparse direct comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with pairwise and network meta-analysis of randomised trials of routine PCI versus conservative management of coronary disease in patients undergoing TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the randomised evidence on revascularisation before TAVI, a contested decision in which guidelines remain cautious.

title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction (TVME) in the systemic circulation is increasingly being reported. However, its feasibility, effectiveness, and safety remain poorly defined.
AIMS: We sought to investigate the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of TVME in the left heart and aortic arch.
METHODS: Consecutive patients from 6 centres in the United States and Canada were included. Feasibility was defined as technically successful mass extraction without unplanned cardiac surgery or intraprocedural mortality. The effectiveness endpoint was feasibility with successful debulking of ≥70% mass volume. The primary safety endpoint was the 30-day composite of procedure-attributable mortality, major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke, all according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 definitions. Intraprocedural events were also reported.
RESULTS: A total of 62 consecutive patients were evaluated. Feasibility was reached in 85.5% of patients and effectiveness in 77.4% of patients - except for 11.3% with suboptimal debulking, 3.2% with access-related case abortion, and 8.1% with case cancellation where no mass was found intraprocedurally. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 14.5% of patients, with a procedure-attributable mortality rate of 3.2%. VARC-3 major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, ACS, and stroke occurred in 3.2%, 8.1%, 3.2%, 3.2%, and 6.5% of patients, respectively. Intraprocedural events included hypoxia (6.5%), hypotension (9.7%), embolism (3.2%), air embolism (1.6%), and increased mitral regurgitation (6.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: TVME in left-sided and aortic arch masses is feasible and demonstrates reasonable effectiveness. However, the considerable rate of safety-related events highlights the need for better case selection and procedural refinement, such as optimal embolic protection.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
title: Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control.
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.
METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index.
RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (LAAC) is plagued by late peri-device leak. We posited that appendage contraction prevents full LAA seal, so conversely, LAA stunning with pulsed field ablation (PFA) of the LAA (left atrial appendage ablation [LAAA]) might promote rapid appendage thrombosis/obliteration.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to assess the impact of LAAA during concomitant procedures on eliminating leaks.
METHODS: At 3 centers, consecutive patients undergoing concomitant PFA and LAAC also underwent LAAA or did not undergo LAAA, at operator discretion. Initial (∼3-4 months) (29% transesophageal echocardiography/71% computed tomography) and 12-month imaging were compared with a primary composite outcome of LAA patency, defined as either detectable flow into the LAA or evidence of echo-free space/contrast medium behind the device.
RESULTS: Among 317 total patients undergoing PFA and LAAC, including 222 patients who underwent LAAA and 95 who did not (control patients), all underwent initial imaging and 126 reached 12-month imaging follow-up. Device compression was 28% with LAAA vs 25% without LAAA (P < 0.001). Implantation success was 100%. The periprocedural adverse event rate was 2% in both groups. The primary composite outcome of LAA patency was significantly reduced with LAAA vs no-LAAA, both at 3-4 months (29% vs 64%; P < 0.001) and at 12 months (4% vs 42%; P < 0.001). Device-related thrombus rates were low and similar (2.3% vs 3.2%; P = 0.7). A validation subset including only patients with alternating LAAA assignment (LAAA: n = 59; no-LAAA: n = 63) again revealed that LAAA was associated with reduced LAA patency (3-4 months: 34% vs 51%; P = 0.06; 12 months: 8% vs 36%; P = 0.2). Final LAA e' velocity was significantly different between groups (17 ± 7 vs 34 ± 16 cm/s; P < 0.001), with higher velocity associated with LAA patency (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: PFA of the LAA has potential to reduce LAA patency during device-based LAAC.
title: Pulsed Field Ablation of the Left Atrial Appendage Before Mechanical Closure to Reduce Peri-Device Leak (STUN-AF).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy is a major cause of late graft failure and mortality after heart transplantation. Revascularization is often limited by the diffuse nature of the disease, whereas redo sternotomy carries substantial risks in immunosuppressed patients.
CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old male developed progressive cardiac allograft vasculopathy with a hemodynamically significant left anterior descending artery stenosis unsuitable for percutaneous coronary intervention, 11 years after heart transplantation. He underwent successful robot-assisted minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass grafting, with robotic left internal thoracic artery harvesting and an off-pump hand-sewn left internal thoracic artery to left anterior descending artery anastomosis through a left anterior thoracotomy. The postoperative course was uneventful.
DISCUSSION AND TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case supports the feasibility of robot-assisted minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting as a sternotomy-sparing revascularization strategy in carefully selected heart-transplant recipients with coronary allograft vasculopathy unsuitable for percutaneous treatment.
title: Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Direct Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy After Heart Transplantation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Device-related thrombus (DRT) is a recognized complication of left atrial appendage occlusion. Persistent iatrogenic atrial septal defect (iASD) has not been described as a source of late left atrial thrombus.
CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man with prior WATCHMAN FLX (Boston Scientific) implantation had a residual iASD on 45-day transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Eighteen months later, transthoracic echocardiography revealed a large left atrial mass. TEE demonstrated a 5.4 × 4.0-cm mobile thrombus and a separate 2.4 × 1.0-cm device-adherent thrombus, interpreted as fragmented or partially separated DRT. After 2 weeks of therapeutic anticoagulation, both persisted. Surgery identified a dominant organized thrombus anchored to the interatrial septum at the iASD, with a separate fibrinous thrombus adherent to the device. Both were excised, and the device was preserved.
DISCUSSION: A persistent iASD may act as a late thrombotic nidus and coexist with true DRT. Surgery can clarify the diagnosis and permit device preservation.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: A persistent iASD after left atrial appendage occlusion may serve as a late nidus for a giant left atrial thrombus and may coexist with true DRT, a distinction that TEE may not resolve. Surgical extraction of a large, highly mobile thrombus persisting despite anticoagulation can be diagnostic and therapeutic while permitting preservation of a stable device.
title: Giant Left Atrial Thrombus After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Surgery Reveals a Transseptal-Site Origin.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct aortic Impella 5.5 implantation has been increasingly used for high-risk cardiac surgery. Delayed complications from thrombus around the retained graft in the ascending aorta (AA) following device explantation is rarely reported.
CASE SUMMARY: A 55-year-old man with a history of coronary artery bypass grafting requiring Impella 5.5 via a Dacron graft on the AA developed acute thromboembolic stroke 3 years after coronary artery bypass grafting. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a right middle cerebral artery occlusion and thrombus within the AA around the retained Impella graft. Successful middle cerebral artery mechanical thrombectomy was performed, and the intra-aortic thrombus was managed medically with oral anticoagulation, resulting in complete resolution on 1-month follow-up imaging.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights an under-recognized source of delayed embolic stroke for which no surveillance or anticoagulation guidelines currently exist.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Intra-aortic thrombus around the graft should be considered in patients presenting with delayed stroke after direct aortic Impella 5.5 explantation.
title: Delayed Embolic Stroke From Thrombus Around Microaxial Flow Pump Insertion Site in Ascending Aorta.

abstract: The implementation of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin assays has significantly improved the prompt diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Nevertheless, early risk stratification and the swift diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain challenging. We report a machine-learning-integrated NLRC3/cTnT dual-analyte time-resolved fluorescent lateral-flow immunoassay biosensor for quantitative ACS screening and discrimination of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) from unstable angina (UA). The biosensor uses europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel lateral-flow setup to simultaneously detect NLRC3 and cTnT within 20 min. The original serum sample is diluted separately for each channel, with 100 µL of the diluted sample applied to each. The optimized NLRC3 and cTnT assays demonstrated strong quantitative performance, precision, minimal cross-reactivity, and acceptable interference resistance. In clinical evaluation, NLRC3 alone identified ACS with 80.5% accuracy but was less effective in distinguishing AMI-UA. By combining NLRC3 and cTnT using a Naïve Bayes classifier, the dual-analyte biosensor improved to 84.6% sensitivity, 89.6% specificity, and 87.8% accuracy for AMI-UA discrimination. This study introduces a dual-pathophysiology lateral-flow biosensor that merges inflammatory-risk and myocardial-injury detection, providing a practical POCT method for decentralized ACS triage.
title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification.
METHODS: In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).
RESULTS: Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).
CONCLUSION: The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.
keywords: Major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events
title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Whether the association of quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with long-term outcomes differs according to multivessel disease (MVD) status is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association of QFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI with 3-year outcomes according to MVD status.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this prespecified secondary analysis of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial, patients were screened across 26 centers in China from December 25, 2018, to January 19, 2020. Eligible participants were adults undergoing PCI for stable or unstable angina or for myocardial infarction (MI) occurring at least 72 hours before screening who had at least 1 lesion with 50% to 90% diameter stenosis in a vessel of 2.5 mm or larger. The analysis compared QFR-guided with angiography-guided PCI according to MVD status. MVD was defined by involvement of at least 2 epicardial vessels or the left main coronary artery. The primary analyses of the current prespecified secondary analysis were completed in October 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: Randomization 1:1 to QFR-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, MI, and ischemia-driven revascularization. The current analysis evaluated 3-year MACE.
RESULTS: Among 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population (mean [SD] age, 62.7 [10.0] years; 2699 [70.6%] male), 2066 (54.0%) had MVD. In the MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 124 of 1023 patients (12.1%) in the QFR-guided group and 188 of 1043 patients (18.1%) in the angiography-guided group (hazard ratio, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.52-0.81; P < .001), driven by lower rates of MI and revascularization. In the non-MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 76 of 890 patients (8.6%) and 95 of 869 patients (11.0%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.04; P = .09). The treatment × MVD interaction was not statistically significant (P for interaction = .35). The findings of landmark, per-protocol, competing-risk, sensitivity, and hierarchical win-ratio analyses were directionally consistent with the main findings.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial of patients undergoing PCI, QFR-guided PCI was associated with a lower 3-year MACE rate among patients with MVD; however, no significant interaction was observed between treatment effect and MVD status. These findings provide longer-term randomized evidence supporting QFR-guided PCI across MVD strata and warrant further confirmation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03656848.

abstract: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.
title: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To resolve the apparent paradox between deterministic physiological laws and probabilistic clinical outcomes by framing clinical variability as epistemic uncertainty within a complex, non-linear system, demonstrating how deterministic mechanisms can account for empirical distributions and outcome heterogeneity.
METHODS: We developed the "Frank" project, a 0-dimensional computational agent-based model (ABM) of human cardiovascular hemodynamics implemented in Julia (Agents.jl). Using Monte Carlo simulations (n=100), myocardial infarction was modeled by varying initial conditions, specifically sampling the infarction area from a Gaussian distribution along with systemic compliance. Cardiogenic shock was defined by a systolic arterial pressure <90mmHg and a cardiac index <2.2L/min/m2, with parameters evaluated via grid search against literature incidence benchmarks (5-10%).
RESULTS: The simulation produced hemodynamically stable, physiologically sound boundary parameters and pressure-volume loops. When initialized with a mean infarction area of 35±5% and systemic compliance of 1.5±0.3mL/mmHg, the model yielded a 7\% incidence of cardiogenic shock, closely matching empirical data. A strong linear inverse correlation was observed between infarction area and post-infarction systolic blood pressure (mean 93.96mmHg).
CONCLUSION: Stochastic-appearing clinical trial outcomes can emerge from deterministic physiological systems characterized by sensitivity to initial parameters and hidden variables. The "Frank" framework establishes a Monte Carlo bridge between mechanistic physiology and epidemiological statistics, offering an approach to explore outcome heterogeneity and refine clinical trial interpretation and patient stratification.
title: Probabilistic clinical studies and deterministic physiology: building a Monte Carlo bridge with the "Frank" project.

abstract: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a time-critical vascular emergency in which delayed recognition may occur because the presenting symptoms and electrocardiographic phenotypes often overlap with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, and other emergency diagnoses. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) remains the confirmatory standard, but the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is usually obtained earlier, is universally available at triage, and may carry distributed signatures of malperfusion, ischemia mimicry, autonomic stress, conduction delay, and hemodynamic compromise. We developed Q-AortaECG, a classically implemented quantum-inspired multi-agent ECG system that integrates multiscale waveform representations, specialist ECG agents, density-state uncertainty fusion, a variational-circuit style consensus layer, and a safety-gated multidisciplinary team-style report for early AAS triage. The system was evaluated in three suspected-AAS/CTA-evaluable cohorts comprising 1,251 patients, including 467 with CTA-, surgery-, or autopsy-confirmed AAS. Across 700 locked-test patients, Q-AortaECG achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.881 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.852-0.908), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.743 (95% CI, 0.695-0.790), sensitivity of 0.955 (231/242; 95% CI, 0.920-0.977), specificity of 0.721 (330/458; 95% CI, 0.677-0.761), positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.643, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.968 at the prespecified high-sensitivity threshold. Performance remained consistent in external retrospective validation and prospective silent-run evaluation, although AUPRC decreased in the lower-prevalence prospective cohort. Ablation experiments supported the contributions of self-supervised ECG pretraining, agent specialization, density-matrix uncertainty fusion, and differential diagnosis modeling. In a counterbalanced paired reader study, Q-AortaECG assistance improved overall clinician sensitivity from 0.696 to 0.870 while preserving specificity (0.851 ver sus 0.846). In prospective silent-run analysis, counterfactual alerts would have advanced the median time to the correct diagnostic pathway from 187 to 61 minutes among initially unsuspected AAS presentations. These findings support ECG first, calibrated, safety-gated decision support as an early warning scaffold for AAS triage, while preserving CTA and expert imaging interpretation as the diagnostic standard.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Q-AortaECG: A Quantum-Inspired Multi-Agent 12-Lead ECG System for Early Triage of Acute Aortic Syndrome.

abstract:
AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant.
CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.
title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.

abstract: Audio signals, as a crucial component of the human perceptual system, can assist video saliency models in semantic localization. However, integrating audio signals requires rich information representations, which may increase computational costs. Additionally, the inherent differences between auditory and visual features can lead to information confusion during the fusion process. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight audiovisual attention cross-perception network (LAAC-Net) for video saliency prediction. Specifically, we introduce a lightweight two-stream audiovisual feature encoder to reduce computational overhead. To integrate multi-modal features, including temporal, spatial, and auditory features, we design an audiovisual cross-perception fusion (ACPF) module that uses multi-head self-attention (MSA) and multi-head cross-attention (MCA) to model inter-modality correlations. In the decoding stage, we employ three multi-level dilated perception (MLDP) modules to aggregate multi-scale spatiotemporal features, where the convolution layers with different dilation rates are cascaded to extend the receptive fields. Experimental results on six challenging audiovisual eye-tracking datasets show that LAAC-Net achieves superior results compared with the evaluated lightweight methods. Moreover, our model has fewer parameters than the fastest competing model, while maintaining comparable running speed.
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
title: Lightweight audiovisual attention cross-perception network for video saliency prediction.

abstract: BackgroundHemolysis is a frequent and clinically relevant complication during extracorporeal life support (ECLS, or ECMO), associated with acute kidney injury, systemic inflammation, and increased mortality. Direct comparisons between pumps regarding hemolysis are limited. This study evaluated and compared hemolysis profiles among several devices in clinical practice.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study adult patients who received veno-arterial (V-A) or veno-venous (V-V) ECMO between January 2020 and December 2023 (N = 230). Patients were categorized by one of four ECMO pump types, and hemolysis was assessed using lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and plasma-free hemoglobin (pfHb) as primary markers. Multivariable linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze associations between pump type and hemolysis, adjusting for several covariates including revolutions per minute (RPM), hematologic indices, ECMO mode, and severity scores.ResultsPartial thromboplastin time (p < 0.005), hemoglobin (p < 0.001), and use of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT, p < 0.001) were positively correlated with both LDH and pfHb concentrations and hemolysis, while fibrinogen (p < 0.03) was inversely correlated. Without RPM adjustment, NovaLung exhibited the highest LDH (680.3 U/L) and pfHb (29.4 mg/dL), followed by the Cardiohelp, Rotaflow, and CentriMag. In the RPM-adjusted analysis, LDH was highest in Cardiohelp (737.4 U/L), followed by the Rotaflow, CentriMag, and NovaLung; whereas pfHb was highest in Cardiohelp (25.8 mg/dL), followed by the Rotaflow, NovaLung, and CentriMag.ConclusionsThis study provides a clinical associations of the safety and performance of four centrifugal pumps in real-world ECMO practice in adults. We demonstrate that pump-specific RPM may be potentially correlated with hemolysis during ECMO in clinical practice, illustrating that the diagonal pump, which operated at the highest RPMs, was associated with the highest hemolysis in models without the RPM adjustment. Future studies are warranted to further clarify the impact of hemolysis on outcomes.
title: Comparing hemolysis among extracorporeal pumps: A large-scale retrospective study.

abstract:
PURPOSE: This retrospective single-center study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of the SOFIA Catheter for percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy (PAT) in periinterventional distal embolization (DE) during lower limb endovascular revascularization.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The radiological information system was retrospectively reviewed for all DEs treated with the SOFIA Catheter between 2017 and 2024. Angiographic findings, vessel diameters, embolic origin, technical success, and complications were assessed. Reperfusion was graded using the Peripheral Arterial Reperfusion Score (PARS). PARS 2-3 was defined as the primary endpoint (angiographic technical success); conversion of PARS 1 to PARS 2-3 after adjunctive therapy as secondary success.
RESULTS: A total of 128 vessels in 104 patients (67 male; median age 69 years) were included. Emboli originated from acute lesions in 52% and chronic disease in 48%; in-stent restenosis was present in 17%. Primary angiographic success (PARS 2-3) was achieved in 81% (95% CI: 72.8-86.4%). After additional PTA or stenting, overall secondary success increased to 88% (95% CI: 80.7-92.2%). Thrombectomy failed in 12%. One patient required major amputation and one surgical embolectomy. No catheter-related dissections or perforations occurred. Prior AngioJet use showed an exploratory correlation with PARS 0 (r = 0.329; p < .001).
CONCLUSION: PAT using the SOFIA Catheter demonstrates high angiographic success rates and a favorable safety profile for periinterventional DE in lower limb arteries. Prior hydrodynamic thrombectomy may reduce embolus retrievability; this finding is exploratory and should be considered hypothesis-generating.
KEY POINTS: · The SOFIA Catheter enables effective aspiration in small distal vessels.. · Primary angiographic success reached 81% (95% CI: 72.8-86.4%).. · Overall success increased to 88% (95% CI: 80.7-92.2%) after adjunctive therapy.. · No catheter-related complications were observed.. · Prior AngioJet use was exploratively associated with lower retrieval success..
CITATION FORMAT: · Trentmann J, Aludin S, Andersson J et al. Percutaneous Aspiration Thrombectomy with the SOFIA Catheter for Periinterventional Distal Embolization in Lower Limb Revascularization. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2942-7381.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) presents a formidable challenge in mitral valve surgery owing to risks of atrioventricular groove disruption, circumflex artery injury, and paravalvular leaks. The optimal operative strategy varies according to the severity of annular calcification, extent of ventricular extension, and the patient-specific risk profile.
METHODS: A narrative expert review was performed synthesizing contemporary surgical series, imaging-guided approaches, and transcatheter strategies for mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC. Technical considerations, complication avoidance strategies, and decision-making frameworks were integrated into a new severity-based operative algorithm.
RESULTS: We developed a decision matrix to stratify patients into four categories to guide preoperative planning and operative decisions. MAC management lies on a spectrum between working around the MAC with no resection ("respect" the MAC) to complete MAC resection with atrioventricular groove reconstruction ("resect" the MAC). Severe or circumferential MAC demands tailored strategies, including transcatheter or hybrid approaches. In patients with mild MAC, mitral valve repair remains feasible and preferred. Moderate MAC requires individualized decision-making; repair is achievable when leaflet mobility is preserved, and decalcification permits secure annuloplasty. Replacement is favored when leaflet restriction or annular rigidity precludes durable reconstruction. The extent of decalcification should be tailored to the patient's risk profile and surgical expertise to ensure durable results.
CONCLUSIONS: Mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC requires an individualized approach. We propose a practical management algorithm, stratified by patient risk and anatomic feasibility.
title: Mitral Annular Calcification: Operative Decision Making and Technical Considerations.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs.
OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs.
METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety.
RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type.
CONCLUSION: These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.
title: Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) often complicate acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The prognostic impact of VA timing relative to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic significance of VA based on their timing of occurrence in relation to PCI.
METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting all-cause mortality with and without VA (sustained or hemodynamically unstable VT/VF) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. The endpoints analyzed were short-term (30 days/in-hospital) and long-term (1 year) mortality. A network meta-analysis comparing VA-before PCI, VA-during PCI, and VA-after PCI with the group not experiencing VA as a reference was conducted.
RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 49,963 patients were included, of whom 3,475 (7.0%) experienced VA. VA was associated with increased short- (OR 5.04, 95%CI 3.78-6.72) and long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95%CI 2.20-3.86). In patients alive at discharge/30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not differ between those with and without VA (OR 0.97, 95%CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis showed that all VA timings are associated with a significantly higher risk compared with the group not experiencing VA. Sensitivity analysis found that VA-after is associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier VA (OR 3.37, 95%CI 1.46-7.82).
CONCLUSIONS: VA substantially increase the risk of death in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Mortality risk emerges to be associated with the timing of VA occurrence, with VA-after PCI associated with the highest risk. These findings highlight the prognostic relevance of arrhythmic events across the entire peri-procedural window, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification.
title: Prognostic Impact of Ventricular Arrhythmia Timing in Acute Coronary Syndromes Treated with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) with the Watchman™ device is typically performed with the use of transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and fluoroscopy. LAAC guided by intracardiac echo (ICE) without the use of fluoroscopy has not been previously described.
OBJECTIVE: In this series, we describe the safety and feasibility of Watchman™ implantation using only ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy.
METHODS: 214 patients undergoing LAAC with the Watchman FLX™ or Watchman FLX™ Pro device and using a planned fluoroscopy-free approach were studied. ICE was used for echocardiographic imaging in all cases. TEE was not used in any cases. Fluoroscopy was used as a bail-out approach when it was felt to be clinically necessary by the operator. Peri-procedural, 45-day, and 1-year efficacy and safety outcomes were assessed.
RESULTS: In 203/214 patients (94.8%), LAAC was completed without the use of fluoroscopy. Bail-out fluoroscopy was required in 11/214 patients (5.1%). Successful device implantation was completed in 212/214 patients (99.1%). The rate of any peri-device leak at 45 days post-procedure was 11.6%. Procedural complications were limited to one pericardial effusion and one case of ventricular tachycardia.
CONCLUSION: LAAC with the Watchman™ device using ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy appears to be safe and effective. The rates of procedural success, complications, and peri-device leaks on 45 day follow up were consistent with that seen in pivotal clinical trials. Further studies are needed to assess the broader applicability of this technique.
title: Zero-fluoroscopy approach to left atrial appendage closure using intracardiac echo guidance.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup.
METHODS: We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT.
RESULTS: After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO.
CONCLUSIONS: AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.
title: Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.
RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.
title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.

abstract: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Prior bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11.0%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs. 10.1%, p=0.17). Major bleeding (BARC ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25.0% vs. 12.5%, p=0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted OR 2.18, 95% CI 0.43-8.71, p=0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after cardiac surgery and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.
title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: a Report from the MARS Registry.

abstract: Real-world data on the adoption and clinical performance of angiography-derived physiology in the United States (U.S.) remain limited. We evaluated the implementation of FFRangio (CathWorks, Tel Aviv, Israel) and associated clinical outcomes across a multicenter U.S. healthcare system. We performed a multicenter observational cohort study across 4 centers involving consecutive adult patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography in whom FFRangio was performed in at least 1 coronary vessel based on clinical indication. The primary endpoint was target-vessel failure (TVF), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction and target vessel revascularization during follow-up, stratified by FFRangio values >0.80 versus ≤0.80. A total of 675 vessels in 469 patients were assessed by FFRangio; 240 (36%) had values ≤0.80 and 435 (64%) >0.80. Among lesions with FFRangio ≤0.80, 182 (76%) underwent PCI, 27 (11%) CABG, and 32 (13%) were managed medically. Among lesions with FFRangio >0.80, revascularization was deferred in 406 (92%), with 22 (5%) undergoing PCI and 12 (3%) CABG. The LAD was the most frequently treated vessel (51%). At a median follow-up of 10.2 months, the incidence rate of TVF was 1.55% per 100 lesion-years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57-3.36) in the FFRangio >0.80 group versus 6.30 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI, 3.25-11.0) in the FFRangio ≤0.80 group (hazard ratio [HR] 4.61, 95% CI: 1.61-13.2; p=0.002). Among deferred lesions with FFRangio >0.80, TVF rate was 1.73 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI: 0.64-3.77). In conclusion, FFRangio supported safe deferral of revascularization and risk-stratification, with low event rates among lesions with values >0.80.
title: Clinical Implementation of Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve for Revascularization Guidance: Initial Multicenter United States Experience.

abstract: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters can provide mechanical protection from pulmonary embolism in selected patients who cannot receive anticoagulation, but filter-related thrombosis is an important complication. A uniform definition is lacking. Thrombus in the filter region may represent emboli captured by the filter, extension of pre-existing deep vein thrombosis, or local thrombus formation around the device. Filter-induced flow disturbance and vessel-wall responses may contribute to local thrombosis, although direct mechanistic evidence in humans remains limited. Reported occurrence varies substantially because study populations, imaging schedules, and outcome definitions differ. Clinically detected caval thrombosis or thrombotic occlusion is uncommon in large databases and prospective cohorts. Planned imaging before retrieval, however, often detects small intrafilter thrombi, most of which are asymptomatic. Accordingly, the clinical importance of an imaging-detected thrombus depends on whether it is accompanied by meaningful caval obstruction or symptoms. Prevention should continue throughout the filter life cycle. Filters should be used only for a time-limited, evidence-based indication. Anticoagulation should be resumed when a separate indication persists and bleeding risk permits, and retrieval should be assessed once filter-mediated pulmonary embolism protection is no longer required. Structured follow-up can help prevent loss to care. Management of established thrombosis should be guided by symptoms, impaired caval outflow, thrombus progression and chronicity, bleeding risk, and the need for filter retrieval. Anticoagulation remains foundational when indicated for active venous thromboembolism. Catheter-directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy, or combined treatment may be considered for selected symptomatic, progressive, or obstructive cases, but most supporting studies are nonrandomized. Future studies require standardized minimum reporting and patient-centered outcomes.
title: Inferior vena cava filter-related thrombosis: Mechanisms, clinical features, prevention, diagnosis, and risk-stratified management.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary obstruction (CO) complicates valve-in-valve (ViV) and redo transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) at higher rates than native TAVR. Leaflet modification mitigates this risk but increases procedural burden. Traditional computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based risk stratification relies on static parameters that may overestimate risk; computational predictive modeling (CPM) uses patient-specific data to refine risk assessment.
OBJECTIVES: The study aims to characterize leaflet modification rates in conventional ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR and evaluate the impact of CPM preprocedural planning augmentation on leaflet modification rates.
METHODS: A total of 157 consecutive ViV TAVR or redo-TAVR patients treated from 2022 to 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. CO risk status was derived from traditional CTA parameters. Leaflet modification rates among CTA high-risk subgroups (non-CPM, n = 62; and CPM, n = 29) were compared using Boschloo's one-sided exact test. CPM risk-reclassification patterns were studied using counterfactual binomial analysis.
RESULTS: Leaflet modification occurred in 26.3% of ViV TAVR and 24.1% of redo-TAVR procedures that used only conventional CTA-based planning methods. Among patients deemed high risk for CO by conventional methods, leaflet modification was significantly lower in the CPM-augmented subgroup vs that in the non-CPM subgroup (24.1% vs 46.8%; OR: 2.76; 95% CI: 1.03-7.40; P = 0.021). CPM-augmented planning reclassified 82.8% of patients to low-risk status, and 79.2% of reclassified patients were managed without leaflet modification. No COs occurred during the study period.
CONCLUSIONS: Among ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR patients at high risk of CO based on conventional CTA-based planning, the use of CPM to augment standard risk assessment was associated with a significant reduction in leaflet modification procedures.
title: Computational Modeling Reduces Leaflet Modification Rates in Valve-In-Valve and Redo Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
