abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in emergency settings is a notorious diagnostic challenge due to their overlapping symptoms and shared electrocardiographic abnormalities, such as precordial T-wave inversion (TWI). This study evaluated the ability of machine learning (ML) algorithms to distinguish acute PE from ACS by analyzing the morphology of inverted T waves in precordial leads.
METHODS: This retrospective, case-control study included 200 patients (100 ACS confirmed by coronary angiography; 100 PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography) admitted to Shahid Madani Hospital, Tabriz, Iran (2023-2024), who exhibited precordial TWI. Image processing with a region-growing technique traced negative T waves in leads V1, V2, and V3. Signals were filtered using Savitzky-Golay and Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) methods to extract time-frequency statistical parameters. Multiple supervised ML models were trained (80% training, 20% test with 5-fold cross-validation) over 50 random iterations.
RESULTS: The Ensemble (AdaBoost) model achieved the highest diagnostic performance, yielding an accuracy of 84.44%, sensitivity of 83.96%, specificity of 84.87%, and F1-score of 83.56%. Neural Network models performed comparably, achieving 84.00% accuracy and 85.14% sensitivity. Other evaluated algorithms (SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes) also generated acceptable discriminative accuracy (ranging from 78% to 82%).
CONCLUSION: Machine-learning algorithms can extract potentially disease-specific features from precordial T-wave morphology to differentiate PE from ACS. These findings support further investigation of AI-enhanced ECG interpretation as a rapid, low-cost, non-invasive adjunct to clinical decision-making in acute care. External validation in larger, clinically representative populations is required before clinical application.
title: Machine-learning differentiation of precordial T-wave inversion in pulmonary embolism and acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological Q waves have traditionally been used to localize myocardial infarction (MI), although their anatomical specificity remains uncertain. We investigated the relationship between Q-wave distribution and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined myocardial infarct burden after anterior MI.
METHODS: We analyzed 102 patients with first anterior ST-elevation MI. Individual Q waves and established anterior Q wave patterns were compared with segmental late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).
RESULTS: Individual Q waves showed broad, overlapping relationships with LGE-defined infarct burden; after false-discovery-rate correction, only Q waves in V1 remained significantly associated with basal anteroseptal and apical septal LGE-defined infarct burden. Established Q wave patterns showed substantial anatomical overlap but a clear gradient in infarct burden. Across the four-level classification based on the most lateral precordial lead with a pathological Q wave (none, V1-V2 only, up to V3, or extending to V4-V6), infarct size increased from 6% to 14%, 17%, and 18% (P for trend<0.001), mid-ventricular LGE burden from 75 to 125, 150, and 175 percentage-points (P < 0.001), and apical LGE burden from 100 to 125, 200, and 200 percentage-points (P < 0.001). LVEF declined across categories (P for trend = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: In anterior MI, pathological Q wave distribution showed limited correspondence with discrete myocardial territories but was associated with increasing infarct size and greater mid-apical LGE-defined infarct burden, suggesting that Q-wave distribution may be better interpreted as a marker of infarct extent than as a geographical map of infarct location. External validation of this simplified extent-based classification is warranted.
title: Pathological Q waves in anterior myocardial infarction: A marker of infarct extent rather than location.

abstract: Early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) critically depends on the ultrasensitive, interference-resistant, point-of-care detection of cardiac troponin I (cTnI). However, conventional lateral flow immunoassays (LFIA) are fundamentally limited by insufficient signal output for trace amounts of cTnI and nonspecific protein adsorption from complex serum matrices, which elevate background noise and undermine both sensitivity and specificity. To simultaneously address these challenges, this study developed SH-PEG-COOH functionalized Au/Pt bimetallic nanoparticles (Au/Pt@PEG NPs) as a dual-functional LFIA probe. The heterobifunctional molecule SH-PEG-COOH integrates a metal-thiol anchoring terminus, a PEG antifouling spacer, and a carboxyl conjugation terminal within a single architecture, enabling one-step self-assembly of a well-defined "anchor-antifouling-conjugation" trilayer interface. The PEG brush suppresses nonspecific protein adsorption through cooperative steric hindrance, hydration repulsion, and conformational entropic repulsion independent of ionic strength, while uniformly exposed carboxyl termini enable orientation-specific antibody immobilization via EDC/NHS chemistry. Meanwhile, accessible Pt sites catalyze TMB/H2O2 oxidation at the test line for in situ colorimetric signal amplification. The platform achieves a limit of detection of 5.2 pg mL-1, representing a 712-fold improvement over conventional AuNP-based LFIA. Systematic evaluation against 13 interfering substances confirms matrix interference elimination, with recovery rates of 92.70%-109.80% in 60% fetal bovine serum. The covalent metal-thiol anchoring maintains PEG brush integrity and antibody conjugation density throughout the probe lifetime, evidenced by stable T/C signal values over 35 days at room temperature. Clinical validity was confirmed across 30 patient samples with strong agreement against commercial ELISA (R2 = 0.998).
journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
title: Au/Pt@PEG Nanozymes Probe for Ultrasensitive and Matrix-Robust Lateral Flow Immunoassay of Cardiac Troponin I.

abstract: Acute myocardial infarction is a life-threatening cardiovascular event, and point-of-care determination of cardiac troponin I (cTnI) is crucial for early diagnosis and timely intervention. Herein, a self-powered point-of-care sensing platform based on a light-driven bipolar electrode (BPE) for synchronous electrochromic and photoelectrochemical dual-readout detection of cTnI was reported. The BPE integrates a photocathodic sensing pole and an electrochromic reporting pole, enabling simultaneous generation of photocurrent and visual color change through a single photoinduced electron-transfer pathway. Magnetic molecularly imprinted microspheres (MMIPs) were employed as robust capture elements to selectively extract cTnI from biophysical samples. Subsequently, cTnI quantitatively bridges MMIPs with Cu-MOF@TiO2 nanoprobes to form a sandwich complex, which is immobilized onto the sensing pole. Upon light irradiation, the Cu-MOF@TiO2 composite generates photogenerated charge carriers, producing a photocurrent at the sensing pole while synchronously driving the reduction of Prussian blue (PB) to Prussian white (PW) at the reporting pole through the BPE circuit. The electrochromic response can be quantitatively analyzed by smartphone RGB imaging, providing visual detection of cTnI from 10-9 to 10-4 mg/mL, while the photoelectrochemical mode exhibits a wider linear range from 10-11 to 10-4 mg/mL. This work offers a portable, instrument-minimized, and self-powered dual-readout strategy for onsite cardiac biomarker analysis, and provides a versatile framework for future multiplexed biosensing applications.
title: Synchronous Visual-Photocurrent Dual-Readout for Cardiac Troponin I Sensing Enabled by Self-Powered Point-of-Care Platform.

abstract: Droplet microarrays hold great promise for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis, yet their biosensing performance is often limited by poor mixing efficiency and nonuniform signal distribution. Here, we report a self-Marangoni-propelled droplet microarray featuring a hydrophobic background, superhydrophilic rings, and hydrophilic cores, enabling solute homogenization and rapid biomarker detection. Continuous water replenishment at the droplet edge creates stable surface tension gradients, driving strong three-dimensional (3D) Marangoni convection and effectively suppressing the coffee-ring effect induced by outward capillary flow. Flow visualization and theoretical analysis reveal that this 3D Marangoni convection not only enhances the internal flow velocity but also fundamentally reconfigures the dominant mass transport direction, achieving an ∼8.7-fold increase in solute mixing efficiency compared with conventional patterned chips. For microRNAs (miRNAs) detection, the platform accelerates hybridization kinetics by ∼17.3-fold, improves sensitivity by ∼500-fold, and lowers the detection limit to 1.0 fM. Further integrated with time-series deep learning algorithms, it achieves accurate identification of AMI patients within 5 min, enabling rapid and precise AMI diagnosis. This convection-generation approach could be readily extended to create versatile droplet-array platforms for combinatorial chemical synthesis, nanomaterial fabrication, and drug combination testing, holding promise for diverse applications beyond biosensing.
title: A Self-Marangoni-Propelled Droplet Microarray for Ultrafast Mixing and Point-of-Care Assay of Acute Myocardial Infarction Biomarkers.

abstract: Atherosclerotic vulnerable plaques pose a risk for acute coronary syndrome and sudden cardiac death due to plaque rupture and thrombosis. While nanomedicines modulating macrophage functions have attracted intensive interest, efficient delivery to plaque macrophages remains challenging. Here, mannose-modified lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are developed for targeted delivery of a novel SHP-1 (Src Homology 2 Domain-containing Phosphatase-1) siRNA to macrophages within atherosclerotic vulnerable plaques, aiming to enhance macrophage function and stabilize plaques. In ApoE-/- mice with vulnerable plaques, both MIC5 and SM-102 LNPs demonstrated robust plaque targeting capabilities (Cy5 fluorescence reaching ∼1010 p/sec/cm2/sr) and significantly reduced plaque area following SHP-1 siRNA delivery. Importantly, the piperazine-based MIC5 LNPs exhibited enhanced plaque targeting efficiency with M2 macrophage uptake efficiency reaching 46.32% as well as superior therapeutic effects. Collectively, these SHP-1 siRNA-loaded LNPs offer a promising targeted therapeutic strategy for atherosclerotic vulnerable plaques and establish a novel nanoplatform for RNA-based macrophage-modulation in various inflammatory diseases.
title: Piperazine-Structured Lipid Nanoparticles Enable Enhanced Targeted Delivery of SHP-1 siRNA to Macrophages for Treatment of Atherosclerotic Vulnerable Plaques.

abstract: Reliable noninvasive discrimination of acute myocarditis (AM) from acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in patients presenting with acute chest pain remains an unmet clinical need. We aimed to identify urinary proteomic markers using mass spectrometry and LASSO regression. Patients with suspected AM or AMI were prospectively enrolled. Urinary proteomes were profiled by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. The discovery cohort was stratified by age and sex and randomly divided into training and internal validation sets at a 3:1 ratio. Differentially expressed proteins were screened, and a diagnostic model was constructed using LASSO with 1000 bootstrap resamplings in the training set. The model was validated internally and further verified in an independent cohort using ELISA. A total of 42 AM and 80 AMI patients were included in the discovery cohort. Differential expression analysis in the training set identified 880 and 1099 differentially expressed proteins in AM and AMI, respectively, compared with controls. A three-protein panel comprising TNFRSF1A, F9, and PRDX3 achieved an AUC of 0.954 in the training set and exceeded the clinical models (all DeLong's P < 0.05). Addition of the protein panel to either clinical model further improved diagnostic performance (both P < 0.001). Similar performance was confirmed in the validation cohorts. A urinary proteomic panel comprising TNFRSF1A, F9, and PRDX3 may provide a noninvasive approach for differentiating AM from AMI.
title: Urinary Proteomic Panel Distinguishes Acute Myocarditis from Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tricuspid valve surgery is neither complex nor time-consuming yet is associated with high surgical mortality. Our goal was to characterize heterogeneity of right heart variables and manifestations of right heart failure in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation and evaluate survival after tricuspid valve surgery.
METHODS: From 1/2007 to 1/2014, 522 adults with severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent cardiac surgery. Median follow-up was 3.7 years. Right heart morphology and function variables were measured de novo from stored echocardiographic images. To discover possible pheno-endotypes, unsupervised cluster analysis was performed by sidClustering.rfsrc using preoperative clinical, morphologic, ventricular function, and hemodynamic variables. Variable priority classification was used to characterize resulting pheno-endotypes. Post-surgery survival was assessed by cluster.
RESULTS: Three pheno-endotype clusters were identified, each with distinct 10-year survival: Cluster 1 (n=220), predominantly patients with left-sided disease, 59%; Cluster 2 (n=78), predominantly patients with the most dilated right ventricles (diastolic area 42±10 cm2), 46%; and Cluster 3 (n=224), predominantly patients with worse right ventricular dysfunction (fractional area change 30%±12%), 21% (worst prognosis). Elevated model for end-stage liver disease with sodium was the most important predictor of time-related mortality and separated Clusters 1 and 2 from Cluster 3.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients presenting for cardiac surgery with severe tricuspid regurgitation cluster into 3 pheno-endotypes, illustrating clinical presentation and patient heterogeneity and predicting distinctive prognosis. Right heart function and right heart failure severity need to be recognized to guide patient selection and management.
journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
title: Right Heart Failure Pheno-Endotype Drives Prognosis after Tricuspid Valve Surgery.

journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
title: Commentary: Despite a promising IMPACT, preemptive impella support in high-risk cardiac surgery is not yet ready for prime time.

abstract: A 74-year-old man with mixed bicuspid aortic valve disease, combining severe calcific stenosis with severe regurgitation, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 26% presented in normotensive cardiogenic shock with anuria and an arterial lactate of 12 mmol/L. Computed tomography showed a fibrocalcific left-right raphe and an aortic angulation of 66 degrees. Emergency transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation was undertaken. The delivery system could not be advanced across the aortic arch despite escalation of guidewire support, and ventricular fibrillation degenerated into pulseless electrical activity refractory to resuscitation. Peripheral venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was established, after which a 29 mm self-expanding prosthesis was implanted with an acceptable haemodynamic result and patent coronary ostia. Pulseless electrical activity nonetheless persisted. Return of spontaneous circulation followed only after a microaxial pump was advanced retrogradely across the freshly deployed prosthesis under fluoroscopic guidance alone, establishing an ECMELLA configuration. The patient died of multiorgan failure two days later. This sequence identifies continued left ventricular loading, rather than any residual valve lesion, as the reason resuscitation failed, and argues for anticipating unloading when extracorporeal support is instituted across a valve just rendered competent in a severely dysfunctional ventricle. The outcome appeared determined by end-organ injury already established before intervention.
title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Mixed Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease With a Horizontal Aorta: Return of Spontaneous Circulation Only After Left Ventricular Unloading.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) assays have demonstrated good analytical agreement with central laboratory (CL) testing, it remains uncertain whether they yield the same clinical triage decisions. We evaluated the clinical concordance of a POC hs-cTnI assay with a CL assay using the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h algorithm.
METHODS: This prospective diagnostic agreement study included 127 patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute coronary syndrome. The primary outcome was concordance of patient classification according to the 0/1-h algorithm, assessed using the quadratic weighted kappa (κ) statistic. Secondary outcomes included quantitative agreement assessed by the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis, and analytical comparability between whole blood and plasma on the POC platform.
RESULTS: Overall, 114/127 patients (89.8%) were assigned to the same triage category (κ = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.878-0.964). All 13 discordant classifications (10.2%) occurred between adjacent categories, with no CL rule-in patient classified as POC rule-out. Quantitative agreement between assays was good (ICC = 0.882; 95%CI 0.835-0.917), with a mean bias of -5.27 ng/L. Whole blood and plasma showed close agreement (ICC = 0.999; 95%CI 0.998-0.999), with a mean bias of 0.50 ng/L.
CONCLUSIONS: The POC assay showed high clinical concordance with CL-based ESC 0/1-h triage classification, with all discordances confined to adjacent categories. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of POC hs-cTnI testing under routine bedside conditions.
journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
title: Clinical triage concordance of a point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay using the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autonomic dysfunction increases the risk of cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Renal denervation reduces renal sympathetic nerve activity and lowers blood pressure independent of long-term pharmacotherapy, with potential downstream effects on metabolic and hepatic pathways. We aimed to evaluate the impact of renal denervation, compared with intensive antihypertensive therapy, on cardiometabolic disease risk.
METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using the TriNetX global federated health research network. Eligible participants were adults with hypertension (ICD-10 code I10) who were treated with either renal denervation therapy and pharmacological treatment (identified via ICD-10 or Current Procedural Terminology codes), acting as the treatment group, or an intensive pharmacological antihypertensive regime (four of a beta blocker, calcium channel blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, angiotensin II receptor blocker, alpha blocker or diuretic), acting as the control group. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced the treatment and control groups, accounting for confounding variables. The primary outcome was of MASLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), while secondary outcomes included T2D, CKD and a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): sudden cardiac death, ischaemic heart disease (IHD), cerebrovascular accident (CVA), peripheral vascular disease (PVD) and heart failure (HF). Cox regression generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: After matching, 1735 patients remained in each group, with well-balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 42 vs. 41 years; standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.05; 52.6% vs. 54.3% male; SMD 0.03). After PSM, renal denervation was associated with a lower risk of MASLD (HR 0.38 [0.29, 0.51]), T2D (HR 0.21 [0.13, 0.33]), CKD (HR 0.26 [0.20, 0.35]), MACE (HR 0.46 [0.34, 0.62]), IHD (HR 0.56 [0.39, 0.80]), CVA (HR 0.33 [0.20, 0.52]) and HF (HR 0.39 [0.25, 0.62]).
CONCLUSION: Control of the sympathetic nervous system with renal denervation therapy in patients with resistant hypertension is associated with a lower risk of incident CKM syndrome including MASLD, T2D, CVD and CKD, supporting the role of autonomic dysfunction in the progression of cardiometabolic disease.
title: Reduced Risk of MASLD and Cardiometabolic Disease Following Renal Denervation Therapy in Patients With Resistant Hypertension.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are a key alternative to drug-eluting stents for coronary artery interventions, offering the advantage of drug delivery without permanent implants. Both paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs) and sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) are valuable treatment options. This systematic review and meta-analysis compare the efficacy and safety of sirolimus-coated versus paclitaxel-coated balloon catheters in patients with coronary artery disease.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines, searching five databases. We exclusively included RCTs. Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using fixed-effects or random-effects models, with sensitivity analysis performed in cases of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Eight trials involving 1043 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant difference between SCB and PCB for late lumen loss (MD 0.06, 95% CI [-0.02 to 0.14]). Only two outcomes showed statistically significant differences favoring PCB: reducing late lumen enlargement (RR 0.66, 95% CI [0.49-0.87], P = 0.004) and, after sensitivity analysis, lowering binary restenosis rates in de novo lesions CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis shows SCB and PCB have similar safety and efficacy in coronary artery interventions, with no significant differences in most outcomes. However, PCB outperforms late lumen enlargement and binary restenosis rates in de novo lesions. Similar outcomes across sirolimus formulations indicate other factors influence success. Both balloon types appear safe and effective, though PCB may retain certain advantages in specific scenarios. Larger, longer-term studies are needed to establish the optimal drug-coated balloon strategy for different patient populations.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.
title: Drug-coated balloons in coronary disease: meta-analysis comparing sirolimus- and paclitaxel-coated technologies.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the correlation between the cardiometabolic index (CMI), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and early risk stratification in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and to evaluate the predictive value of their combination for identifying intermediate- and high-risk patients.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 298 patients with ACS admitted to the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of South China University of Technology from March 2024 to December 2025. According to the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) score, patients were divided into low-risk (n=209), intermediate-risk (n=67), and high-risk (n=22) groups. Univariate analysis and multiple linear regression were used to explore the associations of CMI and NT-proBNP with early risk. Spearman correlation analysis was applied to examine the correlations of CMI and NT-proBNP with early risk. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess the predictive efficacy of CMI combined with NT-proBNP for intermediate- and high-risk patients.
RESULTS: Baseline data analysis showed that CMI and NT-proBNP levels in the high-risk group were significantly higher than those in the intermediate- and low-risk groups ( P < 0.001). Spearman correlation analysis indicated that CMI and NT-proBNP were positively correlated with early risk in ACS patients. Multiple linear regression models revealed that CMI and NT-proBNP were independent influencing factors for early risk. The ROC curve showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of CMI combined with NT-proBNP for identifying intermediate- and high-risk patients was 0.782 (95% CI: 0.718-0.847), with an optimal cut-off value of 0.3, a sensitivity of 74.2%, and a specificity of 83.7%.
CONCLUSION: CMI and NT-proBNP are positively correlated with early risk in ACS patients and serve as independent influencing factors. The combination of CMI and NT-proBNP demonstrates good predictive value for intermediate- and high-risk ACS patients.
title: Predictive value of cardiometabolic index combined with N-Terminal pro-B-Type natriuretic peptide for moderate- to high-risk patients with acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual mortality and heart-failure events remain common after aortic valve intervention for severe aortic stenosis. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes in heart-failure, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease populations, but their role following transcatheter or surgical aortic valve intervention remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, citation tracking, and manually identified eligible studies were screened through June 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing SGLT2i with usual care or no SGLT2i after aortic valve intervention. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251059332). Eligible populations included TAVR, SAVR, and bioprosthetic aortic valve evidence where available. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models while non-HR estimates and non-comparable endpoints were summarized narratively.
RESULTS: Twelve eligible reports were included, comprising one randomized trial and 11 observational studies. Most time-to-event estimates were reported from TAVR cohorts; two SAVR-only studies and one mixed bioprosthetic AVR study added complementary surgical and valve-durability data. In the pooled time-to-event analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60-0.79; I²=5%; p < 0.001). The study-defined composite clinical outcome was also lower (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.89; I²=57%; p = 0.005), although component definitions differed across studies. Estimates for heart-failure hospitalization or exacerbation, atrial fibrillation, and acute kidney injury were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i use after aortic valve intervention was associated with lower all-cause mortality in pooled time-to-event analysis. SAVR data were clinically informative but were not sufficiently homogeneous for separate quantitative pooling. Findings for composite, heart-failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes remain less certain. Dedicated randomized trials are needed to confirm whether the observed association reflects a treatment effect and to define patient selection, treatment timing, and peri-procedural safety.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of reports comprising one randomized trial and 11 observational studies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled estimates are almost entirely observational and prone to confounding by indication and immortal time.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review and meta-analysis of SGLT2 inhibitor use after aortic valve intervention, mostly observational data from TAVR cohorts.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60-0.79; I²=5%; p < 0.001). The study-defined composite clinical outcome was also lower (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.89; I²=57%; p = 0.005).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Identifies a plausible post-TAVI pharmacotherapy question that only a randomised trial can settle.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor therapy following aortic valve intervention for aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of mortality, heart failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes.
