abstract:
BACKGROUND: Until recently, no standard of care has been established for patients with symptomatic native aortic regurgitation (AR) who are unsuitable for surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has been explored in this setting using off-label, non-dedicated valves originally designed for aortic stenosis. The recent ALIGN-AR trial evaluated the Trilogy valve, a dedicated transcatheter device specifically designed for native AR.
METHODS: We performed an indirect comparison between the overall survival (OS) reported for the Trilogy valve in ALIGN-AR and OS from seven single-arm studies using non-dedicated valves. Individual patient data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves using the IPDfromKM method. To ensure homogeneity, the follow-up period for the survival analysis was truncated at 24 months. Survival was analyzed using both hazard ratios (HR) and restricted mean survival time (RMST).
RESULTS: The analysis included 492 patients treated with the Trilogy valve and 867 treated with non-dedicated valves. OS was significantly improved with the Trilogy valve (HR 0.399; 95% CI 0.275-0.578; p = 0.0000011). RMST at 12 months was 11.4 months for the Trilogy valve versus 10.4 months for non-dedicated valves, corresponding to an OS gain of 1.0 months (95% CI 0.72-1.32) over the first year.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with native AR undergoing TAVI, use of the dedicated Trilogy valve was associated with a highly significant survival advantage compared with non-dedicated devices, corresponding to an approximate 1-month gain in OS during the first 12 months after implantation.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Survival benefit in patients with native aortic regurgitation using a dedicated transcatherter valve vs non-dedicated transcatheter valves.
Right ventricular perforation caused by a pulmonary artery catheter under VA-ECMO support.

abstract: Precordial swirl sign may provide a clue to anterior myocardial ischemia in patients whose electrocardiograms do not meet conventional ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction criteria. A 75-year-old man with previous coronary stenting presented with worsening chest pain and an initially negative troponin result. His admission electrocardiogram showed focal ST-segment elevation in V1, a hyperacute T wave in V2, and reciprocal ST-segment depression in V5-V6. Subsequent anterior Twave inversion and troponin elevation supported an ischemic interpretation. Coronary angiography revealed approximately 90% proximal left anterior descending coronary artery in-stent restenosis with TIMI 2 flow. Balloon angioplasty followed by drug-coated balloon treatment restored TIMI 3 flow. This case illustrates the importance of interpreting opposing precordial ST-T changes in relation to the ischemic vector rather than considering ST-segment elevation thresholds alone. Recognition of this pattern may prompt serial electrocardiography, repeat biomarker testing, and timely assessment for coronary intervention.
journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
title: Precordial Swirl Sign: A Subtle ECG Clue Unmasking Anterior Myocardial Ischemia.

abstract: High-pressure drug-coated balloon (HP@DCB) angioplasty enhances vascular drug delivery by overcoming the limitations of passive diffusion-based conventional noncompliant DCB (NC@DCB) systems. We developed a dual-layer HP balloon catheter composed of an outer Nylon 12 layer and an inner Pebax 7233 layer, and evaluated its feasibility and therapeutic efficacy as a paclitaxel (PTX)-coated platform. Shellac-based PTX coating was uniformly applied to HP@DCB and NC@DCB, and coating thickness, drug amount, release behavior, and mechanical properties were compared. Pressure-assisted drug penetration was assessed in a vascular-mimicking agarose gel phantom using fluorescent PTX and confocal microscopy. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in a balloon injury-induced rabbit iliac artery stenosis model using angiography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), histology, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence examinations. Drug amount, coating thickness, and sustained drug release did not differ between groups. The mechanical robustness in HP@DCB was significantly greater than that in NC@DCB. HP@DCB produced significantly greater penetration depth and fluorescence-positive area, indicating enhanced pressure-assisted drug transfer. HP@DCB resulted in superior luminal patency, reduced neointimal hyperplasia, and favorable biological responses compared with that in NC@DCB and the sham control. These findings support DCB use based on a dual-layered HP balloon platform as a promising next-generation strategy for stenotic vascular lesion treatment.
title: Pressure-Assisted Drug Delivery Using High-Pressure Balloon Platform Improves Vascular Drug Penetration and Anti-Restenotic Effects.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides complementary anatomical, inflammatory, calcific, and functional biomarkers, but their interpretation under chronic high-altitude exposure remains uncertain. We characterized CCTA phenotypes according to altitude and type 2 diabetes and explored associations with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This retrospective matched cohort with prospective outcome ascertainment included adults undergoing clinically indicated CCTA for suspected coronary artery disease. Participants were classified by high-altitude residence (≥2,500 m for ≥5 years) or low-altitude residence (<500 m) and by diabetes status, forming four groups. Propensity score matching was performed separately within diabetes strata using age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension, yielding 174 participants in 87 matched pairs. CCTA assessment included pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation, plaque characteristics, coronary artery calcium (CAC), coronary stenosis, and vessel-specific CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR). Primary models evaluated altitude, diabetes, and their interaction with adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension. Associations with MACE were explored using univariable Cox models among participants with follow-up.
RESULTS: In primary covariate-adjusted analyses, diabetes was associated with higher PCAT attenuation, CAC, total plaque volume, plaque burden, and maximum stenosis and with lower left anterior descending (LAD) CT-FFR (all q ≤ 0.018). Compared with the low-altitude Han group, the high-altitude Tibetan group had higher LAD and right coronary artery CT-FFR and lower CAC and plaque burden (all q ≤ 0.037). Among 13 interaction tests, only the altitude × diabetes interaction for LAD-PCAT remained significant after false discovery rate correction (-6.62 HU; 95% CI, -10.32 to -2.91; raw P < 0.001; q = 0.008). Among 119 participants with follow-up, 20 MACE occurred over a median of 28 months. Exploratory univariable analyses showed large but imprecise associations of diabetes and high-risk plaque with MACE, whereas altitude was not statistically associated with MACE (P = 0.557).
CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with a more adverse coronary CCTA phenotype, whereas the high-altitude Tibetan group showed lower CAC and plaque burden and higher vessel-specific CT-FFR than the low-altitude Han group. The association between diabetes and LAD-PCAT attenuation differed between these groups. These findings warrant validation in larger, ethnically comparable longitudinal cohorts.
title: Comprehensive coronary computed tomography angiography assessment in high-altitude diabetic populations: integrating plaque characteristics, pericoronary inflammation, and coronary function.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kounis syndrome manifests as an acute coronary syndrome induced by an allergic or hypersensitivity reaction. Kounis syndrome consists of three types: Type I is characterized by coronary artery spasm in normal or near-normal arteries, Type II by the rupture of coronary artery plaques, and Type III by the formation of thrombus within the coronary artery stent. Recurrent episodes of Kounis syndrome are uncommon in clinical practice. We herein report a case of recurrent Kounis syndrome, in which the second episode presented as Type III Kounis syndrome.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a patient who experienced two acute coronary events triggered by Kounis syndrome within approximately one month-an uncommon presentation. One episode manifested as chest pain accompanied by tongue swelling, and was diagnosed as Type II Kounis syndrome and treated with cetirizine for anti-allergic purposes. The second episode occurred about one month later with persistent chest pain and recurrent tongue swelling, and coronary angiography confirmed acute coronary stent thrombosis. Taken together with the allergic manifestation (tongue swelling) accompanying both events, the second episode fulfilled the criteria for Type III Kounis syndrome. Subsequently, we performed emergency procedures to open the blocked coronary artery and administered glucocorticoid therapy. The patient's symptoms improved.
CONCLUSION: Despite antihistamine therapy with cetirizine in the first episode, this patient still developed subsequent stent-related thrombosis. This case highlights that combined anti-allergic therapy including glucocorticoids may be considered at an early stage for Kounis syndrome patients with unidentified allergens, to mitigate potential allergic-mediated cardiac risk. Nevertheless, we cannot conclude glucocorticoids definitely prevent stent thrombosis, as avoidance of unrecognized allergens may also contribute to clinical improvement.
title: Case Report: Recurrent Kounis syndrome complicated with acute coronary stent thrombosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The platelet-to-hemoglobin ratio (PHR) is a proposed prognostic marker in cardiovascular disease, but it has not been evaluated against a broad major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) endpoint in a dedicated percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) cohort, and whether it adequately summarizes its two components remains untested.
METHODS: We analyzed 1,551 patients pooled from two prospective Korean drug-eluting stent registries (2016-2022). The PHR was calculated as platelet count (×10⁹/L) divided by hemoglobin (g/L). The primary endpoint was 1-year MACE, with follow-up censored at 365 days, a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, repeat revascularization, or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox models included eight prespecified clinical covariates; the functional form was examined with restricted cubic splines, and the PHR was decomposed using nested models and a log-scale ratio-constraint test.
RESULTS: MACE occurred in 107 patients (6.9%) within 1 year. A higher PHR was independently associated with MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1-standard deviation, 1.21; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.40; P = 0.008), with no evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.700). Adding the PHR improved the clinical model (likelihood-ratio P = 0.013); the ratio constraint was not rejected (P = 0.765), and a single log-PHR term retained 98.7% of the two-component likelihood-ratio χ 2 increment over the clinical model in this cohort (bootstrap 95% CI, 21.8%-100%). The PHR was associated with all-cause and cardiovascular death (both HR, 1.28), paralleling hemoglobin. Repeat revascularization was associated with platelet count (HR, 1.39; P = 0.014), but not significantly with PHR (HR, 1.24; P = 0.081). Risk was concentrated in patients with both anemia and a platelet count at or above the median (adjusted HR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.05-3.15). The gain in discrimination was negligible (ΔAUC, +0.003; 95% CI, -0.003 to +0.012), and net benefit was virtually unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: The admission PHR was independently associated with 1-year MACE after PCI, with no evidence of nonlinearity, and its log-scale component effects were compatible with the ratio constraint in this cohort. Given the negligible gain in discrimination and net benefit, the PHR is an independent prognostic marker rather than a tool for risk reclassification.Registry registration: Clinical Research Information Service KCT0003392 and KCT0005008.
title: Admission platelet-to-hemoglobin ratio and 1-year outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention: a multicenter registry cohort study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between rivaroxaban combined with clopidogrel therapy and thrombotic risk, platelet activation, myocardial injury biomarkers, and clinical outcomes in patients with coronary artery ectasia (CAE).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 158 consecutive patients with CAE diagnosed by coronary angiography between June 2023 and June 2025. Patients receiving clopidogrel alone or rivaroxaban plus clopidogrel were compared. A 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching method was applied, generating 70 matched pairs. Thrombotic risk markers, including D-dimer (D-D), thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT), and von Willebrand factor (vWF), platelet activation parameters [ADP-induced platelet aggregation rate (ADP-PAg) and CD62P], thromboelastography parameters [maximum amplitude (MA) and reaction time (R)], and myocardial injury-related biomarkers [high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP)] were evaluated at baseline and 6 months. Clinical outcomes, including thrombotic-related adverse cardiovascular events and bleeding events, were recorded during 12 months of follow-up.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. At 6 months, patients receiving rivaroxaban plus clopidogrel showed lower levels of D-D, TAT, vWF, ADP-PAg, CD62P, MA, hs-cTnT, CK-MB, H-FABP, and NT-proBNP, as well as prolonged R values, compared with those receiving clopidogrel alone (all P < 0.05). During follow-up, thrombotic-related adverse cardiovascular events occurred less frequently in the combination therapy group than in the clopidogrel group (7.14% vs. 20.00%, P = 0.027). Minor bleeding events were numerically higher in the combination therapy group (17.14% vs. 10.00%, P = 0.218), while no intracranial or fatal bleeding events occurred.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with CAE, rivaroxaban combined with clopidogrel was associated with more favorable changes in coagulation activation, platelet activity, myocardial injury biomarkers, and thrombotic-related clinical outcomes compared with clopidogrel alone. These findings suggest that combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy may represent a potential strategy for selected high-risk patients with CAE. Further multicenter prospective studies are required to confirm these observations.
title: Effects of rivaroxaban combined with clopidogrel on thrombotic risk and myocardial injury indicators in patients with coronary artery ectasia.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) addresses valvular obstruction but leaves concomitant ascending aortic dilatation untreated. Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, n = 87; TAV, n = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR. Annualized aortic expansion rates were evaluated utilizing linear mixed-effects models derived from serial computed tomography angiography over a median 27.0-month follow-up.
RESULTS: No ascending aortic dissection, rupture, or elective aortic interventions occurred during follow-up. The adjusted annualized expansion rate at the mid-ascending aorta was low and comparable between the BAV and TAV cohorts (0.43 vs. 0.39 mm/year; interaction P = 0.364). Progression rates at the distal ascending aorta and sinuses of Valsalva similarly demonstrated no significant morphological differences. No patient exhibited rapid progression (>5 mm/year). Although moderate or greater paravalvular leakage occurred exclusively in BAV patients (4.8% vs. 0.0%; P = 0.043), its overall incidence was low (2.2%); however, the extremely small number of cases precluded a definitive statistical assessment of its impact on longitudinal aortic expansion.
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are maintained.
title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves.

abstract:
AIMS: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic valve stenosis, but its effects on coronary physiology remain incompletely understood. CT-derived quantitative flow ratio (CT-QFR) enables non-invasive assessment of coronary physiology. This study aimed to investigate the early changes in CT-QFR following TAVR.
METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography before and within 7 days after TAVR. CT-QFR was calculated for all analyzable coronary vessels. Longitudinal changes in CT-QFR were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with patient identifier as a random effect.
RESULTS: A total of 109 patients (324 coronary vessels) were analyzed. Plaque volume, plaque burden, and minimal lumen diameter remained unchanged after TAVR, whereas transvalvular pressure gradients decreased significantly. Overall, CT-QFR increased modestly following TAVR (β=0.018, P < 0.001). Significant increases were observed in the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries, whereas no significant change was detected in the left circumflex artery. Vessels with baseline %DS ≥50% demonstrated greater CT-QFR increases than those with less severe stenosis (interaction β=0.104, P < 0.001). Likewise, vessels with baseline CT-QFR <0.80 showed significantly larger post-TAVR increases than vessels with baseline CT-QFR ≥0.80 (interaction β=0.117, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: TAVR was associated with modest early increases in CT-QFR, particularly in vessels with greater anatomical stenosis or baseline physiological impairment. These findings suggest that coronary physiological assessment in severe aortic stenosis may be influenced by valve intervention and should be interpreted cautiously during the peri-TAVR period.
title: Early changes in CT-derived quantitative flow ratio after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a serial coronary physiological assessment.

abstract:
CASE SUMMARY: A 2.5-year-old, intact female British Shorthair cat was referred for cardiology evaluation owing to intermittent panting and a heart murmur identified on cardiac auscultation before elective surgery. Physical examination revealed a left parasternal grade II/VI systolic murmur without arrhythmia. Thoracic radiographs showed cardiomegaly without pulmonary infiltration. The echocardiography was prompted by auscultation, history and radiological findings. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated marked right atrial enlargement and eccentric hypertrophy of the right ventricle. Echocardiography revealed a partial atrioventricular septal defect characterised by a large ostium primum defect (0.79 cm) and an anterior mitral valve cleft, resulting in a left-to-right shunt (estimated Qp:Qs ≈ 2.2). Doppler interrogation of the left pulmonary vein entering the lateral wall of the left atrium demonstrated focal turbulence and increased peak velocity (1.08 m/s), corresponding to a pressure gradient of approximately 4.7 mmHg, findings consistent with suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. Tricuspid regurgitation velocity (2.2 m/s) did not reflect increased afterload. Elective surgery was postponed owing to uncertainty regarding peri-anaesthetic haemodynamic risk. Medical treatment with enalapril and clopidogrel was initiated. At the 9-month follow-up, the cat remained clinically stable and echocardiographic findings were unchanged.
RELEVANCE AND NOVEL INFORMATION: Pulmonary vein stenosis is rarely reported in cats. This report describes the concurrent presence of partial atrioventricular septal defect and suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. These findings highlight the detection of a congenital heart defect in a young cat, despite the low-grade murmur.
title: Echocardiographic description of pulmonary vein stenosis in a cat with atrioventricular septal defect.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Contrast media (CM) can potentially cause nephropathy. Trans-sodium crocetinate (TSC) has shown promising antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties in animal studies. This research sought to assess TSC efficacy in contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) prevention.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A randomized triple-blind trial involving 130 patients undergoing elective PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) was conducted. Participants received either TSC (0.5 mg/kg) before the procedure, followed by crocetin tablets thrice daily for five days to evaluate its impact on CIN occurrence, or a placebo. The primary outcome was the occurrence of CIN, with secondary outcomes including blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine (SCr), glomerular filtration rate (GFR), C-reactive protein (CRP), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), and prooxidant-antioxidant balance (PAB) test in a 5-day follow-up.
RESULTS: The study's primary outcome revealed a significantly lower CIN prevalence in the TSC group (7.7%) compared to the placebo group (24.6%) (p = 0.009). Secondary outcomes showing significant inter-group differences included BUN (p<0.001), GFR (p<0.05), CRP (p<0.001), ACR (p<0.05), and PAB test (p<0.05). However, SCr and adverse effects did not differ significantly between the groups.
CONCLUSION: TSC demonstrated its ability to impede nephrotoxic processes and significantly reduce CIN incidence. Additional clinical studies are required to further validate the beneficial effects in this context.
title: Evaluation of the preventive effect of intravenous trans-sodium crocetinate followed by oral crocetin on contrast-induced nephropathy in patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing coronary angioplasty: A randomized placebo-controlled triple-blind clinical trial.

abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the preferred therapy for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, but rare cases of pharmacokinetic resistance have been described, and objective biological confirmation remains scarce in the literature. We report the case of a man who experienced three ischemic strokes between the ages of 57 and 60 over a four-year period. The first episode, of cryptogenic origin, was attributed to a patent foramen ovale (PFO) associated with an interatrial septal aneurysm, leading to percutaneous closure. The recurrence led to a diagnosis of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation via an implantable cardiac monitor. Despite treatment with dabigatran 150 mg twice daily, a third stroke occurred. Pharmacokinetic treatment failure was documented by anti-IIa chromogenic testing, which had dropped to a residual level below 15 ng/mL despite supervised administration, adequate renal function, and no identified drug interactions. Switching to apixaban resulted in satisfactory on-therapy levels from Day 3. This case illustrates the value of prolonged rhythm monitoring after PFO closure and demonstrates apparent pharmacokinetic treatment failure with dabigatran, objectively confirmed by anti-IIa activity testing. Pharmacokinetically guided DOAC switching should be considered when recurrent ischemic events occur despite apparently adequate anticoagulation.
title: Recurrent Ischemic Stroke Despite Dabigatran Therapy: Unexpectedly Low Anti-IIa Activity Revealing Pharmacokinetic Treatment Failure.

abstract: Neurosyphilis is a rare but readily treatable cause of status epilepticus (SE). Nevertheless, SE has a substantial morbidity and mortality if treatment is refractory and/or life-threatening complications occur. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) has previously been successfully employed following life- threatening arrhythmias with refractory circulatory failure due to antiseizure medications (ASM) in the context of SE. Here we describe the combined use of VA-ECMO along with an Impella CP® micro-axial pump to provide full circulatory support and left ventricular unloading in a patient with a presumed drug-induced, refractory cardiac arrest amidst treatment for super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE). This patient presented with a recurrent episode of convulsive SE with subsequent treatment-refractory nonconvulsive seizure activity on incremental ASM therapy. Investigations consistent with neurosyphilis prompted the initiation of antimicrobial therapy. ASM adjustments were made in view of suspected lacoseamide-induced arrhythmias, but subsequently a treatment-refractory cardiac arrest occurred with ensuing pulseless electrical activity and asystole. Mechanical life support followed by VA-ECMO was promptly initiated and an Impella CP® device was then placed given a non-ejecting heart. Subsequently, hemodynamic stabilization and seizure control were readily achieved and full cardiac recovery occurred after seven days. VA-ECMO plus Impella® provided effective circulatory support under which seizure control could be achieved and cardiac function recovered. Increased pro-arrhythmic risks due to possible synergistic inhibition of cardiac ionic channels need to be anticipated when multiple ASM and anesthetic agents are introduced during SE treatment. Neurosyphilis needs to always be considered as a rare cause of SE.
title: Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus (SRSE) Secondary to Neurosyphilis Complicated by a Prolonged Drug-Induced Cardiac Arrest Successfully Bridged With Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) and Impella®: A Case Report.

abstract: Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly time-sensitive cardiovascular emergency in which mechanical obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) by a prolapsing intimo-intimal intussusception flap represents a rare and often fatal complication, producing severe hemodynamic compromise that may be refractory to conventional resuscitative measures. We report a 26-year-old woman with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome who was transferred for evaluation of a large proximal type A aortic dissection and suffered a witnessed cardiac arrest shortly after arrival. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated a dissection flap prolapsing into the subvalvular LVOT during diastole, disrupting aortic valve coaptation and causing aortic insufficiency (AI), while moving anterograde during systole to obstruct forward flow. Despite transient return of spontaneous circulation, resuscitation ultimately failed, and veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was not pursued because of the underlying aortic dissection, AI, prolonged resuscitation, and concern for hypoxic-ischemic brain injury. This case highlights the diagnostic value of real-time TEE in identifying structural causes of cardiac arrest. This case also illustrates the hemodynamic consequences of a rare and often fatal complication of aortic dissection.
title: Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction From Proximal Intimo-Intimal Intussusception: A Fatal Complication of Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in coronary artery disease (CAD), but the relationship between mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) and mitochondrial homeostasis across CAD presentations remains unclear. We investigated mtDNA-CN together with the expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α and TFAM) and mitophagy (PINK1) in patients with stable angina (SA) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: This observational study included 334 patients: 170 ACS, 117 SA and 47 individuals with non-obstructive coronary arteries (NCA). Peripheral blood mtDNA-CN and the expression of PGC-1α, TFAM and PINK1 were quantified by real-time PCR. Associations with clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were evaluated.
RESULTS: ACS patients exhibited significantly lower mtDNA-CN than SA and NCA groups (p = 0.01 and p = 0.004, respectively). PINK1 expression was reduced in both ACS (p = 0.005) and SA (p = 0.01) compared with NCA. TFAM expression was increased in SA (p = 0.009), while PGC-1α expression was higher in ACS (p = 0.02). MtDNA-CN and mitochondrial biomarkers were inversely associated with inflammatory markers, whereas mtDNA-CN and TFAM correlated positively with LVEF. Lower mtDNA-CN was independently associated with ACS (OR = 0.98, p = 0.0004) and SA (OR = 0.99, p = 0.04), while higher PINK1 expression was associated with reduced odds of SA (p = 0.03) and ACS (p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Mitochondrial markers are altered across CAD phenotypes. ACS is characterized by lower mtDNA-CN and altered expression of mitochondrial homeostasis-related genes, whereas SA shows a pattern consistent with a possible compensatory response. Combined assessment of mtDNA-CN and mitochondrial homeostasis-related gene expression may provide a novel biomarker strategy for CAD risk stratification and targeted therapies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: VICTORIA study, (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06313645).
title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number and Mitochondrial Homeostasis Genes in Acute and Stable Coronary Artery Disease.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) Index has shown prognostic value in cardiovascular diseases, but its role in heart transplantation (HTx) and the impact of dynamic preoperative changes remain unclear. This study evaluated the prognostic value of preoperative FIB-4 for mortality after HTx and investigated whether dynamic changes in FIB-4 before transplantation are associated with post-transplant survival.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 791 adult patients who underwent orthotopic HTx between January 2015 and December 2024, with follow-up through June 2025. Patients were stratified by preoperative FIB-4 into low (<1.30), intermediate (1.30-2.67), and high (>2.67) risk groups. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Analyses employed Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and five machine learning survival models, including Random Survival Forest (RSF).
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 28.8 months, 218 patients (27.6%) died. Preoperative FIB-4 showed a non-linear association with mortality (inflection point: 2.03) and was an independent predictor of death [hazard ratio (HR) per unit increase, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.02-1.07; P < .001]. In the RSF model, FIB-4 was the most important prognostic variable (Variable Importance = 0.068), outperforming traditional donor and surgical factors. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that FIB-4's prognostic value was independent of age (interaction P = .745) and superior to its individual components (aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and platelet count). Correlation analyses showed no significant association between FIB-4 and invasive haemodynamic parameters, tricuspid regurgitation severity, or MELD/MELD-XI scores, supporting its distinction from haemodynamic congestion. Among high-risk patients (n = 153), preoperative improvement in FIB-4 category was associated with significantly lower mortality (adjusted HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.29-0.82; P = .007). Preoperative use of glutathione was independently associated with FIB-4 improvement [odds ratios (OR), 1.50; 95% CI, 1.01-2.22; P = .04].
CONCLUSION: Preoperative FIB-4 is a robust and independent predictor of post-transplant mortality, with greater predictive importance than traditional surgical risk factors. Dynamic improvement in FIB-4 before transplantation is associated with better survival. Integrating FIB-4 into routine preoperative assessment may refine risk stratification and guide pre-transplant management.
title: Prognostic value of Fibrosis-4 Index and preoperative dynamic changes in heart transplantation.

abstract: Chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexist, yet prognostic evidence for patients with both conditions remains limited. This retrospective cohort study evaluated factors associated with one-year adverse clinical outcomes and developed a clinical risk score in 214 hospitalized patients with CCS and concomitant COPD. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were collected, and patients were followed for one year. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), rehospitalization for heart failure (HF), or rehospitalization for acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) within one year. Independent prognostic factors were identified using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Model performance was evaluated through discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap internal validation. During follow-up, 53 patients (24.8%) experienced the composite endpoint, including 7 all-cause deaths (3.3%), 8 non-fatal MIs (3.7%), 17 HF-related rehospitalizations (7.9%), and 21 AECOPD-related rehospitalizations (9.8%). Smoking history (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.962, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.093-3.521, P = 0.024), previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (HR = 2.017, 95% CI: 1.157-3.517, P = 0.013), higher Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) grade (HR = 1.488, 95% CI: 1.092-2.028, P = 0.012), and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (HR = 0.933, 95% CI: 0.893-0.975, P = 0.002) were independently associated with the composite endpoint. The model demonstrated a concordance index (C-index) of 0.736 and a one-year area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.773. Event-free survival differed significantly among the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (log-rank P < 0.001). These findings support integrated cardiovascular and respiratory risk assessment in patients with CCS and COPD. However, external validation is required before the risk score can be recommended for broader clinical application.
first_author_country: Affiliated Hospital of Inner Mongolia Minzu University
title: Prognostic Factors for One-Year Adverse Outcomes in Chronic Coronary Syndrome with Concomitant Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiac myxomas are the most common benign primary cardiac tumours and embolise, causing stroke, acute coronary syndrome, limb ischaemia, and visceral infarction. Although previous reviews examined clinical features and embolic risk factors, the frequency, anatomical distribution, management, and outcomes of myxoma-related embolisation have not been comprehensively synthesised.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, and PubMed from inception to February 2026 for observational studies reporting embolic complications of confirmed cardiac myxoma; small (≤10-patient) and pre-2000 case series were excluded. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions estimated patient-level embolic prevalence and event-level anatomical distribution.
RESULTS: Across 47 studies (4,964 patients), pooled embolic prevalence was 19.7% (95% CI 16.7-23.1; I²=75.4%, 95% CI 62.8-87.5). Cerebral events predominated (75.6%), followed by peripheral limb (17.0%). Pooled early mortality was 1.9% (95% CI 1.3-2.7). Villous morphology and high tumour mobility were more associated with embolisation than size. Recurrence was uncommon (crude rate 2.0%) and mainly in familial disease or Carney complex.
CONCLUSION: Embolism is common and predominantly cerebral. Villous surface and tumour mobility were more consistently associated with embolisation than size and may inform the urgency of resection. However, evidence is retrospective; the optimal timing after embolic presentation remains undefined, and prospective validation is required.
title: Embolic complications of cardiac myxoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of frequency, clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution and outcomes in contemporary cohorts.

journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
title: Concomitant Balloon-in-Basket Pulsed Field Ablation and Next-Generation Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Acute Procedural Success and Early Safety and Effectiveness results from the Prospective Multicenter CLEAR Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance measured during acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may reflect pre-existing metabolic vulnerability as well as the response to acute illness. We examined its association with cardiovascular complications arising during the index hospitalization in patients with ACS and no known diabetes.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort, 252 patients with ACS and an admission HbA1c <6.5% had fasting glucose and insulin measured 24-48 hours after admission. Insulin resistance was defined by a HOMA2-IR threshold of ≥1.35 prespecified from independent healthy controls. The composite MACE outcome comprised five prespecified complications occurring between sampling and discharge or death. Logistic and modified Poisson regression were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking, and hypertension.
RESULTS: Insulin resistance was present in 137 patients (54.4%), and the composite MACE occurred in 57 (22.6%): 28.5% with versus 15.7% without insulin resistance; risk difference 12.8 percentage points (95% CI 2.5-22.6). Insulin resistance was associated with the composite (adjusted OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.55-6.14; adjusted RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.39-3.75); each doubling of HOMA2-IR was associated with higher odds (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.09-1.99). The association persisted after GRACE adjustment (adjusted OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06) and was attenuated after adding left ventricular ejection fraction, a possible mediator (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 0.97-5.22). Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, or pulmonary edema accounted for 53 of the 57 events.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR-defined insulin resistance was associated with cardiovascular complications during the index hospitalization, mainly heart-failure-related events. These findings are associational and require confirmation in multicenter cohorts.
keywords: Acute coronary syndrome; acute heart failure; association; HOMA2-IR; in-hospital cardiovascular complications; insulin resistance
title: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR and in-hospital cardiovascular complications in patients with acute coronary syndrome without known diabetes.

abstract:
AIMS: Despite continuous improvements in diagnostic tools, the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is still based on electrocardiogram (ECG) and cardiac biomarkers supported by other non-invasive imaging techniques. However, ECG has limited sensitivity, while high-sensitivity troponin assays may show reduced specificity, particularly in older or multimorbid patients. Widely adopted clinical pathways (e.g. ESC 0/1 h algorithm) have reported high diagnostic discrimination in external cohorts (with AUC ranging from 0.93 to 0.96) which provides clinical context for interpreting our findings. These diagnostic tests have limitations that can be addressed through automated computer-based diagnostic systems using Artificial Intelligence (AI). Several studies in the literature have presented machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) models to quickly and accurately assess the diagnosis of AMI to optimize treatment.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The aim of our analysis was to evaluate the performance of AI-based models for the diagnosis of AMI using data from all validation and test cohorts available in literature. Sensitivity and specificity for all MIs, and for STEMI and NSTEMI separately, were analysed for different types of AI approach (non-DL or DL) and for different data sources (ECG or troponin-based). Hierarchical models were used to estimate the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity and specificity.A total of 24 studies evaluating 27 AI-based diagnostic algorithms were included encompassing 166.052 patients, of which 18.850 (11.3%) had a final diagnosis of AMI. Patients were predominantly male (61.8%) with a median age of 60.7 (IQR 59.0-64.1) years. Discrimination of AI-based algorithms for the diagnosis of AMI was high with an AUC of 0.97 (sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.92). This result remained consistent when considering the ability to diagnose STEMI (AUC 0.96, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.94) or NSTEMI (AUC 0.97, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.90) separately. No significant difference was found regarding type of AI. ECG and troponin-based models were both extremely accurate, with the first ones being less sensitive and the latter less specific.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based diagnostic algorithms for AMI diagnosis were associated with particularly efficient performance. These results were consistent for both STEMI and NSTEMI considered separately. Rather than replacing conventional diagnostic pathways, AI has the potential to enhance existing tools by identifying subtle ECG features and integrating multiple data streams. While direct head-to-head comparisons with traditional statistical models are currently limited, future prospective studies evaluating AI and conventional approaches within the same clinical populations are warranted.AI did not lose accuracy depending on the data source or the type of AI applied.
title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for severely calcified coronary lesions remains technically challenging. Although the combination of atherectomy and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has demonstrated favorable outcomes before drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, it remains unclear whether a stepwise calcium modification strategy using atherectomy followed by IVL can achieve sufficient lesion preparation to enable a stent-less strategy using drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty.
CASE SUMMARY: An 83-year-old woman presented with exertional angina despite optimal medical therapy. Coronary angiography revealed severe calcified stenosis in the proximal left anterior descending artery. Pre-procedural optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated thick circumferential calcification, indicating a high risk of inadequate balloon expansion. Orbital atherectomy (OA) was initially performed and achieved partial superficial calcium modification; however, extensive residual calcification remained (post-OA OCT calcium score of 4). Consequently, additional lesion preparation using IVL was performed, delivering 80 pulses via a 2.5-mm IVL balloon, which successfully created multiple calcium fractures and improved vessel compliance. Post-IVL angiography demonstrated residual stenosis <30% with thrombolysis in myocardial infarction grade 3 flow, and fractional flow reserve was 0.92, supporting the decision to avoid DES implantation. Two paclitaxel-coated balloons were subsequently inflated, resulting in an excellent angiographic and OCT outcome without procedural complications. Follow-up coronary angiography and OCT at 17 months demonstrated sustained vessel patency without restenosis, and the patient remained asymptomatic.
CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the feasibility of a stepwise, OCT-guided stent-less PCI strategy using sequential OA, IVL, and DCB angioplasty for a severely calcified coronary lesion. The complementary calcium-modification mechanisms of OA and IVL achieved effective lesion preparation, enabling safe deferral of stent implantation and successful DCB angioplasty. Favorable angiographic, OCT, and clinical outcomes at 17 months suggest that this stepwise approach may represent a promising treatment strategy for carefully selected patients with severely calcified coronary lesions and warrants further evaluation in larger clinical studies.
title: Stent-less percutaneous coronary intervention for a severely calcified coronary lesion using combined orbital atherectomy and intravascular lithotripsy followed by drug-coated balloon: case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe stenosis at the terminal bifurcation of the brachiocephalic trunk involving the origins of the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery is a rare and highly challenging lesion of the supra-aortic vessels. Endovascular intervention carries a high risk of embolization and difficulty in delivering large-diameter stents.
CASE SUMMARY: We report a 60-year-old male patient who presented with intermittent dizziness and asymmetric blood pressure in the upper limbs. Color Doppler ultrasound and head and neck CT angiography revealed severe stenosis at the terminal bifurcation of the brachiocephalic trunk (stenosis rate approximately 90%), with the lesion involving the origins of the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery, accompanied by right subclavian artery steal phenomenon. The patient underwent brachiocephalic trunk balloon angioplasty and stenting via a single femoral artery access. An embolic protection device was deployed in the C1 segment of the right internal carotid artery for distal cerebral protection. During delivery of the stent, the filter guidewire provided insufficient support; a second guidewire was added as a buddy wire to establish a dual-guidewire rail technique, facilitating successful stent placement. Debris was observed in the retrieved filter. Postoperatively, the severe stenosis was relieved and the steal phenomenon resolved. At 1.5 years of follow-up, the patient reported no recurrence of dizziness, and the inter-arm blood pressure difference remained within the normal range.
CONCLUSION: In this selected case with clear antegrade flow direction, a single-access, single-filter strategy appeared feasible and may offer a simplified alternative for similar anatomical presentations. However, further validation in larger case series is warranted. The application of dual-guidewire rail technique to overcome difficulties in large-diameter stent delivery during brachiocephalic trunk intervention has been rarely reported.
title: Dual-guidewire technique with cerebral embolic protection for brachiocephalic trunk bifurcation stenosis: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) reflect complementary dimensions of ventricular stress and systolic function. Whether the NT-proBNP/LVEF ratio is consistently associated with angiographic coronary disease burden in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), and whether its predictive contribution is robust across conventional and machine-learning approaches, remains uncertain.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 375 patients with AMI who underwent coronary angiography. The continuous Gensini score was the primary outcome, while clinically anchored anatomical outcomes, including multivessel disease and high-burden coronary anatomy, served as sensitivity outcomes. Associations between log-transformed NT-proBNP/LVEF and Gensini score were assessed using multivariable median regression. Direct discrimination of NT-proBNP/LVEF versus NT-proBNP alone was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and paired DeLong testing; the incremental information provided by adding LVEF to NT-proBNP was additionally assessed using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Six multivariable models-logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and CatBoost-were internally validated using leakage-controlled repeated fivefold cross-validation with five repeats. Calibration, decision curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP)-based model interpretation were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Higher NT-proBNP/LVEF was consistently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden. In the fully adjusted model, each doubling of NT-proBNP/LVEF was associated with a 12.20-point increase in median Gensini score (95% confidence interval [CI], 9.33-15.07; P < 0.001). Comparable associations were observed for high-burden anatomy (odds ratio [OR] per doubling, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.44-1.97) and multivessel disease (OR per doubling, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.36-1.84). For the secondary high-Gensini-burden outcome, NT-proBNP/LVEF and NT-proBNP showed comparable discrimination (AUC, 0.783 vs. 0.780; ΔAUC = 0.004; P = 0.362). Adding LVEF to NT-proBNP did not show clear incremental improvement by NRI or IDI. Among the six multivariable models, SVM yielded the numerically highest AUC (0.763; 95% CI, 0.715-0.811), but no pairwise AUC difference remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. XGBoost and CatBoost showed highly concordant SHAP importance rankings (Spearman ρ = 0.978), with NT-proBNP/LVEF ranked first in both models.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher NT-proBNP/LVEF was consistently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden across the continuous Gensini score and clinically anchored anatomical outcomes in patients with AMI. The ratio provides a parsimonious representation of ventricular stress and systolic function and showed stable predictive importance across the two boosting algorithms examined. Its discriminative performance was comparable, rather than superior, to that of NT-proBNP alone, supporting its potential role as a readily available adjunctive marker of coronary disease burden rather than a replacement for established clinical assessment.
title: Association of NT-proBNP/LVEF with angiographic coronary disease burden in acute myocardial infarction: a retrospective study with machine learning analyses.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The growing number of nonagenarian patients with severe aortic stenosis has increased interest in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in this population. However, data on long-term outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate long-term survival and procedural outcomes of TAVI in nonagenarians and to explore clinical factors associated with long-term mortality.
METHODS: We conducted an ambispective multicenter observational cohort study including patients aged ≥90 years who underwent TAVI for severe aortic stenosis between 2013 and 2021 at six centers in the Emilia-Romagna region, Italy. Baseline and procedural data were collected retrospectively, while outcome ascertainment combined prospective follow-up contacts with retrospective verification of dates of death or last confirmed vital status. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and associations with mortality were examined using an exploratory Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 60 nonagenarian patients (mean age 91 ± 1.5 years; 67% female) were included. Procedural success was achieved in 97% of cases. In-hospital mortality was 5%, and 30-day mortality was 8.3%. Over a mean observation period of 5.7 years from TAVI to death or the last confirmed vital-status assessment, the Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 35%. In the exploratory multivariable analysis, male sex and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were associated with higher long-term mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients aged ≥90 years selected by the Heart Team for TAVI, the Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 35%. The procedure demonstrated a high success rate and an acceptable safety profile. Male sex and COPD showed an exploratory association with worse prognosis. These findings suggest that TAVI may be a feasible option in carefully selected nonagenarians when guided by comprehensive clinical assessment and individualized decision-making.
title: Long-term survival after transcatheter aortic valve implantation in nonagenarian patients: a multicenter real-world study.

abstract: Artificial intelligence symptom checkers are used by hundreds of millions of people annually as first-line triage tools, and their outputs may influence whether and how quickly a person seeks emergency care. We conducted a structured, exploratory audit of three widely used platforms, Ada Health, Isabel Healthcare, and Docus AI, across four standardized clinical vignettes [acute coronary syndrome (ACS) with chest pressure, ACS without chest pressure, pulmonary embolism, and panic attack], entering each vignette for matched male and female synthetic patient profiles with sex as the sole variable altered. We observed sex-based divergence in outputs from all three platforms, appearing as differences in differential diagnosis rank, differences in assigned probability, and differences in generated explanatory or advisory text. The direction of this divergence was not uniform: some findings were unfavorable to the female profile and others were favorable to it. Isabel Healthcare ranked Heart Attack first for the male profile but third for the female profile on the ACS with chest pressure vignette, and ranked Heart Attack seventh rather than fifth for the female profile on the panic attack vignette; on the ACS without chest pressure vignette, the same platform ranked Heart Attack first for the female profile, ahead of the male profile. Docus AI assigned a lower ACS probability to the female profile on the ACS without chest pressure vignette while its own text described this presentation as common in women, and applied a mirrored justification, common in males, to support a higher probability for the male profile given identical symptoms; the platform's closing advisory text also described immediate medical attention as crucial for the male profile and prompt evaluation as merely important for the female profile. Ada Health's explanatory text for the female profile stated that heart attacks are slightly more common in men than women, presented alongside a demoted cardiac ranking. These findings indicate that AI symptom checkers can produce sex-based divergence in their outputs, including an internally inconsistent, self-contradictory justification on one platform, and support the case for equity auditing of such systems, with attention to both numerical outputs and generated explanatory text, before and after deployment.
title: Sex-based diagnostic bias in AI symptom checkers: a structured, exploratory audit of three platforms.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stenosis at the origin of the vertebral artery (VAOS) accounts for approximately one in five posterior circulation ischemic events. Bare-metal stents (BMS) have been the conventional endovascular treatment, but restenosis occurs in 11-67% of cases. Drug-coated balloons (DCB) and drug-eluting stents (DES) are alternative strategies; however, no network meta-analysis has compared all three modalities specifically at the vertebral origin.
METHODS: Five databases-PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CNKI, and Wanfang-were searched from 2010 through May 2026 for studies comparing at least two of DCB, DES, or BMS in adults with symptomatic VAOS. The search identified 499 records; 393 underwent title and abstract screening after deduplication, from which 60 full-text articles were assessed. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted using the netmeta package (R 4.5.2), with Bayesian sensitivity analysis. The primary endpoint was imaging-confirmed restenosis (≥50%). The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261413981).
RESULTS: Seven studies (three randomized trials and four observational cohorts, N = 970; range 46-217) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with BMS, both DES (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.17-0.45) and DCB (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.83) reduced restenosis. DES and DCB did not differ significantly from each other (OR 1.42, 95% CI 0.58-3.50). Between-study heterogeneity was modest (I 2 = 20.5%). Although the point estimate suggests modest heterogeneity, the wide confidence interval and the small number of studies limit precision. Low I 2 in a small network should not be equated with clinical homogeneity. P-scores ranked DES first (88.9%), DCB second (60.7%), and BMS last (0.4%). For perioperative safety, DCB ranked highest (P-score 90.0%).
CONCLUSION: Both DES and DCB reduce restenosis compared with BMS in VAOS. Both DES and DCB are associated with lower restenosis rates than BMS. The relative anti-restenosis efficacy of DES versus DCB remains uncertain due to the absence of direct head-to-head comparisons. Treatment selection should be individualized based on lesion characteristics and procedural considerations. The DCB evidence base remains small, and head-to-head comparisons of DES versus DCB at the vertebral origin are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261413981, Identifier: CRD420261413981.
title: Drug-coated balloon, drug-eluting stent, versus bare-metal stent for vertebral artery ostial stenosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

abstract: High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) with severe thrombocytopenia creates competing reperfusion and bleeding risks. A 28-year-old man presented with obstructive shock and central pulmonary arterial filling defects. The last documented platelet count before alteplase was 21 × 10⁹/L; platelet transfusion intervened, and the count at infusion initiation was unknown. Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and hemostatic support were instituted. With increasing vasoactive requirements, the team selected bedside systemic thrombolysis after multidisciplinary consideration of surgical and catheter-based alternatives. Unfractionated heparin was paused at the first 20-mg alteplase infusion at 17:00. Arterial cannulation-site bleeding at 17:20 was treated with compression. The progress note documented that bleeding had stopped by 19:03; despite reduced vasoactive requirements, support dependence persisted. A second 20-mg infusion began at 19:25. Each stage lasted approximately 1 h. Heparin was restarted after the second infusion. Vasopressors were stopped on Day 1 and VA-ECMO was removed on Day 7. Hemoglobin fell from 150 to 117 g/L on Day 0 and reached 75 g/L on Day 8, prompting red-cell transfusion. Major bleeding could not be excluded. The patient was discharged on Day 19; Day 103 imaging showed no obvious residual pulmonary arterial filling defect. This case describes individualized decisions during multimodal care, not a validated alteplase regimen or evidence of its safety.
title: Case Report: Staged alteplase administration under VA-ECMO support for high-risk pulmonary embolism with severe thrombocytopenia.

abstract: The 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines represent the first comprehensive APHRS guidelines dedicated to the management of atrial fibrillation (AF) and comprise four parts covering epidemiology, detection/screening and integrated care; stroke prevention; rate and rhythm control; and lifestyle risk factor and comorbidity management. Part II focuses on stroke prevention in AF, integrating contemporary global evidence with data and clinical considerations specific to the Asia-Pacific region. It provides evidence-based and practical recommendations for stroke and bleeding risk assessment, oral anticoagulation, selection and appropriate dosing of direct oral anticoagulants, management of patients with special or complex clinical characteristics, and left atrial appendage occlusion. Particular attention is given to issues (and evidence) highly relevant to Asia-Pacific populations, including the evolving risk of ischemic stroke, appropriate anticoagulant dosing, renal function assessment, and balancing thromboembolic and bleeding risks. These recommendations aim to support individualized clinical decision-making, promote appropriate use of stroke-prevention strategies, and improve outcomes for patients with AF across the Asia-Pacific region.
first_author_country: Cardiovascular Center Taipei Veterans General Hospital and National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University Taipei Taiwan
last_author_country: Department of Internal Medicine Yonsei University College of Medicine Seoul Republic of Korea
title: 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines (Part II) on Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Carcinoid heart disease (CHD) is a rare cardiac manifestation of neuroendocrine tumors, typically associated with hepatic metastases. Primary ovarian carcinoid tumors represent an uncommon source of CHD and may lead to cardiac involvement in the absence of metastatic disease.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 51-year-old Iranian woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea, bilateral lower extremity edema, and episodes of facial flushing. She had undergone total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for a primary ovarian stromal carcinoid tumor 3 months prior. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe tricuspid regurgitation with thickened, retracted valve leaflets and impaired coaptation, while the pulmonary valve was spared. Laboratory findings were within normal limits except for a markedly elevated 24-h urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) level (128 mg/24 h). Cross-sectional imaging, including chest CT and abdominal-pelvic MRI, showed no evidence of hepatic or pulmonary metastases. A diagnosis of isolated CHD secondary to a primary ovarian carcinoid tumor was established. The patient declined surgical intervention and was discharged against medical advice.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights a rare presentation of CHD originating from a primary ovarian carcinoid tumor without metastatic involvement. Clinicians should consider this diagnosis in patients with unexplained right-sided valvular disease and features of carcinoid syndrome, even in the absence of liver metastases.
title: Carcinoid Heart Disease Associated with a Primary Ovarian Stromal Carcinoid Tumor: A Case Report and a Review of the Literature.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress and apoptosis caused by myocardial ischemia and hypoxia are the core mechanisms of myocardial damage in coronary heart disease (CHD). The myocardial protective effect and related molecular mechanisms of vitamin C (Vit C) have not been fully elucidated.
AIMS: To investigate whether Vit C activates the Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 axis to inhibit oxidative stress and apoptosis, thereby alleviating CHD myocardial injury.
METHODS: A CHD rat model was constructed, and the cardiac function was detected by echocardiography after 6 weeks of Vit C intervention. The effects of Vit C intervention on myocardial injury and myocardial fibrosis in rats were observed by histologic staining. The hypoxia-reoxygenation (H/R) model of H9c2 cells was established. Cell viability, cell survival rate, and apoptosis were evaluated by CCK-8 assay, Calcein-AM/Hoechst staining, and flow cytometry. The levels of cardiac troponin I (cTnI), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), Caspase-3 activity, and inflammatory factors in rat serum and H9c2 cells were measured using biochemical kits; oxidative stress-related indicators of rat myocardial tissue and H9c2 cells were also detected. Western blot was conducted to detect protein expression levels associated with myocardial injury, apoptosis, and the Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 pathway.
RESULTS: Vit C dose-dependently improved cardiac function, and reduced the pathologic damage to myocardial tissue and myocardial fibrosis in CHD rats. Vit C intervention effectively reduced serum cTnI levels and inflammatory factor levels in CHD rats, and inhibited oxidative stress. In vitro, Vit C alleviated H/R-induced H9c2 cell injury, reduced LDH release and Caspase-3 activity, and inhibited oxidative stress and apoptosis. In addition, Vit C intervention promoted the nuclear translocation of Nrf2 in myocardial tissue of CHD rats and H9c2 cells, and up-regulated HO-1 and NQO1 proteins. Intraperitoneal injection of Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 in rats or knockdown of Nrf2 in H9c2 cells weakened the protective effect of Vit C.
CONCLUSION: Vit C inhibits oxidative stress and apoptosis in CHD rats and H/R cardiomyocytes by activating the Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 pathway, affording myocardial protection.
title: Vitamin C inhibits oxidative stress and apoptosis through activating the Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 pathway to ameliorate myocardial injury in coronary heart disease.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the function and basic molecular pathways of miR-222-3p in sepsis-induced myocardial injury (SIMI), focusing on its post-transcriptional regulation of the NFATc3 signalling network, and to explore its use as a therapeutic target for SIMI.
METHODS: Septicemia was induced in rodents by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). The animals were divided into the following seven groups: Sham, Sepsis, Sepsis + miR-222-3p, Sepsis + anti-222-3p, Sepsis + ad-GFP, Sepsis + miR-222-3p + NFAT inhibitor, and Sepsis + anti-222-3p + NFAT inhibitor. A NFAT inhibitor (100 µg/d) was administered intraperitoneally for three days before CLP surgery, and 24 hours prior to CLP, miR-222-3p, anti-222-3p, or ad-GFP (100 μL each) were infused intravenously through the tail vein. The levels of miR-222-3p in myocardial tissue were determined by qRT-PCR, and NFATc3 protein level 24 hours after surgery was determined by western blot. H&E staining of the myocardial cells and TUNEL assays were used to detect apoptosis in myocytes. Echocardiogram was performed to assess the heart, and the plasma levels of CK-MB, cTnI, IL-6, IL-10 and TNF-α were measured by ELISA.
RESULTS: Myocardial miR-222-3p expression was significantly upregulated in septic mice compared to sham-operated controls. NFATc3 levels decreased in the miR-222-3p injection group and increased in the anti-miR-222-3p group. miR-222-3p reduced myocardial cell apoptosis, improved left ventricular ejection fraction, lowered plasma concentrations of CK-MB, cTnI, IL-6 and TNF-α, and promoted IL-10. Suppressing miR-222-3p produced the inverse outcome. The activity of NFAT was also reduced somewhat.
CONCLUSIONS: MiR-222-3p inhibits NFATc3 to reduce myocardial damage in septic mice, suggesting that miR-222-3p may represent a therapeutic target for sepsis-induced heart failure.
title: miR-222-3p reduces myocardial injury in sepsis by regulating NFATc3.
Embolization of a fluoropolymer-coated left atrial appendage occlusion device to the infrarenal aorta presenting with acute neurologic symptoms: A case report.
