abstract:
BACKGROUND: The number of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures is increasing worldwide. However, studies comparing regional differences remain scarce.
AIMS: This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes after TAVI between Japan and France using a database compiled from two large hospitals.
METHODS: The TOTO-TAVI study included patients who underwent TAVI in Japan and France. The primary endpoint was in-hospital death. Periprocedural safety outcomes and 3-year all-cause mortality were also evaluated. A subgroup analysis was performed to assess the independent TAVI risk for each country.
RESULTS: Among 6,967 patients who underwent TAVI between 2016 and 2024, 1,422 in Japan and 4,771 in France were included. Although patients in Japan showed a significantly smaller body size, a smaller aortic valve, and a higher operative risk than those in France, the in-hospital death rate was comparable between the two groups (0.6% vs 1.3%; p=0.068). The new pacemaker implantation rate was lower in Japan than in France. There was no significant difference in 3-year all-cause mortality between Japan and France (22.5% vs 23.5%, hazard ratio 0.678, 95% confidence interval: 0.114-4.033; p=0.583). For the subgroup analysis, there were no statistically significant independent risk factors for composite outcomes, including in-hospital death, stroke, and bleeding, in Japan; however, in France, female sex, higher body mass index, lower haemoglobin levels, previous coronary artery bypass grafting and cerebrovascular disease, bicuspid annulus, and general anaesthesia were independent risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite differences in patient backgrounds, in-hospital and 3-year mortality were comparable between Japan and France, suggesting that procedural safety and medium-term prognosis after TAVI were established regardless of procedural risks.
title: Differences between Japan and France in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the TOTO-TAVI study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR) poses unique technical challenges for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), including annular dilatation and absent calcification for anchoring. Whilst dedicated aortic regurgitation (AR) devices have been developed, their comparative performance against off-label devices specifically via transfemoral access - the contemporary standard approach - remains incompletely defined.
AIMS: We aimed to compare the outcomes of dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for PNAR via transfemoral access in contemporary practice.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed (MEDLINE) and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-November 2025) for studies reporting transfemoral TAVI outcomes in PNAR. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression was performed.
RESULTS: Twenty-four studies (2,956 patients) were included comprising 25 cohorts: 4 cohorts (537 patients) evaluated dedicated devices, and 21 cohorts (2,419 patients) assessed off-label devices. Overall, 30-day mortality was 3.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.3-4.8%). Dedicated devices showed a trend towards lower mortality (1.9% vs 4.1%, odds ratio [OR] 0.45, 95% CI: 0.20-1.00; p=0.051; risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19-0.83). Dedicated devices achieved higher device success (95.8% vs 85.7%, OR 3.64; p=0.012), lower rates of residual AR >=moderate (0.6% vs 6.2%, OR 0.11; p=0.048), reduced valve embolisation (2.0% vs 7.3%, OR 0.26; p=0.048), and fewer reinterventions (2.0% vs 7.9%, OR 0.22; p=0.010). Permanent pacemaker implantation (20.8%), stroke (2.6%), and major bleeding (3.0%) were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary transfemoral TAVI for PNAR, dedicated devices demonstrated superior procedural outcomes compared with off-label devices. These findings support the preferential use of dedicated devices in this population, though randomised trials are needed to establish definite treatment recommendations.
title: Dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for pure native aortic regurgitation via transfemoral access: a meta-analysis of contemporary outcomes.
Direct-visualization implantation of an atrial leadless pacemaker at tricuspid valve surgery.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (pLAAO) offers single-procedure rhythm control and stroke prevention in patients unable to tolerate long-term oral anticoagulation. Patients with prior intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) from suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) have among the strongest contraindications to anticoagulation yet are absent from randomized trials of concomitant procedures, and combining pulsed field ablation (PFA) with pLAAO introduces energy-specific considerations.
CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old woman with persistent AF, cavotricuspid isthmus-dependent atrial flutter and a CHA2DS2-VA score of 3 had been off anticoagulation for 2 years after an ICH. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed microhaemorrhages and siderosis suggestive of CAA. Through a single transseptal puncture, four-vein PFA was performed first to avoid electrical interaction with the nitinol pLAAO frame, followed by WATCHMAN FLX deployment under transoesophageal echocardiographic and computed tomography (CT)-fluoroscopy guidance and radiofrequency cavotricuspid isthmus ablation. She received edoxaban without aspirin for three months. Cardiac CT then confirmed device seal without device-related thrombus, and all antithrombotic therapy was withdrawn.
DISCUSSION: Randomized trials show that anticoagulation after ICH prevents ischaemic stroke at the cost of a marked increase in recurrent haemorrhage, and lobar or CAA-related haemorrhage carries the least favourable balance. Concomitant ablation and pLAAO delivers rhythm control and stroke prevention with one transseptal access and one time-limited exposure to anticoagulation. Combining PFA with pLAAO requires sizing the occluder before ablation, because PFA induces acute pulmonary ridge oedema, and completing pulmonary vein isolation before deployment to avoid arcing against the nitinol frame.
title: Classic case report: concomitant pulsed field ablation, cavotricuspid isthmus ablation and percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion in a patient with prior intracranial haemorrhage.

abstract: Provisional stenting (PS) remains the default strategy for most bifurcation lesions, but the risk of side branch (SB) compromise continues to be a concern. Active SB protection strategies were developed to mitigate this risk, as an extension of PS with a jailed wire. They have a common goal: to preserve SB patency while decreasing the need for complex two-stent strategies, particularly in difficult anatomical or clinical situations. This review aims to provide a comprehensive, case-based overview of different contemporary active SB protection methods, including techniques developed in Asia which have not yet been widely adopted elsewhere. We highlight the practical aspects of conventional, contemporary, and modified jailed balloon techniques; active transfer of plaque; jailed microcatheter strategies; and emerging adaptations, such as jailed drug-coated balloon use. Case examples illustrate the mechanisms of stent deformation, rescue manoeuvres, and correction with intravascular imaging. Ultimately, active SB protection may enhance the safety and consistency of PS across a broad spectrum of patients and lesion types.
title: Active side branch protection in provisional stenting: techniques, case-based insights, and practical considerations.
Real-time visualisation of Impella-mediated left ventricular unloading during surgical repair of blowout free wall rupture.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-eluting stents (SES) are a benchmark in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while biolimus-eluting stents (BES), which combine a more lipophilic analogue with a biodegradable polymer, may enhance healing and reduce thrombosis. Whether these BES features translate into improved survival and cardiac outcomes compared with SES remains uncertain.
AIMS: We sought to perform a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating BES compared with SES in adult patients undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This meta-analysis encompassed randomised and controlled clinical trials that directly compared BES with SES in the setting of percutaneous coronary intervention. A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials up to June 2025. The main outcomes assessed were all-cause and cardiac mortality, while secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularisation (TLR), and stent thrombosis (ST). Outcomes were evaluated at <=1 year (early) and >1-5 years (midterm) using pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) in random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed by the I2 test.
RESULTS: Six trials (12,109 patients: 6,088 BES, 6,021 SES) were analysed. BES reduced 1-year cardiac death by 30% (RR 0.70, 95% CI: 0.52-0.93) and showed a non-significant 19% reduction in all-cause death (RR 0.81; p=0.058). MACE, myocardial infarction, and TLR were similar between stents across timepoints. BES showed a non-significant early increase in ST (RR 1.85; p=0.12) but a 46% reduction in late ST (RR 0.54, 95% CI: 0.33-0.88). Mortality rates converged after 1 year.
CONCLUSIONS: BES offer a short-term reduction in cardiac mortality and late stent thrombosis compared with SES, with otherwise similar morbidity outcomes. These results support the short-term safety of BES and indicate a possible long-term thrombotic and cardiac survival benefit, warranting confirmation in longer-term trials.
title: Biolimus- versus sirolimus-eluting stents in percutaneous coronary intervention: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) and stress-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) are non-atherosclerotic causes of acute coronary syndrome that predominantly affect women. Their overlapping clinical, electrocardiographic, biomarker, and imaging features can make diagnosis challenging, and although their coexistence is increasingly recognized, the relationship between these entities remains poorly understood. A 48-year-old female with cardiovascular risk factors presented with back and scapular pain and ST-segment elevations. Coronary angiography revealed Yip-Saw Class 2 SCAD in the mid-distal LAD with preserved flow. Echocardiography demonstrated wall motion abnormalities extending beyond the LAD territory with a reduced ejection fraction and apical ballooning suggesting concurrent SICM. This case illustrates the concept that SCAD and SICM are important non-atherosclerotic causes of acute coronary syndrome in women and may present with overlapping features that complicate diagnosis. Their coexistence is biologically plausible given their marked female predominance and shared susceptibility related to estrogen-mediated vascular protection, which may be diminished during the perimenopausal transition. Clinicians should consider concurrent SICM when evaluating patients with SCAD, particularly when wall motion abnormalities extend beyond the affected coronary distribution.
title: A Bidirectional Relationship Between Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection and Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy in a Perimenopausal Woman: A Case Report.

abstract: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.
title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Followed by Lung Cancer Resection in an Older Patient: A Case Report.
BASILICA-assisted TAVI: when leaflet laceration takes an unexpected turn.

abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.
title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: As transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) expands, improving deployment efficiency is increasingly important. We developed and implemented a semi-rapid pacing-assisted deployment workflow for the Evolut platform.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the procedural efficiency and early safety of this workflow for transfemoral (TF) Evolut FX TAVI.
METHODS: In a single-centre registry, we performed a retrospective before-and-after analysis of consecutive TF Evolut FX procedures: semi-rapid deployment (n=48) versus conventional deployment (n=53). Device time was defined as the interval from initial advancement of the delivery system to final release of the Evolut FX valve. Prolonged device time was defined as >14 minutes (>75th percentile), and determinants were assessed using Firth's penalised logistic regression.
RESULTS: The device time was shorter with semi-rapid deployment (9.0 [interquartile range [IQR] 6.0-13.0] minutes vs 14.0 [IQR 11.0-16.0] minutes; p<0.001), while operation and procedure times were similar (p=0.13 and p=0.16, respectively). The mean recapture count was higher in the semi-rapid group (0.85±1.09 vs 0.53±0.70; p=0.08), and contrast volume was higher (32.0 [IQR 25.0-42.0] mL vs 25.0 [IQR 15.0-33.0] mL; p=0.008). Paravalvular leak >=mild (31.2% vs 32.1%; p=1.0) and in-hospital pacemaker implantation (2.1% vs 7.5%; p=0.37) did not differ significantly between the groups. In multivariable analysis, recapture predicted a prolonged device time (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.75-14.19; p=0.002), whereas the semi-rapid workflow predicted a reduced device time (adjusted OR 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01-0.66; p=0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Semi-rapid pacing-assisted Evolut FX deployment selectively reduced device time without compromising early in-hospital safety outcomes. Deployment efficiency represents a practical procedural target for workflow refinement in self-expanding TAVI.
title: A semi-rapid deployment workflow to reduce device time in Evolut FX self-expanding transcatheter aortic valve implantation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data regarding intravascular imaging (IVI) in complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain scarce.
AIMS: In this study, we sought to assess the effects of IVI-guided PCI according to procedural complexity.
METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the RENOVATE-COMPLEX-PCI trial that compared IVI-guided PCI with angiography-guided PCI in patients with complex coronary artery lesions. The study population was stratified into three groups of low, moderate, and high risk, according to PCI procedural complexity, following the European Society of Cardiology criteria. The high-risk group included patients meeting at least one clinical risk criterion and at least one procedural risk criterion. The primary endpoint was target vessel failure (TVF), a composite of cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target vessel revascularisation.
RESULTS: At a median 2.1-year follow-up, TVF risk increased significantly in a stepwise manner from the low (reference) to moderate (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.369, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.705-2.660; p=0.353) and high procedural complexity group (adjusted HR 1.619, 95% CI: 0.963-2.723; p=0.069). The benefit of IVI-guided PCI varied by procedural complexity, with significant risk reductions in the moderate-risk group (adjusted HR 0.374, 95% CI: 0.150-0.935; p=0.035) and the high-risk group (adjusted HR 0.633, 95% CI: 0.424-0.945; p=0.025) but not in the low-risk group (adjusted HR 0.735, 95% CI: 0.282-1.914; p=0.528). The interaction between the IVI effect and procedural complexity was statistically significant (pinteraction=0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing complex PCI, an IVI-guided procedure significantly reduced adverse cardiac events, with a greater magnitude of benefit observed in procedures of high complexity.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of the randomised RENOVATE-COMPLEX-PCI trial; stratified into low, moderate and high procedural complexity; median follow-up 2.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup analysis of a single trial; the abstract does not state the sample size.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc RENOVATE-COMPLEX-PCI analysis suggests larger benefit of intravascular imaging guidance with greater procedural complexity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted HR 0.374, 95% CI: 0.150-0.935 in the moderate-risk group and adjusted HR 0.633, 95% CI: 0.424-0.945 in the high-risk group, not in the low-risk group (adjusted HR 0.735, 95% CI: 0.282-1.914); pinteraction=0.009.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs selective use of intravascular imaging in complex PCI.

title: Prognostic impact of intravascular imaging in percutaneous coronary intervention according to procedural complexity.

abstract: The 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/American Diabetes Association/American Society of Nephrology guideline on cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome establishes kidney function as a determinant of cardiovascular risk rather than an adjacent comorbidity. Endpoint architecture in structural heart and cardiac surgical research has not been revised accordingly. Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 standardized acute kidney injury reporting with considerable rigor, staging injury on Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine criteria and requiring that new renal replacement therapy be reported discretely, but its scope is confined to the periprocedural window. No endpoint tracks filtration trajectory across follow-up, no threshold within the standard defines chronic kidney disease stage progression, and initiation of maintenance dialysis years after intervention has no reporting convention distinct from temporary replacement therapy in the immediate postoperative period. Pivotal trials consequently adjudicate cardiovascular outcomes for five years and kidney outcomes for 30 days. Registry evidence suggests the omission is consequential, with rapid filtration decline documented in more than a third of patients carrying preexisting kidney impairment within five years of cardiac surgery. This editorial argues for longitudinal reporting of estimated glomerular filtration rate, prespecification of stage progression and maintenance dialysis as adjudicated endpoints, and nephrology representation on trial steering committees with a defined role in kidney endpoint specification.
title: Kidney Outcomes in Structural Heart and Cardiac Surgical Trials: The Case for Longitudinal Endpoint Reporting.

abstract: Graves' disease is a common cause of autoimmune hyperthyroidism and is frequently associated with cardiovascular manifestations, including sinus tachycardia, atrial fibrillation and high-output heart failure. Severe left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction complicated by LV thrombus is an uncommon presentation. Recognition may be challenging when concurrent illness and antithyroid treatment complicate the interpretation of thyroid function tests. A 27-year-old woman with Graves' disease diagnosed in 2021 presented in March 2025 with progressive dyspnoea, orthopnoea, profound lethargy, jaundice and generalised oedema. Following relapse in September 2024, carbimazole had been recommenced, but adherence was suboptimal, and heart failure symptoms had developed over several months. Examination revealed sinus tachycardia, diffuse goitre, exophthalmos, hepatomegaly and marked anasarca. Community-acquired pneumonia was also diagnosed. Admission free thyroxine was 8.5 pmol/L (reference range: 8.9-17.3), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) was 0.48 mIU/L (0.30-4.40), and free triiodothyronine was unavailable. This biochemical pattern was interpreted in the clinical context as consistent with non-thyroidal illness. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) was elevated at 9,326 ng/L. Electrocardiography demonstrated sinus tachycardia, and transthoracic echocardiography showed LV dilatation with severe global systolic dysfunction and an estimated LV ejection fraction (LVEF) of approximately 10%. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated an LV apical thrombus and hepatic congestion. Graves' disease-associated myocardial dysfunction was considered an important contributor; however, tachycardia-mediated dysfunction, myocarditis and critical illness-related myocardial dysfunction remained potential contributing causes. Management included adjustment of carbimazole, diuresis, bisoprolol, valsartan, spironolactone and dapagliflozin, alongside treatment of pneumonia. Therapeutic anticoagulation was initiated with enoxaparin, followed by intravenous unfractionated heparin and bridging to warfarin. Clinical improvement was accompanied by recovery of LVEF to 36% during admission, approximately 40% in June 2025 and 52%-54% on echocardiography in September 2025. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging during the same time confirmed normal biventricular size and systolic function, with an LVEF of 54% and no residual intracardiac thrombus. A small area of nonspecific non-infarct-pattern fibrosis could represent previous myocarditis. Definitive thyroidectomy was planned. This case highlights severe but reversible LV systolic dysfunction with apical thrombus in a young woman with relapsed Graves' disease and suboptimal treatment adherence. Although the clinical course suggests a thyroid-related contribution, the myocardial dysfunction may have been multifactorial. The reduction in thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSIs) alongside cardiac recovery represents a temporal association and does not establish causation. Careful clinical assessment and cardiac imaging are essential to recognising significant cardiac involvement when thyroid biochemistry is complicated by concurrent illness.
title: Graves' Disease and the Heart: Severe Reversible Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction With Apical Thrombus in a Young Woman With Relapsed Thyrotoxicosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).
METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.
RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).
CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.
first_author_country: Promedica Toledo Hospital Toledo OH USA
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
last_author_country: Oregon Health & Science University Portland OR USA
title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.

abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Complex abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAc) involving visceral and renal vessels can be treated via open surgery or less invasive fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR). Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) minimizes contrast and radiation while improving placement accuracy, though its specific role in FEVAR remains understudied. This CARE-compliant article reports a FEVAR case guided by IVUS. Case Presentation: A 75-year-old male with multiple comorbidities presented with an enlarging AAAc extending to the renal artery ostia, lacking an adequate neck. Anatomical variants included a left renal artery with a caudal origin (pelvic left kidney), a left renal polar artery originating from the right common iliac artery, and a patent inferior mesenteric artery (<3 mm). Following multidisciplinary evaluation, the patient successfully underwent simultaneous FEVAR and coronary angiography. Guided by IVUS, the fenestrated endograft was deployed with preserved visceral patency. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day two. A 30-day CT angiogram detected a stable inferior mesenteric artery endoleak, managed conservatively through a 6-month follow-up. Conclusions: IVUS-guided FEVAR may offer a promising alternative to traditional angiography, reducing radiation and contrast exposure. Further large-scale studies are needed to confirm these findings and establish clinical and economic benefits.
title: Intravascular Ultrasound (IVUS)-Assisted Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair (FEVAR) for Iuxtarenal Aortic Aneurysm with Pelvic Ectopic Left Kidney and Aberrant Left Renal Arteries: A Case Report.

abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Infective endocarditis following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a severe complication that may be associated with prosthetic valve dysfunction, local infectious extension, and systemic embolization. Visceral mycotic aneurysms are uncommon, particularly those involving the hepatic arterial circulation. Case Presentation: We report the case of an 80-year-old woman who developed Streptococcus gallolyticus TAVI-associated prosthetic valve endocarditis (TAVI-PVE) four months after valve implantation. Despite prolonged antimicrobial therapy and subsequent negative blood cultures, the clinical course was complicated by persistent prosthetic and periprosthetic echocardiographic abnormalities, cerebral and splenic embolic events, and new-onset abdominal pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed two hepatic arterial aneurysmal lesions with surrounding inflammatory changes, consistent with mycotic aneurysms. After initially declining surgery, the patient underwent redo surgical aortic valve replacement; cultures of the surgically excised specimens were negative. Abdominal pain resolved and inflammatory markers normalized following surgery and continued antimicrobial therapy. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated marked interval enlargement of the hepatic arterial aneurysmal lesion to 28 mm × 28 mm × 26 mm despite clinical improvement and normalization of inflammatory markers. Conclusions: This case highlights that microbiological, clinical, and biological improvement does not necessarily indicate resolution of local cardiac or extracardiac structural complications and emphasizes the importance of repeated imaging, guideline-based antimicrobial therapy, timely source control, and multidisciplinary vascular management in complicated TAVI-PVE.
title: Hepatic Mycotic Aneurysms in TAVI-Associated Infective Endocarditis Caused by Streptococcus gallolyticus: A Case Report.

abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Multivessel coronary artery spasm (CAS) is an uncommon, high-risk form of vasospastic angina that can produce transient ST-segment elevation mimicking acute myocardial infarction. Evidence to guide management when calcium channel blockers and nitrates fail is scarce, and renal sympathetic denervation (RSD) has been reported in very few patients; Case Presentation: A 53-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and dyslipidemia presented with nocturnal chest pain and inferior ST-segment elevation. Coronary angiography showed severe spontaneous spasm of the right coronary and left anterior descending arteries that resolved completely with intracoronary nitrate; the coronary arteries were otherwise angiographically normal. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I remained below 10 ng/L (reference 0-34 ng/L), and echocardiography was normal, fulfilling the criteria for definite vasospastic angina without myocardial infarction. The same two-vessel spasm was documented at a second angiogram three months later. Despite maximally tolerated dual calcium channel blockade, nitrates, and statin therapy, he required more than ten further admissions. A self-terminating accelerated idioventricular rhythm lasting about two minutes was recorded. No syncope or malignant arrhythmia occurred, and an electrophysiology review found no current indication for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. Radiofrequency RSD was performed off-label for refractory symptoms without complications, but at six months, his symptoms and admissions were unchanged; Conclusions: Our case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic difficulties in refractory CAS. Accelerated idioventricular rhythm after relief of spasm is a reperfusion rhythm and does not by itself indicate device therapy. In this patient, RSD did not control refractory multivessel CAS, a negative observation that adds to the very limited evidence on autonomic modulation in this setting.
title: Refractory Multivessel Coronary Artery Spasm Unresponsive to Renal Sympathetic Denervation, with Recurrent Transient ST-Segment Elevation and an Episode of Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm: A Case Report.

abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) is an established therapy for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in selected patients. Single-leaflet device attachment (SLDA) is the commonest device-related complication, but complete intraprocedural detachment with embolization is rare, and percutaneous retrieval of an embolized tricuspid device has been reported only exceptionally. Case Presentation: An inoperable elderly patient with previous transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and torrential functional TR underwent T-TEER. After implantation of the first clip at the anteroseptal commissure with apparently adequate leaflet capture, anterior SLDA was identified and progressed to complete detachment and right atrial embolization of the device. Despite this, the T-TEER was completed by successful implantation of the second clip, leaving only mild residual central TR. In the same session, the embolized device was retrieved percutaneously from the femoral venous system using a 15 mm gooseneck snare advanced through a 22 Fr sheath, with a safety wire and en-bloc removal, without forcing ensheathing and without venous injury. The patient was discharged on post-procedure day 2 with durable TR reduction and clinical improvement. Conclusions: Complete leaflet detachment is a possible complication of T-TEER. Confirming deep, symmetric insertion in multiple echocardiographic windows before every release is essential. When embolization occurs, knowledge of device dimensions and immediate availability of a complete snare kit is important. Although this approach may be considered in selected patients, particularly those at high surgical risk, the available evidence is limited to isolated case reports and does not allow general conclusions on its safety or efficacy.
title: Intraprocedural Embolization of a Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair Device and Its Percutaneous Retrieval: A Case Report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the surgical outcomes of nonrobotic and robotic minimally invasive mitral valve repair.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair from January 2014 to March 2024. After excluding the learning curve cases, early and midterm outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 422 patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair (nonrobotic, n = 103; robotic, n = 319) were enrolled. The robotic group had a higher EuroSCORE II (P < 0.001). After propensity matching, the final cohort included 84 and 168 patients in each group. In the robotic group after matching, concomitant procedures remained significantly more frequent (P = 0.030). However, operative time (P = 0.782) and cross-clamping time (P = 0.452) were comparable, whereas cardiopulmonary bypass time was significantly longer in the robotic group (P = 0.031). Postoperative blood transfusion (P < 0.001), chest tube output within 24 h (P < 0.001), and intensive care unit stay (P = 0.042) remained higher in the robotic group after matching. Postoperative mitral regurgitation was no greater than mild in both groups (P = 0.146). At 4 years, overall survival was 94.4% versus 98.4% (P = 0.215), and freedom from recurrence of moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5% versus 97.9% (P = 0.230) after matching. These results are consistent with those observed before matching.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic mitral valve repair demonstrated comparable perioperative and midterm outcomes despite greater transfusion requirements and a higher frequency of concomitant procedures. The higher rate of concomitant procedures should be interpreted with caution because it may partly reflect differences in surgical era and patient selection.
title: Advantages and Limitations of the Use of Robots in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Results From a Matched Direct Comparison.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (M-TEER) represents a safe treatment modality for patients with high-grade mitral regurgitation (MR). While clinical decision-making concerning the referral of suitable candidates for M-TEER is guided primarily by clinical and echocardiographic parameters, the potential of hemodynamic parameters obtained at the time of screening in predicting treatment outcomes has not been sufficiently investigated.
METHODS: All patients who underwent M-TEER and who provided sufficient right heart catheterisation (RHC) data prior to M-TEER were enrolled for analysis. The investigated hemodynamic parameters were analysed descriptively and their associations with survival were estimated by univariable Cox regression analysis and Kaplan-Meier's analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 94 patients were analysed, of whom 92.6% (87/94) had concomitant pulmonary hypertension (PH). Analysis of the hemodynamic profile revealed that 46.8% (44/94) of patients had advanced-stage congestive heart failure with a cardiac index < 2 L/min/m2, and 68% (64/94) of patients had a cardiac power index <0.5 W/m2. According to the results of the Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses, a systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP) > 60 mmHg and a mean right atrial pressure (RAP) > 20 mmHg were proven to be significant predictors of long-term survival after M-TEER.
CONCLUSIONS: Analysis of the hemodynamic profile, specifically the identified predictors, contributes to the improved identification of scenarios associated with a favourable prognosis in patients undergoing M-TEER.
title: The predictive value of the hemodynamic profile for survival in patients undergoing transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair.

abstract: BackgroundAccidental hypothermia is an unintentional drop in core temperature below 35 °C, typically resulting from exposure to cold environmental conditions. Clinical presentations may vary widely depending on the severity of hypothermia and the presence of coexisting conditions complicating diagnosis and treatment. We report a case of accidental hypothermia caused by environmental exposure and associated with cardiogenic shock from a myocardial infarction with complete heart block.Case PresentationA group of ski tourers found a 62-y-old male skier at 3000 m in severe distress with abdominal pain, shivering, and profound exhaustion. On arrival at a mountain hut, he was agitated, then became unconscious and bradycardic with a weak femoral pulse. Once advanced medical equipment reached the hut, a 12-lead electrocardiogram showed an inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with complete third-degree atrioventricular block and a ventricular escape rhythm. The first measurable axillary temperature was 32.2 °C. Consciousness progressively improved, but bradycardia persisted during rewarming. The patient was evacuated 6 h after the diagnosis of acute STEMI. He underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and was successfully treated with a stent.ConclusionsThis case illustrates that hypothermia and environmental factors can complicate the diagnosis of atypical presentations of life-threatening conditions, such as STEMI, and how unexpected clinical findings not fully explained by hypothermia may indicate the presence of an underlying condition. In such situations, hypothermia staging systems should be used with caution. Early electrocardiography, awareness of cognitive biases, and the use of safe rewarming practices are essential to ensure timely diagnosis and prevent complications.
title: Mimics and Chameleons: A Patient with Accidental Hypothermia and Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
CASE SUMMARY: A 68-year-old man with Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III angina underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), which delineated mirror-image coronary anatomy and left main trifurcation, providing a preprocedural anatomical roadmap. Angiography confirmed the anticipated lesions, demonstrated the small caliber of the ramus intermedius artery, favoring a stent-sparing strategy, and revealed an additional severe distal left anterior descending artery stenosis not clearly appreciated on CCTA. Optical coherence tomography further characterized the left anterior descending artery lesions, provided calcium scoring, and guided lesion modification and stent optimization. After intervention, final angiography showed TIMI flow grade 3.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: CCTA provided a preprocedural anatomical roadmap in the setting of mirror-image coronary anatomy. Angiography and optical coherence tomography subsequently refined lesion-specific treatment and percutaneous coronary intervention optimization.
title: CCTA Roadmapping and OCT-Guided Multilesion PCI in Situs Inversus Dextrocardia.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy.
RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016).
CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of OPTION-STEMI suggests age modifies the effect of immediate versus staged complete revascularisation in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients 70 years or older: primary endpoint 45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; not in patients <70 years (HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45); multiplicative interaction P = 0.054.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Timing of complete revascularisation in older patients is a live guideline question and the signal needs a powered test.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In high-risk patients requiring coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) we sought to evaluate the differential impact of comorbid and cardiovascular risk factors on perioperative versus one year survival with the hypothesis that different phenotypes of perioperative risk may portend different longitudinal outcomes and that not all high-risk features are equivalent.
METHODS: The Society Thoracic Surgeons (STS) Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (ACSD) was used to assess all patients (n=75,385) ≥65 years of age undergoing isolated CABG with a predicted risk of mortality (PROM) greater than 4% (2012-2022). The database was linked with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) claims data to evaluate one-year mortality. Change in risk-adjusted odds ratios for 30-day and 1-year mortality were assessed using landmark analysis to identify variables associated with early versus late mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 67,376 (89.4%) patients survived 30-days of those 8,998 (13.4%) died between 30 days and one year. Liver disease and home oxygen were associated with increased mortality at both 30 days and 1 year. However, unresponsive state, prior CABG, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within 6 hours, cardiogenic shock, and temporary mechanical support were associated with early mortality but exhibited no significant effects at 1 year. Finally, cancer, Medicaid coverage, and dialysis were initially neutral for 30-day mortality but emerged as independent risk factors for 1-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk CABG, prognostic determinants evolve over time. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating temporal risk dynamics into clinical decisions.
title: One Year Survival of High-Risk Patients Undergoing Coronary Revascularization.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) may improve outcomes in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the optimal timing of initiation remains uncertain, partly because prior comparisons did not restrict controls to patients still in refractory arrest at the same decision point.
METHODS: We employed target trial emulation with a sequential landmark design in the Korean nationwide OHCA registry (2016-2023). Among patients with presumed cardiac aetiology who were still receiving emergency department (ED) CPR 15 minutes after ED arrival, landmarks were set at 15, 30, and 60 minutes, each comparing ECPR initiation within the subsequent window with no ECPR during that window among patients still in refractory arrest. Treatment effects were adjusted risk differences estimated by propensity score overlap weighting with 22 covariates.
RESULTS: Of 58,668 patients with refractory OHCA, 909 received ECPR. Weighted 30-day survival (ECPR vs. control) was 31.0% vs. 16.0%, 21.6% vs. 7.2%, and 10.9% vs. 3.2% at the 15-, 30-, and 60-minute landmarks; adjusted risk differences were +15.0 percentage points (95% CI 8.0 to 22.0), +14.4 (10.4 to 18.4), and +7.7 (3.7 to 11.7) (all P<.001). Favourable neurological outcomes showed a similar pattern, and in the exploratory timing-gradient analysis, the adjusted risk difference decreased with longer door-to-ECMO times but remained statistically significant through 120 minutes.
CONCLUSIONS: ECPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcomes at every landmark, including initiation beyond 60 minutes, where weighted 30-day survival with continued conventional CPR was 3.2%. Benefit was largest with early initiation but did not disappear at the commonly applied 60-minute benchmark, which may be overly restrictive for selected patients in capable systems.

appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data with propensity score overlap weighting; residual confounding and selection of ECPR candidates remain.
appraisal.one_line: Target trial emulation in a Korean national registry associated ECPR with higher 30-day survival than continued conventional CPR at three landmarks.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obese patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remain at high risk of early mortality despite percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Obesity and related cardiometabolic disorders may aggravate vascular and microcirculatory dysfunction, potentially involving impaired endothelial cell function. However, prognostic evidence specifically focusing on obese patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI remains limited. This exploratory, single-center study investigated clinical factors associated with in-hospital mortality and compared the predictive performance of logistic regression and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) using rigorous internal validation.
METHODS: The archived analytic dataset contained 268 patients. After eligibility re-audit, three patients with body mass index (BMI) < 28 kg/m² were excluded, leaving 265 patients with documented AMI-CS treated with PCI. Seven routinely available candidate variables were evaluated in multivariable association and prediction analyses. Logistic regression and regularized XGBoost were compared using 20 repetitions of stratified five-fold nested cross-validation, with all model tuning confined to the inner training folds. Supplemental data on shock severity, serial lactate levels, vasoactive therapy, mechanical circulatory support, ventilation, renal replacement therapy, and hemodynamic variables were additionally evaluated descriptively and in a post hoc sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 265 patients, 202 survived and 63 died during hospitalization. Higher heart rate, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, malignant arrhythmia, and multivessel disease were associated with in-hospital mortality. The seven-variable logistic regression model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.767 (95% CI, 0.696-0.831) and a Brier score of 0.152, compared with an AUC of 0.712 (95% CI, 0.641-0.779) and a Brier score of 0.169 for regularized XGBoost. Serial lactate concentrations at admission, peak, 6 h, 12 h, and 24 h were consistently higher in non-survivors, and cardiac power output was modestly lower. A post hoc severity-augmented logistic model achieved an AUC of 0.922 (95% CI, 0.888-0.951), but its calibration slope was 2.077, indicating that the model was not sufficiently calibrated for clinical deployment.
CONCLUSIONS: In obese patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, heart rate, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, malignant arrhythmia, and multivessel disease were associated with in-hospital mortality. Logistic regression demonstrated more favorable internally validated predictive performance than regularized XGBoost using the same routinely available predictors. The associations of diabetes and hypertension, together with abnormalities in systemic perfusion, are biologically compatible with a potential contribution of endothelial cell dysfunction and impaired microvascular regulation; however, endothelial function was not directly measured in this study. External multicenter validation and studies incorporating endothelial biomarkers are warranted to further clarify the role of endothelial dysfunction in risk stratification for this high-risk population. These findings are exploratory and internally validated only; the modest sample size, absence of external validation, and originally outcome-informed nomination of the seven candidate predictors limit generalizability and preclude claims of clinical readiness.
title: Exploratory clinical predictors and internally validated models of in-hospital mortality after PCI in obese patients with acute myocardial infarction and documented cardiogenic shock: a single-center retrospective study.

abstract: BACKGROUND Delayed traumatic cardiac rupture complicated by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture is an exceedingly rare clinical entity. We report this case to describe the temporal sequence of events from blunt myocardial contusion to left ventricular aneurysm formation and rupture, followed by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture. While the precise mechanism linking these events remains to be determined, we propose a potential pathophysiological connection. CASE REPORT A patient presented with rupture of a posterior left ventricular aneurysm 54 days after a fall from a height. The patient was emergently placed on venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for circulatory support and subsequently underwent surgical repair of the aneurysm. Postoperative echocardiography revealed new-onset tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture, prompting elective mechanical tricuspid replacement. Histopathological examination of resected valve tissues revealed chronic degenerative changes. To our knowledge, this is the first report documenting this temporal sequence of delayed left ventricular aneurysm rupture followed by tricuspid chordal rupture after surgical repair. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the importance of continued clinical and echocardiographic vigilance after severe blunt cardiac injury, particularly for detecting late-emerging structural complications such as aneurysm formation and valvular dysfunction. It also illustrates the potential utility of VA-ECMO as a critical bridging strategy to stabilize patients with traumatic cardiac rupture before surgical repair. The observed temporal association between aneurysm repair and subsequent tricuspid chordal rupture is noted, though the exact causal relationship and underlying mechanism remain uncertain.
journal: The American journal of case reports
title: Tricuspid Chordae Tendineae Rupture Detected After Repair of a Delayed Traumatic Left Ventricular Aneurysm: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major limitation after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents (DESs). However, long-term patency data after chronic total occlusion (CTO) PCI are limited despite high ISR risk. We evaluated long-term ISR incidence and predictors after CTO PCI.
METHODS: This prospective single-centre study (NCT07473596) included patients with successful CTO PCI and DES implantation in 2014-2021. Selected survivors underwent protocol-driven surveillance with coronary computed tomography angiography ≥3 years after the index procedure, with suspected ISR confirmed by invasive coronary angiography (ICA). ISR was also identified through clinically indicated ICA during follow-up in all patients. Patient-, lesion-, and procedure-related ISR predictors were analysed.
RESULTS: The study included 294 patients (median age 66 years (IQR 57-74), 79.9% male) and 294 analysed CTO stents. Median clinical and imaging follow-up were 7.1 (IQR 5.1-8.9) and 4.4 (IQR 3.2-6.2) years, respectively. Follow-up imaging covered 186 patients and 186 analysed CTO stents (63.3%). ISR was diagnosed in 40 stents (13.6%). Aalen-Johansen cumulative ISR incidence was 4.8% (95% CI 2.9-7.9), 10.2% (95% CI 7.1-14.5), and 12.9% (95% CI 9.3-18.0) at 3, 5, and 8 years, respectively. Atrial fibrillation (HR 3.71, 95% CI 1.74-7.91, p < 0.001) and in-stent CTO (HR 3.51, 95% CI 1.53-8.04, p = 0.003) were independently associated with ISR.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term ISR after CTO PCI was infrequent in this high-risk cohort, although estimates should be interpreted in the context of selected imaging follow-up among survivors. ISR was independently associated with atrial fibrillation and in-stent CTO at the index procedure.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
title: Long-term incidence and predictors of in-stent restenosis after chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention: a cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis (As) is the most common valvular heart disease in developed countries, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has expanded across surgical risk groups. However, procedure-related complications remain clinically important, and their reported incidence and management have evolved with newer-generation devices and techniques. This review summarizes major TAVR complications, including their incidence and pathophysiology, risk factors, clinical impact, prevention and management, and outlines remaining knowledge gaps.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted for studies published between 2012 and 2026, including randomized trials, registries, cohort studies, and systematic reviews.
RESULTS: Major complications reviewed included Stroke, Delirium, Conduction disturbances (CD) and Arrhythmias, Bleeding/Vascular(access) site injuries/Paravalvular leak (PVL), Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), Structural valve degeneration and thrombosis, Infective Endocarditis (IE) and Coronary Obstruction (CO).
CONCLUSIONS: TAVR complications remain multifactorial, and their incidence and management continue to shift with device evolution and procedural experience. Optimized patient selection, procedural refinement, frailty assessment, and individualized antithrombotic strategies remain important areas for improving outcomes.
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
title: Latest findings on complications following trans- catheter aortic valve replacement: A literature review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loeffler endocarditis is a form of restrictive cardiomyopathy that affects up to half of patients with hypereosinophilic syndromes. Patients undergoing treatment of Loeffler endocarditis with immunosuppression are at increased risk of mixed cardiogenic and septic shock due to its restrictive ventricular physiology and treatment with immunosuppressive therapy.
CASE SUMMARY: A 64-year-old female with peripheral eosinophilia and heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction reported 6 months of fatigue, worsening lower extremity oedema, palpitations, dyspnoea on exertion, and orthopnoea. She was diagnosed with Loeffler endocarditis based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and was initiated on high-dose prednisone and rituximab. While undergoing treatment of a subsequent angioinvasive fungal infection, she developed mixed cardiogenic and septic shock requiring inotropic support and broad-spectrum antimicrobials. She was eventually weaned off inotropic support and was continued on long-term posaconazole for the angioinvasive fungal infection.
DISCUSSION: Patients undergoing treatment of Loeffler endocarditis with immunosuppression are at an increased risk of mixed cardiogenic and septic shock. Late-stage Loeffler endocarditis predisposes to cardiogenic shock due to restrictive ventricular physiology and thrombi obliterating the ventricular cavities, while immunosuppressive therapy increases risk of opportunistic infections. If immunosuppression is initiated before ventricular fibrosis occurs, progression of Loeffler endocarditis can be halted or reversed.
title: Loeffler endocarditis complicated by cardiogenic shock and angioinvasive Fusarium fujikuroi infection: a case report.

abstract:
AIMS: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides excellent resolution at the cost of shallow penetration, limiting its ability for plaque burden (PB) assessment. A deep learning (DL) algorithm was therefore developed to provide fully automated assessment of PB and vessel size from OCT. We aimed to perform a head-to-head comparison of AI-powered OCT vs. intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for PB quantification, using histopathology as the reference standard.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Ten post-mortem human hearts were harvested. All 29 major epicardial coronary arteries were perfused and underwent OCT and IVUS pullbacks. After imaging, the arteries were serially sectioned at 1-mm intervals for histopathology. Lumen and vessel contours were derived fully automatically from OCT using the DL algorithm and semi-automatically from IVUS. Histopathological measurements were obtained by experienced analysts. Statistical analyses accounted for within-patient clustering. A total of 852 paired OCT-IVUS histopathology cross-sections were obtained. AI-powered OCT showed strong correlations with histopathology for the assessment of lumen area (r = 0.89 [95% CI: 0.88-0.91]), vessel area (r = 0.85 [95% CI: 0.83-0.87]), and PB (r = 0.76 [95% CI: 0.73-0.79]). The corresponding correlations between IVUS and histopathology were 0.90 (95% CI: 0.89-0.92), 0.86 (95% CI: 0.84-0.88), and 0.79 (95% CI: 0.76-0.81), respectively. Comparisons of the OCT-histopathology and IVUS-histopathology correlation coefficients yielded P = 0.336 for lumen area, P = 0.444 for vessel area, and P = 0.161 for PB. Both OCT and IVUS showed good diagnostic performance in identifying PB > 65%, with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve being 0.92 (95% CI: 0.90-0.94) and 0.92 (95% CI: 0.88-0.95), respectively.
CONCLUSION: In this histopathology validation study of 10 post-mortem human hearts, AI-powered OCT enabled fully automated plaque burden quantification and correlated strongly with histopathology, with no statistically significant difference between the OCT-histopathology and IVUS-histopathology correlations.
title: AI-powered optical coherence tomography shows similar performance to intravascular ultrasound for plaque burden quantification: head-to-head benchmark study against histopathology of native coronary arteries.

abstract: Background Non-compliant (NC) balloon catheters are widely used during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for lesion preparation and stent optimization because they allow controlled high-pressure dilation. However, real-world clinical data describing the procedural performance and short-term clinical outcomes of NC balloon catheters across diverse patient and lesion characteristics remain limited. This study evaluated the observed procedural performance, device performance characteristics, and short-term clinical outcomes associated with the use of the Optima NC non-compliant percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) balloon catheter (Translumina Therapeutics Private Limited, New Delhi, India) during routine PCI. Methods This multicenter, retrospective, single-arm observational study included patients aged ≥18 years who underwent PCI using at least one Optima NC PTCA balloon catheter at four cardiology centers in India between January and June 2024. Eligible patients had ≥80% coronary artery stenosis requiring PCI. The primary endpoint was procedural success, defined as successful balloon delivery, inflation, and retrieval without major procedural complications, together with achievement of final Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade III flow. Secondary endpoints included device success, operator-assessed device performance characteristics, and clinical outcomes through three months of follow-up. Results Of 216 patients screened, 196 (90.7%) were included in the final analysis, and 20 (9.3%) were excluded because of incomplete clinical or procedural information. The mean age was 59.20 ± 11.74 years, and 151 (77.0%) patients were male. Acute coronary syndrome was present in 191 (97.45%) patients, and multivessel disease in 111 (56.63%). The left anterior descending artery (LAD) was the most frequently treated vessel (112 (57.14%) patients). Procedural success was achieved in 193/196 (98.5%) procedures, while final TIMI grade III flow was achieved in 196/196 (100%) procedures. Device success was achieved in 193/196 (98.5%) procedures. No major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were reported during the index procedure or at discharge. During follow-up, one myocardial infarction (0.51%) was reported at one month, while one target lesion failure (TLF) (0.51%) and one cardiac death (0.51%) were reported at three months. Conclusion In this multicenter real-world cohort, the Optima NC PTCA balloon catheter demonstrated high observed procedural and device success, with favorable operator-assessed performance and few clinical events during short-term follow-up. Given the retrospective single-arm design and absence of a comparator, these findings are descriptive and do not establish comparative efficacy, superiority, or long-term safety. Prospective comparative studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are warranted to further characterize the clinical performance of the device.
title: Clinical Performance and Safety of the Optima Non-compliant Percutaneous Transluminal Coronary Angioplasty Balloon in Contemporary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Multicenter Real-World Study.

abstract: Stroke prevention after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) requires balancing cardioembolic protection against recurrent cerebral bleeding. Randomized evidence indicates that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) substantially reduce ischemic stroke compared with no anticoagulation but may increase recurrent ICH in susceptible patients. Importantly, previous ICH does not represent a uniform biological risk. Deep hemorrhage related to hypertensive arteriopathy, lobar hemorrhage associated with cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), mixed small-vessel disease, and hemorrhage from a treatable cause have different recurrence profiles. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) markers, including cerebral microbleed distribution, cortical superficial siderosis, convexity subarachnoid hemorrhage, lacunes, and enlarged perivascular spaces, can help characterize cerebral bleeding vulnerability, although no single marker should determine treatment. This editorial proposes an etiology-first, MRI-informed framework for selecting among restarting a DOAC, considering left atrial appendage closure (LAAC), and withholding long-term antithrombotic therapy. LAAC is not a risk-free alternative because it carries procedural risks and generally requires short-term antithrombotic treatment. Until prospective trials validate phenotype-specific pathways, ICH etiology and MRI phenotype should inform multidisciplinary, individualized, and preference-sensitive decisions.
title: Not All Brain Bleeds Are Equal: An Etiology-First Framework for Stroke Prevention After Intracerebral Hemorrhage.

abstract: A 64-year-old male with Stage III urothelial carcinoma of the right ureter presented to the emergency department 3 weeks after a single cycle of combined enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab with chest tightness, neck weakness, drop head, and myalgias. Laboratory findings included markedly elevated high-sensitivity troponin I, creatine phosphokinase, lactate dehydrogenase, and transaminases. Electrocardiography showed anterolateral ST depression and left anterior fascicular block, which was new as compared to a prior tracing. He was managed in the cardiovascular intensive care unit. Cardiac catheterization revealed concurrent 90% mid-left anterior descending artery stenosis, treated with drug-eluting stent placement. Endomyocardial biopsy confirmed focal moderate lymphocytic myocarditis. Cardiac MRI demonstrated mildly reduced biventricular function and a non-ischemic pattern of late gadolinium enhancement consistent with myocarditis sequelae. Given the overlapping multisystem presentation, a multidisciplinary team (cardiology, neurology, and oncology) elected to treat with high-dose methylprednisolone (1 g QOD x 5 days), the guideline-recommended first-line therapy for ICI-associated myocarditis, and intravenous immunoglobulin (400 mg/kg QOD x 5 days), with biochemical improvement. IVIG was added given clinical concern for possible neuromuscular junction involvement in the setting of concurrent myositis and possible overlap syndrome, reflecting a precautionary approach to a potentially rapidly progressive presentation. Myasthenia gravis was considered but not confirmed: repeated neurological examinations demonstrated no fatigable weakness, and serology was negative for acetylcholine receptor binding and muscle-specific kinase antibodies. Both implicated agents were permanently discontinued. This case illustrates the spectrum and severity of multisystem immune-related toxicity from combined antibody-drug conjugate and immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
title: Confirmed Myocarditis-Myositis Overlap Without Myasthenia Gravis: Evaluating for Triple M Syndrome Following Combined Enfortumab Vedotin and Pembrolizumab Therapy.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Older patients often present with complex coronary artery disease alongside multiple comorbidities. There is limited data on the outcomes of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) in octogenarians. We aim to investigate the in-hospital and 1-year outcomes following successful CTO-PCI in octogenarians.
METHODS: Consecutive patients who had successful CTO-PCI at a single center between 01.2017 and 12.2022 were divided into two groups: octogenarians (age ≥ 80 and < 90 years, n = 123) and a control group (age < 80 years, n = 612). Periprocedural complications, in-hospital major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and 1-year target lesion failure (TLF) were investigated.
RESULTS: Octogenarians had a higher prevalence of arterial hypertension (96.7% vs. 91.2%, p = 0.036), atrial fibrillation (28.5% vs. 12.1%, p < 0.001), and chronic kidney disease (CKD) (34.1% vs. 16.5%, p < 0.001) compared to younger counterparts. The rate of failed CTO recanalization was higher in octogenarians (18.5% vs. 8.2%, p < 0.001). Incidence of in-hospital MACCE and periprocedural complications was comparable between the study groups, except for a numerically higher in-hospital mortality in octogenarians (2.4% vs. 0.8%, p = 0.114), and a higher incidence of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) (11.4% vs. 4.9%, p = 0.006). At 1 year, TLF did not differ significantly between the study arms (16.2% vs. 12.3%, aHR 1.52; CI 0.81-2.84, p = 0.191). Notably, higher cardiac mortality rates were observed in the octogenarian arm (7.6% vs. 2.7%, HR 2.82; CI 1.13-7.08, p = 0.027).
CONCLUSION: Despite numerically higher in-hospital mortality in octogenarians, CTO-PCI in those patients was performed with comparable periprocedural, and acute adverse outcomes, as well as 1-year TLF, to their younger counterparts. Octogenarians remain inherently at a higher long-term mortality risk. Graphical Abstract available for this article.
GOV IDENTIFIER: NCT06957613 (retrospectively registered, 03/05/2025).
title: In-Hospital and One-Year Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Coronary Occlusion in Octogenarians.

abstract: Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy is now widely used for iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) across several device platforms, and every procedure yields intact human thrombus that is routinely discarded. Whether this material can be developed into a translational resource linking thrombus biology to clinical outcome has not been systematically addressed. A narrative, non-systematic review was performed. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2010 to August 2026) for studies addressing the biology, histopathology and translational analysis of mechanically retrieved venous thrombi, supplemented by reference-list, trial-registry and congress hand-searching. Published venous series remain small and largely confined to descriptive histology, disconnected from longitudinal outcomes. Intra-thrombus biology could address venous-specific questions that peripheral biomarkers and imaging alone cannot: post-thrombotic syndrome, incomplete recanalization, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and cancer-associated thrombosis. A device-agnostic framework is proposed, comprising structured intra-procedural sampling at the level of the case rather than the anatomical region, centralized specimen processing under harmonized quality standards, a tiered analytic pipeline anchored on quantitative immunohistochemistry, paired peripheral-biomarker collection, pre-specified hypotheses with feasibility-based sample sizes, and biobank infrastructure embedded in existing trial platforms. The equivalent programme in arterial thrombectomy supplies transferable methodology, subject to explicit boundary conditions. The retrieved venous thrombus is among the more underused translational specimens in vascular medicine. A standardized, registry-embedded characterization framework could accelerate progress toward precision venous thrombosis medicine.
title: The retrieved venous thrombus as a translational platform: a methodologic roadmap for venous immunothrombosis.

abstract: A 26-year-old woman presented with palpitations and exertional dyspnea. Echocardiography suggested an inferior sinus venosus atrial septal defect, while cardiac CT angiography revealed a 26 × 32 mm defect with inferior vena cava overriding, a persistent left superior vena cava draining into the left atrium, and a coronary sinus with an intact roof draining independently into the left atrium. Surgical correction involved patch closure of the atrial septal defect and redirection of both venous structures to the right atrium. Postoperative imaging demonstrated no residual interatrial shunt and confirmed patency of the redirected persistent left superior vena cava. This case highlights the essential role of multimodality imaging in defining complex congenital venous anatomy and guiding surgical management .
keywords: inferior sinus venosus atrial septal defect
title: Anomalous Coronary Sinus and Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava Drainage Into the Left Atrium: A Multimodality Imaging Case.

abstract: Currently, myocardial infarction is commonly detected via traditional biomarker analysis, electrocardiography, and echocardiography. In general, conventional clinical approaches are limited by insufficient early-stage sensitivity and time-consuming procedures, thereby delaying therapeutic interventions. To address the above-mentioned drawbacks, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in both ultra-early biomarkers and novel high-sensitivity detection platforms. A panel of ultra-early biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity (e.g., GPBB, cMyC, cfDNA, MPO, D-dimer, miRNAs, and lncRNAs) is explicitly identified in this review. Recent progress in nano-based, graphene-based, and chemical biosensors for biomarker detection is further elaborated. The application of these biosensors delivers amplified signal outputs, enhanced sensitivity, shortened detection time, multiplex detection capability, and successful miniaturization of detection devices. This review also analyzes the integration of artificial intelligence models with conventional diagnostic modalities (electrocardiography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging) and gold-standard diagnostic methods (biomarker testing, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, coronary computed tomography). Such integrated analytical strategies enable objective, rapid, and early diagnosis. When embedde into wearable monitoring devices, these technologies support non-invasive and continuous real-time monitoring and generate preemptive clinical alerts with ultra-high signal sensitivity. Ultimately, this article establishes a comprehensive framework for the ultra-early diagnosis of myocardial infarction by integrating screened ultra-early biomarkers and innovative high-sensitivity detection techniques.
journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
title: Ultra-early diagnosis recently developments of acute myocardial infarction: Emerging biomarkers and advanced sensing technologies.

abstract: Objective: To investigate the effect of mycophenolate mofetil on in-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease. Methods: Patients with autoimmune liver diseases (AILD) [including AIH, primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), and overlap syndrome] complicated with coronary heart disease who underwent PCI at Tianjin Medical University Second Hospital between January 2019 and December 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, they were divided into mycophenolate mofetil group and non-mycophenolate mofetil group according to postoperative use of mycophenolate mofetil, and followed up until March 31, 2026 to compare the baseline characteristics of the two groups of patients. Firth penalized likelihood-corrected Cox regression models and Fine-Gray competing risk models (with all-cause death as the competing event) were used to evaluate the association between mycophenolate mofetil use and ISR after PCI in patients with AIH and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease (because few patients with PBC and PSC received mycophenolate mofetil, this analysis only included patients with AIH and overlap syndrome). The Benjamini-Hochberg method was applied for multiple comparison correction to calculate the FDR q values. A 1∶1 propensity score matching (PSM) was employed to balance baseline characteristics between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier method was used to plot survival curves to compare the ISR-free survival rates. Sensitivity analysis was performed on all AILD patients to validate the robustness of the results. Results: A total of 172 patients with AILD complicated with coronary heart disease were enrolled, including 48 cases (27.9%) in the mycophenolate mofetil group and 124 cases (72.1%) in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The follow-up duration [M(Q1, Q3)] was 13 (7, 16) and 10 (5, 16) months respectively. The proportion of patients with hyperlipidemia [12.5% (6/48) vs 32.3% (40/124), P=0.009] and diabetes mellitus [8.3% (4/48) vs 27.4% (34/124), P=0.007] were lower in the mycophenolate mofetil group than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group, while the proportion of patients with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP)>0.8 mg/L [47.9% (23/48) vs 27.4% (34/124), P=0.010], previous use of prednisone [79.2% (38/48) vs 22.6% (28/124), P<0.001] and azathioprine [54.2% (26/48) vs 9.7% (12/124), P<0.001] were higher than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The levels of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [59.5 (35.5, 76.8) vs 43.0 (32.0, 52.7) U/L, P=0.002] and immunoglobulin G (IgG) [19.6 (15.0, 26.0) vs 15.2 (14.0, 16.8) g/L, P=0.006] were higher in the mycophenolate mofetil group.
