Among 100 patients with AIH and overlap syndrome (82 and 18 cases, respectively), mycophenolate mofetil use was associated with a reduced risk of ISR in both Firth-corrected Cox regression model and competing risk model (Firth-corrected Cox model: HR=0.17, 95%CI: 0.04-0.51, FDR q=0.004; competing risk model: sHR=0.14, 95%CI: 0.05-0.43, FDR q=0.003). After PSM (40 cases in each group), there was no statistically significant difference in all covariates between the two groups (all SMD<0.1). After PSM, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that the follow-up duration was 12 (7, 15) months in the mycophenolate mofetil group and 8 (3, 17) months in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The 12-month ISR-free survival rate was higher in the mycophenolate mofetil group than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group (97.0% vs 64.5%, P<0.001). In the sensitivity analysis, mycophenolate mofetil use is associated with a reduced risk of ISR (Firth-corrected Cox regression model: HR=0.29, 95%CI: 0.09-0.73, FDR q=0.030; competing risk model: sHR=0.26, 95%CI: 0.10-0.72, FDR q=0.022). Conclusion: Mycophenolate mofetil use is associated with a reduced risk of ISR after PCI in patients with AIH and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease.
title: [Effect of mycophenolate mofetil on in-stent restenosis after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with autoimmune hepatitis and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease].

abstract: Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis, with self-expanding valves (SEV) and balloon-expandable valves (BEV) representing the two major platforms. However, their comparative clinical and hemodynamic performance remains uncertain. We systematically searched four electronic databases through August 2026 for studies comparing SEV and BEV in patients undergoing TAVR. The primary outcomes were permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and change in mean pressure gradient (MPG), while secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, paravalvular leakage (PVL), heart failure hospitalization, coronary obstruction, and prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). Twenty-three studies involving 21,609 patients were included. Compared with BEV, SEV was associated with a significantly greater reduction in MPG (MD -4.48, 95% CI -5.29 to -3.67; P < 0.0001) and lower risks of moderate (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.42-0.75) and severe PPM (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.44). Conversely, SEV was associated with higher risks of PPI (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.14-1.72; P < 0.0001), moderate-to-severe PVL (RR 2.28, 95% CI 1.65-3.14; P < 0.0001), and a small but significant increase in all-cause mortality. No significant differences were observed in MACE, stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or coronary obstruction..
title: Comparative Outcomes of Self-Expanding Versus Balloon-Expandable Valves in Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate and efficient risk stratification essential across the care pathway. Numerous tools support emergency triage, disease assessment, procedural decision-making, long-term prevention, atrial fibrillation management, and evaluation of functional status, but no single model is applicable across all clinical settings or populations. This clinician-oriented review categorizes and critically compares commonly used cardiovascular assessment and risk-prediction tools, including History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, Troponin, Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events, and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction for emergency triage; Agatston, Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery for anatomical and clinical assessment; European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation, Society of Thoracic Surgeons, and Revised Cardiac Risk Index, for procedural risk; and Framingham, the pooled cohort equations implemented in the Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Risk Estimator, Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2, QResearch Cardiovascular Risk Algorithm 3, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs for long-term prediction. Congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75, diabetes, stroke/transient ischemic attack (2 points), congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 (2 points), diabetes, stroke/TIA (2 points), vascular disease, age 65-74, sex category (female), and hypertension, abnormal renal/liver function, stroke, bleeding history, labile international normalized ratio, elderly, drugs/alcohol, are discussed in the context of atrial fibrillation, alongside New York Heart Association and the Seattle Angina Questionnaire as measures of functional status and quality of life. For each tool, we examine its clinical purpose, principal variables, strengths, limitations, practical applications, and areas of overlap. Differences in implementation across healthcare systems and patient populations are considered to support context-appropriate selection. Persistent limitations include poor standardization, reliance on data that may be unavailable in resource-constrained settings, limited transportability, and incomplete integration into clinical workflows. Greater harmonization, external validation, digital automation, and the careful incorporation of biomarkers and artificial intelligence may support more accessible, dynamic, and personalized cardiovascular risk assessment.
title: Choosing Cardiovascular Assessment and Risk-Prediction Tools Across the Care Pathway: A Clinician-Oriented Review.

abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia in clinical practice and an independent, well-established risk factor for ischemic stroke. However, restoring sinus rhythm via cardioversion does not eliminate this risk. Cardioversion itself transiently increases thromboembolic risk more than 10-fold, driven by atrial stunning, a state in which the left atrium and left atrial appendage remain mechanically dysfunctional despite normalized electrical activity seen on an electrocardiogram. Retrospective data show that thromboembolic events are clustered heavily within the first 2 weeks postcardioversion, supporting the near-universal recommendation of at least 4 weeks of continued therapeutic anticoagulation postcardioversion for AF duration more than 12 to 48 hours, regardless of baseline stroke risk score. Beyond this initial 4-week recommendation, the decision to continue anticoagulation is based on a comprehensive assessment of the patient's thromboembolic risk profile, rather than rhythm status or cardioversion success. Multiple trials have demonstrated a significant increase in the incidence of ischemic strokes in patients who had a premature discontinuation of anticoagulation postcardioversion. Additionally, having a prior stroke, the heaviest weighted risk-stratification variable, favors indefinite anticoagulation regardless of postcardioversion rhythm outcome. Current guidelines provide a framework for approaching postcardioversion anticoagulation, including a fixed 4-week anticoagulation course encompassing the atrial stunning period, followed by individualized risk-stratification to determine the indication for continued anticoagulation. Nevertheless, future research is still required to better elucidate whether anticoagulation can be safely discontinued after completion of the recommended 4-week postcardioversion anticoagulation course in patients with a prior AF-related stroke.
title: The Illusion of Recovery From Atrial Fibrillation, a Review of Postcardioversion Anticoagulation Guidelines.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) has been associated with greater lesion complexity and lower success rates in chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). In native-vessel CTO PCI, prior CABG may also indicate greater preprocedural complexity and more advanced strategy planning. We examined whether prior CABG was associated with lesion complexity, strategy selection, procedural burden, and technical success in a contemporary multicenter registry.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospective multicenter CTO PCI registry including 1,800 consecutive native-vessel procedures performed between January 2020 and June 2025. Of these, 205 were performed in patients with prior CABG and 1,595 in patients without prior CABG. The primary endpoint was technical success, defined as final TIMI 3 flow with residual stenosis < 30%. The key secondary endpoint was procedural success, defined as technical success without in-hospital major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events.
RESULTS: Prior-CABG procedures had greater lesion complexity, more frequent planned retrograde/hybrid crossing, longer procedural and fluoroscopy times, higher dose-area product, and greater adjusted contrast use. Technical success was lower in prior-CABG procedures (85.9% vs. 93.3%, p < 0.001), as was procedural success (84.9% vs. 92.4%, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, prior CABG was independently associated with technical failure (adjusted OR, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.19-3.18; p = 0.008). Planned retrograde/hybrid strategy was also associated with technical failure (adjusted OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.81-4.40, p < 0.001), a finding interpreted as reflecting case selection and lesion difficulty rather than a causal effect of the strategy. In a companion model, prior CABG was independently associated with the selection of a planned retrograde/hybrid strategy (adjusted OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.40-2.96, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In native-vessel CTO PCI, prior CABG was associated with more complex lesions, more frequent retrograde/hybrid planning, greater procedural burden, and lower technical success. However, its incremental prognostic value beyond the J-CTO score was limited. Prior CABG should therefore be interpreted primarily as a marker of an unfavorable procedural phenotype rather than as a standalone risk-stratification tool.
title: Prior CABG and native-vessel CTO PCI: lesion complexity, strategy planning, procedural burden, and technical success in a multicenter registry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is a life-saving strategy for refractory cardiac arrest (CA), but the mortality rate is still high. Bowel ischemia is associated with the clinical outcomes, and few studies on bowel ischemia following ECPR have been reported.
METHODS: We reported 2 cases of bowel ischemia following ECPR. And we searched literature to describe the incidence, clinical features, and outcomes of bowel ischemia following ECPR. Demographic features, risk factors, clinical features, diagnostic methods, treatment and outcome were analyzed.
RESULTS: We described 2 patients developed bowel ischemia with recurred hematochezia at different phases post ECPR, conservative treatments were not effective, one patient received colectomy after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) weaning and recovered, and the other died without surgery. Our literature search found 3 publications. Non-occlusive mesenteric ischemia(NOMI) was more common for bowel ischemia following ECPR, and the incidence of NOMI in ECPR patients seemed higher than that in conventional CPR patients. Postmortem findings demonstrated signs of bowel ischemia within hours of ECPR. The incidence of bowel ischemia following ECPR could not be identified due to the variability among the studies.
CONCLUSION: Bowel ischemia may initiate early post ECPR, or occur insidiously during the therapeutic process, thus clinicians should have a high suspicion and low threshold for CT scan and endoscopy. Surgical timing for advanced bowel ischemia should be individualized.
title: Bowel ischemia following extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR): case reports and narrative review.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a preoperative machine learning model for predicting myocardial injury after hip replacement surgery in middle-aged and elderly patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 453 middle-aged and elderly patients were included. The clinical outcome was myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS). Feature selection was performed within the training set using recursive feature elimination. Based on the selected variables, nine machine learning models were constructed and compared. Model performance was evaluated using cross-validated AUC, repeated random split validation, calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curves. SHAP analysis was used to interpret feature contributions.
RESULTS: Eight preoperative features were ultimately retained for model construction. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM showed the best overall performance. The mean AUC from cross-validation and repeated random split validation was approximately 0.79, indicating moderate discriminative ability and providing the primary estimate of internal generalizability. In the single held-out internal test set, LightGBM achieved an AUC of 0.9468 (95% CI: 0.897-0.992), although this result was interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size and small number of positive events. The model also showed a relatively low Brier score of 0.061 and favorable net benefit on decision curve analysis within clinically relevant threshold ranges. SHAP analysis indicated that age was the most influential predictor of MINS.
CONCLUSIONS: This single-center study developed and internally validated a preoperative machine learning model for predicting myocardial injury after hip replacement surgery, which may support early risk stratification before surgery.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
title: Machine learning-based prediction of myocardial injury after hip replacement surgery: a single-center study with internal validation.

abstract: Endoscopic Endoclampassisted MViV can expand the armamentarium for complex redo mitral surgery, offering excellent early clinical and haemodynamic results in selected patients. A 50 year-old man with heavy alcohol and tobacco use and two previous mitral operations (repair, then bioprosthetic replacement eight years earlier) presented with progressive dyspnoea (NYHA III). Transthoracic and transoesophageal echocardiography revealed severe mixed stenosis/regurgitation of a 33 mm Medtronic Mosaic bioprothesis. No endocarditis was found preoperatively. After shared decisionmaking, minimally invasive videoassisted right minithoracotomy under endoaortic balloon occlusion (Endoclamp®) was planned. Intraoperatively, the degenerated valve was firmly embedded in the native annulus and could not be safely explanted. A 29 mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra transcatheter heart valve was therefore deployed inside the surgical frame under direct vision on cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Postdeployment echocardiography showed a mean gradient of 8 mmHg without paravalvular leak or LVOT compromise. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 2; aside from temporary difficulties in respiratory weaning, recovery was uneventful, and he was discharged home on day 9.
title: Valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement via totally endoscopic endoclamp-assisted approach after failed bioprosthetic mitral valve: a case report.

abstract: We report a 20-year-old man with a history of Kawasaki disease-related coronary aneurysm who developed acute myocardial infarction after one week of discontinuing aspirin and warfarin. This case highlights the catastrophic risk of even brief interruption of antithrombotic therapy in patients with Kawasaki disease-related coronary aneurysms. It also suggests that vulnerability during transition to adult care, particularly in terms of self-management and medication adherence, may contribute to such events.
title: Acute myocardial infarction after brief antithrombotic interruption in Kawasaki disease-related coronary aneurysm.

abstract: Thyroid storm is the most severe and life-threatening expression of thyrotoxicosis, and its diagnosis remains clinical. Although sinus tachycardia and atrial fibrillation dominate its cardiovascular manifestations, malignant ventricular arrhythmias are rare, and cardiorespiratory arrest as the presenting manifestation of Graves' disease has been reported only in a limited number of cases. We report the case of a 44-year-old man with a one-week history of symptoms consistent with hyperthyroidism who suffered a witnessed out-of-hospital cardiorespiratory arrest with ventricular fibrillation as the initial rhythm. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after three defibrillations, and urgent coronary angiography showed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe thyrotoxicosis with positive thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-receptor antibodies, and thyroid ultrasound findings supported the diagnosis of Graves' disease. Thyroid storm was suspected and treated empirically, but the diagnosis could not be confirmed: the Burch-Wartofsky score reached the diagnostic threshold only when post-arrest coma was included, and the Japan Thyroid Association criteria were not met. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and an ajmaline provocation test did not identify structural heart disease, myocarditis, or a Brugada pattern. Thyroid hormone excess was therefore considered the most likely precipitant of the arrhythmia, although causality cannot be proven. The patient was maintained on antithyroid therapy, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention following an individualized risk-benefit assessment. This case highlights the importance of considering thyrotoxicosis in the etiological workup of unexplained cardiac arrest. When a clearly established and reversible cause of the arrhythmia cannot be confirmed, management, including the decision on defibrillator implantation, should be based on an individualized risk-benefit assessment.
title: Cardiorespiratory Arrest in the Context of Graves' Disease: A Rare Presentation.

abstract: Ticagrelor is a reversible oral P2Y12 receptor inhibitor recommended in preference to clopidogrel for most patients with acute coronary syndrome. In addition to inhibiting platelets, it raises extracellular adenosine, which is thought to explain its underappreciated capacity to cause bradyarrhythmia. We report three consecutive patients with acute coronary syndrome who developed serious bradyarrhythmias after ticagrelor administration. The first, a 58-year-old woman treated with a drug-eluting stent to the left anterior descending artery, developed high-grade atrioventricular block with asystolic pauses that required a temporary pacing wire, after which ticagrelor was stopped, prasugrel was substituted, and she recovered. The second, a 48-year-old woman with an anterior myocardial infarction, had a cardiac arrest with complete heart block after ticagrelor loading, was resuscitated, paced temporarily, switched to prasugrel, and recovered. The third, a 77-year-old man with an inferoposterior and right ventricular myocardial infarction, had recurrent asystole and ventricular arrhythmia that persisted despite switching to prasugrel and required a permanent pacemaker. None of the patients were receiving an atrioventricular nodal blocking drug, and in every patient the treated coronary lesion was patent on a repeat angiogram, which made ongoing ischemia from stent failure an unlikely sole explanation. A formal Naranjo assessment rated the association as possible in each case. A ticagrelor-induced adverse effect should be considered in any patient who develops unexplained bradycardia or syncope after its administration. Early rhythm monitoring and prompt withdrawal are the key steps, and although the rhythm usually recovers, permanent pacing may be needed when conduction disease is superimposed on ischemic injury to the conduction system.
title: Ticagrelor-Induced Bradyarrhythmias in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Case Series of Three Patients.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mediastinal ectopic thyroid tissue is rare and is usually asymptomatic. Intratumoral hemorrhage causing acute mediastinal compression and cardiac arrest is extremely uncommon. We report a case of cardiac arrest caused by hemorrhage of a giant mediastinal ectopic thyroid, successfully managed with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and emergency surgical decompression by tumor removal.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 71-year-old woman with a long-standing anterior mediastinal tumor was transferred to our hospital because of dyspnea and shock after a fall. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a giant anterior mediastinal tumor occupying the left hemithorax, with active extravasation and marked mediastinal deviation. Transarterial embolization was performed; however, she developed cardiac arrest shortly after embolization, presumably due to rapid tumor enlargement and severe mediastinal compression caused by intratumoral hemorrhage. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation was immediately initiated, and VA-ECMO was established. Emergency tumor removal and hemostasis were performed through a 4th-intercostal clamshell incision. The tumor occupied almost the entire left thoracic cavity and was extensively adherent to the chest wall and mediastinum, with particularly firm adhesion to the left brachiocephalic vein. The tumor was removed with combined resection of the left brachiocephalic vein. Histopathological examination revealed benign ectopic thyroid tissue without malignant findings. The postoperative course was complicated by bleeding, infection, acute kidney injury, and prolonged impaired consciousness. Postoperative hypothyroidism was identified after pathological confirmation of ectopic thyroid tissue, and levothyroxine replacement was initiated. The patient was transferred to a rehabilitation hospital on POD 72 and is currently living at home 1 year after surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Giant mediastinal ectopic thyroid tissue can cause fatal circulatory collapse when complicated by intratumoral hemorrhage. Although the patient was in a critical condition, she was successfully rescued by VA-ECMO followed by emergency decompression through surgical tumor removal.
title: Life-Saving Emergency Decompression via a Clamshell Approach for Cardiac Arrest Caused by Hemorrhage of a Giant Mediastinal Ectopic Thyroid: A Case Report.

abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women's cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women's cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.
authors: American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
title: Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Despite successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI), early myocardial injury and stress may contribute to left ventricular dysfunction. The optimal timing of biomarker assessment after STEMI remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the early kinetics of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2), galectin-3 (Gal-3), mid-regional pro-adrenomedullin (MR-proADM), and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) during the first 96 h after STEMI and identify potentially informative sampling time points for future prognostic assessment. Secondary, exploratory objectives were to evaluate differences in biomarker concentrations according to symptom duration, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and infarct-related artery.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center, exploratory pilot study, patients aged 18-75 years with first STEMI treated with pPCI within 6 h of symptom onset were enrolled between September 2024 and November 2025. Blood samples were collected at admission and 12 ± 4, 24 ± 4, 48 ± 8, and 96 ± 8 h after pPCI. Biomarkers were measured by ELISA, with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) as a reference marker of myocardial injury.
RESULTS: Of 46 enrolled patients, 16 were excluded, mostly due to early discharge, and 30 patients with complete samples at all five time points were included in the analysis (mean age 57.9 ± 11.1 years; 66.7% male). sST2, MR-proADM, and hs-cTnI showed significant temporal variation (all p < 0.001), with the highest measured concentrations of sST2 at 12 h and of MR-proADM at 24 h. No significant change over time was found for Gal-3 and GDF-15. In exploratory analyses, sST2 and MR-proADM concentrations were higher in patients with LVEF < 40%, and sST2 concentrations were higher in patients with left anterior descending artery (LAD) infarction. Symptom duration was not associated with biomarker concentrations.
CONCLUSIONS: sST2 and MR-proADM show distinct early post-STEMI kinetics, suggesting potentially informative sampling windows for future prognostic studies. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these kinetics and the exploratory differences according to left ventricular function and infarct location, and to evaluate the prognostic value of these sampling windows with echocardiographic and clinical follow-up.
title: Temporal Dynamics of Emerging Cardiovascular Biomarkers in the Early Phase After Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Prospective Single-Center Pilot Study.

abstract: Background/Aim: The addition of an immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) to chemotherapy improves outcomes in both early-stage and metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, ICIs are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs), such as cardiotoxicity, raising concerns for patients receiving both anthracyclines and ICIs. We sought to determine if combining anthracycline and ICI in TNBC is associated with greater cardiotoxicity than anthracycline alone. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a large academic center. Two cohorts were analyzed: anthracycline plus ICI and anthracycline alone. Demographics, comorbidities, medications, cardiac imaging, and outcomes were reviewed. Time to adverse cardiac events were compared. Results: A total of 382 patients were included: 297 received anthracyclines without ICI, and 85 received both. There were no major differences in baseline characteristics. The rate of acute cardiac events was 3.4% in the anthracycline-alone cohort and 3.5% in the anthracycline-plus-ICI cohort (p > 0.99) over a median of 1232 days of follow up (median of 1336 days in the anthracycline only group; median of 704 days in the ICI group). No significant differences in acute heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, myocarditis, or pericardial effusion were observed. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in cardiac event-free survival (p = 0.60). Furthermore, there was no significant difference in time to cardiac events between the two groups following competing risk analysis when accounting for both prior coronary artery disease (HR = 1.32, 95% CI: [0.42, 4.14], p = 0.64) and age (HR = 1.64, 95% CI: [0.52, 5.19], p = 0.40). Conclusions: This single-institution analysis did not identify a significant increase in cardiotoxicity with the addition of an ICI to anthracycline therapy in patients with TNBC. Active surveillance for cardiotoxicities should continue in patients receiving ICI in addition to anthracycline therapy.
title: Cardiotoxicity of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors with Anthracycline Chemotherapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.

abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Clinical studies have shown that patients who had sepsis with COVID-19 infection had worse clinical outcomes; however, there is a paucity of data on the association between concurrent COVID-19 infection and outcomes among patients with sepsis. Hence, we conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2020 through 2022 to evaluate the association between concurrent COVID-19 infection and outcomes among patients with sepsis.
METHODS: Adult hospitalizations with sepsis were identified using ICD-10-CM codes; hospitalizations with septic shock were excluded, and the remaining cohort was stratified by concurrent COVID-19 infection status. Survey-weighted multivariate regression analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Patients with sepsis with concurrent COVID-19 infection had worse outcomes with higher mortality rate (15.6% vs. 5.4%; aOR 3.70; 95% CI 3.62-3.79), higher need for invasive ventilation (13.1% vs. 6.5%) and NIV (non-invasive ventilation) (10.2% vs. 4.9%), higher incidence of acute kidney injury (37.6% vs. 36.7%), acute respiratory failure (57.5% vs. 20.3%), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) (0.4% vs. 0.3%), cardiac arrest (3.1% vs. 1.5%), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) (7.9% vs. 0.4%), higher need for renal replacement therapy (4.9% vs. 4.5%), tracheostomy (1.6% vs. 0.6%), extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) (0.2% vs. 0.04%), longer length of hospital stay (10.3 days vs. 7.6 days), and higher total charges ($127,632 vs. $93,735, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: The results demonstrate that COVID-19 infection was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes among those hospitalized with sepsis. These results underscore the need for early recognition, aggressive treatment, and targeted therapy in this high-risk clinical group.
title: Clinical Outcomes and Hospital Resource Utilization Among Patients with Sepsis and COVID-19 Infection: Insights from the United States National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2020-2022.

abstract: Background/Objectives: New-onset atrial fibrillation is a common complication of acute myocardial infarction and is associated with increased mortality, heart failure, and recurrent cardiovascular events. Prediction models for the occurrence of atrial fibrillation may facilitate early risk stratification, improve patient monitoring, and support personalized therapeutic decision-making in clinical practice. Methods: A prospective study included 150 patients with acute myocardial infarction admitted within 24 h of symptom onset. Clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic data were collected, and a machine learning model was developed to predict new-onset atrial fibrillation. Model performance was evaluated using ROC-AUC, while SHAP analysis was applied to identify and quantify the contribution of individual predictors. Results: The machine learning model demonstrated excellent predictive performance, achieving an accuracy of 97.0%, ROC-AUC of 0.991, and precision-recall AUC of 0.991 in the independent test set. SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and permutation importance analyses identified the E/e' ratio, left ventricular mass index, left ventricular ejection fraction, left atrial volume index, oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde and superoxide dismutase), NT-proBNP, and complete revascularization as the most influential predictors of new-onset atrial fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction. Conclusions: Machine learning combined with SHAP-based explainability showed high potential for predicting new-onset atrial fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction. This approach may improve individualized risk assessment and clinical decision-making, pending validation in larger multicenter cohorts.
title: Prediction of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Machine Learning Approach.

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an alternative approach to stroke prevention in selected patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. This single-centre retrospective study describes device implantation, peri-procedural complications and clinical outcomes during the first year after Watchman FLX implantation. Methods: We analysed 100 consecutive patients who underwent LAAO with the Watchman FLX device at Helios Frankenwaldklinik-Hospital, Kronach, Germany, between 2021 and 2024. The primary endpoint was device implantation success, defined as correct device deployment and implantation. The secondary safety endpoint was a composite of major peri-procedural complications within 72 h. Additional clinical outcomes were strokes and mortality at 30 days and one year. Results: The mean age was 70.7 ± 6.5 years, and 47% of patients were female. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.9 ± 1.4, and the mean HAS-BLED score was 4.1 ± 1.0. Device implantation was successful in 100% (95% CI 96.4-100%). The reported peri-procedural complication rate was 7% (95% CI 2.9-13.9%), including major bleeding in 6% (95% CI 2.2-12.6%) and pericardial tamponade in 1% (95% CI 0.0-5.4%). Thirty-day mortality was 2% (95% CI 0.2-7.0%), with no reported strokes (0%; 95% CI 0.0-3.6%). One-year mortality was 11% (95% CI 5.6-18.8%), with one reported stroke (1%; 95% CI 0.0-5.4%). Conclusions: Watchman FLX implantation was achieved in all patients in this cohort. Bleeding was the most frequently reported peri-procedural complication. The low observed stroke proportion should be interpreted alongside the 11% one-year mortality and incomplete imaging surveillance. This uncontrolled descriptive study cannot establish comparative efficacy or comprehensive device safety.
title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion with the Watchman FLX Device: A Single-Centre Retrospective Analysis of Procedural and One-Year Clinical Outcomes.

abstract: Chronic total occlusions (CTOs) represent one of the most technically demanding areas of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Despite advances in equipment and operator expertise, CTO PCI remains associated with lower procedural success rates and a higher risk of complications than non-CTO PCI. This review summarizes emerging techniques and technologies designed to improve procedural efficiency, safety, and outcomes in contemporary, personalized patient care. Recent innovations span multiple domains of CTO PCI. The minimalistic hybrid approach (MHA) aims to reduce vascular complications by minimizing the number of access sites and the sheath size. Novel perforation management strategies, including the cut balloon technique (CBT) and the condom technique, offer simple, low-cost options for distal vessel sealing, supported so far only by small series and technical reports. Advanced re-entry methods, such as tip-detection, antegrade dissection and re-entry (TD-ADR), integrate intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) to enhance precision. HydroDynamic contrast recanalization (HDR) revisits hydraulic dissection with a controlled, microcatheter-based contrast strategy whose safety profile remains to be established. The microcatheter anchor technique (MAT) has been proposed to facilitate retrograde CTO PCI in post-CABG anatomy. New plaque-modifying strategies, including RODIN-CUT and ORCAS, leverage high-pressure cutting balloon inflations under real-time IVUS guidance. Additional technologies, such as Plasmawire™, Shockwave Javelin®, and Hertz Contact intravascular lithotripsy (IVL), may expand the armamentarium for crossing and modifying complex CTO lesions, although CTO-specific clinical data are very limited (for Javelin, a 20-patient first-in-human coronary series). CT coronary angiography (CTCA) continues to improve pre-procedural planning, while drug-coated balloons (DCBs) show promise in selected de novo CTO lesions, although the evidence remains limited to retrospective series. Taken together, this rapid pace of innovation is steadily widening the procedural toolkit available for CTO PCI and may improve outcomes. Evidence for most of these techniques comes from case reports, small single-center series, and early-phase single-arm studies. It suggests feasibility in selected patients, but safety data are limited, and some reports signal concerns, including tamponade after the cut balloon technique and a higher perforation rate in a registry of the Carlino technique. The place of these techniques in routine practice will become clear only once larger, multicenter trials are completed.
title: Novel Techniques and Emerging Technologies in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Structured, Narrative Review.

abstract: Background: Surgically implanted microaxial flow pumps are increasingly being utilized to treat cardiogenic shock; however, data on their use in the realm of cardiac surgery are scarce. We report our single-institution experience in low-ejection-fraction, high-risk patients with a planned weaning strategy from cardiopulmonary bypass directly to Impella 5.5 inserted via the brachiocephalic artery or ascending aorta following corrective cardiac surgery. Methods: A prospectively maintained institutional database was queried from 2022 through to 2025. Primary endpoints included feasibility of implantation, weaning rate, and bedside removal; secondary endpoints included freedom from all-cause mortality at discharge and 1 year, in-hospital thromboembolic complications, postoperative pharmacologic hemodynamic support using vasoactive inotropic score (VIS), de novo renal failure, and revision for bleeding. Descriptive statistics were applied. Results: Sixteen patients (median age 66.5 years [IQR; interquartile range, 52.5-70.0], STS score 12.1% [IQR, 5.3-14.2%] and EF 20.0% [IQR, 15.0-31.5%]) underwent coronary revascularization (n = 6), valve procedures (n = 4) or a combination thereof (n = 6) and were weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass to Impella 5.5 implanted via the ascending aorta (25%) or brachiocephalic artery (75%). Primary endpoints were met in 100% (feasibility of implantation), 94% (weaning rate), and 100% (bedside removal). In terms of secondary endpoints, freedom from mortality at discharge and one year was 94.8%; there were two non-disabling strokes (12.6%) while still on Impella 5.5 support; the median VIS at the time of ICU arrival was 12.8 (IQR 10.8-22.1); renal failure occurred in two patients and four patients required revision for bleeding. Conclusions: Impella 5.5-supported cardiac surgery appears safe and may open a new avenue for high-risk patients.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Planned Impella 5.5 Support via Brachiocephalic Artery or Ascending Aorta for Low Ejection Fraction, High-Risk Cardiac Surgery.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) increases mortality but remains undertreated due to high surgical risks. Transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions (TTVI) offer safer alternatives, improving functional status and quality of life. However, many candidates for TTVI have trans-tricuspid CIED leads that may interfere with procedural imaging and device deployment and may be exposed to dislodgement, entrapment, or jailing. Evidence regarding both clinical outcomes and postprocedural CIED function in this population remains limited. Existing trial evidence for this population is scarce, requiring further safety analysis. To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis to address the comparative risk of complications and residual TR in patients with vs. without CIEDs.
METHODS: We searched for relevant articles up to March 2026 from PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. Two independent reviewers extracted data from the selected studies, including baseline information, outcomes, comorbidities, hospitalization metrics, TR severity, and complications. All data analyses were performed using R version 4.4.1.
RESULTS: Ten studies comprising 5415 patients were included. Nine comparative studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis, whereas one single-arm study contributed only to the narrative synthesis of CIED-specific mechanical and electrical outcomes. In patients undergoing TTVI, across two studies, patients with CIEDs had a nominally lower risk of single-leaflet device attachment (RR 0.34, 95% CI 0.12-0.94; nominal p = 0.037); however, this exploratory finding should be considered hypothesis-generating. However, no statistically significant differences were observed between groups for cardiovascular death (RR 1.30, p = 0.815), device embolization (RR 1.62, p = 0.666), device malposition (RR 1.10, p = 0.909), stroke (RR 0.52, p = 0.335), hospitalization for heart failure (RR 1.02, p = 0.931), in-hospital mortality (RR 1.02, p = 0.959), major adverse events (RR 0.74, p = 0.635), major bleeding (RR 0.70, p = 0.187), or residual tricuspid regurgitation of mild (RR 0.98, p = 0.686) or moderate severity (RR 1.01, p = 0.646). CIED-specific outcomes were reported heterogeneously. Lead function was generally preserved after T-TEER in carefully selected patients, whereas studies of TTVR with jailed leads reported lead failure or malfunction ranging from 5.8% to 21% in individual cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Among the comparative outcomes available for quantitative pooling, no statistically significant differences were detected between patients with and without CIEDs for most procedural and postprocedural outcomes. However, CIED-specific risks differed according to the intervention. Lead function was generally preserved after T-TEER in carefully selected patients, whereas lead jailing during TTVR was associated with clinically relevant lead malfunction in some cohorts. Therefore, the absence of significant differences in pooled clinical outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence that TTVI does not affect CIED function.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: The Impact of Preexisting Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices on the Safety of Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Interventions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) mitochondrial respiration is impaired in heart failure and transplanted patients. Severe aortic stenosis (AS), characterized by pressure overload leading to cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction, might also be associated with PBMC mitochondrial respiration alterations, likely related to systemic inflammation and left heart hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction.
POPULATION AND METHODS: We determined PBMC mitochondrial respiration by high-resolution respirometry (Oroboros Instruments) in 9 healthy subjects and 25 AS patients before and until 30 days after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and investigated potential correlates with the clinical, biological and echocardiographic characteristics of the patients.
RESULTS: AS patients with a transaortic valvular gradient of 45 mm Hg were older and demonstrated slightly impaired renal function, inflammation markers, increased brain natriuretic peptide, left ventricular hypertrophy, and impaired diastolic function. PBMC mitochondrial coupling was decreased in the AS patients compared to controls (2.12 ± 0.10 vs. 2.76 ± 0.17, p = 0.003) and mitochondrial complex IV respiration was increased (31.07 ± 2.84 vs. 18.69 ± 2.09, p = 0.017). TAVR did not modify the alterations. Interestingly, increased complex IV mitochondrial respiration was associated with reduced mortality (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Severe aortic stenosis is associated with bioenergetic remodeling of circulating mononuclear cells that were not significantly associated with valvular hemodynamic impairment and ventricular function, before and after the mechanical relief of afterload. Nevertheless, future studies will be useful to determine whether such systemic immuno-metabolic phenotype, particularly PBMC mitochondrial complex IV respiration stimulation, may contribute to reduce the risk following TAVR.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Altered Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell (PBMC) Mitochondrial Coupling and Complex IV Respiration in Severe Aortic Stenosis Before and After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic valve regurgitation is a common valvular heart disease. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are the principal therapeutic modalities, while the comparative efficacy of these two approaches remains controversial.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420261411339). We systematically searched Web of Science, PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library databases for relevant studies from their inception to 26 July 2026. RevMan 5.4 software was used to conduct this analysis. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were used to evaluate the outcomes.
RESULTS: We assessed in-hospital outcomes and post-discharge 30-day outcomes. The primary outcomes were length of hospital stay, perioperative complications, and valve condition. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF), and new permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). Nine articles involving 28,811 patients were included. Compared with SAVR, TAVR reduced length of hospital stay [mean difference (MD) = -4.49, 95% confidence interval (CI): -4.98, -4.01, p < 0.00001, I2 = 80%], perioperative complications [Odds ratios (OR): 0.55, 95% CI: 0.50 to 0.60, p < 0.00001, I2 = 62%) and new-AF(OR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.43 to 0.59, p < 0.00001 I2 = 30%). However, there was a significant increase in perivalvular leakage (OR: 17.13, 95% CI: 4.13 to 71.13, p < 0.0001 I2 = 29%) and new PPI (OR: 2.63, 95% CI: 2.13 to 3.25, p < 0.00001 I2 = 80%). There was no significant difference observed in all-cause mortality (OR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.69-1.20, p = 0.49, I2 = 69%).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with SAVR, TAVR reduced length of hospital stay, perioperative complications, and new AF. However, it was associated with an increase in perivalvular leakage and new PPI. These findings suggest that TAVR may represent a better strategy for patients with pure native aortic regurgitation.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Clinical Outcomes of Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients with Pure Native Aortic Regurgitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is a frequent complication among patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes, making early identification of predictors essential for risk stratification and management. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the prognostic value of the Clinical SYNTAX score (CSS) compared with the anatomical SYNTAX score (SS), GRACE, and CHA2DS2-VASc scores in predicting in-hospital NOAF and long-term outcomes among 979 NSTEMI patients undergoing coronary angiography. Predictors of NOAF, all-cause mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs: death, myocardial infarction, stroke) were identified using logistic and Cox regression models, with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis used to compare the discriminative power of CSS against SS, GRACE, and CHA2DS2-VASc over a median follow-up of 86 months (IQR 36-100; range 0.1-144). NOAF developed in 80 patients (8.2%), with age, female gender, left atrial diameter, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, and CSS (p = 0.014) identified as independent predictors. CSS's AUC for predicting NOAF (0.724; 95% CI: 0.673-0.775) was significantly higher than SS's (0.644; 95% CI: 0.588-0.699; DeLong p < 0.001) and comparable to that of the CHA2DS2-VASc and GRACE scores; a CSS threshold ≥ 17.77 predicted NOAF with 75% sensitivity and 65% specificity. In Cox regression analysis, in-hospital NOAF, age, hypertension, reduced ejection fraction (<60%), and CSS independently predicted long-term all-cause mortality, while NOAF, EF < 60%, age, early AF recurrence, hypertension, and CSS independently predicted MACEs; SS was not a significant predictor in either model. In non-overlapping multivariable models, this advantage reflected the contribution of CSS's clinical components rather than incremental value of the composite score; CSS nonetheless remained an independent predictor of NOAF and long-term outcomes and may serve as a practical single-score tool for risk-guided management.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Evaluation of Clinical SYNTAX Score in Predicting New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation and Long-Term Prognosis in Patients Hospitalized with Non-ST Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Aortic valve disease (AVD), including bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents a complex challenge in sports cardiology. Balancing the cardiovascular benefits of physical activity with the hemodynamic risks associated with valvular dysfunction and aortopathy requires precise risk stratification. The present review comprehensively analyses the contemporary criteria for exercise prescription and competitive sports participation in individuals with AVD, highlighting also the distinctions between the European guidelines (European Society of Cardiology-ESC), the Italian Sports Cardiology Guidelines for competitive sport practice (COCIS 2023) and the recommendations for exercise prescription in cardiovascular diseases promoted by the Italian Sports Cardiology Society (SIC Sport) and the Italian Federation for Sports Medicine (FMSI). Relevant differences with the 2025 AHA/ACC recommendations are also highlighted where they may influence sports eligibility. Eligibility hinges primarily on the degree of valvular defect, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and aortic dimensions. Furthermore, post-operative sports participation is highly contingent on the intervention type, post-operative results and follow-up. Ultimately, safe exercise prescription relies on meticulous clinical surveillance, advanced imaging, maximal stress testing, and a shared decision-making process to maximize cardiovascular health while mitigating the risk of acute adverse events.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Risk Stratification, Exercise Prescription, and Sport Participation in Individuals with Aortic Valve Disease.

abstract: (1) Background: The association between microaxial flow pump (mAFP) timing and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains uncertain. (2) Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of patients with AMI-CS admitted between January 2017 and July 2025. Prespecified 24 h landmark analyses included patients alive 24 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission. The primary analysis compared patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) receiving mAFP within 6 h with STEMI patients managed without temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). Later STEMI implantation (>6-≤24 h) and both non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) timing cohorts were exploratory. The primary endpoint was subsequent in-hospital mortality from the landmark onward. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-weighted models. (3) Results: In the primary STEMI cohort, 106 patients received mAFP within 6 h and 59 received no-tMCS. Subsequeunt in-hospital mortality was 17.0% versus 23.7%, respectively (p = 0.293). Early mAFP implantation was associated with lower mortality in the fully adjusted model (OR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.06-0.99]; p = 0.048). Propensity score-based estimates were directionally consistent, with significance in the doubly robust weighted model (OR, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.06-0.85]; p = 0.028) but not in all weighted models. Later-timing and NSTEMI estimates did not reach statistical significance and were imprecise. (4) Conclusions: Among patients with STEMI who survived the first 24 h after ICU admission, mAFP implantation within 6 h was associated with lower subsequent in-hospital mortality. Exploratory later-timing and NSTEMI estimates were inconclusive. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective single-centre study of AMI-CS patients admitted between January 2017 and July 2025; primary STEMI cohort 106 patients with mAFP within 6 h and 59 with no tMCS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre retrospective design with small comparator group, wide confidence intervals and estimates that were not significant in all weighted models; the authors describe the findings as hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Retrospective single-centre study of microaxial flow pump timing in infarct-related cardiogenic shock, associating implantation within 6 hours with lower subsequent in-hospital mortality in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Subsequent in-hospital mortality was 17.0% versus 23.7% (p = 0.293). Early mAFP implantation was associated with lower mortality in the fully adjusted model (OR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.06-0.99]; p = 0.048) and in the doubly robust weighted model (OR, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.06-0.85]; p = 0.028).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Timing of microaxial flow pump support is a live question after DanGer-Shock, and this signal could inform the design of a timing analysis in larger registries.

journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Timing of Microaxial Flow Pump Support and In-Hospital Mortality in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock: The TIMING-CS Study.

abstract: Kounis syndrome is an acute coronary syndrome occurring in temporal association with an allergic or anaphylactic reaction. Recognition may be particularly challenging in patients with established coronary artery disease, in whom hypersensitivity-mediated mechanisms may coexist with conventional causes of acute myocardial infarction. We report a 62-year-old man with known coronary artery disease and previous percutaneous coronary interventions who developed loss of consciousness, generalized urticaria, facial swelling, dyspnea, and hemodynamic instability shortly after two wasp stings. He received intramuscular adrenaline and supportive treatment for anaphylaxis. Severe chest pain subsequently developed, with ST-segment elevation and a dynamic increase in cardiac troponin. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated a critical lesion extending from the distal left main coronary artery into the proximal left anterior descending artery. Intravascular ultrasound performed before stent implantation demonstrated an intimal flap and dissection plane. Intravascular ultrasound-guided percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent implantation achieved a satisfactory acute result. Subsequent allergological evaluation demonstrated Hymenoptera venom sensitization; baseline serum tryptase measured approximately five weeks after the event was within the reference range. The close temporal relationship between anaphylaxis and myocardial infarction supports suspected type II Kounis syndrome, while coronary dissection was identified as the culprit lesion morphology; its causal relationship to the hypersensitivity reaction remains uncertain.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Suspected Type II Kounis Syndrome with Coronary Dissection Extending from the Distal Left Main into the Proximal Left Anterior Descending Artery After Wasp Sting Anaphylaxis: A Case Report.

abstract: Heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF/HFmrEF) accounts for approximately half of the global heart failure burden and remains a syndrome with limited device-based therapeutic options. It is often characterized by a disproportionate rise in left-sided filling pressure during exercise. Interatrial shunt devices (IASDs) aim to reduce left atrial pressure through controlled left-to-right atrial communication. We performed a structured narrative review of mechanistic studies, early feasibility cohorts, randomized trials, meta-analyses, and ongoing studies indexed through to August 2026. Early proof-of-concept studies consistently demonstrated technical feasibility, durable patency, and favorable hemodynamic effects, particularly through reductions in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), often accompanied by improved functional status. However, larger sham-controlled randomized trials failed to show consistent overall benefit in unselected populations. Recent mechanistic and observational data indicate that pulmonary vascular reserve, right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, rhythm-device status, and device design may affect benefits and harms. Latent pulmonary vascular disease and impaired right-heart reserve may identify patients poorly suited for shunt implantation, whereas carefully selected, promising phenotypes remain under prospective study. IASDs should therefore remain investigational. Future trials should use exercise hemodynamics and validated noninvasive markers to prospectively define responders, assess device-specific effects, and reconcile physiological unloading with clinical outcomes.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
keywords: heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction
heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
title: Interatrial Shunt Devices in Heart Failure: A Therapy in Search of the Right Patient.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and renal dysfunction are each associated with adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We investigated whether their coexistence identifies a clinically relevant high-risk group.
METHODS: In this retrospective two-centre cohort, patients undergoing TAVR were classified into four groups according to moderate-to-severe TR and preprocedural estimated glomerular filtration rate < 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified clinical covariates, and multiplicative interaction between TR and renal dysfunction was assessed.
RESULTS: Among 2227 patients, 1456 had neither condition, 324 isolated renal dysfunction, 315 isolated TR, and 132 both conditions. Patients with the combined phenotype had the highest rates of in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, and renal replacement therapy (all p < 0.001). One-year mortality increased progressively across groups (6.7%, 10.6%, 11.3%, and 22.9%; p < 0.001). After adjustment (n = 1704), the combined phenotype was associated with higher one-year mortality compared with neither condition (OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.62-5.23; p < 0.001), isolated TR (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.16-4.07; p = 0.015), and isolated renal dysfunction (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.16-4.61; p = 0.017). No significant multiplicative interaction was observed (p = 0.187).
CONCLUSIONS: Coexisting moderate-to-severe TR and renal dysfunction identify a clinically relevant high-risk group after TAVR, with higher adjusted one-year mortality than either condition alone. Combined assessment of TR and renal function may improve preprocedural risk stratification.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Coexisting Moderate-to-Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation and Renal Dysfunction Identify a High-Risk Group After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract: Population-based studies of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are often limited by the lack of structured left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) data in administrative registries. We developed a logistic regression model using ICD-10-CM diagnostic codes and two clinical variables to estimate the probability of reduced LVEF (<50%) at discharge after ACS, and examined the prognostic value of the resulting classification in a large population-based cohort. The model was derived from 1596 patients with pre-discharge echocardiographic LVEF. In a 10-fold cross-validation analysis that repeated predictor selection within each train-ing fold, the procedure yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.711 (95% CI, 0.680-0.741). The fixed 28-predictor model, subsequently applied to the population-based cohort, yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.738 in the corresponding cross-validation analysis. The fixed 28-predictor model was then applied to 83,357 patients from the population-based BEAT-HF cohort (Catalonia, 2011-2021), in whom reference LVEF was unavailable. Patients classified as having reduced LVEF had a less favourable clinical profile and significantly higher rates of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Predicted reduced LVEF was associated with higher observed rates of all-cause mortality (HR 2.45, 95% CI 2.35-2.55; p < 0.001), as well as higher risks of heart failure (HF) and major adverse cardiovascular events. The model should not guide individual clinical decisions but may support exploratory population-level characterization of patients in administrative data. Validation against measured LVEF is needed.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Development and Population-Based Prognostic Utility Assessment of an ICD-10-CM-Based Prediction Model to Identify Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction: Discrimination Performance and Population-Based Evaluation in 83,357 Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome.

abstract: Temporary mechanical circulatory support devices are increasingly used to stabilise haemodynamics in patients with compromised cardiac output. While devices vary regarding indications and haemodynamic effects, only left ventricular (LV) unloading by microaxial flow pumps in a specific subset of patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction-associated cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) has shown a reduction in mortality. This review elucidates on this evidence-based indication for LV unloading, namely patients with AMI-CS fulfilling the Danish-German (DanGer)-Shock trial's inclusion and exclusion criteria. Furthermore, the review discusses cardiogenic shock scenarios encountered in everyday clinical practice beyond the trial population. It further extends beyond that, discussing clinical scenarios such as protected percutaneous coronary intervention including critical appraisal of recent trials, the negative results of unloading trials in AMI, as well as the settings of protected ventricular tachycardia ablation, LV unloading in veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (vaECMO) cases, escalated support with Impella 5.5 for postcardiotomy patients and as a bridge-to-decision or bridge-to-LV assist device (LVAD), and emerging indications such as protected cardiac as well as non-cardiac surgery.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
title: Established and Novel Indications for Left Ventricular Unloading-When and for Whom?

abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary artery calcification is a leading cause of stent failure and a strong predictor of adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Accurate characterization of calcium burden, depth, and morphology is central to procedural planning, targeted treatment, and better outcomes. This review summarizes the contemporary armamentarium for imaging calcified coronary lesions, from coronary angiography and computed tomography to advanced intracoronary imaging, and how it facilitates treatment. Methods: We synthesized evidence from landmark studies, validated imaging scoring systems, registries, and current guideline and consensus documents addressing the assessment and imaging-guided treatment of coronary calcification. Results: Invasive angiography shows poor diagnostic accuracy for coronary calcium detection, characterization, and quantification. Coronary CT angiography noninvasively quantifies calcium (Agatston score and three-dimensional volume) and supports preprocedural planning, although it may overestimate calcium volume. Intravascular imaging by means of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) effectively detects coronary calcium. Their use is associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with sole angiographic guidance. The addition of near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS-IVUS) characterizes lipids within calcified plaque and high-risk calcified nodules. OCT provides the highest spatial resolution and uniquely measures calcium thickness and longitudinal calcium length, while the utilization of artificial intelligence further enhances calcium assessment. Integration of these modalities into a morphology-based, imaging-guided approach facilitates calcium detection and modification and supports PCI optimization. Conclusions: Intravascular imaging, along with coronary CT angiography, has transformed the assessment of calcified coronary lesions. Combining their strengths enables precise, lesion-specific preparation; randomized trials show that intravascular imaging guidance improves outcomes in complex PCI, while CT-guided PCI planning is emerging as a complementary strategy whose clinical value is now being tested in randomized trials.
title: Assessing Calcified Coronary Lesions to Guide Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: From Angiography to Intracoronary Imaging.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular inflammation and vasculotoxic heavy metals have each been linked to acute coronary syndrome (ACS) but have rarely been studied together. This study compared serum pentraxin-3 (PTX-3), a proposed marker of local vascular inflammation, and whole-blood lead (Pb), arsenic (As), and nickel (Ni) between ACS patients and controls.
METHODS: In this single-center, cross-sectional case-control study, 50 patients with angiographically confirmed ACS were compared with 50 age- and sex-comparable emergency department controls with minor non-cardiac complaints.
RESULTS: PTX-3, Pb, As, and Ni were higher in ACS patients (all false discovery rate-adjusted q < 0.001). Between-group discrimination was highest for Pb (area under the curve [AUC] 0.962) and PTX-3 (AUC 0.951). PTX-3 and Pb remained independently associated with ACS after adjustment for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking and, separately, for age, diabetes, and renal function. Within the ACS group, PTX-3 was not significantly correlated with the Gensini score (ρ = 0.12, p = 0.41).
CONCLUSIONS: PTX-3 and whole-blood Pb, As, and Ni were markedly elevated in ACS, with PTX-3 and Pb showing the strongest and most robust associations. Prospective multicenter studies in patients with suspected ACS are needed to confirm these findings and establish whether these biomarkers add value beyond established clinical assessment.
title: Evaluation of Serum Pentraxin-3 and Heavy Metal Levels in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) encompasses several coexisting endotypes, complicating management.
CASE SUMMARY: A 56-year-old woman with chronic left bundle branch block presented with exertional angina. Coronary physiology testing suggested a hemodynamically significant left anterior descending myocardial bridge with provocable epicardial vasospasm. Nebivolol reduced angina but caused symptomatic bradycardia from sinus node dysfunction. A dual-chamber pacemaker enabled beta-blocker resumption and angina resolution.
DISCUSSION: ANOCA management is challenging because its endotypes differ mechanistically; comprehensive invasive physiology testing is key to defining them. When myocardial bridging is identified, invasive assessment can help determine clinical significance. Endotype-targeted therapy likely improves outcomes, underscoring the need for endotype-specific strategies.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Comprehensive invasive coronary physiology testing defines coexisting ANOCA endotypes and can identify a clinically significant myocardial bridge, though diastolic fractional flow reserve may lack sensitivity and should be integrated with clinical and treatment-response findings. Permanent pacing is indicated to facilitate medical therapy in patients with chronic angina, including ANOCA.
title: Pacemaker-Facilitated Beta-Blocker Therapy for Symptomatic Concomitant Myocardial Bridge and Vasospastic Angina.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The spiked helmet sign (SHS), or Pickelhaube sign, is a rare pseudo-ST-segment elevation pattern described in critically ill patients without acute myocardial infarction.
CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with class III obesity and diabetes presented in septic shock from extensive Fournier's gangrene. After emergent debridement, telemetry showed anterior ST-segment elevation prompting ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) activation. Serial electrocardiograms demonstrated pre-QRS baseline elevation merging with the QRS and transient anterolateral ST-segment elevation consistent with the Pickelhaube sign. Troponins remained normal, and contrast echocardiography showed hyperdynamic systolic function without regional wall-motion abnormalities. ST elevation resolved spontaneously within 30 minutes, and angiography was deferred. He required vasopressors, continuous venovenous hemofiltration, repeated debridement, and wound vacuum-assisted closure before discharge to long-term acute care.
DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates the Pickelhaube sign during Fournier's gangrene with septic shock. Recognizing its morphology and evolution, along with biomarkers, echocardiography, and clinical context, can distinguish pseudo-STEMI from acute coronary occlusion and avoid unnecessary angiography.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: The Pickelhaube sign can occur in severe necrotizing soft-tissue infection and septic shock and may closely mimic acute STEMI. Serial electrocardiograms, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography, and hemodynamic context help distinguish this pseudo-STEMI pattern from acute coronary occlusion.
title: Fournier's Gangrene-Associated ECG-Pickelhaube Sign: The Evanescent STEMI-Mimic.

abstract: Nephrotic syndrome is associated with a hypercoagulable state, leading to an increased risk of potentially severe thromboembolic events. Although venous thromboses predominantly involve the renal veins and deep veins of the lower extremities, intracardiac thrombosis remains an exceptionally rare manifestation, particularly as the initial presenting feature. We report the case of a 51-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia and recent cholecystectomy, who was admitted for lower-limb edema and hematuria of two weeks' duration. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed multiple thrombotic events, including deep vein thrombosis of the lower extremities, partial thrombosis of the left renal vein, and a left ventricular intracardiac thrombus measuring 23 × 20 mm. Laboratory investigations demonstrated nephrotic syndrome with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 10 g/g and hypoalbuminemia of 23 g/L, associated with stage 2 acute kidney injury. Immunological testing was negative, including anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (anti-PLA2R) antibodies. Kidney biopsy established the diagnosis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Management consisted of therapeutic anticoagulation, diuretic therapy, and corticosteroid treatment, resulting in progressive clinical and biological improvement. This case highlights the exceptional occurrence of a left ventricular thrombus associated with multiple venous thromboses as the presenting manifestation of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. It underscores the importance of systematically investigating underlying glomerular disease in patients presenting with multiple or unusual thrombotic events, particularly in the presence of significant proteinuria.
title: Intracardiac thrombus and multiple venous thromboses revealing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality globally, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention is the standard treatment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction, a life-threatening acute coronary syndrome requiring urgent revascularization. Despite increasing access to this intervention in sub-Saharan Africa, evidence on patients' lived experiences of recovery remains limited. This study explored patients' experiences of recovery and quality of life following primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction in Tanzania.
METHODS: An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed. Fourteen patients who had undergone primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction were purposively sampled at a national referral cardiac centre and interviewed within three months after PCI. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Participants perceived quality of life after PCI as an evolving experience closely linked to their recovery, with improvements in one aspect often accompanied by ongoing challenges in others. Six interrelated themes emerged: physical symptoms, functional capacity and daily activities, emotional responses, coping and illness perceptions, social support and relationships, and health system interactions and communication. Although participants generally reported symptom improvement and gradual functional recovery, persistent fatigue, activity limitations, emotional uncertainty, and unmet informational needs continued to influence their quality of life. Family support and adaptive coping helped participants adjust to life after PCI, while healthcare communication shaped their confidence in managing recovery.
CONCLUSION: Recovery after primary percutaneous coronary intervention extends beyond survival to include physical, emotional, and social dimensions. Holistic, patient-centred post-intervention care is needed to support long-term recovery in resource-limited settings.
title: Recovery experiences and perceptions of quality of life after percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction: An interpretive descriptive qualitative study.
Optimizing US Prehospital Care of ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Because Time Is Life, Not Just Muscle.
Price Variation in Outpatient Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language model (LLM) benchmarking in clinical medicine is increasingly reliant on LLM-based assessment frameworks; in these systems, one AI scores the outputs of another. This practice relies on the assumptions of evaluator neutrality and rubric consistency. These assumptions have not been empirically tested in clinical fields.
OBJECTIVE: In this study, we aim to directly examine these assumptions by using the PARM (Planning-Action-Reflection-Memory) framework as a theoretical lens to characterize endovascular device selection and clinical reflective reasoning as a clinical field.
METHODS: We developed a scoring rubric (C1-C6) with 40 clinical vignettes and 6 criteria across 5 endovascular fields (peripheral artery disease, abdominal aortic aneurysm, chronic venous insufficiency, coronary in-stent restenosis [ISR], and cerebrovascular/neuroendovascular; 8 vignettes per field). Four LLMs were evaluated as clinical decision support systems: GPT-4o (M1), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (M2), Gemini 1.5 Pro (M3), and Llama 3.3 70B (M4). Two LLMs served as independent raters with the same evaluation criteria: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (rater 1) and GPT-4o (rater 2). The rater identity was intentionally disclosed; the primary research question concerned rater scoring behavior rather than the absolute performance of the model. Human assessment was intentionally excluded because its inclusion would have shifted the study question from rater disagreement to rater accuracy, a distinct and secondary question. Interrater reliability was measured using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC 2,1) two-way random effects modeling.
RESULTS: The combined ICC(2,1) was 0.153 (95% CI 0.007-0.295). In this exploratory study, the low ICC was not distributed randomly: the magnitude of score differences varied across models (M2 Δ=+5, M4 Δ=+31, M1 Δ=-46, and M3 Δ=-158 points). Scoring behavior analysis identified 2 intrinsically consistent but mutually inconsistent criterion-interpretation models. Rater 1's scores were most consistent with the reasoning quality approach (partial credit to clinical competence independent of vignette context). Rater 2's scores were most consistent with the context fidelity approach (near-zero scores for wrong vignette responses independent of reasoning quality). Contrary to the self-preference hypothesis, both raters placed the other higher-performing model above their own. Under rater 1, C6 (PARM reflection) was the lowest-scoring criterion across all 4 models, whereas rater 2 showed greater model-dependent variation in C6 scoring.
CONCLUSIONS: AI raters used in LLM-based clinical benchmarking do not behave as interchangeable scoring tools. Their scoring behavior is most consistent with model-specific criterion interpretation patterns that systematically produce different outcomes. The observed low interrater reliability requires interpretation rather than simply being ignored: it reflects structured, direction-specific disagreement concentrated in models with context-tracking failures, not random inconsistency. PARM reflection showed a notable yet evaluator-dependent scoring pattern that warranted further investigation, rather than being interpreted as an evaluator-independent deficit.
