title: Systematic Scoring Differences in Large Language Model-Based Clinical Benchmarking Reveal Evaluator-Dependent Divergence: Controlled Evaluation Study.

abstract: Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) serves as a critical biomarker of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Its serum level is extremely sparse, and the clinical cut-off value reaches merely 0.2 ng mL-1. This poses a significant challenge, requiring highly sensitive analytical techniques for reliable quantification. This study proposes a powerful surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing strategy integrating multistage signal amplification and machine learning to enhance detection performance. By combining T7 RNA polymerase, CRISPR/Cas13a, branched hybridization chain reaction (bHCR), and Fe3O4@COF@Ag magnetic substrate, the strategy constructs an efficient "recognition-amplification-signal output" closed loop for cTnI detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the platform has a linear calibration range of 0.1-104 pg/mL for cTnI, with an estimated limit of detection (LOD) of 0.1 pg/mL, holding promise for future AMI-related biomarker analysis. It also shows excellent selectivity against common serum interferents, good reproducibility (intra-batch RSD = 2.87%, inter-batch RSD = 7.96%), and reliable recovery (100.1%-110%) in human serum samples. Based on Raman signals, the k-nearest neighbor (kNN) classifier demonstrated high accuracy in classifying cTnI concentration levels, while the artificial neural network (ANN) model exhibited strong quantitative predictive performance with an R2 of 0.9997. This platform overcomes the limitations of conventional cTnI assays in terms of sensitivity and signal amplification efficiency, providing a promising analytical platform for future AMI-related biomarker studies.
title: T7 Ribonucleic Acid Polymerase-Triggered CRISPR/Cas13a and Branched HCR Cascade Amplification with Machine Learning for SERS Detection of Cardiac Troponin I.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) have improved, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, ischemic events, and major bleeding remain clinical challenges in patients with severe aortic stenosis.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the incidence, timing, and prognostic impact of these events after TAVR.
METHODS: This two-center retrospective registry included 988 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR. Patients were grouped according to the first clinical event after discharge: HF hospitalization, ischemic events (myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke), major bleeding, or the event-free group. The timing of the first postdischarge event and all-cause mortality after the first event were evaluated.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 665 days after discharge, 165 patients (16.7%) experienced any of these events. As first events, HF hospitalization, ischemic events, and major bleeding occurred in 80 (8.1%), 32 (3.2%), and 53 (5.4%) patients, respectively, whereas 823 (83.3%) were in the event-free group. Among patients with a first postdischarge event, major bleeding occurred earliest among the 3 event groups. One-year all-cause mortality after the first event was high across groups (HF hospitalization, 31.5%; ischemic events, 30.4%; major bleeding, 25.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who experienced a first postdischarge event after TAVR, major bleeding occurred earlier than HF hospitalization or ischemic events. Once a first postdischarge event occurred, subsequent all-cause mortality was high across the 3 event groups. These findings suggest that event timing should be considered and careful clinical reassessment may be warranted when a first postdischarge event occurs after TAVR.
title: Patterns of Postdischarge Heart Failure, Ischemic, and Bleeding Events After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2025 European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery Guidelines introduced a Class I recommendation for transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in selected patients aged 70 years or older with tricuspid aortic stenosis and suitable anatomy, while surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) remains recommended in younger low-risk patients. In patients with long expected survival, this framework requires careful consideration of valve durability, future reintervention, and patient preferences. This expert review, developed by the Italian Cardiac Surgery Working Group, examines contemporary evidence and consensus recommendations from a lifetime-management perspective.
METHODS: We performed a narrative, evidence-based synthesis of randomized trials, trial-based meta-analyses, and propensity-matched real-world registries comparing transfemoral TAVI and SAVR, with primary emphasis on low-risk patients. Lower-intermediate-risk evidence was included only when directly relevant to lifetime management, durability, or reintervention.
RESULTS: Evidence suggests that treatment effects are time-dependent: early non-inferiority of TAVI may attenuate with longer follow-up, particularly in patients with substantial life expectancy. Randomized durability data remain limited, whereas propensity-matched real-world registries have suggested possible higher late mortality after TAVI in younger, lower-risk populations. Reintervention after a transcatheter-first strategy may be associated with increasing technical complexity and procedural risk over time.
CONCLUSIONS: This review supports appropriate application of current guidelines through a pragmatic framework for individualized, Heart Team-based decision-making. Transfemoral TAVI is often appropriate in patients with limited life expectancy or recognized high surgical risk when anatomically feasible. In patients with long expected survival, SAVR should retain a central role as an important reference strategy.
title: Lifetime Management of Aortic Stenosis: Expert Review of Evidence and Consensus Guidelines.

abstract: Recanalization is central to acute ischemic stroke treatment. However, reopening an occluded artery does not always restore microvascular perfusion, and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) can occur regardless of recanalization success. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) may help explain these discordant outcomes because they act within occlusive thrombi, the downstream microcirculation, and the neurovascular interface. This review examines the roles of NETs in thrombolysis resistance, no-reflow, and hemorrhagic injury. Within thrombi, NET-associated chromatin reinforces clot architecture and limits fibrinolysis. Intravascular NETs may impede downstream microvascular flow after recanalization, while NET-related inflammatory signaling may aggravate blood-brain barrier disruption and HT. These findings implicate NETs in impaired recanalization, incomplete tissue reperfusion, and hemorrhagic injury and support their evaluation as an adjunctive target during reperfusion therapy.
title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in ischemic stroke: Thrombolysis resistance, no-reflow, and hemorrhagic transformation.

abstract: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a working diagnosis in which cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) defines the myocardial phenotype, separates ischemic injury from nonischemic mimics, and quantifies the burden of injury, yet usually cannot establish the coronary mechanism that produced it. Paired studies of CMR and intracoronary imaging show that the myocardial footprint and the coronary culprit often fail to correspond, because each test observes a different biological target within its own window of visibility, and a negative result cannot exclude transient or functional mechanisms such as spasm, embolism, or microvascular dysfunction. We synthesize evidence on imaging timing, quantitative tissue characterization, stress perfusion, multimodality reclassification, prognosis, and mechanism-guided treatment, and indicate the type of evidence supporting key claims. On this basis, we propose a conceptual framework, not an evidence-based guideline, that expresses mechanistic confidence in graded terms, places that judgment within an integrated heart-team report, and reserves further testing for questions likely to change diagnosis, treatment, or follow-up.
title: The Myocardial Footprint and the Coronary Culprit: What Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Can and Cannot Establish in MINOCA.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coagulopathy is frequent in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients treated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR), yet its prognostic significance and heterogeneity remain poorly characterised.
OBJECTIVES: To characterize coagulopathy at ECPR initiation, identify coagulation phenotypes, evaluate their association with outcomes, and describe their temporal evolution.
METHODS: All consecutive refractory OHCAs treated with ECPR (2013-2024) were included. Phenotypes were identified by unsupervised K-means clustering on PT-INR, aPTT, platelets, antithrombin, fibrinogen, and D-dimer measured at ECPR initiation. Associations with survival, neurological outcomes, and complications were assessed by multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 406 ECPR patients, 360 had coagulation data for analysis (initial shockable rhythm 67%, low-flow 70 min [IQR 58-81]). Three phenotypes were identified: severe consumptive coagulopathy (phenotype 1, n=49, 13.6%), mild consumptive coagulopathy (phenotype 2, n=175, 48.6%), and preserved coagulation (phenotype 3, n=136, 37.8%). Phenotype 1 had no survivors, compared with survival of 8.6% and 33.1% in phenotypes 2 and 3, respectively; favourable neurological outcome was achieved in 0%, 5.1%, and 17.6%. Phenotype severity correlated with ischaemic burden (lactate, arterial pH, end-tidal CO2, and low-flow duration). On multivariable analysis, phenotype 2 was associated with lower survival (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.55) and favourable neurological outcome (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.12-0.81) versus phenotype 3. Bleeding incidence rates were 38, 12, and 2.5 events per 100 patient-days in phenotype 1, 2, and 3, respectively (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Three distinct coagulation phenotypes at ECPR initiation were independently associated with survival and neurological outcome and appear to reflect ischaemic injury severity. These findings require validation in independent cohorts before clinical application.
journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
title: Defining three coagulation-based phenotypes for OHCA patients undergoing ECPR: an unsupervised cluster analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) uses ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves to modify calcification to enable optimal balloon and stent expansion in calcified lesions. However, the dose-response relationship for creating fractures within calcified lesions of different calcium morphologies is unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of IVL on calcium fracture overall and in the setting of calcification arc <180° vs ≥180°.
METHODS: Micro-computed tomography images were acquired before and after 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 120 pulses of IVL treatment (Shockwave Medical) in an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric human hearts (15 coronary lesions). A total of 30 cross-sections of micro-computed tomography (2 sections per lesion) were analyzed for this study.
RESULTS: Cumulative fracture occurrence increased progressively with the number of IVL pulses delivered, with fractures observed in 33% of sections after 10 pulses, 50% after 40 pulses, and 60% after 120 pulses. Calcification arc ≥180° exhibited a higher fracture occurrence compared with arc <180° (P = 0.028). After adjustment for pulse number, calcification arc ≥180° was associated with significantly higher fracture counts compared with arc <180° (rate ratio = 6.1, P = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Fracture occurrence following IVL increased with cumulative pulse delivery and differed significantly according to calcification concentricity. Calcification arc ≥180° demonstrated a higher and earlier likelihood of fracture occurrence than arc <180°, independent of pulse number. These findings establish a clear dose-dependent relationship between IVL pulse delivery and fracture formation and highlight calcification concentricity as a key determinant of fracture response.
title: Morphology-Dependent Dose-Response of Intravascular Lithotripsy on Coronary Calcium Fracture.
Uncracking the Relationship Between Intravascular Lithotripsy Pulses and Calcium Morphology.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcium fracture is a metric used to assess lesion preparation success. We have shown previously that optical coherence tomography (OCT) misses approximately half of these fractures. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is the most commonly used intravascular imaging modality. The sensitivity of IVUS for detecting calcium fractures after intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to assess the frequency and characteristics of calcium fracture observed on IVUS in comparison to OCT and gold standard micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) using heavily calcified coronary artery cadaveric vessels.
METHODS: In an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric hearts (15 coronary lesions), OCT, IVUS, and micro-CT were obtained before and after IVL coronary artery treatment. Fracture detection rates and appearance patterns were compared across modalities. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated OCT-measured fracture width thresholds for IVUS detectability.
RESULTS: Compared with micro-CT, OCT and IVUS significantly underestimated fracture occurrence, but OCT demonstrated higher detection sensitivity than IVUS (P < 0.05 by McNemar's test). Narrow linear nondisplaced fractures identified on OCT were frequently undetectable on IVUS or appeared as subtle hyperechoic shadows. Fracture width was strongly associated with IVUS detectability; fracture width >115 μm on OCT were identified by IVUS with excellent diagnostic performance (area under the curve: 0.99 [95% CI: 0.98-1.00], sensitivity 100%, specificity 92%).
CONCLUSIONS: OCT and IVUS underestimate the occurrence of IVL-induced calcium fractures compared with micro-CT, with IVUS demonstrating lower sensitivity than OCT. IVUS detectability is strongly dependent on fracture width. Absence of visible fracture on either OCT or IVUS does not exclude calcium modification.
title: Calcium Fracture Detection by Optical Coherence Tomography Versus Intravascular Ultrasound Following Intravascular Lithotripsy.
There Is More Than Meets the Eye: What Imaging Still Misses After Lithotripsy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a promising option to modify calcium.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.
METHODS: FRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]).
CONCLUSIONS: The quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation.
REGISTRATION: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240).

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial (FRACTURE; NCT06181240); 420 patients
appraisal.main_limitation: No randomised comparator, so performance against existing lithotripsy or calcium modification devices cannot be judged.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm multicentre trial of a laser-based quad-emitter intravascular lithotripsy system met its prespecified safety and effectiveness performance goals in severely calcified coronary lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). Procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds a second device class for calcium modification and the pivotal-type evidence base on which regulatory and guideline positions will build.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium: FRACTURE Study.
The Second Generation of Coronary Lithotripsy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH.
METHODS: The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH.
RESULTS: No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24). In contrast, new-onset PH (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH.
CONCLUSIONS: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective registry cohort (OCEAN-Mitral); 3,764 patients enrolled, 3,484 with paired TRPG data
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design using echocardiographic TRPG as a surrogate for pulmonary pressure, with residual confounding likely.
appraisal.one_line: In a large M-TEER registry, residual and new-onset pulmonary hypertension after the procedure were associated with worse outcomes, whereas normalised pulmonary hypertension was not.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation: 17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6% in no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH and residual PH (P < 0.001). Normalized PH adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24; new-onset PH HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93; residual PH HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Identifies a post-procedural risk marker that could refine patient selection and follow-up after M-TEER.

title: Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11).
CONCLUSIONS: recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.
title: Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes.
Beyond Procedural Success: Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation After Edge-to-Edge Repair in Perspective.
Improving the Conversation Around Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Pulmonary Embolism: STORM-PE.
ROBIN to the Rescue: Balloon Laceration for LVOT Obstruction After Incomplete LAMPOON in Valve-in-Ring TMVR.
Snare-Guided Repositioning of a Vascular Plug Device for Device-Related Hemolytic Anemia.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thoracoscopic minimally invasive ablation is effective for lone atrial fibrillation but remains technically challenging. Simplified modifications are needed to improve feasibility while maintaining outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: We proposed a simplified procedure, OC-box clamping ablation, for patients with lone atrial fibrillation and evaluated its safety, effectiveness, and simplicity.
METHODS: A total of 169 patients with lone atrial fibrillation underwent either totally thoracoscopic surgical ablation (n = 63) or OC-box clamping ablation (n = 106) and completed 12-month follow-up. Statistical analysis was performed to compare the rates of freedom from atrial fibrillation/atrial tachycardia without antiarrhythmic drugs at 4, 6, and 12 months postoperatively, as well as complications and adverse events. Logistic regression identified risk factors for atrial fibrillation recurrence.
RESULTS: No perioperative mortality, stroke, cardiovascular injury, or intra-aortic balloon pump/extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support was observed. No significant differences were observed in freedom from atrial fibrillation/atrial tachycardia without antiarrhythmic drugs at 4, 6, and 12 months between totally thoracoscopic surgical and OC-box clamping ablations (84.1% vs 86.8%, P = .631; 81.0% vs 77.4%, P = .581; and 71.4% vs 76.4%, P = .472). However, OC-box clamping ablation demonstrated a significantly shorter operative time compared with the totally thoracoscopic surgical ablation (127.31 ± 22.20 minutes vs 160.29 ± 45.94 minutes; P < .01). An enlarged left atrium was associated with atrial fibrillation recurrence (odds ratio, 2.810; 95% confidence interval, 1.145-6.897; P = .024).
CONCLUSION: OC-box clamping ablation achieves comparable efficacy and safety to totally thoracoscopic surgical ablation, with a simplified process and shorter operative time, making it more beginner-friendly.
title: A simplified and effective thoracoscopic minimally invasive ablation technique for lone atrial fibrillation: OC-box clamping ablation.

abstract: Between 2025 and 2026, our emergency medical service managed 850 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI); eleven (1.3%) of them presented the SAFS on electrocardiogram. This pattern is a rare electrocardiographic finding typically associated with the first diagonal (D1) branch occlusion of the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery 1. It was first described by S. Sclarovsky in 1994, who reported a special form of anterior wall myocardial infarction characterized by ST-segment elevation (STE) in non-contiguous leads DI, aVL, and V2 with reciprocal changes in DIII and aVF 2. In 2016, Littman coined the term 'South African flag sign' to denote a visual mnemonic device or aid for this ECG pattern, with the objective of facilitating earlier detection of 'high lateral' myocardial infarction (MI) 3. We report eleven cases that exhibited this pattern to highlight the electrical aspect and especially its severity.
title: [The South African Flag Sign (SAFS) is a deadly diagnosis not to miss. About eleven cases].

abstract: In secondary prevention, current therapeutic management of dyslipidemia primarily aims to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) levels, as LDL-c is a major driver of atherosclerosis. Elevated LDL-c levels are also one of the main modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. LDL-c lowering is directly, proportionally, and linearly associated with a reduction in cardiovascular events, with no apparent threshold effect. However, patients with chronic coronary syndrome or those who have recently experienced an acute coronary event are still generally undertreated and achieve guideline-recommended targets in only one out of four cases. This article aims to explore the underlying causes of and potential solutions to this therapeutic gap, which is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Treatment adherence varies considerably across studies (randomized controlled trials or real-life studies), as well as across geographical settings, and appears to be approximately 60%. However, non-adherence to treatment alone does not explain the low proportion of patients achieving LDL-c treatment targets, which remains at approximately 25%. The underlying reasons are complex and multifactorial. Paradoxically, although the expanding therapeutic armamentarium allows for increased substantial LDL-c reductions, this has not translated into a corresponding improvement in target attainment. Therapeutic inertia may arise at the patient, physician, and healthcare system levels. Furthermore, patient education and the therapeutic alliance should remain central to patient management and should be regularly reinforced and individualized.
title: [LDL-c and residual cardiovascular risk in patients with coronary artery disease].

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography (FFR-CT) enables combined anatomical and physiological assessment of coronary artery disease using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) data. Real-world evidence comparing downstream utilization and clinical outcomes following CCTA with versus without FFR-CT remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To compare invasive coronary angiography (ICA), coronary revascularization, additional cardiac testing, and one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients undergoing CCTA with versus without FFR-CT.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Research Network, in which 118 healthcare organizations were queried. Adults undergoing CCTA between January 1, 2020, and July 20, 2024, were categorized according to receipt of FFR-CT. The initial cohorts included 17,754 patients receiving FFR-CT and 198,220 undergoing CCTA alone. After 1:1 propensity-score matching on demographic and clinical characteristics, 15,375 patients were retained in each cohort. Outcomes were assessed from days 8 through 365 after the index event. MACE was defined as death, acute myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.
RESULTS: Compared with CCTA alone, CCTA with FFR-CT was associated with higher rates of ICA (24.0% vs 12.5%; risk ratio [RR], 1.920; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.826-2.020), percutaneous coronary intervention (7.6% vs 3.7%; RR, 2.076; 95% CI, 1.883-2.290), and coronary artery bypass grafting (3.3% vs 1.8%; RR, 1.770; 95% CI, 1.533-2.045). Additional noninvasive functional cardiac testing was also more frequent following FFR-CT (7.0% vs 5.1%; RR, 1.370; 95% CI, 1.253-1.497). Conversely, FFR-CT was associated with lower one-year MACE (8.8% vs 10.5%; RR, 0.835; 95% CI, 0.779-0.894), acute myocardial infarction (3.9% vs 4.7%; RR, 0.822; 95% CI, 0.740-0.915), and all-cause mortality (2.0% vs 2.9%; RR, 0.676; 95% CI, 0.585-0.782). All comparisons were significant at p < 0.001.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large propensity-matched cohort, CCTA with FFR-CT was associated with greater downstream invasive and noninvasive testing and higher rates of PCI and CABG, but lower one-year MACE, myocardial infarction, and mortality. These findings may reflect more effective identification of actionable coronary disease; however, differences in underlying anatomical disease severity, site-level practice patterns, and residual confounding preclude causal interpretation.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Downstream invasive testing, revascularization, and major adverse cardiovascular events following coronary CT angiography with and without fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography: A propensity-matched real-world cohort study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the combined predictive value of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)‑derived global longitudinal strain (GLS) and peripheral blood neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with first-time acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, 134 patients with first-time AMI (99 male and 35 female patients aged 33-83 years, mean 60.19±11.7 years) were enrolled between June, 2022 and July, 2025. All the patients underwent PCI and were followed up via outpatient visits or telephone for a median of 538 days post-discharge. The patients were divided into non-MACEs (n=103) and MACEs groups (n=31) for comparison of baseline clinical parameters.
RESULTS: Baseline comparisons revealed that the MACEs group had a significantly older age, higher white blood cell count, neutrophil count, NLR, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and NT-proBNP, and lower monocyte counts (all P<0.05) with had higher Gensini scores and incidences of anterior wall infarction, more frequent left anterior descending artery culprit lesions, but fewer right coronary artery lesions and lower rates of TIMI low-risk chest pain (P<0.05). In patients with MACEs, CMR findings revealed significantly higher frequencies of late gadolinium enhancement, end-systolic volume index, paradoxical motion, and aneurysmal wall formation, decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, and reduced infarct-segment and global radial, circumferential, and longitudinal strains (P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified NLR and GLS as independent predictors for MACEs. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that both GLS (AUC=0.825) and NLR (AUC=0.820) alone had predictive ability for MACEs, but their combination significantly increased the AUC to 0.921 (P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: CMR-derived GLS and peripheral blood NLR are both strongly associated with post-PCI prognosis in first-time AMI patients, and their combination allows more accurate prediction of MACEs to facilitate effective early risk stratification and clinical decision-making.
