title: [Myocardium global longitudinal strain and peripheral blood neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for predicting MACE risks following percutaneous coronary intervention for first-time acute myocardial infarction: a prospective cohort study].

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) can achieve substantial mitral regurgitation (MR) reduction in appropriately selected patients, yet outcomes after technically successful intervention remain heterogeneous. This variability has prompted interest in echocardiographic markers of limited treatment benefit. However, adverse prognosis after TEER and absence of benefit attributable to TEER are fundamentally different concepts, and most available imaging studies evaluate the former rather than the latter.
METHODS: This state-of-the-art review summarizes evidence on echocardiographic assessment of prognosis and treatment response across the mitral TEER pathway, integrating baseline multichamber phenotyping, procedural and immediate hemodynamic assessment, longitudinal imaging, and evidence from randomized trials of TEER in secondary MR.
RESULTS: Baseline left ventricular remodeling and myocardial dysfunction, left atrial disease, pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction and right ventricular-pulmonary arterial uncoupling, and tricuspid regurgitation identify greater cardiovascular disease burden and residual risk after TEER. Procedural assessment extends beyond residual MR to include transmitral pressure gradient, forward flow, and left atrial hemodynamics, whereas serial imaging characterizes subsequent ventricular, atrial, pulmonary, and right-heart trajectories. Persistent structural or hemodynamic abnormalities and absence of reverse remodeling should not be equated with irreversible disease or therapeutic futility. Randomized subgroup analyses in secondary MR have not consistently demonstrated significant treatment-effect modification by several adverse echocardiographic phenotypes; however, these analyses were not adequately powered to exclude clinically meaningful interactions. Moreover, COAPT excluded patients with extreme ventricular remodeling, markedly elevated pulmonary pressures, or advanced RV dysfunction, limiting generalizability to these populations. Differences among COAPT, MITRA-FR, and RESHAPE-HF2 further caution against defining a universal echocardiographic treatment-response phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiography is essential for defining MR mechanism and severity, characterizing multichamber cardiovascular disease, evaluating procedural results, and refining longitudinal risk assessment. However, current evidence does not establish a validated echocardiographic threshold or phenotype that reliably predicts absence of treatment benefit. Randomized subgroup findings require cautious interpretation because of limited statistical power and the exclusion of patients with the most advanced ventricular and pulmonary vascular disease. Future adequately powered comparative studies should evaluate heterogeneity of treatment effect across MR etiologies using standardized multichamber imaging and patient-centered outcomes.
title: Echocardiographic Assessment of Prognosis and Treatment Benefit After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute decompensated severe aortic stenosis may preclude waiting for elective treatment, and evidence for non-elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is limited. We assessed 12-month mortality, 30-day safety, and recovery after urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients undergoing urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI at one centre in 2022-2025. The primary endpoint was 12-month all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included device success, 30-day safety, and functional and echocardiographic recovery.
RESULTS: Among 53 patients, 36 underwent urgent, 14 emergency, and 3 salvage TAVI. Device success was 52/53 (98.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 1/36, 0/14, and 0/3; 12-month mortality was 2/36, 1/14, and 0/3 (3/53). Kaplan-Meier 12-month survival was 94.3% (95% confidence interval 83.5-98.1%). New atrioventricular block was detected in 2/53 on postoperative day 2; by 30 days, haemofiltration or renal replacement therapy occurred in 1/53 and permanent pacemaker implantation in 0/53. At 12 months, cardiovascular mortality was 2/53, heart-failure readmission 4/53, stroke 1/53, a separate Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 type 2 bleeding event 1/53, and permanent pacemaker implantation 0/53. Paired analyses showed improved New York Heart Association class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12, left ventricular ejection fraction, and transvalvular gradients at 30 days and 12 months (all P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Selected patients had high device success and low early event rates after non-elective TAVI; paired data showed sustained functional and haemodynamic improvement. These findings support timely Heart Team assessment and consideration of non-elective TAVI, when appropriate, at experienced centres; comparative benefit over alternative strategies warrants prospective study.
journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
title: Urgent, Emergency, and Salvage Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.

abstract: Fifteen years ago, endovascular recanalization of chronic total occlusion of the subclavian artery relied largely on coronary guidewires and conventional catheters. An early series achieved technical success in 46 of 56 patients (82.1%). Today, dedicated crossing wires, support catheters, improved imaging, and a wider choice of stents provide additional options for complex lesions. Yet published series report variable technical success and patency, and differences in patient selection and follow-up limit comparisons between treatment eras. This review revisits earlier techniques, examines what has changed in practice, and discusses persistent challenges, particularly heavily calcified and ostial occlusions near the vertebral artery. Technological progress has broadened treatment options, but its independent contribution to long-term outcomes remains uncertain.
title: Endovascular recanalization of chronic total occlusion of the subclavian artery: fifteen years of technological evolution.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with myocarditis suffering from cardiogenic shock may benefit from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). However, the characteristics of myocardial injury in these patients are unclear. Using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), we aimed to investigate cardiac changes in survivors with severe myocarditis treated with ECMO.
METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University in Nanjing, China, from July 2018 to July 2022. Patients with severe myocarditis who underwent CMR within 30 days after discontinuing ECMO were included in this study.
RESULTS: In total, 22 patients (median age: 33 years) were included. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was detected within the interventricular septum (IVS) in all patients. The mean T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) values showed similar distribution patterns to LGE. In an exploratory post-hoc age stratification based on the cohort median age of 33 years, we observed that several quantitative CMR parameters (mean ECV, minimum ECV, maximum ECV, mean T1, maximum T1, and minimum T2) were numerically higher in the older subgroup (p < 0.05). Myocardial injury was widespread in patients with severe myocarditis receiving ECMO.
CONCLUSIONS: Survivors of severe myocarditis who required ECMO support presented diffuse myocardial injury as the dominant pattern on early post-weaning CMR examination, with the interventricular septum showing notably prominent lesions among all myocardial segments.
title: Myocardial injury patterns on cardiac magnetic resonance: diffuse myocardial damage with prominent septal involvement in adults with severe myocarditis requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) carries a high risk of in-hospital death. Randomized evidence does not support routine VA-ECMO use in unselected AMI-CS populations. Objective and interpretable risk stratification is clinically important when advanced mechanical circulatory support is considered.
METHODS: This was a retrospective, multi-database model development and validation study with exploratory application in a local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort. An in-hospital mortality prediction model was developed in AMI-CS patients who did not receive ECMO treatment using the MIMIC-IV database. Candidate measurements were summarized using the worst values accumulated during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Variable shrinkage was performed using LASSO logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation, and the model was established using multivariable logistic regression. Internal validation included the original fixed-structure bootstrap and an additional full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis. The latter repeated preprocessing, LASSO selection, post-LASSO handling, and model refitting within each resample. External validation was performed in the eICU cohort. The model was then applied exploratorily to the local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort to describe model transportability and the relationship between observed and predicted outcomes.
RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 355 patients, of whom 127 died in hospital (35.77%). LASSO selected 8 clinical predictors. The apparent AUC was 0.829 (95% CI 0.785-0.874). After the final model was refitted in 200 fixed-structure bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.814. In 500 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples, all repetitions were valid, the mean optimism was 0.0436, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.786 (empirical 2.5th to 97.5th percentile range: 0.745-0.832). The AUCs from the MIMIC-IV complete-case and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses were 0.820 and 0.840, respectively. In the eICU complete-case cohort, the AUC was 0.806 (95% CI 0.691-0.921), O/E was 0.733, the calibration intercept was - 0.986, and the calibration slope was 0.671. After multiple imputation in all 224 eligible eICU patients, the AUC was 0.771, O/E was 0.754, the calibration intercept was - 0.756, and the calibration slope was 0.528. The local cohort included 40 VA-ECMO-treated patients. Overall observed mortality was 42.5% (95% CI 27.0-59.1), mean predicted mortality was 59.2% (95% CI 50.6-67.2), and O/E was 0.717 (95% CI 0.418-1.149).
CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and externally validated a mortality risk model for patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. The model may provide a research reference for early risk stratification and individualized assessment. Uncertainty in variable selection and cross-population calibration drift limit its direct clinical application. Prospective multicenter studies are required for further validation and to evaluate its role in VA-ECMO patient selection.
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
title: Mortality risk model for acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: development, external validation, and exploratory application in a VA-ECMO cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies have demonstrated the superior benefits of clopidogrel compared to aspirin in reducing mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and hospitalization in chronic stable patients with coronary stenting. Furthermore, dual pathway inhibition by combining low-dose rivaroxaban with aspirin (DPI) has shown superior effects in preventing cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke in stable atherosclerotic patients. However, no studies have directly compared these treatment strategies in the same population. This randomized controlled trial aims to compare clopidogrel-based antiplatelet therapy with or without aspirin (CAPT) to DPI in a 1:1 ratio in patients with high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) or in patients with both CAD and peripheral artery disease (PAD).
METHODS: Optimal strategy for treatment of Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-comparison of Clopidogrel-based Antiplatelet agent treatment versus aspirin plus low dose Rivaroxaban Therapy (OACART) trial is a randomized multi-center study comparing the performance of the maintaining CAPT or DPI in a 1:1 ratio. The trial is powered for the non-inferiority of the CAPT in patients with chronic stable high-risk CAD or CAD+PAD to DPI with respect to the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints at 36 months.
RESULTS: Between November 2023 and April 2026, we will recruit 2758 participants from multi-center in Korea, and we will examine the net clinical outcome, including all-cause death, any myocardial infarction, any stroke, any ischemia-driven revascularization (CAD or PAD), acute limb ischemia, any major or minor amputations, any acute thromboembolism, and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis major bleeding at 36 months after study enrollment.
CONCLUSIONS: OACART trial will provide the optimal antithrombotic treatment strategy for patients with stable high-risk atherosclerosis.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS) of Republic of Korea, KCT0008458, registered on May 22, 2023. https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/detailSearch.do?seq=28968&search_page=L.
title: Optimal strategy for treatment of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-comparison of clopidogrel-based antiplatelet agent treatment versus aspirin plus low dose rivaroxaban therapy (OACART study): a study protocol for a multicenter, open-label, randomized, non-inferiority trial.

abstract: This study reports the case of a 74-year-old female patient (aged 70 at the initial 2021 event) with hereditary thrombophilia and a patent foramen ovale (PFO) possessing high-risk anatomical features. The patient presented in December 2021 with pulmonary embolism and acute multiple cerebral infarctions due to PFO-associated paradoxical embolism. Genetic testing confirmed hereditary thrombophilia (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, 4G/4G genotype). Despite standard anticoagulation, she developed recurrent thrombosis. Subsequent transesophageal echocardiography (May 2025) delineated the high-risk PFO anatomy. The Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE) score was 3, corresponding to a PFO‑attributable fraction of approximately 23%. This case illustrates a dual-risk mechanism for stroke: a persistent prothrombotic state coexisting with a definitive structural embolic pathway. The patient subsequently underwent percutaneous PFO closure. This case highlights the conflict between the need for individualized intervention based on dual high-risk mechanisms and the age-based recommendations of current guidelines (ESC 2023, AHA/ASA 2021). Anatomical assessment of the PFO enables a more precise estimation of stroke recurrence risk and the potential value of closure. As a causative therapy aimed at eliminating the structural embolic pathway, PFO closure may represent a reasonable interventional strategy in such carefully selected high-risk patients; however, its definitive net clinical benefit requires validation through prospective, large-scale trials.
title: Decision dilemmas and insights in secondary prevention of ischemic stroke: a case report of an elderly patient with hereditary thrombophilia and high-risk patent foramen ovale.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify the independent risk factors associated with radial artery occlusion (RAO) after right transradial coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and construct a visualized nomogram for individualized RAO risk prediction.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 561 patients with suspected angina pectoris undergoing right transradial CAG/PCI from December 2023 to June 2024; all patients received a uniform 6F radial sheath. Radial artery patency was evaluated 24 h post-procedure via modified reverse Barbeau test (MRBT). Patients were divided into RAO group (n=49) and non-RAO group (n=512). Univariate logistic regression screened candidate variables (screen threshold p<0.1), and backward stepwise multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors. A nomogram was established based on regression coefficients of independent predictors. Model performance was assessed by ROC curve (AUC), calibration curve combined with Hosmer-Lemeshow (HL) test, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: The overall incidence of RAO was 8.7%. Multivariable logistic regression identified four independent risk factors for RAO: prior coronary artery disease, multiple puncture attempts, puncture duration >15 min and radial arterial spasm. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.754 (95%CI 0.671-0.837). The calibration curve showed favorable consistency between predicted and actual RAO incidence, with HL test p=0.536. DCA verified reliable clinical net benefit of the nomogram for risk stratification.
CONCLUSIONS: Four independent predictors of post-transradial RAO were confirmed:prior coronary artery disease, multiple puncture attempts, puncture duration>15min and radial arterial spasm. The nomogram built on these four factors exhibited satisfactory discrimination, calibration and clinical utility. This tool can help clinicians screen high-risk patients and deliver targeted preventive interventions, while avoiding unnecessary prophylaxis for low-risk individuals. Further prospective external validation of this model is required.
title: Risk factors of radial artery occlusion following via transradial coronary catheterization.
Selective coronary hypoxemia during VA-ECMO: limitations of peripheral oxygenation monitoring.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. While percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the definitive reperfusion strategy, residual disease burden and plaque vulnerability both influence clinical recovery. The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) quantifies untreated macroscopic coronary artery disease, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) resolves microscopic plaque architecture, notably thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA). This pilot study explored the descriptive characteristics and short-term outcomes associated with combining rSS and OCT-derived TCFA in a highly selected STEMI cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective observational pilot study included 30 patients with STEMI who underwent primary PCI and culprit lesion OCT evaluation at a tertiary care center. Patients were stratified into four groups according to the presence of culprit TCFA and the post-PCI rSS threshold ( ≤ 4 vs. > 4): group 0 (TCFA absent, rSS > 4), group 1 (TCFA absent, rSS ≤ 4), group 2 (TCFA present, rSS > 4), and group 3 (TCFA present, rSS ≤ 4). The primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE)-a composite of all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, heart failure hospitalisation, and ischemic stroke-assessed over 3 months.
RESULTS: The cohort (mean age, 54.5 ± 10.1 years; 83.3% male, 40% with diabetes mellitus) had a 53.3% prevalence (16 of 30) of culprit lesion TCFA. Complete or reasonable revascularization (rSS ≤ 4) was achieved in 12 patients (40.0%). The overall cumulative 3-month MACE rate was 30.0% (9 of 30). MACE occurred in 1 of 7 patients (14.3%) in group 0, 1 of 7 (14.3%) in group 1, 4 of 11 (36.4%) in group 2, and 3 of 5 (60.0%) in group 3 (Fisher exact test, P = 0.23; log-rank P = 0.38). Patients with TCFA accounted for 7 of 9 clinical events (77.8%). Given the small subgroup sizes (n < 12), multivariable predictive risk modeling was not performed.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot cohort of STEMI patients undergoing PCI, the presence of OCT-derived TCFA was descriptively associated with higher short-term adverse event rates across both complete and incomplete revascularization strata. Given the small sample size and clear indication bias, these findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and support the need for adequately powered prospective registries to evaluate dual anatomical-biological risk stratification.
title: Residual SYNTAX score and optical coherence tomography-derived thin-cap fibroatheroma in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: an exploratory descriptive pilot study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of the Vascular Mimetic Implant-Common Femoral Artery Study (VMI-CFA) investigation is to evaluate the mid-term (24 months) outcome of treatment of the common femoral artery (CFA) with the Supera Peripheral Stent System (Abbott Vascular Inc., Santa Clara, USA) in symptomatic (Rutherford 2-4), de novo stenotic or occlusive lesions.
METHODS: One hundred patients with atherosclerotic lesions in the CFA were recruited for the VMI-CFA trial during routine consultations in hospitals in Belgium and France. The key inclusion criterion was de novo, stenotic (>50%) or occlusive lesions located in the native CFA. The main exclusion criteria were asymptomatic disease, (in-stent) restenosis and occlusion of the deep femoral artery. The primary efficacy and safety endpoint were defined respectively as primary patency at 12 months core lab adjudicated and any periprocedural adverse events up to 30 days post-procedure. The secondary endpoints included technical success rate, primary patency at 1, 6 and 24 months post-procedure, freedom from target lesion revascularization (TLR) at 1, 6, 12 and 24 months post-procedure and clinical success.
RESULTS: The Supera Stent was deployed and implanted successfully in all 100 patients. At 12 and 24 months, the primary patency rate was 95.2% and 92.8%, respectively. Two patients had to undergo a TLR between 6 and 12 months of follow-up, which resulted in a freedom from TLR rate of 97.8%. This rate remained the same at 24-month follow-up. Regarding the primary safety endpoint, there were 17 periprocedural adverse events in the first month after the index procedure, but no device- or procedure-related deaths, TLRs, major target limb amputations or thromboses were reported. Survival rate at 12 months was 91.8%. At 1, 6 and 24 months of follow-up, the survival rate was 100%, 96.9% and 85.5%, respectively. Fourteen patients died during the 2-year follow-up period. None of the deaths was procedure- or study-device related. A clear shift from Rutherford classification 2 to 4 toward 0 to 1 was seen and displays the clinical success of the endovascular therapy with the Supera Peripheral Stent System.
CONCLUSION: The VMI-CFA trial shows that endovascular treatment of the "no-stent zone" CFA atherosclerotic disease with the Supera Peripheral Stent System is a safe and efficient therapy in CFA treatment.Clinical ImpactThis study provides prospective evidence supporting Supera stenting for common femoral artery disease, traditionally treated by open endarterectomy. The encouraging patency and safety outcomes suggest a minimally invasive alternative for selected patients, particularly those with hostile groin anatomy or increased risk of wound complications. By specifically evaluating an interwoven nitinol stent in this challenging arterial territory, these findings may help clinicians individualize revascularization strategies. However, the nonrandomized design does not establish superiority over endarterectomy. Randomized comparative evidence is needed before broader adoption or changes to the current standard of care.
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
title: The 12 and 24 Months Results of the VMI-CFA Study, a Physician-Initiated Trial Investigating the Efficacy of the Vascular Mimetic Implant Supera Peripheral Stent System for the Treatment of the Common Femoral Artery.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in true bifurcation coronary lesions can lead to repeat revascularization and adverse outcomes.
AIMS: To identify independent risk factors for ISR in patients with coronary bifurcation lesions undergoing PCI and to develop a predictive model for ISR-free survival.
METHODS: Patients with coronary artery disease and Medina coronary bifurcation lesions was analyzed. Baseline characteristics, laboratory values, bifurcation anatomy, and PCI details were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify independent predictors of ISR and its performance was evaluated Model interpretability was explored with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and a nomogram was constructed for clinical use.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis showed lesion/procedural factors were strongly predictive. Multivariable Cox analysis identified use of a drug-coated balloon in the side branch and side-branch stenting with a drug-eluting stent as the top independent predictors of ISR. Lesion location in the left circumflex was associated with higher ISR risk The Cox model Calibration plots showed close agreement between predicted and observed ISR probabilities. A SHAP analysis confirmed the direction and relative importance of each predictor, enhancing the model's interpretability.
CONCLUSIONS: In true bifurcation PCI, Side-branch interventions are associated with higher ISR risk, whereas a simple single-stent approach confers lower risk. The developed Cox-based nomogram demonstrated robust ability to predict ISR, which can aid clinicians in risk stratification and personalized management. Early identification of high-risk patients may enable closer surveillance or preventive measures to improve long-term outcomes after bifurcation PCI.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Risk Factors and Predictive Model for In-Stent Restenosis After PCI in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: A Retrospective Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombus in transit (TIT) through a patent foramen ovale (PFO) or atrial septal defect (ASD) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition associated with paradoxical embolism. Despite advances in imaging and interventional techniques, optimal management strategies remain poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes of adult patients with TIT across right-to-left intra-atrial shunts.
DESIGN: Systematic review of published cases.
DATA SOURCES AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through March 2025 for case reports, case series, and letters describing adult patients with TIT visualized by transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography. After screening 1736 records, 278 studies reporting 297 patients were included. Two independent reviewers extracted demographic, clinical, imaging, treatment, and outcome data. Descriptive statistics were summarized, and treatment groups were compared using chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests. Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank testing assessed 120-day survival, and multivariable Cox regression was used to evaluate potential predictors of mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 297 patients from 278 studies were included. The mean age was 58.5 ± 15.8 years, and 50.2% were male. Respiratory symptoms predominated (77.7%), followed by cardiac (29.7%) and neurological (23.0%) manifestations. Provoked events accounted for 70.3% of cases, most commonly in the postoperative setting. Thrombi were detected by transthoracic echocardiography in 92.1% of cases and by transesophageal echocardiography in 100%. Management strategies included surgical embolectomy (57.8%), anticoagulation (36.5%), thrombolysis (13.5%), and percutaneous aspiration (2.7%); 61.1% underwent PFO/ASD closure. Overall mortality was 8.3%. Surgical management was associated with the lowest mortality (3.0%) and the highest short-term clinical improvement (90.5%; p < 0.001). Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality (16.6% and 25.0%, respectively). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated superior 120-day survival with surgical management compared with other treatment strategies (log-rank p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox models, no independent predictors of mortality were identified.
CONCLUSION: In this largest synthesis of TIT cases to date, surgical management and PFO/ASD closure were associated with favorable short-term outcomes. Surgical intervention demonstrated the lowest observed mortality, while anticoagulation provided acceptable outcomes in selected patients. Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality. These findings support the role of definitive management and shunt closure in selected patients, although prospective studies are needed to establish standardized treatment strategies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (INPLASY) (Registration number: INPLASY202630021).
title: Management strategies for right-to-left intraatrial shunt with thrombus in transit: a systematic review of 297 patients and associated mortality outcomes.

abstract: Hybrid coronary revascularization (HCR) is a strategy combining minimally invasive left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery bypass grafting with percutaneous coronary intervention of the remaining vessels. This approach is of particular relevance in elderly (60-74 years) and senile (≥75 years) patients due to high surgical risk and severe comorbidities. This review analyzes current evidence (2016-2025) on the efficacy and safety of HCR in this population. HCR provides long-term survival comparable to conventional coronary artery bypass grafting with lower perioperative trauma, shorter hospital stay, and reduced neurological complications. Key limitations include the need for dual antiplatelet therapy, higher mid-term repeat revascularization rates, technical complexity, and resource intensity. Decisions regarding HCR in elderly patients require thorough multidisciplinary assessment including frailty screening, functional status, and life expectancy evaluation.
keywords: left internal mammary artery – left anterior descending artery
title: [Hybrid myocardial revascularization in elderly and senile patients: Advantages and disadvantages.].

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) combined with valve surgery represent a high-risk surgical population with substantial perioperative hemodynamic disturbances and highly variable organ function, leading to high variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetics. Conventional vancomycin dosing solely on renal function frequently fails to achieve target trough concentrations in this complex subgroup. This study aimed to identify independent correlates c of vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations (Css-min), and to report observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, to inform individualized therapeutic drug monitoring.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery from January 2018 to October 2024. Clinical data and vancomycin TDM records were extracted from electronic medical records. Vancomycin Css-min was detected by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay technique. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) accounting for within-patient repeated TDM measurements were used to identify clinical correlates of Css-min. IABP support was pre-specified and force-entered into the multivariable model based on clinical observations and pathophysiological reasoning, independent of univariate screening results. We performed a sensitivity analysis for patients with at least one TDM within postoperative day 7, prespecified interaction tests for effect modification, and binary logistic-GEE for the supratherapeutic endpoint (Css-min > 20 mg/L). A two-tailed P < 0.05 was set as statistical significance.
RESULTS: A total of 283 eligible patients with 473 valid Css-min measurements were included. Multivariate GEE demonstrated that categorical vancomycin dosing regimen, age, ventilator dependence ≥96 h, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), IABP support, serum creatinine (Scr), and serum urea nitrogen (SUN) were positively associated with higher geometric-mean Css-min. Associations remained largely consistent in the sensitivity-analysis subgroup of patients with at least one early-phase TDM within postoperative day 7. A significant CRRT-by-postoperative-time interaction was detected, indicating that the influence of CRRT on vancomycin exposure varied across different postoperative phases. Of note, the association signal linking IABP to supratherapeutic trough concentrations (Css-min>20 mg/L) was modest and requires cautious interpretation.
CONCLUSION: Multiple clinical factors jointly affect vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations in patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery, including dosing regimen, age, renal biomarkers, and critical-care supportive interventions such as IABP, CRRT and prolonged mechanical ventilation. IABP support represents an intriguing observational signal; this finding remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation before it can guide formal dose-adjustment strategies. Individualized vancomycin management for this population should comprehensively integrate hemodynamic support measures and laboratory indices rather than depend merely on renal-function markers. This study focuses on clinically accessible trough concentration monitoring rather than constructing complex pharmacokinetic models, which is more in line with real-world clinical practice.
title: Independent correlates of vancomycin steady-state trough concentration among patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery: observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump support.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are routinely used in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to prevent gastrointestinal bleeding associated with dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). However, long-term PPI use has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis. Tegoprazan, a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), may exert distinct effects on the gut microbiome. This study compared the longitudinal effects of tegoprazan and pantoprazole on gut microbiota composition in patients with angina undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study randomized 38 patients 1:1:1 to tegoprazan 50 mg once daily, pantoprazole 40 mg once daily, or no acid-suppressive therapy for 24 weeks. Five participants did not provide baseline fecal samples, and nine discontinued participation before week 24. Thus, 24 participants with paired baseline and week-24 fecal samples were included in the final analysis. Fecal samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
RESULTS: No drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in any group. Observed amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness was significantly higher at week 24 than at baseline in the overall cohort (p = 0.003) and P-CAB group (p = 0.016), whereas the Shannon index showed no significant changes. Paired PERMANOVA with permutations restricted by patient ID revealed significant differences in Bray-Curtis beta diversity between baseline and week 24 in the P-CAB group (R² = 0.070, p = 0.031) and PPI group (R² = 0.059, p = 0.008), but not in the no acid-suppressive therapy group (R² = 0.021, p = 0.691). In the formal cross-arm analysis, the treatment group-by-visit interaction was not significant for Bray-Curtis beta diversity (R² = 0.021, pseudo-F = 0.505, p = 0.270). Although nominal within-arm taxonomic changes were observed, no treatment group-by-visit interaction survived Benjamini-Hochberg correction in ANCOM-BC2.
CONCLUSION: Tegoprazan was well tolerated, with no drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding during the 24-week follow-up. Both acid-suppressive treatment groups showed modest longitudinal microbiome changes. The taxon-level findings were exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of treatment-specific differential effects. Larger, adequately powered studies are required to confirm these observations.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
title: Effect of a potassium-competitive acid blocker on the gut microbiota in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomized pilot study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis, a recognised manifestation of systemic metabolic dysfunction, remains incompletely characterised in terms of its independent association with clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), particularly in South Asian populations where prior studies have relied on surrogate markers.
AIM: To evaluate the association of objectively quantified hepatic steatosis with clinical ASCVD events in an Indian cohort.
DESIGN: Hospital-based, frequency-matched (age, sex, BMI) case-control study.
METHODS: 165 ASCVD cases and 165 controls were evaluated. Hepatic steatosis was quantified by vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE; FibroScan®) and examined for its independent association with ASCVD using multivariable logistic regression after adjustment for established cardiovascular risk factors. Dose-response relationships and phenotype-specific associations were additionally assessed.
RESULTS: Hepatic steatosis, modelled as a continuous CAP exposure, was independently associated with ASCVD (aOR 2.02 per 1-SD increase; 95% CI 1.48-2.75; p < 0.001), an association concentrated above an empirically-identified threshold of 260 dB/m (no association below this level, p = 0.73; strong association above it, p < 0.0001). Consistent with this, only severe steatosis (S3, ≥280 dB/m) was independently significant on categorical analysis (aOR 5.13; 95% CI 2.45-10.73; p < 0.001); mild and moderate grades were not. The association was predominantly driven by acute coronary syndrome; analyses for cerebrovascular accident and peripheral artery disease were limited by sample size. Unmatched cardiometabolic risk factors - diabetes, hypertension, smoking, and dyslipidaemia - behaved as expected, supporting model validity; age, sex, and BMI, the matched variables, showed the attenuated associations expected under frequency matching.
CONCLUSION: VCTE-defined hepatic steatosis is independently associated with major ASCVD events in a severity-dependent manner in an Indian cohort. The observed association was primarily driven by ACS; CVA and PAD showed numerically elevated but non-significant associations and require validation in adequately powered cohorts. The association was concentrated at severe steatosis, consistent with a threshold rather than a linear dose-response effect. Given the cross-sectional design, temporal precedence between steatosis and ASCVD cannot be established. These findings suggest hepatic steatosis assessment may merit consideration within cardiovascular risk evaluation, particularly in high-risk South Asian populations, pending validation in prospective cohorts.
title: Association of hepatic steatosis with atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: A hospital-based case-control study from India.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relieving the fixed afterload of severe aortic stenosis can unmask a previously concealed dynamic outflow-tract obstruction.
CASE SUMMARY: A 69-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.65 cm2; 109/64 mmHg), mild concentric hypertrophy (septum 15 mm), and no baseline systolic anterior motion (SAM) underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The invasive peak-to-peak gradient fell from 64 to 7 mmHg, but echocardiography immediately afterwards showed new SAM and severe dynamic left-ventricular-outflow-tract (LVOT) obstruction (170/67 mmHg) with hypotension. Treatment was load-directed (volume expansion, avoidance of vasodilators and inotropes, beta-blockade), with a cardiac myosin inhibitor as an adjunct. Over 4 months the resting LVOT gradient fell to 22/13 mmHg and the provoked peak to 29 mmHg, with SAM no longer seen and preserved ejection fraction.
DISCUSSION: Recognizing this load-dependent obstruction during the procedure and restoring loading, rather than escalating inotropes, is the key lesson.
title: Severe dynamic left-ventricular outflow-tract obstruction unmasked by transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a case report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic value of three-vessel quantitative flow ratio (3V-QFR) in patients with borderline coronary lesions (QFR 0.75-0.80) over a 2-year period; to identify key variables using LASSO regression; and to construct and internally validate a personalized nomogram model for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) over 2 years.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with coronary artery disease who were treated at Ordos Central Hospital from January 2021 to December 2024, underwent coronary angiography revealing at least one borderline lesion in a major coronary artery, and received a QFR assessment. Patients were followed for up to 24 months after discharge through outpatient visits, telephone follow-up, and electronic medical-record review. The primary endpoint was defined as the occurrence of MACE during the 2-year follow-up period. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to explore the nonlinear relationship between 3V-QFR and the risk of MACE. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized regression evaluated 19 prespecified candidate predictors using 10-fold cross-validation and the one-standard-error rule. A nomogram was constructed based on the selected factors, and the model's discriminatory power, consistency, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap resamples that repeated the complete preprocessing, variable-selection, and model-refitting pipeline.
RESULTS: A total of 138 patients with borderline lesions were enrolled (33 in the MACE group and 105 in the non-MACE group). Among 33 first MACE events, 20 were ischemia-driven revascularizations, 9 were non-fatal myocardial infarctions, and 4 were all-cause deaths. RCS analysis showed an overall association between lower 3V-QFR and higher MACE risk, whereas evidence for nonlinearity was not statistically strong; multivariable regression supported 3V-QFR as an independent predictor. LASSO regression identified four optimal predictors of 2-year MACE through 10-fold cross-validation: 3V-QFR, age, diabetes, and NT-proBNP levels. The final model included 3V-QFR, age, diabetes, and NT-proBNP. The apparent AUC was 0.869 (95% CI 0.802-0.936), and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.842 (95% CI 0.771-0.913); calibration and decision-curve findings were considered exploratory.
CONCLUSION: Lower 3V-QFR was associated with higher 2-year MACE risk in this retrospective development cohort. The 3V-QFR-based nomogram showed promising internal performance and may support exploratory risk stratification; independent external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.
title: A 2-year prognostic assessment of patients with coronary borderline lesions based on three-vessel quantitative flow ratio and the development and internal validation of a risk prediction nomogram.

abstract: Guidewire entrapment within an implanted coronary stent is a rare but potentially serious complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and its management can be technically challenging. An 81-year-old woman presenting with acute myocardial infarction underwent PCI for a severely stenotic lesion in the right coronary artery. After drug-eluting stent implantation and post-dilatation, intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed deformation at the distal edge of the stent. During withdrawal of the IVUS catheter, the catheter and guidewire became entangled with the deformed stent. Although the IVUS catheter was successfully removed with careful manipulation, the guidewire remained firmly entrapped within the stent and could not be retrieved despite repeated attempts. A Tornus penetration catheter was subsequently advanced over the entrapped guidewire using rotational manipulation toward the site of entrapment. When the catheter reached the entrapped segment, the guidewire was successfully disengaged from the stent and retrieved. Following successful bailout, distal stent fracture and proximal coronary dissection were identified, requiring additional stent implantation. This case demonstrates a potential bailout technique for guidewire entrapment within a coronary stent. Rotational advancement of a penetration catheter to the site of entrapment may facilitate disengagement of an entrapped guidewire when standard manipulation is unsuccessful.
title: Successful Bailout of Guidewire Entrapment Within a Coronary Stent Using a Tornus Penetration Catheter: A Case Report.

abstract: Sex-based differences in ACS presentation and outcomes have been observed, but limited information is available on sex-specific electrocardiogram (ECG) features and their prevalence in this context. The aim of this study was to compare the prevalence of different ECG patterns between sexes and their prognostic roles for in-hospital mortality in ACS patients. This prospective single-center study (NCT02438085)° was conducted from June 2018 to December 2019, including 841 consecutive patients. Data on baseline characteristics, ECG findings, treatments, and outcomes were collected. Statistical analyses were performed to determine differences in the prevalence of various ECG patterns and identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality. Males more frequently presented with ST-segment elevation (51% vs. 43%, p = 0.031) and hyperacute T waves (13% vs. 7%, p = 0.006) than females. Moreover, females more often had a normal ECG at admission (15% vs. 9%, p = 0.01). In female STEMI negative T waves (50% vs. 38%, p = 0.025) were more common than in males. Hyperacute T waves were linked to a higher risk of in-hospital death in female STEMI cases (OR=6.25, 95% CI: 1.0 -39.7, p = 0.048). Additionally the development of left bundle branch block during hospitalization (OR=14.4, 95% CI: 1.48-14 p = 0.02) was a significant predictor of in-hospital mortality in the female NSTEMI subgroup. No ECG features were found to predict in-hospital mortality in male patients. Compared to males, females with ACS often showed less frequent and less extensive ST-segment abnormalities and were more likely to have a normal initial ECG at admission. These differences could impact clinical evaluation and prognosis. Recognizing these sex-related ECG differences may help optimize the management of ACS patients. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT02438085.
keywords: NSTEMI = non ST elevation myocardial infarction
title: Sex differences in electrocardiographic patterns among patients with acute coronary syndromes.

abstract: Over the past decade, a diverse pipeline of factor XI (FXI)/XIa-targeting agents has entered clinical development, including oral small-molecule inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, antisense oligonucleotides, and small interfering RNAs. Across early- and late-phase clinical trials, these agents have generally shown a favorable safety profile, with consistently low rates of major bleeding, even when used with antiplatelet therapy or compared with standard anticoagulants. However, efficacy signals have varied by clinical setting. In venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after orthopedic surgery and in secondary stroke prevention, FXI/XIa inhibition has shown encouraging antithrombotic activity. In contrast, trials in atrial fibrillation, acute coronary syndrome, and cancer-associated thrombosis have yielded mixed efficacy results, highlighting potential limitations of intrinsic pathway inhibition in conditions with high thrombin generation or platelet-driven thrombosis. Collectively, these findings position FXI/XIa inhibitors as a potential paradigm shift in antithrombotic therapy for targeted indications, with ongoing phase 3 studies expected to further define their clinical role and optimal use across diverse thrombotic disorders.
journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
title: Perspectives: what we are learning from factor XI/factor XIa inhibitor trials.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) requires multimodality evaluation, including cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), intracoronary (IC) imaging, and coronary function testing (CFT). However, real-world uptake of these guideline-recommended modalities varies widely. We conducted a global survey to characterize practice variation in MINOCA evaluation and management across demographic characteristics, continents, and economic settings.
METHODS: A 16-item online survey targeting cardiologists and cardiology trainees was distributed globally between August and December 2024. Respondents provided information on demographic characteristics, institutional context, and routine diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for MINOCA. Descriptive statistics, χ2 tests, and multiple regression analysis were used to assess associations.
RESULTS: A total of 329 cardiology professionals from 6 continents participated (69.6% interventional cardiologists; 45.9% practicing in high-income countries [HIC]). Overall, 64.1% of respondents reported routine statin use and 55.6% reported beta-blocker use in MINOCA management. Advanced diagnostic modalities demonstrated substantial geographic variation. Europe reported the highest use of CMR (80.6%) and CFT (38.9%), whereas IC imaging was most frequently reported in North America (44.1%). Respondents from HIC reported greater routine use of CMR (56.3% vs 31.6%), IC imaging (41.7% vs 28.9%), and CFT (31.1% vs 13.2%) compared with those from lower-income settings (all P < .01). In multivariable analyses, HIC status remained the strongest independent predictor of routine CMR use (odds ratio [OR], 3.95; 95% CI, 2.34-6.68), IC imaging use (OR, 3.01; 95% CI, 1.74-5.20), and CFT use (OR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.26-4.14). Academic or teaching hospital affiliation was independently associated with higher CMR use (OR, 2.19; 95% CI, 1.07-4.51), while female respondents reported higher odds of CFT use (OR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.01-3.54).
CONCLUSIONS: Significant global disparities exist in the diagnostic evaluation of MINOCA. After adjustment, economic context emerged as the most consistent determinant of advanced diagnostic modality use. These findings highlight persistent structural barriers to the implementation of guideline-recommended MINOCA evaluation and underscore the need for strategies that expand access to advanced diagnostics and promote standardized evaluation pathways across diverse health care settings.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
keywords: myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
title: Global Disparities in Diagnostic and Therapeutic Strategies for Myocardial Infarction With Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries: An International Survey.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), a standard therapy for aortic stenosis, is preferred for older or high-risk patients. Various complications, including heart failure (HF), resulting in increased mortality, have been reported in the literature. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are recommended in HF, irrespective of ejection fraction; however, their role in reducing post-TAVR cardiovascular complications remains underexplored. We conducted a retrospective study to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes associated with the use of SGLT2i in post-TAVR patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort was based on a global database of electronic health records of more than 160 million patients. After propensity-score matching, the study population included 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients divided into 2 cohorts based on their exposure to SGLT2i. Exposure to SGLT2i was defined as exposure after 1 day of TAVR.
RESULTS: In this study of 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients, the primary outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events and secondary outcomes, ie, cardiovascular mortality, ischemic stroke, and HF exacerbation, were significantly reduced in SGLT2i-exposed post-TAVR patients at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up. Hemorrhagic stroke was comparable at the 1-month follow-up; however, it was significantly lower in SGLT2i-exposed cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. The risk of new-onset myocardial infarction was significantly reduced at 1 month; however, it was comparable between the 2 cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. Our study also demonstrated a significant reduction in the risk of end-stage renal disease in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort at the 1-year follow-up. The periprocedural risk of acute kidney injury (within 7 days of TAVR) as well as at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up was significantly lower in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, post-TAVR SGLT2i use in diabetic patients was associated with reduced cardiovascular morbidity and mortality for up to 1 year.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort from a global EHR database, propensity-score matched; 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective EHR data with exposure defined after day 1, so immortal time bias and residual confounding are likely.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched electronic health record cohort associated post-TAVR SGLT2 inhibitor use in diabetic patients with fewer cardiovascular events up to one year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major adverse cardiovascular events and secondary outcomes (cardiovascular mortality, ischemic stroke, and HF exacerbation) were significantly reduced in SGLT2i-exposed post-TAVR patients at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up. The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports testing the benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors after TAVR in a target trial emulation or randomised design.

journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Clinical Efficacy of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Diabetes: A Global Retrospective Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous management of high risk, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) needing mechanical support for complex coronary artery disease in patients needing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis remains incompletely defined. We report on the feasibility and safety of a single-session strategy using Impella-assisted complex high-risk PCI (IA-CHIP) followed by transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing simultaneous IA-CHIP and TAVR at 3 tertiary centers between January 2015 and March 2026. All patients received mechanical circulatory support with percutaneous microaxial flow pump Impella CP (Abiomed) during PCI, followed by transfemoral TAVR in the same session. Baseline demographics, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes were collected. The primary endpoint was in-hospital complications, including death, stroke, major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 2, 3, or 5), acute kidney injury, permanent pacemaker implantation, and vascular complications.
RESULTS: A total of 12 patients were included (median age, 79.5 years [IQR, 77.0-81.2]; 91.7% male; median Charlson Comorbidity Index of 7 [IQR, 5.8-9]). Coronary lesions mainly involved left main disease in 66% of cases. Advanced calcium modification was required in 50% of cases. The median aortic valve area was 0.86 cm2, and median mean gradient was 38 mm Hg. Procedural success for IA-CHIP and TAVR was 100%. There were no in-hospital deaths, strokes, or major vascular complications. Conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 25%. An acute kidney injury occurred in 16.7% of cases, with no requirement for dialysis. The majority of patients (91.7%) were discharged home.
CONCLUSIONS: A single-session strategy of IA-CHIP followed by TAVR is feasible and safe in selected patients with complex coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Clinical Outcomes of Concurrent Impella-Assisted High-Risk PCI and TAVR in Patients With Complex Coronary Artery Disease and Severe Aortic Stenosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) programs aim to enhance procedural safety and efficiency in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This analysis evaluates changes in PCI practice patterns and outcomes after implementation of a multidisciplinary catheterization laboratory CQI committee at a large academic center.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted regarding PCI procedures from January 2018 to June 2024 using National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI data. Outcomes and practice patterns were compared before (pre-CQI: 2018-October 2022) versus after CQI implementation (post-CQI: November 2022-2024). Prespecified primary end points were post-PCI acute kidney injury, periprocedural hemoglobin change, and same-day discharge.
RESULTS: Among 2759 PCI cases (1783 pre-CQI; 976 post-CQI), monthly PCI volume increased (30.7-48.2 cases/mo, P < .001). Post-CQI, radial access use increased (33.4%-58.9%, P < .001) and mean contrast volume decreased (188-153 mL, P < .001). Primary outcomes improved post-CQI: acute kidney injury decreased (14.3%-9.7%, P = .01), mean periprocedural hemoglobin change decreased (0.65-0.54 g/dL, P = .004), and same-day discharge increased (13.0%-24.7%, P < .001). Overall complication rates and in-hospital mortality remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a catheterization laboratory CQI committee was temporally associated with improved PCI safety and discharge efficiency alongside increased procedural volume and evolving case mix. These findings support CQI-driven approaches to optimize PCI care delivery.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Impact of a Continuous Quality Improvement Committee on Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract: Poor organelle viability and rapid immune clearance limit mitochondrial transplantation for ischemic disease. Here, we engineer mitochondria-rich cytochalasomes (MRCs) as an intravenously deliverable vesicle platform. MRCs are generated through cytoskeletal remodeling in mesenchymal stem cells. They encapsulate functional mitochondria, protecting them from extracellular stressors and inheriting immunomodulatory proteins, which reduce macrophage phagocytosis by more than sixfold. Mechanistically, MRCs do not fuse with the host mitochondrial network but instead are trafficked to lysosomes and trigger protective autophagy-lysosomal response. In a murine myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) model, a single intravenous injection of MRCs reduced infarct size by 52% and preserved cardiac function for up to 28 days, whereas isolated mitochondria were ineffective. This work positions MRCs as a promising intravenously deliverable vesicle platform for ischemic heart disease and reveals a non-fusogenic mechanism.
title: Mitochondria-rich cytochalasomes as an intravenously deliverable vesicle platform for ischemic heart disease.

abstract: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve can arise across diverse anatomic substrates. We report 5 consecutive patients with systolic anterior motion-mediated left ventricular outflow tract obstruction treated with the PASCAL Ace (Edwards Lifesciences) device at a single center. Technical success, mitral regurgitation reduction to ≤2+, relief of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and symptomatic improvement to New York Heart Association class I to II were achieved in all patients, without clinically significant mitral stenosis.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Mitral Valve Systolic Anterior Motion in Complex Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Phenotypes: A Case Series.

journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Outcomes of Surgical Versus Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair or Replacement in Patients With Myocardial Infarction and Concomitant Mitral Regurgitation: A Retrospective Analysis of Real-World Data.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data exist on the optimal stenting strategy for isolated ostial left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) lesions. The aim of this study was to compare the outcomes in patients who had a significant isolated ostial LAD stenosis treated with either left main crossover stenting (LMCS) or focal ostial LAD stenting (FO-LAD).
METHODS: The primary end point of the study was target lesion failure (TLF), a composite of target lesion revascularization, target vessel myocardial infarction, and cardiac death at 2 years. Secondary end points included the individual components of the primary outcome. Additional secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events, which are a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, and any unplanned revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 522 patients were included in this study, of whom 382 underwent FO-LAD stenting and 140 underwent LMCS. The primary outcome occurred in 32 patients (22.9%) in the LMCS and in 44 patients (11.5%) in the FO-LAD group at a median follow-up of 730 days (IQR, 451-730). LMCS was associated with a higher risk of TLF compared with FO-LAD stenting (adjusted HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.16-2.98; P = .01).With regard to secondary outcomes, LMCS was associated with more major adverse cardiovascular events (31.4% vs 15.5%; adjusted HR, 2.11 [1.41-3.17]; P < .001) and cardiac death (17.1% vs 7.9%; adjusted HR, 2.05 [1.19-3.55]; P = .01]. No significant differences were observed for target lesion revascularization and target vessel myocardial infarction.
CONCLUSIONS: Left main crossover stenting was associated with a higher rate of TLF at a median follow-up of 2 years when compared with FO-LAD stenting in the treatment of patients with significant isolated ostial LAD disease.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Ostial vs Left Main Crossover Stenting in Isolated Ostial Left Anterior Descending Stenosis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary perforation at a bifurcation level is a life-threatening emergency. Covered stents may seal the defect but risk side-branch occlusion. We evaluated the feasibility and technical considerations of guide wire fenestration at coronary bifurcations and present a case where a covered side branch was successfully salvaged.
METHODS: A transparent bifurcation phantom replicating coronary anatomy was constructed and integrated into a pulsatile flow system. Three fenestration strategies were evaluated: (1) a balloon-blocking approach, in which inflation of a balloon in the main branch after covered stent deployment was hypothesized to facilitate wire redirection and fenestration; (2) a microcatheter-assisted approach; and (3) a wire-only approach. These strategies were tested by 15 percutaneous coronary intervention operators with varying levels of experience. Seven guide wires with differing characteristics and tip loads ranging from 3 to 12 g were used.
RESULTS: The balloon occlusion strategy achieved fenestration in all tests (n = 15) using both 12 g and 3 g wires, as did microcatheter-assisted fenestrations (n = 2). Wire-only strategy succeeded in 14 of 17 attempts across wires ranging from 3 to 12 g; however, 3 of 6 attempts using 3 g wires required conversion to balloon occlusion. Median time to fenestration was 69 seconds for both balloon occlusion and microcatheter strategies, compared with 81 seconds, 94 seconds, and 167 seconds for wire-only approaches using 12 g, 6 g, and 3 g wires, respectively. Angiography and micro-computed tomography demonstrated satisfactory results, but endoscopic analysis revealed polyurethane membrane recoil reducing the ostial area by up to 75%, necessitating side-branch stenting. All evaluated side-branch stenting techniques improved the ostial lumen area.
CONCLUSIONS: Covered stent fenestration is a feasible bailout strategy for preserving side-branch patency in critical bifurcation perforations.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Covered Stent Fenestration for Side Branch Salvage in Bifurcation Coronary Perforation: A Systematic Bench-Test Evaluation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the mitral valve is conventionally performed via transfemoral venous access. When this route is not feasible, the right internal jugular vein may provide an alternative, but procedural experience remains limited.
CASE SUMMARY: A 93-year-old woman with refractory heart failure had atrial functional mitral regurgitation and low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis. After transcatheter aortic valve implantation, moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation persisted. Transfemoral edge-to-edge repair was unsuccessful because severe iliac venous tortuosity prevented adequate catheter control. The procedure was subsequently performed via the right internal jugular vein using the MitraClip G4 system. A pre-existing iatrogenic atrial septal defect was reused, and temporary left ventricular apical wire support facilitated advancement of the steerable guiding catheter into the left atrium. Stepwise + knob rotation increased height and working space, improved the markedly under-straddled configuration, and permitted further advancement of the clip delivery system. Subsequent M- and P-knob adjustments achieved an appropriate trajectory towards A2/P2, with an S-shaped fluoroscopic configuration. Leaflet grasping reduced mitral regurgitation to mild without access-site complications. Mild mitral regurgitation was maintained at 6 months without heart-failure rehospitalization.
DISCUSSION: Right internal jugular access may be a feasible alternative when transfemoral access is not possible. Successful navigation requires recognition of access-specific catheter behaviour and adaptation of steering under real-time fluoroscopy and transoesophageal echocardiography. An S-shaped fluoroscopic configuration may serve as a practical landmark of a favourable trajectory towards the mitral valve.
title: Right internal jugular approach for transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair using the MitraClip G4 system after failed transfemoral access: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest compressions form the basis of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in out of hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Recently, mechanical CPR (MCPR) devices have been introduced, particularly in the prehospital environment, avoiding the need for clinicians to perform conventional manual CPR (CCPR). At our institution, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is available for select OHCA patients in refractory arrest (ECPR). Given ECPR patients typically undergo prolonged chest compressions, there may be a higher likelihood of injury; however, evidence directly comparing ECPR and CCPR injury rates is lacking. This study aimed to investigate incidence and type of traumatic injuries following CPR and whether a difference between ECPR and CCPR patients exists.
RESULTS: 313 OHCA were identified between 2021-2024, with 136 meeting criteria. Mean CPR duration was 24 ± 16 min, and 37 patients (27%) received MCPR. Thirteen patients had ECPR with mean time from cardiac arrest to establishment of ECMO blood flow being 63 ± 18 min, of which 11 (85%) received MCPR. Injuries occurred in 58 patients (43%), with 23 (16.9%) sustaining clinically significant injuries. Rates of mortality were higher for the injured patients compared to the non-injured patients (41 [70%] vs 33 [43%] respectively, p = ≤0.05). On multiple variable logistic regression analysis CPR > 20 min, not ECPR or MCPR, was significantly associated with traumatic injury (OR 2.45, CI 1.15, 5.23, p = ≤0.05).
CONCLUSION: CPR-related injuries are common. CPR >20 min, not ECPR or MCPR, is associated with higher rate of injury. CT imaging in this cohort could be considered to identify these injuries.
title: Incidence of traumatic injuries sustained following cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.

abstract: Although a prepulmonic left main coronary artery is usually considered a lower-risk AAOCA subtype, it may still be associated with acute ischemic symptoms when significant atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is present. Multimodality imaging is essential for defining the coronary anatomy, and coronary artery bypass grafting may be the preferred strategy when severe multivessel disease coexists.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conflicting randomized trial results have generated uncertainty regarding percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) vs oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF). Thus, the objective of this study is to estimate the posterior probability that LAAO confers clinically meaningful excess ischemic stroke risk relative to OAC.
METHODS: A Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis was performed of RCT comparing LAAO with OAC in nonvalvular AF. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke, analyzed using Bayesian random-effects Poisson regression under a vague (primary), skeptical, and enthusiastic prior specification.
RESULTS: Six RCT (7004 patients, +18,000 patient-years) were included. Ischemic stroke incidence rate ratio (IRR) was 1.34 (95% credible interval [CrI], 0.91-1.97; P [IRR > 1.0] = 94%). The probability of exceeding 0.5 and 1.0 excess events/100 patient-years was 12% and 0.5%, respectively. The effect on any-stroke was smaller (IRR, 1.09; 95% CrI, 0.76-1.56; P [IRR > 1.0] = 70%; P [absolute rate difference >0.5%/y] = 4.7%), because of a reduction in hemorrhagic stroke (IRR, 0.55; 95% CrI, 0.23-1.18; P [IRR < 1.0] = 94.5%). The decrease in hemorrhagic stroke was attenuated among trials using direct oral anticoagulants for medical management (IRR, 0.80; 95% CrI, 0.33-1.75).
CONCLUSIONS: In AF, there is a high posterior probability that LAAO is associated with a higher rate of any-stroke, driven by an increase in ischemic stroke relative to OAC. However, the 95% CrI for ischemic stroke crossed unity, and the estimated absolute excess is small. This possible excess must be weighed against a substantial reduction in the risk of hemorrhagic stroke.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of RCT; Six RCT (7004 patients, +18,000 patient-years)
appraisal.main_limitation: The credible interval for ischaemic stroke crossed unity, and the hemorrhagic stroke reduction was attenuated in trials using direct oral anticoagulants for medical management.
appraisal.one_line: Bayesian meta-analysis of six randomised trials estimates a high posterior probability that LAAO carries a small excess of ischaemic stroke relative to oral anticoagulation, offset by less haemorrhagic stroke.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ischaemic stroke incidence rate ratio (IRR) was 1.34 (95% credible interval [CrI], 0.91-1.97; P [IRR > 1.0] = 94%). Any-stroke IRR was 1.09 (95% CrI, 0.76-1.56). Hemorrhagic stroke IRR was 0.55 (95% CrI, 0.23-1.18).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Re-expresses the conflicting LAAO versus OAC trial results as posterior probabilities of clinically meaningful excess harm, which bears on guideline positions for LAAO.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) for the treatment of intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE).
METHODS: A combined decision tree and Markov model was developed to estimate lifetime health care costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALY), and net monetary benefit from the perspective of the United States health care system. Event probabilities during PE management were derived from the PEERLESS randomized controlled trial. Resource utilization, costs, and long-term event probabilities were established from published literature. Scenario analyses and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed to characterize uncertainty.
RESULTS: In the base case analysis, LBMT was cost-saving to CDT (ie, lower costs and higher QALY), with a net monetary benefit of $5850 for the willingness-to-pay threshold of $120,000/QALY for LBMT when compared to CDT. In the PE management phase, LBMT yielded a net $4755 cost-saving and 0.009 QALY gained per patient vs CDT, driven in large part by reduced intensive care unit utilization (-$6454), shorter hospital stay (-$2217), avoided thrombolytic costs (-$4068), and fewer 30-day readmissions (-$1134). The long-term care phase yielded a total of $32,012 additional costs per patient over the lifetime with no incremental difference in costs or QALY between groups. These additional costs were driven by venous thromboembolism-related death ($12,377), chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension diagnosis and treatment ($8080), postacute anticoagulation management ($4512), and recurrent venous thromboembolism ($3289). LBMT remained cost-saving across scenarios evaluating CDT cost assumptions and device-specific chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension rates. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings across multiple parameter ranges.
CONCLUSIONS: Intervention with LBMT in intermediate-risk PE patients in the United States is economically attractive when compared with CDT, resulting in reduced costs and marginally improved patient benefit.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Large-Bore Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A PEERLESS Randomized Controlled Trial Post Hoc Analysis.

abstract: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) in the setting of prior transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and severe mitral annular calcification (MAC) can pose procedural challenges. We describe the case of an 82-year-old woman with prior TAVR (29 mm EVOLUT FX+; Medtronic), P2 flail, and heavy circumferential MAC underwent M-TEER with the PASCAL Ace device (Edwards Lifesciences). This case illustrates that M-TEER can be performed safely and effectively in anatomies complicated by severe MAC and prior TAVR with careful preprocedural planning, intraprocedural imaging, and operator experience.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-access percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the Impella CP (Abiomed) has increased in prevalence. Despite this, the optimal PCI sheath remains unknown. We characterized the optimal 7F PCI sheath using the single-access technique.
METHODS: The outer diameter measurement of the sheaths was performed using a Keyence 2-axis laser micrometer (Keyence). The force needed to insert the sheath and the torqueability of the guide catheter were assessed using the Mark-10 M5i Advanced Digital Force/Torque Indicator (Mark-10 Corporation) on a simulated single-access setting in a simulated skin pad. The sample size was determined to be 5 sheaths for each test.
RESULTS: The BRITE TIP 11 cm (Cordis), BRITE TIP 35 cm (Cordis), and Destination sheath (Terumo) had the largest outer diameters; the Prelude IDeal (Merit Medical) and Terumo Glidesheath (Terumo) had the smallest outer diameters. The Glidesheath was easiest for insertion/removal, followed by the Prelude IDeal and Impella Low Profile (LP) Companion sheath (Abiomed). The Impella LP Companion, Prelude Roadster (Merit Medical), and Destination sheaths allowed for the best torqueability and lowest force to remove the guide catheter. The longer Impella LP Companion sheath did not impact torqueability, but the removal force increased by 50% compared with the shorter Impella LP Companion sheath.
CONCLUSION: The Impella LP Companion sheath demonstrated the best torqueability and least effort in advancing the guide catheters, while the Prelude Roadster and Destination also performed well on these metrics. The Prelude IDeal and Glidesheath were good options for single-access because of their smaller outer diameters and hydrophilic coating and were easiest for insertion/removal through the 14F LP sheath.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Optimal Sheath for Single-Access Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Impella CP Hemodynamic Support.

abstract:
RATIONALE: COPD and obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) are both independently associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. It is not clear whether this risk is further increased in COPD-OSA overlap. We aimed to determine whether COPD-OSA overlap has a higher cardiovascular burden compared with COPD or OSA alone.
METHODS: This was a matched cohort study using electronic health records from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum database (England). Exposures of interest were a diagnosis of COPD, OSA or both based on validated code lists. Our primary outcome of interest was cardiovascular mortality defined using ICD-10 codes. Our secondary outcomes of interest included: all-cause mortality, incident acute coronary syndrome (ACS), incident stroke and incident heart failure.
RESULTS: The initial study cohort consisted of 365 667 people with COPD (mean±sd) age 68±11 years, 59 526 with OSA age 57±11 years and 11 040 with COPD-OSA age 65±10 years. Cardiovascular mortality was significantly higher in patients with COPD-OSA overlap compared with OSA alone (adjusted hazard ratio 1.72 (1.58-1.88); p<0.001) but not compared with COPD alone. People with COPD-OSA overlap had 27% and 58% increased risk of developing ACS compared with COPD and OSA alone respectively, and 69% and 101% increased risk of developing heart failure compared with COPD and OSA respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: We have demonstrated that people with COPD-OSA overlap have a significantly higher cardiovascular burden compared with COPD or OSA alone with real-world implications. Earlier and targeted treatment with cardiovascular optimisation can potentially reduce downstream sequelae.
title: Cardiovascular outcomes in COPD, obstructive sleep apnoea and the overlap syndrome.
