abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of concomitant coronary artery disease in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains controversial. Whether routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR provides clinical benefit compared to a strategy of deferral is unclear.
METHODS: We performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCT) comparing routine PCI before TAVR with a strategy of PCI deferral. The primary end points were a composite of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and all-cause mortality. Secondary end points included myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization, and major bleeding. We applied a random-effects model to calculate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% CI. We also performed a pooled time-to-event analysis using reconstructed individual patient data.
RESULTS: We included 3 RCT (ACTIVATION, NOTION-3, and PRO-TAVI) comprising a total of 1156 patients. The pooled cohort had a median age exceeding 81 years and exhibited low anatomic coronary complexity (median SYNTAX score ≤10). Routine PCI did not significantly reduce the risk of MACCE (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.62-1.13; P = .25) or all-cause mortality (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.67-1.17; P = .38). Pooled Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed no difference in all-cause mortality over 48 months (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.68-1.17; P = .41). Although routine PCI was associated with a significant reduction in any revascularization (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.06-0.89; P = .03) and urgent revascularization (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12-0.87; P = .02), it was associated with increased bleeding events (HR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.28-3.00; P < .01). No significant differences were observed regarding myocardial infarction or stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine PCI before TAVR did not reduce mortality or MACCE compared to a deferral strategy. Although routine PCI lowered the risk of subsequent urgent revascularization, it significantly increased the risk of major bleeding.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCT with pooled reconstructed individual patient data; 3 RCT (ACTIVATION, NOTION-3, and PRO-TAVI) comprising a total of 1156 patients
appraisal.main_limitation: Only three trials with low anatomic coronary complexity (median SYNTAX score ≤10), so the findings may not apply to complex coronary disease.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of three randomised trials with reconstructed individual patient data found that routine PCI before TAVR did not reduce mortality or MACCE but increased bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Routine PCI did not significantly reduce the risk of MACCE (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.62-1.13; P = .25) or all-cause mortality (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.67-1.17; P = .38). Bleeding events were increased (HR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.28-3.00; P < .01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs the Heart Team decision on revascularising coronary disease in TAVR candidates, where guidelines rest on limited randomised evidence.

journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Routine Versus Deferred Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.

abstract:
AIM: Timely reperfusion is vital in STEMI care to reduce mortality. An initial audit showed patients transferred from emergency departments outside Dublin often exceeded the 120-minute reperfusion target. In response, Dublin Mid Leinster protocols were updated to recommend pre-transfer thrombolysis. This study evaluates the impact of these changes on reperfusion times and outcomes.
METHODS: This observational study included STEMI patients admitted to St. James's Hospital from 2021-2023, compared to a prior cohort (2017-2020). The primary outcome was time from first ECG to reperfusion. Secondary outcomes included thrombolysis rates, success (TIMI 2/3 flow on angiography) and safety.
RESULTS: Among 1,301 patients, the median ECG-to-reperfusion time among patients transferred from outside Dublin fell from 124 minutes (IQR 96-166) to 113 minutes (IQR 78-151) (p<0.0001), while the proportion achieving reperfusion within 120 minutes increased from 235/507 (46.4%) to 308/530 (58.1%). Overall thrombolysis use increased from 27/1161 (2.3%) to 131/1301 (10.1%). Among thrombolysed patients, 85/131 (64.9%) achieved successful reperfusion and severe bleeding occurred in 2/131 (1.5%). Mapping demonstrated markedly lower rates of timely reperfusion at the periphery of the DML region.
DISCUSSION: A regional protocol promoting thrombolysis substantially increased thrombolysis utilisation and improved overall timely reperfusion among STEMI patients transferred from outside Dublin. Persistent geographical disparities support further optimisation of regional pathways and consideration of prehospital thrombolysis strategies.
title: Timely Reperfusion in STEMI: A Closed-Loop Audit of Guideline Compliance and Practice Improvements.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular/left ventricle (LV) overload remains a major limitation of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in patients with cardiogenic shock. Left atrial veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (LAVA-ECMO) has been proposed to facilitate LV unloading; however, data regarding its optimal timing and clinical role remain limited.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a preventive single-inflow cannula LAVA-ECMO strategy, defined as an a priori LV unloading approach implemented at extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation, either through primary LAVA-ECMO implantation or planned early conversion from VA-ECMO within 60 minutes. Between January 2020 and July 2025, eligible patients supported with VA-ECMO or LAVA-ECMO were screened. After predefined exclusions, 42 patients managed with preventive LAVA-ECMO were compared with 64 contemporaneous patients receiving conventional VA-ECMO.
RESULTS: Thirty-day all-cause mortality was lower in the LAVA-ECMO group than in the VA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 76.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.31-0.95). Failure to wean from ECMO tended to occur less frequently with LAVA-ECMO (31.0% vs 56.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.18-1.01). Signs of LV overload during ECMO support were significantly reduced in the LAVA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 82.8%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.19, 95% CI, 0.08-0.49). Overall complication rates were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, preventive LAVA-ECMO was associated with lower short-term mortality and a reduced incidence of LV overload without an apparent increase in complications. Preventive LAVA-ECMO may represent a feasible mechanical circulatory support strategy in carefully selected patients with cardiogenic shock.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

abstract: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygos continuation is a rare congenital venous anomaly characterized by the absence of the hepatic segment of the inferior vena cava, with venous return from the lower extremities redirected through a dilated azygos vein into the superior vena cava. Although typically clinically silent, this anomaly can pose significant challenges during transcatheter procedures requiring femoral venous access. We describe a case of interrupted inferior vena cava with azygos continuation that was incidentally discovered during transcatheter aortic valve replacement after difficulty advancing a temporary transvenous pacemaker via the femoral venous approach.
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
title: Interrupted Inferior Vena Cava With Azygos Continuation-A Procedural Challenge During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Case Report.

abstract: A 69-year-old man presented with sudden-onset crushing chest pain, diaphoresis, and syncope with ECG findings prompting treatment as a ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated no obstructive coronary artery disease. Subsequent investigations including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) scan demonstrated an infiltrative mass. Biopsy of a supraclavicular lymph node established a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with cardiac involvement. The patient was treated with corticosteroids and immunochemotherapy (DA-R-EPOCH), achieving complete remission on surveillance imaging. This case therefore contributes valuable evidence regarding the varied cardiovascular manifestations of lymphoma and reinforces the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in patients presenting with features of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA).
title: Myocardial Infarction with Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries; Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Presenting as an Acute Coronary Syndrome.

abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, but the optimal timing of initiation in those with acute coronary syndrome is not known. This study aims to assess if early therapy at discharge is superior to delayed or no therapy in reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events.
METHODS: This retrospective, observational cohort study included individuals with type 2 diabetes admitted with an acute coronary syndrome at a single regional heart centre between July 2018 and December 2023. Individuals were stratified into three groups based on the timing of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor initiation: (1) discharge group (initiated at hospital discharge), (2) post-discharge group (initiated after discharge during follow-up) and (3) no therapy group. The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major adverse cardiovascular event.
RESULTS: Among 970 eligible patients (median age, 70.2 years [IQR, 61.0-78.5 years]; 73.9% male), the median follow-up duration was 29.9 months (IQR, 20.1, 43.0 months). Compared with the discharge group, the risk of primary outcome was significantly higher in both the post-discharge group (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.50; 95% CI [1.13, 1.99], p = 0.005) and the no therapy group (aHR, 1.65; 95% CI [1.24, 2.20]; p < 0.001). Analyses were adjusted using clone-censor-weight methods and multivariable Cox-proportional hazards models.
CONCLUSIONS: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor therapy at hospital discharge was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes and acute coronary syndrome.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective, observational single-centre cohort of 970 eligible patients with type 2 diabetes and ACS (July 2018 to December 2023), median follow-up 29.9 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre retrospective design with residual confounding and selection of who receives early therapy, despite clone-censor-weight adjustment.
appraisal.one_line: Retrospective cohort in type 2 diabetes and ACS associating SGLT2 inhibitor initiation at discharge with fewer major adverse cardiovascular events than delayed or no initiation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with the discharge group, the risk of the primary outcome was higher in the post-discharge group (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.50; 95% CI [1.13, 1.99], p = 0.005) and the no therapy group (aHR, 1.65; 95% CI [1.24, 2.20]; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The timing of SGLT2 inhibitor initiation after ACS is unsettled, and the clone-censor-weight approach gives a template for a larger target trial emulation.

journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
title: Early sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor initiation is associated with improved cardiovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes and acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: It is unknown whether high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) measured on the Alinity platform (hs-cTnI-Alinity), can be used with the same clinical decision values as the Architect platform (hs-cTnI-Architect).
METHODS: In an international prospective study, hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect were measured from the same blood samples obtained at 0 h, 1 h, and 2 h from patients presenting to the emergency department with acute chest discomfort. The final diagnosis was centrally adjudicated by two cardiologists. We tested four hypotheses: hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect have (1) excellent analytical agreement, (2) high concordance at common analytical benchmarks (limit-of-detection and upper-reference-limit); (3) high diagnostic accuracy for AMI; and (4) comparable clinical performance for early rule-out and rule-in of AMI.
RESULTS: Among 1,573 eligible patients (median age 60 years, 34.7 % women) 7,438 measurements of hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect from the same samples were performed. The prevalence of AMI was 17.7 % (279/1,573). Analytical agreement between hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect was excellent (mean bias -3.6 ng/L [95 % CI -17.3 to 10.1]). Using limit-of-detection and upper-reference-limit as benchmarks, agreement was high. However, major disagreement occurred in 2.5 %, including only one AMI. Diagnostic accuracy for AMI was very high and comparable between hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect (area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve 0.95 [95 % CI 0.95-0.96] and 0.96 [95 % CI 0.95-0.96]). Sensitivity for ruling-out AMI were >99 % and specificity >93 % and comparable between both assays when applying the ESC 0/1h and ESC 0/2h algorithm derived for hs-cTnI-Architect.
CONCLUSIONS: Analytic benchmarks and ESC 0/1h and 0/2h algorithm cut-offs originally derived for hs-cTnI-Architect might be safely applied when using hs-cTnI-Alinity.
title: Validation of hs-cTnI-Alinity in the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prompt recognition and early management of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are crucial for improving outcomes. This study investigates the association between system delay and in-hospital mortality in patients with STEMI.
METHODS: Using data from the Seoul GOLDEN-time emergency medical system registry, a multicentre retrospective registry in Seoul, this study analysed patients with STEMI who were transported to an emergency department via emergency medical service for cardiac complaints between July 2020 and December 2022. System delay included the response time (first medical contact to an ambulance on the scene), scene time (ambulance on the scene to departure), scene-to-door time (departure to hospital arrival), and door-to-balloon time.
RESULTS: Among 654 patients with STEMI who received percutaneous coronary intervention, survivors had shorter overall system delay, prehospital time, scene time, scene-to-door time, and door-to-balloon time than non-survivors. A system delay > 127.5 minutes was associated with high mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.07; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-4.13). Prolonged prehospital time (aOR, 2.35; 95% CI, 1.16-4.95), scene time (aOR, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.24-5.75), and door-to-balloon time (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.09-4.39) were each independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSION: Prolonged system delays were associated with increased in-hospital mortality. These findings highlight the need for a comprehensive, system-level approach to reducing system delay across the entire STEMI care pathway.
title: System Delay and Mortality in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Multicentre, Retrospective, Observational Study in Seoul.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment.
RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N = 10, sham: N = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication (N = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN.
CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, prospective, randomised, sham-controlled, blinded trial; 20 subjects (uRDN: N = 10, sham: N = 10) completed the 6-month visit; stopped prematurely because of slow enrolment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination left the trial underpowered, with only 20 completers and a surrogate blood pressure endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Small sham-controlled randomised trial of ultrasound renal denervation in CKD stage 3 with uncontrolled hypertension, stopped early, with no significant effect on systolic ambulatory BP.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P = 0.170). Sham-corrected 24-h diastolic ABP changed by -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P = 0.035).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It adds sham-controlled data for renal denervation in CKD, a population of interest for confirmatory trials, but cannot settle efficacy.

title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Aortic annular enlargement (AAE) during surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is performed to facilitate implantation of larger prostheses in patients with small aortic annuli and mitigate prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). However, the clinical impact of residual PPM after AAE remains uncertain.
METHODS: All adult patients who underwent SAVR with AAE for small aortic annuli were retrospectively identified from a prospectively maintained institutional database (2011-2024). PPM was defined based on indexed effective orifice area thresholds derived from published reference tables. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and secondary outcomes included heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and longitudinal echocardiographic performance.
RESULTS: A total of 169 patients were identified (age 68 years [61-73], 119 female [70.4%]). Median STS risk was 2% [1-4%], and preoperative mean gradient was 45.0 mmHg [36.8-57.2]. Overall median valve size after AAE was 23 mm (21-25), and PPM occurred in 25 patients (14.8%), including 24 (14.2%) with moderate and 1 (0.6%) with severe PPM. Early outcomes were comparable between PPM and no-PPM groups: postoperative stroke 0 (0%) vs. 3 (2.1%, p > 0.999), and 30-day mortality 1 (4.0%) vs. 5 (3.5%, p > 0.999). Over 4 years follow-up, survival (HR 0.94, 95%CI 0.40-2.21, p = 0.896) and freedom from HF hospitalization (HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.45-2.95, p = 0.760) were similar. Echocardiographic trends showed no differences in LVEF (p = 0.123) or mean gradient (p = 0.879) during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with small aortic annuli undergoing SAVR with annular enlargement, the incidence of PPM was low, and residual PPM did not adversely impact early postoperative outcomes, mid-term survival, or valve hemodynamics.
title: Prosthesis-patient mismatch after surgical aortic valve replacement with aortic annular enlargement in small aortic annuli.

abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.
title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
SGLT2 Inhibition in Aortic Stenosis: Is the Valve the Next Therapeutic Frontier?

abstract: Angina pectoris is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome that may reflect obstructive coronary atherosclerosis, coronary vasomotor dysfunction, microvascular dysfunction, or myocardial oxygen supply-demand imbalance. We used Mendelian randomization (MR) to prioritize circulating proteins that may influence the broad risk of angina while distinguishing atherosclerosis-related pathways from other potential mechanisms. This study aimed to identify genetically supported candidate therapeutic targets for angina pectoris and characterize the relative strength and potential mechanisms of the evidence supporting each candidate. The primary analysis combined European cis-protein quantitative trait locus instruments with a broad genome-wide association study -defined angina phenotype. Steiger testing, Bayesian co-localization, phenotypic scanning, external validation, supplementary European trans- protein quantitative trait locus and Asian-ancestry analyses, phenotype-stratified MR, two-step mediation MR, enrichment analysis, bulk RNA-seq, protein-protein interaction analysis, and exploratory single-cell transcriptomic analyses were used to evaluate robustness and biological context. Seven protein-angina associations met the primary Bonferroni threshold; 6 proteins (LPA, TMEM106B, APOA5, TIRAP, PCSK9, and SWAP70) were retained after TGFB1 failed Steiger filtering. Independent external MR supported LPA in UK Biobank and LPA, PCSK9, and APOA5 in FinnGen. Phenotype-stratified analyses generally supported associations across stable angina, unstable angina, coronary artery disease, and myocardial infarction, although instrument availability and the strength of evidence differed among proteins. Two-step MR supported indirect pathways through coronary artery calcification for LPA, through LDL cholesterol for PCSK9, and through triglycerides for APOA5, but not through C-reactive protein for TIRAP. Exploratory single-cell analyses localized TMEM106B, TIRAP, and SWAP70 to relevant vascular and immune cell populations and provided limited, context-dependent functional support. LPA, PCSK9, and APOA5 have the strongest convergent genetic and external-replication evidence and appear to influence angina risk predominantly through atherosclerotic lipid-related pathways. TMEM106B, TIRAP, and SWAP70 remain potentially novel, genetically supported candidates with exploratory cellular evidence but without direct experimental validation. These candidates should not be considered established therapeutic targets until proteomic, functional, rescue, and clinical studies are completed.
title: Identification of genetically supported candidate therapeutic targets for angina pectoris using mendelian randomization.

abstract: Background/Objectives: We evaluated the feasibility of a near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS)-guided selective strategy based on a single absolute regional tissue oxygen saturation (rSO2) threshold and described clinically overt limb ischemia. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 110 adults receiving femoral venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation between April 2020 and December 2024. All underwent bilateral lower-extremity NIRS monitoring. In 83 patients, distal perfusion catheter (DPC) placement was triggered by rSO2 < 40% in the cannulated limb or clinically evident limb ischemia; 27 received routine prophylactic DPC placement at cannulation. Primary endpoints were DPC avoidance and clinically overt limb ischemia. Results: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) accounted for 64.5% of patients. Under the selective strategy, 45/83 patients (54.2%; exact 95% CI, 42.9-65.2%) avoided DPC placement, with no clinically overt limb ischemia (0/45; exact 95% CI, 0-7.9%). Limb ischemia occurred in 2/83 versus 2/27 patients (2.4% versus 7.4%; risk difference, -5.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -21.1 to +3.0; p = 0.252). Because threshold crossing triggered DPC placement, the reported threshold characteristics reflect the operation of the management protocol rather than independent diagnostic accuracy. Conclusions: A single-threshold NIRS-guided selective strategy was feasible in this ECPR-dominant population, allowing just over half of patients to avoid prophylactic DPC placement. No clinically overt limb ischemia was observed in this subgroup, but the upper 95% confidence limit of 7.9% precludes a definitive safety conclusion. Prospective studies are needed to assess limb ischemia risk and refine selection criteria.
title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy-Guided Selective Distal Perfusion in Femoral Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Feasibility Study.

abstract: Background: New-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common complication of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes. We evaluated whether admission calculated serum osmolality is associated with new-onset AF in NSTEMI. Methods: This retrospective study included 656 eligible NSTEMI patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between March 2021 and April 2022. Only patients in sinus rhythm at admission whose blood sample preceded any AF episode were analyzed. Osmolality was calculated as 2 × sodium + glucose/18 + blood urea nitrogen/2.8. Prespecified logistic models were assessed for discrimination, bootstrap internal validation, calibration, and incremental value. Results: New-onset AF developed in 136 patients (20.7%). Osmolality was higher in patients with AF (297.4 ± 8.9 vs. 291.6 ± 15.7 mOsm/kg, p < 0.001). In the complete-case model (n = 570; 130 events), osmolality was associated with AF (adjusted OR 1.565 per 10 mOsm/kg, 95% CI 1.102-2.223; p = 0.012). Adding osmolality increased the AUC from 0.927 to 0.933 (DeLong p = 0.081; likelihood-ratio p = 0.012; optimism-corrected AUC 0.924). The association was attenuated without renal-function adjustment (p = 0.060). Conclusions: Admission calculated serum osmolality was associated with new-onset AF in NSTEMI patients undergoing PCI, but its incremental predictive value was modest. External validation is required.
title: Association Between Admission Calculated Serum Osmolality and New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being investigated across the acute coronary syndrome (ACS) care pathway, including early diagnosis, coronary lesion characterization, procedural guidance, and risk prediction. This comprehensive review examines the current evidence across the entire ACS trajectory, with particular emphasis on clinically actionable and interventional applications. AI-enabled electrocardiography (ECG) may improve detection of myocardial infarction, including occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) that does not meet conventional STEMI criteria. Models combining clinical data and high-sensitivity troponin may improve early rule-out and rule-in. In coronary imaging, AI can quantify plaque characteristics and assist with the interpretation of OCT and IVUS, while image-derived physiology may help assess non-culprit lesions. However, better diagnostic accuracy does not necessarily translate into better revascularization decisions. AI-based models can also estimate post-ACS ischemic, bleeding, and mortality risk, although evidence that their use improves treatment or outcomes remains limited. The next priority is prospective evaluation of whether these tools improve decisions, workflow, and patient outcomes across diverse clinical settings.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Acute Coronary Syndromes: From Early Diagnosis to Culprit Lesion Characterization, Coronary Physiology, and Risk Stratification.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indications for right ventricular assist device (RVAD) insertion include right heart failure after implantation of a left ventricular assist device or early graft failure following heart transplantation. This study aimed to investigate how the upstream and downstream circulatory network interacts with the Impella RP® device.
METHODS: A numerical model of the Impella RP® device was implemented within the CARDIOSIM© software platform for this study. In the numerical configuration, the RVAD aspirated blood from either the right atrium (RA-PA connection) or the right ventricle (RV-PA connection) and delivered it to the pulmonary artery. Only RA-PA connection is the currently used setting for the Impella RP® device in clinical practice. Based on right ventricular (RV) decompression and total flow, our study may help define the need for a direct RV-unloading Impella RP®.
RESULTS: The simulations showed that while activating the RVAD in RA-PA mode, regardless of its rotational speed, the mean pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) percentage change was higher than that in the unsupported condition when the mean systemic venous pressure (SVP) and the pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) were both set to 20 [mmHg]. When RV-PA connection was applied, a similar trend was observed, although the PAP percentage changes were approximately halved compared to those when the RA-PA connection was applied.
CONCLUSIONS: The Impella RP® device has the potential to become a valid option for RV support based on current experimental and simulation data. Although already in use, further evaluation in the clinical setting will likely confirm its potential and lead to a more routinely application for RV support.
title: The Impact of the Impella RP® Device on a Failing Right Heart: A Modelling and Simulation Approach to Ascertain Its Potential.

abstract: Clinical redox studies usually sample a single compartment. In a single-centre, cross-sectional case-control study, we measured serum thiol-disulfide homeostasis, a bulk extracellular thiol measure, and erythrocyte glutathione, an intracellular measure, in the same blood draw from 82 patients presenting to an emergency department with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and 75 controls. Cases and controls differed substantially in sex and in cardiovascular risk profile. All nine redox indices differed between groups in the direction consistent with greater oxidation in patients. The standardized case-control difference was larger for erythrocyte reduced glutathione (Hedges g 1.14) than for serum native thiol (0.56). The post hoc bootstrap ratio of the two was 2.04 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.31 to 4.08) before adjustment and 1.60 (0.99 to 3.23) after adjustment for age, sex and smoking, and no asymmetry was seen in the small subgroup free of recorded risk factors. In exploratory analyses within patients, serum indices were associated with the Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score and reduced glutathione with ejection fraction. Each assay reports its own pool and is not a global measure of oxidative stress. In this sample, the compartment chosen determined the size of the observed case-control difference, a result that needs confirmation in a design with comparable groups.
title: Erythrocyte Glutathione Shows a Larger Case-Control Difference than Serum Thiol-Disulfide Homeostasis at Emergency Department Presentation with Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a major contributor to myocardial ischaemia and angina, both in the presence and absence of obstructive coronary artery disease, yet it remains underdiagnosed and therapeutically challenging. The mechanistic links between CMD, myocardial ischaemia, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) are incompletely understood. Emerging mechanistic, imaging, and clinical evidence suggests that CMD and vulnerable plaque (VP) could be connected through shared inflammatory, metabolic, and haemodynamic pathways. This review synthesises data across these domains to propose a bidirectional plaque-microcirculatory crosstalk framework, whereby each process may amplify the other. Evidence indicates that plaque-derived inflammatory mediators and haemodynamic disturbances can impair microvascular function, while CMD-related flow abnormalities may, in turn, accelerate plaque inflammation, progression, and destabilisation. Furthermore, distinct CMD endotypes (e.g., structural or functional) have different underlying pathophysiology and present with different phenotypes. Identifying mediators of coronary-microvascular crosstalk presents an opportunity to refine cardiovascular risk stratification and uncover novel therapeutic targets. Current anti-inflammatory therapies have shown variable effects, and CMD-directed vasomodulatory interventions have produced mixed results, partly due to limited endotype stratification. Emerging approaches, including coronary sinus reducer therapy and precision anti-inflammatory strategies, may offer dual benefits by improving CMD and stabilising vulnerable plaques. This review examines the bidirectional crosstalk hypothesis, aiming to provide an integrative framework linking epicardial atherosclerosis and microvascular pathology and may guide future phenotype-specific mechanistic and interventional studies aimed at reducing residual cardiovascular risk.
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
title: Bidirectional Crosstalk Between Vulnerable Coronary Plaque and Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction: A Narrative Review.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Ventricular recovery after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is commonly assessed using either structural (volumetric) or functional (ejection-fraction) criteria, although these may capture different aspects of recovery. We examined whether their cross-classification identifies distinct recovery patterns and whether myocardial mechanics and left atrial function provide additional information. Methods: We prospectively followed 101 patients with first STEMI and single-vessel coronary artery disease treated with PCI. Echocardiography was performed 12-24 h after reperfusion and at 12 ± 2 months. Structural recovery (≥15% reduction in 3D LV end-systolic volume) and functional recovery (≥5-point absolute LVEF increase) were cross-classified into four recovery patterns. Results: Among 53 patients with complete paired measurements, 10 (18.9%) showed concordant recovery, 7 (13.2%) isolated structural recovery, 9 (17.0%) isolated functional recovery, and 27 (50.9%) no recovery; 30.2% therefore showed discordant recovery. The no-recovery group was heterogeneous, including both volumetric deterioration and stable or improving volumes below the recovery threshold. Continuous changes in 3D-ESV and LVEF were only moderately correlated (ρ = 0.353, p = 0.0095), and discordance persisted in sensitivity analyses. Myocardial mechanics and LASR did not differentiate recovery patterns, but several of these baseline markers showed exploratory associations with clinical outcomes after false-discovery-rate correction. Conclusions: Structural and functional recovery after STEMI are complementary rather than interchangeable, and this discordance persisted across extensive sensitivity analyses; however, assignment of individual patients to specific recovery categories remained sensitive to the chosen thresholds and LVEF measurement method. Myocardial mechanics and LASR may provide additional information about clinical expression.
title: Beyond Remodeling: Four Structural-Functional Recovery Patterns as a Framework for Interpreting Ventricular Recovery After Reperfused STEMI.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute myocardial infarction is accompanied by thromboinflammation, immune-cell redistribution and changes in nutritional reserve. We compared six routinely calculable indices under a common modelling strategy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This retrospective cohort included 2613 patients. The primary endpoint was long-term all-cause mortality, analysed with Cox regression; angiographic no-reflow, in-hospital mortality and 30-day mortality were analysed with logistic regression. The global immune-nutrition-inflammation index (GINI), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), controlling nutritional status (CONUT) score, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Naples prognostic score (NAPLES) were evaluated in separate models. Continuous indices were modelled flexibly, and every effect estimate compared the 75th with the 25th percentile. Results: No-reflow occurred in 353 patients (13.5%), in-hospital death in 102 (3.9%), 30-day death in 157 (6.0%) and long-term death in 466 (17.8%). Median recorded follow-up was 34 [14-46] months. After clinical adjustment, the Q3-versus-Q1 hazard ratios for long-term mortality were 1.17 (95% CI 1.00-1.36) for GINI, 0.79 (0.68-0.91) for PNI, 1.19 (1.01-1.40) for CONUT, 1.20 (1.04-1.39) for SII, 1.24 (1.07-1.44) for NLR and 1.13 (0.98-1.31) for NAPLES. After Holm correction across the six primary tests, PNI, SII and NLR retained evidence of association. In angiographically expanded no-reflow models, GINI and NLR retained Q3-versus-Q1 associations. Conclusions: Admission inflammatory and immune-nutrition indices showed outcome-specific prognostic associations. PNI, SII and NLR had the most consistent multiplicity-sensitive long-term associations, whereas GINI and NLR retained associations with no-reflow after angiographic adjustment. These findings do not establish causal effects, predictive superiority or readiness for clinical decision-making.
title: Comparative Associations of Inflammation and Nutrition-Based Indices with No-Reflow and Mortality After Primary PCI for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Background/Objectives: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) is frequently elevated in decompensated heart failure (DHF), but its prognostic association may vary according to clinical context. We evaluated baseline and serial hs-cTnT in relation to in-hospital mortality across clinical presentation, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and diabetes status. Methods: A total of 653 patients hospitalized with DHF were prospectively analyzed. Baseline hs-cTnT was assessed globally and across clinical presentation, LVEF and diabetes status. Among 334 patients with repeated measurements, serial hs-cTnT was evaluated using continuous measures and threshold-based trajectories. Results: In-hospital mortality was 9.0%. Baseline hs-cTnT showed moderate discrimination for mortality (AUC 0.658). The internally derived 38.4 pg/mL threshold identified higher mortality above versus below the threshold (14.8% vs. 5.1%, p < 0.001) but showed limited bootstrap stability. Clinical presentation significantly modified the association between hs-cTnT and mortality (global interaction p = 0.022), driven by a stronger association in decompensated right-sided versus left-sided HF (ratio of ORs 2.77, 95% CI 1.26-6.07). No significant modification effect was observed by LVEF or diabetes status. In a serial subgroup, repeated hs-cTnT remained associated with mortality after multivariable adjustment (OR 1.59 per doubling, 95% CI 1.14-2.21), although the increase in discrimination over the baseline model was not significant (AUC 0.750 vs. 0.777, p = 0.205). The above-above trajectory remained associated with mortality in Firth regression (adjusted OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.02-5.61). Conclusions: hs-cTnT was associated with in-hospital mortality in DHF, with heterogeneity by clinical presentation. Serial measurements were associated with outcome, but their incremental discrimination value was limited. Threshold-based trajectories should be considered exploratory pending external validation.
title: Association of Baseline and Serial High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T with In-Hospital Mortality Across Clinical Presentation, LVEF and Diabetes Status in Decompensated Heart Failure.

abstract: Background: Premature acute myocardial infarction (AMI) has become an important public health challenge. Young survivors face prolonged residual cardiovascular risk, yet real-world implementation of long-term secondary prevention across medication use, health behaviors, and risk-factor monitoring remains insufficiently characterized in China. Methods: In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, we included 1377 young AMI survivors aged 18-44 years who attended follow-up at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between 2023 and 2025. Current use of major secondary prevention medications, achievement of four health-behavior targets (smoking abstinence/cessation, physical activity, diet, and sleep), and lipid monitoring during the preceding 12 months were assessed using standardized interviews and medical records. Recurrent myocardial infarction (MI) and repeat coronary revascularization occurring between discharge after the index AMI and the study visit were retrospectively identified. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations between secondary-prevention implementation domains and recurrent events. Results: Participants had a mean age of 39.1 years, and 95.9% were male. Recurrent MI occurred in 9.2% and repeat revascularization in 13.7%. The proportion concurrently using four major medication classes decreased from 50.0% at discharge to 25.9% at follow-up. Overall, 45.1% achieved good behavioral implementation, defined as meeting at least three of four ideal behaviors. In fully adjusted models, good behavioral implementation was associated with lower odds of recurrent MI (odds ratio [OR] 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.32-0.73) and repeat revascularization (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00). Concurrent use of all four medication classes and frequent lipid monitoring were not independently associated with recurrent outcomes. Conclusions: Among young AMI survivors in China, substantial gaps in long-term secondary prevention were observed, particularly for healthy behaviors. These findings support the public health importance of strengthening lifestyle-oriented and multidisciplinary follow-up strategies for young survivors of AMI. Because exposure and outcome periods overlapped partially, findings should be interpreted as associational rather than causal.
title: Long-Term Secondary Prevention Gaps Among Young Survivors of Acute Myocardial Infarction in China: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) remains one of the most challenging conditions in neonatal critical care. Despite advances in prenatal assessment and neonatal management, substantial uncertainty persists regarding ECMO selection, mode and duration of support, and timing of diaphragmatic repair. This review summarizes the available evidence and critically examines the major unresolved questions in the management of infants with CDH requiring ECMO. Methods: A narrative review was conducted based on a literature search in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between June 2005 and June 2026. Additional relevant publications were identified through reference screening, and selected foundational studies predating the search period were included when appropriate. Prospective and retrospective studies, registry-based analyses, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant consensus statements were considered. Evidence was narratively synthesized, with particular attention to disease severity, methodological limitations, and survivor bias. Results: Available evidence highlights substantial heterogeneity in disease severity and management. Prenatal and postnatal markers aid risk stratification, but no single parameter reliably predicts ECMO requirement or defines the optimal management strategy. To date, no clear survival advantage has been demonstrated for either veno-arterial or veno-venous ECMO, although veno-arterial ECMO remains the predominant mode of support in most centers; mode selection should therefore be individualized according to cardiopulmonary physiology, patient characteristics, anatomy, and institutional expertise. Surgical timing remains particularly controversial. While repair after ECMO decannulation has been associated with favorable outcomes, recent observational analyses suggest that early repair during ECMO may be beneficial in selected patients, although the optimal timing remains uncertain. Prolonged ECMO may provide additional time for pulmonary and cardiovascular recovery, although this potential benefit must be weighed against the cumulative morbidity of prolonged support. Conclusions: Management should be individualized according to disease severity, clinical trajectory, cardiopulmonary recovery, and institutional expertise. Current evidence does not support a universal strategy for ECMO initiation, mode, surgical timing, or duration. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized definitions and adequately accounting for disease severity are needed to reduce practice variation and better define optimal management.
title: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Requiring ECMO: Current Evidence, Controversies, and Unresolved Questions.

abstract: Background: Optimal stenting for distal unprotected left main coronary artery (LMCA) bifurcation disease remains uncertain. We evaluated long-term outcomes by initially intended strategy. Methods: This retrospective, single-centre cohort included 234 consecutive patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) without acute coronary syndrome, classified by intended strategy irrespective of crossover. Cox models for all-cause mortality were adjusted for strategy, age, left ventricular ejection fraction, SYNTAX score, and diabetes, with anatomical and propensity-score sensitivity analyses. Secondary and subgroup analyses were exploratory. Results: Provisional and upfront two-stent strategies were intended in 145 and 89 patients. Two-stent patients had greater anatomical complexity. During median 49-month follow-up, mortality did not differ significantly (two-stent versus provisional: 16.9% versus 21.4%; p = 0.499; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-1.60; p = 0.579), with consistent sensitivity analyses. Older age, lower ejection fraction, and higher SYNTAX score were associated with mortality. Target-lesion revascularisation (7.8% versus 2.1%; p = 0.033) and in-hospital stroke (5.6% versus 0.7%; p = 0.031) were more frequent with intended two-stent PCI; other secondary outcomes did not differ significantly. Exploratory unadjusted comparisons showed lower target-lesion and target-vessel revascularisation with double-kissing crush (n = 74) versus conventional culotte (n = 15), limited by small samples and selection bias. Intravascular ultrasound was associated with lower mortality in exploratory adjusted analyses. Mortality was numerically lower with elective intra-aortic balloon pump support at ejection fraction ≤40%, without statistical significance. Conclusions: No, statistically significant association between initially intended bifurcation strategy and long-term all-cause mortality was observed. Limited precision precludes an inference of equivalence, and exploratory differences in target-lesion revascularisation and in-hospital stroke warrant caution. These findings provide a long-term real-world perspective on individualised distal LMCA PCI, integrating lesion complexity, ventricular reserve, procedural technique, and intravascular imaging.
title: Long-Term Outcomes According to the Initially Intended Stenting Strategy for Unprotected Distal Left Main Bifurcation PCI: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract: Background: This study aims to investigate the value of a SYNTAX score (SS) based on coronary computed tomographic angiography (cCTA)-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR), termed "Functional SYNTAX score" (FSSCTA), to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This cohort study included 876 patients who underwent cCTA and underwent PCI within 30 days during 2016-2020. CT-FFR was calculated by a machine learning algorithm. All 876 patients were divided into a low-risk group (≤22) and an intermediate-to-high-risk group (>22) with cCTA-based SS (SSCTA) as the control. Results: Based on the FSSCTA, 10.4% (91/876) of patients were reclassified to the low-risk group, and 2.9% (25/876) of patients were reclassified to the intermediate-to-high-risk group. MACEs occurred in 16.6% (145/876) of patients over a median follow-up period of 19.4 months. FSSCTA and invasive coronary angiography-based SS (SSICA) were independently associated with the risk of MACEs regardless of whether they were in continuous or categorical form (FSSCTA: c continuous HR 1.082, 95% CI 1.038-1.128; categorical HR 1.865, 95% CI 1.138-2.305. SSICA: continuous HR 1.045, 95% CI 1.012-1.079; categorical HR 1.520, 95% CI 1.128-2.048). FSSCTA showed the best predictive power for MACEs compared with SSCTA and SSICA (all comparisons with FSSCTAp < 0.05). Conclusions: FSSCTA, SSCTA and SSICA were all independent predictors of MACEs in patients undergoing PCI, and FSSCTA showed a significantly better predictive value for MACEs than SSCTA and SSICA.
title: Prognostic Implication of a CT-FFR-Based Functional SYNTAX Score in Coronary Artery Disease Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract: Background: Data directly comparing the atrioventricular (AV)-synchronous leadless pacemaker (MicraAV) with a dual-chamber transvenous pacemaker (DDD) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remain limited. Methods: We retrospectively studied patients undergoing pacemaker implantation for advanced or complete AV block within one month after TAVR at a single Japanese center between 2016 and 2025. After exclusions, the primary cohort comprised 74 patients (MicraAV, n = 29; DDD, n = 45). Clinical outcomes were assessed through 12 months, with death treated as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes. Device and echocardiographic parameters were evaluated longitudinally. Results: MicraAV recipients were less frequently female than DDD recipients (48.3% vs. 75.6%, p = 0.025). In the MicraAV and DDD groups, respectively, all-cause mortality was 6.9% and 6.7% (unadjusted HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.19-6.68; p = 0.904), heart failure rehospitalization occurred in 17.2% and 4.4% (subdistribution HR, 4.44; 95% CI, 0.86-22.92; p = 0.075), and device-related complications occurred in 6.9% and 4.4% (subdistribution HR, 1.60; 95% CI, 0.23-11.40; p = 0.636). The median MicraAV tracking index was 88.4% [IQR, 66.4-95.1]. No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for device electrical performance or echocardiographic left ventricular parameters. Tricuspid regurgitation worsened over time in the MicraAV group. Conclusions: All-cause mortality and device-related complications were infrequent in both groups, whereas heart failure rehospitalization occurred more frequently in the MicraAV group. Given the small number of events and wide confidence intervals, these findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in larger contemporary cohorts.
title: MicraAV Versus Dual-Chamber Transvenous Pacemakers in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A 12-Month Single-Center Retrospective Study.

abstract: Background: The platelet-albumin-bilirubin (PALBI) and albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) scores integrate routinely available laboratory parameters with potential relevance to microvascular injury. We investigated their associations with angiographic no-reflow and incremental predictive value in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 1539 consecutive patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. No-reflow was defined by final TIMI flow < 3 and/or myocardial blush grade 0-1 in the absence of a mechanical cause. Associations of PALBI and ALBI with no-reflow were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Discrimination, calibration, reclassification, internal bootstrap validation, and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed. Results: No-reflow occurred in 146 patients (9.5%). Both PALBI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] per 0.1-point increase, 1.315; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.228-1.408; p < 0.001) and ALBI (aOR, 1.165; 95% CI, 1.115-1.218; p < 0.001) were independently associated with no-reflow. PALBI showed greater discrimination than ALBI (AUC, 0.722 vs. 0.681; DeLong p = 0.018). Adding PALBI to the clinical model increased the AUC from 0.688 to 0.785 (ΔAUC = 0.098; p = 0.001), with significant NRI (0.777) and IDI (0.102), and improved the Brier score from 0.083 to 0.073. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.762. PALBI demonstrated a non-linear association with no-reflow (p for non-linearity <0.001), whereas ALBI showed a predominantly linear association. Conclusions: Higher PALBI and ALBI scores were independently associated with angiographic no-reflow after primary PCI in STEMI. PALBI demonstrated stronger discrimination and incremental predictive performance; however, external validation and prospective evaluation are required to determine its potential clinical utility.
title: Association of Platelet-Albumin-Bilirubin and Albumin-Bilirubin Scores with Angiographic No-Reflow in Patients with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary PCI.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Real-world data comparing treatment strategies and in-hospital outcomes across no index revascularization, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in NSTEMI patients remain limited. Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 1906 NSTEMI patients undergoing coronary angiography were categorized into no index revascularization (n = 946), PCI (n = 709), or CABG (n = 251) groups. The primary endpoint was in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all-cause mortality, cardiac arrest requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation, sustained ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation, dialysis-requiring acute kidney injury, or stroke. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation with chained equations (MICE), and propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used as a sensitivity analysis. Results: In-hospital MACE was higher in the no index revascularization group than in the PCI and CABG groups (9.8% vs. 3.5% vs. 4.8%; p < 0.001). Patients managed with no index revascularization were older and had a greater comorbidity burden, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, and more frequent Killip class ≥ 2. In the primary multivariable model, chronic kidney disease, Killip class ≥ 2, lower LVEF, CRP, and male sex were associated with in-hospital MACE, whereas neither PCI nor CABG strategy was independently associated with MACE. IPTW sensitivity analyses yielded similar directions of association; however, the PCI estimate crossed the conventional significance threshold after 1st-99th percentile weight truncation. Conclusions: Patients managed with no index revascularization had a higher baseline risk profile and higher unadjusted in-hospital MACE and mortality. The observed between-group differences should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects of treatment strategy because of substantial confounding by indication.
title: In-Hospital Outcomes According to Treatment Strategy in NSTEMI Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: No Index Revascularization, PCI, or CABG?

abstract: Background/Objectives: Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) is increasingly used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), where rapid recovery of consciousness may facilitate early postoperative neurological assessment. Remimazolam provides sedation that can be pharmacologically reversed with flumazenil. We compared emergence from sedation between a remimazolam-flumazenil-based MAC strategy and a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy in patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR. Methods: In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 84 patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR were randomized 1:1 to remimazolam-remifentanil (R group) or dexmedetomidine-propofol-remifentanil (D group) MAC. Flumazenil was administered at the initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt in the R group. The primary outcome was arousal time, assessed using two prespecified measures: time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal and time from initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt to arousal. Arousal was defined as a Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation score of 5. Results: Eighty-three patients were included in the analysis (R group, n = 42; D group, n = 41). The time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal was shorter in the R group than in the D group (19.05 [15.77-23.59] vs. 24.09 [19.25-34.78] min; p = 0.0045). The time from initiation of the awakening attempt to arousal was also shorter (0.60 [0.33-1.00] vs. 1.00 [0-4.72] min; p = 0.0117). No patient in the R group required rescue propofol. No significant between-group differences were observed in major procedural or postoperative outcomes. Conclusions: A remimazolam-based MAC strategy with flumazenil reversal provided faster and more reliable emergence from sedation than a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy during transfemoral TAVR. These findings suggest that a reversible sedation strategy may facilitate rapid recovery of consciousness when early postoperative assessment is desired, although its impact on neurological or other clinical outcomes remains to be established.
title: Rapidly Reversible Monitored Anesthesia Care with Remimazolam and Flumazenil Reversal for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract: Background: Cardiovascular interventions such as transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) have become standard options for high-risk patients with valvular heart disease. However, iatrogenic type A aortic dissection (AAD) remains a rare but life-threatening complication, and its optimal management is controversial. Case presentation: We present four patients who developed AAD following cardiovascular interventions at our institution between 2020 and 2024, including three after TAVR and one after TEER. Three patients underwent the Bentall procedure (each requiring removal of the pre-existing transcatheter valve, and one with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting), and one underwent aortic sinus repair with ascending aorta and total arch replacement using a frozen elephant trunk, together with removal of the previously implanted TEER clip and mitral valve replacement. One patient recovered and was discharged home, another was transferred back to the cardiology department and was discharged home with no sequelae, and two left the hospital against medical advice while still in critical condition, both of whom subsequently died-one 2 days after discharge and the other immediately upon arriving home. Conclusions: Our experience indicates that patients with cardiovascular intervention-related AAD are at particularly high risk owing to pre-existing cardiac dysfunction and deterioration of other organ functions. In such patients, emergency surgical rescue can be life-saving, and the Bentall procedure proved feasible in this selected cohort; however, surgery in this setting is more complex than in routine cases. Careful evaluation, individualized surgical planning, and meticulous perioperative management are essential to improve outcomes.
title: Experiences in the Management of Type A Aortic Dissection Following Cardiovascular Interventions: A Case Series Report.

abstract: Background: Drug-refractory epilepsy (DRE) poses a persistent clinical burden, and the identification of reversible extracranial contributing factors represents a promising strategy to improve seizure control. Patent foramen ovale (PFO) with right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been recognized as a potential modifiable driver of epileptic seizures, yet clinical data on patients with extremely long-standing DRE exceeding 40 years remain exceedingly scarce. Methods: We report a 46-year-old female patient with a 44-year history of DRE, who experienced daily secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCSs) despite sequential treatment with six mechanistically distinct antiseizure medications. Systematic workup was performed and the patient underwent percutaneous transcatheter PFO closure, with a follow-up period of 14 months. Results: Systematic workup confirmed severe PFO-related RLS (grade III by contrast transthoracic echocardiography, grade IV by contrast transcranial Doppler), while brain MRI revealed no definite structural epileptogenic lesions other than an old ischemic infarct in the right corona radiata. At the latest follow-up, the patient had achieved complete freedom from GTCS with a markedly reduced antiseizure medication burden, retaining only infrequent mild focal absence-like seizures. Follow-up video electroencephalography unmasked previously occult focal epileptiform discharges in the left temporal region. Conclusions: This case suggests that severe PFO-related RLS may serve as a reversible aggravating factor even in decades-long refractory epilepsy, and provides electroclinical evidence supporting a hypothetical two-hit model of seizure generalization. PFO screening may be considered in selected patients with cryptogenic drug-refractory epilepsy, particularly those with non-lesional MRI, non-localizing EEG, and morning-predominant seizures.
title: Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Alleviates Long-Term Drug-Refractory Epilepsy: A Case Report.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation through the common carotid artery (TC-TAVI) is one of the possible treatment options for patients with ineligible transfemoral approach. The aim of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of patients treated with TC-TAVI in early and long-term follow-up. Methods: The study included patients with severe aortic stenosis treated with TC-TAVI. In-hospital outcomes, early, long-term follow-up were presented in accordance with the VARC-3 recommendations. Results: The analysis presented 101 patients. We observed high procedural success-97% (n = 98). The number of VARC-3 incidents: 3.96% major vascular complications; 0.99% myocardial infarction; 0.99% cardiac tamponade; 0.99% life-threatening bleeding; 3.96% cerebrovascular incidents. The NYHA class decreased significantly compared to the pre-procedure value (2 [1-2] vs. 3 [3-3]; p < 0.001). There was a significant improvement in postprocedural cerebral oximetry values compared to baseline on both the implanted and contralateral sides (67.5 [63-71]% vs. 70 [63.5-75]%; p < 0.05) and (67 [64-71]% vs. 71 [64-76]%; p < 0.05), respectively. The 30-day, 1-year, and 2-year survival rates were 94.1%, 80.2%, and 69.3%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, BAV (HR 4.54; 95% CI: 1.14-17.99; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 7.32; 95% CI: 2.59-20.65; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with two-year mortality. In an exploratory adjusted Cox regression analysis, BAV (HR 2.63; 95% CI: 1.07-6.45; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 3.48; 95% CI: 1.67-7.24; p < 0.001) were associated with higher 2-year mortality. Conclusions: Our single-center, observational report indicated feasibility and good observed outcomes of the TC-TAVI procedure in an experienced clinical team.
title: Early and Long-Term Results of 101 Consecutive Patients After Transcarotid Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.

abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a clinically relevant complication following percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). This systematic review evaluated its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact while separately examining the procedural feasibility and renal outcomes of contrast-sparing and zero-contrast LAAO strategies. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from database inception through 6 October 2026. Eighteen studies met the eligibility criteria. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively, with AKI-focused evidence considered separately from contrast-sparing procedural studies. Results: Four studies primarily evaluated AKI following conventional LAAO. Three creatinine-based cohorts reported AKI incidences ranging from 5.3% to 13.7%, whereas one large administrative database study reported coded AKI in 5.3% of index hospitalizations; these estimates were not considered directly comparable. Pre-existing renal dysfunction was the most consistent marker of AKI susceptibility, and AKI was associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Fourteen studies evaluated contrast-sparing or zero-contrast approaches and generally demonstrated high procedural success. However, renal outcomes were inconsistently assessed; several studies did not systematically report AKI, and AKI occurred even after zero-contrast implantation. Conclusions: Available evidence supports the procedural feasibility of contrast-sparing and zero-contrast LAAO but does not establish that contrast avoidance prevents AKI or provides a proven nephroprotective benefit. A renal-tailored framework remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective comparative validation using standardized renal endpoints.
title: Acute Kidney Injury After Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Incidence, Risk Factors, Clinical Impact, and Contrast-Sparing Strategies-A Systematic Review.

abstract: Background: Antiphospholipid antibodies have been found in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV). This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of the global antiphospholipid syndrome score (GAPSS) derivatives in predicting cardiovascular diseases in Korean patients with AAV, and to derive a simple candidate index for cardiovascular diseases. Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study including 170 patients with AAV. The adjusted GAPSS (aGAPSS), aGAPSS specific for cardiovascular diseases (aGAPSScvd), and aGAPSS for Korean patients with APS (aGAPSS [KAPS]) were calculated in each patient. The cardiovascular diseases were defined as cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The accuracy of each index was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC). An exploratory multivariable Cox proportional hazards model with a backward elimination method was performed to derive a candidate index. Covariates consisting the aGAPSScvd were included in the model. Results: The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for CVA were 0.507 (p = 0.926), 0.531 (p = 0.676), and 0.493 (p = 0.923), respectively. The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for ACS were 0.613 (p = 0.441), 0.752 (p = 0.086), and 0.796 (p = 0.043), respectively. The exploratory multivariable model revealed a candidate index, aGAPSScvd for ACS in Korean patients with AAV (aGAPSScvd [KAAV]) = 2 × lupus anticoagulant (LA) + 2 × obesity. The AUC of the aGAPSScvd (KAAV) in predicting ACS was 0.843 (p = 0.019). Conclusions: The two-item candidate index aGAPSScvd (KAAV), consisting of LA and obesity, showed discriminatory ability for ACS, which warrants further validation in larger studies.
title: Exploratory Risk Assessment of Cardiovascular Diseases Using Antiphospholipid Antibody-Related Scores in Patients with ANCA-Associated Vasculitis.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Musculoskeletal pain and balance impairments are common in patients referred for cardiac rehabilitation (CR), but their influence on early exercise participation and aerobic capacity remains unclear. This study examined whether pain and muscle mass are associated with initial exercise tolerance test (ETT) participation and VO2 peak. Methods: This retrospective, single-center cohort included 162 of 189 patients referred to CR after percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction; 105 who completed a symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise test were analyzed for VO2 peak. Pain intensity was assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS 0-10), and the skeletal muscle index (SMI) was measured using a bioelectrical impedance analysis. Determinants of ETT participation and VO2 peak were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regressions, respectively, with pain analyzed as a binary, three-category, and continuous variable. Results: More than half the patients reported musculoskeletal pain during physical activity, and 24.7% had balance problems. Patients with pain (VAS 1-10) had lower appendicular skeletal muscle mass and poorer functional status than pain-free patients. Among the 105 who completed the ETT, the pain group showed significantly lower workload-estimated metabolic equivalents [METs (Q)], respiratory exchange ratios, and peak minute ventilation and a shorter exercise time, but VO2 peak did not differ between the groups. ETT participation rates were similar across pain categories (63.4%, 67.2%, and 63.0% for VAS 0, 1-5, and 6-10, respectively). In the multivariable logistic regression, older age, hypertension, and low SMI scores were independently associated with reduced ETT participation. In the linear regression, age was the only significant predictor of VO2 peak; the SMI score showed a borderline association (p = 0.065), but pain intensity was not independently associated with VO2 peak. Conclusions: Musculoskeletal pain is prevalent among patients entering CR after myocardial infarction, and it is accompanied by low muscle mass and functional limitations. However, after adjustment, pain itself was not an independent determinant of ETT participation or VO2 peak. Low SMI scores were independently associated with reduced test participation and showed only a borderline association with aerobic capacity. These cross-sectional findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.
title: Pain, Low Muscle Mass, and Exercise Participation After Myocardial Infarction: Determinants of Initial Exercise Testing at a Tertiary Center Serving a Rural Region.

abstract: Background: Mechanical complications (MCs) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) are now uncommon but remain highly lethal, and contemporary data encompassing the full spectrum of rupture phenotypes are limited. Methods: We retrospectively identified all consecutive adults with post-AMI MCs managed at a tertiary regional referral center from 2015 to 2025. MCs included ventricular septal rupture (VSR), left ventricular free-wall rupture (LVFWR), contained rupture/pseudoaneurysm, and papillary muscle rupture (PMR). The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Exploratory analyses assessed treatment patterns by age, sex, geographical distance, and area-level income. Results: Among 59 patients (mean age 71.2 ± 10.7 years; 50.8% women), 17 (28.8%) had isolated VSR, 21 (35.6%) LVFWR, 10 (16.9%) combined VSR and contained LVFWR/pseudoaneurysm, and 11 (18.6%) PMR. Temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) and surgery were each used in 35 patients (59.3%). Thirty-day mortality was 59.3%. Among patients undergoing definitive invasive treatment, mortality was 45.7%. Older age was associated with higher 30-day mortality (OR per year 1.09, 95% CI 1.03-1.16), whereas surgery was associated with lower observed mortality (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.73), acknowledging major treatment selection and survivor biases. Patients aged ≥75 years received MCS less frequently than younger patients (29.2% vs. 80.0%), and women underwent surgery less frequently than men (46.7% vs. 72.4%). Distance and area-level income were not associated with 30-day mortality. Conclusions: In a contemporary regional referral network, post-AMI MCs remained associated with extreme early mortality. Age and treatment selection were major determinants of observed outcomes, while marked age- and sex-related differences in treatment intensity warrant confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts.
title: Mechanical Complications After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Contemporary Management, Treatment Selection, and Outcomes in a 10-Year Regional Referral Network.

abstract: High bleeding risk (HBR) patients represent a significant proportion of those who undergo percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI). The accurate diagnosis of the HBR population is essential because they suffer significantly higher rates of mortality and bleeding compared with non-HBR patients. Although many bleeding risk scores have been developed, the Academic Research Consortium for HBR (ARC-HBR) criteria have established their superiority over the others. In HBR patients without an indication for oral anticoagulant (OAC), shortening the duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is an effective way to minimize bleeding complications in HBR patients with chronic coronary syndromes (CCS). In cases of an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) however, HBR patients combine increased thrombotic burden with an augmented risk of bleeding. Early antiplatelet interruption could result in stent thrombosis with catastrophic consequences. Therefore, in HBR patients with an ACS choosing the optimal DAPT duration, the right P2Y12 inhibitor and the correct time for de-escalation from a potent P2Y12 inhibitor to clopidogrel are of paramount importance. Similar considerations apply to patients with an OAC indication who, according to the ARC-HBR criteria, are HBR. Although new-generation drug-eluting stents (DES) have been developed to induce faster stent endothelization, only few DES have been examined in a HBR population, and these stents should be preferred. The aim of this review is to present the current knowledge of the HBR population and provide comprehensive algorithms to optimally treat HBR patients who undergo PCI with or without an OAC indication and for both ACS and CCS.
title: High Bleeding Risk Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: How to Choose the Optimal Antithrombotic Therapy, Its Duration and the Right Stent; A Comprehensive Review of the Current Literature and Proposed Treatment Algorithms.

abstract: Background: Assessment of native cardiopulmonary circulation is essential during combined veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-A ECMO) and Impella® support (ECPELLA). Pulmonary artery catheter (PAC)-derived pulmonary artery pulse pressure (PAPP) is associated with RV stroke volume and pulmonary arterial compliance; however, PAC monitoring has procedure-related risks and technical limitations. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is a simple, continuous, noninvasive indicator of pulmonary blood flow; however, its relationship with PAPP during ECPELLA support remains unclear. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed adult patients who underwent simultaneous ECPELLA and PAC monitoring between April 2024 and December 2025. Hemodynamic variables and EtCO2 were evaluated on ECPELLA support day 1 and on the final day of V-A ECMO support. Correlations between EtCO2 and PAPP, as well as their temporal changes during ECPELLA support, were assessed using Spearman correlation analysis. Results: Sixteen patients were included. EtCO2 showed significant positive correlations with PAPP on ECPELLA support day 1 (r = 0.63, p = 0.009), on the final day of V-A ECMO support (r = 0.67, p = 0.007), and for changes over time (ΔPAPP vs. ΔEtCO2, r = 0.76, p = 0.001). Conclusions: EtCO2 was associated with PAPP and its temporal changes during ECPELLA support. Although these findings suggest a potential role for EtCO2 in noninvasive assessment of PAPP trends, further studies in larger cohorts are needed to better characterize this relationship.
title: Association Between End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide and Pulmonary Artery Pulse Pressure During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation with Impella®: A Retrospective Exploratory Study.

abstract: The rapid expansion of transcatheter therapies is reshaping the management of mitral valve (MV) disease and the role of cardiac surgery. Surgery remains particularly valuable when it can provide durable repair, comprehensive anatomical correction, and treatment of concomitant cardiac disease, but these advantages must be balanced against procedural burden and individualized risk. As therapeutic options diversify, the surgeon's role must extend beyond technical performance to disease-specific judgment across surgical and transcatheter strategies, including their implications for future intervention.
