We propose the concept of the contemporary MV specialist and a corresponding specialized-center model in which reconstructive expertise, multimodality assessment, multidisciplinary decision-making, and longitudinal outcome evaluation are integrated to support individualized treatment. The future relevance of MV surgery will therefore depend not on competition with transcatheter therapies but on delivering durable surgical value within an increasingly comprehensive and patient-centered treatment framework.
title: From Mitral Valve Surgeon to Mitral Valve Specialist: Redefining Expertise in Contemporary Mitral Care.

abstract: Background: Reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and acute kidney injury (AKI) are common in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and adversely influence prognosis. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the association between admission eGFR and one-year mortality following STEMI, accounting for admission AKI and cardiovascular risk factors. Methods: Consecutive adults (n = 2903) admitted with STEMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at a tertiary center were analyzed, selected from 2949 initially screened patients after excluding those treated conservatively or with thrombolysis (n = 14), those with a final discharge diagnosis other than STEMI (n = 21), and early deaths within 24 h of presentation (n = 11). Admission eGFR was calculated using the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation and categorized into quintiles. The primary outcome was all-cause one-year mortality, assessed using multivariable logistic regression and secondary Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: Both one-year and 30-day crude mortality decreased markedly across increasing eGFR quintiles (p < 0.001), a pattern that was maintained among patients presenting without admission AKI (30-day mortality: Q5 4.4% vs. Q1 0.0%, p < 0.001). In crude analysis, 30-day mortality was 9.1% in the lowest eGFR quintile overall. Multivariable logistic regression identified advancing age (OR 1.05 per year, p < 0.001) and admission AKI (OR 7.07, p < 0.001) as the dominant independent predictors of one-year mortality, whereas individual eGFR quintiles were attenuated after adjustment (global Wald p = 0.047). Conclusions: Lower admission eGFR is significantly associated with one-year mortality after STEMI in crude and unadjusted analyses, but its predictive contribution is substantially attenuated following multivariable adjustment for advancing age and admission AKI, which serve as the dominant prognostic determinants. Rather than acting as a strong isolated independent predictor, admission renal function primarily serves as an indicator of baseline cardiorenal reserve and baseline patient vulnerability.
title: Association Between Admission Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate and Long-Term Mortality in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Background/Objectives: The optimal stent deployment strategy for low-complexity Type A and B1 coronary lesions remains poorly defined. We compared direct stenting (DS) and predilatation followed by stenting (PS) in elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for these lesions. Methods: This single-center, retrospective study included adults undergoing elective PCI with drug-eluting stents for ACC/AHA Type A or B1 lesions between June 2020 and December 2025. Procedure duration, cumulative contrast volume, and cumulative reference air kerma were compared using generalized estimating equations accounting for within-patient clustering, adjusted for clinical, lesion-related, procedural, and operator-related factors. Results: In total, 324 patients contributed 334 PCI observations (PS: 239; DS: 95). After adjustment, DS was associated with lower contrast volume (-18.12 mL; 95% CI -28.08 to -8.17; p < 0.001) and lower cumulative reference air kerma (-223.54 mGy; 95% CI -259.98 to -187.11; p < 0.001), whereas procedure duration did not differ significantly (-0.92 min; 95% CI -4.56 to 2.71; p = 0.619). Findings were consistent when restricted to the first PCI per patient. Conclusions: In these lesions, DS was associated with lower contrast volume and cumulative reference air kerma, without a significant adjusted difference in procedure duration. As nonrandomized observations, these findings do not establish equivalence in clinical safety or effectiveness, nor do they demonstrate cost-effectiveness.
title: Procedural Efficiency of Direct Stenting Versus Predilatation in Type A and B1 Coronary Lesions.

abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute and usually reversible form of myocardial dysfunction associated with emotional or physical stress. Solid organ transplantation (SOT) combines several potential triggers, including major surgical stress, hemodynamic instability, systemic inflammation, and exposure to exogenous catecholamines. Respiratory failure, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and altered cardiac innervation may also contribute. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on organ-specific timing, potential triggers, diagnostic challenges, management, and outcomes of TTS in SOT recipients. Reported cases predominantly occur early after liver and kidney transplantation, whereas presentations after heart transplantation range from the immediate postoperative period to years later. After heart transplantation, distinguishing TTS from early graft dysfunction and considering donor-side TTS are particularly important. Diagnostic certainty varies among published cases because formal criteria and the exclusion of competing diagnoses are inconsistently documented. Management largely follows recommendations for the general TTS population, with temporary mechanical circulatory support used in selected severe cases. Although ventricular function usually recovers, cardiogenic shock, arrhythmias, and multiorgan dysfunction may complicate the acute course, and persistent ventricular impairment has been associated with poorer long-term outcomes after liver transplantation. Comparisons with the general TTS population suggest a high proportion of severe presentations among reported transplant-associated cases; however, publication and ascertainment bias preclude firm conclusions about differences in incidence or severity. Evidence remains dominated by case reports, small series, and retrospective studies, underscoring the need for standardized reporting and prospective multicenter research.
title: Takotsubo Syndrome in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: Current Evidence, Clinical Challenges, and Future Perspectives-A Narrative Review.

abstract: Background: Intracardiac thrombus is a clinically important complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), particularly in patients with ventricular aneurysm. We examined the contemporaneous associations of anterior ventricular involvement and D-dimer with echocardiographically documented intracardiac thrombus with incomplete chamber-specific localization among hospitalized AMI patients with ventricular aneurysm. Methods: This retrospective analysis included 1684 patients with documented ventricular aneurysm from a final cohort of 17,950 hospitalized AMI patients treated between January 2018 and October 2025. The first D-dimer measurement obtained at our hospital after AMI confirmation was used for D-dimer analyses. Ventricular aneurysm and intracardiac thrombus status were determined from the available echocardiographic documentation during the index hospitalization. Aneurysm locations were coded as linked patient-level, non-mutually exclusive indicators. Logistic regression evaluated anterior involvement; missing model covariates were multiply imputed and regression estimates were pooled using Rubin's rules. Collinearity diagnostics and sensitivity analyses restricted to patients with apical aneurysm, including a complete-case analysis, were performed. Model-performance measures were interpreted as exploratory apparent performance in the development dataset. Results: Intracardiac thrombus was documented in 211 of 1684 patients (12.5%). Anterior involvement was more frequent among patients with thrombus than among those without thrombus (57.3% vs. 45.0%; p < 0.001) and remained associated with thrombus in the primary anatomical and clinical model (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.20-2.21; p = 0.002). D-dimer was available in 1633 patients. On the log2-transformed scale, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with higher odds of echocardiographically documented intracardiac thrombus (adjusted OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.14-1.34; p < 0.001). As a complementary descriptive analysis, the observed thrombus proportion increased from 3.63% in Q1 to 22.30% in Q4; compared with Q1, the adjusted ORs were 3.71, 5.22, and 9.50 in Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. The combined model had a mean apparent AUC of 0.716, compared with 0.713 for the model containing D-dimer without anterior involvement; the mean absolute increment was approximately 0.003. Conclusions: Among hospitalized patients with AMI and ventricular aneurysm, higher D-dimer levels and anterior ventricular involvement were associated with echocardiographically documented intracardiac thrombus. Chamber-specific localization was incomplete, and these contemporaneous associations do not establish causality or prospective prediction. Anterior involvement provided minimal incremental discrimination beyond D-dimer.
title: Association of Anterior Ventricular Aneurysm and D-Dimer with Intracardiac Thrombus in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Analysis.

abstract: Background: Whether the initial clip type selected during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) of the mitral valve-grasping width and arm length-independently influences procedural and echocardiographic outcomes remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 138 consecutive patients undergoing mitral TEER. The first implanted clip was classified as narrow standard-length (NT), long narrow-arm (XT), or long wide-arm (XTW). Determinants of initial clip selection and its association with procedural success (residual mitral regurgitation [MR] ≤ 1+), post-procedural transmitral gradient, and the need for ≥2 clips were assessed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Results: Median age was 74.0 (66.0-80.0), 74.5 (66.0-82.5), and 75.0 (70.0-79.0) years, and median LVEF was 35.0% (30.0-50.0), 30.0% (25.0-45.0), and 40.0% (25.0-45.0), for the NT, XT, and XTW groups, respectively; 66% of patients overall were male. An XTW clip was implanted first in 61.6% of patients. XTW selection was independently associated with larger effective regurgitant orifice area, lower LVEF, longer posterior leaflet length, and secondary MR (all p < 0.05), whereas NT selection favored younger age, smaller orifice, and higher LVEF. After adjustment for these factors, no statistically significant independent association was detected between initial clip type and residual MR ≥2+, post-procedural transmitral gradient, or the need for additional clips (all p > 0.05); however, confidence intervals were wide. On univariable analysis, larger left atrial size and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation were associated with residual MR ≥ 2+, but neither remained significant after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions: Initial clip selection was associated with valve anatomy, LVEF and MR etiology. No statistically significant independent association between initial clip type and procedural or short-term echocardiographic outcomes was detected in this cohort. Given the observational design, confounding by indication, limited sample size and wide confidence intervals, clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded, and these findings do not establish the superiority or equivalence of any clip-selection strategy.
title: Initial Clip Selection and Outcomes After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Single-Center Experience.

abstract: Chronic total occlusion (CTO) occurs in 16-52% of patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and is often accompanied by variable development of coronary collateral circulation (CCC). The aim of this work was to study the associations between circulating plasma microRNAs (miRNAs) and the development of CCC in patients with CTO. This exploratory study included 43 patients: a control group-patients without significant coronary artery stenosis (n = 20), and two CTO groups with good (n = 13) and poor (n = 10) CCC based on the Rentrop classification. The study was performed simultaneously on two types of plasma samples (K2EDTA and sodium citrate). Total RNA was isolated using the miRNeasy Serum/Plasma Advanced Kit. Libraries were prepared using the QIAseq miRNA UDI Library Kit and then sequenced on the NextSeq 550 using a 1 × 75 bp protocol. A total of 18 miRNAs were found to be differentially expressed (DE) in EDTA plasma and 13 in citrate plasma; only one miRNA in citrate plasma (hsa-miR-92a-3p) was differentially expressed between the good and poor CCC groups. However, given the limited sample size, the findings should be considered hypothesis-generating, and further studies are required for validation in larger, independent cohorts and to establish the roles of these miRNAs in CCC development.
title: Association of Circulating microRNAs in Plasma with Coronary Collateral Circulation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion.

abstract: (1) Background: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) links innate immune activation to myocardial injury and adverse outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), yet the relationship between local intracoronary and systemic peripheral IL-6, and their prognostic value, remains unclear. (2) Methods: This prospective single-center study aimed to compare intracoronary and peripheral venous IL-6 and other inflammatory biomarkers in AMI, included 83 consecutive STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction) or NSTEMI (non ST-elevation myocardial infarction) patients undergoing coronary angiography. Paired intracoronary and peripheral venous samples were obtained before revascularization and analyzed for IL-6, CRP, and ferritin, and correlated with LVEF (left ventricle ejection fraction), NT-proBNP, and a 30-day composite endpoint (death or heart failure hospitalization). (3) Results: Peripheral IL-6 exceeded intracoronary levels in 86.7% of patients (p < 0.001), with both peripheral IL-6 and the venous-to-coronary difference higher in STEMI than NSTEMI. IL-6 in both compartments correlated inversely with LVEF and positively with NT-proBNP and troponin I. Patients reaching the composite endpoint (10.8%) had markedly higher IL-6 and CRP. ROC analysis showed discriminatory ability for the endpoint by intracoronary and peripheral IL-6. (4) Conclusions: Intracoronary and peripheral IL-6 are associated with infarction phenotype, ventricular dysfunction, and short-term outcomes in AMI, supporting its role as an early prognostic biomarker.
title: Coronary and Peripheral Venous Inflammatory Biomarkers in Acute Myocardial Infarction: Associations with Myocardial Injury, Cardiac Function, and Clinical Outcomes.

abstract: Perceval Plus and TAVI are increasingly used for severe aortic stenosis, both relying on a self-expanding nitinol stent design, yet evidence specific to Perceval Plus remains limited regarding postoperative clinical outcomes and hematological and inflammatory dynamics. We compared postoperative clinical outcomes and longitudinal platelet/CRP dynamics between Perceval Plus and TAVI in a retrospective single-center cohort, in which 26 propensity score-matched pairs were obtained (1:1 matching) from patients undergoing Su-AVR (Perceval Plus, n = 53) or TAVI (self-expanding Medtronic devices, n = 101). Mortality, echocardiographic outcomes, and rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation and conduction disturbances showed no statistically significant differences between groups, while TAVI was associated with shorter ICU and hospital stay and Su-AVR required higher FFP transfusion (p = 0.016). Platelet count declined in both groups, with a deeper nadir in Su-AVR (postoperative day 3: 66% decline) versus TAVI (day 4: 27% decline), with a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.013); CRP rose in both groups but more rapidly and to a greater magnitude in Su-AVR (time and group × time interaction, both p < 0.001). Su-AVR and TAVI showed no statistically significant differences in the clinical safety outcomes assessed but differed in postoperative hematological and inflammatory magnitude, likely reflecting multifactorial procedure- and device-related mechanisms, warranting confirmation in larger, prospective, multicenter studies.
title: Sutureless Aortic Valve Replacement with the Perceval Plus® Versus TAVI: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Postoperative Outcomes, Hematological Dynamics, and Inflammatory Response.

abstract: Non-invasive ventilation relieves acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema and reduces intubation. Whether it saves lives is disputed; restricting the pooled record to the least biased trials leaves neither endpoint significant. My hypothesis: raising pleural pressure subtracts venous return; whether that subtraction is banked as unloading or paid as lost output depends on preload responsiveness, for which left ventricular filling pressure is a candidate effect modifier and not a measure. One radiographic label may contain two gas-exchange phenotypes, proposed for groups, not patients: carbon dioxide accumulates far more slowly than an ischemia-driven presentation floods the alveolus, and the remodeled ventricle arrives hypercapnic. Applied pressure inflates flooded air spaces without removing lung water, lowers left ventricular transmural pressure, and reaches two cardiac submechanisms. The left ventricular arm follows the sign rule; the renal arm follows it only through volume status; and in right ventricular infarction, the recorded filling pressure misleads, while the pulmonary arm does not reverse. In acute coronary syndromes, the first prediction fails if transmural pressure falls no more in the elevated than in the normal stratum, or if stroke volume index does not fall in the latter. The outer boundary is the requirement for emergency reperfusion, a limit inferred rather than measured directly.
title: One Pressure, Many Targets: Left Ventricular Filling Pressure as a Candidate Effect Modifier for Non-Invasive Ventilation in Acute Coronary Syndromes.

abstract: Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an established calcium modification strategy for severely calcified coronary lesions. The Shunmei ShockFast™ IVL system is a novel device that appeared safe and feasible in an initial clinical experience. However, its calcium fracture typology, depth distribution, and quantitative stent optimization characteristics have not been characterized by serial optical coherence tomography (OCT). Objectives: To provide the first dedicated serial OCT sub-study of calcium modification patterns and stent optimization metrics achieved with the ShockFast™ IVL system in a cohort of patients with severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. Methods: This is a prospective, single-center OCT imaging sub-study nested within the Cardio-FR registry (NCT04185285). We included 14 patients with OCT assessment performed at three mandatory time points-baseline (before any device delivery), post-IVL, and post-stenting-who underwent PCI with the ShockFast™ IVL system between June 2025 and April 2026. The primary endpoint was OCT-confirmed calcium fracture rate following IVL treatment. Secondary endpoints included calcium fractures ≥2 and type, post-lesion-preparation lumen gain, minimum stent area (MSA), stent expansion (SE), malapposition, and edge dissection rates. Exploratory correlative analyses between baseline calcium morphology and post-IVL stent optimization outcomes were performed. Results: Median baseline OCT MLA was 2.22 mm2 (IQR 1.4-3.61). Calcium fractures were identified in 10 of 14 lesions (71%, 95% CI 45-88%) following a lesion-preparation strategy incorporating ShockFast™ IVL, with ≥2 fractures in 43%. Fractures were classified as partial-thickness (non-transmural) in 30% and full-thickness (transmural) in 70% of cases. Median post-lesion-preparation lumen gain was 0.53 mm2 (IQR 0.3-0.84). Median final MSA was 4.77 mm2 (IQR 3.59-5.34) and median SE was 89.5% (IQR 85-94), with SE >80% achieved in 100% of lesions. No major malapposition or medial edge dissections were recorded. Conclusions: Applied as the central calcium-modification component of a comprehensive lesion-preparation strategy, the ShockFast™ IVL system was associated with OCT-confirmed calcium fractures in the majority of the lesions, with favorable stent expansion and optimization metrics in the absence of major malapposition or edge dissections. These findings provide the first dedicated serial OCT sub-study of calcium modification mediated by a lesion-preparation strategy incorporating ShockFast™ IVL, consistent with feasibility as a novel IVL platform suitable for further investigation in adequately powered comparative studies.
title: Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Findings After Lesion-Preparation Incorporating the ShockFast™ Intravascular Lithotripsy: A Prospective Single-Center Imaging Sub-Study.

abstract: Background and Objectives: Routine records may conflate valvular heart disease (VHD), functional classification, and shared diagnostic assessment. We quantified the cross-sectional association between a registry VHD label and explicitly documented heart failure (HF), while recognizing that every observed valve lesion was regurgitant. Materials and Methods: The analytic sample comprised all 224 eligible adults admitted to the Internal Medicine II Department of a railway-affiliated hospital between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026: 38 with documented VHD and 186 without documented VHD. The primary outcome was an explicit HF diagnosis; a combined HF/NYHA-positive field was examined as an over-inclusive sensitivity outcome. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking history, and total cholesterol. Results: Explicit HF was documented in 24/38 patients with VHD (63.2%) and 72/186 without VHD (38.7%; adjusted OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.38-5.99). The combined outcome was present in 28/38 (73.7%) and 101/186 (54.3%), respectively (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.09-5.21). All 38 exposed patients had documented mitral, aortic, and/or tricuspid regurgitation; no stenosis, prolapse, or prior valve intervention was recorded. Conclusions: Documented valvular regurgitation was associated with explicit HF documentation. Because regurgitation may be secondary to ventricular or atrial disease, reverse causation, shared ascertainment, non-adjudicated diagnoses, and residual confounding preclude causal, temporal, prognostic, or lesion-specific inference.
title: Documented Valvular Regurgitation and Explicit Heart Failure in an Internal Medicine Registry: A Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) remain the dominant operational categories for acute coronary syndrome triage because they are simple, widely implemented, and closely linked to reperfusion pathways. However, diagnostic ST-segment elevation and acute coronary occlusion are not synonymous. A clinically important subgroup of patients classified as NSTEMI have total or near-total culprit-artery occlusion and may experience delayed angiography despite ongoing myocardial ischemia. This structured narrative review examines the rationale, evidence, electrocardiographic patterns, quantitative bedside criteria, and emerging technologies relevant to occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI), with particular emphasis on STEMI-negative coronary occlusion. Conventional STEMI criteria are highly specific but incompletely sensitive for acute coronary occlusion, particularly in posterior or circumflex infarction, early anterior occlusion, left bundle branch block, ventricular paced rhythm, and transient reperfusion. Recognition of OMI therefore requires integration of ECG morphology, reciprocal changes, serial ECG evolution, clinical presentation, troponin kinetics, and adjunctive imaging rather than reliance on ST-segment thresholds alone. Practical patterns include hyperacute T waves, the de Winter pattern, posterior OMI, modified Sgarbossa-positive conduction abnormalities, subtle anterior OMI, and selected high-risk ischemic patterns. Artificial intelligence may improve scalable detection of subtle occlusion patterns, although external validation, workflow integration, explainability, and prospective outcome studies remain necessary. Current evidence supports OMI as a promising complementary diagnostic framework rather than an established replacement for guideline-based STEMI/NSTEMI classification. Prospective implementation studies are required to determine whether OMI-guided pathways improve clinical outcomes without unacceptable false-positive catheterization-laboratory activation.
title: Occlusive Myocardial Infarction: A Practical Review of STEMI-Negative Coronary Occlusion in Acute Coronary Syndromes.

abstract: Background and Objectives: Unstable angina has traditionally been considered the least severe acute coronary syndrome presentation, but ten-year prognostic data remain limited. We compared the clinical characteristics and ten-year prognosis of unstable angina versus non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included consecutive patients older than eighteen years admitted with suspected acute coronary syndrome to a Spanish tertiary hospital between January 2009 and December 2015. Ten-year survival and clinical outcomes were evaluated retrospectively through long-term tracking of electronic medical records and official regional death registries. Results: Of 3029 patients (10.6% with unstable angina, 45.0% with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, and 44.4% with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction), those with unstable angina had a median age of 66.0 years (vs. 67.0 and 62.0 years in the other cohorts, respectively; p < 0.001) and a significantly higher prevalence of prior myocardial infarction (31.5% vs. 21.9% and 11.4%, respectively; p < 0.001). However, unstable angina presented lower-risk acute profiles (Killip class >I: 2.5% versus 17.5% and 20.7%; p < 0.001; median GRACE score: 89.9 versus 107.6 and 113.3; p < 0.001) and 0% in-hospital mortality (versus 3.3% and 5.4%; p < 0.001). At ten years, cumulative mortality reached 23.4% in unstable angina, converging with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (29.1%; p > 0.05) but remaining lower than non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (35.3%; p < 0.05). In multivariable Cox analysis, unstable angina was not independently associated with ten-year mortality (overall p = 0.066; vs. STEMI p = 0.743; vs. NSTEMI p = 0.133). Conclusions: Despite favorable acute stabilization and the absence of in-hospital mortality, the survival advantage of unstable angina over ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction appears to attenuate over a ten-year period. This trend toward mortality convergence is likely associated with the baseline comorbidity burden, highlighting the clinical need for intensive secondary prevention.
title: Long-Term Prognosis of Unstable Angina: A Ten-Year Follow-Up Study Comparing Clinical Outcomes with Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Background and Objectives: Coronary drug-coated balloons (DCBs) deliver antiproliferative therapy during a single inflation without leaving a permanent scaffold or implanted drug reservoir. Their performance therefore depends on preservation of the coating during delivery, efficient vessel-wall transfer, and sufficient tissue exposure after balloon removal. This review critically examines the evidence for platform engineering, tissue exposure, and angiographic or intravascular imaging response. Materials and Methods: This narrative review synthesized English-language experimental, pharmacokinetic, imaging, and clinical evidence identified through the original PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar searches and a documented PubMed search during revision on 9 September 2026. Exact queries, record dispositions and descriptive study appraisals are supplied; conference abstracts, preprints and unpublished data were excluded. Results: DCB performance is platform-specific rather than determined by drug class alone. Within both paclitaxel- and limus-based devices, excipient chemistry, coating or carrier architecture, release behavior, and retention strategy may influence drug delivery. Bench and computational studies identify potential transfer and drug-loss pathways, pharmacokinetic studies measure tissue exposure, and imaging and clinical studies assess morphology and outcomes separately. The cited human studies do not quantify coronary tissue drug exposure. Findings from unrelated platforms and models cannot establish a causal delivery-to-outcome pathway. Conclusions: Coronary DCBs should be evaluated as integrated, device-specific drug-delivery platforms. Standardized studies linking engineering performance and tissue exposure with imaging and clinical outcomes are needed.
title: Coronary Drug-Coated Balloons as Brief-Contact Drug-Delivery Platforms: Engineering, Tissue Pharmacokinetics, and Angiographic/Imaging Response.

abstract: Background and Objectives: Composite indices from routine inflammatory, haematological and nutritional measurements are widely reported as prognostic markers after acute coronary syndromes, but whether they add information beyond their components is uncertain. Materials and Methods: In 30-day survivors of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) undergoing coronary angiography at a single centre, thirteen composite indices and six prespecified components were evaluated for five-year all-cause mortality using ROC analysis, Cox regression and the change in Harrell's C-index (ΔC) over a study clinical model. Each index was also compared with a freely weighted model of its own constituents and with a reference model adding CRP and albumin. Results: Among 561 patients (median follow-up 5.48 years), 94 died, 86 within five years. Composite-index AUCs ranged from 0.616 to 0.689; none exceeded CRP alone after multiplicity correction. Eight indices were nominally associated with mortality after adjustment (hazard ratios 1.26-1.38 per 1 SD), but every bootstrap confidence interval for ΔC over the clinical model included zero. Fixed indices and freely weighted constituents performed similarly (cross-validated ΔC -0.0089 to +0.0053), with one small exploratory difference favouring the fixed MLR ratio. Adding CRP and albumin raised the C-index from 0.7720 to 0.7826; over this reference, no estimable composite showed evidence of association (all p ≥ 0.19). Conclusions: In 30-day survivors of NSTEMI, composite indices showed no evidence of improved long-term mortality discrimination over a study-specific clinical model and contained no information beyond their measured constituents. Their independent associations may largely reflect information already present in the components. Small gains cannot be excluded; the findings do not establish equivalence.
title: Composite Haematological and Nutritional Indices Show No Evidence of Improved Long-Term Mortality Discrimination Beyond Their Own Components in Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Oncology and cardiology use paclitaxel, a powerful cell-division inhibitor. Paclitaxel-eluting coated metal stents in oncology prevent tumor growth by modulating proliferation, apoptosis, and angiogenesis. Paclitaxel-eluting stents reduce in-stent restenosis and maintain arterial patency in cardiology. Paclitaxel encapsulated in liposomes improves targeted administration, pharmacokinetics, and therapeutic efficacy. Liposome-loaded paclitaxel has a stronger anti-tumor effect than standard formulations. Paclitaxel plus sirolimus in a stent may synergistically prevent restenosis and inhibit tumors. Liposomal formulations with supplemental medications offer promising prospects for improving therapeutic accuracy and efficacy. Liposomal paclitaxel enhances targeted drug delivery, which may improve cancer treatment and cardiovascular treatments such as drug-eluting stents and drug-coated balloons in interventional radiology. Advanced delivery technologies have changed paclitaxel drug delivery methods for therapeutic use by overcoming its low solubility and systemic toxicity. Nanocrystals and liposomes enable high drug loading and precise targeted delivery, and, by eliminating toxic solvents such as Cremophor EL, they improve the safety and efficacy of cancer therapy.
title: Advanced Paclitaxel Delivery Systems in Oncology and Cardiovascular Medicine: Current Formulations and Emerging Technologies.

abstract: In this manuscript, a miniaturized ultrasonic Renal Denervation (RDN) catheter for removing sympathetic nerves around the renal artery is proposed. The RDN catheter consists of an ultrasonic transducer, a balloon catheter and a control system. Owing to the use of a piezoelectric ceramic tube as the ultrasonic transducer, the RDN catheter is designed to provide 360° circumferential acoustic exposure around the renal artery. The piezoelectric ceramic tube has an active length of 6 mm, an inner diameter of 1.1 mm, and an outer diameter of 1.6 mm and the material of piezoelectric ceramic tube is PZT8. The balloon catheter of the proposed RDN catheter is designed and optimized so that the diameter of the portion inserted into the vessel is ≤1.8 mm, with the aim of enabling access to the renal artery via Transradial Access (TRA). In addition, a liquid circulation system is integrated into the balloon catheter to cool the ultrasonic transducer, with the aim of limiting heating near the renal artery wall. The measured resonant and anti-resonant frequencies of the ultrasonic transducer are 8.72 MHz and 9.69 MHz, respectively. Under 70 W input electrical excitation at 9.69 MHz, the average acoustic pressure measured at 6-7 mm from the catheter surface is 2.11 MPa. In addition, the control system prototype is also developed. Finally, the thermal feasibility of the proposed catheter is evaluated through phantoms and ex vivo tissues. In the phantom, visible whitening appears by 0.5 s, and an annular whitened region is evident by 8 s; at 15 s, its image-estimated thickness is approximately 3.6 mm, with an adjacent transparent interval of approximately 1.2 mm. Ex vivo porcine liver also shows macroscopic discoloration consistent with thermal denaturation. These observations support the preliminary acoustic and thermal feasibility of the proposed RDN catheter.
title: Development of Renal Denervation Catheter Based on Piezoelectric Ultrasonic Transducer.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes increasingly shapes acute-care demand through cardiovascular disease, critical illness, frailty, stroke and preventable metabolic emergencies. Yet in health systems without mature diabetes registries, much of this burden may be visible only indirectly through national clinical audits and registries.
AIM: To assess how Ireland's National Office of Clinical Audit (NOCA) captures diabetes-related intelligence across major healthcare pathways and what this reveals about national chronic disease surveillance capacity.
METHODS: A structured narrative review of publicly available NOCA reports and audit publications from 2021 to 2025 was undertaken. Eligible reports had direct diabetes relevance or addressed conditions in which diabetes is a major comorbidity, risk factor or outcome modifier. Data extraction focused on population coverage, diabetes-related variables, temporal trends, hospital-level variation and reporting limitations.
RESULTS: Diabetes-specific reporting was recent and uneven. The 2022 paediatric diabetes feasibility study identified 3332 children and young people with type 1 diabetes across 19 centres, with major variation in multidisciplinary staffing, transition pathways, HbA1c measurement and data systems. Paediatric critical care reporting identified 232 DKA admissions among 15,288 admissions during 2014-2023. In adult acute care, diabetes was recorded in 430/1615 STEMI cases in 2024, rising from 18% in 2021 to 27% in 2024, while overall timely reperfusion declined from 67% in 2017 to 58% in 2024. Stroke, ICU, hip fracture and mortality audits were highly diabetes-relevant but did not publish diabetes-stratified outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: National clinical audit infrastructures may function as distributed chronic disease intelligence systems even in the absence of mature integrated diabetes registries.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
title: National clinical audits as distributed diabetes surveillance infrastructure: Consensus lessons from Ireland.
Myocardial Fibrosis Reflects Prior Heart Failure Burden and Predicts Persistent Heart Failure After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-induced type B aortic dissection is a rare complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation with uncertain long-term behavior.
CASE SUMMARY: An 85-year-old woman developed a focal aortic isthmus dissection during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Initial computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed no malperfusion or rupture; conservative management and serial CTA surveillance were selected. Despite persistent clinical stability, follow-up CTA demonstrated progressive focal outpouching and pseudoaneurysmal remodeling. At 17 months, elective thoracic endovascular aortic repair achieved complete exclusion of the lesion.
DISCUSSION: Catheter-induced dissection may represent a mechanistically distinct entity from spontaneous type B aortic dissection, limiting direct extrapolation of conventional management pathways. Morphological progression, rather than symptoms or absolute aortic diameter, prompted intervention.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Clinical stability does not establish aortic wall healing. Long-term serial CTA can identify silent adverse remodeling and guide elective thoracic endovascular aortic repair in selected patients.
title: Catheter-Induced Type B Aortic Dissection After TAVI: Delayed Adverse Remodeling.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthetic mitral valve degeneration in adults with repaired congenital heart disease (CHD) can produce rapid hemodynamic collapse and is challenging when surgery and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) are unavailable.
CASE SUMMARY: A 20-year-old woman with congenital mitral stenosis and multiple ventricular septal defects initially palliated as a single ventricle, then converted to biventricular circulation, with prior mechanical and bioprosthetic mitral valve replacements (the latter for menorrhagia, outside our care), presented in cardiogenic shock with prosthetic mitral stenosis and acute left atrial thrombus. Hypoplastic peripheral vessels precluded MCS. Salvage valve-in-valve was performed with bilateral cerebral protection, FlowTriever thrombectomy (Inari Medical), and a 26-mm SAPIEN 3 valve (Edwards Lifesciences).
DISCUSSION: Transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve can be lifesaving in adults with repaired CHD when intracardiac thrombus is present, and MCS is unavailable.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In highly selected, life-threatening presentations without alternatives, salvage transcatheter mitral intervention may be considered despite intracardiac thrombus. Peripheral vascular anatomy must be evaluated preprocedurally in complex CHD.
title: Salvage Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve With Aspiration Thrombectomy in a Young Adult With Repaired CHD.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis may present with nonspecific systemic symptoms that mimic other conditions, creating diagnostic challenges in high-risk patients.
CASE SUMMARY: A 44-year-old man with advanced Fabry disease, bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, and a chronic Port-A-Cath presented with fever, chills, and malaise shortly after pegunigalsidase alfa infusion, initially raising concern for an infusion reaction. Persistent methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia prompted further evaluation, revealing right-sided native tricuspid valve infective endocarditis with septal leaflet perforation and severe tricuspid regurgitation. Prosthetic aortic valve involvement remained clinically suspected despite nondiagnostic imaging. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multifocal septic embolic infarctions. He received targeted intravenous antibiotics, catheter removal, multidisciplinary care, and cardiothoracic surgical evaluation, with continued medical management recommended.
CONCLUSION: This case emphasizes maintaining suspicion for infective endocarditis despite a plausible alternative diagnosis and highlights the role of multimodality imaging in guiding management.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent S aureus bacteremia should prompt evaluation for infective endocarditis in high-risk patients even when symptoms initially suggest a plausible alternative diagnosis. Multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary assessment are essential when initial imaging is nondiagnostic or clinical findings suggest embolic complications.
title: Fabry's Disease, Valvular Disease and Infective Endocarditis: A Rare Intersection.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A new index, the neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol ratio (NHR), has been reported to predict atherosclerosis and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This study aimed to investigate the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent complications in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (MPA/GPA).
METHODS: Clinical data of 150 patients with MPA/GPA were analysed retrospectively. Baseline demographic data, the Birmingham vasculitis activity score (BVAS), the five-factor score (FFS), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded. All-cause mortality, relapse, end-stage kidney disease, cerebrovascular accident (CVA), and ACS were evaluated as subsequent complications. NHR was calculated using the following formula: neutrophil count (× 1000/mm3) / HDL-cholesterol levels (mg/dL). NHR was analysed both as a continuous variable and using exploratory categorical cut-offs. Death before CVA was treated as a competing event in the cumulative incidence analysis.
RESULTS: The median age was 63.5 years (64.0% female). Baseline NHR was significantly correlated with baseline BVAS, ESR, and CRP levels. Of the five subsequent complications, only subsequent CVA demonstrated a significant area under the curve in a receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of baseline NHR. Continuous NHR was not significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP. In complementary exploratory analyses using the cohort-derived cut-off, patients with baseline NHR ≥ 0.17 had a higher frequency of subsequent CVA and a lower CVA-free survival rate than those with baseline NHR < 0.17. The former group also had a higher cumulative incidence of CVA when death before CVA was treated as a competing event. NHR ≥ 0.17 remained significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent CVA in patients with MPA/GPA. Key Points • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio was significantly correlated with baseline Birmingham vasculitis activity score, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein levels in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis. • Patients with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 had a significantly higher risk of subsequent cerebrovascular accident and a lower cerebrovascular accident-free survival rate than those with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio <0.17. • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 remained independently associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident after adjustment for age and C-reactive protein.
title: Baseline neutrophil-to-HDL cholesterol ratio is associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

title: Analytical Evaluation of 5 High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin Assays at New Lower Sex-Specific 99th Percentile Upper Reference Limits.
