abstract: Despite advancements in resuscitation guidelines, in-hospital cardiac arrests (IHCA) remain associated with high mortality and morbidity. We aimed to evaluate predictive factors associated with survival in patients suffering an IHCA. A systematic literature search was conducted to identify studies reporting factors associated with survival to hospital discharge following IHCA (2000-2024; English language). Data were extracted for all reported variables including patient demographics, arrest characteristics, and interventions. Variables with low heterogeneity were meta-analyzed using a random-effects model to generate odds ratios (OR) or standardized mean differences (SMD) for survival. Twelve studies comprising 5,088 patients were included. Key predictors of survival included witnessed arrest (OR 2.99, p=0.009), arrest in the operating room (OR 2.19, p=0.005), initial shockable rhythm (OR 3.96, p<0.001), and cardiac cause for arrest (OR 3.44, p<0.001). Conversely pulseless electrical activity as the initial rhythm (OR 0.47, p<0.001) and older age (SMD -0.30, p=0.03) were associated with increased mortality. Sex, baseline comorbidities, CPR duration, and requirement of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation were not significant, and high heterogeneity was observed for CPR (I²=97%), witnessed arrest (I²=89%), and shockable rhythm (I²=83%), which should be considered when interpreting the pooled estimates. In conclusion, survival following IHCA is more strongly associated with arrest characteristics and clinical context than baseline comorbidity burden. These findings may support early risk stratification and guide peri-arrest decision-making. STUDY REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024520780 CLINICAL PERSPECTIVES: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) carries persistently high mortality despite advances in resuscitation. This meta-analysis of 12 studies comprising 5,088 patients demonstrates that survival is predominantly determined by arrest-specific and contextual factors rather than baseline comorbidity burden. Shockable initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, cardiac etiology, and procedural arrest location were the strongest predictors of survival, while non-shockable rhythms, intubation and older age predicted mortality. Sex and traditional cardiovascular risk factors were not significantly associated with outcomes. These findings support early peri-arrest risk stratification, resuscitation decisions and inform goals-of-care discussions in patients experiencing IHCA.
title: Clinical Factors Associated With Survival in In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USAT) may enhance right ventricular recovery in intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, but evidence is limited.
OBJECTIVES: We compared the safety, efficacy, and net benefit of USAT versus standard anticoagulation.
METHODS: We analysed a propensity-matched prospective cohort of 432 intermediate-high-risk patients (216 USAT vs 216 anticoagulation) from the Italian USAT-HI and OPTIRAPE registries. Outcomes included all- cause, cardiovascular (CV) and PE-related death, major bleedings, and a composite net clinical benefit (NCB), with a day-7 landmark analysis distinguishing early (0-7 days) from late (8-30 days) events. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression with Hazard ratios (HRs) and relative 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Baseline demographics (mean age 64 ± 12 years; 48% female) and comorbidities were balanced between cohorts. USAT was associated with lower all-cause (7.4% vs 13.9%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.01), cardiovascular (3.2% vs 8.3%; HR 0.39; p < 0.001), and PE-related mortality (2.3% vs 6.5%; HR 0.34; p = 0.02) compared with anticoagulation. Major bleeding was similar (2.7% vs 1.9%; p = 0.56). USAT significantly improved net clinical benefit (13.4% vs 25.9%; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.001), mainly driven by reductions in early mortality and clinical deterioration. Landmark analysis indicated that benefits were largely confined to the first 7 days, with favourable but non-significant effects during days 8-30.
CONCLUSIONS: In intermediate-high-risk PE, USAT was associated with lower early mortality, improved net clinical outcomes, and a safety profile comparable to standard anticoagulation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Propensity-matched prospective cohort of 432 intermediate-high-risk patients (216 USAT vs 216 anticoagulation) from the Italian USAT-HI and OPTIRAPE registries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised registry comparison with residual confounding; benefit was largely confined to the first 7 days.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched analysis of two Italian registries associating ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis with lower early mortality than anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: USAT was associated with lower all-cause mortality (7.4% vs 13.9%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.01) and similar major bleeding (2.7% vs 1.9%; p = 0.56). Net clinical benefit favoured USAT (13.4% vs 25.9%; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Catheter-directed therapy for intermediate-high-risk PE lacks mortality evidence from randomised trials, so a mortality signal in matched registry data is relevant to ongoing trial interpretation.

title: Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis versus anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism.

abstract:
PURPOSE: A multidisciplinary team-based approach became one of the main paradigms in health care. Current evidence regarding the efficacy of Shock Teams and related advanced shock care models in cardiogenic shock (CS) comes from observational studies, with limited synthetic data available. We aimed to assess the association between advanced shock care models and short- and mid-term outcomes of CS patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO registration: CRD42024581904) were conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 Statement. We included observational studies of at least 25 adult CS patients managed with or without a Shock Team or related advanced shock care models. We searched Embase, Medline Ultimate, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 01.01.2016 to 13.08.2024. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Meta-analyses were performed with a random-effects model. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Nine studies with a total of 658,708 patients met the inclusion criteria. For medium-term mortality, follow-up ranged from 60 to 365 days. Treatment of patients within the included models was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.81, 95%CI: [0.74, 0.90], p<0.0001, I2=58%), lower intensive care unit mortality (OR: 0.58, 95%CI: [0.43, 0.78], p=0.0004, I2=45%), and lower medium-term mortality (HR: 0.59, 95%CI: [0.48, 0.72], p<0.00001, I2=0%). These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses, although clinical and methodological heterogeneity persisted.
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced shock care models may be associated with improved short- and mid-term outcomes in CS patients including lower in-hospital and medium-term mortality. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these results.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies (PROSPERO CRD42024581904); Nine studies with a total of 658,708 patients
appraisal.main_limitation: All included studies were observational and the abstract reports persistent clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of observational studies associated advanced shock care models, including shock teams, with lower mortality in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Treatment within the models was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.81, 95%CI: [0.74, 0.90], p<0.0001, I2=58%), lower intensive care unit mortality (OR: 0.58, 95%CI: [0.43, 0.78]) and lower medium-term mortality (HR: 0.59, 95%CI: [0.48, 0.72]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first pooled estimate for the systems-of-care question on shock teams, although confounding limits any causal reading.

title: Shock Teams May Improve Outcomes of Patients with Cardiogenic Shock (STOP-CS): a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract: Reduced nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability contributes to endothelial dysfunction and increases myocardial susceptibility to ischemic injury. In addition to NO, carbon monoxide (CO) functions as an important endogenous gasotransmitter that regulates vascular tone, mitochondrial respiration, and cellular defense mechanisms. Although NO- and CO-related interventions activate distinct proximal signaling pathways, it remains unclear whether they converge on a common anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanism under conditions of chronic NO deficiency. We therefore investigated cardioprotective signaling induced by the NO donor Nicorandil and the CO-releasing molecule CORM-3 in L-NAME-induced hypertensive rats subjected to myocardial infarction. Male Wistar Kyoto rats received L-NAME (20 mg/kg/day) for four weeks to induce chronic NO-deficient hypertension. Myocardial infarction was induced by left coronary artery occlusion followed by reperfusion. Before reperfusion, Nicorandil or CORM-3 was administered intramyocardially. Seven days later, blood pressure, infarct size, collagen deposition, inflammatory markers, NO synthase (NOS) activity, protein expression of eNOS, iNOS, NF-κB, Nrf2, HO-1, and antioxidant enzymes were assessed. Both Nicorandil and CORM-3 significantly reduced myocardial infarct size and attenuated fibrotic collagen deposition compared with untreated infarcted animals. Furthermore, both treatments reduced circulating TNF-α and IL-6, suppressed myocardial NF-κB activation, decreased iNOS expression, and restored antioxidant enzyme levels. However, the interventions exhibited distinct upstream molecular signatures. Nicorandil preferentially enhanced NO-related signaling, increased total NOS activity and eNOS expression, whereas CORM-3 produced stronger activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Nicorandil and CORM-3 produce a common structural, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory cardioprotective phenotype associated with distinct molecular signaling profiles under conditions of chronic NO deficiency.
title: Convergent cardioprotection through distinct nitric oxide and carbon monoxide signaling pathways after myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: New-onset conduction disturbances (CDs) remain the most frequent and clinically relevant complications after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The anatomical mechanisms underlying conduction injury are not fully understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between inferoseptal recess (ISR) anatomy and post-TAVR conduction disturbances, and to validate its predictive value using an interpretable machine learning algorithm.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 307 patients who underwent TAVR between 2017 and 2024. Pre-procedural computed tomography (CT) was used to quantify ISR morphology and aortic root anatomy. The primary endpoint was new-onset CDs (bundle branch block, high-grade atrioventricular block, or need for permanent pacemaker implantation). Machine learning algorithms were applied to integrate CT-derived anatomical and clinical variables and to validate the predictive value of ISR metrics, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) applied for interpretability.
RESULTS: CDs occurred in 57 of 307 patients (18.6%). Wider WOISR (per 1-mm increment) was independently associated with reduced risk of CDs (OR: 0.76, 95% CI 0.66-0.89; P<0.001), along with counter-clockwise aortic root rotation (OR: 0.91, [95% CI, 0.87-0.95]; P<0.001), smaller ΔMSID (OR: 0.83, [95% CI, 0.76-0.91]; P<0.001), larger left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (P=0.004), with pre-existing right bundle-branch block (P<0.001). Among ML models, the RF model achieved an AUC of 0.91 in the temporal holdout cohort and showed favorable net benefit across a range of clinically relevant threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified non-coronary sinus calcification score, LVEDD, and WOISR as dominant contributors to model output.
CONCLUSIONS: WOISR (≤4 mm) is an anatomical predictor of CDs following TAVR. WOISR was independently associated with post-TAVR conduction disturbances and provided incremental discriminatory information beyond established clinical predictors. These findings support further prospective evaluation of ISR morphology as a complementary component of CT-based conduction-risk assessment before and after TAVR.
journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese
title: Inferoseptal Recess Anatomy Predicts Conduction Disturbances After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract: Right heart failure (RHF), both acute and chronic is increasingly recognized as a distinct and clinically significant syndrome across the spectrum of cardiovascular disease. Estimates suggest RHF complicates >25-30% of hospitalizations for acute decompensated HF and is nearly universal in advanced pulmonary hypertension (PH) (1) Despite recent diagnostic and therapeutic advancements, RHF remains associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and impaired quality of life. Addressing RHF requires dedicated strategies tailored to its pathophysiology, including early identification, risk stratification, and novel therapies. (2) While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the topic remain limited, there has been increasing emphasis on early recognition and management of RHF (especially in the setting of left ventricular [LV] failure). In addition, there is an expanding role for temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in acute RHF and percutaneous tricuspid interventions in chronic RHF. Yet, the field remains limited by its under-recognition, lack of standardized definitions, and limited therapeutic options, which underscore the urgent need for consensus and guidance.
title: HFSA Scientific Statement on Right Heart Failure.

abstract: Chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is associated with substantial ischemic risk, yet the optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after successful CTO-PCI remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing extended DAPT (>12 months) with short-term DAPT (≤12 months) following CTO-PCI. Four electronic biomedical databases were searched from inception to September 2026. Comparative studies evaluating adult patients undergoing successful CTO-PCI with drug-eluting stent implantation were eligible. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Three retrospective cohort studies including 3362 patients were identified, with 1761 receiving extended DAPT and 1601 receiving short-term DAPT. Extended DAPT was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared with short-term DAPT (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.55-0.84; P = 0.0004). There was no significant difference in all-cause death (RR 0.25; 95% CI 0.04-1.41; P = 0.116), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, major bleeding, or revascularization outcomes. However, extended DAPT was associated with a significantly higher risk of total bleeding (RR 2.34; 95% CI 1.31-4.20; P = 0.0043). Among patients undergoing successful CTO-PCI, extended DAPT was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events but increased total bleeding compared with DAPT ≤12 months.
title: Extended Versus Short Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Duration After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiac tamponade is an uncommon but potentially catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), particularly when caused by iatrogenic hemopericardium, with high mortality among patients requiring emergency cardiac surgery. We describe a structured minimally invasive subxiphoid protocol modification for immediate intraprocedural tamponade management and place this experience in the context of current evidence.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between January 2023 and April 2026, cardiac tamponade developed intra- or peri-procedurally in 4 consecutive patients among approximately 350 TAVI procedures at a single tertiary center. The protocol comprised immediate subxiphoid decompression; insertion of two 16 Fr radiopaque Redon drains, placed anteriorly and posteriorly, each connected to a separate Drainobag bottle sustaining high negative pressure; hermetic layered closure; mechanical ventilation under sedation after decompression for at least 12 hours and progressive drain removal after 72 hours.
RESULTS: All 4 patients achieved immediate hemodynamic recovery without conversion to emergency sternotomy. No hospital deaths or procedure-related complications occurred. No late pericardial reaccumulation, constrictive pericarditis or ventricular pseudoaneurysm occurred.
CONCLUSION: In this small single-center series, dual-drain subxiphoid drainage with continuous high-vacuum aspiration was feasible and associated with hemodynamic recovery without emergency sternotomy in 4 selected TAVI patients. Larger comparative studies are required before broader use can be recommended. These observations should be considered hypothesis-generating.Clinical ImpactCardiac tamponade during TAVI requires rapid, mechanism-directed treatment. Image-guided pericardiocentesis remains the usual first drainage step, whereas ongoing iatrogenic hemopericardium or failure to stabilize requires immediate surgical escalation. In 4 carefully selected patients, dual-drain subxiphoid decompression with continuous high-vacuum aspiration restored hemodynamic stability without emergency sternotomy. These findings support its feasibility as a rescue option in carefully selected cases, while larger comparative studies are needed to define its hemostatic effectiveness and its role relative to conventional drainage. Persistent bleeding or recurrent hemodynamic instability should prompt surgical conversion.
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
title: Minimally Invasive Management of Cardiac Tamponade Complicating Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Technical Note.
Letter: Commentary on "CALLY May Refine Risk Prediction in Older Adults Acute Coronary Syndrome".
Letter: Clarifying the Incremental Prognostic Value of the CALLY Index in Elderly Acute Coronary Syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), which integrates inflammation, lipid metabolism, and glucose metabolism, has emerged as a composite biomarker for metabolic and cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to evaluate the association between CTI and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebral events (MACCEs) in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and to determine whether CTI adds prognostic information beyond conventional clinical variables and its individual components.
METHODS: This single-center observational cohort study included 5,472 patients with ACS and T2DM treated at the Cardiovascular Centre of Beijing Friendship Hospital from January 2013 to January 2021. CTI was calculated as 0.412 × ln(C-reactive protein [mg/L]) + ln(triglyceride [mg/dL] × fasting plasma glucose [mg/dL]/2). The primary endpoint was MACCEs, defined as a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and ischemia-driven revascularization. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression were supplemented by comparisons of CTI, the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, and ln(CRP), Harrell C-index, time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), calibration, decision curve analysis, ACS-subtype analyses, multiple imputation, proportional-hazards diagnostics, landmark analyses, and competing-risk analyses.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 3.04 (IQR: 1.07-5.02) years, 1,075 MACCEs occurred. In univariable Cox analysis, each 1-unit increase in CTI was associated with a higher risk of MACCEs (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.32; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, CTI remained independently associated with MACCEs (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.17-1.36; P < 0.001). When analyzed by quartiles, compared with Q1, the multivariable-adjusted HRs (95% CIs) were 1.09 (0.90-1.33) for Q2, 1.44 (1.19-1.74) for Q3, and 1.75 (1.43-2.14) for Q4. Per 1-SD increase, the adjusted HRs were 1.27 (1.18-1.36) for CTI, 1.10 (1.02-1.17) for TyG, and 1.29 (1.20-1.39) for ln(CRP). Adding CTI to the clinical model increased the C-index from 0.688 to 0.694 and the 3-year AUC from 0.727 to 0.737, with an NRI of 0.293 and an IDI of 0.009. The corresponding ln(CRP) model achieved a C-index of 0.698 and a 3-year AUC of 0.744. Associations were consistent across UAP, NSTEMI, and STEMI (P for interaction = 0.59).
CONCLUSION: CTI was independently associated with an increased risk of MACCEs in patients with ACS and T2DM and provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond conventional clinical variables. However, its discriminatory performance was not clearly superior to ln(CRP) alone or to jointly modeled ln(CRP) and TyG. CTI should therefore be considered an adjunctive admission biomarker rather than a replacement for established clinical assessment.
title: Association of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index with adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome and type 2 diabetes: findings from an observational cohort study in China.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in cardiac arrest management, survival with favorable neurological outcomes remains limited. Physiological monitoring may complement standardized resuscitation by providing real-time information about circulatory effectiveness, reversible causes, and treatment responses. However, whether physiology-guided interventions improve patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the current evidence and clinical applicability of physiological monitoring during resuscitation, physiology-informed rescue strategies, and individualized post-cardiac arrest care.
MAIN BODY: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive arterial pressure monitoring, waveform capnography, and echocardiography provide complementary information about the circulation generated by chest compressions and potential mechanisms of resuscitation failure. Although observational and experimental studies support their physiological relevance, no adult diastolic pressure target or pressure-guided vasopressor strategy has been validated to improve survival or neurological recovery. Recent randomized trials of transesophageal echocardiography have demonstrated physiological or procedural effects without establishing clinical benefit. Among rescue strategies, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation has yielded inconsistent results across randomized trials, with potential benefits dependent on patient selection, intervention timing, and system capabilities. Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta has not improved clinical outcomes in randomized evaluation, while head-up resuscitation remains investigational. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, randomized trials have challenged the benefits of uniformly higher blood pressure and oxygenation targets, mild hypercapnia, and deeper or prolonged temperature control. Individualized approaches incorporating cerebral autoregulation, venous congestion, and cardiopulmonary physiology are physiologically appealing but lack prospective validation.
CONCLUSION: Physiological assessment may complement established resuscitation algorithms by refining clinical decisions during and after cardiac arrest. However, improvements in physiological measurements should not be equated with improved patient outcomes. Future trials should determine whether predefined, physiology-guided treatment strategies improve survival and neurological recovery.
title: Physiological monitoring and physiology-informed strategies in cardiac arrest: current evidence and clinical translation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natriuretic peptides (NPs) and copeptin are established cardiovascular biomarkers which can partly affect human metabolism. However, impact of human metabolism on their postprandial regulation in high-risk patients remains insufficiently understood. We aimed to characterize meal-induced changes in MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, and copeptin and to assess how these dynamics relate to acute cardiovascular (CV) events, type 2 diabetes (T2D) and insulin resistance (IR).
METHODS: Within the BeLOVE cohort, a subset of 373 participants with acute coronary syndrome, stroke or very high chronic CV risk underwent standardized study-specific mixed-meal testing approximately 3 months after the acute event or 1 month after enrollment for the chronic high-risk group. Fasting and 120-min postprandial concentrations of MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, copeptin, insulin and glucose were assessed. Structural equation models were used to evaluate direct and indirect associations of acute CV events, T2D, and IR (HOMA-IR) with fasting levels and postprandial changes, adjusted for age, sex and BMI.
RESULTS: MR-proANP showed the most pronounced meal-induced suppression. NT-proBNP demonstrated only minor and inconsistent postprandial changes. For all peptides, fasting concentrations were the main determinant of their postprandial changes. A recent acute CV event was associated with higher fasting NP levels (MR-proANP: standardized β = 0.22 [0.09; 0.34]; NT-proBNP: β = 0.28 [0.15; 0.41]), but not substantially with their postprandial changes after accounting for their baseline levels. T2D showed no consistent association with fasting or postprandial NP responses. In contrast, higher HOMA-IR was associated with lower fasting MR-proANP (β=-0.19 [-0.30; -0.07]) and a stronger postprandial decline (β=-0.18 [-0.33; -0.04]). Similarly, higher HOMA-IR was linked to lower fasting NT-proBNP (β=-0.15 [-0.28; -0.03]) but showed no clear association to its postprandial change. Copeptin dynamics were largely independent of acute CV disease and metabolic status.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients after a recent ACS or stroke, postprandial MR-proANP dynamics are linked to insulin resistance, rather than diabetes status. In contrast, the limited postprandial variability of NT-proBNP and the largely fasting-related changes of copeptin make these markers less suited for capturing short-term metabolic responses. Together, these findings highlight the value of postprandial phenotyping for understanding cardiometabolic regulation and support further evaluation of MR-proANP as a potential biomarker in future prospective studies with cardiovascular outcomes across subjects with and without acute CV event.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was approved by the institutional ethics committee (EA1/066/17) and registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00016852).
title: Meal-induced changes in cardiometabolic peptides in the context of acute cardiovascular diseases and glucose metabolism.

abstract: As life expectancy in patients with congenital heart disease continues to increase, coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndromes are encountered more and more in this population, with a higher level of complexity, especially in the acute setting. We present a case of acute thrombotic occlusion of the left circumflex coronary artery in a patient with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. This case highlights several challenges from ECG and computed tomography interpretation to coronary angiography and PCI performance. Key pre-procedural and procedural steps are revised to guide toward prompt and successful revascularization.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patient With Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries-Wiring Towards the Unknown.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study synthesized published meta-analyses to assess the quality, bias, and strength of evidence regarding mortality risk factors in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).
METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane database were used to search the literature up to May 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses investigating AF-related mortality risk factors. AMSTAR tool was used to assess methodological quality and GRADE was used to evaluate evidence certainty.
RESULTS: A total of 216 risk factors were identified. Among them, 86 showed significant associations with mortality, while 130 did not. Based on GRADE ratings, 11 were high-quality significant factors, and 9 were of moderate-quality. Factors linked to increased mortality included certain medications (digoxin, dronedarone, sotalol; warfarin/VKA vs. NOAC was associated with higher mortality), comorbidities (cancer, COPD, diabetes, anemia, frailty, LVH, peripheral artery disease), demographic characteristics (older age, smoking, BMI <18.5, Latin American ethnicity), and AF subtype (persistent or non-paroxysmal). In contrast, reduced mortality was associated with NOAC or DOAC use, higher BMI (25-30 or ≥30), surgical interventions (catheter ablation, LAAC/LAAO), other medications (SGLT2 inhibitors, statins), and early rhythm control.
CONCLUSION: This review highlights key factors associated with mortality in AF. Increased risk was observed with warfarin/VKA use (vs. NOAC), certain antiarrhythmic drugs, comorbidities, low BMI, older age, smoking, and non-paroxysmal AF. In contrast, NOAC use, surgical interventions, high BMI, statin and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, and early rhythm-control strategies were linked to reduced mortality risk.Systematic Review Registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024533372, PROSPERO CRD42024533372.
title: Factors associated with mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory markers with the formation of microvascular obstruction (MVO) and their exploratory predictive performance in STEMI patients after PCI.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted based on a prospective cohort, which included the patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. All patients underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging within 7 days post-surgery, and were classified into MVO and non-MVO groups based on the examination results. Emergency and first post-PCI routine blood test and other clinical data were collected from patients, and various cell ratios were calculated, including the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI). The risk factors for MVO were evaluated by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 311 patients with STEMI were included. Among them, 198 developed MVO and the other 113 were MVO free. After adjustment for clinical covariates, higher post-PCI WBC, NEU, SIRI and NLR and greater peri-PCI eosinophil decline were associated with MVO. In the correlation-reduced joint analysis, post-PCI SIRI retained the most robust association.
CONCLUSION: Postoperative WBC, NEU, SIRI, NLR, ΔEOS, ΔEOS% showed exploratory predictive performance for the formation of MVO after PCI in STEMI patients, and post-PCI SIRI showed the most robust association after accounting for biomarker intercorrelation.
title: Exploratory predictive value of novel inflammatory biomarkers for microvascular obstruction after emergency revascularization in STEMI patients.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) remain common after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) despite advances in stent technology and secondary-prevention pharmacotherapy. Blood-based biomarkers have been proposed as tools for individualised risk stratification, but reported prognostic associations vary widely across studies.
OBJECTIVES: This review addressed two prespecified and analytically separate questions. The primary (prognostic) question was: among adults undergoing PCI, are elevated concentrations of blood-based biomarkers associated with subsequent MACE and mortality? The secondary (treatment-effect) question was: among adults undergoing PCI, do specified pharmacotherapeutic strategies reduce MACE? The two questions were addressed using separate eligibility criteria, separate effect measures, separate risk-of-bias instruments and separate syntheses; prognostic associations and treatment effects were not pooled together.
METHODS: MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase (via Ovid), Web of Science Core Collection and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from 1 January 2010 to 28 February 2025, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, the WHO ICTRP, OpenGrey and backward and forward citation searching. Records were restricted to English-language reports. Eligible studies for the primary question enrolled adults (≥18 years) undergoing PCI, measured a blood-based biomarker at a defined time point relative to the index procedure, and reported MACE or mortality with an extractable adjusted or unadjusted effect estimate. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS for prognostic factor studies, supported by ROBINS-I, Cochrane RoB 2.0 and AMSTAR 2 as appropriate to design. Random-effects meta-analysis was to use the restricted maximum likelihood estimator for between-study variance with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, with DerSimonian-Laird estimates as a sensitivity analysis. No analyte met the minimum study count required to trigger pooling (Section 3.5), so no meta-analysis was performed. Pooling was restricted to biomarker-outcome pairs with at least three methodologically comparable primary studies. Prediction intervals accompany every pooled estimate derived from five or more studies. Certainty of evidence was rated using a GRADE framework adapted for prognostic factor reviews.
RESULTS: Forty-two studies were included, comprising 41 primary reports and one systematic review retained for cross-referencing only, together contributing 37,524 participants to the prognostic synthesis. The evidence base was dispersed across 42 distinct analytes: 38 were evaluated in a single study and four in two studies, so no analyte reached the minimum of three studies prespecified for quantitative pooling. Meta-analysis was therefore not undertaken, and the evidence is reported as a structured narrative synthesis. Elevated concentrations of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, C-reactive protein and its high-sensitivity assay, interleukin-6, the systemic immune-inflammation index and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were each reported as associated with increased risk of MACE, consistently in direction but on the basis of one or two studies per analyte. Evidence for microRNA-497-5p and other emerging analytes rested on single small studies and is reported as preliminary. Thirteen studies were rated at high overall risk of bias, seventeen at moderate and twelve at low. Certainty was very low for the 38 single-study analytes and low for the remainder. Treatment-effect evidence identified under the secondary question is reported separately and was not combined with the prognostic synthesis.
CONCLUSIONS: Blood-based biomarkers show consistent directional associations with MACE after PCI, but the evidence is too dispersed for quantitative synthesis: no analyte was evaluated in more than two of the included studies. Heterogeneity in assay platform, sampling time, cut-off derivation and endpoint definition compounds this dispersion. These findings support further evaluation of a small number of candidate markers in adequately powered cohorts with standardised measurement, not the incorporation of any biomarker into routine post-PCI decision-making. No included study randomised patients on the basis of a biomarker result, so no biomarker-guided treatment recommendation can be made.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251076074, PROSPERO CRD420251076074.
title: Blood-based biomarkers and major adverse cardiac events after percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review with narrative synthesis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of intracardiac thrombus varies by cardiac chamber, yet large-scale comparative long-term outcome data across all four chambers remain limited.
METHODS: In this retrospective propensity-matched cohort study using the Chang Gung Research Database (2001-2022), we identified 1,541 patients in the final propensity-matched analytic cohorts with echocardiographically confirmed single-chamber intracardiac thrombus [left atrial (LA) n = 619, left ventricular (LV) n = 774, right atrial (RA) n = 125, right ventricular (RV) n = 23]. Patients were 1:4 matched with controls without thrombus for demographics, comorbidities, and medications. Primary outcomes included ischemic stroke/systemic embolism, pulmonary embolism, myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiac death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of the above). Follow-up continued until the first event, death, or December 31, 2022.
FINDINGS: Compared with matched controls, LA thrombus was associated with increased risks of ischemic stroke/systemic embolism (hazard ratio, HR = 1.85), heart failure (HR = 1.30), cardiac death (HR = 2.02), and MACE (HR = 1.61). LV thrombus was associated with increased risks of ischemic stroke/systemic embolism (HR = 1.38), myocardial infarction (HR = 1.58), heart failure (HR = 1.40), cardiac death (HR = 1.32), and MACE (HR = 1.36). RA thrombus was associated with pulmonary embolism (HR = 4.63), heart failure (HR = 1.70), and MACE (HR = 1.63), whereas cardiac death was not significantly increased (HR = 1.96). RV thrombus was rare and showed no significant associations with any outcome. Left atrial appendage thrombus did not confer additional risk compared with non-appendage LA thrombus.
CONCLUSIONS: The prognostic impact of intracardiac thrombus is strongly location-dependent. LV and LA thrombi carried the broadest cardiovascular risks, RA thrombus was disproportionately linked to pulmonary embolism and mortality, and RV thrombus had limited long-term impact. These findings support chamber-specific risk stratification and management strategies for patients with echocardiography-detected intracardiac thrombus.
title: Chamber-specific long-term prognosis of intracardiac thrombus: a 21-year propensity-matched cohort study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The CHAGALL (CHordArt System Study for the Treatment of Mitral ReGurgitAtion due to Leaflet ProLapse or fLail) study is a prospective, first-in-human early feasibility study evaluating the technical feasibility, the long-term safety, and device durability of a novel chordal replacement system for the treatment of primary degenerative mitral regurgitation.
METHODS: Five patients with symptomatic severe primary degenerative mitral regurgitation attributable to isolated central posterior leaflet prolapse or flail underwent surgical implantation of the ChordArt chordal replacement system through a left atrial approach under cardiopulmonary bypass combined with ring annuloplasty. Clinical and transthoracic echocardiographic follow-up was prospectively performed at discharge and through 60 months.
RESULTS: Technical device success was achieved in all patients. Mitral regurgitation was reduced to none or trace immediately after implantation and remained stable throughout the 5-year follow-up. No device-related major adverse events, structural device failure, implant dislodgement, chordal rupture, reoperation, or rehospitalization occurred. Reverse cardiac remodeling was observed, including reduction in left ventricular end-diastolic diameter and left atrial volume, whereas left ventricular function remained preserved during long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical implantation of the ChordArt chordal replacement system was simple to perform and demonstrated excellent long-term technical durability and sustained clinical performance over 5 years. These findings support further clinical evaluation of this technology and the ongoing development of a fully transcatheter transseptal delivery platform.
title: Five-year outcomes of chordal replacement therapy for primary mitral regurgitation: The CHAGALL (CHordArt System Study for the Treatment of Mitral ReGurgitAtion due to Leaflet ProLapse or fLail) study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, underscoring an urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Panax ginseng C. A. Meyer, a cornerstone herb in traditional medicine with exceptional pharmacological value, is widely regarded as the "King of Herbs". Ginsenoside Rg1 (G-Rg1), one of the principal bioactive protopanaxatriol-type saponins isolated from Panax ginseng C. A. Meyer, exhibits well-documented cardioprotective effects. However, a systematic and quantitative synthesis of its efficacy and mechanisms in preclinical IHD models is still lacking.
METHODS: In this study, we conducted a preclinical systematic review to evaluate the efficacy of G-Rg1 in animal models of IHD and to synthesize current evidence on its underlying mechanisms. A search of four major biomedical databases from inception to May 2026 identified nine eligible studies (236 animals). Methodological quality, rigorously assessed using the 9-item CAMARADES checklist, yielded scores of 4 to 6, indicating moderate overall quality. Data were pooled and analyzed using RevMan 5.3.
RESULTS: Meta-analysis showed that G-Rg1 administration reduced myocardial infarct size and decreased plasma levels of cardiac injury biomarkers (creatine kinase-MB [CK-MB] and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP]), and improved key functional parameters. One study reported that G-Rg1 attenuated the inducibility of ventricular tachyarrhythmias following ischemia-reperfusion injury. Mechanistically, the cardioprotective effects of G-Rg1 were consistently associated with anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic and mitochondrial protection pathways.
CONCLUSION: These preclinical findings support future translational research and provide a basis for subsequent clinical studies on G-Rg1 in IHD.
title: Ginsenoside Rg1 for ischemic heart disease injury: preclinical evidence and possible mechanisms.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is common after mitral valve (MV) repair or replacement in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR). This study aims to evaluate the trajectory of postoperative LVEF reduction after MV surgery and determine whether this change in LVEF is associated with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This is a retrospective study of 625 patients who underwent MV surgery for moderate/severe MR between 2015 and 2023. Patients with aortic valve pathology, concomitant aortic procedures, endocarditis, and previous MV operations were excluded. Patients were divided into 4 quartiles on the basis of pre- and postoperative percent difference in LVEF. In-hospital outcomes and long-term mortality using Kaplan-Meier analysis were compared between groups. Cubic spline adjusted for preoperative LVEF was used to determine the impact of percent LVEF difference on mortality. Spaghetti plots depicted the trajectory in LVEF over a 2-year follow-up period.
RESULTS: Patients were divided into percent LVEF reduction quartiles as follows: severely reduced (159 [25.4%], greater than -19%), moderately reduced (157 [25.1%], between -19% and -8%), stable (171 [27.4%], between -7% and +4%), and increased (138 [22.1%], greater than a +4%). Baseline characteristics were similar. There was no difference in the percent of patients undergoing MV repair versus replacement across LVEF reduction groups (P = .55). Postoperative outcomes were similar between groups, including reoperation for bleeding, stroke, and atrial fibrillation. Long-term survival probability over 7 years was similar between all 4 groups (P = .35). There was no significant change in hazards ratio for long-term mortality across range of LVEF differences. Patients with severely or moderately reduced LVEF postoperatively remained with a depressed LVEF during the 2-year follow-up period, whereas patients with the same or increased postoperative LVEF returned to baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Reduction in LVEF is common after MV repair or replacement with effects persisting after 2 years. Changes in LVEF after MV operation do not appear to affect clinical outcomes and may by itself not accurately reflect myocardial dysfunction related to MR and subsequent intervention.
keywords: reduction in LVEF after MV operation
title: Left ventricular ejection fraction decline shortly after mitral valve operation and associated survival.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) carries mortality risk comparable to untreated severe aortic stenosis, yet specialist referral rates remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We analyzed 1000 patients with severe TR from CardioCare registry from a single center in Georgia. The primary outcome was the absence of structural heart disease (SHD) specialist evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of referral failure adjusted for age, heart failure (HF), kidney and liver disease, symptoms, right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), and ejection fraction, with an extended model adding coronary artery disease, conduction delay, and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III-IV. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses assessed survival by evaluation status and clinical subgroup.
RESULTS: Only 328 patients (32.8%) underwent SHD evaluation despite symptoms (86.4%), HF (86.5%), kidney disease (65.1%), and liver disease (32.0%). HF was the strongest referral predictor (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.36); NYHA class III-IV, coronary artery disease, and conduction delay were also independently associated, whereas kidney disease, liver disease, and symptoms were not, and higher RVSP paradoxically predicted lower referral (OR 1.02/mmHg; both p < 0.001). Only 13.2% of symptomatic patients without HF were evaluated, and those with combined HF, kidney, and liver disease had the highest mortality (22.4%) but no preferential referral. Survival was worse with HF, increasing organ burden, and RVSP ≥40 mmHg; these factors plus age remained independent mortality predictors on Cox analysis, though this association attenuated in sensitivity analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: More than two-thirds of patients with severe TR never reach an SHD specialist despite substantial clinical burden, highlighting the need for echocardiography-triggered referral pathways and quality metrics.
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
title: Marked Underreferral to Structural Heart Specialists in Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation Despite High Clinical Burden: An Adjusted Registry Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with pre-existing right bundle branch block (RBBB) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are at a high risk of complete heart block, often requiring prolonged temporary pacing. Conventional temporary pacing leads are associated with lead dislodgement, immobilization, and intensive care unit (ICU) monitoring. The objective of this study was to compare screw-in versus conventional temporary pacing leads after TAVR in patients with pre-existing RBBB.
METHODS: This multicenter observational study included consecutive patients with pre-existing RBBB undergoing TAVR between 2018 and 2024. Patients receiving left ventricular pacing or no postprocedural temporary pacing were excluded. Outcomes included procedural complications, ICU utilization, hospital stay, permanent pacemaker implantation, and 30-day clinical events.
RESULTS: Among 544 patients, 124 received a screw-in lead and 420 a conventional lead. Screw-in leads were associated with significantly lower ICU utilization after TAVR (23% vs. 99%, p < 0.001). Despite longer temporary pacing duration (2.4 ± 1.4 days vs. 1.2 ± 1.6 days, p < 0.001), lead dislodgement was infrequent and numerically lower with screw-in leads (0.8% vs. 3.3%). Rates of major vascular complications, bleeding, tamponade, and atrial fibrillation were similar between groups. At 30 days, permanent pacemaker implantation rates were comparable (50.0% vs. 46.2%; p = 0.455), whereas hospital stay was shorter with screw-in leads (5.2 ± 4.2 days vs. 7.4 ± 7.8 days, p < 0.001). Mortality and major adverse events were similar.
CONCLUSIONS: In TAVR recipients with pre-existing RBBB, screw-in temporary pacing leads were associated with reduced ICU utilization and shorter hospitalization without increasing complications or adverse outcomes, supporting their use for prolonged postprocedural monitoring.
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
title: Temporary Active Fixation Leads in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Patients With Baseline Right Bundle Branch Block.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The management of patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome with tricuspid regurgitation remains controversial. We evaluate risk factors for mortality/transplant/Fontan takedown in patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome with tricuspid regurgitation and the effect of tricuspid valve surgery on clinical trajectories.
METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed for all hypoplastic left heart syndrome primary surgical Norwood recipients at our center who had moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (2006-2023). Freedom from a primary outcome of combined mortality/transplant/Fontan takedown was compared between those who underwent tricuspid valve surgery (N = 30, 67%) and those who did not (N = 15, 33%; Cox regression, log-rank). Among those who developed tricuspid regurgitation anytime post-Norwood (N = 37), tricuspid valve repair efficacy was assessed (Wilcoxon signed-rank, McNemar's test). Cumulative incidence of recurrent tricuspid regurgitation and right ventricle dysfunction was estimated (Aalen-Johansen estimator, death/transplant as competing risks).
RESULTS: Patients with pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation experienced a mortality-dominated trajectory (5-year freedom from mortality 37.5%), whereas patients with post-Norwood/pre-Glenn tricuspid regurgitation experienced a transplant-dominated trajectory (5-year freedom from mortality 88.5%, composite outcome 55.9%). On univariable Cox regression, pre-Norwood right ventricle dysfunction (hazard ratio, 9.75, P < .001) was associated with the primary outcome; pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation tended toward association (hazard ratio, 2.40, P = .10). On multivariable analysis, pre-Norwood right ventricle dysfunction (hazard ratio, 12.79 [3.16-51.80], P < .001) and pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation (hazard ratio, 3.10 [1.03-9.31], P = .04) were both independently associated with the primary outcome. Among those with post-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation who underwent tricuspid valve surgery, tricuspid regurgitation severity decreased, with 43% achieving preserved freedom from moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation.
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-Norwood right ventricle dysfunction and pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation were found to be associated with the primary outcome. In those with post-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation, tricuspid valve repair reduced tricuspid regurgitation but was not associated with improved survival.
title: Risk factors and outcomes of tricuspid valve surgery in hypoplastic left heart syndrome patients with tricuspid regurgitation.
