abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.
title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite improvements in rescue strategies, postoperative cardiac arrest in adults undergoing cardiac surgery has not been examined in the contemporary era. This study assesses the incidence, outcomes, and predictors of survival in patients who had an in-hospital cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: Adult patients with cardiac arrest after open surgery from January 2012 to May 2019 at a single institution were studied. Patients were excluded if they underwent heart transplantation or left ventricular assist device implantation, experienced preoperative or intraoperative cardiac arrest, received preoperative or intraoperative temporary mechanical circulatory support, or were deemed as do not resuscitate or care was withdrawn before the arrest.
RESULTS: Of 9946 patients, 162 (1.6%) experienced a postoperative arrest with failure to rescue in 59 patients (36.4%). The etiology of cardiac arrest was cardiovascular in 101 patients (62.3%), respiratory in 27 patients (16.7%), metabolic in 15 patients (9.3%), other in 12 patients (7.4%), and unknown in 7 patients (4.3%). Thirteen patients (8.0%) were placed on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation postarrest with only 4 (30.8%) surviving to discharge. Patients were more likely to die in-hospital if they had postoperative, prearrest organ dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio, 7.08, 95% CI, 2.92-17.16).
CONCLUSIONS: Although the incidence of cardiac arrest was low, more than one-third of patients failed to be rescued. Prearrest major organ dysfunction portended a significantly worse prognosis. Early recognition of a nonthriving patient and rapid escalation of specialized care may be critical in successful rescue from cardiac arrest and aborting catastrophic outcomes.
title: Postoperative cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery: Can we improve our rescue rate?

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: For patients with end-stage ischemic cardiomyopathy undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), the indications for concomitant repair of moderate mitral regurgitation (MR) remain controversial. This study evaluated outcomes of concomitant mitral valve repair (MVr) for moderate ischemic MR in patients with advanced left ventricular (LV) remodeling and severely impaired LV function undergoing CABG.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 341 patients (mean age, 67 ± 9 years) with ischemic cardiomyopathy (LV ejection fraction, ≤40%) and less-than-severe MR who underwent CABG. Of these, 108 (32%) underwent concomitant MVr for clinically relevant moderate MR, and 233 (68%) underwent CABG alone for mild or absent MR. All patients had a prior myocardial infarction. The primary end point was overall survival. Secondary end points included postoperative changes in MR grade and LV function at 1 year. Median follow-up was 4.5 years (interquartile range, 2.4-7.3 years).
RESULTS: Despite higher preoperative surgical risk in the CABG + MVr group (European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II score, 6.7% vs 2.9%; P < .001), 30-day mortality did not differ between groups (1.9% vs 2.1%; P = .88). Five-year overall survival was 73% versus 77% (log-rank P = .25). At 1 year, the CABG + MVr group demonstrated greater LV reverse remodeling (median LV end-diastolic volume index reduction: -26% vs -19%; P = .001), higher LV ejection fraction (46 ± 13% vs 42 ± 12%; P = .044), and a lower prevalence of significant MR (6% vs 13%; P = .032).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with advanced ischemic cardiomyopathy and moderate MR, concomitant MVr can be performed with acceptable operative risk and promotes superior LV reverse remodeling. Long-term survival was comparable to patients with nonsignificant MR who did not require mitral intervention, suggesting that targeted mitral repair may normalize the adverse prognostic influence of moderate ischemic MR.
title: Mitral repair for moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation in patients with end-stage ischemic cardiomyopathy.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare long-term outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 70 to 89 years with aortic stenosis (AS).
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 1100 patients who underwent primary TAVR (n = 599) or SAVR (n = 501) between 2008 and 2023 were included. An overlap-weighted propensity-score analysis was conducted using 36 baseline variables, including age, procedural year, frailty scale, Society of Thoracic Surgeons risk score, New York Heart Association class, history of coronary artery and cerebrovascular disease, and AS severity. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality or cerebrovascular events.
RESULTS: During long-term follow-up, the composite end point occurred more frequently after TAVR than after SAVR. In the overlap-weighted analysis, TAVR was associated with a greater risk of the composite outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 1.8; 95% CI, 1.1-3.0; P = .024), with Kaplan-Meier curves diverging early and remaining separated. All-cause mortality did not differ between the groups (HR, 1.2; 95% CI, 0.7-2.1; P = .426); however, cerebrovascular events occurred predominantly after TAVR and remained significantly more frequent after overlap weighting (HR, 15; 95% CI, 2.8-89; P = .002).
CONCLUSIONS: In the overlap-weighted population of patients aged 70 to 89 years with AS, SAVR and TAVR were associated with comparable all-cause mortality; however, cerebrovascular events occurred more frequently after TAVR.
title: Long-term outcomes of transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in patients aged 70 years and older: An overlap-weighted analysis.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) is a sensitive biomarker of myocardial injury. We hypothesized that cTnI measured in pericardial drainage fluid (PCF), which reflects the cardiac microenvironment, may enhance risk stratification for postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after coronary artery bypass grafting.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 114 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting were enrolled. The primary end point was new-onset POAF within 7 days postoperatively. Blood and PCF cTnI at 6 hours postoperatively were measured. Variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and were then incorporated into multivariable logistic regression to construct a predictive model. A simplified risk score (CALT score) was developed. Model performance was compared with existing POAF tools, including the POAF score, CHA2DS2-VASc, and the atrial fibrillation risk index.
RESULTS: POAF occurred in 30.7% of the cohort. Postoperative 6-hour PCF-cTnI was an independent predictor of POAF (odds ratio, 5.502; 95% CI, 1.887-16.045; P = .002) and significantly enhanced continuous net reclassification improvement (0.562; 95% CI, 0.189-0.921; P = .002). The CALT score comprised left circumflex artery lesions, left atrial diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, postoperative 0-hour serum calcium, and postoperative 6-hour PCF-cTnI. The PCF-cTnI-based model demonstrated good discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.821), with favorable calibration and clinical utility. Compared with commonly used risk scores, the CALT score exhibited superior discrimination and calibration.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides novel evidence that PCF-cTnI is a strong predictor of POAF. The CALT score, integrating PCF-cTnI with clinical factors, provided superior predictive performance by capturing both the vulnerable atrial substrate and localized myocardial injury.
title: Pericardial fluid cardiac troponin I predicts postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Anticoagulation during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) remains challenging. Direct thrombin inhibitors such as argatroban are increasingly proposed as alternatives to unfractionated heparin (UFH). We sought to characterize the dose titration and monitoring reliability of argatroban compared with UFH in adult patients who received ECMO.
METHODS: This prespecified subanalysis of a randomized controlled pilot trial (2021-2024) included 40 adults on venovenous or venoarterial ECMO randomized to argatroban (target diluted thrombin time 0.6-0.8 μg/mL; n = 20) or UFH (target anti-factor Xa 0.2-0.3 IU/mL; n = 20). The primary outcome was the pooled proportion of measurements within the therapeutic target range. Secondary outcomes included dose requirements, time to target, dose-assay correlations, and platelet count trajectories.
RESULTS: Patients who were treated with argatroban achieved therapeutic targets significantly less often than those receiving UFH (38% vs 51% of pooled active measurements; P < .001). The median argatroban dose required to reach the initial target was 0.40 μg/kg/min (interquartile range, 0.34-0.49). Correlations between anticoagulant dose and monitored effect were weak-to-moderate for both agents (repeated measures correlation coefficient = 0.29 for argatroban vs diluted thrombin time, and repeated measures correlation coefficient = 0.31 for UFH vs anti-Xa). Both groups experienced a comparable decrease in platelet counts.
CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating subanalysis, patients receiving argatroban achieved therapeutic targets less reliably than those receiving UFH. However, this variability likely reflects challenges in dosing strategy optimization and differing target stringencies rather than intrinsic pharmacokinetic instability of the drug.
title: Challenges in monitoring and titration of argatroban versus unfractionated heparin in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation, the influence of concomitant mitral valve (MV) intervention at the time of revascularization on late survival remains unclear. The purpose of this study was to compare the lifetime survival of patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation who underwent revascularization alone versus concomitant MV repair or replacement.
METHODS: Retrospective review was performed for 776 consecutive patients, ages 65 years and older with coronary artery disease and moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation who underwent isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (n = 372), CABG with MV repair (n = 131, CABG + MV repair), or CABG with MV replacement (n = 273, CABG + MV replacement) from 1976 to 2005. Propensity score matching, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox regression were used to compare perioperative and long-term survival. Cross-sectional follow-up utilized the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Death Index as well as government and genealogical internet sites, publicly available online obituaries, and death notices. Follow up was 98% complete.
RESULTS: The mean age of the cohort was 74.1 ± 5.8 years with 42.4% female patients. Preoperatively, 54.5% had prior myocardial infarction, 47.7% had a history of congestive heart failure, and 69.1% had an abnormal ejection fraction. Matched patients undergoing CABG or CABG + MV repair had similar incidence of major perioperative morbidity (29.0% vs 22.1%; P = .202) and operative mortality (8.4% vs 6.1%; P = .475). Late survival was similar between groups (P = .630). Among matched patients undergoing CABG versus CABG + MV replacement, those undergoing concomitant replacement had significantly increased perioperative major morbidity (35.2% vs 20.9%; P < .001) and operative mortality (16.9% vs 7.7%; P < .001). CABG + MV replacement patients experienced an increased risk of late mortality (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.01-1.49; P = .035), compared with those undergoing isolated CABG.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing surgical revascularization, concomitant MV repair did not demonstrate a clear late survival benefit over isolated CABG, whereas concomitant MV replacement was associated with increased early and late mortality risk.
title: Influence of concomitant mitral valve intervention on late survival in patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing surgical revascularization.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mechanical circulatory support strategies for cardiogenic shock have traditionally relied on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. However, newer high-flow ventricular support devices such as the Impella 5.5 device, capable of providing effective circulatory support, ventricular unloading, and early mobilization with fewer device-related complications, have begun to challenge the systematic use of an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-first approach. The clinical evolution of patients treated with the Impella 5.5 device and the impact of different support trajectories remain poorly characterized. We describe the clinical evolution of patients treated with the Impella 5.5 device according to initial support trajectory, distinguishing primary implantation from transition after venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
METHODS: This multicenter observational study included 114 consecutive patients with advanced heart failure or cardiogenic shock who underwent Impella 5.5 implantation in Spanish heart transplant centers. Patients were classified according to initial support trajectory: primary Impella 5.5 implantation (n = 72) or initial venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support followed by transition to Impella 5.5 (venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation to Impella 5.5 transition, n = 42). Baseline characteristics, clinical trajectories, complications, and in-hospital outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: All patients ultimately received Impella 5.5 device support. In-hospital mortality was 27.8% in the primary Impella group and 69.0% in the extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-Impella group (P < .001), with an overall mortality of 43.0%. Heart transplantation as definitive therapy was achieved in 76.4% and 31.0% of patients, respectively (P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: In transplant-oriented centers, outcomes among patients supported with the Impella 5.5 device appear to differ according to support trajectory. Primary implantation was associated with lower mortality and greater access to heart transplantation than transition from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation to the Impella 5.5 device.
title: Clinical outcomes of primary Impella 5.5 versus transition from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in cardiogenic shock: A Spanish multicenter cohort.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: New onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) occurs in approximately 25% to 40% of patients undergoing heart surgery and is associated with increased perioperative morbidity and mortality. We evaluated the safety and exploratory efficacy of amiodarone-infused CardiaMend (Helios Cardio) biatrial patches for POAF prevention.
METHODS: A single-center pilot clinical trial enrolled 40 patients after applying inclusions and exclusion criteria, randomized in 1:1 fashion. Patients in the treatment group received the CardiaMend patch, a porous acellular matrix derived from fetal bovine dermis, infused with 70 mg amiodarone, placed on both atria, whereas the control group received standard care. The primary end point was safety, defined as major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Secondary end points included POAF, length of hospital stay, 30-day readmission, and POAF duration.
RESULTS: The 2 randomized groups had similar baseline characteristics. There were 2 major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events: 1 patient in the control group experienced an embolic stroke with full recovery before discharge, and 1 patient in the treatment group died from an acute abdominal event following intra-aortic balloon pump removal, deemed unrelated to the study device. The incidence of POAF (4 patients [20%] vs 8 patients [40%]; P = .30) and mean atrial fibrillation duration (2.5 ± 2.4 days vs 3.8 ± 4.1 days) were lower in the treatment group. Mean length of hospital stay was shorter in the treatment group (5.8 ± 1.2 days vs 9.3 ± 7.5 days; P = .07). At 30-day follow-up, Holter monitoring revealed no atrial fibrillation in the treatment group and 3 (15%) patients in the control group (P = .23), and readmission rates were also lower in the treatment group (5% vs 15%; P = .6).
CONCLUSIONS: This pilot randomized clinical trial showed that amiodarone-infused CardiaMend biatrial patches were safe, with no evidence of systemic amiodarone toxicity. Treatment with amiodarone-infused CardiaMend patches was associated with a clinically noticeable reduction in POAF, length of stay, and postdischarge atrial fibrillation.
title: Pilot safety and efficacy trial of amiodarone-infused biologic acellular biatrial patches to prevent new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether tricuspid leaflet multiplicity is associated with divergent postoperative hemodynamic trajectories after surgical repair.
METHODS: One hundred seventeen patients undergoing tricuspid valve surgery (January 2023 to March 2025) were prospectively enrolled, with leaflet morphology classified by intraoperative visualization and serial echocardiography over 1 year. The prespecified primary end point was a Doppler-derived tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) increase, defined as a 5-mm Hg-or-greater increase in TRPG from discharge to 1 year.
RESULTS: Among 100 patients with paired data, the primary end point occurred more frequently in the 4/5-leaflet group despite similar residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and discharge TRPG (48.5% vs 26.9%; odds ratio, 2.56; 95% CI, 1.07-6.12; P = .034); the age-adjusted association was borderline (aOR, 2.39; P = .054) and the within-group rise significant only in that cohort (P = .024). Severe-or-greater TR recurrence was rare (3.0% vs 0.0%; P = .327). Discharge tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion was lower in the 4/5-leaflet group (0.96 ± 0.36 vs 1.15 ± 0.36 cm; P = .010) but converged by 1 year (P = .585).
CONCLUSIONS: Tricuspid leaflet multiplicity was associated with a subphenotype showing preserved early TR reduction, lower discharge tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, and a greater 1-year frequency of Doppler-derived TRPG increase. Morphology-based stratification may refine postoperative surveillance pending external validation.
title: Tricuspid valve leaflet multiplicity and Doppler-derived right-heart hemodynamic trajectories after surgical repair.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: As the result of procedural complexity and risk of sternal wound infections, the adoption of multiarterial grafting (MAG) in coronary artery bypass surgery is lower in patients with diabetes despite a high prevalence of multivessel coronary artery disease. We conducted a randomized controlled study to evaluate the safety, graft patency at 1 year, and long-term survival at 5 years in MAG compared to single arterial grafting (SAG). This interim analysis reports 1-year mortality, morbidity, and graft patency.
METHODS: A total of 950 patients with diabetes and multivessel coronary artery disease were enrolled between February 2022 and January 2025 at 15 hospitals across 7 states in India and randomized to SAG (n = 477) or MAG (n = 473) groups in a multicenter, prospective, randomized trial. Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events and graft patency assessed by computed tomography coronary angiography at 1 year were analyzed (CTRI/2020/09/027692).
RESULTS: One-year composite outcome (SAG: n = 7 [1.5%] vs MAG: n = 7 [1.5%], P = .98) and mortality (SAG: n = 4 [0.8%] vs MAG: n = 6 [1.3%], P = .51) were low and comparable. Myocardial infarction occurred in 1 patient in each group. Stroke rates were comparable (SAG: n = 2 vs MAG: n = 1). One patient with SAG required repeat revascularization (percutaneous coronary intervention). Sternal wound infection occurred in 7 patients in the SAG group (1.5%) and 12 patients in the MAG group (2.6%) (P = .36). Sternal reconstruction was required in only 3 patients in the MAG group (0.6%). In total, 350 patients underwent protocol computed tomography graft angiography for graft assessment (SAG: n = 170, MAG: n = 180). Although overall graft patency did not differ between the SAG and MAG groups, vein graft patency was greater with MAG only after statistical adjustment for the effect of on-pump or off-pump status and involved coronary artery. Off-pump coronary artery bypass surgery, right internal mammary artery grafts, and right coronary artery and left circumflex coronary artery territory grafting were associated with lower overall graft patency.
CONCLUSIONS: Interim results from the trial demonstrate similar safety and 1-year clinical outcomes for SAG and MAG. We show superior venous graft patency with MAG after adjustment, but additional studies are required to validate this finding.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial in 15 hospitals in India; 950 patients with diabetes and multivessel coronary disease (SAG n = 477, MAG n = 473).
appraisal.main_limitation: Interim analysis at 1 year with very few events; the 5-year survival endpoint is not yet reported.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of multiarterial versus single arterial grafting in patients with diabetes, interim 1-year report.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year composite outcome (SAG: n = 7 [1.5%] vs MAG: n = 7 [1.5%], P = .98) and mortality (SAG: n = 4 [0.8%] vs MAG: n = 6 [1.3%], P = .51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is one of few randomised tests of multiarterial grafting in diabetes, a group in which uptake is low, and the 5-year survival result will inform surgical revascularisation guidance.

title: Prospective Randomized Evaluation of DIabetics for graft patency and outcomes following Coronary artery bypass grafting using one (single) versus two or More (mulTi) arterial grafts (PREDICT) trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The GLIDE score is a 5-point imaging-based tool to predict residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER). Lower residual TR is associated with better prognosis, but long-term associations between GLIDE score and outcomes are uncertain.
METHODS: We performed an analysis of a multinational registry of patients undergoing T-TEER for severe or greater TR from January 2017 to November 2022. GLIDE scores were assessed using preprocedural transesophageal echocardiography. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year, and the secondary endpoints included TR grade of moderate or less at 1 year.
RESULTS: In 336 patients (81 [interquartile range 77-84] years; 44.6% male, TRI-SCORE 5 [interquartile range 4-6]), survival and HFH follow-up at 1 year was available in 90.5%. One-year mortality was 15.8%. The GLIDE score was significantly associated with the combined primary endpoint (hazard ratio: 1.20; 95% CI 1.03-1.40; p = 0.019), even after adjustment for TRI-SCORE. Freedom from death or HFH was significantly higher among patients with GLIDE scores ≤1 compared to those ≥2 (p = 0.032). Of the 251 1-year survivors, follow-up echocardiography was available in 170 (68%). The GLIDE score predicted 1-year TR severity (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.73; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with moderate or less residual TR achieved in 80.6%, 54.9%, and 18.8% of patients with GLIDE scores of 0-1, 2-3, and ≥4, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The GLIDE score is associated with 1-year survival and HFH after T-TEER as well as ≤ moderate TR.
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
title: The GLIDE Score: One-Year Outcomes Following Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a serious complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), even with contemporary devices. The objective of the study was to evaluate the incidence, predictors, and prognosis of in-hospital stroke in patients undergoing TAVR with contemporary valve platforms.
METHODS: We analyzed 5123 patients from the multicenter OCEAN-TAVI registry who underwent TAVR with SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA, Evolut FX, or Navitor between May 2022 and December 2024. Stroke incidence across valve types was compared using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Predictors were assessed using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: In-hospital stroke occurred in 2.5% of patients. After IPTW adjustment, stroke incidence differed among valve types: 1.7% of patients treated with SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR), 4.5% with Evolut FX, and 2.4% with Navitor (p = 0.044). Disabling stroke was more frequent with Evolut FX (2.5%) compared with S3UR (0.4%) and Navitor (0.7%; p < 0.001). Self-expanding valve use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.64, 95% CI 1.67-4.16 for Evolut FX; aOR 2.37, 95% CI 1.35-4.18 for Navitor; both vs. S3UR), prior stroke (aOR 1.83, 95% CI 1.19-2.73), reduced renal function, and nontransfemoral access (aOR 2.11, 95% CI 1.29-3.45) were independently associated with in-hospital stroke. One-year survival was significantly lower among patients with stroke than among those without stroke (73.0% vs. 90.3%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital stroke remains an important complication after contemporary TAVR and is associated with worse clinical outcomes. Differences in stroke incidence across valve types were observed, highlighting the need for improved risk assessment.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort (OCEAN-TAVI); 5123 patients, inverse probability of treatment weighting.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison of valve types with residual confounding by anatomy and operator choice.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre Japanese registry of in-hospital stroke after TAVR with three contemporary valve platforms.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In-hospital stroke occurred in 2.5% of patients. After IPTW adjustment, stroke incidence differed among valve types: 1.7% of patients treated with SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR), 4.5% with Evolut FX, and 2.4% with Navitor (p = 0.044).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Differences in disabling stroke between current valve platforms are a signal relevant to device selection and cerebral protection research.

journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
title: Stroke After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Contemporary Valves: Insights From the OCEAN-TAVI Registry.

abstract:
AIMS: The expected clinical and functional trajectory after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with left ventricular dysfunction remains uncertain. Recent trials have highlighted substantial heterogeneity in both clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement, underscoring the need for improved post-PCI prognostic risk stratification in this high-risk population. This study aimed to develop machine learning models predicting clinical outcomes and LVEF improvement after PCI in patients with reduced LVEF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective single-centre study included adults undergoing PCI between 2004 and 2025 with baseline LVEF <45%. Two CatBoost models were developed using 53 routinely available pre- and intra-procedural predictors. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of death, myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or coronary artery bypass grafting. The secondary endpoint was an absolute LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), and enrichment analysis. The dataset included 3336 procedures from 2793 patients (median LVEF 35%). For the primary endpoint (n = 2152; event rate 37.5%), the model achieved an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.73-0.83) and a PR-AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.63-0.77), with event rates of 83.7% in the highest-risk decile and 9.3% in the lowest-risk decile. For LVEF improvement (n = 2551; 34.7% improved), performance was moderate (AUC 0.73), with enrichment to 76.9% in the highest-probability decile.
CONCLUSION: Machine learning models using routinely available patient and procedural data enabled meaningful prognostic stratification in patients with left ventricular dysfunction undergoing PCI, supporting individualized estimation of clinical and functional trajectories after revascularization.
title: Machine learning-based prediction of clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with reduced ejection fraction.

abstract: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a clinical syndrome in which integrated multimodality imaging is central to diagnosis, timely referral, procedural selection, and assessment of treatment success. This narrative state-of-the-art review focuses on the imaging information that changes decisions along the surgical pathway while positioning surgery within contemporary transcatheter practice. Transthoracic echocardiography remains the gateway examination; three-dimensional transoesophageal echocardiography refines leaflet and annular anatomy; cardiac magnetic resonance provides the most reproducible assessment of right ventricular volumes and function; and cardiac computed tomography defines annular geometry, adjacent structures, device leads, and access. We distinguish guideline-endorsed thresholds from observational or consensus-derived decision aids and link mechanism, annular dilatation, leaflet tethering, right ventricular reserve, pulmonary haemodynamics, and end-organ risk to the choice of repair, replacement, transcatheter therapy, or surveillance. Particular emphasis is placed on perioperative imaging: the effects of anaesthesia and loading conditions, accurate septolateral annular measurement, the definition of an acceptable post-bypass result, and the significance of central vs. eccentric residual jets. A dedicated section compares imaging requirements for transcatheter edge-to-edge repair and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement and summarizes post-procedural surveillance. The central message is that imaging does not replace clinical judgement; it provides the shared language through which the Heart Team selects the right intervention before irreversible right-heart and end-organ damage develops.
journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract

register_verdicts.note: A narrative imaging review of surgical decision-making in TR reports no new randomised or pooled trial data on transcatheter treatment effects.

title: Multimodality imaging for surgical decision-making in tricuspid regurgitation: from referral to intraoperative assessment.

abstract:
AIMS: Potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is the default antiplatelet strategy after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), though de-escalation to clopidogrel-based DAPT and abbreviated DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy are increasingly adopted to mitigate bleeding risk. However, their relative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Network meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials were performed to compare three guideline-endorsed strategies: (i) short-term potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based DAPT de-escalation to clopidogrel-based DAPT, (ii) abbreviated DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy, and (iii) standard 12-month potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based DAPT. The primary efficacy endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary efficacy endpoints included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, and stroke. The primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. The key net clinical endpoint was net adverse clinical events (NACE). PROSPERO (CRD420251144892) Seven randomized controlled trials involving 20 673 patients were included. Both the de-escalation and abbreviation strategies significantly reduced major bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.25-0.74, P = 0.002; and RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.33-0.58, P < 0.001, respectively) and NACE (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.70, P < 0.001; and RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.61-0.84, P < 0.001, respectively) without increasing MACE or other ischaemic outcomes. Indirect comparison indicated that de-escalation vs. abbreviation strategies demonstrated comparable MACE, NACE, and bleeding outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Following ACS, both de-escalation to clopidogrel-based DAPT and abbreviated DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy effectively reduce bleeding risk without compromising ischaemic protection. Given that the only available comparison between the two simplified strategies was indirect and showed comparable MACE and NACE outcomes, further research is warranted to determine the optimal individualized approach.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomised trials; 7 randomized controlled trials involving 20 673 patients (PROSPERO CRD420251144892).
appraisal.main_limitation: Only seven trials with heterogeneous designs and populations, which limits the indirect comparison between de-escalation and abbreviation.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of de-escalation, abbreviated and standard potent P2Y12 inhibitor DAPT after acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Both the de-escalation and abbreviation strategies significantly reduced major bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.25-0.74, P = 0.002; and RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.33-0.58, P < 0.001, respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The relative merit of de-escalation versus abbreviated DAPT is a live guideline question after ACS, and this synthesis bears on D8 evidence.

title: Comparative efficacy and safety of de-escalation, abbreviation, and standard potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based dual antiplatelet therapy strategies after acute coronary syndrome: a network meta-analysis.

abstract: Subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) is a rare but catastrophic complication in patients supported by biventricular assist devices (BiVADs). While mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is a life-saving bridge to transplantation, it introduces complex haemostatic challenges. We report the case of a 32-year-old male with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who developed cardiogenic shock. He was bridged from central veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (cVA-ECMO) to BiVAD support. His clinical course was complicated by suspected heparin-induced thrombocytopaenia (HIT), but further testing proved he was HIT negative. After weeks of haemodynamic stability and the commencement of physical rehabilitation for heart transplant listing, the patient suffered a sudden and profound neurological decline. Imaging revealed a diffuse, non-aneurysmal SAH occupying the basal cisterns. Neurosurgical intervention included placement of an external ventricular drain; however, he further declined, and support was withdrawn. This case highlights the challenging haemostatic landscape inherent to ventricular assist devices (VADs), where standard laboratory tests fail to reflect profound functional coagulopathy. Ultimately, this case serves as a critical reminder that BiVADs create a challenging haemostatic environment that demands more sophisticated solutions.
title: Fatal Non-aneurysmal Subarachnoid Haemorrhage During Bridge-to-Transplant Rehabilitation in a Patient With Biventricular Assist Devices.

abstract: Arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase (5-LO) and its activating protein, encoded by ALOX5 and ALOX5AP respectively, are two leukotriene pathway proteins suspected to play a role in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) through inflammatory mechanisms. Prior genetic association studies linking ALOX5 and ALOX5AP to ASCVD have motivated clinical trials of 5-LO inhibitors, such as atreleuton, which was associated with reduced atherosclerotic plaque progression in patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome in a phase II trial. However, the effect of 5-LO inhibition on ASCVD clinical outcomes remains unclear. Using data from the UK Biobank, we revisit previously reported genetic associations of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP with ASCVD using a multi-ancestry meta-analysis including data from 378,962 participants. We characterize ancestral differences in previously studied ALOX5 and ALOX5AP polymorphisms which could have led to population stratification. When adequately accounting for ancestry, these previous associations were not replicated. In addition to our replication efforts, we used association scans and transcriptome-wide association studies to test the involvement of leukotriene pathway genes with ASCVD. Overall, our results do not support a role for genetic variation in ALOX5 or its activating protein in ASCVD risk.
title: Revisiting the genetic support of leukotriene pathway drug targets in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

abstract: Left atrial appendage closure is an increasingly used stroke prevention therapy for patients with atrial fibrillation who are unable to maintain long-term anticoagulation. Imaging quality and consistency are central to procedural safety and long-term outcomes, yet practice varies widely across centers. This review presents a practical, phase-based multimodality imaging framework intended to provide guidance and minimum standards for image acquisition and interpretation across all phases of left atrial appendage closure care, including preprocedural planning and thrombus exclusion, intraprocedural guidance and complication detection, and postprocedural surveillance for device-related thrombus and peridevice leak. Because sizing rules, sealing mechanisms, and leak patterns differ between the 2 contemporary platforms, device-specific considerations for the Watchman and Amulet systems are addressed throughout. Transesophageal echocardiography remains the reference standard for thrombus detection and procedural guidance, while cardiac computed tomography offers high spatial resolution, detailed 3-dimensional characterization, and complementary leak assessment, with optimal modality selection influenced by patient characteristics, operator expertise, and institutional resources. Intracardiac echocardiography and mini transesophageal echocardiographic support anesthesia-sparing workflows. Standardized device-related thrombus and peridevice leak classification and harmonized imaging protocols can enhance reproducibility and facilitate cross-center comparisons. Emerging technologies including computed tomography first workflows, 4-dimensional imaging, AI applications, and computational modeling further advance precision planning and surveillance.
authors: Left Atrial Appendage International Working Group
title: Multimodality Imaging for Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Practical Guidance Across Preprocedural, Intraprocedural, and Postprocedural Phases.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular ejection fraction reserve (LVEF-R), defined as stress EF minus rest EF, is a marker for high-risk coronary artery disease in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging, but its prognostic and diagnostic significance in large real-world populations remains incompletely defined. We aimed to analyze the association of LVEF-R with mortality and high-risk obstructive coronary artery disease in a large multicenter cohort.
METHODS: We analyzed 34 976 patients from 13 sites who underwent gated rest and vasodilator stress positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging from the Registry of Flow and Perfusion Imaging for Artificial Intelligence with PET. Associations between LVEF-R and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death were assessed using multivariable Cox regression models. In a subset with invasive coronary angiography (n=6843), the relationship between LVEF-R and angiographic disease was evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 9392 (26.9%) patients had an LVEF-R<0%. Over a median follow-up of 4.1 years, lower LVEF-R demonstrated a graded association with higher mortality. Compared with LVEF-R>5%, adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.20 for LVEF-R 0% to 5% ([95% CI, 1.13-1.28]; P<0.001), 1.32 for -5% to 0% ([95% CI, 1.23-1.42]; P<0.001), and 1.38 for ≤-5% ([95% CI, 1.24-1.52]; P<0.001). A negative LVEF-R was also associated with high-risk coronary artery disease, including left main and 3-vessel disease.
CONCLUSIONS: LVEF-R is an independent predictor of mortality, with a graded association between impaired reserve and adverse outcomes. A negative LVEF-R identifies patients with a higher likelihood of multivessel or left-main coronary artery disease, supporting its role as a clinically relevant marker of high-risk disease.
title: Prediction of All-Cause Mortality, Cardiovascular Mortality, and Angiographic Coronary Disease From LVEF Reserve: Findings From the Multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
Three medication experience profiles after percutaneous coronary intervention show no detected differences in questionnaire networks.

abstract: Glucagon-like-peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are an antihyperglycemic group of drugs that have emerged as potentially preventing the risk of cardiovascular events. This meta-analysis assesses the effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists on cardiovascular outcomes. A detailed search of existing literature was based on MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov. The search included all the studies from inception to February 2026. Statistical analyses were performed using the RevMan software, and a random-effects model was used to conduct the meta-analysis. Data were represented via forest plots, and dichotomous outcomes were evaluated using the Mantel-Haenszel method. This meta-analysis includes 12 randomized control trials (RCTs) with 82,669 patients. The analysis showed that GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce risk of cardiac death [relative risk (RR): 0.89, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.96, p=0.003, I²=0%], all-cause mortality (RR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.93, p<0.00001, I²=0%), stroke (RR: 0.85, 95% CI: 0.77-0.94, p=0.001, I²=0%), non-fatal stroke (RR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.79-0.96, p=0.005, I²=0%) and revascularization (RR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95, p=0.007, I²=59%). There was no statistically significant reduction in myocardial infarction (MI) (RR: 0.92, 95% CI: 0.84-1.01, p=0.09, I²=42%), fatal MI (RR: 1.15, 95% CI: 0.80-1.66, p=0.44, I²=0%), non-fatal MI (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.82-1.01, p=0.09, I²=51%), fatal stroke (RR: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.55-1.00, p=0.05, I²=0%), heart failure hospitalization (RR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.85-1.03, p=0.20, I²=17%), or hospitalization for unstable angina (RR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.85-1.12, p=0.71, I²=0%). This meta-analysis demonstrates that GLP-1 receptor agonists have a significant impact on cardiovascular death. More thorough RCTs with longer follow-up periods are required to completely understand the possible cardiovascular advantages of GLP-1 receptor agonists.
journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
title: Effect of glucagon-like-peptide-1 receptor agonists on major cardiovascular outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).
CONCLUSION: LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 6 RCTs (n = 7,004) with IPD reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves.
appraisal.main_limitation: Reconstructed rather than true patient-level data, a small number of trials, and devices and comparators that differ between trials.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis with reconstructed individual patient data comparing left atrial appendage occlusion with oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD analyses gave lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It updates the LAAO versus anticoagulation evidence after recent conflicting trials, though D9 is monitored at lower weight.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.

abstract: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI) restores epicardial coronary flow in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but microvascular and tissue-level reperfusion may remain impaired. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined microvascular obstruction (MVO) and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) both mark severe reperfusion injury but reflect distinct tissue processes. This structured narrative review synthesizes evidence on MVO mechanisms, multimodal phenotypes, and interventions. Available evidence implicates interacting contributions from distal embolization, endothelial barrier and vasomotor dysfunction, pericyte-mediated capillary constriction, immunothrombosis, and tissue edema. IMH reflects more extensive microvascular destruction with erythrocyte extravasation. Angiography, electrocardiography, invasive physiology, angiography-derived indices, echocardiography, and CMR assess different pathophysiologic levels. Discordance between modalities is therefore not necessarily contradictory. Across trials, improvements in surrogate endpoints have often not translated into long-term clinical benefit, partly because of mechanistic heterogeneity and misaligned treatment timing and endpoints. A conceptual, reperfusion-centered T- to T5 research framework is proposed for serial within-patient assessment. It links early physiology, inflammatory and thrombotic biomarkers, acute-phase CMR, and long-term remodeling. Future trials should align mechanistic enrichment, intervention timing, and endpoint selection to establish a continuous evidence chain from target engagement to clinical outcomes.
title: Microvascular Obstruction After Reperfusion in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Structured Narrative Review.

abstract: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established intervention for patients having severe mitral regurgitation (MR) with prohibitive surgical risk. Complications during deployment related to device malfunction are uncommon but necessitate prompt decision-making and management. A 54-year-old gentleman with dilated cardiomyopathy, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and severe MR underwent TEER using the MyClip system (Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd., Vapi, Gujarat, India). Initial deployment across the A2-P2 scallops of mitral leaflets achieved partial MR reduction. Significant residual MR required a second clip for optimal leaflet coaptation. While deploying the second clip, it failed to close because of a mechanical locking failure. So, we everted the clip, pulled back to LA, and it stayed in open position and failed to close. We report a novel bailout snare technique that enabled safe retrieval without the need for a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal minimized the risk of tearing the atrial septum and facilitated the successful completion of the TEER procedure. Another clip was deployed successfully, resulting in significant MR reduction. This case demonstrates a rare complication during deployment, a malfunction of the device, and a novel strategy for safely bailing out a challenging intra-procedural complication.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Snare-Assisted Retrieval of a Mechanically Locked-Open TEER Device: A Novel Bailout Technique.

abstract: There is a growing need for large-bore femoral access across cardiac interventions. This has led to a need for more widely accessible vascular closure techniques to facilitate reliable vascular closure and wider access to these interventions. We present a stepwise approach to femoral artery closure using two Angioseal devices in a case of Impella-assisted PCI. This case demonstrates a simple and easy-to-perform method to achieve hemostasis in large-bore femoral access. A larger series to confirm safety and reproducibility would help support this approach.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: The Triple Wire Dual Angioseal Technique for Large Bore Femoral Access Closure.

abstract: BackgroundHeat exposure increases cardiovascular risk, but its relationship with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) in emergency department (ED) patients is unknown. This study examined whether heat exposure increases NSTEMI risk in ED patients with chest pain.MethodsThis observational cohort study of adults with chest pain from 5 US EDs (April 1, 2019-October 31, 2023) used the Wake Forest Chest Pain Registry. Heat data were collected from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Heat exposure was defined as maximum daily heat index ≥80°F, the National Weather Service's cautionary threshold. The primary outcome was index NSTEMI, determined using validated diagnosis codes. Logistic models assessed the association between heat and NSTEMI. Multivariable models were adjusted for common cardiovascular confounders, and pollution-given its potential to exacerbate cardiovascular disease. Lagged analysis evaluated heat exposure over 5-d lags. Unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) are reported with 95% confidence intervals.ResultsAmong 21,367 patients with chest pain, 52.7% (11,260/21,367) were female, the median age was 53.5 y (IQR 40-65), and 63.1% (13,486/21,367) had heat-exposed days. Index NSTEMI occurred in 5.9% of patients. NSTEMI rates were similar between those with and without heat exposure (5.8% [778/13,486] vs 6.2% [487/7881]; OR: 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.05). After adjustment, heat exposure remained unassociated with index NSTEMI (aOR: 0.91, 95% CI 0.80-1.03). Lagged analysis showed no association between NSTEMI and heat exposure in unadjusted (OR: 0.92, 95% CI 0.82-1.04) or adjusted (aOR: 0.94, 95% CI 0.82-1.07) models.ConclusionHeat exposure was not associated with NSTEMI in chest pain ED patients.
title: Ambient Heat Exposure Is Not Associated with Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction among Emergency Department Patients with Acute Chest Pain.

abstract: Hepatic fibrosis indices have emerged as potential prognostic markers in cardiovascular disease. This observational study included 760 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndrome (STEMI, NSTEMI, and unstable angina pectoris) admitted between March 2020 and May 2024 to evaluate the distribution of APRI, FIB-4, FIB-5, and FIB-6 across ACS subtypes and their predictive value for in-hospital mortality and cardiogenic shock. Fibrosis indices were calculated from admission laboratory values, and multivariate logistic regression and ROC curve analyses were performed. STEMI patients had significantly higher APRI (0.95±1.43 vs. 0.41±0.71 vs. 0.20±0.11), FIB-4 (3.68±4.03 vs. 1.98±2.17 vs. 1.17±0.52), and FIB-5 (5.16±1.08 vs. 4.66±0.84 vs. 4.38±0.43) than NSTEMI and unstable angina patients (all p<0.001). In-hospital mortality and cardiogenic shock occurred in 3.8% and 3.2% of patients, respectively. Cardiogenic shock, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and lower serum albumin independently predicted mortality, whereas older age independently predicted cardiogenic shock. None of the hepatic fibrosis indices independently predicted either outcome, and their discriminative performance was limited (AUC 0.526-0.632 for mortality and 0.570-0.662 for cardiogenic shock). These findings indicate that although hepatic fibrosis scores are elevated in STEMI, they primarily reflect the severity of acute myocardial injury rather than providing incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical predictors in patients with acute coronary syndrome.
title: Prognostic Value of Non-Invasive Hepatic Fibrosis Scores Across Acute Coronary Syndrome Subtypes.
Mid-deployment steering technique for Watchman FLX implantation in a complex retrobend chicken-wing anatomy.

abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is often poorly controlled in patients with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and evidence for renal denervation in this population remains limited.
CASE SUMMARY: We describe a 38-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis because of thrombotic microangiopathy who developed refractory hypertension with recurrent hypertensive emergencies despite 6 antihypertensive agents and aggressive ultrafiltration, precluding kidney transplant listing. After a thorough secondary hypertension work-up, he underwent off-label catheter-based bilateral renal denervation, after which his blood pressure improved substantially, hypertensive emergencies ceased, and he was subsequently added to the transplant waitlist.
CONCLUSION: Renal denervation may serve as adjunctive therapy to help dialysis patients with resistant hypertension reach transplant candidacy.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Understand the limitations of pharmacologic and dialytic therapy for blood pressure control in dialysis-dependent patients. Appreciate how refractory hypertension may serve as a barrier to kidney transplant listing and how renal denervation may address it.
title: Renal Denervation to Enable Kidney Transplant Listing in Resistant Hypertension Patient on Hemodialysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the growing field of interventional radiology, emerging technologies implement the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help tackle growing demands for treatment. Due to the anatomical differences in animals, volunteers offer the most realistic training and testing scenario, however safety considerations restrict rapid prototyping of these new technologies. Simulators have been a key facilitator in the testing of new technologies among numerous medical engineering studies, but often lack the realism to reliably test AI.
PURPOSE: This proof-of-concept study presents methods to create or enhance hyper-realistic radiographic simulators that can effectively function with a medical-grade AI software.
METHODS: Iron-filled plastic was used to three-dimensionally (3D) print a series of blocks of heights up to 30 mm. By analyzing the intensities generated by different thicknesses of plastic, anonymous fluoroscopic images were turned into height maps (lithophanes) and 3D-printed. A static scene from transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was then 3D-printed and imaged with different presets using two different x-ray systems for mathematical analysis. Lithophanes were then used as a radiographic background to experimental and commercial interventional simulators to test Caranx Medical's TAVIPILOT AI. Finally, fluoroscopies from 5 3D-printed lithophanes were mixed with 5 real images and presented to 5 expert volunteers to establish their realism in a structured survey.
RESULTS: The 3D-printed x-ray lithophanes test-plates' radiographic appearance was rated as "Adequate" to "Good" across all fields of the survey, with participants praising their realism. The test-plate was able to reliably recreate the TAVI scene in different x-ray systems, with joint-histogram correlation coefficients above 0.9, and global structural similarity above 0.8. The lithophanes were imaged as a standalone test plate and as a backing to dynamic TAVI interventional simulators; in both cases, TAVIPILOT AI responded to the simulator as if it was operating on a real anatomical image.
CONCLUSIONS: Lithophane plates present an easy-to-implement solution to recreate monoplane x-ray scenes, which can be deployed to test software at the point of care with minimal logistical, ethical, or safety concerns. This study opens the door for a new range of interventional simulators able to recreate human-like appearance to test AI, offering a non-exclusive alternative to patient volunteers and anonymous data.
title: Development and evaluation of X-ray lithophanes as test objects for interventional procedure simulation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with high thrombus burden often shows impaired myocardial perfusion despite successful epicardial recanalization. Intracoronary recombinant human TNK tissue-type plasminogen activator (rhTNK-tPA) may reduce microvascular obstruction and preserve ventricular function, but evidence is limited.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 136 STEMI patients with high thrombus burden undergoing primary PCI between May 2022 and February 2025. Patients receiving intracoronary rhTNK-tPA (n=62) were compared with controls receiving standard PCI alone (n=74). The primary endpoint was left ventricular regional wall motion status within 7 days after PCI, assessed by WMSI and normal ventricular wall motion. Secondary endpoints included cTFC, ST-segment resolution, final TIMI flow grade, and clinical and safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally comparable. The rhTNK-tPA group had lower WMSI values (P<0.001) and a higher incidence of normal ventricular wall motion (41.7% vs. 19.6%; P=0.014). rhTNK-tPA was also associated with lower post-PCI cTFC (18.18 ± 6.91 vs. 21.24 ± 9.20; P=0.033) and higher ST-segment resolution (83.9% vs. 68.9%; P=0.043), while final TIMI grade 3 flow was similar. In multivariable analysis, rhTNK-tPA was independently associated with lower odds of ventricular wall motion abnormalities (OR=0.214; 95% CI, 0.106-0.433; P<0.001). MACE were infrequent, and no intracranial hemorrhage occurred.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive intracoronary rhTNK-tPA during primary PCI was associated with better early preservation of regional wall motion and improved reperfusion indices without an observed increase in major bleeding.
keywords: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction; primary percutaneous coronary intervention; intracoronary thrombolysis; recombinant human TNK tissue-type plasminogen activator.
title: Adjunctive Intracoronary rhTNK-tPA During Primary PCI and Early Regional Left Ventricular Function in STEMI Patients With High Thrombus Burden: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Virtual patients (VPs) are widely used in medical education, but creating high-quality cases requires clinical expertise, iterative revision, and alignment with educational objectives. Generative AI may support VP authoring, but direct comparisons between AI-generated and clinician-developed cases delivered within the same educational setting remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare medical students' learner-perceived ratings of 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed virtual cardiology patient scenario with those of 1 clinician-developed virtual cardiology patient scenario delivered through the same mobile platform.
METHODS: A randomized, participant-blinded 2-arm controlled study was conducted in October 2025 during scheduled fifth-year emergency medicine course sessions. Eligible participants were fifth-year medical students who had completed the cardiology course. Students were assigned 1:1 to complete either a clinician-developed VP (CD-VP; n=64) or a ChatGPT-generated VP (GPT-VP; n=67). Both scenarios followed a shared acute coronary syndrome blueprint and were delivered through the same mobile-optimized app (mobile VPs app [MobiViP]) with identical interface structure and branching logic. The GPT-VP was generated using GPT-5 and refined through iterative follow-up prompting under expert review; direct manual rewriting was prohibited. After completion, students completed a mandatory 19-item questionnaire covering realism and validity, cognitive load, self-reported learning and reflection, and engagement and satisfaction. Analyses included reliability testing, 1-sample tests against a neutral midpoint, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Spearman correlations. Full scenario content and development details are provided as multimedia appendices.
RESULTS: A total of 131 complete questionnaires were analyzed, with no item-level missing data. Mean subscale scores in the CD-VP group were 3.81 (SD 0.64) for realism and validity, 3.67 (SD 0.74) for cognitive load, 3.64 (SD 0.73) for self-reported learning and reflection, and 4.16 (SD 0.64) for engagement and satisfaction; corresponding GPT-VP scores were 4.11 (SD 0.56), 3.03 (SD 0.76), 3.86 (SD 0.77), and 4.28 (SD 0.58), respectively. Compared with the CD-VP, the GPT-VP received higher ratings for realism and validity (Mann-Whitney U=1503.0; P=.003) and lower cognitive load ratings, indicating a lower perceived burden (Mann-Whitney U=1070.5; P<.001). Self-reported learning and reflection showed a marginal difference between groups, with a higher rating for the GPT-VP (Mann-Whitney U=1719.0; P=.05), whereas engagement and satisfaction did not differ significantly (Mann-Whitney U=1922.5; P=.31). Internal consistency was acceptable to good for most subscales, although internal consistency for the realism and validity subscale in the GPT-VP group was moderate (Cronbach α=0.67).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center randomized study, 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed cardiology VP scenario was rated similarly to or more favorably than 1 clinician-developed scenario in selected learner-perceived domains. Future research should expand to objective learning, retention, development workload, and scalability outcomes.
title: Perceived Ratings of AI-Generated and Expert-Reviewed vs Clinician-Developed Virtual Cardiology Patient Scenarios Among Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with no obstructive coronary arteries is often due to coronary vascular dysfunction, which is increasingly described as a contributor and predictor of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. We tested the hypothesis that coronary vascular dysfunction contributes to cardiac dysfunction.
METHODS: Sixty-eight participants with suspected coronary vascular dysfunction underwent LV pressure-volume assessment at rest and during isometric handgrip stress. Coronary function testing was performed by infusing standard doses of adenosine, acetylcholine, and nitroglycerine through a guiding catheter placed in the left main coronary artery, per established protocols.
RESULTS: Of the participants studied, 12 had normal coronary vascular function while 56 had coronary vascular dysfunction. At rest, there were no differences between groups in any invasive pressure or volumetric measurement. With isometric handgrip, peak filling rate increased significantly in participants with normal coronary vascular function (0.56 ± 0.31 vs. 0.85 ± 0.68 1/s/mmHg) but remained unchanged in participants with coronary vascular dysfunction (0.51 ± 0.22 vs. 0.55 ± 0.43 1/s/mmHg; group x time interaction, p = 0.04). Moreover, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure decreased significantly with isometric handgrip in participants with normal coronary vascular function (12 ± 3 vs. 9 ± 4 mmHg) but increased in participants with coronary vascular dysfunction (14 ± 4 vs. 15 ± 6 mmHg; group x time interaction, p = 0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary vascular dysfunction was associated with an impaired ability of the LV to adapt its filling during stress. Further work is needed to assess potential clinical significance.

title: Coronary vascular dysfunction is associated with adverse left ventricular filling in patients with angina but no obstructed coronary arteries.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging evidence points on an increased mortality risk associated to moderate aortic stenosis (AS), yet this population remains insufficiently characterized. We tested the prognostic value of two echocardiographic coupling indices reflecting right and left-sided cardiac function: the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio (TAPSE/PASP) and the left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI).
METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study including 135 patients with moderate AS. TAPSE/PASP was used as a non-invasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary circulation (RV-Pc) coupling, and LACI was defined as ratio of left atrial volume index to mitral a' velocity. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess the prognostic value of both indices.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 1.61 ± 0.79 years, 33 patients (24%) died. Reduced TAPSE/PASP (< 0.67 mm/mmHg) and elevated LACI (> 5.17) were independently associated with an increased mortality (HR: 3.03 and 3.16, respectively, p < 0.01). These associations remained significant even after adjusting for age. Stratification into three groups - preserved, single, or combined uncoupling -showed progressively lower 1-year survival rates, ranging from 95% to 49% (p < 0.0001). None of the coupling-derived variables was associated with hemodynamic progression or need of aortic valve replacement.
CONCLUSION: TAPSE/PASP and LACI are independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate AS. These parameters may provide incremental prognostic information in this often-overlooked population. These findings may prompt further studies evaluating the potential role of these parameters in helping to refine prognostic phenotyping.
title: Echocardiographic atrial and right heart to pulmonary circulation coupling indices identify high-risk in moderate aortic stenosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the first line treatment of aortic stenosis, a condition predominantly affecting elderly patients. In absence of a specific indication for antithrombotic therapy, lifetime aspirin is recommended after TAVI while it may be discontinued 3 months after bioprosthetic surgical valve replacement. Primary prevention, using aspirin compared to placebo among elderly patients is associated with an increased risk of major bleeding and no reduction rates of thrombotic events. Hence, there is a gap of knowledge on whether aspirin should be continued >3 months after TAVI.
STUDY DESIGN: SOLOTAVI is a multicenter, open label, blinded endpoint assessment, 1:1 randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing aspirin discontinuation 3 months after TAVI (experimental) to long-term therapy (control). Adult patients with successful transfemoral TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis and no indication or contraindication for long-term antithrombotic therapy will be enrolled. Randomization is stratified on center and valve type. The primary endpoint is the 12-month composite of all cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and non-procedure-related major or disabling bleeding. A hierarchical analysis is performed for the primary and 3 principal secondary endpoints. The sample size is computed for demonstrating the non-inferiority of the experimental strategy compared with the control strategy, with a conservative non-inferiority margin of 6.5%. A total of 1400 patients will be enrolled.
CONCLUSIONS: The SOLOTAVI trial will assess the non-inferiority of a 3-month duration of aspirin compared to the long-term therapy after successful transfemoral TAVI in terms of thrombotic and bleeding events. NCT06518317 clinicaltrials.org.

abstract: Introduction and objectives This report presents the 2025 activity of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (ACI-SEC). Methods All interventional cardiology laboratories in Spain were invited to complete an online survey. Data were analyzed by an external company and subsequently reviewed and presented by the ACI-SEC board. Results A total of 125 hospitals participated, compared with 118 in the previous year. The number of diagnostic procedures and coronary angiograms increased by 4% and 4.5%, respectively, both reaching record highs. Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) increased by 3.3%. The trend toward lower relative stent use was confirmed, with a marked increase in the use of drug-coated balloons, both as a standalone strategy and as part of hybrid strategies. The use of intracoronary imaging and coronary physiology techniques increased, reaching record absolute numbers. Interventional treatment of myocardial infarction increased by 3.6%, with primary PCI accounting for 98% of procedures. Structural heart interventions continued to expand: transcatheter aortic valve implantation (+10.1%), percutaneous mitral interventions (+25.2%), tricuspid interventions (+7.9%), and left atrial appendage closure (+8.4%). Renal denervation procedures, interventional treatment of acute pulmonary embolism, and interventions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension increased significantly. Conclusions The 2025 Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry shows overall growth in both coronary and structural activity. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.
