abstract: A 47-year-old man presented with dyspnea and presyncope. Initial electrocardiography showed sinus bradycardia without ST-segment elevation, whereas telemetry revealed recurrent sinus arrest with a maximum pause of 3.3 s. Emergency coronary angiography revealed total occlusion of the obtuse marginal branch. Although the sinoatrial node artery originated near the occlusion, intravascular ultrasound confirmed the preservation of blood flow. Immediate revascularization led to complete resolution of sinus arrest. This case suggests that isolated lateral wall ischemia may represent an unusual manifestation of the Bezold-Jarisch reflex without direct sinoatrial node artery involvement. Therefore, acute coronary syndrome should be considered in unexplained sinus node dysfunction, even in the absence of typical chest pain.
title: Isolated Obtuse Marginal Branch Occlusion Presenting as Recurrent Sinus Arrest without ST-segment Elevation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching. At the frame level, we compared post-procedural OCT findings in NALS to 2 comparators: non-NA-leading lesions (lesions without neoatherosclerosis); and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions. Of 144 lesions with serial OCT, neoatherosclerosis occurred in 17 (11.8%). In NA-leading segments, compared to non-NA-leading lesions and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions, the proportion of frames with lipid-rich plaque was higher (71% vs. 54% [odds ratio (OR) 2.72; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.23-6.01] and 58% [OR 2.62; 95% CI 0.99-6.96], respectively). Similarly, the mean (±SD) in-stent atherothrombotic material area was larger in NA-leading segments (0.41±0.39 vs. 0.24±0.31 [geometric mean ratio (GMR) 2.00; 95% CI 1.21-3.29] and 0.16±0.16 mm2[GMR 2.33; 95% CI 1.26-4.31], respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Underlying lipid-rich plaque and a higher burden of in-stent atherothrombotic material were associated with neoatherosclerosis at 3 years in STEMI patients, indicating that plaque composition at the time of DES implantation may critically influence neoatherosclerosis formation.
journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
title: Underlying Plaque Type and Neoatherosclerosis After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction - Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Substudy of the CONNECT Trial.

abstract: Traditional management of atherosclerosis focuses primarily on cholesterol and triglycerides; however, lipoproteins also transport bioactive lipids that critically regulate systemic inflammation and metabolic health. This review highlights the diverse physiological and clinical roles of apolipoproteins and bioactive lipids beyond classical lipid accumulation. First, we discuss how hepatic transporters NPC1L1 and ABCG5/8 modulate glucose metabolism and handle non-cholesterol lipids, including phytosterols. Second, we emphasize the apolipoprotein M (ApoM) and sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) axis. ApoM protects S1P from degradation and directly mediates the pleiotropic benefits of high-density lipoprotein (HDL), including anti-apoptotic, antithrombotic, and renoprotective effects. Third, reverse translational research utilizing genome-wide association studies identifies apolipoprotein D (ApoD) as a key anti-inflammatory modulator. Finally, clinical lipidomics underscores the importance of "minor" lysophospholipids, such as lysophosphatidylinositol and lysophosphatidylserine, alongside lysophosphatidic acid in the pathogenesis of acute coronary syndrome. Understanding the dynamic crosstalk between lipid transporters, apolipoproteins, and bioactive lipids provides novel mechanistic insights into cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, paving the way for innovative biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies.
title: Multifaceted Physiological Roles of Lipoproteins and Understanding Atherosclerosis: Crosstalk Between Lipoproteins and Bioactive Lipids.

abstract: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is an acquired hemostatic abnormality characterized by quantitative or qualitative defects of von Willebrand factor (VWF). In high-shear conditions, such as aortic stenosis (AS) or mechanical circulatory support (MCS), excessive proteolytic cleavage of von Willebrand factor (VWF) by its specific protease ADAMTS13 leads to the loss of large-molecular-weight VWF multimers. AVWS is increasingly recognized as a potential risk factor for bleeding in patients on MCS. Current management strategies for AVWS associated with MCS include VWF supplementation with fresh frozen plasma or VWF concentrate; however, the therapeutic effect is only transient due to persistent VWF degradation. Our research group developed a humanized anti-ADAMTS13 antibody (HA10), and we are currently developing a novel therapeutic strategy to control bleeding symptoms associated with AVWS by inhibiting ADAMTS13 activity. We demonstrated the efficacy of HA10 in inhibiting VWF degradation in MCS-implanted male cynomolgus monkeys and further established its safety profile in a GLP-grade single-dose intravenous toxicity study in male cynomolgus monkeys. Our data indicate a potentially low risk of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, a potentially severe complication associated with HA10.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity or maximally tolerated statin therapy has robust evidence for secondary prevention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), and is strongly recommended in international guidelines. However, comprehensive real-world data on its use and associated factors remain limited.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Using data from the JROAD-DPC database (2017-2022), we analyzed ACS and CCS patients who underwent revascularization and were discharged alive. We assessed temporal trends in lipid-lowering therapy and examined associated factors, including patient demographics, comorbidities, treatment strategies, and hospital structural characteristics, using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models. Among 358,570 patients with ACS and 392,821 with CCS, the use of maximum-dose statins increased from 8.6% in 2017 to 34.1% in 2022 in ACS and from 7.8% to 19.1% in CCS, but remained suboptimal. After multivariable adjustment, older age, underweight status, and coronary artery bypass grafting were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins in ACS. In CCS, older age, underweight status, and higher comorbidity burden were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins. Hospital structural factors, including a higher number of cardiologists, were also associated with a greater use of maximum-dose statins.
CONCLUSIONS: Maximum-dose statin use among ACS and CCS patients remains suboptimal in Japan. Multilevel factors contribute to this evidence-practice gap, underscoring the need for comprehensive interventions at multiple levels to reduce disparities in care delivery.
journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
title: Temporal Trends, Underuse, and Multilevel Factors Associated With Maximum-Dose Statin Therapy in Acute and Chronic Coronary Syndromes - A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty is an established treatment for in-stent restenosis (ISR), and its procedural success mainly depends on optimal lesion preparation. Angiography alone offers limited assessment of acute procedural effects, and sequential vessel and lumen changes have not been comprehensively characterized with intracoronary imaging (ICI). Therefore, we aimed to characterize the stepwise vessel and lumen changes during DCB angioplasty for ISR across three procedural stages: pre-lesion preparation, post-lesion preparation and post-DCB inflation.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 20 patients (21 lesions) undergoing DCB angioplasty for ISR with available ICI pullbacks (intravascular ultrasound (IVUS), n = 16; optical coherence tomography (OCT), n = 5) at three stages: pre-lesion preparation, post-lesion preparation, and post-DCB inflation. Lesions treated with DCBs were identified on angiography and co-registered to the ICI pullbacks.
RESULTS: Median age was 69 years, 15 patients (75%) were male, and lesion preparation was performed with non-compliant balloons in 76%. On IVUS, minimal lumen area (MLA) increased from 2.7 [2.2-3.5]mm2 at baseline to 4.8 [4.1-6.0]mm2 after lesion preparation (median difference (95% confidence interval) +2.6 (1.8-2.7)mm2, p < 0.001), and 5.9 [4.5-7.0]mm2 post-DCB (+0.6 (0.4-1.1)mm2, p < 0.001). On OCT, MLA increased from 1.9 [1.4-2.1]mm2 at baseline to 3.8 [2.9-4.2]mm2 after lesion preparation (+2.0 [0.3-2.8]mm2), and 4.5 [3.9-5.3]mm2 post-DCB (+0.6 [0.3-1.0]mm2). Neointimal burden decreased after lesion preparation and decreased further after DCB treatment.
CONCLUSION: ICI demonstrates that the principal morphologic changes are achieved after lesion preparation, with smaller yet significant additional acute mechanical effects following DCB treatment.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Stepwise intracoronary imaging assessment of lumen and vessel changes during drug-coated balloon angioplasty for in-stent restenosis.

abstract: Atrioventricular conduction disturbances and the need for cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) therapy are frequently required after transcatheter tricuspid valve implantation (TTVI). The interaction between the annulus, transcatheter heart valve and the leads is often complex and the optimal management under debate. We prospectively included 36 patients undergoing TTVI between June 2021 and January 2025. 14 patients had a preexisting CIED. 11 patients experienced right ventricular lead-jailing without signs for early or delayed lead failure after one year, one patient underwent lead extraction and two patients had a leadless pacemaker. In four patients, a pacemaker in LBBAP was successfully implanted due to new-onset postoperative atrioventricular block. The device measurements as well as the valve function remained stable over a follow-up of at least one up to 2.5 years with persistent LBB-capture. This case series demonstrates that LBBAP following TTVI is feasible with encouraging early outcomes. Careful patient selection and dedicated follow-up are essential for patients with CIED treated with TTVI.
title: Feasibility of Left Bundle Branch Pacing and Management of Jailed Leads After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Implantation.

abstract: Patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) alongside a recent or concurrent non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) occupy one of the least evidence-supported decision points in acute stroke care, excluded from every pivotal thrombolysis trial. The recent approval and guideline endorsement of tenecteplase-an agent separately licensed for myocardial infarction at twice the cerebral dose-adds a dimension the alteplase-derived literature does not address. This narrative review synthesizes the evidence on intravenous thrombolysis, specifically tenecteplase, in this setting and distinguishes infarct-related from treatment-related barriers to eligibility. Concomitant NSTEMI complicates approximately 1.6% of acute ischemic stroke hospitalizations and carries an adjusted 3.6-fold increase in in-hospital mortality. The historical contraindication derives from mechanisms-myocardial hemorrhage with free-wall rupture, postinfarction pericarditis with hemopericardium, and left ventricular thrombus embolization-that scale with transmurality and are therefore largely ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction phenomena. Registry data from more than 40,000 thrombolyzed patients show no significant excess of thrombolysis-related complications with recent NSTEMI, and fatal ruptures cluster in subacute ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction; the excess mortality is of similar magnitude without thrombolysis, marking a sicker patient rather than a more dangerous drug.
title: Intravenous Tenecteplase for Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Recent or Concurrent Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Narrative Review.

abstract: Concomitant coronary artery disease affects 40-75% of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Three recent randomized trials yielded conflicting findings: NOTION-3 demonstrated reduced composite events with pre-TAVI percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PRO-TAVI showed non-inferiority of PCI deferral with less bleeding; neither demonstrated mortality benefit. No previous meta-analysis combined all 3 trials with observational evidence, applied design-stratified GRADE certainty, or explored cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (3 randomized trials, 13 observational cohorts; 8,207 patients). Ten prespecified outcomes were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); 30-day all-cause mortality was primary. GRADE certainty was assessed separately for randomized and observational evidence. Prespecified design-based subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Pre-TAVI PCI was not associated with significant differences in 30-day all-cause mortality (RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.90-1.77; I2 = 32%) or 1-year mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15; I2 = 0%). Major bleeding (RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.98-1.44) and major vascular complications (RR 1.48, 95% CI 0.95-2.30) showed borderline non-significant trends favoring PCI deferral (both I2 = 0%). Excluding Griese et al. 2014, the principal driver of harm and heterogeneity, reduced cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity (RR 0.91; I2 = 24%). No significant differences occurred in stroke, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, pacemaker implantation, or rehospitalization. Routine pre-TAVI PCI confers no mortality benefit and may increase bleeding and vascular complications; PCI should be individualized according to coronary complexity, lesion significance, and bleeding risk.
title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10). In 8 studies reporting both AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, separate syntheses showed sensitivity of 0.91 (0.86-0.94) for AI versus 0.78 (0.69-0.85) for clinicians, specificity of 0.91 (0.82-0.96) for both, and AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90, respectively. In 7 studies using physician ECG interpretation as the comparator, AI sensitivity was 0.85 (0.70-0.94), specificity 0.99 (0.96-1.00), and AUC 0.98 (0.96-0.99). Sensitivity analyses excluding case-control designs, influential studies, and restricting analyses to deep-learning models or raw-waveform ECGs produced similar findings.
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) encompasses new or worsened cardiac abnormalities that arise after acute stroke, most often within the first 30 days and with an early peak. Its spectrum includes acute myocardial injury, electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmia, ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and heart failure, but similar findings may reflect antecedent cardiac disease or systemic illness. This Review defines the accepted clinical boundaries of SHS and integrates central autonomic network disruption, neuroendocrine stress, inflammation, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, oxygen supply-demand imbalance, and premorbid substrate into a time-resolved framework. Eight provisional, non-mutually-exclusive phenotypic domains are proposed to organize current evidence without implying validated endotypes. A diagnostic approach based on symptom chronology, prior cardiac data, serial troponin and electrocardiography, rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, selective coronary assessment, and cardiac magnetic resonance is presented to distinguish stroke-triggered injury from recent myocardial infarction, pre-existing atrial fibrillation, chronic myocardial injury, and established heart failure. No syndrome-specific treatment is validated; care should prioritize recognized cardiac emergencies, correction of reversible stressors, and coordinated stroke-cardiology decision-making. Prospective studies with documented premorbid status, standardized time points, and blinded adjudication are needed to validate the proposed phenotypes and determine whether they improve outcomes.
title: Stroke-Heart Syndrome: Mechanisms, Temporal Phenotypes, and Diagnostic Reasoning.

abstract: Energy drink (ED) consumption has been temporally associated with acute coronary events, particularly in young individuals; however, causality remains uncertain. We aimed to characterize coronary events reported following ED consumption and evaluate their clinical features, underlying mechanisms, and causal plausibility. Two new cases of premature myocardial infarction (MI) were combined with cases identified through a systematic review of the literature published through September 2026. Patient-level data on ED exposure, cardiovascular risk factors, coronary mechanisms, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Causality was assessed using an adapted World Health Organization-Uppsala Monitoring Centre (WHO-UMC) framework. The cohort comprised 31 male patients (29 previously published cases and two new cases; mean age, 25.6 +- 5.4 years). Twenty-eight patients (90.3%) met strict criteria for MI or acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and 25 (80.6%) presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Coronary thrombosis was documented in 13 patients (41.9%), coronary vasospasm in eight (25.8%), and spontaneous coronary artery dissection in three (9.7%). Additional exposures or physiological stressors were identified in 22 patients (71.0%). The initial left ventricular ejection fraction was below 50% in 10 of the 19 evaluable patients (52.6%). Cardiac arrest occurred in six patients (19.4%), and two patients died (6.5%). Causality was classified as probable/likely in five patients (16.1%), possible in 23 (74.2%), and unlikely in three (9.7%). Coronary events temporally associated with ED consumption predominantly affected young men, involved heterogeneous mechanisms, and were associated with potentially severe outcomes. The frequent presence of coexisting risk factors and limited causal evidence preclude definitive attribution of these events to ED consumption. Prospective controlled studies are needed to clarify the independent cardiovascular risks associated with ED consumption.
journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
title: Energy Drink Consumption and Premature Coronary Events: Two Case Reports and a Systematic Patient-Level Review of 31 Published and Newly Reported Patients.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy is an emerging treatment for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism. We report outcomes from an Australian cohort.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis compared patients with intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, defined according to the 2019 European Society of Cardiology guidelines, who were managed before large-bore mechanical thrombectomy implementation (May 2023-April 2024) with those treated with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (May 2024-October 2025) at a teaching hospital within a multidisciplinary pulmonary embolism response team framework. The primary endpoint was procedural feasibility and safety. Secondary endpoints included hemodynamic changes, intensive care unit utilization and 30-day mortality.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients were included: 24 treated with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (median age 66.5, interquartile range 51.8-73.0 years; 58.3% male) and 43 treated with anticoagulation and/or thrombolysis (median age 76.0, interquartile range 65.5-82.5 years; 34.9% male). Technical success was 100%. Mean pulmonary arterial pressure decreased from 28.5 ± 8.7 to 21.2 ± 5.6 mmHg (p < 0.001). Heart rate and respiratory rate improved at 24 hours (both p < 0.001), although adjusted analyses showed no significant between-group differences in hemodynamic changes. Intensive care unit length of stay was shorter in the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group (20.1 ± 7.9 vs 32.2 ± 17.3 hours, p = 0.003), with multivariable analysis confirming an independent 43% reduction (exp(β) = 0.57, 95% confidence interval 0.42-0.79, p = 0.001). No major bleeding events or deaths within 30-days occurred in the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group, compared with two major bleeding events (4.7%) and three mortalities (7.0%) in the non-large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group.
CONCLUSIONS: Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy appears to be a safe and feasible treatment modality for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism and was associated with reduced intensive care unit utilization compared with conventional therapies. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies.
title: Large-bore Mechanical Thrombectomy for Treatment of Intermediate-high Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Single-center Australian Experience.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate a salvage method using coronary stent fixation of the left ventricular (LV) lead to manage refractory LV lead dislodgement caused by unfavorable coronary venous anatomy during cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator (CRT-D) implantation, and to evaluate its technical feasibility and clinical value.
METHODS: We retrospectively included three patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) at our center who developed LV lead dislodgement during or early after CRT-D implantation. Conventional methods failed to maintain a stable lead position. A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent was deployed within the target coronary vein to achieve mechanical anchoring of the LV lead via gentle compression against the venous wall. Procedural details, perioperative complications, and follow-up data were collected and analyzed.
RESULTS: All three patients completed stent fixation of the LV lead. No acute severe complications, such as coronary venous rupture, pericardial tamponade, or lead conductor damage, occurred intraoperatively. No significant change in pacing threshold was observed before and after stent deployment. Cases 1 and 2 were followed for 30 and 26 months, respectively, and lead parameters remained stable. Case 3 was followed for only 2 months and then lost to follow-up; lead parameters were stable at that time point. No clinically meaningful improvement in LV ejection fraction (LVEF) was observed in Cases 1 and 2 during follow-up. Because Case 3 was followed for only 2 months, shorter than the usual 6-12-month window for assessing CRT reverse remodeling, functional response could not be evaluated. This procedure constitutes off-label device use; after full stent deployment, the lead position cannot be readjusted. If device-related infection occurs, transvenous lead extraction may be difficult and uncertain, and surgical removal may be required.
CONCLUSIONS: After all conventional methods have failed, stent fixation may serve as a salvage option for refractory LV lead dislodgement caused by unfavorable coronary venous anatomy. This report describes the clinical observations of sirolimus-eluting stent use in this off-label salvage procedure and details the relevant procedural parameters and techniques. However, the sample size is small, and potential long-term risks, including stent fracture, lead insulation damage, and stability of lead electrical parameters, require further evaluation in larger studies. This technique only addresses the mechanical fixation of the lead and does not guarantee functional benefit from CRT.
title: Coronary stent fixation of left ventricular lead during CRT-D implantation: a case series of three patients.

abstract:
UNLABELLED: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) entails a health burden associated with a higher risk of organ ischemia and mortality, which can cause postoperative complications, such as acute kidney injury (AKI) or myocardial injury (MI). However, there is no unified definition of IOH, and the evidence regarding the association between IOH under different definitions and postoperative complications is still limited and uncertain. We searched PubMed, Web of Science and Embase databases from inception to December 24, 2024 and conducted an evidence map and a systematic review. To further confirm the threshold of IOH and explore the relationship between the duration of IOH and AKI/MI, we conducted sub-analyses by threshold of IOH, and dose-response meta-analyses based on the most commonly used threshold. A total of 81 studies involving 686,153 participants were included. We found that the publication rate of IOH and AKI/MI studies has been increasing in the last 10 years. In total, 52 unique studies were included for AKI and 12 studies were included for MI. The corresponding odds ratios (ORs) were 1.10 [95% Confidence Interval (CI), 1.08-1.12] and 1.27 (95% CI, 1.07-1.50), respectively. We further conducted sub-analysis by definition of IOH. The pooled ORs for AKI among mean arterial pressure (MAP) < 65 mmHg, MAP < 60 mmHg, MAP < 55 mmHg and systolic blood pressure (SBP) < 90 mmHg were 1.09 (95% CI, 1.04-1.13), 1.04 (95% CI, 1.00-1.07) , 2.22 (95% CI, 1.37-3.60) and 1.10 (95% CI, 0.99-1.23), respectively. The pooled ORs for MI among MAP < 65 mmHg, MAP < 60 mmHg, and SBP < 90 mmHg were 1.22 (95% CI, 0.95-1.57), 1.17 (95% CI, 1.08-1.27), and 2.17 (95% CI, 0.48-9.81), respectively. When the threshold of IOH was 65 mmHg, there was a linear relationship between IOH and AKI. For every 10-minute increase, the risk of AKI in patients with IOH was 12% higher than the risk in patients without IOH. IOH is significantly associated with increased risks of postoperative AKI and MI, with stronger effects at lower MAP thresholds. The linear relationship between IOH duration and AKI risk highlights the need to minimize IOH. Targeted hemodynamic management strategies are essential to reduce postoperative complications, especially in high-risk patients.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s43657-025-00249-2.
title: The Effects of Intraoperative Hypotension on Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury and Myocardial Injury: A Systematic Review and modelling study.

abstract:
AIMS: To review the effects of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and in mixed populations treated with contemporary interventional, surgical and pharmacological therapy.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42025630588) including randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective/retrospective controlled cohort studies (pCCS/rCCS) was performed with total mortality as main endpoint. Additional endpoints were cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal cardiovascular events, and hospital readmissions. Subgroup analysis was performed for age and sex. From 40 included studies, 29 studies encompassing 308 514 patients were eligible for this meta-analysis, including 5 newly identified (published between 11/2018-09/2025) studies with 92 571 patients. In pCCS and rCCS, CR-participation was associated with significantly reduced total mortality in patients with ACS (n = 41 740; pCCS: HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.15-0.69; rCCS: HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.55-0.75) and with CABG (n = 17 998; rCCS: HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.56-0.76). The effects regarding total mortality were similar in sex and age subgroups. Cardiovascular mortality and non-fatal stroke were decreased in ACS and CABG patients. In mixed populations, CR was associated with reduced hospital readmissions for any reason and for any cardiovascular event. Methodological and structural heterogeneity and low patient numbers prevented robust results.
CONCLUSION: Based on observational data, participation in CR is associated with an improved prognosis in current patients after ACS, CABG and mixed populations, similarly for sex and age subgroups. Hence, CR should be an integral part of secondary prevention in those patients. Nevertheless, high-quality studies are needed to increase the CR evidence base further.
title: Beneficial effects of cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery bypass grafting: Real-world evidence from the Cardiac Rehabilitation Outcome Study update (CROS-III).

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a working diagnosis in patients who fulfil the diagnostic criteria for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) but have no coronary artery stenosis ≥50% and no clinically evident alternative diagnosis that adequately explains the presentation. It encompasses heterogeneous coronary mechanisms.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence and clinical characteristics of MINOCA at a tertiary cardiac centre in Bosnia and Herzegovina and to compare demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, electrocardiographic presentation, laboratory parameters and echocardiographic findings with those of patients with obstructive myocardial infarction (OMI).
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre observational study comprised a prevalence analysis and a comparative analysis. For the prevalence analysis, medical records of 2,341 patients admitted to the Intensive Cardiac Care Unit between April 2022 and February 2024 were reviewed, of whom 1,104 fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for AMI. For the comparative analysis, 40 patients with MINOCA identified between January 2020 and February 2024 were compared with a simple random sample of 155 eligible patients with OMI. Demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, electrocardiographic presentation, laboratory parameters and echocardiographic variables were analysed.
RESULTS: MINOCA accounted for 32 (2.9%) MIs in the prevalence analysis. Patients with MINOCA (N = 40) were younger than patients with OMI (N = 155) (52.1 ± 15.2 vs. 59.8 ± 11.7 years; p = 0.005). Among patients with available sex data, female sex was more frequent in the MINOCA group (19 {47.5%}) than in the OMI group (43 {29.9%}; p = 0.037). The MINOCA group had a shorter hospital stay and a lower prevalence of hypertension, dyslipidaemia and active smoking. Diabetes mellitus was numerically less frequent, but the difference was not statistically significant. MINOCA more frequently presented as non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI; 19 {51.4%} vs. 20 {13.9%}; p < 0.001) and was characterised by lower peak troponin T and CK-MB concentrations, higher left ventricular ejection fraction and a lower wall motion score index.
CONCLUSION: MINOCA should be approached as a heterogeneous working diagnosis rather than a uniform final diagnosis. The absence of obstructive coronary artery disease should prompt continued clinical evaluation and a structured, individualised diagnostic approach. Standardised diagnostic pathways and prospective multicentre studies incorporating comprehensive imaging and long-term clinical follow-up are needed to refine risk assessment and guide management.
title: Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Myocardial Infarction With Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries Compared With Obstructive Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Tertiary-Centre Study.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: It remains unclear whether endoscopic intervention affects the prognosis of patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) complicated by gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). This study aimed to evaluate the association between endoscopic intervention and the risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality in patients with AMI complicated by GIB.
METHODS: The study had a single-center retrospective cohort design and included consecutive adult patients with AMI complicated by GIB who were hospitalized at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2020 and February 2026. The patients were divided into an endoscopic intervention group and a no-endoscopic intervention group according to whether or not they underwent endoscopic intervention during hospitalization. Baseline differences between the two groups were further addressed using propensity score methods. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. For the primary survival analysis, follow-up began at recognition of GIB, and endoscopic intervention was modeled as a time-varying exposure in Cox regression. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used as a sensitivity analysis to address measured baseline confounding. The secondary outcome was serious in-hospital clinical adverse events after GIB.
RESULTS: A total of 155 hospitalized patients with AMI complicated by GIB were included in the study (endoscopy group, n = 57; non-endoscopy group, n = 98). In the adjusted time-varying Cox regression model using the recorded intraday times, endoscopic intervention was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.478, 95% confidence interval 0.240-0.951, P = 0.035). In the adjusted 24-hour landmark analysis, the association was directionally similar but did not reach statistical significance (hazard ratio 0.433, 95% confidence interval 0.184-1.020, P = 0.056). In the propensity-score-matched cohort, endoscopic intervention remained associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality after further adjustment for residual imbalance (adjusted hazard ratio 0.346, 95% confidence interval 0.152-0.786, P = 0.011). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in serious in-hospital clinical adverse events after GIB (odds ratio 1.340, 95% confidence interval 0.660-2.724, P = 0.406).
DISCUSSION: In this retrospective cohort, endoscopic intervention was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality in patients with AMI complicated by GIB, although residual confounding and the uncertainty observed across complementary analyses should be considered when interpreting this association.
title: Endoscopic intervention is associated with a lower risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by gastrointestinal bleeding.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: antithrombotic therapies are essential in the management of cardiovascular diseases but carry a risk of bleeding complications. This study aimed to describe the use of antithrombotic agents and associated complications in a Cardiac Intensive Care Unit, and to analyse trends in their prescription over time.
METHODS: we conducted a retrospective, observational, descriptive, and analytical study including 1,000 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit of the Institute of Cardiology of Abidjan who received at least one antithrombotic therapy over 12 years. Data were collected in two phases, from 2013 to 2017 and from 2018 to 2024, allowing for the analysis of temporal trends.
RESULTS: the mean age was 59.5 ± 14.1 years. Hypertension was the most prevalent cardiovascular risk factor, and acute coronary syndrome was the main indication for antithrombotic therapy. The proportion of patients receiving antithrombotic treatment increased significantly between the two study periods (76.5% vs 78.7%, p = 0.004). The use of fibrinolytic agents also increased significantly (2.6% vs 6.6%). Adverse events related to antithrombotic therapy were predominantly hemorrhagic, with independent risk factors including advanced age (>65 years), use of fibrinolytics, and concomitant use of multiple antithrombotic agents. In-hospital mortality was higher in patients with hemorrhagic events, with no significant difference between the two periods.
CONCLUSION: antithrombotic therapies remain widely used in Cardiac Intensive Care Units in sub-Saharan Africa, with an increasing trend in prescriptions. Rigorous clinical and laboratory monitoring is essential to improve patient outcomes.
title: [Clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of patients receiving antithrombotic therapy in a cardiac intensive care unit in sub-Saharan Africa: a retrospective comparative study at the Cardiology Institute of Abidjan].

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries a clinically significant risk of late high-grade atrioventricular block (AVB), yet no validated tool exists to predict this complication in Latin-American populations. The D-PACE score was developed in European cohorts for this purpose.
METHODS: In a retrospective cohort of 175 consecutive TAVR procedures at a Colombian center (2012-2025), 141 patients met inclusion criteria for D-PACE validation. The primary outcome was late high-grade AVB (≥Mobitz type II) occurring between 24 h and 30 days post-TAVR. Discrimination, logistic-regression calibration, and decision curve analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Late AVB occurred in 31 patients (22.0%), with 80.6% of events within 72 h. The D-PACE score demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71-0.92; sensitivity 77.4%, specificity 86.4% at a cutoff of 5.5 points; NPV 93.1%). Late AVB rates rose progressively across strata: 5.9% (low-risk, score 0-3), 8.8% (intermediate, 4-5), and 61.5% (high-risk, ≥6), with the high-risk group concentrating 77.4% of all events. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities from 8% to 60%. All four low-risk events occurred among valve-in-valve patients assigned a score of 0 per the original algorithm; excluding this subgroup (N = 114), the AUC rose to 0.91 (95% CI 0.85-0.96) with zero low-risk events. In an exploratory analysis applying the full seven-variable scoring uniformly, including valve-in-valve cases, the AUC was 0.90 (95% CI 0.85-0.95; NPV 96.7%), and 0.91 (95% CI 0.78-1.00) within the valve-in-valve subgroup (N = 27, 4 events).
CONCLUSIONS: Applied as originally specified, the D-PACE score showed good discrimination for late high-grade AVB in this cohort (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71-0.92). The algorithm's automatic low-risk classification of valve-in-valve patients was not supported (14.8% AVB rate). Discrimination was higher both in the sensitivity analysis excluding valve-in-valve cases and in the exploratory analysis applying the seven-variable scoring uniformly, indicating that the scoring variables transfer well while the valve-in-valve exemption warrants reconsideration. These findings provide the first external validation of D-PACE in Latin America.
title: External validation of the D-PACE score for predicting late high-grade atrioventricular block after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a Colombian cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: This study aimed to investigate the association between dynamic lactate clearance and the development of pressure injuries in adult patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support and to evaluate its incremental value for early risk prediction.
MEHODS: This was a retrospective longitudinal cohort study. A total of 317 adult patients receiving ECMO support were enrolled. Lactate concentrations were measured at ECMO initiation and at 6, 24, and 48 h thereafter. Lactate clearance rates were calculated for each corresponding time point. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors for pressure injury development. The predictive performance of lactate clearance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, five-fold cross-validation, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: Pressure injuries occurred in 95 patients (30.0%). Compared with those without pressure injuries, affected patients exhibited significantly lower lactate clearance rates throughout the first 48 h post-ECMO initiation (all P < 0.001). Independent predictors of pressure injury included higher body mass index, elevated vasoactive-inotropic score, VA-ECMO mode, and concomitant renal replacement therapy. The baseline clinical model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.710. Incorporating lactate clearance significantly improved model discrimination, with AUCs increasing to 0.796, 0.825, and 0.899 for the 6-hour, 24-hour, and 48-hour models, respectively. Consistent enhancements in predictive accuracy were confirmed by cross-validation, NRI, and IDI analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Impaired lactate clearance is independently associated with pressure injury development in critically ill adults supported by ECMO. Dynamic monitoring of lactate clearance substantially enhances risk stratification beyond traditional clinical parameters.
title: Dynamic lactate clearance within the first 48 hours predicts pressure injury during ECMO support: a longitudinal cohort study.

abstract: The Watchman FLX versus Novel Oral Anticoagulation for Embolic Protection in the Management of Patients with Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation (CHAMPION-AF) trial compared left atrial appendage (LAA) closure using the Watchman FLX device with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation eligible for long-term anticoagulation. LAA closure demonstrated non-inferiority for the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death, stroke, or systemic embolism and reduced non-procedure-related bleeding. However, interpretation is limited by a permissive non-inferiority margin, reliance on a composite endpoint, exclusion of procedural bleeding from the primary safety outcome, and a numerical excess of ischaemic strokes. Overall, CHAMPION-AF represents a shift in risk profile rather than therapeutic equivalence, supporting LAA closure in selected patients rather than as a routine first-line alternative to NOAC therapy.
journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
title: CHAMPION-AF and left atrial appendage closure: non-inferiority or a trade-off in risk?

abstract:
PURPOSE: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a prevalent and high-mortality valve disease. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is a minimally invasive treatment with outcomes often better than surgery, requiring a multidisciplinary team. This study analyzes outcomes and trends from a high-volume TAVR program in an urban, low-income setting since 2017 to guide future practices.
METHODS: Medical records of patients that underwent TAVR were analyzed retrospectively from 2018 to 2023, dividing them into two cohorts to analyze trends in operative details, complications, length of stay (LOS), and readmission/mortality rates. The learning curve (LC) was assessed by operative time.
RESULTS: Risk-adjusted cumulative sum (RA-CUSUM) analysis identified the transition point at case 76, dividing the cohort into early LC phase group (n = 76) and post-LC phase group (n = 190). Median operative time decreased from 106 to 80 minutes. After adjustment, operative time was 14% shorter in the post-learning-curve cohort (GMR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.96; p = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: Operative time serves as a useful benchmark for institutional maturation. In our program, reaching 76 cases represented a key transition point toward optimized workflows, enhanced efficiency, and improved resource utilization.
journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
title: Developing proficiency in a transcatheter aortic valve replacement program: lessons from a single academic center's learning curve.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Current cardiac biomarkers lack specificity and are limited by instrumental constraints in diagnosing acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Therefore, research has focused on identifying new cardiac biomarkers, e.g., neuropeptide Q (NPQ), associated with the pathophysiological response to myocardial injury. NPQ plays an important role in metabolic regulation and cardiac protection. As there are limited studies on the role of NPQ in ACS, we assessed serum NPQ levels in ACS patients and healthy populations to evaluate serum NPQ's clinical utility in ACS.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We recruited ACS patients (n = 120) and non-hospitalized healthy participants (n = 40). The baseline characteristics and history were recorded. Biochemical investigations, including serum NPQ and heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), were measured using blood samples collected at a mean of 24 hours after the onset of chest pain in ACS patients and at the time of enrolment of healthy participants. Appropriate statistical tests were performed.
RESULTS: ACS patients had significantly higher serum NPQ and H-FABP levels as compared to healthy participants. Serum NPQ levels showed a significant positive correlation with weight, waist circumference, creatine kinase-total, creatine kinase-MB, and H-FABP levels and showed a significant negative correlation with white blood cells (WBCs) and serum high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-C) levels. In univariate logistic regression, weight, WBC, HDL-C, and NPQ levels were linked with ACS outcome in study participants. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, after adjusting for potential confounders, WBC and NPQ were independently linked with ACS outcome in the study population. Receiver operating characteristic curve evaluation showed that the cut-off value of serum NPQ level for prediction of ACS was 2.53 ng/mL, with a specificity of 67.5%, sensitivity of 71%, and an area under the curve of 0.808 (95% CI: 0.731-0.886).
CONCLUSION: The study showed that the reported performance characteristics of serum NPQ levels strictly differentiate between established ACS patients and apparently healthy participants. Its diagnostic utility when facing a standard chest-pain differential diagnosis remains completely unknown. However, our findings should be confirmed by further studies.
title: Clinical Utility of Serum Neuropeptide Q in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Case-Control Observational Pilot Study.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Discordance between resting and hyperemic epicardial physiology is commonbut mechanistically unclear. Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR), a novelindex of vasodilatory capacity, may provide insight. We aimed to characterizethe prevalence and microvascular substrate of FFR/RFR discordance, andwhether MRR is independently associated with discordant phenotypes.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 891 vessels from 723 consecutive patients with paired resting full-cycle ratio (RFR) and fractional flow reserve (FFR) measurements (June 2018-October 2024). Vessels were categorized as concordant or discordant. An operator-selected subset of 210 underwent coronary flow reserve (CFR), index of microvascular resistance (IMR), and MRR assessment. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of each discordant phenotype (FFR-/RFR+ and FFR+/RFR-).
RESULTS: Discordance was present in 195 vessels (22%); 121 (13.6%) FFR-/RFR+ and 74 (8.3%) FFR+/RFR-. Discordance was more common in the LAD (25% vs. 17%, OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.20-2.36, p = 0.003), driven predominantly by the FFR-/RFR+ phenotype (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.56-3.78, p < 0.001). In the microvascular subset (n = 210), reduced CFR (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.59-0.97, p = 0.039) and reduced MRR (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.65-0.97, p = 0.037) were independently associated with the FFR-/RFR+ phenotype, while neither predicted the FFR+/RFR- phenotype. However, among 45 discordant vessels with microvascular data, MRR provided greater discrimination than CFR (AUC 0.712, 95% CI 0.539-0.884 vs. 0.608, 95% CI 0.434-0.783, p = 0.018).
DISCUSSION: These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that impaired microvascular vasodilatory reserve, expressed predominantly as elevated resting flow, may contribute mechanistically to the FFR-/RFR+ phenotype.
title: Microvascular resistance reserve: insights into discordant resting and hyperemic epicardial coronary physiology.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Managing patients with concurrent ampullary carcinoma and severe coronary artery disease (CAD) poses a formidable surgical dilemma. Pancreatoduodenectomy (PD) is a highly invasive procedure with significant bleeding risks, while symptomatic CAD requires urgent revascularization. Standard percutaneous coronary intervention necessitates dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), which increases perioperative hemorrhagic complications. However, delaying PD to complete cardiac treatment risks tumor progression. We present a strategic "ultra-short-interval" staged approach to balance oncological urgency with cardiac safety.
CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 70s presented with severe anemia (Hb 6.6 g/dL) and exertional dyspnea (CCS class III/IV). Investigations revealed stage IB ampullary adenocarcinoma and severe CAD, including 90% stenosis in the left anterior descending artery. To avoid the bleeding risks of DAPT and the systemic trauma of conventional coronary artery bypass grafting, minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass (MIDCAB) was performed. An ultra-short-interval staged approach was strategically planned, with PD scheduled just 7 days after MIDCAB. Despite transient postoperative hematochezia after the first procedure, the patient remained stable. As planned, subtotal stomach-preserving PD was successfully performed 1 week later without cardiovascular events. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 31.
CONCLUSION: This ultra-short-interval staged approach - MIDCAB followed by PD within seven days - is a potent strategy for high-risk candidates. It facilitates essential coronary revascularization without DAPT or cardiopulmonary bypass, thereby minimizing oncological delay and tumor progression risks while mitigating the risk of catastrophic perioperative myocardial infarction or hemorrhage.
keywords: Minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass
title: Ultra-Short-Interval Staged Pancreatoduodenectomy after Minimally Invasive Direct Coronary Artery Bypass for Ampullary Carcinoma in a Patient with Severe Coronary Artery Disease: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic myocarditis is a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy that may clinically mimic acute coronary syndrome and should be considered in patients with non-obstructive coronary arteries, often resulting in diagnostic delay.
CASE SUMMARY: A 27-year-old man presented with recurrent chest pain and was initially misdiagnosed with a panic attack. On admission, laboratory evaluation revealed marked peripheral eosinophilia (1800/mm3), mildly elevated troponin, and increased serum IgE levels. Echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and a large apical intracavitary thrombus. Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed myocardial oedema and circumferential subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement consistent with eosinophilic myocarditis. Extensive aetiological workup was negative. Although endomyocardial biopsy showed non-specific findings, the diagnosis was established through multimodal integration of clinical, imaging, and laboratory data. High-dose corticosteroid therapy and anticoagulation resulted in rapid clinical improvement, recovery of ventricular function, and near-complete thrombus resolution.
DISCUSSION: Eosinophilic myocarditis should be considered in young patients presenting with chest pain and non-obstructive coronary arteries. Multimodality imaging-particularly cardiac magnetic resonance-plays a key role in diagnosis, while early corticosteroid therapy may lead to rapid clinical and functional recovery.
CONCLUSION: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of clinical suspicion for EM in young patients presenting with chest pain and peripheral eosinophilia. A multimodal diagnostic approach integrating cMRI findings, laboratory data, and exclusion of alternative aetiologies is essential when biopsy results are inconclusive. Early immunosuppressive therapy is key to reversing myocardial damage and preventing progression to end-stage heart failure.
keywords: MINOCA (Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries)
title: The clinical chameleon: eosinophilic myocarditis presenting as acute coronary syndrome-a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caval valve implantation (CAVI) using the TricValve system is an emerging treatment option for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in patients who are unsuitable for surgery or orthotopic transcatheter intervention. Lancisi's sign is a classical manifestation of severe TR; however, its resolution after CAVI has not been described.
CASE SUMMARY: An 85-year-old woman with recurrent right heart failure and torrential TR presented with prominent bilateral Lancisi's sign. Echocardiography revealed severe annular dilatation (48 mm), right ventricular dysfunction (TAPSE, 13 mm), and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40%. Owing to prohibitive surgical risk (EuroSCORE II 18.4%; TRI SCORE 14), she underwent successful implantation of 29-mm superior vena cava and 35-mm inferior vena cava TricValve prostheses. At 3 months, Lancisi's sign had completely resolved, NYHA functional class improved from III-IV to I-II, NT-proBNP decreased from 25 000 to 2 000 pg/mL, TAPSE increased from 13 to 20 mm, and no rehospitalization or device-related adverse event occurred. We report a structured single-patient case using clinical examination, echocardiography, invasive hemodynamic assessment, laboratory markers, and 3-month follow-up after bicaval TricValve implantation.
DISCUSSION: Bicaval TricValve implantation resulted in marked symptomatic, biochemical, echocardiographic, and bedside clinical improvements. The resolution of Lancisi's sign may represent a simple marker of hemodynamic recovery after CAVI.
title: Resolution of Lancisi's sign following bicaval TricValve implantation for torrential tricuspid regurgitation: a case report defining a novel bedside marker of haemodynamic recovery.

abstract: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established treatment for chronic neuropathic pain, and patients with an implanted stimulator are presenting with increasing frequency for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We describe an 88-year-old man with a high-frequency (10 kHz) spinal cord stimulator for chronic back pain who underwent transfemoral TAVI under sedation for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. After consultation with the implanting pain service, the stimulator was switched off with the patient's own remote control, which was kept in the procedure room; rapid ventricular pacing was delivered through a bipolar right ventricular lead so that the pacing current was confined to the myocardium and remote from the pulse generator; and external defibrillator pads were positioned away from the generator and the course of the leads. The procedure was uneventful. The patient tolerated the interruption of therapy without clinically significant pain; a new left bundle branch block after valve deployment was identified on an artefact-free trace, stimulation was resumed after the procedure with analgesia equivalent to baseline, and subsequent interrogation confirmed normal device function. The case illustrates the application of a precautionary strategy informed by manufacturer labelling and analogous evidence; because the stimulator was off throughout, it does not establish that any individual measure was necessary. We examine how the hazards of the cardiac catheterisation laboratory differ from those of the operating theatre and propose a structured six-step approach to the management of a spinal cord stimulator during TAVI.
title: Perioperative Management of a Spinal Cord Stimulator During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Case Report.

abstract: Hemoglobin (Hb)-based transfusion triggers are the most commonly used transfusion triggers in clinical practice at present, despite of having many drawbacks. In daily clinical practice, the traditional 10/30 rule (Hb 10 g/dL - hematocrit 30%) has been the most commonly used trigger for blood transfusions. The physiological rationale for this approach is that both Hb and hematocrit are key determinants of arterial oxygen delivery (DO2) and thus the lower limit of oxygen transport and adequate tissue oxygenation. Transfusions with allogeneic red blood cells (RBCs) can be avoided in most patients with Hb thresholds above 7 g/dL with stable hemodynamics. Although physiological transfusion triggers appear to be the most suitable for blood transfusion yet due to the lack of sufficient clinical trials their significance has not been proved. Venous oxygen saturation (SvO2), central venous oxygen saturation, arterial lactate, and near-infrared spectroscopy, when combined together seem to be most useful in avoiding premature blood transfusion. However, large clinical trials are needed to prove their suitability. Blood centers faced a huge challenge in devising a preparedness strategy to withstand COVID-19 outbreak globally. A drastic fall in the red cell inventory was observed as compared to pre-COVID-19 time period due to disproportionate decrease in blood collection and demand. A restrictive transfusion strategy was also applied in hospitals using a threshold for transfusion based on a drop in the Hb level below 7 g/dl in patients with stable hemodynamics. In patients having anemia with acute coronary syndromes, the RBCs transfusion threshold is when Hb levels fall below 8 g/dl and hematocrit below 24%. There was an increase in the demand of convalescent plasma in the initial phase of the pandemic as its benefits were overestimated. The efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma are questionable. Implementation of the most recent evidence-supported transfusion guidelines and eliminating unnecessary transfusions are considered the main goals of patient blood management programs during COVID-19 pandemic.
title: Do we have different transfusion practices in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients?

abstract: Spontaneous coronary recanalization after a Type F dissection may behave as a chronic total occlusion (CTO)-like lesion despite angiographic flow, requiring CTO-level expertise to ensure true lumen wiring and optimal stent deployment. We present the case of a 70-year-old woman who developed spontaneous coronary recanalization after an attempted percutaneous coronary intervention complicated by a Type F dissection, with the recanalized right coronary artery (RCA) developing a complex CTO-like recanalized segment despite restoration of antegrade flow. After treatment with contemporary CTO strategies using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) guidance, symptoms resolved. This case highlights the importance of recognizing the unique morphology and physiology of recanalized vessels and underscores the role of advanced imaging in the evaluation of complex post-dissection coronary anatomy.
title: Spontaneous Coronary Recanalization After Iatrogenic Type F Dissection: A Chronic Total Occlusion-Like Lesion Requiring Advanced Percutaneous Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel monotherapy has shown superior efficacy compared with aspirin after completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, whether treatment effects differ according to overall atherothrombotic risk integrating clinical and angiographic factors remains unclear.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SMART-CHOICE 3 (Smart Angioplasty Research Team: Choice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) randomized trial included patients who completed guideline-directed dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI. Atherothrombotic risk was defined using the a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention and complex PCI. Patients with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention ≥3 or complex PCI were classified as higher risk, and those with a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention <3 without complex PCI were classified as lower risk. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke). Bleeding was defined as Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2, 3, or 5.
RESULTS: Among 5506 patients, 4486 (81.5%) were at higher risk and 1020 (18.5%) were at lower risk. Over a median 2.3 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events was higher in the higher-risk group (6.1% versus 3.1%; hazard ratio, 1.83 [95% CI, 1.17-2.78]; P=0.007). In higher-risk patients, clopidogrel reduced major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events compared with aspirin (4.6% versus 7.4%; hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.50-0.89]; P=0.006), with no difference in lower-risk patients (3.0% versus 3.2%; hazard ratio, 1.03; P=0.945; interaction P=0.242). Bleeding was similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: After completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with lower ischemic risk than aspirin in patients with higher atherothrombotic risk, without increased bleeding.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04418479.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major adverse renal and cardiovascular events (MARCE) have been proposed as a comprehensive end point reflecting both cardiac and renal outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, existing prediction tools lack accuracy and generalizability for this high-risk population.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and externally validate explainable machine learning models and a nomogram for predicting in-hospital MARCE among patients with AMI and CKD.
METHODS: We enrolled patients with AMI and CKD who underwent emergency treatment at the First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University as the discovery cohort and those at Wenzhou TCM (traditional Chinese medicine) Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University as the external validation cohort. Clinical features, including demographic details, comorbidities, laboratory results, echocardiography measurements, procedural details, and medication parameters, were collected for all participants. Important variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression in the training set. We developed extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest, decision tree, and logistic regression (LR) models and evaluated their discrimination, calibration, and classification metrics in the hold-out test set and external cohort.
RESULTS: In the training set, we identified 6 important variables (Killip class, lactate, estimated glomerular filtration rate, use of diuretics, use of beta-blockers, and use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors). In the test set, model discrimination was comparable across XGBoost (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.882, 95% CI 0.816-0.947), LR (AUC 0.875, 95% CI 0.799-0.950), and random forest (AUC 0.870, 95% CI 0.800-0.940), while decision tree showed lower performance (AUC 0.814, 95% CI 0.720-0.886). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values illustrated both global and individual feature contributions in the XGBoost model. A nomogram based on LR achieved an AUC of 0.873 (95% CI 0.714-0.926) in external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study identified 6 important predictors and provided a series of prediction models to enhance risk stratification of MARCE for patients with AMI and CKD. These models might aid in stratifying risk and choosing appropriate therapeutic strategies in the management of patients with AMI and CKD.
keywords: major adverse renal and cardiovascular events
title: Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Major Adverse Renal and Cardiovascular Events in Acute Myocardial Infarction With Chronic Kidney Disease: Algorithm Development and Validation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergence of direct oral anticoagulants as the first-line therapy for stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation has redefined the comparator benchmark for left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO).
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare the efficacy and temporal safety of LAAO vs oral anticoagulation (OAC).
METHODS: Randomized trials of LAAO vs OAC in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation were pooled for incidence rate ratios (IRRs) per patient-year; key endpoints were assessed with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).
RESULTS: Across 6 trials (N = 7,004), LAAO vs OAC was associated with higher ischemic stroke (130 vs 76 events; IRR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.07-1.91; P = 0.01; number needed to harm: 101; GRADE: low); however, this was sensitive to individual trial exclusion and TSA indicated insufficient information (41% of required size). All-cause stroke (152 vs 114; IRR: 1.11; 95% CI: 0.86-1.43; P = 0.43) and all-cause mortality (403 vs 368; IRR: 0.93; 95% CI: 0.78-1.10; P = 0.39) were comparable. Total major bleeding did not differ (IRR: 0.91; P = 0.29), but LAAO significantly reduced nonprocedural major bleeding (194 vs 232; IRR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.55-0.91; P = 0.01; number needed to treat: 19; GRADE: high) and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (145 vs 303; IRR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.39-0.58; P < 0.001; number needed to treat: 15).
CONCLUSIONS: LAAO significantly reduces nonprocedural major bleeding (TSA-confirmed) and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding vs OAC. A trend toward higher ischemic stroke was not TSA-confirmed and was sensitive to trial exclusion; all-cause stroke and mortality were similar. These findings quantify the benefit-harm tradeoff central to LAAO decisions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) complicated by vasoplegia requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) often need escalating vasopressor support and face high mortality. Norepinephrine equivalent dose (NEE) quantifies vasopressor burden, yet its prognostic value in VA-ECMO remains undefined.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship between NEE and 30-day mortality, identify a clinically relevant NEE threshold, and determine factors associated with high vasopressor burden.
METHODS: This bicentric retrospective study included 572 consecutive patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO. We collected vasopressor regimens, NEE trajectories, and hemodynamic parameters at predefined intervals. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response linearity. Maximally selected rank statistics with bootstrap validation identified optimal thresholds. Cox models estimated mortality risk. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with high vasopressor burden.
RESULTS: The median NEE at ECMO initiation was 0.30 (IQR: 0.09-0.72) μg·kg-1·min-1; 86.2% received norepinephrine. NEE showed a linear dose-response with mortality (HR: 1.06 per 0.1 μg·kg-1·min-1 increment; 95% CI: 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001). A threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 identified high vasopressor burden with elevated 30-day mortality (61.8% vs 42.6%; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.11-1.81; P = 0.005). Factors associated with high vasopressor burden included mechanical ventilation (OR: 2.96; 95% CI: 1.08-8.07), prior epinephrine use (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.12-3.14), renal replacement therapy before VA-ECMO (OR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.02-3.03), baseline lactate (OR: 1.05 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 1.01-1.09), and lower Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score (OR: 0.96 per point; 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Left ventricular unloading was inversely associated (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.34-0.87).
CONCLUSIONS: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.
