abstract: Suspected myocardial infarction in patients with acute chest pain at rest is one of the most common diagnostic categories leading to emergency hospital admission and emergency department overcrowding worldwide. Efforts are being made to improve the efficiency of currently used triage and diagnostic work-up strategies. Despite major advances in recent years with the use of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, challenges still exist regarding how to accurately and rapidly rule out or rule in myocardial infarction, as current strategies are relatively slow due to the need for serial troponin measurements. The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommend a 0 h/1 h or a 0 h/2 h high-sensitivity troponin diagnostic algorithm, instead of the previously suggested 0 h/3 h diagnostic protocol, to reduce the time required to discharge patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction. The ESC endorsed algorithms are not without difficulty, and alternative ways of improving triaging have been proposed, particularly a dual biomarker rule-out strategy involving the combined measurement of copeptin and troponin. Supporters of the dual biomarker strategy argue that a timely optimized algorithm can potentially allow the safe rule-out of myocardial infarction earlier than currently used strategies. In the present Great Debate article, two expert teams discuss the 'pros' and 'cons' of implementing single vs dual biomarker strategies for the rule-in and rule-out of myocardial infarction, under the moot topic 'A dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome'. They address in detail many of the controversial issues currently affecting everyday clinical practice and provide insightful comments on how to best triage patients presenting with suspected acute myocardial infarction.
title: Great debate: a dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coexistence of severe aortic stenosis (AS) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently encountered in contemporary practice, particularly amongst elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combined with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an alternative strategy, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the reference treatment for these patient groups. The introduction of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves (RDAV) has considerably expanded the surgical armamentarium by facilitating implantation and reducing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp times. Appropriate application of these technologies requires specific technical considerations that ultimately influence operative planning and execution.
AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes contemporary evidence associated with the use of sutureless and RDAVs in combined CABG and SAVR procedures. To ensure relevant literature is included, a literature search across PubMed and ScienceDirect has been carried out, spanning the last 20 years, utilizing relevant medical subject headings (MeSH) terms and keywords.
EXPERT OPINION: As evidence on sutureless and RDAVs technologies continues to accumulate, with associated advancements in perioperative planning, these valves are expected to become valuable adjuncts in combined procedures, by minimizing operative burden while also allowing for robust, aortic valve pathology correction.
title: Aortic valve replacement and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting: technical considerations in the era of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prompt immunosuppressive therapy is recommended for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis; however, the optimal timing in asymptomatic patients remains uncertain.
CASE SUMMARY: A woman in her 60s receiving adjuvant pembrolizumab for melanoma developed asymptomatic cardiac troponin I (cTnI) elevation (93 pg/mL) before her ninth cycle. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging met diagnostic criteria for myocarditis; however, immunosuppressive therapy was withheld because of the absence of symptoms and mild cTnI elevation. One week later, she developed symptomatic myocarditis with a marked cTnI increase (4,115 pg/mL), requiring intensive care, corticosteroid pulse therapy, and temporary mechanical circulatory support.
DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that asymptomatic immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis can progress rapidly despite seemingly low initial risk, underscoring the importance of ongoing risk assessment following diagnosis.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Early diagnosis alone may not be sufficient to prevent disease progression. Risk stratification and timely intervention during the presymptomatic phase may improve patient outcomes.
title: Early Diagnosis, Delayed Treatment, and Fulminant Progression of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis.
Intravascular ultrasound guidance for complex percutaneous coronary intervention: still useful or eventually obsolete?

abstract: Echocardiographers (ECs) often stand close to the patient during structural heart interventions (SHIs) and may receive higher occupational radiation exposure than interventional cardiologists (ICs). Previous studies have relied on cumulative dose measurements, leaving the per-event determinants of occupational radiation dose poorly characterized. We quantified the per-event personal dose equivalent rate at a 10-mm depth [Hp(10)] for ECs and ICs during SHIs and identified its determinants. We prospectively analyzed 37 SHI cases (20 mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair procedures and 17 left atrial appendage occlusion procedures) at a single center between March 2024 and March 2025. The EC and IC each wore two semiconductor dosimeters (on the front and side of the neck) sampling at 1 Hz, and the higher reading was used for analysis. Per-event Hp(10) rates were calculated by integrating dosimetry data, radiation dose structured report information, and video-based shielding labels. A prespecified linear mixed-effects model with a case-level random intercept assessed X-ray output, beam geometry, operator shielding, and C-arm angulation as candidate determinants for each operator. Among 3,222 exposure events, the EC-to-IC ratio of the Hp(10) rate was 2.3 during fluoroscopy and 3.8 during cine acquisition (both p < 0.001). In the multivariable model, log10(Ka,r rate), protocol, C-arm angle, source-to-detector distance, field of view, and operator shielding were independent predictors of the Hp(10) rate for both operators. The EC experienced substantially higher per-event Hp(10) rates than the IC, particularly during cine acquisition. Operator-specific shielding strategies and per-event optimization of X-ray output are warranted.
title: Quantifying per-event dose-equivalent rates of echocardiographers and interventional cardiologists during structural heart interventions.

abstract: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.
title: Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comorbidity scores such as the Charlson and Elixhauser indices are widely used for risk adjustment in health-economic and clinical outcomes research. Yet the existing weighting schemes, originally designed for mortality prediction, may no longer reflect today's patient populations or perform equally well across diverse outcomes. This study aimed to reweight both indices using a data-driven approach and to evaluate their predictive validity for multiple clinical and health-economic outcomes.
METHODS: Using administrative data from a large tertiary care teaching hospital in Germany (N = 198,819 hospitalizations), we applied adaptive lasso regression to recalibrate the Charlson (Deyo weights) and Elixhauser (van Walraven weights) comorbidity indices. Reweighting was performed for in-hospital mortality as the development endpoint. Penalized coefficients were converted into integer-based weights. Model performance was assessed for three dichotomous endpoints (in-hospital mortality, severe bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation) and two continuous outcomes (length of hospital stay, total reimbursement). External validation was performed in three independent cohorts: Elective endometrial cancer (N = 85,204), interventional left atrial appendage closure (N = 28,039), and emergency ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI; N = 248,062). AUC, R², and RMSE were used as complementary measures of discrimination and predictive accuracy. Pooled relative improvements of AUC, R², and RMSE across the three validation cohorts was calculated using random effects meta-analyses.
RESULTS: Reweighting consistently improved predictive performance across endpoints and cohorts, with modest absolute gains for in-hospital mortality and more pronounced gains for severe bleeding and continuous outcomes. When analysing in-hospital mortality in the three validation cohorts, the reweighted Charlson improved AUC from 0.679 to 0.714 in left atrial appendage closure, 0.588 to 0.594 in STEMI, and 0.798 to 0.810 in endometrial cancer (pooled relative increase: 2.05% [95% CI 0.56-3.53]); the reweighted Elixhauser showed larger gains, particularly in STEMI (0.708 to 0.766) and left atrial appendage closure (0.780 to 0.818; pooled relative increase: 4.86% [0.07-9.65]). The Elixhauser reweighting demonstrated consistently larger gains for severe bleeding (pooled AUC increase: 6.57% [4.23-8.92]). For continuous outcomes, the reweighted Elixhauser index yielded the largest gains in explained variance, with a pooled relative R² increase of 39.66% [33.72-45.60] for total reimbursement. Corresponding reductions in RMSE were modest and often not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Adaptive lasso reweighting consistently enhances the predictive validity of the Charlson and Elixhauser indices across both clinical and health-economic endpoints. Our multi-endpoint evaluation shows consistent performance gains across the three examined German validation cohorts, offering a practical basis for risk adjustment in health-economic studies using German claims data. Because development and validation were based exclusively on German data and a single coding system (ICD-10-GM), international validation across other coding systems and healthcare systems is required before broader applicability can be assumed.
title: Data-driven reweighting of the Charlson and Elixhauser comorbidity indices using German claims data: development for in-hospital mortality only, external validation across clinical and health-economic outcomes.

abstract: The paradigm of STEMI/NSTEMI (ST segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction/Non-ST segment Myocardial Infarction) is being supplanted by the new OMI (Occlusion Myocardial Infarction) ideology to better capture those patients who do not present with classic ST segment elevation on initial and even subsequent electrocardiograms (ECGs) but still represent patients with myocardium at risk from coronary artery occlusion and would benefit from timely, less than 2-hour, percutaneous coronary intervention. The first needle in the haystack from this case report was the prompt recognition of evolving "South Africa Flag" ECG changes of OMI in the setting of possible allergic reaction and its subsequent treatment, also known as Kounis syndrome, which represents the second possible but unconfirmed needle.
title: Two Needles in a Haystack: Acute Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Presenting With South Africa Flag Sign Possibly Due to Kounis Syndrome-A Review and Case Report.

abstract: Ischemic heart disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Its diagnosis largely relies on detecting dynamic changes in the ST segment of the electrocardiogram (ECG). However, alterations in other ECG waves and intervals have also been reported. One factor that is often overlooked is the presence of a prior myocardial infarction and its influence on the myocardial response to a new ischemic event. This study aimed to quantify the magnitude and temporal dynamics of ECG changes during acute myocardial ischemia and to evaluate how a previous infarction modifies these changes. Twelve-lead ECG recordings obtained before and during acute ischemia induced by percutaneous coronary intervention in one of the three major coronary arteries were analyzed. Dynamic heartbeat averages were computed to extract and track features related to ECG depolarization (QRS width, amplitude, and area) and repolarization (T-wave amplitude and area, ST-segment deviation and area, and T-to-QRS amplitude ratio). The results show that, beyond ST-segment deviation, multiple ECG markers evolve over time during coronary artery occlusion. Repolarization features showed earlier and more pronounced alterations than depolarization features, reaching approximately 37-fold and 23-fold changes at 4 minutes of occlusion compared with baseline, respectively. Males showed faster and more sustained ST increases (up to ~47-fold vs ~30-fold in females); older patients had abrupt early ST peaks (~38-fold at ~2 min after occlusion), whereas younger patients exhibited a more gradual increase. Moreover, patients with a prior infarction showed a stronger association between ECG changes and both the extent and severity of ischemia, reaching maximum correlation coefficients of 0.75 for repolarization markers and 0.57 for depolarization markers. Distinct spatial lead patterns were also identified according to the occluded artery and the presence of a prior infarction. In conclusion, acute ischemia induces dynamic changes across multiple ECG markers beyond the ST segment, where repolarization changes precede and exceed depolarization. These responses are modulated by age and sex; furthermore, prior infarction tightens their correlation with ischemic burden and alters spatial lead patterns.
title: Characterizing acute ischemia via ECG: A study of severity, extent, and spatial variability in myocardial infarction and non-infarction groups.

abstract: Prognostication after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) predominantly relies on characteristics available before or at initiation of extracorporeal support. We investigated whether the early metabolic response to extracorporeal reperfusion provides complementary information on subsequent recovery. We retrospectively analyzed 91 patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated with ECPR. Lactate was assessed before and 12 h after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, successful ECMO weaning, cerebral edema/hypoxic brain injury, and favorable neurological survival. Associations were adjusted for low-flow duration. Twelve hour lactate was lower in survivors than nonsurvivors (5.45 vs. 9.04 mmol/L; p = 0.002), whereas prereperfusion lactate did not differ. In paired measurements (n = 38), mortality discrimination increased from an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.47 before reperfusion to 0.80 at 12 h. Each 5 mmol/L higher 12 h lactate was associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR] = 2.73), lower odds of ECMO weaning (OR = 0.44), and cerebral edema/hypoxic injury (OR = 2.07) after low-flow adjustment. Early metabolic response after extracorporeal reperfusion was associated with survival and both circulatory and cerebral recovery. Dynamic post-reperfusion physiology may provide complementary information beyond static pre-reperfusion assessment.

title: Dynamic Early Postreperfusion Physiology Is Associated With Organ Recovery After Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid identification of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain remains challenging. Tongue capillary refill time (CRT) and tongue imaging may reflect systemic perfusion, but their value in ACS is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of standardized tongue-derived perfusion, macroscopic, and imaging parameters for identifying ACS.
METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 208 consecutive adult ED patients presenting with chest pain. Standardized tongue imaging and tongue CRT were assessed. A separate 20-patient pilot assessed interobserver reliability using ICC and kappa coefficients. Blinded ACS adjudication used clinical findings, serial high-sensitivity troponin measurements, electrocardiography, imaging studies, specialist consultations, and follow-up data. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed.
RESULTS: Among 208 patients, 61 (29.3%) had ACS: 16 STEMI, 41 NSTEMI, and four unstable angina cases. Tongue CRT was significantly prolonged in ACS patients (2.6 [2.2-2.9] vs. 1.3 [1.1-1.6] seconds; p<0.001). Tongue CRT demonstrated excellent discrimination for ACS (AUC 0.941, 95% CI 0.903-0.980), outperforming the HEART score (0.860), admission troponin (0.831), and TIMI score (0.788). A CRT threshold ≥2s yielded 86.9% sensitivity and 93.2% specificity. Tongue CRT and macroscopically dry tongue remained associated with ACS after adjustment (both p<0.001). Quantitative RGB and HSV parameters showed no significant between-group differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Standardized tongue CRT showed excellent discrimination for ACS in this cohort, in which most ACS cases were myocardial infarction. Its diagnostic value in unstable angina and incremental clinical utility remain unestablished. External validation is required before routine clinical use.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
title: Tongue capillary refill time and imaging parameters for acute coronary syndrome identification: A prospective ED study.

abstract: We report the case of a patient with late-onset inverse decremental conduction following transcatheter aortic valve replacement. We emphasize the importance of recognizing this phenomenon, as it may predict progression to advanced atrioventricular block and the need for permanent pacemaker implantation.
title: Late-onset inverse decremental conduction after TAVR: Cause for concern?
Faster troponin, same time in the emergency department: what is next for acute coronary syndrome assessment?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: After out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), deciding which patients without ST-segment elevation warrant emergency coronary angiography is difficult, as standard electrocardiogram (ECG), troponin, and echocardiography are limited in the early post-arrest window. We aimed to develop a sequential rule-based decision tree to identify post-ROSC patients in whom acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is unlikely to be the arrest etiology.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with OHCA were divided into development (2020-2024; n=329) and temporal validation (2025; n=71) cohorts. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECGs were analyzed by a deep-learning platform generating ten digital biomarkers. Five candidate biomarkers were combined into a rhythm-stratified sequential decision tree under a zero false-negative constraint; its performance was compared with that of individual biomarkers and validated in the temporal cohort.
RESULTS: The tree classified 171/329 (52.0%) and 32/71 (45.1%) patients in the development and validation cohorts, respectively, as "ACS not likely," with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified at any node. Yield concentrated in the non-shockable subgroup, in which the model excluded 169/261 (64.8%) non-ACS cases (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], 0.824), outperforming each individual biomarker. In the shockable subgroup, which carries a high pretest probability of ACS, 38/40 patients (95.0%) were retained as "ACS not excluded."
CONCLUSIONS: A rhythm-stratified, rule-based decision tree combining AI-assisted ECG-derived biomarkers classified approximately half of post-OHCA patients as "ACS not likely" with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified, principally in the non-shockable subgroup. This transparent, bedside-deployable framework warrants prospective multicenter evaluation.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted, Electrocardiogram-Derived, Sequential Rule-Based Decision Tree for Exclusion of Acute Coronary Syndrome as the Etiology of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract: Snakebite envenomation is a critical public health issue, with Naja kaouthia representing a species of high medical importance. Despite its neurotoxic potential, the ontogenetic variability of its venom remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated three distinct captive broods across multiple developmental stages. Analysis of venom protein profiles (via SDS-PAGE and RP-HPLC) and enzymatic activities (, LAAO, proteases, and hyaluronidase) revealed that venom composition is strongly influenced by brood origin and age. A consistent ontogenetic pattern was observed: juvenile venoms were characterized by higher-molecular-weight components and elevated proteolytic, hyaluronidase, and LAAO activities, whereas adult venoms exhibited a progressive accumulation of low-molecular-weight proteins and increased activity. These findings highlight a progressive, time-dependent transition in venom composition and functionality, underscoring the value of longitudinal studies across developmental stages. Such ontogenetic characterization offers relevant translational insights, as age-related variations in toxin profiles may inform antivenom formulation strategies and provide useful guidance for bioprospecting efforts seeking specific bioactive compounds across distinct developmental stages.
title: A longitudinal multi-brood study reveals a developmental shift toward dominance of low-molecular-weight toxins in monocled cobra (Naja kaouthia) venom.

abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Osimertinib provides durable progression-free survival in EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance is inevitable. Histologic transformation to small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a recognized resistance mechanism, typically presenting with widespread metastatic disease and a poor prognosis. Optimal post-transformation treatment strategies have not been established.
CASE REPORT: We report a patient with EGFR exon 19 deletion-positive lung adenocarcinoma who achieved prolonged disease control on osimertinib for mediastinal lymph node recurrence before developing a new endobronchial lesion in the left main bronchus. Rigid bronchoscopic resection and temporary airway stenting relieved the critical obstruction. Pathologic examination confirmed SCLC, and immunohistochemistry of both the initial adenocarcinoma and the endobronchial lesion demonstrated concordant p53 over-expression and loss of Rb expression, supporting a clinical diagnosis of probable histologic transformation. The patient was bridged to sequential chemoradiotherapy, followed by successful stent removal and the resumption of osimertinib, resulting in long-term disease control exceeding four years.
CONCLUSION: An individualized, multidisciplinary approach comprising rigid bronchoscopic resection, temporary airway stenting, chemoradiotherapy, and osimertinib resumption may achieve prolonged disease control in locoregionally confined SCLC arising during osimertinib therapy. Further case accumulation is warranted to establish optimal treatment strategies.
title: Long-term Disease Control After Probable Endobronchial Small-cell Transformation During Osimertinib Therapy for EGFR-mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma.

abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Takayasu arteritis (TAK) is a rare, chronic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly affecting young women, characterized by progressive stenosis and occlusion of the aorta and its major branches. Despite advances in biologic therapy, refractory disease with recurrent vascular complications remains a significant clinical challenge. Molecular hydrogen-based adjuvant (HydroBox) therapy has emerged as a promising adjuvant approach owing to its antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties. This report aims to describe the long-term clinical course and therapeutic outcomes of a patient with refractory TAK managed with sustained tocilizumab and HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy over 11 years.
CASE REPORT: We report the case of a 25-year-old female with refractory TAK first diagnosed at age 13, presenting with sudden vision loss, dizziness, and pulseless upper extremities. Disease course was complicated by extensive great-vessel involvement, multiple cerebral infarctions, and recurrent in-stent restenosis despite ongoing interleukin-6 (IL-6) blockade. Over 50 courses of tocilizumab (Actemra) were administered from 2014 onward, combined with multiple percutaneous transluminal angioplasty and stenting procedures. HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy was subsequently introduced as an adjunctive treatment. During continued follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable with sustained suppression of inflammatory markers and favorable cerebrovascular findings on serial imaging.
CONCLUSION: This 11-year case report documents the feasibility of sustained long-term tocilizumab therapy combined with adjunctive HydroBox therapy in a patient with refractory TAK. Despite extensive multi-vessel involvement, recurrent in-stent restenosis, and prior cerebrovascular ischemia, the patient achieved progressive hemodynamic stabilization, durable suppression of inflammatory markers, and continued disease control. The potential immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties of HydroBox-assisted therapy warrant further prospective investigation to establish standardized protocols and confirm efficacy in larger cohorts.
title: Sustained Tocilizumab and Adjunctive HydroBox Therapy in Refractory Takayasu Arteritis: An 11-year Case Report.

abstract: PET myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) provides excellent diagnostic and prognostic performance for ischemic heart disease. It offers multiparametric evaluation of myocardial perfusion, left ventricular function at rest and peak stress, coronary calcium (on PET/computed tomography scanners), and myocardial blood flow, which can diagnose epicardial and microvascular coronary disease, stratify risk, and guide management patients with known or suspected ischemic heart disease. The purpose of this article is to deliver a practical approach of PET MPI techniques and interpretation.
title: Cardiac PET Imaging in Coronary Artery Disease: Myocardial Perfusion and Flow Reserve Assessment.

abstract: Severely calcified coronary artery disease complicates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) by limiting lesion compliance, balloon expansion, stent delivery, and optimal stent deployment. This review compares intravascular lithotripsy (IVL), rotational atherectomy (RA), and orbital atherectomy (OA), focusing on their mechanisms, procedural characteristics, comparative evidence, and disparities in access. RA uses a high-speed diamond-coated burr to ablate calcified plaque, whereas OA uses an eccentrically mounted diamond-coated crown to modify calcium through orbital motion. IVL delivers acoustic pressure waves that fracture superficial and deep calcium without mechanically removing plaque. Recent randomized trials, including ROTA.shock, DIRO, and the three-arm ROLLER COASTR-EPIC22 trial (RA, IVL, and excimer laser coronary angioplasty [ELCA]), suggest that IVL achieves stent expansion comparable to RA in balloon-crossable lesions, while RA produced greater stent expansion than OA in one small trial, without established clinical superiority. However, available comparative studies remain limited by small sample sizes and reliance on imaging-based rather than clinical endpoints. Beyond procedural efficacy, contemporary U.S. data indicate disparities in the use of atherectomy and IVL associated with socioeconomic status, race, sex, insurance status, income, and geographic region. These disparities suggest that access to advanced calcium-modification technologies remains inequitable among patients with potentially treatable disease. Expanding equitable access will require improved reimbursement, referral pathways, regionalization of complex PCI, and broader availability of advanced devices at hospitals serving underserved populations. Future research should integrate comparative clinical outcomes with evaluation of the health-system and socioeconomic factors influencing technology access.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions

title: Beyond calcium modification: Comparative evidence and disparities in access to intravascular lithotripsy, rotational atherectomy, and orbital atherectomy.

title: Beyond mortality prediction after mitral TEER: Which risks remain modifiable?

abstract: Statins produce marked reductions in total and LDL cholesterol, C-reactive protein (CRP), and help prevent stroke, re-infarction, and subsequent risk of death. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the role of atorvastatin in comparison with rosuvastatin in lowering levels of inflammatory biomarkers and lipid parameters in patients with ACS. Online databases were searched, and results from random-effects meta-analysis are presented as weighted mean differences (WMDs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. The outcomes were assessed at the short-term (≤1 month) and long-term (>3 months) follow-up. A total of 15 studies (13 RCTs and 2 observational studies) were included. The level of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (P = 0.13), oxidized LDL (P = 0.94), and long-term HDL-C (P = 0.28) showed no significant difference between the two statin groups. No significant differences were observed between atorvastatin and rosuvastatin in total cholesterol and LDL-C at short-term or long-term follow-up. A significant decrease in CRP levels (WMD 4.08; 95% CI 1.53-6.63; P = 0.002; I2 = 98%) and a significant rise in HDL-C (WMD -1.15; 95% CI -1.99 to -0.32; P = 0.007; I2 = 39%) was reported in the rosuvastatin group compared to the atorvastatin group in the short-term. Atorvastatin was associated with a significant reduction in triglycerides at short-term follow-up (WMD -8.69; 95% CI -14.97 to -2.40; P = 0.007; I2 = 35%), while the overall long-term comparison was borderline and did not reach conventional statistical significance. Our findings suggest that rosuvastatin may provide greater short-term reductions in CRP and modest increases in HDL-C compared with atorvastatin; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity and the absence of significant differences at longer follow-up.
title: Effect of Atorvastatin and Rosuvastatin on Lipid Parameters and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: The comparative effectiveness of catheter-based mechanical thrombectomy in intermediate to high-risk acute PE remains uncertain. We reviewed comparative evidence to determine how thrombectomy performs against anticoagulation alone. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through September 13, 2026. We selected adult studies that compared mechanical thrombectomy plus anticoagulation with anticoagulation alone in intermediate to high-risk PE. Random-effects pooling was supplemented by sequential study removal, influence assessment, and Baujat plots. Seven studies including 9371 participants were eligible: 2 randomized trials and 5 cohort studies. Thrombectomy was associated with fewer 30-day deaths (odds ratio [OR], 0.28; 95% CI, 0.17-0.47) and a greater improvement in RV/LV ratio (mean difference, -0.25; 95% CI, -0.36 to -0.13). The groups did not differ significantly in bleeding (OR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.57-1.18) or PE-related mortality (OR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.22-7.28). ICU and hospital stays were not significantly reduced, and these endpoints varied substantially between studies. Mortality and bleeding were less sensitive to individual reports than length-of-stay outcomes. Thrombectomy was linked to lower early all-cause mortality and more favorable right ventricular recovery without a significant bleeding excess. Its effects on PE-specific death and resource use remain uncertain. More adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define which intermediate to high-risk patients should receive the procedure.
title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Mechanical Thrombectomy and Anticoagulation in Intermediate- to High-Risk Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmia (VA) substantially contributes to sudden cardiac death in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits; however, their influence on post-AMI ventricular arrhythmogenesis remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,873 patients with concurrent AMI and T2DM admitted between January 2018 and December 2022. Using propensity score matching (1:2, nearest-neighbor), 277 GLP-1RA users were matched with 554 controls. The primary endpoint was incident VA. Cox proportional hazards regression, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), Firth's penalized likelihood regression, and Fine-Gray competing risk analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 2.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a reduced risk of VA (adjusted HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.37-0.98, P = 0.040), MACE (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96, P = 0.030), cardiovascular death (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.32-0.86, P = 0.010), and heart failure rehospitalization (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.26-0.68, P < 0.001). All-cause mortality showed a non-significant trend (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59-1.18, P = 0.310). Firth's penalized regression confirmed the primary finding (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.36-0.95, P = 0.029). The Fine-Gray model yielded a subdistribution HR of 0.63 (95% CI 0.39-1.02, P = 0.058) after accounting for competing mortality risk. The 90-day landmark analysis (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.39-1.06, P = 0.085) and the time-varying exposure Cox model (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.40-1.08, P = 0.097) were directionally concordant but did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA therapy was associated with a lower risk of VA and improved cardiovascular outcomes in patients with AMI and T2DM. Because several sensitivity analyses, including the Fine-Gray competing-risk, landmark, and time-varying models, were borderline non-significant, these findings should be interpreted with caution and regarded as hypothesis-generating, warranting confirmation in prospective randomized trials.
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and the risk of ventricular arrhythmia in patients with acute myocardial infarction and type 2 diabetes mellitus: a propensity score-matched cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) often results in microvascular injury, including intramyocardial haemorrhage (IMH), despite successful reperfusion. This study explored whether the stress hyperglycaemic ratio (SHR) is independently associated with IMH in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI).
METHODS: We screened 650 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent pPCI at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University (2019-2024). After exclusions, 508 patients were included in the final analysis. SHR was calculated as admission glucose (mmol/L) divided by estimated average glucose from HbA1c converted to mmol/L: ([28.7 × HbA1c (%) - 46.7] ÷ 18). IMH was evaluated with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging performed within 3-7 days post-pPCI using T2*-mapping sequences. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of IMH, and Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the predictive performance of SHR.
RESULTS: Higher SHR was independently associated with IMH. Among 508 patients, IMH was present in 179 (35.2%). Patients with IMH had significantly higher SHR (0.87 vs. 0.81, p < 0.001). After adjusting for age, sex, WBC count, and haemoglobin, an elevated SHR remained independently associated with IMH (adjusted OR 1.18; 95% CI 1.07-1.29; p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.625 (95% CI 0.577-0.673, p < 0.001), indicating modest predictive ability, with an optimal cutoff of 0.86 (sensitivity 59.2%, specificity 63.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: SHR is independently associated with IMH in reperfused STEMI patients and may warrant further investigation as a research tool for risk stratification in future studies. These findings support cardiometabolic research in STEMI management strategies.
title: Stress hyperglycaemic ratio is independently associated with intramyocardial haemorrhage in STEMI patients: a cardiac magnetic resonance study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) has become the main myocardial infarction subtype in type 1 diabetes compared to ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), accounting for nearly 80% of myocardial infarction-related hospitalizations. Yet, prior studies in type 1 diabetes have assessed myocardial infarctions as a single entity, potentially overlooking clinically relevant heterogeneity between subtypes in risk assessment. We aimed to study the role of lipids, apolipoproteins, insulin resistance, and the metabolic syndrome in risk stratification of all myocardial infarctions, STEMI and NSTEMI in individuals with type 1 diabetes stratified by the presence of microvascular complications.
METHODS: The current study is an observational follow-up study of 4215 individuals from the Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study. We verified 449 first-ever myocardial infarctions from medical records and death certificates and further categorized them into either STEMI or NSTEMI. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to assess the effect of a comprehensive lipid and apolipoprotein panel and insulin resistance on the risk of all myocardial infarctions, STEMI, and NSTEMI. Risk estimates for all myocardial infarctions were additionally stratified based on the presence of microvascular complications.
RESULTS: For STEMI, apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I) (hazard ratio per 1 standard deviation 0.77 [95% confidence interval 0.60-0.99]; P = 0.043), HDL2 cholesterol (HDL2-C) (0.72 [0.55-0.95]; P = 0.019), and HDL-C/total cholesterol ratio (0.76 [0.59-0.98]; P = 0.035) were associated with reduced risk, while no variables were associated with increased risk. Regarding NSTEMI, apolipoprotein B-100 (ApoB-100) (1.31 [1.15-1.50]; P < 0.001) and ApoB-100 to apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I) ratio (1.29 [1.18-1.41]; P < 0.001) showed the strongest association with an increased risk, while the HDL-C/total cholesterol ratio was associated with reduced risk (0.71 [0.62-0.82]; P < 0.001). In stratified analyses, associations between selected lipid and apolipoprotein variables and myocardial infarction risk appeared stronger among individuals without microvascular complications. Higher estimated glucose disposal rate, indicating lesser insulin resistance, was associated with reduced risk of both STEMI (0.82 [0.73-0.92]; P < 0.001) and NSTEMI (0.92 [0.86-0.99]; P = 0.024).
CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrated that the risk profile between STEMI and NSTEMI differs regarding lipids and apolipoproteins, while insulin resistance was associated with increased risk of both MI subtypes.
title: Lipids and apolipoproteins affect the risk of ST-elevation and non-ST-elevation myocardial infarctions differently in type 1 diabetes: a nationwide finnish cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate in-hospital mortality and to identify predictors of mortality in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) patients receiving veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed data from adult patients who received VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock after CABG at our centre between 2014 and 2025. Among the 10,256 patients who underwent CABG, 74 received ECMO postoperatively. Among these, 33 patients (44.6%) died during ECMO support, 15 patients (20.3%) died after ECMO removal, and 26 patients (35.1%) survived to hospital discharge. For distinguishing hospital mortality, the lactate level at 24 h after ECMO initiation (LAC-T24) (> 4.35 mmol/L, AUROC: 0.916) performed the best, followed by the lactate clearance at 24 h (LC-T24) (< 55.73%, AUROC: 0.915). Other predictive factors included CKMB activity at 24 h (CKMB-T24) (> 157 U/L; AUROC: 0.848), mean arterial pressure at 24 h (MAP-T24) (< 77.5 mmHg; AUROC: 0.844), SOFA-2 scores (> 11.5; AUROC: 0.835), and the pre-ECMO Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (SOFA-1) (> 10.5; AUROC: 0.815). The best model revealed the pre-ECMO updated SOFA-2 scores (P < 0.001) (OR: 1.793, 95% CI: 1.029-3.124, P = 0.039), LAC-T24 (OR: 1.395, 95% CI: 1.045-1.861, P = 0.024), CKMB-T24 (OR: 1.015, 95% CI: 1.003-1.026, P = 0.013), and MAP-T24 (OR: 0.895, 95% CI: 0.809-0.989, P = 0.029) as independent predictors of hospital mortality after VA-ECMO.
CONCLUSION: In patients receiving ECMO treatment after CABG, in-hospital mortality rates remains high. In this study, LAC-T24, LC-T24, CKMB-T24, pre-ECMO SOFA-1 and SOFA-2 scores were identified as predictors of mortality.
title: Mortality-related predictors in patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism is still debated. Interventional therapy is being increasingly widely applied in clinical practice. Numerous studies have confirmed that interventional therapy is effective. Both catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT) showed improvement in some efficacy outcomes compared with anticoagulation monotherapy. A recent study showed that MT has lower rates of clinical deterioration and/or bailout and postprocedural intensive care unit use compared with CDT, with no difference in mortality or bleeding, which makes the application of MT in clinical practice increasingly widespread. Recently, STORM-PE, the first randomized controlled trial to test the efficacy and evaluate the safety of MT combined with anticoagulation compared with anticoagulation monotherapy for the treatment of intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, showed that treatment with MT combined with anticoagulation resulted in a significantly greater reduction in right ventricular/left ventricular (RV/LV) diameter ratio at 48 h versus anticoagulation monotherapy, with comparably low rates of major adverse events in both treatment arms. However, whether MT combined with anticoagulation is more effective than anticoagulation monotherapy needs more evidence, especially in Asian populations.
METHODS: The CAPE study is a currently enrolling national multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing MT with MPA 8F guiding catheter [Cordis (Shanghai) Medical Device Co., Ltd] combined with anticoagulation vs anticoagulation monotherapy. A total of 156 patients with acute intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism stratified by the classification of the latest guideline of European Society of Cardiology (ESC) will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio. The primary efficacy endpoint was reduction of RV/LV diameter ratio assessed by computed tomographic angiography (CTPA) at 48 h. The secondary efficacy endpoint was the incidence of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary disease including chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. The primary safety endpoint was serious adverse events including major bleeding through 3 months visit.
DISCUSSION: CAPE is a RCT to compare the short and long efficacy of MT combined with anticoagulation and anticoagulation monotherapy for acute intermediate-high pulmonary embolism. The result will give more evidence for selection of different strategies for physicians.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: CAPE study is registered in Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier (ChiCTR2500095253, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn/clinicalResearch/researchInfo?id=c57630b7-51ec-4b24-83e1-85b9c0a835d6 ). Registered on November 26 2024.
title: Effects of mechanical thrombectomy combined with anticoagulation vs anticoagulation monotherapy for acute intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial (CAPE study, ChiCTR2500095253, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn/clinicalResearch/researchInfo?id=c57630b7-51ec-4b24-83e1-85b9c0a835d6).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies found that glycolysis-related metabolic markers-particularly lactate and glucose-are associated with short-term mortality after myocardial infarction (MI). However, information on glycolysis-wide metabolite alterations and short-term post-MI mortality remains insufficient. Therefore, this study investigated the associations of glucose, lactate, pyruvate, and citrate with short-term mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
METHODS: This study was based on data from 724 STEMI patients enrolled in the population-based Augsburg Myocardial Infarction Registry. Arterial EDTA blood samples were drawn at the start of the catheterization procedure and plasma concentrations of the metabolites were quantified using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy platform developed by Nightingale Health (Finland). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the associations between glycolysis-related metabolites and 28-day mortality. P values were adjusted for multiple testing using the false discovery rate (FDR) method.
RESULTS: Overall, 677 patients survived the first 28 days after hospitalization, whereas 47 died within this period. Elevated plasma levels of glucose, lactate, pyruvate, and citrate were each significantly associated with an increased risk of short-term mortality. In the multivariable logistic regression models, the strongest association was observed for glucose (OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.53-2.88, padj ≤ 0.001) and the weakest association for pyruvate (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.22-2.10, padj = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that metabolic disturbances, reflected by glycolysis-related metabolites, are associated with short-term mortality in STEMI patients, suggesting their potential prognostic value.
title: Associations between glycolysis related metabolites and short-term mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kounis syndrome refers to acute coronary syndrome precipitated by an allergic or anaphylactic reaction that has a slight predominance in male patients. The most frequently reported symptom is chest pain. Kounis syndrome is a rare and frequently underdiagnosed condition that demands a high degree of clinical suspicion. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of type I Kounis syndrome after the Nuss procedure with clinically obscured chest pain.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 32-year-old Taiwanese woman underwent the Nuss procedure and received intravenous Clindamycin and Ketorolac postoperatively. Generalized wheals, pruritus, and shock developed, and she was treated in accordance with the diagnosis of anaphylaxis. Postoperative pain from the Nuss procedure and the use of analgesics masked ischemic chest pain, delaying prompt clinical evaluation. Electrocardiographic findings demonstrated elevation of the ST-segment in the precordial leads V4, V5, and V6 and an elevated high-sensitivity troponin I level. Echocardiography revealed no left ventricular wall motion abnormalities or pericardial effusion. Coronary angiography was omitted because imaging artifacts from the surgical bars introduced during the Nuss procedure limited visual field, compromising its diagnostic value. The high-sensitivity troponin I level improved progressively with conservative treatment. The subsequent hospital course was uneventful, with the patient remaining stable. A diagnosis of Kounis syndrome was established, and the patient was discharged.
CONCLUSIONS: Kounis syndrome is an underdiagnosed disease with newly proposed etiologies but no treatment guidelines. Clinical awareness is essential when treating anaphylaxis given the possibility of concurrent acute coronary syndrome, especially in patients undergoing the Nuss procedure, as chest pain may be masked. Kounis syndrome should be considered alongside other differential diagnoses.
title: Type I Kounis syndrome after the Nuss procedure-diagnostic challenge for thoracic surgeons: a case report.

abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the feasibility, safety, and short-term clinical outcomes of in situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (ISF-TEVAR) employing an electrocautery-connected guidewire combined with a novel, pump-less, extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass for cerebral perfusion in patients with complex aortic arch pathology.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration. Fenestrations were performed with an electrocautery-connected 0.018-inch chronic total occlusion-dedicated guidewire. Patients' demographics, procedural details, perioperative outcomes, and early follow-up data were analyzed, with stratification according to the number of fenestrated supra-aortic branches.
RESULTS: A total of 37 supra-aortic branches were targeted: 3-branch fenestrations in 6 patients (31.6%), 2-branch in 6 patients (31.6%), and single-branch in 7 patients (36.8%). Technical success, defined as successful graft fenestration with patent branches on completion angiography, was achieved in 94.5% (35/37). One failed innominate artery fenestration was managed with chimney-assisted TEVAR, and 1 left subclavian artery fenestration was successfully completed in a subsequent procedure. Operative time increased with procedural complexity (140 ± 12 minutes for 1 branch, 152 ± 10 minutes for 2 branches, and 162 ± 13 minutes for 3 branches; P = .004). No intraprocedural mortality occurred. Two perioperative strokes (10.5%) and 2 in-hospital deaths (10.5%) were recorded, 1 death was due to vertebrobasilar stroke and the other due to retrograde type A aortic dissection with rupture. Median hospital stay was 8 days. During a mean follow-up of 9.2 months, there was no aorta-related mortality, with an overall survival rate of 89.5%. All stented branches remained patent, and 2 endoleaks (10.5%) were successfully treated endovascularly.
CONCLUSION: In situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair using an electrocautery-connected wire combined with a temporary, pressure gradient-driven extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass is a feasible, reproducible, and safe technique for complex aortic arch repair. This fully percutaneous approach ensures continuous cerebral perfusion, demonstrates efficient procedural metrics, and yields favorable short-term outcomes, representing a practical alternative when custom-made devices or hybrid surgical procedures are not available.Clinical ImpactIn situ fenestration-assisted TEVAR combined with a temporary pumpless extracorporeal femoral-carotid bypass enables continuous cerebral perfusion during complex aortic arch interventions without the need for cardiopulmonary bypass or surgical debranching. This technique expands the feasibility of fully endovascular multibranch arch repair in urgent or anatomically challenging cases where custom-made devices are unavailable. For clinicians, this approach offers a practical and reproducible strategy to mitigate cerebral ischemic risk while maintaining procedural efficiency and percutaneous access. This technique may facilitate broader adoption of in situ fenestration by providing a cerebral protection strategy using readily available endovascular equipment.
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
title: In Situ Fenestration-Assisted TEVAR in Patients With Complex Pathology Involving the Aortic Arch.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postprocedural thrombocytopenia is frequently observed after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and surgical aortic valve replacement (sAVR), but its independent prognostic value remains unclear. We investigated whether platelet reduction after TAVI and sAVR independently predicts short-term mortality beyond baseline procedural risk.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients who underwent aortic valve replacement between 2015 and 2020. Sixty-seven patients underwent TAVI and 149 underwent sAVR. Mechanical valve recipients were retained in the overall cohort but excluded from the primary TAVI-sAVR comparison. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to reduce baseline differences between groups. Longitudinal changes in platelet count (PLT), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were evaluated using generalized estimating equation models, and factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: The primary comparative cohort included 67 TAVI and 93 sAVR patients. After overlap weighting, adequate balance was achieved for all measured baseline covariates. Significant treatment × time interactions were observed for PLT (p = 0.001), NLR (p < 0.001), and PLR (p = 0.002). On postprocedural day 3, moderate thrombocytopenia was more frequent after sAVR than TAVI (33.5% vs. 8.3%), whereas normal platelet levels were more frequent after TAVI (45.6% vs. 8.2%; overall p < 0.001). Weighted 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between TAVI and sAVR (12.6% vs. 17.5%, p = 0.487). In Firth regression models, only EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with 90-day mortality.
CONCLUSION: Postprocedural platelet and inflammatory responses showed different temporal patterns after TAVI and sAVR. However, these biomarker changes were not independently associated with 90-day mortality after adjustment, whereas EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with mortality. Serial hematological changes should therefore be interpreted together with baseline clinical risk rather than as isolated prognostic markers.
title: Does thrombocytopenia predict short-term mortality after transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement?
Angiographic ambiguity resolved by intravascular ultrasound: acute distal filling defects after balloon angioplasty for in-stent restenosis.

abstract: To treat acute myocardial infarction (MI), we previously engineered an infusible decellularized extracellular matrix (iECM) biomaterial that reduces vascular permeability and exerts immunomodulatory and pro-reparative effects. To probe the heterogenous contents of iECM and its contribution to infarct localization and downstream biological function, we separated iECM into high and low molecular weight (MW) components. Though mass spectrometry showed similar compositions, biochemical analysis and transmission electron microscopy revealed higher sGAG content within the nanofibrillar high MW, while the globular low MW had more exposed functional groups. These differences translated to a higher binding efficiency of the high MW to ECM proteins and cell surface receptors under flow, while the low MW drove the reduction in vascular permeability. Neither component alone achieved the infarct retention levels of complete iECM, showing that the two components exhibit dependent infarct localization and both are necessary for iECM's overall function. Via single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, both components elicited comparable immunomodulatory and pro‑reparative transcriptional profiles, suggesting that the similarity in composition likely drives the transcriptional response. These findings elucidate the material properties of an intravascularly deliverable ECM biomaterial and how those properties relate to downstream biological behavior, enabling future work investigating nanomaterial mimicry and improvements in material processing and potency.
title: An Infusible Decellularized Extracellular Matrix Material Binds to Vasculature in Infarcted Myocardium and Induces Pro-Reparative Gene Expression Following Acute Myocardial Infarction Through Inherent Avidity and Bioactive Signaling.

abstract:
PURPOSE: No consensus exists on which cardiac phase to use for virtual valve-to-coronary ostium (VTC) distance measurement to predict risk of coronary obstruction in valve-in-valve (ViV). Our study aimed to investigate whether cardiac phase influences VTC measurements in ViV for failing stented surgical heart valves (SHV).
METHODS: All adult patients with stented SHV referred for a pre-planning CT for ViV between 2020 and 2025 were retrospectively eligible. For each patient, VTC was measured for two transcatheter heart valve options at both the right and left coronary ostia. VTC measurements were compared between systole, diastole, and phase with best image quality (best phase). Prevalence of changes in coronary obstruction risk (based on 4-mm cutoff) depending on the phase was assessed. Inter- and intraobserver reliability was evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 398 VTC measurements derived from 116 included patients (69 male, 71 ± 13 years) were evaluated. Best phase was more often diastolic. Median VTCs differed between systole and diastole (P < .001), and systole and best phase (P < .001), but not between diastole and best phase (P = .47) (systole 4.8 [3.1-6.5] mm vs diastole 4.6 [3.1-6.2] mm vs best phase 3.9 [2.5-6.2] mm). Measurements were slightly higher in systole than in diastole (mean difference +0.24 mm, [95% CI: 0.16, 0.32]; P < .001), but similar between diastole and best phase (P = .47). Risk of coronary obstruction changed between systole and diastole in 41 coronary arteries (41/398, 10%). Intra- and interobserver reliability was good-to-excellent.
CONCLUSIONS: VTC measurements differed and were slightly higher in systole than in diastole, which may influence the coronary obstruction risk classification.
journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
title: Influence of Cardiac Phase on Valve-to-Coronary Ostia Distance in Valve-in-Valve Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.
title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.

abstract:
UNLABELLED: Atrioesophageal fistula is a rare but fatal complication of catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation(AF). It may present with infection, dysphagia or other swallowing-related symptoms, neurologic events, and systemic air embolism; coronary air embolism is even less common.
CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old woman was admitted with recurrent palpitations lasting 1 h, approximately 1 month after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation and left atrial appendage closure(RFCA & LAAC). On admission, she was in sinus rhythm and had a normal cardiac troponin level. Four hours after admission, she abruptly became unresponsive and developed fever and severe respiratory abnormalities. Electrocardiography subsequently showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated gas in the mid right coronary artery with TIMI 0 distal flow, and catheter aspiration was performed. Computed tomography (CT) of the head and chest revealed gas at multiple sites, including the intracranial compartment, cardiac chambers, and great vessels. Blood cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus and other streptococci. Given the recent left atrial ablation, acute neurologic and myocardial ischemic manifestations, multisite intravascular gas, and bacteremia with organisms associated with the oropharyngeal or gastrointestinal flora, an atrioesophageal fistula complicated by systemic air embolism was strongly suspected. Her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she developed cardiac arrest and died approximately 27 h after admission.
CONCLUSION: Atrioesophageal fistula and coronary air embolism should be considered in patients who develop fever, impaired consciousness, or acute ST-segment elevation within several weeks of atrial fibrillation ablation. Coronary angiography can directly visualize intracoronary gas and allow catheter aspiration; however, the certainty of an atrioesophageal fistula diagnosis should remain commensurate with the available imaging evidence.
title: Suspected atrioesophageal fistula complicated by coronary air embolism after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: direct angiographic visualization and catheter aspiration in a case report.

abstract: Cardiovascular (CV) disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease, including those evaluated for kidney transplantation. Pretransplant CV screening has traditionally focused on detecting occult coronary artery disease and guiding revascularization to reduce perioperative risk. However, emerging evidence, most notably from the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial, has challenged this paradigm, demonstrating no clear benefit of routine invasive strategies or prophylactic revascularization in stable, asymptomatic patients over optimal medical therapy. Risk assessment in kidney transplant candidates should rely on an integrated clinical evaluation that incorporates symptoms, functional capacity, baseline electrocardiography and echocardiographic findings, and the presence of major CV risk factors. When further evaluation is indicated, stress echocardiography is generally preferred as the noninvasive modality. Invasive coronary angiography should be reserved for patients with cardiac symptoms or findings suggestive of significant ischemia, including reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, regional wall motion abnormalities, or moderate-to-large ischemia on stress testing. Pre-emptive revascularization should be limited to established guideline-based indications, such as left main disease, multivessel disease with reduced ejection fraction, or refractory angina despite optimal medical therapy. Noncoronary CV disorders, including heart failure, valvular disease, and pulmonary hypertension, require systematic assessment and cardiology referral. In conclusion, pretransplant CV assessment is shifting from protocol-driven screening toward individualized, clinical suspicion-based evaluation, prioritizing optimal medical therapy, avoidance of unnecessary testing, and timely access to transplantation.
title: Evolving practices in pretransplant cardiovascular screening: moving toward personalized assessments.

abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a rare cause of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Here, we describe a case of multivessel SCAD in a 48-year-old Indian male who presented with ACS. His echocardiography confirmed a picture of moderate ischemic cardiomyopathy complicated by the presence of an apical clot, and coronary angiography confirmed SCAD in both the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA). He was also found to have an occlusion of the subclavian artery, raising the possibility of vasculitis, including Takayasu arteritis. The patient was managed conservatively with guideline-directed medical therapy for ACS and heart failure, along with anticoagulation for the left ventricular (LV) apical thrombus. He remained hemodynamically stable without recurrent ischemia or arrhythmias and was discharged in stable condition. This case highlights the importance of considering SCAD in ACS presentations and evaluating for associated arteriopathies or vasculitis in patients with multivessel involvement.
title: Double-Vessel Involvement: A Case Report of Simultaneous Left Anterior Descending Artery (LAD) and Right Coronary Artery (RCA) Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection Causing Acute Coronary Syndrome.

journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
title: Comment on "Adequate enrollment of women in cardiovascular drug trials and the need for sex-specific assessment and reporting".

abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is typically characterized by transient left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction with recovery occurring within days to weeks. Persistent regional wall motion abnormalities beyond the expected recovery period are uncommon. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who presented with nausea, vomiting, epigastric discomfort, dyspnea, ST-segment depressions, and markedly elevated high-sensitivity troponin (9,848 ng/L). Coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive coronary artery disease, while echocardiography confirmed TTS with apical akinesis and an LV ejection fraction of 35%. A large hiatal hernia was also identified. Although the patient experienced complete symptomatic recovery and returned to baseline functional status, serial echocardiography demonstrated persistent apical akinesis through four months of follow-up. This case highlights an unusual recovery pattern in TTS and demonstrates that marked troponin elevation can occur despite nonobstructive coronary artery disease.
keywords: takotsubo syndrome vs. acute myocardial infarction
title: Persistent Apical Akinesis Following Takotsubo Syndrome With Marked Troponin Elevation: A Case Report.

abstract: Across the mechanical circulatory support (MCS) spectrum, from temporary devices in acute cardiogenic shock to durable left ventricular assist devices, the right ventricle (RV) and tricuspid valve are often underestimated determinants of outcome. This narrative review centers on the RV-tricuspid unit across advanced heart failure and cardiogenic shock, with MCS-temporary and durable and left-, right-, or biventricular-as its principal setting; transcatheter tricuspid trials conducted largely outside MCS are used as the best available causal evidence on whether correcting tricuspid regurgitation changes symptoms and events, and are explicitly distinguished from MCS-specific observational data. Three fields have advanced largely in isolation: transcatheter tricuspid intervention, right ventricular failure risk stratification, and mechanical support of the failing right heart. This review synthesizes the pathophysiology of the RV-tricuspid unit and its prognostic role in durable LVAD therapy and acute shock. It appraises the arrival of transcatheter tricuspid repair and replacement and the limits of the supporting evidence. It also confronts three persistent controversies: concomitant tricuspid surgery at LVAD implantation, the split between symptom and survival benefit after tricuspid intervention, and the timing of right ventricular support. Throughout, we distinguish established evidence from reasonable inference and untested hypothesis. We propose a unified, RV-first framework (assess the unit, stage the ventricle, time the intervention) that recasts these controversies as testable hypotheses, and we present its treatment triggers as research propositions for stage-stratified trials rather than as validated clinical recommendations.
title: The right ventricle as the Achilles' heel: tricuspid regurgitation and right heart failure in the era of mechanical circulatory support.

abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia. Global Burden of Disease estimates indicate that 52.6 million individuals were living with AF or atrial flutter in 2021, and one in three to one in five persons are expected to develop AF during their lifetime. AF is associated with an increased risk of stroke, systemic thromboembolism, and death. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) is the first-line strategy for preventing AF-associated embolism. However, embolic events still occur in 1%-4% of anticoagulated patients per year, major bleeding occurs in 2%-4% per year, and long-term adherence to direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) is incomplete. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) was developed as a mechanical alternative to address these unmet needs. The evidence base has changed substantially over the last 2 years: three randomized controlled trials comparing LAAO with DOAC-OPTION, CHAMPION-AF, and CLOSURE-AF-have now reported. In this update, we summarize the pathophysiological rationale, the technical aspects of the procedure, and the totality of the randomized and observational evidence, including a 2026 meta-analysis of 5,890 randomized patients. Taken together, these data indicate that LAAO reduces non-procedure-related bleeding but does not decrease all-cause major bleeding, intracranial haemorrhage, or mortality, and may carry a higher risk of ischaemic stroke than DOAC. LAAO remains an established option for patients with contraindications to or intolerance of long-term OAC. In DOAC-eligible patients, it has become a randomized-tested alternative, but current evidence supports an individualized, shared decision rather than a universal offer. We outline the remaining controversies-patient selection, device-related thrombus, peri-device leak, post-procedural antithrombotic therapy, and the interpretation of observational data-and the trials designed to resolve them.
title: Left atrial appendage occlusion: an alternative to anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.

abstract: Cholesterol embolization syndrome (CES) is an underrecognized complication of arterial instrumentation caused by embolization of atheromatous debris into small- and medium-sized arteries. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is well described after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but biopsy-proven CES after TAVR is rarely reported. Its delayed presentation may be mistaken for contrast-associated nephropathy, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, or systemic vasculitis. A 77-year-old man with chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral artery disease underwent transfemoral TAVR for severe aortic stenosis. Preprocedural computed tomography angiography showed a "shaggy aorta." One month later, he developed intermittent, painless violaceous discoloration of the left first through third toes. Approximately 2.5 months after TAVR, serum creatinine had risen from a baseline of 1.2-1.5 mg/dL to 4.24 mg/dL, prompting admission. Microscopic hematuria, mild eosinophilia (0.64 ×10³/µL), elevated inflammatory markers, and dysmorphic erythrocytes raised concern for glomerulonephritis and vasculitis, and empiric intravenous methylprednisolone was given while diagnostic evaluation proceeded. Kidney biopsy demonstrated atheroembolic cholesterol clefts in intrarenal arteries with ischemic changes, without glomerulonephritis or immune complex deposition. Preserved pedal pulses with an ankle-brachial index of 1.21 and toe-brachial index of 0.98 supported distal microembolization rather than large-vessel occlusion. Corticosteroids were stopped, nephrotoxins withheld, aspirin resumed, and high-intensity statin therapy was initiated; creatinine improved to approximately 3.1 mg/dL by discharge. CES should remain in the differential for progressive AKI with blue toe syndrome after TAVR, even when presentation is delayed, and initial findings suggest immune-mediated disease.
title: Blue Toe Syndrome and Acute Kidney Injury Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Biopsy-Proven Case of Cholesterol Embolization Syndrome.

abstract:
AIMS: Uncertainty persists regarding the comparative efficacy of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) vs. angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We synthesized randomized evidence using reconstructed individual participant data (IPD) and compared the two modalities indirectly.
METHODS AND RESULTS: MEDLINE and CENTRAL were searched up to 31 March 2026. IPD were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Primary analyses used one-stage stratified Cox models; secondary analyses included random-effects and Bayesian hierarchical models. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Twenty-three randomized controlled trials enrolling 21 176 patients were included (16 IVUS, N = 15 209; 7 OCT, N = 5967). IVUS-guided PCI reduced MACE [hazard ratio (HR) 0.74; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-0.83; P < 0.001], target-vessel revascularization (TVR; HR 0.70; 0.60-0.82), and stent thrombosis (ST; HR 0.54; 0.37-0.78). OCT-guided PCI reduced MACE (HR 0.75; 0.63-0.91; P = 0.003), cardiac death (HR 0.48; 0.27-0.83), myocardial infarction (HR 0.79; 0.63-0.99), ST (HR 0.40; 0.22-0.74), and TVR (HR 0.74; 0.57-0.97). Bayesian posterior probabilities of benefit exceeded 82% for all IVUS and 94% for all OCT endpoints. Indirect comparison detected no significant between-modality difference. Meta-regression of IVUS trials revealed heterogeneity by geographic region (P < 0.001) and attenuation of benefit over time (β = +0.034/year; P = 0.004); OCT analyses were non-significant.
CONCLUSION: Both IVUS and OCT reduced MACE, revascularization, and ST compared with angiography-guided PCI. These findings support intravascular imaging as a routine adjunct to PCI in the populations studied.
title: Intravascular imaging-guided versus angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention: a reconstructed individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of intravascular ultrasound- and optical coherence tomography-guided strategies.
