title: Comment on "Symptom phenotypes and coronary microvascular function in non-obstructive coronary artery disease: Insights beyond epicardial ischemia".

abstract: Rhabdomyolysis is a potentially life-threatening condition characterized by skeletal muscle injury, marked elevation of creatine kinase (CK), and potential development of acute kidney injury (AKI). Statins are a well-recognized cause of rhabdomyolysis, although the risk may be influenced by concomitant medications and patient-related factors. We present a case of severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI following initiation of high-intensity rosuvastatin therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention. A 66-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted with acute coronary syndrome. Coronary angiography revealed a critical lesion in the left anterior descending artery, and a drug-eluting stent was implanted. Her low-density lipoprotein cholesterol was 184 mg/dL, and her triglycerides were 356 mg/dL. She was discharged on rosuvastatin 40 mg once daily, ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily, aspirin 75 mg once daily, perindopril, and amlodipine. One month later, she developed generalized weakness, fatigue, and severe myalgia. Initial laboratory investigations demonstrated elevated serum creatinine, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase. Two days later, she developed anuria, severe muscle pain, and dark-red urine. On admission, CK and serum creatinine were markedly elevated. She denied other medication use, toxic exposure, or recent muscle trauma. Rhabdomyolysis with severe AKI was suspected, and she was admitted to the intensive care unit. Rosuvastatin was immediately discontinued, and ticagrelor was replaced with clopidogrel. Despite intravenous hydration and supportive treatment, metabolic acidosis and renal dysfunction worsened, with a serum creatinine level of 6.3 mg/dL, BUN of 82 mg/dL, and bicarbonate of 15 mmol/L. Hemodialysis was initiated. On the fourth day, she developed severe dyspnea and hypoxemia associated with pulmonary congestion, requiring additional consecutive hemodialysis sessions. Cardiac causes of pulmonary edema were excluded by electrocardiography and echocardiography. Her clinical condition subsequently stabilized, and CK and creatinine levels progressively decreased. She was discharged with continued renal monitoring, and serum creatinine decreased to 1.3 mg/dL by the third week after discharge. This case highlights the potential for severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI following high-intensity rosuvastatin therapy, particularly in patients with multiple comorbidities. Early recognition of myalgia, dark urine, oliguria, and markedly elevated CK levels is essential. Prompt discontinuation of the suspected medication, aggressive supportive management, and timely initiation of renal replacement therapy can be crucial in preventing further complications and facilitating recovery.
title: Severe Rhabdomyolysis and Acute Kidney Injury Following Rosuvastatin Reinitiation During Ticagrelor Therapy: A Case Report and Literature Review.

abstract: Historically, the complexity of patients being evaluated for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge therapy (M-TEER) has been divided into 3 main categories: green zone: defined as cases where M-TEER is straightforward and not complex, yellow zone: cases with medium complexity where M-TEER is feasible but not entirely straightforward, and red zone: cases where you would not consider M-TEER as the first option and may be swayed toward consideration of other options like transcatheter mitral valve (MV) replacement or surgical management. However, the advancement in preprocedural planning with precise anatomical definition by 3-dimensional imaging modalities has changed how we address complex mitral regurgitation cases. The expansion of available devices for management of MV disease has changed the way we think about undertaking challenging M-TEER procedures. Management in the current era emphasizes meticulous preprocedural assessment of mitral regurgitation pathology, strategic planning for device implantation, judicious device choice, and early consideration of transcatheter MV replacement or other innovative transcatheter devices. This review article provides a comprehensive overview of the available data on M-TEER and outlines treatment strategies for complex cases within the context of contemporary transcatheter technologies.
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
keywords: Mitral transcatheter edge to edge repair (M-TEER)
title: Stuck in the Traffic-Light: Moving Past Color Signals to Real Decisions in Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Therapy Management.

abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS), also known as allergic angina, is a rare but serious condition defined by acute coronary syndrome occurring alongside a hypersensitivity reaction. We report the case of a 42-year-old male smoker who developed Type II KS after a hymenoptera sting. The patient came to the emergency department with a sudden decreased level of consciousness and retrosternal chest pain. Electrocardiography showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads, and coronary angiography revealed total proximal left anterior descending artery occlusion. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed successfully. Echocardiography documented a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with regional wall motion abnormalities, indicating significant myocardial injury. The patient was discharged with a treatment plan that included valsartan, spironolactone, bisoprolol, ticagrelor, acetylsalicylic acid, and atorvastatin. This case highlights the diagnostic and treatment challenges of KS and stresses the need for early recognition and a team-based approach to achieve better clinical results.

last_author_country: Baylor College of Medicine Houston Texas USA
title: A Rare Case Report of Type II Kounis Syndrome With Literature Review: Acute Anterior ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction Following Bee Sting.

abstract: To compare perioperative complications and recovery outcomes between neuraxial and general anesthesia in adult patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from 2000 to April 25, 2026. Studies comparing neuraxial and general anesthesia were included. Outcomes included mortality (in-hospital, 30-day, 90-day, 1-year), intraoperative hypotension, postoperative delirium, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), pneumonia, acute kidney injury (AKI), length of hospital stay, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled effect estimates. Nineteen RCTs (n = 4,742) were included. No significant differences were observed between neuraxial and general anesthesia for mortality at any time point, postoperative delirium, ACS, pneumonia, or PONV. Neuraxial anesthesia was associated with a lower risk of intraoperative hypotension (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.40-0.77) and AKI (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.84), and shorter length of hospital stay (MD - 0.58 days, 95% CI - 1.08 to - 0.07). Heterogeneity was substantial for some outcomes. Neuraxial anesthesia decreases the risk of intraoperative hypertension and acute kidney injury in comparison to general anesthesia in patients undergoing hip fracture repair.
title: Comparing perioperative complications and recovery outcomes of neuraxial versus general anesthesia in hip fracture surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The goal of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is not only survival, but long-term satisfaction with life. Whether functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale; mRS), cognition, emotional symptoms, fatigue, and physical activity relate to life satisfaction in ECPR survivors remain unknown. We evaluated these aspects of health and their association with life satisfaction and self-rated health.
METHODS: This cross-sectional follow-up included survivors ≥1 year after ECPR at Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden (2010-2021). Primary outcomes were life satisfaction (World Values Survey) and self-rated health (EQ-5D-5L VAS). Secondary outcomes were mRS, Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Mental Fatigue Scale (MFS), and self-reported physical activity. Exploratory multivariable linear regression assessed associations with primary outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 34 survivors, 26 (76.5%) participated; median follow-up was 5 [IQR 2-7] years; 96% had mRS 0-3. Median life satisfaction was 8 [6-9]/10 and self-rated health 81 [70-90]/100, similar to population reference values (7.55 and 80). Positive screen for cognitive impairment (MoCA < 26) was present in 56%, anxiety (HADS-A ≥ 8) 42%, depression (HADS-D ≥ 8) 15%, and fatigue (MFS ≥ 10.5) 50%. In exploratory multivariable analysis, moderate physical activity was associated with life satisfaction (B 0.36 per day/week; 95% CI 0.06-0.67; p = 0.023) and self-rated health (B 4.60; 0.71-8.50; p = 0.024).
CONCLUSION: Long-term ECPR survivors reported life satisfaction and self-rated health similar to population reference values. In exploratory multivariable analysis, moderate physical activity was the only variable associated with both. This supports assessing life satisfaction and physical activity in post-ECPR follow-up.
title: Life satisfaction and self-rated health in long-term survivors after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR): associations with functional outcome, cognition, anxiety, depression, fatigue, and physical activity.

abstract:
AIMS: Identifying the infarct-related artery (IRA) before coronary angiography in non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) is difficult because current approaches have limited sensitivity. We evaluated whether a non-invasive 90-s optically pumped magnetometer magnetocardiography (OPM-MCG) recording can estimate pre-angiography IRA probabilities in these patients and provide information beyond standard-care variables.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This prospective two-campus study within one hospital system included a Campus 1 development cohort (n = 493) and a geographically separate Campus 2 test cohort (n = 118). All patients underwent OPM-MCG before angiography. An XGBoost model using 65 prespecified OPM-MCG features was developed with nested cross-validation, locked, and evaluated once in Campus 2. IRA adjudication followed a core-laboratory hierarchy. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were compared with ECG and TTE. Among 611 patients, 43% had LAD, 23% LCx, and 34% RCA IRA. In Campus 2, overall accuracy was 63.6%, macro-F1 was 60.0%; LAD/LCx/RCA vessel-specific areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.87/0.79/0.79 and top-1 sensitivity was 76.6%/34.5%/69.0%. Accuracy was 51.7% for matched ECG-only XGBoost and 55.9% for integrated standard care. In an exploratory stacked analysis, adding locked OPM-MCG probabilities to standard care increased accuracy to 67.8% (paired difference 11.9%, 95% CI 4.2-19.5; P = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: In haemodynamically stable patients with NSTEMI already selected for invasive management, a locked OPM-MCG model provided informative vessel-level probabilities in Campus 2 and complementary signal with standard care. Performance was strongest for LAD and RCA. Prospective multicentre, cross-platform testing is needed before clinical use.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2300070211.
title: AI-enabled OPM-magnetocardiography for pre-angiography infarct-related artery probability estimation in NSTEMI: a two-campus prospective cohort study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study elucidated the association between acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and Neogenin-1 (NEO-1) using proteomics to identify NEO-1 as a promising circulating biomarker for AMI risk prediction.
METHODS: A total of 107 participants were included in the analysis, comprising 45 control subjects without coronary heart disease (non-coronary heart disease [NCHD]; as a control group) and 62 patients with AMI. Furthermore, mRNA levels were elucidated via RT-qPCR, whereas the protein content was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Lastly, the acquired data were elucidated and compared.
RESULTS: The data showed that relative to the NCHD group, the AMI group's NEO-1 mRNA level in peripheral blood (PB) mononuclear cells was 1.47 times higher (p<0.05), whereas NEO-1 protein levels were 1.50 times higher (p<0.05). Furthermore, in AMI patients, the expression of NEO-1 was not related to smoking, total cholesterol, alcohol consumption, triglycerides, age, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, hypertension, or platelets. Moreover, Logistic regression assessment revealed that AMI was associated with elevated NEO-1 expression and enhanced fasting blood glucose.
CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that relative to the NCHD patients, AMI patients had elevated PB NEO-1 expression, which was an independent risk factor for AMI. These findings indicate that NEO-1 expression is a potential bio-index for AMI.
title: The NEO-1 gene may serve as a potential biomarker for predicting acute myocardial infarction.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ventricular septal rupture (VSR) remains a life-threatening mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction. Basal VSR is particularly challenging because of its deep location and close proximity to the atrioventricular valves. We report a case of successful repair of basal VSR through a right atrial approach using a double-patch sandwich technique.
CASE PRESENTATION: An 88-year-old woman developed an 18-mm basal VSR following inferior myocardial infarction despite successful percutaneous coronary intervention. Mechanical circulatory support with an Impella CP (Abiomed, Danvers, MA, USA) was instituted; however, worsening pulmonary congestion and device-related hemolysis necessitated surgical intervention. Through a right atriotomy, the defect was directly exposed. After debridement of necrotic tissue, full-thickness sutures were placed through the ventricular septum, and the defect was closed using bovine pericardial patches on both the left and right ventricular aspects. Because the subvalvular apparatus of the septal leaflet was incorporated into the repair, concomitant tricuspid valve replacement was performed. Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated complete closure of the defect without residual shunt or deterioration of mitral valve function. The patient was discharged 7 weeks after surgery and remains free from recurrent heart failure, with no evidence of residual shunt at 5.5 years postoperatively.
CONCLUSIONS: The right atrial approach combined with a double-patch sandwich technique provides excellent exposure of basal VSR and facilitates secure closure while avoiding ventriculotomy. This technique may represent a useful surgical option for selected patients with basal VSR.
title: Right Atrial Repair of Basal Ventricular Septal Rupture with Long-Term Follow-Up: A Case Report.

abstract: Congenital coronary artery anomalies are quite uncommon-they are observed in 1.3% of the coronary angiograms. Although most of them are benign, some coronary anomalies are associated with poor clinical outcomes. The exact mechanism of these outcomes in patients with anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with interarterial course is hypothesized to be either compression of the coronary artery during its course between the aorta and the pulmonary artery, or obstruction of the coronary flow during exercise due to the acute angulation of the RCA ostium. We present the case of a 54 y/o patient with NSTEMI, who, after a diagnostic coronary angiogram and coronary CT, was found to have complex coronary artery disease, including an anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with "malignant" interarterial course. In order to determine the optimal treatment, we proceeded with IVUS assessment of the ostial and proximal RCA with dobutamine challenge, which showed significant stenosis of both the RCA ostium and the interarterial segment at the peak dose of the dobutamine challenge. As a result a decision was made to treat both the RCA ostium and its interarterial segment with PCI, producing an excellent final result. Our case underscores the importance of the combination of IVUS and dobutamine challenge in order to answer the ever-important pathophysiologic mechanism of a lesion and accordingly provide tailor-made treatment for anomalous coronary arteries.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: IVUS-Guided Dobutamine Challenge to Guide Anomalous RCA PCI: An Interesting Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recovery after ischemic stroke is limited by persistent cerebrovascular dysfunction, but the mechanisms regulating vascular repair remain poorly understood. Prnd (Prnd/Doppel) is a prion family protein expressed in the cerebrovascular endothelium during development. We tested the hypothesis that endothelial Prnd promotes vascular repair and functional recovery in the adult brain after stroke.
METHODS: Using middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice, we compared wild-type and Prnd-null mice and evaluated endothelial-specific Prnd overexpression. Functional recovery was assessed by behavioral testing, while infarct volume, brain atrophy, vascular architecture, blood-brain barrier integrity, and macrophage/microglia infiltration were evaluated histologically. Vascular signaling and endothelial cell junctional proteins were examined mechanistically.
RESULTS: Acute infarct volumes were comparable between wild-type and Prnd-null mice, indicating that Prnd does not substantially affect initial ischemic injury. During recovery, however, Prnd-null mice exhibited disrupted cerebrovascular architecture, increased blood-brain barrier disruption, greater brain atrophy, and increased macrophage/microglial infiltration. Conversely, endothelial Prnd overexpression improved long-term functional recovery without altering acute infarct size and was associated with enhanced blood-brain barrier integrity and vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, Prnd manipulation was associated with enhanced VEGF-A (vascular endothelial growth factor-A) signaling and increased endothelial cell tight junction protein expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Prnd is dispensable for acute ischemic injury but promotes cerebrovascular remodeling, blood-brain barrier restoration, and functional recovery after stroke. These findings identify endothelial Prnd as a regulator of poststroke vascular repair and a potential therapeutic target for enhancing long-term recovery.
title: Endothelial Cell-Expressed Prion Protein Prnd/Doppel Promotes Long-Term Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown.
METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR.
RESULTS: 3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804).
CONCLUSIONS: In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.
title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

abstract:
AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical assessment of coronary stenoses, its ability to determine their functional significance is limited. Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) has emerged as a non-invasive method for lesion-specific ischaemia assessment. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR using 15O-water positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging as the reference standard.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively reviewed 193 patients who underwent hybrid CCTA and 15O-water PET at Kuopio University Hospital between 2017 and 2022. Patients with low-to-moderate pretest probability of CAD in whom CAD could not be ruled out by CCTA were eligible. After exclusions, 165 patients were included. CT-FFR values were calculated using a research prototype algorithm and compared with PET-derived perfusion abnormalities. In the overall cohort, CT-FFR showed moderate diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.672-0.740. In a subgroup of 83 patients with high-quality CCTA and stenosis >50%, diagnostic performance improved substantially (AUC 0.836). Using a CT-FFR threshold of 0.80, sensitivity and specificity were 85% and 87%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: In an unselected clinical population referred for PET perfusion imaging after CCTA, CT-FFR did not significantly improve diagnostic performance compared with CCTA alone. However, in patients with high-quality CCTA and obstructive coronary stenoses, CT-FFR demonstrated good accuracy for identifying functionally significant disease, supporting its role as a complementary non-invasive diagnostic tool.
title: 15O-water PET-detected myocardial ischaemia and CT-derived FFR: Predicting the functional significance of anatomical stenosis.

abstract: Interindividual variability in clopidogrel response remains a significant limitation of antiplatelet therapy, particularly in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. Cytochrome P450 2C19 is a major determinant of clopidogrel bioactivation but accounts for only part of the variability in platelet inhibition, suggesting additional hepatic regulatory mechanisms. The main competing hydrolytic pathway is mediated by carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), which converts most absorbed clopidogrel into inactive metabolites. However, CES1 activity cannot be inferred from protein abundance alone, as active-metabolite formation also depends on catalytic function, intracellular localisation, isoform composition, substrate accessibility and residual CYP capacity.Recent evidence indicates that intracellular trafficking and lysosomal degradation can regulate hepatic CES1 abundance. Sortilin 1 (SORT1) may facilitate CES1 lysosomal targeting, while a cytosolic pool of SORT1 has been reported to undergo chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA)-associated turnover involving HSPA8 and LAMP2A. These relationships were observed in hepatic cell systems and mouse models of lipid metabolism, but not in humans treated with clopidogrel, and thus they support a mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established pharmacological pathway.This review synthesises recent evidence on clopidogrel metabolism, CES1 regulation, lysosomal trafficking, CMA, and platelet P2Y12 signalling. We suggest that the lysosome-CMA-SORT1-CES1 axis may contribute to the heterogeneity of clopidogrel response by shifting the balance between hydrolytic inactivation and oxidative bioactivation. Although the individual molecular relationships are supported across different experimental models, their integration as a determinant of human clopidogrel response remains untested. Before the proposed axis can be considered clinically or pharmacologically established, direct causal validation is required.
title: Beyond CYP2C19: The Lysosome-CMA-SORT1-CES1 Axis as a Potential Regulator of Clopidogrel Response.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region are limited. We synthesized available evidence on post-TAVR clinical outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through May 2025 for studies reporting TAVR outcomes in this region. Outcomes included device success, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, new-onset atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe paravalvular leak, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Overall incidence rates were pooled via Poisson analysis and reported per 100 person-years with 95% CIs.
RESULTS: Forty-eight studies encompassing 7331 patients (mean age, 76.9±8.5 years; 52.4% women) were included. Pooled device success rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.0%). At latest follow-up, pooled incidence rates per 100 person-years were 13.7 for all-cause death (95% CI, 12.9-14.6), 4.8 for cardiovascular death (95% CI, 4.1-5.7), 1.0 for myocardial infarction (95% CI, 0.7-1.4), 1.6 for stroke (95% CI, 1.3-1.9), 2.7 for moderate to severe paravalvular leak (95% CI, 2.2-3.4), 6.5 for new-onset atrial fibrillation (95% CI, 5.5-7.7), and 10.0 for permanent pacemaker implantation (95% CI, 9.2-10.9). Post hoc exploratory meta-regression identified significant study-level modifying effects, with higher mean age and greater use of first-generation versus second-generation valves associated with higher overall all-cause mortality incidence following TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: TAVR in the Middle East and North Africa region was associated with high device success rate and relatively low cardiovascular death. Permanent pacemaker implantation was the most prevalent post-TAVR complication. Further studies are warranted to optimize TAVR practice in this region.

abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains the cornerstone of revascularization in coronary artery disease. However, despite advances in stent technology, adverse outcomes related to suboptimal stent placement including under-expansion, malapposition, incomplete coverage, edge dissection, and neoatherosclerosis persist. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the highest resolution widely available intravascular imaging modality, allowing unparalleled visualization of stent-vessel interactions and plaque morphology. However, there are significant barriers to large-scale OCT adoption, including time-consuming manual interpretation and dependence on the operator, resulting in significant variability between analysts. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based automated OCT analysis promises to assist PCI by delivering rapid, reproducible, and standardized stent optimization, but current analysis systems lack important features to optimize stent placement. This review summarizes the principles of OCT in PCI, the evidence for OCT-guided optimization, and recent advances in AI-driven automated OCT analysis. We discuss plaque analysis and classification, highlighting how AI-driven automated OCT analysis can identify fibrous, lipid-rich, and calcified lesions and guide tailored lesion preparation using balloons, specialty balloons, drug-coated balloons, intravascular lithotripsy, and atherectomy. We outline emerging AI-enabled workflows for fully automated PCI optimization, evaluate clinical outcomes, interpretability, and workflow integration. Finally, we explore future directions including AI imaging-physiology fusion, multiomics integration, and robotics. If successful, automated AI-empowered OCT analysis could become a central imaging platform for precision PCI, enabling tailored lesion preparation, optimal stent deployment, and improved clinical outcomes in coronary artery disease management.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Automated Optical Coherence Tomography Analysis for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Planning: From Plaque Analysis to Precision Lesion Preparation and Stent Optimization.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) provides bi-ventricular support for patients with myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (MI-CS); comparative effectiveness data relative to other mechanical circulatory support remain limited. We characterize contemporary ECMO utilization for MI-CS and compare short-term mortality across ECMO and non-ECMO treatment strategies.
METHODS: We compared baseline characteristics and temporal trends in mechanical circulatory support utilization among Medicare beneficiaries hospitalized with MI-CS from 2016 to 2023 and treated with ECMO, Impella, intra-aortic balloon pump, or medical management alone. Patient outcomes for each group were evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting, G-formula approach, and grace period analysis. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: The cohort included 102 718 patients: 1165 (1.1%) treated with ECMO, 10 064 (9.8%) Impella, 24 631 (24.0%) intra-aortic balloon pump, and 66 858 (65.1%) medical management alone. From 2016 to 2023, ECMO use for MI-CS increased from 0.8% to 1.8%. The percentage of hospitals using ECMO increased from 9.2% to 17.1%. Unadjusted 30-day mortality was higher for ECMO (69%) compared with Impella (60%), intra-aortic balloon pump (39%), and medical management (46%) (all P<0.0001). Adjusted inverse probability of treatment weighting and G-formula analyses revealed a 30-day mortality rate of 68%-70% for ECMO, which was higher than that for other therapies. The grace period analysis revealed similar mortality between patients treated with ECMO (54%) and Impella (54%).
CONCLUSIONS: ECMO use in a contemporary Medicare cohort of patients with MI-CS was infrequent (1.1%) and associated with high 30-day mortality. Despite use of complementary causal inference methods, we were unable to establish valid causal inferences on ECMO use and patient survival.

title: National Use Patterns and Comparative Effectiveness of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]).
CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year.
RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.
first_author_country: Smidt Heart Institute Los Angeles CA USA
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
last_author_country: Smidt Heart Institute Los Angeles CA USA
title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of childhood cancer (CCS) have higher risk of developing ischaemic heart disease (IHD), however, data on coronary anatomy, revascularisations, and prognosis remain limited. The objective was to investigate angiographic findings, invasive treatment patterns and mortality in CCS with IHD compared with controls without a history of childhood cancer.
METHODS: This was a nationwide retrospective cohort-study of all 5-year survivors of leukaemia, lymphoma, or central nervous system cancer who subsequently developed IHD, with index cancer between 1958-2021. CCS were compared with population-based controls with IHD matched on cancer date by age, sex and residence.
RESULTS: 136 CCS and 667 controls with IHD were included. CCS were a median of 5.2 years younger than controls at diagnosis of IHD. CCS had a higher prevalence of left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis (25.0% vs. 6.5%; p < 0.001) and multivessel disease (51.2% vs. 39.4%; p = 0.043). Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) was more frequently performed in CCS (22.8% vs. 11.4%; p < 0.001), although after adjusting for relevant covariates the difference was attenuated. After a median follow-up of 5.4 years following IHD diagnosis, CCS had higher hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 1.83, 95% CI 1.31-2.54; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.42-2.95; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CCS who developed IHD demonstrate a higher burden of extensive coronary artery disease, characterized by increased prevalence of LMCA stenosis and multivessel disease. Although overall revascularisation rates were similar, CCS experienced significantly higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality following IHD-diagnosis compared with controls.

title: Angiographic findings, revascularisations and mortality in childhood cancer survivors with ischaemic heart disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of death, limb loss, and impaired functional recovery despite revascularisation. Drug-coated balloons may reduce restenosis and repeat intervention after infrainguinal endovascular therapy, but long-term safety and effectiveness data in patients with CLTI remain limited.
METHODS: We performed a prespecified subgroup analysis of BIOLUX P-III, a prospective international post-market all-comers registry evaluating the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon for infrainguinal peripheral artery disease. Outcomes were compared between patients with and without CLTI through 60 months. Endpoints included freedom from major adverse events, clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation, major target-limb amputation, amputation-free survival and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Because follow-up completeness declined substantially by 60 months, late estimates were interpreted in the context of censoring, attrition and competing mortality.
RESULTS: Among 877 treated patients, 328 (37.4%) had CLTI. Technical success exceeded 98% in both groups. Patients with CLTI had greater baseline comorbidity, more advanced limb threat and more frequent below-the-knee disease. At 60 months, freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation was 85.3% in patients with CLTI and 78.3% in those without CLTI (P = .59), and freedom from major adverse events was similar (76.5% vs 74.3%; P = .13). In contrast, 5-year survival was substantially lower in patients with CLTI (47.9% vs 76.7%; P < .001). Freedom from major target-limb amputation was lower (93.3% vs 99.3%; P < .001), and amputation-free survival was reduced (47.1% vs 75.7%; P < .001). Patients with CLTI received a lower cumulative paclitaxel dose despite higher mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Passeo-18 Lux treatment was associated with preserved lesion-level durability through 5 years, but CLTI identified a high-risk prognostic phenotype with poor survival and limb outcomes. These findings suggest that long-term outcomes in CLTI are influenced by systemic comorbidity, early limb vulnerability, competing mortality and wound-related factors beyond lesion-level device performance alone.Clinical ImpactThis study provides clinically relevant insights into the long-term outcomes of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) undergoing endovascular revascularisation with drug-coated balloons. Despite high procedural success, patients with CLTI experience substantially greater long-term mortality and adverse limb outcomes than those with intermittent claudication. These findings highlight the importance of recognising CLTI as a high-risk clinical phenotype requiring comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction, multidisciplinary management, and structured postprocedural surveillance. The study's principal contribution is its evaluation of five-year outcomes in a real-world, all-comers population, providing valuable evidence to inform patient counselling, individualised treatment strategies, and long-term clinical decision-making.
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
title: Five-Year Prognostic Outcomes After Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Treatment According to Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia Status: Insights From the BIOLUX P-III Registry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is the most widely used mechanical circulatory support device for patients with advanced heart failure (HF) in our setting. However, femoral implantation restricts patient mobility during support.
OBJECTIVE: To report the initial experience of a Brazilian advanced HF referral center with percutaneous axillary IABP implantation.
METHODS: Consecutive patients hospitalized for HF who underwent percutaneous axillary IABP implantation at a tertiary cardiology referral center were included. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Between December 2020 and December 2023, 22 patients underwent percutaneous axillary IABP implantation. The mean age was 53 ± 10.7 years. All patients were hospitalized with refractory HF and were listed for heart transplantation. The procedure was successfully performed in all patients selected for the axillary approach. The median duration of support was 15 days (interquartile range: 7-28 days). Observed complications included device migration (18.2%), limb ischemia (9.1%), and isolated infectious and neurological events. Half of the patients either underwent heart transplantation or were successfully weaned from mechanical support.
CONCLUSION: The initial experience with percutaneous axillary IABP implantation demonstrated that the technique is feasible, safe, and reproducible. Further studies are needed to establish the role of this strategy within the continuum of care for patients hospitalized with advanced HF while awaiting heart transplantation.
title: Percutaneous Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Implantation in Patients Hospitalized with Heart Failure: Initial Brazilian Experience.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sympathetic overactivation contributes to ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Preclinical study demonstrated that low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) modulation of the left stellate ganglion (LSG) reduced post-STEMI VAs.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate whether LIFU modulation of LSG reduces VAs following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with STEMI.
METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled exploratory study, 41 STEMI undergoing primary PCI were assigned to LIFU modulation (n = 20) or sham stimulation (n = 21). LIFU was initiated in the catheterization laboratory and continued in the ward. All patients were followed up for 7 days and underwent Holter monitoring, serum biomarker assessment, echocardiographic evaluation, and safety assessment.
RESULTS: LIFU significantly reduced VA burden within 72 hours after PCI. Heart rate variability analysis indicated reduced low-frequency power and a decreased low-frequency/high-frequency ratio. Exploratory analyses also showed lower levels of proinflammatory cytokines and sympathetic neurotransmitters. Myocardial injury markers did not differ significantly between groups, whereas left ventricular ejection fraction was higher in the LIFU group on day 7. Furthermore, no significant organ dysfunction or thermal injury was observed following LIFU intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: LIFU modulation of LSG might attenuate sympathetic activity and reduce VAs in patients with STEMI undergoing PCI. This study provides the first clinical evidence supporting LIFU as a promising noninvasive neuromodulatory strategy for VA prevention in the STEMI setting. Larger multicenter trials (NCT07587294/ChiCTR2600122798, ongoing) are warranted to confirm these findings. This study offers a novel strategy for the management of VAs following STEMI.
title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound Modulation of Stellate Ganglion Attenuates Post-STEMI Ventricular Arrhythmias: First-in-Human Feasibility Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: A short posterior mitral leaflet (PML) length is challenging anatomy for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER); however, its prognostic impact remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the association between PML length and M-TEER outcomes.
METHODS: A total of 2,441 patients with functional mitral regurgitation (MR) were stratified by preprocedural PML length: very short (7 mm or less, n = 82), short (>7-10 mm, n = 736), and adequate (>10 mm, n = 1,623) groups. Procedural outcomes, echocardiographic data, and all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization were compared.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 14.4 months [Q1-Q3: 10.2-27.5]. At discharge, MR grade 1+ or less was comparable among the 3 groups (very short: n = 63/82, 77% vs short: n = 598/736, 81% vs adequate: n = 1,259/1,623, 78%; P = 0.129). At 1 year, MR grade numerically worsened in the very short group (MR grade 1+ or less, n = 31/52, 60%). The rate of achieving both MR grade 1+ or less and transmitral mean pressure gradient <5 mm Hg was similar among groups at discharge, but it was significantly lower in the very short group (n = 14/39, 36%) than in the short (n = 201/306, 66%) and adequate (n = 440/665, 66%) groups (P < 0.001) at 1 year. Although the incidence of the composite outcome was higher in shorter groups (P = 0.018), the PML length was not an independent risk factor in the multivariate analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: M-TEER may be feasible in selected patients with shorter PML; however, very short PML might have less favorable echocardiographic durability, warranting anatomical assessment and follow-up. Given the small subgroup and limited follow-up, these findings require cautious interpretation and validation.
CLINICAL TRIALS: OCEAN-Mitral registry (UMIN000023653).
title: Posterior Mitral Leaflet Length and Outcomes After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: From The OCEAN-Mitral Registry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary obstruction is a catastrophic complication of transcatheter valve-in-valve procedures, as the prosthesis frame can form a neo-skirt compromising coronary perfusion.
CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old woman presented with a degenerated 23-mm balloon-expandable transcatheter valve, heart failure, and reduced left ventricular function. Computed tomography showed high-risk anatomy for right coronary obstruction: valve-to-right coronary artery distance 3.1 mm and valve-to-sinotubular junction distance 1.3 mm. Multimodality fusion imaging-guided electrosurgical leaflet modification using the leaflet laceration with balloon-mediated annihilation to prevent coronary obstruction with radiofrequency needle (LLAMACORN) technique, followed by implantation of a 26-mm self-expanding valve, achieved excellent hemodynamics and preserved coronary perfusion.
DISCUSSION: This case shows how computed tomography planning and multimodality imaging enable safe management of complex transcatheter aortic valve-in-transcatheter aortic valve anatomies. When conventional coronary protection is not feasible, LLAMACORN leaflet modification offers a safe alternative to mitigate obstruction risk.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recognize anatomical predictors of coronary obstruction in transcatheter aortic valve-in-transcatheter aortic valve. Understand multimodality imaging's role in guiding leaflet modification. Describe LLAMACORN as a leaflet-modification strategy when a self-expanding valve is preferred.
title: Echocardiographic Fusion Imaging to Guide LLAMACORN and Prevent Coronary Obstruction With Self-Expanding Valve-in-Valve TAVI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The South African Flag Sign (SAFS) is a rare electrocardiographic pattern associated with occlusion myocardial infarction, typically involving the first diagonal branch.
CASE SUMMARY: A 74-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain and a transient neurological deficit following intense emotional stress. The admission electrocardiogram demonstrated the SAFS. Emergency coronary angiography revealed nonobstructive coronary artery disease, whereas echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance confirmed Takotsubo syndrome with apical ballooning and an initial left ventricular ejection fraction of 36%. Clinical and functional recovery was achieved with guideline-directed medical therapy.
DISCUSSION: High-risk ST-segment elevation equivalents like the SAFS, though excluded from standard ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction criteria, indicate occlusion myocardial infarction requiring emergent reperfusion. This case illustrates how severe catecholaminergic discharge in Takotsubo syndrome can induce microvascular dysfunction and vasospasm, faithfully mimicking epicardial occlusions and acute cerebrovascular events.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: High-risk electrocardiogram patterns such as the SAFS are not exclusive to occlusion myocardial infarction and may indicate other mechanisms of acute myocardial injury.
title: South African Flag Sign on Electrocardiogram: Not Always an Obstructive Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The safety of same-day discharge (SDD) following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established strategy in patients undergoing the transfemoral approach. The feasibility of SDD in patients undergoing transaxillary TAVI has not been reported.
CASE SUMMARY: We present a 76-year-old male patient who underwent successful elective transaxillary TAVI. He had severe aortic stenosis, normal left ventricular function, and a background of diabetes, chronic liver disease, and right above-knee amputation. The access site was managed with 2 ProGlide devices with excellent hemostasis. There were no significant electrocardiogram changes postprocedure. Comprehensive postdischarge surveillance was provided, including a welfare telephone call on the following day.
DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first case in the literature of SDD following transaxillary TAVI. Such a strategy requires appropriate patient selection, meticulous procedural planning, rigorous postdischarge monitoring strategy, and can only be considered in highly selected cases.
title: Same-Day Discharge After Percutaneous Transaxillary Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using Self-Expanding Valve.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histologically confirmed myxedematous myocardial involvement is rare and may be difficult to recognize when another cause of ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis coexists.
CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old man with longstanding, inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism presented with exertional dyspnea and a large goiter. Echocardiography showed severe bicuspid aortic stenosis, moderate aortic regurgitation, marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 26% of myocardial mass. After thyroid optimization, he underwent aortic valve replacement. Myocardial biopsy showed severe cardiomyocyte atrophy, interstitial mucin deposition, and extensive replacement fibrosis; Congo red staining was negative.
DISCUSSION: Severe aortic stenosis provided an alternative explanation for the myocardial phenotype, and multimodality imaging alone could not distinguish pressure-overload remodeling from hypothyroidism-related myocardial injury.
CONCLUSION: Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.
title: Histologically Confirmed Myxedematous Myocardial Involvement in Severe Hypothyroidism With Concomitant Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Prior imaging studies (predominantly using intravascular ultrasound) have demonstrated modest plaque regression with lipid-lowering therapy in stable coronary artery disease (CAD). The effect of initiating intensive lipid-lowering therapy on coronary plaque regression across the entire coronary tree in treatment-naive patients remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To report the prespecified secondary imaging end points of the FLOWPROMOTE trial by comparing the effects of intensive vs more intensive lipid-lowering therapy on plaque regression in statin-naive patients with stable CAD and to assess the association between achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and plaque regression.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: FLOWPROMOTE was a multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolling statin-naive patients with newly diagnosed stable CAD, defined by a coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) stenosis greater than 50% and fractional flow reserve CT less than or equal to 0.80. Coronary CTA was performed at baseline and repeated at 9 and 18 months. Study data were analyzed from February 2025 to January 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to intensive lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg) or more intensive lipid-lowering therapy (rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg) for 18 months.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prespecified secondary end points included changes in total plaque volume (TPV), noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV), and calcified plaque volume (CPV) across all coronary vessels at 9 and 18 months compared with baseline.
RESULTS: A total of 104 patients (mean [SD] age, 64 [9] years; 82 male [79%]) were included in this analysis, with 52 patients in the intensive group and 52 patients in the more intensive group. LDL-C levels decreased from 119.7 to 69.5 mg/dL (-38%) with intensive therapy and from 127.4 to 42.5 mg/dL (-65%) with more intensive therapy (between-group P < .001). At 18 months, both TPV and NCPV decreased in both groups, with significantly greater regression in the more intensive-therapy group. TPV was reduced by -69.8 mm3 (-21.1%) with more intensive therapy vs -39.0 mm3 (-13.6%) with intensive therapy (between-group difference, -30.9 mm3; 95% CI, -57.2 to -4.5 mm3; P = .02), and NCPV was reduced by -82.3 mm3 (-28.2%) vs -53.5 mm3 (-20.0%), respectively (between-group difference, -28.9 mm3; 95% CI, -53.2 to -4.6 mm3; P = .02). CPV increased similarly in both groups. Regression of TPV occurred in 90% of patients receiving more intensive therapy compared with 76% receiving intensive therapy (47 of 52 [90%] vs 38 of 51 [75%]; P = .05), and regression of NCPV was observed in 98% vs 77% (51 of 52 [98%] vs 39 of 51 [77%]; P =.001). Lower achieved LDL-C levels were linearly associated with greater regression of TPV and NCPV.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This secondary analysis of the FLOWPROMOTE randomized clinical trial demonstrated that in statin-naive patients with CAD, more intensive lipid-lowering therapy was associated with significantly greater regression of total and noncalcified coronary plaque burden compared with intensive therapy. The extent of plaque regression was related to achieved LDL-C levels, supporting the potential for partial reversal of coronary atherosclerosis with intensive lipid reduction.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04737408.
title: Intensive vs More Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Plaque Regression in Statin-Naive Patients: Prespecified Analyses From the FLOWPROMOTE Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Romosozumab is highly effective for severe osteoporosis, but its cardiovascular safety is debated. The ARCH trial found more major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) with romosozumab than with alendronate, whereas the placebo-controlled FRAME trial found no signal. Real-world head-to-head data against alendronate are lacking.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network, we identified women aged ≥55 years with severe osteoporosis (pathological, lumbar vertebral, or hip fracture within 2 years) who initiated romosozumab or alendronate, excluding those with any MACE in the prior 12 months. Cohorts were matched 1:1 by propensity score on demographics, cardiovascular comorbidities, medications, and laboratory parameters, and followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was a composite of MACE; secondary outcomes were myocardial infarction (MI), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and ischemic stroke. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models.
RESULTS: After matching, 5930 women remained per group (mean age 72 years; median follow-up 365 days). Romosozumab was not associated with an increased risk of MACE (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.70-1.07), MI (HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.67-1.28), or ACS (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.72-1.32). Ischemic stroke was significantly lower with romosozumab (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.46-0.89; P=0.008). Findings were consistent in event-naïve analyses and across subgroups, including chronic kidney disease and diabetes; however, the advanced-CKD stratum (stage 4-5 or end-stage renal disease) could not be analyzed because event counts were too small for estimation.
CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women with severe osteoporosis, romosozumab was not associated with higher 12-month cardiovascular risk than alendronate. These findings are reassuring in the populations that could be evaluated, although cardiovascular safety in advanced CKD remains uncertain and prospective confirmation is warranted.
journal: Journal of bone and mineral metabolism
title: Cardiovascular safety of romosozumab versus alendronate in postmenopausal women with severe osteoporosis: a propensity-matched real-world study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite timely reperfusion and guideline-directed therapies, the recovery of left ventricular function after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains suboptimal. Adjunctive metabolic therapy may enhance post-infarction cardiac repair. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺), a key regulator of cellular bioenergetics and redox homeostasis, has cardioprotective effects in experimental ischemia-reperfusion injury. However, its clinical impact in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 120 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI were assigned to receive intravenous NAD⁺ (10 mg/day) or placebo for 7 days, in addition to standard medical therapy. The primary endpoint was the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) at 30 days. The secondary endpoints included N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels at 7 and 30 days, echocardiographic parameters at 30 days, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) at 6 months.
RESULTS: At 30 days, the NAD⁺ group demonstrated a modest but significant improvement in LVEF compared with the placebo group (56.32 ± 8.04% vs. 53.37 ± 8.12%, p = 0.048). NT-proBNP levels were lower in the NAD⁺ group at follow-up. However, findings for LV remodeling parameters were mixed, and no significant between-group difference was observed in 6-month MACCE rates.
CONCLUSIONS: Short-term intravenous NAD⁺ therapy following primary PCI improved left ventricular systolic function and reduced NT-proBNP levels in patients with STEMI. These findings suggest that restoring NAD⁺ availability may facilitate post-ischemic cardiac recovery, potentially through mechanisms related to mitochondrial energy metabolism and NAD⁺-dependent stress-response signaling. Larger trials are required to confirm its long-term clinical benefits and elucidate the underlying biological pathways.
REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier number ChiCTR2200059333.
journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
title: Effect of Intravenous Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide on Left Ventricular Function After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the predictive efficacy and risk stratification potential of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent CCTA at our hospital between June 2017 and June 2020, with 5-year follow-up for MACE occurrence. Patients were grouped by MACE status. Machine learning was applied to construct and compare three models: PCAT radiomics model, fat attenuation index (FAI) model, and clinical model. Prospective validation was conducted in 578 patients with suspected CAD undergoing CCTA, who were stratified into high- and low-risk groups by the optimal cutoff of the PCAT radiomics model. The predictive and risk stratification performance of all models was assessed.
RESULTS: Fourteen PCAT radiomics features (5 first-order and 9 texture features) were finally screened. The PCAT radiomics model showed significantly superior MACE predictive performance over the FAI and clinical models (P < 0.001). Only the PCAT radiomics model identified significantly higher MACE risk in the high-risk versus low-risk group (HR=2.611, 95% CI: 1.806-3.775, P < 0.001), with progressively reduced MACE-free survival in the high-risk group during follow-up (P < 0.001). No such significant between-group differences were found in the FAI and clinical models (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The PCAT radiomics model showed favorable performance for predicting the composite MACE endpoint, which was predominantly driven by worsening stable or unstable angina, and provided better risk stratification than the FAI and clinical models.
title: Predictive and risk stratification performance of CCTA-derived pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events: retrospective development and prospective validation.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has expanded into younger and lower-risk patients, making long-term valve durability increasingly important. Leaflet thrombosis, most commonly identified on computed tomography as hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), is common after TAVI. Whether leaflet thrombosis contributes to structural valve deterioration (SVD) remains incompletely understood. To summarize the current evidence on the relationship between leaflet thrombosis and SVD after TAVI, with a focus on clinical outcomes, imaging findings, antithrombotic therapy, and pathophysiological mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes available clinical, imaging, mechanistic, histopathological and antithrombotic literature addressing leaflet thrombosis and valve durability after TAVI. CT studies show that leaflet thrombosis occurs in 13-32% of patients within the first post-procedural year. Although some lesions resolve spontaneously, longitudinal imaging studies demonstrate persistence in a substantial proportion of patients, supporting the presence of an underlying valve-related substrate. HALT has not consistently been associated with adverse valve hemodynamics during the first year after implantation. Long-term TAVI durability studies report low rates of severe SVD (0.8-1.5% up to 10 years), although outcomes vary according to valve generation and study population. The 10-year NOTION and PARTNER 2A data provide important long-term durability information, but neither study included systematic longitudinal CT assessment of leaflet thrombosis. Observational studies linking early HALT to subsequent hemodynamic valve deterioration have yielded conflicting results. Indirect evidence from anticoagulation studies and histopathological investigations supports biological plausibility for a relationship between leaflet thrombosis and progressive leaflet injury, but does not establish causality. Leaflet thrombosis is a frequent imaging finding after TAVI and may persist over time, but its contribution to long-term SVD remains uncertain. Current evidence supports a potential biological relationship between leaflet thrombosis and valve degeneration but does not demonstrate that HALT is a causal precursor of clinically relevant SVD. Prospective studies combining serial CT imaging with long-term, standardized assessment of structural valve outcomes are required to resolve this question.
title: The impact of leaflet thrombosis on transcatheter aortic valve degeneration: a narrative review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of coronary calcification informs procedural planning in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet neither optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) nor intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) alone provides comprehensive diagnostic information. The dual sensor system (DSS) was developed to integrate and complement both imaging modalities.
AIMS: To determine the diagnostic value of DSS for detecting and characterizing calcification compared with either modality alone.
METHODS: Twenty coronary arteries from 17 cadaver hearts underwent DSS pullbacks. Eighty-seven histological sections and their co-registered DSS images were analyzed, with histology serving as the reference standard. Four cardiologists blinded to histology independently assessed calcification using OFDI alone, IVUS alone, and DSS. OFDI signal attenuation and IVUS reverberation artifacts were examined as potential indicators of maximum calcification thickness.
RESULTS: DSS demonstrated the highest sensitivity (DSS 98.0%; OFDI 85.5%, p < 0.001; IVUS 94.4%, p = 0.019) and accuracy (DSS, 97.7%; OFDI, 86.5%, p < 0.001; IVUS, 92.8%, p = 0.004) for detecting calcification. Inter-observer agreement was also highest in DSS (κ: DSS, 0.82; OFDI, 0.53; IVUS, 0.53). In subgroup analysis, sensitivity was significantly higher in DSS for sections with calcification arc < 180° (DSS, 98.6%; OFDI, 83.8%; IVUS, 94.0%), but not for those with ≥ 180°. Maximum calcification thickness was greater in calcifications only with OFDI attenuation than in those without (1423.8 [988.8-1994.1] vs. 686.4 [552.8-906.3] µm, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: DSS provides accurate and consistent detection of coronary calcification and may help stratify calcification by thickness. Future studies should assess whether these advantages translate into clinical benefits.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Diagnostic Performance of a Dual Sensor System in Assessment of Coronary Calcification: An Ex Vivo Cadaveric Study.

abstract: Cardiovascular disease is an increasingly significant cause of morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, driven by demographic growth, population ageing, and epidemiological transition. Despite the growing burden of ischaemic heart disease and other cardiovascular conditions, access to interventional cardiology services remains severely limited across the region. Critical shortages of percutaneous coronary intervention facilities, catheterisation laboratories, and trained interventional cardiologists contribute to delayed treatment and preventable mortality. Additional barriers include high infrastructure and equipment costs, limited financing mechanisms, inadequate insurance coverage, workforce shortages, and geographic inequities in access to care. Nevertheless, emerging programs in Uganda, Kenya, and Ethiopia demonstrate that sustainable progress is achievable through strategic partnerships, local workforce development, public-private collaboration, and regional professional networks. Expanding interventional cardiology capacity will require coordinated investments in infrastructure, training, financing, referral systems, and policy prioritisation. Strengthening these systems is essential to achieving equitable cardiovascular care and improving outcomes across sub-Saharan Africa.
title: Expanding interventional cardiology in sub-Saharan Africa: Progress, barriers, and a path forward.

abstract:
AIMS: To address a critical knowledge gap, this is the first scoping review to systematically map and describe the evidence on cognitive frailty in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS), including its prevalence, assessment tools, associated factors, and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: The Joanna Briggs Institute methodology guided the conduct of this scoping review, which has been reported in line with the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Following the PCC framework, a systematic search was conducted across five databases: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science. The search was performed up to August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality.
RESULTS: A total of 9 studies were included. The prevalence of cognitive frailty ranged from 8% to 55%, the differences attributed to the heterogeneity of assessment tools and diagnostic criteria. Regarding assessment tools, the FRAIL scale combined with the Short Portable Mental Status Questionnaire was the most commonly used combinations. Risk factors covered sociodemographic, physical health, and clinical domains. Prognostically, cognitive frailty was linked to higher composite short‑term (in‑hospital complications, prolonged stay, 30‑day events) and medium‑term (6‑month MACCE) risks, and also to elevated long‑term mortality and readmission.
CONCLUSION: Cognitive frailty is commonly reported in patients with ACS, with considerable variation across studies, and an association with adverse outcomes has been noted in multiple reports. However, the lack of standardized assessment tools and criteria makes results difficult to compare and synthesize. Existing prospective studies have primarily relied on baseline measurements of cognitive frailty to predict subsequent outcomes, without repeated assessments over time. This limits the ability to characterise the dynamic trajectory of cognitive frailty during the ACS course. Future research should focus on longitudinal studies, the development of rapid screening tools, and the exploration of multidisciplinary interventions.
title: Cognitive frailty in patients with acute coronary syndromes: A scoping review.

abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), particularly among individuals at increased risk of bleeding. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and safety of LAAC versus OAC in AF. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) was conducted to evaluate the sufficiency of cumulative evidence. Six randomized trials involving 7,004 patients were included. Compared with OAC, LAAC demonstrated similar risks of stroke, systemic embolism, cardiovascular death, all-cause mortality, and transient ischemic attack. LAAC showed a nominally higher risk of ischemic stroke or systemic embolization (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.04-1.79), although this finding was not robust to sensitivity analysis, with a borderline increase in ischemic stroke. In contrast, LAAC significantly reduced non-procedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.42-0.58), while major bleeding and hemorrhagic stroke were comparable between groups. TSA confirmed sufficient evidence supporting the reduction in bleeding outcomes but indicated that current evidence remains insufficient to establish definitive conclusions regarding thromboembolic efficacy. Overall, LAAC was not associated with statistically significant differences in several thromboembolic and mortality outcomes compared with OAC, while providing a substantial reduction in non-procedural clinically relevant bleeding. However, the potential signal toward increased ischemic events warrants further investigation in adequately powered randomized trials, particularly against contemporary DOAC-based therapy.
title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes of Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO PCI) may fail at several stages. The authors evaluated factors associated with collateral channel crossing failure during retrograde CTO PCI and its associations with technical success and procedural complications.
METHODS: The authors analyzed procedures from a multicenter CTO PCI registry with attempted retrograde or retrograde-assisted strategies and recorded the retrograde result. The primary endpoint was collateral channel crossing failure. Secondary endpoints included retrograde success, overall technical success, collateral/coronary perforation, donor-vessel injury, vascular complications, and an extended complication composite.
RESULTS: Among 577 retrograde CTO PCI procedures with recorded retrograde result, retrograde success was achieved in 375 (65.0%), and collateral channel crossing failure occurred in 135 (23.4%). Overall technical success was lower with collateral crossing failure than without it (51.9% vs 88.7%), with higher rates of collateral and coronary perforation, vascular complications, and the extended complication composite. In the primary adjusted model restricted to procedures with known collateral connection (CC) grade, corkscrew collateral morphology (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.85; 95% CI, 3.63-12.91) and CC0 grade (adjusted OR, 4.70; 95% CI, 1.97-11.26) were associated with higher odds of crossing failure, whereas CC2/CC3 grade was associated with lower odds (adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.22-0.92).
CONCLUSIONS: Collateral channel crossing failure was common in retrograde CTO PCI and was associated with lower technical success and greater complication burden. Unfavorable collateral morphology was associated with a higher risk of crossing failure; repeated collateral attempts may indicate escalating procedural difficulty and may warrant strategy reassessment.
title: Collateral channel crossing failure during retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention: predictors and associated procedural outcomes from a multicenter registry.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The modified jailed balloon technique (M-JBT) decreases side branch (SB) occlusion during bifurcation percutaneous coronary intervention by simultaneously inflating an SB balloon alongside main vessel stent deployment. Conventionally, M-JBT requires subsequent proximal optimization (POT), SB rewiring, and final kissing balloon inflation (KBI), adding complexity to the procedure. The authors defined a simplified approach-the Simplified Jailed Balloon Technique (S-JBT)-where postdilation is performed using only the stent delivery balloon, omitting POT, rewiring, and final KBI.
METHODS: To validate the physiological rationale of S-JBT, the authors measured SB resting full-cycle ratio (RFR) at 3 time points (baseline, post-M-JBT, and postdilation) in 6 consecutive patients undergoing S-JBT for LAD-diagonal bifurcation lesions using the jailed pressure wire technique.
RESULTS: RFR was maintained at all timepoints (baseline: 0.82 ± 0.17; post-M-JBT: 0.84 ± 0.14; postdilation: 0.86 ± 0.15), with no angiographic SB compromise.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the favorable SB ostial geometry established with simultaneous inflation persists after stent balloon postdilation, and that the primary mechanism of SB protection resides in the simultaneous inflation step. S-JBT may offer a practical, simplified SB protection strategy, particularly for bifurcation lesions with small side branches.
title: Simplified jailed balloon technique: proof-of-concept for side branch preservation without routine proximal optimization or final kissing balloon.

abstract: Axillary intra-aortic balloon pump (axi-IABP) support has emerged as an alternative to femoral access for patients with advanced heart failure, offering improved mobility and potential benefits in pretransplant conditioning; however, data on associated complications remain limited. We conducted a retrospective study of 55 patients who underwent axi-IABP placement between January 2019 and July 2025 at our institution. The cohort had a median age of 59 (interquartile range [IQR], 52-65) years and presented with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Axi-IABP successfully bridged 87.3% of patients to advanced therapies. A total of 83 complications were identified in 60.0% of patients, most commonly malposition in 23.6% of patients, gas leak alarms in 16.4% of patients, and kinking in 16.4% of patients. Serious vascular complications were infrequent. The median time to first complication was 10.5 (IQR, 2.75-25.5) days. Female sex was associated with a higher hazard of first complication when controlled for height (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04-7.27; p = 0.041). In conclusion, axi-IABP is an effective bridging strategy that enhances patient mobility but is associated with a high rate of device-related complications, predominantly mechanical in nature, underscoring the importance of careful patient selection and monitoring.
journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
title: Outcomes and Complications of Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Single-Center Experience.
