The treatment effect of BB on clinical endpoints was not modified by baseline PICP concentrations (p-for-interaction=0.404). Conclusion Circulating levels of PICP were lower 7 days and 6 months post-MI, in EF≥ 40% patients with a primary endpoint, suggestive of an impaired fibrotic response. PICP levels were unaffected by 6 months of BB treatment. A recent meta-analysis incorporating BETAMI-DANBLOCK reported neutral effects of prolonged BB therapy in MI patients with preserved EF, and our data provide a mechanistic correlate to this conclusion.Table
title: Effects of beta-blocker treatment on circulating biomarkers of fibrosis in patients with myocardial infarction without heart failure: A substudy of the BETAMI-DANBLOCK trial

abstract: Abstract Background Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) is associated with high thromboembolic and mortality risk, and is typically diagnosed post-myocardial infarction or in patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). The clinical trajectory of LVT patients with preserved LVEF is less well-studied, hence our study aimed to characterise this cohort of patients and to evaluate the prognostic significance of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS), a marker of subclinical systolic dysfunction not captured by LVEF. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study of 135 patients with transthoracic echocardiographically (TTE) confirmed LVT and LVEF ≥40% at a tertiary centre between 2011 and 2021. Patients were stratified by LVGLS on initial TTE into abnormal (less negative than -16%; n=108) and normal (more negative than -16%; n=27) groups for analysis. The primary endpoint was a composite outcome including stroke/transient ischaemic attack, acute myocardial infarction, acute decompensated heart failure, and all-cause mortality on follow-up. Results Among 135 LVT patients with preserved ejection fraction (mean age 58.4 ± 13.9 years, 83.0% male), 20.0% (n = 27) had abnormal LVGLS of less negative than -16%. Baseline demographics, co-morbidities, LVT aetiology and characteristics on TTE, and medical therapy including anticoagulation were similar across both groups. Patients with abnormal LVGLS had lower initial LVEF (44.7 ± 5.4% vs. 49.3 ± 8.7%, p &lt;0.001), and encountered higher incidence of composite outcome (47.2% [n = 56] vs. 18.5% [n = 5], p = 0.007). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly lower event-free survival for composite outcome in the abnormal LVGLS group (log-rank p=0.021). On Cox proportional hazards regression model, less negative LVGLS (per %) was independently associated with higher hazard of composite outcome (aHR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01 – 1.21, p = 0.033) after adjusting for age, sex, ischaemic heart disease, haemoglobin, and estimated glomerular filtration rate, across a mean follow-up duration of 5.2 ± 3.4 years. LVGLS was not associated with all-cause mortality or LVT resolution. Conclusion Abnormal LVGLS was associated with higher risk of adverse cardiovascular events in LVT patients with LVEF ≥40%, and provided incremental prognostic information beyond LVEF, aiding risk stratification.Table 1
title: Prognostic value of left ventricular global longitudinal strain for adverse outcomes in patients with left ventricular thrombus and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction

abstract: Abstract Background Residual left ventricular (LV) remodeling, defined as persistent cardiac enlargement after surgical correction of severe primary valvular regurgitation, is associated with adverse long-term outcomes. While guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) has been proven to promote LV reverse remodeling (LVRR) in patients with new-onset dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), the characteristics of LVRR after optimized medical therapy in patients with post-valvular correction residual remodeling, and its difference from that in new-onset DCM, remain unclear. Purpose This propensity score-matched cohort study aimed to compare the six-month LVRR and cardiac function recovery between patients with residual LV remodeling after corrected primary valvular regurgitation and those with new-onset DCM. Methods Patients with LVEF &lt; 40% at baseline in two single-center cohorts were enrolled in this study. The ReReRe (Residual left ventricular Remodeling in corrected primary valvular Regurgitation) cohort included patients with residual left ventricular remodeling after primary valvular regurgitation correction, who received angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI)-based optimized medical therapy. And the New-onset DCM cohort enrolled patients diagnosed with DCM within sixth months, who received standard GDMT. Results After 1:1 propensity score matching of age, gender, and baseline LVEF, a total of 121 patients were included in each cohort. At baseline, the ReReRe cohort had a higher proportion of patients with NYHA class III/IV (40.5% vs. 6.6%) and higher N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels (1145.00 vs. 609.00 pg/mL), but smaller LVEDD (59.40 ± 10.15 vs. 65.66 ± 7.06 mm), LV end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (222.45 ± 59.60 vs.152.87 ± 65.47 mm), and LV end-systolic volume (LVESV) (108.63 ± 56.98 vs. 154.12 ± 49.92 mm) (P &lt; 0.05). After six-month follow-up, NYHA class has no difference between the two cohorts (P &gt; 0.05), and the percentage of LVEDV change was larger in the ReReRe cohort (-30.08 ± 22.87% vs. -23.00 ± 20.36%, P &lt; 0.05). Also, a higher LVEF was observed in the ReReRe cohort (LVEF ≥ 50%: 55.4% vs. 48.8%, 40% ≤ LVEF &lt; 50%: 32.2% vs. 22.3%, P &lt; 0.01). Meanwhile, more patients in the ReReRe cohort had their LVEDD restored to the normal level (LVEDD &lt;55 mm [male] / &lt;50 mm [female]). Conclusions In this propensity score-matched study, the ReReRe cohort achieved better cardiac function recovery and higher reduced scale of heart cavity volume at sixth month. These findings highlight the better reversibility of load-induced myocardial injury in this population, and call for early optimized medical therapy to address valvular heart disease management.
title: Reversal of residual left ventricular remodeling in corrected primary valvular regurgitation: is it different from dilated cardiomyopathy

abstract: Abstract Background The prognosis of patients with acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) treated with veno-arterial extracorporeal life support (VA-ECLS) combined with Impella (i.e., ECPELLA) remains poor. Whether management at LVAD center confers a prognostic advantage compared with non-LVAD center remains uncertain. Purpose This study aimed to compare 30-day mortality between LVAD center and non-LVAD center among patients with AMI-CS receiving ECPELLA support, using data from the prospectively collected nationwide J-PVAD registry. Methods Among 4,910 patients who underwent Impella placement for AMI-CS between 2020 and 2023, those receiving ECPELLA were included in the final analysis. Exchange of Impella to the 5.0/5.5 device was defined as device upgrade. Cumulative mortality and adverse events were retrospectively compared between LVAD center and non-LVAD center. Results A total of 1,549 patients (median age 69 years; LVAD center 21.1%) were analyzed. The 30-day mortality was significantly lower at LVAD center than at non-LVAD center (45.5% versus 54.5%, p = 0.002; Figure). Management at LVAD center and Impella upgrade were independently associated with lower 30-day mortality, with adjusted hazard ratio of 0.791 (95% CI 0.658-0.953, p = 0.013) and 0.483 (95% CI 0.339-0.690, p &lt; 0.001), respectively, instead of LVAD implantation. Conclusions Impella upgrade and management at LVAD center were associated with reduced 30-day mortality in patients with AMI-CS receiving ECPELLA. Further approaches are warranted to establish a standardized and regionalized network of care for cardiogenic shock.
title: Does management at specialized LVAD center improve survival in AMI-related cardiogenic shock treated with ECPELLA?

abstract: Abstract Background Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) is frequently required to stabilise advanced heart failure patients (AHF) awaiting heart transplantation (HTx) under Status 2 criteria. Contemporary practice has shifted towards greater use of surgically implanted microaxial pumps (Impella CP, 5.0, or 5.5) compared with intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), yet comparative post-transplant outcomes remain uncertain. Purpose This study aimed to compare post-transplant outcomes in patients with AHF awaiting heart transplantation who received either Impella microaxial pumps or IABP as temporary mechanical circulatory support until the transplant. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were systematically searched. We included studies comparing Impella versus IABP as a bridge-to-transplant in adult Status 2 candidates and pooled effect estimates using random-effects models. Across the provided eligible studies, 15,872 transplanted recipients were analysed. Results Compared with IABP, Impella support was associated with similar 1-year mortality (RR 0.49 [95% CI 0.05–4.66], P=0.53), short-term mortality (RR 1.66 [95% CI 0.46–5.94], P=0.4344), acute rejection (RR 1.23 [95% CI 0.65–2.32], P=0.52), first graft dysfunction (RR 1.08 [95% CI 0.70–1.66], P=0.73), dialysis post-transplant (RR 0.91 [95% CI 0.73–1.13], P=0.40), length of hospital stay (MD −0.05 days [95% CI −1.92 to 1.82], P=0.95), and bleeding at insertion (RR 2.84 [95% CI 0.61–13.20], P=0.16), with lower chronic rejection (RR 0.95 [95% CI 0.91–1.00], P=0.03) but higher post-transplant stroke risk (RR 1.64 [95% CI 1.18–2.28], P=0.003); Impella use was also associated with longer duration of mechanical circulatory support (MD 9.31 days [95% CI 2.34–16.27], P=0.008), greater need for mechanical ventilation at transplantation (RR 1.31 [95% CI 1.04–1.65], P=0.01), and nonsignificant trends towards longer waiting list time (MD 2.20 days [95% CI −0.07 to 4.47], P=0.05) and higher inotrope use at transplant (RR 1.09 [95% CI 0.98–1.21], P=0.09). Conclusions Compared with IABP, Impella support showed no clear mortality or graft-survival advantage and was associated with greater peri-transplant support requirements and higher post-transplant stroke risk.Grafical Abstract
title: Bridge to transplant in the contemporary allocation era: a systematic review and meta-analysis of impella versus intra-aortic balloon pump

abstract: Abstract Background In patients with heart failure (HF) and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, guideline-directed medical therapy improves survival. For advanced HF refractory to medical and device therapies, durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation is indicated. Although LVADs provide substantial left ventricular unloading, preservation of native cardiac function remains important to maintain exercise capacity and quality of life and to prevent aortic regurgitation and right ventricular failure. However, the impact of post-implant HF medical therapy on outcomes has not been well established. Purpose To evaluate the association between HF medical therapy and clinical outcomes after durable LVAD implantation using a nationwide Japanese registry. Methods We analyzed data from the Japanese Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS) between June 2010 and December 2025, including consecutive patients undergoing durable LVAD implantation. Patients who died during the index hospitalization were excluded. Associations between discharge prescriptions of ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blockers, and MRA and all-cause death, right ventricular failure, ventricular arrhythmia, and hemocompatibility-related adverse events were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for key clinical covariates. The association between the number of HF drug classes and outcomes was also examined. Results A total of 1,623 patients were included (mean age 44.9 ± 14.3 years; 73.3% male). At discharge, ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blockers, and MRA were prescribed in 75.3%, 93.2%, and 72.3%, respectively. Beta-blockers were more frequently used in dilated cardiomyopathy and less in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, whereas MRA use was more common in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Patients receiving ACEi/ARB/ARNI had higher estimated glomerular filtration rates and lower loop diuretic use; beta-blocker users had lower pre-implant left ventricular ejection fraction, and MRA users more frequently required loop diuretics. Post-discharge mortality and right ventricular failure were lower in patients treated with ACEi/ARB/ARNI and beta-blockers, whereas MRA was not associated with these outcomes (Figure 1). No significant associations were observed between any medication class and ventricular arrhythmia or hemocompatibility-related adverse events. The number of HF drug classes was associated with all-cause death and right ventricular failure, but not with ventricular arrhythmia or hemocompatibility-related adverse events (Figure 2). Prescription rates remained stable from discharge to one year after LVAD implantation. Conclusion These findings suggest a potential role for selected HF medical therapies in post-LVAD management; however, causal inference is limited by the observational design. RCTs are warranted to confirm these associations and define the optimal medical therapy strategy after durable LVAD implantation.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Association between heart failure medical therapy and clinical outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Severe mitral regurgitation (MR) in advanced chronic heart failure can lead to refractory haemodynamic deterioration requiring Impella support. Evidence for a transcatheter strategy in this population remains limited. Purpose To evaluate short-term outcomes of a transcatheter strategy versus a conservative strategy in this high-risk population. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study using the nationwide Japanese Registry for Percutaneous Ventricular Assist Devices. Consecutive patients with severe MR and advanced chronic heart failure requiring Impella (2.5, CP, 5.0, or 5.5) for haemodynamic stabilisation between 1 February 2020 and 31 December 2023 were included. A transcatheter strategy was defined as transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (MitraClip) during Impella support, whereas a conservative strategy consisted of Impella support with intensive medical therapy without mitral intervention. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Propensity scores were estimated using logistic regression including prespecified baseline covariates: age, body mass index, out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, pre-Impella heart rate, pre-Impella systolic blood pressure, lactate, creatinine, and left ventricular ejection fraction. Overlap weighting was applied and treatment effects were assessed using an overlap-weighted Cox model with robust standard errors. Results A total of 33 patients met the inclusion criteria (transcatheter strategy n=17; conservative strategy n=16). Covariate balance was achieved after overlap weighting (all standardised mean differences &lt;0.20). In-hospital mortality was 29% (5/17) with the transcatheter strategy and 69% (11/16) with the conservative strategy. In the primary overlap-weighted analysis, the transcatheter strategy was associated with a significantly lower risk of in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio 0.24; 95% confidence interval 0.08–0.74; P=0.013). Results were consistent in sensitivity analyses using LASSO-adjusted Cox modelling (hazard ratio 0.29; 95% confidence interval 0.08–0.97) and restricted mean survival time at 60 days (difference 22 days; 95% confidence interval 5–39). Conclusion(s) Among patients with severe MR and advanced chronic heart failure requiring Impella support, a transcatheter strategy was associated with substantially lower in-hospital mortality than a conservative strategy. These findings suggest that a transcatheter strategy during Impella support may be a reasonable therapeutic option in carefully selected patients with refractory haemodynamic compromise.Study flowGraphical abstract
title: Transcatheter strategy for severe mitral regurgitation requiring percutaneous ventricular assist device support

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) frequently requires temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) as part of a bridge-to-decision (BTD) strategy. With the availability of destination therapy (DT) using durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs), treatment pathways have evolved. However, how the DT Era has reshaped practice patterns within BTD strategies and whether such shifts have translated into improved early outcomes remain uncertain. Purpose To describe changes in device utilization and patient outcomes within a BTD strategy before and after the introduction of the DT Era, and to identify consistently high-risk subgroups. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, we analyzed patients with CS who received their first BTD device between January 2017 and December 2025. Temporary MCS devices included extracorporeal LVAD and high-flow percutaneous ventricular assist devices (PVADs). Patients were categorized into a pre-DT Era group (January 2017–April 2021) and a DT Era group (May 2021–December 2025). The primary outcome was 60-day mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses focused on age ≥65 years and ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM). Results Among 191 patients (pre-DT Era: n=104; DT Era: n=87), the use of high-flow PVAD increased markedly from 27.9% to 54.0% in the DT Era (p&lt;0.01), indicating a substantial shift in device allocation. Overall 60-day mortality was 17.8%, with no significant difference between the Eras (17.3% vs. 18.4%, p=0.82). Age ≥65 years and ICM consistently conferred higher risk across both periods (≥65 years: pre-DT Era 50.0% vs. 13.0%, p=0.01; DT Era 45.5% vs. 14.5%, p&lt;0.01; ICM: pre-DT Era 32.4% vs. 9.0%, p&lt;0.01; DT Era 35.7% vs. 10.2%, p&lt;0.01). Conclusions In the DT Era, clinical practice within the BTD strategy shifted toward greater adoption of high-flow PVADs, yet early outcomes remained comparable to those in the pre-DT Era. This discrepancy may reflect the expanded application of BTD strategies to higher-risk patients or persistent constraints in device–patient matching and timing. Across Eras, advanced age and ICM consistently identified high-risk subgroups, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification and optimization of BTD algorithms in the DT Era.
title: Shifts in MCS utilization and early outcomes within a bridge-to-decision strategy for cardiogenic shock across the destination therapy Era

abstract: Abstract Background In the Surgical Treatment for Ischemic Heart Failure Extension Study (STICHES), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) improved long-term survival in patients with ischemic left ventricular (LV) dysfunction compared with medication alone. In contrast, in the Revascularization for Ischemic Ventricular Dysfunction trial (REVIVED-BCIS2), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) did not reduce all-cause mortality compared with medical therapy. Whether baseline symptom profile modifies the treatment effect of revascularization across a broader spectrum of clinical end points remains unknown. Purpose To determine whether the clinical benefit of revascularization over medical therapy differs according to baseline heart failure (HF) severity and angina burden using a win ratio approach applied to pooled patient-level data from STICHES and REVIVED-BCIS2. Methods Patient-level data from both trials (N=1912; all with LV ejection fraction ≤35%) were pooled. The primary end point was a hierarchical composite evaluated by win ratio (WR) using time-to-first event: (1) all-cause death, (2) myocardial infarction, (3) hospitalization for HF, and (4) unplanned revascularization. WRs were computed within each trial (median follow-up 80.5 vs. 40.6 months) and combined via fixed-effects meta-analysis. Inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusting for age, sex, and comorbidities was applied as a sensitivity analysis. Participants were classified into 4 strata by NYHA class (I–II vs III–IV) and CCS angina grade (0–1 vs 2–4). Results Of 1905 patients (median age 63.6, 88% male, mean LVEF 28.2%; 67% NYHA I–II, 35% CCS ≥2), WRs were directionally consistent across all 4 strata: NYHA I–II/CCS 0–1 (47%; WR 1.12, 0.93–1.35), NYHA I–II/CCS 2–4 (20%; WR 1.21, 0.93–1.58), NYHA III–IV/CCS 0–1 (18%; WR 1.26, 0.96–1.66), NYHA III–IV/CCS 2–4 (15%; WR 1.09, 0.82–1.44) (Figure 1). The overall meta-analytic WR was 1.17 (95% CI, 1.04–1.32; p=.011; I²=34.2%); trial-specific WRs were 1.22 (1.06–1.41) in STICHES and 1.03 (0.81–1.30) in REVIVED-BCIS2. Of 902,496 pairwise comparisons, 64% were resolved at all-cause death, with unplanned revascularization showing the largest asymmetry favoring revascularization (24,807 vs 3216 wins). Cox models showed reduced all-cause death (HR 0.87; 0.76–0.98), HF hospitalization (HR 0.77; 0.64–0.92), and unplanned revascularization (HR 0.20; 0.14–0.29); myocardial infarction did not differ significantly (HR 0.82, 0.59–1.14). A 30-day landmark analysis confirmed consistent mortality benefit beyond the periprocedural period. Conclusions In pooled data from STICHES and REVIVED-BCIS2, the direction of revascularization benefit was consistent across all 4 symptom strata defined by NYHA class and CCS grade, though individual strata were likely underpowered. Overall, revascularization demonstrated significant clinical benefit over medical therapy.
title: Does symptom profile modify revascularization benefit in ischemic LV dysfunction? A win ratio analysis pooling STICHES and REVIVED-BCIS2

abstract: Abstract Background The existing evidence on TAVI outcomes in patients with depressed left ventricle ejection fraction (LVEF) is limited, as most major clinical trials excluded this population. At present, there is no evidence available to guide the choice of transcatheter heart valve type in the setting of severely altered LVEF. Methods An observational cohort study was conducted on 631patients with LVEF≤35% who underwent TAVI in different European centers (France, Canada and Spain). Data concerning baseline characteristics, TAVI procedures and transthoracic echocardiography were analyzed. The present study aims to evaluate differences in survival outcomes and changes in LVEF according to valve type (self-expanding (SEV) versus balloon-expandable (BEV)) after TAVI in patients with LVEF ≤35%. Results Baseline characteristics of study population and TAVI procedures were almost comparable between study groups. The rates of TAVI success (97.8% vs 98%), per-TAVI complications and in-hospital complications including death (4.3% vs 2%), vascular complications (2.6% vs 4% for major events, 8.2% vs 7.5% for minor events), stroke (1.3% vs 0.8%), pacemaker implantation (12.9% vs 15.3%), bleeding (6.2% vs 1.9% for major events, 6.8% vs 3.3% for minor events) and severe paravalvular leak (4.7% vs 5.5%) were comparable between groups, except for per-TAVI valve migration, which was more frequent (3% vs 0.5%) in SEV-group (N=232). At hospital discharge and at last follow-up, LVEF was significantly higher in SEV-group vs BEV-group (37.2±11.2 vs 34.9±11.1, 43.2±13.8 vs 39.9±14.6, respectively). The mean trans aortic gradient was significantly lower in patients treated with SEV (8.0±4.5 vs 9.9±4.2) only at hospital discharge. The difference in change of LVEF over 3.5 years tends to be significant in favor of SEV (Δ=14.7±13.1 vs Δ=12.3±13.2, p=0.070). Over a mean follow-up of 3.5±2.4 years, the all-cause mortality rate was 47.4%. No difference in survival outcomes according to valve type was observed despite the difference in LVEF (p=0.39). Conclusion A sustained improvement in LVEF after TAVI in patients with severe cardiac dysfunction was observed. The valve type itself was not associated with differences in survival outcomes after TAVI. However, SEV may be associated with greater improvement in LVEF.
title: Differences in survival outcomes and LVEF of self-expanding versus balloon expandable valves after TAVI in patients with severe cardiac dysfunction

abstract: Abstract Background Heart failure (HF) patients often require contrast-based diagnostic and interventional procedures, yet they remain particularly susceptible to contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI), a complication linked to longer hospital stay and adverse outcomes. While periprocedural IV hydration and contrast minimization are standard preventive measures, data are sparse on whether contemporary HF therapies - angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) and SGLT-2 inhibitors - are associated with CA-AKI risk when patients undergo contrast exposure. Aims To investigate the association of ARNI, SGLT-2 inhibitors, and their combination with CA-AKI in HF patients undergoing iodinated contrast procedures. Methods In a retrospective, single-centre cohort, we analysed 706 HF patients (HFrEF/HFmrEF/HFpEF) exposed to iodinated contrast between 2020 and 2024 via coronary angiography/PCI or contrast-enhanced CT. Pre-procedural exposure was defined as &gt;=30 days of ARNI and/or SGLT-2 inhibitor use before the index procedure, yielding four groups: control (neither), ARNI only, SGLT-2 inhibitor only, and combined ARNI+SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy. CA-AKI was defined per ESUR as a creatinine increase &gt;0.3 mg/dL or &gt;1.5x baseline within 48-72 h after contrast administration. Multivariable logistic regression assessed independent associations, incorporating procedural factors (contrast volume, pre-procedural IV hydration) and clinical/laboratory covariates. Results CA-AKI occurred in 127/706 patients (18%). Those developing CA-AKI received higher contrast volumes (149+/-60 vs 98+/-42 mL; p&lt;0.001) and had higher age and baseline creatinine. Crude CA-AKI rates were 23.5% in controls, 16.4% with ARNI only, 15.7% with SGLT-2 inhibitor only, and 15.7% with combined therapy (overall p=0.123). After adjustment, combined ARNI+SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy was independently associated with markedly lower CA-AKI odds (OR 0.366, 95% CI 0.168-0.799; p=0.012), whereas ARNI alone (OR 0.548; p=0.127) and SGLT-2 inhibitor alone (OR 0.782; p=0.423) were not independently associated. Pre-procedural IV hydration remained an independent protective factor (OR 0.381; p=0.017). Independent risk factors included diabetes (OR 1.963; p=0.015), diuretic use (OR 2.264; p=0.003), greater contrast volume (OR 1.022 per 1 mL; p=0.001), higher uric acid (OR 1.140; p=0.047), and higher CRP (OR 1.008; p=0.029), supporting internal consistency of the model. Conclusion In a real-world HF cohort undergoing iodinated contrast procedures, a protective association with CA-AKI was observed only for combined ARNI+SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy - not for either drug class alone - in addition to the expected benefit of IV hydration. These hypothesis-generating findings support prospective validation and may inform future guidance on periprocedural GDMT management in HF.
title: In heart failure patients, is ARNI and SGLT-2 inhibitor use protective against contrast-associated acute kidney injury?

abstract: Abstract Background Vasospastic angina with non-obstructive coronary artery stenosis (ANOCA) is an underdiagnosed cause of ischemia, usually identified with invasive testing. Objective To evaluate hyperventilation stress echocardiography (HYPSE) for identifying coronary vasospastic endotypes. Methods In a prospective, multi-center study we enrolled 131 patients with ANOCA (mean age 57 ± 12 years; 73% women. All enrolled patients, with the exception of six, demonstrated normal coronary flow velocity reserve during the vasodilator test. HYPSE was performed off anti-ischemic therapy in 6 accredited laboratories. Clinical suspicion of coronary vasospasm was present with at least one of the following criteria: angina at rest (n=84) and/or on exercise with variable threshold (n=89), marked circadian variation with early morning peak (n=24), angina precipitated by cold exposure (n=30) or emotion/stress (n=22), or myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary stenosis (n=18). The HYPSE protocol consisted of 5 minutes of hyperventilation at a respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute. Previously validated criteria of abnormal vasospastic response were inducible RWMA (a marker of epicardial spasm) or a ≥ 10% reduction in CFV from baseline (a marker of microvascular spasm) in the mid-distal left anterior descending coronary artery. Follow-up at 12 months was available in all. Results HYPSE was completed in all patients, without significant side effects. The double product increased after hyperventilation (9570 ± 2303 to. 13017 ± 3202 mmHg*bpm; p &lt; 0.001). HYPSE response was abnormal for either one (inducible RWMA or CFV reduction) or both in 48 patients (36.6%). Inducible RWMA occurred in 8/131 (6.1%), CFV reduction was observed in 44/131 (33.6%). Figure 1 and 2. All diagnosed patients received targeted therapy (calcium-antagonists/nitrates). At follow-up, 2 had unstable angina, and event rates were similarly low in patients with normal (0/83, 0%) and abnormal HYPSE (2/48, 4.16%, p=ns). Conclusion In ANOCA patients with clinical suspicion of coronary vasospasm and with normal coronary flow velocity reserve on conventional stress echo testing, a multi-marker HYPSE approach, using RWMA and CFV as complementary markers of vasospasm is feasible and safely identifies vasospastic endotypes, guiding personalized therapy.CFV at rest and after HYPSENormal and abnormal CFV response
title: Noninvasive identification of coronary vasospasm by hyperventilation stress echocardiography with a multi-marker protocol

abstract: Abstract Background Renal dysfunction in advanced heart failure (HF) patients critically influences heart transplant eligibility and the choice between heart-only transplantation and simultaneous heart-kidney transplantation (SHKT). In many patients, kidney injury reflects potentially reversible cardiorenal syndrome driven by hemodynamic derangements, particularly elevated venous congestion, rather than intrinsic renal disease. Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) devices, such as the Impella 5.5, offers rapid hemodynamic stabilization and may unmask reversible renal dysfunction. Early identification of renal recovery during support could meaningfully impact transplant strategy. Purpose To evaluate whether short-term changes in invasive hemodynamics during Impella 5.5 support are associated with renal function recovery. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients with HF supported with Impella 5.5 as bridge-to-transplant. Invasive hemodynamics and renal function were assessed at baseline and 72 hours post-Impella 5.5 implantation. The primary outcome was the change in estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (ΔeGFR). Univariate and multivariate linear regression analyses evaluated associations between ΔeGFR and changes in Cardiac Index (ΔCI), Pulmonary Artery Pulsatility index (ΔPAPi), Stroke Volume (ΔSV), Mean Arterial Pressure (ΔMAP), and Right Atrial Pressure (ΔRA), adjusting for baseline clinical characteristics. Results The study cohort included 61 patients supported with Impella 5.5 with complete pre- and post-Impella hemodynamic profiles. The majority were male (80.3%), white (58.3%), and 57.4% had hypertension. The median baseline eGFR was 47 mL/min/1.73 m² (27-63). On univariate analysis, ΔGFR was positively associated with ΔCI (β 8.17, p=0.002), ΔPAPi (β 0.86, p=0.020), and ΔSV (β 0.22, p=0.032), but not with ΔMAP or ΔRA (Table 1). In multivariate hemodynamic modeling, both ΔCI (β 13.29, p=0.011) and ΔPAPi (β 0.72, p=0.036) remained independently associated with renal recovery (model R²=0.24) (Table 2). However, in fully adjusted analyses incorporating baseline clinical characteristics, ΔCI emerged as the dominant predictor (β 15.44, p=0.005), whereas baseline hypertension attenuated renal recovery (β −9.80, p=0.023). Other pressure-based indices were not independently predictive. The final model demonstrated moderate explanatory power (R²=0.321, p=0.0066). Additionally, to evaluate potential effect modification, we tested the interaction between ΔCI and baseline hypertension (Table 3). We found no evidence of effect modification by baseline hypertension. Conclusion Collectively, these data reinforce the concept that dynamic hemodynamic response at 72 hours, particularly improvement in cardiac index, may serve as a biologically meaningful marker of reversible cardiorenal physiology and may help inform transplant strategy and timing decisions.Tables
title: Predictors of change in estimated glomerular filtration rate post-impella 5.5 implantation in heart failure patients bridged to transplant

abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) remains associated with substantial post-discharge mortality despite optimized guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Traditional markers such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and natriuretic peptides incompletely capture residual risk at discharge, and determinants of vulnerability across heart failure phenotypes remain insufficiently defined. Aim To identify independent predictors of 24-month all-cause mortality among clinical, biochemical, and echocardiographic parameters assessed prior to discharge in patients hospitalized with ADHF. Methods We prospectively enrolled 556 consecutive patients hospitalized with ADHF in intensive care unit between January 2023 and January 2024. All patients were discharged hemodynamically stable on GDMT. Pre-discharge assessment included clinical characteristics; renal function; natriuretic and myocardial injury biomarkers; inflammatory and fibrosis-related indices (including CRP/albumin ratio, platelet-to-leukocyte ratio, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and FIB-4); and comprehensive echocardiography. Patients were classified according to LVEF as HFrEF (n=194), HFmrEF (n=110), or HFpEF (n=252). Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier analyses assessed associations with 24-month mortality. Results The cohort was elderly (74.3 ± 10.6 years), with atrial fibrillation (AF) present in 64% of patients; 59.2% were discharged in AF. Mean LVEF was 43.8 ± 13.6%, mean eGFR 61.8 ± 23.3 ml/min/1.73 m², and mean hemoglobin 131.8 ± 21.1 g/L. During 24-month follow-up, all-cause mortality was 36.3% (202/556). In multivariable Cox regression analysis (Table 1), AF emerged as the strongest independent predictor of mortality. Lower eGFR, lower hemoglobin, and higher FIB-4 index were also independently associated with increased risk. In contrast, traditional cardiac markers (including LVEF, NT-proBNP, and high-sensitivity troponin I) were not independently predictive after adjustment. Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed significantly reduced survival among patients with AF (mean survival 17.6 vs 20.4 months; log-rank p=0.001)- figure 1. The AF × LVEF interaction was not significant (p=0.107), indicating a consistent prognostic effect of AF across HF phenotypes. Conclusion In this contemporary ADHF cohort discharged euvolemic on optimized GDMT, AF emerged as the strongest phenotype-independent predictor of 24-month mortality, surpassing conventional systolic markers and natriuretic peptides. Renal dysfunction, anemia, and elevated FIB-4 further defined a high-risk phenotype. These findings underscore the need for integrated, discharge-based risk stratification and suggest that rhythm status at discharge may represent a modifiable therapeutic target in ADHF.Figure 1
title: Multisystem risk profiling at discharge identifies a high-risk phenotype in acute decompensated heart failure

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high 30d mortality. After the first 24 hours, clinicians may benefit from routinely available bedside variables to inform ongoing clinical decision making and for supporting patient and family counselling. Purpose To assess whether 24-hour urinary output is associated with 30-day mortality in cardiogenic shock patients who survive the first 24 hours, and to determine whether a simple clinical model incorporating diuresis, lactate, and age improves 30-day risk discrimination compared with SCAI stage assessed at 24 hours. Methods The Multimodal Phenotyping in Patients Referred with Acute Cardiac Failure (MIRACLE) study is an ongoing prospective multicenter cohort of patients with CS, complemented by an accompanying retrospective cohort. For the present analysis, patients with completed in hospital follow up were screened (n=696). Cases with leading triggers of hypoxia, peri interventional complications, unknown cause, infection or sepsis, or ventricular obstruction were excluded (n=26). We then restricted the cohort to patients who survived more than 24 hours and were not discharged from the ICU within 24 hours (n=557). Diuresis was dichotomised at 1 L/ 24 h. Kaplan Meier analyses and Cox regression were performed overall and in predefined subgroups. Adjustment was done for age, lactate at 24h, and SCAI stage at 24h. Discrimination for 30-day mortality was assessed using ROC curves for a model including age, diuresis, and lactate at 24 hours, and compared with SCAI stage at 24 hours using DeLong testing. Results Among 557 day one survivors (median age 69 years, 72% male, 50% AMI CS), median 24-hour diuresis was 1.7 L. Diuresis at least 1 L per 24 hours was associated with lower 30-day mortality (adjusted HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.89). The association was directionally consistent in several subgroups, including male patients (adjusted HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.77), AMI CS (adjusted HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.80), and age 75 years or younger (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.97), but was not statistically significant in females (adjusted HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.61 to 2.04) or non-AMI CS (adjusted HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.49 to 1.21). A model including age, 24 hour diuresis, and lactate at 24 hours showed better discrimination than SCAI at 24 hours alone (AUC 0.78, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.82 vs 0.69, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.73; p &lt; 0.001). Conclusion In day one survivors of CS, higher 24-hour diuresis was associated with lower 30 day mortality. Subgroup analyses suggested that this relationship may not be uniform across clinical strata, with weaker or non significant associations in female patients and in non AMI-CS. These subgroup differences should be examined in more detail to determine whether they represent clinically relevant implications between patient groups. External validation is warranted.
title: First 24-hour diuresis as a prognostic marker in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Survival to hospital discharge in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) marks the beginning of a long journey toward cardiac and functional recovery. Multidimensional disorders and long-term functional disability are increasing, contributing to a growing assistance burden due to improved acute care leading to increased survivorship. However, limited data exist on long-term survival and the implementation of 4-pillar guideline-directed optimized medical therapy (OMT) prescription at follow-up. To address this gap and promote post-discharge medical optimization and functional recovery, we developed the ENIGMA-shock project (framEwork for aN InteGrated assessMent of cArdiac rehabilitation programmes in patients acutely managed for cardiogenic shock) with the aim of improving the management of post-critical syndrome in CS fostering quality improvement strategies starting from patient admission. Purpose To evaluate the 1-year status of CS survivors treated at 13 Italian hub centers experienced in the care of CS patients and a high intensity cardiac rehabilitation, using a hierarchical composite outcome of survival and OMT administration. Methods We analyzed 687 patients from the ALT SHOCK - ENIGMA registry who survived to hospital discharge. The primary 1-year endpoint was assessed using a proportional odds ordinal logistic regression model. The model was adjusted for age, sex, etiology, diabetes, renal insufficiency, SCAI stage, lactate, ejection fraction, and creatinine. The outcome Y was ranked hierarchically from worst to best status: death; alive on 0 drugs; alive on 1 drug; alive on 2 drugs; alive on 3 drugs and alive on OMT (4 drugs). This method predicts the probability of having at least a given number of therapeutic pillars. A nomogram is reported to visually represent the contribution of baseline variables to the probability of reaching a specific ordinal clinical status. Results At 1-year of follow-up, an estimated 45% of patients were dead; 5% of patients were alive without drugs, 14% with one, 16 % with two, 7% with three, and 13% with OMT (Fig 1). Older Age, higher creatinine, lower LVEF, higher SCAI Stage were independent predictor of failure to achieve OMT (Fig. 2). Conclusion In a contemporary cohort of CS patients, 1-year mortality is still high and occurs mostly in the first six-months after hospital discharge. Among survivors, OMT remains underutilized. Future analyses should clarify the determinants of OMT underuse and limited up-titration (e.g., in-hospital complications, clinical status at hospital discharge, tolerability, and adherence to follow-up). To truly redefine the metrics of the treatment in CS, a multidisciplinary alliance has to be promoted since the patient’s admission, involving all the stakeholders in a new early integrated care perspective.Fig 1Fig 2
title: Therapy optimization and 1-year outcomes in cardiogenic shock: insights from the ENIGMA-shock initiative

abstract: Abstract Background Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) has long been deemed a benign condition of acute reversible cardiac dysfunction with favorable long-term prognosis. This assumption has since been questioned, as TTS has shown outcomes similar to matched ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction cohorts.1 Though acute cardiac dysfunction is often quickly reversible, not all patients recover swiftly and identification of vulnerable TTS patients susceptible to critical in-hospital course remains difficult. Purpose This multicenter analysis of TTS patients aimed to (I) investigate factors associated with short-term recovery of systolic function and wall motion abnormalities (WMAs) and (II) identify vulnerable patients susceptible to critical in-hospital outcomes. Methods Patients diagnosed with TTS between January 2013 and December 2024 were retrospectively analyzed across 13 German tertiary care centers. Stratification by severity of left ventricular (LV) dysfunction at admission (LVEF &lt;40%, 40-49%, and &gt;50%) was undertaken to compare three systolic phenotypes. Conditional on a set of confounders, propensity scores and inverse probability weights (IPW) for LV systolic phenotype (LVEF &lt;40%, 40-49%, or &gt;50%) as an outcome were estimated using multinomial logistic regression models. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models were then fitted to analyze three binary outcomes: (I) in-hospital recovery of LV systolic function and (II) wall motion abnormalities (WMAs) from baseline, as well as (III) critical in-hospital course. Critical course was defined by in-hospital mortality, need for inotropic support, mechanical ventilation, development of cardiogenic shock, or requirement of mechanical circulatory support. Results 488 patients with diagnosed TTS were included for analysis. Median LVEF at admission was 40% [IQR 35, 50]. Apical WMAs (echocardiography (85%), ventriculography (82%), MRI (76%)) were more common than non-apical WMAs (echocardiography (29%), ventriculography (29%), MRI (51%)). 34% of patients achieved recovery of initially recorded WMAs to discharge. In patients with an admission LVEF &lt;40%, only 39% achieved recovery of systolic function (LVEF &gt;50%) to discharge. Factors independently associated with WMA reversal to discharge were higher LVEF at admission and atypical TTS. Higher age was associated with lower odds of LV systolic recovery to discharge. Higher odds of critical in-hospital course were seen in patients with lower admission LVEF, younger age, lower pH, and acute neurologic disease. Conclusion Severity of systolic impairment at presentation is a dominant determinant of both limited early recovery and critical in-hospital course. These findings challenge the assumption of uniform reversibility in TTS and emphasize the need for early risk stratification and awareness for high-risk features and variation in presentations.Critical Course ModelRecovery Model
title: Myocardial recovery and critical course in takotsubo syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Myocarditis associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been linked to adverse cardiovascular outcomes; however, contemporary national data evaluating its independent association with in-hospital mortality and critical care utilisation remain limited. Purpose To assess in-hospital mortality and identify independent predictors of death among patients hospitalised with COVID-associated myocarditis compared with non-COVID myocarditis. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a nationally representative inpatient database from 2021. Adult hospitalisations with myocarditis were identified and stratified by COVID status. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiogenic shock, mechanical ventilation, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and arrhythmia. Multivariable logistic regression was performed adjusting for age, sex, cardiogenic shock, mechanical ventilation, ECMO, and arrhythmia. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported. Results Among 2,200 myocarditis admissions, 850 were COVID-associated. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in COVID-associated myocarditis compared with non-COVID myocarditis (24.5% versus 3.7%). After multivariable adjustment, COVID-associated myocarditis remained independently associated with mortality (aOR 4.13, 95% CI 2.80–6.17). Mechanical ventilation demonstrated the strongest association with death (aOR 26.99, 95% CI 18.32–40.4), followed by ECMO (aOR 2.29, 95% CI 1.06–4.84). Increasing age was independently associated with mortality (aOR 1.04 per year, 95% CI 1.03–1.05). Conclusion(s) COVID-associated myocarditis is associated with substantially higher in-hospital mortality compared with non-COVID myocarditis, independent of critical illness markers. Mechanical ventilation and ECMO strongly correlate with mortality, reflecting a severe disease phenotype. These findings highlight the importance of early risk stratification and aggressive supportive management in this high-risk population.Mortality Bar GraphMortality Forest Plot
title: Covid-associated myocarditis and in-hospital mortality: a national inpatient analysis of predictors and outcomes

abstract: Abstract Secondary ischemic mitral regurgitation (SIMR) remains associated with an unfavourable prognosis. Mitral valve replacement (MVR) or restrictive mitral annuloplasty (RMA) combined with coronary artery bypass grafting represent the most common surgical techniques. Nevertheless, 5-year mortality rates remain high and up to half of patients may experience hospitalization for heart failure (HF) within a few years following surgery(1). The Six-Minute Walk Test (6-MWT) is a well-validated measure of functional capacity widely used in patients with HF: it’s sensitive to strongly predicts mortality, morbidity and quality of life(2). A 6-MWT distance ≤300m is a strong independent predictor of adverse outcome(3). The primary composite endpoint was all-cause mortality or HF–related readmission at 5 years in patients undergoing surgery for SIMR. The secondary endpoint was to assess the role of the 6-MWT in monitoring early and mid-term postoperative functional capacity. On-hundreds and thirty-seven consecutive patients with SIMR undergoing RMA or MVR plus CABG were analysed. A 6-MWT was performed at baseline, at 30 days, and at 1 year. ROC analysis was used to identify the optimal pre-operative 6-MWT cut-off for prediction of the primary endpoint. Predictors of adverse outcomes were assessed using Cox regression analysis. Mean age was 66.9±8.6 years, 24.6% were female, median LVEF was 35.8±8.4%, complete revascularization was achieved in all, RMA and MVR were performed in 63 (46%) and 74 (54%) patients, respectively. The ROC analysis identified 217m as the optimal threshold for predicting the primary endpoint (AUC 0.64; sensitivity 77%; specificity 49%). Patients were stratified into impaired (&lt;217m, n=82) and preserved (≥217m, n=55) functional capacity. Patients with preserved functional capacity demonstrated significantly higher event-free survival at 2 years (90.9±7.6% vs 70.7±9.8%, p=0.0238) and at 5 years (81.8±10.2% vs 58.5±10.3%; log-rank p=0.0036) (Figure 1). Age was strongly associated with adverse outcome while MVR was independently associated with a lower risk of events compared with RMA. At 30 days, both groups (impaired and preserved) showed slight or stable improvement. At 1 year, patients with pre-operative preserved 6-MWT showed a dichotomous response pattern, with approximately 50% showing significant improvement whereas the remaining 50% showed a significant decline. By contrast, patients with impaired pre-operative 6-MWT showed a more evenly distributed functional trajectory (Figure 2). These preliminary findings further corroborate the 6-MWT as sensitive and robust tool for long-term functional capacity assessment in patients with SIMR. In this context, our findings suggest a systematic inclusion of the 6-MWT into pre-operative algorithms in order to identify high-risk patients, to improve the decision-making process and to monitor the efficacy of therapy.FIGURE 1FIGURE 2
title: Role of six-minute walk test as a risk stratification tool in patients undergoing surgery for secondary ischemic mitral regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Individuals with diabetes mellitus are at high-risk of heart failure. Despite guideline recommendations, cardiac biomarker–based screening is not routinely performed in current clinical practice. We have developed the iDiabetes platform to enable protocolised, system-level testing embedded within routine diabetic care workflows. Purpose To determine the prevalence of elevated cardiac biomarkers and heart failure in a general diabetic population utilising the iDiabetes Platform. Methods We studied 4,341 patients with diabetes enrolled in the prospective, cluster-randomised iDiabetes trial conducted in primary care. NT-proBNP was measured during routine annual diabetes review, and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-TnI) in patients aged ≥40 years. Echocardiography was performed where clinically indicated in those with elevated biomarkers. Associations between biomarkers were assessed using logistic regression. Results Among 4,194 patients without prior heart failure history (mean age 66 ± 13 years; 60% male; 91% with type 2 diabetes), median NT-proBNP was 92 ng/L (IQR 41–219), and median hs-TnI was 4 ng/L (IQR 2.5–7.2). NT-proBNP levels ≥125 ng/L were observed in 1,653 patients (38%), including 1,008 (23%) with 125–399 ng/L, 528 (12%) with 400–1,999 ng/L, and 117 (3%) with ≥2,000 ng/L. Elevated hs-TnI was observed in 109 (2.5%). Isolated NT-proBNP elevation occurred in 1561 (36%), whereas isolated hs-TnI elevation was present only in 29 patients (0.7%). 79 (2%) had both biomarkers elevated. NT-proBNP and hs-TnI were moderately correlated (Spearman’s rho = 0.492, 95% CI 0.468–0.515; p &lt; 0.001). 315 patients (mean age 75 ± 9 years; 60% male; 90% with type 2 diabetes) underwent echocardiography. Mean LVEF was 55 ± 10%. New clinically significant echo findings were identified in 111 individuals (35%). 267 (85%) had LVEF &gt;50%; 26 (8%) had LVEF 41-49%, and 22 (7%) had LVEF &lt;=40%. Structural abnormalities were common, including left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in 101 (32%), left atrial (LA) dilatation in 87 (28%) and right atrial (RA) dilatation in 75 (24%). Other new cardiac diagnoses were made in 25 individuals (8%), including valvular heart disease in 19 (6%), atrial fibrillation in 4 (1.3%), LV thrombus in 1 (0.3%), and tricuspid valve mass in 1 (0.3%). 204 (65%) had no clinically significant echocardiographic abnormalities. Conclusions Integrating cardiac biomarker screening into routine diabetes care identified subclinical cardiac disease in a substantial proportion of individuals without known heart failure. Over one-third had an NT-proBNP≥125 ng/L, and among those undergoing echocardiography, one-third had new clinically significant cardiac findings. These findings highlight the feasibility and utility of routine biomarker testing to support early detection of heart failure and cardiovascular disease in patients with diabetes, potentially enabling earlier intervention and improved outcomes.Cardiac Biomarker LevelsCardiac Abnormalities
title: Cardiac biomarkers-based screening in patients with diabetes mellitus at a population level

abstract: Abstract Background Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure driven by transthyretin (TTR) misfolding and amyloid deposition. Effective therapies exist that slow progression, but diagnosis often occurs at advanced stages when substantial myocardial damage is already present 1. Current diagnostics primarily detect established amyloid burden or downstream injury rather than underlying molecular events 3. Here, we describe the development of the Amyfold plasma assay, a minimally invasive Covalent Protein Painting (CPP)-based assay2 that enables direct detection of TTR misfolding in human plasma - the earliest and most actionable pathogenic step in ATTR-CM, which precedes amyloid fibril formation by years. Methods The Amyfold assay quantifies solvent accessibility patterns reflecting circulating TTR conformational states. Performance was evaluated using recombinant TTR, biopsy-derived amyloid fibrils and plasma samples (up to 850 samples from up to 212 individuals). Analytical validation included intra-assay precision and interlaboratory reproducibility testing. Translational evaluation was performed in blinded validation studies including wtATTR-CM, hereditary ATTR (hATTR), and a longitudinal cohort of genetically confirmed asymptomatic ATTR carriers (288 samples, 32 patients). Misfolding signatures were correlated with cardiac functional and structural measures including IVS thickness, myocardial biomarkers (NT-proBNP, hsTn), disease progression, and treatment response. Results Analytical validation demonstrated robust performance (intra-assay CV 2.3%; interlaboratory CV 7.7%). Circulating TTR misfolding signatures differentiated ATTR-CM from controls and correlated strongly with interventricular septal thickness (R² = 0.82), high-sensitivity troponin (R² = 0.80), and left ventricular ejection fraction (R² = 0.72) in a blinded validation study with confirmed wtATTR-CM patients. Discriminatory analysis yielded 95% sensitivity and specificity for ATTR-related cardiac involvement, independent of sex. Observed conformational patterns aligned with cryo-EM structures. Longitudinal analyses revealed distinct molecular trajectories, identifying progressive misfolding dynamics in some asymptomatic carriers, while others exhibited substantial baseline misfolding, suggesting capture beyond the earliest disease phase. Conclusion Plasma-based structural profiling of circulating transthyretin protein identifies upstream disease related-TTR misfolding as a potential early marker for ATTR-CM development associated with structural remodeling, myocardial injury, and functional decline in ATTR-CM. Clinical Implications. Blood-based detection of TTR misfolding may facilitate diagnostic workup of suspected ATTR-CM patients, enable minimally invasive early identification of at risk individuals, and support monitoring of disease progression and treatment response in ATTR-CM.
title: Detecting transthyretin protein misfolding before amyloid deposition: a structural proteomics blood test for early identification of transthyretin amyloid (ATTR) cardiomyopathy

abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) often results from atherosclerotic plaque rupture, causing thrombotic coronary occlusion and myocardial ischaemia. The VEGF family promotes post-ischaemic repair via angiogenesis and vascular homeostasis. VEGF-A, upregulated by hypoxia (HIF-1α), inflammation, and stress, acts via VEGFR-1/2 to drive beneficial neovascularization but also increases permeability, potentially contributing to maladaptive remodelling. VEGF-D supports angiogenesis (VEGFR-2) and lymphangiogenesis (VEGFR-3), with emerging yet limited clinical relevance in ACS. Purpose Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A and VEGF-D have distinct roles in angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis. We investigated their associations with cardiac recovery and prognosis in the acute and sub-acute period after an acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Methods We measured baseline plasma VEGF-A and VEGF-D within 24 hours of admission in a prospective cohort of 525 ACS patients and repeated the measurements six weeks later in a follow-up subgroup (n = 117). Incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality were followed via national registries. Echocardiography was performed at 1-year post-ACS in the follow-up subgroup. Results During a median follow-up of 25.8–39.5 months, 87 patients experienced MACE, 41 were hospitalised for HF, and 63 died. In Cox regression analyses adjusted for clinical parameters, baseline VEGF-A was independently associated with incident MACE (HR per 1-SD increase 1.46, 95 % CI 1.14–1.89, p = 0.030), HF (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.18–2.58, p = 0.006), and mortality (HR 1.33, 95% CI 1.004–1.77, p = 0.047). Baseline VEGF-D showed no associations with the outcomes. In contrast, follow-up VEGF-D was associated with HF independently of all considered confounders (HR 2.22 per 1-SD increase, 95 % CI 1.07–4.58, p = 0.032). Baseline VEGF-A was identified as the strongest independent predictive biomarker at baseline for all outcomes and follow-up VEGF-D was the strongest biomarker for HF, in Cox proportional regression models including TnT and NT-proBNP. In ROC analyses, addition of baseline VEGF-A and follow-up VEGF-D to clinical parameters improved outcome discrimination. In the follow-up subgroup, higher baseline VEGF-A and higher six-week VEGF-D were correlated with lower LVEF at 1-year, supporting the associations between biomarkers and HF. Further, among the 44 patients discharged with an LVEF &gt;50% and no prevalent HF, elevated baseline VEGF-A independently predicted LVEF decline (defined as &gt;5% absolute decrease) (OR 2.65 per 1-SD increase, 95 % CI 1.06–6.64, p = 0.038). Conclusion VEGF-A and VEGF-D have distinct and complementary predictive values in the acute and sub-acute periods post-ACS. Our study identifies baseline VEGF-A as a strong independent predictor of negative prognosis and follow-up VEGF-D as a potential candidate biomarker to identify patients at high risk for HF.The inclusion of the study population
title: Vascular endothelial growth factors A and D as independent prognostic factors in acute coronary syndrome patients

abstract: Abstract Background Early acute heart failure (HF) following ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is conventionally attributed to impaired systolic function. However, a clinically relevant subset develops acute HF despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), suggesting alternative pathophysiological drivers. Purpose To determine independent determinants of early acute HF among STEMI patients with preserved LVEF (&gt;50% by CMR) and evaluate the incremental predictive value of structural myocardial injury. Methods Within the multicenter SINERGY-ACUTE cohort, patients with preserved LVEF (&gt;50% by CMR) were analyzed (n=143 of 268 patients). Early acute HF was defined as Killip class ≥II and/or elevated NT-proBNP at admission. Structural parameters included infarct size (LGE%), LV volumes, microvascular obstruction (MVO), and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH). Penalized multivariable logistic regression was applied. Hierarchical models were constructed: (1) clinical; (2) clinical + LVEF; (3) clinical + LVEF + structural CMR parameters. Interaction between preserved EF and infarct size was formally tested. Discrimination was assessed by AUC (95% CI) with DeLong testing. Incremental value was evaluated by ΔAUC, Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), and Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI). Internal validation used 1000-bootstrap resampling with calibration and decision curve analyses. Results Among patients with preserved LVEF (n=143), early acute HF occurred in 20.3%, 54.5 were male and 45.5% female with the median age of 60 years. Within the preserved EF range, LVEF was not independently associated with HF after adjustment. Independent determinants were infarct size (OR 1.27 per 5% increase; p&lt;0.001), LV end-systolic volume (OR 1.21 per 10 mL; p&lt;0.001), MVO (OR 1.93; p&lt;0.001), IMH (OR 2.18; p&lt;0.001), and log NT-proBNP (OR 1.51; p&lt;0.001). The interaction between preserved EF and infarct size was not significant. Clinical model AUC was 0.69, increasing to 0.71 with LVEF and to 0.86 with structural CMR integration (ΔAUC +0.15; p&lt;0.001). Reclassification improved significantly (NRI 0.41; IDI 0.18; both p&lt;0.001). Bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.84 with preserved calibration. Conclusions In STEMI patients with preserved LVEF, early acute HF is driven by structural myocardial injury and microvascular damage rather than systolic dysfunction. CMR-derived infarct size, MVO, and IMH provide substantial incremental discrimination beyond EF-based assessment, challenging reliance on preserved LVEF as a marker of low early HF risk.
title: Acute heart failure despite preserved ejection fraction after STEMI: structural and microvascular injury as dominant determinants

abstract: Abstract Background Adverse left ventricular (LV) remodeling after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a principal mechanistic driver of subsequent heart failure and mortality. Although cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) enables comprehensive quantification of infarct size and microvascular injury, the incremental prognostic value of a structured imaging-based risk score beyond clinical assessment has not been definitively established. Purpose To develop and internally validate an Integrated CMR Risk Score for early prediction of adverse LV remodeling following primary PCI. Methods Consecutive STEMI patients from the multicenter SINERGY-ACUTE project, undergoing early CMR (n=268), were evaluated. Adverse remodeling was defined as ≥20% increase in LV end-systolic volume or ≥10% decline in LVEF at follow-up. Independent predictors were identified using penalized multivariable logistic regression. The Integrated CMR Risk Score (0–5 points) incorporated: infarct size (highest tertile, 2 points), LVESV above median (1 point), presence of microvascular obstruction (MVO, 1 point), and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH, 1 point). Model discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis with DeLong testing. Incremental value was evaluated using ΔAUC, Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), and Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI). Internal validation used 1000-bootstrap resampling. Calibration and decision curve analyses were performed. Results A total of 268 STEMI patients with early CMR was included in the study of whom 18 patients fulfilled criteria for adverse LV remodeling during the follow-up. Independent predictors of adverse LV remodeling were: infarct size (per 5% increase: OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.15–1.42; p&lt;0.001), LVESV (per 10 mL: OR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10–1.35; p&lt;0.001), MVO (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.48–3.09; p&lt;0.001), and IMH (OR 2.67, 95% CI 1.72–4.13; p&lt;0.001). Clinical model AUC was 0.66 (95% CI 0.62–0.70) versus 0.79 (95% CI 0.75–0.83) for the Integrated Score (ΔAUC +0.13; p&lt;0.001). Reclassification improved significantly (NRI 0.32; IDI 0.11; both p&lt;0.001). Optimism-corrected AUC was 0.77. Calibration was preserved (slope 0.94; Hosmer–Lemeshow p&gt;0.20). Remodeling rates increased stepwise (9%, 24%, 51% across score strata). Conclusions An Integrated CMR Risk Score combining infarct size, microvascular injury, and baseline LV remodeling parameters provides statistically robust, independently validated, and clinically meaningful prediction of adverse LV remodeling after STEMI, substantially outperforming clinical assessment alone and enabling early high-risk stratification.
title: An imaging-based integrated CMR risk score robustly predicts adverse left ventricular remodeling after STEMI

abstract: Abstract Background Microvascular obstruction (MVO) and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) represent the most severe phenotypes of reperfusion injury following primary PCI in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Their structural and clinical determinants, as well as the incremental prognostic contribution of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), remain incompletely defined in contemporary practice. Purpose To identify independent predictors of MVO and IMH and quantify the incremental predictive value of CMR-derived parameters beyond clinical and angiographic assessment. Methods In consecutive STEMI patients from the multicenter SINERGY-ACUTE cohort undergoing early CMR (n=268), MVO was assessed by late gadolinium enhancement and IMH by T2* imaging. Penalized multivariable logistic regression was applied to account for collinearity. Hierarchical models were constructed: (1) clinical, (2) clinical + angiographic, and (3) clinical + angiographic + CMR (infarct size, LV volumes, MVO/IMH). Discrimination was evaluated using AUC with 95% CI and DeLong testing. Incremental value was assessed by ΔAUC, Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), and Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. Results A total of 268 STEMI patients with CMR was included in the study with the median age of 60 years. MVO was detected in 40.8%, while IMH was detected in 19% of patients. Independent predictors of MVO were infarct size (per 5% increase: OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.17–1.36; p&lt;0.001), LVESV (per 10 mL: OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.10–1.27; p&lt;0.001), angiographic no-reflow (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.42–2.66; p&lt;0.001), and log peak troponin (OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.22–1.63; p&lt;0.001). Clinical AUC was 0.63 versus 0.86 for the CMR-integrated model (ΔAUC +0.23; p&lt;0.001; NRI 0.38; IDI 0.14). Independent predictors of IMH were infarct size (OR 1.31 per 5%; p&lt;0.001), LVESV (OR 1.22 per 10 mL; p&lt;0.001), presence of MVO (OR 2.48; p&lt;0.001), and log NT-proBNP (OR 1.47; p&lt;0.001). Clinical AUC improved from 0.67 to 0.91 with CMR integration (ΔAUC +0.24; p&lt;0.001; NRI 0.44; IDI 0.18). Bootstrap-corrected AUC values remained robust with preserved calibration. Conclusions Infarct size is the dominant structural determinant of both MVO and IMH after STEMI. Notably, MVO was independently associated with peak troponin, reflecting the magnitude of acute myocardial necrosis, whereas IMH was independently linked to NT-proBNP, consistent with greater hemodynamic stress and early ventricular dysfunction. CMR-derived parameters provide substantial and statistically robust incremental discrimination beyond clinical and angiographic assessment, supporting systematic early imaging-based phenotyping of reperfusion injury in contemporary STEMI care.
title: Structural myocardial injury and microvascular damage independently determine severe reperfusion phenotypes after STEMI: results from a large contemporary CMR cohort

abstract: Abstract Background The percutaneous ventricular assist device (PVAD) is an established mechanical circulatory support modality for cardiogenic shock (CS). While its primary effect is left ventricular unloading, venous return remains a fundamental determinant of systemic hemodynamics. Venous return is governed by stressed blood volume (SBV), yet the impact of PVAD support on SBV has never been systematically evaluated. Purpose To determine whether PVAD modifies SBV in patients with CS and to validate the physiological reproducibility of clinically observed SBV changes in an experimental model using a reverse translational approach. Methods Clinical study: We organized a prospective multicenter registry of patients with CS supported by PVAD therapy (UNLOADERS-PVAD registry, N = 189). SBV was estimated from right atrial pressure (RAP), left atrial pressure (LAP), and CO using a generalized circulatory equilibrium model (Fig. 1A). SBV trends were analyzed at four points: pre-PVAD, just after PVAD, 24-hrs after PVAD, and before PVAD weaning. Temporal changes were assessed using a linear mixed-effects model. Experimental study: Acute heart failure was induced in four anesthetized canines (Beagles, 10.40.3 kg) by coronary microembolization. We implanted PVAD under fluoroscopic guidance. SBV was calculated using the same generalized circulatory equilibrium model as human. Hemodynamic measurements were obtained at minimum support (P1), maximum support (P3–7)), and after returning to minimum support for 30-min at each stage. Results In UNLOADERS-PVAD registry, compared with pre-PVAD, SBV showed significant reduction just after PVAD initiation (p &lt; 0.001) and PVAD achieved a 16.5 mL/kg decrease in SBV from pre-PVAD implantation to before PVAD weaning (p &lt; 0.001) (Fig. 1B). In the canine model, the increase of PVAD support immediately reduced SBV, which returned to baseline after minimum PVAD support, reproducing the clinical findings. In a representative case, plasma epinephrine levels varied inversely with changes in PVAD flow, paralleling SBV dynamics (Fig. 2A). SBV decreased at maximum support and returned to baseline levels upon returning to minimum support in all four animals, demonstrating a consistent directional response. Additionally, SBV demonstrated an inverse relationship with PVAD-induced increases in arterial pressure (r = −0.51) (Fig. 2B), suggesting baroreflex-mediated sympathetic withdrawal and redistribution of venous blood volume. Conclusion PVAD support induces immediate SBV reduction in CS in both clinical and experimental settings. These findings suggest that PVAD therapy not only unloads the left ventricle but also modulates autonomic tone and systemic venous return through baroreflex-mediated mechanisms.Fig.1FIg.2
title: Immediate reduction in stressed blood volume after percutaneous ventricular assist device implantation in cardiogenic shock: Reverse translational study suggesting baroreflex-mediated redistribution

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac index (CI) guides haemodynamic management in critically ill patients with cardiogenic shock or advanced cardiac failure. Continuous thermodilution and indirect Fick-derived CI are frequently used interchangeably, although their relative prognostic value is uncertain. Purpose To compare the prognostic performance of continuous thermodilution and indirect Fick-derived CI for ITU mortality. Methods We retrospectively analysed 1,045 consecutive critically ill cardiac patients admitted to a quaternary ITU undergoing invasive hemodynamic monitoring (mean age 58.9±16.2 years; 67% male; 65% on inotropes; mortality 24.9%). CI was assessed simultaneously by continuous thermodilution and indirect Fick method using estimated oxygen consumption (VO2). Multivariable models included both CI measurements and were adjusted for age, sex, inotrope use, mechanical ventilation, and renal ultrafiltration. Results Agreement analysis showed minimal mean bias (0.11 L/min/m²) but wide limits (−1.83 to +2.07) and percent error of 64%, well above accepted interchangeability thresholds. Both CI measurements demonstrated strong physiological coherence, showing robust associations with SvO2 (R²=0.60, p&lt;0.001). In univariable analysis, continuous thermodilution predicted ITU mortality (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.52–0.76, p&lt;0.001), whereas indirect Fick-derived CI did not (OR 1.13, p=0.156). Continuous thermodilution showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.71), while indirect Fick-derived CI showed poor discrimination (AUC &lt;0.6). In multivariable analysis including both measurements and clinical confounders, only continuous thermodilution retained independent prognostic significance. Prognostic value was stronger in patients receiving inotropes (OR 0.59). A CI threshold of 2.35 L/min/m² identified high-risk patients for mortality with high specificity (81.5%). Conclusions Continuous thermodilution and indirect Fick-derived CI are not clinically interchangeable. Although both methods are positively associated with SvO2, only continuous thermodilution provides independent prognostic information for mortality, supporting its preferential use for invasive risk stratification in high-risk critically ill cardiac ITU patients.
title: Continuous thermodilution, but not indirect Fick-derived cardiac index, independently predicts mortality in 1045 cardiac ICU patients

abstract: Abstract Background Outcomes in high-acuity transplant candidates may be influenced by admission hemodynamic profile and the timing of escalation to temporary mechanical circulatory support. Objectives Evaluate the association between admission hemodynamic profile, time-to-Impella escalation, and 1-year post-transplant mortality. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of Impella 5.5–bridged heart transplant recipients from 2020 to 2025. Admission hemodynamic parameters were defined by the first invasive profile obtained prior to Impella 5.5 insertion. Timing metrics included admission-to-Impella and right heart catheterization-to-Impella intervals. We defined early tMCS placement as &lt;12 days from admission. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality. Continuous variables are reported as median (IQR) and categorical variables as n (%). Groups were compared using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test and Fisher’s exact test, as appropriate. Given the low event rate, Firth-penalized logistic regression was used for univariable and parsimonious multivariable analyses, adjusting for age, admission hemodynamic severity, and time-to-Impella. Cox proportional hazards models were used as sensitivity analyses. Results Among 165 recipients, 9 deaths (5.5%) occurred at 1 year. 59 patients were classified as delayed, and 106 as having an early implant timeframe. The median admission-to-Impella time was 8 days (IQR 3–17). Baseline age and admission hemodynamic measures, including right atrial pressure (RAP), mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), and cardiac index (CI), were similar between groups. Time-to-Impella was significantly longer in the delayed group (median 22 vs 5 days, p &lt; 0.001). One-year mortality was numerically higher in the delayed group compared with the early group (10.2% vs 2.8%), although this difference did not reach statistical significance (unadjusted OR 3.89, 95% CI 0.93–16.16; p = 0.071). In univariable analyses, admission hemodynamic variables, RAP showed a borderline association (OR 1.09 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.00–1.20; p = 0.061) with mortality. In parsimonious multivariable Firth models adjusting for age and admission hemodynamic severity, time-to-Impella (per 5 days) was not independently associated with mortality (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.84–1.35; p = 0.37). Higher baseline RAP remained associated with increased 1-year mortality, with a borderline association (OR 1.10 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.00–1.21; p = 0.049). Conclusions Our single-center experience highlights that patients with elevated RAP are associated with an independent risk of 1-year mortality. Although delayed support was associated with numerically higher unadjusted mortality, timing was not an independent predictor after adjustment, highlighting the dominant role of physiologic severity at presentation and the need for earlier recognition of high-risk hemodynamic profile.Univariable and Multivariable AnalysisBaseline Characteristics
title: Admission hemodynamics and timing of impella 5.5 as predictors of 1-year mortality after heart transplantation

abstract: Abstract Aims Targeted protein degradation, particularly extracellular TPD (eTPD), represents a promising therapeutic strategy for traditionally undruggable targets. However, its application in cardiovascular disease remains limited. This study aimed to develop CardioTAC, a novel heart-targeting bispecific antibody platform using Natriuretic Peptide Receptor 1 (NPR1) to degrade extracellular proteins in myocardial tissue. Methods and Results Combining Human Protein Atlas database with multi-organ immunofluorescence staining, we observed that NPR1 is highly expressed in cardiac tissue. Screening with EVOLVEpro directed evolution technology, we designed NPR1 Targeting Chimeras (CardioTAC), a heterobispecific antibody modality for disease-relevant targets depletion through NPR1-dependent lysosomal in cardiomyocytes. Biological experiments demonstrate that CardioTAC can achieve high degradation efficacy for three extracellular soluble proteins (S100 calcium-binding protein A8/A9, growth differentiation factor-15, and human epididymis protein 4) in myocardial infarction and ischemia/reperfusion mice models, which highlighting the generalizability and modularity of our approach. Multi-organ immunohistochemistry and cardiac proteomics demonstrated the specific targeted degradation of CardioTAC in cardiac tissue. Comprehensive assessment of hepatic/renal function parameters and multi-organ histopathology demonstrated an excellent safety profile for CardioTAC. Integrated spatial transcriptomic and proteomic analyses indicate that CardioTAC ameliorates cardiomyocyte injury, reduces fibrosis, and attenuates infiltration of inflammatory cells in cardiac tissue. Conclusion Our findings establish CardioTAC as a novel and versatile eTPD platform technology. By harnessing the internalization function of NPR1, CardioTAC enables the efficient degradation of specific extracellular targets, offering a powerful new approach for modulating pathogenic factors in cardiovascular diseases.Graphical abstract
title: Natriuretic peptide receptor 1 targeting chimeras for cardiovascular selective degradation of extracellular proteins

abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute heart failure (AHF) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with persistently high in-hospital death rates despite advances in guideline-directed therapy (1). Sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have demonstrated rapid hemodynamic and renal benefits across the spectrum of left ventricular ejection fraction (2). Although both dapagliflozin and empagliflozin have proven efficacy in heart failure, direct comparative data, particularly when initiated early during cardiac ICU admission, remain limited (3). Objective To compare early in-hospital initiation of dapagliflozin versus empagliflozin in patients admitted for acute heart failure and evaluate their impact on in-hospital survival and safety. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,800 consecutive adults admitted to the cardiac ICU for acute heart failure (de novo or acute decompensation) between July 2023 and April 2025. Early initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors was defined as treatment within 48 hours of admission.
