After applying exclusion criteria, including dialysis, prior transplantation, eGFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m², cardiogenic shock, diabetic ketoacidosis, symptomatic hypotension, or early transfer, 1,546 patients were included. Patients were categorised into dapagliflozin (n=450), empagliflozin (n=398), or no early SGLT2 inhibitor groups. The primary endpoint was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression assessed independent associations with mortality. Results Among 1,546 included patients (mean age 63.4 ± 15.1 years; 57.5% male; mean LVEF 44.4 ± 14.6%), early SGLT2 inhibitors were initiated in 848 patients. Overall, in-hospital survival did not differ significantly between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin (P=0.29). Subgroup analyses showed higher survival with dapagliflozin in patients with reduced LVEF (76% vs 61%; P=0.001), whereas empagliflozin was associated with higher survival in patients with right ventricular dysfunction (36.8% vs 11.8%; P=0.02) and chronic kidney disease (33.3% vs 25%; P=0.032). Hypotension was rare (0% empagliflozin vs 0.5% dapagliflozin; P&lt;0.001), and rates of acute kidney injury were similar between groups. Low event rates were observed in patients receiving combined SGLT2 inhibitor and sacubitril/valsartan therapy. Conclusion Early initiation of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin was associated with comparable overall survival and favourable safety profiles. Subgroup findings suggest differential benefits according to ventricular function and renal status, supporting early SGLT2 inhibitor use in acute heart failure.
title: Early in-hospital initiation of dapagliflozin versus empagliflozin in acute heart failure: impact on in-hospital survival and safety

abstract: Abstract Background The prognostic relevance of pre-event heart failure (HF) guideline-optimized medical therapy (OMT) intensity in HF-related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) remains poorly defined. Purpose To assess the association between pre-event OMT intensity—defined by the four HF pharmacological pillars—and in-hospital mortality in HF-CS and in the acute decompensated HF-CS (ADHF-CS) subgroup. Methods Multicentre registry including patients with HF-CS (N=248) and the ADHF-CS subgroup (N=135). Pre-event OMT intensity was defined as the number of HF drug classes (0–4) among the four pillars (beta-blocker, RAAS inhibitor and/or ARNI, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, SGLT2 inhibitor) and reported as 0-4 pillars, including OMT4 (4/4 pillars) and OMT≥3 (≥3 pillars). The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality; associations with mortality were estimated using robust Poisson regression (risk ratios, RR) adjusted for age, sex, SCAI class (A-B/C/D-E), admission lactate, baseline haemoglobin and use of mechanical circulatory support (Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump (IABP)/Impella/VA-ECMO). Results In-hospital mortality was 27.0% (67/248) in HF-CS and 31.9% (43/135) in the ADHF-CS subgroup. OMT4 (4/4 pillars) was present in 22/248 (8.9%) HF-CS patients and 21/135 (15.6%) in ADHF-CS patients (p=0.070); OMT≥3 was present in 80/248 (32.3%) and 65/135 (48.1%), respectively (p=0.003). In HF-CS, OMT4 was associated with lower mortality versus &lt;4 pillars (4.5% vs 29.2%, p=0.011; adjusted RR 0.17, 95%CI 0.03–0.96, p=0.045), whereas OMT≥3 was not associated with lower mortality (18.8% vs 31.0%, p=0.061; adjusted RR 0.63, 95%CI 0.38–1.03, p=0.067). In ADHF-CS, both OMT4 (4.8% vs 36.8%, p=0.004; adjusted RR 0.13, 95% CI 0.02–0.74, p=0.021) and OMT≥3 (18.5% vs 44.3%, p=0.002; adjusted RR 0.45, 95%CI 0.26–0.78, p=0.004) were associated with lower mortality. Each additional pre-event pillar was associated with lower risk (adjusted RR per +1 pillar 0.78, 95%CI 0.66–0.92, p=0.003). In ADHF-CS, in-hospital mortality by pre-event OMT score (0–4 pillars) is shown in Figure 1. Conclusions In this real-world HF-CS registry, greater pre-event OMT intensity—most consistently in ADHF-CS—was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective confirmation.Fig 1
title: Pre-event guideline-directed optimized medical therapy intensity and in-hospital mortality in heart failure–related cardiogenic shock: insights from the ALT-SHOCK registry

abstract: Abstract Background Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) after cardiogenic shock is increasingly recognized as a determinant of long-term outcomes, yet most data describe heterogeneous shock etiologies. In acute myocardial infarction–related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the clinical factors that influence discharge GDMT prescription remain unclear, especially across left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) phenotypes. Purpose We aimed to describe discharge GDMT patterns in AMI-CS survivors grouped by discharge LVEF and to model AMI-CS-specific clinical predictors of GDMT prescription. Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of adult AMI-CS survivors and stratified patients by discharge LVEF (≤40% vs &gt;40%). Discharge GDMT was categorized by class (beta-blocker; renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system inhibitors [RAASi: ACEi/ARB/ARNI/MRA]; SGLT2 inhibitor). We used a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of discharge RAASi and beta-blocker prescription. Results Among 892 AMI-CS survivors, 829 with discharge echocardiography data were analyzed (LVEF &gt;40%: n=297; LVEF ≤40%: n=532). Patients with LVEF &gt;40% were more often female (32.0% vs 24.8%, p=0.026) and were revascularized more often (86.2% vs 77.6%, p=0.003). Patients with LVEF ≤40% more often required mechanical circulatory support (74.1% vs 67.3%, p=0.040), with no difference in device type. Discharge creatinine was higher in LVEF ≤40% (median 1.1 [0.9–1.5] vs 1.0 [0.8–1.3], p&lt;0.001), while discharge hemodialysis rates were similar (5.7% vs 7.1%, p=0.43). At discharge, RAASi use was lower in LVEF &gt;40% vs ≤40% (44.8% vs 53.9%, p=0.011), beta-blocker use was similar (p=0.30), and SGLT2 inhibitor use was low overall but prescribed more in LVEF ≤40% (4.3% vs 1.0%, p=0.009). Multivariable analysis showed that older age (aOR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97–0.99; p&lt;0.001) and severe renal dysfunction (creatinine &gt;2.5 mg/dL and/or discharge hemodialysis: aOR 0.27, 95% CI 0.17–0.43; p&lt;0.001) reduced odds of RAASi prescription, while LVEF ≤40% predicted higher odds (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.22–2.15; p&lt;0.001). Similarly, older age (aOR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96–0.99; p=0.001) and renal dysfunction (aOR 0.55, 95% CI 0.33–0.94; p=0.023) were associated with lower odds of beta-blocker prescription. Conclusion In AMI-CS survivors, discharge GDMT varies by LVEF phenotype and is limited by renal dysfunction and age. Our findings emphasize a high-risk subgroup that may benefit from prospective optimization strategies for post-discharge medical therapy after AMI-CS.RAAS-inhibitor and Beta-blocker Prescription
title: Patterns and predictors of discharge guideline-directed medical therapy in survivors of acute myocardial infarction–related cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Comprehensive guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) improves survival in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). However, real-world implementation and its longitudinal impact on outcomes remain incompletely characterized. Purpose This study evaluated temporal trends in GDMT implementation and their association with 1-year clinical outcomes using a large-scale nationwide registry Methods We analyzed patients with HFrEF (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≤40%) enrolled in the KorHF III registry. Prescription patterns of four foundational pillars—renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors, beta-blockers (BB), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA), and SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i)—were assessed at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Patients were categorized by the number of combined therapies. The primary outcomes were all-cause death and HF re-admission at 1 year. Results Among 4,010 patients (age, 65.8 years; 65.7% male; mean LVEF 27.1%), discharge prescription rates were 83.5% for RAS inhibitors, 77.3% for BB, 67.1% for MRA, and 20.8% for SGLT2i. RAS inhibitors and BB prescriptions remained stable, whereas MRA use declined significantly to 54.1% and SGLT2i use increased to 25.7% at 12 months (P for trend&lt;0.001 for both). Over 12 months, MRA use significantly declined to 54.1%, while SGLT2i use increased to 25.7% (both P for trend &lt;0.001). Notably, the proportion of patients receiving triple or quadruple therapy decreased from 55.3% to 50.7% (P for trend = 0.002), whereas those on no therapy increased from 3.3% to 8.1% (P for trend&lt;0.001). Patients receiving triple or more therapies had significantly lower risk of all-cause death (hazard ratio [HR], 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.59-0.87; P&lt;0.001) and HF re-admission (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.72-1.00; P = 0.049) compared with those receiving ≤2 agents. Conclusion Comprehensive GDMT was associated with significantly improved 1-year survival and reduced HF readmission in HFrEF. Nevertheless, substantial underutilization and treatment de-escalation were observed over time, highlighting a persistent implementation gap in real-world practice.Table.Cox analysis
title: Temporal trends and prognostic impact of comprehensive guideline-directed medical therapy in HFrEF: a 1-year follow-up from the KorHF III registry

abstract: Abstract Background Recent studies increasingly point to the significance of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices in treating refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) due to an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Nevertheless, there is a notable absence of large, randomized trials focusing on the direct head-to-head comparison of Impella and extracorporeal veno-arterial membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in managing AMI-related CS. Consequently, evidence from thorough retrospective studies or meta-analyses plays a crucial role in clarifying the utility of these devices in such circumstances. Purpose This meta-analysis aims to a head-to-head comparison Impella vs VA-ECMO in 30-day mortality rates and device-related complications, including limb ischemia and bleeding rates, in the specific subgroup of patients with an AMI-CS. Method This meta-analysis included only clinical trials and observational studies focusing on patients treated with Impella or VA-ECMO for managing CS resulting from an AMI, aiming to a crude head-to-head comparison of these devices in the setting of AMI-mediated CS. The main outcome evaluated was the 30-day mortality rate, with secondary outcomes including major bleeding and ischemic vascular complications. Results Ten studies comprising a total of 3,949 patients were included in the present meta-analysis (Figure 1). Impella showed a statistically significant lower 30-day mortality rate compared to VA-ECMO (0.91, Confidence Interval (CI) 0.84 to 0.99). Moreover, vascular complications (0.41, CI 0.31 to 0.57) and major bleeding events (0.67, CI 0.49 to 0.93) were also significantly lower in the Impella-group (Figure 2). Lactate levels on admission, consistently recorded in seven of ten studies, ranged between 3.3 and 8.6 mmol/l in the Impella cohort and 5.5 to 14.1 mmol/l in the ECMO cohort, indicating a severe state of shock. The comparison of these two groups showed a statistically significant between the two groups (SMD -0.68, 95% C.I.: -1.03 to -0.33, p-value &lt; 0.0001). Furthermore, the available data on ejection fraction on admission indicated severe impairment, with values ranging from 21% to 36% (Impella group) and 20% to 35% (VA-ECMO group) (SMD 0.05, 95% C.I.: -0.28 to 0.38; p=0.6). pH values were on average to a similar extent (7.25 ± 0.16 in Impella- and 7.2 ± 0.2 in the ECMO group), p=0.8. In a subgroup analysis of patients with similar lactate levels, Impella continued to offer superior 30-day survival (0.89, CI 0.84 to 0.98, p=0.04). Conclusion This meta-analysis suggests that Impella may be associated with a lower mortality compared to VA-ECMO in AMI-mediated CS, mainly due to less vascular complications and bleeding events. Though not evident, our data may suggest a possible mode of escalation therapy in the setting of AMI-associated CS.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Head to head comparison of Impella with extracorporeal veno-arterial membrane oxygenation in myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocarditis is a heterogeneous condition with a wide range of potential infectious, and/or immune-mediated causes. While recent guidelines have questioned the routine use of systematic etiological investigations in all patients, comprehensive non-invasive work-ups remain frequently performed. However, the diagnostic yield of such systematic strategies and their impact on therapeutic decision-making and prognosis remains insufficiently defined. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic performance and the prognostic implications of a standardized, non-invasive etiological assessment in acute myocarditis patients. Methods We analyzed consecutive patients enrolled in the AMPHIBIA registry between 2019 and 2024 with confirmed acute myocarditis, diagnosed either by endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) or cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Both fulminant and non-fulminant forms were included. All patients underwent a systematic and extensive etiological evaluation, comprising detailed microbiological screening and comprehensive autoimmune blood testing. For each testing panel, we quantified the rate of testing, analytical positivity, and final etiological yield. The primary composite endpoint included all-cause mortality, need for temporary mechanical circulatory support, heart transplantation, or occurrence of severe ventricular arrhythmia. Logistic regression models were used to determine whether clinical infectious prodromes and routinely available biomarkers could predict microbiological findings considered etiologically contributory. Results A total of 236 patients were included during the study period. The median age was 32 years, and 69% were male and 34% were hospitalized in ICU. Overall, 59% of patients had at least one positive microbiological result; however, only 27% were considered etiologically contributory, and merely 18% led to a modification in treatment. Viral serologies showed limited clinical utility, whereas nasopharyngeal PCR testing appeared more informative. A similar discrepancy was observed for autoimmune testing: among 203 tested patients, 56% had at least one positive result, but only 6% were judged etiologically relevant and treatment-modifying. The primary endpoint occurred among 21% of our population, with a median follow-up of 1.4 years. Patients with a completely negative etiological work-up demonstrated the most favorable outcomes. In multivariable analysis, the combination of simple infectious prodromes and routine biomarkers predicted contributory microbiological findings with good discrimination (AUC 0.84). Conclusions In this contemporary cohort of acute myocarditis, systematic infectious and autoimmune blood testing was common but provided limited additional etiological and therapeutic benefit. Importantly, straightforward clinical features may help refine patient selection and better target microbiological investigations toward those most likely to derive meaningful diagnostic benefits.
title: Diagnostic yield of etiologic workup in acute myocarditis: insights from the AMPHIBIA Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Myocarditis may have fulminant presentation, requiring cardiac intensive cardiac unit (ICU) admission for invasive diagnosis and treatment, including mechanical circulatory support (MCS). ICU management, length of stay and therapeutic strategies have not been specifically studied in endomyocardial biopsy (EMB)-proven myocarditis cohorts. Purpose The aims of our study are: (1)To investigate details of ICU treatments and hospital-stay in EMB-proven myocarditis patients requiring ICU admission, and (2)to evaluate long-term prognostic factors. Methods Our retrospective longitudinal study included EMB-proven myocarditis patients admitted to our third-level referral Hospital ICU, in 1993-2025. All EMBs underwent guideline-based analysis, including polymerase chain reaction (PCR) search for viral genomes. Predictors of death and heart transplant (HTx) were identified by univariable and multivariable regression. Results Among 428 patients with EMB-proven myocarditis, 65 (15%) required ICU admission. Admission SCAI shock stages were A (56%), B (11%), C (20%), D (10%), and E (3%). Lymphocytic myocarditis was the predominant histotype (90%) but rare histotypes were also found (eosinophilic 5%, giant cell 3%, polymorphic 2%). Notably, viral genomes were found on EMB in 58% of cases. Virus-negative cases were treated with immunosuppression (27/65). While 28 patients were directly admitted to our center, 37 came from a spoke center. About half cases received inotropes (for a median duration of 8 days) and 22% necessitated MCS (for a median duration of 15.5 days). Patients from spoke centers more often required MCS (35% vs 3.6% at the hub) and had longer non-hub stays (median 20.5 days, IQR 11.5–43.5). At 66 months follow-up, the composite endpoint of death/HTx occurred in 15% of patients (12% death, 3% HTx). Event rates clustered in patients with higher SCAI stage, need for vasopressors/MCS, and/or lower LVEF. Long-term survival tended to be lower in patients with viral PCR positivity (p=0.06) on EMB and was similar, when Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) was performed in the acute phase, if CMR was performed before or after EMB (p=0.76). An inverse relationship was found between left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and SCAI shock class (p=0.046). On univariable analysis, lower LVEF (HR 1.06 per 1% LVEF increase), inotrope (HR 4.44) and MCS use (HR 9.10) predicted death/HTx; in multivariable models, both LVEF (HR 1.05 per 1% increase) and MCS use (HR 5.03) were confirmed as death/HTx independent predictors. Conclusions In EMB-proven myocarditis patients requiring ICU admission, outcomes are driven by hemodynamic severity and need for intensive cardiac support. EMB remains indispensable for etiological diagnosis, revealing a high prevalence of virus positive cases and a trend towards lower survival in these cases. Our data support early SCAI staging and invasive assessment of myocarditis patients admitted in the ICU.
title: Biopsy-proven myocarditis in the intensive care unit: diagnostic and prognostic insights from a monocentric cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Exercise echocardiography (ExE) may assess left ventricular (LV) systolic and diastolic function, LV outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and mitral regurgitation (MR). We aimed to assess the impact of these variables for assessing long-term outcome in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) patients, and to elucidate if ExE findings and outcome are worse in patients with genetic abnormalities. Methods LV systolic and diastolic function, LVOT gradients, and MR were evaluated during ExE in 368 patients with HCM (age 60±13 years, 42% women). Genetic testing performed in 241 subjects showed pathological results in 97 (40%). Considered composite events were overall death, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), cardiac failure, stroke, defibrillator (DF) implantation, myomectomy/septal ablation, new atrial fibrillation (AF), new syncope, and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT). Results Thirty-six patients (10%) had LVOT obstruction at rest (&gt;30 mmHg), and 91 (25%) developed exercise-induced LVOT obstruction (&gt;50 mmHg). Abnormal ExE based on exercise wall motion abnormalities (WMAs) was found in 63 patients (17%). E/e´&gt;14 was observed in 178 patients at rest (48%) and in 180 at exercise (49%). Corresponding figures for significant MR (moderate or severe) were 24 (7%) and 24 (7%).During follow-up of 7.7±3.9 years, 148 patients had a first event, (overall death, 34; ACS, 17; cardiac failure, 6; stroke, 13; DF implantation, 16; myomectomy/septal ablation, 4; new AF, 41; new syncope, 3; and NSVT, 14. Independent predictors of a first event were treatment with nitrates (HR=4.8; 95% CI=1.7-13.8, p=0.004), maximal wall thickness (HR=1.1; 95% CI=1.1-1.2, p&lt;0.001), LVOT obstruction at rest (HR=1.7; 95%CI=1.1-2.8, p=0.01), E/e´ at exercise (HR=1.04; 95%CI=1.01-1.06, p=0.004) and LVEF at peak exercise (HR=0.96; 95% CI=0.94-0.99, p=0.006). Independent predictors of overall death (n=48) were age (HR=1.05; 95% CI=1.02-1.09, p=0.002), WMSI at rest (HR=23.8; 95% CI=1.02-556.5, p=0.049), LVOT obstruction at rest (HR=2.8; 95% CI=1.5-5.3, p=0.001) and achieved workload in metabolic equivalents (HR=0.88; 95% CI=0.80-0.98, p=0.02) Patients with genetic abnormalities were younger, had lower prevalence of hypertension and of treatment with ACEI/ARAII. The presence of abnormal ExE, LV obstruction, significant MR, and raised E/e´ values at either rest or exercise were similar between patients with/without pathological genetic testing. Patients with genetic abnormalities had slightly lower peak LVEF, although within normal limits (p=0.049). A positive genetic testing was not predictive of events. Conclusions A comprehensive ExE assessment provides long-term prognostic information in patients with HCM. Both LV systolic and diastolic function with exercise performed well for this purpose. There were no significant differences regarding the presence/absence of genetic testing abnormalities.Kaplan Meier curves
title: Prognostic value of treadmill exercise echocardiography with systolic and diastolic evaluation in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and impact of genetic abnormalities in findings and outcome

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocarditis (AM) may overlap with inherited cardiomyopathies, with genetic variants influencing susceptibility to injury and adverse remodeling. Genetic testing is increasingly integrated into AM evaluation, as recommended by recent ESC guidelines for high-risk groups. We aimed to determine the proportion of AM patients meeting ESC testing criteria and the gap between eligibility and testing performed. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational single-center study including all patients diagnosed with acute myocarditis (2017–2025). Clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected (Fig.1). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) was reviewed using Lake Louise criteria, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was categorized by pattern; septal and/or ring-like involvement were deemed significant. Genetic testing eligibility followed 2025 ESC recommendations. Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) results were recorded when available. Results A total of 164 patients with AM were included (median age 40 years (IQR 24–55), 28% female). Nearly all patients were hospitalized (98%), and 12% had a complicated course, including cardiogenic shock (11%, n=18), ventricular arrhythmias (4.3%, n=7), complete AV block (3.7%, n=6), and cardiac arrest (3.1%, n=5) (Fig.2). Most cases represented first presentations (156, 95.1%), with 8 patients (4.9%) presenting with a recurrent episode. CMR was performed in 151 patients (92.1%). Significant LGE was present in 67 (40.8%), LV systolic dysfunction in 34 (20.7%), and biventricular dysfunction in 10 (6.1%). The pattern of LGE significantly influenced left ventricular functional recovery (p &lt; 0.001) and the absence of significant LGE had a markedly higher likelihood of LVEF normalization than those with septal or ring-like patterns (OR = 8.36, 95% CI 2.26–30.96, p = 0.001). Of the 164 patients with AM, 77 (47%) met the 2025 ESC indications for genetic testing, yet only 5 (6.5% of eligible) underwent testing. Among the 5 patients who underwent genetic testing, 3 had negative results and 2 carried pathogenic variants (LMNA and MYBPC3). EMB was performed in 25 patients, with 17 confirming myocarditis. Conclusions Nearly half of AM patients in our pre-guideline cohort would have met the current ESC indications for genetic testing, yet very few underwent testing. These findings underscore the need to align practice with the newly released guidelines to improve detection of inherited risk and support appropriate patient and family management.Image 1
title: Acute myocarditis and genetic testing: real-world practice before ESC guidance

abstract: Abstract Background Risk stratification in acute myocarditis is critical to guide monitoring intensity and therapeutic decision-making1. The Spanish Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocarditis has proposed a classification which integrates clinical, functional and imaging findings to identify patients at higher risk2. However, external validation has yet to be evaluated. Purpose To externally validate the discriminative performance of the model proposed by the Spanish group in an independent contemporary myocarditis cohort (PRE-MYO). Methods Four hundred and forty-six patients with acute myocarditis from the PRE-MYO cohort were evaluated. Patients were stratified as low (n=25), intermediate (n=334) or high-risk (n=87) according to predefined criteria. Baseline characteristics were compared across groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis evaluated major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) free survival (all-cause death, heart transplant, LV assist device implant, heart failure hospitalization, cardiogenic shock or sustained ventricular arrhythmias). Cox regression assessed association between risk stratification and MACE. Model discrimination was evaluated using Harrell’s C-statistic. Results Risk categories identified clinically distinct phenotypes. High-risk patients were significantly older (44.9±20.5, p&lt;0.001) and exhibited a higher burden of adverse events, with significantly higher mortality (9.5%, p=0.001) compared to low and intermediate-risk patients. MACE-free survival significantly differed between groups (log-rank p&lt;0.001), with an increasing gradient from low to high-risk. No association was observed between intermediate-risk group and MACE (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.14–8.01, p=0.964). However, high-risk group exhibited a fourfold increased hazard (HR 4.24, 95% CI 0.55–32.39, p=0.164), although statistical significance was not reached. The model showed moderate discriminative performance (Harrell’s C statistic 0.652, 95% CI 0.55–0.755). Conclusions In the PRE-MYO cohort, the proposed risk model identified clinically distinct patient profiles and demonstrated a graded separation in event-free survival. Although independent prognostic significance was not confirmed in multivariable Cox analysis, likely due to limited event numbers and group imbalance, the consistent gradient in mortality and MACE across categories suggests that the model captures clinically meaningful risk stratification.MACE events according to risk groupBaseline characteristics
title: External validation of a contemporary risk stratification model in acute myocarditis: prognostic implications from the PRE-MYO cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocarditis (AM) is associated with a non-negligible risk of mortality, heart transplantation, and major ventricular arrhythmias. While low QRS voltages (LQRSV) have shown prognostic value in other cardiac diseases, their role in AM remains poorly investigated. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of LQRSV and its association with clinical outcomes in this population. Methods This analysis included patients hospitalized for AM between 2015 and 2024 at our Hospital (France) and enrolled in the AMPHIBIA registry (an observational ambispective cohort study). ECGs recorded at hospital admission were analyzed, and LQRSV was defined as an R-to-S peak-to-peak amplitude ≤0.5 mV in all limb leads. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart transplantation, temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS), or sustained ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation (sVT/VF) at 5 years. Secondary endpoints included arrhythmic events and all-cause mortality analyzed separately. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations with outcomes. Results Of the 439 patients enrolled in the AMPHIBIA registry after January 2015, 78 were excluded due to the absence of an available admission ECG, resulting in 361 patients included in the analysis. LQRSV was present in 9.9% of patients. Those with LQRSV had a more severe clinical presentation, with lower LVEF at admission (45% vs 56%) and a greater need for temporary mechanical circulatory support (30.6% vs 8.6%). At 5 years, the primary endpoint occurred in 50% of patients with LQRSV versus 13.5% without LQRSV (Figure 1). This difference was consistent across secondary outcomes, including all-cause mortality (16.7% vs 1.2%) and incidence of sVT/VF (19.4% vs 3.7%). Findings remained consistent after excluding patients with pericardial effusion. In multivariable analysis including established prognostic factors, LQRSV was independently associated with the composite endpoint (HR 2.20, 95% CI 1.23-3.93), together with LVEF &lt;50%, sVT/VF at presentation, and female sex. A second model using best-subset selection confirmed LQRSV as an independent factor associated with worse clinical outcomes (HR 2.27, 95% CI 1.29-3.99). Conclusions In this large real-world AM cohort, LQRSV at admission identified a distinct high-risk phenotype characterized by greater hemodynamic compromise, increased need for intensive therapies, and markedly worse arrhythmic and survival outcomes at 5 years. As a simple and readily available ECG marker, LQRSV may improve early risk stratification in AM and support closer monitoring of affected patients. Further studies integrating genetic data may clarify its relationship with underlying cardiomyopathy substrates.Figure 1
title: Low QRS voltages and risk stratification in acute myocarditis : insights from the AMPHIBIA registry

abstract: Abstract Background Myocarditis is a polymorphic disease characterized by marked heterogeneity in both clinical presentation and disease course. A fundamental clinical challenge in myocarditis is explaining why only a subset of individuals exposed to common triggers—predominantly viral infections—develop clinically significant myocardial inflammation, exhibiting highly variable phenotypes from spontaneous resolution to fulminant heart failure or chronic dilated cardiomyopathy. Genome-wide association studies identify immune loci (e.g., HLA-DR4) linked to excessive cytokine production (IL-1β, IL-17, TNF-α), matrix metalloproteinase dysregulation, and fulminant phenotypes.(1) Concurrently, cardiomyopathy-associated variants—particularly in titin (TTN), desmoplakin, and lamin —enrich in myocarditis cohorts (8-30% prevalence vs. &lt;1% controls), supporting a "two-hit" hypothesis: genetic predisposition (hit 1) plus environmental insult (hit 2). (2) Specially (TTN), a giant structural and signaling protein of striated muscle, participates in intracellular signaling networks and cytoskeletal organization, potentially influencing cell activation, trafficking, and interactions with other tissues, including the heart. Methods In this pilot study, 29 patients with acute myocarditis and 10 healthy individuals were prospectively enrolled. Peripheral blood was obtained on the first day of hospital admission, total RNA was isolated from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), and TTN mRNA expression was quantified. All participants underwent a standard M-mode and two-dimensional (2D) echocardiographic examination as well 2D speckle-tracking strain analysis. Cardiac MRI with LGE protocols within the first week of hospital admission. Results TTN expression in Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs ) was significantly higher in patients with acute myocarditis compared with healthy controls (p = 0.015), corresponding to a 2.8-fold median increase. Moreover, TTN expression showed a strong positive correlation with global longitudinal strain impairment (Spearman’s r = 0.576, p &lt; 0.001), a moderate positive correlation with peak hs-cTnI levels (r = 0.435, p = 0.021; Figure 2), a moderate inverse correlation with baseline LVEF (r = −0.421, p = 0.025). Conclusions These findings support a pathophysiological link between TTN-related pathways in peripheral immune cells and myocardial injury in acute myocarditis and raise the hypothesis that TTN expression in monocytes may serve as a novel biomarker of disease severity and long-term ventricular remodeling. Further studies in larger cohorts are warranted to validate these results and to elucidate the mech-anistic role of titin in immune-cardiac cross-talk.Parameters in control and myocarditis grou
title: Titin expression in peripheral monocytes as a biomarker of left ventricular dysfunction in acute myocarditis

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is one of the most frequent causes of heart failure. In patients presenting with suspected ACS, it is currently unknown whether peak high-sensitivity troponin-T (hsTnT) is correlated with the short- and long-term risks of subsequent heart failure. Purpose To examine the short- and long-term associations between peak hsTnT and subsequent hospitalization or outpatient contact for heart failure in subjects with suspected ACS. We hypothesized that a higher peak hsTnT would be associated with an increased risk of incident heart failure. Methods Using Danish national registries, we identified persons without known heart failure who underwent two hsTnT measurements (99th percentile: 13.5 ng/l) separated by 1-7 hours, during hospitalization for myocardial infarction, unstable angina, observation for suspected myocardial infarction, or chest pain from 2012 through 2019. Individuals were stratified into quartiles (Q1-Q4) according to their peak hsTnT concentration based on these first two measurements (Q1: &lt;=9 ng/l, Q2: 10-19 ng/l, Q3: 20-263 ng/l, Q4: &gt;=264 ng/l) to explore whether the risk of heart failure was greater with higher hsTnT concentrations. We calculated standardized absolute and relative risks (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) of hospitalization or outpatient contact for heart failure at 0-30 days and 31-365 days after hsTnT measurement using multivariable logistic regression with average treatment effect modeling. Results A total of 26,835 individuals were included; 38.8% were discharged with a diagnosis of myocardial infarction, 5.1% with unstable angina, and 56.1% with observation for suspected myocardial infarction or chest pain. Median age was 64.2 years, 59.5% were male, 18.1% had coronary artery disease, and 7.2% had undergone prior revascularization. A total of 1,122 individuals received a diagnosis of heart failure within the first 30 days and an additional 707 were diagnosed from days 31-365. The association between hsTnT and heart failure risk is shown in Figure 1 using spline curves. The absolute risk of heart failure increased in a stepwise fashion with higher hsTnT concentrations within both 30 days (Q1: 0.18%; Q2: 0.56%; Q3: 3.55%; Q4: 12.42%) and 31-365 days (Q1: 0.38%; Q2: 0.75%; Q3: 2.52%; Q4: 7.66%). There was a significantly increased risk of heart failure in groups with higher peak hsTnT, within 30 days (Q4 vs. Q1, RR: 68.79, 95% CI 25.56 to 112.02; Q3 vs. Q1, RR: 19.66, 95% CI 7.15-32.17) and 31-365 days (Q4 vs. Q1, RR: 19.86, 95% CI 10.49 to 29.23; Q3 vs. Q1, RR: 6.53, 95% CI 3.34 to 9.71). Absolute and relative risks of heart failure at days 0-30 and 31-365 according to peak high-sensitivity troponin-T are shown in Figure 2. Conclusions Among individuals with suspected ACS, those with higher peak hsTnT concentrations had higher risks of subsequent hospitalization or outpatient contact for heart failure, within 30 days and at 31-365 days.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Peak high-sensitivity troponin-T concentration and risk of heart failure in patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Heart failure (HF) is a frequent complication following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. The E/e′ ratio by echocardiography and serum NT-proBNP levels are widely used for diagnosing HF in clinical practice, however combined these parameters as a predictor for subsequent heart failure events in patients with ACS remains limited. Objective To determine the prognostic value of the E/e′ ratio and NT-proBNP levels for heart failure events following hospital discharge after acute coronary syndrome. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients who were diagnosed as ACS at our Hospital between July 1st, 2021, and August 31st, 2025. Data were obtained from electronic medical records. The primary endpoint was late-onset heart failure events defined as outpatient department or emergency room visits requiring diuretic therapy, hospitalization due to HF within 90 days after discharge. Patients were classified to concordance or discordance of E/e′ ratio and NT-proBNP levels. Hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models, and survival outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan–Meier curves. Results A total of 195 patients with ACS were included in the study. During the 90-day follow-up period, patients with concordantly elevated E/e′ ratio and NT-proBNP levels demonstrated a significantly higher incidence of late-onset heart failure events compared with those with concordantly low values (HR 4.50; 95% CI, 1.05–24.12; P = 0.042). Patients with discordant findings showed a non-significant increase in risk (HR 2.36; 95% CI, 0.51–10.93; P = 0.271). The incidence rates of late–onset heart failure events were 3.21 per 1,000 person-days (95% CI, 2.11–4.87) in the concordantly high group, 1.64 per 1,000 person-days in the discordant group, and 0.68 per 1,000 person-days in the concordantly low group. Conclusions The concordance of elevated E/e′ ratio and NT-proBNP levels is a strong predictor of heart failure events after discharge in patients with acute coronary syndrome. Combined assessment of these parameters may enhance early risk stratification and guide post-ACS management.Primary and secondary outcomesKaplan–Meier curves
title: Concordance between E/e′ratio and NT-proBNP levels for predicting late-onset heart failure events in patients with acute coronary syndrome(CONCORD-ACS Study)

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock is an increasing problem with an in-hospital mortality rate reaching 60%. Early and accurate risk stratification is critical for guiding therapeutic decisions and improving patient outcomes. Arterial blood gas analysis provides rapid and objective information on metabolic and respiratory disturbances in critically ill patients and may support mortality prediction. Purpose To develop and validate a neural network–based model using sequential blood gas data to predict in-hospital mortality in patients with cardiogenic shock and enable clinically meaningful risk stratification. Methods This retrospective observational study included adult patients with cardiogenic shock admitted to a tertiary academic hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Demographic and clinical data, including serial arterial blood gas measurements, were extracted from electronic health records. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural network was employed to model temporal dependencies in sequential blood gas data and predict in-hospital mortality. The model was trained using the Adam optimizer and feature importance was assessed using permutation feature importance. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results A total of 333 patients with cardiogenic shock were included, with an overall in-hospital mortality rate of 56.8%. After exclusion of incomplete datasets, 10,880 arterial blood gas analyses from 298 patients were analyzed. Feature importance analysis identified lactate, base excess, pH, standard base excess, ionized calcium, partial pressure of oxygen, and sodium as the most influential blood gas parameters. Lactate demonstrated the highest relative importance for mortality prediction. The GRU-based model showed high discriminative performance, achieving an AUROC of 0.893. Conclusions A GRU-based neural network model using blood gas analysis data can accurately predict in-hospital mortality in patients with cardiogenic shock.
title: Prediction of in-hospital mortality in cardiogenic shock using blood gas analysis data and a neural network model

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries a high in-hospital mortality exceeding 40–50%. Accurate and rapidly responding markers of perfusion are essential for early risk stratification and treatment optimization. Recent SCAI recommendations evidence supports lactate clearance (LC) as a key marker of shock trajectory, being an easily accessible bedside marker to guide management decisions, including mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Methods Retrospective observational study including consecutive CS patients admitted to the CICU between 2017 and 2024. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data, SCAI stage, and aetiology of CS were collected. Lactate measurements at admission, 6h, and 24h were obtained, and patients with any missing values were excluded. A significant LC was defined as a reduction &gt;10%, and lactate normalization as lactate &lt;2 mmol/L at 24h. Outcomes included mortality at 30 days and 1 year. Survival analysis was conducted using Kaplan–Meier estimates, with group comparisons performed by the log-rank test. Results A total of 251 patients were analysed (mean age 69±16 years; 66% male). Most presented with AMI-CS (54%), and initial SCAI stages C and D accounted for 86% of admissions. Median CICU stay was 6 [3–13] days. MCS was required in 34%. At admission, median lactate was 3.4 [2.1–5.4] mmol/L, decreasing to 2.2 [1.4–3.8] mmol/L at 6h, and 1.6 [1.1–2.5] mmol/L at 24h. LC &gt;10% at 6h was observed in 65% of patients, while 64% achieved lactate &lt;2 mmol/L by 24h. Mortality reached 41% in the CICU, 45% during the index hospitalization, and 53% at one year. In Cox regression analysis, only lactate normalization at 24 hours independently predicted both CICU mortality (HR 0.245, 95% CI 0.165–0.365; p &lt; 0.001) and in-hospital mortality (HR 0.277, 95% CI 0.190–0.402; p &lt; 0.001). Kaplan–Meier survival analysis demonstrated that both LC &gt; 10% at 6h and lactate normalization at 24h predicted 30-day and 1-year survival, with 24h normalization demonstrating the greatest separation of survival curves. In patients supported with MCS, baseline lactate levels were higher (3.7 [2.2–6.2] vs. 3.2 [1.9–5.1] mmol/L), as expected. At 6h, 20 out of 85 patients without a LC &gt;10% were receiving MCS. Of these, 50% achieved lactate normalization by 24h. In subgroup analysis by aetiology, the association between LC at 6h and 24h and survival persisted across all etiologic subgroups. Conclusion In this contemporary cohort of cardiogenic shock patients, early lactate clearance demonstrates a strong association with improved survival. Specifically, lactate normalization at 24 hours is highly discriminatory and independently associated with significantly reduced in-hospital and 1-year mortality across all aetiologies. These findings underscore the utility of dynamic lactate monitoring as a crucial bedside marker for risk stratification and real-time assessment of therapeutic efficacy in the management of cardiogenic shock.Lactate trajectoryKaplan-Meier curves
title: Lactate clearance as a prognostic marker in cardiogenic shock: a retrospective study from a tertiary cardiac intensive care unit

abstract: Abstract Background Sex-based differences in the management of myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock remain a concern, particularly with respect to the use of advanced mechanical therapies. Whether these differences persist after accounting for frailty and illness severity is not well defined. Methods Using data from the National Inpatient Sample (2018–2022), we identified adult hospitalizations for myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock through specific ICD-10 codes. Primary exposures were sex and frailty burden, with frailty categorized as non-frail, mild, moderate, or severe based on the presence of malnutrition, dementia, pressure ulcers, debility, falls/gait disorders, and sarcopenia, each defined by relevant ICD-10 codes. Outcomes included the use of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices—namely intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), Impella, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and left ventricular assist device (LVAD)—and in-hospital mortality, identified via procedure codes. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographics, Elixhauser comorbidity burden, illness severity, and hospital characteristics, with testing for sex–frailty interaction. Results In a survey-weighted analysis of patients with MI-related cardiogenic shock, MCS was utilized in 31% of patients, predominantly driven by IABP use. Significant disparities in MCS utilization were observed across sex, race, insurance status, socioeconomic status, and geographic location. Women received MCS less frequently than men (27.9% vs. 33.0%). After multivariable adjustment, female sex was independently associated with lower odds of receiving any MCS ( 0.73, 0.69–0.77, p&lt;0.001), with consistent findings across all MCS modalities, including IABP, Impella, ECMO, and LVAD. Racial disparities were evident, with Black patients showing markedly lower adjusted odds of receiving MCS compared to White patients (0.54, 0.51–0.57, p&lt;0.001). Insurance status and socioeconomic factors also influenced MCS use; private insurance was associated with higher odds of MCS receipt (1.31, 1.23–1.40, p&lt;0.001), and higher income quartiles correlated with modestly increased utilization. Stratification by frailty demonstrated that women consistently had lower predicted probabilities of MCS use across all frailty categories, from non-frail to severely frail. Despite lower MCS utilization, women experienced higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.07–1.19, p&lt;0.001) and the composite outcome of death or non-home discharge (aOR 1.33, 95% CI 1.25–1.41, p&lt;0.001), underscoring persistent inequities in advanced cardiac care outcomes. Conclusion This study highlights key disparities in MCS use for MI-related cardiogenic shock, with lower use in women, Black patients, and disadvantaged groups, alongside worse outcomes in women. Addressing these inequities is essential to improving care.
title: Sex-specific utilization patterns of advanced therapies in MI-related cardiogenic shock : a five year US National Analysis

abstract: Abstract Aim Current study aim is to investigate the clinical association of hypoxic liver injury with hypoxic hepatitis pertaining to in-hospital and 12 months mortality in cardiogenic shock patients. Material and Method A total of 1,274 cardiogenic shock patients from September of 2019 to August of 2023 were enrolled. 22 tertiary hospitals from South Korea actively participated in this study. Hypoxic liver injury (HLI) was defined as 2-fold increase of the upper limit of hepatic enzyme at index emergency room visit and hypoxic hepatitis (HH) was defined as 20-fold increase of hepatic enzyme at 48hrs from admission. Patients were divided into 4 groups according to their liver injury status; groups 1: HLI (-)/HH (-), group 2: HLI (-)/HH (+), group 3: HLI (+)/HH (-), group 4: HLI (+)/HH (+). Primary end point was in-hospital mortality. Secondary endpoints were in-hospital cardiac mortality, 12 months; all-cause mortality, cardiac mortality, ischemic stroke, readmission for heart failure and major bleeding. Results The prevalence of HLI and HH were 48.9% and 56.9% respectively. Amongst the groups categorized respectful to their liver injury status, group 4 had the highest peak CK-MB (42.79±82.96, 224.35±208.98, 166.69±189.41, 249.49±203.45, p&lt;0.001), lactic acid (3.58±3.51, 4.94±3.43, 6.48±4.89, 7.69±4.79, p&lt;0.001), sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) score (7.05±3.63, 7.70±3.561, 8.30±3.49, 8.76±3.47, p&lt;0.001) and left ventricular ejection fraction (38.05±17.97, 36.48±16.55, 33.81±16.32, 29.12±15.75, p&lt;0.001) respectfully. Utilization of mechanical support was significantly higher (ECMO: 28.2%, 48.9%, 51.6%, 64.1%, p&lt;0.001; CRRT: 17.5%, 25.3%, 23.9%, 42.2%, p&lt;0.001; mechanical ventilation: 49.7%, 57.0%, 65.1%, 72.1%, p&lt;0.001) in group 4. The risk of in-hospital mortality (HR=1.44, 95% CI=1.001-2.070, p=0.049), in- hospital cardiac mortality (HR=1.562, 95% CI=1.052-2.318, p=0.027) and 12 months all-cause mortality (HR=1.597, 95% CI=1.139-2.239, p=0.007), cardiac mortality (HR=1.756, 95% CI=1.202-2.656, p=0.004) were the highest in group 4 even after adjusting relevant risk factors. Conclusion Cardiogenic shock patients with HLI at index emergency room visit who had developed HH were at a higher risk of in-hospital all-cause/cardiac mortality and 12 months all-cause/cardiac mortality. Identification of HLI at index emergency room visit and early detection of escalation to HH can be beneficial in cardiogenic shock patients. Further study regarding the management of such acute hypoxic liver damage resulting from cardiogenic shock is warranted.KM curve for in-hospital mortalityCox regression model for clinical endpoints
title: Clinical association between hypoxic liver injury and hypoxic hepatitis in cardiogenic shock patients regarding in-hospital and 12 months mortality: from the RESCUE II trial

abstract: Abstract Background Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) strategies such as Impella CP, veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), and combined ECMELLA provide temporary hemodynamic stabilization in refractory cardiogenic shock. Despite advanced support, mortality remains high and vasoactive therapy is frequently required. While norepinephrine, epinephrine, and dobutamine represent standard treatment, the prognostic relevance of levosimendan administration in this setting remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluate the association between levosimendan administration and short- and long-term survival in patients treated with MCS, including those undergoing prior cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 307 consecutive patients treated with MCS at our facility between 2014 and 2024. Baseline characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory values, vasoactive medication exposure, resuscitation status, and device strategy were collected. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality. Secondary endpoints included survival to hospital discharge and long-term survival. Vital status was obtained through official registry data. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, device strategy, lactate at admission, resuscitation status, and peak norepinephrine dose within the first 24 hours. Long-term survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier estimates. Results Among 307 patients, 84 (27%) received levosimendan within 24 hours of MCS initiation. Thirty-day mortality was lower in patients receiving levosimendan compared with those who did not (67.9% vs. 83.9%). After multivariable adjustment, early levosimendan use remained independently associated with reduced 30-day mortality (adjusted OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.22–0.98; p = 0.045). Higher peak norepinephrine dose (adjusted OR 1.78 per mg/h; p &lt; 0.001), elevated lactate, and increasing age were independently associated with mortality. In patients undergoing CPR prior to MCS initiation, levosimendan was strongly associated with improved survival (adjusted OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.09–0.65; p = 0.006). Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated sustained survival differences during long-term follow-up. Conclusion In this retrospective real-world MCS cohort, levosimendan administration was independently associated with reduced short-term mortality and improved long-term survival, including in resuscitated patients. While residual confounding inherent to the observational design cannot be excluded, these findings support prospective evaluation of levosimendan as adjunctive therapy in advanced cardiogenic shock.

title: Levosimendan administration and survival in patients receiving mechanical circulatory support: insights from an unselected real-world cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock represents the severest form of acute circulatory failure and remains associated with high mortality despite advances in supportive care. Beyond hemodynamics, inflammation and metabolic dysregulation are recognized as contributors to multi-organ failure. The gut-heart axis has emerged as a potential modulator of cardiovascular outcomes, with microbiome-derived metabolites such as trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) implicated in inflammation and cardiovascular disease. However, their role in shock is poorly understood. Purpose To investigate whether gut microbiome and microbiome-derived metabolites are associated with 30-day mortality in patients with cardiogenic shock. Methods In this prospective, cross-sectional trial, patients with cardiogenic shock were enrolled within 24 hours of admission. Forty patients (28 male, median age 64 years) were included; 73% presented after cardiac arrest and 58% had infarct-related cardiogenic shock. Stool and peripheral blood samples were collected at baseline and after 72 hours. Gut microbiome composition was assessed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and microbiome-derived metabolites were quantified. Systemic inflammatory markers were measured. Thirty-day survival was defined as the primary outcome. Results At 30 days, 19 patients survived and 21 died. Baseline characteristics did not differ. Overall microbial diversity was comparable; however, non-survivors exhibited a four-fold enrichment of Clostridiales. Non-survivors demonstrated significantly higher TMAO concentrations and an unfavorable SCFA profile, characterized by reduced isovaleric and valeric acids. Procalcitonin levels were significantly elevated in non-survivors, with trends toward higher hs-CRP and IL-6. Conclusions Distinct gut microbiome and metabolite signatures are associated with mortality in shock. Elevated TMAO, altered SCFA composition, and enrichment of Clostridiales reflect gut–heart–immune interactions that contribute to reduced survival. These findings warrant larger mechanistic studies and exploration of microbiome-targeted interventions in cardiogenic shock.
title: Gut microbiome and metabolites linked to short-term mortality in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Heart failure–related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) is the leading etiological subtype of CS, accounting for more than 50% of cases in contemporary registries. Within this CS subset, the impact of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) on clinical trajectories and outcomes remains insufficiently characterized. Purpose The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical characteristics and outcomes in patients with HF-CS with and without OHCA. Methods Patients with HF-CS treated at 16 tertiary-care centers across five countries between 2011 and 2021 were analyzed. To evaluate differences in clinical characteristics, 30-day mortality, and in-hospital complications, patients with and without OHCA were compared using multivariable logistic and Cox regression models, adjusted for age and sex. Results Among 1,024 patients with HF-CS, 395 (38.6%) presented with OHCA. The median age was 64 years (interquartile range [IQR] 52–75), 289 (28.2%) were female. At admission, median lactate was 5.0 mmol/L (IQR 2.6–8.6), and the baseline left ventricular ejection fraction was 20% (IQR 15-30). Among patients with OHCA, 233 (59.0%) presented with previously known HF (acute-on-chronic HF-CS), whereas 162 (41.0%) had no prior history of HF (de novo HF-CS). Overall, a prior history of HF was inversely associated with OHCA (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39–0.68; p&lt;0.001), whereas ischemic cardiomyopathy alone was independently associated with increased odds of OHCA (OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.27–2.62; p=0.001). Higher lactate levels upon admission were more frequently associated with OHCA (OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.96–2.98; p&lt;0.001). Patients with HF-CS and OHCA had an approximately 10% higher absolute 30-day mortality compared with those without OHCA (57.2% vs. 47.4%; adjusted hazard ratio 1.62, 95% CI 1.34–1.95, p&lt;0.001, Figure 1). Patients with OHCA more frequently experienced hypoxic brain injury compared with those without OHCA (17.3% vs. 1.0%, p&lt;0.001). Other in hospital complications, including ischemic and bleeding events, stroke and sepsis, were comparable between groups. Conclusions In this multicenter observational study, OHCA appears to represent a substantial risk modifier in patients with HF-CS. These findings call for external validation.
title: Cardiac arrest in patients with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock: results from an international, multicentre cohort study

abstract: Abstract Aims Early prediction of unfavourable outcome in patients with cardiogenic shock is important to guide resource allocation during acute and intensive care. Shock-specific biomarkers are not yet available. We evaluated whether stress-inducible growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) measured immediately on admission is useful to estimate mortality in any type of cardiogenic shock patients (acute coronary syndrome as well as non-ischemic) based on its pathophysiological importance as a marker for acute stress and hypoperfusion. Methods GDF-15 was measured in patients receiving mechanical circulatory support with an Impella microaxial flow pump for acute cardiogenic shock enrolled in a local registry. GDF-15’s association with 30-day mortality alone and in combination with admission lactate were evaluated. Results A total of 116 patients were analysed. Mean age (±SD) was 58±13 years, and 80% were male. Of the whole population, 44% died within 30-days. GDF-15 concentrations were higher in deceased patients than in survivors (25,555 ± 21,851 ng/l vs. 17,364 ± 15,176 ng/l; p=0.025). In multivariate analysis, elevated GDF-15 emerged as an independent predictor for mortality (HR=4.182; 95% CI 1.316-13.289; p=0.015). Elevated GDF-15 had high prognostic performance in the subgroup with lower lactate levels (HR 4.85 (95% CI 1.45-16.20)). Conclusions GDF-15 measured on admission is an independent marker of mortality in patients with cardiogenic shock receiving a microaxial flow pump for mechanical circulatory support particularly in those with low lactate levels. GDF-15’s usefulness for informed management decisions in these highly vulnerable patients should be further explored.Mortality

title: GDF-15 as an early marker for prognosis in patients with cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is increasingly used for refractory cardiogenic shock (CS), but it augments left ventricular (LV) afterload and may impede myocardial recovery. Mechanical LV unloading with intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or Impella is frequently adopted; however, the optimal unloading strategy during VA-ECMO remains controversial, and etiology-specific comparative data are limited. Purpose To compare clinical outcomes of Impella versus IABP as LV unloading strategies in patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO and to examine its differences according to CS etiology. Methods From the Japanese Registry of All Cardiac and Vascular Diseases–Diagnosis Procedure Combination database (2012–2023), we identified adult patients with CS treated with VA-ECMO plus Impella or IABP. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, duration of mechanical circulatory support (MCS), and hospitalization costs. Propensity score–based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to adjust for baseline differences. Results Among 18,906 patients (Impella n=1,688; IABP n=17,218), in-hospital mortality was 57.3% in the Impella group and 67.2% in the IABP group. After IPTW adjustment, Impella use was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.70–0.88). In etiology-specific analyses, Impella was associated with lower mortality in heart failure (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.44–0.88) and arrhythmia (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.37–0.76), whereas associations were attenuated and not statistically significant in acute myocardial infarction and other etiologies. Impella use was also associated with longer hospital stay (median 22 vs 12 days), longer MCS duration (7 vs 4 days), and higher hospitalization costs (56.1 vs 27.3 thousand USD; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion In this large nationwide cohort, Impella unloading during VA-ECMO was associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with IABP, particularly in selected etiologies such as heart failure and arrhythmia, while requiring greater resource utilization. These findings support the need for etiology-informed patient selection and prospective randomized trials to clarify the optimal LV unloading strategy in CS.figure2
title: Left ventricular unloading with impella versus IABP in cardiogenic shock requiring VA-ECMO

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high in-hospital mortality. Invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) is frequently required in patients with haemodynamic instability; however, its association with mortality in contemporary national cohorts is not well characterised. Purpose To evaluate the association between IMV use and in-hospital mortality among hospitalisations with CS in the United States. Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of the 2021 Nationwide Inpatient Sample. Adult hospitalisations with cardiogenic shock were identified using validated administrative coding. Survey weights were applied to generate national estimates. Weighted mortality rates were calculated using survey-adjusted methods. Multivariable logistic regression accounting for survey design was performed to assess the association between IMV and in-hospital mortality, adjusting for age, sex, race, primary payer, median income quartile, hospital teaching status and hospital region. Results A weighted total of 215,830 hospitalisations with CS were identified. IMV was used in 95,525 (44.3%) cases. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in patients receiving IMV compared with those not receiving IMV (52.0% vs 18.6%, p&lt;0.001). In unadjusted analysis, IMV was associated with increased odds of mortality. After multivariable adjustment, IMV remained independently associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 5.26, 95% CI 5.03–5.51; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion(s) In a contemporary nationally representative cohort, IMV use in cardiogenic shock was strongly associated with increased in-hospital mortality, even after adjustment for patient and hospital characteristics. These findings highlight the severe risk profile of mechanically ventilated patients with CS and underscore the need for strategies aimed at earlier intervention and optimisation of respiratory and haemodynamic support.
title: In-hospital mortality associated with invasive mechanical ventilation in cardiogenic shock: a weighted national analysis of the 2021 nationwide inpatient sample

abstract: Abstract Introduction Venoarterial (VA) extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-support modality used as a rescue intervention in patients with refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) or cardiac arrest (CA). Although several predictors of survival in VA-ECMO have been described, clinical variables have received less attention. Therefore, we analysed a single-centre cohort from a high-complexity cardiovascular centre in a low-income country. Purpose To identify pre-cannulation clinical variables, ECMO run characteristics, and post-cannulation predictors of in-hospital mortality in VA-ECMO patients with refractory CS or CA. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted including consecutive adult patients with refractory CS or CA requiring VA-ECMO between February 2014 and August 2025. Data were collected from a prospectively maintained ventricular assistance database. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality and the secondary endpoint was ECMO mortality. Relevant clinical variables were analysed, including pre-cannulation data, ECMO characteristics, and run-related variables. Independent risk factors for in-hospital and ECMO mortality were identified through multivariate analysis using stepwise logistic regression. A p &lt; 0.05 was considered as statistically significant. Results During the study period, 130 patients required VA-ECMO due to refractory CS or CA. Sixty one percent were male, median age was 58 (IR 25-75: 47 - 64), 38.6% had hypertension and 27% a history of myocardial infarction. The median left ventricular ejection fraction was 38% (IR 25-75: 23 - 60). Peripheral cannulation was used in 86.7%, and 18.6 % of VA ECMO runs were for extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. In-hospital mortality was 56.9%, and ECMO mortality was 41.5%. Median ECMO run was 6 days (IR 25-75: 3-9). Male sex was an independent protective factor (OR 0.4, 95% CI 0.18–0.92, p=0.03) of in-hospital mortality. After multivariable analysis, venting strategy for left ventricle unloading (OR 5.8, 95% CI 1.8-18.3, p=0.003), major bleeding (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.8, p=0.01) and requirement of haemodialysis (OR 5.8, 95% CI 1.7-19, p=0.004) were ECMO run predictors of in-hospital mortality. Placement of a left ventricular vent (OR 0.4, 95% CI 0.18–0.92, p=0.03), heart transplant (OR 0.26, 95% IC 0.08-0.8, p=0.018), haemodialysis (OR 5.1, 95% IC 1.4-18.2, p=0.01), and run infections (OR 0.2, 95% CI 0.07-0.6, p=0.004) were associated with ECMO mortality. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was a protective factor for both in-hospital and ECMO mortality. Conclusions In our cohort, venting strategy for left ventricular unloading, major bleeding and haemodialysis requirement were independent ECMO-related predictors of in-hospital mortality; whereas male sex and prolonged mechanical ventilation were protective factors. Venting strategy, hemodialysis requirement, infections and heart transplant were independently associated with ECMO mortality.
title: Clinical predictors of in-hospital mortality in adult patients with refractory cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest supported with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation

abstract: Abstract Background Isolated left main (LM) occlusion in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (STEMI-CS) represents a distinct and particularly high-risk phenotype, characterized by abrupt loss of perfusion to a large myocardial territory. Unlike patients with multivessel disease—where residual perfusion and collaterals may influence hemodynamics—isolated LM occlusion results in immediate, global ischemic burden. Purpose To evaluate the effect of microaxial flow pump (mAFP) vs. standard care in STEMI-CS patients with isolated LM occlusion. Methods This is a substudy of the multicenter, randomized DanGer shock trial investigating STEMI-CS patients. Baseline characteristics include data on diseased coronary vessels. Dividing patients into single vessel and multivessel disease groups, with isolated LM occlusion also classified as multivessel disease. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 180 days. Hazard ratios were estimated in in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population using Cox regression models. Results Of the 355 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 256 patients were recorded with multivessel disease. Isolated LM culprit was present in 35 patients. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the standard of care and mAFP groups. Median age was 71 (interquartile range (IQR): 64,77), and all 35 (100%) were men. Two (5.7%) patients had been resuscitated from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Median systolic blood pressure was 80 mm Hg (IQR 69, 90), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was 20 % (IQR: 15, 25) and lactate 4.70 mmol/L (IQR: 3.50, 8.00). All but two patients (94%) had ≥99% stenosis of the LM vessel. At 180 days survival was markedly higher in patients treated with mAFP compared to standard care 50.0% (26.9-73.1%) vs. 17.6% (0.0-35.8%) The unadjusted HR for all-cause mortality was 0.43 (95% CI 0.18 – 1.01). After adjusting for lactate, LVEF, and age, mAFP remained associated with lower mortality (Adjusted HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.14-0.87) Conclusion This exploratory post-hoc analysis suggests that mAFP treatment in STEMI-CS patients with isolated LM occlusion as the culprit lesion had a substantial benefit of mAFP.ESC Kaplan Meier
title: Effect of microaxial flow pump on survival in isolated left main infarction related cardiogenic shock. A DanGer Shock substudy analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Chronological age is a major risk factor for adverse outcomes in cardiogenic shock (CS), yet substantial heterogeneity exists within age groups. Frailty has emerged as an important prognostic marker, but its impact across different age strata remains insufficiently defined. Purpose To evaluate the prognostic impact of frailty in patients with CS and to determine whether its association with outcomes differs between younger and older patients. Methods This nationwide retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to intensive care units with CS between 2012 and 2022. Frailty was assessed using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS ≥5), and age was stratified as younger (&lt;70 years) and older (≥70 years), yielding four groups. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. Among hospital survivors, long-term outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure–related rehospitalization, and post-intensive care syndrome (PICS). Multivariable logistic and Cox regression models were used with adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and advanced supportive therapies. Results Among 207,419 patients with CS, frailty was present in 40.3% of older and 26.1% of younger patients. In-hospital mortality was highest in older frail patients (39.3%), followed by older non-frail (29.8%), younger frail (24.5%), and younger non-frail patients (16.2%). After adjustment, frailty was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality in both older (adjusted OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.52–1.61) and younger patients (adjusted OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.29–1.42). Notably, younger frail patients had higher mortality than older non-frail patients. Among 150,433 hospital survivors (median follow-up 3.7 years), frailty remained strongly associated with long-term mortality in both older (adjusted HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.28–1.34) and younger patients (adjusted HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.31–1.42). Younger frail patients also exhibited worse cognitive outcomes. Older patients were less likely to receive advanced therapies, including mechanical circulatory support and heart transplantation, irrespective of frailty status. Conclusion Frailty is independently associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes in CS across all age groups and may outweigh chronological age in prognostic assessment. Incorporating frailty assessment into treatment decision-making may improve risk stratification and help avoid age-based undertreatment.Main results
title: Prognostic impact of frailty beyond age in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Introduction Electrical storm (ES) is often associated with cardiogenic shock thus making a deadly combination sustained by a self-perpetuating vicious cycle of hemodynamic deterioration resulting in a sympathetic hyperactivity. Percutaneous left stellate ganglion block (PSGB) is an emerging autonomic neuromodulation strategy helpful for refractory ES. However, its use remains limited because of its feared negative effects of sympathetic blockade on hemodynamics. Purpose To evaluate the impact of PSGB on cardiac function, hemodynamic profile, and clinical outcomes in patients with ES and cardiogenic shock. The primary endpoint was the impact of PSGB on hemodynamic status (SCAI shock classification1 and lactate levels) and biventricular function. Secondary endpoints included antiarrhythmic efficacy—defined as reduction in arrhythmic burden in the 12 hours after PSGB compared with the preceding 12 hours—and the association between SCAI class and in-hospital mortality. Methods We performed a multicenter retrospective and prospective study including centers participating in the STAR study2. A total of 115 PSGB procedures, performed between July 2017 and September 2025 in patients with ES and cardiogenic shock were analyzed. Standard measures of left and right ventricular function were analyzed, SCAI classification was used to grade cardiogenic shock severity. Standard descriptive statistics and logistic regression models were used. Results Within 24 hours after PSGB, the proportion of patients in advanced shock (SCAI ≥C) significantly decreased (47.8% vs. 29.2%, p&lt;0.001), along with median lactate levels (2.02 vs. 1.03 mmol/L, p&lt;0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 30% at PSGB to 35% at discharge (p&lt;0.0001), and right ventricular fractional area change increased from 40% to 42% (p=0.02). An improving trend was observed at 24 hours, although not statistically significant. SCAI class independently predicted in-hospital mortality both at the time of PSGB (C: OR 6.09, p=0.0346; D: OR 17.12, p=0.001; E: OR 15.03, p=0.001) and at 24 hours (C: OR 6.71, p=0.025; D: OR 18.85, p&lt;0.001; E: OR 66.72, p&lt;0.001). PSGB significantly reduced the number of treated arrhythmic events (median 3 [1–7] vs. 0 [0–1] in the 12 hours before vs. after PSGB, p&lt;0.001), with effect evident at 1 hour (1 [0–4] vs. 0 [0–0], p&lt;0.001). Notably, greater arrhythmia reduction was associated with a lower probability of severe CS at 24 hours, with each shock avoided reducing the likelihood of SCAI C–D–E by 3% (OR 0.97 [0.94–0.99], p=0.03). Conclusions PSGB is safe and effective in suppressing ventricular arrhythmias irrespective of baseline hemodynamic status. The reduction of the number defibrillation was also associated with improved biventricular function and hemodynamic stabilization, suggesting a potential positive role of PSGB on survival of patients with ES complicated by cardiogenic shock.
title: Efficacy and safety of percutaneous stellate ganglion block technique in patients with electrical storm complicated by cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background In patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) but without pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD), worsening kidney function may provide prognostic information beyond established biomarkers such as serum lactate. Purpose To determine the effect of baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) on short-term mortality across different aetiologies of cardiogenic shock and to evaluate whether kidney dysfunction carries prognostic relevance depending on the underlying cause of CS. Methods Consecutive patients presenting with CS without a prior history of CKD and treated between 2009 and 2019 at a large tertiary cardiovascular centre were retrospectively analysed. Multivariable regression models adjusted for clinically relevant confounders, including age, comorbidities, haemodynamic parameters, and lactate levels, were constructed to assess the association between baseline eGFR and 30-day mortality. Analyses were additionally stratified according to CS aetiology, particularly acute myocardial infarction–related CS (AMI-CS) and heart failure–related CS (HF-CS). Results Among 935 eligible patients (median age 69 years; 269 women [28.8%]; median lactate concentration 4.6 mmol/L; mean eGFR 46.2 ml/min; AMI-CS 50.7%), lower eGFR values were associated with increased 30-day mortality. The risk of death increased by 6% for every 10 ml/min decrease in eGFR (HR 0.94; 95% CI 0.90–0.99; p=0.016). In patients with eGFR at or below the cohort median (41.74 ml/min), this association remained significant only in HF-CS (HR 1.32; 95% CI 1.00–1.73; p=0.047), whereas no significant relationship was observed in AMI-CS (HR 1.03; 95% CI 0.77–1.37; p=0.86). Conclusions In patients with cardiogenic shock without pre-existing CKD, impaired renal function is an independent predictor of increased 30-day mortality even after adjustment for lactate levels. This prognostic effect appears to be primarily driven by patients with HF-CS, in whom myocardial recovery options are limited compared with revascularisation strategies such as PCI in AMI-CS. These findings underscore the importance of rapidly restoring and maintaining end-organ perfusion to prevent irreversible extracardiac organ damage, particularly in HF-CS patients, and suggest that assessment of renal function may aid risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making in this high-risk population.Kaplan Meier eGFRAssociation eGFR Mortality
title: Low eGFR in cardiogenic shock without CKD indicates hypoperfusion and increased 30-day mortality risk

abstract: Abstract Background Heart rate control may represent a key therapeutic target in cardiogenic shock (CS), particularly in patients who experience failure of catecholamine weaning. Ivabradine, a selective sinus node inhibitor, could improve ventriculo-arterial coupling and hemodynamic stability; however, clinical data in this setting remain scarce. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the Cardiology Department of our University Hospital, between July 2024 and May 2025. Thirty-nine critically ill patients with CS requiring continuous catecholamine infusion and unsuccessful initial weaning attempts received ivabradine at a dose of 5 mg twice daily. Hemodynamic, echocardiographic, and biological parameters were assessed at baseline and after 48 hours. Results The median dobutamine dose at the time of ivabradine introduction was 8 μg/kg/min. Norepinephrine was used in 64.1% of cases, with a median dose of 1 μg/min. After 48 hours, ivabradine significantly reduced heart rate (103 ± 25.5 to 84.9 ± 19.3 bpm; p &lt; 0.001). This reduction was associated with improved stroke volume (21.98 [18.84–25.12] to 29.83 [25.12–31.40] mL; p &lt; 0.001), increased cardiac power output (0.39 ± 0.16 to 0.46 ± 0.14 W; p = 0.001), and better ventriculo-arterial coupling (6.08 ± 3.20 to 4.5 ± 2.11; p &lt; 0.001). Mean arterial pressure increased (+8.6 mmHg; p &lt; 0.001), while lactate levels significantly decreased (3 [2.8–4] to 1.8 [1.5–3] mmol/L; p &lt; 0.001). Successful catecholamine withdrawal was achieved in 77% of patients. Conclusions In this single-center retrospective study, ivabradine safely improved hemodynamic parameters and ventriculo-arterial coupling, facilitating catecholamine withdrawal in the majority of patients with cardiogenic shock and prior weaning failure. These findings support further prospective evaluation of ivabradine in this high-risk population
