title: Loss of pulsatility during impella support: incidence, predictors, and impact on short- and long-term outcomes from the IMMERGE registry

abstract: Abstract Background Acute kidney injury frequently complicates cardiogenic shock; however, whether its mortality impact differs by shock phenotype remains unclear. Objectives To evaluate the association between AKI severity and in-hospital mortality in heart failure–related cardiogenic shock and to determine whether this association differs between AMI-related and non-AMI shock. Methods We analyzed the 2023 National Inpatient Sample to identify adult hospitalizations with heart failure (I50) and cardiogenic shock (R57.0). AKI was defined using N17 codes and stratified by dialysis requirement (5A1D procedure codes). AMI-related shock was identified using I21–I22 codes. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, payer status, income quartile, hospital teaching status, and bed size. Interaction testing assessed effect modification by shock phenotype. Results An estimated 174,784 HF-CS hospitalizations were identified nationally; 36.7 percent were women. AKI occurred in 31.3 percent of hospitalizations, and 13.2 percent required dialysis. In-hospital mortality increased stepwise across AKI severity: No AKI: 22.4 percent AKI without dialysis: 28.1 percent AKI with dialysis: 45.8 percent After multivariable adjustment: AKI without dialysis: OR 1.30, 95 percent CI 1.23–1.37 AKI with dialysis: OR 3.10, 95 percent CI 2.84–3.39 A significant interaction was observed between AKI severity and AMI-related shock (p for interaction = 0.0018). In AMI-CS: AKI without dialysis: OR 1.44, 95 percent CI 1.32–1.57 AKI with dialysis: OR 3.34, 95 percent CI 2.91–3.84 In non-AMI CS: AKI without dialysis: OR 1.23, 95 percent CI 1.14–1.32 AKI with dialysis: OR 2.98, 95 percent CI 2.67–3.32 Conclusions AKI confers substantial mortality risk in cardiogenic shock; however, its impact is phenotype-specific. Non-dialysis AKI is associated with significantly amplified mortality in AMI-related shock compared with non-ischemic shock. These findings highlight differential cardiorenal vulnerability in ischemic cardiogenic shock and underscore the importance of early renal preservation strategies in AMI-CS.
title: Phenotype specific amplification of acute kidney injury mortality risk in cardiogenic shock complicating heart failure: a contemporary national analysis

abstract: Abstract Background/Purpose Coronary lipid-rich plaque (LRP) is likely to cause distal embolization during PCI, which is associated with microvascular injury. Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index of coronary microvascular function regardless of epicardial stenosis. This study assessed the impact of LRP identified by NIRS-IVUS on coronary microvascular function including MRR during PCI. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 100 patients who underwent NIRS-IVUS–guided PCI. Coronary physiological assessment using a pressure–temperature sensor guidewire was performed pre- and post PCI. Lesions were stratified into two groups with or without LRP (maxLCBI4mm ≥500) and physiological measurements were compared. Results In total, lesions with LRP were identified in 39 patients (39%). Baseline clinical characteristics were similar between two groups. Fractional flow reserve (FFR) and resting full-cycle ratio (RFR) improved in both groups, whereas MRR decreased significantly in LRP lesions (ΔMRR −1.49±0.46 vs −0.32±0.37, p=0.04). On multivariable logistic regression, maxLCBI4mm ≥500 emerged as an independent predictor of post-PCI coronary microvascular dysfunction defined by MRR (odds ratio 3.06, 95% confidence interval 1.01–9.29). Conclusion In lipid-rich lesions, MRR decreased during PCI despite of improvement in epicardial physiological indices, suggesting that MRR may be superior index to predict coronary microvascular dysfunction.
title: Impact of NIRS-IVUS-identified lipid-rich plaques on microvascular resistance reserve after PCI

abstract: Abstract Background In patients with angina and non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA), fractional flow reserve (FFR) reflects the functional burden of epicardial atherosclerosis, even within the non-ischemic range. However, the extent to which age and sex modulate the interplay between epicardial conductance (FFR) and vasomotor dysfunctional endotypes—ranging from epicardial spasm to microvascular vasomotor dysfunction—remains poorly understood. Methods We analyzed ANOCA patients from the nationwide, multicenter, prospective J-CMD registry (UMIN000047609) (stenosis &lt;50% and FFR &gt;0.80). Endotypes were classified into coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD; CFR &lt;2.5), epicardial vasospasm (EVS), and microvascular spasm (MVS). CMD was further stratified into functional (IMR &lt;25) and structural (IMR ≥25) phenotypes. Sex- and age-specific associations between FFR and these endotypes were investigated using multivariable regression models. Results Among 889 patients (45.1% men; mean age 62.9 ± 13.9 years), 27.8% had CMD (13.7% functional; 14.1% structural). Men were younger and exhibited significantly lower FFR values than women (0.90 vs. 0.92, P&lt;0.001), reflecting a higher epicardial atherosclerotic burden. Although FFR showed a modest inverse correlation with age (R=−0.104, P=0.002), its association with vasomotor dysfunction was markedly sex-dependent. In women, preserved FFR (mid-to-highest tertiles) was paradoxically yet strongly associated with MVS (OR: 2.62, 95% CI: 1.66–4.13, P&lt;0.001) and functional CMD (OR: 2.13, 95% CI: 1.08-4.21, P=0.029), independent of BMI (OR: 0.89, 95% CI: 0.84-0.96, P&lt;0.001). Conversely, FFR showed no significant correlation with specific endotypes in men, suggesting a decoupling of epicardial resistance and microvascular vasomotor dysfunction. Conclusions FFR in ANOCA is fundamentally governed by sex rather than age. In women, higher FFR values identify a distinct microvascular vasomotor phenotype (MVS and functional CMD) that manifests inversely (paradoxically) related to epicardial disease. Conversely, the absence of such an association in men underscores a divergent physiological coupling between the epicardial and microvascular compartments, necessitating a sex-specific paradigm shift in ANOCA profiling and management.
title: Sex-specific physiological landscapes in ANOCA: the interplay between epicardial resistance and coronary vasomotor dysfunction—insights from the J-CMD Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) immediate post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a heterogeneous condition comprising distinct "endogenous" and "classical" endotypes1. However, the specific determinants and long-term prognostic implications of these endotypes in chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) remain under-investigated. Purpose This study sought to identify the predictors of post-PCI CMD endotypes and evaluate their respective impacts on clinical outcomes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 591 patients with CCS undergoing elective PCI with post-PCI comprehensive microvascular assessment. Post-PCI CMD (coronary flow reserve [CFR] &lt; 2.0) was subclassified into endogenous (resting 1/transit-time &gt; 1.85) and classical (resting 1/transit-time &lt; 1.85) endotypes. The 1.85 cutoff was derived from the 29.3rd percentile of resting 1/transit-time values, corresponding to the distribution of impaired CFR. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE), a composite of all-cause death, heart failure, and nonfatal myocardial infarction. The secondary endpoint was vessel-oriented composite outcomes (VOCO), a composite of target vessel related cardiac death, target vascular myocardial infarction and target vascular revascularization. Results Post-PCI CMD was present in 29.3% of patients (endogenous: 17.1%; classical: 12.2%). The endogenous endotype was associated with advanced age, female sex, and higher comorbidity, whereas classical CMD was characterized by an elevated index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR). Pre-PCI microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) was a robust independent predictor of post-PCI CMD. Over a median 4.75-year follow-up, classical CMD was independently associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE (Hazard Ratio [HR]: 1.84; 95% CI: 1.04–3.24; P=0.035), whereas endogenous CMD was not. In contrast, VOCO was independent of CMD status but was significantly predicted by post-PCI fractional flow reserve (HR: 0.0014; P=0.027). Conclusions Post-PCI CMD in CCS is a phenotypic mosaic. While pre-PCI MRR effectively predicts overall post-PCI microvascular impairment, only the classical endotype serves as a driver of long-term patient-oriented adverse events. These findings underscore the necessity of endotype-specific risk stratification to refine post-PCI management strategies.Distribution of post-PCI CMD endotypesKaplan-Meier curve for MACE
title: Predictors and differential prognostic impact of post-PCI coronary microvascular dysfunction endotypes in chronic coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) refers to a broad spectrum of structural and functional abnormalities of the coronary microcirculation and, in clinical practice, is commonly defined by impaired flow augmentation in response to a pharmacological vasodilator in the presence of nonobstructive coronary artery disease. In chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), CMD is frequent, yet its prognostic significance has not been consistently quantified. Objectives To evaluate the association between invasively assessed CMD and adverse clinical outcomes in CCS. Methods Databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science) were searched from inception to March 2025. We included studies enrolling CCS patients undergoing invasive assessment of coronary microvascular function (using study-specific CMD definitions/cut-offs) with subsequent reporting of clinical events. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), myocardial infarction (MI), and repeat revascularization. Random-effects models were used to pool risk ratios (RRs). Heterogeneity was quantified with I². Results Eighteen studies including 9,290 CCS patients (CMD: 3,229; no CMD: 6,061) were included. CMD was associated with a higher risk of MACE (RR 2.65, 95% CI 2.19–3.20; P&lt;0.001; I²=51.0%). All-cause mortality was increased in CMD across 12 studies (n=8,443; RR 3.22, 95% CI 2.44–4.26; P&lt;0.001; I²=55.4%), as was cardiovascular mortality across 8 studies (n=5,067; RR 2.60, 95% CI 1.82–3.71; P&lt;0.001; I²=0%). CMD was also associated with HHF (2 studies; n=407; RR 2.23, 95% CI 1.52–3.29; P&lt;0.001; I²=0%) and MI (6 studies; n=3,941; RR 1.88, 95% CI 1.07–3.31; P=0.028; I²=0%). Repeat revascularization did not reach statistical significance (3 studies; n=1,841; RR 1.78, 95% CI 0.99–3.22; P=0.055; I²=0%). Conclusions In CCS, invasively assessed CMD identifies a markedly higher-risk phenotype, with an approximately 3-fold higher risk of MACE and ~3-fold higher risk of both all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. CMD was also associated with an elevated risk of HHF and MI, whereas repeat revascularization was not significantly increased. These findings indicate that CMD is not a benign condition. In line with the 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of chronic coronary syndromes1, invasive CMD assessment should be an integral component of the diagnostic work-up in patients with angina and non-obstructive coronary arteries, to improve risk stratification and management of this high-risk, underdiagnosed population.CMD in CCS: MACE and MortalityCMD in CCS: MI, Revasc, HF Hosp, Stroke
title: Invasive assessment of coronary microvascular dysfunction and its prognostic significance in stable coronary artery disease: a meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Introduction Invasive assessment of coronary microvascular function relies on pharmacologically induced maximum hyperaemia; however, the interpretation of derived physiological indices may be influenced by the choice of hyperaemic agent. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and nicorandil are commonly used, but they differ in their systemic haemodynamic effects, including blood pressure changes. Unlike fractional flow reserve, indices of coronary microvascular dysfunction are influenced by haemodynamic conditions; therefore, measured values may vary depending on the hyperaemic agent used. Nevertheless, the effect of different hyperaemic agents on invasively derived microvascular indices has not been adequately evaluated in direct within-patient comparisons. Purpose This study aimed to determine whether the choice of hyperaemic agent influences the interpretation of invasive microvascular function in patients with suspected ischaemia and non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA). Methods This prospective observational study enrolled patients with suspected INOCA without significant epicardial stenosis (fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≧0.80). Coronary physiology of the left anterior descending artery was assessed using a pressure wire and bolus thermodilution technique. Maximum hyperaemia was induced by continuous intravenous ATP infusion (180 μg/kg/min) and intracoronary nicorandil (2 mg), with both agents administered in each patient. The sequence of administration was at operator discretion. A ≧5-minute washout period was observed, and the second agent was administered only after confirmation that heart rate and blood pressure had returned to baseline, to minimise potential order effects. Results A total of 47 patients were analysed. In comparison with nicorandil, ATP was associated with a significantly greater reduction in blood pressure (ΔBP) (14.6 ± 9.84 mmHg vs. 7.63 ± 6.12 mmHg; p &lt; 0.001). Coronary flow reserve (CFR) was significantly lower during ATP-induced hyperaemia than during nicorandil-induced hyperaemia (geometric mean ratio (GMR) [ATP/nicorandil] 0.83, 95% CI 0.73–0.95; p=0.007). In contrast, index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) and microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) exhibited comparable characteristics across the agents (IMR: GMR 1.07, 95% CI 0.94–1.22; p=0.27; MRR: GMR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84–1.07; p=0.386). The FFR values were comparable (0.91 ± 0.03 vs. 0.91 ± 0.03; p=0.33). Conclusions In comparison with intracoronary nicorandil, intravenous ATP resulted in a greater decrease in blood pressure and a lower CFR, while IMR, MRR and FFR were comparable. These findings suggest that systemic blood pressure changes induced by hyperaemic agents may influence the interpretation of CFR and should be taken into consideration when assessing coronary microvascular function. In this context, evaluation using MRR, which accounts for haemodynamic conditions, may provide a complementary approach for microvascular assessment.
title: The impact of hyperemic agent selection on the interpretation of invasive coronary microvascular function

abstract: Abstract Background Chronic coronary syndromes frequently occur in the absence of flow-limiting epicardial stenosis. Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a key mechanism underlying angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries, yet its relationship with epicardial atherosclerosis remains incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests a potential interplay between plaque development, arterial remodeling, and microvascular impairment. Purpose To investigate the association between epicardial atherosclerotic characteristics assessed by quantitative coronary CT angiography (CCTA) and coronary microvascular dysfunction, integrating invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR), positron emission tomography (PET)–derived myocardial blood flow, and microvascular resistance reserve (MRR). Methods This post hoc analysis included 599 vessels from 208 patients with suspected coronary artery disease enrolled in the PACIFIC-1 trial. All patients underwent [15O]H2O PET, CCTA with AI-based quantitative plaque analysis, and invasive coronary angiography with routine FFR. Vessels were classified as non-ischemic (normal FFR and hyperemic myocardial blood flow [hMBF]), CMD (normal FFR, impaired hMBF), or epicardial flow-limiting (FFR ≤0.80). MRR was calculated as (CFR/FFR) × (Pa,rest/Pa,hyper). Vessel-level associations were analyzed using generalized estimating equations. Results Of 599 vessels, 352 (58.8%) were non-ischemic, 88 (14.7%) CMD, and 159 (26.5%) epicardial flow-limiting. Atherosclerotic burden increased progressively across groups. CMD vessels demonstrated intermediate plaque volume and percentage atheroma volume compared with non-ischemic and epicardial flow-limiting vessels (all P&lt;0.001) (Figure 1). Notably, CMD vessels exhibited the largest lumen volume and area, consistent with pronounced positive remodeling. Among 508 vessels with complete physiological data, CMD vessels had significantly lower MRR than non-ischemic and epicardial flow-limiting vessels (median 2.22 vs. 3.86 and 3.40; P&lt;0.001). In multivariable analysis within CMD vessels, higher remodeling index was independently associated with higher MRR (Table 1). In non-ischemic vessels, greater non-calcified plaque burden was associated with lower MRR, whereas in epicardial flow-limiting vessels, hypertension was independently associated with reduced MRR. Conclusion CMD vessels demonstrate a distinct structural–functional phenotype characterized by intermediate plaque burden and marked positive remodeling. The independent association between remodeling and preserved MRR suggests a potential adaptive epicardial response in the presence of microvascular dysfunction. These findings highlight a complex interplay between early atherosclerosis and CMD and may indicate a clinically relevant window for early detection and intervention in coronary artery disease.
title: Advanced imaging to understand the relation between coronary microvascular dysfunction, coronary plaque burden, and vascular remodeling

abstract: Abstract Background Chronic total occlusion (CTO) carries high ischemic risk and variable procedural success. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), derived from platelet, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts, reflects thrombo-inflammatory activity and may refine risk stratification in CTO. This meta-analysis evaluated the association between SII and CTO outcomes. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar through September 2025 in accordance with PRISMA. Six observational studies assessing SII and CTO outcomes (mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events [MACE], and coronary collateral circulation [CCC]) were included. Data on demographics, comorbidities, SII cut-offs, and outcomes were extracted. Random-effects models were used to pool area-under-the-curve (AUC) estimates. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I² statistic. Association effect sizes (adjusted odds ratios [ORs]) were summarized when pooling was not feasible because SII was reported on different scales (categorical vs continuous). Results Of 19 records identified, six studies comprising 4,182 patients (mean age- 62 years, mean follow up- 61 months) met inclusion criteria. Four studies reported the diagnostic performance of SII for poor CCC. The pooled AUC was 0.72 (95% CI 0.67–0.77, I² = 74%), indicating fair discrimination. Three studies linked higher SII with poor CCC, including one diabetic-CTO cohort with a strong adjusted association (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 2.54–3.45, p &lt; 0.001). For clinical outcomes, two CTO–percutaneous coronary intervention cohorts showed that higher SII independently predicted MACE (adjusted ORs 2.04, p = 0.02 and 3.32, p = 0.0001). One cohort reported that higher SII was independently associated with all-cause mortality in CTO patients (adjusted OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.03–7.75). Conclusions SII is a simple, low-cost biomarker which shows fair discriminatory ability for poor CCC and is consistently associated with adverse prognosis in CTO including higher MACE, poorer collateralization, and increased mortality. Additional prospective, multicenter validation with standardized cut-offs are needed to confirm its clinical significance and prognostic potential.
title: Impact of the systemic immune-inflammation index (sii) on prognosis in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO): a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) inflammation on coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the prognostic value of its spatial extent and its interaction with structural plaque vulnerability markers such as low-attenuation plaque (LAP) remain insufficiently defined in chronic coronary artery disease (CAD). Purpose To assess the prognostic impact of multivessel PCAT inflammation and to determine whether integrating inflammation extent with LAP burden improves risk stratification for cardiovascular events in chronic CAD. Methods This retrospective observational study included 839 patients with chronic CAD undergoing CCTA. PCAT inflammation was defined as vessel-specific PCAT FAI in the highest quartile for each major coronary artery; inflammatory extent was categorized by the number of inflamed vessels (0, 1, or ≥2). High LAP burden was defined as LAP &gt;4%. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and unstable angina requiring coronary revascularization. The secondary endpoint comprised cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, unstable angina requiring coronary revascularization, and any coronary revascularization. Cox regression with time-dependent PCI was performed. Discrimination was assessed using area under the curve (AUC). Results Over a median follow-up of 3.8 years, 29 primary and 74 secondary events occurred. Event rates increased stepwise with higher inflammatory vessel count (Figure), and were also significantly higher in patients with LAP &gt;4%. In multivariable Cox models, multivessel PCAT inflammation independently predicted the primary endpoint (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.33–5.74; p=0.007). The combined phenotype (multivessel PCAT inflammation and LAP &gt;4%) identified the highest-risk group (HR 7.94, 95% CI 2.45–25.8; p&lt;0.01). Predictive performance was modest for multivessel PCAT inflammation (AUC 0.614) and LAP &gt;4% (AUC 0.598), but their combination significantly improved discrimination for both the primary (p=0.038) and secondary endpoints (p=0.038). Conclusions Diffuse pericoronary inflammation and high LAP burden represent complementary biological and structural markers of coronary vulnerability on CCTA. Their integration refines risk stratification beyond anatomical assessment and may identify patients with heightened residual inflammatory risk who could benefit from intensified preventive strategies.Figure
title: Spatial extent of pericoronary adipose tissue inflammation combined with coronary plaque burden improves risk stratification in chronic coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Lipid profile plays a central role in cardiovascular risk assessment. Elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and reduced high-density lipoprotein (HDL) are well-established markers of atherosclerosis, while higher HDL levels are traditionally considered protective. However, systemic inflammation may alter HDL composition and impair its anti-atherogenic functions. Serum amyloid A (SAA), a major acute-phase protein, can associate with HDL particles and potentially modify their biological properties. Aim To evaluate the association between circulating SAA levels and lipid profile characteristics in patients with acute and chronic coronary artery disease (CAD). Methods Fifty-five patients with clinically confirmed CAD were recruited from a tertiary cardiology center and classified into acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable chronic CAD groups, together with healthy controls. Serum SAA concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Levels HDL and LDL were determined using routine biochemical laboratory methods. Statistical analysis was conducted using the Mann–Whitney U test. Continuous variables are reported as medians (Mdn) with interquartile ranges (IQR). Results Serum amyloid A levels were significantly higher in patients with CAD compared with controls and peaked in ACS group (Mdn = 1.24 ng/mL, IQR 0.50–2.21) compared with chronic CAD (Mdn = 0.97 ng/mL, IQR 0.60–1.33), p = 0.004. High-density lipoprotein concentrations did not differ between ACS and chronic CAD, p = 0.673. In contrast, LDL levels were significantly elevated in ACS (Mdn = 2480 ng/mL, IQR 1640–3020) compared with chronic CAD (Mdn = 1200 ng/mL, IQR 1050–1545), p &lt; 0.001. These findings suggest inflammation-driven alterations in lipoprotein composition during acute disease. Conclusion Acute coronary syndrome is characterized by a potent inflammatory response evidenced by markedly elevated SAA. Our findings demonstrate that systemic inflammation drives HDL remodeling, compromising its atheroprotective capacity despite stable quantitative levels. The serum amyloid A protein acts as a critical biomarker linking inflammatory burden to qualitative lipid metabolism alterations in coronary artery disease.
title: Inflammation-associated HDL dysfunction in acute coronary syndrome: role of serum amyloid A

abstract: Abstract Background There is increasing evidence that plasma ceramide lipids (Cers) reflect cardiovascular risk beyond traditional risk predictors. In this context C16, C24, and the C16-C24 ratio have previously been associated with coronary plaque characteristics, cardiovascular events, and all-cause mortality. However, underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Investigating the plasma proteome in relation to Cers may uncover key biological drivers of these associations. Purpose We investigated the pathways linking plasma Cers and coronary artery disease using a targeted proteomic approach. Methods We examined 581 patients with chronic or acute coronary syndrome. Normalized protein expression levels(NPX) of 369 cardiometabolic plasma proteins were measured with proximity extension assays. Cers, quantified by mass spectrometry, were log2-transformed for analysis. Possible associations between Cers and NPX were assessed with univariable linear regression, with correction for age, sex, and multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg), and multivariable analyses with regularisation-based protein selection using Mini Concave Penalty (MCP). Effect sizes (ß), expressed as the difference in NPX per two-fold increase in Cers level, their 95% confidence intervals (CI), and corresponding marginal false discovery rate (mFDR) were depicted. Furthermore, Reactome pathway over-representation analysis (ORA) was performed on significant Cers-related proteins using a panel-restricted background with fold enrichment (FE) and p-values (p) derived from hypergeometric testing and multiple testing correction. Results were visualized as bubble plots, where bubble size represents FE and color encodes −log10 (p). Results Mean age was 62 (standard deviation: 11) years and 76% were men. Univariable analyses revealed C16, C24 and the C16-C24 ratio significantly associated with 255, 175 and 151 proteins, respectively. In MCP-based analyses, vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 ([VCAM1], ß: 0.29, CI [0.23, 0.35], p &lt;0.0001) and inter-alpha-trypsin inhibitor heavy chain H3 ([ITIH3], ß: 0.12, CI [0.09, 0.16], p &lt;0.0001) exhibited the strongest positive associations with the C16-C24 ratio, while tyrosine-protein kinase ([KIT], ß: -0.14, CI [-0.19, -0.10], p &lt;0.0001) and integrin beta-2 ([ITGB2], ß: -0.18, CI [-0.24, -0.12], p &lt;0.0001) demonstrated the most negative association (Figure 1). Figure 2 shows ORA predicted biological processes, with the strongest C16-C24 ratio enrichment observed in interleukin-4 / interleukin-13 inflammatory signaling pathways (FE 2.18, p &lt; 0,001). C24- and C16-associated proteins were respectively enriched mostly in hemostasis (FE 1.58, p &lt; 0.001) and broader immune system pathways like the adaptive immune system (FE 1.29, p &lt; 0.01). Conclusion The C16-C24 ratio was associated with a novel and distinct proteomic signature - including VCAM1, ITIH3, ITGB2, and KITLG - enriched in inflammatory, metabolic, and extra cellular matrix pathways.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Proteomic pathways linking plasma ceramides to coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Inflammation, macrophage activation, and angiogenic remodeling play central roles in coronary artery disease (CAD) progression and plaque instability. Biomarkers reflecting these complementary biological pathways may improve risk stratification beyond conventional clinical assessment. We evaluated the combined diagnostic and prognostic significance of chitotriosidase (CHIT), resistin (RTN), and vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGF-A) in patients undergoing coronary angiography. Methods In this prospective observational cohort, 275 consecutive patients undergoing coronary angiography were categorized as normal coronary arteries or CAD, including stable angina pectoris (SAP), unstable angina pectoris (UAP), non–ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Serum CHIT, RTN, and VEGF-A levels were measured before angiography. Patients were followed for one-year all-cause mortality. Prognostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results All biomarkers were significantly higher in CAD compared with controls and demonstrated a progressive increase from SAP to STEMI presentations (p&lt;0.001). ROC analysis showed good discriminatory performance for mortality prediction (AUC: VEGF-A 0.773, CHIT 0.740, Troponin 0.742, RTN 0.703). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, CHIT remained the only independent predictor of adverse outcome (HR 18.8, 95% CI 2.48–142.34, p=0.005). Addition of CHIT significantly improved prognostic discrimination (C-index increase from 0.64 to 0.79; ΔC=0.15, p&lt;0.001). Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed significantly higher mortality among patients with elevated biomarker levels. Conclusion Combined assessment of inflammatory and angiogenic biomarkers reflects biological disease activity across the CAD spectrum and provides incremental prognostic value beyond conventional markers. Multimarker evaluation may enhance individualized risk stratification in patients undergoing coronary angiography.ROC curves for one-year mortalityKaplan–Meier survival by biomarkers
title: Combined inflammatory and angiogenic biomarkers predict disease severity and mortality in patients undergoing coronary angiography

abstract: Abstract Background ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) induces long-term immune remodeling. Double-positive (DP) CD3+CD4+CD8+ T-lymphocytes represent a minor but functionally plastic subset involved in chronic inflammation and immune adaptation. However, their long-term dynamics following STEMI, particularly in patients with concomitant COVID-19, remains unclear. Purpose To compare immune profiles 3-4 years after STEMI in patients (pts) treated before the COVID-19 pandemic and in pts with STEMI and concomitant COVID-19, focusing on DP T-cells and their associations with metabolic, inflammatory, endothelial, and senescence-associated markers. Methods Sixty post-STEMI pts were examined: 30 pts experienced STEMI in pre-pandemic period (group 1, G1), and 30 – during pandemic with concomitant COVID-19 (group 2, G2). Peripheral blood immunophenotyping was performed by flow cytometry. Senescent-associated heterochromatin foci (SAHF) were assessed by fluorescent microscopy. In addition, glucose metabolism markers, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) were analyzed. Correlations between DP T-cells (%) and clinical or immunological variables were evaluated. Results In group 1, DP T-cells were integrated into a classical acute-phase inflammatory profile characterized by higher NLR, relative lymphopenia and monocytosis (Table 1). Their positive association with FMD suggests that this inflammatory pattern was not accompanied by endothelial dysfunction. Group 2 demonstrated higher proportions of CD31−CD38+ and SAHF-positive cells, along with elevated glucose and HbA1c levels compared with group 1 indicating persistent immune activation and features of senescence. In this group, DP T-cells were increased and showed a strong positive correlation with SAHF-positive cells, as well as an inverse correlation with CD31−CD38+ activated lymphocytes accompanied by a loss of associations with NLR and FMD. An inverse relationship between CD4+CD8+ and CD4+CD8− cells, together with a direct correlation with CD4−CD8+ cells was observed. This pattern may reflect functional plasticity of DP T cells with a relative CD8-dominant phenotype, consistent with cytotoxic skewing in the context of chronic immune activation. Conclusion Years after STEMI, CD4+CD8+ DP T-cells in non-COVID survivors remain associated with acute-phase inflammatory markers and preserved endothelial and metabolic function, suggesting coordinated immune adaptation. In contrast, concomitant STEMI and COVID-19 are associated with persistent immunosenescence and long-term metabolic dysregulation, along with a cytotoxic shift in the DP subset, potentially reflecting a compensatory response to the accumulation of senescence-prone T-cells following combined ischemic and viral injury.Table 1
title: Long-term cytotoxic skewing of CD4+CD8+ T cells after STEMI: association with immune senescence in COVID-19 patients

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remain major contributors to global morbidity and mortality. Endothelial dysfunction and inflammation drive disease progression, yet the extent to which an individual’s genetic makeup modifies these processes is hard to pinpoint. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) retain the donor’s genome while largely removing age- and lifestyle-related epigenetic patterns, making them a powerful platform for disease modelling. For this purpose, we employed iPSC-derived endothelial cells (iPSC-ECs) to investigate cellular mechanisms of endothelial dysfunction in ACS patients. Purpose Our aim was to compare endothelial function in iPSC-ECs derived from ACS patients versus donors without coronary artery disease. Methods iPSC-ECs were generated from ACS patients and controls without CAD. We characterised the cells using DNA-methylation array and RNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, functional assays (proliferation, tube formation, scratch-wound healing, and nitric-oxide (NO) production), qRT-PCR (SIRT1, p21), Western blot (SIRT1), and senescence associated-β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining. Additionally, we performed Seahorse Flux analyses (mitochondrial stress test, glycolysis stress test) and a mitophagy-specific dye assay. Finally, we examined the impact of direct (SRT1720) and indirect (metformin) SIRT1 activation on the observed phenotypes. Results ACS iPSC-ECs displayed an RNA-Seq signature enriched for senescence, autophagy, and DNA-damage pathways. DNA methylation data showed distinct methylation profiles and enrichment for negative regulation of protein targeting to mitochondrion. Under inflammatory stimuli, ACS iPSC-ECs showed heightened adhesion-molecule expression. Functionally, ACS iPSC-ECs proliferated more slowly, migrated less efficiently in wound-healing assays, and produced less NO. Senescence markers were elevated (higher p21 mRNA, increased SA-β-gal) while SIRT1 mRNA and protein levels were reduced. Metabolically, the ACS cells relied less on oxidative phosphorylation for ATP generation and compensated with greater glycolytic ATP production (Warburg effect) accompanied by impaired mitophagy. Treatment with metformin or SRT1720 partially reversed the senescent and dysfunctional phenotype, improving metabolic and functional readouts. Conclusion iPSC-ECs derived from ACS patients demonstrate a distinct, premature-senescent phenotype characterised by metabolic and mitochondrial impairment. Lower SIRT1 levels and compromised mitophagy appear to underpin persistent endothelial dysfunction in ACS iPSC-ECs. Pharmacologic activation of SIRT1, either directly or indirectly, emerges as a promising strategy to restore vascular health in ACS patients.
title: iPSC-derived endothelial cells from ACS patients show mitochondrial dysfunction and premature senescence

abstract: Abstract Background Chronic inflammation and coronary artery disease(CAD) have been research hotspots in recent years. In 2025, the American College of Cardiology (ACC) issued a Scientific Statement highlighting a broader panel of inflammatory markers for risk refinement, including clinically accessible indicators, including the established high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), as well as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and fibrinogen (FIB). Aims This study aimed to investigate the association of hsCRP, NLR, and FIB—individually and in combination—with the risks of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and cardiac death in patients with CAD, using two large independent cohorts with different follow-up durations. Methods We analyzed two independent cohorts of patients with CAD: a 10-year single-center cohort (n=10,724) and a 2-year multicenter cohort (n=18,701). After excluding patients without complete follow-up data or missing measurements of inflammatory markers, the final analytic sample included 5,663 and 15,804 patients, respectively. A total score (range 0–6) was calculated by summing the tertile-based scores of hsCRP, NLR, and FIB(T1=0, T2=1, T3=2). Patients were then categorized as low (score 0–2), intermediate (3–4), high (5), or very high (6) risk. The primary endpoint was MACCE, defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization, and non-hemorrhagic stroke. The secondary endpoint was cardiac death. Results In the 10-year PCI cohort (n=5663, mean age 58.6±10.4 years, 77.7% male), MACCE and cardiac death occurred in 39.2% and 4.5%, respectively; in the 2-year cohort (n=15804, mean age 60.9±10.5 years, 74.9% male), rates were 10.7% and 1.9%. Each inflammatory marker independently predicted both outcomes (Figure2), with a clear dose-response pattern when assessed jointly via a tertile-based score. In the 10-year cohort, relative to the low-risk group, MACCE risk increased progressively across intermediate, high, and very high inflammatory burden groups (HR 1.14, 1.24, 1.45; all P &lt; 0.05). A similar trend was observed for cardiac death (HR 1.61, 2.47, 3.52). In the 2-year cohort, MACCE risk also rose across groups (HR 1.13, 1.53, 1.90), with stronger associations for cardiac death (HR 1.99, 3.41, 5.99). Conclusion Based on two large cohort studies, we demonstrated that the three inflammatory markers recommended in the ACC scientific statement independently predicted MACCE and cardiac death in patients with CAD, with a consistent dose-response relationship across cohorts. This is the first study to jointly assess these markers, showing that increased inflammatory burden correlates with higher adverse event risk. These findings support routine combined assessment for enhanced risk stratification and highlight a very high-risk subgroup that may benefit from intensive monitoring and anti-inflammatory therapy.
title: Assessment of individual and combined ACC scientific statement-recommended inflammatory markers for long-term prognostication in coronary heart disease: a two-cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Left atrioventricular coupling (LACI) integrates left atrial (LA) and left ventricular (LV) function and may provide mechanistic insight into early hemodynamic impairment following acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although LACI has demonstrated incremental prognostic value in this population, its clinical utility when derived from three-dimensional (3D) echocardiography remains incompletely established. Purpose To assess whether 3D LACI provides incremental prognostic value beyond established functional and deformation indices in patients with AMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods In this prospective longitudinal study, we enrolled 120 consecutive patients with AMI treated with primary PCI. All patients underwent comprehensive echocardiography within 24 hours of admission. We acquired 3D full-volume datasets to quantify LV and LA volumes and ejection fraction. 3D LACI was calculated as the ratio of 3D LA end-diastolic volume to 3D LV end-diastolic volume. Speckle-tracking analysis provided LV global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and LA reservoir strain (LASr). Patients were followed for 12 months. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE): all-cause mortality, hospitalization for heart failure, and reinfarction. Multivariable Cox regression analysis adjusted for clinical risk score and conventional echocardiographic indices. Results During 12-month follow-up, MACE occurred in 18.3% of patients. Patients with events showed higher 3D LACI than those without events (23.6% vs. 18.2%, p = 0.001). 3D LACI demonstrated higher discrimination for MACE (AUC 0.794, p &lt; 0.001) compared with LVEF (0.702), LVGLS (0.732), LASr (0.708), and LAEF (0.784). The combination of 3D LACI and 3D LVEF further improved prognostic performance (AUC 0.806). In multivariate Cox regression analysis, 3D LACI remained independently associated with MACE (HR 1.42 per 1% increase, 95% CI 1.11–1.81; p = 0.005). A cut-off value of 23.5% identified a higher-risk subgroup (log-rank p &lt; 0.001). Conclusion 3D LACI independently predicts adverse outcomes after AMI and provides incremental prognostic value beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters. Quantitative assessment of left atrioventricular coupling by 3D echocardiography may refine early post-infarction risk stratification.ROC for predicting MACE
title: Incremental prognostic value of three-dimensional left atrioventricular coupling index beyond conventional echocardiography in acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background ST- elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) typically reflects an acute event within chronic systemic atherosclerosis. (1) It remains unclear whether STEMI is associated with accelerated progression of atherosclerosis in extracoronary vascular beds, whether such progression carries prognostic relevance, and whether it is related to infarct severity at the tissue level. (2) We therefore investigated 1-year extracoronary plaque progression in patients with STEMI compared with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), examined its association with long-term outcomes, and evaluated the relationship between infarct severity and subsequent plaque progression. Methods In this prospective cohort study, 173 patients (CCS n=84, STEMI n=98) underwent three-dimensional ultrasound quantification of carotid and femoral plaque volume at baseline and 12 months. Plaque progression was defined as absolute change in cumulative plaque volume. Determinants of progression were assessed using multivariable linear regression. In STEMI patients, myocardial infarct severity was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) and tested for association with plaque progression. Major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and its association with plaque progression were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. Results Baseline cumulative plaque volume was higher in CCS (mean age: 65.0 years, 26.2% female) than STEMI patients (mean age: 58.6 years, 21.11% female) (161.00 ±325.75 mm3 vs 66.50 ±114.75 mm3, respectively, p &lt; 0.001). Over 12 months, cumulative plaque volume increased more in STEMI than in CCS (median 61.5 (±90.25) vs 37.5 (±76.25) mm³, p = 0.001 (Figure 1)). In multivariable regression, STEMI presentation was independently associated with greater plaque progression (β 54.6 mm³, 95% CI 27.9 to 81.2, p &lt; 0.001.) During a median follow up of 6.6 years, high plaque progression was independently associated with MACCE (hazard ratio 5.50, 95% CI 1.59 to 19.05, p = 0.007) with good model discrimination (C- index 0.758). Unsupervised clustering revealed three distinct systemic progression phenotypes within the STEMI cohort, showing markedly different plaque progression levels, p = 0.003, and characterized by divergent metabolic and inflammatory risk constellations. CMR-derived Infarct size and presence of microvascular obstruction was not associated with plaque progression (p = 0.713). Conclusions STEMI is associated with accelerated extracoronary atherosclerotic plaque progression compared with CCS. Extracoronary plaque progression independently predicts long-term adverse cardiovascular outcomes and exhibits marked heterogeneity across biologically distinct phenotypes, whereas no association with tissue-level infarct severity was observed.Progression of Atherosclerotic Plaque Volume
title: Systemic progression of atherosclerosis after STEMI: a prospective cohort analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Diabetes mellitus (DM), reduced kidney function (KF) and previous cardiovascular disease (CVD) are associated with an increased risk of adverse prognosis and recurrent cardiovascular events after myocardial infarction (MI). There are little data about the prognosis in patients with DM in whom MI is the first CVD event. The aim of this study was to analyze the impact of kidney function on the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) following MI in patients with DM and no previous CVD events. Method we analyzed 496 STEMI patients with DM and without previous MI, angina, stroke or peripheral artery disease. All patients were treated with primary PCI. Kidney function was assessed at hospital admission (before iodine contrast administration) by calculating estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Reduced KF was defined as eGFR &lt;90ml/min/m2 and it was staged into mildly (eGFR 60-89ml/min/m2), moderated (eGFR 30-59ml/min/m2) and severely reduced (eGFR 15-29ml/min/m2). Composite end point MACE included cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal recurrent infarction, target vessel revascularization and non-fatal stroke. The follow-up period was 8 years. Results The median age of analyzed was 58 years (interquartile range 51, 68) and 186(36.9%) patients were females. Reduced KF was present in 308 (62%) patients and among them 59% had mildly reduced KF, 31.4% had moderately reduced KF and 9.6% had severely reduced KF. Patients with reduced KF have significantly higher MACE rate as compared with patients with preserved KF. MACE rate was higher with declining KF, as shown in Figure 1. Cox regression model was used for defining independent predictors for the occurrence of MACE. Variables defined in univariable model as predictors of MACE and clinically relevant variables based on data from literature were included in the multivariable model. We identified six independent predictors: moderated and severely reduced KF (HR 3.12 95%CI 1.58-6.91 and HR 5.22 95%CI 1.68-12.7 respectively); pre-discharge ejection fraction &lt;50% (HR 0.92, 95%CI 0,89-0,98); new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR 2.02, 95%CI 1.08-3.27); left-main stenosis (HR 2.01, 95%CI 1.02-4.02); heart failure at admission (HR 1.84, 95%CI 1.18-3.331) and post-procedural flow TIMI&lt;3 (1.68 95%CI 1.01-2.89). Conclusion Moderately and severely reduced kidney function were the strongest independent predictors for 8-year MACE after MI in analyzed patients with DM and no previous CVD events, while mildly reduced kidney function had no independent impact on the occurrence of long-term adverse events.
title: The impact of kidney function on long-term outcomes following myocardial infarction in patients with diabetes mellitus

abstract: Abstract Background Inflammation is widely recognized as a central contributor to the pathogenesis and prognosis of repeat revascularization (RR) and in-stent restenosis (ISR) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only markedly increases the risk of coronary artery disease (CAD) but also accelerates atherosclerosis progression by exacerbating insulin resistance, promoting chronic low-grade inflammation, and impairing endothelial function. Recent evidence indicates that elevated inflammatory indices independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes, particularly in patients with DM. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of twelve inflammatory indices for predicting RR and ISR in diabetic patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) undergoing PCI. Methods A total of 2,079 patients were enrolled, including 867 with diabetes mellitus (DM). Patients were categorized into tertiles based on each inflammatory index. The primary endpoint was a composite of PCI-related complications, including repeat revascularization (RR) and in-stent restenosis (ISR). Associations between the twelve inflammatory indices and outcomes were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses. Results During a median follow-up of 60 months, 961 patients (46.2%) experienced at least one composite endpoint. In the overall population, LnSII remained an independent predictor of the composite endpoint after adjustment (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01–1.28, P=0.037), while other inflammatory indices showed no significant association. Among non-diabetic patients, none of the indices were predictive. In diabetic patients, SII, NLR, and PAR remained significant independent predictors after adjustment (SII: HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.06–1.47, P=0.009; NLR: HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01–1.47, P=0.040; PAR: HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.04–1.84, P=0.028). Compared with the lowest tertile (T1), patients in the highest tertile (T3) had a 37%, 33%, and 38% higher risk, respectively. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a nonlinear association between SII and the composite endpoint in diabetic patients, while NLR and PAR showed linear associations. Kaplan–Meier analysis further confirmed significantly higher event rates in the T3 groups of SII and NLR among diabetic patients (SII P=0.026; NLR P=0.037), with no significant differences observed in the overall population. Conclusions In diabetic patients with CCS, inflammatory indices such as SII, NLR, and PAR are strong predictors of PCI-related complications, including RR and ISR, and may serve as practical tools for risk stratification.
title: Prognostic value of twelve systemic inflammatory indices for composite cardiovascular events in chronic coronary syndrome patients with or without diabetes undergoing PCI

abstract: Abstract Background Same-day discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has been increasingly adopted worldwide; however, nationwide data from France remain scarce. A comprehensive evaluation is needed to describe current practices and assess safety in real-world settings. Objectives To describe the current use of same-day discharge PCI in France, compare clinical and procedural characteristics between ambulatory and overnight hospitalization strategies, and evaluate 30-day clinical outcomes. Methods We conducted a nationwide retrospective observational study using the France PCI registry including elective PCI procedures performed between 2022 and 2023 in stable patients. Acute coronary syndromes were excluded. Patients were classified according to discharge strategy: same-day discharge or overnight hospitalization. Clinical outcomes at 30 days were compared between groups. Results A total of 21,874 patients were included, of whom 6,089 (27.8%) underwent same-day discharge PCI and 15,785 (72.2%) overnight hospitalization. Ambulatory patients were slightly younger (68 vs 70.1 years) and had fewer comorbidities, including severe chronic kidney disease (0.6% vs 1.2%) and left ventricular dysfunction (LVEF &lt;40%: 4.9% vs 7.8%). Radial access was more frequently used in the ambulatory group (95.1% vs 92%). Same-day discharge procedures involved less complex coronary disease, fewer treated vessels and stents, and were associated with shorter fluoroscopy time and lower radiation exposure. At 30 days, major adverse cardiovascular events were rare and comparable between groups, with very low rates of stent thrombosis (0.1% vs 0.2%), myocardial infarction, stroke, and urgent revascularization. Major bleeding events (BARC ≥3) were infrequent and occurred less often in the ambulatory group (0.1% vs 0.3%). Conclusions In the France PCI registry, same-day discharge accounts for more than one quarter of elective PCI procedures. In carefully selected stable patients, ambulatory PCI appears safe, with 30-day outcomes comparable to overnight hospitalization. These findings support broader implementation of same-day discharge PCI in France, particularly with systematic radial access and appropriate patient selection.
title: Same-day discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention in France: a nationwide analysis from the France PCI registry

abstract: Abstract Introduction Premature CAD (onset ≤45 years) has disproportionate lifetime impact, with adverse outcomes and decades of treatment burden. South Asian populations are typically aggregated, yet Indian, Pakistani, and Bangladeshi communities experience markedly different CAD burden. We hypothesised aggregation masks clinically important heterogeneity and examined 14.8 million English adults to quantify differences. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) primary care electronic health records linked to hospital admission and mortality data (2004–2024), including 14,821,240 adults (≥18yrs, ≤45yrs) free of CAD at baseline. Ethnicity was defined using CPRD records, supplemented by hospital records when missing. CAD was defined as first MI or revascularisation (PCI/CABG) at age ≤45 using validated codes. Follow-up ran from registration until incident CAD, death, transfer out of practice, age 45, or study end. Cox models estimated associations by sex and ethnicity (including subtypes), adjusting for age and socioeconomic deprivation. Results Among 14,821,240 adults, 15,989 experienced CAD ≤45 over 80.9 million person-years at risk (median follow-up 4.2 years [IQR 2.0–8.1]). South Asian men had a two-fold higher premature CAD risk than White men (HR [95% CI]: 2.07 [1.96, 2.18]), and Black men a lower risk (0.61 [0.55, 0.68]). Within South Asian subgroups, risks were higher for Bangladeshi (3.13 [2.83, 3.47]) and Pakistani (2.54 [2.35, 2.75]) than Indian men (1.46 [1.35, 1.59]). South Asian women had a 22% higher premature CAD risk compared to White women (1.22 [1.07, 1.38]), and Black women a 28% lower risk (0.72 [0.61, 0.86]). Within South Asian subgroups, risk was much higher for Pakistani (1.81 [1.52, 2.17]) and Bangladeshi women (1.38 [1.02, 1.88]), whilst Indian women had a lower risk than White women (0.81 [0.66, 0.99]). Deprivation partially explained excess risk in Bangladeshi and Pakistani populations (entirely accounted for Bangladeshi women's excess risk), though marked heterogeneity between South Asian sub-groups persisted. Ethnic patterns differed significantly by sex (p&lt;0.001 for interaction). This was marked for Indians, where men had 42% higher risk than White men, while Indian women had 21% lower risk than White women. Conclusion Disaggregating South Asian populations reveals marked heterogeneity in premature CAD risk, with significant sex differences. Bangladeshi and Pakistani men face more than two-fold excess risk, while Pakistani women remain moderately elevated. Indian men show modest elevation, but Indian women have lower risk than White women. Black ethnicity showed 50% lower risk in both sexes. Deprivation partially explains excess risk in Pakistani and Bangladeshi groups. This support targeted prevention incorporating South Asian subgroup, sex, and socioeconomic context rather than broad ethnic groupings.Sex-Specific Ethnic Disparities in CADAssociations between ethnicity
title: Ethnic differences in premature CAD incidence in 14.8 million adults in england, 2004-2024: a retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndromes remain a leading cause of premature mortality. Many fatal events occur before patients reach medical care. Understanding long-term trends in both non-fatal and fatal coronary events is essential for guiding prevention and emergency response strategies. Although declines in coronary events have been reported in many countries, contemporary reports on population-level trends that separately quantify out-of-hospital and in-hospital fatality are limited. Purpose To quantify contemporary population trends in incidence and fatal outcomes of a first major coronary event. Methods The Swedish population register, the cause of death register and the hospital discharge register were linked to identify all individuals aged 18 to 74 years residing in Sweden during 1997 – 2023 who experienced a first major coronary event. Events were defined as out-of-hospital death from coronary artery disease or hospital admission for acute myocardial infarction. In-hospital case fatality was defined as death occurring within 28 days of hospital admission. Annual incidences were age- and sex-standardized to the 2023 Swedish population. Results 249,630 cases of a first major coronary event were identified. The standardised annual incidence of first major coronary events decreased by 42% from 198 to 105 per 100,000 population between 1997 and 2023 (figure 1). Over the same period, standardised annual incidence of case fatality decreased by 71% for out-of-hospital (from 58 to 17 per 100,000) and 67% for in-hospital events (12 to 4 per 100,000). Conclusion Over the past 27 years, Sweden experienced substantial reductions in both the occurrence and fatality of first major coronary events. These trends likely reflect sustained progress in cardiovascular prevention, early detection, and acute care. Despite these improvements, most fatal cases continue to occur out-of-hospital, highlighting the need for enhanced strategies to prevent sudden coronary death and improve early response.Figure 1
title: Long-term declines in incidence and mortality of first major coronary events in Sweden 1997-2023

abstract: Abstract Introduction Coagulation factor XI (FXI) inhibitors are emerging anticoagulants for the prevention of atherothrombotic events with lower bleeding rates than current anticoagulants, but inconsistent data on efficacy and some concern regarding an increase in heart failure (HF). Revisiting the association between FXI levels and the incidence of cardiovascular events could provide additional insights. Purpose We aimed to test the association between FXI levels and 1) the prevalence of HF, 2) the incidence of HF, and 3) the incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and stroke. We hypothesized that FXI levels would not be associated with the prevalence or incidence of HF, but lower FXI levels would be associated with a lower risk of MACE. Methods This analysis included patients from a prospective cohort study with suspected functionally relevant coronary artery disease (fCAD) and available FXI measurements. The prevalence of HF was centrally adjudicated by an independent cardiologist according to guidelines based on cardiac imaging and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations. FXI levels were measured in a blinded fashion using the SomaScan (version 4.1) assay. The incidence of HF and MACE were adjudicated by independent cardiologists using 8-year clinical follow-up. Cox and logistic regression models adjusting for confounders were used to test the associations. Results Among 2,073 patients eligible for the MACE analysis (median age 68 years, 32% female, 47% known CAD), 504 patients developed MACE during follow-up. Lower FXI levels were associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE, even after adjustment for confounders (HR 1.91 (95%CI, 1.41-2.59), adjusted HR 1.49 (95%CI, 1.07-2.06), Figure). FXI levels were neither associated with the prevalence (adjusted HR 1.37 (95%CI, 0.93-2.02) nor the incidence of HF (adjusted HR 1.62 (95%CI, 0.83-3.19)). Conclusion In contrast to our hypothesis, lower FXI levels were associated with a higher (not lower) incidence of MACE. This finding raises concern as it challenges the widespread assumption of beneficial effects of low FXI levels. No association with prevalent and incident HF was found.Figure
title: Association between coagulation factor XI level and cardiovascular events: a prospective cohort study in patients with suspected functionally relevant coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background In clinical studies, the selection of endpoints faces challenges and indirect results may mislead their interpretation The use of all-cause mortality for the comparison of therapies in chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) patients have shown similar results, however, when mortality causes are depicted, noncardiac ones, that are not related to therapies, may interfere in the final results. Thus, a specific analysis of mortality causes in this population is needed to compare therapeutic strategies. Purpose The aim of this study is to analyze the cardiac and noncardiac mortalities in a CCS population with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in a 10-year follow-up of medical (MT), percutaneous (PCI) or surgical (CABG) treatments. Methods Retrospective cohort of patients with multivessel CCS, preserved LVEF and presence of myocardial ischemia, treated by MT, PCI or CABG. The primary endpoint was cardiac or noncardiac death in 10 years, with all deaths revised and reclassified using hospitalization summaries, death certificates, autopsies, access to federal government database and family information, with deaths adjudication made by a blinded medical committee. Results The population comprised 1729 patients, 460 (27%) MT, 468 (27%) PCI, and 801 (46%) CABG. There were 558 deaths, 43% of them cardiac causes, while 47% of noncardiac ones. Regarding all-cause mortality, MT presented with 40%, PCI 28% and CABG 30% (p = 0.007). A trend of less cardiac mortality was observed in the CABG group (12%), while in the PCI and MT arms it was 14% and 17%, respectively (p = 0.1). In relation to noncardiac deaths, the MT group presented 19%, PCI 11% and CABG 15% (p = 0.01). In the multivariate analysis, only CABG was associated with a 31% reduction in cardiac mortality comparing to the MT arm – HR 0.69 (CI 95%, 0.50-0.94, p = 0.02), with a 53% reduction of fatal myocardial infarction (MI) – HR 0.47 (CI 95%, 0.31-0.72, p &lt; 0.001). Surgery was associated with a 27% reduction of all-cause mortality – HR 0.73 (CI 95%, 0.60-0.89, p = 0.002); while PCI with a 28% reduction comparing to the MT arm – HR 0.72 (CI 95%, 0.57-0.90, p = 0.005), the last one due to a 39% of reduction in noncardiac deaths – HR 0.61 (CI 95%, 0.43-0.86, p = 0.005). Conclusion Coronary artery bypass surgery was associated with a reduction of cardiac mortality in CCS patients during a 10-year follow-up due to the reduction of fatal MI. The predominancy of noncardiac mortality, in the MT arm, enforces the complexity of mortality analysis to compare coronary treatment strategies.1
title: Beyond all-cause mortality: reduction of coronary deaths after CABG - MASS Registry analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Angina pectoris remains a common clinical manifestation of chronic coronary syndrome, yet contemporary prognostic data from the general population are lacking, particularly in relation to coronary pathology. Purpose To evaluate the long-term prognostic importance of angina pectoris, in relation to coronary artery disease (CAD) severity, determined by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) in a randomly selected general population-based cohort. Methods This cohort study included 24, 176 participants (aged 50-64 years) from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study (SCAPIS) who completed the Rose Angina Questionnaire and had valid CCTA without prior myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure, or coronary revascularisation. Participants were categorised as having angina or no angina, and according to coronary findings as no coronary atherosclerosis, non-obstructive CAD (NO-CAD; &lt;50% stenosis), or obstructive CAD (O-CAD; ≥50% stenosis). Cox regression models evaluated associations between angina and MI or coronary death and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; MI, coronary revascularisation, heart failure hospitalisation, coronary or heart failure death), including stratification by CAD categorisation and sequential multivariable adjustment, including sociodemographic and medical background variables, CAD severity and plaque burden. Results Angina was present in 3.0% of participants. Over a median follow-up time of 7.7 years, 293 primary events occurred. Angina was associated with a higher incidence of MI or coronary death (2.9% vs. 1.2%; HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.60–3.90), with increasing event rates across CAD severity categories and no evidence of interaction between symptoms and coronary findings. After multivariable adjustment, the association remained significant (HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.04–2.63). Similar patterns were observed for MACE (adjusted HR 2.34, 95% CI 1.73–3.16). Conclusion In this large contemporary population study, angina pectoris independently predicted adverse cardiovascular outcomes beyond coronary pathology assessed by CCTA. These findings highlight functional coronary microvascular disorders as contributing pathogenesis in angina pectoris and suggest that symptom assessment remains clinically relevant in modern cardiovascular risk stratification, providing incremental prognostic information.Kaplan-Meier primary endpointHazard rates
title: Long-term prognosis of angina pectoris in a general population – insights from the SCAPIS cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] has emerged as an independent contributor to residual atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk. However, its association with angiographic disease burden among patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains incompletely characterized. Purpose To evaluate the relationship between Lp(a) levels and coronary artery disease (CAD) extent, and to determine whether Lp(a) independently predicts multivessel CAD (MVD). Methods During a 6-month period, we analyzed 260 consecutive patients undergoing PCI at our tertiary center. Cardiovascular risk factors, lipid profile, C-reactive protein (CRP), and HbA1c were recorded. Coronary angiography was used to classify patients into single vessel disease (SVD) or MVD. Lp(a) levels were assessed at index presentation. Group comparisons were performed using non-parametric testing. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted to identify independent predictors of MVD, adjusting for age, hypertension, HbA1c, lipid markers, CRP, and Lp(a). Results Among the cohort, patients with MVD were older [69 (58-77) vs 63 (55-74) years, p=0.01] and exhibited higher Lp(a) levels [Figure 1, 19 (9-40) vs 9 (8-20) mg/dL, p=0.001] and HbA1c [6.2 (5.9-7.0) vs 5.9 (5.6-6.3), p&lt;0.001]. CRP was also elevated in MVD [3.6 (1.5-7.4) vs 2.1 (1-4.8) mg/L, p=0.005]. LDL-C and triglycerides did not differ significantly between groups. In multivariable analysis (Figure 2), Lp(a) remained independently associated with MVD (OR 1.20 per 10 mg/dL increase, 95% CI 1.05-1.38, p=0.009), alongside age (OR 1.04 per year, p=0.039) and HbA1c (OR 1.50 per 1% increase, p=0.034). CRP showed a borderline association (p=0.094).When modeled categorically, a clear dose-response relationship was observed across increasing Lp(a) quartiles. Compared with patients in the lowest quartile, those in the intermediate and highest quartiles had progressively higher odds of MVD (OR 3.8 and OR 5.1, respectively, global p=0.002). In a trend analysis, each increment in Lp(a) quartile was associated with nearly a twofold increase in odds of MVD (OR 1.98, 95% CI 1.28-3.07, p=0.002), confirming a graded association independent of traditional risk factors. Conclusions In this contemporary PCI cohort, elevated Lp(a) levels were independently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden. A clear dose–response relationship was observed, with progressively higher odds of multivessel CAD across increasing Lp(a) quartiles. This association persisted after adjustment for age, glycemic status, and inflammatory markers, underscoring the contribution of Lp(a) to residual atherosclerotic risk beyond traditional cardiometabolic factors. These findings support routine assessment of Lp(a) in patients undergoing PCI and highlight its potential role as a determinant of coronary disease complexity.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Lipoprotein(a) and extent of coronary artery disease in patients undergoing PCI

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is an abnormal vascular dilatation (≥1.5x normal diameter) predominantly associated with atherosclerosis. Altered haemodynamics predispose patients to acute coronary syndromes; however, the optimal antithrombotic strategy remains controversial due to a lack of randomised data. Purpose To determine the prevalence of CAE, characterise clinical and angiographic profiles, and evaluate the 10-year ischaemic, haemorrhagic and survival impact of antithrombotic strategies. Methods A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted identifying 1,674 patients with CAE from 18,593 consecutive coronary angiograms performed at a single centre. Outpatient antithrombotic regimens were categorised into single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT), dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), anticoagulation alone (AC), double therapy (AC + SAPT), and triple therapy (AC + DAPT). Haemorrhagic events were adjudicated via BARC criteria. Unadjusted 10-year survival (Kaplan-Meier) and independent predictors of long-term outcomes (Firth penalised Cox regression) were calculated. Results The prevalence of CAE was 9.0% (95% CI 8.6–9.4). Age had a median of 69 years (Q25:60, Q75:77). Unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis showed near-universal 10-year freedom from reinfarction across SAPT, DAPT, and AC regimens (99%–100%; p=0.50). Firth penalised Cox regression confirmed that antithrombotic therapy intensity did not independently predict recurrent myocardial infarction. Ischaemic recurrence was driven by anatomical severity (Markis Type III: HR 3.60, 95% CI 1.10–9.90, p=0.038) and dyslipidaemia (HR 2.10, p=0.049). Antithrombotic selection impacted safety; compared to AC alone, SAPT and DAPT were associated with reductions in bleeding risk (HR 0.31, p=0.033; and HR 0.36, p=0.044, respectively). All-cause mortality was dictated by baseline patient characteristics, notably kidney disease (HR 2.52, p&lt;0.001). Conclusions Prevalence of CAE in this cohort (9%) was notably higher than the rates typically reported in the literature (1–5%), suggesting possible contributing factors influencing disease detection. Absence of antithrombotic therapy in CAE is associated with higher mortality. Age distribution of the cohort, suggest that further research is needed to distinguish influence of baseline frailty and CAE-associated atherosclerotic burden in mortality. Survival appears to be driven by patient’s baseline characteristics over treatment regime. In the absence of absolute indications for AC, SAPT or DAPT showed to be non-inferior in ischaemic protection while actively diminishing bleeding events. Avoiding prophylactic overtreatment with antithrombotic intensive therapies safely improves long-term outcomes in CAE. Adequately tailored, patient-centred antithrombotic strategies could effectively bridge the current gap in formal treatment consensus for this condition.10 year survival by outpatient therapyDistribution of outpatient therapy regimens
title: 10-year outcomes and antithrombotic management strategies in coronary artery ectasia: insights from a retrospective cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Over the past decade, the role of the Heart Team has strengthened, evolving from general recommendations based on expert consensus to current guidelines that formally endorse its use in complex revascularization decisions. Multidisciplinary Heart Team consultation is now recommended for selected patients undergoing coronary angiography, particularly those with complex coronary anatomy or multiple clinical comorbidities that affect procedural risk and long-term outcomes. However, despite formal recognition, real-world data on temporal trends and determinants of Heart Team referral remain limited. Purpose To evaluate temporal trends in Heart Team consultation rates after coronary angiography and to identify clinical, angiographic, and procedural predictors of referral. Methods Data from the Polish Registry of Invasive Cardiology Procedures (ORPKI) from the years 2014-2024 were extracted and analyzed. Results A total of 1 898 420 consecutive coronary angiographies were included. Temporal trends in Heart Team consultation varied by clinical presentation, but showed a general upward trend (p&lt;0.001). Referral rates remained stable in patients with acute and chronic heart failure, and in cardiac arrest. In contrast, upward trends over years were observed in congenital heart disease (p&lt;0.001), stable angina (p&lt;0.001) and across acute coronary syndromes, including NSTEMI (p&lt;0.001), STEMI (p&lt;0.001), and unstable angina (p&lt;0.001). In the overall cohort, older age (OR 1.009; 95%CI 1.008-1.009; p&lt;0.001) and male sex (OR 1.19; 95%CI 1.17-1.21; p&lt;0.001) were associated with referral. Among comorbidities, chronic kidney disease was the strongest predictor (OR 1.42; 95%CI 1.39-1.46; p&lt;0.001), followed by hypertension (OR 1.14; 95%CI 1.12-1.15; p&lt;0.001), and diabetes mellitus (OR 1.05; 95%CI 1.04-1.07; p&lt;0.001). Prior revascularization procedures were associated with lower odds of consultation, for both prior percutaneous coronary intervention (OR 0.52; 95%CI 0.51-0.53; p&lt; 0.001) and prior coronary artery bypass grafting (OR 0.46; 95%CI 0.44-0.47; p&lt;0.001). Considering angiographic findings, multivessel disease with left main coronary artery (LMCA) involvement significantly increased referral likelihood (OR 2.61; 95% CI 2.57-2.66; p&lt;0.001), as did isolated LMCA disease (OR 3.25; 95% CI 3.05-3.47; p&lt;0.001) compared with multivessel disease without LMCA involvement. Conclusions In this nationwide cohort, Heart Team referral patterns have changed substantially, particularly for acute coronary syndromes and congenital heart disease, while remaining stable in heart failure. Referral decisions were primarily driven by angiographic complexity, particularly left main and multivessel disease, and selected comorbidities. These findings highlight the importance of multidisciplinary evaluation in contemporary interventional cardiology and the need to optimize Heart Team implementation in real-world practice.Figure 1.Figure 2.

title: Temporal trends and clinical predictors of Heart Team consultation after coronary angiography: a nationwide registry-based analysis

abstract: Abstract Background In 2019, the European Society of Cardiology changed the guidelines regarding initiation of optimal medical therapy in the presence of cardiovascular disease e.g. after coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)[1] and findings of plaques with or without obstructive stenosis. Purpose This study aims to investigate if medical treatment changed post guidelines regarding medical compliance and the mid-term effects on outcome. Method This project collated data from the national quality registry SWEDEHEART[2], and from the Drug, Death and Specialized Care Registry, including nationwide data from CCTA in Sweden, retrieved cardiovascular prescriptions, visits to specialized care and data/causes of death. Patients with CCTA in 2017–2018 (PRE-guidelines) and 2020–2021 (POST) with clinically indicated contrast-enhanced CCTA and/or non-contrast calcium score (CACS) were included. Analysis was stratified by stenosis severity (0: No stenosis; 1: &lt;50%; 2: ≥50%), and Calcium score (CACS 0; 1–99; 100+). Drug change was defined as the difference in unique subclasses before CCTA to directly after CCTA or directly after to mid-term (after 2–3 years). Primary endpoint (MACE) was infarction, unstable angina, cardiovascular death post-CCTA or revascularization more than 6 months after CCTA. Follow-up time was 2 years 11 months. Results 17,308 patients were included, of which 5068 PRE and 12240 POST guidelines. 17,269 had CCTA and 6,409 CACS. Patients in the POST group had more cardiovascular drugs directly after CCTA than PRE, except in patients with stenosis &lt;50% where it was similar (Table 1). The POST group had more lipid lowering drugs than PRE directly after CCTA and at mid term. Drug changes before and directly after CCTA, and after CCTA to mid-term were overall similar between groups. While lipid lowering drugs were similar at mid-term, antihypertensives and anticoagulants decreased (Figure 1). The greater the stenosis severity the higher proportion of drugs were removed in both PRE and POST groups at mid-term. MACE occurred in 1,945 patients, of which 615 (12.1%) in the PRE group and 1330 (10.9%) in POST (p=0.01). In POST time to MACE increased by 1.8% (p=0.02) for stenosis severity 1. For CACS, no difference in MACE between PRE and POST was significant. Conclusion After the 2019 ESC guidelines on chronic coronary syndrome, cardiovascular drug compliance increased on a national level in patients investigated with CCTA in Sweden. However, lipid lowering drugs were largely unchanged at mid-term. The decrease in antihypertensives and anticoagulants at mid-term indicates lower drug compliance 2-3 years after CCTA. Disadvantageously, the drug compliance decreased the most in patients with obstructive stenosis (&gt;50%). Still, the POST guidelines group appears to have fewer events, especially in patients with any type of stenosis. This emphasizes the importance of prescription compliance of optimal medical therapy.
title: Cardiovascular medication after coronary computed tomography angiography: Impact of the 2019 ESC guidelines

abstract: Abstract Background and Purpose Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is a metabolically active fat depot associated with coronary artery disease (CAD) and adverse cardiovascular outcomes, suggesting its role as a potential risk biomarker. However, clinical implementation has been limited by the challenges in standardized and reproducible quantification. We therefore developed and validated an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled approach for automated EAT measurement from coronary CT and evaluated its prognostic value in patients with suspected CAD. Methods This multicenter study was conducted within the APOLLO cohort, comprising 5000 Asian Admixture patients undergoing coronary CT across three hospitals in Singapore. For this analysis, 947 patients were included. EAT volume was quantified using a validated deep learning algorithm and indexed to body surface area to derive the EAT index (mL/m2).
