The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, acute coronary syndrome, or coronary revascularization. Associations between EAT index and outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary logistic regression estimated hazard ratios for MACE. Event-free survival stratified by EAT index was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results Over a median follow-up of 111 months, 113 patients (11.9%) experienced MACE. Patients with events had a higher EAT index than those without (73±26 vs. 65±25 mL/m2, P&lt;0.01). In multivariable Cox analysis, EAT index was independently associated with MACE (HR 1.011 per 1 mL/m2 increase; 95% CI 1.004–1.018; P=0.002). Binary logistic regression showed an approximately twofold higher risk of MACE with elevated EAT index (HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.25–2.76; P=0.002). Kaplan–Meier analysis further demonstrated significantly higher incidence of MACE with elevated EAT index (log-rank P=0.0013). Conclusion AI-derived EAT index independently predicts long-term MACE in patients with suspected CAD. Automated EAT quantification from coronary CT provides incremental prognostic value and may improve clinical risk stratification.
title: Artificial intelligence–derived epicardial fat predicts major adverse cardiovascular events in suspected CAD

abstract: Abstract Introduction Ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) is increasingly identified in patients undergoing evaluation for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD). The risk of incident heart failure in patients with INOCA remains insufficiently characterized. Purpose To evaluate the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and heart failure hospitalization in patients with INOCA compared with non-ischemic individuals and patients with obstructive CAD. Methods In this retrospective registry-based cohort study, 26,412 consecutive patients undergoing cardiovascular magnetic resonance perfusion imaging (n=1,292) or myocardial scintigraphy (n=25,120) between 2010 and 2023 at two tertiary centres in southern Sweden were included. Coronary angiography data were retrieved from the SWEDEHEART SCAAR registry. INOCA was defined as reversible ischemia on functional imaging without significant obstructive coronary stenosis. Patients were categorized as no ischemia, INOCA, or obstructive CAD. Patients with history of heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, coronary angiography before index imaging, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, or missing coronary angiography despite ischemia were excluded.The primary outcome was MACE, including cardiovascular death, stroke, or acute myocardial infarction within 3 years. The secondary outcome was incident heart failure hospitalization during the same follow-up period. Results Among 26,412 patients, 388 (1.5%) had INOCA, 23,017 (87%) had no ischemia, and 3,007 (11%) had CAD. During 3-year follow-up 2,943 MACE events and 321 heart failure hospitalizations occurred. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated similar rates of MACE between INOCA and the non-ischemic group (Figure 1). There was a higher risk of heart failure in INOCA patients compared to non-ischemic individuals, with risk intermediate between non-ischemic individuals and patients with obstructive CAD (Figure 2). Non-proportional hazards were addressed using time-dependent Cox regression analyses (0–1.5 and 1.5–3 years), adjusted for age, sex, type 2 diabetes, and imaging modality. The association between INOCA and incident heart failure were more pronounced beyond 1.5 years of follow-up (HR 3.4, 95% CI 1.4–8.4), than during the first time interval (HR 2.5, 95% CI 0.9–6.8). Corresponding HRs for CAD were 3.8 (95% CI 2.8–5.3) in the first time interval, and 1.1 (95% CI 0.7–1.7) in the second time interval. Type 2 diabetes was independently associated with heart failure in both time intervals (HR 2.0 [95% CI 1.5–2.7] and HR 2.6 [95% CI 1.8–3.6]). Conclusion Patients with INOCA have a significantly higher risk of incident heart failure compared with non-ischemic individuals, with risk approaching that of patients with obstructive CAD over three years of follow-up. These findings challenge the perception of INOCA as a benign condition and underscore the need for improved clinical surveillance in this patient population.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries is associated with increased risk of incident heart failure: a large registry-based imaging cohort

abstract: Abstract Introduction and Purpose Cancer patients with severe coronary artery disease (CAD) pose important management challenges, particularly when revascularization is not undertaken. Evidence describing the natural history and outcomes of medically managed severe CAD in oncology populations remains limited. This study aims to characterize the clinical profile and long-term outcomes of cancer patients with severe CAD treated exclusively with optimal medical therapy. Methods A retrospective cohort study was performed including cancer patients who underwent coronary angiography between 2017 and 2022. Patients with severe CAD managed medically rather than with PCI or CABG were identified. Demographic, cardiovascular, oncologic, laboratory, and angiographic characteristics were extracted from electronic records. Follow-up began at angiography, and predefined outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, acute coronary syndromes (ACS), repeat angiography, revascularization, and major bleeding. Results Among 318 cancer patients who underwent angiography, 53 had severe CAD managed medically. The cohort was elderly (mean age 77 ± 7), predominantly male, and presented with a substantial burden of cardiovascular comorbidities. Genitourinary (44%) and gastrointestinal (24%) cancers were most frequent. Functional status was generally preserved, with 70% ECOG 0–1, while 24% had stage IV disease. Nearly half (45%) underwent angiography for ACS. Cardiovascular risk factors were prevalent: hypertension (93%), diabetes (40%), dyslipidemia (68%), smoking history (51%), prior MI (26%), prior PCI (26%), and chronic kidney disease (51%). Severe multivessel CAD was common, involving the LAD (54%), circumflex (58%), and RCA (61%). Despite angiographic severity, ischemic complications were infrequent: 4 patients (7.5%) developed ACS, 6 (11.3%) required repeat angiography, and 2 (3.8%) underwent revascularization. Major bleeding occurred in two patients. Overall mortality reached 63%. Among the 35 deaths with a documented cause, non-cardiovascular mortality predominated (74%), whereas cardiovascular causes accounted for 26%, indicating outcomes were largely driven by cancer-related or other non-cardiac conditions rather than CAD progression. Conclusion In cancer patients with severe CAD managed conservatively, long-term survival is poor and primarily shaped by non-cardiovascular mortality. Recurrent ischemia, repeat angiography, and revascularization were uncommon, suggesting that in selected oncology patients a conservative strategy may be appropriate, as prognosis depends mainly on the underlying malignancy.Baseline characteristics of the patientsDeath distribution: CV and non-CV
title: Avoiding revascularization in cancer patients with severe coronary artery disease: what to expect?

abstract: Abstract Background The European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-hour algorithm is recommended for the rapid triage of patients with suspected non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). While this strategy is well-established for the reference high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) assay, the algorithm is assay-dependent, and clinical data defining specific 0/1-hour cut-offs for alternative platforms are currently lacking. Purpose This study evaluated the diagnostic performance and safety of a novel hs-cTnT assay within this clinical protocol. Methods In this prospective, single-center study at a general hospital, 397 adult patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of acute coronary syndrome were enrolled. The final diagnosis of NSTEMI was adjudicated by two independent cardiologists based on ESC guidelines. We assessed the correlation between the novel hs-cTnT assay and the established reference assay and derived optimal cut-offs for a 0/1h algorithm. Results NSTEMI was diagnosed in 11.6% of the population. The novel assay showed an excellent correlation with the reference assay (R2=0.995). At presentation (0h), the AUC-ROC for NSTEMI diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.90–0.98). The derived 0/1h rule-out criteria (0h &lt; 5 ng/L if onset &gt; 3h, or 0h &lt; 12 ng/L and 1h-delta &lt; 2 ng/L) triaged 41.7% of patients with a Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of 99.4% and sensitivity of 97.0%. The rule-in criteria (0h ≥ 57 ng/L or 1h-delta ≥ 7 ng/L) identified 17.1% of patients with a Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of 56.0% and specificity of 92.1%. The 30-day all-cause mortality in the rule-out group was 0.9%, and the MACE rate was 0.96%. Conclusions The novel hs-cTnT assay is safe and effective for use in the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm. It successfully meets the ESC safety requirement (NPV &gt; 99%) for rapid rule-out, making it a viable and promising platform for emergency department triage of suspected NSTEMI.
title: Diagnostic performance of a novel high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T assay in the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm for the early diagnosis of NSTEMI

abstract: Abstract Introduction The rapid and accurate non-invasive diagnosis of significant and functionally relevant coronary artery disease (fCAD) is a crucial yet unmet clinical need. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) may be involved in the development of CAD. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of GDF-15 in patients with suspected fCAD. Methods In this prospective cohort study, consecutive patients with suspected fCAD underwent myocardial perfusion imaging with single-photon-emission computed tomography, and coronary angiography plus fractional flow reserve, when available. The presence of fCAD was centrally adjudicated. GDF-15 concentrations were measured in a blinded fashion. Prognostic endpoints included all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death over five years. Results Among 3,379 patients eligible for this analysis (median age 68 years, 33% female, 44% known CAD), 1,160 patients (34%) had adjudicated fCAD. GDF-15 concentrations were significantly higher in patients with adjudicated fCAD compared to those without (1,325 ng/L (95%CI, 1,258-1,364) versus 1,041 ng/L (95%CI, 1,009-1,074), p&lt;0.001). However, the diagnostic accuracy of GDF-15 for identifying fCAD was modest, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.598. When combined with clinical judgment, GDF-15 significantly increased the diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.659). During a 5-year follow-up, 437 deaths (14%) occurred, of which 231 were cardiovascular. GDF-15 had very high prognostic accuracy for all-cause death and cardiovascular death (e.g. time-dependent AUC 0.815 and 0.834 at 2 years), at least comparable to high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn)T, and higher than hs-cTnI (Figures 1 and 2). Conclusion While GDF-15 has limited diagnostic utility, it exhibits high prognostic value in patients with suspected fCAD.
title: Diagnostic and prognostic value of growth differentiation factor 15 in suspected functionally relevant coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) is advocated as first line in the assessment of chronic coronary syndrome in patients with a lower pre-test probability of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). However, recent PROMISE data showed no difference in long term mortality between CTCA or functional assessment. Therefore, tests requiring no iodinated contrast or ionising radiation, such as stress echocardiography (SE) may be a safer alternative to patients with a broader spectrum of pre-test probability scores. Long term outcomes specifically for SE vs CTCA have not yet been explored. Purpose To assess long term hard outcomes (combined all-cause death and myocardial infarction) and revascularisation rates in patients undergoing either CTCA or SE and whether these are affected by pre-test probability score. Method A single centre retrospective database search of patients presenting for assessment between 2013-2014 with no history of CAD who subsequently underwent CTCA (including either coronary calcium score alone or combined with CT angiography) or SE was undertaken. These results were propensity matched in a 1:1 ratio using 11 predisposing CAD risk factors. Patients' pre-test probabilities for obstructive CAD were scored using the risk factor clinical likelihood (RF-CL) model and NICE chest pain typicality groups. Results Over a median follow up of 10.4 years (interquartile range 9.9 to 10.9 years) 1964 patients (984 CTCA and 980 SE) were analysed (age 59.3 ± 12.3, 47.8% males). There was no difference in hard outcomes (HR 0.92; 95% CI, 0.73-1.17; p=0.5) between modalities but a significant increase in revascularisations in the CTCA arm (HR 1.47; 95% CI 1.06-2.05, p=0.02). Furthermore, there was no differences in hard events between modalities for any RF-CL group (A: ≤5%, B: &gt;5-≤15%, C: &gt;15%) but revascularisations were higher in the low (p=0.03) and moderate (p=0.04) RF-CL groups in the CTCA arm. Patients grouped according to NICE chest pain typicality also showed no differences between modalities for any of the groups (angina equivalent, non-anginal, atypical and typical symptoms). A secondary propensity matched sub analysis, excluding those with calcium scoring only, compared patients that underwent full CTCA (n=638) vs SE (n=633). No difference in hard outcomes (HR 0.85; 95% CI 0.63-1.17, p=0.32) or revascularisations (HR 1.39; 95% CI 0.9-2.16, p=0.14) between modalities were noted, including the RF-CL groups, with the exception of the &gt;15% group where there was an increase in revascularisations in the CTCA arm (HR 2.3; 95% CI 1.11-4.78, p=0.03). Conclusion In patients requiring investigation for chronic coronary syndrome, there were no differences in combined all-cause death and MI when using SE or CTCA as a first line test at any patient risk level. There was an increase in revascularisation in the CTCA arm but this did not translate into a difference in hard endpoints.
title: 10 year hard outcomes in stable chest pain patients following stress echocardiography vs computed tomography coronary angiography: a retrospective propensity matched analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Wall shear stress (WSS) is a tangential hemodynamic force acting on the arterial endothelium and is a key modulator of early atherosclerosis development. Although WSS has traditionally been computed using invasive intracoronary imaging (e.g., intravascular ultrasound), recent advances in coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-based computational fluid dynamics now enable non-invasive derivation of WSS. However, data on the incremental value of CCTA-WSS for detecting hemodynamically significant CAD beyond conventional CCTA-derived stenosis assessment are scarce. Purpose The present study aimed to investigate the incremental value of CCTA-WSS for the detection of significant CAD, the latter defined as an invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≤0.80. Methods This post-hoc analysis of the PACIFIC-I trial considered 208 participants with suspected CAD who underwent routine 256-slice CCTA followed by invasive coronary angiography with three-vessel FFR interrogation. Using in-house arterial 3D reconstruction software and a dedicated commercial computational fluid dynamics package, patient-specific 3D coronary models were generated and segmented into equidistant 0.5-mm contours to derive cross-sectional mean and maximum WSS. For reader orientation, WSS is considered low at 0–1 Pascal (Pa), normal at 1–7 Pa, and elevated at &gt;7 Pa [1]. CCTA stenosis grade was assessed and reported as a categorical variable (0%, 1–25%, 25–49%, 50–69%, 70–100%). Generalized estimating equations were applied to determine the incremental value of CCTA-WSS beyond stenosis grade. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves (AUC); AUCs were compared with DeLong’s test. Results CCTA-WSS was successfully computed in 170 patients (417 vessels; mean age 59 ± 9 years; 63% male); 68 (40%) subjects had significant CAD. On a per-vessel level, patients with significant CAD showed higher mean WSS compared to those with non-significant CAD (6.2 [4.6–9.3] vs 3.7 [2.5–5.6] Pa; p&lt;0.01). Similarly, maximum vessel WSS was higher in the significant CAD group (40.6 [19.3–80.4] vs 16.9 [9.0–34.1] Pa; p&lt;0.01). Figure 1 shows the CCTA-derived coronary models used for prediction. Adding WSS parameters to stenosis grade improved discrimination by increasing the AUC, suggesting incremental value beyond stenosis grade alone. Conclusion CCTA-derived WSS computation was feasible in the majority of patients and was higher in those with hemodynamically significant CAD. On a per-vessel level, mean and maximum WSS improved model discrimination beyond stenosis grade alone, albeit with a subtle increase in AUC. These findings support a potential adjunctive role for CCTA-derived WSS for the detection of significant CAD.Figure 1.ROC analysis
title: Incremental value of coronary computed tomography angiography-derived wall shear stress over stenosis grade in detecting significant coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Undifferentiated acute chest pain is one of the most challenging scenarios in emergency medicine. Several life-threatening conditions, including acute coronary syndromes (ACS), aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism (PE), myocarditis, spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), and takotsubo syndrome (TTS), may present with overlapping clinical and biochemical features but necessitate fundamentally different management strategies. Existing disease-specific scores do not account for simultaneous multi-disease probabilities and do not reflect the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Purpose To develop and internally validate an interpretable Bayesian network capable of simultaneous differential diagnosis across major life-threatening cardiovascular diseases in patients presenting with acute chest pain. Methods Seven diagnostic cohorts of patients presenting with acute chest pain were analysed, including ACS, aortic dissection, myocarditis, PE, TTS, SCAD, and non-life-threatening conditions. A probabilistic graphical model (Bayesian Network) was developed using a hybrid modelling strategy that combined an expert-defined clinical structure with data-driven structure learning. Multiple structure learning algorithms were evaluated, with final model selection being based on performance optimisation. The network incorporated 43 clinical variables spanning demographic characteristics, medical history, ECG features, and laboratory findings, enabling simultaneous estimation of posterior disease probabilities and inference irrespective of data completeness. Internal validation was performed using 15-fold cross-validation and leave-one-out validation. Discriminative performance for each disease entity was assessed using area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curves (AUC). Results A total of 1,954 patients were included: 701 with ACS (35.9%), 273 with aortic dissection (14.0%), 153 with myocarditis (7.8%), 128 with PE (6.6%), 173 with SCAD (8.9%), 386 with TTS (19.8%), and 140 with non-life-threatening conditions (7.2%). In 15-fold cross-validation, the Bayesian network demonstrated high discriminative performance across all diagnostic entities: ACS (AUC 0.918), aortic dissection (0.915), TTS (0.931), myocarditis (0.895), SCAD (0.889), and PE (0.826). Non-life-threatening conditions were also accurately identified (AUC 0.914). Performance remained stable in leave-one-out validation (ACS 0.919; aortic dissection 0.915; TTS 0.932; myocarditis 0.896; SCAD 0.889; PE 0.831; non-life-threatening conditions 0.918). Derivation AUCs were consistently high across entities. Conclusions In patients presenting with acute chest pain, simultaneous probabilistic modelling of multiple life-threatening conditions is feasible and accurate. Pending external validation, this approach may support emergency decision-making, reduce diagnostic uncertainty, optimise resource allocation, and ultimately improve patient outcomes.Figure 1
title: A Bayesian network to support differential diagnosis in patients with acute chest pain

abstract: Abstract Introduction Angina pectoris is a common clinical presentation with a wide range of differential diagnoses. Structured risk stratification tools are essential as they help estimate the pre-test probability (PTP) of coronary artery disease (CAD). This balance reduces the risks of over- and under-diagnosis. In primary care, the Marburg Heart Score (MHS) offers a pragmatic approach, based on five easily accessible clinical variables. In contrast, the 2024 ESC Guidelines for chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) recommend a more comprehensive risk assessment, operationalised in the ESC risk factor-weighted clinical likelihood model (RF-CL). As clinical decision support systems become more widespread, models must be both information-rich and parsimonious to maximise discriminatory performance while maintaining efficiency. Purpose The aim of this retrospective secondary analysis was to assess how the MHS and RF-CL differ in categorising PTP in patients with suspected CCS. Methods Data were extracted from the ENLIGHT-KHK cohort. For each patient, both the MHS and RF-CL PTP category were calculated and compared with findings from invasive coronary angiography. Relevant CAD was defined as significant stenosis requiring PCI, CABG, or optimised medical therapy. Subsequently, supervised machine learning models (AutoGluon, LightGBM, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression) were applied to evaluate the potential influence of additional clinical variables, including BMI, creatinine, haemoglobin, sex, known CAD, smoking status, symptom duration, and physical performance. Results The MHS classified 88% (n = 598) of patients for (non)-invasive diagnostics, while 11% (n = 79) were assigned to alternative diagnoses. In contrast, the RF-CL classified 53% (n = 363) for (non)-invasive evaluation and 46% (n = 314) for alternative strategies (cut-off PTP &lt; 15%). Agreement between both scores was low, with a Cohen’s kappa of 0.13, indicating slight concordance. Diagnostic performance showed substantial differences: the sensitivity of the MHS for implying relevant CAD was 0.93, compared with 0.53 for the ESC RF-CL, whereas specificity was 0.18 and 0.63, respectively. However, a non-inferiority analysis focusing on sensitivity found the MHS to be non-inferior to the ESC RF-CL, with a sensitivity difference of 0.40 (95% CI 0.36–0.44). Supervised machine learning algorithms were applied to assess predictive performance. The AUROC values were as follows: AutoGloun (0.656), LightGBM (0.655), XGBoost (0.644), and logistic regression (0.628). Conclusion While the MHS showed higher sensitivity, it had lower specificity compared with the RF-CL, with limited agreement between the models. Furthermore, although applying machine learning models with the aim of enhancing PTP did not yield an improved predictive accuracy in this study, they offer substantial potential for further refining risk stratification in clinical practice by incorporating more exogenous variables.
title: Stepwise risk stratification in suspected coronary artery disease: from guideline-based scores to machine learning augmentation

abstract: Abstract Background The coronary sinus Reducer (CSR) is a treatment option for patients with refractory angina due to obstructive coronary artery disease who are not candidates for further revascularization. Although symptomatic improvement is well established, its effect on objective measures of ischaemia is less well defined. Purpose To evaluate the effect of CSR implantation on objective measures of inducible ischaemia in patients with refractory angina, and to identify baseline predictors of clinical non-response. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing CSR implantation between 2011 and 2024. Patients underwent baseline assessment—including CCS angina class, six-minute walk test (6MWT), stress echocardiography (stress-Echo) and/or SPECT—and repeated evaluation six months post-procedure. The co-primary outcomes were the change in wall motion score index (WMSI) on stress-Echo and the change in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischaemia on SPECT. Clinical non-responders were defined as those without a ≥1-class improvement in CCS angina class at 12 months. Results Of 153 treated patients, 136 had complete stress-Echo or SPECT data. Median WMSI during stress improved from 1.38 to 1.23 (p &lt; 0.001), and median LVEF at stress increased from 55% to 60% (p = 0.019). SPECT imaging showed a significant reduction in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischaemia from 55% to 25% (p &lt; 0.001). Clinically, 88% of patients experienced an improvement of ≥1 CCS angina class at six months. Responders had higher baseline LVEF and lower WMSI than non-responders. Conclusions CSR implantation significantly reduced inducible ischaemia on functional stress testing in patients with refractory angina. Baseline myocardial function may help identify patients most likely to benefit from therapy.
title: The impact of coronary sinus reducer on the extent of ischaemia in functional stress tests

abstract: Abstract Background Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) are central to contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet image interpretation remains time-intensive and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) enable automated plaque characterization and may improve consistency and scalability of imaging-guided PCI. Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of AI/ML/DL-enabled IVUS and OCT for identifying high-risk coronary plaque features. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed of studies applying AI/ML/DL to intravascular imaging with a predefined reference standard. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to November 2025. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves were estimated for studies with extractable 2×2 data. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Results Ten studies comprising 2,632 participants were included; four contributed to quantitative synthesis and six to qualitative assessment. AI-enabled IVUS demonstrated pooled sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 80%, with strong rule-out performance (negative predictive value [NPV] 96%) and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.81. OCT-based AI/ML/DL models showed lower sensitivity (64%) but higher specificity (91%), similarly high NPV (96%), and an AUC of 0.91. Positive predictive values were modest across modalities. Qualitative synthesis confirmed consistently high diagnostic performance, and one multimodality IVUS+OCT study reported strong discriminative accuracy (AUC 0.88). Limited lesion-level data restricted quantitative pooling. Conclusion AI-enabled intravascular imaging demonstrates promising diagnostic performance for coronary plaque characterization, particularly for excluding high-risk features. Prospective, outcome-driven validation and standardized reporting are warranted to support clinical integration into PCI workflows.Graphical Abstract
title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence for coronary plaque characterization using OCT and IVUS: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) results in a significant reduction of transvalvular gradients, which may influence coronary hemodynamics. Whether the severity of aortic stenosis affects angiography-derived coronary physiology remains uncertain. We investigated the impact of baseline aortic stenosis severity on paired Quantitative Flow Ratio (QFR) measurements obtained before and after TAVI. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included patients undergoing TAVI between October 2020 and September 2025 with available paired pre- and post-procedural invasive coronary angiographies. QFR was computed retrospectively using Medis QFR® 3.0. Only post-TAVI angiographies performed within six months were included. Vessel-level QFR values were compared before and after TAVI. Exploratory analyses were performed according to baseline hemodynamic severity. Results A total of 56 patients with paired pre- and post-TAVI coronary angiographies were included in the analysis. The median age at the time of TAVI was 82.0 [78.0 - 86.0] years. The median interval between baseline coronary angiography and TAVI was 4.0 [2.0 - 31.0] days, while the interval between TAVI and follow-up angiography was 57.0 [12.0 - 103.0] days. Baseline hemodynamic assessment revealed a median peak transvalvular gradient of 61.0 [40.0 - 79.3] mmHg and a median mean gradient of 36.0 [25.0-49.0] mmHg, reflecting a heterogeneous severe aortic stenosis population. Following valve implantation, gradients decreased substantially to 17.0 [11.0 - 23.0] mmHg and 9.0 [6.0 - 12.0] mmHg, respectively. (Table 1). Of 336 screened vessels, 81 (24.1%) were excluded due to overlap, tortuosity, occlusion, missing projections, or wire artefacts. Median ΔQFR values were comparable between groups, with no statistically significant differences in any coronary territory (left anterior descending artery p=0.314, left circumflex artery p=0.845, right coronary artery p=0.601) (Table 2). Conclusions Despite substantial reductions in transvalvular gradients, angiography-derived coronary physiology assessed by QFR remained stable across the TAVI timeline. Baseline severity of aortic stenosis did not translate into systematic changes in QFR following valve intervention. These findings suggest that coronary lesion assessment using QFR may be accurate and clinically applicable prior to valve intervention. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm these observations.
title: Five years of evidence: impact of aortic stenosis severity on angiography-derived QFR before and after TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) often experience chest pain caused by myocardial ischemia, arising from a mismatch between coronary blood oxygen supply and myocardial oxygen demand. Myocardial perfusion imaging and invasive coronary angiography fractional flow reserve (ICA-FFR) are established modalities for the diagnostic evaluation of patients with suspected obstructive CAD. However, discordance between FFR and the extent of myocardial perfusion defects is frequently observed in moderate stenosis. The coronary volume-to-left ventricular mass ratio (V/M-ratio) has been suggested to describe this relation in supply-demand imbalance. However, it remains unknown whether the V/M-ratio can predict agreement between stress cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) and ICA-FFR. Purpose To investigate the impact of V/M-ratio on the agreement between stress CMR and ICA-FFR measurements in patients with possible myocardial ischemia. Methods This analysis was based on a prospective, multi-center study of 4407 patients referred for cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) due to symptoms suggestive of obstructive CAD. In total 461 patients with suspected stenosis at CCTA underwent CMR and ICA. ICA-FFR was performed in 205 patients with 30-90% diameter stenosis. Patients with severe stenosis (&gt;90%), did not undergo ICA-FFR and were excluded from the analysis. Abnormal CMR were defined as clinically relevant subendocardial or transmural signal changes during stress imaging or irreversible defects in ≥ 2 continuous segments by late gadolinium enhancement imaging. An abnormal ICA-FFR was defined as ≤0.80. Results In the analysis, 205 patients (mean age 63 years, 69% male) were included. The mean total coronary volume was 2911mm3 (sd:875), mean left ventricle mass was 141g (sd:40) and the mean V/M-ratio 21.2 mm3/g (sd:5.8). CMR perfusion test had 36 (18%) diagnosed with abnormal perfusion and ICA-FFR had 73 (36%) with abnormal flow measurements. V/M-ratio evaluated as a predictor of abnormal ICA-FFR or abnormal CMR perfusion using multivariable adjusted logistic regression models showed OR: 0.90 ([0.85:0.96], p&lt;0.01) and OR: 0.91 ([0.84:0.98], p&lt;0.02) respectively, per 1mm3/g increase in V/M-ratio (Figure 1). The V/M-ratio’s impact on concordance between CMR and ICA-FFR result based on CMR normal (p=0.049) or abnormal (p=0.071) perfusion is shown in figure 2. Conclusions In this study, V/M-ratio was shown as an independent predictor of both abnormal CMR and abnormal ICA-FFR results when adjusted for established clinical covariates. Furthermore, V/M-ratio impacted the discordance between CMR and ICA-FFR results. Our results indicated that the rate of false negative CMR results is higher in patients with low V/M-ratio and the false positive rate is higher in patients with higher V/M-ratios.Figure 1 - log.reg.models of outcomes.Figure 2 - CMR and ICA-FFR agreement
title: Coronary volume-to-left ventricular mass ratio as a predictor of agreement between myocardial perfusion- and invasive fractional flow reserve measurements

abstract: Abstract Background Clinical history is the cornerstone for diagnosing chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) and the classification of patients according to the character of chest pain. Current guidelines recommend Computed Tomography Coronary Angiogram (CTCA) for patients with a low clinical likelihood of Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) and no prior history. Furthermore, optimised medical therapy (OMT) should be established prior to any invasive strategy. Purpose To evaluate and improve the management of angina in patients and ongoing invasive treatment, to assess the proportion of angina patients who need a Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI), and to reduce unnecessary invasive procedures through a two-cycle quality improvement audit in patients with an index presentation of CCS. Methods Cycle 1 (Baseline): A cohort of 262 patients was screened over four months. Inclusion criteria specified patients with no prior CAD history were evaluated through the cardiology chest pain clinic. The number of included patients with index presentation chest pain was 160. Data was collected through descriptive analysis, and the patients were interviewed face-to-face. Intervention: Following Cycle 1 findings, we implemented a "Guideline-Directed Referral Checklist," conducted educational workshops for physicians on OMT titration, and established a streamlined pathway for CTCA. Cycle 2 (Re-audit): A subsequent cohort of 140 patients was audited using the same inclusion criteria to measure the impact of these interventions. Results In the first cycle; Over 50% were current or former smokers, and hyperlipidemia (63.1%) was the most prevalent comorbidity. Only 17.5% of patients were prescribed two anti-anginal drugs prior to Coronary Angiography (CAG) or PCI. Non-invasive imaging (that was CTCA or stress echocardiography) was performed in only 13.1% of cases; the majority (82.5%) proceeded directly to CAG or PCI without non-invasive imaging. Notably, 74.3% of patients who underwent CAG were found to have non-cardiac chest pain. Regarding interventions, 20.6% required revascularisation (16.2% PCI; 4.4% CABG). The comparison between the two cycles demonstrated a significant shift toward guideline-directed care, as illustrated in Table 1. Furthermore, the proportion of smokers receiving no cessation counselling decreased from 24.6% to 9.8%. The "negative" CAG rate in patients who had prior non-invasive imaging dropped to near zero. Conclusion(s) OMT is frequently underutilised prior to non-invasive or invasive investigation. Physicians should prioritise OMT and non-invasive screening according to guidelines before referring to a cardiology clinic. On the other hand, directing patients toward CAG or PCI can reduce the duration of waiting and expedite a definite diagnosis without requiring multiple modalities of non-invasive imaging. A primary limitation of this study was the selection bias toward patients who ultimately received CAG or PCI.Table 1
title: Improving adherence to guidelines in the management of chronic coronary syndrome with index presentation through cardiology clinic resulting in invasive procedure: a quality improvement project

abstract: Abstract Background Angiographic phenotypes of coronary artery disease (CAD) in Afro-Caribbean populations remain poorly described, despite CAD’s major contribution to heart failure and overall mortality. Purpose To characterize angiographic phenotypes of coronary artery disease (CAD) and their clinical correlates in Afro-Caribbean patients undergoing coronary angiography, providing population-specific insights into anatomical patterns and clinical presentation. Methods We performed a single-center retrospective analysis of coronary angiography records from a high-volume tertiary cardiac catheterization laboratory (2006–2024). Using Python 3.11, we parsed structured and semi-structured reports to characterize coronary lesion patterns and generate descriptive statistics for demographics, coronary dominance, disease burden, stenosis severity, revascularization patterns, comorbidities, medications, and clinical measurements. Among a total patient population of 80,644, 2,410 patients underwent coronary angiography and were included in the final analysis. Results CAD was confirmed in 68.7% of angiograms, of which 68.5% were obstructive. Overall CAD prevalence in the total population was 1.93%. Mean age at first angiographic encounter was 61.2±12.2 years; 57.1% were male. Coronary dominance was right coronary artery (RCA) in 78.4%, left circumflex (LCx) in 13.8%, and codominant in 7.8%. Disease burden was single-vessel disease 23.9%, two-vessel disease 13.2%, and multivessel disease 8.1%. Left anterior descending (LAD)-predominant disease occurred in 34.9% of CAD cases, with mean stenosis severity of 75.3%±22.8%. Revascularization was performed in 42.9% of CAD patients (PCI 24.7%, CABG 2.8%). Hypertension (66.5%), dyslipidemia (42.3%), and diabetes (39.3%) were the most common comorbidities. Aspirin, statins, and beta-blockers were used in 57.6%, 56.9%, and 55.8% of CAD patients, respectively. Mean systolic blood pressure was 138.8±20.3 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure 80.4±11.4 mmHg, and body mass index 29.3±5.6 kg/m². Chronic total occlusion prevalence was 0.086% and spontaneous coronary artery dissection prevalence was 0.11%. Conclusion In this Afro-Caribbean angiography cohort, CAD was frequently obstructive and commonly LAD-predominant, with substantial multivessel burden and high cardiometabolic comorbidity prevalence. The high RCA dominance highlights population variation in coronary anatomy. These findings support population-specific cardiovascular risk stratification and may inform refinement of guideline implementation for Afro-Caribbean populations.Temporal trendsTop 20 segment-level disease prevalence
title: Angiographic phenotypes of coronary artery disease in an Afro-Caribbean cohort: a real-world catheterization laboratory analysis (2006–2024)

abstract: Abstract Background Angiogram-derived fractional flow reserve (FFRangio) is a less-invasive alternative to wire-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR); however, its reliability near the clinical decision threshold remains uncertain. Purpose This study aimed to assess the agreement between FFRangio and wire-derived FFR in lesions with values close to the clinical cut-off. Methods This multicenter registry included patients with FFRangio values near the threshold for hemodynamically significant ischemia (0.70–0.89) measured during diagnostic coronary angiography. Wire-derived FFR was subsequently assessed during percutaneous coronary intervention. Agreement was analyzed using Bland–Altman analysis and a generalized linear model to identify determinants of measurement differences. Results Seventy patients were enrolled in this study; the mean age was 75.2 years, and 47 patients (67.1%) were male. Target lesions were located in the left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) in 36 patients (51.4%), the left circumflex coronary artery (LCx) in 15 (21.4%), and the right coronary artery (RCA) in 19 (27.1%). Wire-derived FFR was successfully obtained in all patients at the same distance from the target vessel ostium as used for FFRangio analysis. In the overall cohort, the mean FFRangio value was significantly lower than the mean wire-derived FFR value (0.76 vs. 0.82, p&lt;0.001). FFR values differed significantly according to target vessel; the mean FFRangio value was higher in LAD lesions than in LCx and RCA lesions (0.77 vs. 0.74 vs. 0.74, p=0.010), whereas the mean wire-derived FFR value was lower in LAD lesions (0.80 vs. 0.82 vs. 0.86, p=0.049). In Bland–Altman analysis, the difference between FFRangio and wire-derived FFR varied across the range of mean FFR. In a generalized linear model including mean FFR, target vessel, and their interaction, mean FFR was significantly associated with the measurement difference (p = 0.0015), indicating proportional bias. Both target vessel (p &lt; 0.0001) and the interaction between mean FFR and vessel type (p &lt; 0.0001) were significant, demonstrating vessel-specific proportional bias. When mean FFR was fixed at 0.80 using prediction profiling, the predicted difference between FFRangio and wire-derived FFR was smallest in LAD lesions and close to zero, whereas larger negative differences were observed in RCA and LCx lesions. Conclusions FFRangio demonstrates vessel-specific proportional bias relative to wire-derived FFR. In lesions near the clinical decision threshold, agreement between FFRangio and wire-derived FFR is closest in LAD lesions, whereas FFRangio tends to provide lower FFR values in RCA and LCx lesions, leading to more frequent positive ischemia classification. These findings suggest that vessel type should be carefully considered when FFRangio is used for clinical decision making near the cut-off value.
title: Agreement between angiogram-derived and wire-derived fractional flow reserve near the clinical cut-off range

abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND/INTRODUCTION Interventional diagnostic procedures (IDPs) are essential for characterizing coronary vasomotor and microvascular physiology in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Although IDPs effectively identify coronary spasm and microvascular dysfunction (CMD), the independent impact of prior percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) on these functional phenotypes remains poorly defined in the ANOCA population. Purpose We aimed to clarify the impact of prior PCI history on epicardial coronary spasm, microvascular spasm (MVS) and CMD phenotypes. Methods This sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter J-CMD Registry included 674 ANOCA patients undergoing comprehensive IDPs, comprising acetylcholine provocation and bolus thermodilution-based physiological assessment. We compared the prevalence of epicardial spasm, microvascular spasm (MVS), and CMD between patients with and without prior stenting. MVS was defined as induced ischemic symptom and electrocardiographic change without angiographic during SPT. CMD was defined as coronary flow reserve &lt;2.5. Propensity score matching was employed to adjust for baseline clinical disparities. Results Prior stenting was present in 10.1% (n=68) of the cohort. In the unadjusted analysis, rates of positive spasm provocation (48.5% vs. 48.5%, P=0.10) and MVS (17.6% vs. 20.5%, P=0.70) were comparable, whereas CMD was significantly more prevalent in stented patients (38.2% vs. 26.1%, P=0.04). However, after propensity score matching (n=56 pairs), this association was eliminated; no significant differences were observed in the prevalence of positive epicardial spasm provocation, MVS, or CMD between the groups. Conclusions In this prospective nationwide multicenter registry, prior coronary stenting was not independently associated with functional coronary abnormalities. The higher crude prevalence of CMD among stented patients likely reflects a burden of clinical comorbidities rather than a direct sequela of stenting. These findings suggest that stenting per se does not predispose patients to subsequent coronary vasomotor or microvascular dysfunction.
title: Association between prior stenting and coronary vasomotor and microvascular function in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries

abstract: Abstract Background Ischemia with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries (INOCA) is associated with a more than three-fold increase in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, including myocardial infarction and heart failure, compared to the healthy population. Despite current guidelines recommending invasive functional testing, its implementation remains limited in routine clinical practice. We present our experience in implementing a standardized acetylcholine (Ach) provocation protocol for precise endotyping of INOCA patients. Purpose To improve the diagnostic efficiency and personalized treatment of patients with INOCA by differentiating clinical endotypes and optimizing the diagnostic algorithm. Methods The study enrolled 68 patients with symptoms of coronary artery disease who presented to our center between February 2025 and January 2026. All patients underwent a clinical evaluation, including echocardiography and a graded exercise stress test. Subsequently, all patients underwent coronary angiography, supplemented by an acetylcholine provocation test. In patients with evidence of coronary atherosclerosis, fractional flow reserve (FFR) was measured to exclude the hemodynamic significance of stenoses Results The mean age of the patients was 57.7 ± 10.5 years. Women accounted for 42.6%. Among the risk factors, hypertension (91.2%), dyslipidemia (50.0%), smoking (23.5%), and diabetes mellitus (13.2%) prevailed. Following the acetylcholine provocation test, the following conditions were verified: endothelial dysfunction – 26.5%, vasospastic angina – 44.1%, microvascular spasm – 11.8%, and symptomatic myocardial bridges – 17.6%. Overall, 54.4% of bridges were detected, but they were not associated with spasm in all patients. The procedure was safe; transient complications, including AV blocks (13.2%) and supraventricular arrhythmias (4.4%), were self-limiting and successfully managed in the catheterization laboratory. Conclusion Invasive endotyping via acetylcholine provocation is safe and provides essential diagnostic clarity in patients with INOCA. Our findings highlight the significant role of symptomatic myocardial bridges in triggering vasospasm, a mechanism often overlooked during routine angiography. Implementing this standardized protocol—the first of its kind in Ukraine—facilitates a paradigm shift from empirical management to personalized, endotype-specific therapy, which is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in this underserved patient population.
title: Endotyping of patients with INOCA: a single Ukrainian center experience

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Incomplete revascularization after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is commonly assessed using the residual Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score (rSS), an anatomical measure of residual coronary artery disease. The residual Functional SYNTAX score (rFSS), incorporating ischemia-producing lesions, may better reflect clinically relevant residual disease. The comparative impact of anatomical versus functional residual disease on symptom improvement remains unclear. Purpose To compare the association of anatomical residual disease (rSS) and functional residual disease (rFSS) with symptomatic improvement after PCI. Methods Consecutive patients with at least Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) angina class II undergoing PCI between October 2018 and December 2019 at a general hospital were evaluated (n=236). Offline Quantitative Flow Ratio (QFR) analysis was estimated for each patient. rSS was calculated according to the standard SYNTAX methodology to quantify the anatomical burden of residual coronary disease after PCI. The rFSS was derived by summing the individual SYNTAX scores only for residual lesions associated with ischemia, defined as vessel QFR ≤0.89. CCS improvement was defined as a reduction in CCS class at follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, left ventricular ejection fraction (EF), and glomerular filtration rate were constructed to assess the independent association of rSS and rFSS with symptomatic improvement. Results In the anatomical model, rSS was not independently associated with CCS improvement (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.24–1.13; p=0.098), whereas EF was independently associated with symptomatic improvement (OR 1.07 per 1% increase, 95% CI 1.02–1.11; p=0.002). In the functional model, rFSS was independently associated with a reduced likelihood of CCS improvement (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.09–0.88; p=0.028), while EF was no longer statistically significant. Conclusions Functional residual ischemia, but not anatomical residual disease, independently predicts reduced symptomatic improvement after PCI. These findings indicate that functional assessment of residual disease may provide additional information regarding symptomatic recovery beyond anatomical evaluation alone.
title: Functional residual ischemia and ventricular function drive symptomatic outcomes after PCI

abstract: Abstract Background The index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) combines hyperaemic distal coronary pressure with thermodilution transit time. Both components require invasive pressure wire instrumentation and pharmacological hyperaemia. We assessed whether resting angiographic measurements predict each component of hyperaemic coronary physiology independently, and validated these predictions prospectively. Methods We studied 300 patients with unobstructed coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary physiology at a regional cardiac centre. A multi-layer perceptron regressor predicted hyperaemic distal coronary pressure from resting aortic pressure and fractional flow reserve (FFR). A linear model predicted resting coronary transit time from TIMI frame count, and a second multi-layer perceptron predicted hyperaemic transit time from the predicted resting transit time and TIMI frame count, modelling the non-linear resting-to-hyperaemic transformation. Development performance was assessed by stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The model was then applied to a distinct group of 119 prospective patients undergoing thermodilution. TIMI frame count and thermodilution measurements were obtained from the same coronary artery in all prospective patients. Results In the development cohort, TIMI frame count correlated with thermodilution resting transit time (r = 0.53, p &lt; 0.001) and hyperaemic transit time (r = 0.62, p &lt; 0.001). Cross-validated predictions of hyperaemic distal coronary pressure (r = 0.75, mean absolute error [MAE] 6.7 mmHg), hyperaemic transit time (r = 0.61, MAE 0.10 s), and resting transit time (r = 0.52, MAE 0.32 s) were obtained. In the prospective cohort, distal coronary pressure prediction was preserved (r = 0.62, MAE 8.7 mmHg) and resting transit time prediction exceeded development performance (r = 0.59, MAE 0.39 s). Hyperaemic transit time prediction was attenuated but remained significant (r = 0.39, p &lt; 0.001, MAE 0.16 s), with a corresponding TIMI-to-thermodilution correlation of r = 0.39. All three components showed minimal bias (pressure −2.1 mmHg; resting transit time +0.04 s; hyperaemic transit time −0.01 s) (Figure). Conclusions Resting aortic haemodynamics and angiographic contrast transit predict the individual components of invasive hyperaemic coronary physiology. Pressure prediction generalised well to a prospective cohort; transit time prediction was attenuated, reflecting the greater stochastic variability of thermodilution-derived transit measurements relative to deterministic angiographic frame counts. These findings establish the physiological basis for wire-free estimation of coronary microvascular resistance without reliance upon computational fluid dynamics principles.Figure 1
title: Resting angiography encodes hyperaemic coronary physiology: component-level prospective validation

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal long-term antiplatelet monotherapy in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains a subject of ongoing debate. In particular, it remains unclear whether different P2Y12 inhibitors provide comparable clinical benefits when used as long-term monotherapy. We investigated the efficacy and safety of antiplatelet monotherapy following dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) in patients with ACS, using a Japanese nationwide administrative claims database. Methods This retrospective study included patients with ACS who underwent PCI with drug-eluting stent implantation and received antiplatelet monotherapy after a minimum of 6 months of DAPT between April 2014 and March 2020. Net adverse clinical events (NACE), a composite of thromboembolism, major bleeding, and all-cause death, were compared between patients receiving clopidogrel 75 mg or prasugrel 3.75 mg and those receiving aspirin 75–100 mg using an inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) analysis. Results Of the 109,077 patients included, 50,189 (46.0%) were aged 70 years and older, and 25,123 (23.0%) were female. Of these, 19,479 (17.9%), 9,067 (8.3%), and 80,531 (73.8%) patients received clopidogrel, prasugrel, and aspirin monotherapy, respectively. With a median (IQR) follow-up of 1,542 (1,071–2,092) days after the index PCI, NACE occurred in 1,423 patients (3.53 per 100 person-years) in the clopidogrel group, 408 patients (2.68 per 100 person-years) in the prasugrel group, and 5,490 patients (3.05 per 100 person-years) in the aspirin group after the 18-month landmark period. The IPTW-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of NACE was 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.96–1.10, p=0.40) in the clopidogrel group and 1.01 (95% CI: 0.89–1.14, p=0.92) in the prasugrel group compared with the aspirin group. The prasugrel group showed a lower hazard ratio of thromboembolism (HR: 0.74 [95% CI: 0.60–0.92], p=0.008) and no differences in major bleeding event (HR: 1.13 [95% CI: 0.87–1.48]). Conclusions In patients after PCI for ACS, long-term monotherapy with clopidogrel or prasugrel showed no significant difference in NACE compared with aspirin. Prasugrel use was associated with a lower risk of thromboembolic events without an increased risk of severe bleeding.
title: Clopidogrel or prasugrel vs. aspirin monotherapy for long-term secondary prevention after percutaneous coronary intervention for acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Inflammation plays an important role in the development of atherosclerosis and the occurrence of ischemic events. In addition to inflammation, thrombosis is also directly involved in the pathogenesis of acute coronary syndromes. Colchicine has effects on cell adhesion molecules and inflammatory chemokines, in addition to suppressing interleukin 1. In patients with coronary artery disease (CAD), there is convincing evidence showing a decrease in cardiovascular events with the use of colchicine. However, the mechanisms behind these benefits are not fully understood, with the antiplatelet effect of the drug remaining a hypothesis. Objective The main objective of the study was to analyze the role of low dose colchicine on platelet reactivity (PR), utilizing Multiplate aggregometry with thrombin receptor-activating peptide (Multiplate TRAP). The main secondary endpoints were the analysis of PR using Multiplate adenosine diphosphate (Multiplate ADP) and Multiplate aspirin (Multiplate ASP). Methods This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Eighty patients with proven chronic CAD (72.5% males, mean age 62.75 years) were randomized to receive colchicine 0.5mg once daily (intervention group, N=40) or placebo (placebo group, N=40). All patients were taking aspirin 100 mg daily. Randomization was carried out in two blocks of 40 patients at a rate of 1:1. Blood samples were collected at baseline visit and the end of follow-up (30 ± 3 days). Results The figure shows the median difference (25th,75th percentiles) in PR between baseline and follow-up for the colchicine and placebo groups, considering the three methods utilized. The median differences between the groups were, respectively, 7.0 AU (-8.75 to 22.0) vs -3.5 AU (-14.75,12.5) considering Multiplate TRAP, -1.0 AU (-17.5,22.5) vs 2.5 AU (-10.0,22.5) by Multiplate ADP analysis, and 1.5 AU (-6.5,9.75) vs. -1.0 AU (-10.5,8.00) by Multiplate ASP. Conclusion In this population of stable patients with CAD, colchicine did not influence platelet reactivity, indicating that modulation of platelet reactivity is unlikely to be a major contributor to the clinical benefit previously demonstrated with the drug.Comparison of Platelet Reactivity
title: Effects of colchicine on platelet reactivity among stable post-myocardial infarction patients: a double-blind randomized controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) frequently experience ongoing angina, diminished quality of life (QoL), and face a heightened need for revascularisation procedures. Purpose The present analysis aimed to consolidate clinical and health economic data regarding the use of ranolazine in CCS. By combining predictive modelling with systematic review findings, we assessed the drug's influence on patient symptoms, overarching cardiovascular events, and financial viability. Methods We conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis and systematic review of existing clinical and cost-effectiveness data. To forecast five-year treatment trajectories and disease advancement from a healthcare payer's viewpoint, a Markov state-transition model was constructed. This simulation accounted for Canadian Cardiovascular Society angina grades I through IV, the occurrence of acute coronary syndromes (ACS), utilisation of optimal medical therapy (OMT), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and mortality rates. Primary endpoints evaluated were quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), additional expenditures, and the duration of life lived free from ACS or revascularisation interventions. Results Treatment with ranolazine led to a substantial decrease in the need for CABG by 37% (risk ratio [RR] = 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.53–0.75), PCI by 54% (RR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.12–1.76), and overall revascularisation interventions by 17% (RR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.75–0.93). Patients demonstrated enhanced functional capacity, noting extended exercise times (+42.9 seconds), postponed angina onset (+28.9 seconds), and a delay in ST-segment depression (+28.0 seconds). Furthermore, self-reported metrics across the Seattle Angina Questionnaire showed marked improvement. From an economic standpoint, incremental cost-utility ratios were calculated at 36,356 United States dollars (USD) per QALY after one year and 40,505 USD per QALY at the five-year mark, consistently staying under the accepted 50,000 USD willingness-to-pay threshold. Every month of ranolazine administration yielded an additional two weeks without the need for procedures, accumulating to 1.8 years of procedure-free time over a five-year span. For every 1000 individuals treated, the therapy averted 1.41 CABG operations, 23.21 PCI interventions, and 36.15 ACS occurrences. Conclusion Ranolazine effectively lowers the incidence of myocardial infarction (MI) and the demand for revascularisation while enhancing patients' quality of life, symptom control, and exercise capabilities. Offering both sustained cardiovascular benefits and strong cost-effectiveness, these results endorse the incorporation of ranolazine into standard CCS treatment protocols and broader healthcare resource strategies.
title: The role of ranolazine in managing chronic coronary syndrome: a synthesis of clinical outcomes and health economic modelling

abstract: Abstract Background Because prior evidence has involved heterogeneous anticoagulant regimens and coronary treatment strategies, the optimal antithrombotic strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluate the efficacy and safety of oral anticoagulant (OAC) monotherapy versus OAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) in patients with AF and CCS, stratified by anticoagulant type and coronary treatment strategy. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), major bleeding, and net adverse clinical events (NACE). Subgroup-specific data were extracted when trials included heterogeneous anticoagulant types or coronary treatment strategies. The study was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Results Six RCTs including 5,924 patients were analyzed. Anticoagulant type significantly modified treatment effect (P for interaction = 0.02). Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) monotherapy reduced MACCE compared with DOAC plus SAPT (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.59–0.88; P = 0.002), whereas vitamin K antagonist monotherapy showed no significant difference (HR 1.22; 95% CI 0.83–1.78; P = 0.32). DOAC monotherapy also significantly reduced major bleeding (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.35–0.64; P &lt; 0.00001) and NACE (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.49–0.68; P &lt; 0.00001). Treatment effect differed by coronary treatment strategy (P for interaction = 0.03). In patients with prior coronary revascularization, DOAC monotherapy reduced MACCE, driven by those with prior percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), in whom MACCE was reduced by 34% (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.53–0.83; P = 0.0004), whereas no benefit was observed with medical therapy alone (HR 1.26; 95% CI 0.73–2.17; P = 0.40). In prior PCI, DOAC monotherapy also reduced major bleeding (HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.27–0.66; P = 0.0001), NACE (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.52–0.72; P &lt; 0.00001), all-cause mortality (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.43–0.77; P = 0.0002), and cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.34–0.73; P = 0.0004), without differences in myocardial infarction or stroke. Conclusions In patients with AF and CCS, the efficacy and safety of OAC monotherapy vary according to anticoagulant type and coronary treatment strategy. Compared with DOAC plus SAPT, DOAC monotherapy reduces mortality and major bleeding, with benefits most evident in patients with prior PCI.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Efficacy and safety of antithrombotic strategies for atrial fibrillation in patients with chronic coronary syndrome according to coronary treatment strategy: a meta-analysis of randomized trials

abstract: Abstract Background Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide and is characterized by inflammatory processes involved in plaque development. The leukotriene pathway contributes to vascular inflammation and may play a role in atherosclerosis. By modulating this pathway, leukotriene receptor antagonists (LTRA), currently used in asthma, could potentially reduce inflammatory mechanisms relevant to plaque formation and have potential for repurposing in cardiovascular prevention. Objective To evaluate whether LTRA use is associated with lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with asthma compared with long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) use. Methods We first formed a base cohort of patients aged ≥40 years with active asthma between 2000 and 2023 from the United Kingdom Clinical Practice Research Datalink. Using a prevalent new-user design, all patients initiating LTRAs (montelukast or zafirlukast) were identified to create time-based exposure sets including all eligible LABA comparators with the same age, sex, prior coronary artery disease status, and prior LABA use. Each LTRA initiator was then matched 1:1 without replacement to a comparator LABA user with the closest time-conditional propensity score. Patients were followed until outcome occurrence, treatment discontinuation or switch to the other exposure group, end of registration, death, or end of the study period, whichever occurred first. We used a Cox proportional hazards model to estimate hazard ratio (HR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) for MACE, defined as myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, or cardiovascular death. We also assessed the individual components of MACE and MACE+, defined as an extended composite of MACE plus transient ischaemic attack and unstable angina, as secondary outcomes. Results The study cohort included 55,997 patients LTRA users matched to 55,997 LABA users. Mean age was 59.4 (standard deviation 11.0) years, 66.8% were female and 5.0% had prior coronary artery disease. During 123,810 years of follow-up, 891 MACE occurred. LTRA use was associated with lower risk of MACE compared with LABA use, with adjusted incidence rates of 6.64 vs 7.91 events per 1,000 person-years (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.73–0.95). For individual components of the MACE, myocardial infarction (HR 0.90; 95% CI 0.74–1.10), ischaemic stroke (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.69–1.11), and cardiovascular death (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.51–0.88) showed similar patterns. LTRA use was also associated with lower risk of MACE+ (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.79–1.00). Findings did not differ by age and sex. Results using an intention-to-treat approach with follow-up restricted to 1 year were consistent with the primary analyses. Conclusion LTRA use was associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with LABA use in patients with asthma and supports further evaluation of LTRA for cardiovascular prevention.Primary analyses
title: Leukotriene receptor antagonists and lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with asthma

abstract: Abstract Background Genotype-guided P2Y12-inhibitor de-escalation instead of routine prasugrel or ticagrelor based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) reduces bleeding without compromising the ischemic risk in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Early aspirin withdrawal after uneventful ticagrelor-based DAPT is another option to mitigate bleeding risk. Whether genotype-guided P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy is safe and effective in patients undergoing PCI is unknown. We performed a pharmacodynamic study in patients undergoing elective PCI. Objective To evaluate the pharmacodynamic response of genotype-guided P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in patients undergoing elective PCI. Methods Patients were randomized 1:1 to genotype-guided P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy (n=44) or standard DAPT with clopidogrel and aspirin (n=44). In the monotherapy group, carriers of a loss of function (LoF) allele received prasugrel or ticagrelor, while non-carriers received clopidogrel. Allocated treatment started the day after PCI. Baseline platelet function was measured in venous blood directly after PCI and at 30 days post-randomization. The primary endpoint was PRU levels measured with the VerifyNow system at 30 days. PRU levels at 30 days were assessed with an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), using PRU levels at baseline as covariate. Results There were no differences in baseline characteristics between groups. In the monotherapy group, 14 patients were carriers of a LoF allele, of which 10 were discharged on prasugrel and 4 on ticagrelor. Standard DAPT with clopidogrel was prescribed in 43 patients in the control group. The adjusted mean PRU at 30 days was 94.2 (95%: CI 81.4–107.0) in the standard DAPT group and 68.7 (95% CI: 56.2–81.2) in the monotherapy group. The model-adjusted mean difference was -25.5 (95% CI: -43.0 to -8.0; p=0.0058), which was statistically significant. High platelet reactivity, defined as PRU≥208, was observed in 3 patients in the standard DAPT group and 1 patient in the monotherapy group at baseline. There was no HPR at 30 days as there was no PRU ≥208 measured. Stent thrombosis occurred once in both groups and there were two major bleeding events in the standard DAPT group. Conclusion Patients undergoing elective PCI treated with genotype-guided P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy have significantly lower P2Y12-inhibitor induced platelet reactivity compared to those treated with standard DAPT with clopidogrel. A clinical study to demonstrate the efficacy and safety of genotype-guided P2Y12 monotherapy compared to clopidogrel-based DAPT after elective PCI is needed.PRU levels according to allocated groupFlow diagram study design
title: A pharmacodynamic analysis of genotype-guided P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI in patients with chronic coronary syndrome – the POPular STRATEGY study

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal long-term antiplatelet monotherapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains debated, with aspirin traditionally recommended despite emerging evidence supporting P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. Purpose The comparison of clinical outcomes between clopidogrel and aspirin monotherapy in patients following PCI. Methods Our systematic review and meta-analysis was performed in accordance with the updated PRISMA guidelines. We conducted an electronic bibliographic screening in the three major databases of the literature (Cochrane, Medline and Scopus), to identify relevant studies published up to February 15th, 2026. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included all-cause and cardiac mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic and haemorrhagic stroke, major bleeding, repeat revascularization, target vessel revascularization and stent thrombosis. Relative risks (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated and pooled using random-effects models. Results A total of 164,361 post-PCI patients were included (clopidogrel: 81,869, aspirin: 82,492). Clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of MACE compared to aspirin (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.69-0.88, I²=54%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.59-1.37, I²=88%), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.67-1.13, I²=33%), MI (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.65-1.13, I²=52%), ischemic stroke (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.64-1.06, I²=0%), haemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.35-1.80, I²=49%), major bleeding (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.74-1.23, I²=30%), repeat revascularization (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.85-1.09, I²=0%), target vessel revascularization (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.81-1.17, I²=0%), or stent thrombosis (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.49-1.35, I²=0%). Funnel plot assessment showed significant publication bias in MACE, MI and stent thrombosis. Conclusions Clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with reduced MACE compared with aspirin among post-PCI patients, without increasing bleeding or ischemic complications. These findings support clopidogrel as an effective alternative antiplatelet monotherapy following PCI and warrant further randomized evaluation to inform guideline recommendations.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Comparative efficacy of clopidogrel and aspirin monotherapy after dual antiplatelet therapy in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Despite statin therapy, residual inflammation contributes to cardiovascular events in acute or chronic coronary syndromes (ACS/CCS). While colchicine is a potent anti-inflammatory adjunct, its simultaneous use with high-intensity atorvastatin raises safety concerns regarding rhabdomyolysis. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of this combination on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) reduction. Methods This interim analysis of a double-blind, randomized controlled trial included 60 ACS/CCS patients undergoing angiography or PCI. Patients were randomized (1:1) to atorvastatin 40 mg plus colchicine 0.6 mg daily (n = 31) or atorvastatin 40 mg plus placebo (n = 29). The primary outcome was the change in hsCRP over 3 months. Results Baseline geometric mean (GM) hsCRP was comparable between combination and monotherapy groups (2.95 vs. 3.07 mg/L; p = 0.904). At 3 months, GM hsCRP was significantly lower in the combination group (0.93 vs. 1.89 mg/L; p = 0.038), representing a 51% greater reduction (GM ratio 0.49; 95% CI 0.25–0.96). Severe diarrhea was more frequently observed in the colchicine group (16.7% vs. 0%; p=0.053), but there was no rhabdomyolysis or hepatitis reported. Clinical events (MACE) were infrequent and similar between groups (10.0% vs. 7.1%; p = 1.000). Conclusion The simultaneous initiation of low-dose colchicine and atorvastatin 40 mg significantly reduced systemic inflammation in ACS/CCS patients. Despite an increased incidence of severe diarrhea, the potent synergistic effect and favorable muscle safety profile support its potential to target residual cardiovascular risk.Figure 1 Geometric mean of hsCRP levelsTable 1 Baseline Characteristics
title: Anti-inflammatory effects of atorvastatin and colchicine combination in patients with acute or chronic coronary syndrome undergoing coronary angiography and/or PCI

abstract: Abstract Background Clopidogrel response is highly variable due to both CYP2C19 loss-of-function (LOF) alleles and acquired mechanisms related to comorbidity and drug–drug interactions. Where platelet function testing (PFT) is not routinely available, genotyping alone may miss residual risk. We evaluated clopidogrel non-responsiveness using an integrated strategy combining CYP2C19 genotyping with clinical variables and risk tools (ABCD-GENE and PARIS). Purpose To determine profiles and outcomes in LOF carriers versus non-LOF metabolizers and to assess phenotype-driven escalation of P2Y12 inhibition. Objective To compare the clinical profiles of patients with CYP2C19 LOF-related genetic resistance and non-LOF metabolizers and to assess a clinically driven precision strategy for identifying non-responsiveness and guiding treatment decisions, including revascularization, switching to ticagrelor, and/or prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Methods Observational cohort study of consecutive coronary artery disease patients undergoing CYP2C19 genotyping (N=117). Participants were grouped as LOF carriers (intermediate/poor metabolizers) or non-LOF (normal metabolizers). We recorded baseline demographics, risk factors, presentation, and revascularization (PCI/CABG) and followed patients for &gt;12 months for adjudicated new atherothrombotic events and antithrombotic treatment changes (clopidogrel, ticagrelor, and/or oral anticoagulation). Haemoglobin and renal function were collected when available to derive PARIS and ABCD-GENE scores. Results Genetic resistance (CYP2C19 LOF) was present in 26.5% (31/117), indicating that 1 in 4 patients had a baseline genetic predisposition to reduced clopidogrel responsiveness. A “genetic blind spot” emerged: among non-LOF (normal) metabolizers, 51.8% experienced a new atherosclerotic event during follow-up. Genotype did not discriminate event occurrence (p=0.957), suggesting that residual risk was largely driven by acquired factors. The strongest predictors of new events were proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use (OR 3.81; p = 0.094), statin therapy (OR 1.87), reflecting higher baseline risk, renal dysfunction (eGFR &lt; 60 mL/min/1.73 m²; OR 1.73), and diabetes (OR 1.45), supporting an acquired resistance phenotype. Risk scores added clinical value: ABCD-GENE may identify high-risk patients despite a “normal” genotype, while PARIS aligned with real-world decisions—among those classified as high ischemic risk (particularly patients with renal dysfunction and diabetes), 74.4% were switched to ticagrelor, suggesting phenotype-driven escalation of antiplatelet therapy. Conclusion CYP2C19 genotyping alone did not predict ischemic events. An integrated, phenotype-driven approach—highlighting proton pump inhibitor exposure and cardiometabolic/renal comorbidity—may better identify patients who require escalation to more potent P2Y12 inhibitors when PFT is unavailable.
title: Beyond CYP2C19: clinical phenotype drives events and P2Y12 escalation in a real-world Andean population

abstract: Abstract Background Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is visceral fat located between the myocardium and visceral pericardium. Without an anatomical barrier, EAT influences cardiac and vascular function through metabolic and paracrine pathways. Pathological alterations in EAT volume and function are implicated in the progression of various cardiovascular diseases. Clinical evidence shows that type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) alters EAT volume and is a recognized risk factor for coronary atherosclerosis (CAS). Accumulating evidence suggests that T2DM may mediates the development of CAS via EAT; however, its mechanism remains unclear. Purpose This study aimed to investigate whether T2DM deteriorates coronary atherosclerotic lesions through its effect on adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) and explored its molecular mechanism. Methods A total of 480 chronic total occlusion (CTO) patients were enrolled and divided into two groups based on the presence of T2DM. Baseline clinical characteristics, medical history, and imaging data were collected. Computed tomography (CT) was used to quantify EAT volume, and the Gensini score was applied to assess the severity of CAS. Logistic regression was used to identify risk factors and multiple linear regression to analyze correlations between significantly different variables. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) was applied to characterize SLC5A2 expression across populations and cell types.Human adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) were treated with palmitic acid and glucose to establish a diabetic model in vitro, then induced to adipogenic differentiation. The mRNA and protein levels of PPARγ, C/EBPα, IL-6 and IL-8 were quantified. Results Of a total of 480 patients enrolled , 198 were T2DM patients.EAT volume and coronary atherosclerosis severity were significantly higher in the T2DM group than in the non-T2DM group. After adjusting for confounders, EAT volume remained an independent risk factor for coronary atherosclerosis severity. Subgroup analysis within the T2DM group revealed that 45 patients treated with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors had lower EAT volume and less severe coronary atherosclerotic lesions compared to controls. SnRNA-seq of human EAT showed elevated SLC5A2 expression in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and T2DM, particularly in adipocytes, where expression was significantly upregulated compared to non-diabetic controls. In vitro, ADSCs-derived adipocytes in the diabetic model group exhibited enhanced adipogenic capacity and increased expression of senescence- and inflammation-related genes. All these abnormalities were ameliorated by empagliflozin treatment.
