Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was performed, with all parameters entered as difference (∆) between cases and controls to identify the strongest predictors for ∆IL-6 levels. A stability selection approach was used: parameters with non-zero coefficients in ≥4 out of 5 independent LASSO runs were tested by linear regression for association with ∆IL-6 levels. “Iron status” was defined as a combined parameter of transferrin saturation (TSAT) and serum iron by principal component analysis, given their value as early markers of change in iron status in acute inflammation. Associations between infarct size, IL-6, iron status and HF were tested by serial LMM correcting for key confounders. The hypothesized path from high-sensitivity troponin-T (hsTnT) through IL-6 and iron status to N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) was tested by serial mediation analyses. Results IL-6 levels were higher in cases than controls (25.7 ng/l vs. 20.0 ng/l, p = 0.035). Patients presenting with signs of acute HF (Killip Class ≥ 2) showed higher IL-6 levels. Implementing LASSO regression, hsTnT, IL-1b and tumor necrosis factor a were identified as robust determinants of IL-6 levels (Figure 1). Patients with increased IL-6 showed evidence of impaired iron status, which in turn associated with levels of NT-proBNP after adjustment for confounders. Further analyses confirmed significant partial mediation of the interaction between hsTnT and NT-proBNP by IL-6 and iron status (Figure 2). Conclusions IL-6 levels were increased in AMI patients who suffered death or re-infarction at one year. Our findings suggest a partially mediated connection between infarct size (hsTnT), inflammation (IL-6), impaired iron status (serum iron & TSAT) and HF (NT-proBNP). Future studies may investigate early IL-6 blockade and/or iron substitution in patients with large AMI and excessive IL-6 levels.
title: Increased interleukin-6 levels associate with worse 1-year outcome after acute myocardial infarction and link infarct size, impaired iron status and heart failure

abstract: Abstract Background Inflammation influences outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, the relative impact of local coronary inflammation versus systemic inflammation on vessel-oriented outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare their prognostic value for vessel-oriented composite endpoints (VOCE) in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) undergoing PCI. Methods In 2,075 CAD patients undergoing PCI with pre-procedural coronary CT angiography, pericoronary fat attenuation index (FAI) in major coronary vessels were quantified. Systemic inflammation was evaluated by high-sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP). Multivariable Cox analyses, restricted cubic splines, Kaplan–Meier analyses were used. Subgroup analyses were conducted. VOCE was analyzed including vessel-related cardiac death, vessel-related myocardial infarction (nonprocedural) and targeted vessel revascularization (TVR). Results Over median 3 years follow-up, 126 target vessels (4.9%) experienced VOCE. After multivariable adjustment, local inflammation (FAI-LAD, FAI-LCX, FAI-RCA, FAI-MAX, FAI-MEAN, FAI-MIN) was independently associated with VOCE. XGBoost identified FAI-MAX as the most important local predictor (SHAP value 1.44 for VOCE). Patients with combined high local (FAI-MAX ≥-70.00HU) and high systemic inflammation had the highest risk (VOCE: HR 4.23, 95% CI 2.44-7.33; both P&lt;0.001). Notably, high local inflammation with low systemic inflammation conferred greater risk than low local with high systemic inflammation for VOCE (FAI-targeted for HR 1.66 vs. 1.20). Integration of FAI with hs-CRP significantly improved prognostic prediction over either marker alone (AUC 0.711 for FAI-MAX + hs-CRP vs. 0.589 for hs-CRP alone, DeLong P&lt;0.05). Conclusion In CAD patients after PCI, local coronary inflammation (FAI-MAX and FAI-targeted) may demonstrate a stronger and more direct association with adverse outcomes than systemic inflammation. Integrating both improves risk stratification, supporting inflammation-guided management in CAD.
title: Comparative impact of local and systemic inflammation on vessel-oriented outcomes following PCI in coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease exacerbated by innate immune activation. Trained immunity, characterised by metabolic reprogramming and enhanced inflammatory response of innate immune cells, has been implicated in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and provides a potential therapeutic target. Purpose To establish whether functional characteristics of "trained" phenotype in peripheral monocytes is associated with extent of coronary artery disease (CAD) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Methods In 56 participants who had presented with non-STE ACS, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and plasma were isolated at follow-up, median 56 (range 45-81) days from discharge. PBMCs were cultured in DMEM (5mM glucose), rested overnight, then stimulated with LPS 100ng/mL and IFNγ 10ng/mL (M1) or left unstimulated (M0). Monocytes were positively selected from these PBMCs for bulk RNA sequencing. To quantify pathway activity, Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) was used to assign enrichment scores for 50 predefined Hallmark gene sets (Broad Institute) to each sample, based on ranked gene expression. To examine inflammatory responsiveness, we calculated the change in pathway activity for each participant as the difference between stimulated (M1) and unstimulated (M0) monocytes. Pathways with correlated stimulation-induced activity were grouped into modules using unsupervised hierarchical clustering. In this way, correlated pathway responses were condensed into a smaller number of biologically meaningful modules, then principal component analysis (PCA) was used to derive composite scores summarising the shared activity between modules. Results Two modules reflecting key features of trained immunity were identified: an interferon signalling module, and a metabolic module comprising oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Participants were dichotomised according to the median composite score derived from these modules. A lower score—characterised by reduced oxidative phosphorylation pathway activity together with enhanced interferon signalling following stimulation—was associated with greater coronary disease burden (median SYNTAX 29 [21.5–34.6] vs 18 [11.0–26.0], p=0.009). In multivariable linear regression adjusting for age, sex, BMI, and diabetes, the composite score remained independently associated with SYNTAX score (p=0.04). No significant associations were observed between the score and plasma CRP, IL-6, or IL-18 levels. Conclusion A peripheral monocyte phenotype consistent with trained immunity—defined by impaired oxidative phosphorylation coupled with enhanced interferon signalling—is associated with more extensive coronary artery disease. These findings support transcriptomic profiling of innate immune reprogramming as a strategy to identify patients who may derive greatest benefit from targeted anti-inflammatory therapies.Figure 1
title: Transcriptomic signature of trained immunity associates with the extent of coronary artery disease in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Residual coronary inflammation remains a driver of recurrent cardiovascular risk after myocardial infarction (MI), even in clinically stable patients receiving guideline-directed secondary prevention. The Fat Attenuation Index (FAI)-Score, derived from coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA), noninvasive measures local coronary inflammation associated with major adverse cardiovascular events. In a phase 2a pilot study, orticumab reduced coronary inflammation in patients with a high baseline FAI-Score. FORTIFY is a randomised clinical trial that aims to enroll patients with elevated FAI-Score after MI despite well-controlled risk factors. FORTIFY will test whether the monoclonal antibody orticumab reduces local inflammation. Methods FORTIFY is an ongoing, multicenter, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial of orticumab in clinically stable patients &gt;6 months after type 1 MI. Participants must be on guideline-directed secondary prevention with well-controlled LDL-C, blood pressure, and glycemia. The entry criteria include elevated coronary inflammation defined as FAI-Score ≥75th centile in at least 1 coronary artery or ≥50th centile in at least 2 arteries. Eligible participants are randomised 2:2:1:1 to high-dose orticumab, low-dose orticumab, or matched placebo regimens. Follow-up CCTA is performed at 6 months. The primary endpoint is percent change from baseline in mean FAI-Score across the 3 major coronary arteries. Results of screening by FAI As of 25 February 2026, 185 participants underwent screening CCTA with FAI-Score assessment; 97 were eligible and 88 were not eligible for randomisation. In this clinically stable population &gt;6 months after type 1 MI, FAI-Score centiles showed broad distribution in LAD, LCx, RCA, and the mean, providing the first description of FAI-Score centile distribution in a stable post-MI trial population. Across all screened participants, values spanned nearly the full 0–100 scale. LAD FAI-Score centiles ranged from 1% to 99% (mean 49.9%, SD 29.4). In the LAD, FAI score in eligible participants (n=97) ranged from 12% to 99% (mean 70.7%, SD 18.8), versus 1% to 72% (mean 26.5%, SD 20.0) in non-eligible participants (n=86). Similar patterns were observed for LCx and RCA. Conclusions These findings support the feasibility of use of FAI score as an enrichment strategy for residual coronary inflammation and support the choice of studying a stable population &gt;6 months post-MI, where substantial coronary inflammation persists despite contemporary secondary prevention.FAI Score centile distribution
title: FORTIFY: a phase 2b randomised trial evaluating the effect of orticumab on coronary inflammation (FAI-Score) in post myocardial infarction patients selects for patients with high residual FAI-Score

abstract: Abstract Background Inflammation is crucial to the pathogenesis, progression, and prognosis of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Routine complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices—neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR)—are proposed as prognostic markers, but their relative value and incremental contribution beyond conventional risk factors in STEMI patients remain unclear. Purpose To evaluate the association of these inflammatory indices with one-year all-cause mortality in STEMI patients and quantify their incremental prognostic value over a baseline clinical model. Methods This retrospective cohort study enrolled 44,802 consecutive STEMI patients with complete one-year follow-up for all-cause death. NLR, PLR, SII, and MLR were calculated from admission complete blood count results. Cox proportional hazards regression models were constructed to assess the independent association of inflammatory indices with mortality: Model 0 (clinical variables only: age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, prior myocardial infarction [MI]); Model 1 (Model 0 + NLR); Model 2 (Model 0 + NLR + PLR + SII + MLR). Discriminative performance was evaluated using Harrell’s C-index (with standard error [SE]) and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves (area under the curve [AUC]) for individual inflammatory indices. All statistical analyses were performed with R software; p &lt;0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results A total of 7,103 deaths occurred, with a one-year mortality rate of 15.85%. All inflammatory indices were independently associated with one-year mortality (all p &lt;0.003). The AUC values of individual indices were modest: NLR and MLR 0.593, PLR 0.587, SII 0.573 (all poor-to-moderate range: 0.50–0.70) (Figure 1). In multivariable Cox analysis, NLR (HR 1.016, 95%CI 1.014–1.019, p &lt;0.001) and MLR (HR 1.192, 95%CI 1.160–1.224, p &lt;0.001) were the strongest predictors. The C-index was 0.663 (SE 0.0031) for Model 0, 0.682 (SE 0.0032, Δ+0.019) for Model 1, and 0.688 (SE 0.0032, Δ+0.025) for Model 2 (Figure 2). Conclusions Inflammatory indices from routine blood tests, especially NLR and MLR, independently predict one-year all-cause mortality in STEMI patients and provide significant incremental prognostic value over conventional risk factors (Δ C-index +0.025). Adding NLR alone improves risk stratification (Δ C-index +0.019). These simple, low-cost markers facilitate early risk stratification and personalized management.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Inflammatory indices significantly improve one-year mortality prediction in STEMI patients: a large-scale multi-center study

abstract: Abstract Background Residual cardiovascular risk remains high in STEMI survivors despite guideline-directed high-intensity statins, driven by persistent dyslipidaemia and low-grade inflammation. Evidence in statin-treated coronary patients suggests inflammatory residual risk may outweigh cholesterol risk, but this is poorly studied in contemporary, intensively treated STEMI cohorts. Purpose To compare the prognostic impact of residual lipid versus inflammatory risk on early events in STEMI patients on high-intensity statins. Methods We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study including 428 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI and were discharged on maximally tolerated high-intensity statin therapy between 2020 and 2025. Residual lipid profile was assessed at 3 months (LDL-C, non-HDL-C, triglycerides, apolipoprotein B); residual lipid risk was defined as LDL-C ≥55 mg/dL and/or non-HDL-C ≥85 mg/dL. Residual inflammatory risk was evaluated using high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), defined as hsCRP ≥2 mg/L or NLR in the upper tertile. Patients were categorized into four groups (no residual risk, isolated lipid risk, isolated inflammatory risk, combined risk) and followed 6–12 months for a composite endpoint of MACE, unplanned revascularization, or heart-failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression provided adjusted hazard ratios for each group. Results Of 428 STEMI patients (mean age 61±11 years, 29% women), LDL-C &lt;55 mg/dL was achieved in 177 (41.4%). Overall, 77 patients (18.0%) had no residual risk, 88 (20.6%) isolated lipid risk, 118 (27.6%) isolated inflammatory risk, and 145 (33.9%) combined residual risk. During a median follow-up of 9.2 months, 74 patients (17.3%) experienced the composite endpoint. Event rates were 6.5% (no residual risk), 10.2% (isolated lipid), 21.2% (isolated inflammatory), and 25.5% (p&lt;0.001). In multivariable analysis, isolated inflammatory risk (adjusted HR 1.82; p=0.03) and combined risk (HR 2.11; p=0.003) independently predicted events, whereas isolated lipid risk did not (HR 1.14; p=0.71). Among patients with LDL-C &lt;55 mg/dL, elevated hsCRP/NLR identified higher risk (22.4% vs 8.1%; HR 2.36; p=0.03), while LDL-C quartiles within target were not predictive (p for trend=0.48). Adding hsCRP and NLR improved discrimination (C-statistic 0.72 to 0.79; p=0.01), whereas adding LDL-C/non-HDL-C did not (p=0.45). Conclusion(s) Residual inflammatory risk was a more powerful determinant of early recurrent cardiovascular events than residual lipid risk. These data support systematic post-STEMI assessment of hsCRP and NLR and indicate that risk stratification based solely on LDL-C underestimates residual vulnerability. Our findings suggest that targeted anti-inflammatory strategies, in addition to aggressive lipid lowering, may be necessary to meaningfully reduce residual cardiovascular risk in this very-high-risk population.
title: Residual inflammatory versus lipid risk after STEMI in statin-treated patients: impact on early recurrent events

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Inflammation plays a central role in myocardial healing and ventricular remodelling after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Current post-AMI risk stratification relies predominantly on infarct severity and left ventricular function, while the prognostic significance of early temporal inflammatory changes following reperfusion remains uncertain. Purpose To determine whether early post-reperfusion inflammatory trajectories, assessed by serial neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) measurements within the first 48 hours after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), are associated with mortality and cardiovascular events. Methods The TIRANA-ACS registry prospectively enrolled 900 consecutive patients aged 18–85 years presenting with ST / non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI / NSTEMI) treated with PCI. NLR was measured at admission, 24h, and 48h and a validated cut-off of ≥4 was applied. Patients were classified into four predefined inflammatory trajectories: (1) persistently normal (&lt;4 at all times), (2) progressive activation (≥4 with rising trend), (3) resolving (≥4 with decreasing trend), and (4) biphasic (rise at 24h followed by fall at 48h). The primary endpoint was 6-month all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included in-hospital mortality, cardiovascular death, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, recurrent MI, or unplanned revascularization), and heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for prespecified clinically relevant confounders: age, STEMI presentation, peak troponin, baseline LVEF, cardiogenic shock, and CRP. Results Complete serial data were available for 892 patients (67.3±10.7 years; 23.3% female; 49.7% STEMI; median LVEF 45% [IQR 40–50]). Trajectory distribution: persistently normal 28.4%, progressive activation 18.9%, resolving 28.7%, biphasic 24.0% . Among 758 patients with follow-up, 6-month mortality was 8.7%, varying significantly across trajectories (p&lt;0.001): persistently normal 1.9%, progressive activation 18.2%, resolving 7.8%, biphasic 10.1% (Figure 1). After multivariable adjustment, progressive activation was independently associated with higher mortality versus persistently normal (adjusted OR 4.60, 95% CI 1.32–16.08; p=0.017). Resolving (adjusted OR 2.40, 95% CI 0.66–8.75; p=0.185) and biphasic (adjusted OR 2.80, 95% CI 0.78–10.04; p=0.114) trajectories were not significant. Similar trends were observed for secondary endpoints, including MACE and heart failure hospitalization. Conclusions Early post-reperfusion inflammatory trajectories, assessed by serial NLR measurements, are independently associated with 6-month mortality after AMI. Progressive inflammatory activation identifies a high-risk phenotype, indicative of impaired inflammatory resolution. Serial inflammatory assessment may facilitate early phenotypic risk stratification and guide interventions targeting residual inflammatory risk.NLR_Trajectories_6moMortality
title: Early post-reperfusion inflammatory trajectories and 6-month mortality after acute myocardial infarction: insights from the TIRANA-ACS prospective registry

abstract: Abstract Background Residual inflammatory risk predicts adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While hs-CRP≧2.0mg/L defines residual risk in Western populations, its prognostic significance in the early post-acute coronary syndrome (ACS) phase remain uncertain in East Asians, who have lower baseline inflammation. Purpose To investigate the clinical impact of residual inflammatory risk after ACS in a low inflammatory Japanese population using the Clinical Deep Data Accumulation System (CLIDAS) registry. Methods We used the CLIDAS-PCI database integrating electronic medical records from 7 cardiovascular centers. We analyzed 1555 patients who underwent PCI between April 2014 and March 2019 and had hs-CRP measured at approximately 1 month and again within 4 months after index PCI. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events plus (MACCE+), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary endpoints included each component of MACCE+, target vessel revascularization and major bleeding. Patients were stratified into 4 groups based on an hs-CRP cutoff of ≧1.5 mg/L: persistently low, elevated, reduced, and persistently high (Figure 1A). Clinical outcomes were evaluated starting4 months after index PCI. Multivariable Cox models were adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, smoking, body mass index ≥25 kg/m2, prior PCI, lipid levels, and left anterior descending artery PCI lesion. Results In this cohort, the median age was 71 years and 77% were male. Median hs-CRP levels at 1 and 4 months were 2.0 and 0.8 mg/L. Median LDL cholesterol was 94 mg/dL, BMI 23.8 kg/m², and eGFR 62 mL/min/1.73m². Over 4 years, MACCE+ occurred in approximately 10% of the study population. Persistently high hs-CRP showed a higher risk for MACCE+ compared with persistently low hs-CRP (adjusted HR: 2.00, 95% CI: 1.34-2.99, P = 0.002, Figure 1B). Subgroup analysis showed that persistently high hs-CRP was associated with a higher risk of CV death, but not myocardial infarction or stroke. Persistently high hs-CRP was also associated with a higher risk of heart failure hospitalization and major bleeding, but not target vessel revascularization (Figure 1C). Conclusion In this low inflammatory Japanese population, persistent inflammation after ACS was associated with worse cardiovascular prognosis, particularly heart failure and bleeding events, but not with myocardial infarction, stroke, or target vessel revascularization. hs-CRP may reflect systemic vulnerability rather than thrombotic risk or chronic coronary progression. Given the lower baseline hs-CRP levels in East Asians, dynamic assessment using a lower cutoff (1.5 mg/L) may better identify residual inflammatory risk and stratify post-ACS prognosis in Japanese populations.
title: Persistent inflammation after acute coronary syndrome identifies systemic vulnerability in a low inflammatory Japanese population: insights from the clinical deep data accumulation system (CLIDAS)

abstract: Abstract Background High-risk plaque (HRP) in non-culprit arteries confers future risk of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), yet plaque phenotype is dynamic and potentially modifiable with optimal medical therapy. Photon-counting coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), with superior spatial resolution compared with conventional CT, may allow improved identification and longitudinal assessment of HRP. Purpose To use serial photon-counting CCTA to 1) to determine the prevalence of HRP in patients with symptomatic CAD, 2) to define the natural history of HRP on clinician-directed care, 3) to investigate clinical factors that associate with HRP, and 4) assess whether dynamic HRP changes associate with changes in quantitative plaque burdens. Methods 100 patients underwent clinically-indicated invasive coronary angiography followed by serial photon-counting CCTA within 30 days and at 12-months as part of a prospective multicentre research study. Residual coronary lesions were analysed for the four HRP features: positive remodelling, low-attenuation plaque, spotty calcification, and napkin-ring sign (Figure 1A-D). Plaque volume quantification was performed using artificial-intelligence-enabled software (Autoplaque v3.0). Results In this high-risk cohort with median age 62 years, 85% of participants had a recent ACS and 79% underwent stenting, while 64% had residual lesions causing obstructive (≥50%) stenosis. At baseline, 94% had at least one HRP feature across the whole coronary tree and 51% at least one HRP containing ≥2 high-risk plaque characteristics in the same lesion. Conventional cardiovascular risk factors and baseline LDL-cholesterol did not differentiate patients with high-risk plaques from those without. Over follow-up, 88% of patients were on a high-intensity statin with median LDL-cholesterol reducing from 2.7 mmol/L (IQR 1.9, 3.2) to 1.4 mmol/L (IQR 1.1, 1.8). HRP prevalence did not change (51% vs 45%, P=0.40) (Figure 2A), although there was a decrease in the frequency of low-attenuation plaque (63% vs 56%, P=0.0005) (Figure 2B). Persistent HRP features were more abundant in patients who did not reach LDL-cholesterol &lt;1.4mmol/L (median number 4.5 [IQR 2.0-6.0] vs 3 [IQR 1.0-5.0], P=0.03) (Figure 2C) and remained more common in those with residual obstructive stenoses (99% vs 84%, P=0.012) (Figure 2D). HRP presence did not associate with progression of total plaque burden (Figure 2E). Serial photon-counting provided high-resolution images for tracking HRP (example in Figure 3). Conclusions HRP features are prevalent in residual plaques post-ACS. Intensive lipid-lowering is associated with a more favourable plaque-phenotype. Obstructive stenosis associates with HRP persistence. This demonstrates a need for more personalised anti-atherosclerotic treatment, and a potential role for serial photon-counting CCTA to monitor HRP morphology in patients with established CAD.picture 1picture 2
title: Serial photon-counting CCTA reveals the natural history of high-risk plaques in patients after ACS

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary vulnerable plaques are the primary pathological substrate of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) facilitates non-invasive evaluation of plaque morphology and perivascular inflammation through the fat attenuation index (FAI). However, the systematic correlation between these CCTA-derived parameters and high-risk plaque (HRP) characteristics defined by high-resolution intracoronary optical coherence tomography (OCT) remains unclear. Objectives This study aims to assess the correlation between CCTA-derived plaque characteristics, FAI, and OCT-defined HRP. Methods Patients with non-ST-segment elevation ACS (NSTE-ACS) who underwent CCTA within one month before OCT examination were consecutively enrolled. The final cohort included 165 patients (262 plaques). Plaque characteristics on CCTA, including low-attenuation plaque (LAP), positive remodeling (PR), napkin-ring sign (NRS), spotty calcification (SC), and the FAI were assessed. OCT served as the reference standard for identifying HRP features, such as thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFAs) or plaque rupture. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to determine independent predictors of OCT-defined HRP, with diagnostic performance examined through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results Compared to non-HRP lesions, OCT-defined HRP lesions demonstrated a markedly elevated prevalence of LAP (53.8% vs. 33.1%, P &lt; 0.001), NRS (48.7% vs. 26.2%, P &lt; 0.001), and SC (35.0% vs. 22.8%, P = 0.028) on CCTA. These lesions also showed greater total plaque volume, non-calcified plaque volume, fibrous plaque volume, and fibrofatty plaque volume (P &lt; 0.05). The FAI was notably higher in HRP lesions (-70.8±0.7 vs. -74.9±0.6, P &lt; 0.001). Multivariable analysis revealed LAP (OR = 2.068, 95%CI:1.215-3.519, P = 0.007), FAI (OR = 1.069, 95%CI:1.030-1.109, P &lt; 0.001), and fibrous plaque volume (OR = 1.025, 95%CI:1.009-1.042, P = 0.002) as independent predictors of OCT-defined HRP. The combination of these three parameters yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.705 (P &lt; 0.001) for diagnosing OCT-HRP. In the TCFA with plaque rupture subgroup, LAP (OR = 6.628, 95%CI:2.067-21.255, P = 0.001), PR (OR = 2.897, 95%CI:1.011-8.302, P = 0.048), and FAI (OR = 1.091, 95%CI:1.012-1.177, P = 0.023) were independent predictors, and their combined use yielded an AUC of 0.842 (P &lt; 0.001). Conclusions CCTA-derived plaque characteristics and FAI show significant associations with OCT-defined vulnerable plaques. The integrated use of these parameters enhances diagnostic accuracy for identifying OCT-HRP, particularly the very-high-risk phenotype of TCFA with plaque rupture. Multi-parametric CCTA assessment provides a robust imaging foundation for non-invasive risk stratification and precision management of individuals with coronary artery disease.
title: Fat attenuation index and plaque characteristics on coronary computed tomography angiography correlation with high-risk plaques identified by optical coherence tomography

abstract: Abstract Background Recent advances with artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled rapid and accurate non-invasive plaque quantification and characterization from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). AI-guided quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) is a novel AI-based software solution with approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. However, the characteristics of future culprit-lesions according to AI-QCT are unknown. Objectives We aimed to determine the characteristics of future culprit-lesions according to AI-QCT and to derive and validate cut-offs to predict future acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Methods Two independent cohorts from two tertiary care centers in Europe were analyzed by AI-QCT on lesion-level; 2148 patients for derivation and 568 patients for validation. The median follow-up duration was 6.8 years. AI-QCT plaque characteristics of future ACS culprit-lesions were assessed in the derivation cohort, and lesion-level plaque volume thresholds were derived to predict future culprit-lesions. These thresholds were then tested for their prognostic value for patient-level ACS in the derivation and validation cohort. Results 72/79 (91%) culprit-lesions had a matching lesion on index CCTA. Culprit (N=72) vs. non-culprit lesions (N=657) of ACS patients and vs. lesions from non-ACS patients (N=13’046) demonstrated markedly higher median total plaque volume (TPV) (106 vs. 16 vs. 10 mm3), non-calcified plaque volume (NCPV) (65 vs. 10 vs. 8 mm3), and calcified plaque volume (CPV) (24 vs. 3 vs. 1 mm3) (p&lt;0.001 for all) (Figure 1). They depicted ≥50% stenosis in 30.6% vs. 12.8% vs. 6.1% (p≤0.003) and low-attenuation plaque in 30.6% vs. 9.0% vs. 6.5% (p&lt;0.001). Thresholds of TPV ≥54.65 mm3 (area under the curve (AUC) 0.80) and NCPV ≥32.15 mm3 (AUC 0.80) were derived to predict future ACS culprit-lesions with similar performance (p=0.971), while both outperformed CPV in ACS prediction (AUC 0.74, p≤0.049). TPV ≥54.65 mm3 (derivation: HRadj 3.73, 95% CI 1.87-7.43, p&lt;0.001; validation: HRadj 10.56, 95% CI 2.42-45.97, p=0.002) or NCPV ≥32.15 mm3 (derivation: HRadj 5.10, 95% CI 2.25-11.49, p&lt;0.001 (Figure 2 A/B); validation: HRadj 8.27, 95% CI 1.89-36.12, p=0.005 (Figure 2 C/D)) were associated with significantly higher rates of patient-level ACS in the derivation and validation cohort. Conclusions 91% of future culprit-lesions had a matching lesion on index CCTA by AI-QCT. Future culprit-lesions vs. non-culprit lesions demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes of all types, were non-obstructive in 69% and had low-attenuation plaque in 30%. Thresholds of TPV ≥54.65 mm3 and NCPV ≥32.15 mm3 were derived and associated with increased rates of ACS in two independent cohorts.Figure 1.Stenosis and plaque volumesFigure 2.Kaplan Meier Curves
title: Characteristics and thresholds of coronary lesions to predict acute coronary syndrome from artificial intelligence-guided coronary computed tomography angiography

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) increased the risk of cardiovascular events and atherosclerotic disease. More than 10% of the population has isolated lipoprotein(a) elevation in the absence of hypercholesterolemia. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the coronary plaque features in patients with isolated lipoprotein(a) elevation by using optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging. Methods This single-center, observational study included 827 patients with acute coronary syndrome and without hypercholesterolemia who underwent OCT imaging during coronary intervention. Baseline serum samples were obtained and the level of lipoprotein(a) was measured. Patients were divided into the elevated Lp(a) group (Lp(a) ≥75nmol/L, n=124, 15.0%) and the normal Lp(a) group (Lp(a) &lt;75nmol/L, n=703, 85.0%). Coronary plaque features were analyzed by using OCT. Results The average age of all patients was 57.6±10.7 years, with 74.1% of male. A total of 827 culprit lesions and 3285 non-culprit lesions were measured. In culprit lesion, the prevalence of plaque rupture (60.5% vs. 50.1%, P=0.032) and thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA, 59.7% vs. 46.2%, P=0.006) was significantly higher in the elevated Lp(a) group than the normal Lp(a) group. The elevated Lp(a) group also had thinner fibrous cap (56.7 [40.0, 76.7]μm vs. 61.6 [46.7, 90.8]μm, P=0.013). As for non-culprit segments, patients with elevated Lp(a) levels had more prevalent TCFA (38.7% vs. 26.3%, P=0.005). Similar findings were also found at the lesion-level analyses. Non-culprit lesions in the elevated Lp(a) group presented with a higher incidence of TCFA (13.5% vs. 9.7%, P=0.022), and they also had a smaller minimal lumen area (3.9 [2.5, 5.3]mm2 vs. 4.0 [2.6, 5.9] mm2, P=0.015) and thinner fibrous cap (95.0[70.0,123.3]μm vs. 100.0 [73.3,136.7]μm, P=0.025). Multivariate analysis showed Lp(a) ≥75nmol/L was independently associated with culprit TCFA (adjusted odds ratio [95%CI]: 1.87 [1.19 - 2.93], P=0.006) and non-culprit TCFA (adjusted OR [95%CI]: 1.91 [1.19- 3.05], P=0.005). Conclusion In patients with acute coronary syndrome and without hypercholesterolemia, elevated lipoprotein(a) levels are independently associated with a higher prevalence of high-risk coronary plaques in both culprit and non-culprit lesions. These findings highlight the prognostic value of Lp(a) for identifying vulnerable coronary plaque even in the absence of elevated LDL-C or hypercholesterolemia, supporting the role of Lp(a) as an independent risk marker for coronary vulnerability in this population.Figure
title: Does lipoprotein(a) associate with coronary high-risk plaque in patients without hypercholesterolemia? Insights from optical coherence tomography imaging

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndromes (ACS) caused by atherosclerotic plaque rupture show a well-established morning peak in incidence, attributed to circadian fluctuations in sympathetic activity, blood pressure, and platelet reactivity.1 Whether spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) exhibits a comparable circadian pattern remains unclear. Objectives To characterize the circadian distribution of symptom onset in SCAD and to explore differences in clinical, trigger-related, and angiographic characteristics across time-of-day intervals. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 195 consecutive SCAD patients included in our institutional registry. Time of symptom onset, or first medical contact when onset was unavailable, was categorized into four 6-hour intervals: night (00:00–05:59), morning (06:00–11:59), afternoon (12:00–17:59), and evening (18:00–23:59). Trigger type was classified as emotional, physical, intense Valsalva, pregnancy, labor and delivery, hormone modulators, or none/unclear. Baseline characteristics, trigger distribution, and angiographic presentation were compared across time bins using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests, as appropriate. Results Among 195 patients with SCAD, the circadian distribution demonstrated a bimodal pattern. Events occurred during the night in 12% (n=23) patients, in the morning in 35% (n=69), in the afternoon in 28% (n=54), and in the evening in 25% (n=49). Rather than a single morning predominance, SCAD showed two peaks, occurring in the late morning/early afternoon and in the evening. Smoking status differed significantly across time intervals, with a higher proportion of current smokers among patients presenting in the afternoon (30%) compared with the night (4%), morning (9%), and evening (14%) (p = 0.020). Trigger type did not vary significantly between time bins. Fibromuscular dysplasia was more frequently observed in patients presenting in the evening (31%) compared with the night (13%), morning (27%), and afternoon (11%) (p = 0.032). SCAD type 1 was more prevalent in patients presenting during the night (17%) and evening (12%) compared with the morning (3%) and afternoon (4%) (p = 0.039). Conclusions In contrast to the established morning predominance of atherosclerotic ACS1, SCAD in this cohort showed a distinct bimodal circadian distribution. These findings support the concept that SCAD follows distinct temporal and potentially pathophysiological patterns, which may have implications for disease characterization and future research into tailored management strategies.SCAD onset during a 24-hour period
title: Circadian patterns of symptom onset in spontaneous coronary artery dissection

abstract: Abstract Background and Purpose Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is frequently associated with fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), two predominantly female arteriopathies often diagnosed in middle-aged women. However, the reported overlap between SCAD and FMD varies widely (11–86%), and data regarding the prognostic impact of FMD on outcomes after SCAD remain inconsistent. Therefore, we aimed to assess the prevalence of FMD and its association with clinical outcomes following SCAD in a large prospective study. Methods We analyzed SCAD patients who had complete angiographic data, at least one follow-up visit and a complete FMD screening. FMD was defined according to American Heart Association criteria as multifocal disease with a “string-of-beads” appearance in at least one extracoronary vascular bed. The primary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) including death, recurrent myocardial infarction, stroke and heart failure hospitalisation. Results Of 1,114 patients with SCAD, 456 patients (40.9%) had FMD in at least one vascular bed. Patients with FMD were significantly older than those without FMD (median age 54 vs. 51 years; p &lt; 0.001) and had a higher prevalence of hypertension (37.5% vs. 31.2%; p=0.036). In addition, the proportion of women was significantly higher in the FMD group compared with the non-FMD group (95.6% vs. 86.6%; p &lt; 0.001). Patients with FMD exhibited a significantly higher incidence of MACE over a 3-years compared to patients without FMD (14.9% vs. 10.3%; log-rank p = 0.023). Considering the substantial proportion of early events, a landmark analysis was conducted: During the early post-SCAD phase, the incidence of MACE was comparable between groups (log-rank p = 0.261). However, beyond the 10-day landmark, patients with FMD demonstrated a significantly higher event rate than those without FMD (7.8% vs. 4.7%; log-rank p = 0.033) (Figure 1). After multivariable adjustment the presence of FMD remained an independent predictor of MACE at 3 years (hazard ratio [HR] 1.55; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08–2.21; p = 0.016). Conclusion FMD is present in approximately 40% of patients with SCAD and an independent predictor of MACE at 3 years. These findings highlight the importance of systematic FMD screening and long-term surveillance in this high-risk subgroup.Figure 1
title: Impact of fibromuscular dysplasia on early and late clinical outcome in patients with spontaneous coronary artery dissection

abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a rare but significant cause of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), particularly in younger women without traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The pathophysiology involves the development of an intramural hematoma or an intimal tear within the coronary artery, leading to luminal narrowing, impaired blood flow, and myocardial ischemia. The exact etiology of SCAD remains unclear, but various triggers have been identified that may contribute to its onset. Purpose The present abstract aims to explore the potential triggers associated with SCAD, including physical and emotional factors. Methods Patients were enrolled both prospectively and retrospectively from a multicentre registry comprising 10 centres across six countries. SCAD was diagnosed and angiographically classified according to the criteria proposed by Saw et al. All coronary angiograms were independently reviewed by two experienced interventional cardiologists. Information regarding potential precipitating events prior to symptom onset was systematically collected. For the purpose of this analysis, triggers were categorized as emotional or physical and further subclassified according to their nature. Results A total of 289 patients were included in this study, with a median age of 51 years (range: 43 to 59 years). Of the 289 patients, 226 (78%) were female. Among these patients, 162 (56%) reported experiencing either an emotional or physical stressful event prior to the SCAD event. Twenty patients (7%) reported both an emotional and physical stressful event. Regarding physical stressors, 29 patients (10%) identified an isometric exercise or Valsalva maneuver performed immediately before the event, 18 patients (6%) reported a hypertensive crisis, and 14 patients (5%) were engaged in endurance exercise. Other contributing factors included neurological disorders, exogenous hormones, and pregnancy-related causes. For emotional stressors, 23 patients (8%) reported stress related to financial or employment problems, 11 patients (4%) cited highly frustrating or anger-inducing events, and 9 patients (3%) experienced acute anxiety or depression. Other emotional triggers included positive events ("happy SCAD"), grief/loss, and interpersonal conflicts. The most frequent combined triggers were work- or financial-related stress together with physical exertion (n=8), while one patient experienced a happy SCAD in combination with a physical trigger. Conclusions SCAD is frequently preceded by identifiable triggers, with emotional and physical stressors playing a substantial role in its onset. Emotional stress, particularly financial or work-related concerns, along with physical exertion and hypertensive episodes, were the most commonly reported precipitants. Understanding these triggers may help identify at-risk individuals and aid in developing prevention strategies.Table 1.
title: Triggers in patients with spontaneous coronary artery dissection

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve devices are manufactured to a nominal geometry, yet deployment within a patient-specific annulus and aortic root can alter frame morphology. However, systematically acquired post-implant cardiac CT datasets after TAVI are uncommon, and consequently only limited published data exist that quantitatively characterize real-world, in vivo valve geometry after implantation. Leveraging a structured post-implant CT cohort, we quantified the difference between manufacturer-derived valve volume and in vivo post-implant valve volume using STL-based volumetric analysis from CT reconstructions. Purpose To compare post-implant CT-derived segmented valve volume with nominal factory valve volume and quantify the magnitude, direction, and variability of volumetric deviation in vivo. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 75 patients who underwent post-implant cardiac CT. Three-dimensional valve models were reconstructed from CT DICOM datasets using dedicated cardiovascular imaging software, exported as STL meshes, and valve volumes were computed in mm³. These in vivo volumes were compared with the corresponding manufacturer (factory) valve volumes for each valve size. We evaluated signed and absolute volume differences and summarized relative (%) change. Paired testing assessed whether mean signed differences differed from zero. Results Among 75 patients, segmented valve volume exceeded factory volume in 61 (81.3%), was lower in 13 (17.3%), and was identical in 1 (1.3%). Mean segmented valve volume was 2060.0 mm³ versus 1649.6 mm³ for factory volume. Mean signed difference was +410.4 mm³ (95% CI 311.4–509.3; p&lt;0.001). Mean absolute difference was 470.5 mm³, with a median of 401 mm³ and a range of 0–1629 mm³. Mean relative change was +25.9% (median +23.1%). Absolute deviation was substantial across all nominal valve sizes, while proportional change was greatest in smaller valves, with mean relative increases of 35.1% for ~1243 mm³ valves, 25.7% for ~1569 mm³ valves, and 20.2% for ~1977 mm³ valves. Conclusions Post-implant CT demonstrates frequent and quantitatively substantial divergence between nominal factory valve volume and in vivo segmented valve volume after TAVI, most often in the direction of expansion. Smaller nominal valves show the greatest proportional change. CT-based volumetry may provide a practical framework for understanding post-deployment valve geometry in real-world patientsSegmented ValvesSegmented Valves on Factory Valves
title: Post-implant CT volumetry shows frequent divergence between segmented and nominal factory valve volume after TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Inflammatory cell infiltration represents a fundamental pathological mechanism that contributes to adverse ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) participates in processes including inflammation and apoptosis and is linked to a variety of cardiovascular diseases. Inclisiran, a small interfering RNA drug specifically targeting PCSK9, is currently employed for lipid-lowering therapy. Nevertheless, its function in myocardial I/R injury still awaits clarification. Objective This study aims to explore the role of Inclisiran in myocardial I/R injury and cardiac remodeling, and to clarify the molecular mechanism by which Inclisiran alleviates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury through regulating the M1 differentiation of macrophages, thereby providing new measures for the clinical prevention and treatment of myocardial I/R injury. Methods A myocardial ischemia/reperfusion model was established by ligating the left anterior descending coronary artery of mice. Echocardiography, laser speckle contrast imaging and TTC/Evans Blue staining were used to evaluate the cardiac function of mice. The degree of myocardial inflammation and apoptosis was assessed by histopathological staining, quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blot. ChIP-seq, ChIP-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assay were used to verify the interaction between HIF-1α and Myo1d. Results Inclisiran attenuates I/R-induced cardiac dysfunction, reduced blood perfusion, increased infarct size, and myocardial cell inflammation and apoptosis. Mechanistically, Inclisiran reduces the M1 differentiation of macrophages by down-regulating the expression of HIF-1α and Myo1d, thereby alleviating myocardial I/R injury. Conclusion Inclisiran alleviates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury through blocking HIF-1α/Myo1d-mediated M1 differentiation of macrophages. To provide experimental evidence for the diagnosis of clinical myocardial I/R injury and the screening of new therapeutic targets.
title: Inclisiran alleviates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury by blocking the HIF-1a/Myo1d-mediated M1 differentiation of macrophages

abstract: Abstract Aims Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) has demonstrated cardioprotective effects in an ex vivo model of myocardial ischaemia, but its effects in vivo during ischaemia-reperfusion injury remain unclear. This study assessed suPAR’s therapeutic potential in a small animal model of myocardial infarction (MI) with ischaemia-reperfusion. Methods A left anterior descending coronary artery occlusion for 60 minutes was conducted on 10–12-week-old Sprague-Dawley rats, followed by reperfusion, and recovery to 2 days post-MI. Animals were randomised to receive suPAR or saline via intravenous bolus injection 5 minutes before reperfusion. Cardiac function was assessed at baseline pre-MI and again at 48 hours post-MI using transthoracic echocardiography (Phillips, iE33). Myocardial injury was quantified by serial cardiac troponin I at 4-, 24- and 48 hours (Abbott) and endpoint high-sensitivity Troponin T (Roche). At termination, cardiac tissue was harvested, formalin-fixed, and sectioned into the basal, mid-cavity, apical and apex regions. Histology of infarct size and immune infiltration was conducted using haematoxylin and eosin staining with subsequent quantification using a colour-based semi-automated algorithm, and apoptosis by TUNEL. Results At 48 hours post-MI, rats treated with suPAR (n=16) demonstrated markedly preserved cardiac function compared with controls (n=16). suPAR-treated animals showed significantly higher left ventricular ejection fraction (p=0.02), fractional shortening (p=0.005), and stroke volume (p=0.03). Cardiac troponin concentrations were substantially lower in the suPAR group, with reductions of 58% in serial sampling and 70% at endpoint (p=0.0003) (i.e. mean hscTnT= 400 ng/L (95%CI: 250-540) in the suPAR group versus 1320 ng/L (840-1800) in controls). Histological assessment confirmed a 76% mean reduction in infarcted area at the apex and a 57% reduction across the apical region (p=0.04). Immune cell infiltration surrounding infarcted tissue decreased by at least 30% (p=0.03), and TUNEL-positive cells were reduced by more than 50% in suPAR-treated hearts (p=0.01). Conclusion Our study reveals the first evidence of suPAR’s cardioprotection in vivo MI, reducing myocardial injury, preserving cardiac function, decreasing inflammatory response and cell death. These findings support suPAR as a promising therapeutic candidate for ischemic heart disease and warrant further ongoing research.
title: Cardioprotection by soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) in an in vivo model of myocardial infarction with ischaemia-reperfusion

abstract: Abstract Background Despite primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), up to 60% of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients experience the no-reflow phenomenon driven by ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury1-2. AXL is a prominent member of the TAM (Tyro3, Axl, MerTK) receptor tyrosine kinases family. With its strong kinase activity, AXL regulates cell fate by directly phosphorylating downstream targets. However, the precise function and underlying mechanisms of AXL in vascular endothelial cells during I/R injury remain elusive3. Aims We aim to investigate the role of AXL in cardiac microvascular reperfusion injury, specifically focusing on its regulation of intracellular calcium homeostasis and ferroptosis in endothelial cells. Method Bulk mRNA sequencing was performed on mouse heart tissues and primary endothelial cells to identify transcriptomic changes at various reperfusion time points. These results were then integrated with clinical data from patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and a re-analysis of single-cell datasets from mouse and human hearts. Endothelial cell (EC) specific conditional AXL knockout mice and mice treated with AXL degrader were subjected to cardiac ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. Downstream interacting proteins of AXL were identified using immunoprecipitation-liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (IP-LC-MS). Results The expression of AXL was significantly downregulated in endothelial cells following cardiac I/R injury(Fig.1A-C,E-F). Linear correlation analysis demonstrated that AXL was negatively correlated with the extent of myocardial fibrosis(Fig.1D). Endothelial-specific knockout of AXL or treatment of an AXL degrader reduced microvascular perfusion and expanded the no-reflow area and infarction sizes in the acute phase, and aggravated cardiac fibrosis and cardiac dysfunction in the long-run(Fig.1G-L). KEGG enrichment analysis of DEGs between AXL-positive (AXL+) and AXL-negative (AXL-) endothelial cells identified calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis as significantly enriched pathological processes in the MI group(Fig.2 A).Deficiency of AXL in HCMECs leads to severe calcium overload and ferroptosis after OGD.R injury(Fig.2 C-G). Mechanistically, AXL directly bound to and inhibited ITPR3, thereby restoring mitochondrial calcium and iron homeostasis and ultimately attenuating endothelial ferroptosis(Fig.2 H-I). Conclusion In conclusion, we reveal the protective role and molecular mechanism of AXL in maintaining endothelial homeostasis after I/R injury. Our study suggests that for cardiovascular diseases characterized by mitochondrial calcium and iron overload, targeting endothelial AXL may be a valuable strategy.
title: Axl improves cardiac microvascular injury via mitochondrial Ca2+ and Fe2+ homeostasis in cardiac ischemia-reperfusion injury

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac power (CP), calculated from mean arterial pressure and cardiac output, reflects global cardiac pumping capability. Its prognostic role in relation to infarct-related artery and contemporary echocardiographic parameters after acute myocardial infarction (MI) remains incompletely defined. Purpose To determine whether early post-revascularization CP predicts left ventricular (LV) dysfunction and adverse clinical outcomes at 6 months following acute MI. Methods In this prospective study, 99 consecutive patients with acute MI undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were enrolled. CP was measured 24–48 hours post-procedure. LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were assessed by transthoracic echocardiography. Patients were followed for 6 months. The primary adverse outcome was a composite of “Very low” or “Bad” clinical status at 3 or 6 months, based on a pre-specified scale integrating symptoms, functional class, and echocardiographic findings. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, Killip class, and time to revascularization. Discriminative performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results Patients with left anterior descending (LAD) culprit artery had lower CP compared with non-LAD infarctions (0.76±0.19 vs 0.91±0.24 W, p&lt;0.001). CP correlated with LVEF (r=0.59, p&lt;0.001) and GLS (r=0.64, p&lt;0.001). CP remained independently associated with LVEF (β=2.3 per 0.1 W, p&lt;0.001) and GLS (β=−0.8 per 0.1 W, p&lt;0.001). Eighteen patients (18.2%) experienced adverse outcomes and had lower baseline CP than event-free patients (0.62±0.15 vs 0.86±0.21 W, p&lt;0.001). CP independently predicted adverse outcomes (OR 0.68 per 0.1 W, p&lt;0.001). ROC analysis showed AUC 0.82 for predicting LVEF &lt;40% and 0.80 for adverse outcomes. CP improved from baseline to 6 months (0.82±0.23 to 0.90±0.20 W, p&lt;0.001), with attenuated recovery in patients with adverse outcomes (interaction p=0.04). Conclusions Early cardiac power measurement after acute MI independently predicts LV dysfunction and 6-month adverse clinical outcomes. CP provides integrated hemodynamic information beyond conventional parameters and may assist in early risk stratification.CP Correlation with Key VariablesMultivariable Predictors
title: Cardiac power as an integrative hemodynamic marker of risk stratification and ventricular dysfunction following acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Abstract Despite advances in contemporary treatment strategies, patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) continue to face a substantial risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Early identification of patients with high risk of adverse cardiac remodeling (ACR) remains a major clinical challenge as post-infarction ACR drives heart failure progression and increases long-term mortality. Aim to assess left ventricular (LV) mechanical dispersion (MD) and global longitudinal strain (GLS) as predictive markers of ACR in patients with STEMI after successful revascularization after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) over a 12-months period. Materials and Methods Patients with acute STEMI who had no prior MI, no arrhythmias and no severe comorbidities were included. A total of 119 STEMI patients were enrolled. Clinical, hemodynamic, ECG and echocardiographic including Doppler and speckle-tracking markers were assessed in the acute phase and at 12 months post-event. Blood biomarker levels were measured at baseline. ACR was defined as an increase in LV end-systolic and/or end-diastolic volumes &gt;10% at 12 months. Results Among 119 patients after STEMI with successful revascularization, TIMI III the majority were men (88.2%) with a mean age of 59 years. Patients were stratified into four groups according to MD levels. Univariate regression analysis identified the GRACE score, NT-proBNP, Troponin I levels, LV ejection fraction (LVEF), LV GLS, and LV MD as predictive markers of ACR in 1-year follow-up period. Multivariate regression analysis showed that GLS &gt;–8%, high LV MD quartile, and NT-proBNP &gt;953 pg/mL remained independent predictors of ACR. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that all three predictive models based on LV MD (AUC=0.84, p&lt;0.001; sensitivity 80.8%, specificity 87.5%), LV GLS (AUC=0.62; p&lt;0.001; sensitivity 82.0%, specificity 66.7%), and NT-proBNP (AUC=0.60, p&lt;0.001; sensitivity 78.2%, specificity 73.5%) significantly differed from the baseline model allowing identification of high-risk post-infarction patients. Adding LV MD to the baseline predictive model (NT-proBNP &gt;953 pg/mL) significantly improved model discrimination (AUC 0.84 [0.72–0.90], p=0.001; NRI Median 95% CI =0.54, p=0.018; IDI Median 95% CI =0.53, p=0.042), whereas adding LV GLS did not enrich the predictive model either alone (AUC 0.62 [0.58–0.69], p=0.49; NRI Median 95% CI =0.30, p=0.25; IDI Median 95% CI=0.04, p=0.62) or when combined with all parameters (AUC 0.83 [0.73–0.91], p=0.001; NRI Median 95% CI =0.52, p=0.02; IDI Median 95% CI=0.052, p=0.044). Thus, LV MD proved to be an independent prognostic factor for ACR significantly improving predictive accuracy when applied. Conclusion Our study demonstrated that LV GLS and LV MD were the most independent markers of ACR. Measurement of the markers in the acute phase of STEMI may be useful for identifying patients at high risk of ACR during 12 months of follow-up.
title: Early echocardiographic markers of adverse left ventricular remodeling in STEMI patients: mechanical dispersion and global longitudinal strain

abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the effect of effect of Sodium–Glucose Co-Transporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors on left atrial (LA) deformation and heart failure biomarkers in patients with Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and diabetes mellitus (DM) Methods This prospective, case-control, single-center study enrolled 50 diabetic patients with recent ACS (&lt;14 days). Participants were randomized into SGLT2i (empagliflozin/ dapagliflozin, n=25) and control (n=25) group. Echocardiographic parameters including LA strain by speckle-tracking echocardiography and NT-proBNP levels were assessed at baseline and 3 months. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. At 3-month follow-up, SGLT2i group demonstrated significant improvement in LA reservoir (29.08±7.23% to 33.36±6.45%, p&lt;0.001), contractile strain (-17.16±5.27% to -19.88±5.41%, p=0.002), and conduit strain in 4-chamber view (-13.12±4.75% to -14.56±3.96%, p=0.007). Left ventricular systolic and diastolic functions also improved, with significant increases in LVEF (49.9% to 51.9%, p&lt;0.001), reductions in E/e′ and LVESV, and enhanced GLS. NT-proBNP decreased markedly in the SGLT2i group (5541.6±8443.5 to 1179.6±1644.6 pg/ml, p=0.004). In the control group, only modest improvements in selected parameters were noted. Conclusions Early initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors in post-ACS diabetic patients significantly improved LA strain, LV remodelling and NT-proBNP, suggesting favourable cardiac reverse remodelling. These findings support the early incorporation of SGLT2i in secondary prevention strategies post-ACS, though larger trials with long-term outcomes are warranted.central illustration
title: Effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on left atrial strain in patients of acute coronary syndrome and diabetes mellitus

abstract: Abstract Background It is increasingly recognized that patients might suffer from acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in the absence of standard modifiable risk factors (SMuRFs). Their treatment remains empirical. Purpose We examined the impact of SMuRF-less status on in-hospital management and long term outcomes. Methods CALLINICUS-Hellas Registry is an observational prospective study evaluating the adherence to lipid-lowering therapy among ACS patients. Two groups were created according to SMuRF status. The presence of diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolaemia, hypertension or smoking history (either previously known or newly detected) was necessary to include the patient in the SMuRF group, while when all of them were absent; patients were classified as SMuRF-less. The patients were followed for 12 months after hospital discharge and the study’s endpoints were myocardial reinfarction or/and cardiac death. Results A total of 2718 consecutive patients with ACS were included and 68 cases (2.5%) were SMuRF-less. LDL-cholesterol [90 (74-104) mg/dl vs 114 (83-144) mg/dl , p&lt;0.001], triglycerides [114 (83-144) mg/dl vs 124 (91-169) mg/dl , p=0.02] and waist circumference [97 (90-105) cm vs 101 (93-110) cm, p=0.03] were higher among patients with SMuRFs. SMuRF-less patients were more likely to have one vessel (63% vs 49%, p=0.01) or non-obstructive coronary artery disease (13% vs 4%, p=0.001) and less likely to receive reperfusion (78% vs 88%, p=0.01) or dual antiplatelet therapy (88% vs 96%, p=0.006). B-blockers and ACEi/ARB were equally prescribed between groups, yet patients with SMuRFs were more likely to receive ezetimibe combined with high intensity statins at discharge (31% vs 58%, p&lt;0.001). SMuRF-less patients were more likely to attain lower LDL-cholesterol levels after 12 months of follow up [48 (36-61) mg/dl vs 57 (45-71) mg/dl, p=0.01) and to achieve values below 55 mg/dl (64% vs 45%, p=0.006). Nevertheless, myocardial reinfarction (4/68 vs 76/2650, Log Rank test p=0.223) and cardiac death rates (0/68 vs 47/2650, Log Rank test p=0.352) did not differ between groups. Conclusions SMuRF-less status is associated with treatment inequalities among contemporary ACS patients and the absence of SMuRFs does not dictate benign prognosis.Figure 1
title: Treatment differences and outcomes among myocardial infarction patients without standard modifiable risk factors: Data from CALLINICUS-Hellas Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Young patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) represent a distinct clinical population with a substantial residual risk of recurrent ischemic events despite contemporary therapies and guideline-directed management. Traditional risk models are primarily derived from older populations and may not adequately capture the interplay between cardiac dysfunction and systemic stress in younger individuals. Biomarkers reflecting integrated cardiorenal stress may provide additional prognostic insights and improve individualized risk stratification. Purpose To investigate whether cardiorenal stress phenotyping using the log-transformed blood urea nitrogen to left ventricular ejection fraction ratio (log[BUN/EF]) provides incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical risk factors for predicting recurrent ischemic events in a young ACS population beyond conventional clinical risk factors. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 672 consecutive patients presenting with ACS. A baseline clinical model incorporating age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, smoking status, clinical presentation, and multivessel diseases was developed. The incremental value of log(BUN/EF) was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, net reclassification improvement, integrated discrimination improvement, calibration metrics, and decision curve analysis to evaluate clinical utility. Median follow-up was 3.5 years (IQR 2.0–4.7 years). Results During follow-up, 50 patients (7.4%) experienced recurrent ischemic events. Addition of log(BUN/EF) significantly improved model discrimination, increasing the area under the curve from 0.78 to 0.84 (ΔAUC +0.056; p=0.0005). Continuous net reclassification improvement was 0.65 (95% CI 0.37–0.91; p&lt;0.001), and the integrated discrimination improvement was 0.063 (95% CI 0.03–0.09; p&lt;0.001). The calibration remained robust with a calibration slope near unity and a lower Brier score (0.060 vs 0.064), indicating a reduced prediction error. Decision curve analysis demonstrated higher net clinical benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities, supporting the clinical relevance of incorporating log(BUN/EF) into the risk assessment. Conclusions Cardiorenal stress phenotyping using log(BUN/EF), a simple and widely available biomarker integrating renal function and ventricular performance, provides significant incremental prognostic information beyond traditional risk factors and may enhance individualized risk stratification in young patients with ACS.tablesfigures
title: Cardiorenal stress phenotyping using the log-transformed bun-to-ejection fraction ratio improves prediction of recurrent ischemic events in young patients with acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Standard modifiable risk factors (SMuRFs), including hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes, and smoking, contribute substantially to atherosclerosis. However, patients with SMuRF-less remain at risk of mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The mechanisms underlying this risk are not well understood. Purpose This study aimed to identify clinical pathways mediating short- and long-term mortality among SMuRF-less patients undergoing PCI. Methods Data from a multicenter Thai PCI registry was used including patients who underwent PCI at 39 cardiac centers between 2018-2019. Patients with prior coronary artery syndromes were excluded. Clinical data, procedural characteristics, medication use during PCI and at discharge, and outcomes (in-hospital and 1-year-death) were collected. Mediation analyses were performed using generalized structural equation modeling to assess indirect effects of SMuRF-less on death through STEMI presentation, antiplatelet therapy, procedural complications, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT: RAAS, beta-blocker and statins). Results Among 12,190 eligible patients, 684 (5.6%) were SMuRF-less. In-hospital death was significantly higher in SMuRF-less than at-least-one SMuRF (5.6% vs 3.5%). After adjusting covariates, SMuRF-less was significantly higher odds of death [OR = 1.70 (95% CI: (1.31, 2.23)]. STEMI significantly mediated this association [indirect OR = 1.33 (1.20, 1.88)], whereas mediation through clopidogrel and procedural complication was minimal. Among hospital survivors, SMuRF-less was not significantly associated with 1-year death [OR= 0.96 (0.66, 1.25)]; however, lower use of RAAS blockade [OR = 1.29 (1.16, 1.45)], beta-blocker[OR=1.05 (1.01, 1.12)] and statins [OR = 1.38 (1.10, 1.76)] significantly mediated increased 1-year-death. Conclusion Early mortality among SMuRF-less patients undergoing PCI is largely driven by STEMI presentation, whereas long-term risk is influence by underuse of secondary prevention therapies. Ensuring equitable GDMTs is essential to improving outcomes in this population.
title: In-hospital and 1-year mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients without standard modifiable risk factors: a mediation analysis from Thai PCI registry

abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute myocardial injury is defined by cardiac troponin (cTn) levels above the 99th percentile with a dynamic rise/fall pattern (Δ), usually suggesting acute coronary syndrome (ACS) when associated with compatible symptoms. Patients presenting with chest pain, elevated cTn and a flat curve (Δ&lt;20%) represent a diagnostic challenge, as current guidelines do not associate this pattern with ACS. Early prognosis has been described, but the temporal evolution of risk and the adequacy of initial clinical management remain uncertain. We aimed to assess 12-month outcomes according to initial management strategy: admission in cardiology, admission in other departments or discharge from emergency department. Methods We prospectively analyzed 753 consecutive patients with suspected ACS and a cTn-flat-curve (Δ&lt;20% in two high-sensitivity cTn-T determinations at 0 and 3 hours) between May 2023 and January 2026. Management decisions were based on comprehensive clinical evaluation. Six- and twelve-month follow-up assessed mortality, other major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and re-admissions. Results Mean age was 75.7±11.9 years and 63.3% were male. ACS was diagnosed predominantly in patients admitted to cardiology. Six-month follow-up was available in 614 patients and 12-month follow-up in 484 patients. At 12 months, patients admitted to non-cardiology departments showed the highest mortality (29.5%) and MACE rate (39%), largely driven by non-cardiovascular causes. Patients admitted to cardiology had intermediate event rates, whereas discharged patients maintained low mortality (7.5%) throughout follow-up, although they were not event-free. Kaplan–Meier curves demonstrated early and persistent separation between management groups, confirming distinct risk trajectories over time (Figure 1). Conclusions In patients with a cTn-flat-curve, risk extends beyond the early phase and differs markedly according to initial management. The sustained separation of survival curves supports the prognostic relevance of clinical decision-making. Importantly, the low long-term mortality among discharged patients validates the safety of careful, clinically guided risk stratification in this heterogeneous population.Table 1Figure 1:Kaplan-Meier curves
authors: de la Serna Real de Asua M
title: Risk stratification and long-term outcomes in patients with chest pain and cardiac troponin flat curve

abstract: Abstract Introduction Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and concomitant cancer experience excess in-hospital mortality. Whether this excess risk is consistent across age groups and aligned with invasive management strategies remains unclear. Purpose To assess age-specific associations between cancer comorbidity and in-hospital mortality and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) use in patients hospitalised with AMI. Methods This nationwide study used Swiss hospital discharge data (1998–2022). AMI admissions were identified using ICD-10 codes. Cancer comorbidity was defined by malignant neoplasm codes excluding non-melanoma skin cancer. Associations with in-hospital mortality and PCI were estimated using multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance. Age-stratified risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were derived from fully adjusted models, and the interaction between cancer and age group was tested. Results Among 356,024 AMI admissions, 7,334 (2.1%) involved cancer comorbidity. In patients &lt;65 years, cancer was associated with a nearly threefold higher in-hospital mortality compared with patients without cancer (RR 2.97, 95% CI 2.37–3.71). This excess mortality attenuated progressively with age and was no longer evident in patients ≥85 years (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.90–1.12; P for interaction &lt;0.001). In contrast, PCI use was consistently lower among cancer patients across all age groups, with the strongest relative reduction observed in those aged 75–84 years (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.70–0.79; P for interaction &lt;0.001). Conclusions Cancer comorbidity is associated with a pronounced age-dependent risk–treatment mismatch after AMI. Younger patients with cancer face the highest relative mortality risk despite lower PCI use, whereas the relative excess risk attenuates in the very elderly.Figure
title: Age-dependent risk–treatment mismatch in cancer comorbidity after acute myocardial infarction: nationwide evidence

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) carry a residual risk of adverse events and all-cause mortality. Traditional risk scores such as TIMI and GRACE focus on short-term outcomes and are not designed to capture the complex interplay of post-intervention clinical, lifestyle, and socioeconomic factors. Machine learning (ML) offers a novel approach to adaptive risk stratification by identifying patterns across diverse patient data. Purpose To develop, externally validate, and explain a ML-based model for predicting all-cause mortality in ACS patients following PCI. Methods Data from 1,261 ACS patients (mean age 61±11.1 years, 16.6% women) treated with PCI were obtained from the Santiago de Compostela Cardiac Rehabilitation program (2015–2020). The dataset included demographics, socioeconomic factors, medical history, laboratory results, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and lifestyle data. The central electronic health record system was accessed to retrieve date and cause of death within 12.0 ± 20.9 months of follow-up. Seven ML algorithms were trained using 50 repeats of 4-fold stratified cross-validation. Key performance metrics, including AUC, specificity, sensitivity, accuracy, and balanced accuracy, were compared across all models. Feature selection was performed using random mutation implementation of the Genetic Algorithm and model predictions were explained using SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) values. External validation was conducted on 566 ACS patients post-PCI and a broader population of 1,386 CAD patients from the European multicentre EU-CaRE cohort. Model replicability was assessed using the independent validation screening (IVS) tool. Results LightGBM, Random Forest, and SVM outperformed logistic regression (mean AUC &gt;0.8). LightGBM achieved the highest balanced accuracy (0.87), with sensitivity of 0.86 and specificity of 0.88. External validation in ACS post-PCI patients confirmed reliable identification of true positives (sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.73). SHAP analysis identified nine key predictors: diabetes, physical exercise capacity (peak METs), average daily sitting duration, statin prescription, family history of heart disease, number of affected vessels, revascularization history, serum creatinine, and chronic hepatopathy. Notably, patients achieving &lt;6 METs or sitting ≥9 hours/day showed substantially increased mortality risk. The model received an overall IVS rating of “recommended.” Conclusions The ML-based model provides a transparent, high-accuracy tool for identifying ACS patients post-PCI at elevated mortality risk, integrating clinical, lifestyle, and socioeconomic factors derived from standard assessments and electronic health records. It may serve as a decision support tool to identify high-risk patients who could benefit from intensified personalized treatment and lifestyle interventions.
title: A machine learning approach predicts mortality in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)

abstract: Abstract Background The impact of a cumulative favorable environment across the cardiovascular risk spectrum, from primary prevention of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) to secondary prevention of recurrence and mortality, remains unclear. We evaluated the association between a favorable multi-exposure scale and these outcomes. Methods We pooled four cohorts (N=17,216), including two ACS patient registries (1992-1993; 2004-2014) and two Israeli population surveys (1999-2001; 2005-2006, excluding participants with prevalent cardiovascular disease), to capture individuals both with and without prior ACS. We assessed four environmental exposures—greenness, traffic-related air pollution, residential socioeconomic status, and walkability—calculating a cumulative score based on the number of exposures in the most favorable quartile. Mortality and ACS hospitalization data were obtained from the Ministry of Health (through December 2021). Incident ACS was identified among those without prior disease, and recurrent events within the ACS registries. Cox regression models, using age as the time scale and adjusting for potential confounders, were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality and ACS hospitalization associated with number of favorable exposures. Results A total of 14,887 individuals [median age 67 (IQR 56–76) years; 32% female] were followed for a median of 15.6 (IQR 11.7–16.0) years; 6,359 (42.7%) deaths and 5,402 (36.3%) ACS events were recorded. Number of favorable exposures was associated with lower mortality risk in a dose-response fashion (p-for-trend&lt;.005), with no effect modification by prior ACS status (Table). In the ACS cohorts, the number of favorable exposures was monotonically associated with a lower risk of subsequent ACS hospitalization; no such association was observed among the ACS-free cohort (p-for-interaction=.09; Table). Conclusions A higher number of favorable environmental exposures was associated with lower risks of mortality and recurrent ACS events, but not with incident ACS events. These findings support the role of a favorable environment in secondary prevention of ACS.Table
title: Association of Multiple Environmental Exposures and Acute Coronary Syndrome Outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background This study examines sex-specific differences in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), utilising data drawn from the Hungarian National Myocardial Infarction Register. The analysis spans a decade and includes 179,386 individuals, with all-cause mortality evaluated alongside major risk factors and treatment outcomes. Methods Patient data reporting for ACS has been mandatory in Hungary since January 2014. This retrospective investigation encompasses all cases recorded from the registry’s inception through to 2024, with a mean follow-up of 3.8 years. The principal outcome measured was all-cause mortality. Propensity score matching (PSM) was conducted using a 1:1 nearest neighbour algorithm, with age, ACS subtype, percutaneous revascularisation, and diabetes mellitus as fixed covariates to account for baseline clinical disparities. Results The study included 179,386 patients, with a median age of 68 years and a male proportion of 60.5%. Mortality across all intervals was significantly affected by age, diabetes, and ACS subtype. Female patients exhibited higher incidences of diabetes, hypertension, and were generally older; they also experienced more complications related to myocardial infarction. In contrast, male patients were more likely to have undergone prior interventions, received timelier treatment, and had a greater rate of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Women were less frequently discharged with guideline-recommended drug therapies and had greater observed, unadjusted mortality at each evaluated time point (47.9% vs. 39.3%, p &lt; 0.001). The PSM procedure achieved high quality balance (Mean Bias: 2.5%, Rubin’s B: 6.5) and revealed that the previously observed poorer prognosis among women was attenuated. Adjusted for these clinical variables, women demonstrated a 10.3 percentage point lower all-cause mortality compared to men (Average Treatment effect on the Treated [ATT] = -0.103; t = -22.83; p &lt; 0.001).
