Patients were classified by primary etiologic cause into cardiac/coronary, cardiac/non-coronary, systemic, or indeterminate groups. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause death; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular death, and recurrent MI. Cox and Fine–Gray competing-risk models were used, with cardiac/coronary MI as the reference. A sensitivity analysis compared atherothrombotic and non-atherothrombotic mechanisms within the cardiac/coronary endotype. Results Among 6282 patients, 5330 (84.9%) had cardiac/coronary MI, 302 (4.8%) cardiac/non-coronary MI, 503 (8.0%) systemic MI, and 147 (2.3%) indeterminate MI. 1-year all-cause mortality occurred in 9.8%, 15.9%, 25.8%, and 1.4% of patients, respectively. Compared with cardiac/coronary MI, adjusted mortality risk was higher in systemic MI (HR: 2.50; 95% CI: 2.05–3.05) and cardiac/non-coronary MI (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.08–1.96), and lower in indeterminate MI (HR: 0.22; 95% CI: 0.06–0.89). Mortality differences were largely driven by non-cardiovascular death. Recurrent MI risk was lower in cardiac/non-coronary and systemic MI, while MACE rates were similar across endotypes. Atherothrombotic and non-atherothrombotic coronary mechanisms showed comparable outcomes. Conclusions A causal endotype–based classification identifies distinct MI groups with meaningful prognostic differences and competing risks, offering incremental insight beyond the current UDMI.K-M curvesK-M curves 2
title: Prognostic implications of a causal endotype–based classification of myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background and aim Despite their higher risk of complications, there are currently no specific guideline recommendations for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients with liver disease. The aim of this analysis was to investigate the association of liver disease with treatment modalities and outcomes for patients with AMI in Switzerland. Methods We included patients who had been enrolled in the Acute Myocardial Infarction in Switzerland (AMIS) Plus registry between 2003 and 2023. We compared patients with no liver disease (NLD), mild liver disease (MLD) and moderate to severe liver disease (MSLD), as defined by the Charlson Comorbidity Index. Descriptive and multivariable-adjusted logistic regression analyses were conducted. In addition, temporal trends in treatment and outcomes across predefined observation periods (2003-2009 vs. 2010-2016 vs. 2017-2023) were evaluated. Treatment modalities included the use of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), while outcomes encompassed the occurrence of in-hospital bleeding and in-hospital mortality. Results A total of 54,263 patients with AMI were included in this study, 386 of which presented with MLD (0.7%) and 335 with MSLD (0.6%). Patients with liver disease were less likely to receive PCI (NLD 82.8%, MLD 72.8%, MSLD 68.8%, p&lt;0.001) and DAPT (NLD 84.2%, MLD 75.9%, MSLD 70.9%, p&lt;0.001), and had higher crude event rates (bleeding: NLD 3.0%, MLD 3.4%, MSLD 6.7%, p=0.002, in-hospital mortality: NLD 4.8%, MLD 7%, MSLD 11.6%). After multivariable adjustment, patients with MSLD had consistently lower rates of PCI (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.31-1.03, p=0.048) or DAPT (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.28-0.98, p=0.03) compared to patients with NLD. In-hospital mortality and bleeding were increased in patients with MSLD (mortality: OR 2.67, 95% CI 1.00-6.06, p=0.031, bleeding: OR 2.52, 95% CI 1.52-3.92, p&lt;0.001), compared to patients with NLD, whereas no increase was observed among patients with MLD (mortality: OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.17-2.10, p=0.6, bleeding: OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.53-1.90, p=0.8). Over the observed time periods, there were no changes in bleeding rates (MLD p=0.834, MSLD p=0.154) or in-hospital mortality (MLD p=0.261, MSLD p=0.194). However, the use of PCI and DAPT significantly increased over time in patients with MSLD (PCI: 54.9% vs. 71.9% vs. 79.1%, p&lt;0.001, DAPT: 56.4% vs. 79.1% vs. 77.8%, p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Patients presenting with AMI and MSLD were less likely to receive PCI and DAPT and showed higher rates of in-hospital mortality and bleeding than patients without liver disease. Despite an increase in PCI and DAPT over time in patients with MSLD, in-hospital mortality and bleeding were not affected.
title: The impact of liver disease on treatment and in-hospital outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction. Insights from the nationwide AMIS Plus registry

abstract: Abstract Background Valve replacement is the standard treatment for severe valvular heart disease, with bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) increasingly favored due to lower thrombogenicity and improved hemodynamics. Despite advances in biomaterials, BHVs remain susceptible to structural valve degeneration (SVD), largely driven by calcification. While coronary calcium scoring is standardized, there is no validated quantitative approach for assessing native or bioprosthetic valvular calcification. Conventional CT provides limited material characterization. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT), with improved spatial resolution, reduced artifacts, and spectral material discrimination capabilities, offers a promising platform for quantitative assessment of BHV degeneration. Purpose To evaluate the feasibility of PCCT and its spectral imaging techniques for quantitative characterization of BHV calcification and structural valve degeneration. Methods 11 calcified BHV explants were obtained from our Biobank. Valves were positioned in a plastic phantom and suspended in 9 mg/mL iodine solution. Imaging was performed using the NAEOTOM Alpha PCCT system (Siemens Healthineers) with a 140 kV Ultra High-Resolution Quantum Plus protocol (reconstruction: iMAR 0.40 mm, Qr40, QIR 3). DICOM datasets were processed in 3D Slicer to segment regions containing calcium. Calcium density for each segmented voxel was calculated using an adapted virtual unenhanced workflow on Siemens Syngo Via VB60. Low and high energy images were generated from spectral datasets. Maximum intensity projection (MIP) maps were created to visualize the spatial distribution and concentration of calcification. Results Among the 11 explanted valves, 8 were from the aortic position and 3 from the mitral position. Mean age of patients at explantation was 70.82 ± 5.06 years. Mean implantation duration was 9.91 ± 4.21 years (maximum 17 years). Segmented calcium volume ranged widely from 4.27 mm³ to 889.82 mm³, reflecting heterogeneous degeneration patterns. The mean low-to-high energy ratio was 1.74 ± 0.24. Calculated calcium densities ranged from 360.10 to 763.87 mg/mL (mean 590.05 ± 131.47 mg/mL). Maximum intensity projection maps demonstrated heterogeneous spatial distribution of calcification within valve leaflets (Figure 1). Conclusion PCCT enables high-resolution, quantitative assessment of bioprosthetic valve calcification, providing both volumetric and density-based characterization beyond conventional CT capabilities. PCCT-based calcium mapping may represent a novel imaging biomarker for early detection and monitoring of BHV degeneration. Furthermore, quantitative characterization of leaflet calcification could support procedural planning and risk stratification in transcatheter valve-in-valve interventions. These findings highlight the potential of PCCT to bridge the current gap between structural imaging and mechanistic understanding of bioprosthetic valve failure.
title: Quantitative assessment of bioprosthetic heart valve calcification using photon-counting CT

abstract: Abstract Abstract Intro There is a lack of contemporary data describing how the female survival advantage is affected by age and left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the interaction between sex, age, and ejection fraction (EF) regarding long-term all-cause mortality in a nationwide population. We further examined sex-specific differences in baseline comorbidities and secondary prevention strategies over a 17-year period. Methods We studied a cohort of 167,174 patients from the SWEDEHEART registry, aged ≥18 years, presenting with a first-time AMI and echocardiographic assessment during hospitalisation. Relative risks were calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression models (Model 1: age-adjusted; Model 2: age + comorbidities; Model 3: age + comorbidities + discharge treatment). Analyses were stratified by age categories and four temporal periods (2005–2022). Results Women were older at presentation (median 74 vs. 67 years) and had a higher prevalence of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease. Women were less frequently treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), P2Y12 inhibitors, and statins at discharge. Among individuals &lt;70 years, age-adjusted mortality was consistently higher in women regardless of EF, whereas the opposite was observed in those aged ≥70 years (Figure 1). The pattern with the highest age-adjusted hazard ratio for women in those &lt;60 years, with decreasing hazard ratios across increasing age groups, has become increasingly evident over time (Figure 2), with similar results when analyses were stratified by EF. Adjusting for comorbidities and discharge treatment did not materially change the models. Conclusion Post-AMI prognosis is characterised by a sex-dependent inversion of risk. In young women (&lt;60 years), the traditional survival advantage is reversed, with women facing a higher mortality risk than men. This shift from protection to vulnerability is seen in all EF classes but most pronounced in those with significant LVSD. The interaction between age and sex has increased over the years which warrants more studies.
title: Sex differences in myocardial infarction patients with or without reduced ejection fraction

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) requires prompt antithrombotic therapy, which increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). When GIB occurs during ACS hospitalisation, clinicians face a therapeutic dilemma between bleeding control and continuation of cardioprotective treatment. Although endoscopy is commonly performed in this setting, the clinical yield and actionable findings may differ between overt and occult bleeding presentations. Data comparing these phenotypes in patients with ACS remain limited. Purpose To compare endoscopically actionable findings between ACS patients presenting with overt versus occult GIB. Methods We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study at Siriraj Hospital between 2011 and 2024. The study included adults admitted with ACS who were diagnosed with gastrointestinal bleeding and underwent endoscopy within 30 days. Patients were classified as overt or occult GIB. The primary endpoint was a pragmatic composite of endoscopically actionable outcomes at index endoscopy: endoscopic haemostasis, high-risk bleeding lesions, or a management-change lesions (defined as gastrointestinal cancer/tumour, inflammatory bowel disease, or colitis). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify predictors of the composite and management-change endpoints. Results Among 119 patients (overt n=84; occult n=35), the composite actionable endpoint occurred in 34.5% overall and was more frequent in overt versus occult GIB (40.5% vs 20.0%; OR 2.72, p=0.032). The difference was driven mainly by management-change lesions (19.0% vs 2.9%; OR 8.00, p=0.021), whereas high-risk bleeding lesions were similar between groups (16.7% vs 11.4%; p=0.467). In adjusted analyses, overt presentation remained independently associated with management-change lesions (Firth aOR 6.31, p=0.030) and showed a borderline association with the composite endpoint (Firth aOR 2.59, p=0.053). Conclusion In ACS patients undergoing endoscopy within 30 days of GIB diagnosis, actionable endoscopic findings were common in both bleeding phenotypes. Overt GIB was associated with a substantially higher likelihood of management-changing pathology, supporting timely endoscopic evaluation when clinically indicated.revisedSlide2
title: Endoscopic actionable findings in acute coronary syndrome with gastrointestinal bleeding: overt versus occult presentations

abstract: Abstract Introduction The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) introduced major updates, including refined invasive strategy in high-risk patients, a more selective use of pretreatment with P2Y12 inhibitors, and a stronger recommendation for complete revascularization in STEMI. These changes aimed to improve outcomes through safer and more individualized care. Purpose To assess the impact of the implementation of the 2023 ESC ACS guidelines on clinical practice and patient outcomes in a real-world setting. Methods Single-centre retrospective study including patients hospitalized with ACS and enrolled in the Portuguese Registry of Acute Coronary Syndromes between October 2010 and July 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: before (Group A) and after August 2023 (Group B). Baseline characteristics, management strategies, and outcomes were compared. Results A total of 1455 patients were included (73.3% male, mean age of 67.0±12.8 years); 1154 (79.3%) in Group A and 301 (20.7%) in Group B. Patients in group A were older (67.3±12.7 vs 65.6±12.9 years, p=0.043), less often smokers (23.2% vs 30.2%, p=0.012) and had fewer previous percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) (10.8% vs 15.6%, p=0.022). After guideline implementation, STEMI admissions increased (56.8% vs 45.4%, p&lt;0.001). There was a higher rate of coronary angiography (99.7% vs 96.6%, p=0.004), PCI (85.0% vs 76.8%, p=0.002) and staged PCI (28.9% vs 19%, p=0.002), with greater use of radial access (94% vs 70.9%, p&lt;0.001). In NSTEMI patients, the time to coronary angiography was reduced (18.7 vs 36.8 hours, p&lt;0.001). In STEMI patients, fibrinolysis decreased (2% vs 11.6%, p&lt;0.001) and pre-catheterization P2Y12 loading was less frequent (59.6% vs 85.1%, p&lt;0.001). Regarding medical therapy, use of potent P2Y12 inhibitors (prasugrel/ticagrelor) and additional lipid-lowering agents increased, while clopidogrel, nitrates, and beta-blockers were less prescribed. In-hospital complications decreased, including heart failure (14.0% vs 21.0%, p=0.006), cardiogenic shock (1.3% vs 4.9%, p=0.006), and mechanical complications (0% vs 1%, p=0.035), with shorter hospital stay (5±3 vs 6±4 days, p=0.003). In-hospital mortality remained similar (1.0% vs 1.8%, p=0.318). Referral for cardiac rehabilitation increased significantly (52.7% vs 16.9%, p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Implementation of the 2023 ESC ACS guidelines was associated with significant changes in clinical management, particularly in invasive strategy and antiplatelet therapy, leading to fewer in-hospital complications and shorter admissions. These results support their positive impact on real-world clinical practice.
title: Impact of the 2023 ESC acute coronary syndromes guidelines on clinical practice and in-hospital outcomes - a registry-based study

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs) reportedly have lower short-term mortality after myocardial infarction (MI) than those without SMuRFs (SMuRFless). Unrecognised and untreated standard risk in first MI patients may underlie this difference. Purpose To assess the contribution of cardiovascular comorbidities and adverse presentation to differences in in-hospital mortality between first MI patients with and without SMuRFs. Methods We analysed first MI patients from nationwide MI cohorts in Switzerland (AMIS Plus) and Hungary (HUMIR) between 2014 to 2024. First MI was defined by excluding patients with a history of either prior MI, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass grafting. SMuRF status was defined by a history of hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes mellitus, or smoking. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Patient characteristics included SMuRFs, cardiovascular comorbidities (stroke, heart failure, chronic kidney disease [CKD], and peripheral vascular disease [PVD]) and adverse MI presentation (heart failure or cardiac arrest). Outcome analyses used sequential additive multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models (odds ratio [OR], 95% confidence intervals [CI]). Results Among a total of 12,827 first MI patients in Switzerland (mean age: 64.0 years; 25.4% female) and 25,394 first MI patients in Hungary (mean age: 64.9 years; 36.0% female), 680 (5.3%) and 1,675 (6.6%) were SMuRFless, respectively. ST-elevation MI (STEMI) prevalence was higher in SMuRFless patients in Switzerland (69.3% vs. 61.3%, p &lt; 0.001) and Hungary (61.9% vs. 55.3%, p &lt; 0.001). Cardiovascular comorbidities were higher in SMuRF patients in both countries (PVD: 2.6% vs.0.6%, stroke: 3.2% vs. 0.9%, CKD: 4.5% vs. 1.2%; Hungary: heart failure: 9.3% vs. 5.0%, PVD: 10.8% vs. 3.2%, stroke: 7.0% vs. 2.7%, CKD: 19.3% vs. 11.2%; all p &lt;0.001), except heart failure in Switzerland (1.1% vs. 0.3%, p = 0.051). Cardiovascular comorbidity was higher among SMuRFless patients in Hungary compared with Switzerland. Adverse MI presentations did not differ significantly between groups in either country (p &gt; 0.15 for all). Unadjusted in-hospital mortality rate was higher in SMuRFless patients in Switzerland (3.7% vs. 2.3%, p = 0.023; OR: 1.61, 95%CI: 1.04-2.39), but not in Hungary (4.8% vs. 5.6%, p = 0.144; OR: 0.84, 95%CI: 0.67-1.06). After full adjustment for cardiovascular comorbidities and adverse MI presentation, mortality differences in Switzerland were no longer significant (Model 3; Figure 1). Conclusion In this binational study, differences in in-hospital mortality between SMuRF and SMuRFless first MI patients appear to be explained by baseline cardiovascular comorbidities and disease presentation. Further studies should explore whether SMuRFless patients carry unrecognised standard modifiable risks rather than non-traditional risk factors.
title: Contribution of cardiovascular comorbidity and adverse presentation to in-hospital mortality differences with first myocardial infarction in patients with and without standard modifiable risk factors

abstract: Abstract Background Of all patients presenting with suspected myocardial infarction (MI), around 30% remain in the observe group after initial triage using rapid diagnostic algorithms. These patients are at high risk for mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), making early risk stratification crucial. As a strong prognostic biomarker which has been thoroughly evaluated in different patient groups, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) may be useful in this setting. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the prognostic utility of hs-CRP in patients in the observe group, initially presenting with suspected MI, and comparing it to the established risk prediction model of GRACE Score. Methods We prospectively enrolled patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected MI and measurements of hs-cTn and hs-CRP were obtained and GRACE-Score (1.0) was calculated in each patient. Individuals with STEMI and patients with infectious cause of hs-CRP elevation were excluded from further analyses. Patients were categorized into three groups using the 0/1h hs-cTnI (Architect) algorithm: Rule-in, observe, or rule-out. For patients in the observe group, quintiles of hs-CRP were defined. All-cause mortality and MACE at 90 days, 1, 3, and 5 years were assessed. Event rates, Cox-regression, and c-indices were calculated for hs-CRP, GRACE-Score, and their combination, unadjusted as well as adjusted for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. Results Of 2,843 patients (median age 63 years; 36.1% female), 917 remained in the observe group. Median hs-CRP concentration in the observe group was 2.9mg/l. Patients with hs-CRP concentrations in the highest quintile (&gt;12.57mg/l) had significantly higher 1-year (16% vs. 1.7%), 3-year- (29.4% vs. 4.2%) and 5-year mortality (41.2% vs. 6%) as well as 3-year- (39.5% vs. 24%) and 5-year MACE (47.5% vs. 28.2%) compared to the lowest quintile (≤0.95mg/l) (Figure 1). Hs-CRP resulted in a higher c-index compared to the GRACE-Score for 3-year (C-index 0.716 vs. 0.649) and 5-year mortality (C-index 0.705 vs. 0.649) (Table 1). Combined interpretation of hs-CRP and GRACE Score even further improved model performance (C-index5-year mortality 0.761). No relevant differences between hs-CRP quintiles and GRACE Score could be identified regarding MACE. Elevated hs-CRP concentrations in the highest quintile independently predicted 1-year- (adjusted HR1-year 6.72 [2.03, 22.23], p &lt; 0001), 3-year- (adjusted HR3-years 5.37 [2.42, 11.93], p &lt; 0.001) and 5-year mortality (adjusted HR5-years 6.44 [95%CI 3.07–13.50], p &lt; 0.001) as well as 5-year MACE (adjusted HR 1.57 [95% CI 1.06, 2.31], p = 0.023) compared to the lowest quintile. Conclusion We identified hs-CRP as a strong and independent predictor of mortality and MACE in patients with suspected MI, classified into the observe group, further improving risk-prediction beyond established models.Figure 1:Kaplan-Meier curvesTable 1:Regression analyses and C-indices
title: High-sensitivity C-reactive protein in patients with suspected myocardial infarction classified to the observe zone

abstract: Abstract Background Complete atrioventricular block (AVB) is a serious complication of ischemic heart disease that may require temporary cardiac pacing. Although AV block occurring during acute myocardial infarction, particularly inferior infarction, is often reversible after reperfusion, predictors of atrioventricular conduction recovery remain poorly defined. Coronary anatomical complexity assessed by the SYNTAX score reflects the severity of coronary artery disease and may influence the reversibility of ischemia-related conduction disturbances. Purpose To evaluate the association between coronary anatomical complexity, assessed by the SYNTAX score, and recovery of atrioventricular conduction in patients presenting with complete atrioventricular block in the setting of ischemic heart disease. Methods We conducted an observational study including consecutive patients presenting with complete AV block and angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease. Clinical, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic and biological data were collected. Coronary complexity was assessed using the SYNTAX score. Culprit artery location, completeness of revascularisation and delay to revascularisation were analysed. The primary endpoint was recovery of atrioventricular conduction during hospitalisation. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified independent predictors of conduction recovery. Results A total of 131 patients presenting with complete atrioventricular block in the setting of acute coronary syndrome underwent coronary angiography with or without PCI (mean age 64±12 years, 70% men). Inferior myocardial infarction was the most frequent presentation, and temporary pacing was required in most patients at admission. Recovery of AV conduction occurred in 46 patients (35%). Patients with reversible AV block had significantly lower SYNTAX scores than those with persistent block (11.9±6.3 vs 23.5±9.1; p&lt;0.001). Recovery was more frequent in patients with right coronary artery involvement, complete revascularisation, and early revascularisation. In multivariable analysis, the SYNTAX was independently associated with AV block reversibility (OR 0.87 per point increase; 95% CI 0.82–0.93; p&lt;0.001). A SYNTAX ≤14 predicted AV conduction recovery with good discriminative performance (AUC=0.81), whereas scores &gt;22 were associated with a markedly higher probability of persistent AV block requiring permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). Conclusions Coronary anatomical complexity assessed by the SYNTAX score is strongly associated with reversibility of complete AV block in ischemic heart disease and carries prognostic implications. Low SYNTAX score identify patients with a high probability of atrioventricular conduction recovery after revascularisation, whereas higher scores are associated with persistent AV block requiring PPI.These findings may help identify patients in whom permanent pacing can be safely deferred after revascularisation.ROC analysis of SYNTAX score for AV recovery
title: Coronary complexity and reversibility of complete atrioventricular block in ischemic heart disease: the predictive role of the SYNTAX score

abstract: Abstract Background Nationwide European registries have reported a significant temporal decline in post-discharge heart failure hospitalization (HFH) following acute myocardial infarction (AMI), reflecting advances in acute management and secondary prevention. However, contemporary long-term data focusing specifically on post-discharge HFH in Japanese AMI populations remain limited. Purpose To clarify temporal trends in post-discharge HFH and its prognostic impact in a contemporary Japanese AMI cohort. Methods Among 6,394 consecutive AMI patients registered in the Mie ACS Registry between January 2013 and December 2022 who survived to hospital discharge, the cumulative incidence of HFH within 2 years was evaluated. Temporal comparisons were performed between the early (2013–2017) and late (2018–2022) periods. The association between HFH and 2-year all-cause mortality was assessed using multivariable Cox regression analysis. Results The cumulative incidence of HFH was 2.7% at 1 year and 3.4% at 2 years. HFH occurred predominantly within the first year after discharge, with a 3.7-fold higher incidence compared with the second year (P&lt;0.001, Figure1). The first-year HFH incidence was significantly lower in the late period than in the early period (2.2% vs. 3.2%, P&lt;0.001, Figure1), whereas no significant difference was observed during the second year (0.6% vs. 0.8%, P=0.33, Figure1). Patients who developed HFH within the first year had markedly higher 2-year all-cause mortality compared with those without HFH (30.8% vs. 6.0%, P&lt;0.0001, Figure 2). Furthermore, HFH within the first year was identified as the strongest independent predictor of 2-year all-cause mortality (HR 2.38, 95%CI 1.70–3.30, P&lt;0.001). Conclusion In this contemporary Japanese AMI cohort, post-discharge HFH significantly declined over time, particularly within the first year after discharge. Early HFH remains a powerful predictor of subsequent mortality, underscoring the importance of intensive early post-discharge management and optimized secondary prevention to further improve long-term outcomes.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Temporal decline in post-discharge heart failure hospitalization after acute myocardial infarction in the contemporary era: insights from the Mie ACS registry

abstract: Abstract Background Primary ventricular fibrillation (PVF) is a life-threatening complication of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The widespread implementation of reperfusion strategies and improvements in post-resuscitation care may have modified the prevalence and prognosis of PVF in recent years. Purpose To assess temporal changes over the last 15 years, following the implementation of the STEMI Code network, in the prevalence, management, reperfusion times, and short- and long-term mortality of PVF in patients with STEMI. Methods In 2009, the STEMI Code network was officially launched in Catalonia, Spain, prioritizing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) as the reperfusion strategy for STEMI. The Ruti-STEMI registry prospectively included all consecutive STEMI patients admitted to the Cardiac Critical Care Unit of a tertiary university hospital between January 2009 and December 2023. According to year of admission, patients were classified into three 5-year periods: Period 1 (2009–2013), Period 2 (2014–2018), and Period 3 (2019–2023). We analyzed temporal trends in PVF prevalence, reperfusion therapy, ischemia time (symptom onset-to-reperfusion), 30-day case fatality, and 2-year all-cause mortality. Results A total of 5,455 STEMI patients were included: 1,808 in Period 1, 1,674 in Period 2, and 1,973 in Period 3. Overall PVF prevalence was 8% (n=436). Mean age was 62.6±11.7 years, and 21.7% were women, with no differences across periods. PVF prevalence increased significantly over time (6.3%, 8.0%, and 9.5% across Periods 1–3, respectively; p&lt;0.001). Overall reperfusion therapy increased from 90.1% in Period 1 to 92.3% in Period 3 (p=0.002), exclusively with PPCI. Reperfusion rates were higher in PVF compared with non-PVF patients (94.5% vs. 91.4%; p=0.023). Median ischemia time was shorter in PVF patients (150 minutes [IQR 113–209]) than in non-PVF patients (190 minutes [IQR 133–318]; p&lt;0.001). Overall 30-day case fatality was 6.3%, with no significant differences across periods. However, 30-day mortality was significantly higher in PVF versus non-PVF patients (21.1% vs. 5.0%; p&lt;0.001). Two-year mortality was 12.6%, without temporal differences. Among 30-day survivors, long-term mortality was similar between PVF and non-PVF patients (5.3% vs. 5.9%; p=0.693). The main results are shown in Table 1. Conclusions The incidence of PVF in STEMI patients increased from 6.3% to 9.5% over 15 years following STEMI Code implementation. Although reperfusion rates were higher and ischemia times shorter in PVF patients, no reduction in short- or long-term mortality was observed over time.Table 1Figure 1
title: Temporal trends in primary ventricular fibrillation in the STEMI code era: a 15-year registry. Analysis of prevalence, acute-phase and long-term mortality

abstract: Abstract Introduction Extracellular volume (ECV) reflects diffuse myocardial fibrosis and has been increasingly associated with adverse outcomes in severe aortic stenosis (AS). Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) technology enables reliable ECV quantification during routine pretranscatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) assessment. In this context, we sought to determine the prognostic value of myocardial ECV quantified by DECT, performed as part of the routine pre-TAVI assessment Methods Retrospective cohort of patients with severe AS undergoing pre-TAVI CT (April 2024–April 2025). A delayed dual-energy acquisition was performed for ECV quantification. Global ECV was defined as the mean of basal and mid-ventricular short-axis values. Patients were included irrespective of subsequent management strategy. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included unplanned cardiovascular hospitalization and urgent aortic valve replacement. Results A total of 248 patients were included (median age 81 years; 49% male). Median follow-up was 11 months [9–15]. Median ECV was 30.4% [27.6–33.7%]. 145 patients underwent valve implantation (136 TAVI, 9 SAVR), and 103 were managed conservatively. ECV did not differ between management strategies (p = 0.118). During follow-up, 20 deaths occurred. Higher ECV was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.16 per 1% increase; 95% CI 1.07–1.25; p &lt; 0.001) and remained independently predictive after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.15; 95% CI 1.06–1.25; p = 0.001). In a time-dependent Cox model adjusting for AVR as a time-varying covariate, ECV remained independently associated with mortality (p&lt;0.001). Using ROC analysis, the optimal ECV threshold for mortality prediction was 30.05% according to Youden’s index. For clinical applicability, this value was rounded to 30%. Kaplan–Meier estimates demonstrated a 12-month survival of 98.3% (95% CI 95.9–100%) for patients with ECV &lt; 30%, compared with 86.0% (95% CI 79.8–92.7%) for those with ECV ≥ 30% (log-rank p &lt; 0.001). In the time-to-first unplanned cardiovascular hospitalisation analysis, higher ECV was associated with an increased risk of events (HR 1.12 per 1% increase; 95% CI 1.07–1.17; p &lt; 0.0001). This association remained significant after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR 1.10; 95% CI 1.04–1.17; p = 0.001). Among treated patients, ECV was also higher in those requiring urgent AVR compared with elective procedures (33.9% [31.96–36.35] vs. 29.3% [26.95–31.75]; p &lt; 0.001) and remained independently associated after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.15; 95% CI 1.03–1.30; p = 0.018) Conclusions CT-derived ECV is a marker of adverse prognosis in severe AS. Higher ECV identified patients at increased risk of death, hospitalization, and urgent valve intervention. These findings support the potential role of ECV in routine pre-TAVI evaluation for improved risk stratification.
title: ECV by dual-energy CT enhances risk stratification in severe aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Insulin resistance (IR) is a critical modifiable risk factor in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), prevalent in ACS, is associated with adverse outcomes and may also affect IR. We elucidated the relationship between IR and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in ACS patients with or without OSA. Methods This study enrolled ACS patients who underwent portable sleep monitoring from June 2015 to January 2020. OSA was defined as an apnea hypopnea index ≥15 events/hour. IR status was assessed using the Triglyceride glucose index (TyG), the Triglyceride glucose-waist circumference (TyGWC), and triglyceride glucose-waist to height ratio (TyGWHtR). The relationships between IR and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events were analyzed. Results A total of 1662 patients in the analysis, 873 patients (52.5%) were diagnosed with OSA. At a median follow-up of 3.6 years, OSA was independently associated with increased MACCE risk in patients with TyG&gt;8.94 (adjusted HR=1.351, 95%CI=1.035-1.763, P=0.027), TyG-WC&gt;892.31 (adjusted HR=1.344, 95%CI=1.023-1.766, P=0.034), and TyG-WHtR&gt;5.26 (adjusted HR=1.330, 95%CI=1.016-1.739, P=0.038), but not in those with TyG level ≤median (HR 1.139, 95% CI 0.889-1.460, P= 0.303), TyG-WC level ≤median (HR 1.137, 95% CI 0.885-1.460, P= 0.316) and TyG-WHtR level ≤median (HR 1.112, 95% CI 0.859-1.440, P= 0.419). Baseline data showed that higher TyG derivatives were associated with more metabolic abnormalities and severe OSA-related characteristics. There were consistently increases of HRs for MACCE in the OSA group with insulin resistance indicators risin. Conclusions TyG and its derivatives (TyG-WC, TyG-WHtR) modify the association between OSA and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in ACS patients. These IR surrogate markers can effectively identify high-risk subgroups of OSA patients who may benefit from targeted interventions.Insulin resistance in ACS with OSA patients
title: Obstructive sleep apnea, insulin resistance and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains associated with high in-hospital mortality despite contemporary revascularization and increasing use of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). Established scores (CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, GRACE, ENCOURAGE) were derived in heterogeneous or pre–device-era populations and may not reflect contemporary AMI-CS cohorts. Purpose To develop and temporally validate an admission-based mortality model and compare its performance with established scores. Methods In this single-center study at the Department of Cardiology, 479 consecutive AMI-CS patients were analyzed. The primary endpoint was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Admission variables associated with mortality were entered into multivariable logistic regression to derive a parsimonious prediction model. Temporal validation used a derivation cohort (2017–2022; 2/3) and a validation cohort (2023–2025; 1/3). Discrimination was assessed using AUC with 95% CI; calibration was assessed using slope and calibration-in-the-large; and comparative performance was assessed using DeLong testing. Subgroup analyses were performed in the no-tMCS, Impella, VA-ECMO, and ECMELLA cohorts. Results In-hospital mortality was 42.6% (204/479). The final admission-based model included age, left ventricular ejection fraction, prior cardiopulmonary resuscitation, glomerular filtration rate, vasoactive-inotropic score, and ST-segment elevation on admission ECG. In the derivation cohort (n=338), discrimination was good (AUC 0.81; 95% CI 0.76–0.86). Performance remained stable in the validation cohort (n=141) (AUC 0.81; slope 0.93; calibration-in-the-large −0.04). In the overall cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI 0.769–0.851), exceeding CardShock (AUC 0.74; ΔAUC 0.08; p=0.0015), IABP-SHOCK II (AUC 0.70; ΔAUC 0.13; p&lt;0.001), and GRACE (AUC 0.69; ΔAUC 0.14; p&lt;0.001). Established scores showed heterogeneous and attenuated discrimination, particularly in VA-ECMO– and ECMELLA-treated patients. Across treatment strata, the admission-based model maintained consistent accuracy (AUC range 0.79–0.85). Conclusions In a contemporary AMI-CS cohort, an admission-based model demonstrated stable temporal validation and consistent discrimination across mechanical support strategies. Established scores showed variable performance, particularly in device-escalated patients. These findings highlight the need for next-generation risk models that incorporate early integrative predictors and explicitly account for the growing heterogeneity of AMI-CS in the era of device-supported care.Figure 1 Abstract
title: Early risk stratification in contemporary acute myocardial infarction–associated cardiogenic shock: development and temporal validation of an admission-based mortality model

abstract: Abstract Background Socioeconomic disparities persist and may impact both the implementation of recent therapeutic advances in the early management of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and long-term outcomes. While area-level deprivation has been linked to AMI incidence and short-term mortality, contemporary nationwide data from European healthcare systems remain limited, particularly as regards long-term outcomes. Purpose To evaluate the association between area-level socioeconomic deprivation and long-term mortality following AMI in a large nationwide multicentre French cohort. Methods We analysed data from the 2015 FAST-MI registry, including 5,291 patients admitted for AMI to cardiac intensive care units in 204 centres across metropolitan France (78% of French centres managing AMI patients). Socioeconomic status was assessed using the French Deprivation Index (FDep), an ecological index derived from four municipality-level sociodemographic variables and categorised into quintiles (Q1: least deprived; Q5: most deprived). Baseline characteristics and in-hospital management were compared across FDep quintiles using ANOVA or χ² tests as appropriate. Long-term survival was analysed using Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression. Results Among 5,104 patients (96.5%) with available FDep, prevalence of FDep quintile 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 was 28%, 21%, 16%, 16%, and 19%, respectively. Higher deprivation was associated with a higher body mass index (p=0.027), a greater prevalence of diabetes (p=0.007) and current smoking (p=0.044) (Table 1, for readability, only Q1 and Q5 are displayed). No significant differences were observed across FDep quintiles with respect to other baseline demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, or prior medical history, although direct comparisons between Q1 and Q5 could differ. Patients from more deprived areas were less frequently admitted to university hospitals (p&lt;0.001), and were more likely to receive thrombolysis (p=0.013). In STEMI patients (N=2,520, 49%), both symptom-to-angiography and ECG-to-angiography times increased with deprivation (p&lt;0.001). In-hospital mortality and discharge medications were similar across quintiles. Over an 8-year follow-up, patients in the most deprived quintile had higher long-term mortality after multiple adjustment (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.22-1.67; p&lt;0.001, Figure 1). Conclusions In a large multicentre AMI cohort within a universal healthcare system, area-level socioeconomic deprivation was independently associated with higher long-term mortality. These findings suggest that social gradients in outcomes persist beyond acute management. They underscore the need for targeted preventive strategies and long-term follow-up interventions focused on socially disadvantaged populations to reduce residual inequalities in cardiovascular risk and improve post-AMI prognosis.Figure 1
title: Socioeconomic disparities among patients hospitalized for acute myocardial infarction: insights from the FAST-MI 2015 registry

abstract: Abstract Background Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPL) are chronic macular signatures visible on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and are considered sequelae of ischemia in the deep retinal capillary plexus within the spectrum of paracentral acute middle maculopathy. Recent studies suggest that RIPL may reflect systemic vascular vulnerability and have been associated with cardiovascular diseases, including myocardial infarction. However, their relationship with coronary anatomical complexity in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains poorly explored. Objective To evaluate the association between the presence of RIPL detected by SD-OCT and the severity of coronary artery disease assessed by coronary angiography in patients presenting with ACS. Methods This observational study included consecutive patients admitted for ACS who underwent coronary angiography, with or without percutaneous coronary intervention, followed by systematic retinal SD-OCT imaging. To minimize confounding related to diabetic microangiopathy, patients with diabetes were excluded. RIPL were defined according to established OCT criteria as focal perivenular thinning of the inner nuclear layer. Coronary disease severity was assessed using the SYNTAX and lesion burden, defined by the total number of coronary lesions and the number of significant stenoses. Associations between RIPL presence and angiographic parameters were evaluated using non-parametric tests, Spearman correlations and multivariable regression models adjusted for major cardiovascular risk factors. Results Among 150 non-diabetic patients presenting with ACS, RIPL were detected in 27 patients (18%). Patients with RIPL exhibited significantly higher coronary anatomical complexity compared with those without RIPL. The median SYNTAX was 25 [22–30] in the RIPL group versus 14 [8–20] in the non-RIPL group (p &lt; 0.001). RIPL presence was significantly correlated with the SYNTAX (ρ ≈ 0.50; p &lt; 0.001). High coronary complexity (SYNTAX ≥22) was significantly more frequent in RIPL-positive patients (≈70% vs ≈25%; adjusted OR ≈5–6; p &lt; 0.001). Lesion burden was also higher in patients with RIPL, with a greater number of significant coronary stenoses (4 [3–5] vs 2 [1–3]; p &lt; 0.001). Importantly, RIPL remained independently associated with high coronary complexity after multivariable adjustment for age, sex, smoking and dyslipidaemia. Conclusion In non-diabetic patients presenting with ACS, the presence of RIPL detected by retinal OCT is associated with greater coronary anatomical complexity and higher lesion burden. These findings suggest that retinal micro-ischemic footprints may reflect systemic atherosclerosis and could represent a simple, non-invasive biomarker for coronary risk stratification. These findings support the concept of the retina as a non-invasive window to systemic atherosclerotic disease. Larger prospective studies are needed to further evaluate their prognostic value.Coronary complexity according to RIPL
title: The retina as a window to the coronary arteries: retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPL) identify coronary angiographic complexity in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Liver fibrosis and cardiovascular disease share common metabolic risk factors. However, the relationship between liver fibrosis and traditional cardiovascular risk factors and their combined prognostic impact in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains incompletely understood. Objective This study aimed to investigate the association between traditional cardiovascular risk factors and liver fibrosis, as assessed by the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and to evaluate their independent and combined effects on cardiovascular outcomes. Methods This was a post-hoc analysis of the OSA-ACS study. Patients were stratified into three groups based on FIB-4 cut-offs: &lt;1.3 (minimal fibrosis), 1.3–2.67 (moderate fibrosis), and ≥2.67 (advanced fibrosis). Standardized modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs), including hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and smoking, were assessed. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as a composite of hospitalization for ACS, cardiovascular death, ischemia-driven revascularization, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure. Results A total of 1,909 patients with a median follow-up of 2.9 years were analyzed. Of these, 912 (47.8%) had low FIB-4 scores, 663 (34.7%) had intermediate scores, and 334 (17.5%) had high scores. After multivariable adjustment for traditional cardiovascular confounders including obesity, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, smoking, drinking, a high FIB-4 level remained the strongest independent predictor of MACCE (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.23–2.08, P&lt;0.001). Notably, the coexistence of elevated FIB-4 with more than one SMuRF was associated with a markedly increased MACCE risk (P=0.02 for intermediate fibrosis; P&lt;0.001 for advanced fibrosis). Conclusions Advanced liver fibrosis, as staged by the FIB-4 index, is independently associated with an increased risk of MACCE in patients with ACS. Furthermore, the combination of liver fibrosis with multiple traditional cardiovascular risk factors confers a synergistic, markedly higher risk. These findings suggest that integrating FIB-4 into routine risk stratification may improve the identification of high-risk ACS patients.CENTRAL ILLUSTATION
title: Fibrosis-4 –defined liver fibrosis, traditional risk factors, and cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Standard modifiable risk factors (SMuRFs) – including hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, smoking, and overweight - are major determinants of cardiovascular risk. However, a considerable proportion of acute coronary events occurs in the absence of such SMuRFs. Evidence regarding the real-world prevalence of SMuRFs and their impact on diagnostic assessment in the acute setting of suspected myocardial infarction (MI) is sparse. Purpose We therefore sought to investigate the prevalence of SMuRFs, distribution of diagnoses according to SMuRF burden, and its impact on the diagnostic performance of the 0/1-hour algorithm by the European Society of Cardiology (ESC). Methods Patients with suspected MI were prospectively enrolled in an observational cohort study at a tertiary medical center in Germany. Final diagnoses were independently adjudicated by two cardiologists based on the Fourth Universal Definition of MI. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTn I) was measured in serial blood samples at admission and after one hour. Patients were categorized according to the presence of the five SMuRFs into three SMuRF burden categories: SMuRF-less, SMuRF=1, SMuRF&gt;=2. Rule-out (negative predictive value [NPV], sensitivity) and rule-in (positive predictive value [PPV], sensitivity) performance of the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm for non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) was calculated for each SMuRF burden category. Results Among 3,522 patients (median 63 years, 64.4% male) with symptoms suggestive of an acute MI, 116 patients were SMuRF-less (3.3%), 720 had one SMuRF (20.4%), and 2686 had at least two SMuRFs (76.3%). Overall, hypertension was the most prevalent SMuRF (91.1%), followed by overweight (55.9%), hyperlipidemia (46.5%), current smoking (22.7%), and diabetes (12.6%). Hs-cTnI levels at baseline were higher with increasing SMuRF burden: 2.3 ng/L (95% CI 1.8 – 5.1) in SMuRF-less, 3.9 ng/L (95% CI 1.9 – 9.8) in SMuRF=1, and 6.9 ng/L (95% CI 3.1 – 25.2) in SMuRF&gt;=2 (p&lt;0.0001). Among 176 patients with STEMI, two patients were SMuRF-less (1.1%), while 159 (90.3%) had at least two SMuRFs. In NSTEMI type 1, none of the 281 patients was SMuRF-less; 91.8% had at least two SMuRFs. In 72.1% of SMuRF-less patients, an acute MI was ruled-out with an NPV of 100 (Table 1). Rule-out performance was lowest in patients with diabetes (rule-out proportion 25.1%, NPV 99%; Table 2). The proportion of patients remaining in the observe zone increased with higher SMuRF burden category from 18.9% in SMuRF-less to 37.7% in SMuRF&gt;=2. Conclusion SMuRFs are highly prevalent among patients with suspected myocardial infarction and only a small proportion is entirely SMuRF-less. Among patients with diagnosed MI, &lt;1% was SMuRF-less. Absence or presence of SMuRFs seem to impact diagnostic performance of pathways for suspected MI.
title: Prevalence and diagnostic impact of standard modifiable risk factors in suspected myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Heart failure (HF) is a serious but common complication after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).1 Previous studies have shown that the risk of hospitalization for HF is highest within the first year after STEMI but remains substantial beyond one year.2 HF occurring shortly after STEMI likely reflects the direct consequence of the infarction, whereas late-onset of HF may reflect progression in disease.3 This study aims to assess the long-term prognostic impact associated with timing of hospitalization for HF after STEMI. Methods This study included patients from the DANAMI-3 trial who were followed up to 10 years. Main exposure was hospitalization for HF ≤1 year after STEMI (early HF) while hospitalization for HF &gt;1 year (late HF) were explored in secondary analyses. Logistic regression was applied to determine predictors for early and late HF hospitalization. Cox proportion hazard models were applied to evaluate the association between timing of HF hospitalization and mortality. HF was modeled as a time-dependent exposure in Cox regression analyses. Follow-up began at the index STEMI hospitalization, with patients contributing person-time to the unexposed group until first HF hospitalization and to the exposed group thereafter. Results A total of 2217 patients were included; 227 were admitted with HF of whom 56 (25%) had early HF and 171 (75%) had late HF. Age, hypertension, congestive HF, heart rate, and Killip class&gt;1 were independent predictors of early HF hospitalization. Both early-HF and late-HF significantly increased the risk of all-cause mortality compared to patients with no HF (early HF: adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.44-2.98; late HF: adjusted HR 5.19, 95% CI 4.06-6.63; both p&lt;0.001). Among patients who were hospitalized for HF, mortality risk differed by timing with early HF associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality compared to patients with late HF (adjusted HR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.32-0.78, p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Both early and late HF hospitalization after STEMI were independently associated with increased 10-year all-cause mortality compared with patients without HF. However, among patients who were hospitalized for HF, early HF was associated with a lower mortality risk compared with late HF.Landmark analyses of HF-timing and mortality
title: Timing of heart failure after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and its association with long-term mortality

abstract: Abstract Background Multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) is the gold standard imaging modality for preprocedural planning of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Several dedicated software tools have been developed for morphometric aortic root assessment. However, comparative data on measurement agreement and reproducibility across platforms are limited, and the clinical relevance of software-related measurement discrepancies remains underexplored. Purpose The study aimed (1) to compare morphometric aortic root measurements obtained using three MDCT postprocessing tools; and (2) to evaluate the impact of measurement discrepancies on prosthesis sizing and clinical outcome following TAVI. Methods In 104 consecutive TAVI patients, aortic root dimensions essential for prosthesis sizing were measured using postprocessing software of GE Healthcare, 3mensio ValvesTM and FEops HEARTguideTM. Prosthesis sizing was performed according to the standardised Medtronic sizing matrix, and agreement in sizing across platforms was evaluated. Clinical outcomes were compared between patients with concordant (agreement across all three platforms) and discordant sizing recommendations (disagreement across ≥ 2 platforms). Results Compared with 3mensio ValvesTM, GE software yielded larger annulus perimeter measurements (mean difference: 0.8 mm and limits of agreement: [-2.1,3.8]) (Figure 1), whereas FEops HEARTguideTM yielded smaller measurements (mean difference: -0.6 mm and limits of agreement: [-4.9,3.6]). Importantly, measurement discrepancies resulted in discordant prosthesis sizing in up to 16% of cases (Figure 2). Sizing discordance was associated with a trend toward a higher incidence of new-onset left bundle branch block (26.0% versus 33.3%), particularly in cases where GE software recommended a larger prosthesis size compared with 3mensio ValvesTM and FEops HEARTguideTM. Conclusion(s) Differences in aortic root measurements exist among MDCT software tools for TAVI planning. These discrepancies translate into discordant prosthesis sizing in a substantial proportion of patients, particularly those with borderline annular dimensions, and may have implications for postprocedural clinical outcomes.Figure 1.Bland-Altman Plot Annulus PerimeterFigure 2.Distribution of Prosthesis Sizes
title: Comparative analysis of TAVI planning software: implications for prosthesis sizing and clinical outcome

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) registries are largely derived from national referral centres. Data from regional urban centres distant from national cardiac hubs remain limited, particularly in Southeast Asia, with implications for healthcare equity. Purpose To assess nine-year trends in ACS presentation, coronary anatomy and revascularisation in a regional centre remote from a national cardiac institute, and to evaluate age–sex disparities. Methods We retrospectively analysed 3,316 consecutive ACS admissions over nine years. Patients were stratified using sex-specific thresholds (young: ≤45 years men, ≤55 years women). Clinical characteristics and angiographic findings were compared. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of STEMI. Results Mean age was 55.7±8.8 years; 81.2% were male. STEMI accounted for 41.1% of presentations and remained proportionally stable across study years. Cardiometabolic burden was high: hypertension 74.7%, dyslipidaemia 58.7%, diabetes 34.1% and active smoking 58.4%. Compared with younger patients (n=562), older patients (n=2,754) had significantly higher prevalence of hypertension (75.7% vs 69.8%, p=0.004), dyslipidaemia (59.5% vs 54.6%, p=0.035), multivessel disease (69.2% vs 57.1%, p&lt;0.001) and left main involvement (21.0% vs 13.3%, p&lt;0.001). STEMI proportion did not differ between age groups (41.0% vs 41.5%, p=0.875). Sex-stratified analysis showed marked disparities (interaction p&lt;0.001). Young men had the highest STEMI proportion (51.4%) compared with older men (42.8%), young women (24.3%) and older women (30.5%) (p&lt;0.001). Smoking was most prevalent in young men (72.2%, p&lt;0.001). Conversely, diabetes was disproportionately common in young women (43.7%) compared with young men (26.7%) and older women (40.3%) (p&lt;0.001). Multivessel disease and left main involvement were most frequent among older men (71.7% and 21.9%, respectively; p&lt;0.001). In multivariable analysis, male sex (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.28–1.92, p&lt;0.001) and smoking (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.51–2.05, p&lt;0.001) independently predicted STEMI, whereas hypertension was inversely associated (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.52–0.72, p&lt;0.001). Age, diabetes, dyslipidaemia and multivessel disease were not independently associated with STEMI. Percutaneous coronary intervention was performed in 67.6% of cases. Conclusion Despite practice outside a tertiary cardiac hub, this nine-year registry demonstrates a persistently high STEMI burden and frequent multivessel disease. Distinct phenotypes emerge: smoking-driven premature ACS in young men and a disproportionate diabetes burden in young women. Geographic remoteness does not lessen disease complexity and underscores the need for equitable invasive capacity and targeted prevention within regional health systems.Supporting visualBaseline
title: Nine-year acute coronary syndrome trends in a regional centre distant from a national cardiac centre: implications for healthcare equity and access

abstract: Abstract Introduction Atherosclerosis is a systemic disease affecting multiple arterial territories, and extracoronary involvement reflects a higher global atherosclerotic burden and worse cardiovascular prognosis. However, its association with coronary anatomical complexity has not been fully established. The aim of this study was to evaluate the correlation between peripheral atherosclerotic plaques detected by vascular Doppler ultrasound and coronary disease complexity in patients presenting with acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Methods This was a prospective, single-centre observational study including consecutive patients admitted with ACS between January 2023 and February 2026. The presence of peripheral atherosclerotic plaques was assessed using vascular Doppler ultrasound in four arterial territories (right and left carotid and femoral arteries), generating a score ranging from 0 to 4 according to the number of affected territories. Coronary complexity was determined using the SYNTAX score and the number of major epicardial coronary vessels with ≥50% stenosis. Spearman’s correlation and linear regression analyses were performed to assess the association between peripheral atherosclerotic burden and coronary disease. In addition, the SYNTAX score was compared across categories of peripheral burden (low: 0–1; moderate: 2; high: 3–4 territories), defined according to a stratification analogous to that employed in the PESA study. Results A total of 315 patients with ACS were included. Baseline characteristics are presented in Table 1. Coronary angiography was performed in 95% (n=300), and the SYNTAX score was available in 74.6% (n=235). Vascular Doppler ultrasound was performed in 93.7% (n=295) of the cohort. A positive correlation was observed between the number of affected peripheral territories and the SYNTAX score (ρ=0.18; p&lt;0.01) (Figure 1A). In linear regression analysis, each additional affected territory was associated with a mean increase of 1.04 points in the SYNTAX score (β=1.04; 95% CI 0.27–1.81; p=0.008). The number of affected peripheral territories was also correlated with greater coronary disease extent, as assessed by the number of diseased epicardial vessels (ρ=0.31; p&lt;0.01) (Figure 1B). A progressive increase in SYNTAX score was observed across categories of peripheral atherosclerotic burden (p=0.035) (Figure 1C). In sex-stratified analysis, no significant interaction was observed (p=0.083). Conclusions In patients presenting with ACS, peripheral atherosclerotic burden was significantly associated with greater coronary anatomical complexity and extent of disease, demonstrating a progressive relationship between systemic vascular involvement and coronary burden. These findings suggest that peripheral vascular assessment may provide additional information for anatomical risk stratification.Baseline characteristics
title: Correlation between polyvascular atherosclerotic burden and coronary complexity in acute coronary syndromes

abstract: Abstract Background Swedish healthcare mandates prioritize equity, yet regional disparities in Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) outcomes remain poorly characterized. Frequentist methods often lack sensitivity for rare outcomes in registry data. We used a Bayesian framework to quantify regional disparities in clinical presentation and survival across the healthcare system. Methods A cohort of 5,431 patients from the SWEDEHEART registry (2005–2026) was stratified into six healthcare regions (North, Uppsala-Örebro, Stockholm-Gotland [Reference], West, Southeast, and South). These regions are administrative collaborations for specialized care. Baseline imbalances were assessed via Max Standardized Mean Difference (Max SMD). To understand differences in survival rates, we used Bayesian Cox proportional hazards models to look at the risk of dying within 30 days and 1 year, which helped us calculate the likelihood of different risk A Bayesian logistic regression was also used to figure out how likely it was that someone would have cardiogenic shock when they first came in. All models were adjusted for a comprehensive set of baseline covariates, including comorbidities and socioeconomic status, to ensure that regional estimates were independent of demographic and clinical risk profiles. Primary outcomes (30-day/1-year mortality; cardiogenic shock) were analyzed using adjusted Bayesian models. Results Baseline risk for 5,255 patients showed significant imbalances in sex (Max SMD: 0.220; 18% males in the South vs. 29% in the West), smoking (0.146), hypertension (0.145), and age (0.118), but not diabetes (0.059). Regional cardiogenic shock risk was relatively uniform, with posterior probabilities of higher risk vs. reference ranging from 11.9% (North) to 57.0% (South). Smoking (95% CrI: 0.13–0.26) and hypertension (0.01–0.25) were strong predictors of shock. Conversely, survival disparities were substantial after adjustment. Uppsala-Örebro and Southeast showed 96.9% and 92.5% probabilities of superior 30-day survival. At 1 year, Uppsala-Örebro maintained a 97.8% probability of lower mortality (aHR: 0.77). Simultaneously, the South region showed an 89.4% probability of higher mortality (aHR: 1.31). Conclusion Swedish TTS outcomes exhibit a significant mortality gradient not explained by baseline risk. While shock risk is uniform, survival probabilities (up to 98%) suggest regional variations in longitudinal care delivery. These findings highlight regional inequities and the need for national standardization of care to ensure equitable survival.Figure 1
title: Regional variations in Takotsubo syndrome outcomes: a nationwide Bayesian analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Cardio-renal-metabolic (CRM) multimorbidity, encompassing hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease, is highly prevalent in patients presenting with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). While CRM is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, its relationship with infarct extent versus myocardial structural and functional profile in acute STEMI remains insufficiently defined. Objective To determine whether CRM burden is associated with infarct extent or defines a distinct myocardial structural–functional phenotype using integrated echocardiography and CMR in contemporary STEMI cohort. Methods This prospective study included 782 first-time STEMI patients treated with primary. CRM burden was defined as the coexistence of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease and categorized as 0, 1, 2, or 3 conditions according to established clinical criteria. Early advenced echocardiography was performed in all patients and discharge CMR in 249 patients. Group comparisons were assessed using ANOVA. Results Infarct characteristics did not differ across CRM groups, including infarct size (14.0±10.6% vs 16.9±11.3% vs 15.5±9.1% vs 12.5±10.1%; p=0.278), MVO (p=0.623), and IMH segments (p=0.357). In contrast, increasing CRM burden was associated with a graded deterioration in myocardial structural and functional parameters. E/E′ rose from 8.95±2.59 to 12.71±4.40 (p&lt;0.001), septal E′ decreased from 6.14±1.95 to 4.14±1.14 cm/s (p&lt;0.001), and GLS worsened from −14.0±4.1% to −11.1±3.7% (p=0.001). Global wasted work increased (203.7±191 to 393.4±663 mmHg%, p&lt;0.001), while global work efficiency declined (86.6±8.2% to 80.4±10.6%, p&lt;0.001). Left atrial volume index increased (27.2±7.1 vs 35.5±12.4 mL/m²; p&lt;0.001) with concomitant reduction in atrial strain (p&lt;0.001). In the CMR subgroup, infarct extent remained similar across CRM strata; however, cardiac index declined from 2.75±0.69 to 2.10±0.50 L/min/m² (p&lt;0.001), with a parallel reduction in RV cardiac index (2.55±0.67 to 2.08±0.43 L/min/m²; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion In acute STEMI, cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity is not associated with greater infarct size or reperfusion injury. However, increasing CRM burden defines a distinct myocardial structural and functional phenotype characterized by concentric remodeling, diastolic dysfunction, impaired longitudinal mechanics, reduced myocardial work efficiency, and diminished forward flow. These findings indicate that CRM burden identifies a distinct cardiac structural–functional phenotype independent of infarct extent.Figure 1Graphical abstract
title: Cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity defines a distinct cardiac structural–functional phenotype in acute STEMI independent of infarct extent

abstract: Abstract Background Chest pain is a frequent cause of Emergency Department (ED) attendance, yet only a minority are diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Concern about missed ACS often leads to extensive testing and admissions, highlighting the need for efficient diagnostic strategies. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin assays enable rapid rule-out of acute myocardial infarction using the ESC-recommended 0h/1h algorithm. However, evidence is limited on whether performance is sustained after support cessation. Purpose To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the ESC 0h/1h high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) algorithm one year after implementation, during routine clinical use without continued educational support. Methods This observational cohort study included adult patients with non-traumatic chest pain presenting to three EDs in Sweden. The ESC 0h/1h hs-cTnT protocol was implemented in 2018 with structured educational support, including staff training and reminders to ensure 1-hour sampling and algorithm use. Patients presenting February–November 2019, when the protocol remained available as a local guideline without educational reinforcement, were compared with a prospectively enrolled 2018 cohort using identical inclusion criteria. The protocol was applied alongside clinical assessment and electrocardiogram (ECG), with risk stratification into low, intermediate, and high ACS risk. Primary outcomes were 30-day myocardial infarction or all-cause death among discharged patients and ED length of stay. Secondary outcomes included discharge rates, 30-day revisits, and resource utilization among patients without ACS. Outcomes were compared using regression models adjusted for age, diabetes, and prior myocardial infarction. Results A total of 15,661 ED visits were included (2018: n=6,993; 2019: n=8,668), with similar baseline characteristics. Key outcomes are in Table 1. Among discharged patients, 30-day acute myocardial infarction or all-cause death remained rare and did not increase in 2019 (2018: 0.4% [19/4,917] vs 2019: 0.3% [18/6,339]; adjusted odds ratio (OR) 0.72, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.38–1.39, p=0.33). Median ED length of stay among discharged patients increased modestly from 266 (IQR 197–375) to 276 minutes (Interquartile range [IQR] 206–390). The proportion of patients discharged increased significantly in 2019 (73.1% vs 70.3%; adjusted OR 1.11, 95% CI 1.03–1.20). Discharge rates increased across all risk strata, while 30-day acute myocardial infarction or death among discharged patients remained low in each group. Conclusion One year after implementation and without continued educational reinforcement, the ESC 0h/1h hs-cTnT protocol remained safe, with very low 30-day acute myocardial infarction or death rates among discharged patients. ED length of stay increased modestly, while discharge rates increased across risk strata without evidence of compromised safety.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational before-after cohort, 15,661 ED visits (2018: n=6,993; 2019: n=8,668).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised before-after design with short follow-up of the implementation effect.
appraisal.one_line: Swedish three-ED cohort found the ESC 0h/1h hs-cTnT pathway remained safe one year after implementation without educational support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 30-day myocardial infarction or death among discharged patients was 0.4% [19/4,917] in 2018 versus 0.3% [18/6,339] in 2019 (adjusted OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.38–1.39, p=0.33).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports sustained safety of accelerated troponin rule-out pathways that determine who undergoes invasive assessment.

title: Long-term safety and effectiveness of the ESC 0h/1h troponin protocol in routine clinical care

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) outcomes are strongly influenced by systemic inflammation and nutritional status. The Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index (ALI) integrates both aspects in a single metric. Originally developed in oncology, ALI is based on BMI, albumin, and the neutrophil-to- lymphocyte ratio and is now being evaluated in cardiovascular cohorts. This meta-analysis assesses the prognostic value of ALI in ACS. Methods We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar through September 2025 using a PRISMA-compliant approach. Studies evaluating the association between ALI and ACS outcomes were included. Binary random-effects models were used to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs). Heterogeneity was measured with I2 statistic. Results Of 36 records, 8 studies (11 cohorts) were included for qualitative synthesis, and 6 studies (9 cohorts) contributed to the quantitative meta-analysis, encompassing 8,397 ACS patients from China, Italy, and Turkey. The included studies were prospective or retrospective cohorts. Pooled analyses showed that patients with low ALI had a significantly higher risk of mortality compared with those with high ALI (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.92-3.95, p &lt; 0.01), with low between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 11.3%). Similarly, low ALI was strongly associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular/cerebrovascular events (MACE/MACCE) when analyzed as a categorical variable (HR 2.37, 95% CI 1.87-3.01, p &lt; 0.01; I2 = 0%). However, when ALI was analyzed as a continuous variable, no significant association with MACE/MACCE was observed (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p = 0.08), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 94.1%). Discriminative analyses showed that ALI had moderate predictive accuracy for mortality (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.67-0.78, I2 = 86.3%) and for MACE/MACCE (AUC 0.68, 95% CI 0.63-0.73, I2 = 83.2%), though heterogeneity was high for both. Conclusion ALI is a robust prognostic biomarker for adverse outcomes in ACS, particularly when applied categorically, while its role as a continuous measure remains uncertain due to heterogeneity. Further prospective studies with standardized cut-offs are needed to clarify mechanisms and confirm clinical utility.
title: Prognostic significance of the advanced lung cancer inflammation index in acute coronary syndrome patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background There is uncertainty among physicians regarding the optimal clinical application of the novel high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI)-VITROS assay within the widely implemented upper reference limit (URL)-based ESC 0/3h-algorithm. Methods This prospective, international, multicenter study aimed to validate and compare different modifications of the URL-based ESC 0/3h-algorithm among adult patients presenting with suspected acute myocardial infarction (AMI) to the emergency department. Final diagnoses of AMI were centrally adjudicated by two independent cardiologists, blinded to hs-cTnI-VITROS concentrations. Discrimination was compared to the best validated hs-cTnT/I-assays. Clinical follow-up for cardiovascular death and AMI was conducted until five years. Results Among 1225 eligible patients (median age 63 years (IQR 52-75), 31.9% women), 18.9% were adjudicated as NSTEMI. Diagnostic discrimination of hs-cTnI-VITROS at 0h was very high (AUC 0.949, 95% CI 0.941–0.958), and comparable to hs-cTnI-Architect and hs-cTnT-Elecsys. Using the ESC 0/3h algorithm, 30.9% of patients were classified as rule-out (sensitivity 99.1%, NPV 99.5%) and 19.0% as rule-in (specificity 96.0%, PPV 82.8%). Substituting the HEART score for the GRACE score increased rule-out efficacy to 43.9%, while maintaining very high safety (sensitivity 99.6%; NPV 99.8%). Findings were consistent across predefined subgroups, in sensitivity analyses restricted to type 1 NSTEMI, using the 2h study blood sample (n=2249), and for the composite of cardiovascular death or AMI during five-year follow-up Conclusions The ESC 0/3h-algorithm demonstrated excellent performance for rule-out of NSTEMI with greater efficacy when combined with the HEART- instead of the GRACE score.ESC 0/3h-algorithmsLong-term prognosis
title: Validation of the ESC 0/3h-algorithm with a novel high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay in patients with suspected myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices, with a turnaround time &lt;20 minutes, may reduce time to diagnosis compared to central laboratory testing. However, it remains unclear whether the diagnostic accuracy of hs-cTn POC assays is comparable to that of central laboratory assays. Purpose We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four hs-cTn POC assays to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). Methods We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November 2025. Studies were eligible for inclusion if they investigated adult patients (≥18 years) presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value (PPV)) as an outcome measure. The search strategy identified 436 articles, of which 11 were included in this systematic review, describing four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Results The described hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single test rule-out upon arrival at the ED. The Atellica VTLi demonstrated a sensitivity &gt; 98.8% for troponin values &lt;7 ng/l, and a specificity of 97.7% for troponin values &gt; 52 ng/l. The i-STAT assay showed a sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin values &lt;5 ng/l and a specificity 96.4% at troponin values &gt; 25 ng/l. The Pathfast achieved a sensitivity &gt; 99.1% for troponin values &lt;4 ng/l and a specificity &gt; 96.4% for troponin values ≥ 90 ng/l. VTLI, Pathfast and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99th percentile with a 0+1/2/3 hour troponin protocol, reporting sensitivities of 64.8-100.0% and specificities of 85.8-96.0%. Conclusion This systematic review indicates that hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration in the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule out of ACS in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.
title: What is the diagnostic accuracy of different high sensitive point-of-care troponin assays for the assessments of patients presenting with chest pain at the emergency department?

abstract: Abstract Background Premature myocardial infarction(PMI) patients face significant residual risk linked to metabolic inflammation and thrombosis. While homocysteine (Hcy) contributes to these processes, its synergistic effect with other metabolic risk factors on the long-term prognosis of PMI patients has not yet been established. Purpose To evaluate the independent prognostic value of Hcy on long-term MACE and to investigate its synergistic effects with metabolic and inflammatory risk factors. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort research of 1,220 consecutive PMI patients underwent percutaneous coronary intervention(PCI) (men ≤45 years, women ≤55 years) from January 2017 to December 2024. Baseline plasma Hcy was measured and categorized as either high (≥15 µmol/L) or normal (&lt;15 µmol/L). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiac death, rehospitalization for severe heart failure, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, readmission for unstable angina, and target lesion revascularization. Independent and synergistic associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox models and joint effect analysis. Results 136 patients (11.1%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 582 days. High Hcy continued to be independently linked to MACE after multivariable correction(aHR=2.72; 95%CI 1.87–3.95, P&lt;0.001). This risk was amplified by coexisting cardiometabolic factors, increasing from a 3-to 4-fold higher risk when combined with high D-Dimer, Lp(a), or hs-CRP (aHRs 3.13-4.12), to a 6.5-fold higher risk with obesity (aHR=6.54; 95%CI 3.01-14.20, P&lt;0.001) compared to patients with normal Hcy and normal BMI.In three-way interaction analyses, the combination of high Hcy, obesity, and elevated D-Dimer(D-Dimer&gt;0.5mg/L) conferred a nearly 10-fold higher risk (aHR=9.91;95%CI 3.68–26.66,P&lt;0.001), while the triad of high Hcy, obesity, and high hs-CRP(hs-CRP &gt;2 mg/L) was associated with a 17.5-fold higher risk (aHR=17.51;95% CI 2.28–134.52,P=0.006). Conclusions In PMI patients , elevated homocysteine is an independent predictor of long-term MACE. Importantly, Hcy is a powerful "risk multiplier," increasing the negative consequences of inflammation and obesity.Our results give a clear justification for a significant upgrade in secondary prevention strategy and mechanism-driven nutritional therapies.
title: Homocysteine multiplies risks of adverse outcomes in premature myocardial infarction: synergistic effects with obesity and inflammation

abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute myocardial injury is defined by cardiac troponin (cTn) levels above the 99th percentile with a dynamic rise/fall pattern (Δ), usually suggesting acute coronary syndrome (ACS) when associated with compatible symptoms. However, patients presenting with chest pain, elevated cTn and a Δ&lt;20% (flat curve) represent a diagnostic grey zone, as current guidelines do not clearly associate this pattern with ACS. We aimed to analyze clinical characteristics, management strategies and six-month outcomes of these patients according to initial management: admission to cardiology, admission to another department or discharge from the emergency department.
