Methods We prospectively analyzed 753 consecutive patients with suspected ACS and a cTn-flat-curve (Δ&lt;20% in two high-sensitivity cTn-T determinations at 0 and 3 hours) between May 2023 and January 2026. Six-month follow-up was available in 614 patients (median 185 days). Results Mean age was 75.7±11.9 years and 63.3% were male. Management differed significantly across groups. As detailed in Table 1 and Table 2, patients admitted to cardiology were younger (71.6±12.7 years), more frequently male, and more often presented with high-probability ischemic chest pain, dynamic ECG changes and new wall motion abnormalities. They underwent coronary angiography in 90.8% of cases and were diagnosed with ACS in 78.7%. Patients admitted to other departments were older (80.8±9.7 years), had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, heart failure, chronic kidney disease and oncological disease, and more frequently presented with low-probability symptoms. This group showed the highest six-month mortality (26.5%) and MACE rate (32.6%). Discharged patients had lower troponin levels, fewer high-risk clinical findings and low six-month mortality (3.7%), supporting the safety of discharge when guided by comprehensive clinical assessment. Conclusions In patients with suspected ACS and a cTn-flat-curve, management decisions reflected distinct clinical profiles and were strongly associated with outcomes. A flat troponin pattern did not exclude ACS, and careful integration of clinical, ECG and echocardiographic findings allowed appropriate risk stratification and safe discharge in selected patients.Table 1Table 2
title: Decision making and prognosis of a cohort of patients with chest pain and cardiac troponin flat curve

abstract: Abstract Background Timely recognition of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains challenging, particularly in women who more often present with atypical symptoms and less overt electrocardiographic findings. Artificial intelligence–enabled electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) analysis offers automated risk estimation based solely on raw waveform data, but prospective evidence supporting sex-consistent diagnostic performance and safe rule-out capability is limited. Purpose To assess sex-stratified discrimination, rule-out safety, and phenotype robustness of an AI-ECG model for AMI in a prospective, multicenter emergency department cohort. Methods In a prospective validation study conducted across 18 emergency departments, consecutive adults presenting with suspected AMI were enrolled. AI-ECG analyzed the initial 12-lead ECG and generated a continuous probability score using prespecified thresholds for low- and high-risk classification.1 The primary endpoint was adjudicated AMI during index hospitalization. Diagnostic discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Rule-out safety at the predefined low-risk threshold was assessed by sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), and missed AMI rate. Analyses were performed separately in women and men, with additional evaluation across ST-segment elevation (STEMI) and non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) phenotypes. Results Among 8,493 patients, 3,186 (37.5%) were women. AMI prevalence was lower in women than men (10.5% vs 23.6%). AI-ECG demonstrated comparable discrimination in women and men (AUROC 0.875 vs 0.871). (Table 1) At the prespecified low-risk cutoff, sensitivity was 98.8% in women and 99.8% in men, with high NPV (99.2% and 99.1%, respectively) and missed AMI rates below 1% in both sexes. Performance remained stable across STEMI and NSTEMI, without systematic attenuation in women. In addition, AI-ECG enabled a larger proportion of women to be classified as low risk at presentation. (Figure 1) Conclusion In a prospective, multicenter emergency department cohort, AI-ECG demonstrated sex-consistent discrimination and preserved rule-out safety for AMI. Stable performance across myocardial infarction phenotypes supports AI-ECG as an early triage adjunct with potential to enhance diagnostic equity during initial evaluation.Figure 1Table 1
title: Sex-specific validation of an artificial intelligence–enabled electrocardiogram for early triage of acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) is associated with an increased risk of death and major cardiovascular events (MACE). Purpose Our objective was to determine the 6th generation high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (TnT hs Gen 6) thresholds associated with 30-day death or MACE after noncardiac surgery and externally validate them. Methods We performed a nested VISION biobank cohort study. We measured the TnT hs Gen 6 daily, preoperatively and up to postoperative day 3. An iterative Cox proportional hazard model determined peak postoperative TnT hs Gen 6 thresholds independently associated with the primary outcome. We followed the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki, and all participants provided informed consent. Results The primary outcome occurred in 72/4275 patients (2.0%). Peak TnT hs Gen 6 values of &lt; 45 ng/L, 45 ng/L to &lt; 140 ng/L, and ≥ 140 ng/L demonstrated 30-day incidences of death or MACE of 25/3539 (0.7%), 19/561 (3.4%) and 28/175 (16%), respectively. Compared to peak postoperative TnT hs Gen 6 &lt; 45 ng/L (reference), values from 45 ng/L to &lt; 140 ng/L and ≥ 140 ng/L were independently associated with the primary outcome, with adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) of 3.99 (95% CI, 2.12-7.50) and 20.06 (95% CI, 11.21-35.90), respectively. Participants with peak postoperative TnT hs Gen 6 ≥ 45 ng/L without an ischaemic feature had an aHR of 4.10 (95% CI, 1.89-8.88) for the primary outcome. Validation results in the PMI-VITAL cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05866874) were consistent. Conclusion A peak postoperative TnT hs Gen 6 threshold ≥ 45ng/L was associated with 4-fold increase in the risk of 30-day death or MACE compared to levels &lt; 45 ng/L. This assay threshold is prognostically relevant and can be used as a diagnostic criterion for MINS. (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00512109)Picture 1

appraisal.design_and_n: Nested cohort from the VISION biobank, 4275 patients, with external validation in the PMI-VITAL cohort.
appraisal.main_limitation: Prognostic thresholds only; no evidence that acting on them alters outcomes, and abstract-level reporting.
appraisal.one_line: Nested VISION biobank study proposes a 6th generation hs-cTnT threshold of 45 ng/L as prognostically relevant for myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 72/4275 patients (2.0%). Peak values 45 ng/L to <140 ng/L and ≥ 140 ng/L had aHR of 3.99 (95% CI, 2.12-7.50) and 20.06 (95% CI, 11.21-35.90) versus <45 ng/L.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines assay thresholds for diagnosing MINS (D7), where management remains unsupported by trials.

title: The new 6th generation high-sensitivity troponin T identifies increased risk of perioperative mortality and major cardiovascular events in noncardiac surgery

abstract: Abstract Background Growing evidence supports the presence and clinical relevance of coronary microvascular dysfunction in both acute and chronic myocardial ischemic syndromes, highlighting the need for a diagnostic biomarker algorithm, with a subset of markers plausibly shared across conditions. Material and methods The circulating levels of 67 markers referred to inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, atherogenity, oxidative stress, hemostasis, NETosis, dysbiosis, neuroendocrine activation, and cardiovascular remodeling were determined after 7 days since angioplasty in consecutive 83 pts with STEMI, 83 pts with NSTEMI and at admission in 83 pts with primary diagnosed INOCA. Control series comprised 76 healthy persons. Results In regard to inflammation in all 3 series a similar significant increment (up to 86.9%) of IL-1β and soluble receptor of IL-6 level vs control (5.28±0.84 and 1.29±0.53 pg/ml respectively) was established. Commonly for endothelial dysfunction was the rise of endocan by up to 69.4%. Two markers of atherogenic statement had a common change: decrease of paraoxanase-1 by up to 56.3% and elevation of oxiHDL. The ratio Willebrand/ADAMTS13 was alone marker of hemostasis having a significant increase in all series up to 131.5% (especially in STEAMI and NSTEMI). NETosis, oxidative stress and dysbiosis assessment didn’t underline common markers. However, neuroendocrine activity exhibited by more biomarkers with matched changes in all 3 series: increase of ACE1, Ang II, ET-1, neprylisin and decrease of catestatin, ACE2 and Ang I-7. From 10 biomarkes of cardiovascular remodeling only GDF-15 elevated in all 3 series: by 108.6-112.3 in STEMI and NSTEMI and by 96.2% in INOCA vs control (1.35±0.68 ng/ml). Conclusion Application of a comprehensive multi-biomarker panel in patients with STEMI and NSTEMI (7 days post-angioplasty) and in newly diagnosed INOCA identified 13 biomarkers with similar changes vs control. The most pronounced change was observed for GDF-15, while the majority of shared markers reflected neuroendocrine activation (ACE1, ACE2, angiotensin-(1–7)/angiotensin II balance, catestatin, and neprilysin). These findings suggest a common pathophysiological basis underlying INOCA and support the diagnostic relevance of coronary microvascular dysfunction.
title: Common changes of biomarkers in acute and chronic coronary syndromes: an anchored glance on pathophysiology as well as coronary microcirculation disorder prediction

abstract: Abstract Background The new high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) T-Generation (gen) 6 assay has higher analytical sensitivity than the current hs-cTnT-gen5 assay and performs excellently when embedded in a guideline-recommended early triage algorithm, such as the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1h- or 0/2h-algorithm. However, its performance in the vulnerable cohort of patients with prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) presenting to the Emergency Department (ED) with chest pain is unclear. Purpose Therefore, we aimed to directly compare the performance of the hs-cTnT-gen6 assay with that of the established hs-cTnT-gen5 assay in patients who underwent CABG. Methods In this secondary analysis of an international, prospective, diagnostic study with central adjudication, patients with prior CABG who presented with suspected myocardial infarction (MI) to the emergency department (ED) were enrolled. hs-cTnT-gen6 and gen5 were measured at the same timepoints. The diagnostic performance of hs-cTnT-gen6 was compared with that of hs-cTnT-gen5. Results Among 191 patients, MI was the final diagnosis in 74 (38.8%) patients. The proportion of patients with concentrations above the upper reference limit and therefore myocardial injury was lower for hs-cTnT-gen6 (64.4%) than for hs-cTnT-gen5 (76.4%; P&lt;0.001). Diagnostic accuracy at ED presentation, expressed as AUC, was 0.864 (95%CI: 0.812–0.916) for hs-cTnT-gen6 and 0.867 (95% CI: 0.816–0.919) for hs-cTnT-gen5 (P=0.542). Applying the previously derived cutoffs for the ESC 0/1h- and 0/2h-hs-cTnT-gen6-algorithms triaged patients with 100% negative predictive value and sensitivity to rule-out MI. When hs-cTnT-gen6 was used within guideline-recommended early triage algorithms (ESC 0/1h or ESC 0/2h), the efficacy (defined as the proportion of patients receiving a definitive triage decision and not remaining in the observe zone) was comparable between hs-cTnT-gen6 and hs-cTnT-gen5. (e.g., 47% remaining in the observe zone when using the ESC 0/1h- hs-cTnT-gen6 algorithm versus 51% when using the ESC 0/1h- hs-cTnT-gen5 algorithm; P=0.289). Conclusions In patients with prior CABG surgery presenting with chest discomfort in the ED, the novel hs-cTnT-gen6 assay demonstrated excellent and comparable diagnostic performance to the established hs-cTnT-gen5 assay with fewer patients identified as having myocardial injury. Use-optimized, assay-specific cut-offs for the ESC 0/1h- and 0/2h-algorithms provided very high sensitivity.Central Illustration
title: Performance of the novel high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T- Generation 6 assay in the early diagnosis of myocardial infarction in patients with prior coronary artery bypass grafting

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) is a cornerstone of the diagnosis of myocardial infarction (MI), but mild elevations of hs-cTnT are common also in chronic cardiac conditions. Early troponin release in type 1 MI is dominated by large cTnT-I-C complexes, yet the current commercial hs-cTnT assay detects both intact and fragmented cTnT forms. To potentially enable more specific detection of myocardial injury, a novel immunoassay has been developed to selectively measure only intact and mildly truncated cTnT (“long cTnT”). The influence of age and comorbidities on these long cTnT forms is unknown in patients with severe heart disease but no MI. Purpose To determine whether long cTnT is less affected by age and comorbidities than hs-cTnT in patients referred for elective open-heart surgery. Methods Lithium-heparin plasma samples were collected from 144 patients before elective open-heart surgery. Participants were clinically stable at the time of sampling. Long cTnT was measured using a novel immunoassay and hs-cTnT with the Elecsys Troponin T hs kit (cobas e801, Roche Diagnostics). The influence of age and comorbidities (dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease and pulmonary hypertension) on long cTnT and hs-cTnT concentrations was evaluated. Results The median [25th-75th percentile] age of the study population was 66 [58-71] years. The median hs-cTnT and long cTnT concentrations were 12.0 [8.0-19.0] and 3.9 [2.6-5.8] ng/l, respectively. The hs-cTnT and long cTnT concentrations exceeded their 99th percentile upper reference limit (URL) in 42% and 15% of patients, respectively. Long cTnT concentrations remained low regardless of age and showed no significant correlation with age (Spearman’s rs = 0.106, p = 0.207), whereas hs-cTnT concentrations demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with age (rs = 0.354, p &lt; 0.001) (Figure 1). The hs-cTnT concentrations were significantly associated with all of the studied comorbidities, with median concentrations near or above the 99th percentile URL (Table 1). The long cTnT concentration was significantly associated only with diabetes (p = 0.031) and hypertension (p = 0.010), and median concentrations remained below the 99th percentile URL in all comorbidity groups (Table 1). Conclusions Unlike the hs-cTnT concentration, the long cTnT concentration is only minimally influenced by age and comorbidities. This suggests that long cTnT forms may enable more specific detection of myocardial injury regardless of age and common chronic comorbidities.
title: The concentration of long cardiac troponin T forms is independent of age and common comorbidities in patients referred for elective open-heart surgery

abstract: Abstract Background Functional antibodies targeting GPCRs have gained a role in homeostatic processes whose imbalance may contribute to autoimmune, cardiovascular, and other diseases.Autoantibodies anti-apolipoprotein-A1(AAA-1) are elevated in autoimmune and high cardiovascular-risk condition correlating with adverse outcome. Purpose Because AAA-1 shares in vitro and in vivo characteristics with other anti-GPCR antibodies, we sought to assess its association with anti-GPCRs in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients and to evaluate its potential to trigger GPCR activation in vitro. Methods AAA-1, anti-Adrenoreceptor α1, β1, and β2, anti-CXCR3, anti-PAR-1, anti-PAR-4 antibodies were measured by ELISA technique (CellTrend) on serum samples from 221 consecutive ACS patients. Spearman associations were tested using STATISTICA software. AAA-1 screening activation of GPCRs was tested using the in vitro PathHunter®b-Arrestin assay (Eurofins Discovery). Results Significant Spearman associations were found between AAA-1 and anti-GPCR antibodies continuous values. AAA-1 and anti-GPCRs titers are differentially and significantly associated with clinical variables related to cardiovascular and metabolic conditions and outcomes. In vitro screening experiments on 336 GPCRs targets, highlight the capacity of AAA-1 to activate four GPCR members, showing AAA-1 being a direct agonist for PAR-1, PAR-4, and a positive allosteric modulator for Adrenoreceptor-β1, and β2 but not α1. Conclusion These results clearly show the potential AAA-1 as a novel class of anti-GPCRs antibodies. Anti-GPCRs antibodies and AAA-1 emerge as significant players in MI and metabolic conditions. Continued research is warranted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and to develop targeted therapies that could improve the management and outcomes of patients with MI and metabolic disorders.
title: Autoantibodies against apolipoprotein A1 as potential anti–G protein-coupled receptor class antibodies

abstract: Abstract Background Commercial cardiac troponin (cTn) assays may be significantly affected by circulating cTn-binding autoantibodies (cTnAAb), which can lead to falsely low levels of cTn or elevations in the absence of myocardial injury. Despite the risk of analytical interference, data on the prevalence and clinical correlates of cTnAAbs remain limited. Purpose To determine the prevalence of cTnAAbs in patients with cardiac conditions and in a healthy population, and to investigate whether age, sex, and comorbidities are associated with the production of cTnAAbs. Methods Lithium-heparin plasma (Li-Hep) samples were obtained from 30 patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), preoperatively from 19 patients with aortic stenosis scheduled for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and 151 patients scheduled for open-heart surgery, and from 314 healthy individuals. The presence of cTnAAbs was detected using a previously established in-house immunoassay. High-sensitivity cTnT (hs-cTnT) was measured with the Elecsys Troponin T hs kit (cobas e801, Roche Diagnostics). Associations between cTnAAbs and age, sex, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes were investigated. Statistical comparisons were performed using nonparametric tests. Results We detected cTnAAbs in 2 out of 30 (6.7%) NSTEMI patients, 2 out of 19 (10.5%) elective TAVI operation patients and in 16 out of 151 (10.6%) elective open-heart surgery patients. Overall prevalence of cTnAAbs was 20 out of 200 (10%) in all cardiac patients and 19 out of 314 (6.1%) in healthy individuals (p&gt;0.05). Median [25th-75th percentile] age of NSTEMI patients, TAVI patients, open-heart surgery patients, and healthy individuals were 70 [64-79], 82 [77-84], 66 [58-71], and 50 [33-62] years, respectively. No significant differences in ages were found between cTnAAb-positive and cTnAAb-negative individuals within groups. Measured hs-cTnT levels were similar in individuals with and without cTnAAbs across all groups (Figure 1). The prevalence of cTnAAbs was consistent in both females and males irrespective of cardiac conditions (Table 1). Furthermore, no associations were found between the production of cTnAAbs and smoking, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or diabetes. Conclusions The prevalence of cTnAAbs is comparable in patients with significant cardiac conditions and healthy individuals. Moreover, cTnAAb production appears independent of age, sex, smoking and common comorbidities. Roche hs-cTnT assay seems unaffected by cTnAAbs. Due to the consistent ~10% cTnAAb prevalence in both cardiac patients and the general population, clinicians should be aware of possible cTnAAb-mediated interferences when interpreting cTn results.
title: The prevalence of cardiac troponin autoantibodies is comparable in cardiac patients and healthy individuals and irrespective of age, sex and comorbidities

abstract: Abstract Background In acute coronary syndromes (ACS), high-sensitivity troponin (hs-cTn) elevation prompts an early (&lt;24h) invasive strategy1. However, this binary approach treats all elevations similarly, potentially leading to unnecessary procedures for minor elevations while failing to identify patients with very high hs-cTn who may have an underlying occlusive myocardial infarction (OMI) and require emergent catheterisation2. We hypothesised that hs-cTnI magnitude could refine risk stratification, as previously demonstrated for hs-cTnT 3. Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of admission hs-cTnI and its early dynamics in predicting OMI and critical coronary lesions in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Methods Single-centre retrospective cohort of 396 consecutive AMI patients who underwent coronary angiography within 7 days (September 2024–August 2025). hs-cTnI was measured using a high-sensitivity troponin I assay (99th percentile URL 11 ng/L). Two primary endpoints were assessed: OMI(TIMI flow 0–1 in culprit artery) and Critical Lesion (CL: TIMI flow ≤ 2, or stenosis ≥90% in epicardial vessel, or ≥70% with plaque instability features). Absolute and relative delta troponin were analysed in a subgroup with serial sampling per ESC 0/1-hour protocol 4 (n=318). ROC curves were constructed; Youden index, ≥90% sensitivity (Se) and ≥90% specificity (Sp) cut-offs were determined. Results Mean age 64.1±11.4 years; 69.2% male. OMI occurred in 23.5% and CL in 57.6%. 42.4% of AMI patients had neither CL nor OMI by angiography. Median admission hs-cTnI was significantly higher in patients with OMI (11,040 vs 495 ng/L, p&lt;0.001) and CL (3,006 vs 307 ng/L, p&lt;0.001). Admission hs-cTnI showed moderate accuracy for OMI (AUC 0.736; 95%CI 0.674–0.799) and CL (AUC 0.672; 95%CI 0.620–0.725). Youden-optimal cut-offs were ≥ 2,991 ng/L for OMI and ≥ 1518 ng/L for CL. A high hs-cTnI cutoff for OMI (≥ 35,050 ng/L) had 90.4% Sp and a positive likelihood ratio (LR+) of 3.7. For CL, a cutoff of ≥ 11,790 ng/L yielded 90.5% Sp and a LR+ of 3.56. Absolute hs-cTnI change also predicted OMI (AUC 0.725; 95%CI 0.647–0.802); notably, a change &lt; 28.6 ng/L had 95.8% NPV for ruling out OMI (LR- 0.188). In contrast, relative (%) hs-cTnI change showed no discriminative ability for either endpoint (AUC 0.442 and 0.469). Conclusion The magnitude of hs-cTnI elevation and its early absolute change provide moderate, yet clinically valuable, predictive accuracy for acute coronary occlusion and critical coronary anatomy. Very high hs-cTnI levels can identify patients with a high probability of OMI, supporting an emergent invasive approach. Conversely, a minimal early rise in hs-cTnI could contribute to ruling out OMI, potentially allowing for safe de-escalation of care. These findings suggest that hs-cTnI quantification, beyond its current binary interpretation, may serve as an additional tool to refine invasive strategy timing in AMI.Central Figure: ROC curves and key findingsDiagnostic Performance of hs-cTnI
title: High-sensitivity troponin I magnitude predicts occlusive myocardial infarction and critical coronary lesions: a tool for invasive strategy timing?

abstract: Abstract Background Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) can underestimate left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) diameter (LVOTdECHO) leading to discordant aortic stenosis (AS) grading, particularly in patients with suboptimal image quality. Cardiac computed tomography (CT), routinely performed before transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) allows accurate LVOT assessment. Our aim was to assess whether inserting CT-derived LVOT diameter (LVOTdCT) into the continuity equation to calculate indexed AVA (AVAi_CT), improves AS grading compared with echocardiography-derived AVAi (AVAi_ECHO), particularly when echocardiographic image quality is suboptimal. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 426 TAVI candidates (82.3±7.3 years; 50.2% women) who underwent both CT and echocardiography. LVOTdCT was measured on a plane replicating the parasternal long-axis view and used to compute AVAi_CT. Image quality was graded (good/fair/poor). Reclassification was defined as AVAi_ECHO ≤0.6 cm²/m² and AVAi_CT &gt;0.6 cm²/m². Association with echocardiographic parameters (dimensionless index, DI, acceleration time/ejection time, AT/ET) and CT-derived aortic valve calcium score (AVC) and annulus-indexed AVC (AVCdCT) were examined. Results LVOTdECHO were smaller than CT (median 2.0 [1.7–2.3] vs 2.2 [1.9–2.5] cm; p&lt;0.001). Agreement declined with image quality (ICC good/fair/poor: 0.900/0.689/0.481). AVAi_CT exceeded AVAi_ECHO (0.82±0.22 vs 0.70±0.18 cm²/m²; p&lt;0.001). Overall, 51/426 (12.0%) were reclassified, 82.4% of whom had fair/poor image quality (OR 5.508; 95% CI 2.6–11.6; p&lt;0.001). Most reclassification occurred in normal-flow/low-gradient AS (38.1%). Reclassified patients had DI&gt;0.25 (72.5% vs 20.2%; p&lt;0.001), AT/ET≤0.32 (52.9% vs 38.5%; p=0.043), and lower AVC/AVCdCT. Conclusions Incorporating LVOTdCT into the continuity equation improves AS grading, particularly in normal-flow, low-gradient AS patients and suboptimal echocardiographic quality, and may refine TAVI selection.
title: CT-derived LVOT diameter refines aortic stenosis assessment in TAVI candidates with suboptimal echocardiographic image quality

abstract: Abstract Background BNP is predominantly synthesized in the ventricular myocardium and is released into the circulation in response to ventricular distention in heart failure and secondary to ventricular dysfunction in an acute coronary syndrome (ACS). ANGPTL4 is an important modulator of lipid metabolism and is involved in the regulation of vascular integrity and angiogenesis. Elevated levels of both biomarkers play a pivotal role in cardiovascular disease and serve as prognostic indicators of ACS and heart failure. Their prognostic significance has previously been explored [1]. Aims To assess the prognostic weighting in ACS of ANGPTL4 and BNP in a crosscontinental setting. Methods Patients admitted with chest pain of suspected coronary origin were recruited in Norway and Argentina, applying similar protocols, and matched by propensity scoring according to age, sex and use of statins, yielding 507 subjects in each group. A Cox regression model, adjusting for traditional cardiovascular risk factors, was ﬁtted for standardized logANGPTL4 and logBNP, respectively, with all-cause mortality within 5 years as the dependent variable. Multivariable analysis was performed for the assessment of the hazard ratio (HR) 95% confidence interval (95%CI). Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) for calculation of Area Under Curve (AUC) (95%CI) was performed in the combined populations for evaluation of crosscontinental biomarker utility. Results There was no significant difference in death rates at 5 years follow-up in the Argentinian (20.1%) and Norwegian (22.7%) cohort of patients, p=0.32. In the multivariable adjusted analysis, ANGPTL4 was independently associated with all-cause mortality in each cohort: [HR 1.65 (95%CI 1.35-2.01), p&lt;0.001] and [HR 1.30 (95%CI 1.07-1.57), p=0.008], respectively. The corresponding results for BNP were: [HR 1.61 (95%CI 1.28-2.04), p&lt;0.001] and [HR 1.65 (95%CI 1.29-2.10), p&lt;0.001]. AUC for ANGPTL4 in both populations combined was 0.718 (95%CI 0.680-0.756) and for BNP 0.730 (95%CI 0.691-0.769). Conclusion In the Argentinian cohort, ANGPTL4 carries the same risk for 5-years’ mortality as BNP does in the Norwegian cohort (Z=0.004; p= 0.997). In the combined population, BNP performs better than ANGPTL4 as judged by the AUC in the ROC analysis.
title: Angiopoietin like 4 (ANGPTL4) protein challenges brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) as a prognostic biomarker in patients admitted with chest pain of suspected coronary origin

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac troponins (cTn) are central to the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome. Fulfilment of the criteria for myocardial injury (cTn&gt;99th percentile) is common in non-cardiac diseases and cTn-release mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Cardiac troponin T (cTnT) release from skeletal muscle has been demonstrated in patients with skeletal muscle disorders. We hypothesized that re-expression of fetal cTn transcripts occurs in skeletal muscle of hospitalized patients without primary skeletal myopathy. Purpose To investigate skeletal muscle mRNA expression of cardiac and skeletal troponin isoforms in hospitalized patients with rhabdomyolysis (rhabdo), sepsis, and chronic kidney disease stage 5 (CKD5) compared with healthy controls. Methods In this prospective single-center study, patients with rhabdo (n=28), sepsis (n=49), and CKD5 (n=48) were enrolled within 48 hours of admission. All underwent ECG, echocardiography and high-sensitivity cTn measurement; patients with underlying cardiac disease were excluded. Patients with cTnT &gt;99th percentile, underwent fine-needle biopsy of the vastus lateralis muscle. Relative gene expression was quantified by RT-qPCR (TaqMan assays). Cardiac (TNNT2, TNNI3) and skeletal muscle troponin genes (TNNT1, TNNT3, TNNI1, TNNI2) were analyzed. Expression levels were normalized to PPIA (housekeeping gene) and calculated using the 2−ΔΔCt method relative to controls. Between-group differences were assessed using Welch’s t-test on ΔCt values without multiple-testing correction. Results Biopsies were obtained from controls (n=10), patients with sepsis (n=5), rhabdomyolysis (n=6), and CKD5 (n=7). All skeletal troponin gene-transcripts were downregulated in sepsis compared with controls (all p≤0.038) (figure 1). A similar downregulation was observed in patients with rhabdo for TNNI1, TNNI2 and TNNT3 (all p≤0.036). For the cTn genes, TNNI3 was significantly downregulated in sepsis (ΔCt difference 2.51 [95% CI −4.33 to −0.69], p=0.016), with a similar but non-significant trend in rhabdo (p=0.061). No significant changes were observed for TNNI3 in CKD5. In contrast, TNNT2 was not reduced in sepsis or in rhabdo and differed significantly in CKD5 (ΔCt difference −1.64 [95% CI 0.30 to 2.98], p=0.020), indicating relatively preserved or higher TNNT2 expression compared with controls. Conclusion Cardiac troponin transcripts were detectable in skeletal muscles in both healthy individuals and hospitalized patients with CKD5, Rhabdo and sepsis. Overall, acute systemic illness was associated with broad downregulation of skeletal muscle troponin gene transcripts, whereas TNNT2 expression appeared preserved and relatively increased in CKD5. These findings suggest disease-specific regulation of cTn genes in skeletal muscle and potential contribution to circulating cTn patterns. Confirmation at the protein level is warranted to clarify the contribution of skeletal muscle to circulating cTn.
title: Cardiac troponin I and T transcripts are detectable in skeletal muscle of patients hospitalized with non-cardiac disease

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac troponins (cTn) are biomarkers of myocardial injury and a cornerstone in the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome (ACS); However, cTn elevations are frequently observed in non-cardiac diseases and have been associated with adverse outcomes. The prognostic implications and differences between high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) and I (hs-cTnI) remain incompletely understood. Data on the comparative prognostic performance of cTnT and cTnI across disease states in patients with paired measurements are limited. Purpose To investigate the prevalence and prognostic value of hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI in five non-cardiac disease groups and to compare their relative prognostic performance. Methods We prospectively included patients with five non-cardiac conditions: chronic kidney disease stage 5 (CKD5), rhabdomyolysis, sepsis, stroke, and major orthopedic surgery, over a 1.5-year period. Patients were enrolled within 48 hours of admission and underwent ECG, echocardiography, and measurement of hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI . The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) defined as all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, or stroke. Secondary endpoints included prevalence of cTn elevation defined as &gt;99th percentile. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations between cTn levels and MACE. cTn concentrations were log2-transformed to model risk per doubling, with analyses performed separately and with mutual adjustment for the other troponin. Results Among 226 patients (mean age 73.6±14.1 years; 49.6% female), 166 (73.5%) had hs-cTnT above the sex-specific 99th percentile compared with 45 (19.9%) with elevated hs-cTnI (p&lt;0.001). Distribution of cTn elevations across disease groups are shown in fig 1. During a median follow-up of 1.44 years (IQR 1.09–1.86; reverse Kaplan–Meier), 29 patients (12.8%) experienced MACE: 25 (11.1%) died, 7 (3.1%) had a stroke, and none had myocardial infarction. In the overall cohort, both hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI were associated with incident MACE in separate models (hs-cTnT: HR 1.33 [1.15–1.54]; hs-cTnI: HR 1.13 [1.03–1.24] per doubling). In mutually adjusted models, hs-cTnT remained independently associated with MACE (HR 1.36 [1.10–1.69]), whereas hs-cTnI did not (HR 0.98 [0.86–1.12]) (fig 2). In subgroup analyses, the associations differed across disease groups. In CKD5, hs-cTnT was associated with MACE (HR 2.21 [1.33–3.67]), whereas in stroke, hs-cTnI was (HR 1.98 [1.10–3.56]) and hs-cTnT was not. Conclusion In patients with non-cardiac diseases, hs-cTnT elevations were significantly more prevalent than hs-cTnI elevations. Both cTnI and cTnT were associated with subsequent MACE. Notably, hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI demonstrated differential prognostic patterns across disease states, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms of myocardial injury and supporting a disease-specific interpretation of troponin elevations beyond ACS.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Cardiac troponin elevations and risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in five non-cardiac diseases

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined lipoprotein with proatherogenic, proinflammatory, and prothrombotic properties. Elevated Lp(a) levels are genetically determined and have been established as an independent causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Beyond its role in plaque initiation, Lp(a) has been implicated in the progression and calcification of atherosclerotic lesions through different mechanisms. In the setting of acute coronary syndromes (ACS), Lp(a) may play a dual pathophysiologic role, contributing not only to atherosclerotic plaque burden but also to plaque instability and thrombosis. Purpose To assess the prevalence and pattern of coronary artery disease (CAD) on Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) among ACS patients with elevated Lp(a). Methods We analyzed a subgroup of 74 patients with elevated Lp(a) from a prospective cohort of 1001 individuals with an ACS undergoing CCTA. Patients over 18 years of age with a diagnosis of ACS without ST elevation who did not meet high-risk criteria (hemodynamic instability, dynamic changes in the ST segment or T wave, ventricular arrhythmia, GRACE score &gt;140, refractory angina, heart failure or cardiorespiratory arrest) were included. Data collection was carried out between May 11, 2022 and February 20, 2026. Results 74 patients were included, with a mean age of 59 years, of which 40% were women and 60% men. Among the admission diagnoses, 20% were NSTEMI and 80% were unstable angina according to the 4th universal definition of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The median high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T value was 8 nanograms per litre (interquartile range, 5 to 15) for the first troponin sample, and 8 nanograms per litre (interquartile range, 7 to 20) for the second one. CCTA was not performed in 3 patients due to a CAC score &gt;400 AU. Among patients who underwent CCTA, 5% had no coronary plaques and 39% had non-obstructive coronary artery disease (&lt;50% stenosis), while 50% had obstructive disease and 6% had nondiagnostic studies. High-risk plaque features were identified in 20%. All 4 patients with normal coronary arteries were women (mean age 56 years). Conclusion In patients with an ACS undergoing CCTA, elevated Lp(a) identifies a population with a markedly low likelihood of normal coronary arteries and a high burden of both obstructive and non-obstructive CAD (95%), supporting its role as a potent pro-atherogenic driver of anatomical coronary disease. The observation that all normal studies occurred in women suggests potential sex-specific differences in the anatomical expression of Lp(a)-associated risk, warranting further investigation. Possible mechanisms may include hormonal influences, differences in plaque composition, microvascular predominance, or delayed phenotypic conversion to obstructive epicardial disease.CCTA findingsTable 1
title: Lp(a) rarely coexists without coronary atherosclerosis

abstract: Abstract Background Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) regulates lipid metabolism and inflammation and has been linked to plaque vulnerability and thrombosis. However, its prognostic value in stable post-ACS patients is unclear, and clinical data on its association with recurrent atherothrombotic events, independent of traditional risk factors, are lacking. Aim To investigate the association between ANGPTL4 levels measured one-year post-acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and the long-term risk of recurrent myocardial infarction (MI) and ischemic stroke, and independently of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors, including triglycerides. Methods Serum ANGPTL4 levels were measured by ELISA in 900 ACS patients from the SPUM-ACS registry one year post-event. Patients were grouped by ANGPTL4 tertiles (T1: ≤7.55, T2: 7.55–18.23, T3: ≥18.23 ng/mL). The primary endpoint was MI or ischemic stroke from day 365 onward. Associations were assessed via Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, triglycerides, obesity, statins, hypertension, and smoking. Baseline characteristics are shown in Table 1. Results For the composite outcome of myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke occurring from one year post-ACS onward, the adjusted event-free survival analyses demonstrated a clear gradient across ANGPTL4 tertiles. ANGPTL4 tertile 3 had the lowest event-free survival over 2920 days post-1year-landmark, tertile 2 showed an intermediate pattern, and tertile 1 had the most favourable event-free survival (T2 vs T1, p = 0.114; and T3 vs T1, p = 0.002), independent of age, sex, and 1-year diabetes, triglycerides, obesity (BMI), statin use, hypertension, and smoking (Figure 1). In an adjusted hazard ratio for composite MI or ischemic stroke from one year post-ACS onward, higher ANGPTL4 levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke during follow-up to day 2920 after multivariable adjustment. Compared with the lowest ANGPTL4 tertile (T1), the adjusted HR for the composite outcome was 1.35 (95% CI 1.15–1.59; p = 0.0003) for the middle tertile (T2) and 1.49 (95% CI 1.26–1.75; p = 2.0×10⁻⁶) for the highest tertile (T3). Among the covariates, higher 1-year triglyceride levels were also associated with a higher risk of myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke (HR 1.11; 95% CI 1.02–1.20; p = 0.012), whereas age, sex, diabetes, obesity, statin use, hypertension, and smoking at 1 year were not significantly associated with the composite endpoint in this model (all p &gt; 0.05) (Figure 2). Conclusion In stable post-ACS patients, elevated ANGPTL4 levels at one year emerged as an independent predictor of long-term recurrent myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke, after adjustment for traditional risk factors, including triglycerides, positioning ANGPTL4 as a biomarker of residual atherothrombotic risk.
title: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 identifies residual risk for atherothrombotic events in stable post-acute coronary syndrome patients: insights from the SPUM-ACS study

abstract: Abstract Background Point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays provide rapid turnaround times and are increasingly considered for use within guideline recommended 0/1-hour accelerated diagnostic protocols (ADPs). However, higher per-test costs raise concerns regarding overall economic impact. Randomised evaluations of real-world implementation remain limited. Purpose To assess the effect of implementing POC hs-cTnI testing within a 0/1-hour ADP on total index admission costs and 30-day specialist care costs. Methods This pre-specified secondary analysis of a single-centre randomised controlled trial included 1,494 adults presenting with suspected acute coronary syndrome. Participants were randomised 1:1 to 0/1-hour POC hs-cTnI testing or central laboratory hs-cTnT testing. Costs were estimated from the healthcare provider perspective using Norwegian patient-level costing and Diagnosis-Related Group frameworks. Resource use was extracted from electronic hospital records. Unadjusted mean cost differences were estimated using non-parametric bootstrap resampling. To account for potential confounders, a generalised linear model with gamma distribution and log link was fitted, adjusting for age, sex, adjudicated diagnosis, and disposition. Results Mean total index admission cost was €3,083 in the POC group and €3,126 in the control group (mean difference −€43; 95%CI −510 to 423). In adjusted analyses, costs remained similar between groups (adjusted mean difference €11; 95%CI −183 to 204). Mean total specialist care costs from admission to 30 days were €3,517 in the POC group and €3,413 in the control group (mean difference €105; 95%CI −405 to 615). Cost patterns were consistent across diagnostic and disposition subgroups. Conclusion In this randomised evaluation, implementation of POC hs-cTnI testing within a 0/1-hour ADP was cost-neutral at both index admission and 30 days. Despite higher per-test costs, overall episode costs were not increased. These findings suggest that biomarker pricing alone is unlikely to be a major driver of total healthcare expenditure when POC hs-cTn testing is integrated into emergency department pathways.Mean total index admission costs
title: Impact of point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin testing on index admission and 30-day costs: secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity (hs) cardiac troponin assays detect lower troponin concentrations, but the prognostic significance of these values in STEMI is uncertain. Methods We studied 5,136 STEMI patients. Initial and peak hs-cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) levels were stratified into deciles. Logistic regression assessed the association between hs-cTnT deciles and in-hospital mortality, using decile 1 (initial) and decile 2 (peak) as references. Results Each one-decile increase in initial hs-cTnT was associated with a 25% higher odds of in-hospital mortality (OR 1.25; 95% CI 1.17–1.33; p&lt;0.001). Mortality increased from 0.58% in decile 1 to 7.8% in decile 10, with decile 10 conferring &gt;15-fold higher odds of death (OR 15.22; 95% CI 4.70–49.72; p&lt;0.001). Peak hs-cTnT showed a bell-shaped association with mortality; decile 10 was associated with a sevenfold higher odds of death versus decile 2 (OR 7.01; 95% CI 3.43–14.33; p&lt;0.001), while higher mortality in decile 1 likely reflected early death before peak troponin levels. Conclusion Initial hs-cTnT shows a strong dose–response relationship with in-hospital mortality in STEMI. Very high peak hs-cTnT identifies a particularly high-risk subgroup that may benefit from intensified monitoring and management.Figure
title: Initial versus peak high-sensitivity troponin T for risk stratification in STEMI

abstract: Abstract Background Quantification of myocardial fibrosis carries important diagnostic and prognostic value. As access to biopsies for gold-standard histological evaluation is limited, and imaging has limited specificity and low accessibility, blood biomarkers reflecting fibrosis are an alternative strategy. Myocardial fibrosis comprises excessive fibrillar collagens, mainly type I, deposited by activated fibroblasts. Procollagen has peptides that are cleaved off by proteases prior to fibril incorporation that can reach the circulation; the type I collagen C-terminal propeptide (PICP) provides a stoichiometric representation of collagen type I production. Aims To assess circulating levels of a collagen I synthesis biomarker in association with patient characteristics, infarct size, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in elderly patients with a recent acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Methods The OMEMI trial (Omega-3 Fatty acids in Elderly with Myocardial Infarction) was a multicenter, randomized controlled trial of omega-3 supplements vs. placebo recruiting 1027 patients aged 70-82 years with AMI 2-8 weeks before the baseline visit, from 2012-2020. The overall trial was neutral. In this substudy, PICP was measured in serum (n=1022 baseline, n=896 at 2 years) using a commercially available ELISA kit (Microvue). Cox proportional hazards regression was used to analyze time to MACE (comprising stroke, AMI, heart failure, unscheduled revascularization, and death). Results Median (Q1-Q3) CICP levels were 94 (74-122) ng/mL at baseline and 97 (78-121) ng/ml at two-years follow-up. At baseline, higher PICP correlated with higher cardiac troponin T (cTnT, r=0.15, p&lt;0.001) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP, r=0.24, p&lt;0.001), but not with creatinine, demographics or comorbidities. Peak cTnT during the index AMI was not associated with PICP. Higher PICP associated with higher risk of MACE in unadjusted models (HR 1.48 [95%CI 1.10-2.00], p=0.009 per log unit increase in PICP), and after adjustment for age, sex, current smoking, BMI, systolic blood pressure, hypertension, diabetes and heart failure (HR 1.38 [1.02-1.86], p=0.034), but was no longer significant after adjustment for creatinine, cTnT and NT-proBNP (HR 1.18 [0.86-1.63], p=0.31). From baseline to two years, there was a small increase in PICP (median +4 [-15 to +23] ng/mL, p&lt;0.001). Greater delta PICP associated with male sex, but not peak cTnT during the index AMI. Baseline PICP ldid not modify the treatment effect of omega-3 on MACE (p-for-interaction=0.89). Conclusion Circulating levels of PICP 2-8 weeks post-AMI are associated with myocardial injury and stress, and patients with higher levels had greater risk of cardiovascular events during two years follow-up. PICP levels remained overall stable from baseline to two years. Our findings warrant further exploration into the use of collagen I fragment biomarkers in patient monitoring.Figure:Time to MACE by Q of PICP post-AMI
title: Circulating fragments of collagen I synthesis are associated with heart failure hospitalization and death two years after acute myocardial infarction in elderly patients

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) has enabled earlier risk stratification of patients with possible myocardial infarction to identify those suitable for discharge with a single measurement. However, early presenters require serial testing, which has limited the effectiveness of this approach. We hypothesize that the greater abundance and earlier release of cardiac myosin-binding protein C (cMyBP-C) could improve the effectiveness of single sample rule-out pathways. Methods In a secondary analysis of two prospective multi-centre cohort studies, cMyBP-C and hs-cTnT (fifth-generation) concentrations were measured using an automated high-throughput immunoassay analyser in stored lithium heparin plasma obtained at presentation from patients with possible myocardial infarction. The primary outcome was an adjudicated diagnosis of type 1, type 4b, or type 4c myocardial infarction or cardiac death at 30 days. Discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for cMyBP-C and cTnT in all participants and early presenters (≤3 hours from symptom onset) and compared using DeLong’s nonparametric test. The risk stratification threshold was defined as the highest cMyBP-C concentration achieving a negative predictive value (NPV) of 99.5% and sensitivity of 99%. The proportion of patients identified as low-risk were quantified and effectiveness determined within a single-sample rule out pathway for cTnT and a new pathway combining cTnT and cMyBP-C (Figure 1). Results In total 2,022 patients (61 [52-72] years, 38% females) were included with 39% (725/2,022) presenting within 3 hours in whom 12% (235/2,022) had a myocardial infarction or cardiac death at 30 days. The median cMyBP-C and cTnT concentration was 12 [6-36] and 7 [4-15] ng/L at presentation, respectively. Discrimination was higher for cMyBP-C compared to cTnT in all participants (AUROC 0.95 [95% CI 0.93-0.96] versus 0.93 [95% CI 0.92-0.95]; P=0.006) and in early presenters (0.94 [95% CI 0.93-0.96] versus 0.92 [95% CI 0.90-0.94]; P=0.005) (Figure 2). When testing was incorporated into a single-sample rule out pathway, the proportion of low-risk patients identified at presentation increased from 18% (313/1,788) using cTnT alone to 38% (681/1,788) when cTnT and cMyBP-C were combined (P&lt;0.001, McNemar’s test). Conclusions A novel cMyBP-C assay had greater discrimination for myocardial infarction at presentation compared to the current hs-cTnT assay. The combination of cMyBP-C for risk stratification with a normal cTnT concentration doubled the proportion of patients identified as low-risk at presentation compared to risk stratification using hs-cTnT alone.Figure 2
title: Cardiac myosin-binding protein C and the early risk stratification of patients with possible acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract The GRACE 2.0 risk score is a widely used tool for estimating mortality in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). However, it incorporates high-sensitivity troponin (hs-Tn) as a binary variable (elevated vs. non-elevated), which may limit its prognostic precision in contemporary practice. While a modified GRACE (modGRACE) model using continuous hs-troponin T (hs-TnT) has shown superior performance, evidence regarding its efficacy using continuous hs-troponin I (hs-TnI) is limited. This study aimed to validate the modGRACE score using continuous hs-TnI across two independent ACS cohorts. Data were analyzed from two prospective studies: the Freeman cohort (Newcastle, UK) and the GREECS cohort (Athens, Greece). The modGRACE score was calculated by substituting continuous hs-TnT with continuous hs-TnI using previously established regression coefficients. Predictive performance was evaluated by comparing the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and net reclassification improvement (NRI) for short-term (in-hospital, 30-day) and long-term (up to 20-year) outcomes. In the Freeman cohort, modGRACE demonstrated modest improvements in discrimination for in-hospital mortality (AUC 0.884 vs. 0.870) and 30-day mortality (AUC 0.883 vs. 0.868). A significant improvement in discrimination was observed for 1-year mortality (ΔAUC 0.015, p=0.01). Furthermore, risk reclassification was significantly improved for in-hospital (NRI=0.67), 30-day (NRI=0.69), and 1-year mortality (NRI=0.49; all p&lt;0.001). In the GREECS cohort, modGRACE significantly improved risk reclassification for 30-day mortality (NRI=0.56), 20-year cardiovascular mortality (NRI=0.85), and 20-year Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE; NRI=0.79; all p&lt;0.001). Integrating continuous hs-TnI into the modGRACE score leads to consistent and clinically meaningful improvements in risk reclassification compared to the standard GRACE 2.0 score. These findings support the clinical implementation of modGRACE for long-term risk stratification in ACS patients, regardless of whether hs-TnT or hs-TnI assays are utilized. Improved risk reclassification may help clinicians better tailor follow-up intensity and secondary prevention strategies.ROC curves for GRACE vs modGRACEReclassification value of modGRACE vs GRACE
title: Expanding the modified GRACE risk score to high-sensitivity troponin i: a multinational validation cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have enabled safe early discharge of patients at very low risk for myocardial infarction. We previously developed a single-sample rule out pathway using the ARCHITECT hs-cTnI assay and showed that it was safe and effective when implemented in practice. In a secondary analysis of the POC-ET (Point of Care Evaluation of High-sensitivity Cardiac Troponin) study, we evaluated this pathway with the Alinity hs-cTnI assay. Methods Patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction in the POC-ET (NCT05665127) study were included. The primary outcome was type 1, 4b or 4c myocardial infarction or cardiac death at 30 days. Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) was measured in stored materials at presentation and at 2 hours using the ARCHITECT and Alinity hs-cTnI assays. The sex-specific 99th percentile upper reference limit (URL) are 34 ng/L in male and 16 ng/L in female for both assays. Agreement was assessed with Bland-and-Altman method, Passing Bablok regression, and Pearson’s correlation coefficient. Distributions of presentation values were compared with KS test. Pathway performance was evaluated in the overall population and prespecified subgroups, excluding those with ischaemia on the electrocardiogram. The negative predictive value (NPV) and sensitivity were determined and proportion of patients identified as low and high risk compared with McNemar's test. Results In 986 patients (60 [51-70] years, 38% female), 78 (7.9%) had a primary outcome. Strong agreement was found in the raw cTnI measurements (99% samples within the limit of agreement; correlation coefficient : 0.98 [0.96-0.97], P&lt;0.001; Passing Bablok regression: slope 1.12 [1.11-1.13], intercept -0.16 [-0.18 to -0.13]). At presentation, distributions of cTnI values determined by the two assays were similar (Figure 1, P=0.810). Both assays showed comparable diagnostic performance using a risk stratification threshold of &lt;5 ng/L and the sex-specific diagnostic threshold, with identical NPV (100 [99.6-100]%) and sensitivity (100 [95.6-100]%) and similar proportions of patients stratified as low- (Alinity 67% versus ARCHITECT 67%) and high-risk (10% versus 9%). Overall, both assays identified 86% and 14% of patients as low- or high-risk, respectively (P=1.0; Figure 2). The corresponding NPV and sensitivity were 100 (99.7-100)% and 100 (95.6-100)% with Alinity, and 99.7 (99.0-99.9)% and 95.2 (85.6-99.0)% for ARCHITECT. Similar performance was observed across subgroups stratified by age, sex, symptom duration, history of myocardial infarction, and renal function. Conclusions The Alinity and ARCHITECT hs-cTnI assays can be used interchangeably in clinical practice with comparable safety, efficacy, and performance within a single-sample rule out pathway for patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome.
title: Single-sample rule out pathway for acute myocardial infarction using the Alinity high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) accelerated diagnostic pathways are central to acute coronary syndrome assessment. However, many centres continue laboratory-based strategies where turnaround time limits effective delivery of rapid rule-out algorithms. The system-level impact of implementing bedside point-of-care (POC) hs-cTn testing has not been robustly evaluated using time-series methodology. Purpose To evaluate the real-world operational impact of implementing a 0/2-hour POC hs-cTnI pathway in a high-volume tertiary emergency department (ED) using interrupted time series (ITS) and winter-matched difference-in-differences (DiD) analyses. Methods A hard-switch implementation of a bedside 0/2-hour high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I point-of-care pathway (i-STAT Alinity) replaced a laboratory-based 0/3-hour pathway (Alinity i). All adult (≥18 years) ED attendances undergoing troponin testing were included. Outcomes were emergency department length of stay (LOS) and 4-hour breach rate. A 75-day pre-implementation period was matched to a 75-day post-implementation period. Daily aggregated segmented regression was used to estimate immediate step and slope changes with Newey–West standard errors. Counterfactual modelling projected continuation of the laboratory 0/3-hour trajectory. Seasonal robustness was assessed using winter-matched DiD analysis. Results During the 75-day window, 2,769 troponin-tested attendances were analysed (mean 36.9/day). Baseline characteristics were comparable. Serial-testing patients demonstrated substantial raw improvement, with median LOS reducing from 466 to 417 minutes and 4-hour breach decreasing from 94.6% to 86.1%. ITS demonstrated significant immediate step reductions in median LOS overall (−65.4 minutes, 95% CI −123.0 to −7.8; p&lt;0.05) and in serial patients (−147.7 minutes, 95% CI −233.5 to −62.0; p&lt;0.001). Parallel reductions occurred in 4-hour breach rate (overall −11.7%; p=0.041; serial −15.2%; p&lt;0.001). No significant slope change was detected, consistent with an immediate structural effect attributable to bedside availability of hs-cTn results following POC implementation. Counterfactual modelling estimated a mean post-implementation LOS gap of 82.3 minutes (95% CI 54.9 to 109.7) overall and 178.0 minutes (127.2 to 228.8) in serial patients. Conclusion Implementation of bedside point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin testing was associated with significant and sustained reductions in ED LOS and 4-hour breach rates, most pronounced among serial-testing patients. Time-series and winter-matched analyses indicate these improvements were not explained by seasonal variation. These findings support POC hs-cTn as a scalable operational intervention to unlock effectiveness of accelerated rule-out pathways in high-pressure emergency care systems.ITS Median Length of Stay OverallWinter Matched DiD for Serial Patients
title: Real-world impact of implementing a 0/2-hour point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin pathway: interrupted time series and winter-matched difference-in-differences analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Chest pain is a common complaint and encompasses potentially life-threatening pathologies including acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but its diagnosis and management might be delayed by relying on conventional laboratory troponin. Point-of-care-testing (POCT) troponin I (TnI) assays may represent an emerging option to facilitate rapid diagnosis and expedite interventional measures. There is a paucity of data describing the diagnostic performance of POCT TnI, particularly in the Asian population. Purpose To evaluate the association between POCT TnI and conventional laboratory testing as well as clinical outcomes. Methods All patients presenting with acute chest pain to a hospital (a tertiary referral center in Hong Kong, China serving a population of 530,000) who underwent POCT TnI testing from 31/07/2023 to 30/06/2024 were included. The turnaround time for POCT TnI assays were compared against that of conventional laboratory troponin T (TnT). Cut-offs used for elevated POCT include 4ng/L (1) and 22.9ng/L (99th percentile). It was compared against final diagnoses including ACS. We compared the area under curve for POCT TnI vs conventional TnT in association with ACS diagnosis. The association between elevated TnI and modified HEART (mHEART) score as well as ACS diagnosis were evaluated. Results A total of 996 patients (mean age 68years, 48% female) underwent POCT TnI. The median (interquartile range [IQR]) turnaround time were 10 (8–14) minutes vs 145 (121–169) minutes for POCT TnI and conventional TnT, respectively (P&lt;0.001). The area under curve (95%CI) for POCT TnI and conventional TnT in association with ACS diagnosis were 0.879 (0.827–0.932) and 0.898 (0.863–0.93s), respectively (Fig.), and the difference was not significant (P=0.280). POCT TnI with level &lt;4ng/L has a negative predictive value (NPV) of 98.8 (95% confidence interval [CI] 97.6 – 100.0) % for ACS diagnosis, comparable to that of TnT (98.9, 95% CI 98.0-100.0). The median (IQR) of mHEART score for patients with and without elevated POCT TnI were 6 (5–8) and 3 (2–4), respectively (P&lt;0.001). When POCT TnI ≥ 99th percentile was combined with mHEART score ≥7, the positive predictive value for ACS diagnosis was 96.8% (95% CI 97.4-99.5). Conclusion(s) This is the first study evaluating utilization of POCT TnI testing in a large tertiary care centre in the Asia-Pacific region. Notably, a single measurement of POCT TnI&lt;4ng/L has achieved 98.8% NPV for ACS. Our results highlight that POCT TnI testing represents an emerging, rapid, and readily available test that may facilitate diagnosis and management of patients with chest pain. The scope of implementing POCT TnI needs to be broadened.Figure 1
title: Utilization of Point-Of-Care Testing (POCT) or troponin in patients with acute chest pain

abstract: Abstract Background Adiponectin exerts anti-inflammatory and vasculoprotective effects in healthy individuals. Conversely, in patients with established cardiovascular disease, elevations in circulating adiponectin are paradoxically linked to adverse outcomes; however, the underlying mechanisms remain completely unclear. Purpose To investigate the association between circulating adiponectin and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and to explore its effects on endothelial pro-thrombotic activity. Methods Plasma adiponectin was measured by ELISA in 4,787 ACS patients (SPUM-ACS) prior to coronary angiography. The primary endpoint was 1-year MACE. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and multivariable Cox regression, including age-stratified and restricted cubic spline analyses. Event-free survival across adiponectin tertiles was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis and log-rank testing. Early-passage (p6) as well as senescent (p16) primary human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) were exposed to adiponectin, and prothrombotic pathways were investigated by Western Blot and colorimetric activity assays. Results Circulating adiponectin correlated with age (Spearman ρ=0.32, p&lt;0.001). In multivariable Cox analysis, each doubling was associated with higher 1-year MACE, with a significant age interaction (P-interaction=0.020) (Figure 1). In patients ≥55 years, adiponectin independently predicted MACE (adjusted HR per doubling 1.28, 95% CI 1.14–1.44; p&lt;0.001), whereas no association was observed in those &lt;55 years (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.62–1.17; p=0.318). In older patients, risk increased across tertiles, with T3 vs T1 showing higher risk (adjusted HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.24–2.26; p&lt;0.001), while T2 vs T1 was not significant (HR 1.25, 95% CI 0.91–1.73; p=0.172). No tertile association emerged in younger patients. Restricted cubic splines confirmed a progressive risk increase with higher adiponectin only in older patients. In vitro, 50 µg/mL adiponectin increased TF activity in senescent vs early-passage HAECs, without changes in TF, PAI-1, or TFPI expression (Figure). Conclusions Elevated adiponectin predicts adverse cardiovascular outcomes after ACS in an age-dependent manner. Its ability to increase TF activity in senescent HAECs suggests a novel link between adiponectin and pro-thrombotic risk during vascular aging.
title: Adiponectin predicts MACE in older patients with an acute coronary event and augments endothelial tissue factor activity in senescent cells

abstract: Abstract Background Chest pain is one of the most frequent causes of emergency department (ED) visits and cardiology referrals. However, the diagnostic yield and outcomes of patients referred for outpatientreassessment after suspected unstable angina (UA) remain poorly characterized in real-world practice. Purpose To describe the demographic and clinical profile of patients referred to a tertiary outpatient clinic for chest pain and to evaluate the rate and predictors of diagnostic reclassification, as well as itsimplications on DAPT use and clinical outcomes." Methods Retrospective observational study including 892 consecutive patients evaluated between January 2024 and December 2025. Continuous variables are presented as mean (SD) and categoricalvariables as frequencies (%). Associations were assessed using the chi-square test, with p&lt;0.05 considered statistically significant. Analyses were performed using R version 4.4.2. Results Mean age was 63.9±11.9 years and 60.2% were male. Most referrals originated from the ED (96.7%). The leading referral diagnosis was UA (90.7%), followed by stable coronary artery disease(CAD) (6.9%) and other chest pain diagnoses (2.4%). At first outpatient visit, 58.2% were on DAPT and 86.0% on statins. Hypertension (77.6%), dyslipidaemia (59.4%), and diabetes (36.9%) were common; prior CAD was documented in 46.7%. After evaluation, the majority of patients initially referred to as UA were reclassified as chest pain without functionally significant ischemia (53.8%) or without obstructive coronary artery disease on invasive angiography (26.9%). Most patients were managed conservatively or discharged. Percutaneous coronary intervention occurred predominantly in UA referrals (89.7%). Conclusions In this real-world cohort, most patients discharged from the emergency department with suspected unstable angina (UA) were ultimately reclassified as having non-obstructive or functionally non-significant disease after structured outpatient evaluation. These findings raise important questions regarding the diagnostic accuracy of UA classification in the emergency setting. The high reclassification rate may reflect the inherent challenges of chestpain differential diagnosis under time pressure and clinical uncertainty. Alternatively, a subset of these patients may represent ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) or microvascular disease, entities systematically underdiagnosed without targeted investigation. Structured outpatient reassessment is essential to refine diagnosis, prevent overtreatment ( including prolonged and unnecessary use of DAPT) and optimize resource allocation in suspected acute coronary syndrome cases.Outpatient Diagnostic Reclassification FlowPatient Pathway, Profile and Outcomes
title: How often is unstable angina truly unstable? Insights from outpatient chest pain evaluation

abstract: Abstract Background The co-stimulatory signaling dyad of CD40 and CD40L is known as a potent inducer of cardiovascular inflammation and vulnerability of atherosclerotic plaques. A cytosine-to-thymidine transition (-1C&gt;T) in the Kozak sequence of the CD40 gene (rs1883832) lowers CD40 protein expression. The clinical implications of this variant in patients with acute coronary syndrome remains unkown. Purpose To determine whether CD40 rs1883832 genotypes are associated with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) at presentation and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods In the prospective Biomarkers in Acute Cardiac Care (BACC) cohort, 1,298 patients presenting with acute chest pain were genotyped for rs1883832 using a TaqMan assay (C/C, C/T, T/T). Patients were followed up to 7 years on a census-based system for the occurrence of MACE, defined as a composite of cardiovascular mortality, acute myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization, and hospitalization due to cardiac disease. The genotype-adjusted risk for MACE was tested using multivariable cox regression analysis. Associations between CD40 genotypes, presence of cardiovascular risk factors and confirmation of AMI were assessed by logistic regression. Results Relative abundances of the genotypes among all participants were 55.8% for C/C, 37.1% for C/T, and 7.2% for T/T. None of the genotype variants was associated with diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipoproteinemia, or a history of coronary artery disease (CAD). T/T carriers showed a strong trend towards an increased sex- and age-adjusted risk for AMI at admission (OR 1.58, 95% CI 0.95-2.64, p=0.078) and had a significantly increased risk for a composite endpoint of confirmed AMI and a history of previous AMI (OR 1.66 95% CI 1.04-2.65, p=0.035) in logistic regression analysis. During a median follow-up period of 5.2 years MACE occurred more often in patients with the T/T genotype (HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.01-2.11, p=0.046) compared to C/T (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.19, p=0.70) and C/C (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.76-1.16, p=0.54) carriers. This effect was independent of diabetes mellitus, hyperlipoproteinemia, arterial hypertension, smoking status and left ventricular ejection fraction in multivariable regression analysis. Conclusion Our data indicate that – unexpectedly – the T/T genotype of rs1883832 is associated with an enhanced risk for myocardial infarction and subsequent MACE. As this SNP impedes effective CD40 translation, our findings suggest a previously unrecognized protective dimension of CD40 signalling in human cardiovascular disease.
title: Enhanced risk for recurrent adverse cardiovascular events in homozygous carriers of the T-allele of CD40 SNP rs1883832

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin assays are integral to evaluating suspected myocardial infarction (MI) and form the cornerstone of the ESC 0/1h-hour diagnostic algorithm. Recently, a novel high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T assay (TnT hs Gen 6 assay) has been developed, but independent data on its diagnostic and prognostic performance remains limited. Purpose This study aims to determine the diagnostic and prognostic performance of the newly developed TnT hs Gen 6 assay using an ESC 0/1h-hour algorithm and to assess its prognostic value for 1-year overall mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Methods In a prospective cohort of patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected non-ST-elevation MI, diagnostic discrimination of TnT hs Gen 6 measured at time of presentation and after 1 hour was tested using area under the curve (AUC) analyses. Diagnostic performance was assessed using priorly derived cut-off concentrations according to the ESC 0/1h algorithm-approach. Head-to-head comparisons between the new TnT hs Gen 6 assay and established assays were performed. Prognostic performance of TnT hs Gen 6 for 1-year overall mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE) was analyzed using Cox regressions adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, arterial hypertension, hypercholesterinemia, diabetes mellitus, and history of coronary artery disease (CAD). Results Among 1,415 patients (mean age 64 years and 64.2% male), MI was diagnosed in 12.1%. The novel TnT hs Gen 6 assay demonstrated excellent discrimination with an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI 0.84,0.90) on admission and 0.91 (95% CI 0.89,0.93) after 1 hour. Using a 0h cut-off &lt;8ng/L or &lt;18 ng/L and Δ 0/1h of &lt;2 ng/L enabled rule-out in 54.3% (95% CI 51.7%, 57.0%) with a NPV of 99.5% (95% CI 98.7%, 99.9%); sensitivity was 97.7% (95% CI 94.1%, 99.4%). For rule-in, a 0h cut-off ≥112 ng/L or a Δ 0/1h ≥10 ng/L yielded a PPV of 58.5% (95% CI 51.9%, 64.9%) and specificity of 92.2% (95% CI 90.6%, 93.6%) with rule-in of 16.5% (95% CI 14.6%, 18.6%). In the rule-out group, overall mortality at one year was extremely low with 0.9% compared with 7.1% in the observe group and 12.0% in the rule-in group (p&lt;0.001). Irrespective of triage category and adjusted for age, sex, and cardiovascular risk factors, TnT hs Gen 6 concentrations were independently associated with 1-year overall mortality (hazard ratio 1.39 [95% CI 1.28,1.51) and MACE (hazard ratio 1.22 [95% CI 1.15,1.29]). Conclusions The novel TnT hs Gen 6 assay demonstrates high safety and diagnostic accuracy for rapid rule-out and rule-in of MI and offers valuable prognostic information regarding 1-year overall mortality and MACE. These findings support its clinical utility for both diagnosis and risk stratification in patients with suspected MI.Graphical Abstract TnT hs Gen 6
title: Diagnostic validation of a novel high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T assay

abstract: Abstract Background Early risk stratification is paramount for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). While various uric acid-based indices exist, their comparative prognostic value remains unclear. Purpose We aimed to identify the optimal index and explore potential non-linear relationships. Methods We analyzed 39,941 STEMI patients from a large-scale real-world database. The primary endpoint was three-month hard cardiac events (cardiac death and re-infarction). The secondary endpoint was a composite of cardiac death, re-infarction, and non-fatal stroke (3-point major adverse cardiovascular events [MACE]). Phase one involved a head-to-head comparison of five indices: serum uric acid (SUA), SUA/estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), SUA/albumin (UAR), SUA/high-density lipoprotein (HDL) (UHR), and SUA/creatinine. Phase two assessed the incremental predictive value via net reclassification index (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to examine nonlinear associations. Results Among all tested indices, SUA/eGFR demonstrated the highest discriminatory power for three-month hard endpoints (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.658 vs. 0.550–0.620 for others, Figure 1B) and three-month three-point MACE (AUC: 0.644 vs. 0.550–0.610 for others, Figure 1C). Notably, restricted cubic spline analysis unveiled a significant J-shaped association between SUA/eGFR and hard endpoints (P for non-linearity &lt; 0.05), indicating that both excessively low and high ratios confer elevated risk—a finding that reframes the traditional linear risk paradigm (Figure 1A). Adding SUA/eGFR to the clinical baseline model significantly improved discrimination (AUC increased from 0.747 to 0.752, P &lt; 0.001, Figure 2A) and yielded meaningful risk reclassification (NRI: 0.98%, 95% CI 0.38%–1.56%, P &lt; 0.05; IDI: 0.57%, P &lt; 0.05). Decision Curve Analysis further confirmed that the SUA/eGFR-enhanced model provided a higher net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities (Figure 2B). Conclusion The SUA/eGFR ratio is the superior uric acid-based index for predicting early hard cardiac events in STEMI patients. Its distinctive J-shaped relationship with outcomes—challenges conventional linear risk assessment and identifies a vulnerable window at both extremes. Integrating this simple, readily available ratio into established clinical models significantly enhances prognostic accuracy and supports personalized risk management at the bedside.J-shaped risk and index AUC comparisonIncremental model value and DCA curves
title: Superiority of the SUA/eGFR Ratio in predicting early hard events in STEMI: A large-scale head-to-head comparison and J-shaped risk discovery

abstract: Abstract Background The diagnostic approach to symptomatic acute myocardial injury without overt signs of myocardial infarction remains poorly standardized. Cardiac computed tomography (CT) is usually used to exclude vascular causes (pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection and coronary disease), while cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference for myocardial tissue characterization. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) represents a major technological advancement of CT; however, its improvement of soft-tissue characterization remains poorly explored in this setting. Purpose To evaluate if PCCT can aid in the differential diagnosis of myocardial injury combining vascular and myocardial tissue evaluation. Methods From November 2023 a prospective cohort of patients was enrolled. Inclusion criteria were: symptomatic laboratory evidence of acute myocardial injury, and either a low-to-intermediate pre-test probability of coronary artery disease (CAD) - with PCCT used as first-line imaging - or documented angiographically unobstructed coronary arteries. Main exclusion criteria were: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, severe renal impairment (eGFR ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m²), iodine contrast allergy. Results 24 consecutive patients were enrolled. PCCT was feasible and provided a diagnosis in 100% of patients confirmed by CMR: 14 (58%) myocarditis, 1 (4%) “hot-phase” of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) due to delayed enhancement and fatty infiltration of the right ventricle (subsequent genetic testing revealed a DSG2 class IV mutation), 1 (4%) Takotsubo syndrome, 8 (33%) ischemic aetiologies. In 10 patients (42%) there was an agreement between clinical suspicion and PCCT diagnosis, all suspected of myocarditis. In the remaining 14 patients (58%), PCCT led to diagnostic reclassification: ischemic lesions were found in two patients suspected of aortic dissection affected by Marfan and Takayasu syndrome respectively. A myocarditis and an ACM were diagnosed in two patients with suspect ischemic aetiology due to the angiographic finding of anomalous origin of coronary arteries. A myocarditis was found in a suspected pulmonary embolism due to previously undocumented right ventricular dilatation in Ebstein anomaly. Two myocarditis were diagnosed in patients with a suspected ischemic aetiology. Five suspected myocarditis had a limited ischemic lesion with microvascular obstruction (in one case a paradoxical embolism was suspected due to the detection of an interatrial defect). One patient with suspected Takotsubo syndrome showed a complex CAD with ischemic lesion in the distal anterior and apical segments. One patient suspected of recurrent myocarditis was reclassified as Takotsubo syndrome. Conclusions PCCT enables early and accurate differentiation between ischemic and non-ischemic causes of myocardial injury, impacting diagnostic classification and guiding subsequent management.Central illustrationbaseline characteristics
title: Photon counting cardiac CT for differential diagnosis of myocardial injury

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) is among the most dreadful complications of acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Endothelial dysfunction and vascular leakage are hallmarks of CS pathophysiology; however, biomarkers reflecting these early processes are lacking. The adrenomedullin (ADM) system—the inactive precursor glycine-extended ADM (ADM-Gly), the activating enzyme peptidylglycine α-amidating monooxygenase (PAM), and bioactive ADM (bio-ADM)—modulates vascular tone and permeability. Purpose To investigate associations of ADM system components with CS risk after ACS. Methods ADM-Gly, PAM, and bio-ADM were measured in 4,098 (SPUM-ACS, Switzerland) and 824 (FAST-MI, France) ACS patients without CS on admission. The primary endpoint was in-hospital CS. Associations were evaluated using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models with sequential adjustment for demographic and clinical risk factors, NT-proBNP, and haemodynamic indices. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were applied to assess potential nonlinear dose–response relationships across biomarker concentrations. Incremental prognostic value beyond the ORBI risk score was quantified by comparing models with and without ADM biomarkers, assessing changes in discrimination (ΔAUC), reclassification (NRI), and model fit (ΔAIC), with external validation in FAST-MI.
