Results Higher ADM-Gly and bio-ADM, but not PAM, were associated with systemic inflammation and haemodynamic compromise (Figure 1). In RCS analyses, both biomarkers showed non-linear dose–response relationships with CS risk. Both ADM-Gly and bio-ADM independently predicted CS in SPUM-ACS (adjusted odds ratio (OR) per log2 increase, 1.44, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.22–1.71, P&lt;.001 and OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.10–1.70, P=.004) and FAST-MI (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.34–2.48, P&lt;.001 and OR 1.55, 95% CI 1.15–2.10, P=.004). Addition of these two biomarkers to the ORBI score improved discrimination (ΔAUC 0.02), reclassification (NRI 0.229), and model fit (ΔAIC −26.9), with consistent findings in the external validation cohort (Figure 2). PAM showed no independent prognostic value. Conclusions ADM-Gly and bio-ADM, but not PAM, independently predict in-hospital CS in patients with ACS and improve early risk stratification.
title: The adrenomedullin system predicts cardiogenic shock in acute coronary syndromes

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) lowering therapy with statins is effective for secondary prevention in patients with cardiovascular disease after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Epidemiological studies have shown that serum apolipoproteins (Apos) (A1, A2, B, C2, C3, and E) are associated with atherosclerosis risk, but their role in secondary prevention remains unclear, as statins strongly influence their levels. Our preliminary study showed that single apolipoprotein levels were insufficient to evaluate residual risk under statin therapy. Based on the pathological role of each apolipoprotein and our previous findings on apolipoprotein A2 (Apo A2), we hypothesized that combining Apo A2 and apolipoprotein C3 (Apo C3) may help identify high-risk patients for future cardiovascular events. Purpose We aimed to evaluate whether Apo A2 and Apo C3 levels predict major cardiovascular events (MACEs) in post-PCI patients on statins. Methods We analyzed 649 patients who underwent PCI for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), had serum apolipoprotein A1, A2, B, C2, C3, and E measured, and were on statin therapy between 2016 and 2022. Based on median values of Apo A2 and Apo C3, we defined lower Apo A2 (&lt;24.2 mg/dL) or higher Apo C3 (&gt;8.3 mg/dL) as potential risk factors. Patients were categorized into three groups: 1) L–A2 and H–C3 group (both low–Apo A2 and high–Apo C3), 2) L–A2 or H–C3 group (either low–Apo A2 or high–Apo C3), and 3) H–A2 and L–C3 group (both high–Apo A2 and low–Apo C3). Moreover, patients were categorized into two groups using a receiver operating characteristic curve based on the Apo A2/Apo C3 ratio and the incidence of MACEs, yielding an optimal cut–off ratio of 2.418. The primary endpoint was MACEs, which included cardiovascular death, non-fatal ACS, ischemic stroke, heart failure hospitalization, and any repeat revascularization. Results During a median follow-up of 622 days, 124 patients (19.0%) experienced MACEs. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that both the L-A2 and H-C3 group and the low Apo A2/Apo C3 ratio group had a significantly higher MACE incidence than the other groups, respectively (L–A2 and H–C3: 51.5% vs L–A2 or H–C3: 34.7% vs H–A2 and L–C3: 22.3%, log-rank test, p = 0.030; 54.0% vs 27.4%, log-rank test, p = 0.001, Figure 1). Multivariable Cox proportional hazard analysis indicated the L–A2 and H–C3 group as an independent predictor of MACEs (hazard ratio [HR] 1.59, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06–2.38, p =0.025). Analysis of the Apo A2/Apo C3 ratio as a continuous variable indicated that a higher ratio was associated with a lower HR for MACE (Wald test, p = 0.02, Figure 2). Conclusion Patients with low Apo A2 and high Apo C3 levels remain at a high cardiovascular risk despite statin therapy. The Apo A2/Apo C3 ratio may serve as a novel marker for residual cardiovascular risk stratification beyond LDL-cholesterol.Kaplan–Meier curves for MACEsContinuous analysis for MACEs
title: The Apolipoprotein A2/Apolipoprotein C3 ratio predicts future cardiovascular events after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients receiving LDL-cholesterol-lowering therapy

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is recognized as an independent cardiovascular (CV) risk factor, with the ESC defining high risk at ›105 nmol/L. While Lp(a) is genetically determined and considered stable over time, its interaction with acute inflammatory responses and myocardial injury during acute coronary syndrome (ACS) has not been fully elucidated. Purpose To investigate associations between Lp(a), demographic characteristics, risk factors, and biomarkers of myocardial necrosis in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ACS. Methods We determined Lp(a) levels, clinical and laboratory parameters in patients admitted to our institution over 18 months for ACS with PCI (n=281, STEMI: 154, NSTEMI: 75, UAP: 52). Results Lp(a) showed non-normal distribution with median 20.8 nmol/L (IQR: 8.7-80.6). Sixty patients (21%) were in the high CV risk group based on ESC Lp(a) criteria. Patients were divided into quartiles based on Lp(a) levels (Q1 median: 7.0 nmol/L [IQR: 7.0-7.3] vs. Q4 median: 162.7 nmol/L [IQR: 113-213]). No significant differences were found in demographic parameters (hypertension, diabetes, smoking, prior ACS and stroke, statin use; p›0.05). Female sex showed a trend toward higher Lp(a) (p=0.1). Importantly, patient age did not differ significantly between the lowest and highest Lp(a) quartiles (Q1 median: 55 years [IQR: 48-67] vs. Q4 median: 58 years [IQR: 50-68], p=0.26). Both pre- and post-PCI hsTroponin T levels were significantly higher in the highest Lp(a) quartile (pre-PCI hsTroponin T: Q1 median: 146 ng/L [IQR: 27-797] vs. Q4 median: 580 ng/L [IQR: 111- 1288], p=0.015; post-PCI hsTroponin T: Q1 median: 279 ng/L [IQR: 70-1261] vs. Q4 median: 944 ng/L [IQR: 288-3215], p=0.016). Significant positive correlations were found between Lp(a) and both pre-PCI hsTroponin T (ρ=0.15, p‹0.05) and post-PCI hsTroponin T in the total population (ρ=0.17, p‹0.05). Similarly, hsCRP was significantly higher in the highest Lp(a) quartile (Q1 median: 3.66 mg/L [IQR: 1.33-9.4] vs. Q4 median: 9.2 mg/L [IQR: 3.7-37.8], p=0.0001), and a significant positive correlation was detected between Lp(a) and hsCRP (ρ=0.24, p‹0.05). Conclusions Twenty-one percent of ACS patients undergoing PCI in our cohort had Lp(a) levels exceeding the ESC-recommended high cardiovascular risk threshold. Significantly higher pre- and post-PCI hsTroponin and hsCRP levels were observed in patients with elevated Lp(a) in the upper quartile. These findings were corroborated by significant positive correlations between Lp(a) and both hsCRP and hsTroponin biomarkers. Our results indicate that elevated Lp(a) is associated with increased atherothrombotic and inflammatory burden in acute coronary syndrome, suggesting a potential role for Lp(a) assessment in risk stratification during the acute phase.
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) is associated with increased inflammatory and myocardial injury markers in acute coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac troponin T (cTnT) can be found in the circulation in intact, mildly fragmented and short, highly fragmented forms. During the early stages of myocardial infarction intact and mildly fragmented long cTnT forms predominate. In contrast, in later myocardial infarction stages, as well as in renal disease, Takotsubo syndrome, atrial fibrillation and after strenuous exercise cTnT elevations are mainly due to short highly fragmented cTnT forms. However, the molecular forms contributing to postoperative cTnT elevation in cardiac surgery remain unclear. Purpose To investigate the composition of circulating cTnT after on-pump and off-pump cardiac surgery Methods Lithium-heparin plasma samples were obtained from 149 patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery preoperatively and at 3–6 hours, 1 day, and 3–7 days postoperatively. Intact and mildly fragmented cTnT forms were measured with an in-house investigational high-sensitivity (hs) long cTnT assay and hs-cTnT was measured with Roche Elecsys 5 gen assay in each sample. Statistical comparisons were performed using nonparametric tests and median values [25th-75th percentiles] are reported. Results None of the included patients met the criteria for clinical perioperative myocardial infarction. Peak hs-cTnT exceeded 70x upper reference limit (URL) in 34 (23.0%) patients with a median peak concentration of 636 ng/L. Long cTnT peaked at 3–6 h (542 [250–880] ng/L) with 79 (53.4%) patients exceeding 70x URL. Long cTnT declined rapidly reaching 11 [7–17] ng/L at 3–7 days values. Only one patient (0.7%), who developed new left bundle branch block, exceeded 10x URL at 3–7 days. In contrast, hs-cTnT remained elevated at 3–7 days (161 [100–293] ng/L), and 57% of patients exceeded 10x URL. Peak long cTnT correlated with cardiopulmonary bypass duration (r= 0.398, p&lt;0.001) and was significantly higher after on-pump surgery vs off-pump surgery (603 [361–924] ng/L vs. 23 [11–52] ng/L, p&lt;0.001). The ratio of long cTnT to hs-cTnT at peak release was also higher after on-pump surgery (91% [72–118] vs. 24% [13–34], p&lt;0.001). Conclusions The results show that long cTnT constitutes the main component of early troponin release after on-pump surgery while smaller fragments dominate after off-pump surgery. The rapid decline of long cTnT may offer diagnostic advantages later in the postoperative course.Figure
title: Composition of circulating cardiac troponin T after on-pump and off-pump cardiac surgery

abstract: Abstract Background and Aim Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality despite advances in primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Current risk stratification tools lack precision in predicting recurrent cardiovascular events, highlighting the need for novel biomarkers. This study aimed to evaluate the synergistic prognostic utility of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) mutations and C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. Methods In this prospective, longitudinal cohort study, we enrolled ACS patients and performed deep targeted sequencing of 42 CHIP-associated genes alongside CTI quantification. Results In a prospective cohort of 1,388 ACS patients, CTI combined with CHIP identified a high-risk phenotype. Patients with high CTI (≥cutoff) and any CHIP mutation had a significantly higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) compared to those with no CHIP (58.1% vs. 35.9%, p=0.020). Multivariable analysis revealed that in the low-CTI cohort, CHIP mutations—particularly common CHIP, TET2, and ASXL1 mutations—were independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (adjusted HR up to 1.94 for common CHIP mutation, 95% CI 1.09–3.45, p=0.024). Conversely, no significant association between CHIP and mortality was observed in the high-CTI cohort. When analyzed as a continuous parameter, a higher CTI per standard deviation increment was an independent predictor of MACE. This association was significantly modified by the presence of CHIP mutations, type 2 diabetes (p for interaction=0.022), and chronic kidney disease (p for interaction=0.014). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed significantly worse survival and higher mortality (log-rank p&lt;0.001), MACE rates (log-rank p=0.023)and cardiac death (log-rank p=0.019) in patients with concomitant high CTI and CHIP mutations. Conclusion Our findings advocate for integrating CHIP and CTI into risk models to guide personalized post-PCI management, while future studies should explore targeted anti-inflammatory therapies for CHIP-positive ACS patients and validate these biomarkers in diverse populations.KM curve of MACE by CTI and CHIPKM curve of death by CTI and CHIP
title: The predictive value of C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index and clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential among patients with STEMI---from a prospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) frequently mimics acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and its diagnosis currently relies on clinical history, cardiac imaging, and exclusion of obstructive coronary artery disease, often resulting in delayed diagnosis and unnecessary invasive coronary angiography. Purpose To develop and externally validate a biomarker-based score for early differentiation of TTS and ACS. Methods In 3,615 consecutive patients with ACS (n=3,469, SPUM-ACS) or TTS (n=146, InterTAK) enrolled between 07/2011 and 07/2023, established and emerging cardiovascular biomarkers were measured before invasive coronary angiography. We applied machine learning-based recursive feature elimination to assess the importance of variables for diagnosing TTS. Top-ranking variables were included in a biomarker-based version of the InterTAK diagnostic score (short BioTAK) for early diagnosis of TTS. The score was developed in 1,823 patients presenting with TTS or ACS at a university hospital between 07/2011 and 01/2018 and externally validated in 1,792 patients presenting with TTS or ACS at a different time and/or study centre. Diagnostic performance of the score was assessed according to a range of performance metrics. Results Based on diagnostic variable importance and clinical considerations, biomarkers of congestion (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, peptidylglycine α-amidating monooxygenase), atherosclerotic plaque instability (soluble lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor-1), and lipid metabolism (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol), as well as female sex were incorporated into the score. BioTAK achieved excellent discrimination and good calibration (development cohort: AUC 0.96, [95%CI 0.94–0.98], calibration slope 1.00 [0.81–1.19], calibration-in-the-large 0.00 [-0.43–0.43]) and maintained similarly high performance on external validation (AUC 0.93 [0.90–0.96], calibration slope 0.95 [0.77–1.14], calibration-in-the-large 0.00 [-0.37–0.38]). Score values ≥35 points ruled in TTS with 98.6% specificity (PPV 60.7%) and ≤28 points ruled out TTS with 91.3% sensitivity (NPV 99.6), classifying 89.7% of patients into rule-in or rule-out categories prior to angiography. Conclusions A simple biomarker-based score enables accurate early rule-in and rule-out of TTS before coronary angiography. BioTAK has the potential to streamline diagnostic pathways and reduce unnecessary diagnostic procedures in patients presenting with suspected ACS.Figure 1:Variable importance diagnosing TTS.Figure 2:BioTAK Diagnostic performance.
title: Biomarkers for early diagnosis of Takotsubo syndrome: a model development and validation study

abstract: Abstract Background Young women presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) represent a distinct clinical phenotype with heterogeneous mechanisms: premature atherosclerosis and non-obstructive coronary disease. In the WAMIF study (Women with Acute Myocardial Infarction), a French national multicenter cohort of women under 50 years, 15.6% had no significant coronary stenosis. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], a genetically determined atherogenic lipoprotein, is associated with long-term cardiovascular risk and may improve risk stratification when combined with LDL cholesterol and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). To date, there are no data on the evaluation of these biomarkers, particularly the lipid profile, in a population of young women in the acute phase of myocardial infarction. Purpose To characterize Lp(a) levels in women &lt;50 years presenting with myocardial infarction (MI) and to explore their distribution across coronary disease severity as well as within combined lipid-inflammatory biomarker profiles. Methods This is a post-hoc analysis of the prospective, observational WAMIF cohort including women &lt;50 years hospitalized for ACS. Lp(a) levels were measured from the centralized biobank. LDL cholesterol and hs-CRP were previously collected. Elevated Lp(a) was defined according to established high-risk thresholds. High Lp(a) categories and a combined lipid-inflammatory biomarker burden, defined by the number of elevated biomarkers, were described according to atherosclerosis status and coronary disease severity. Results Among 314 women (median age: 44.0 years [IQR: 39.0–47.0]), 60.8% had ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The median LDL-C level was 1.21 g/L (IQR: 0.9–1.46), with 22.3% of patients having a level greater than 1.5 g/L. The median hs-CRP level was 6 mg/L (IQR: 3.0–12.3), with 51.5% of patients having a level greater than 5 mg/L. Preliminary analyses show that elevated Lp(a) levels are common in this population, with 21.7% of patients having Lp(a) levels ≥ 0.50 g/L. Elevated Lp(a) levels appear to be associated with a greater atherosclerotic burden, with elevated Lp(a) levels observed in 23.5% of patients with atherosclerosis, compared to 12.8% in those without. A progressive increase in the prevalence of atherosclerosis was observed with increasing biomarker burden, from patients without elevated biomarkers to those with at least two elevated biomarkers (Figure 1). The extent of coronary artery disease also worsens with the cumulative effect of elevated biomarkers (Figure 2). Conclusion We report the first descriptive analyses in this population suggesting that higher Lp(a) levels and an increased burden of combined lipid and inflammatory biomarkers are more frequently observed in patients with more extensive atherosclerosis. These findings support the measurement of Lp(a) in young women with ACS and could help identify candidates for treatments aimed at reducing Lp(a).Biomarkers and extent of CAD
title: Lipid risk profile in ACS in young women: contribution of Lp(a) measurement: ancillary analysis of the WAMIF study

abstract: Abstract Background Growing evidence supports a central role of inflammation and immune activation in the pathophysiology of myocardial infarction. Endothelial inflammatory response is a key component of this process. Vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), a mediator of leukocyte–endothelium interaction, reflects endothelial dysfunction and immune activation in acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Purpose To assess the association between baseline soluble VCAM-1 (sVCAM-1), left ventricular systolic function assessed by three-dimensional echocardiography (3DE), and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ACS. Methods This prospective, single-center, observational study included 150 consecutive ACS patients. Baseline sVCAM-1 levels were measured using ELISA at admission. Left ventricular volumes and ejection fraction were assessed by 3DE within 24 hours. Patients were followed for 4 years for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, recurrent myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, or unstable angina requiring revascularization. Correlation, ROC, and Kaplan–Meier survival analyses were performed. Results Mean age was 54.7 years, 35% were women, and STEMI was present in 64% of patients. Mean 3D-LVEF was 47.6%. During follow-up, 31 patients (21%) experienced MACE, and 8 (5.3%) died from cardiovascular causes. Baseline sVCAM-1 levels were inversely correlated with 3D-LVEF (r = −0.45, p = 0.04) (Figure 1A). ROC curve analysis demonstrated that baseline sVCAM-1, the optimal cut-off value derived from the Youden index being 4.76 (log10 scale), provided good discrimination for cardiovascular events (AUC 0.77, 95%CI 0.68–0.86) (Figure 1B). Kaplan–Meier analysis showed progressively lower event-free survival across increasing tertiles of sVCAM-1 (Figure 1C). Conclusions Baseline sVCAM-1 is associated with impaired left ventricular systolic function and adverse cardiovascular outcomes following acute coronary syndromes. These findings reinforce the central role of endothelial activation and persistent inflammation in the pathophysiology of post-infarction remodeling. sVCAM-1 may serve as a prognostic biomarker for risk stratification, but also as a potential tool to identify patients who could benefit from future targeted anti-inflammatory strategies.Prognostic significance of sVCAM-1 in ACS
title: Baseline VCAM-1 predicts left ventricular dysfunction and cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndromes

abstract: Abstract Introduction Early identification of patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains challenging in the emergency department (ED), as current diagnostic pathways rely mainly on serial high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) measurements and may delay decision-making. Artificial intelligence–based electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) models may enable rapid, non-invasive risk stratification at presentation. A novel AI-ECG model, AiTiA MI v2.0.0, was developed in a South Korean population to perform the early triage of patients with chest pain. Its performance in large European ED cohorts remains unknown. Methods In this secondary analysis of two prospective cohorts, adult patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) were enrolled in cohort A, an international multicenter study, and in cohort B a single-center study. Cohort A required written informed consent for participation, whereas Cohort B consecutively enrolled all eligible patients. All cases underwent central adjudication of the final diagnosis. Patients were excluded if a 12-lead ECG at presentation was unavailable or deemed invalid by the AI-ECG. As part of routine care, hs-cTnT was measured at presentation in all patients. Prespecified cut-offs from the original model were applied for initial rule-out and rule-in classification, followed by the baseline thresholds of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-hour algorithm following a theoretical ED workflow integration. AMI was defined as a composite of type 1 and type 2 MI. Findings Among 5,031 and 7,565 patients with an available AiTiA MI v2.0.0 probability and hs-cTnT measurement in cohort A and cohort B, respectively, the median age was 60 years (p25–p75: 47–73) and 58 years (p25–p75: 44–73), and 1584 (32%) and 2933 (39%) were female. AMI occurred in 964 patients (19%; 769 type 1 MI and 195 type 2 MI) and in 1384 patients (18%; 1,125 type 1 MI and 257 type 2 MI, 2 missing). When predefined thresholds were applied in cohort A (Figure 1) AiTiA MI v2.0.0 ruled out 706 patients (14%), achieving a sensitivity of 97.6% (95% CI: 96.6–98.5%) and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 96.7% (95% CI: 95.3–97.9%). In cohort B (Figure 2), the model ruled out 1,437 patients (17.5%), with a sensitivity of 97.5% (95% CI: 96.7–98.3%) and an NPV of 97.6% (95% CI: 96.8–98.3%). Among the 23 false-negative patients in cohort A, 9 had type 1 MI. Among the 34 false-negative patients in cohort B, 14 had type 1 MI. All had hs-cTnT superior to 5ng/l. Interpretation When validated in two prospective European cohorts recruiting consecutive adult patients presenting to the ED with symptoms suggestive of AMI, the raw thresholds performance of AiTiA MI v2.0.0 had good performance, comparable to its development. The number of false negatives could be explained from a distribution shift in AMI adjudication, with a higher ratio of type1 MI/type 2 MI in the European cohorts.AiTiAMI Triage Followed by hs-cTnT (Cohort A)AiTiAMI Triage Followed by hs-cTnT (Cohort B)
title: External validation of an artificial intelligence-based electrocardiogram algorithm for early rule-out of acute myocardial infarction in two large European cohorts

abstract: Abstract Background The Queen of Hearts (QoH) model is an electrocardiogram (ECG)-based convolutional neural network (CNN) model for the early diagnosis of occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI), showing good diagnostic performance. Because model derivation was performed in a retrospective cohort of patients presenting to a cardiovascular facility with acute coronary syndrome, external validation in an emergency department (ED) setting in unselected patients is lacking. Purpose To externally validate the performance of the QoH model and compare it with standard ischemic ECG features and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT). Methods In a multicentre international diagnostic study, we prospectively enrolled unselected patients presenting to the ED with symptoms suggestive of myocardial infarction. For this analysis, patients were excluded if a digital ECGs was not available. Final diagnoses were centrally adjudicated by two independent cardiologists using all available medical records. The primary endpoint was OMI, defined as angiographic evidence of an acute culprit lesion with a TIMI flow 0-1, or TIMI flow 2-3 with a peak hs-cTnT ≥1000 ng/L. TIMI flow grades were assessed from coronary angiography reports and images by two interventional cardiologists. Model performance was assessed by means of discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) and calibration. Results Among 4728 patients with an available digital ECG, OMI was the final diagnosis in 300 (6.3%) patients. Patients with OMI had a higher probability score (40.4% vs 0.12%, Figure 1a). Model discrimination was high (AUC 0.88; 95% CI:0.85-0.90), outperforming ischemic ECG features, Figure 1b. The calibration plot showed risk underestimation at low and overestimation at high predicted probabilities, improving after recalibration, Figure 2. When QoH was added to a rich-for-prior-information model including hs-cTnT, discrimination was improved (AUC base model: 0.94 [0.93-0.95] vs extended model: 0.96 [0.95-0.97]). The originally derived rule-in probability ≥50% triaged 222 (4.7%) patients towards rule-in (specificity 98.2% [97.8-98.5]; positive predictive value [PPV] 64.0% [57.5-70.0]), resulting in a better performance compared to the European Society of Cardiology rule-in hs-cTnT cutoff ≥52 ng/L (specificity 93.1% [92.4-93.8]; PPV 41.8% [37.7-46.1]). Conclusions In ED patients with chest pain, an ECG-based CNN model demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting OMI, outperforming traditional ECG features of ischemia and providing added value to hs-cTnT. Rule-in performance was good showing superior accuracy for detecting OMI compared to the established ESC single-measurement hs-cTnT strategy.
title: External validation of an electrocardiogram-based convolutional neural network model for the early diagnosis of occlusion myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Introduction Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined lipid particle associated with residual cardiovascular risk and its measurement is recommended at least once in adulthood. Although recent evidence suggests that Lp(a) should ideally be measured outside acute inflammatory states, it is still frequently assessed during hospitalisation for acute coronary syndromes. However, evidence remains limited regarding whether acute-phase measurement during acute myocardial infarction (AMI) differs meaningfully from delayed testing. Purpose To compare Lp(a) concentrations measured during the acute phase of MI with values obtained after clinical stabilisation, and to characterise the clinical profile of the studied cohort. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted at a tertiary centre, comparing Lp(a) levels obtained during hospitalisation with results from the first outpatient visit ≥6 weeks post-infarction. Paired samples were analysed using a paired t-test. Clinical, angiographic, and laboratory data were collected, including lipid profile, inflammatory markers, cardiac biomarkers and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Results A total of 89 patients were included (mean age 59 ± 13 years; 81% male). Most of them presented with STEMI (71%), Killip class I (67%) and single-vessel disease (49%); 97% underwent PCI and 82% achieved complete revascularisation. LVEF remained stable from hospitalisation to follow-up (46.4 ± 9.1% vs 46.1 ± 7.5%). LDL-C fell markedly (122 ± 47 to 53 ± 22 mg/dL), as did total cholesterol, triglycerides, hs-TnI, NT-proBNP and C-reactive protein, all with p&lt;0.001 (as shown in Table 1). In contrast, Lp(a) rose significantly from the acute to stable phase (53.0 ± 44.7 to 66.2 ± 61.3 mg/dL; p = 0.002), without notable changes in haematological or renal parameters, suggesting biological stability despite the acute stress. Conclusion In patients with AMI, Lp(a) levels measured during the acute phase are significantly lower than those obtained after clinical stabilisation. These findings support measuring Lp(a) outside the acute phase to ensure accurate cardiovascular risk stratification. Nevertheless, given that Lp(a) is genetically determined and the observed variation is modest, post-acute measurements remain appropriate for long-term prognostic assessment.
title: Acute-phase versus post-stabilisation lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a paired analysis

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) elevation is frequent in critically ill patients without acute coronary syndrome (ACS). However, its independent prognostic value and incremental contribution beyond established severity scores in real-world cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) populations remain debated, especially over long periods with potential assay drift. Purpose To evaluate the association between peak hs-cTn and in-hospital mortality in non-ACS CICU admissions and to quantify its incremental discriminative value over SAPS3 severity score using year-standardized troponin. Methods Retrospective single-center cohort including 15,271 CICU admissions (July 2011–February 2025). ACS admissions were excluded based on primary diagnosis code consistent with myocardial infarction (I21–I22) or unstable angina (I20.0). Exposure was defined as the peak troponin concentration during the CICU stay; high-sensitivity troponin assays were used throughout the entire study period at our institution. To address temporal drift, troponin was log-transformed [log(1+hs-cTn)] and standardized within admission year (z-score). The primary endpoint was in-hospital death. Incremental discrimination was assessed by comparing ROC AUC of a base model including SAPS3 points only versus an extended model SAPS3 + year-standardized hs-cTn, using 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Association adjusted for SAPS3 was estimated with logistic regression. Results After excluding ACS (n=1,740), 13,531 non-ACS admissions remained; troponin was available in 9,329 (68.9%). Median age was 67 years (IQR 53–80) and 52.8% were male. In-hospital mortality was 5.6% (520/9,329). Mortality increased across troponin quartiles: Q1 3.6% (83/2,333), Q2 5.3% (123/2,332), Q3 5.8% (136/2,332), Q4 7.6% (178/2,332). After adjustment for SAPS3, hs-cTn remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted OR 1.16 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI 1.08–1.25, p&lt;0.001); Q4 vs Q1 showed higher risk (adjusted OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.44–2.65, p&lt;0.001). Discrimination improved from AUC 0.862 (SAPS3-only) to AUC 0.866 (SAPS3 + hs-cTn), ΔAUC +0.004. Conclusion In a large real-world CICU cohort of non-ACS admissions, peak hs-cTn—standardized by admission year—was independently associated with in-hospital mortality and do not provided a incremental gain in discrimination beyond SAPS3.
title: High-sensitivity troponin and in-hospital mortality in non-ACS cardiac ICU admissions: a 14-year cohort

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) triggers myocardial injury, systemic inflammation with potential fatal sequelae. The ischaemia burden may be associated with dysfunction of peripheral organs such as liver and intestine. Circulating proteins released from these organs may mirror patient risk. Purpose To investigate the association of early circulating hepato-intestinal proteins with heart failure (HF) and the risk of 1y-mortality in AMI patients. Methods From the SPUM-ACS cohort, 77 AMI patients who died within 1y follow-up (66 cardiovascular deaths) were matched 1:1 to event-free controls by age, sex, AMI subtype, symptom onset to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) time window, and recruiting site. Heparin plasma (collected &lt;24h after symptom onset) was analyzed by Olink proteomic panels and mass spectrometry using a library-free workflow. Differential expression was assessed by moderated linear models (limma). Conditional logistic regression and unsupervised clustering were applied to proteins remaining changed after false discovery rate adjustment. Results 24 proteins showed higher expression levels in patients who died than controls (Fig.1A). STRING analyses clustered them into three groups: acute inflammatory response, histones, and metabolic proteins mainly expressed in liver or intestine (Fig.1B). Pathway analysis revealed enrichment in growth factor signaling, cytokine regulation, and ethanol oxidation pathways. Differences of these metabolic proteins between cases and controls were more evident in patients who came with shorter symptom onset to PCI time (&lt;6h) (Fig. 1C). After excluding proteins with less than 50% detection rate, FABP6 (fatty-acid binding protein 6), HAO1 (hydroxyacid oxidase 1), and LDHA (lactate dehydrogenase A) were identified to associate with risk of death after adjustment for renal function (eGFR, estimated glomerular filtration rate) (adjusted p=0.028; Fig.2A). Clustering using these hepato-intestinal proteins identified a subgroup with high expression of these proteins and Killip Class ≥2 (p&lt;0.001, Fig.2B), indicating a close association between hepato-intestinal markers in blood and clinical signs of acute HF in AMI patients. Conclusions We identified a group of soluble hepato-intestinal proteins associated with clinical signs of HF and 1-year mortality in AMI patients. This study may provide novel insights into multi-organ damage and death risk in patients with AMI.
title: Proteomic profiling identifies hepato-intestinal proteins as novel biomarkers for multi-organ injury and 1-year mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background The Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction defines myocardial injury as an elevation in cardiac troponin (cTn) above the 99th percentile upper reference limit (URL) of a healthy reference population. Establishing precise URLs for cTn assays is therefore important, however recommended URLs across studies are heterogeneous and URLs for cTnI and cTnT are not bioequivalent. This study assesses the robustness of current methods for establishing cTn reference limits. Methods Generation Scotland participants (N=17,328) with high-sensitive cTnI and cTnT measurements and without self-reported cardiovascular disease were available for analysis, including 9,039 participants that fulfilled criteria of a healthy subcohort according to International Federation of Clinical Chemistry (IFCC) recommendations. Percentiles were determined using the non-parametric statistical method as recommended by the IFCC. To assess how the confidence interval around the 99th percentile varies with group size, we drew 50 independent samples for group sizes of 200, 400, 800, 1,600, and 6,000 individuals. Results Across key percentiles (0.5, 1, 2.5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95, 97.5) , cTnI values were lower than cTnT (median [IQR]: 1.8 [0.6–2.9] ng/L versus 3.0 [1.5–5.6] ng/L), yet this reversed at the 99th percentile with cTnI higher than cTnT (20.4 ng/L versus 17.6 ng/L), consistent with the presence of more uncommon high values in the upper tail of the cTnI distribution. At sample sizes of 400 male and female individuals recommended by the IFCC, the estimated 99th percentile is associated with a wide confidence interval, spanning approximately 10 ng/L from the lower to the upper bound for cTnT and 30 ng/L for cTnI. Increasing the size of reference cohorts (N&gt;1,600) partially improved the robustness of the estimates of the 99th percentile, but did not resolve the fundamental fragility of relying on extreme tail 99th percentile values, even when applying stringent IFCC criteria for a healthy cohort. Sex-specific analyses showed similar results. Conclusion Our findings underscore fundamental limitations in the current definition of cardiac troponin URL. The 99th percentile is unstable at recommended minimum sample sizes and remains sensitive to extreme values even as sample sizes increases. Future approaches should consider more statistically robust thresholds, combined with greater individualization by sex, age, and comorbidity, to improve clinical relevance and precision.Percentiles Generation Scotland
title: Towards a more robust estimation of the decision threshold for high-sensitivity cardiac troponins

abstract: Abstract Background ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) may be complicated by left ventricular thrombus (LVT) formation, which increases the risk of systemic thromboembolism five-fold. Given the role of inflammation in LVT formation, inflammatory biomarkers could be useful markers of LVT risk. Purpose To investigate whether inflammatory biomarkers are associated with LVT formation in patients treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI) after STEMI. Methods Patients were sampled from a single-center prospective cohort study of STEMI patients treated with pPCI from 2006-2008. Inflammatory biomarkers were analyzed in samples obtained immediately before pPCI and included, C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell (WBC) count, mannose-binding lectin (MBL), osteoprotegerin (OPG), ostepontin (OPN), alpha-defensin, and neutrophil gelatine-associated lipocalin (NGAL). The endpoint was LVT detected on echocardiography during the index event or any follow-up echocardiogram. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression was applied to investigate the association between log-transformed inflammatory biomarkers and LVT. A p-value&lt;0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The study included 372 patients with STEMI treated with pPCI of whom 177 (48%) had an anterior infarction. The mean age was 62 ± 11 years, and 280 (75%) were men. Of these, 31 (8%) developed LVT. No significant difference was found in troponin I (TnI), CRP, or WBC count between patients who developed LVT formation compared with patients who did not (TnI: 148 vs 100 ng/L, p=0.17; CRP: 4 vs 3 mg/L, p=0.11; WBC count: 13.6 vs 12.4 x 109/L, p=0.058). By extension, no differences in MBL, OPG, or OPN were observed. However, patients with LVT formation had significantly higher alpha-defensin (280 vs 223 μg/L, p=0.009) and NGAL (154 vs 118 μg/L, p=0.005) levels at baseline. Similarly, only alpha-defensin and NGAL were significantly associated with LVT in univariable logistic regression (alpha-defensin: OR 1.10 (1.03-1.17), p=0.005, per 10% increase; NGAL: 1.09 (1.02-1.17), p=0.013, per 10% increase, Figure 1a-b, respectively). After multivariable adjustment, the results were unchanged (alpha-defensin: OR 1.12 (1.04-1.20), p=0.002, per 10% increase; NGAL: 1.10 (1.01-1.20), p=0.025, per 10% increase). Both alpha-defensin and NGAL increased AUC compared with established predictors of LVT formation (LVEF, LAD culprit lesion, LV aneurysm), albeit not significantly (AUC baseline 0.787; AUC baseline and alpha-defensin=0.813, p=0.17; AUC baseline and NGAL=0.833, p=0.056). Conclusion In patients with STEMI treated with pPCI, alpha-defensin and NGAL were associated with LVT formation, indicating that these inflammatory biomarkers may be useful for identifying patients at risk of LVT formation.Figure 1aFigure 1b
title: Inflammatory biomarkers and left ventricular thrombus formation after ST-elevation myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Single-sample rule-out pathways for myocardial infarction are safe and effective, reducing length of hospital stay and unnecessary admission. However, one in four patients require a second high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) measurement as they present early or have intermediate values. We evaluated novel approaches to further optimise the performance of the single-sample rule-out pathway. Methods In patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome undergoing hs-cTnI measurements in the Emergency Department, we evaluated whether use of the limit of detection (&lt;2 ng/L) in early presenters and earlier serial measurements (1 versus 2 hrs) would increase the proportion ruled out and reduce length of stay without compromising diagnostic performance for spontaneous myocardial infarction or cardiac death at 30 days (Figure 1). Performance was validated in three external cohort studies and the effectiveness was modelled in a real-world cohort of consecutive patients. Results In 1,840 patients (59 [51-71] years, 64% males), 495 presented within 2 hours of symptom onset and 301 (16%) had a spontaneous myocardial infarction or cardiac death at 30 days. The proportion ruled out using a threshold of &lt;5 ng/L at presentation was 39% for a negative predictive value (NPV) of 99.6% (95% confidence interval 98.9 to 99.9%) and a sensitivity of 98.8% (97.4-99.7%). Use of a lower 2 ng/L threshold in early presenters increased the proportion ruled-out at presentation from 39% to 47% with similar NPV (99.5 [98.9-99.8]%) and sensitivity (98.7 [96.9-99.5]%). In 2,846 patients from the external validation cohorts, the optimised pathway increased the proportion ruled out at presentation by 2-13% with similar diagnostic performance compared to the original single sample rule-out pathway (Figure 2). In 6,096 consecutive patients evaluated using the original pathway, applying the optimised pathway would reduce the proportion of patients requiring a second measurement from 33% to 29% and the average length of hospital stay by 24 mins (6.8±4.1 versus 6.4±3.9 hrs, P&lt;0.001). Conclusions An optimised single-sample rule-out pathway incorporating a lower risk-stratification threshold for early presenters and earlier serial hs-cTn measurements in those not ruled out at presentation could further improve effectiveness and reduce length of hospital stay without compromising diagnostic performance.Figure1.pngFigure2.png
title: Optimisation of the single-sample rule-out pathway for acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background The ESC 0/1-hour algorithm effectively facilitates the rapid rule-out of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), yet the subsequent identification of unstable angina (UA) remains a diagnostic bottleneck. Current pathways often rely on resource-heavy, radiation-intensive imaging, exacerbating Emergency Department (ED) overcrowding. While our validated No Objective Testing Rule novel (NOTR novel) regression model, based on the original No Objective Testing Rule (NOTR), offers a robust solution, the capacity for State-of-the-Art (SOTA) Machine Learning (ML) to capture high-dimensional, non-linear clinical interactions remains under-utilised. Methods In a secondary analysis of a large-scale, multicentre prospective international cohort (n=3,395), we included patients with suspected ACS in whom AMI was ruled out via the ESC 0/1h-algorithm. The primary outcome was 30-day adjudicated Major Adverse Cardiac Events (MACE), comprising AMI, UA, and cardiovascular death, including index events. We benchmarked the NOTR novel against two sophisticated architectures: Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), a high-performance gradient-boosting framework, and Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN), a revolutionary Transformer-based tabular foundation model designed for in-context learning. All models utilised identical predictors: original NOTR variables plus sex, 1h-high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), absolute change of hs-cTnT (1h–0h), ST-segment depression, and exercise-induced chest pain. Findings were validated in an international cohort (n=704) and a national cohort (n=2,423). Results In this first application of a tabular foundation model for ED risk stratification, TabPFN achieved high safety for the primary 30-day endpoint, demonstrating a sensitivity of 99.3% and NPV of 99.9% in the national cohort (n=2,423), and 100% sensitivity and NPV in the international cohort (n=704). While discriminative performance (AUC 0.81–0.85) was comparable to established XGBoost and regression models, TabPFN uniquely leveraged in-context learning to provide the highest diagnostic efficacy. Specifically, TabPFN achieved a rule-out proportion of 47.5%, exceeding the 45.9% and 41.4% observed for the regression baseline and XGBoost, respectively. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and potential of integrating Transformer-based architectures into clinical decision support systems. Conclusion(s) This study represents a successful implementation of TabPFN for risk-stratifying chest pain patients after AMI rule-out. These results mark a significant step toward a new paradigm in AI-driven triage; further refinement of such foundation models holds the potential to surpass traditional machine learning benchmarks and fundamentally transform emergency cardiac evaluation.TabPFN vs. ML: Safety and Efficacy in Triage
title: Next-generation risk stratification: leveraging TabPFN to Predict MACE in chest pain patients after acute myocardial infarction rule-out in the emergency department

abstract: Abstract Background Advances in high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) assay technology have improved the accuracy of detecting and quantifying cardiomyocyte injury in patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS). However, hs-cTnT concentrations may still be influenced by confounding factors unrelated to myocardial infarction. The novel sixth-generation high-sensitivity troponin T assay (hs-TnT-Gen6) offers enhanced analytical sensitivity and improved tolerance to haemolysis. Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance and reclassification safety of the hs-cTnT Gen 6 assay in a prospective, unselected real-world cohort. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study including 423 consecutive patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) of a tertiary university hospital in whom current standard hs-cTnT levels were measured. For each patient, a parallel blinded measurement using a hs-cTnT-Gen6 assay was performed in the hospital’s central laboratory. Categorical classification (low vs. high) was defined using a pre-specified threshold of 13 ng/L for standard hs-cTnT and the sex-specific 99th percentile upper reference limits for the Gen6 assay (18 ng/L for females; 32 ng/L for males). All patients were followed until discharge, and final diagnoses were adjudicated. Results Baseline characteristics of the study population (n = 423; median age 65.0 years [50.0–79.5]; 58.9% male), stratified according to sex-specific 99th percentile thresholds, are summarised in Table 1. A strong correlation was observed between the standard hs-cTnT and hs-cTnT-Gen6 assays (r = 0.98; p &lt; 0.001). Bland–Altman analysis showed minimal differences within the normal range (≤13 ng/L), with deviations generally within ±5 ng/L. Above the 99th percentile, the absolute difference increased with concentration; at 200–400 ng/L, hs-cTnT Gen 6 values exceeded standard hs-cTnT by approximately 180–260 ng/L. Compared with the standard assay, hs-cTnT-Gen 6 reclassified 44 of 423 patients (10.4%): 43 cases (10.2%) were reclassified as normal, whereas only one (0.2%) was reclassified as high (Figure 1). Among the 43 downwardly reclassified patients, who represented 21% of initial high values with standard hs-cTnT, ACS was ruled out in 41 cases (95%), whereas the remaining two patients presented early with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, respectively. The single upwardly reclassified patient had not a final diagnosis of ACS. The categorical Net Reclassification Improvement was −9.9% (95% CI −12.9% to −7.0%). Conclusion The hs-cTnT Gen 6 assay may improve the precision of troponin-based risk stratification in the emergency department. In particular, it accurately reclassified a substantial proportion of low-risk individuals, which may contribute to more efficient resource utilisation.
title: Clinical performance of a sixth-generation high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T assay compared with standard high-sensitivity troponin T in a real-world cohort

abstract: Abstract Introduction Serum lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] has been considered an important biomarker of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. While large trials such as ODYSSEY OUTCOMES have demonstrated the prognostic value of comprehensive apolipoprotein profiling including ApoB, ApoC-III, and Lp(a) in post-acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients, data from Central Asian populations remain scarce. Our study was performed in a tertiary hospital in our city, Kyrgyzstan. Nevertheless, there is a shortage of studies on Lp(a) together with ApoC and ApoB in this population. Aim of the study To investigate the possible association of Lp(a) with ApoC and ApoB and the severity of coronary stenosis in patients with acute coronary syndrome. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted on patients with ACS to evaluate the association of serum Lp(a) with ApoB, total ApoC, and the severity of coronary stenosis. The diagnosis of ACS was confirmed by appropriate ECG signs and elevated serum troponin. Blood samples for measurement of Lp(a) (nmol/L), ApoB (mg/dL), and ApoC (mg/dL) were collected within 24 hours of admission. All patients with ACS underwent coronary angiography with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in a tertiary hospital. Stenosis severity was assessed as the percentage of diameter stenosis in major epicardial coronary vessels (left anterior descending, left circumflex, right coronary artery, and left main coronary artery). Written informed consent for participation in the study was obtained from all participants. The study protocol was approved by the local Bioethics Committee. SPSS version 16.0 was used for statistical analysis. Data were presented as Me (25th; 75th percentiles). Statistical significance was considered at p &lt; 0.05. Results A total of 90 patients (69 men, 21 women) with ACS were included, with a median age of 56.5 (51; 63) years overall: 54 (47; 61) years for men and 60 (58; 65) years for women (p &lt; 0.001). The median Lp(a) level was 3.0 (1.32; 10.9) nmol/L overall: 3.3 (1.4; 11.7) nmol/L in men and 1.37 (1.1; 3.14) nmol/L in women (p &lt; 0.05). The median ApoB level was 27.1 (21.1; 33.1) mg/dL overall: 26.8 (21.5; 33.1) mg/dL in men and 27.3 (21.1; 32.9) mg/dL in women, with no significant difference. The median ApoC level was 659.1 (141.5; 887.5) mg/dL overall: 665.9 (141.5; 838.6) mg/dL in men and 592.0 (152.9; 895.4) mg/dL in women (not significant). Correlation analysis revealed that Lp(a) correlated with gender: r = 0.247; p &lt; 0.05. Lp(a) was not correlated with the percentage of stenosis in major coronary vessels. Coronary angiography was performed within the first 2 hours of admission with evaluation of stenosis severity. Conclusion Lp(a) levels in patients with ACS were significantly higher in men than in women. However, no association was confirmed between Lp(a) and ApoB, ApoC, or the percentage of stenosis in major coronary vessels. Further, larger-scale prospective studies are needed in the future.
title: Gender differences in lipoprotein(a) levels among patients with acute coronary syndrome in a tertiary hospital in our city: a cross-sectional study

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac troponin concentrations are lower in females than males. Therefore, sex-specific 99th percentile upper reference limits are recommended to identify myocardial injury and for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction, to ensure similar performance in both sexes. We assessed equivalence of sex-specific diagnostic thresholds using high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) I and T assays in an interrupted time series study cohort, where all sites initially used a hs-cTnI assay and later switched to a hs-cTnT assay. Methods This secondary analysis was conducted in the two periods when a hs-cTnI or a hs-cTnT assay was used to assess patients presenting with suspected acute coronary syndrome. The association between identified myocardial injury and the outcome of subsequent myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalisation, or cardiovascular death at 1 year and was evaluated using cause-specific regression models adjusting for age, sex, history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ischaemic stroke, and diabetes. Index diagnoses were adjudicated according to the fourth universal definition of myocardial infarction in a subset of consecutive patients (n = 1,000 in the hs-cTnI period and n = 1,000 in the hs-cTnT period). The proportion of patients with adjudicated diagnosis was compared using chi-squared test. Results In the study period using the hs-cTnI assay, 21% (1,431/6,961) males (median age 69 IQR [59-79] years) and 22% (1,369/6,185) females (76 [66-84] years) were identified with myocardial injury, among whom 16% (229) and 15% (199) had previous myocardial infarction. In the period using the hs-cTnT assay, 35% (2,384/6,825) males (72 [61-81] years) and 41% (2,397/5,878) females (76 [67-83] years) were identified with myocardial injury, and 9% (211) and 7% (158) had previous myocardial infarction. Similar proportions of patients had an adjudicated diagnosis of myocardial infarction using both the hs-cTnI and the hs-cTnT assays (male: 15% versus 13%, P=0.607; female: 10% versus 12%, P=0.379; Figure 1). Those identified with myocardial injury had higher risk of subsequent myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalisation, or cardiovascular death at 1 year using both the hs-cTnI assay (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 4.28 95% confidence interval [3.43, 5.34] in males and 6.17 [4.46, 8.54] in females) and the hs-cTnT assay (aHR: 7.50 [5.32, 10.58] in males and 22.80 [9.62, 54.00] in females). Conclusions Sex-specific thresholds identified an equivalent proportion of males and females with myocardial injury using the hs-cTnI assay, but not the hs-cTnT assay. Similar proportion of males and females had an adjudicated diagnosis of myocardial infarction using both assays despite greater proportions were identified with myocardial injury using the hs-cTnT assay.Figure1.pngFigure2.png
title: Sex-specifc thresholds using cardiac troponin I and T assays for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Introduction Assessment of suspected acute coronary syndrome involves a triad of high sensitive troponins, electrocardiogram and clinical assessment. However, it is a matter of controversy whether early rule-out and discharge is better affected by formal risk score evaluation, which seeks to incorporate all 3 of these parameters. We investigated the optimum means of rule out using a single presentation hs-cTn in a preplanned analysis of the MACROS 2 randomised controlled trial. Methods Early rule-out by risk scores (using hs-cTn) was compared to the guideline recommended SSRO threshold for the 3 hs-cTns [including hs-cTnT Roche elecsys, hs-cTnI (Siemens Attellica) and hs-cTnI (Quidel triage true, point of care)]. In total, 3543 patients were enrolled in the MACROS 2 randomised controlled trial of the ESC 0/1 versus 0/3 hour accelerated pathway. Clinical details and symptom evaluation were undertaken directly by patient interview at the time of presentation with acute chest pain. Event adjudication for myocardial infarction (MI), by paired consultant cardiologists, was undertaken using Abbott Alinity hs-cTnI following the 4th universal definition. The following risk scores (RS) were determined (by code) with relevant details, including specific symptoms automatically extracted from the research database: HEART, recalibrated HEART (recalibrated to limit of detection[LOD]), TIMI and T-MACS. National follow up was achieved by means of a Unique ID linked database. Clinical effectiveness was denoted by percentage of cohort that could be rule-out and safety by 30 day MACE (major adverse cardiac event rate- adjudicated type 1 myocardial infarction, unplanned coronary revascularisation and cardiovascular death) Results From December 2021 to July 2024, 3543 individual patients with suspected ACS were prospectively recruited from two major emergency departments (EDs) in Northern England and 100% follow-up was achieved from 13 hospitals nationally. The mean age was 59 years, 53% were male, 6.9% had an index type 1 myocardial infarction and 7.8% had a MACE within 30 days. The results are demonstrated in the table. For hs-cTnT (Roche elecsys) only recalibrated HEART≤3, T-MACS &lt;2% and hs-cTnT &lt;5 ng/l alone had &gt; 98% sensitivity for 30-day MACE rule-out. However, T-MACS was most efficient in terms of discharge followed by recalibrated HEART≤3. For hs-cTnI (both Quidel TT POC and Siemens attellica) however all risk scores ruled out considerably less patients than using SSRO alone. Conclusion SSRO with low level hs-cTn alone was consistently safe across all troponins, hs-cTn T or I. T-MACS and recalibrated HEART were both safe and modestly effective in improving rule-out with single presentation hs-cTnT. However, the converse was true for hs-cTnI, with RSs ruling out considerably less patients than low level hs-cTnI alone.Risk score performance across hs-cTn's
title: Can composite risk scores improve upon single sample rule-out performance in suspected acute coronary syndrome? A preplanned analysis of the MACROS 2 randomised controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) is the cornerstone biomarker for diagnosing myocardial injury and risk stratification in acute coronary syndromes (ACS). However, troponin reflects myocardial necrosis and does not capture other major pathophysiological pathways influencing prognosis. Systemic inflammation and renal dysfunction are key determinants of adverse outcomes in ACS and may provide complementary prognostic information beyond myocardial injury alone. Purpose To assess the incremental prognostic value of a multimarker strategy integrating hs-cTnI, C-reactive protein (CRP), and creatinine for early prediction of in-hospital mortality in patients presenting with ACS. Methods This prospective cohort study included 2,567 consecutive adults admitted with ACS between January 2023 and June 2025. Biomarkers were measured at emergency department presentation. Prespecified thresholds were hs-cTnI ≥17.5 µg/L, CRP &gt;6 mg/L, and renal injury defined as creatinine &gt;11 mg/L and/or urea &gt;0.36 g/L. Clinical variables including symptom-to-admission delay and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were recorded and incorporated into multivariable models. The primary endpoint was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration was assessed using calibration intercept and slope, and clinical usefulness was examined using decision-curve analysis. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations). Results The median age was 61 years (interquartile range 44–71), and 55% were men. In-hospital mortality occurred in 503 patients (19.6%). In multivariable analysis, all three biomarkers were independently associated with mortality:hs-cTnI ≥17.5 µg/L (OR 2.61, 95% CI 2.04–3.35; p&lt;0.001)CRP &gt;6 mg/L (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.42–2.41; p&lt;0.001)renal injury (OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.76–3.07; p&lt;0.001) Compared with hs-cTnI alone, the multimarker model provided significant incremental prognostic discrimination for in-hospital mortality (AUC 0.71 vs 0.65; p&lt;0.001) and demonstrated excellent calibration (calibration slope 0.99). Decision-curve analysis showed a consistent net clinical benefit across predicted risk thresholds between 10% and 50%, supporting the clinical utility of the multimarker approach. Conclusion A multimarker strategy integrating hs-cTnI, CRP, and creatinine significantly improves early mortality prediction in ACS compared with troponin alone. By simultaneously capturing myocardial injury, systemic inflammation, and cardio-renal dysfunction, this simple and widely available biomarker triad enhances early risk stratification and may support rapid triage and risk-guided management in patients presenting with acute coronary syndromes.ROC curves hs-cTnI vs triad model in ACS
title: Incremental prognostic value of a cardio-renal-inflammatory biomarker triad for early mortality prediction in acute coronary syndromes

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiovascular disease has become the leading cause of death worldwide. The invasiveness and associated risks of traditional diagnostic methods, such as imaging and coronary angiography, limit their utility for early diagnosis and prognosis prediction. Our previous study had confirmed that growth stimulation expressed gene 2 (ST2) presented fundamental values in diagnosing coronary artery disease (CAD), providing early warning of myocardial infarction and reflecting prognosis of critically ill patients with CAD. Methods We retrospectively recruited 7228 CAD patients undergoing coronary angiography and ST2 examination from January 2022 to July 2025. These patients were divided into four groups as coronary atherosclerosis group, coronary heart disease (CHD) group, non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) group and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) group according to the results of coronary angiography and other examinations. Results In coronary atherosclerosis group (313 males and 535 females), we found that the level of ST2 was higher in males than in females (20.98 ± 17.02 ng/mL vs. 16.27 ± 14.12 ng/mL, P=0.025). However, age-related difference wasn’t observed among age subgroups (≤50yrs, 51-74yrs, ≥75yrs). Significant difference of ST2 expression was observed among the four disease groups as ST2 level were 19.71 ± 23.29 ng/mL, 23.32 ± 27.04 ng/mL, 44.20 ± 55.99 ng/mL and 67.79 ± 80.61 ng/mL for coronary atherosclerosis group, CHD group, NSTEMI group and STEMI group (P&lt;0.001). Patients undergoing in-hospital rescue also presented with higher level of ST2 compared those CAD patients with stable condition (23.10 ± 26.74 ng/mL vs. 55.15 ± 69.59 ng/mL, P&lt;0.001). What’s more, in 412 critically ill patients with CAD, patients being successfully rescued were more likely to have lower level ST2 compared with those unsuccessfully resuscitated patients (64.46 ± 74.91 ng/mL vs. 84.95 ± 76.28 ng/mL, P&lt;0.001). Using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, the optimal cutoff value of ST2 for discriminating coronary atherosclerosis from CHD and myocardial infarction was 14.55 ng/mL, with a sensitivity of 69.9% and a specificity of 51.8% (AUC = 0.642, 95% CI: 0.622–0.661, P&lt;0.001). The optimal cutoff value of ST2 for discriminating coronary atherosclerosis and CHD from myocardial infarction was 26.75 ng/mL, with a sensitivity of 58.1% and a specificity of 78.2% (AUC = 0.732, 95% CI: 0.712–0.751, P&lt;0.001). Conclusion ST2 levels differ by gender, degree of coronary artery stenosis and severity of illness. It could be used as a promising biomarker to not only distinguish coronary atherosclerosis from CHD and myocardial infarction, but also distinguish coronary atherosclerosis and CHD from myocardial infarction, which may facilitate the diagnosis and prognosis assessment of CAD in routine clinical practice.comparisons between/among groupsdiagnostic value of ST2
title: The diagnostic and prognostic value of growth stimulation expressed gene 2 in patients with coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has emerged as a non-invasive imaging modality for evaluating suspected acute coronary syndromes (ACS). CCTA, owing to its high negative predictive value, allows reliable exclusion of coronary artery disease (CAD) and provides detailed anatomical information on plaque presence, burden, and morphology. Beyond excluding obstructive disease, CCTA offers insights not routinely obtained from Invasive Coronary Angiography (ICA), including improved assessment of total plaque burden and identification of high-risk plaque features. Several studies have demonstrated that CCTA can effectively reduce unnecessary ICAs while ensuring patient safety. However, its role in patients presenting with non-ST-elevation ACS (NSTE-ACS) without high-risk features remains undefined. The purpose of this study is to assess the diagnostic yield and clinical impact of a CCTA-first strategy in low- and intermediate-risk patients presenting with NSTE-ACS. Methods We analyzed 1,001 consecutive patients ≥18 years presenting to the emergency department with NSTE-ACS who did not meet high-risk criteria (hemodynamic instability, dynamic ST-T changes, ventricular arrhythmias, GRACE score &gt;140, refractory angina, heart failure, or cardiorespiratory arrest). They underwent CCTA as the initial coronary imaging modality. Data collection was carried out between May 11, 2022 and February 20, 2026. Results 1001 patients were included, with a mean age of 57 years, of which 44% were women and 56% men. Among the admission diagnoses, 21% were NSTEMI and 79% were unstable angina according to the 4th universal definition of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The median high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T value was 6 nanograms per litre (interquartile range, 4 to 13) for the first troponin sample, and 9 nanograms per litre (interquartile range, 6 to 22) for the second sample. CCTA was not performed in 7% due to a CAC score &gt;400 AU. Among patients who underwent CCTA, 27% had no coronary plaques and 40% had non-obstructive coronary artery disease (&lt;50% stenosis), while 25% had obstructive disease and 8% had nondiagnostic studies. High-risk plaque features were identified in 13%. Invasive coronary angiography was performed in 36% of patients, with coronary revascularization required in 23%. Conclusion In this large real-world cohort of low- and intermediate-risk NSTE-ACS, two-thirds of patients had no obstructive coronary disease on CCTA. A CCTA-first strategy may safely reduce invasive angiography while improving detection and characterization of non-obstructive coronary artery disease, supporting its integration into the diagnostic algorithm of selected ACS patients. Furthermore, the identification of nonobstructive CAD in 40% of our patients underscores a critical window to guide initiation or optimization of preventive medical therapy.Table 1CCTA findings
title: Coronary CT angiography in acute coronary syndromes: a contemporary real-world experience

abstract: Abstract Background Early identification of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains challenging, particularly in non–ST-segment elevation presentations and occluded myocardial infarction, where conventional electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation has limited sensitivity. Artificial intelligence–enabled ECG (AI-ECG) has emerged as a promising strategy to enhance early triage and diagnostic accuracy. Purpose To systematically evaluate the diagnostic performance of AI-enabled ECG algorithms for the detection of AMI, including ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), across diverse clinical settings. Methods This diagnostic systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through January 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based ECG models for AMI detection and reporting sufficient data to reconstruct 2×2 contingency tables were included. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were estimated using random-effects models (restricted maximum likelihood). Summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) were generated. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed for STEMI and NSTEMI. Results Ten observational studies comprising 94,510 participants were included. For overall AMI detection, AI-ECG demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 89.4% (95% CI, 79.7–94.8) and specificity of 96% (95% CI, 91.2–98.2). The pooled NPV was 98.7% (95% CI, 94.1–99.7), and the pooled PPV was 73.3% (95% CI, 50.2–88.2). The SROC AUC was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.92–0.98). In STEMI, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 94.4% and 97.5%, respectively (AUC 0.98). In NSTEMI, pooled sensitivity was lower at 65.0%, with specificity of 87.5% and an AUC of 0.71. Heterogeneity was substantial, particularly among NSTEMI cohorts. Conclusions AI-enabled ECG demonstrates high sensitivity and consistently excellent negative predictive value for AMI detection, supporting its role as a scalable, noninvasive triage adjunct at first medical contact. These findings highlight the potential of AI-ECG to facilitate early rule-out strategies and improve prioritization of patients requiring urgent ischemic evaluation.Graphical Abstract
title: Artificial intelligence–based ECG as a triage tool for acute myocardial infarction: a diagnostic systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background The acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is one of the most common working diagnoses in emergency departments worldwide. The 2023 ESC guidelines for the management of ACS recommend an initial assessment of patients presenting with acute chest pain via electrocardiogram (ECG) and serial troponin assessment, classifying patients into rule-in, rule-out, or observe pathway. Purpose We aimed to evaluate whether an initial point-of-care (POC) echocardiography can improve the prediction of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) above initial ECG and troponin evaluation alone. Methods The present analysis is based on the prospective EPIC-ACS study (Epicardial adipose tissue thickness predicts obstructive CAD in ACS patients) of patients presenting with acute chest pain, suggestive of ACS, to the emergency department of our Hospital. Patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction, haemodynamic instability or known CAD were excluded. A blinded echocardiographer, assessed left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF, ≥50% or &lt; 50%), regional wall motion abnormalities (yes or no, RWMA), left-atrial diameter in parasternal long axis view, and an epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) thickness of &lt; vs. ≥ 5.5mm. The primary endpoint was defined as the presence of obstructive CAD detected in subsequent invasive coronary angiography. Results Between 2019 and 2020, a total of 511 patients (Age: 57.52 ± 18.1 years; 52% male) were included in this prospective observational cohort study. Among those, 214 were transferred to invasive coronary angiography, of which 97 patients had obstructive CAD requiring revascularization therapy. These patients had RWMA (26.8% vs. 6.1%, p &lt; 0.001) and EAT of ≥ 5.5mm (88.7% vs. 11.3%, p &lt; 0.001) significantly more often. LVEF and left-atrial diameter were not significantly different between patients with vs. without obstructive CAD (LVEF &gt;= 50%: 81.4% vs. 87.7%, p = 0.48, LA-Diameter &gt; 4.5cm: 5.2% vs. 6.3%, p = 0.44). Figure 1 shows the presence of obstructive CAD, stratified by echocardiographic parameters, with normal and abnormal values showing that EAT &gt; 5.5mm was markedly more frequently present in patients with obstructive CAD (p &lt; 0.001, overall). In addition, the presence of RWMA differentiated patients with and without obstructive CAD in the rule-in (76% vs. 40%, p = 0.003) and rule-out (26% vs. 6%, p = 0.028) pathways, while no significant difference was observed in the observe group (p = 0.173). LVEF (rule-in: p = 0.313, observe: p = 0.441, rule-out: p = 0.685) and LA-Diameter (rule-in: p = 0.084, observe: p = 0.832, rule-out: p = 0.531) did not qualify for differentiating. Conclusion POC- echocardiography can help re-stratify patients with acute chest pain in addition to the guideline-recommended rule-in or rule-out pathway. Our results support the frequent use of POC- echocardiography for clinical decision-making in patients presenting with suspected ACS.
title: Point-of-care echocardiography for decision making in patients with acute chest pain – the EPIC-ACS-Study

abstract: Abstract Introduction In patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) invasive coronary angiography (ICA) is performed to identify those in need of coronary revascularization. However, a considerable proportion of these patients do not have obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). With improved image quality, reduced radiation exposure and a high negative predictive value, coronary CT angiography (CCTA) has become the diagnostic method of choice for stable patients with low to intermediate risk for CAD. The use of CCTA in acute coronary syndromes is less explored and current guidelines do not recommend CCTA in the diagnostic work-up of patients with NSTEMI. This population accounts for a large proportion of referrals to cath labs. If CCTA can safely identify patients with NSTEMI who do not need revascularization, unnecessary ICAs may be avoided. This will reduce procedural risk, limit interhospital transfers, shorten hospital stays and lower healthcare costs. Aim The aim of this study was to evaluate whether CCTA can safely identify patients with NSTEMI who do not need invasive evaluation. Methods We conducted a prospective, blinded, multicenter observational study including one university hospital and seven local hospitals. Patients with NSTEMI and a clinical indication for ICA were eligible for inclusion. The main exclusion criteria were indications for immediate ICA, GRACE score &gt; 140, age &gt; 75 years, previous coronary revascularization and more than two hypokinetic segments on echocardiography. CCTA was performed prior to ICA, analyzed at an independent core lab and evaluated regarding the need for ICA. The core lab was blinded to clinical data and ICA results. Revascularization, either performed or not performed, was defined as the gold standard. Results A total of 274 patients (mean age 62, 32% women) were included. Mean GRACE score was 92 and median troponin-T was 146 (IQR 366). Following ICA, 37% did not undergo revascularization. With revascularization as the gold standard, CCTA demonstrated a sensitivity of 89%, specificity of 90%, positive predictive value of 84% and negative predictive value of 83 %. Conclusions A substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI do not need revascularization. Our findings suggest that CCTA may have a role in the evaluation of patients with low risk NSTEMI. Further studies are warranted to explore the potential of CCTA in this large patient group.
title: Coronary CT angiography in non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, established independent cardiovascular risk factor associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Beyond its role in plaque initiation, Lp(a) has been implicated in the progression and calcification of atherosclerotic lesions through different mechanisms. In the setting of acute coronary syndromes (ACS), Lp(a) may play a dual pathophysiologic role, contributing not only to atherosclerotic plaque burden but also to plaque instability and thrombosis. However, its clinical significance in patients with a coronary artery calcium (CAC) score of 0 Agatston Units (AU) remains insufficiently characterized. Purpose We analyzed the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and the presence of coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients with CAC = 0 undergoing Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) for low- to intermediate-risk acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Methods We conducted an observational analytical study including 119 patients with CAC = 0 AU who underwent CCTA for low- to intermediate-risk ACS. Patients were stratified into elevated Lp(a) (n = 15) and normal Lp(a) groups (n = 104). The primary endpoint was the presence of CAD of any degree. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated to assess the association between elevated Lp(a) and CAD prevalence. Data collection was carried out between May 11, 2022 and February 20, 2026. Results CAD was identified in 10 of 15 patients (66.7%) in the elevated Lp(a) group compared with 35 of 104 patients (33.7%) in the normal Lp(a) group. Elevated Lp(a) was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of CAD (RR 1.98; 95% CI 1.26–3.10; p = 0.002). Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a higher prevalence of CAD (RR 1.98; 95% CI 1.26–3.10; p=0.002) and remained a strong predictor in multivariable analysis (OR 3.94; 95% CI 1.29–12.05; p=0.002). Conclusion In patients with an ACS and a CAC score = 0 AU, elevated Lp(a) levels were associated with nearly a fourfold higher odd of coronary artery disease (OR 3.94; 95% CI 1.29–12.05; p = 0.002). Our data appear to identify a hidden risk phenotype—patients with elevated Lp(a) who harbor coronary artery disease despite a CAC score =0. These findings highlight Lp(a) as a marker of residual atherosclerotic risk even in the absence of coronary calcification, with potential implications for enhanced risk stratification and preventive strategies in this subgroup of patients.CAD prevalence in patients with CAC=0Association between Lpa and CAD in CAC=0
title: Lp a and CAC score 0: the hidden risk phenotype

abstract: Abstract Background Strain echocardiography is uniquely positioned for early risk-stratification in suspected acute coronary syndromes (ACS), yet its diagnostic utility is limited by time-consuming analyses, operator dependency, and rigid anatomical assumptions on coronary perfusion territories. Deep learning (DL) enables fully automated, fast, and reproducible quantification of segmental strain during image acquisition1–3, potentially improving detection of high-risk ACS. Purpose To validate a fully automated DL-based method that measures and integrates regional strain from all 18 myocardial segments into a transparent and interpretable vessel-specific occlusion prediction model. Methods We prospectively included participants with acute myocardial infarction undergoing coronary angiography. Longitudinal strain was measured in the three standard apical views by a fully automated DL method developed by our group. Standardized segmental strain values were automatically integrated into the occlusion prediction model, using learning-based segment-specific weights to evaluate the strain patterns and generate probabilities of LAD, CX, and RCA occlusion. Diagnostic performance for angiographically confirmed occlusion was evaluated using ROC statistics and compared with conventional regional strain based on hypothetical perfusion territories. Results 1232 participants were included (mean age 74 ± 12, 77% male), of whom 58% presented with NSTEMI and 42% with STEMI. 23% had a prior history of coronary artery disease. Coronary occlusion was confirmed angiographically in 654 participants. The DL-based model had a feasibility of 94% and completed measurements within 1 second. Our model demonstrated high predictive performance for LAD (AUC 0.84), for CX (AUC 0.83), and RCA (AUC 0.80, Figure 1), consistently outperforming conventional territorial strain (AUCs 0.79, 0.67, and 0.59, respectively).
