All improvements were significant (p &lt;0.0001), with the largest improvements for CX and RCA. Model outputs included interpretable vessel-specific probability maps that visualized the predicted occlusion patterns (Figure 2). Conclusion A fully automated DL method integrating weighted longitudinal strain from all 18 segments accurately identified vessel-specific coronary occlusion, outperforming conventional territorial strain. This approach may facilitate early risk stratification and improve detection of occlusive ACS.ROC Curve for the DL-based modelBullseye representing LAD occlusion in NSTEMI
title: Fully automated deep learning echocardiographic strain model for vessel-specific detection of coronary occlusion

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) accounts for 6–10% of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) cases and presents similarly to classic AMI, yet involves diverse pathophysiological mechanisms with distinct management and prognosis. Conditions mimicking MINOCA, such as myocarditis, Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), and non-ischemic cardiomyopathies (CMP), share overlapping features, complicating diagnosis. This study aims to define the clinical features, presentation, and outcomes of these conditions, with a focus on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) findings, to enhance therapeutic decision-making and patient care. Methods This study represents a predefined sub-analysis of the multicentre prospective registry AMIPE. We included consecutive patients admitted between January 2019 and August 2024 with a working diagnosis of AMI and non-obstructive coronary arteries (&lt;50% stenosis). Patients were categorized as true MINOCA or MINOCA mimickers (myocarditis, TTS, or CMP) based on clinical evaluation and CMR findings. Clinical characteristics, in-hospital events, discharge therapies, and long-term outcomes—including all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)—were analysed. Results A totality of 461 patients was enrolled: 218 MINOCA, 126 myocarditis, 97 TTS, and 20 CMP. Myocarditis patients were younger and predominantly male, whereas TTS patients were older and mostly female. TTS and CMP were associated with higher in-hospital mortality and greater long-term event rates. Over a median follow-up of 35 months, MACE occurred in 17.4% of patients, being most frequent in CMP (45%) and TTS (26%). Independent predictors of MACE included age (HR 1.05 per year), smoking (HR 1.95), and CMP diagnosis (HR 4.60). Conclusions Patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS)-like presentations and non-obstructive coronary arteries exhibit heterogeneous clinical and prognostic profiles. While true MINOCA and myocarditis are generally associated with favourable outcomes, TTS and, especially, CMP carry significantly higher long-term mortality and MACE rates. Accurate phenotyping through integrated clinical, imaging, and laboratory evaluation is essential for diagnosis, risk stratification, and optimized management.Distribution of cardiovascular risk factors.
title: Clinical profile and prognosis of MINOCA and its mimickers

abstract: Abstract Background Takotsubo syndrome often mimics acute myocardial infarction (AMI) on electrocardiograms (ECGs), making differentiation challenging, especially in patients involving recanalized AMI. Purpose We assessed the hypothesis that artificial intelligence (AI) models could distinguish Takotsubo syndrome from anterior AMI with or without coronary recanalization using ECGs. Methods Patients who were diagnosed with Takotsubo syndrome between 1996 and 2024 were included. Among patients diagnosed with anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to occlusion of the mid-left anterior descending artery between 2010 and 2024, 321 were randomly included. Healthy volunteers were also included. ECGs recorded within 2 weeks of the index event were labeled as Takotsubo or AMI groups. ECGs between 2 weeks to 1 year after the index event were excluded, and the remaining were managed as non-Takotsubo/AMI. ECGs from heathy volunteers were also treated as non-Takotsubo/AMI. Three deep neural network-based models were pretrained and fine-tuned using the study datasets with both 3-class and 2-class labelling, and the final ensemble model for binary prediction (Takotsubo/AMI) was developed. The performance of the models was evaluated using an external test dataset from an independent institute. Results Among 308 patients with Takotsubo Syndrome and 321 with anterior STEMI we developed the models. The final model achieved an accuracy of 0.914, a receiver-operating-characteristics area-under-curve (AUC) was 0.970, precision-recall AUC was 0.984, the Expected Calibration Error was 0.0253, Brier Score 0.0654, and Brier Skill Score was 0.712 using external dataset (positive AMI, Figure 1, 2). Conclusions The AI model could differentiate Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI on ECGs and has the potential to assist clinicians.
title: Deep learning-based differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome and anterior acute myocardial infarction using electrocardiograms

abstract: Abstract Introduction Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a frequent complication in Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) with established prognostic impact. Early pre-procedural risk stratification is crucial, particularly with the emergence of nephroprotective therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i). The widely used Mehran score shows only moderate discrimination and relies on post-procedural variables, limiting its applicability before contrast exposure. Machine learning models have demonstrated improved predictive performance for CA-AKI; however, to our knowledge, none have specifically incorporated contemporary nephroprotective therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors into pre-procedural risk prediction models. Integrating these therapies into non-linear pre-procedural models may enable more accurate early risk assessment. Objectives To evaluate whether a pre-procedural Machine Learning Random Forest (RF) model, including prior SGLT2i therapy, improves CA-AKI risk prediction compared with the standard post-procedural Mehran score. Methods Prospective observational study including 884 ACS patients undergoing coronary angiography. The cohort was temporally split into derivation (n=538) and validation (n=346) samples. A Random Forest model was trained using pre-procedural variables: age, sex, diabetes, Killip class, admission hemoglobin, baseline eGFR (CKD-EPI), and prior SGLT2i use. Performance was compared with the Mehran score using C-statistics and categorical Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI). Results CA-AKI incidence was similar in derivation and validation cohorts (7.4% vs 7.2%, p=0.740). In the validation cohort, the RF model showed higher discrimination than the Mehran score (AUC 0.755 vs 0.641), although the difference did not reach statistical significance (DeLong p&gt;0.05), likely due to the low event rate. Reclassification analysis suggested meaningful clinical utility, with a total NRI of 19.8%, mainly driven by correct down-classification of non-events (non-event NRI 44.8%). Using its optimal threshold, the RF model identified 78.4% of patients as low risk prior to contrast exposure, with a CA-AKI rate of 2.2% (NPV 97.8%), compared with 31.0% using Mehran (NPV 96.2%). Conclusions A simple Random Forest model based exclusively on pre-procedural clinical variables, including SGLT2i therapy, improves early CA-AKI risk stratification compared with the standard Mehran score. This approach enables identification of low-risk patients before contrast exposure, potentially supporting tailored nephroprotective strategies.
title: Pre-procedural machine learning model including prior SGLT2 inhibitor therapy improves early risk stratification for contrast-associated kidney injury in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Intravascular imaging (IVI) is a well-established tool to guide and optimize percutaneous coronary interventions in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients, resulting in reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events. It is also useful in ACS patients without angiographically significant coronary artery disease, or with ambiguous or multiple culprit lesions. Thus, usage of IVI is strongly recommended by the current ESC guidelines. However, data regarding its adoption in daily practice is still needed. Purpose To assess usage of IVI in patients with ACS across 7 countries contributing to the EuroHeart ACS-PCI registry, and to identify disparities between different patient categories. Methods We assessed use of IVI in the EuroHeart ACS-PCI registry collaboration database, collected in 2024 from participating centres from 7 countries, which recorded consecutive admissions of patients with ACS. Data were stratified by country, according to the final diagnosis of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), IVI method used – ultrasound (IVUS) or optical coherence tomography (OCT), and characteristics of age (divided by 10-year bands: &lt;60, 60-69, 70-79 and &gt;80 years), sex, and diabetes. All analyses are descriptive. Results Data from a total of 102,926 admissions were collected (STEMI: 41.7% and NSTEMI: 58.3%). NSTEMI patients were older (mean average age 68.4 vs 65.4 years) and more frequently had diabetes (34.8% vs 23.3%). In STEMI, IVUS was used in 8.4% of cases, but with significant variations between countries (lowest and highest individual country mean: 0.3 – 16.4%), while OCT was used in only 1.7% of cases, with the same disparities between countries (0.0 – 7.4%). For both methods, there were no disparities driven by sex or presence of diabetes across countries. There was less usage of imaging for elderly patients, except for IVUS. In NSTEMI, both methods were more frequently used, but with persistent country variations: overall mean use of IVUS was 12.4% (0.8 – 26.7%) and 2.7% for OCT (0.0 – 8.8%). There were no disparities driven by sex or presence of diabetes across countries. When stratified by age, IVUS did not show significant disparities between age groups, while OCT was less frequently used in elderly patients. Conclusions In our analysis of more than 100,000 patients enrolled in the EuroHeart ACS-PCI registry collaboration, usage of IVI remains generally low across contributing countries but with important national differences. While use of these methods is homogenous when reporting to sex and diabetic status, age stratification reveals less use in the elderly patients.NSTEMISTEMI
title: Intravascular imaging in patients with acute coronary syndromes: insights from the EuroHeart ACS-PCI registry collaboration

abstract: Abstract Background Presence of coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) predicts adverse outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Continuous thermodilution (CTh) has recently been described as a more precise technique for CMD assessment, enabling measurement of absolute coronary blood flow (Q), hyperaemic microvascular resistance (Rhyper), coronary flow reserve (CFR), and microvascular resistance reserve (MRR). However, whether microvascular function recovers following ACS remains unknown. Purpose To prospectively measure coronary microvascular function using CTh in patients with ACS in infarct-related (IRA) and non-IRA vessels at index catheterisation and following 3 months of recovery. Methods The microSTREAM ACS is a prospective, single-centre study enrolling patients with STEMI or NSTEMI undergoing invasive angiography. CTh using a dedicated microcatheter was performed in IRA and non-IRA vessels at baseline (index catheterisation) and repeated at 3 months. Primary endpoints were change in CFR, MRR, and Rhyper. Resting flow (Qrest) and resistance (Rrest) were assessed to determine the magnitude of vasodilatory recovery. CMD was defined as MRR &lt;3.0. Paired changes were assessed by Wilcoxon signed-rank test; CMD prevalence change by McNemar test. Results Twenty patients (14 NSTEMI, 6 STEMI; 95% male; median age 57 years [IQR 45–65]) underwent CTh in 36 vessels at baseline; 25 vessels in 14 patients completed paired 3-month follow-up (n=6 were lost to follow-up). Baseline CMD was present in 50.0% (18/36 vessels) with median CFR 2.62 [IQR 2.0–3.6], MRR 3.00 [2.4–4.0], Rhyper 494 WU [418–634]. At 3 months (Table 1, Figure 1A), Rhyper decreased significantly (457→400 WU; Δ −67; p=0.001). CFR and MRR also improved (2.63→2.96; Δ +0.59; p=0.026 and 3.11→3.68; Δ +0.99; p=0.039, respectively) but resting parameters were unchanged (Qrest: p=0.125; Rrest: p=0.833). Rhyper improved in both IRA (Δ −73; p=0.017) and non-IRA (Δ −62; p=0.032) vessels. CFR and MRR improved directionally across both territories, though subgroup significance was not reached. In vessels with paired data, CMD prevalence decreased from 48.0% to 24.0% (Figure 1B). Conclusions In this first prospective application of CTh in ACS, significant microvascular recovery was demonstrated by 3 months, characterised by reduced Rhyper and improved CFR and MRR while resting parameters remained similar. These early observations suggest microvascular recovery may be mediated by improvement in smooth muscle vasodilatory capacity rather than a global change in resting tone and occurred in both IRA and non-IRA territories, consistent with global microvascular suppression at the time of ACS. These findings support the feasibility of CTh in ACS and for the first time, provide insight into the pattern and magnitude of microvascular recovery post-ACS. The full microSTREAM ACS cohort will provide further characterisation of this recovery.
title: Prospective assessment of coronary microvascular function using continuous thermodilution among patients with acute coronary syndrome: early observations from the microSTREAM ACS study

abstract: Abstract Background Type 2 myocardial infarction (MI) carries a high mortality risk, yet no randomized clinical trials exist to guide treatment (1). Standard secondary preventive therapies—such as beta blockers and renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors—are frequently prescribed despite the lack of trial evidence (2). Target trial emulation provides a framework for estimating treatment effects using observational data when randomized studies are not feasible (3). Purpose To evaluate the prognostic effect of routinely initiating beta blockers and RAAS inhibitors after type 2 MI in patients without other clear indications for these therapies. Methods Two hypothetical target trials were specified and then emulated using Swedish registry data to estimate the intention-to-treat effects of initiating a beta blocker versus no initiation, and initiating a RAAS inhibitor versus no initiation, following type 2 MI. In both emulations, the primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, readmission for myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. Confounding was addressed using inverse probability weighting. Results A total of 12,889 patients with a diagnosis of type 2 MI in the SWEDEHEART registry between September 2010, and June 2021, who were discharged alive, were included. After excluding patients with other indications or contraindications according to prespecified eligibility criteria, 4,213 and 4,242 patients were eligible for the beta blocker and RAAS inhibitor trial emulations, respectively (Figure 1). Beta blockers were initiated in 2,341 patients and withheld in 1,872 with no significant difference in the primary endpoint between groups (adjusted hazard ratio 0.93; 95% confidence interval 0.84-1.03; P = 0.15). RAAS inhibitors were initiated in 1,506 patients and withheld in 2,736 with no significant difference in the primary endpoint (adjusted hazard ratio 0.94; 95% confidence interval 0.85-1.04; P = 0.21) (Figure 2). Conclusion Initiating beta blockers and RAAS inhibitors after type 2 MI does not seem to offer any prognostic benefit unless supported by other established clinical indications.Figure 1.Patient selectionFigure 2.Adjusted survival curves
title: Beta blockers and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors after type 2 myocardial infarction, a target trial emulation study

abstract: Abstract Background Previous studies have demonstrated that intravascular imaging during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes after the procedure. However, it remains uncertain whether intravascular imaging modifies the effects of an aspirin-free strategy at the time of PCI in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Purpose To evaluate the interaction between the intravascular imaging guidance and the relative effects of an aspirin-free strategy compared with dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) in PCI for ACS patients. Methods This is a post-hoc subgroup analysis of the STOPDAPT-3 (Short and Optimal Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy-3) trial, a multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled study conducted in Japan. The participants were randomized to either prasugrel monotherapy without aspirin (no-aspirin group) or the DAPT group just before PCI. ACS patients enrolled in STOPDAPT-3 were stratified by intravascular imaging use (intravascular ultrasound or optical coherence tomography) during index PCI. The two coprimary endpoints were a bleeding endpoint (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium [BARC] type 3 or 5) and a cardiovascular endpoint, comprising death, myocardial infarction, definite stent thrombosis, or ischemic stroke at 30 days. Results Among 4,476 ACS patients, intravascular imaging was used in 4,111 patients (91.8%), whereas 365 (8.2%) underwent PCI guided by angiography alone. In the non-imaging subgroup, the 30-day cumulative incidence rates of the coprimary bleeding endpoint were 7.3% in the no-aspirin group and 6.4% in the DAPT group (hazard ratio [HR] 1.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.52–2.54), while in the imaging subgroup, the rates were 4.7% and 5.2%, respectively (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.68–1.18), with no significant interaction (P interaction=0.56). The 30-day cumulative incidence rates of the coprimary cardiovascular endpoint were 5.2% and 3.5% (HR 1.51, 95% CI 0.55–4.17) in the non-imaging subgroup, and 4.7% and 3.9% in the imaging subgroup (HR 1.20, 95% CI 0.89–1.61), with no significant interaction (P interaction=0.66). Conclusions Among patients with ACS undergoing PCI, the clinical effects of an aspirin-free antiplatelet strategy compared with standard DAPT were not significantly affected by intravascular imaging guidance. These findings reinforce the conceptual independence of pharmacologic and procedural optimization strategies and provide important guidance for the global application of contemporary antiplatelet therapy, particularly in regions with limited routine use of intravascular imaging.
title: Impact of intravascular imaging guidance on the effects of aspirin-free strategy for percutaneous coronary intervention for acute coronary syndrome: a post-hoc analysis from the STOPDAPT-3 trial

abstract: Abstract Background Clinical guidelines for beta-blocker use after ACS are largely based on evidence from the pre-reperfusion era. However, the evidence for the long-term clinical utility and safety profile of beta-blocker therapy remains unclear in patients with coronary revascularisation and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥40%). Purpose To evaluate the association between long-term beta-blocker therapy and clinical outcomes in patients with revascularised ACS and preserved LVEF (≥40%). Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using target trial emulation and data from a global federated research network (January 2013–December 2021). Adults aged ≥18 years who underwent coronary revascularisation for ACS and had preserved LVEF (≥40%) were included. Patients with beta-blocker use within one year before the index event or with predefined contraindications (including severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma) were excluded. Long-term beta-blocker therapy was defined as initiation within 14 days after the index event and continued up to one year. Patients receiving long-term beta-blockers were compared with those not treated with beta-blockers. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within three years. Secondary outcomes included recurrent revascularisation and incident heart failure within three years. Safety outcomes comprised bradycardia, hypotension, and atrioventricular block. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline covariates. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. Results A total of 5,471 patients were eligible in the study period. After propensity score matching analysis, 3,254 patients (mean age 62 ±12.5 years; 32.6% women) were analysed (1,627 per group). In the primary outcome, no significant differences were found in 3-year all-cause mortality between patients with and without long-term beta-blocker therapy (6.5% vs 5.3%; hazard ratio [HR] 1.09; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.82–1.45; p=0.54). In secondary outcomes, patients receiving long-term beta-blocker therapy had higher risk of recurrent revascularisation (HR 1.82; 95% CI 1.66–1.99; p&lt;0.0001) and risk of heart failure (HR 2.86; 95% CI 2.49–3.29; p&lt;0.0001) compared to those without beta-blocker therapy. Patients with long-term beta-blocker therapy also experienced higher risks of adverse events, including bradycardia (HR 2.38; 95% CI 1.92–2.95; p&lt;0.0001), hypotension (HR 3.06; 95% CI 2.39–3.91; p&lt;0.0001), and AV block (HR 2.14; 95% CI 1.27–3.61; p&lt;0.001) compared to those without beta-blocker therapy, which are considered beta-blocker-related pharmacological adverse effects. Conclusion In patients with revascularised ACS and preserved LVEF (≥40%), long-term beta-blocker therapy was not associated with reduced mortality and was linked to higher risks of recurrent revascularisation, heart failure, and adverse haemodynamic events.
title: Long-term beta-blocker therapy after revascularised acute coronary syndrome (ACS) with preserved ejection fraction: a multi-centre retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor is the standard treatment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndromes (ACS). However, prolonged DAPT increases major bleeding risk. Early aspirin discontinuation with ticagrelor monotherapy may reduce bleeding while maintaining ischaemic protection. Purpose To evaluate the efficacy and safety of early aspirin withdrawal followed by ticagrelor monotherapy compared with standard DAPT in contemporary PCI populations, specifically focusing on the high-risk ACS cohort. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ticagrelor monotherapy after short-term DAPT (2 weeks–3 months) versus continued DAPT was conducted. Five trials (T-PASS, TICO, TWILIGHT, ULTIMATE-DAPT, and NEO-MINDSET) were identified, totaling 19,755 patients (80–90% with ACS). Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using random-effects models for ischaemic and bleeding outcomes. Result Ticagrelor monotherapy significantly reduced all bleeding (RR 0.54; 95% CI 0.47–0.62; P&lt;0.00001) and major bleeding (RR 0.44; 95% CI 0.36–0.55; P&lt;0.00001). There were no significant differences in all-cause mortality (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.75–1.20; P=0.42), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.63–1.17; P=0.33), or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.76–1.18; P=0.63). Individual ischaemic endpoints including myocardial infarction (RR 1.10; 95% CI 0.85–1.42), stent thrombosis (RR 1.15; 95% CI 0.68–1.95), and stroke (RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.70–1.53) were similar between groups. Conclusion In patients undergoing PCI, predominantly for ACS, early de-escalation to ticagrelor monotherapy after a short course of DAPT significantly reduces major bleeding without increasing the risk of mortality or ischaemic events. These findings support ticagrelor monotherapy as a viable alternative for patients who remain event-free in the early post-PCI period.1. Figure 3A: Major Bleeding (BARC 3–5)2. Figure 1B: MACCE

title: Ticagrelor monotherapy vs. standard DAPT after PCI: an updated meta-analysis of early aspirin withdrawal

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is routinely prescribed to prevent recurrent ischaemic events and stent thrombosis. Although guidelines generally recommend 12 months of therapy, the benefit of extending DAPT beyond one year remains uncertain because potential reductions in ischaemic events must be balanced against bleeding risk. Purpose To compare the efficacy and safety of standard-duration (≤12 months) versus extended-duration (&gt;12 months) DAPT after PCI in adults with ACS. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library (inception-November 2025) identified randomised and comparative observational studies enrolling adults with ACS treated with PCI using any stent type. Studies directly comparing standard duration versus extended duration DAPT were included. Primary outcomes were myocardial infarction and clinically relevant bleeding (BARC-defined events). Secondary outcomes included mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, target-vessel revascularisation (TVR), and definite stent thrombosis. Pooled risk ratios were calculated using random-effects models. Results Fourteen studies (13 cohort studies and 1 randomised trial), including 69,087 patients, were analysed. During overall follow-up, extended DAPT did not reduce myocardial infarction (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.57–1.65), MACE (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.52–1.31), stroke (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.85–1.60) or definite stent thrombosis (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.20–2.21). All-cause mortality was higher with extended therapy (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.61–3.80). Target-vessel revascularisation was lower with standard-duration DAPT (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30–0.89). Bleeding risk was similar between strategies, both for any bleeding (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.72–1.28) and clinically relevant bleeding (BARC 2/3/5 RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.78–1.49). In a landmark analysis at 12 months, extended DAPT did not reduce myocardial infarction (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.12–2.62), MACE (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.25–1.68), definite stent thrombosis (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.11–2.79), cardiac death (RR 2.24, 95% CI 1.00–5.00) or all-cause mortality (RR 1.85, 95% CI 0.68–5.03), nor increase clinically relevant bleeding (BARC 2/3/5 RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.55–1.77). Conclusions In patients with ACS undergoing PCI, extending dual antiplatelet therapy beyond 12 months does not provide consistent reductions in major ischaemic outcomes, including myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, or mortality. The absence of benefit was confirmed both during overall follow-up and in landmark 12-month analyses, with a reduction observed only in repeat revascularisation, a softer endpoint. These findings support an individualised approach to DAPT duration rather than routine prolongation beyond one year. Further adequately powered randomised trials are needed.OUTCOMESCENTRAL ILLUSTRATION
title: Standard versus extended dual antiplatelet therapy after pci in acute coronary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Current guidelines recommend dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor – prasugrel or ticagrelor preferred over clopidogrel – in virtually all patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While clopidogrel (1998) was the first drug introduced, prasugrel (2009) and ticagrelor (2011) subsequently emerged as more potent alternatives. Methods For this study, we interrogated the AMIS Plus database of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI patients admitted to Swiss hospital between 2009 and 2024 with available data on immediate treatment (within 24 hours after hospital admission) with P2Y12 inhibitors. We plotted yearly percentual application of the different P2Y12 inhibitors together with bleeding and in-hospital mortality prevalences over time. Then, we used multinomial propensity scores to balance baseline characteristics across the P2Y12 inhibitors, assessed covariate balance, and estimated weighted odds ratios for bleeding and in-hospital mortality. For the latter analysis, we excluded patients on oral anticoagulation as well as patients with P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. Results Among the 41,244 AMI patients enrolled in AMIS Plus during the study period, 29.3% were on clopidogrel, 21.1% on prasugrel, 35.9% on ticagrelor, and 34,736 (84.2%) patients were on DAPT. The median ages of patients on clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticagrelor were 66.8 [interquartile range (IQR) 56.4, 76.9] years, 59.5 (IQR 52.2, 67.0) years, and 65.9 (IQR 56.5, 75.6) years, respectively. Out of the patients who received prasugrel, 83.5% were male, compared with 73.8% in the clopidogrel group and 75.4% in the ticagrelor group. Overall, crude bleeding and in-hospital mortality rates were 3.8% and 4.8%, respectively. Application frequencies of the three different P2Y12 inhibitors across the study period are displayed in Figure A. Pairwise comparisons of the three P2Y12 inhibitors in terms of bleeding complications showed no significant differences between the drugs (Figure B). In terms of in-hospital mortality, clopidogrel showed the highest and prasugrel the lowest odds (Figure B). Conclusion Over the study period, we observed no difference between the drugs for bleeding complications. Prasugrel use was associated with the lowest odds of in-hospital mortality, while clopidogrel had the highest odds.Figure P2Y12 Inhibitors Abstract
title: Temporal trends in the use of P2Y12 inhibitors over 15 years and their impact on in-hospital bleeding and mortality among patients with acute myocardial infarction in Switzerland

abstract: Abstract Background The impact of routinely prescribed cardiovascular (CV) medications on the development of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) post percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains insufficiently explored, especially with the emerging therapies such as sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitors (ARNi). Purpose To evaluate the association between commonly used CV medications and the risk of CIN. Methods We conducted a case-control study that included all patients who underwent revascularization with PCI at the main tertiary cardiology center in Qatar between 2016-2023. The use of routine CV medications, including P2Y12 inhibitors (clopidogrel, ticagrelor), high-intensity statin (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin), Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitors/ Angiotensin Receptor Blockers/ ARNi (ACEi/ARB/ARNi), and loop diuretics, was defined as the established use before PCI or early initiation within 24 hours of contrast exposure. Cases were patients who developed CIN defined as an increase in serum creatinine by more than 0.3mg/dL or more than 50% of the baseline value within 48-72 hours of contrast exposure, while controls were patients without CIN. The primary outcome was the risk of CIN with the routine CV medications use. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used with P-value &lt;0.05 indicating statistical significance. Results We included 16463 patients who met the eligibility criteria (91% male, mean age 52±11 years). Clopidogrel was used in 98% of patients, while atorvastatin 40 mg was the predominant statin prescribed. CIN occurred in 2.5% of the study population. Using multivariable logistic regression, diuretic use was the strongest predictor of CIN (OR 10.39, 95% CI 8.38–12.87; p&lt;0.001). SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with increased odds of CIN (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02–2.00; p=0.038), whereas ACEi/ARB/ARNi use was independently associated with lower odds (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55–0.86; p&lt;0.001). No significant associations were observed for P2Y12 inhibitors or statins. Conclusion The use of CV medications peri-PCI, including diuretics and SGLT2 inhibitors was associated with increased CIN risk, while ACEi/ARB/ARNi use lowered the risk of CIN, suggesting a potential protective effect. Our findings highlight the importance of medication-related risk stratification in patients undergoing PCI and warrant further prospective validation.
title: Impact of routine cardiovascular medications on contrast induced nephropathy post percutaneous coronary intervention: a national experience

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) after an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) face a severe inflammatory response driven by the combination of the acute ischaemic event and surgical trauma. Although colchicine has been widely studied in stable coronary disease, its efficacy and safety in this highly inflammatory perioperative setting remain unknown. Purpose To evaluate whether perioperative colchicine administration reduces periprocedural myocardial infarction, post-operative atrial fibrillation, and post-pericardiotomy syndrome in patients with ACS undergoing CABG. Methods In this investigator-initiated, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint trial, 100 patients with ACS referred for CABG were randomised in a 1:1 ratio to receive either colchicine (0.5 mg twice daily) or standard of care. Treatment commenced pre-operatively and continued for 30 days after hospital discharge. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of periprocedural myocardial infarction (Type 5), post-operative atrial fibrillation, and post-pericardiotomy syndrome, evaluated throughout the follow-up period. Safety endpoints included the incidence of hospital-acquired infections. All clinical events were adjudicated by an independent blinded committee. Results The median age of the 100 randomised patients was 62 years. The primary composite endpoint occurred in 42.0% of patients in the colchicine group and 46.0% in the control group (hazard ratio [HR] 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54-1.84; p=0.995). There were no significant differences in the individual components of the primary endpoint, including periprocedural myocardial infarction (28.0% vs. 28.0%), post-operative atrial fibrillation (20.0% vs. 24.0%), and post-pericardiotomy syndrome (10.0% vs. 22.0%). Conversely, the colchicine group exhibited a significantly higher incidence of hospital-acquired infections compared with the control group (26.0% vs. 10.0%; HR 3.47; 95% CI 1.19-10.12; p=0.023). Serial laboratory analysis revealed that colchicine induced early intravascular neutrophil retention, correlating temporally with this increased infectious vulnerability. Conclusion(s) In patients with ACS undergoing CABG, perioperative colchicine administration did not reduce the incidence of periprocedural myocardial infarction, post-operative atrial fibrillation, or post-pericardiotomy syndrome. Furthermore, the intervention significantly increased the risk of hospital-acquired infections.Graphical Abstract
title: Perioperative colchicine increases hospital-acquired infections without reducing major cardiovascular complications in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting after acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background There is a lack of randomized data to guide clinical practice regarding the prescription of single versus dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD) who are managed conservatively. Methods We analyzed and compared cardiovascular outcomes of patients with SCAD who were conservatively managed throughout their index hospitalization and discharged on either single (SAPT) or dual (DAPT) antiplatelet therapy. We excluded patients who were revascularized during the initial angiogram (n=93) or after a recurrent event in-hospital (n=17), died prior to discharge (n=1), or who did not receive antiplatelet therapy (n=29), including those with an indication for oral anticoagulation (n=28). We assessed 1yr major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which included death, recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), unplanned revascularization, stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), and congestive heart failure (CHF). Results Of 750 prospective patients, 582 received either SAPT (40.4%) or DAPT (59.6%) at discharge. Mean age was 51.7 years and 88.8% were women. The presentation was ST-elevation MI in 26.3% and NSTEMI in 73.7% of cases. Angiographic SCAD type was Type 1 in 32%, Type 2A in 40%, Type 2B in 29% and Type 3 in 13%. Baseline demographics and angiographic characteristics were similar between groups. The proportion of patients receiving DAPT decreased over time, as expected; 45.8% at 6 months, 23.7% at 1yr and 6.2% at 2yrs post-discharge. The cumulative rate of MACE in the cohort was low (3.4% with SAPT vs 4.6% with DAPT at 1-year) (Figure 1). There were also no significant differences between antiplatelet groups either at 1-month or 1-year post-discharge (p=0.530 and p=0.530, respectively). Similarly, rates of unplanned revascularization, stroke and CHF were low at 1-year and similar between groups (p=1.0, p=1.0 and p=0.163, respectively). Conclusions In a large cohort of prospectively enrolled patients with SCAD who were treated conservatively throughout their hospitalization, we found no significant difference with regard to outcomes at 12-months in those prescribed either SAPT or DAPT at discharge.Figure 1
title: Antithrombotic strategies in conservatively managed patients with spontaneous coronary artery dissection

abstract: Abstract Background The 2025 ESC/EAS Focused Update on the Management of Dyslipidaemias recommends upfront combination therapy (high-intensity statin + ezetimibe) during index hospitalization for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in lipid-lowering therapy (LLT)-naïve patients unlikely to achieve LDL-C goals with monotherapy. Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] contributes a fixed cholesterol fraction that is largely unresponsive to statins. Consequently, in patients with intermediate admission LDL-C, high Lp(a) levels could identify a subgroup with a low probability of achieving therapeutic targets with statin monotherapy. Purpose To identify the proportion of LLT-naïve ACS patients eligible for upfront combination therapy due to Lp(a)-driven predicted monotherapy failure (Lp(a)-PMF), and to evaluate the real-world benefit of this strategy in achieving the absolute therapeutic target (LDL-C &lt;55 mg/dL). Methods This prospective, single-centre study analysed 649 consecutive ACS patients from the CARTACS registry (July 2023–August 2025) with measured Lp(a) and estimated LDL-C at admission. We estimated Lp(a)-cholesterol [Lp(a)-C] using the Rosenson equation (Lp(a) nmol/L × 0.077). In LLT-naïve patients with intermediate admission LDL-C (55–110 mg/dL), Lp(a)-PMF was defined as [Admission LDL-C + Lp(a)-C] &gt;110 mg/dL, representing the threshold at which an expected ~50% LDL-C reduction with high-intensity statin monotherapy would fail to achieve the &lt;55 mg/dL target. Given that guideline targets are dual (≥50% reduction and &lt;55 mg/dL), we prioritized the absolute goal, as the fixed Lp(a)-cholesterol fraction is largely unresponsive to statins and may limit the achievable relative LDL-C reduction despite adequate response of the modifiable LDL fraction. We compared 3-month absolute target attainment (&lt;55 mg/dL) between upfront combination therapy and statin monotherapy according to Lp(a)-PMF status. Results Of 649 ACS patients, 314 (48%) were LLT-naïve; 116 had intermediate admission LDL-C (55–110 mg/dL). Among them, 23 (20%) met criteria for Lp(a)-PMF, while 93 (80%) did not (figure 1). In the Lp(a)-PMF subgroup, upfront combination therapy (n=7) showed higher target attainment than statin monotherapy (85.7% vs. 31.3%; p=0.027) despite similar baseline levels of LDL-C and Lp(a) (both p&gt;0.4). Conversely, without Lp(a)-PMF, statin monotherapy (n=76) achieved the target in 60.5%, with a non-significant increase with upfront ezetimibe (n=17; 76.5%; p=0.273; Figure 2). Conclusions One in five LLT-naïve ACS patients with intermediate admission LDL-C have a high predicted risk of statin monotherapy failure based on their Lp(a) burden. Integrating Lp(a) concentration with LDL-C may help identify patients who derive greater benefit from upfront combination therapy versus statin monotherapy.
title: Benefit of upfront combination lipid-lowering therapy in statin-naïve acute coronary syndrome patients with intermediate admission LDL-C and Lp(a)-driven predicted monotherapy failure

abstract: Abstract Background Aspirin is the cornerstone of antiplatelet therapy for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), while indobufen serves as an alternative for patients with aspirin intolerance. However, comparative data on their long-term efficacy and safety in real-world NSTEMI populations are limited. Purpose This study aimed to compare the 1-year clinical outcomes of aspirin versus indobufen in a large real-world cohort of NSTEMI patients. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study including 68,514 NSTEMI patients from 82 hospitals in China (2010–2024). Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline imbalances, including age, sex, Killip's class, and comorbidities. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for clinical endpoints. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardio-cerebrovascular events (MACCE) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included net adverse clinical events (NACE) and gastrointestinal bleeding. Results Among 68,514 included patients, 67,496 received aspirin and 1,018 received indobufen. Prior to matching, the indobufen group was significantly older (mean age 72.50 vs. 64.87 years) and had higher prevalences of prior cerebral infarction (45.2% vs. 24.4%), diabetes (44.5% vs. 30.2%), and hypertension (75.3% vs. 51.6%) (all P &lt; 0.001). After PSM, 1,012 matched pairs were formed. Aspirin was associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause death compared to indobufen (aHR 0.751, 95% CI 0.587–0.961, P=0.023). No significant differences were observed for MACCE (aHR 1.101, P=0.286) or NACE (aHR 1.065, P=0.483). Notably, aspirin demonstrated a significantly lower risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (aHR 0.412, 95% CI 0.328–0.518, P&lt;0.001). Subgroup analyses revealed that the survival benefit of aspirin was more pronounced in males, patients aged ≥65 years, those with hypertension, and those treated with clopidogrel (P for interaction = 0.083). Conclusions In this real-world NSTEMI population, aspirin was associated with superior 1-year survival and a more favorable bleeding safety profile compared with indobufen. The survival advantage of aspirin appears particularly evident when used in combination with clopidogrel.Figure 1
title: One-year clinical outcomes of aspirin versus indobufen in patients with NSTEMI: a multicenter retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Early aspirin discontinuation with continuation of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy has been proposed to reduce bleeding after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndromes (ACS). However, prior meta-analyses predominantly assessed shortened dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) rather than aspirin-free strategies, and the net impact on ischemic and bleeding outcomes in ACS remains uncertain. Purpose To assess the safety and efficacy of early aspirin withdrawal with continued P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy compared with standard 12-month DAPT by assessing major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major or clinically relevant bleeding. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults with ACS undergoing PCI, comparing early aspirin withdrawal followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus standard 12-month DAPT. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through February 2026. The primary efficacy outcome was MACE (all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent/unplanned revascularization), and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (BARC 2–5 or ISTH major). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Analyses were performed with Review Manager version 10.0.1. Results Of 3,019 records screened, 11 RCTs comprising 34,283 patients were included. Early aspirin withdrawal was not associated with a significant difference in MACE compared with standard DAPT (RR 1.01; 95% CI 0.85–1.22; p=0.874; I²=48.3%; Figure 1). However, early aspirin discontinuation significantly reduced clinically relevant bleeding (BARC 2–5) (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.47–0.60; p&lt;0.001; I²=0%; Figure 2A) and major bleeding (RR 0.54; 95% CI 0.43–0.66; p&lt;0.001; I²=42.7%; Figure 2B). Accordingly, net adverse clinical events (NACE) were significantly lower in the early withdrawal group (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.64–0.84; p&lt;0.001; I²=44.0%; Figure 2C). Conclusions In this meta-analysis of RCTs, early aspirin discontinuation with continuation of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy reduced major bleeding and NACE without increasing MACE compared with standard 12-month DAPT.Figure 1.Figure2

title: Early aspirin withdrawal to P2Y12 monotherapy after PCI for ACS: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is a leading cause of death worldwide. Guidelines recommend initiation of high-intensity statin therapy after ACS, followed by combination therapy in patients who are unable to achieve target low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) lowering. Upfront combination lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) has shown promise in reducing the time taken to achieve the target LDL-C level and improved efficacy in reducing recurrent events. Purpose This study aims to compare the efficacy of various upfront LLT combinations on LDL-C and the incidence of three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods This study was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for eligible studies published before 6 August 2025. Studies enrolling adult ACS patients with upfront (in-hospital or within 4 weeks of ACS) combination LLT (statin plus ezetimibe or PCSK9 (proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) inhibitors or both (triple therapy)) were included. Three independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and the senior author resolved disagreements. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the RoB2 scale. Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed in R using a random-effects model with weakly informative priors. Results LDL-C The network had 39 studies. Combination strategies achieved significantly greater LDL-C reduction versus statin monotherapy (S) (Figure 1). Mean differences (95% Credible Interval) were 11.9 mg/dL (10.9–13.0) for ezetimibe + statin (E+S), 36.0 mg/dL (34.0–38.1) for PCSK9 inhibitor + statin (P+S), and 44.4 mg/dL (37.9–50.8) for triple therapy. Node-splitting confirmed consistency between direct and indirect evidence (p≥0.23). Between-study heterogeneity was substantial (τ=0.49 mg/dL; I²=91%). Triple therapy ranked first with near-certainty (SUCRA=1.00), followed by P+S (0.67), E+S (0.33), and S (0.00; Figure 2). Findings were robust to priors on sensitivity analysis. MACE The network had 16 studies. Combination strategies showed a trend toward fewer MACE events versus S: odds ratio (95% Credible Interval) 0.86 (0.50–1.31) for E+S, 0.70 (0.50–1.02) for P+S, and 0.42 (0.07–2.09) for triple therapy. Between-study heterogeneity was low (τ=0.21; I²=11%). Convergence was satisfactory (Gelman–Rubin≤1.02). Triple therapy ranked highest for MACE reduction (SUCRA=0.80), followed by P+S (0.67), E+S (0.42), and S (0.11), though non-deterministic. Sensitivity analyses confirmed directional consistency across priors. Conclusions Upfront combination LLT showed substantial LDL-C reduction, with triple therapy demonstrating the highest efficacy. While all combinations showed a trend towards fewer MACE events, none reached significance. The consistent ranking hierarchy across both the outcomes and the robustness of findings to priors supports the consideration of upfront combination LLT in ACS.Figure 1:Network plot for LDL-C reductionFigure 2:SUCRA and rank probability plots
title: Upfront combination lipid-lowering therapy in acute coronary syndrome: a bayesian network meta-analysis of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and major adverse cardiovascular events

abstract: Abstract Background Achieving the low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets recommended by the ESC/EAS guidelines remains challenging in routine practice for very-high-risk patients. Purpose We aimed to evaluate LDL-C target attainment following inpatient initiation of intensive combination lipid-lowering therapy in statin-naïve acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients and to explore factors associated with successful attainment. Methods In this prospective single-center cohort study, we enrolled statin-naïve ACS patients undergoing coronary revascularization. All patients were prescribed high-intensity combination therapy (rosuvastatin 20 mg or atorvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg daily) at discharge. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving LDL-C &lt;1.4 mmol/L at 1 and 6 months. For patients not achieving the target, the therapeutic gap (absolute distance to target and percentage reduction required) was analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with goal attainment. Safety outcomes were also assessed. Results A total of 277 patients were recruited. Mean LDL-C levels decreased from 2.56 mmol/L at baseline to 1.06 mmol/L at 1 month and 1.08 mmol/L at 6 months. LDL-C target attainment rates (&lt;1.4 mmol/L) were 83.8% and 83.4%, respectively. Among the 45 non-attainers at 6 months, 35.6% had a residual therapeutic gap &gt;0.5 mmol/L, and only 5 patients (11.1% of non-attainers; 1.8% of total cohort) required &gt;50% additional LDL-C reduction. (Figure 1) Higher baseline LDL-C was associated with lower goal attainment at 6 months (OR 0.60, p=0.004). Additionally, good medication adherence was significantly associated with 6-month goal attainment (OR 4.97, p = 0.007) (Table 1). Combination therapy was safe and well-tolerated. Elevated liver enzymes or treatment discontinuation due to possible adverse reactions occurred in only 1.35% of patients. Conclusions Inpatient initiation of high-intensity statin plus ezetimibe enabled over 80% of statin-naïve ACS patients to achieve stringent ESC/EAS LDL-C targets with an acceptable safety profile. Most non-attainers were close to the target, and medication adherence emerged as a critical determinant of goal attainment. Patients with very high baseline LDL-C may require closer monitoring or consideration of additional therapies to close the residual therapeutic gap.
title: Early intensive combination lipid-lowering therapy in statin-naïve acute coronary syndrome: real-world attainment of lipid targets and analysis of therapeutic gaps

abstract: Abstract Background Previous clinical trials have demonstrated the cardioprotective effects of sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in patients with heart failure and acute coronary syndrome beyond glycemic control. Improvement in mitochondrial function has been proposed as a key mechanism underlying these cardioprotective effects in preclinical studies. However, the effects of SGLT2i on circulating mitochondrial function in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) have not been investigated. Purpose To determine whether SGLT2i improves circulating mitochondrial function in patients with STEMI. Methods This prospective, double-blind, randomized trial enrolled 45 patients with STEMI who were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either SGLT2i (dapagliflozin 20 mg loading dose followed by 10 mg daily for 12 weeks) or placebo. Cardiac function was assessed by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were collected at baseline, and at 2 days, 2 weeks, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to evaluate mitochondrial function. The primary endpoint was ATP production in PBMCs. Secondary endpoints included LVEF and additional mitochondrial respiratory parameters. Results At baseline, ATP levels and LVEF were comparable between groups (Fig.1A,B). In the placebo group, ATP levels increased at 2- and 12-weeks post-PCI compared with their baseline (p&lt; 0.05), whereas ATP levels remained unchanged in the SGLT2i group (Fig.1B). LVEF did not differ between groups at 12 weeks post-PCI (Fig.1A). Temporal improvement in mitochondrial function was observed in the placebo group, including increased basal respiration at 2 weeks post-PCI and enhanced spare respiratory capacity and maximal respiration at 2- and 6- weeks post-PCI; these parameters returned to baseline levels by 12 weeks (Fig.1C-E). Notably, at 12 weeks post-PCI, patients receiving SGLT2i exhibited significantly higher spare respiratory capacity compared with placebo (mean difference= −46.01; 95% CI= −90.71 to −1.41; p= 0.04, Fig.1E). Conclusion Although SGLT2i did not improve LVEF or ATP production within 12 weeks in STEMI patients, it enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance, as reflected by increased spare respiratory capacity. Longer treatment duration may be required to fully elucidate the mitochondrial and cardioprotective benefits of SGLT2i in STEMI.
title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor enhances mitochondrial stress resistance without altering ATP production in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Dual antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of secondary prevention after acute myocardial infarction. In randomized trials, the potent P2Y12 inhibitors ticagrelor and prasugrel reduced ischemic events compared with clopidogrel. However, ticagrelor’s clinical advantage over clopidogrel has been debated, and head-to-head comparisons suggest that prasugrel is noninferior and potentially superior to ticagrelor. Contemporary patterns of P2Y12 inhibitor use and associated treatment costs across countries are not well characterized. Purpose To describe temporal trends in P2Y12 inhibitor use and associated treatment costs in Germany and the United States from 2011 through 2024. Methods Cohort study using longitudinal, nationwide health care claims data from Germany and the US. Country-specific cohorts included adults aged 18 years or older who newly initiated P2Y12 inhibitor therapy within 30 days after hospitalization for acute myocardial infarction. Annual proportions of patients initiating clopidogrel, ticagrelor, or prasugrel and absolute changes over time were assessed. 12-month treatment costs were estimated using net price estimates accounting for average manufacturer rebates, and potential savings associated with substitution of lower-cost alternatives were calculated. Results From 2011 to 2024, the proportion of patients initiating clopidogrel after acute myocardial infarction decreased by 39% in Germany and 13% in the US. Ticagrelor use increased through 2018 (+41% in Germany; +40% in the US), coinciding with guideline recommendations favoring potent P2Y12 inhibitors (Europe, 2011; US, 2014). After results of the ISAR-REACT 5 randomized trial in 2019 showed lower ischemic event rates with prasugrel than with ticagrelor, and subsequent European guideline updates favored prasugrel, use of prasugrel in Germany increased by 18%, without an observed increase in major adverse cardiovascular events. In contrast, uptake in the US remained limited, with continued predominant use of ticagrelor. Following generic entry of prasugrel in the US in 2017, the 12-month treatment cost declined from $4,518 to $115, whereas ticagrelor costs remained largely unchanged at $2,843. If patients had initiated prasugrel instead of ticagrelor from Q4 2019 through 2024, estimated drug spending would have been up to $3 billion lower in the US. Conclusions Despite similar patient populations, prescribing patterns diverged between Germany and the United States. Earlier and greater adoption of prasugrel in Germany after 2019 contrasted with continued predominant use of ticagrelor in the US after randomized trials suggested prasugrel’s superiority over ticagrelor. Greater uptake of prasugrel in the US may have reduced drug spending without compromising post-myocardial infarction care.
title: Use and costs of P2Y12 inhibitors after myocardial infarction in germany and the US

abstract: Abstract Background The optimal timing of P2Y12 inhibitor administration in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial. While early pretreatment at first medical contact may reduce ischemic complications, concerns persist regarding bleeding risk and uncertain impact on mortality. Purpose To evaluate the clinical impact of P2Y12 pretreatment compared with periprocedural administration in patients with STEMI undergoing PCI. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases to identify eligible studies comparing P2Y12 inhibitor administration at first medical contact versus in the catheterization laboratory. The primary outcomes were in-hospital and 30-day all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary clinical endpoints included in-hospital and 30-day myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, and major bleeding events. Additional procedural endpoints included TIMI flow before and after PCI, thrombus aspiration, and no-reflow phenomenon. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, and effect estimates were expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Results Twenty-three studies comprising 83,955 patients were included in the meta-analysis. P2Y12 pretreatment was associated with lower rates of both in-hospital (RR: 0.78, 95%CI: 0.67-0.89, I²=0%) and 30-day MACE (RR: 0.82, 95%CI: 0.75-0.88, I²=19%). Conversely, there was no difference regarding in-hospital (RR: 0.74, 95%CI: 0.52-1.05, I²=59%) and 30-day all-cause mortality (RR: 0.81, 95%CI: 0.63-1.04, I²=59%). In addition, P2Y12 pretreatment was associated with a reduced risk of myocardial infarction (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74–0.98; I²=0%) and stent thrombosis (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.42–0.99; I²=31%) at 30 days, without a significant difference in major bleeding risk (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.84–1.12; I²=14%). No significant difference was observed in in-hospital myocardial infarction or stent thrombosis. Procedural outcomes, including initial TIMI 0/1 flow (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.89–1.01; I²=14%), post-procedural TIMI 3 flow (RR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00–1.05; I²=69%), thrombus aspiration (RR: 1.04, 95%CI: 0.89-1.21, I²=85%), and no-reflow phenomenon (RR: 0.84, 95%CI: 0.64-1.11, I²=39%), were similar between groups. Conclusion P2Y12 inhibitor pretreatment in patients with STEMI undergoing PCI was associated with a significant reduction in early ischemic events, including MACE, myocardial infarction, and stent thrombosis, without an increase in major bleeding. However, no mortality benefit was observed. These findings suggest a potential advantage of early antiplatelet loading in selected patients, while underscoring the need for additional randomized trials.
title: Timing of P2Y12 inhibitor administration in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Despite widespread use of inotropic agents in the management of cardiogenic shock (CS) the scientific evidence is limited. DOBERMANN-D was the first double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, clinical trial (RCT) to evaluate the effects of an early 24-hour infusion of low-dose dobutamine in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) at risk of CS development. The primary endpoint was neutral, with no difference in peak N-terminal Pro B-type Natriuretic Peptide (NT-proBNP) within 48 hours. Purpose This predefined DOBERMANN-D sub-study evaluated the effect of inotropic support with dobutamine on hemodynamic parameters. Methods DOBERMANN-D enrolled 100 AMI patients at risk of CS development (ORBI risk score ≥10 corresponding to ≥8% risk). Patients were randomized 1:1 to a 24-hour infusion of dobutamine (dbt, 5 μg/kg/minute) or placebo initiated &lt;2 hours after revascularization with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Hemodynamic status was evaluated by serial measurements of blood pressure, heart rate, serum lactate, and creatinine concentrations within 48 hours from admission. The extent of myocardial injury was assessed with peak and temporal changes of troponin T (TnT) concentrations. Temporal changes were assessed using linear mixed models adjusted for the baseline value. Echocardiographic parameters obtained at admission and 3-month follow-up included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), LV outflow tract velocity time integral (LVOT VTI), E/e’ lateral, and LV global longitudinal strain (GLS) and analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). Patients were followed during admission and for three months for adverse events (AE) and serious AE (SAE). Results Of the 100 included patients (68 years; 23% female), 99% had STEMI, 39% Killip Class &gt;1, and the median ORBI score was 12. During dbt infusion, mean arterial blood pressure (MAP) was lower (-7% difference, p=0.001, Figure 1A) and heart rate was higher (14% difference, p&lt;0.001) but returned to levels after 24 hours comparable to those in the placebo group. Temporal changes in lactate (Figure 1B), creatinine, and TnT were similar between groups. No differences in echocardiographic parameters of LVEF (dbt: 37% vs placebo: 40%), LVOT VTI (dbt: 18 cm vs placebo: 19 cm), E/e’ lateral (dbt: 11.5 vs placebo: 10.5), or GLS (dbt: -12% vs placebo: -12%) were detected during admission nor at follow-up (Figure 1C-E). In the dbt group, LVEF and LVOT VTI increased and GLS decreased from admission to follow-up. In contrast, only LVEF changed in the placebo group. There were no differences in the incidence of AE or SAE between the groups during hospitalization nor at follow-up. Conclusions In this RCT of inotropic support with low-dose dobutamine in AMI patients at risk of CS, heart rate increased and MAP decreased, but did not confer measurable benefit in filling pressures, cardiac output surrogate, myocardial function, AE nor SAE compared with placebo.Figure 1
title: Hemodynamic impact of low-dose dobutamine in patients with acute myocardial infarction at risk of cardiogenic shock – a randomized clinical trial

abstract: Abstract Background Oxidative stress and inflammation are central drivers of platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction, and myocardial injury in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Redox-sensitive pathways regulate platelet reactivity and vascular inflammation and may interact bidirectionally with P2Y₁₂ inhibition. Circulating biomarkers of oxidative and tissue/inflammatory stress provide insight into these processes and may reflect residual biological risk beyond platelet aggregation. Whether contemporary oral P2Y₁₂ inhibitors differentially modulate these pathways remains incompletely defined. Purpose To compare circulating biomarkers of oxidative stress, tissue stress, and platelet activation in AMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI) treated with prasugrel or ticagrelor. Methods This laboratory substudy of a multicentre randomized trial included 476 AMI patients with complete laboratory data (prasugrel n=234; ticagrelor n=242). Baseline demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics were well balanced between treatment groups (all p&gt; 0.05). Blood samples were obtained 24±6 hours after pPCI. Serum and plasma biomarkers of oxidative stress (thioredoxin-1, 8-isoprostane, superoxide dismutase 3, NADPH oxidase 2), tissue/inflammatory stress (soluble ST2, interleukin-33, α-klotho, growth differentiation factor 15), and platelet activation (thromboxane B₂, soluble P-selectin) were quantified. Unadjusted and multivariable analyses were performed adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, diabetes, smoking, and glomerular filtration rate. Exploratory subgroup analyses assessed treatment-by-subgroup interactions. Correlations were evaluated using Spearman’s rank coefficient. Results In unadjusted analyses, no significant differences were observed between prasugrel and ticagrelor treatment across oxidative and tissue stress biomarkers, or platelet activation in the whole cohort. Exploratory subgroup analyses identified isolated differences, including higher 8-isoprostane levels in ticagrelor vs prasugrel treated smokers (33.52 pg/ml [9.60–514.51] vs 26.39 [9.11–217.63]; p=0.041) and lower NADPH oxidase 2 levels in statin users on ticagrelor compared to prasugrel (2.10 U/ml [1.98–21.14] vs 2.54 [2.00–44.37]; p=0.022). However, no treatment-related differences were observed in the overall cohort or within any subgroup after multivariable adjustment (Table, Figure). In the whole study population, thioredoxin-1 correlated with soluble P-selectin (Spearman ρ=0.59). Conclusions In this randomized study of AMI patients undergoing pPCI, no differences in oxidative stress, tissue/inflammatory stress, or platelet activation were observed between prasugrel- and ticagrelor treatment, suggesting similar biological effects beyond platelet aggregation. The observed association between thioredoxin-1 and soluble P-selectin indicate a link between redox activity and platelet activation in AMI, independent of treatment.Figure
title: Comparison of oxidative and tissue stress biomarkers and platelet activation in myocardial infarction treated with prasugrel or ticagrelor

abstract: Abstract Introduction Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), comprising aspirin and a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (P2Y12i), remains the cornerstone of secondary prevention of thrombotic complications after acute coronary syndrome (ACS). However, the optimal P2Y12i to use as part of DAPT in patients with ACS remains uncertain. Purpose We aimed to perform a frequentist network meta-analysis comparing 1-year DAPT strategies based on different P2Y12 inhibitors after ACS. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception through January 2026 for randomised controlled trials (RCTs). Outcomes of interest were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, cardiac death, major bleeding, myocardial infarction (MI), stent thrombosis, and stroke. Random effects models were used to generate risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Treatments were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking (SUCRA). Results Thirteen RCTs comprising 54,215 patients were included (clopidogrel-based DAPT: n=23,557; ticagrelor-based DAPT: n=14,245; prasugrel-based DAPT: n=16,413). Compared with clopidogrel-based DAPT, prasugrel-based DAPT significantly reduced cardiac death (RR 0.89; 95% CI 0.80–1.00), MI (RR 0.85; 95% CI 0.72–0.99), and stent thrombosis (RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.38–0.62). Ticagrelor-based DAPT reduced cardiac death (RR 0.84; 95% CI 0.75–0.94) and stent thrombosis (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.58–0.89) compared with clopidogrel-based DAPT. Major bleeding was lower with clopidogrel-based DAPT compared with ticagrelor-based DAPT (RR 0.79; 95% CI 0.66–0.95). SUCRA analysis ranked prasugrel-based DAPT as most effective for reducing MACE (0.94), MI (0.95), stent thrombosis (0.99), and stroke (0.79). Ticagrelor-based DAPT ranked highest for reducing all-cause mortality (0.74) and cardiac death (0.90), while clopidogrel-based DAPT ranked highest for minimizing major bleeding (0.96). Conclusion Among 1-year DAPT strategies following ACS, prasugrel-based DAPT appears to provide the most favorable balance in reducing ischemic outcomes without a significant increase in major bleeding.Figure
title: Prasugrel-, ticagrelor-, or clopidogrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy after acute coronary syndrome: a frequentist network meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background The benefit of complete revascularization after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is well established in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, but the long-term effect in older patients remains uncertain. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the 10-year outcome of complete revascularization in older patients (aged ≥75 years) compared with younger patients. Methods Patients with STEMI and multivessel disease were randomized to either culprit-only or fractional flow reserve-guided complete revascularization in the DANAMI-3–PRIMULTI trial. This sub-study stratified the included 627 patients by ≥ 75 years (517) and &lt; 75 years (110). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, recurrent myocardial infarction, or any revascularization occurring during a median follow-up of 10.5 years. Results Of the older patients, 50 underwent complete and 60 culprit-only revascularization. Of the younger patients, 264 were completely revascularized compared to 253 who had culprit-only PCI performed. In the older group, complete revascularization showed no association with the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.29, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.82-2.03, P=0.27). In contrast, complete revascularization was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted HR 0.68, 95% CI: 0.53-0.88, P=0.003) in younger patients, primarily driven by a reduction in any revascularization (adjusted HR 0.60, 95% CI: 0.44-0.83, P=0.002). Conclusions In patients aged ≥75 years, evidence of a 10-years benefit of complete revascularization was not found. Complete revascularization was associated with a 32% lower risk of adverse outcomes among younger patients, primarily driven by a reduction in repeat revascularization.Abstract illustration
title: Complete revascularization according to age in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease: 10-year outcome from the DANAMI-3–PRIMULTI trial

abstract: Abstract Introduction and aim The role of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in elderly patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a subject of ongoing debate. Registries show that older patients are less frequently offered invasive coronary angiography, despite evidence supporting its superiority over conservative management. The aim of our study was to investigate the percentage of patients aged 75 years or older with ACS undergoing PCI and the mortality rates among those who underwent PCI compared with those who did not. Results We included 1036 consecutive patients aged 75 years or older (80.9±4.4) with ACS in our observational study. 488 (47.1%) were female, and 548 were male (52.9%). Myocardial infarction with ST-segment elevation (STEMI) was diagnosed in 40.69% of patients; myocardial infarction without ST-segment elevation (NSTEMI) in 53.33%; and non-stable angina pectoris in 5.98%. PCI was performed in 320 (30.9%) patients: 48.4% with STEMI, 19.1% with NSTEMI, and 19.7% with non-stable angina (p&lt;0.001). During hospitalization, 178 patients (17.2%) died, of whom 33 (10.31%) underwent PCI, while 145 patients (20.25%) did not (p&lt;0.001). In patients with Killip class I at admission, PCI was performed in 36.4%; in 35.9% with Killip class II; in 24.1% with Killip class III; and in 21.4% with Killip class IV (p=0.255). Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was similar in those with and without PCI (46.8 ± 12.6 vs. 46.1 ± 14.0%, p=0.485). Systolic blood pressure was similar between those with and without PCI (134.0 ± 27.4 vs. 132.6 ± 26.0 mmHg, p=0.5), heart rate was lower in PCI group (78.1 ± 18.9 vs. 86.5 ± 24.3 bpm, p&lt;0.001). Troponin I levels did not differ between PCI and non-PCI groups (2.14 vs. 1.42 ng/mL, p = 0.7), whereas brain natriuretic peptide levels were lower in the PCI group (322.6 vs. 784.4 pg/mL, p &lt; 0.01). CRP levels were lower in the PCI group (23.7 ± 44.0 vs. 38.5 ± 58.7 mg/L, p &lt; 0.001). The estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was significantly higher in the PCI group than in the non-PCI group (55.2 ± 23.0 vs. 48.3 ± 20.6 mL/min/1.73 m², p &lt; 0.001), as were hemoglobin levels (133.8 ± 77.5 vs. 124.6 ± 37.6 g/L, p = 0.015). LDL cholesterol levels were significantly higher in the PCI group (2.83 ± 1.09 vs. 2.60 ± 1.58, p &lt; 0.05). Conclusions PCI was performed in only a third of our patients, yet it appears highly protective, reducing in-hospital mortality in elderly ACS patients by nearly half. However, there was significant selection bias: patients who received PCI generally had better renal function, higher hemoglobin, lower BNP, reduced inflammation, and were hemodynamically stable. Paradoxically, those without PCI were on higher ischemic risk and might benefit most from revascularization. In elderly patients with ACS, a more thorough risk assessment should be performed when deciding on PCI, with age not being a contraindication.
title: Ageism camouflaged as medical judgment – why is PCI reserved for more stable elderly ACS patients?

abstract: Abstract Background As global life expectancy rises, elderly patients constitute an expanding proportion of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) presentations. Although the evidence-based treatment goal is complete revascularization, it is often not feasible in this population due to frailty, diffuse calcific and complex disease, and elevated procedural risk. Elderly patients therefore require tailored revascularization strategies, yet evidence to guide optimal decision making remains limited. Objective To evaluate whether residual coronary disease after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), quantified by the residual SYNTAX score (rSS) and the SYNTAX Revascularization Index (SRI), can define clinically meaningful targets of incomplete revascularization in elderly ACS. We hypothesized that a range of incomplete revascularization would yield clinical outcomes comparable to those achieved with complete revascularization in this population. Methods This retrospective study included 500 patients aged ≥65 years who underwent PCI for ACS at a tertiary cardiac center and were followed for a median of 46 months. Three interventional cardiologists independently calculated the baseline SYNTAX score (bSS), rSS, and SRI ([1 − rSS/bSS] × 100). Patients were categorized into three predefined SRI groups: &lt;50%, 50%–&lt;100%, and 100% to reflect increasing degrees of revascularization completeness, consistent with prior literature. Primary outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and the log-rank test. Following predefined SRI categorization, ROC analyses were performed separately for mortality and MACE to refine outcome specific prognostic thresholds, followed by Cox proportional hazards modeling. Patients were subsequently reclassified according to ROC-derived cut-offs for further analyses. Results Lower SRI values were associated with greater anatomical complexity and higher event rates. All-cause mortality increased from 17.8% in patients with SRI 100% to 37.5% in those with SRI &lt;50% (p&lt;0.001), with similar gradients observed for cardiovascular death and MACE (both p&lt;0.001). ROC analysis identified an optimal SRI threshold of approximately 40% for predicting all-cause mortality (AUC:0.605; p &lt; 0.001), with SRI &lt;40% independently associated with increased risk of death (HR 2.48; p&lt;0.001). For MACE, an optimal threshold near 70% was identified (AUC:0.611; p &lt; 0.001) and SRI &lt;70% independently predicted events (HR 1.39; p=0.006). Above these thresholds, clinical outcomes were comparable to those observed after complete revascularization. Conclusion This study moves beyond the binary concept of complete versus incomplete revascularization by identifying distinct mortality and MACE related thresholds, defining a clinically acceptable range of incomplete revascularization to guide personalized treatment in elderly ACS patients.
title: Is there an acceptable level of incomplete revascularization after PCI in elderly ACS?

abstract: Abstract Background The slow flow phenomenon during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is associated with adverse outcomes and impaired myocardial salvage. Excessive expansion of the culprit lesion may increase distal embolization and lead to slow flow phenomenon, thereby limiting myocardial salvage. Although filter devices are designed to prevent embolization during stent deployment, their impact on myocardial salvage remains uncertain. Purpose We investigated whether culprit lesion expansion volume (CEV) assessed by intravascular imaging is associated with myocardial salvage and whether distal filter device use modifies this relationship in STEMI patients. Methods Consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI with intravascular imaging (IVUS, OCT, or OFDI) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) at approximately 4 days and 6 months between 2017 and 2025 were included. Culprit expansion volume (CEV) was calculated as the difference between pre- and post-stent lumen volumes, approximated as two combined conical frustums. Myocardial salvage index was derived from acute phase area-at-risk (T2-weighted imaging) and chronic phase infarct size (late gadolinium enhancement). Correlation analyses were performed according to filter device use. Multivariable linear regression analysis was conducted to identify independent determinants of myocardial salvage index. Results A total of 64 patients were analyzed (median age 69 years [IQR 62–75], 86% male). In patients without filter device use, CEV was significantly negatively correlated with salvage index (r=0.58, p=0.02). In contrast, no significant association was observed in patients using filter devices (r=－0.05, p=0.75), suggesting attenuation of the adverse effect of excessive expansion. In multivariable regression analysis (R²=0.20), chronic kidney disease was negatively associated with salvage index (β=−0.17, 95% CI −0.31 to −0.03, p=0.02), whereas filter device use (β=0.15, 95% CI 0.003 to 0.33, p=0.04) and final myocardial blush grade 3 (β=0.17, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.30, p=0.02) were independently associated with higher salvage index. CEV itself was not independently associated with salvage index after adjustment. Conclusions Excessive culprit lesion expansion is associated with impaired myocardial salvage in STEMI when distal protection is not used. Distal filter device use and achievement of myocardial blush grade 3 are independently associated with improved myocardial salvage.
