The reduction in MACCE with an invasive strategy was observed in patients without or moderate frailty (CFS 1–6), but the benefit decreased as frailty increased (interaction p=0.01) and was not statistically significant in severely frail patients (CFS 7–8; HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.48–1.06) (table 2). Conclusion Among elderly patients with NSTEMI, an invasive strategy was associated with lower 1-year risk of cardiovascular events, including those with moderate frailty (CFS 5–6). In severely frail patients (CFS 7–8), the benefit was numerically lower but not statistically significant. These findings support considering angiography in selected older adults, with individualized risk assessment based on frailty.Outcomes

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 15,537 patients aged ≥70 years with NSTEMI from 2017 to 2021; 11,743 (75.6%) underwent invasive coronary angiography, while 3,794 (24.4%) were managed conservatively.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with residual confounding despite the instrument; frailty scored retrospectively and conference abstract only.
appraisal.one_line: SWEDEHEART analysis of invasive management by frailty in older patients with NSTEMI using instrumental variable and propensity matching.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In IV-adjusted models, an invasive strategy was associated with lower risk of 1-year MACCE (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.44–0.64), mortality (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.38–0.60) and MI (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.30–0.64), with no significant effect on stroke (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.41–1.72). In severely frail patients (CFS 7–8) MACCE HR was 0.68, 95% CI 0.48–1.06 (interaction p=0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an older and frail population under-represented in invasive-strategy trials, where the benefit appears to attenuate with severe frailty.

title: Frailty and invasive management in elderly patients with myocardial infarction. A report from SWEDEHEART registry

abstract: Abstract Background In an aging population, concomitant valvular heart disease is increasingly prevalent. While aortic stenosis (AS) is a known driver of reduced life expectancy, its specific impact on the prognosis of patients presenting with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) remains insufficiently characterized. This study sought to determine whether AS severity independently exacerbates NSTEMI outcomes, focusing on in-hospital mortality and major complications. Methods Consecutive NSTEMI patients referred for coronary angiography were prospectively enrolled in a single-center, all-comers, real-world registry. AS severity was stratified by initial transthoracic echocardiography, typically performed in the emergency department before angiography or, if deferred for urgent invasive management, afterwards in the coronary care unit. Adverse in-hospital events were a composite of in-hospital all-cause death, cardiogenic shock, and mechanical ventilation. To determine the independent association between AS and in-hospital outcomes a regression analysis adjusting for age, sex, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, troponin, ejection fraction, myocardial infarction type, culprit lesion diameter stenosis and culprit vessel was performed. The final multivariable regression model exclusively included covariates that demonstrated statistical significance in the preliminary univariable analysis. Results Of 1414 registry patients, 1380 underwent echocardiographic assessment of the aortic valve and comprised the study cohort. The median age was 70 (IQR 60–79) years, and 414 (30.0%) were female. Regarding AS severity, 1232 (89.3%) patients had no AS, while 45 (3.3%), 52 (3.8%), and 51 (3.7%) had mild, moderate, and severe AS, respectively. Increasing AS severity was associated with older age (p&lt;0.001), higher creatinine levels (p&lt;0.001), lower hemoglobin (p&lt;0.001), and lower ejection fraction (p=0.007). No significant difference in peak troponin was observed across AS classifications (p = 0.132), however. Adverse in-hospital events occurred in 14.9% of patients with no AS, 17.8% with mild, 23.1% with moderate, and 37.3% with severe AS (p &lt; 0.001). In-hospital mortality rates were 5.0%, 8.9%, 15.4%, and 23.5% across the respective groups (p &lt; 0.001). Following multivariable adjustment, severe AS remained independently associated with both adverse in-hospital events (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.1–4.0, p=0.031) and in-hospital death (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.2–6.1, p=0.011). Conclusions Concomitant severe AS is independently associated with significantly worse outcomes and increased mortality in patients presenting with NSTEMI. Hence, patients with severe aortic stenosis at high risk for acute coronary syndromes might benefit from early interventional or surgical treatment to mitigate adverse outcomes and improve overall prognosis.Figure
title: Impact of concomitant aortic stenosis on in-hospital outcomes in non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Among patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) presenting in a pre-shock state, a subset deteriorates to cardiogenic shock within 24 hours (“delayed shock”). Purpose To identify predictors of delayed shock progression and to derive a clinically applicable risk score. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study of consecutive ACS patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between 2021 and 2025 (n=336). Patients presenting with SCAI stage A or B at hospital arrival were included. We excluded patients who underwent PCI more than 24 hours after arrival and those with procedure-related complications. Patients who progressed to SCAI stage C–E within 24 hours were classified as the Worsened group, while those who remained at SCAI stage A–B were classified as the Stable group (Figure 1). A final age- and sex-adjusted model was constructed using Firth penalized logistic regression. A point-based risk score was derived from the regression coefficients. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Internal validation was performed with 500 bootstrap resamples to estimate the optimism-corrected AUC. Results Among 336 patients, 240 presented with SCAI stage A or B at hospital arrival. Of these, 32 patients progressed to SCAI stage C–E within 24 hours (Worsened group, n = 32; Stable group, n = 208). The median age was 76 years in the Worsened group versus 71 years in the Stable group, and 65.6% (21/32) were male in the Worsened group versus 70.2% (146/208) in the Stable group. ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) was present in 78.1% (25/32) of the Worsened group and 62.0% (129/208) of the Stable group (p = 0.116), Killip class II or III was observed in 25.0% (8/32) versus 4.8% (10/208), respectively. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the Worsened group compared with the Stable group (28.1% [9/32] vs. 0.5% [1/208], log-rank p &lt; 0.001), and was comparable to that of patients presenting with cardiogenic shock at hospital arrival (33.3% [10/30]). Based on the Firth penalized logistic regression model, the derived risk score assigned 1 point for STEMI, 2 points for Killip class II or III, and 3 points each for multivessel disease and heart rate ≥100 bpm (Figure 3). The apparent AUC was 0.764; the optimism-corrected AUC after 500 bootstrap resamples was 0.763 (optimism = 0.001). Higher scores were significantly associated with delayed shock progression (Figure 4). Conclusion In ACS patients presenting with SCAI stage A–B, progression to SCAI stage C–E within 24 hours was associated with markedly worse in-hospital survival, comparable to patients presenting with overt cardiogenic shock. A simple four-variable risk score demonstrated good discriminative ability and may facilitate early risk stratification for delayed shock.
title: Risk factors for 24-hour progression to cardiogenic shock in acute coronary syndrome presenting with pre-shock state

abstract: Abstract Backgroud Although emergency mitral valve surgery (MVS) is the preferred treatment for papillary muscle rupture (PMR) post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI), cardiogenic shock (CS) patients may be denied, due to high surgical risk. These patients may benefit from mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) as a bridge therapy or permanent solution. Purpose We aimed to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis of the literature regarding therapeutic options for PMR post-AMI patients complicated with CS. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and SCOPUS from January 1990 to February 2026. Studies reporting CS in patients with PMR post-AMI and mortality as a primary outcome have been included. The secondary outcomes were use of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) and associated mortality. Single-arm meta-analysis of proportions was performed in R (v. 4.5.2) using a random-effects model with Hartung–Knapp adjustment, given the absence of direct comparative studies between MVS and M-TEER. Outcomes were reported with 95% confidence interval (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Results A total of 10 observational studies were analyzed: three M-TEER articles, five MVS articles, one extra-corporeal life support (ECLS) article, and one article which included patients with and without interventions. The latter was not included in the meta-analysis of proportions, as it didn’t report separate data for CS patients who underwent interventions as opposed to those without interventions. The remaining nine studies, with 933 adult patients, were included in this meta-analysis. Across seven studies with PMR post-AMI and CS (n=875), the pooled in-hospital mortality was 31% (95% CI: 28–35%), with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 43%). In subgroup analyses, pooled in-hospital mortality was: 31% (95% CI: 26–36%; I² = 54%) in the MVS cohort (n=839), respectively 42% (95% CI: 27–58%; I² = 29%) in the M-TEER cohort (n=36). Four studies reporting 1-year outcomes (n=87) demonstrated a pooled 1-year mortality of 29% (95% CI: 16–46%), with moderate-to-low heterogeneity (I² = 27%). The pooled proportion of patients requiring MCS (n=173) was 90% (95% CI: 65–98%), indicating a high need for hemodynamic support in this population. Among patients requiring MCS (n=100), pooled mortality was 50% (95% CI: 34–66%; I² = 41%), highlighting the severe prognosis once advanced support is needed. All these findings represent indirect comparisons across non-randomized cohorts and should be interpreted cautiously. Conclusion PMR after AMI complicated by CS is associated with high mortality and frequent use of MCS. Although MVS showed numerically lower mortality than M-TEER, the available evidence is limited and non-comparative. Overall outcomes remain poor despite contemporary management, highlighting the severity of the condition and the need for further studies directly comparing surgical and transcatheter strategies.Procedural (MVS or M-TEER) mortalitiesMCS use & mortality
title: Cardiogenic shock in patients with papillary muscle rupture post-acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background In contemporary settings, the trajectory and patterns of blood pressure after discharge in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) with heart failure (HF) remain unclear. Purpose We evaluated the serial changes and predictors of systolic blood pressure (SBP) after discharge in patients with AMI complicated by HF. Methods This prospective, multicenter registry included patients with AMI and HF who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention between November 2021 and March 2024. SBP was measured at discharge and at 1, 3, and 12 months in an outpatient setting. We illustrated the trajectory of SBP and the proportions of elevated blood pressure (SBP ≥140 mmHg) and hypotension (SBP &lt;90 mmHg) during follow-up. In the multivariable analysis, predictors of elevated blood pressure at 1 or 3 months were also assessed. Results A total of 1050 patients were included in the present study, among whom 788 (75.0%) had hypertension at baseline. During the follow-up, the mean SBP increased from discharge to 1 month, with no significant differences thereafter (Figure). The proportions of patients with elevated SBP also increased from discharge to 1 month and then plateaued at 3 and 12 months, while those with hypotension remained low during the follow-up period (Figure). No prior history of myocardial infarction, a culprit vessel in the right or left circumflex coronary artery, and lower peak creatine kinase levels were independently associated with SBP ≥140 mmHg at 1 or 3 months. Conclusions In patients with AMI and HF, SBP increased from discharge to 1-month follow-up, with no significant changes thereafter, suggesting that elevated blood pressure may be masked during hospitalization. Patients with less severe manifestations of AMI were likely to have higher SBP in an outpatient setting. Our findings highlight the importance of recognizing blood pressure trajectories and patterns in the management of hypertension.Figure
title: Patterns and trajectories of long-term trajectory of blood pressure in patients with acute myocardial infarction and heart failure

abstract: Abstract Background Although early outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) have improved, late residual risk beyond the first year remains insufficiently defined. We investigated predictors of late mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients who remained event-free during the first year after AMI. Methods From the Korean Acute Myocardial Infarction Registry-V (KAMIR-V), a nationwide multicenter registry including 38 primary PCI centers in South Korea, 16,177 consecutive AMI patients were enrolled between January 2016 and June 2020. Among them, 14,979 underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) during index hospitalization and comprised the study population. Of these, 13,884 patients were free from MACE at 12 months and formed the landmark cohort. The primary endpoint was all-cause death between 12 and 36 months; the secondary endpoint was MACE (death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke) during the same period. Multivariable Cox regression was performed to identify independent predictors. Results In the 12-month event-free PCI cohort (n=13,884), mean age was 63.5±12.3 years and 78.7% were male; 15.7% had renal dysfunction (eGFR&lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m²), 27.0% had diabetes, 17.1% had Killip class ≥II, 11.2% had LVEF&lt;40%, and 52.7% had multivessel disease. ST-elevation myocardial infarction accounted for 6,890 patients, with a median door-to-balloon time of 63 (50–83) minutes. Between 12 and 36 months, all-cause death occurred in 2.2% and MACE in 3.5% of patients. Independent predictors of late death, ranked by adjusted hazard ratio (HR), were renal dysfunction (HR 2.25), LVEF&lt;40% (HR 1.90), prior heart failure (HR 1.83), diabetes (HR 1.72), Killip ≥II (HR 1.58), prior myocardial infarction (HR 1.46), male sex (HR 1.35), and older age (HR 1.07 per year), whereas higher BMI was inversely associated (HR 0.95 per kg/m²). For late MACE, renal dysfunction (HR 1.91), diabetes (HR 1.69), prior myocardial infarction (HR 1.67), prior heart failure (HR 1.70), LVEF&lt;40% (HR 1.53), Killip ≥II (HR 1.43), and older age (HR 1.04 per year) remained significant predictors. Conclusions Among AMI patients undergoing PCI who were free from major events at 12 months, clinically meaningful late mortality and MACE persisted between 12 and 36 months. Renal dysfunction, residual clinical severity, diabetes, and left ventricular dysfunction were key determinants of late adverse outcomes, supporting the need for continued risk stratification beyond the first year after AMI.
title: Late residual risk between 12 and 36 months after event-free survival following acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Introduction Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) may arise from genetic susceptibility, particularly through mechanisms involving coronary microvascular dysfunction and thrombotic events. Behavioral triggers — such as smoking, substance use, stress, cold exposure, and certain medications — can also provoke coronary artery spasm. However, the underlying genetic contributors remain incompletely defined. Aim Identify the genetic, behavioral, and traditional risk factors associated with obstructive myocardial infarction (MI-CAD) compared with non-obstructive (MINOCA) in a Southern European population. Methods This prospective, single-centre observational cohort study included 1,633 patients fulfilling myocardial infarction criteria and admitted between January 2000 and December 2019. All underwent coronary angiography, evaluated by two interventional cardiologists using the Leaman Score; a score of 0 defined MINOCA. Traditional risk factors, behavioral variables, and biochemical markers were analysed. Peripheral DNA was genotyped using TaqMan assays for 33 CAD-related SNPs. Associations between genetic variants and traditional risk factors associated with MI-CAD were examined using bivariate and multivariate logistic regression. Results Among the 1,633 patients, 1,546 (94.7%) had MI-CAD. Compared with MINOCA, MI-CAD individuals showed significantly higher prevalence of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome, and reported lower physical activity. In bivariate analyses, five SNPs were significantly associated with MI-CAD when compared with MINOCA group: TCF21 rs12190287 GC+CC (90.8% vs 80.5%, respectively; p=0.002), PON rs662 RR (9.4% vs 1.1%; p=0.009), CDKN2B rs4977574 GG (38.2% vs 26.4%; p=0.027), ADIPOQ rs266729 CG+GG (42.4% vs 54.0%; p=0.034), and PCSK9 rs2114580 GA+AA (45.1% vs 32.2%; p=0.018) (dominant and recessive models). After multivariate adjustment, four variants remained independently associated with MI-CAD: TCF21 GC+CC (OR=2.67;p=0.001), CDKN2B GG (OR=1.94;p=0.011), PCSK9 GA+AA (OR=1.93; p=0.008), and PON RR (OR=9.20;p=0.030). Among traditional risk factors, type 2 diabetes (p=0.017), age (p&lt;0.0001), and male sex (p&lt;0.0001) were also independent predictors of MI-CAD. Conclusions Patients with MI-CAD presented higher rates of cardiometabolic risk factors than those with MINOCA. Genetic variants in TCF21, CDKN2B, PCSK9, and PON emerged as independent contributors to obstructive MI.Dissecting Genetic and Clinical Determinants
title: Dissecting genetic and clinical determinants of obstructive and non-obstructive myocardial infarction: a southern european cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Some studies showed that the prognosis for patients with Myocardial Infarction (MI) with Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease (MINOCA) is more favourable compared to those with Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease (MI-CAD). However, it has been proven to be worse than the general population. Objective Evaluate the prognostic value of MINOCA compared with a general population without apparent CAD from a Southern European population. Methods A single-centre, prospective, and observational cohort study was performed from January 2000 to December 2023 with a total of 1,524 individuals. Patients were considered MINOCA if their coronary angiogram was classified as zero by the Leaman score. All participants underwent clinical observation, completed a survey form including demographic and traditional risk factors, and underwent biochemical analysis. The primary outcome was all-cause cardiovascular (CV) events [MI, revascularisation, heart failure, stroke, peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and death]. Cox regression analysis identified variables independently associated with CV events and assessed the risk (HR) in these populations. The Kaplan-Meier estimated event-free survival over time. Results Of the 1,524 participants, 87 (5.7%) had MINOCA and 1,437 (94.3%) were normal individuals without symptomatic CAD. Among the 87 MINOCA patients, 14 (16.1%) had CV events, vs 108 (7.5%) in the normal group. The Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated that patients with MINOCA had a lower event-free probability throughout the follow-up period. Specifically, at the end of 15 years, the event-free probability was 52.2% in MINOCA vs 88.7% in the normal group. After Cox regression analysis, the risk of CV for patients with MINOCA was approximately 5 times higher compared with the normal group (p&lt;0.0001). The other variables identified as independently associated with CV events were male sex (p=0.018), age (p&lt;0.0001), smoking (p=0.001), and hypertension (p=0.001). Conclusion In this prospective cohort, patients with MINOCA had a substantially higher long-term risk of CV events than individuals without CAD. Event-free survival was markedly reduced, and MINOCA remained a strong independent predictor of adverse CV outcomes. These findings reinforce that MINOCA is not a benign condition and highlight the need for rigorous risk stratification and sustained secondary prevention in this population.MINOCA vs controls
title: Beyond “normal” coronaries: the hidden long-term risk of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Introduction Some studies showed that the prognosis for patients with Myocardial Infarction (MI) with Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease (MINOCA) is more favourable compared to those with Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease (CAD). However, it has been proven to be worse than the general population. Objective Evaluate the prognostic value of the MINOCA compared to MI with obstructive CAD in a Southern European population. Methods A prospective, single-centre, observational cohort study was performed from January 2000 to December 2023. A total of 1,633 patients with MI were admitted and underwent coronary angiography, being followed for a mean of 7.6±6.7 years. Angiography was evaluated by two interventional cardiologists, who classified it according to the Leaman Score (which quantifies the total burden of CAD based on plaque location, type, and degree of stenosis). A score of zero was established to define MINOCA. Demographic, traditional risk factors and biochemical data were obtained from all patients. Patients with MINOCA were compared to those with obstructive coronary arteries. The primary outcome was the occurrence of cardiovascular events (CVEs) from all causes (MI, revascularisation, heart failure, stroke, peripheral arterial disease, and death). Cox regression analysis identified variables independently associated with CVEs and estimated risk in these populations. Kaplan-Meier assessed event-free survival over time. Results Of 1,633 patients with MI, only 87 patients (5.3%) had MINOCA, and 1,546 (94.7%) had obstructive CAD. Within MINOCA, 16.1% had CVEs, and 42.2% had CVEs in those with obstructive CAD. The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that MINOCA patients had a higher event-free probability throughout follow-up. Specifically, at 10 years, the event-free rate was 79.6% vs 40.3% in the MI with obstructive CAD. After Cox regression analysis, the risk of CVEs for patients with MI with obstructive CAD was three times higher than that of those with MINOCA (HR=3.2; 95% CI: 1.9-5.4; p&lt;0.0001). The other variables independently associated with CVEs were diabetes (p=0.041) and physical inactivity (p=0.005). Conclusion Although MINOCA patients show a significantly better prognosis than those with obstructive MI, the condition is not benign. The broader MINOCA spectrum remains associated with recurrent symptoms, frequent healthcare use, and a long-term risk profile that, while lower than obstructive CAD, progressively converges over time.Obstructiva CAD vs MINOCA
title: MINOCA: better than obstructive myocardial infarction, but not harmless — long-term outcomes from a Southern European registry

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) non-invasively detects coronary lesions potentially causing myocardial infarction, but its early diagnostic role in myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) remains unclear. Objectives To assess the value of early CCTA combined with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) in a non-invasive approach to MINOCA. Methods In this prospective, multicentric study, MINOCA patients underwent invasive coronary angiography (ICA), followed within 7 days by CMR and CCTA. Non-ischaemic aetiologies were excluded. ICA evaluated coronary stenosis, myocardial bridges (MB), epicardial spasms, and non-obstructive spontaneous coronary artery dissections (SCAD). CCTA assessed high-risk plaques (HRP), MB, and non-obstructive SCAD. Patients were grouped as MINOCA-CT+ or MINOCA-CT− based on CCTA findings. Fat attenuation index (FAI) and CT fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) were assessed per-vessel. The primary endpoint was concordance between CCTA-detected lesions and CMR-identified ischaemic damage within the same territory, compared with ICA. ROC analysis evaluated diagnostic performance. Results Among 77 confirmed MINOCA patients, 42 (54.6%) had coronary lesions on CCTA. HRP were found in 35 (45.5%) patients, MB in 7 (9%), and no non-obstructive SCAD was observed. MINOCA-CT+ patients exhibited greater total plaque volume, greater myocardial edema (9.2% vs 4.3% of the left ventricle; P=0.003), and infarct size (6% vs 2.4%; P=0.003). FAI ≥–70 HU or FFR-CT &lt;0.80 correlated with edema and myocardial injury on CMR (all P&lt;0.05). Concordance between CCTA lesions and CMR ischaemic pattern was 49.4% (vs 45.5% with ICA; P=0.084 per-patient, P=0.029 per-vessel). CCTA’s positive predictive value for CMR ischaemia was 91% (per-patient) and 78% (per-vessel); negative predictive value was 49% and 89%, respectively—both exceeding ICA. ROC confirmed CCTA's strong performance (AUC 0.74 per-patient, 0.78 per-vessel) to detect concordant ischaemic damage at CMR. Conclusions Combined CCTA and CMR identified ischaemic injury and coronary abnormalities in many MINOCA patients. CCTA demonstrated strong diagnostic value elucidating underlying coronary mechanisms.
title: Early diagnostic role of coronary computed tomography angiography combined with cardiac magnetic resonance in MINOCA

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a heterogeneous condition with incompletely understood mechanisms. Early diastolic filling contributes to ventricular efficiency and reflects myocardial relaxation and compliance, which may be altered by coronary microvascular dysfunction. Purpose We aimed to determine whether patients with MINOCA demonstrate impaired early diastolic filling efficiency, quantified by early filling blood kinetic energy using four-dimensional flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (4D flow CMR). Methods 46 MINOCApatients and 50 healthy controls without known cardiovascular disease were included in this study, and all underwentcine and 4D flow MRI. Using MASS software, automated segmentation of the LV endocardial and epicardial borders was performed using an artificial intelligence–based algorithm to derive conventional LV volumes and myocardial mass, with manual adjustments performed when necessary, according to Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance recommendations. Four LV flow components (direct flow, retained inflow, delayed ejection flow and residual volume) and LV kinetic energy parameters normalized to LV end-diastolic volume (KEiEDV) were derived. Results See Table. Compared with controls, patients with MINOCA exhibited marked alterations in LV flow energetics, characterized by reduced LV direct flow (15% vs. 33%, P&lt;0.001) and increased LV residual volume (47% vs. 35%, P&lt;0.001), together with significantly decreased KEiEDV parameters. Peak E-wave KEiEDV demonstrated excellent discriminatory performance for identifying MINOCA (AUC = 0.898). Applying a threshold derived from the control population (mean − 1 SD; 12.50 μJ/mL), impaired early filling efficiency was detected in 74% of MINOCA patients. Conclusion These findings indicate that a substantial proportion of MINOCA patients have reduced early diastolic blood kinetic energy, reflecting impaired ventricular filling efficiency and potentially underlying abnormalities in myocardial relaxation, ventricular compliance, and coronary microvascular function.
title: Characterizing early ventricular inefficiency in MINOCA using four-dimensional flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance

abstract: Abstract Background Severe coronary artery vasospasm can provoke malignant ventricular arrhythmias and represents an important cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Several studies worldwide have reported that vasospastic angina (VSA) accounts for approximately 2–11% of OHCA cases. However, the clinical benefit of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation for secondary prevention in this population has not been clearly established. Methods Between January 2015 and December 2023, 3,578 patients with OHCA were transferred to our institution. Of these, 318 achieved return of spontaneous circulation and underwent coronary angiography (CAG) to determine the underlying cause. Among them, 28 patients were diagnosed with VSA. Inclusion criteria were as follows: a positive acetylcholine provocation test; severe stenosis or occlusion on initial CAG that completely resolved with vasodilator therapy alone; or transient ischemic electrocardiographic changes accompanied by anginal symptoms without explanatory coronary lesions on CAG. One-year adverse events—defined as all-cause mortality, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, and ventricular arrhythmia (including ICD therapy)—were compared. Neurological status was evaluated using the Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) scale, with favorable neurological outcome defined as CPC 1–2. Results VSA was identified as the cause of OHCA in 28 patients (0.8%). The initial cardiac rhythm was shockable in 83% of cases. Twenty-four patients (85.7%) survived to hospital discharge, and 22 patients (78.6%) achieved favorable neurological outcomes. Of the 25 patients followed for 1 year after discharge, 20 (80%) survived with favorable neurological status (figure). All 24 survivors received vasospasm-preventive therapy, including calcium channel blockers, nitrates, and/or nicorandil. ICD implantation was performed in 14 patients (58.3%). During follow-up, appropriate ICD therapy occurred in 1 of 14 patients (7.1%), while inappropriate therapy occurred in 2 of 14 patients (14.3%). No significant differences were observed in the incidence of adverse events between the two groups. Likewise, there were no significant differences in 1-year survival or favorable neurological outcomes (13/14 [92.6%] vs. 7/7 [100%], P = 1.000). One patient with poor medication adherence experienced recurrent OHCA within 1 year despite ICD implantation. Conclusions No statistically significant differences in adverse events were observed between patients with and without ICD implantation. The occurrence of recurrent OHCA in a patient with poor medication adherence despite ICD therapy highlights that device therapy cannot replace optimal medical management. Routine ICD implantation for secondary prevention in patients with VSA-related OHCA may not be warranted; instead, management should be individualized, with strict adherence to optimal vasodilator therapy.Kaplan Meier
title: The impact of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator on long-term prognosis of successfully resuscitated patients with vasospastic angina after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest

abstract: Abstract Background Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a reversible acute heart failure syndrome. Electrocardiographic (ECG) abnormalities are common at presentation and may reflect underlying disease severity, but their prognostic significance remains incompletely understood. Purpose We aimed to determine whether distinct ischemic ECG patterns at admission identify TTS patients at higher risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Methods In this nationwide, register-based cohort study, we included all patients with a first-time TTS diagnosis between 2008 and 2021 who had an ECG recorded within 24 hours of admission. Patients were stratified by ECG pattern: ST-segment elevation, ST-segment depression, T-wave inversion, or no ischemic changes. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality; cardiovascular death was assessed as a secondary outcome. Cox regression models were adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, atrial fibrillation, acute coronary syndrome, hypercholesterolemia, and cancer, with death from other causes treated as a competing risk. Results A total of 1,244 patients were included (mean age 70.8 years; 89.1% women) and stratified by ECG pattern as follows: no ischemic changes (n = 707, 56.8%), ST-segment elevation (n = 226, 18.2%), ST-segment depression (n = 95, 7.6%), and T-wave inversion (n = 216, 17.4%). One-year all-cause mortality was highest among patients with ST-segment elevation (15.0%) compared with no ischemic changes (7.6%), T-wave inversion (6.5%), and ST-segment depression (5.3%). After adjustment, ST-segment elevation was independently associated with a significantly increased risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.19–1.96) whereas ST-segment depression and T-wave inversion were not. Cardiovascular death occurred infrequently but was more common among patients with ST-segment elevation. In adjusted analyses, patients with ST-segment elevation had a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular death (HR 2.65, 95% CI 1.16-5.70) compared with those without ST-segment elevation. Conclusions ST-segment elevation on admission ECG identifies TTS patients at higher risk of both all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, highlighting its potential role in risk stratification and guiding closer monitoring and management.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Ischemic ECG patterns at admission identify Takotsubo patients at increased risk of mortality

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Takotsubo (Stress) cardiomyopathy is an uncommon but increasingly recognized condition causing acute heart failure, with severe complication rates comparable to those of acute coronary syndrome (1-3). The contemporary epidemiology and outcomes of this condition have not been studied since the release of the 2018 International Takotsubo Diagnostic Criteria (4) and after the COVID-19 pandemic in a large, nationwide sample in the United States. Purpose To evaluate trends in the incidence and outcomes of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy in the United States. Methods We used Epic Cosmos, a nationwide dataset built in collaboration with U.S. health systems using the Epic electronic medical record, which includes inpatient and outpatient records for more than 300 million patients across nearly 43,000 clinics and 1,915 hospitals. Trends in the annual age and sex-adjusted cumulative incidence of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, identified via ICD-10-CM I51.81 in any inpatient admission, were estimated using Poisson regression. We examined trends in in-hospital mortality, cardiovascular and neurological complications, and length of stay (LOS) from 2015-2025. For each calendar year, the denominator included patients who were alive and had at least one encounter in the preceding two years as of January 1. Results Of 67,763,731 patients at risk in 2015 and 166,450,170 at risk in 2025, 4,039 (5.96 per 100,000) and 24,902 (14.96 per 100,000) developed Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, respectively. This corresponded to age and sex-adjusted cumulative incidences of 6.36 (95% CI 6.16-6.55 per 100,000) and 14.55 (95% CI 14.37-14.73 per 100,000), yielding an annual percent change (APC) of 7.42% (95% CI 5.23-7.62%, p&lt;.001). Trends are visualized graphically in Figure 1, stratified by age (A) and sex (B). Rates of complications (A), including atrial fibrillation, cardiac arrest, cardiogenic shock, acute heart failure, myocardial rupture, and stroke, as well as in-hospital mortality (B) are shown in Figure 2. In general, rates of most complications increased from 2015-2025, especially cardiogenic shock, which was observed in nearly 1 in 5 patients by 2025. In-hospital mortality rose from 7.3% in 2015 to 9.9% in 2021 and then fell to 8.4% in 2025. The proportion of patients with LOS &lt;3 days decreased from 26.0% to 22.8%, (APC -1.33%, 95% CI -1.69 to -0.98%, p&lt;.001) and the proportion of patients with a LOS&gt;14 days increased from 13.8% to 15.6% (APC 1.57%, 95% CI 1.11-2.04%, p&lt;.001). Conclusions The incidence of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy increased substantially from 2015 to 2025, with associated increases in rates of mortality and complications during this time. Notable increases in mortality were observed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Future research to improve outcomes for patients with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is needed.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Nationwide trends in incidence and outcomes of takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy, 2015-2025

abstract: Abstract Introduction Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is characterized by transient regional systolic dysfunction, dilatation, and oedema involving most frequently left ventricular apex and/or mid-ventricle in the absence of obstructive coronary disease. It frequently mimics acute coronary syndromes and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. In 2019, Wischnewsky et al. developed the InterTAK Prognostic Score for the prediction of short- and long-term mortality in this population. However, external validation of the InterTAK Prognostic Score in large nationwide cohorts remains limited. Purpose The aim of our study is to evaluate the prognostic value of InterTAK Prognostic Score in a large nationwide cohort. Methods It is a retrospective cohort study based on the Spanish multicentre TTS registry (RETAKO). For this analysis, we included all eligible patients registered between January 2012 to May 2025. The InterTAK Score was applied at admission following its definition (variables considered consist of: TTS secondary to neurologic disorders; TTS secondary to physical activities, medical conditions or procedures; age; systolic blood pressure; diabetes mellitus; left ventricular ejection fraction; sex; heart rate; and TTS without triggering factor). The discriminative ability of the score was assessed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves and the area under the curve (AUC). Results 2,174 patients were included. The median age was 73±9 years and 85.5% were women. Cardiovascular risk factors were highly prevalent: hypertension (66.4%), dyslipidaemia (50.9%) and diabetes mellitus (24.4%); though obesity (14.1%) and active smoking (13.5%) were less common. Chronic comorbidities included chronic kidney disease (10.3%), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (8.6%) and neurological diseases (9.9%). Patients were followed for a median of 657 days (IQR: 147-1,798 days) from the index hospitalization; more than 25% of patients had follow-up extending beyond 6 years. InterTAK score showed poor discrimination for in-hospital mortality (64 deaths, AUC 0.649, Figure 1A), with an optimal cut-off of 22.5 (sensitivity 56%, specificity 70%; OR 3.04, 95% CI 1.84-5.03; p &lt;0.001). In addition, considering 5-year mortality, InterTAK again showed poor performance (277 deaths, AUC 0.629, Figure 1B); the optimal cut-off identified was 16.5 (sensitivity 71%, specificity 53%; OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.72-2.88; p &lt;0.001). Furthermore, in time-to-event analysis (Cox regression), the score InterTAK &gt;16.5 was not significantly associated with 5-year mortality (HR 1.22, 95% CI 0.93-1.60; p = 0.14, Figure 2). Conclusion In this large nationwide real-world cohort, the InterTAK Prognostic Score showed poor discrimination for both short- and long-term mortality and did not independently predict long-term mortality. These findings question its utility for risk stratification in contemporary TTS patients and highlight the need for improved prognostic models.ROC curve for InterTAKKaplan-Meier survival curve for 5y mortality
title: Prognostic performance of the InterTAK Score in a nationwide Takotsubo syndrome registry

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. The GEIST score is one of the few TTS-specific prognostic tools described and has been proposed to predict in-hospital complications and, secondarily, long-term outcomes. It was developed based on 1007 patients from the GEIST registry and externally validated with 946 patients from the RETAKO registry. Further external validation in larger, contemporary cohorts is required. Purpose The aim was to evaluate the prognostic performance of the GEIST score for predicting short and long-term outcomes in the expanded Spanish RETAKO national registry, including a substantially larger cohort with extended follow-up. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 2,174 patients with TTS included in the RETAKO registry (until May 2025). GEIST was calculated at admission. Variables considered incorporated male sex, history of neurological disease, right ventricular involvement, and left ventricular ejection fraction. Its prognostic performance was evaluated for each predefined endpoint based on its corresponding components and time frame. The primary endpoint was a composite of in-hospital complications (death, acute pulmonary oedema, invasive mechanical ventilation, cardiogenic shock), and the secondary endpoint was 5-year all-cause mortality. Discrimination was assessed using ROC curves (AUC), and optimal cut-offs were determined by Youden’s index. Associations between score values above the cut-off points and the outcome were expressed as OR. Finally, time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Cox proportional hazards models and reported as HR; survival was depicted with Kaplan-Meier curves and compared by log-rank test. Results Baseline clinical characteristics are summarized in Table 1, stratified by the selected GEIST cut-off, with the variables considered in the score underlined. Composite in-hospital complications occurred in 493 patients (22.7%), and 277 patients (12.7%) died at 5 years. GEIST demonstrated moderate discrimination for the composite in-hospital endpoint (AUC 0.704), with an optimal cut-off of −33.5 (sensitivity 61%, specificity 72%). At this threshold, the association with in-hospital complications was not statistically robust in adjusted analysis (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.47–1.81; p=0.804). For long-term prognosis, GEIST performed poorly (AUC 0.566); optimal cut-off was −42.0 (sensitivity 70%, specificity 69%) and no statistically significant association was found with 5-year mortality (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.80–1.50; p=0.609; Cox HR 1.30, 95% CI 0.99–1.71; p=0.064). Conclusions In this large, national, contemporary TTS cohort, the GEIST score achieved moderate discrimination for in-hospital complications but did not reliably predict long-term mortality. These findings support its use for short-term risk stratification during the acute phase, while highlighting its apparently limited utility for long-term prognostication.Baseline characteristics according to GEISTPrognostic performance of GEIST
title: External validation of the GEIST score for short- and long-term risk stratification in Takotsubo syndrome: insights from the RETAKO registry

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA) is a life-threatening complication of Takotsubo syndrome (TTS). Conversely, TTS may also develop secondary to the physiological stress of CPA or its resuscitation. Despite potentially distinct underlying mechanisms, these scenarios are often considered a single clinical entity. Whether TTS triggering CPA and TTS occurring after CPA represent distinct clinical phen9otypes with different prognostic implications remains unclear. Purpose To determine whether TTS-associated CPA comprises distinct clinical phenotypes and to evaluate differences in clinical characteristics, in-hospital events, and long-term mortality. Methods In this retrospective registry of 447 consecutive patients with TTS, we identified 38 patients who experienced CPA immediately prior to TTS diagnosis. CPA included ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF), pulseless electrical activity, or asystole. Patients were categorized into two groups: (1) TTS-induced CPA, defined as CPA without an alternative identifiable cause, suggesting TTS as the precipitating event (n=16); and (2) post-CPA TTS, defined as TTS occurring after CPA due to a separate identifiable condition (e.g., sepsis or subarachnoid hemorrhage) (n=22). Baseline characteristics and in-hospital cardiovascular events (including cardiogenic shock and recurrent VT/VF) were compared between groups. Long-term survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results There were no significant differences in age (65.8±9.2 vs. 60.0±18.0 years, p=0.81) or sex distribution (56.2% vs. 77.3% female, p=0.29) between the groups. In-hospital cardiogenic shock occurred with similar frequency (43.8% vs. 54.5%, p=0.74). However, all-cause in-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the TTS-induced CPA group (43.8% vs. 9.1%, p=0.02). Recurrent VT/VF after TTS diagnosis occurred in 100% of the TTS-induced CPA group compared with 13.6% in the post-CPA TTS group (p&lt;0.01). During follow-up, the TTS-induced CPA phenotype was associated with significantly worse long-term survival (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.31–0.90, p=0.022). Conclusions TTS-associated CPA comprises two clinically distinct phenotypes with markedly different arrhythmic burden and mortality risk. TTS-induced CPA is associated with substantially worse short- and long-term outcomes, underscoring the need for intensified monitoring and risk stratification in this high-risk subgroup.figure1
title: Distinct clinical phenotypes of takotsubo syndrome with cardiopulmonary arrest: impact on outcomes

abstract: Abstract Introduction Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is characterized by transient regional systolic dysfunction, dilatation, and oedema involving most frequently left ventricular apex and/or mid-ventricle in the absence of obstructive coronary disease. Nevertheless, although a reversible condition, complications such as heart failure, cardiogenic shock, ventricular arrhythmias, and thromboembolic events, occur with relative frequency and significantly impact both short- and long-term prognosis. Several studies have shown morbidity and mortality rates comparable even to those of acute coronary syndromes. Purpose The aim of our study is to evaluate the mortality of TTS in a large nationwide cohort. Methods It is a retrospective observational study based on the Spanish multicentre TTS registry (RETAKO). For this analysis, we included all eligible adult patients registered between January 2012 and May 2025. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality and the secondary outcomes were cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality. Results 2,174 patients were included. The median age was 73 (64-80) years old and 85.5% were women. Cardiovascular risk factors were highly prevalent: hypertension (66.4%), dyslipidaemia (50.9%) and diabetes mellitus (24.4%); though obesity (14.1%) and active smoking (13.5%) were less common. Chronic comorbidities included chronic kidney disease (10.3%), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (8.6%) and neurological diseases (9.9%). Patients were followed for a median of 657 days (147-1,798 days) from the index hospitalization; notably, more than 25% of patients had follow-up beyond 6 years. In-hospital all-cause mortality occurred in 64 patients (2.9%). All-cause mortality was 3.5% (n=76) at 14 days and 3.8% (n=83) at 30 days. During follow-up, mortality increased to 5.2% (n=114) at 6 months and 6.9% (n=150) at 1 year, reaching 12.7% (n=277) at 5 years. Of all deaths, 66 (17.6%) were attributed to cardiovascular causes, 235 (62.8%) to non-cardiovascular causes, and 77 (20.6%) to unknown causes. Among cardiovascular deaths, heart failure and/or cardiogenic shock was the leading cause (n=35, 53.0%), followed by ischemic stroke (n=11, 16.7%), acute coronary syndrome (n=3, 4.5%), bradyarrhythmia (n=2, 3.0%), tachyarrhythmia (n=2, 3.0%), pulmonary embolism (n=1, 1.5%), and other cardiovascular causes (n=12, 18.2%). Conclusion In this large nationwide real-world cohort of patients with Takotsubo syndrome, mortality was not negligible in the short-term and continued to increase during long-term follow-up. Although most deaths were non-cardiovascular, cardiovascular mortality was mainly driven by heart failure and cardiogenic shock. These findings highlight the clinical complexity of Takotsubo syndrome and the need for structured clinical follow-up in this population.All-cause mortality during follow-up.
title: Short- and long-term mortality in Takotsubo syndrome: a nationwide multicentre registry analysis

abstract: Abstract Background A striking female predominance characterizes Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), yet the impact of biological sex on clinical outcomes remains debated. While women constitute the majority of cases, some evidence suggests that males may experience a more severe clinical course. We wanted to explore how men and women differ in their symptoms, including heart function and cardiogenic shock, and how these differences relate to short- and long-term survival rates. Methods We analyzed data from 5,431 patients from the SWEDEHEART registry. To address missingness in baseline variables, random forest-based imputation was employed. Multivariable Cox regression was used for mortality, adjusting for age, traditional risk factors, socioeconomic status, and comorbidities. Secondary analyses included ordinal logistic regression for LV function categories and logistic regression for cardiogenic shock. Results Population characteristics: Of the 5,431 patients (77.9% female, 22.1% male), the mean age was 69±11 years. Males were significantly younger than females (66±12 vs. 70±11 years; SMD: -0.299). Baseline cardiovascular risk factors were more prevalent in males, including diabetes (23% vs. 12%), hypertension (58% vs. 53%), smoking (49% vs. 41%), and hyperlipidemia (47% vs. 29%). Clinical presentation: At admission, males presented with significantly more severe LV dysfunction than females (OR for a worse LV category: 0.60; 95% CI: 0.51–0.72; P &lt; 0.001). While the incidence of cardiogenic shock was numerically higher in males, the difference was not statistically significant after adjustment (1.98% vs. 1.77%; aOR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.38–1.39; P = 0.33). Mortality: Female sex was associated with a robust survival advantage. At 30 days post-admission, females exhibited a 45% lower risk of death (aHR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.39–0.77; P &lt; 0.001, Fig. 1). This survival benefit persisted throughout the first year, with an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.60 (95% CI: 0.47–0.76; P &lt; 0.001, Fig. 2). The increased mortality risk in males remained independent of age, socioeconomic status, baseline comorbidities, and initial clinical severity. Conclusion In this nationwide registry analysis, biological sex emerged as a critical determinant of both presentation and survival in TTS. Male patients present with significantly worse LV function and face a substantially higher risk of death in both the acute phase (30-day mortality) and during the first year of follow-up. These findings suggest that the poorer prognosis in men is not fully explained by traditional risk factors or acute clinical markers, which points to the importance of intensified monitoring and sex-specific risk stratification for male patients.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Impact of biological sex on presentation and mortality in Takotsubo syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Management of spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is guided by clinical instability and angiographic severity in the absence of randomised data. The long-term impact of upfront percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in SCAD remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluate the use of upfront PCI, procedural success rates and long-term risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) following upfront PCI versus conservative management among patients with SCAD. Methods Patients with core laboratory–adjudicated SCAD enrolled in the Australian–New Zealand SCAD Registry1 (2009–2025) were analysed. PCI success was defined as residual stenosis &lt;20% post- stent implantation or &lt;50% post-balloon angioplasty, with achievement of thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) flow grade 2 or 3. Angiographic improvement was defined as an increase of ≥1 TIMI flow grade. PCI-related complications were recorded. Predictors of PCI success were identified using logistic regression.The association between upfront PCI and MACE (all-cause death, recurrent MI, recurrent SCAD,unplanned revascularisation,stroke/TIA,or heart failure) was estimated using adjusted Cox proportional hazards models. Results Among 788 patients, 86 (10.9%) underwent upfront PCI and 702 (89.1%) were managed conservatively. PCI-treated patients had higher-risk presentations, including STEMI(73.0% vs 28.0%), cardiac arrest (8.2% vs 1.8%), left main SCAD(7.1% vs 0.6%), proximal SCAD (37.0% vs 10.0%), and baseline TIMI 0–1 flow (74.0% vs 19.0%) (all p&lt;0.001)[Table 1]. PCI procedural success was achieved in 67.4% and angiographic improvement in 69.8%. Stent implantation was performed in 58.1%, balloon angioplasty in 43.0%, and cutting balloon angioplasty in 10.5%.PCI-related complications occurred in 39.5%, including propagation of dissection (82.4% of complications),slow flow/no-reflow (32.4%) and emergency CABG (2.9%). PCI failure occurred in 32.6%,most commonly due to inability to wire the true lumen(46.4%). Moderate-to-severe coronary tortuosity was independently associated with a lower likelihood of PCI success(adjusted OR 0.15, 95% CI 0.05–0.41). At 3 years, MACE occurred in 19.8%(17/86) of PCI-treated patients and 9.5%(67/702) of conservatively managed patients. In adjusted analysis, upfront PCI was associated with a twofold higher hazard of MACE; however, this did not reach statistical significance (adjusted HR 2.30, 95% CI:0.96–5.52; p=0.062)[Figure 1]. Conclusions In this large contemporary SCAD registry, patients selected for PCI represented a markedly higher-risk phenotype. PCI was associated with modest procedural success and a high complication rate, with coronary tortuosity strongly predicting PCI failure. While unadjusted MACE rates were higher among PCI-treated patients, there was no statistically significant association after adjustment. These findings highlight the complexity of revascularisation in SCAD and support careful patient selection strategies.Long term MACETable 1 PCI vs No PCI
