title: Association of pre-existing sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy with outcomes in patients presenting with cardiogenic shock: a retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) with Impella has demonstrated improved hemodynamics and survival benefits in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), particularly in selected populations, as shown in the DanGer Shock trial [1-3]. However, outcomes of dialysis patients treated with Impella for AMI-CS remain poorly characterized. While dialysis patients with AMI experience higher rates of ischemic and bleeding complications compared with non-dialysis patients [4-6], the specific incidence of complications in dialysis patients treated with Impella for AMI-CS has never been investigated. Purpose To evaluate 30-day mortality and complication rates in dialysis patients with AMI-CS treated with Impella. Methods Data were extracted from the Japanese registry for Percutaneous Ventricular Assist Device (J-PVAD) in which all Japanese patients treated with Impella were registered. Among 4,032 patients registered in J-PVAD between February 1, 2020, and December 31, 2022, a total of 1,920 AMI-CS patients with available renal function data were included in the present study. Patients were stratified into three groups: dialysis (n=65, 3.4%), non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) (n=824, 42.9%), and non-CKD (n=1,031, 53.7%). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 30 days after Impella implantation. Multivariable Cox-proportional hazards model was applied to compare all-cause mortality between the three groups. Secondary endpoints included cardiovascular mortality at 30 days analyzed using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models with non-cardiovascular death as a competing event, and complication rates including major bleeding, ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke, hemolysis, infection, and limb ischemia. Results Both the all-cause mortality (Figure 1) and the cardiovascular mortality (Figure 2) differed significantly among the three groups (P&lt;0.01), with the highest mortality observed in the dialysis group; however, no significant difference was observed between the dialysis and the CKD groups. Limb ischemia occurred most frequently in the dialysis group (12.3%) and differed significantly between the three groups (P=0.02); however, no significant differences were observed in the incidence of other complications between the three groups. Conclusions Among patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock treated with Impella, dialysis patients demonstrated comparable all-cause and cardiovascular mortality to non-dialysis CKD patients, but significantly higher mortality than patients without CKD. Notably, patients on dialysis had a significantly higher risk of limb ischemia than those not on dialysis.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Mortality and complications of Impella use in dialysis patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: insights from the J-PVAD Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high morbidity and mortality. Early risk stratification at first medical contact (FMC) in the emergency department (ED) is critical for the timely management of CS. The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system improves risk stratification but does not directly reflect microcirculatory dysfunction, a key determinant of tissue perfusion and organ failure, which may occur despite apparently preserved macrocirculation. Sublingual microcirculation imaging enables real-time bedside visualization of microvascular perfusion. Whether microcirculatory parameters correlate with SCAI stage and predict adverse outcomes in emergency CS patients remains unclear. Purpose To investigate whether sublingual microcirculatory parameters assessed in the emergency department are associated with SCAI shock stage and predict adverse clinical outcomes in CS. Methods This retrospective single-center study included consecutive CS patients who underwent sublingual microcirculation assessment in the ED at FMC. Microcirculatory parameters included Microvascular Flow Index (MFI), Heterogeneity Index (HI), Proportion of Perfused Vessels (PPV), Perfused Vessel Density (PVD), Red Blood Cell velocity (RBCv), and Perfused Boundary Region (PBR). Their associations with SCAI stage and composite adverse outcome were evaluated using Spearman correlation and logistic regression. The composite outcome included SCAI stage deterioration, in-hospital mortality, mechanical circulatory support escalation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or heart transplantation. Results From May 1st, 2025, to January 30th, 2026, a total of 94 patients were included (age 59±17 years; 67.0% male; median Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction 27.5% [21.75%–35.25%]). SCAI distribution was A (25.5%), B (10.6%), C (58.5%), D (4.2%), and E (1.0%). Higher SCAI stages were associated with impaired microvascular flow, including lower MFI and RBC velocity, and increased flow heterogeneity. In univariate analysis, MFI, HI, and RBCv were associated with higher SCAI stages. In multivariate analysis, MFI remained independently associated with advanced SCAI stage (OR 0.312, 95% CI 0.134–0.729, p=0.007). Microcirculatory impairment was also associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Lower MFI (OR 0.435, 95% CI 0.210–0.902, p=0.025) and higher HI (OR 5.193, p=0.035) were associated with composite adverse events in univariate analysis. In multivariate analysis, MFI remained an independent predictor of adverse outcomes (OR 0.435, 95% CI 0.210–0.902, p=0.025). Conclusion Sublingual microcirculatory dysfunction is detectable at FMC in the ED and independently predicts CS severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Early microcirculatory assessment may provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional staging, supporting improved risk stratification and early therapeutic decision-making in CS.Correlation heatmapLogistic regression results
title: Microcirculatory dysfunction at first medical contact predicts shock severity and clinical outcomes in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background The microaxial flow pump Impella was introduced in Japan in 2017. Although it has been primarily used in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), limited data are available on temporal trends in clinical outcomes. Purpose This study aimed to investigate temporal trends in clinical outcomes of Impella support in patients with AMI-CS. Methods The J-PVAD Registry enrolls all consecutive patients who receive Impella support in Japan. We analyzed patients with AMI-CS who underwent successful Impella implantation between 2020 and 2023. Temporal trends in clinical outcomes, including complications, the timing of Impella initiation, and mortality were evaluated. Results Among 5,216 patients, Impella use for AMI-CS increased annually (2020: 683; 2021: 1,133; 2022: 1,539; 2023: 1,861, Figure 1A). The median age was 71 years; 81% were men, and 39% received concomitant venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, with no temporal differences. The composite complication rate decreased (2020: 45% vs 2023: 38%; p=0.001), with the most pronounced reductions observed in bleeding and hemolysis. The proportion of Impella-supported percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) increased and bailout use decreased, with a progressive rise in pre-PCI initiation (2020: 48% vs 2023: 59%; p&lt;0.001, Figure 2A). Pre-PCI Impella initiation was associated with lower 30-day mortality than initiation during or after PCI (Figure 2B). Nevertheless, 30-day mortality showed no significant temporal change (2020: 37% vs 2023: 38%; p for trend=0.36, Figure 1A and 1B). Conclusions The use of Impella for AMI-CS increased over time. Best practices improved, including reductions in complication rates and greater use of pre-PCI Impella initiation. However, no significant improvement in overall mortality was observed.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Trends in clinical outcomes of Impella support in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock in japan: insights from the J-PVAD

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac arrest (CA) profoundly impacts outcomes in cardiogenic shock (CS), but differences between CS with and without CA remain unexplored. Methods The Cardiogenic Shock Working Group registry was queried for patients with CA. Comparisons were made between patients with and without CA. Continuous variables were compared using Wilcoxon’s test. Categorical variables were compared using Chi squared analyses. Results Out of 7,644 patients with CS, 2038 (26.7%) experienced CA. There was no difference in age or in male/female representation between those with and without CA. In-hospital mortality was 1156 (20.6%) in patients with no CA and 1094 (53.7%) in those with CA, p&lt;0.001. Treatment intensity, including both vasoactive drugs and mechanical circulatory support (MCS), was higher in survivors of CA, and they had lower chances of having durable LVAD or heart transplantation (5.0% vs 17.9%, p&lt;0.001). In terms of co-morbidities, patients with CA had a smaller proportion of individuals with the history of hypertension , diabetes, atrial arrhythmias, stroke, chronic kidney disease, valvular disease, percutaneous coronary interventions, and implantable defibrillators (Table). By echocardiography, patients with CA had higher left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (25 [17, 40] vs 22.5 [15, 35], p&lt;0.001). they also had smaller LV end diastolic dimension (5.0 [4.3, 5.8] vs 5.6 [4.7, 6.6], p&lt;0.001) and lower proportion of patients with severe mitral regurgitation. While the systemic blood pressure and cardiac output, as well as right atrial pressure, were similar, pulmonary arterial pressures were lower in the CA group, and their cardiac power output was higher. Conclusions In cardiogenic shock, patients with cardiac arrest displayed some favorable features, such as fewer chronic comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, atrial arrhythmias, history of stroke, chronic kidney disease, valvular disease, percutaneous coronary interventions, and implantable defibrillators), higher LVEF, smaller LV, lower pulmonary arterial pressures, less tachycardia, and higher cardiac power output that those who did not have CA. Despite that, they have higher mortality. Cardiac arrest, therefore, constitutes a separate entity within CS, and should not be automatically considered a complication of the latter. This questions the common practive of inclusion of patients with cardiac arrest in the studies on cardiogenic shock.Table
title: Cardiac arrest in cardiogenic shock: a complication or a different condition?

abstract: Abstract Background The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock classification provides a standardized framework for risk stratification in cardiogenic shock, integrating clinical presentation, biochemical markers, and hemodynamic parameters across five stages (A–E). While its prognostic value at baseline has been demonstrated, data on the dynamic evolution of SCAI stages under temporary mechanical circulatory support remain limited. Purpose To evaluate the prognostic performance of serial SCAI stage assessment at 0 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h in patients with cardiogenic shock treated with microaxial flow pump (mAFP) support, and to determine the impact of early changes in SCAI stage on 30-day mortality. Methods We analyzed a prospective registry of a tertiary care center including 608 consecutive patients with cardiogenic shock receiving mAFP support. In 390 of those patients SCAI stage was determined at implantation (0 h) and after 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h. In addition, the SCAI subitems “physical examination,” “biochemical parameters,” and “hemodynamic” were documented at each time point. Mortality was assessed using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis, and differences between SCAI stages were compared using the log-rank test. Discriminatory performance of SCAI stages was evaluated across time points, and hazard ratios (HR) for mortality were calculated for temporal changes in SCAI stage. Results Median age was 67 years (IQR 59–76) and 72% were male. A cardio-pulmonary resuscitation before mAFP was performed in 47.8%, and initial serum lactate was 5.2 mmol/l (IQR 2.7-10.0 mmol/l). At baseline (0 h), patients were distributed across SCAI stages A–E, with the majority in advanced stages D and E (Tab. 1). Thirty-day mortality increased stepwise with higher SCAI stages at all time points. Discrimination for 30-day mortality was modest at 0 h but improved substantially at 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h. Only patients classified as SCAI stage A or B at 0 h showed a misclassification signal with respect to 30-day mortality (Fig. 1). These findings were consistently reflected in the individual SCAI subitems. A worsening of SCAI stage within the first 24 h was associated with a markedly increased risk of 30-day mortality (HR [95% CI] 3.9 [2.5-6.0]; p&lt;0.001). Similar associations were observed for deterioration between 24–48 h (HR [95% CI] 2.7 [1.7-4.4]; p&lt;0.001) and 48–72 h (HR [95% CI] 2.5 [1.1-5.6]; p=0.031). Conclusion In patients with cardiogenic shock treated with a mAFP support, serial assessment of SCAI stage provides robust discrimination of 30-day mortality, particularly beyond the initial 24 hours. Early worsening within the first 24 hours identifies a subgroup at very high risk of death. Dynamic SCAI staging may therefore serve as a clinically practical tool for ongoing risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making in patients receiving temporary mechanical circulatory support.Fig. 1
title: Prognostic value of serial SCAI staging in microaxial flow-pump-treated cardiogenic shock: impact of early hemodynamic trajectory on 30-day survival

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high short-term mortality despite advances in management. Traditional haemodynamic parameters are often insufficient to assess tissue perfusion and guide therapy. Central venous oxygen saturation (ScvO2) and central venous–arterial pCO2 gap (pCO2 gap) are potential bedside surrogates of perfusion, yet their prognostic value and dynamic behaviour in CS are not fully established. Purpose To evaluate the prognostic impact of early ScvO2 and pCO2 gap normalization in patients admitted with CS. Methods We conducted a single-centre retrospective study on consecutive patients admitted to CICU with CS between 2015 and 2025. Patients with both baseline and 24 to 48h follow-up measurements of ScvO2 and/or pCO2 gap were analysed. Normalization thresholds up to 48h were defined as ScvO2 &gt; 60% and pCO2 gap &lt; 6 mmHg. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality or advanced heart-failure therapy (heart transplantation or LVAD). Survival analysis was conducted using Kaplan–Meier estimates, and prognostic factors evaluated through univariate and multivariate Cox regression models. A discriminative analysis was performed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results Among 446 patients with CS, 92 had paired ScvO2 measurements, and 79 had paired pCO2 gap measurements. Mean age was 67±17 years; 32% women. Regarding the CS aetiology, 159 (55%) presented with AMI-CS, 63 (23%) with HF-CS, and 58 (21%) with secondary-CS. Median ScvO2 and pCO2 gap were 58% [46-68] and 9 mmHg [7-12] at admission, and 60% [53-68] and 7 mmHg [5-9] at re-evaluation. Across patients with paired ScvO2 and pCO2 gap measurements available, 46 (50%) had ScvO2 normalized and 30 (38%) had pCO2 gap normalized at 48h. Normalization of ScvO2, but not pCO2 gap, within 48 hours was significantly associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint (log-rank p &lt; 0.001 and 0.090, respectively). In multivariate analysis, normalization of ScvO2 (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.18-0.70, p=0.003), but not pCO2 gap (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.39-1.49, p=0.43), remained an independent predictor of the primary outcome after adjustment for age, sex, SCAI stage at admission, occurrence of cardiac arrest, and baseline lactate level. The area under the curve (AUC) for ScvO2 value on re-evaluation over the first 48h was moderate but statistically significant (AUC = 0.66 [0.56–0.77], p=0.002) whereas the AUC for pCO2 gap did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions In patients with CS, early ScvO2 normalization within the first 48 hours of intensive care was independently associated with improved short-term outcomes. In contrast, correction of the pCO2 gap did not demonstrate a significant prognostic impact in this cohort. These findings suggest that ScvO2 may serve as valuable, non-invasive tool for risk stratification and treatment guidance in acute cardiac critical care.Figure 1AFigure 1B
title: Prognostic value of early ScvO2 and pCO2 gap kinetics and normalisation in patients with cardiogenic shock: a new management target?

abstract: Abstract Background In-hospital mortality remains 45 % in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI)-related cardiogenic shock. Benefits of mechanical circulatory support (MCS), including an axial flow pump and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, are limited. Purpose This study aimed to identify AMI patients likely to benefit from MCS using DanGer Shock eligibility and to clarify the actual medical costs of patients treated with MCS. Methods Using the Japanese nationwide administrative dataset (JROAD-DPC) from 2022 to 2023, the associations of DanGer Shock eligibility with in-hospital mortality, failure of discharge to home, and medical costs were evaluated. DanGer Shock eligibility was defined by the absence of mechanical complications, out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with persistent coma, and severe dementia. Results Of 52,927 AMI patients, 2,223 were treated with MCS. Among these patients, in-hospital death and failure of discharge to home occurred in 1,338 (DanGer Shock–eligible, 944; ineligible, 394) and 379 (DanGer Shock–eligible, 281; ineligible, 98), respectively. DanGer Shock eligibility was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47–0.73) and lower failure of discharge to home (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.25–0.54). Among survivors and those discharged to home, DanGer Shock ineligibility was associated with higher medical costs (eligible survivors, €36,700 [28,400–49,300]; ineligible survivors, €41,000 [28,400–58,200]; p = 0.058; eligible survivors discharged to home, €33,400 [27,400–42,300]; ineligible survivors discharged to home, €38,800 [26,600–53,100]; p = 0.063). In contrast, among patients who died, medical costs were higher in eligible than ineligible patients (€26,300 [13,500–44,200] vs. €23,000 [12,600–39,800]; p = 0.032). There was no significant difference in medical costs between eligible and ineligible survivors who were not discharged to home (p = 0.570). Conclusions DanGer Shock ineligibility identified AMI patients at high risk of in-hospital mortality and failure of discharge to home. DanGer Shock–ineligible patients incurred substantial medical costs, underscoring the need for careful consideration of MCS use in this population.Figure 1Figure 2

appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DanGer Shock eligibility was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.47-0.73) and lower failure of discharge to home (aOR 0.37, 95% CI 0.25-0.54).

title: DanGer shock eligibility, outcomes, and costs in acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background The clinical use of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has increased substantially over the past decade. As a consequence, a marked rise in the detection of incidental findings such as intramural coronary arteries (IMC) are being reported. The outcome of patients with intramural coronary arteries has not been extensively studied. Purpose The aim of the study is to study the prognostic impact of intramual coronary arteries. Methods All patients undergoing CCTA are prospectively registered in the SWEDEHEART registry which captures the presence of an intramyocardial coronary artery course in the proximal and middle left anterior descending artery as an optional variable. We included consecutive patients referred for evaluation of suspected myocardial ischemia between January 2016 and August 2025 and excluded patients with a history of myocardial infarction, coronary artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, or anomalous coronary arteries, in addition to patients with obstructive coronary artery disease on CCTA. Outcomes in patients with and without an IMC were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards regression models. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction requiring revascularization, or any coronary revascularization within five years of the index CCTA. Secondary endpoints comprised the individual components of the primary endpoint. Results A total of 11,762 patients were included, of whom 3,473 (29.5%) had an IMC. Patients with an IMC were more frequently male (47.8% vs 44.6%) and had a slightly lower mean body mass index (27.2 vs 27.5 kg/m²). There were no clinically relevant differences in age (55.7 vs 56.2 years) or in the prevalence of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, or smoking between groups. Atypical chest pain was the predominant presenting symptom (80.0%), with only minor between-group differences despite statistical significance (p &lt; 0.001). An Agatston score of 0 was more common among patients with IMC (61.9%) compared with those without IMC (57.6%)p &lt; 0.001. No significant differences were observed between patients with and without IMC in 5-year risk of MACE (4.0% vs 3.7%; adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72–1.21) , all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.64–1.28), myocardial infarction (adjusted HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.68–3.13) or any coronary revascularization (adjusted HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.67–1.43). The degree of encasement (partial or full) was not associated with outcome and several subgroup analyses showed consistent results. Conclusion We found no association between IMC and risk of MACE or its components. These findings support the notion that the presence of intramural segments can be regarded as a benign finding.Abstract figure
title: Intramyocardial coronary artery course and risk of major adverse cardiac events: a nationwide CT coronary angiography study

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a severe complication of acute myocardial infarction with high morbidity and mortality. Data from acute heart failure cohorts suggest that transitional haemodynamic instability (“PRESHOCK”) is associated with adverse outcomes. Whether this concept applies to ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), a leading cause of CS, has not been systematically studied. Early identification may offer a window for timely haemodynamic support. Purpose To assess the prevalence and short-term outcomes of the PRESHOCK phenotype at admission in STEMI patients compared with no-shock and shock phenotypes, and to evaluate its predictive value for clinical deterioration. Methods This multicentre metropolitan STEMI registry included patients enrolled between January 2024 and October 2025. Classification was based on a single haemodynamic assessment at admission to evaluate early instability as a predictor of subsequent shock (see A). Categorical variables were analysed using χ² or Fisher’s exact tests, and continuous variables using Mann–Whitney U or Kruskal–Wallis tests. Outcomes included overt CS (developed after coronary angiography, adjudicated by the treating physician), mechanical circulatory support (MCS), and in-hospital mortality. Results Among 1,128 STEMI patients, 300 had complete haemodynamic data and were analysed: 109 no-shock, 125 PRESHOCK, and 66 shock (see B). In the PRESHOCK group, 108 had isolated hypoperfusion and 17 isolated hypotension. Estimated PRESHOCK prevalence was ≥11.1% in the overall registry and 41.7% in the analysed cohort. Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. Overt CS occurred in 9.8% of STEMI cases. Based on admission status, rates were 0.9% in the no-shock group, 8.8% in the PRESHOCK group, and 26.6% in the shock group (see C, p&lt;0.001). Patients in the PRESHOCK group had a significantly higher risk of progressing to overt CS than those in the no-shock group (p&lt;0.01). After exclusion of resuscitated cases, this finding remained broadly consistent (0.9% vs. 5.7%, p=0.053). MCS was utilised in 32 cases overall, with differences mainly driven by the shock group (31.8%), while rates were comparable between no-shock (2.8%) and PRESHOCK (6.5%) patients (p=0.18). In-hospital mortality was highest in the shock group (45.5%), with no significant difference observed between the no-shock (3.7%) and PRESHOCK groups (4.8%, p=0.66). Conclusion At least one in nine patients with STEMI met the criteria for PRESHOCK at admission. The novel STEMI-PRESHOCK status identified a subgroup at increased risk of developing overt CS. Recognition of this phenotype on admission may facilitate proactive risk stratification and the timely initiation of haemodynamic support. Future research should further characterise the STEMI-PRESHOCK population, and evaluate targeted therapeutic approaches aimed at preventing progression to CS.Figure
title: Hemodynamic profiles of STEMI patients at admission - prevalence and short-term outcomes of the novel PRESHOCK phenotype

abstract: Abstract Background Mechanical circulatory support with Impella may improve outcomes in cardiogenic shock [1, 2] ; however, device-related complications remain frequent and occasionally fatal [3]. The incidence and predictors of complications in dialysis patients have not been fully characterized. Purpose To determine the incidence and predictors of Impella-related complications in dialysis patients. Methods We analyzed 4,032 patients enrolled in the Japanese Registry for Percutaneous Ventricular Assist Device (J-PVAD) between February 2020 and December 2022. Among them, 212 were receiving dialysis. Complication rates were compared between dialysis and non-dialysis patients. Predictors of lower extremity ischemia in dialysis patients were assessed using logistic regression. Survival was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results Dialysis patients had a significantly higher incidence of lower extremity ischemia compared with non-dialysis patients (11% vs. 4.5%, P&lt;0.001). In the dialysis cohort, age ≥70 years was associated with lower extremity ischemia in univariable analysis (odds ratio [OR] 5.85; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.08–16.4; P&lt;0.001). ECMO use and acute coronary syndrome were not significant predictors. Multivariable analysis confirmed age ≥70 years as an independent predictor (OR 6.00; 95% CI 2.11–17.1; P&lt;0.001). Overall, lower extremity ischemia was significantly associated with reduced 30-day survival (log-rank P&lt;0.001). However, this association was not observed within the dialysis cohort (log-rank P=0.66, Figure). Conclusions Dialysis patients undergoing Impella support for cardiogenic shock are at increased risk of lower extremity ischemia. Advanced age (≥70 years) is an independent predictor, highlighting the need for targeted preventive strategies in elderly dialysis patients.30-day Survival
title: Impella use in elderly dialysis patients is associated with an increased risk of lower extremity ischemia: insights from the japanese registry for percutaneous ventricular assist device

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a significant cause of mortality in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), despite early interventions, such as coronary revascularization. Mechanical circulatory support devices, particularly venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), are increasingly being utilized to address this issue. Limited randomized controlled trials exist to evaluate the efficacy of VA-ECMO in CS related to ACS. Purpose In order to assess this gap in literature, we performed this meta-analysis of trials investigating VA-ECMO in this clinical setting of ACS related CS. Methods A meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of VA-ECMO in adult patients with infarct-related CS. Trials were identified through database searches and selected based on specific inclusion criteria. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality, with secondary outcomes including bleeding and vascular complications. Major bleeding, considered as bleeding BARC (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium) &gt; 2, TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction) Major or GUSTO (Global Utilization of Streptokinase and Tissue Plasminogen activator for Occluded coronary arteries) severe bleeding and critical limb ischemia were secondary outcomes. Statistical pooling for incidence estimates was performed according to a random-effect model with generic inverse-variance weighting, computing risk estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Small study bias was appraised by graphical inspection of funnel plots. Meta-regression analysis and leave-one-out analysis were performed to assess the impact of baseline features on the primary end point with Comprehensive Meta-analysis software. Results A total of 24 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the meta-analysis, involving 4706 patients (Figure 1). The median age of the patients was 61.8 ± 4.1 years, 76% of them being males. Admission lactate levels ranged from 5.6 to 14 mmol/l, suggesting a state of profound shock. The analysis revealed that 30-day mortality rates for patients with cardiogenic shock receiving VA-ECMO were still high with a mortality of 63%. Vascular complications were identified as factors associated with a worse prognosis. The overall ischemia rate averaged 12.9 ± 5.1%, with a range from 7.1% to 22%. Regarding bleeding complications, an overall incidence of 21 ± 6.9%, varying from 3.2% to 33%, was demonstrated (Figure 2). Conclusions The meta-analysis highlights the ongoing challenge of high mortality rates in CS patients despite the use of VA-ECMO. While VA-ECMO shows promise in providing circulatory support, further research is needed to explore ways to improve outcomes and reduce complications associated with the use of these devices. The complexity of patient management in CS cases underscores the need for a multidisciplinary approach to optimize treatment strategies and enhance patient outcomes.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Venoarterial Membrane Oxygenation in cardiogenic shock complicated from an acute myocardial infarction: an overview and comprehensive meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a life-threatening condition most commonly caused by acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While timely revascularization has improved outcomes in AMI-related CS, effective therapies for non-AMI CS remain limited, highlighting etiological differences. However, data on long-term outcomes and their prognostic determinants are scarce. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate differences in short- and long-term prognostic determinants according to etiology in patients with cardiogenic shock. Methods Consecutive patients admitted to our institute with AMI or acute decompensated heart failure between January 2015 and December 2024 were retrospectively identified. Patients requiring vasopressors and/or mechanical circulatory support during hospitalization were defined as having CS and included. To account for time-dependent effects, landmark analyses at 30 days were performed, separating early (0–30 days) and late (30–365 days) phases, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were constructed for each phase. Results Among the 567 patients included, 243 had AMI-related CS and 324 had non-AMI-related CS. In the AMI-related CS group, the median age was 74 years (IQR, 64–81). SCAI stages C, D, and E were observed in 23.1%, 51.9%, and 25.1% of patients, respectively. IABP, Impella, and ECMO were used in 49.0%, 25.9%, and 25.1% of patients. PCI was performed in 97.5% of patients, and CABG in 2.1%. Among patients with non-AMI CS, the median age was 78 years (IQR, 71–85). The underlying etiologies included ischemic heart disease (34.3%), cardiomyopathy (32.1%), valvular heart disease (18.2%), and myocarditis (1.5%). Early outcomes did not differ between AMI-related and non-AMI-related CS (log-rank P = 0.38). However, during the late phase, AMI-related CS was associated with significantly better event-free survival (log-rank P &lt; 0.01) (Figure 1). Early outcomes were driven by shock severity, whereas late outcomes were primarily determined by etiology, with AMI-related CS associated with better prognosis (HR 0.27 95%CI 0.12-0.61, P value&lt;0.01). (Figure 2) Early outcomes were driven by shock severity, including hypotension, renal dysfunction, and SCAI stage E, regardless of etiology. In AMI-related CS, frailty emerged as the main determinant of late outcomes, whereas in non-AMI-related CS, prior heart failure and lower systolic blood pressure at shock onset remained independently associated with adverse late outcomes. Conclusions Prognostic determinants in cardiogenic shock varied by etiology and time phase, with early outcomes driven by shock severity and late outcomes by etiology-specific factors. These findings highlight the importance of phase- and etiology-specific risk stratification in patients with cardiogenic shock.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Differences in short- and long-term prognostic determinants according to etiology in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Oxidized phospholipids (OxPL) bind to circulating proteins, including plasminogen, apoB, and apo(a), with carrier-specific biological effects. While OxPL on apoB/apo(a) are linked to atherothrombosis, OxPL bound to plasminogen (OxPL-PLG) mediate faster fibrinolysis ex vivo and have been associated with lower risk of type I myocardial infarction and major cardiovascular events in human studies. Cardiogenic shock (CS) is characterized by oxidative stress and thrombo-inflammatory dysregulation that may persist despite temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). Whether OxPL are pathophysiologically involved in CS remains unknown. Purpose To determine whether longitudinal changes in OxPL carriers and plasminogen are associated with native heart survival (NHS) in tMCS-treated CS. Methods Serial plasma samples (pre-tMCS, explant, discharge) were analyzed in 70 adults with tMCS-treated CS enrolled in a prospective registry. OxPL-PLG (primary biomarker), total plasminogen, OxPL-apoB, and OxPL-apo(a) were quantified by validated ELISAs. NHS was defined as survival to discharge without cardiac replacement therapy (NHS n=33; no NHS n=37 [death n=26, durable LVAD n=6, heart transplantation n=5]). Linear mixed-effects models assessed within-patient trajectories over time, allowing patterns to differ by NHS status. Models adjusted for age, chronic heart failure (HF), SCAI stage, and VA ECMO use. Results Baseline demographics, shock etiology, clinical and hemodynamic severity, and tMCS modality were comparable between groups. Chronic HF (40.5% vs 18.2%, p=0.038), CKD stage III-IV (24.3% vs 3%, p=0.027), and valvular heart disease (27% vs 3%, p=0.004) were more prevalent without NHS. Baseline OxPL-PLG levels were similar (NHS: 216.6 [152.0-281.2] vs no NHS: 235.4 [174.3-296.4] nmol/L). Over time, trajectories diverged: NHS patients demonstrated progressive increases (216.6 [152.0-281.2]-&gt;289.2 [221.4-357.0]-&gt;483.6 [406.2-561.1], p&lt;0.001), whereas no NHS patients showed attenuated changes (235.4 [174.3-296.4]-&gt;266.7 [200.1-333.4]-&gt;323.3 [233.3-413.4], p=0.11). The time-by-NHS interaction was significant (p=0.002) and consistent across adjusted models. OxPL-apoB and OxPL-apo(a) showed no longitudinal association with NHS. Total plasminogen was higher at discharge in NHS patients (10.9 [8.4-13.4] vs 3.9 [1.0-6.9], p&lt;0.001) but similar at baseline. After inclusion of total plasminogen, the time-by-NHS interaction was attenuated and no longer statistically significant, although the trajectory difference remained directionally consistent with similar magnitude. Conclusions In tMCS-treated CS, serial increases in OxPL-PLG were associated with NHS. The absence of similar trajectories in other OxPL carriers supports a carrier-specific association. Whether OxPL-PLG-associated fibrinolytic activity contributes to NHS warrants further mechanistic and multicenter validation.
title: Temporal increases in oxidized phospholipids on plasminogen are associated with native heart survival in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cardiogenic shock (CS) requiring intensive care unit (ICU) treatment is associated with high mortality. Survivors frequently experience long-term physical and psychological impairments, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). This study aimed to investigate the quality of life (QoL) and mental health (MH) outcomes of patients surviving ICU treatment for CS. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted for patients treated for CS in the ICU between 2010 and 2023. Health-related QoL and MH were assessed after ICU discharge using the Short Form-36 (SF-36), Post-Traumatic Stress Syndrome 14-item questionnaire (PTSS-14), and the EuroQol 5-Dimension (EQ-5D). Subgroup analyses were performed to identify predictors of impaired QoL and PTSD symptoms. Results A total of 285 patients with a mean age was 62 ± 14 years were included. 44% of patients presented with a maximum SCAI shock stage C. Mean lactate at admission was 3.3 ± 3 mmol/L. Mean PTSS-14 score was 30 ± 15, with 21.4% of patients exceeding the diagnostic cutoff (&gt;40), indicating clinically relevant PTSD symptoms. Mean EQ5DTTO was 0.88 ± 0.2 and mean EQ5DRCW was 0.85 ± 0.2. SF-36 revealed significant impairments, particularly in role physical (13 ± 31), role emotional (11 ± 32), and mental health (39 ± 11), with significantly lower scores compared to age-matched German normative values. Multivariable analysis identified higher age and use of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) as independent predictors of reduced EQ-5D scores. Non–acute myocardial infarction (non-AMI) CS was associated with significantly higher PTSS-14 scores. Conclusion Survivors of CS requiring ICU treatment exhibit a considerable burden of PTSD symptoms and impaired health-related QoL. Older age, MCS use, and non-AMI aetiology are associated with worse outcomes. These findings underscore the importance of structured post-ICU follow-up and multidisciplinary rehabilitation strategies to improve long-term recovery.
title: Impact of cardiogenic shock on quality of life and post-traumatic stress disorder

abstract: Abstract Background percutaneous microaxial flow pump support (mAFP – Impella®) is increasingly adopted in cardiogenic shock (CS) for its ability to actively unload the ventricles, reduce end-diastolic pressure, minimize cardiac work and augment cardiac output. However, pathophysiological differences exist between acute myocardial infarction-related CS (AMI-CS) and non-AMI-CS. Purpose To assess differences in baseline features, in-hospital complications, and outcomes after Impella implantation according to CS etiology in a real world contemporary cohort of patients with CS treated with mAFP. Methods We analyzed 449 CS patients treated with Impella from the internatonal multicenter IMMERGE registry, including 266 AMI-CS and 180 non-AMI-CS. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 180 days and at long term follow-up. Additional outcomes included a composite of all-cause death, durable LVAD implantation, or heart transplantation. Baseline characteristics, in-hospital complications and follow up outcomes were compared between the two groups, with further analyses stratified by SCAI shock stage. Results At baseline, AMI-CS patients were older (64 versus 52 years) and had a higher prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension 62% vs 27%, hypercholesterolemia 57% vs 26%, diabetes 40% vs 22%). Nearly half of those presented with STEMI while 15% had NSTE-ACS. Non-AMI-CS cohort was predominantly due to dilated (48%) or ischemic (27%) ADHF in cardiomyopathy, myocarditis (20%) or postcardiotomy shock (5%). Compared with AMI-CS, non-AMI-CS patients had larger LV dimensions and more frequent right ventricular dysfunction, longer support duration (7 vs 3 days, p&lt;0.0001) and greater need for Impella 5.0 and 5.5 (27% vs 7%). Intrahospital complications were similar, except from higher incidence of hemolysis and device thrombosis in non-AMI CS. At 180 days, mortality was higher in AMI-CS (65.7% vs 51.7%, p=0.001), a difference persisting at long-term (p=0.01). Non-AMI-CS patients had lower mortality but higher rates of LVAD (20% vs 6%, p&lt;0.0001) and heart transplantation (19% vs 4%, p&lt;0.0001). According to SCAI stratification, 180-day mortality in AMI-CS cohort rose progressively with advancing SCAI stage (50% in C, 69% in D, and 78% in E), showing a clear stage-dependent gradient of risk. Conversely, in non-AMI CS cohort, mortality was 34% in C, 56% in D, and 64% in E, with overlapping D/E curves. Conclusions AMI-CS and non-AMI CS treated with mAFP in real world practice have different baseline characteristics and different outcomes. In AMI-CS, Impella may facilitate myocardial recovery, but outcomes are poor if implantation is delayed to advanced shock stages. In non-AMI-CS, Impella provides a safe bridge to LVAD or transplantation. Early implantation (SCAI C) should be pursued in both settings before progression to refractory shock.
title: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) vs. Non-AMI cardiogenic shock treated with microaxial flow pump support: insights from the multicenter MMERGE registry

abstract: Abstract Background Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is increasingly applied in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), yet mortality despite VA-ECMO remains high and patient selection remains unresolved. Conventional analyses focus on treatment effects in subgroups, whereas biological heterogeneity of shock phenotypes is less well understood. Purpose To identify baseline characteristics defining opposite clinical extremes, recovery without VA-ECMO versus death with VA-ECMO, in order to characterise phenotypic signatures associated with and without refractory AMI-CS. Methods Patients from the randomised ECLS-SHOCK trial in AMI-CS were analysed. Two predefined extreme phenotypes were evaluated: (1) patients surviving to 30 days without VA-ECMO and (2) patients treated with VA-ECMO who died within 30 days (Figure). Baseline demographic, clinical, haemodynamic and laboratory variables available at presentation were compared. Continuous variables were dichotomised using receiver operating characteristic-derived thresholds. Univariable logistic regression quantified associations with the refractory phenotype. Multidimensional phenotype structure was explored using integrated radar plot visualisation. Results Marked differences between extreme phenotypes were observed across all physiological domains. Death with VA-ECMO was consistently associated with indicators of advanced systemic hypoperfusion and organ dysfunction, including elevated lactate, prolonged cardiopulmonary resuscitation duration, impaired renal function, increased inflammatory activation and reduced haemoglobin levels. Lower left ventricular ejection fraction and increasing age further characterised the refractory phenotype, alongside greater comorbidity burden. Effect estimates demonstrated a coherent severity gradient rather than isolated predictors. Multidimensional phenotype mapping revealed uniform expansion across metabolic, haemodynamic and clinical domains among VA-ECMO non-survivors, suggesting the presence of a “global collapse signature” already detectable at baseline. Conclusion Phenotype analysis of both shock extremes identified a distinct “collapse signature” of AMI-CS characterised by systemic metabolic failure and multiorgan dysfunction despite advanced mechanical support. These findings highlight biological heterogeneity within AMI-CS and support phenotype-based risk stratification as a potential framework for future personalised mechanical circulatory support strategies.
title: Phenotype analysis reveals a “global collapse” cardiogenic shock signature despite VA-ECMO support in acute myocardial infarction – a subanalysis from ECLS-SHOCK

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high mortality despite increasing use of microaxial flow pump (mAFP) support, with or without veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Biomarkers measured at initial assessment may not capture early response to MCS support. The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) integrates metabolic stress and inflammatory burden and has shown prognostic value in several critical illness populations; however, its value as a serial marker during mAFP support in CS is uncertain. Purpose To evaluate the prognostic utility of serial LAR after mAFP initiation and to identify the optimal time point for predicting 180-day outcomes in CS. Methods The UNLOADERS-PVAD registry is a multi-center observational study in Japan. Between April 2018 and December 2023, 501 patients received mAFP support; 32 who died within 48 hours were excluded, leaving 469 patients for analysis. LAR was calculated as lactate/albumin. Serial LAR was assessed at pre-support and at 24, 48, and 72 hours after mAFP initiation. The primary endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and area under the curve (AUC). Kaplan–Meier analyses were used for 180-day all-cause mortality. Independent associations were evaluated using stepwise Cox proportional hazards regression adjusting for demographics, etiology and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (E-CPR), support strategy (mAFP alone vs mAFP with VA-ECMO), and severity indices (vasoactive–inotropic score, APACHE II, SAVE score, and pre-MCS SCAI stage). Results Among 469 patients, LAR measured at 48 hours demonstrated the highest discriminative ability for 180-day mortality among serial measurements (AUC 0.739 vs 0.657 at pre-support, 0.705 at 24 hours, and 0.712 at 72 hours). When patients were stratified by 48-hour LAR quartiles, 180-day survival decreased stepwise with increasing quartiles (log-rank p&lt;0.001). In stepwise Cox models with comprehensive adjustment up to the final model incorporating support strategy and multiple severity scores, 48-hour LAR remained independently associated with 180-day mortality (hazard ratio per 0.1 increase 1.051, 95% confidence interval 1.039–1.064; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Serial LAR assessment after mAFP initiation identifies prognostic separation, with 48-hour LAR providing the strongest prediction of 180-day mortality. This simple composite marker may serve as an early treatment-response biomarker to refine risk stratification in mechanically supported CS.Kaplan-Meier analysis for 180-day survivalCox models: 48-h LAR and mortality
title: 48-hour lactate-to-albumin ratio predicts 180-day mortality after microaxial flow pump support in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Early risk stratification in cardiogenic shock (CS) is essential for guiding therapeutic decision-making. The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock classification is widely used and provides structured baseline risk assessment. However, CS represents a dynamic condition in which evolving metabolic responses may convey additional prognostic information. Serial lactate measurements may therefore refine outcome prediction beyond admission severity assessment, as recently highlighted by the SCAI Door-to-Lactate Clearance Initiative.¹ Purpose To investigate whether early lactate trajectories during intensive care treatment improve prediction of 30-day mortality beyond baseline clinical risk assessment in patients with cardiogenic shock. Methods Data were obtained from an ongoing prospective multicentre cohort study including consecutive patients with cardiogenic shock of all causes. Patients with uncertain shock aetiology or pulmonary embolism were excluded. Lactate trajectories at 4, 8, 16, and 24 hours after ICU admission were categorised as clearance (≥50% reduction or lactate &lt;2 mmol/L), partial clearance (10–50% reduction), or no clearance (&lt;10% reduction). Associations with 30-day mortality were analysed using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, SCAI stage at admission, and baseline lactate. Model discrimination was assessed using Harrell’s concordance index (C-index). Incremental prognostic value of lactate trajectories was evaluated by changes in C-index (ΔC) and likelihood ratio testing compared with baseline models. Results A total of 571 patients were included in the analysis. Impaired lactate trajectories were consistently associated with increased mortality across all timepoints. Trajectory-based models demonstrated moderate discrimination, with an adjusted C-index of 0.72 as early as 8 hours after ICU admission (Fig. 1). Addition of lactate trajectories to baseline risk assessment significantly improved model discrimination, with incremental prognostic value detectable from 8 hours onwards and increasing over time (ΔC +0.06 at 24 hours, Figure 2). The incremental benefit was more pronounced in clinically relevant subgroups. In patients with non-AMI cardiogenic shock, inclusion of lactate trajectories markedly improved prediction from 8 hours onward (ΔC +0.13 at 24 h, LRT p &lt;0.001). Similarly, enhanced discrimination was observed in women (ΔC +0.06 at 8 h, LRT p &lt;0.001). Conclusion Lactate trajectories provide early prognostic information in cardiogenic shock beyond baseline SCAI severity classification. Incremental improvement in risk discrimination is detectable as early as 8 hours after ICU admission. While gains in the overall population are modest, substantial improvement is observed in non-AMI cardiogenic shock and in female patients, suggesting particular value for risk stratification in clinically heterogeneous and traditionally underrepresented phenotypes.C_Index_over_time_per_subgroupdelta_c
title: Dynamic lactate trajectories improve risk prediction beyond baseline severity assessment in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Imaging studies interpretation in clinical practice may differ substantially from centralized Core Laboratory assessment, particularly in complex patients with severe calcification or stents. In the CORE PRECISION study, ultra–high-resolution computed tomography (UHR-CT) and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) demonstrated similar diagnostic performance under standardized Core Lab conditions, although statistical non-inferiority was not formally met. Whether real-world interpretation narrows or widens this performance gap remains clinically relevant. Purpose To compare the diagnostic performance of UHR-CT and ICA to detect hemodynamically significant stenosis according to local versus centralized core lab assessment. Methods In a prospective multicenter study conducted in Brazil, Japan, and the United States, 173 patients with a calcium score ≥400, known coronary stenosis ≥ 50% or stents underwent UHR-CT prior to an invasive coronary angiography (ICA) due to suspected obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). UHR-CT and ICA images were analyzed locally at each site and by blinded and centralized Core Labs. Stenosis ≥70% on UHR-CT or ICA were deemed obstructive, and functional significance (reference standard) was defined by an abnormal quantitative flow ratio. The diagnostic accuracy of UHR-CT and ICA for detecting significant stenosis was calculated based on both Core Lab and site-level assessments. Results Among the 173 patients (mean age 65.2 years, 72% male), obstructive CAD was present in 115 (66%). The mean calcium score in patients without stents (n=115) was 1,004 (± 1,108). In real-world site-level readings, ICA accuracy decreased from 83.2% to 74.0% (p for difference=0.009), whereas UHR-CT showed a more modest decline, from 80.3% to 74.0% (p for difference=0.04). The reduction in performance was more pronounced for ICA specificity, resulting in convergence of diagnostic accuracy between modalities in routine practice (Fig 1A). Intercontinental variability further highlighted differences between controlled Core Lab conditions and real-world interpretation (Fig 1B). Conclusion In patients with severe coronary calcification or stents, UHR-CT offered similar diagnostic accuracy to ICA in detecting patients with significant CAD. The diagnostic performance gap between UHR-CT and ICA was narrower in real-world practice than under Core Lab adjudication, suggesting that variability in routine interpretation may influence comparative effectiveness analyses and the pragmatic performance of UHR-CT may be closer to ICA than suggested by controlled trial conditions, with important implications for real-world decision-making and study design.Figure 1
title: Ultra-high-resolution CT versus invasive angiography for obstructive coronary artery disease: real-world and core laboratory diagnostic performance in a multicenter study

abstract: Abstract Background Most studies on cardiogenic shock (CS) focus on selected subgroups (predominantly acute myocardial infarction) or single interventions. Comprehensive longitudinal analyses across heterogeneous CS populations over extended time periods remain scarce. Purpose To evaluate temporal changes in patient characteristics and to assess trends in mortality and morbidity in relation to evolving therapeutic strategies within a broad CS population. We hypothesized that structured adaptations in intensive care management contributed to improved clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective dual-center cohort study included 2,029 CS patients treated between 2013 and 2025. Temporal trends were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multivariate logistic regression. Era-specific effects (2013–2018 vs. 2019–2025) were investigated using 1:1 propensity score matching. The primary endpoint was 90-day mortality; secondary endpoints comprised complications (bleeding, sepsis, thrombosis, and stroke), neurological outcome at ICU discharge, and shock progression. To quantify the contribution of evolving treatment strategies, domain-specific therapy-shift analyses using g-computation standardization were performed, with counterfactual mortality using Monte Carlo resampling and subclass-cluster bootstrapping. Results Despite stable baseline demographics (mean age 65.9 years; 72% male), admission profiles shifted toward less advanced shock and ischemic etiology declined over time. Ninety-day mortality decreased significantly (odds ratio per year, 0.95; p &lt; 0.001). After matching, survival gains were most pronounced in patients with moderate shock severity, absence of cardiac arrest, and a non-ischemic cause. Shock progression and major bleeding – including severe bleeding – declined significantly, whereas rates of sepsis, thrombosis, and stroke remained stable. Neurological recovery improved modestly. Outcomes paralleled distinct therapeutic shifts: transition from midazolam- to propofol-based sedation, increased use of dobutamine combined with noradrenaline and reduced epinephrine exposure, more selective deployment of mechanical circulatory support, and expanded senior intensivist involvement. Counterfactual modeling suggested that optimization of sedation and catecholamine strategies accounted for a substantial proportion of the observed reduction in mortality. Conclusions Over 13 years, outcomes in cardiogenic shock improved substantially, with declining mortality, reduced shock progression, fewer bleeding complications, and better neurological recovery. These findings suggest that the evolution of contemporary ICU management and treatment strategies in CS has translated into meaningful clinical benefits for patients. Gains were most evident in moderate and non-ischemic phenotypes, whereas outcomes in refractory shock remain poor, underscoring the persistent need for novel therapeutic approaches beyond current standards of care.Kaplan-Meier: 90-Day Survival by SCAITherapeutic Trends in Cardiogenic Shock
title: Evolving ICU strategies and improved survival in cardiogenic shock: a 13-year cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Microaxial flow pump percutaneous ventricular assist devices are increasingly utilised in cardiogenic shock (CS) and complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary intervention (CHIP). However, real-world outcome data, particularly in heterogeneous aetiologies and across the spectrum of Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock stages, remain limited. We report outcomes from a large consecutive cohort of patients supported with microaxial flow pump devices at two tertiary hospitals. Methods We retrospectively analysed consecutive patients who received microaxial flow pump support (January 2018–February 2026) at two tertiary hospitals. Baseline demographics, haemodynamics, procedural characteristics, and outcomes were collected. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included myocardial recovery/device weaning, escalation to durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) or heart transplantation, and procedural complications. Results A total of 268 patients were included in our analysis. Their median age was 56 years (interquartile range [IQR] 43–63), and the majority of them (75.7%) were male. The most frequent indications were ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI; 36.2%), dilated cardiomyopathy with acute decompensated heart failure (DCM-ADHF; 24.3%), non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS; 12.3%), and acute myocarditis (10.8%). The majority presented in SCAI stage ≥D (67.2%), and 33.2% had cardiac arrest. Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed in 54.1%, with complete revascularisation achieved in 41.3% of PCI cases. Median duration of microaxial flow pump support was 5 days (IQR 1–9). Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 45.5% (101/222). Myocardial recovery with successful device weaning was achieved in 76.4% (68/89) of evaluable patients. Bridge to durable LVAD occurred in 7.8% and heart transplantation in 5.2% of patients. Access-site complications occurred in 7.3%, and haemodynamic instability/loss of pulsatility during support was observed in 27.3%. Conclusions In this large two-centre experience, microaxial flow pump support was used predominantly in patients with advanced cardiogenic shock (SCAI ≥D) from diverse aetiologies. Despite the high acuity, with two-thirds in SCAI stage D–E and one-third post-cardiac arrest, myocardial recovery was achieved in over three-quarters of evaluable patients. These findings underscore the role of microaxial flow pump as a bridge to recovery, durable device, or transplantation in a real-world cardiogenic shock population.Figure
title: Outcomes of microaxial flow pump mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Backgrounds Although the prognosis of patients with vasospastic angina (VSA) is generally considered favorable, patients who experience cardiac arrest presumed to be caused by coronary artery spasm, while rare, are thought to have poor outcomes. However, detailed data on the prognosis of these patients remain limited. Purpose In this study, we examined differences in clinical outcomes between patients with VSA diagnosed by acetylcholine (ACh) provocation testing, stratified by the presence or absence of resuscitated cardiac arrest. Methods From April 2012 to October 2025, a cohort of 1,191 patients who underwent ACh provocation testing in our institution was screened. Among them, patients with a positive ACh provocation test were included and were divided into two groups according to the presence or absence of cardiac arrest. In our institution, ACh provocation testing is routinely performed in clinically stable post-resuscitation patients with favorable neurological status in whom no identifiable cause of cardiac arrest is identified. The primary endpoint was a composite outcome of all-cause death or cardiac arrest during the follow-up period. Secondary endpoints included cardiovascular death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, non-fatal myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization, hospitalization for heart failure and hospitalization for chest pain. Results Among 597 patients diagnosed with VSA, 24 patients (4%) had undergone ACh provocation testing following resuscitated cardiac arrest. Compared with the no cardiac arrest group, patients in the cardiac arrest group were younger, more likely to be male, and had a significantly lower body mass index and lower prevalence of dyslipidemia. Left ventricular ejection fraction was also significantly lower in the cardiac arrest group. (Table) During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, the primary composite endpoint of all-cause death or cardiac arrest occurred significantly more frequently in the cardiac arrest group than in the no cardiac arrest group (16.7% vs. 3.1%, Log rank p = 0.017). (Figure) Hospitalization for heart failure was also significantly higher in the cardiac arrest group (12.5% vs. 0.3%, p = 0.001). In contrast, no significant differences were observed between the two groups with respect to other clinical events. Notably, no patients in the cardiac arrest group were admitted to the hospital with chest pain during follow-up. (Table) Conclusions Patients diagnosed with VSA by ACh provocation testing after resuscitated cardiac arrest had a significantly higher risk of recurrent cardiac arrest compared with those without a history of cardiac arrest. These findings suggest that patients who experienced cardiac arrest may require more intensive medical therapy than those without such a history.Patient CharacteristicsKaplan–Meier Curves for the Primary Endpoint
title: Prognosis of patients diagnosed with vasospastic angina by acetylcholine provocation testing with and without resuscitated cardiac arrest

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial infarction is a leading cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). In select patients with OHCA due to suspected acute coronary occlusion, direct transfer to a centre capable of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) has been shown to improve short-term outcomes. However, practice remains heterogeneous, and the impact on longer-term survival is unclear. Purpose To evaluate whether direct transfer of OHCA patients with ST-elevation to a PPCI centre is associated with improved long-term survival compared with indirect transfer from hospitals without a PPCI service. Methods This retrospective cohort study collected data from a national myocardial infarction registry within a regional emergency service network. Adults with OHCA, return of spontaneous circulation and ST-elevation on post-arrest ECG were included between April 2015 and June 2022. Patients were categorised according to direct transfer to a PPCI centre or indirect transfer via a non-PPCI hospital. The primary outcome was survival at 30 days, 1 year and 3 years. Survival was analysed using adjusted flexible parametric survival models. Covariates included age, sex, witnessed event, presenting rhythm and time to emergency service response. Results A total of 702 patients were included; 415 (59%) were transferred directly and 287 (41%) indirectly. Call-to-balloon time was shorter following direct transfer (153 vs. 245 mins; p&lt;0.001). Survival to discharge was higher in the direct group (79% vs. 68%, p&lt;0.001). Following adjustment for covariates, direct transfer was associated with higher survival at 30 days (risk ratio 1.10, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.13), 1 year (1.12, 1.09-1.16) and 3 years (1.14, 1.10-1.19). Conclusions In patients with OHCA and ST-elevation, direct transfer to PPCI centres was associated with improved survival up to three years. This survival advantage appears to be driven predominantly by early in-hospital outcomes, supporting direct triage to PPCI centres for rapid reperfusion and optimised post-resuscitation care.Baseline characteristics of patientsAdjusted flexible parametric survival curves
