title: Direct transfer to primary percutaneous coronary intervention centres after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: long-term survival outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background The DanGer Shock trial demonstrated a survival benefit with routine Impella use in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. However, resuscitated cardiac arrest patients were excluded from that study, and the clinical impact of Impella in this high-risk population remains uncertain. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) secondary to acute coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently associated with profound hemodynamic instability, large infarct burden, and poor neurological outcomes. Although mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is often used in this setting, comparative data between Impella and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in resuscitated OHCA patients are limited. We therefore evaluated the clinical impact of Impella compared with IABP in successfully resuscitated OHCA patients with CAD. Methods In this retrospective single-center cohort study, 3,578 consecutive OHCA patients transferred to our critical care center between January 2015 and December 2023 were screened. Seventy-nine patients who achieved return of spontaneous circulation and had obstructive CAD confirmed by coronary angiography were included. Patients received either Impella or IABP support at the discretion of the treating physicians. Baseline characteristics, prehospital variables including witnessed arrest and bystander resuscitation, initial arrest rhythm, electrocardiographic findings, angiographic characteristics, duration of ECMO and MCS support, MCS-related complications, infarct size assessed by peak CK-MB, and survival and favorable neurological outcomes at 30 days and 1 year were analyzed. Neurological status was evaluated using the cerebral performance category (CPC) scale. Results Nineteen patients (24.1%) received Impella and 60 (75.9%) received IABP. There were no significant differences in baseline characteristics, cardiovascular risk profiles, quality of resuscitation, initial arrest rhythm, or presence of ST-segment elevation. Angiographic findings and the duration of ECMO, Impella, and IABP use were comparable between groups. The incidence of MCS-related complications—including bleeding, hemolysis, lower limb ischemia, and acute kidney injury—did not differ significantly. Infarct size assessed by peak CK-MB tended to be lower in the Impella group (median 133.0 vs. 336.5 U/L; p=0.064). Survival rates and favorable neurological outcomes (CPC 1–2) at 30 days and 1 year were similar between groups. Conclusions In successfully resuscitated OHCA patients with CAD, Impella support was not associated with improved survival or neurological recovery compared with IABP. Nevertheless, a signal toward smaller infarct size was observed with Impella. Given the limited sample size and retrospective design, larger prospective studies are warranted to clarify the role of Impella in resuscitated cardiac arrest patients.
title: Impella versus intra-aortic balloon pump in resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients with coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac arrest (CA) is a major risk modifier in acute myocardial infarction–related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), yet presence of CA is typically reported as a binary variable without accounting for arrest location. Whether out-of-hospital (OHCA) and in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) represent clinically distinct phenotypes with divergent management patterns and differential mechanisms of death remains unclear. Purpose To evaluate whether CA location in AMI-CS identifies biologically and therapeutically distinct phenotypes associated with differential management intensity and mode of death. Methods Adults with AMI-CS and CA were analysed from our shock registry, a multicentre registry of CS including patients treated between 2016–2022. AMI was defined as STEMI or NSTEMI. CA was categorised as OHCA or IHCA. Clinical characteristics, management strategies, and adjudicated causes of in-hospital death were compared. Results Among 376 patients, 147 (39%) had OHCA and 229 (61%) IHCA. OHCA patients were younger (64±13 vs 68±13 years; p&lt;0.01), more frequently male (84% vs 65%; p&lt;0.01), and more often presented with STEMI (80% vs 70%; p=0.03). Initial rhythm distribution differed significantly. Ventricular fibrillation was more frequent in OHCA (41% vs 25%; p&lt;0.01), whereas ventricular tachycardia (8% vs 26%; p&lt;0.01) and PEA (14% vs 22%; p=0.045) predominated in IHCA. Rearrest and CPR rates were similar. OHCA patients underwent less coronary angiography (63% vs 77%; p&lt;0.01) and PCI (43% vs 54%; p=0.03) and received less MCS (47% vs 62%; p&lt;0.01), but more frequently required mechanical ventilation (93% vs 86%; p=0.04). In-hospital mortality was high and similar in both groups (52% vs 51%; p=0.7). However, mechanisms of death differeted markedly. Neurologic withdrawal of care accounted for nearly half of deaths after OHCA (48% vs 10%; p&lt;0.01), while refractory shock or multiorgan failure (48% vs 26%; p&lt;0.01), and comorbidity-driven withdrawal of care (19% vs 5%; p&lt;0.01) were more common in IHCA. Conclusion In AMI-CS, OHCA and IHCA identify distinct clinical phenotypes with similar overall mortality but fundamentally different modes of death; neurologic injury after OHCA and refractory shock after IHCA. Treating cardiac arrest as a single covariate may obscure important biological and therapeutic differences. These findings have implications for risk stratification and future CS study design.Figure
title: In-hospital versus out-of-hospital cardiac arrest define distinct phenotypes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background Aortic regurgitation (AR) frequently remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods, with guideline recommendations for intervention largely guided by imaging-based assessment of left ventricular remodeling. While renal dysfunction has been linked to adverse outcomes in AR, prior studies have predominantly focused on advanced disease stages and post-interventional outcomes, with limited data on pre-interventional progression, offering limited insight into pre-interventional disease progression or biologically informed approaches to risk stratification. Methods We investigated renal biomarkers in individuals with AR from the UK Biobank (n=2,493) and assessed associations with time to aortic valve replacement (AVR) using Cox proportional hazards models. Associations with cardiovascular imaging and hemodynamic phenotypes were examined via logistic regression. To place clinical findings in a biological context, we performed genome-wide colocalization analyses between AR phenotypes, blood pressure, and renal traits, followed by regulatory annotation, single-cell RNA sequencing, and phenome-wide association analyses. Results Among patients with AR, higher circulating UMOD levels were independently associated with a lower risk of subsequent AVR (adjusted HR per SD 0.57, 95% CI 0.34–0.98; p = 0.041), whereas conventional renal markers (creatinine, urea, microalbumin) showed no association. UMOD levels were strongly correlated with lower arterial stiffness (β = −5.32 ± 0.27; p &lt; 0.001 and lower systolic blood pressure (β = −0.91 ± 0.13; p &lt; 0.001), but not with left ventricular volumes. Genome-wide colocalization identified a shared genetic signal at the UMOD locus linking AR fraction, systolic blood pressure, and kidney function traits (PP.H4 = 0.91 for each comparison). Regulatory annotation and single-cell data localized UMOD expression to the thick ascending limb of Henle’s loop, supporting a tubular-specific mechanism. Phenome-wide analyses further implicated UMOD variants in renal tubular and hemodynamic traits. Conclusions These findings identify uromodulin as a genetically anchored, kidney-specific biomarker associated with pre-interventional progression and timing of valve intervention in AR. Our study shifts the renal–AR paradigm from post-operative risk modification toward a mechanistically grounded model of tubular-driven disease progression, with implications for earlier risk stratification and surgical referral, warranting further validation.Graphical Abstract
title: Uromodulin as a genetically anchored biomarker stratifies time to valve intervention in aortic regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been shown to occur frequently in patients with severe degenerative aortic stenosis (AS) and to be associated with significant increase in mortality even after successful transcatheter aortic valve replacement. However, limited data exist on the impact of CHIP-driver mutations on progression of mild-to-moderate AS. Purpose The aim of this study was to assess the association between baseline CHIP-driver mutations and a worsening course of AS. Methods Seventy patients with mild or moderate AS from the PROGRESSA trial with available peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples and an echocardiographic follow-up between 5 and 10 years were included. Next-generation sequencing was performed using a pre-defined panel of 56 genes. Frequency of CHIP-driver mutations and their impact on progression of AS severity were assessed. Progression was defined as an increase in AS category (mild AS to moderate AS or moderate AS to severe AS) or progression to AS requiring aortic valve replacement. Results Median age of the population was 70 years. A total of 14 patients (20%) were carriers of at least one CHIP-driver mutation with a variant allele frequency (VAF) ≥ 2%, with most common mutations being DNTM3A, TET2, and ASXL1. There were no differences in baseline clinical, echocardiographic, or laboratory parameters between patients with and without CHIP-driver mutations. Among patients with a CHIP-driver mutation, 85.7% showed AS progression compared with only 50% among those without CHIP (p-value=0.018). The annualized progression rate was 12.4% per year in CHIP-carriers compared with 6.8% per year in non-carriers. When excluding patients who had only a DNMT3A-CHIP-driver mutation (n=6), all (100%) carriers showed AS progression vs only 51.6% of non-carriers (p-value=0.009), with an annualized progression rate of 13.9% vs 7.1% per year, respectively. Analysis of the most widely used echocardiographic parameter to assess AS severity showed that patients with a CHIP-driver mutation exhibited a greater annual increase in mean transvalvular gradient (Pmean) compared with those without mutations (median [IQR]: 1.05 [0.69-1.92] vs 0.49 [0.16-1.35] mmHg per year, p-value= 0.034). A trend was observed in the annual increase in Pmean with increasing numbers of CHIP-driver mutations (no CHIP-driver mutations: 0.49 (0.16-1.35); 1 CHIP-driver mutation: 0.96 (0.65-1.43), and 2 CHIP-driver mutations: 2.37 (1.21-3.53) mmHg per year). Conclusion The presence of CHIP-driver mutations (VAF ≥ 2) at baseline was associated with increased progression and echocardiographic worsening of AS. These findings could provide new insights into the mechanisms driving AS progression and pave the way for personalized therapeutic strategies aimed at slowing its course.
title: Impact of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential on progression and echocardiographic worsening of mild-to-moderate aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence–guided quantitative coronary computed tomography angiography (AI-QCT) enables comprehensive coronary plaque quantification and has demonstrated strong prognostic value in coronary artery disease (CAD). A validated CAD staging system shows stepwise risk increase with greater total plaque volume (TPV). Although patients with CAD stage 1 (TPV 1–250 mm³) are considered low risk, their event rates are approximately twofold compared with those without plaque. However, whether detailed AI-QCT plaque characteristics further stratify risk within this early-stage population remains insufficiently explored. Purpose To determine whether AI-QCT–derived plaque characteristics provide incremental prognostic stratification among patients at stage 1 CAD. Methods CONFIRM2 is a multicenter, international, observational cohort study of symptomatic patients without prior CAD undergoing clinically indicated CCTA with follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Coronary plaque presence, extent, and composition were quantified using AI-QCT. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, late revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. The present analysis focused on patients with TPV 1–250 mm³. Associations between plaque characteristics and MACE were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. Results Among 6,550 patients (58.6±12.1 years; 48.6% male; median follow-up 4.4 years), 4,901 had stage 1 CAD (TPV 1–250 mm³) with a 4-year MACE rate of 3.5%, compared with 1.7% in TPV 0 and 13.3% in TPV 250–750 mm³ (Table 1). Within stage 1, risk increased across TPV tertiles (2.2%, 2.7%, and 5.6%; HR tertile 3 vs 1: 2.44, 95% CI 1.64–3.63). Larger individual plaques were associated with higher risk, including any plaque &gt;50 mm³ (HR 2.21, 95% CI 1.62–3.02) or &gt;100 mm³ (HR 2.65, 95% CI 1.82–3.85). Obstructive stenosis (&gt;50%) (HR 2.26, 95% CI 1.61–3.18), greater plaque number, larger individual plaque, longer plaque length, and increasing vessel diffuseness showed stepwise associations with MACE (Figure 1 and Table 1), with the highest diffuseness quartile conferring a 3.29-fold higher risk versus the lowest. However, adding diffuseness to TPV tertiles did not significantly improve discrimination in stage 1(Harrell’s C 0.625 vs 0.629). Conclusion Among patients with early-stage CAD, AI-QCT–derived measures of plaque diffuseness provide meaningful incremental prognostic stratification. Even within this conventionally low-risk group, greater plaque volume, larger individual plaques, and more diffuse disease are associated with substantially increased MACE risk. Comprehensive plaque characterization may therefore improve risk assessment and support earlier preventive strategies in early CAD.
title: Refining risk stratification in patients with a small burden of coronary atherosclerosis by AI-guided quantitative CCTA

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is the treatment of choice for high-surgical-risk patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR). While persistent pulmonary hypertension (PH) predicts adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery, its prognostic impact after TEER remains incompletely defined. Purpose To evaluate early changes in systolic pulmonary arterial pressure (sPAP) following TEER and their association with long-term outcomes. Methods This multicenter international retrospective cohort study included 378 patients who underwent TEER between December 2012 and January 2023 across four centers. sPAP was measured by transthoracic echocardiography before the procedure and on day 1 post-TEER. PH was defined as sPAP &gt;50 mmHg pre-TEER and &gt;40 mmHg post-TEER. Patients were stratified into four groups: No PH, New PH, Normalized PH, and Persistent PH. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or mitral valve reintervention. Results Median age was 80 years (IQR 74–85), and 57% were women. One hundred and sixty nine patients (46%) had degenerative mitral regurgitation. Baseline PH was present in 149 patients (39%). After TEER, 139 (37%) had No PH, 90 (24%) New PH, 48 (13%) Normalized PH, and 101 (27%) Persistent PH. Elevated post-TEER sPAP (aHR 2.0, 95% CI 1.4–2.9, p&lt;0.01), residual MR ≥ moderate (aHR 2.9, 95% CI 1.8–4.5, p&lt;0.01), and EuroSCORE II (aHR 1.1, 95% CI 1.0–1.1, p&lt;0.01) independently predicted adverse events. A spline curve of the hazard ratio for the primary endpoint as a function of post-TEER sPAP (Figure 1) demonstrated a marked increase in risk above 40 mmHg. Event rates differed significantly across groups (Figure 2): compared with Persistent PH, Normalized PH (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.15–0.54, p&lt;0.01) and No PH (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.33–0.73, p&lt;0.01) were associated with lower risk, whereas New PH showed similar outcomes (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.67–1.46, p=0.95). Chronic lung disease (aOR 3.5, 95% CI 0.9–13.2, p=0.04) and baseline NYHA class III–IV (aOR 0.4, 95% CI 0.2–1.0, p=0.04) were associated with persistent PH. Degenerative MR independently predicted new-onset PH (aOR 4.6, 95% CI 1.7–12.8, p&lt;0.01). Conclusion(s) Early reduction in sPAP after TEER is independently associated with improved long-term outcomes. Routine post-procedural sPAP assessment provides incremental prognostic value and should be systematically integrated into post-TEER echocardiographic evaluation.Spline curve of HR for combined eventSurvival according to evolution of sPAP
title: Pulmonary arterial systolic pressure evolution after transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair and its association with outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background Risk stratification after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) focuses largely on aortic valve performance and baseline clinical characteristics. The prognostic relevance of residual transmitral haemodynamics after TAVR is uncertain. Purpose To assess whether post-TAVR transmitral mean pressure gradient (TMPG) and its periprocedural change (ΔTMPG) are associated with late mortality. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing TAVR with paired pre- and post-procedural transthoracic echocardiography were analysed. Post-TAVR TMPG was measured on the first post-discharge study (1–6 months) and analysed both continuously and categorically (≥5 mmHg). ΔTMPG was defined as post- minus pre-TAVR TMPG. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality during follow-up. Associations were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for predefined baseline clinical variables. Results Among 849 patients (median age 81 years; 47% women), over a median follow-up of 4.6 years, 322 deaths occurred. Higher post-TAVR TMPG was independently associated with late mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1 mmHg increase 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08–1.19; p&lt;0.001). A TMPG ≥5 mmHg was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.43–2.44; p&lt;0.001). Increasing ΔTMPG was also independently associated with mortality (HR per 1 mmHg increase 1.15, 95% CI 1.07–1.23; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Residual transmitral haemodynamic burden after TAVR is independently associated with mortality and may inform post-procedural risk assessment.figure2figure1
title: Transmitral mean pressure gradient after transcatheter aortic valve replacement and late mortality

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older and medically complex patients. Functional dependency, reflected by the need for domiciliary care, can help identify patients with limited physiological reserve. However, the prognostic impact of domiciliary care prior to TAVI remains unclear. Purpose To examine all-cause mortality and cumulative all-cause hospitalization days after TAVI according to domiciliary care prior to TAVI. Method In this nationwide cohort study, we included all adult patients undergoing first-time TAVI with an aortic stenosis diagnosis in Denmark between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2023. Patients were categorized according to receipt of domiciliary care within 1 year prior to TAVI. We examined one-year all-cause mortality from date of TAVI and cumulative all-cause hospitalization days after TAVI discharge. All-cause mortality was assessed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and multivariable Cox regression. Cumulative all-cause hospitalization days were categorized as 0-14 or &gt;14 days and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. All multivariable models were adjusted for sex, calendar period of TAVI, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, previous cancer, prior stroke, chronic heart failure, malignancy and peripheral vascular disease and frailty. Frailty was defined using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score, which was based on ICD-10 diagnosis codes. Results Among 7,607 patients undergoing TAVI, 541 (7.1%) received domiciliary care prior to the procedure. These patients were older (median age 83 vs. 81 years), more frequently lived alone (76.7% vs. 40.5%), and had a higher burden of comorbidity and frailty based on diagnosis codes. The absolute 1-year mortality from discharge was 21.5% in patients receiving domiciliary care compared with 6.4% in those without. After multivariable adjustment, domiciliary care was independently associated with increased 1-year mortality (HR 3.30; 95% CI 2.65–4.10), (Panel A). Furthermore, domiciliary care was associated with higher odds risk of prolonged hospitalization (&gt;14 cumulative days) within 1 year after TAVI (OR 2.94; 95% CI 2.41–3.59), (Panel B). Conclusion Pre-procedural domiciliary care identifies a subgroup of TAVI patients with markedly increased mortality and cumulative all-cause hospitalization days despite adjustments. Incorporating functional dependency into preprocedural assessment may enhance risk stratification and support patient counseling.Domiciliary care figures
title: Pre-procedural domiciliary care marks a high-risk TAVI population – a nationwide study

abstract: Abstract Background Right ventricular–pulmonary arterial (RV–PA) uncoupling influences outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Effective pulmonary arterial elastance (EPA), calculated non-invasively as right ventricular systolic pressure divided by stroke volume (RVSP/SV), integrates pressure and flow to quantify total right ventricular afterload. Its prognostic significance after TAVR remains uncertain. Purpose To determine whether echocardiography-derived EPA predicts mortality after TAVR and whether it provides incremental prognostic information beyond conventional RV–PA coupling metrics. Methods Consecutive adults undergoing first TAVR for severe aortic stenosis between 2010 and 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. EPA was derived from transthoracic echocardiography at baseline and 1 month. Patients were categorized by EPA quartiles (&lt;0.35, 0.35–&lt;0.45, 0.45–&lt;0.60, ≥0.60 mmHg/mL) and by baseline-to-1-month trajectories (persistent low, improved, worsened, persistent high). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Associations were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression adjusting for age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, left ventricular ejection fraction and aortic valve area. Incremental prognostic value was assessed using hierarchical modelling with Harrell’s C-index and likelihood ratio testing. Results Among 2,273 patients (mean age 80 ± 8 years; 57% men), median EPA was 0.45 (IQR 0.35-0.60) mmHg/mL. Higher EPA identified a high-risk phenotype characterized by lower stroke volume index, higher pulmonary pressures and adverse remodeling. During median follow-up of 3.5 years, 984 deaths occurred. At baseline, the highest EPA quartile was independently associated with increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 2.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.75–2.65). At 1 month, the highest quartile demonstrated even greater risk (adjusted HR 2.71, 95% CI 2.18–3.37). Trajectory analysis (n=1,500) showed persistently high EPA (30%) and worsened EPA (9%) conferred the greatest mortality risk (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.64–2.44 and HR 1.93, 95% CI 1.48–2.51, respectively). In hierarchical analyses performed in the TAPSE-complete (n=898) and S′-complete (n=1,628) cohorts, EPA improved model performance beyond clinical variables (ΔLR χ²=23.96 and 42.01; both p&lt;0.001; C-index +0.042 and +0.028), whereas adding TAPSE/RVSP or S′/RVSP after EPA yielded negligible discrimination gain (ΔC=+0.001; p=0.002 and 0.44). Conclusions Echocardiography-derived EPA independently predicts mortality after TAVR and provides prognostic information beyond conventional RV–PA coupling metrics. Persistent or worsening EPA identifies a high-risk phenotype, supporting EPA as a practical pressure–flow marker for risk stratification in severe aortic stenosis.Association between EPA and mortalityIncremental prognostic value of EPA
title: Echocardiography-derived effective pulmonary arterial elastance predicts mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Circumferential (360°) coronary calcification is traditionally regarded as a homogeneous plaque morphology on intravascular imaging. However, its structural characteristics on coronary CT angiography (CCTA) remain incompletely defined. Objective To evaluate structural heterogeneity of circumferential coronary calcification using CCTA. Methods Between May 2014 and January 2025, patients undergoing rotational atherectomy, orbital atherectomy, or intravascular lithotripsy with pre-procedural CCTA and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) were screened. Circumferential calcification was defined as a 360° calcium arc identified by both modalities. For each CCTA frame corresponding to IVUS-confirmed segments, calcium density distribution was extracted. Structural heterogeneity was quantified using Shannon entropy derived from density values. Calcium was categorised into 351–649 HU, 650–999 HU, and ≥1000 HU, and dominant density proportion was calculated. Principal component analysis (PCA) incorporating entropy, dominant proportion, and total calcified area was performed, followed by k-means clustering to identify structural phenotypes. Results Among 246 patients (267 vessels) screened, 47 patients (53 vessels) met inclusion criteria for circumferential calcification on both CCTA and IVUS. A total of 385 matched CCTA frames were analysed. Mean age was 73.5 ± 8.2 years (median 74 [71.5–79.5]); 36 patients (76.6%) were male. Of 385 frames, 345 were from LAD and 40 from non-LAD vessels. PCA identified three distinct structural phenotypes (mean silhouette coefficient 0.41): a large-area, high-entropy phenotype, an intermediate phenotype, and a small-area, low-entropy phenotype. All three clusters demonstrated significant differences in entropy, dominant proportion, and total calcified area (all p &lt; 0.001). Cluster classification was largely independent of clinical background variables, although a modest association with renal function was observed for the large-area phenotype. Vessel type was significantly associated with cluster distribution (p &lt; 0.001). Conclusion Circumferential coronary calcification demonstrates substantial structural heterogeneity on CCTA. CT-based structural classification is feasible and largely independent of clinical background characteristics, while showing vessel-specific distribution. This framework may provide refined structural characterization of complex calcified plaques.ESC_2026_figure1ESC_2026_figure2
title: Structural heterogeneity and CT-based classification of circumferential coronary calcification

abstract: Abstract Background Conduction system disorders are frequent complications following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), with persistent conduction abnormalities often necessitating permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation. Aim To evaluate the predictive value of isolated PR interval prolongation for PPM implantation within one year after TAVI. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively enrolled patients who underwent TAVI at our Hospital between September 2011 and March 2024. Patients with prior PPM, previous TAVI, patients in atrial fibrillation or missing ECG data were excluded. Baseline characteristics, procedural details, and serial ECGs were analyzed. The primary endpoint was PPM implantation within one year. Statistical analyses included logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival estimates, and Cox proportional hazards models. Results The cohort included 600 patients, divided into a study group (isolated PR prolongation, n=205) and a control group (no PR or QRS prolongation, n=395). At one year, PPM implantation occurred more frequently in the study group (13%) compared to controls (6.8%, p=0.01). Isolated PR prolongation was a predictor of PPM implantation (HR 2.22, 95% CI 1.25–3.93, p=0.006), particularly in patients with wide baseline QRS complexes, consistent after multivariable adjustment (aHR 1.01, CI 1.00–1.02, p= 0.013). Most patients reached maximum PR prolongation by day three post-TAVI. Conclusion Isolated PR prolongation after TAVI was an independent predictor of PPM implantation at one year, especially in patients with wide QRS complexes, highlighting the need for intensified monitoring in this subgroup.Graphical Abstract
title: Role of isolated PR Prolongation in conduction defects after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly recommended across a broad spectrum of patients with severe aortic stenosis, yet the prognostic impact of social inequity remains poorly characterized. Purpose To examine all-cause mortality and cumulative all-cause hospitalization days after TAVI according to the cumulative burden of markers of social inequity. Methods In this nationwide registry-based cohort study, we included all adults undergoing first-time TAVI in Denmark between 2015 and 2023. Patients were categorized by number of social inequity markers (0, 1, 2, ≥3). Markers included domiciliary care, polypharmacy, age ≥85 years, intermediate/high frailty (ICD-10), non-Western immigrant status, mental illness, rural residence, and living alone. Outcomes were one-year all-cause mortality after TAVI and cumulative hospitalization days within one year after discharge. Cumulative hospitalization days were categorized as 0, 0-14 or &gt;14 days and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Mortality was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and multivariable Cox regression. All Models were adjusted for sex, calendar period, and comorbidities. Results Among 7,607 patients undergoing TAVI, 806 (10.6%) had 0 markers of social inequity (28% female; median age 79 years), 1,966 (25.8%) had 1 marker (33.6% female; median age 80 years), 2,149 (28.3%) had 2 markers (40.4% female; median age 81 years), and 2,686 (35.3%) had ≥3 markers (53.7% female; median age 84 years). Increasing markers of social inequity were associated with a higher comorbidity burden and a graded increase in mortality. One-year mortality was 9.3% in patients with ≥3 markers versus 3.6%, 6.3%, and 6.1% in those with 0, 1, and 2 markers, (Panel A). In multivariable analyses, the presence of ≥3 markers of social inequity were independently associated with increased one-year mortality with HR 2.04, (95% CI 1.35–3.00). In adjusted analyses of one-year mortality, the following individual markers were associated with higher hazard ratios: domiciliary care with HR 3.35 (95% CI 2.69-4.18), polypharmacy with HR 1.47 (95% CI 1.23-1.75), ≥85 years with HR 1.28 (95% CI 1.06-1.54), frailty with HR 1.28 (95% CI 1.06-1.54), and non-Western immigrant status with HR 1.27 (95% CI 0.63-2.57), (Panel B). Additionally, ≥3 markers of social inequity were independently associated with increased odds of prolonged hospitalization (&gt;14 cumulative days) within 1 year after TAVI, with OR 2.26 (95% CI 1.71-2.99), (Panel C). Conclusions A higher burden of markers of social inequity were associated with greater comorbidity and increased mortality following TAVI. Domiciliary care and polypharmacy emerged as the strongest markers of adverse outcomes. These findings suggest that markers of social inequity capture prognostic information beyond traditional clinical risk factors and may support more comprehensive risk stratification in TAVI populations.Social inequity figures
title: Stepwise increase in mortality and re-hospitalization with accumulating markers of social inequity after TAVI– a nationwide cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Although outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) have improved, long-term heart failure (HF), ischemic, and bleeding events remain important clinical challenges in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), and their timing and prognostic impact are not fully understood. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the incidence, timing, and prognostic impact of HF, ischemic, and bleeding events after TAVI. Methods This was a two-center retrospective registry study including 988 patients with severe AS who underwent TAVI. Patients were classified according to the first clinical event after discharge: HF hospitalization, ischemic events (myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke), major bleeding (Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 type 2-4), or event-free group. All-cause mortality and time to first event after discharge were evaluated among the 4 groups during the follow-up of up to 5 years. Results During a median follow-up of 665 days after discharge, 165 patients (16.7%) experienced clinical events. Based on the first event after discharge, 80 (8.1%), 32 (3.2%), and 53 (5.4%) patients were classified into the HF hospitalization, ischemic events, and major bleeding groups, respectively, while the remaining 823 (83.3%) were categorized as the event-free group. All-cause mortality after discharge was significantly higher in patients with clinical events than in those without (P&lt;0.001). Major bleeding occurred earlier than HF and ischemic events (median 142 [interquartile range, 47-328], 294 [52-1008], and 339 [44-741] days after discharge, respectively, P=0.004: Figure 1). Among the 3 event groups, all-cause mortality did not differ when assessed from the time of the first event (1-year mortality 31.5% [95% CI 21.6-44.4] for HF hospitalization, 30.4% [15.4-54.4] for ischemic events, and 25.4% [14.6-42.0] for major bleeding; P=0.970; Figure 2). Conclusions In patients with severe AS, major bleeding occurred earlier, and any post-discharge clinical events were associated with increased mortality after TAVI, without significant between-group differences in prognostic impact. These findings support tailored follow-up for HF, ischemic, and bleeding events after TAVI.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Timing and prognostic impact of first post-discharge heart failure, ischemic, and bleeding events after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Current guidelines recommend evaluating signs suggestive for valve dysfunction within the first year after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, the prognostic value of natriuretic peptides and their trajectories for mortality and left ventricular functional recovery has remained unclear. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of baseline levels and dynamic changes of brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) on all-cause mortality and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery following TAVI. Methods We analysed 1,373 patients from three European cohorts. BNP (UK cohort) and NT-proBNP (Swiss and German cohorts) were measured at baseline and during follow-up. Biomarker levels were analysed on a continuous (log-transformed) and a categorical (high vs. low) scale. Long-term mortality was assessed in the Swiss (median follow-up 3.7 years) and UK (median follow-up 5.1 years) cohorts using Cox models. In the German cohort, LVEF changes from 7 days to 1 year were analysed using linear regression. Results On multivariable-adjustment for clinical characteristics, baseline natriuretic peptide levels independently predicted mortality in the Swiss cohort (hazard ratio [HR] per log2 increase 1.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13–1.31, P &lt; 0.001) and in the UK cohort (HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.02–1.34, P = 0.023). Patients with persistently high levels (high/high vs. low/low) exhibited a significantly increased risk of long-term mortality in both cohorts (Swiss cohort: HR 1.99, 95% CI 1.45–2.74, P &lt; 0.001; UK cohort: HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.14–4.17, P = 0.019; Figure 1 and Figure 2, top). Furthermore, in the German cohort, both baseline levels (β 1.10, 95% CI 0.26–1.94, P = 0.011) and dynamic changes (β 4.41, 95% CI 0.90–7.92, P = 0.015; Figure 2, bottom) were independently associated with impaired LVEF recovery from 7 days to 1 year. Conclusion Monitoring BNP/NT-proBNP dynamics is essential for post-TAVI risk stratification. Persistent biomarker elevation is a powerful predictor of both increased mortality and poor functional recovery, aiding in personalised patient management.Mortality in pooled data (UK & Switzerland)Analysis summary on BNP/NT-proBNP dynamics
title: Natriuretic peptide dynamics predict long-term mortality and left ventricular functional recovery after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most common valvulopathy requiring intervention (1, 2), an increasingly important cause of morbidity and mortality in Sweden. While progress has been made in improved diagnosis, earlier referral and broader indications for valve interventions (3), it is unclear how this translates into survival benefit. In addition, detailed knowledge of the major causes of death, place of death, and rates of autopsy verification in AS is limited. Purpose To quantify long-term all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in individuals with incident AS compared with matched population controls, and to characterize detailed cause-of-death patterns. Methods All individuals aged ≥50 years with incident aortic stenosis were identified from the Swedish National Patient Register using ICD codes. Individuals with AS were matched on sex and year of birth to individuals without valvulopathies. Baseline comorbidities, aortic valve interventions (time-updated), socioeconomic variables, vital status and causes of death were identified through linkage with other registers. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality. Secondary outcomes included detailed cause-specific mortality, place of death, and autopsy verification rates. Survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier estimates and using Cox proportional hazards models. Results Among the 432 848 individuals (83 041 with AS and 349 807 without), the mean age was 76 years. Individuals with AS were older than comparators and had more comorbidities. During a mean follow-up time of 6,6 years, 192 467 (44.5%) deaths were recorded. Crude all-cause and cardiovascular mortality rates were substantially higher among individuals with AS (Figure 1). After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and time-updated valve interventions, AS was associated with a more than two-fold increased risk of all-cause mortality (HR 2.63, 95% CI 2.60–2.67) and a more than three-fold of cardiovascular mortality (HR 3.59, 95% CI 3.52–3.66). Older age, male sex, and higher comorbidity burden were independently associated with increased mortality, while aortic valve intervention was associated with improved survival. Cardiovascular disease was the leading cause of death in both groups, followed by malignancy, while in the third position were respiratory disease (for AS individuals) and psychiatric disorders (for comparators) (Figure 2). Individuals with AS were more likely to die in hospital and underwent autopsy more frequently. Conclusions Individuals with aortic stenosis remain at increased risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality compared with general population. Although cardiovascular disease and malignancy were the leading causes of death in both groups, individuals with AS exhibited a substantially higher proportion of cardiovascular and respiratory deaths, and more frequent in-hospital death, indicating a persistent prognostic burden.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Long-term prognosis and causes-specific mortality in incident aortic stenosis - a Swedish nation-wide cohort study

abstract: Abstract Introduction Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most common valvular disease requiring intervention while mitral regurgitation (MR) is the most common valvular disease. Although combined moderate disease is frequently coexisting, clinical evidence about this group prognosis is lacking. Purpose We aimed to evaluate long-term mortality in patients with combined moderate AS and moderate MR. Methods This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who undergone echocardiography at a large tertiary medical center between 2009 and 2025. Clinical and echocardiography data were collected. We identified patients with moderate AS and moderate MR as defined by the valvular guidelines. For survival analysis, additional groups of patients were identified: I - severe AS and moderate MR, II - severe AS and severe MR, III - severe AS with no MR. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, left ventricular ejection fraction (EF), atrial fibrillation (AF), kidney disease (CKD). Results A total 3,049 patients were included: 119 with moderate AS and moderate MR (age 80±10 years, 34% female); 161 with severe AS and moderate MR (age 82±10 years, 65% females); 99 with severe AS and severe MR (age 81±11 years, 63% females); and 2,670 with severe AS and no significant MR (age 77±11 years, 47% females). Over a median follow-up of 3 years, 1,475 deaths (48%) occurred. All-cause mortality of patients with moderate AS and moderate MR was comparable to patients with severe AS and moderate MR. However, mortality was better compared to severe AS and severe MR group and worst then severe AS with no MR group (Figure 1). In cox analysis: all groups maintained increased mortality (with reference to severe AS and no MR group) after adjustment to age and sex, blood pressure and BMI, presence of AF and CKD as well as EF (Figure 2). In general, the moderate AS and moderate MR group showed lower HR compared to severe AS and severe MR group but higher than severe AS moderate MR group. Conclusion Concomitant moderate AS and moderate MR disease is associated with significantly higher mortality than severe AS with no MR. These finding suggest that this group represents a higher-risk patients population that may require close surveillance and earlier therapeutic consideration.Kaplan MeierCox analysis
title: Prognosis of combined moderate aortic stenosis and moderate mitral regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Aortic valve replacement (AVR) improves morbidity and mortality in patients with severe aortic stenosis with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) being the most common mode of intervention. Life expectancy after TAVR relative to the general population provides an absolute, population-referenced measure integrating population-specific mortality with long-term effectiveness. Purpose The present study aims to quantify the loss in life expectancy after successful transfemoral TAVR compared with the age-, sex-, and calendar year-matched general population in Switzerland. Methods The study population consists of consecutive patients with native severe aortic stenosis who underwent successful transfemoral TAVR between February 2011 and December 2023 enrolled in the nationwide, prospective SwissTAVI registry. Loss in life expectancy was defined as the difference between the expected and observed restricted mean survival time truncated at 5, 8, and 10 years of follow-up. Expected survival for each patient was derived from age-, sex-, and calendar year-matched Swiss general population data obtained from the Human Mortality Database. Results In the analysis of 13,651 patients (median age 82 years; 46.2% female; median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality [STS-PROM] score 3.3%), 5,096 deaths occurred during 39,266 patient-years of observation (truncated at 10 years). The mean loss in life expectancy after successful transfemoral TAVR was 0.37 years (95% CI 0.34 to 0.39), 1.05 years (95% CI 1.01 to 1.09), and 1.58 years (95% CI 1.51 to 1.64) at 5, 8, and 10 years, respectively. The loss was largest in younger patients (&lt;70 years: 3.86 years [95% CI 3.55 to 4.16]) and smallest in the very elderly (≥90 years: -0.09 years [95% CI -0.25 to 0.05]). High surgical risk was associated with larger loss in life expectancy (STS-PROM &lt;4%: 1.28 years [95% CI 1.18 to 1.35]; STS-PROM &gt;8%: 2.21 years [95% CI 2.04 to 2.39], respectively). Cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular comorbidities, as well as markers of extra-valvular cardiac damage, were associated with a more pronounced reduction in life expectancy. Conclusion Life expectancy after successful transfemoral TAVR did not normalize relative to the reference population, with the largest loss in life expectancy observed among younger and high-surgical risk aortic stenosis patients.Loss in life expectancy after successful TAVR

title: Loss in life expectancy in patients with aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has been proposed to estimate myocardial extracellular volume (ECV) fraction, reflecting myocardial edema or fibrosis. Purpose We aimed to explore the clinical determinants of CCTA-derived ECV in patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). Methods We retrospectively enrolled patients with NSTE-ACS who underwent CCTA on ECV protocol with subtraction method before catheterization. Patients with prior history of revascularization, known myocardial infarction, hemodialysis were excluded. Results A total of 172 patients were studied. Among them, 99 showed epicardial obstructive stenosis requiring revascularization, while 63 did not. Median age was 72 [61-79] years and 65.1% (112/172) were man. Median global ECV value was 32.8 [29.6-37.8] %. Univariable logistic regression analysis showed that women, diabetes mellitus, statin-naïve, high NT-pro BNP level, multivessel disease, low left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and high E/e’ ratio were associated with the highest global ECV tertile, while the presence of epicardial stenosis was not. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that the independent determinants of global ECV value were women (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.122-0.944, P=0.038), high E/e’ ratio (adjusted OR 1.13, 95% CI x1.01-1.27, P=0.033), and LVEF (adjusted OR 0.929, 95% CI 0.88-0.981, P=0.008). Furthermore, the same procedure was performed on 67 patients diagnosed with MINOCA out of 172 patients. Median age was 72 [61-79] years and 46.3% (31/67) were man. Median global ECV value was 32.9 [29.6-37.8] %. Univariable logistic regression analysis showed that women, renal function decline, Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, high NT-pro BNP level and high E/e’ ratio were associated with the highest global ECV tertile, while the presence of epicardial stenosis was not. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that the independent determinants of global ECV value were women (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.162, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.025-1.02, P=0.0525), high E/e’ ratio (adjusted OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.945-1.32, P=0.194), and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (adjusted OR 4.99, 95% CI 0.565-44.10, P=0.148). Conclusions In patients with NSTE-ACS, global ECV was associated with multiple clinical characteristics, echocardiographic and angiographic factors. Our results suggest that clinical factors such as sex, left ventricular systolic or diastolic function should be taken into account in the assessment of ECV fraction using CCTA.
title: Determinants of extracellular volume fraction on computed tomography angiography in patients with acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Risk stratification in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains challenging. Traditional risk models, developed primarily for surgical populations, may not adequately capture key pathophysiological drivers of outcomes in this setting, such as systemic congestion and inflammation. Carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA-125), a biomarker associated with congestion and adverse outcomes in heart failure, has been explored as a prognostic marker in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI. However, available evidence remains heterogeneous, and its clinical utility has not been conclusively defined. Purpose To perform a systematic review and meta-analysis of available evidence to determine the association between elevated baseline CA-125 levels and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVI. Methods We conducted a systematic review of observational studies evaluating the prognostic role of baseline CA-125 in patients undergoing TAVI. Only studies reporting multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for either all-cause mortality or a composite outcome (all-cause mortality and/or heart failure rehospitalization) were included. Study quality was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. Adjusted HRs were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Results Five observational studies comprising 1,251 patients met inclusion criteria. Overall methodological quality ranged from low to moderate risk of bias according to QUIPS assessment. Three studies reported adjusted HRs for all-cause mortality. Elevated baseline CA-125 levels were independently associated with increased mortality risk (pooled HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.60–2.96; I² = 0%).Three studies evaluated a composite endpoint of mortality and/or heart failure rehospitalization. Elevated CA-125 was significantly associated with adverse outcomes (pooled HR 2.27, 95% CI 1.56–3.28; I² = 0%). No statistical heterogeneity was observed across analyses. Conclusions This meta-analysis shows that elevated preprocedural CA-125 is independently associated with a twofold increased risk of mortality and composite adverse outcomes following TAVI. These findings support the potential role of CA-125 as an adjunctive biomarker for risk stratification in this population. Prospective studies are warranted to determine its incremental value beyond established risk models.aHR All cause MortalityaHR composite end point
title: Carbohydrate antigen 125 as a predictor of mortality and heart failure outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Aims Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established therapy improving outcome in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS). Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI) has demonstrated prognostic value, however, its prognostic utility in severe AS remains unknown. Methods and Results Between January 2017 and September 2023 138 patients (80 years (70-83), 62% male) consecutive patients with severe AS referred for TAVR were prospectively recruited for pre-procedural CMR imaging. LACI was defined as the ratio of the left atrial (LA) end-diastolic volume index (LA EDVi) and left ventricular (LV) end-diastolic volume index (LV EDVi). The primary endpoint was cardiovascular (CV)-mortality. The cohort was dichotomized at a median of 44.1% (high vs. low LACI). Patients with increased LACI (≥44.1%) had higher symptom burden (NYHA III/IV prevalence (68.1% vs.44.9%; p=0.047)), more frequently atrial fibrillation (50.7% vs.14.5%; p&lt;0.001), and elevated NT-proBNP (2017 ng/L vs.1012 ng/L; p=0.007). Over a median follow-up of 2.7 years (IQR 1.7–3.6), high LACI was associated with higher CV mortality (log-rank p=0.016). In multivariable Cox regression models, LACI remained independently associated with CV-mortality after adjustment for established parameters of left atrial or ventricular function (LA reservoir strain: HR 2.10, 95% CI 1.05–3.57, p=0.036; LV GLS: HR 2.21 95% CI 1.00 – 4.9, p=0.049). Conclusion CMR-derived LACI yields independent prognostic value for mortality in patients with severe AS undergoing TAVR. Its simplicity and routine availability may optimize periprocedural risk stratification.
title: Prognostic impact of cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived left atrioventricular coupling index in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a progressive and underdiagnosed condition associated with poor prognosis. Although the TRI-SCORE is a validated risk model for patients undergoing tricuspid valve surgery, it does not incorporate echocardiographic measures of right ventricular (RV) function or RV–pulmonary artery coupling, which are increasingly recognized as major prognostic determinants. Objectives To evaluate whether integration of simple, widely available echocardiographic indices—TAPSE/PASP, TAPSE/RV end-diastolic area (RVAD), and TAPSE/RV end-systolic area (RVAS)—improves the prognostic performance of the TRI-SCORE in patients with moderate-to-severe TR. Methods We retrospectively included 93 patients with isolated moderate-to-severe TR treated with medical therapy, surgery, or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality; the secondary endpoint was a composite of mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to assess the incremental predictive value of each TAPSE-derived ratio beyond the TRI-SCORE. Optimal thresholds were derived using spline regression and maximally selected rank statistics. Results Lower TAPSE/PASP, TAPSE/RVAD, and TAPSE/RVAS values were independently associated with worse outcomes. Each parameter significantly enhanced risk discrimination when added to the TRI-SCORE (C-index improved from 0.614 to 0.710 for TAPSE/PASP, 0.685 for TAPSE/RVAD, and 0.696 for TAPSE/RVAS; all p &lt; 0.001) (figure 1). Prognostically relevant cut-offs were identified at 0.44, 0.80, and 1.3, respectivel (figure 2). Conclusions Simple echocardiographic indices of RV function provide substantial incremental prognostic value when combined with the TRI-SCORE and may improve risk stratification and timing of intervention in isolated TR.tr--graphical--abstract.jpegcut-off--tapse.jpeg
title: Integrating RV and PA coupling and geometry based indices into the TRI SCORE improves prognostic assessment in tricuspid regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Current guidelines advocate intervention in primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) based upon detection of ‘severe’ mitral regurgitation (MR), using transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) thresholds applied equally to both sexes. Given that females demonstrate significantly lower MR severity compared to males, waiting for females to reach the same degree of MR severity as their male counterparts before offering intervention may lead to sub-optimal outcomes. Nevertheless, whether these disparities in MR severity have long-term prognostic significance remains unknown. Purpose To quantify sex-related differences in TTE-derived quantitative MR severity and subsequent long-term mortality after transcatheter and surgical intervention for PMR. Methods 420 patients (70.5±8.5 years, 40% women) undergoing intervention for significant PMR between June 2010 and November 2023 were identified from the APEX registry. MR severity was quantified using validated vena contract (VC) measurements on TTE. The primary endpoint of all-cause mortality was investigated using Cox models adjusted for established PMR risk-factors for mortality (age, atrial fibrillation [AF], LA volume index, left ventricular [LV] end-systolic diameter index, LV ejection fraction [LVEF], tricuspid regurgitation [TR] grade, pulmonary artery systolic pressure [PASP]). VC was modelled as a restricted cubic spline, with the reference value set at 0.7cm, the guideline threshold for severe MR. Results There were no significant differences in rates of concomitant tricuspid (p=0.103) or aortic (p=0.214) interventions, nor in the type of mitral intervention performed (surgical repair/ surgical replacement/ transcatheter repair: 106 (63%)/ 54 (32%)/ 8 (4.8%) vs. 162 (64%)/ 77 (31%)/ 13 (5.2%), p=0.934). Females underwent less coronary revascularisation with bypass grafting (34 [20%] vs 77 [31%], p=0.019). On TTE, females had significantly smaller VC (0.60 [0.55-0.80] vs. 0.70 [0.60-0.80] cm, p=0.003) and lower MR severity grades (II/III/IV: 103 (61%)/ 36 (14%)/ 32 (13%) vs. 103 (61%)/ 40 (24%)/ 25 (15%), p=0.024). There were no significant sex differences in LA volume index, LVEF and LV end-systolic diameter, or pulmonary pressures, although females had higher TR grades (p=0.043). Over 5.8±3.9 years of follow-up, 105 (25.0%) patients died, with no significant sex difference (p=0.814). After adjustment, VC showed a significant non-linear relationship with all-cause mortality and a significant interaction with sex (Pinteraction=0.013) was found. Above a VC of ~0.9cm, mortality associated with increasing VC was higher in males compared to females. Conclusions For the first time, we have demonstrated sex-related differences in TTE-measured VC and subsequent prognosis following intervention for PMR. This supports a nuanced sex-specific assessment to quantifying MR severity, which may warrant individualised thresholds.Vena Contracta DistributionMultivariable Cox Regression Analysis
title: Prognostic implications of sex-related disparities in severity assessment of primary mitral regurgitation following intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction in severe primary mitral regurgitation (MR) reflects advanced disease and poor prognosis, yet resting echocardiography may fail to detect early RV impairment. Exercise stress echocardiography (SE) enables assessment of RV contractile reserve and RV–pulmonary arterial (RV–PA) coupling, potentially unmasking subclinical dysfunction. Purpose To identify echocardiographic determinants of exercise tolerance and predictors of RV dysfunction following mitral valve (MV) intervention in patients with severe primary MR. Methods Thirty-two patients with severe primary MR underwent symptom-limited bicycle SE. Exercise tolerance was classified according to median achieved workload. RV contractile reserve was assessed using exercise-induced changes in tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), systolic annular velocity (S′), and fractional area change (Fig. 1). The ratio of TAPSE to pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) was used as RV-PA coupling index. Logistic regression identified predictors of exercise tolerance and moderate-to-severe RV dysfunction after MV intervention. Results Mean age was 65 ± 16 years, and 72% of patients were male. RV contractile reserve was present in 66% and left ventricular (LV) contractile reserve in 78%. Median workload was 88 [50–125] Watts. In univariable analysis, age, NYHA class, resting LV global longitudinal strain, left atrium reservoir strain at rest, LV contractile reserve and stress RV-PA coupling index were associated with workload. After age adjustment, only stress RV-PA coupling index remained independently associated with workload (β = 11.61, 95% CI 1.29–21.93; p = 0.029). ROC analysis demonstrated good discrimination of high versus low workload (AUC 0.82, 95% CI 0.67–0.97), and a cut-off of 0.35 yielded 93% sensitivity and 60% specificity (Fig. 2). Six patients developed significant RV dysfunction post MV intervention. RV contractile reserve and higher resting TAPSE were protective, whereas higher resting pulmonary vascular resistance and stress RV–PA uncoupling increased risk of RV dysfunction. Multivariable modelling was limited by the small number of events. Among treated patients (surgery n = 15, TEER n = 7, NeoChord n = 1), SE altered management in three cases by prompting transcatheter rather than surgical intervention due to lack of RV contractile reserve. No in-hospital mortality was observed, and mechanical circulatory support was not required during hospital admission. Transcatheter treatment was associated with shorter hospital stay and minimal intensive care requirements. Conclusion In severe primary MR, stress-derived RV-PA coupling index is a robust marker of functional capacity and identifies patients at risk of post-interventional RV dysfunction. Dynamic RV–PA coupling assessment provides incremental information beyond resting parameters and may support individualized treatment decision-making.RV contractile reserve definitionPredictors of Exercise Capacity
title: Determinants of exercise tolerance and post-interventional right ventricular dysfunction in severe primary mitral regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Introduction Aortic stenosis is highly prevalent in the elderly population, and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly used for symptomatic severe disease. While left heart remodeling after TAVI has been extensively studied, the prognostic implications of right atrial (RA) functional adaptation remain poorly defined. Aims We aimed to evaluate the association between right atrial remodeling following TAVI and all-cause mortality during follow-up. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on a prospective and consecutive cohort of patients treated with TAVI at a tertiary hospital between 2022 and 2023. Baseline and 1-year follow-up echocardiographic parameters were collected. RA remodeling (RAR) was defined as an improvement in RA reservoir strain (RArS) &gt;15%. The association between changes in RA strain following TAVI and the incidence of all-cause mortality during follow-up was assessed. Results A total of 185 patients were analyzed (median age: 83 years, 45.9% female, median EuroSCORE II: 2.4 [1.7-4.0]. Mean RArS at baseline was 20.7% (10.3), and median RArS at 1-year follow-up was 25.1% (12.6), and 98 patients (53%) experienced significant RAR. The association of clinical and echocardiographic parameters with the occurrence of significant RAR is presented in Figure 1. LAVI and LArS were the only variables significantly associated with RAR. During a mean follow-up of 18 months, 29 patients (15.7%) died. On univariable analysis, baseline mitral regurgitation, right-ventricular arterial coupling, left ventricular function, and biatrial function at 1-y follow-up, were associated with outcomes. After adjustment on multivariable analysis, variables independently associated with all-cause mortality during follow-up include significant mitral regurgitation, 1-y postTAVI LV GLS, and the occurrence of RAR (Figure 2). Conclusions Approximately half of patients undergoing TAVI exhibited significant RAR at follow-up. RAR was strongly associated with markers of left atrial function, suggesting interatrial coupling. In multivariable Cox analysis, RAR after TAVI was significantly associated with lower mortality. These findings highlight RA functional adaptation as a potential marker of post-procedural risk deserving further investigation in larger prospective studies.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Impact of right atrial remodeling on mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (cCTA) is now indicated as a non-invasive tool for ruling out obstructive coronary artery disease (O-CAD) in patients who are candidate to transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) showing low-intermediate pre-test probability of O-CAD. In elderly, comorbid TAVI candidates, the safety and accuracy of cCTA as an alternative to invasive coronary angiography (ICA) to ruling out O-CAD remain to be established. Aim To assess the feasibility and clinical safety of cCTA for ruling out proximal O-CAD in elderly high-risk patients undergoing TAVI. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including all consecutive patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis who underwent TAVI between January 2019 and December 2020. All patients underwent pre-TAVI cCTA. Patients with positive or non-diagnostic cCTA underwent ICA selectively (ICA group). In patients with no-O-CAD, ICA was omitted and proceeded directly to TAVI (no-ICA group). Accordingly, patients were divided into two groups: no-ICA and ICA group. Clinical follow-up extended up to 5 years, with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), mortality, heart failure hospitalizations and unplanned revascularization assessed. Results Among 355 patients enrolled, 210 patients were included in the study. Among them, 140 (66.7%) had negative cCTA for O-CAD, and ICA was safely omitted in 132 patients (62.8%). cCTA was inconclusive in 43 patients (20.5%) and positive in 27 (12.9%). ICA confirmed O-CAD in 53 of 78 patients (67.9%). PCI was performed in 35 patients. The no-ICA group showed comparable periprocedural complications, 1-year and 5-year MACE, heart failure hospitalizations, mortality and unplanned revascularization to the ICA group. The accuracy of cCTA for ruling in O-CAD was low 66.28%. Median follow-up was 1513 ± 508 days. Conclusions Our data show that cCTA is a feasible, safe, and effective non-invasive strategy to rule out proximal O-CAD in a substantial proportion of elderly high-risk TAVI patients, allowing selective deferral of ICA without compromising short- or long-term outcomes. While diagnostic performance is limited by calcification and motion artifacts, a selective cCTA-guided approach can optimize pre-TAVI workflows, reduce procedural risk, and minimize contrast exposure. Future prospective studies incorporating advanced cCTA techniques are warranted to further refine patient selection for ICA.Graphical AbstractPatient selection flowchart
title: Value of coronary CT Angiography in ruling-out coronary ar-tery disease in elderly patients candidates to TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Aortic stenosis (AS) causes ongoing pressure overload on the left ventricle and leads to progressive myocardial remodeling. Early diffuse interstitial fibrosis often remains difficult to detect with conventional imaging techniques. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)–targeted positron emission tomography (PET) can visualize activated fibroblasts and profibrotic activity. However, the usefulness of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI PET in evaluating myocardial remodeling in patients with severe AS has not yet been determined. Methods This post-hoc analysis involved 18 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent [⁶⁸⁻Ga]Ga-FAPI PET/CT scans before transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Myocardial tracer uptake was measured as the tracer retention fraction through dynamic PET imaging, evaluated both globally and segmentally. The study also examined correlations between tracer retention and clinical data, cardiac magnetic resonance parameters, and invasive hemodynamics using correlation and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Results All patients showed widespread myocardial [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI uptake throughout the heart without focal hotspots, indicating diffuse tracer retention. Segmental retention was inversely related to age at both, 60 and 120 minutes post-injection, especially in basal, mid-ventricular, and apical regions at 120 minutes. Uptake in the mid-septal region was also inversely associated with mean transaortic gradients. ROC analysis showed the tracer could effectively distinguish hemodynamic severity in mid-septal segments, with AUC values up to 0.89. Conclusion In patients with severe aortic stenosis, [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated diffuse left ventricular fibroblast activation, with higher tracer retention in mid-septal segments and in younger individuals. These findings suggest that FAPI-PET may serve as a non-invasive biomarker of early myocardial fibrotic remodeling prior to transcatheter aortic valve replacement.Figure 1.Scatter PlotFigure 2.Tracer uptake patterns
title: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI PET to detect early myocardial fibrotic activity in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR

abstract: Abstract Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide significant cardiorenal benefits, yet are frequently discontinued after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) due to perioperative safety concerns. The clinical impact of this discontinuation remains unknown. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of continuing SGLT2i after TAVI, hypothesizing that continuation improves survival and cardiorenal outcomes without increasing perioperative adverse events Methods We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. We identified adult patients who underwent TAVI and possessed an active SGLT2i prescription before their TAVI procedure. Patients were stratified into a 3-month post-TAVI continuation cohort versus a discontinuation cohort, with follow-up extending up to one year. To mitigate immortal time bias, active 6-month follow-up was required. Following 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 1-year Kaplan-Meier survival analysis assessed mortality, progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD), hospitalization, new-onset atrial fibrillation (AFib), and safety outcomes. Results Propensity score matching established two well-balanced, high-risk cohorts (N=1,104 each) with excellent cohort balance (all standard mean differences &lt;0.10). The matched population had a mean age of 76.3 years, a baseline ejection fraction of ~52%, and high burdens of diabetes (78%) and chronic kidney disease (53%). Over the 1-year follow-up, SGLT2i continuation conferred a 29% relative reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.52–0.96, p=0.026) and a profound 55% reduction in progression to ESRD (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.25–0.81, p=0.006). Continuation also significantly decreased all-cause hospitalizations (HR 0.84, p=0.011) and new-onset AFib (HR 0.83, p=0.021). No significant differences existed for heart failure (HR 1.01, p=0.89), stroke, or myocardial infarction. Crucially, continuing SGLT2i demonstrated excellent renal and hemodynamic safety, with no increased risk of acute kidney injury (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.79–1.20, p=0.82), clinically significant hypotension (HR 1.12, p=0.28), or urinary tract infections (HR 0.80, p=0.11). Conclusion Continuing SGLT2i after TAVI safely reduces mortality, progression to ESRD, hospitalizations, and new-onset AFib without increasing perioperative risks. These findings strongly challenge routine perioperative cessation, suggesting clinicians should proactively maintain SGLT2i therapy post-discharge to optimize patient survival and preserve renal function.Forest plot of all the endpointsKaplan-Meier estimates of major endpoints
