title: Continuing sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors after transcatheter aortic valve implantation improves survival and renal outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial fibrosis (MF) represents a key player in transition to heart failure in aortic stenosis (AS), and patients with high baseline MF are at increased risk to die within 12 months after TAVI. Purpose The objective of this early clinical trial was to assess the impact of anti-fibrotic medication on MF-regression after TAVI in patients with high baseline MF. Key secondary objectives included reverse LV remodeling and symptomatic improvement. Methods Reduce-MFA represents a prospective, randomized, parallel group, multi-center early clinical trial with blinded outcome assessment. At baseline and 12 months, MF was assessed by cardiac MRI (CMR) via quantification of the extracellular volume fraction (ECV%)-derived LV matrix volume. Only patients with a prognostically relevant baseline MF (ECV% ≥25.9%) were randomized into 3 parallel groups. Antifibrotic treatment was administered for 12 months. Due to asymmetric withdrawals and treatment crossovers, the intention-to-treat-analysis of the primary endpoint remained inconclusive. Therefore, an as-treated analysis according to the “treatment-received” principle was performed, with patients pertaining to the treatment arms as follows: A: TAVI alone (n=52), B: + Spironolactone (n=34), and C: + Spironolactone + low-dose Dihydralazine (n=34). Changes of ECV%-derived LV matrix volume, measures of heart failure (6MWT, KCCQ) and cardiac hospitalisations were evaluated. Results The study cohort comprised 120 patients (46% women; mean age 81 years) characterised by preserved EF and renal function, but a high heart failure burden. Whereas the decrease of LV cellular volume (i.e. cellular hypertrophy) was similar in all groups (comparison A vs. B+C: P=0.87), the regression of LV matrix volume (i.e. extracellular matrix) was significantly greater under antifibrotic treatment (Arm B: -16.0%; Arm C: -15.7%) as compared to TAVI alone (Arm A: -2.6%) (P=0.046). Regarding the primary endpoint (hierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and regression of LV matrix volume), a win ratio of 1.64 (95% CI 1.0.-2.67; P=0.049) could be achieved. Furthermore, improvement in quality of life was greater under anti-fibrotic medication (KCCQ: +6 points in Arm A, +12 points in Arm B, and +23 points in Arm C at 12 months; P=0.01). The secondary clinical benefit endpoint, a hierarchical composite consisting of CV mortality, cardiac hospitalisations, improvement in KCCQ, and improvement in 6 MWT, demonstrated a win ratio of 1.60 (95% CI 1.05-2.42; P=0.03) for antifibrotic treatment, indicating a clinically meaningful benefit. Conclusions In TAVI-patients with preserved EF and high baseline MF burden, the early administration of antifibrotic medication including spironolactone and dihydralazine shows clinically meaningful effects on LV matrix volume regression as a surrogate for diffuse MF, and on clinical endpoints including quality of life.
title: Effect of anti-fibrotic therapy on regression of myocardial fibrosis after TAVI: 'As-treated' analysis of the Reduce-MFA DZHK 25-trial

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is now the standard of care for patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have demonstrated significant benefits in patients with heart failure (HF), regardless of ejection fraction; however, their specific effects in patients undergoing TAVR with HF remain understudied, as individuals with valvular heart disease were excluded from major clinical trials assessing the efficacy and safety of SGLT2 inhibitors in HF. The Dapa-TAVI trial reported a reduction in the composite outcome of all-cause mortality or worsening HF in patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors post-TAVR, although the observed effect size was smaller than expected (1).Given this critical evidence gap, we sought to evaluate the association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and major adverse outcomes in HF patients following TAVR using a large, multi-institutional real-world database. Methods We conducted a retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study analyzing de-identified electronic medical records from the TriNetX federated health research network, a globally distributed platform comprising 68 healthcare organizations. Patients with nonrheumatic aortic stenosis and HF who underwent TAVR and subsequently received SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin; n=660) were propensity score-matched to patients who did not receive SGLT2 inhibitors post-TAVR (n=660). Primary outcomes included acute myocardial infarction (MI), all-cause mortality, stroke, cardiac arrest, and acute kidney injury (AKI), assessed from one day post-TAVR to final follow up. Risk metrics including risk differences, risk ratios (RR), and odds ratios (OR) were calculated with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors post-TAVR exhibited significantly reduced all-cause mortality compared to controls (18.9% vs. 28.6%; RR=0.661, 95% CI: 0.542-0.807, p&lt;0.001) and reduced risk of stroke (9.5% vs. 13.0%; RR=0.733, 95% CI: 0.539-0.995, p=0.045). Acute MI (14.4% vs. 13.8%; RR=1.044, 95% CI: 0.800-1.363, p=0.752), cardiac arrest (4.2% vs. 3.8%; RR=1.120, 95% CI: 0.660-1.900, p=0.674), and AKI (32.6% vs. 27.9%; RR=1.168, 95% CI: 0.991-1.378, p=0.063) were comparable between cohorts. Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated significantly improved survival probability in the SGLT2 group. Conclusions In HF patients undergoing TAVR, post-procedural treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors is associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality and stroke risk in this large, real-world, multi-institutional cohort. These findings suggest potential benefit in incorporating SGLT2 inhibitors into the post-procedural management of these patients and support the need for larger, randomized controlled trials to confirm these observations and establish definitive treatment guidelines for this high-risk population.KM Curve
title: SGLT2 inhibitors improve clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement: real world evidence from the trinetx database

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) provides afterload relief in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS). While global longitudinal strain (GLS) is considered a sensitive marker of LV systolic function, myocardial work (MW) indices, may provide a more robust measure of myocardial performance. Purpose We aimed to assess early changes in myocardial deformation, left atrial reservoir strain (LARS), and MW indices following TAVI with the Myval balloon-expandable valve, and to evaluate their association with functional improvement. Methods We prospectively studied 31 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe AS undergoing TAVI with MyVAL. Comprehensive echocardiography, including LV and RV GLS, and LARS, was performed at baseline and 30-day follow-up. MW indices [global work index (GWI), global constructive work (GCW), global wasted work (GWW), global work efficiency (GWE)] were computed. Clinical status and major adverse cardiac events were assessed at 30 days. Results Procedural success was 100%. At 30 days, a ≥1-class NYHA improvement occurred in 97% of patients. Aortic valve mean gradient decreased significantly (Δ−32.8 mmHg, p&lt;0.001). When assessing myocardial deformation, LV GLS paradoxically became less negative following TAVI, with mean values moving from −14.7±3.7% at baseline to −13.4±3.5% at 30 days (p=0.028). RV global strain remained unchanged (−17.6±5.2% vs. −17.1±5.5%, p=0.46). By contrast, left atrial performance showed a favorable trajectory, with LARS increasing from 20.9±7.5% to 22.9±8.2% (p=0.079), GWW decreased substantially from 287±118 mmHg% at baseline to 210±93 mmHg% at follow-up (p&lt;0.001), indicating a significant reduction in energy loss due to dyssynchronous or ineffective myocardial contraction. In parallel, GWI improved markedly, rising from 91.0±4.1% to 95.9±3.8% (p&lt;0.001), reflecting the more favorable redistribution of energy toward effective ejection. GCW also increased significantly, from 1996±570 mmHg% to 2120±545 mmHg% (p=0.039), suggesting that TAVI enhances the ability of the LV to perform useful systolic work once the afterload burden is alleviated. GWI demonstrated a modest but consistent upward shift, from 2094±534 to 2178±488 mmHg% (p=0.051), a change consistent with improved overall stroke work while accounting for normalized loading conditions. At 30-day follow-up, one death was reported (3%). Conclusions In patients with severe AS undergoing Myval-TAVI, GLS demonstrated only modest attenuation at 30 days, whereas MW indices consistently improved, with reduced wasted work, increased constructive work, and higher efficiency, indicating enhanced myocardial performance once afterload was normalized. LARS also showed early improvement, suggesting beneficial effects on atrial function. MW indices and atrial strain are more sensitive and physiologically meaningful markers of early reverse remodeling after TAVI than GLS alone.
title: Myocardial work indices outperform GLS for early reverse remodeling after Myval-TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) effectively reduces mitral regurgitation (MR) and improves symptoms, yet the ventricular and atrial mechanical changes underlying clinical benefit remain incompletely characterized. Purpose To evaluate left ventricular (LV), right ventricular (RV), and left atrial (LA) reverse remodeling using strain imaging after M-TEER and examine associations with functional and quality-of-life outcomes. Methods Between January 2022 and January 2025, 118 patients with symptomatic (NYHA III–IV) moderate-to-severe (3+) or severe (4+) degenerative or functional MR underwent TEER. Clinical, echocardiographic, and quality-of-life data were collected at baseline, 30 days, and 1 year. LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), RV free-wall strain (RV-FWS), and LA reservoir strain (LARS) were assessed. Endpoints included NYHA class, heart failure hospitalization, and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire–Overall Summary (KCCQ-OS). Results Procedural success was 100%, with short device (27 min [IQR 21–35]) and total procedure times (56 min [IQR 48–66]), low complication rates, and median hospital stay of 3 days; 1-year mortality was 9.3%. MR reduction was durable (MR ≤2+ in 98.3% at 1 year), accompanied by sustained NYHA improvement (97.4% NYHA I–II at 1 year) and KCCQ-OS increase (52 ± 19 to 71 ± 15; p&lt;0.001) (Figure 1). High-quality strain analysis was available in 92 patients (78%), with no baseline differences versus excluded patients. LV GLS improved from −11.8 ± 3.2% at baseline to −13.6 ± 3.1% at 30 days and −14.1 ± 3.3% at 1 year (p&lt;0.001), despite no significant change in LVEF (42 ± 11% vs 43 ± 10% at 1 year; p=0.38) (Table 1). Improvement in LV GLS correlated with NYHA class improvement (r=0.42, p&lt;0.001) and KCCQ-OS gain (r=0.39, p&lt;0.001) and predicted KCCQ-OS improvement (β=2.6 points per 1%; p=0.002) (Table 2). RV-FWS also improved from −15.4 ± 4.1% at baseline to −17.1 ± 4.0% at 30 days (p=0.002) and −18.2 ± 4.3% at 1 year (p&lt;0.001), paralleling a significant reduction in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (48 ± 12 to 38 ± 10 mmHg; p&lt;0.001). Patients with ≥2% RV-FWS improvement had fewer heart failure hospitalizations at 1 year (7.8% vs 19.4%; p=0.04). LARS showed the most pronounced response, increasing from 13.2 ± 5.1% at baseline to 18.6 ± 5.4% at 30 days and 21.1 ± 5.9% at 1 year (both p&lt;0.001). LARS correlated strongly with NYHA improvement (r=0.48, p&lt;0.001) and KCCQ-OS gain (r=0.51, p&lt;0.001) and emerged as the strongest independent predictor of quality-of-life improvement (β=1.9 points per 1% increase; p&lt;0.001). Combined improvement in LV GLS and LARS explained 46% of the variance in KCCQ-OS gain (adjusted R²=0.46), outperforming conventional echocardiographic parameters. Conclusions M-TEER induces early and sustained ventricular and atrial reverse remodeling which independently predicts functional recovery and quality-of-life improvement,Figure 1
title: Atrial and ventricular strain remodeling after M-TEER

abstract: Abstract Background Residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR) remains common after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) and is consistently associated with worse clinical outcomes. While post-procedural assessment has traditionally focused on right ventricular (RV) systolic function, the relative contribution of right atrial (RA) remodeling to persistent TR remains poorly defined. Objectives To investigate the longitudinal relationship between RA remodeling and residual TR severity after TEER, and to compare its mechanistic and discriminative value with conventional RV systolic indices. Methods We retrospectively studied 131 consecutive patients with severe TR treated by TEER between 2021 and 2025. Comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography was performed at baseline, predischarge, 6-month, and 12-month follow-up. RA remodeling was quantified using the right atrial volume index (RAVI) and right atrial sphericity index (RASI). RV systolic function was assessed using tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, fractional area change, tissue Doppler–derived systolic velocity, and RV free-wall longitudinal strain. Associations with residual TR severity were explored using Spearman correlation, cumulative ordinal logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. Results Residual TR severity correlated with RAVI at 6 months (ρ = 0.33, p &lt; 0.001) and with both RAVI (ρ = 0.23, p = 0.030) and RASI (ρ = 0.21, p = 0.047) at 12 months. In multivariable ordinal logistic regression, RAVI emerged as the sole independent determinant of residual TR severity at both timepoints, whereas RV systolic indices were not independently associated. ROC analyses revealed a time-dependent pattern: RASI best discriminated severe residual TR at predischarge, whereas RAVI provided the strongest discrimination at 6 and 12 months (AUC up to 0.76). Conclusions After TEER, right atrial remodeling—particularly persistent volumetric enlargement—dominates the burden of residual TR, while conventional RV systolic measures offer limited explanatory value. These findings reposition the right atrium as a central mechanistic and prognostic target in functional TR management.Central figure
title: Right-atrial remodeling and residual tricuspid regurgitation after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair

abstract: Abstract Introduction New-onset conduction disturbances (NCD) are common after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and frequently require permanent pacemaker implantation (PMI). While cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is generally recommended in heart failure patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) who require ventricular pacing, its role following TAVR remains unclear. Purpose To evaluate the impact of CRT after TAVR on all-cause mortality compared to sole right ventricular pacing (RVP) and NCD without PMI. Methods We analyzed all patients undergoing TAVR between 2020 and 2023 in the prospective German Aortic Valve Registry (GARY). NCD was defined as new bundle branch block and/or atrioventricular block after TAVR. Outcomes were compared using 2:1 propensity score (PS) matching based on age, sex, intervention mode, and baseline LVEF. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. Results Of 16,779 patients undergoing TAVR between 2020 and 2023, 12% of patients received RVP and 1% CRT after TAVR. In the entire cohort, irrespective of baseline LVEF, CRT was not associated with improved 1-year survival compared with RVP (P=0.31). Among 4,286 patients with baseline LVEF ≤50%, 636 (15%) underwent new PMI. Of those, 107 patients (20%) received CRT, while 529 patients (80%) underwent RVP. In the unmatched heart failure cohort, 1-year mortality was higher in RVP versus CRT patients (23% vs. 8%; Hazard ratio [HR] 3.26 [1.18-9.00]; P=0.016). After PS matching, RVP remained associated with increased mortality compared to CRT (HR 3.93 [1.37-11.28]; P=0.006). Compared to patients with reduced LVEF and NCD after TAVR, but who did not undergo PMI, CRT showed a trend toward lower 1-year mortality after matching (HR 0.37 [0.13-1.09]; P=0.06). Conclusion In TAVR patients with reduced LVEF, CRT was associated with improved 1-year survival compared with RVP and showed a trend toward benefit compared with NCD without device therapy. Randomized trials are needed to define optimal pacing strategies after TAVR in patients with impaired LVEF.
title: Cardiac resynchronization therapy in transcatheter aortic valve replacement recipients – insights in the GARY registry

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in patients with a small aortic annulus represents a technical challenge due to the higher risk of patient-prosthesis mismatch, suboptimal haemodynamics, and procedural complications. Whether self-expanding valves (SEV) or balloon-expandable valves (BEV) offer superior outcomes in this anatomically challenging subgroup remains unknown. Purpose Purpose of our analysis is to compare SEV vs. BEV in patients with small annulus undergoing TAVI Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospective, multicentre, observational investigator-initiated registry including consecutive patients undergoing TAVI at two high-volume tertiary centres between 2012 and 2024. The primary endpoint was long-term all-cause mortality over a median follow-up of 60 months. Secondary endpoints included VARC-3–defined technical success, device success, in-hospital mortality, periprocedural complications, and post-procedural echocardiographic valve performance. Survival was analysed using Kaplan-Meier estimates with log-rank testing. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was performed adjusting for clinically relevant confounders. Results A total of 737 patients were included (BEV n=318, SEV n=419). The two groups were comparable for age, sex, BMI, and the majority of comorbidities. Pre-procedural echocardiography was comparable between groups. However, SEV patients had a higher prevalence of paced rhythm and more severe pre-TAVI mitral regurgitation. Technical success was high and comparable between groups (BEV 97.2% vs. SEV 97.3%, p=0.976), as was device success (BEV 90.3% vs. SEV 90.6%, p=0.919). In-hospital mortality was low and did not differ significantly. No significant differences were observed in permanent pacemaker implantation, stroke, vascular complications, or bleeding events. SEV were associated with significantly superior haemodynamic performance: lower mean gradient (9.0 [6.0–12.0] vs. 12.4 [10.0–16.0] mmHg, p&lt;0.001), lower peak gradient (17.0 [12.0–22.5] vs. 23.0 [18.6–29.0] mmHg, p&lt;0.001), and larger effective orifice area (AVA 1.77 [1.40–2.08] vs. 1.60 [1.29–1.98] cm², p=0.028). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in overall survival between BEV and SEV over 5-year follow-up (log-rank p=0.394). On multivariable Cox regression adjusting for paced rhythm and pre-TAVI mitral regurgitation, valve type was not independently associated with mortality. Conclusions In patients with small aortic annuli treated with contemporary TAVI devices valve choice did not significantly affect long-term survival, technical success, device success, or major in-hospital outcomes. SEV provided superior post-procedural haemodynamics, which might offer clinical benefit in reducing patient-prosthesis mismatch in this challenging population. Prospective randomised trials specifically targeting the small annulus population are warranted.Figure
title: Self-expanding vs. balloon-expandable valves in small annulus patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background The efficacy of transcatheter mitral edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) has been demonstrated in patients with severe secondary mitral regurgitation (MR). In clinical practice, some patients with moderate MR on transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) are considered to have clinically severe MR based on their clinical course, pulmonary vein flow patterns, transesophageal echocardiography, or stress echocardiography. Outcomes of M-TEER in patients with moderate secondary MR have not been thoroughly investigated. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the impact of M-TEER on clinical prognosis in patients with moderate MR compared with those with severe MR. Methods We assessed consecutive patients who underwent M-TEER for secondary MR between April 2018 and June 2023 in the OCEAN-Mitral registry, a prospective, multicenter registry. Patients were stratified according to MR severity at baseline TTE into two groups: moderate MR (2+) and severe MR (≥3+). The primary endpoint was technical success, defined according to Mitral Valve Academic Research Consortium (MVARC) criteria. Secondary outcomes included hemodynamic parameters during procedure, MR severity, left ventricular volume, hospitalization for heart failure, and mortality. Results Among 2,638 patients, 438 (16.6%) had moderate MR, and 2,200 (83.4%) had severe MR. Among 438 patients with moderate MR, parameters suggestive of clinically relevant MR included severe MR in transesophageal echocardiography (n=146), abnormal pulmonary vein flow pattern (n=304), positive stress TTE (n=118), history of heart failure admission within one year (n=329), and elevated brain natriuretic peptide levels (n=431). Technical success was comparable (97.9% vs. 96.1%, p=0.085). Residual MR ≤ mild was more frequently achieved in patients with moderate MR than in those with severe MR, both at discharge (88.2% vs. 77.3%, p &lt;0.001) and at one month (83.2% vs. 72.4%, p &lt;0.001). At one year, left-ventricular reverse remodeling was modest in moderate MR. Patients with severe MR demonstrated significant reductions in left atrial volume index and tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient, whereas these changes were not significant in the moderate MR group. The one-year cumulative heart failure hospitalization rate decreased after M-TEER in both groups (moderate MR: from 0.75 to 0.17, p &lt;0.001; severe MR: from 1.21 to 0.21, p &lt;0.001). Patients free from heart failure hospitalization within one year after M-TEER had significantly higher three-year survival compared with those with hospitalization (68.0% [95% CI 65.1-70.8%] vs. 36.4% [95% CI 29.9-43.0%]; log-rank p &lt;0.001). Conclusions In the OCEAN-Mitral registry, M-TEER was safely performed in patients with moderate MR and resulted in a meaningful MR reduction. Although cardiac reverse remodeling was modest compared with severe MR, heart failure hospitalization rates were significantly reduced, suggesting potential benefit in selected patients with moderate MR.

appraisal.design_and_n: 2,638 patients; 438 (16.6%) moderate MR and 2,200 (83.4%) severe MR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised, no control arm for moderate MR; the abstract is truncated at the heart failure hospitalisation result.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry of M-TEER for moderate MR, showing high technical success but modest reverse remodelling.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Technical success was 97.9% vs. 96.1% (p=0.085); residual MR of mild or less at discharge 88.2% vs. 77.3% (p <0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Moderate MR is a population without trial evidence for TEER, so the data inform the case for a randomised trial.

title: Outcomes of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for moderate mitral regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter tricuspid valve edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has developed as a treatment option for patients presenting with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) at prohibitive surgical risk. While two T-TEER devices are commercially available in Europe, their efficacy has not been compared. Objective To compare procedural performance, durability of TR reduction, and clinical outcomes according to T-TEER device. Methods Data were taken from the EuroTR (European Registry of Transcatheter Intervention for Tricuspid Regurgitation) registry and included patients undergoing T-TEER in 26 European centers between 2016 and 2024. Characteristics and outcomes of patients were compared at discharge and latest follow-up, according to the device used, in the global population and after propensity score matching. Results Overall, 1,814 consecutive patients treated with T-TEER were included (824 with TriClip and 990 with PASCAL). After propensity matching creating two balanced groups of 713 patients each, improvement in TR was observed in both groups with similar rates of residual TR≤2+ at discharge and follow-up (82.7% vs. 84.7%, p=0.456; and: 64.6% vs. 71.6%, p=0.093; for TriClip vs. PASCAL, respectively). Symptomatic improvement at one year was similar in both cohorts (NYHA class ≤ II TriClip vs. PASCAL: 63.7% vs. 62.8%, p=0.833). Significant right ventricular reverse remodeling was observed with both devices (TriClip: difference in right ventricular end-diastolic area from -2.2 [IQR -6.7 to 2.6] cm2, p=0.018, PASCAL: -2.4 [IQR -7.2 to 2.4] cm2, p=0.001). There was no difference in Kaplan–Meier estimates of two-year survival and survival free from heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.90, 95%CI 0.70- 1.71, p=0.444 and HR 1.11, 95%CI 0.90-1.37, p=0.349). Conclusions TriClip and PASCAL yielded comparable TR reduction, symptomatic improvement, right ventricular reverse remodeling and two-year survival free from heart failure hospitalizationTwo-year survival stratified by device type

appraisal.design_and_n: 1,814 consecutive patients (824 TriClip, 990 PASCAL) from 26 centres; 713 per group after propensity matching.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised device comparison; device choice may reflect anatomy.
appraisal.one_line: European registry comparing TriClip with PASCAL for tricuspid TEER, with similar outcomes after matching.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Residual TR 2+ or less at discharge 82.7% vs. 84.7% (p=0.456); two-year survival HR 0.90, 95%CI 0.70- 1.71, p=0.444.
appraisal.why_it_matters: First sizeable head-to-head comparison of commercial T-TEER devices.

title: Comparison of commercially available tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair devices in real-world practice: data from EuroTR

abstract: Abstract Introduction Comparative data between balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and self-expanding valves (SEVs) in the treatment of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) stenosis is limited. Asymmetric calcification, elliptical annular geometry, and aortic root dilation may influence valve expansion and clinical outcomes following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in BAV. Purpose We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the clinical outcomes comparing BEVs with SEVs in patients undergoing TAVR for BAV stenosis. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane were systematically searched for studies comparing BEV with SEV for TAVR in BAV stenosis from inception through February 2026. Outcomes of interest included procedural, 30-day, and 1-year mortality, annulus rupture, coronary obstruction, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI), moderate or severe paravalvular leakage (PVL), and need for additional valve implantation. Random effects models were applied to generate risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results 22 observational studies with 5,466 patients (BEV: 2,918; 53%) were included. PPI (RR 0.67; 95%CI 0.57-0.78), PVL (RR 0.34; 95%CI 0.17-0.69), and need for additional valve implantation (RR 0.35; 95%CI 0.22-0.58) were lower with BEV compared with SEV. (Figure) However, annulus rupture was higher with BEV (RR 2.80; 95%CI 1.19-6.57) compared with SEV. (Figure) Other outcomes were comparable between BEV and SEV. Conclusion BEVs in TAVR for BAV stenosis showed a lower risk of PPI, PVL, and additional valve implantation, but a higher risk of annulus rupture compared with SEVs. Careful patient selection is crucial, and additional randomised trials are necessary to determine the optimal strategy.Figure
title: Balloon-expandable valves vs self-expanding valves for transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid aortic valve stenosis: a meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) may be a promising option for patients with residual or recurrent tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after prior surgical or transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) repair, but evidence in this setting remains limited. Purpose This study assesses the safety and effectiveness of TTVR after prior repair versus primary TTVR in patients with severe TR. Methods Between 2024 and 2026, consecutive patients with severe TR undergoing either primary TTVR or TTVR after prior TV repair were included in this subanalysis of the Berlin registry of right heart interventions. Clinical and procedural data were prospectively collected at the time of the procedure, at hospital discharge, and at 30–60 days of follow-up. Results In this subanalysis, 69 patients with TR were included, of whom 9 patients (13%) underwent post-repair TTVR after prior tricuspid valve intervention or repair (tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair [T-TEER] n=1, percutaneous annuloplasty [PA] n=7, and surgical TV repair n=1). Median age, proportion of women, and baseline NYHA class III/IV were 82 (68-84) years, 78%, and 78% in the post-repair TTVR group versus 80 (76-83) years, 65%, and 78% in the primary TTVR group, respectively. Procedural success was achieved in all patients. In-hospital mortality was 1%, with no procedure-related deaths. In-hospital adverse events included bleeding in 11% of patients with post-repair TTVR and 3% of patients with primary TTVR, vascular complications in 0% and 2%, new pacemaker implantation in 22% and 20%, stroke in 0% and 2%, myocardial infarction in 0% and 0%, thromboembolic events in 0% and 2% as well as acute kidney injury in 0% and 3%, respectively. At discharge, TR severity was markedly reduced and comparable between groups (none/mild TR: 89% in post-repair TTVR vs. 98% in primary TTVR). At follow-up, NYHA functional class improved in both groups without significant intergroup differences: 33% (post-repair TTVR) versus 45% (primary TTVR) in class I/II at follow-up (vs. 22% in both groups at baseline). During follow-up, heart failure rehospitalization occurred in 11% in the post-repair TTVR group versus 3% in the primary TTVR group. Conclusion In this hypothesis-generating subanalysis of the Berlin registry of right heart interventions, post-repair TTVR was technically feasible and showed a favorable early safety and performance profile. Outcomes were broadly similar to those observed after primary TTVR in patients with significant TR.
title: Post-repair transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement for severe tricuspid regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is established in clinical guidelines for diagnosing chronic coronary syndrome (CCS). New Photon-counting CT provides superior spatial resolution, markedly enhancing coronary lumen visualisation in calcified lesions. Computed fractional flow reserve (cFFR) enables a non-invasive functional evaluation of flow limitations, potentially reducing unnecessary diagnostic invasive coronary angiographies. Purpose This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of cFFR derived from photon-counting computed tomography compared to invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) in CCS patients, with a specific focus on those with a high coronary calcification burden. Methods Consecutive CCS patients underwent both dual-source photon-counting CCTA and invasive coronary angiography between January 2024 and January 2025. cFFR analysis was performed using dedicated scientific software in a blinded manner. Flow-limiting stenoses were defined as invasive FFR ≤0.80 or angiographic stenosis &gt;90%. Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV)) was evaluated with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Agreement was assessed via Cohen's kappa (κ), interpreted according to Landis and Koch, while McNemar (p) tests evaluated systematic differences between methods. Results Analysis included 145 coronary vessels from 87 patients (77% male, mean age 70, range 40-92 years). The Coronary Artery Calcium Score was available for 64 patients (108 vessels) with a mean Agatston score of 1181. Overall group (n=145 vessels): Sensitivity was 89.3% (95% CI: 82.2–93.8%), specificity 69.7% (95% CI: 52.7–82.6%), accuracy 84.8% (95% CI: 79.0–90.7%), PPV 90.9% (95% CI: 84.1–94.9%), and NPV 65.7% (95% CI: 49.2–79.2%). Agreement was moderate (κ=0.577) with no systematic bias (p=0.832). In the high-risk subgroup (Agatston &gt;1000, n=53 vessels from 29 patients), cFFR maintained excellent diagnostic performance with sensitivity 90.4% (95% CI: 78.3–97.5%), specificity 88.9% (95% CI: 51.8–99.7%), accuracy 90.6% (95% CI: 82.7–98.4%), PPV 97.6% (95% CI: 87.1–99.9%) and NPV 66.7% (95% CI: 34.9–90.1%). Agreement was substantial (κ=0.705; p=0.375). Mean radiation dose for CCTA was 7.5 mSv. Conclusions Photon-counting CT–derived cFFR accurately identifies haemodynamically significant coronary stenoses, even in patients with severe coronary calcification, demonstrating high concordance with invasive FFR and a high PPV. These findings support its role as a reliable non invasive gatekeeper for invasive coronary angiography, addressing a major limitation of conventional CCTA in heavily calcified vessels.
title: Diagnostic accuracy of photon-counting CT-derived fractional flow reserve in chronic coronary syndrome patients with severe coronary calcification

abstract: Abstract Abstract It has been shown that female gender is independent predictor of decreased functional capacity. Gender specific effect of early surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) on exercise capacity in asymptomatic patients with severe AS and normal left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is unknown. The aim of our study was to determine whether there is a difference in gender related changes in functional capacity after early SAVR in a group of asymptomatic patients with severe AS and normal LVEF randomized within AVATAR trial. Method 157 asymptomatic patients with severe AS were enrolled prospectively and underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on a bicycle ergometer (patient supine, RAMP protocol, 15 W/min) as a measure for functional capacity. Patients with proven ischemia, any symptom or LVEF &lt; 50% were excluded from the study. Results 157 patients (mean age, 67 years; 68 were women) were randomly allocated to early surgery or conservative treatment. 46 men and 32 women underwent early SAVR. There were no baseline gender differences in age (66.11 vs 64.8, p=ns), echo parameters of AS severity (Vmax 4.51 vs 4.54 m/s, and Pmean 52.2 vs 53.42 mmHg, or LVEF 67.7 vs 66.6%, all p=ns) . Women had higher body mass index (29.5 vs 27.3, p = 0.018), higher VE/VCO2 slope (35.6 vs 28, p=0.039), lower VO2max (12.70 vs 18.5ml/kg/m2 p&lt;0.05), and achieved lower workload (129.4 vs 73.1watts, p&lt;0.05) at baseline CPET. After 12 months in both genders in early SAVR group there was statistically insignificant increase in VO2max (men 18.5 to 22.2 ml/kg/m2, women 12.7 to 15.7 ml/kg/m2, p=ns respectively) and decrease in VE/VCO2 slope (35.6 to 32.8, p=ns) while only women significantly increased workload (73.2 to 90.3 watts, p=0.047, compared to 129.4 to 135 watts in men, p=ns) Conclusion For the same severity of AS and LVEF, in comparison to males, asymptomatic females have lower functional capacity but potentially greater functional benefit after early SAVRWorkload by Sex: Baseline to 12M Post-SAVR
title: Gender related improvement in functional capacity after early aortic valve replacement in asymptomatic patients with severe aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) measured during the postoperative period is a strong predictor of adverse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). The magnitude of postoperative cTnI release is typically higher in patients undergoing valve surgery compared with CABG. However, only a limited number of studies have evaluated the prognostic value of cTnI after valvular cardiac surgery. This study aimed to assess the independent prognostic value of troponin I levels measured at different time points during the first 72 hours after isolated valvular heart surgery and to determine cTnI cut-off values associated with in-hospital mortality according to valve surgery type. Methods All patients who underwent isolated valvular heart surgery at a single tertiary center between 2011 and 2020 were included. Troponin levels were categorized according to postoperative time intervals: ≤12 h, 12–24 h, 24–48 h, and 48–72 h. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between cTnI levels and in-hospital mortality after adjustment for clinical and operative variables. ROC curves were constructed to assess the discriminative performance of cTnI for in-hospital mortality, and optimal cut-off values were determined using Youden’s index. Results A total of 4,100 patients were included. Median age was 57 years (IQR 46–66), 54% were female, and 32% had undergone prior cardiac surgery. The predominant etiology was rheumatic heart disease (44%). Median logistic EuroSCORE ranged from 0.9 to 5.1, and 12% of procedures were urgent or emergent. LVEF was 62 (IQR 57-66), with 329 patients (8,1%) presenting LVEF ≤40%. In-hospital mortality was 11.4% (n=470). Troponin levels at all measured time points (≤12 h, 12–24 h, 24–48 h, and 48–72 h) were significantly associated with in-hospital mortality (p&lt;0.001). The highest discriminative performance was observed in the 24–48 h interval (AUC 0.722). Across all surgery types, non-survivors consistently exhibited higher cTnI levels. Optimal cTnI cut-off values for predicting in-hospital mortality were: aortic valve surgery — 132× the upper reference limit (URL) at 24–48 h and 68× URL at 48–72 h; mitral valve surgery — 209× URL at 24–48 h and 100× URL at 48–72 h; multiple valve surgery — 263× URL at 24–48 h and 130× URL at 48–72 h. In the multivariable model with imputed data, cTnI levels measured after 12 h remained independently associated with in-hospital mortality, with the strongest association observed for measurements obtained at 48–72 h (OR 1.91, 95% CI 1.81–2.03; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Postoperative cTnI levels measured between 24 and 72 hours after isolated valvular heart surgery were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. The observed cut-off values were substantially higher than currently recommended thresholds for clinically relevant periprocedural myocardial injury, particularly in multiple valve procedures.
title: Risk stratification based on troponin I as a predictor of mortality in isolated valve surgeries

abstract: Abstract Background Bicuspid aortic valves (BAV) exhibit diverse morphological patterns. The two most common phenotypes are the 2-sinus BAV and the fused BAV. These phenotypes differ in their geometric characteristics, and their valve dysfunction may arise from distinct underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, both of which could influence outcomes following aortic valve replacement (AVR). Purpose To evaluate differences in short-term complications and long-term prognosis following aortic valve surgery among patients with bicuspid aortic valve according to valve morphology. Methods From a prospective cohort study of adult BAV outpatients followed in the period 2018-2024, we identified 276 cases who underwent AVR during follow-up and who had either a 2-sinus (n=44/15.9%) or fused (n=232/84.1%) BAV morphology. Short-term complications were assessed at 30-days following surgery and we compared a composite of re-interventions (redo-AVR, surgery to stop major bleeding, pericardiocentesis, or re-hospitalization with pleuracentesis) and all-cause mortality using logistic regression. Furthermore, the following complications were assessed at end of follow-up: re-do AVR, endocarditis, and all-cause mortality. We estimated the overall event-free survival using the Kaplan Meier-estimator and compared the hazard of having any of these events using Cox regression. We considered sex and age at time of surgery as possible confounders. Results Median age of the cohort was 62.5 [54.9, 69.3] years with no difference between morphology subgroups (p=0.6). Surgical details are compared between the subgroups in Table 1. Groups were very similar, with the exception that the frequency of pericardial patch repair during surgery was slightly higher in the 2-sinus BAV subgroup (9.1% vs. 1.3%, p=0.01). In total, 75 (27.2%) patients experienced one of the short-term complications and the risk was increased in patients with 2-sinus BAV (unadjusted odds ratio= 2.13, 95% CI (1.09; 4.16), p=0.03) and (adjusted odds ratio=2.26, 95%CI (1.14; 4.46), p=0.02). During a median follow-up of 4.4 years (interquartile range: 2.1- 5.6), there were 10 cases (3.6%) of endocarditis, 8 re-do surgeries (2.9%) and 10 patients died (3.6%). In total, 14 patients developed a primary composite endpoint and the estimated event-free survival 5 years after surgery was 89.4%, 95%CI (85.3%; 93.6%). The hazard of the composite endpoint was higher in patients with 2-sinus BAV with a crude hazard ratio of 2.34, (95% CI (0.97; 5.64), p = 0.06) and an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.62 (95%CI (1.08; 6.35), p=0.03, figure 1 Cumu). Conclusion In this observational study of bicuspid aortic valve patients undergoing aortic valve surgery, a 2-sinus BAV morphology was associated with increased risks of short-term and longer-term complications.
title: Aortic valve morphology and complications after aortic valve surgery in patients with bicuspid aortic valve disease

abstract: Abstract Background Long-term nationwide data comparing mitral valve repair versus replacement and age-dependent outcomes of mechanical versus bioprosthetic valves remain limited. Objectives To evaluate 25-year national trends and long-term outcomes of mitral valve surgery and to determine age-modified associations between mechanical and bioprosthetic prostheses. Methods Using Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database (1997–2022), we identified 19,844 patients undergoing mitral valve repair or replacement. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included heart failure (HF) hospitalization, stroke or systemic embolization (SSE), major bleeding, and reoperation. Kaplan–Meier analyses and multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and comorbidities were performed. Age interactions were evaluated using restricted cubic splines. Results Among 19,844 patients, 8,877 underwent repair and 10,967 replacement (3,833 mechanical; 5,408 bioprosthetic). Replacement patients were older (62.9±14.2 vs 53.4±13.3 years, p&lt;0.001) and had higher comorbidity burden. Over a median follow-up of 70.9 months, 7,513 deaths occurred. Compared with repair, replacement was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.70–2.07; p&lt;0.001), HF hospitalization (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.54–1.98; p&lt;0.001), and stroke/SSE (HR 2.35, 95% CI 2.08–2.65; p&lt;0.001). Among replacement strategies, mechanical valves were associated with increased major bleeding (HR 2.67, 95% CI 2.37–3.00; p&lt;0.001) and hemorrhagic stroke (HR 2.82, 95% CI 2.23–3.57; p&lt;0.001) compared with bioprosthetic valves, but lower reoperation risk (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49–0.79; p&lt;0.001). Spline-adjusted modeling demonstrated significant age interaction for mortality (P for interaction&lt;0.001). Mechanical valves were associated with lower mortality in younger patients, with survival advantage most pronounced below 60–65 years, but this benefit attenuated with advancing age and was no longer observed in patients ≥70 years (HR 1.03 at age 70; 95% CI 0.90–1.17). In contrast, excess bleeding risk with mechanical valves persisted across all age strata. Conclusions In this nationwide 25-year cohort, mitral valve repair was associated with superior long-term outcomes compared with replacement. Mechanical valves provided an age-dependent survival advantage in younger patients but at the cost of substantially increased bleeding risk, with diminishing mortality benefit in older individuals. These findings support individualized, age-tailored prosthesis selection.Cubic spine curve
title: Long-term outcomes after mitral valve surgery in a 25-year nationwide cohort with age-dependent prosthesis effects

abstract: Abstract Background Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), even when left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) is preserved. However, the interplay between structural (echocardiographic) and electrical (electrocardiographic) remodeling and their impact on clinical outcomes after Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) remain poorly defined. This study aims to evaluate the prognostic value of a combined echocardiographic and electrocardiographic staging of AtCM in patients without a history of atrial fibrillation (AF). Methods We analyzed 122 consecutive patients with severe AS and preserved EF who underwent TAVI between 2017 and 2024. Patients were stratified based on two AtCM risk domains: The primary composite endpoint was all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization. The risk goup secondary endpoint was new-onset AF. Results Mean age was 82.3 ± 5.6 years. At baseline, 54.1% of patients had High Echo-Risk (Stage 3-4) and 19.7% had High ECG-Risk (Score 2). Multivariate analysis showed divergent predictive capabilities:Composite Endpoint (Death/HF): High Echo-Risk was a strong independent predictor (HR 4.17; 95% CI 1.46–11.95; p=0.0079), whereas High ECG-Risk was not significant (HR 1.46; p=0.604).New-Onset AF: High ECG-Risk was the sole predictor of AF (HR 3.00; 95% CI 1.02–8.76; p=0.045), while High Echo-Risk was not predictive (HR 1.02; p=0.960).Combined analysis identified distinct phenotypes: High Echo-Risk/Low ECG-Risk patients had significantly increased risk of HF/Death (HR 4.86, p=0.0078), while Low Echo-Risk/High ECG-Risk patients had the highest risk of AF (HR 8.99, p=0.0045). A double-risk profile (High Echo/High ECG) conferred the worst prognosis for both outcomes (figure 1, 2) Conclusion In patients with severe AS and preserved EF, atrial cardiomyopathy manifests through distinct pathophysiological domains. Echocardiographic staging (based on LAVI and strain) predominantly identifies the risk of "pump failure" (HF/mortality), while specific ECG scoring (focusing on advanced inter-atrial block) stratifies arrhythmic risk (AF). A comprehensive multimodal approach is essential for accurate pre-TAVI prognostic stratification and may help identify patients who require more intensive evaluation.Atrial Cardiomyopathy StagingUnivariate and Multivariate Cox Analysis
title: Prognostic impact of integrated echocardiographic and electrocardiographic staging of atrial cardiomyopathy in severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Older adults undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) often have impaired functional reserve that is not fully captured by conventional risk scores. In contemporary practice, frailty is frequently assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS); however, CFS is inherently subjective and may not quantify lower-extremity performance. The Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) provides an objective, multidomain assessment of physical function, yet its prognostic utility after TAVI, particularly beyond CFS, remains unclear. Purpose To assess whether preprocedural SPPB is independently associated with long-term all-cause mortality after TAVI. We also examined whether SPPB provides incremental prognostic information beyond established clinical variables and the CFS. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing TAVI between February 2016 and May 2025 at a single centre. SPPB was assessed preprocedurally and categorised as low (≤9) vs high (&gt;9). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Time-to-event analyses were administratively censored at 5 years. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, Society of Thoracic Surgeons risk score, access route, haemoglobin, and NT-proBNP. Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for the CFS. In addition, we constructed three prespecified risk models to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of SPPB. Model 1 included age, the STS risk score, access route, haemoglobin, and NT-proBNP. Model 2 added the CFS to Model 1. Model 3 further added SPPB category to Model 2. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and reclassification was assessed using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI). Results Among 968 patients with available SPPB (median age 84 years; 60.2% women), 415 (42.9%) had low SPPB. Over a median follow-up of 2.61 years, 118 deaths occurred. Low SPPB was associated with higher mortality (log-rank P&lt;0.001) and remained independently associated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR 2.62, 95% CI 1.74–3.96; P&lt;0.001). The association was robust to additional adjustment for CFS (adjusted HR 1.99, 95% CI 1.28–3.09; P=0.002). When modelled as a continuous variable, lower SPPB was similarly associated with higher mortality (per 1-point lower SPPB: adjusted HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08–1.19; P&lt;0.001), including after additional adjustment for CFS (adjusted HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04–1.16; P=0.001). Adding SPPB to a model including conventional variables plus CFS improved discrimination (AUC 0.704 vs 0.679; P=0.029) and risk reclassification (NRI 0.288, 95% CI 0.092–0.485; P=0.004). Conclusion Low preprocedural SPPB is common and independently associated with higher post-TAVI mortality. Incorporating SPPB into preprocedural assessment provides incremental, clinically interpretable prognostic information beyond standard risk variables and clinician-rated frailty.Figure_1Figure_2
title: Association between short physical performance battery and mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Statins have been shown to be linked to improved survival after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, age-specific effects of statins are unclear. Therefore, the present analysis assessed the association between statin use at TAVI and 5-year mortality across age. Methods We retrospectively analyzed the prospective, multicenter-TAVI registry (n=5,797). Exposure was any statin at the time of TAVI. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality until 5 years since TAVI. Unadjusted survival was compared by Kaplan–Meier with log-rank testing. Multivariable Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for statin use across continuous age using restricted cubic splines, adjusting for sex, diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), renin–angiotensin system inhibitor (RASI), and renal function; age-specific effects were displayed as aHRs referenced to 100 years. Results Statins were used in 52.7% of patients, who were more often complicated by diabetes and ASCVD. Statin use was associated with lower 5-year mortality overall and among patients aged ≥90 years (log-rank p=0.00325) (Figure A). In adjusted spline analyses, the aHR for statins was consistently &lt;1 across most of the age range, with a sustained association between ages 65 and 100 years, indicating lower mortality among statin users despite greater baseline comorbidity (Figure B). Conclusions In this large contemporary TAVI registry, statin use at TAVI was associated with reduced 5-year mortality across nearly the entire age spectrum, including the very elderly. These data support considering routine statin therapy in TAVI recipients when clinically appropriate.Figure AFigure B
title: Statins are linked to better survival after TAVI across the oldest ages,: analysis from the multicenter TAVI registry

abstract: Abstract Aims Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. While coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) offers excellent anatomical assessment, its ability to determine the functional relevance of intermediate stenoses remains limited. Computed tomography–derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) has emerged as a noninvasive method for assessing lesion-specific ischaemia. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR using 15O-water positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging as the reference standard. Methods and results A retrospective cohort of 193 patients who underwent hybrid CCTA and 15O-water PET at Kuopio University Hospital (2017–2022) was reviewed. Patients with a low-to-intermediate pretest probability of CAD and at least one stenosis &gt;50% were eligible. After exclusions, 165 patients were included. The CT-FFR values were derived using a research prototype algorithm and compared with PET-derived perfusion abnormalities. PET identified impaired perfusion in 58 patients (35%). In the overall cohort, CT-FFR demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.740 (right coronary artery), 0.681 (left anterior descending artery), and 0.672 (left circumflex artery). In a subset of 83 patients with high-quality CCTA and stenosis &gt;50%, diagnostic performance improved substantially (AUC 0.836). Using a CT-FFR threshold of 0.80, sensitivity was 85% and specificity was 87%. Conclusion CT-FFR provides a clinically meaningful assessment of the functional significance of coronary stenoses in selected patients with high-quality CCTA. Its performance is reduced in unselected populations, particularly when image quality is suboptimal. Therefore, CT-FFR should be considered a complementary tool rather than a replacement for 15O-water PET in complex diagnostic settings.
title: Correlation between 15O-water PET–detected myocardial ischaemia and CT-derived FFR: Predicting the functional significance of anatomical stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Aortic stenosis is associated with cognitive decline and dementia, potentially due to cerebral hypoperfusion and microemboli. Whether aortic valve replacement (AVR) confers long-term neuroprotection compared with medical management remains unclear, particularly comparing transcatheter (TAVR) and surgical (SAVR) approaches. Purpose To evaluate the association between AVR and long-term risks of dementia subtypes and stroke in a large, propensity score-matched cohort. Methods Retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (167 healthcare organisations). Patients with aortic stenosis undergoing AVR were compared with those managed medically. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, including frailty indicators, sensory impairment, mental health, cardiovascular medications, and prior stroke/TIA. Hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals were estimated using Cox regression for Alzheimer’s disease, vascular dementia, other dementias, unspecified dementia, mild cognitive impairment, senile degeneration, and cerebral infarction. Results In the main matched cohort (159,823 vs 159,823), AVR was associated with reduced risk of Alzheimer’s disease (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.70-0.82), vascular dementia (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.71-0.84), other dementias (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.74-0.85), unspecified dementia (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.77-0.85), and senile degeneration (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.90). No significant differences were observed for mild cognitive impairment (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95-1.10) or cerebral infarction (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.96-1.05). SAVR showed substantially stronger protection than TAVR across dementia subtypes (e.g., Alzheimer’s: SAVR HR 0.49 vs TAVR HR 0.91). Benefits were consistent in both sexes, with slightly stronger Alzheimer’s protection in women (HR 0.70 vs 0.78 in men), and persisted in patients with prior stroke/TIA. Conclusion AVR is associated with significant long-term reductions in dementia risk across multiple subtypes, independent of early peri-procedural effects, with SAVR demonstrating more pronounced neuroprotective benefits than TAVR. These findings support the potential cognitive benefits of valve intervention in aortic stenosis, though residual confounding by disease severity cannot be excluded.Figure 1
title: Neuroprotective effects of aortic valve replacement: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Sex-specific disparities in patient-reported outcomes amongst patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are not fully investigated. Objectives To evaluate sex-based differences in clinical outcomes and health status following transfemoral TAVR in patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Methods Patients in the investigator-initiated, multicenter SCOPE I randomized trial were stratified by sex. Outcomes of interest included vital status and patient-reported disease-specific health status, with an integrated patient-centered outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score [KCCQ-OS] ≥75 without a decline of &gt;10 points from baseline). Results Of 732 patients who underwent TAVR, 692 (394 female and 298 male) were included in the analysis of patient-centered outcome. At baseline, female patients had a higher surgical risk and higher prevalence of advanced heart failure symptoms and frailty, whereas male patients had a greater comorbidity burden. Female patients had lower baseline KCCQ-OS, which persisted after TAVR, leading to a lower likelihood of achieving KCCQ-OS ≥75 at 1 year (64.4% vs. 74.2%). In contrast, male patients had consistently higher all-cause mortality throughout 3 years of follow-up (26.3% vs. 19.5%). These contrasting patterns in patient-reported health status and survival resulted in a similar proportion of patients who were alive with good health status at 3 years between groups (42.7% vs. 46.1%). Conclusions In this post-hoc analysis of SCOPE I, male and female patients achieved a similar rate of the patient-centered outcome up to 3 years after TAVR, despite contrasting patterns in patient-reported health status and survival.
title: Sex-specific differences in patient-centered outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Based on the TAVI model, new generations of sutureless surgical devices, such as the Perceval bioprosthesis, have emerged as innovative alternatives for surgical aortic valve replacement. Purpose Although safety and efficacy of the sutereless devices are well established, data regarding their durability are lacking. Methods This monocentric study included consecutive patients who underwent aortic valve replacement with the Perceval sutureless bioprosthesis between Novembre 2013 and March 2022 for severe aortic stenosis. The primary endpoint was bioprosthetic valve failure (BVF) free survival at mean follow-up defined according to the 2021 Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Secondary endpoints included aortic valve reintervention or structural valve deterioration (SVD) free-survival , incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI), stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA), cardiac-related rehospitalization, and cardiac-related mortality at mean follow-up. Results A total of 191 patients were included, with a mean age of 75 years. Early mortality and PPI rate (≤ 30 days) was 3.7 % (n=7) and 13.6 % (n=26), respectively. With a mean follow-up of 4.5 years, BVF-free survival was 88.5% (95%CI= 82.2; 92.6), free from SVD was 95.7% (95%CI= 90.6; 98.1), and reintervention-free survival was 97.9% (95%CI= 93.5; 99.3) (figure) . At 6 years follow-up, it was 81.4%, 88.2% and 92% respectively. PPI was required in 20.4% of patients, with conduction abnormalities at cardiopulmonary bypass weaning (p=0.0003) and pre-existing conduction disorders (p=0.007) identified as independent predictors. Stroke/TIA-free survival, cardiac rehospitalization-free and freedom from cardiac-related death rates were 79.5%, 65.4% and 88.5% respectively. Conclusions The Perceval sutureless bioprosthesis demonstrates good short-term outcomes in terms of mortality and efficacy. However mid-term durability and high rate of conductive disorders requiring PPI may be a concern.
title: Long-term clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of the Perceval aortic sutureless bioprosthesis

abstract: Abstract Background The 2025 European Guidelines, define normal-flow, low-gradient (NFLG) aortic stenosis (AS) as less likely severe AS. NFLG is regarded as pathophysiologically equivalent to moderate AS with differences in exercise gas exchange and hemodynamic that remain undefined. Purpose We sought to examine the exercise gas exchange, and clinical features of less likely severe AS with preserved EF (NFLG ASpEF) compared to moderate ASpEF and true-severe ASpEF. Methods 88 patients divided in 26 NFLG ASpEF (AVA &lt;1.0 cm2 or AVA index &lt;0.6 cm2/m2, PV &lt;4 m/s or MPG &lt;40 mmHg, SVi &gt;35ml/m2, LVEF ≥50%), 27 moderate ASpEF and 35 severe ASpEF patients underwent CPET imaging. Results There were no significant differences in baseline patient characteristics or medication use among the three groups. Although the mean pressure gradient (MPG) during exercise differed significantly across the groups (moderate ASpEF 25±11, NFLG ASpEF 39±10, severe ASpEF 52±22 mmHg, p &lt;0.001), exercise SVi (43±12 ml/m2), heart rate (122±22 bpm), and cardiac output (8.8±2.8 L/min) did not (p &gt;0.05). Indices of left atrial pressure, left atrial stiffness, and right ventricular–pulmonary circulation coupling showed no significant differences at rest as well; however, these parameters worsened significantly during exercise in the severe ASpEF group. As to exercise gas-exchange, a signifcant reduction of the arteriovenous oxygen content difference was observed in the NFLG ASpEF group (moderate ASpEF 15.0±5.9, NFLG ASpEF 11.5±2.8, severe ASpEF 15.9±4.8 mLO2/100ml, p =0.002). During follow-up, aortic valve replacement was performed more frequently in the NFLG ASpEF than in the moderate ASpEF group (moderate AspEF 4%, NFLG ASpEF 31%, severe ASpEF 26%, Log-rank test p =0.034). Over a median follow-up of 926 days, age- and sex-adjusted Cox proportional hazards analyses showed that the hazard ratios for the composite endpoint of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality were comparable among the three groups (p = 0.64). Conclusions Data show that the NFLG ASpEF phenotype exhibits an exercise hemodynamic pattern comparable to moderate ASpEF; nonetheless despite a preserved O2 delivery an impaired O2 extraction emerges as peculiar feature of this clinical entity of AS.
title: Exercise gas exchange, hemodynamics and clinical outcomes in patients with normal flow low gradient aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background In the setting of aortic stenosis (AS), long-standing pressure overload leads to myocardial damage and subjects patients to an increased risk of heart failure (HF) and death even after successful aortic valve replacement (AVR). Conventional HF medications may have the potential to target this residual HF component, but current evidence on the efficacy in severe AS after AVR is limited. Aims The aims of this study were to assess HF medication prescription patterns and their association with outcomes in severe AS after AVR. Methods Consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing successful AVR between 2013 and 2024 were included. Treatment status with HF medications (Renin-angiotensin-system inhibitors [RASi], Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [MRA], beta-blockers [BB], Sodium glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors [SGLT2i]) at discharge after AVR was recorded. Nearest neighbor propensity score (PS) matching for age, sex, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP], estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR], glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c], hypertension and coronary artery disease was performed. All-cause and cardiovascular (CV) mortality at month 60 were assessed in the overall population and prespecified subgroups: a) surgical (SAVR) vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) b) left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥50% vs. &lt;50%. Results In total, 4,882 patients (75.9 years, 56.4% male, 51.8% TAVR, 48.2% SAVR) were included. RASi were prescribed in 35.1%, MRA in 30.5%, SGLT2i in 14.3%, and BB in 10.4%. Patients receiving RASi (LVEF &lt;50%: 17.2% vs. 10.1%; NT-proBNP: 1,238 pg/ml vs. 971 pg/ml), MRA (LVEF &lt;50%: 18.7% vs. 9.8%; NT-proBNP: 1,372 pg/ml vs. 962 pg/ml) and SGLT2i (LVEF &lt;50%: 20.6 vs. 11.1; NT-proBNP: 1,450 pg/ml vs. 1,037 pg/ml) were at a more advanced stage of cardiac disease compared to patients not receiving respective medications. Treatment with RASi (HR: 0.68; 95%CI: 0.59-0.78; HR: 0.68; 95%CI: 0.56-0.82), MRA (HR: 0.74; 95%CI: 0.63-0.86; HR: 0.70; 95%CI: 0.57-0.85), and SGLT2i (HR: 0.69; 95%CI: 0.53-0.91; HR: 0.56; 95%CI: 0.38-0.80) was independently associated with a reduced hazard for all-cause and CV mortality, respectively. Treatment benefits were confirmed across evaluated subgroups. Conversely, no outcome signals for BB treatment were found. Conclusions Prescription of HF medications in AS undergoing AVR is impacted by the stage of cardiac disease. Treatment with RASi, MRA and SGLT2i, but not BB, is associated with favourable clinical outcomes, including subgroups of TAVR/SAVR and reduced/preserved LVEF.All-cause mortality in severe AS after AVRAll-cause mortality in investigated subgroups

title: Heart failure therapy in severe aortic stenosis after surgical or transcatheter aortic valve replacement (The HF-STAR cohort study)

abstract: Abstract Background Sex-specific Agatston unit (AU) thresholds are recommended for the diagnosis of severe aortic stenosis (AS)1-3, and contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) derived calcium volume scores (CVS) have been proposed as an alternative4,5. However, the diagnostic performance of them has not yet been validated against invasively confirmed, hemodynamically true severe AS. Purpose We aimed to determine the prevalence of invasively confirmed true severe AS, to evaluate whether conventional sex-specific AU thresholds discriminate it, and to derive optimal cutoffs for AU and CVS. Methods Patients were enrolled from the prospective Invasive PPM Study between October 2024 and July 2025, designed to evaluate valve hemodynamics before and after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) using right- and left-heart catheterization. Patients who underwent non-contrasted CT and CECT prior to TAVR were included. Hemodynamically true severe AS was defined as an invasively measured aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm² calculated using the thermodilution-based Gorlin formula, whereas AVA &gt;1.0 cm² was classified as non-severe AS. The AVC score was quantified using the Agatston method with sex-specific AU thresholds (&gt;2000 in men and &gt;1200 in women)1,3. CVS was calculated from CECT using a threshold of ≥ 850 HU. Results Of 100 enrolled patients, 85 were eligible for analysis. True severe AS was present in 51 (60%). Invasive AVA was lower in the true severe AS group than in the non-severe AS group (0.71 vs. 1.17; p &lt; 0.01), as was echocardiography-derived AVA (0.55 vs. 0.70; p &lt; 0.01). Both the AVC score and CVS were higher in true severe AS (AVC score: 2336.3 vs. 1654.1; CVS: 273.0 vs. 164.5; both p &lt; 0.01). ROC analysis showed good discriminatory performance of the AVC score for identifying true severe AS, with an AUC of 0.76 in men and 0.85 in women. Using guideline-based sex-specific thresholds, sensitivity (Sn) and specificity (Sp) were 0.85 and 0.58 in men and 0.87 and 0.67 in women, respectively. The optimal cutoffs were 2272 AU for men (Sn 0.85, Sp 0.68; Figure A) and 1429 AU for women (Sn 0.74, Sp 0.93; Figure B). For CVS, AUC was 0.73 in men and 0.76 in women. The optimal cutoffs were 430 mm³ for men (Sn 0.50, Sp 0.90; Figure C) and 178 mm³ for women (Sn 0.61, Sp 0.93; Figure D). In men, there was no significant difference in AUC between the AVC score and CVS (p = 0.62), whereas in women, the AVC score demonstrated significantly superior discriminatory performance compared with CVS (p = 0.03). Conclusions Sex-specific AVC score provided robust discrimination of invasively-confirmed true severe AS. The optimal cutoffs were higher than the conventional thresholds in both sexes. Although its performance was similar to CVS in men, the AVC score significantly outperformed CVS in women. This is the first study to validate the diagnostic utility of AVC score against invasively-confirmed true severe AS, supporting their clinical relevance.Figure A, BFigure C, D
title: Sex-specific CT-derived aortic valve calcification predicts hemodynamically true severe aortic stenosis defined by invasive catheterization

abstract: Abstract Background Fractional flow reserve derived from coronary computed tomography angiography (FFR-CT) is recommended for non-invasive evaluation of intermediate coronary artery stenoses. However, a recent meta-analysis showed that contemporary anatomy-only FFR-CT methods provide moderate agreement with invasive FFR with reduced discrimination in the intermediate “gray-zone” where clinical decisions are often most challenging. We hypothesized that integrating individual pressure-waveform hemodynamics into FFR-CT computation could improve functional assessment of coronary lesions, particularly in this diagnostically challenging range. Methods We developed a waveform-enhanced FFR-CT algorithm that incorporates Continuous Non-invasively measured Blood Pressure (CNBP) waveforms as patient-specific physiological to determine boundary conditions for Computational Fluid Dynamics models of coronary flow. FFR-CT values were computed along the coronary tree and adjusted to the invasive FFR measurements, with FFR ≤0.80 considered hemodynamically significant. In this multicenter study, 167 vessels from 132 patients enrolled in the NCT04777513 trial were analyzed. Diagnostic performance of waveform-enhanced FFR-CT was compared against invasive FFR and benchmarked against collected off–site FFR-CT results from a recent temporary meta-analysis including 2423 vessels, restricted to prospective diagnostic accuracy studies reporting vessel-level FFR-CT versus invasive FFR. Results Per-vessel analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance of waveform-enhanced FFR-CT, with an AUC of 0.916 (95% CI 0.868–0.956) and overall diagnostic accuracy of 88.6% for detecting functionally significant stenoses versus invasive FFR. Sensitivity and specificity were 92.5% and 87.4%, respectively, compared with 81.5% and 77.7% for benchmark FFR-CT (p=0.027 and p=0.0021), and AUC was significantly higher (0.916 vs 0.858; p=0.026). Bland–Altman analysis demonstrated minimal bias between invasive FFR and waveform-enhanced FFR-CT (mean difference −0.01, 95% limits of agreement −0.21 to 0.19) and a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.69 with a regression slope close to unity. In the clinically relevant grey-zone subgroup (FFR 0.75–0.85), diagnostic accuracy remained high with waveform-enhanced FFR-CT (81.2% vs 65.4% for benchmark FFR-CT; p=0.003), with higher specificity (79.6% vs 59.7%; p=0.0014) and numerically higher sensitivity (85.0% vs 72.7%; p=0.14). Conclusion An individual physiology-enhanced FFR-CT approach that integrates patient-specific pressure–waveform dynamics into coronary CFD modeling improves diagnostic accuracy and agreement versus benchmark anatomy-only FFR-CT, including within the grey zone of intermediate lesions. These findings support the use of physiology-integrated FFR-CT to refine non-invasive selection of patients for invasive coronary angiography and revascularization.Accuracy of Cardiolens FFR-CT Pro
title: Beyond anatomy: individual physiology-enhanced approach to improve accuracy of fractional flow reserve from computed tomography

abstract: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) has complex interplay with aortic stenosis (AS), and has been identified as a predictor of adverse clinical outcomes for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) patients[1,2]. Angiographic microvascular resistance (AMR), a marker of coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), may link AS-related cardiac remodeling and AF. Purpose To evaluate the association between AMR and the presence of pre-existing AF in TAVR patients and to determine the impact of these factors on clinical outcomes of patients after TAVR. Methods A total of 1118 patients with severe AS who underwent TAVR at a single center from November 2012 to May 2025 were screened for inclusion in this retrospective study, and 742 patients who met all criteria were included. AMR was calculated using a quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-based approach from coronary angiography[3]. AF was diagnosed through electrocardiogram according to current guidelines. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure readmission, and acute myocardial infarction. Results AF was present in 111 (15.0%) patients. Patients with AF had significantly higher AMR levels than those without (248 ± 74 vs 226 ± 68, P=0.004). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that AMR was a significant independent predictor of AF after adjustment for age, body mass index, hyperlipidemia, previous heart failure, log-transformed NT-proBNP, left atrial diameter and left ventricular ejection fraction (OR: 1.054; 95% CI: 1.022–1.086; P &lt; 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant linear association between AMR and the risk of AF (P for overall &lt; 0.001, P for non-linearity = 0.567). Subgroup analyses confirmed the consistency of the association between elevated AMR and the presence of AF across various clinical strata. During a follow-up of 1440 days, a total of 206 patients (27.8%) experienced MACE. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated significant differences in MACE-free survival among the four groups stratified by AF status and AMR levels (log-rank P &lt; 0.001). Patients with AF and elevated AMR had the lowest MACE-free survival, followed by those with AF and lower AMR levels. Multivariable Cox regression analysis confirmed that the coexistence of AF and high AMR remained a robust predictor of MACE (adjusted HR: 2.16; 95% CI: 1.33–3.50; P = 0.0018). Conclusions AMR is an independent predictor of pre-existing AF for TAVR patients. The coexistence of AF and CMD was associated with adverse prognosis in TAVR patients. As a marker of advanced cardiac remodeling, microcirculatory assessment should be incorporated into risk stratification to help refine individualized management.Distribution and restricted cubic splineKaplan-Meier survival analysis for MACE
title: Prognostic value of angiographic microvascular resistance for atrial fibrillation and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Introduction Photoplethysmography (PPG) captures the blood volume curve under the skin, which may be altered in the presence of aortic valve stenosis (AS) due to the slower opening of the stenotic valve. If so, PPG could serve as a simple, low-cost method for remote screening of AS. Purpose To explore the impact of AS on wrist-derived PPG features before and after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Methods PPG data were collected at 128Hz using a PPG-sensor incorporated in a wristband worn by patients during TAVI. Data were filtered (bandpass: 0.5-7Hz) and motion artefacts removed. PPG features were calculated using the systolic peak and dicrotic notch and the median of 300 heartbeats was taken. Differences in features before and after TAVI were tested using the paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed rank test, whichever appropriate. Results In total, 121 patients were included. Patients had a median age of 79 (IQR 76-84) and the majority was male (55%). Heart rate did not differ before and after valve replacement (p=.052). Time to systolic peak was longer before TAVI (0.27 (0.25-0.30) vs 0.25 (0.22-0.28), p&lt;.001), as was the time until dicrotic notch (0.42 (0.40-0.46) vs 0.41 (0.38-0.45), p=.005). The ratio of diastolic to systolic area under the curve decreased after TAVI (diastolic / systolic AUC: 0.49 (0.41-0.60) vs 0.57 (0.41-0.71), p=.010), indicating a relatively greater systolic contribution before the procedure. Conclusion This explorative study demonstrates differences in features of the PPG signal before and after aortic valve replacement. This is an incentive to further study the impact of AS on the PPG signal. If patients with AS can be distinguished using PPG, this may allow individuals to be screened for AS using their own smartwatch.Figure 1
title: Wrist-derived photoplethysmography features prior to and after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: Towards smartwatch-based screening for aortic valve stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background We developed Cardioverse-BAV, an AI platform for population-wide Type 0-bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) screening. It leverages ECG-gated cardiac CT (CTA) while circumventing its need for specialized radiologists. Methods Derived from the Three-Province transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) Registry, Cardioverse-BAV platform leverages a deep learning model trained on 1156 core lab-confirmed ECG-gated CTAs from 1156 TAVR patients. The development set was randomly assigned to training and internal test sets at a 7:3 ratio. Its diagnostic performance was validated in an external surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) cohort from a Hospital University between Jan 2018 and Sept 2025 (n=736 with both preoperative ECG-gated CTA and surgical confirmation) and a large-scale cohort receiving screening coronary CTA and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) (n=16,770) from two tertiary hospitals between Jan 2020 and Aug 2025. Results In the internal test set, Cardioverse-BAV platform accurately predicted BAV (AI model: 32.2% vs. core lab: 30.0%), achieving weighted aggregated scores as follows: accuracy 98.9%, recall 96.7%, specificity 100%, precision 100%, and F1-score 98.3%. In external test sets, the AI model identified BAV in 5.3% of cases, outperforming TTE (2.4%) and comparable to surgical confirmation (5.0%). It achieved 99.2% accuracy, with recall of 94.6%, specificity of 99.4%, precision of 89.7%, and F1-score of 92.1%. Compared to TTE, the AI model showed a significant improvement in recall (+81.1%, P &lt; 0.001), achieving 94.6% recall vs. 13.5% for TTE. While its specificity (99.4%) was slightly higher than TTE (98.1%), the difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.999). In a cohort of 16,770 patients, ECG-gated CTA identified BAV in 1.3% of cases versus 0.4% by TTE (P &lt; 0.001), with weak agreement between methods (kappa = 0.193). Conclusion The Cardioverse-BAV platform is a tool for BAV diagnosis with the potential to enhance early detection, as evidenced by its validation in multiple distinct cohorts.
