These findings highlight the need for targeted post-discharge management and long-term cardiovascular monitoring in COVID-19 survivors with myocardial injury.Graphical abstract
title: Long-term effects of myocardial injury on one-year outcomes in COVID-19 survivors: a prospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background and aims Patients with LMNA gene variants are at high risk for dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure (HF), but no prediction model for severe HF events exists. This study aimed to describe the incidence of severe HF events and develop a prediction model in a large cohort of patients with adult-onset laminopathies. Methods From a population of 660 patients enrolled in the French LMNA nationwide registry, 470 adults were included in the derivation cohort. An independent international validation cohort included 245 additional patients (from Australia, Italy, Netherlands, UK, USA). Baseline characteristics at genetic testing were assessed and the cumulative incidence of the primary endpoint HF-MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) was calculated, defined as HF hospitalization, HF-related death, mechanical circulatory support or heart transplantation.Predictors of HF-MACE were studied after excluding patients with LVEF &lt;30% at baseline using a Fine-Gray competing risk model, adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) with 95% confidence interval (CI), and Harrell’s concordance (C-) index. A secondary composite end-point, without hospitalization, was also studied. Results Among 470 patients of the derivation cohort, HF-MACE occurred in 65 over a median follow-up of 7.1 years (IQR 3.4; 12.1). Four independent predictors of HF-MACE were identified: male sex (aHR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.060-3.290), LVEF &lt;50% (aHR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.080-4.400), missense variants in head & rod domains (aHR, 2.91; 95% CI, 1.110-7.630), and complete left bundle branch block (aHR, 2.99; 95% CI, 1.400-6.400). The C-index of the model was 0.750 (95% CI, 0.720–0.780) in the derivation cohort and 0.758 (95% CI, 0.720–0.800) in the validation cohort. The 5-year cumulative incidence of HF-MACE was 1.5% (95% CI, 0.6–3.6), 5.0% (95% CI, 1.8–8.2), and 22.0% (95% CI, 15.6–28.4) among patients with 0, 1, and ≥2 risk factors, respectively. In patients with LVEF &lt;30% at baseline, the 1-year incidence of HF-MACE was 50%, and those patients were excluded from the risk score. Conclusions The first prediction model for severe HF events in adult laminopathies was developed, which has the potential to guide the selection of patients who may benefit from enhanced monitoring protocols, early medical treatment, and timely referral for heart transplantation management.Figure LMNA & HF ESC Congress
title: Laminopathies : natural history and risk prediction of heart failure

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Acute myocarditis (AM) is defined as inflammation of the myocardium, characterized by a variable clinical presentation. The PREMYO cohort is the first Spanish multicentre registry to characterise patients with clinically suspected AM. Purpose The aim of our study was to analyse clinical differences and outcomes in patients with a confirmed diagnosis of AM according to sex. Methods This multicentre registry included 1.321 patients with clinically suspected AM between September 2023 and February 2026. A confirmed diagnosis was established by a national clinical committee, following the 2025 ESC Guidelines for the management of myocarditis and pericarditis criteria. Patients were classified in two groups according to sex. Baseline characteristics and a primary endpoint of major adverse cardiac events (heart failure, cardiogenic shock, mechanical circulatory support, pacemaker or cardioverter-defibrillator implantation and death) and ventricular complications (arrhythmias and dysfunction) during follow-up were recorded and compared between groups. Results Among 315 patients with a diagnosis of AM confirmed by the clinical committee,264 (83.8%) were male and 51 (16,2%) women. Women were older than men (53.22 vs 33.92 years), with a greater prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, previous cardiac disease,cancer and autoimmune disease (table 1).Dyspnoea at presentation (23.5% vs 9.8%; p = 0.010) was more frequent in women, whereas chest pain (91.7% vs 80.4%; p=0.022) and fever (44.5% vs 21.6%; p=0.004) were in men. Higher levels of troponin I and CRP were observed in men (5,442 vs 1,277 pg/mL; p=0.001) and (5.52 vs 2.30 mg/dL; p=0.009) respectively. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and TAPSE were lower in women (43.09% vs 53.36%; p&lt;0.001) and (18.04 mm vs 22.7 mm; p&lt;0.001) respectively. Coronary angiography and endomyocardial biopsy were performed more frequently in women (49.3% vs 31.9%; p&lt;0.001) and (12.7% vs 5.5%; p=0.012). The presence of late gadolinium enhancement on MRI was higher in men (93.9% vs 83.3%; p = 0.024). During hospitalization, women experienced a worse clinical course, with a higher prevalence of heart failure (19.6% vs 2.7%; p&lt;0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (21.6% vs 3%; p&lt; 0.001), ventricular dysfunction (19.6% vs 8.7%; p=0.041), need for inotropic support (9.8% vs 1.9%; p=0.001) and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (5,9% vs 1,1%;p=0,022) or pacemaker implantation( 5,9% vs 0%; p=0,032). During follow-up, women exhibited higher rates of the primary endpoint (p&lt;0.001, log-rank test), driven by increased mortality (8.2% vs 1.2%; p = 0.015) and persistent ventricular dysfunction (4.1% vs 0%; p=0.026)(Figure 1) Conclusions Clinical presentation of AM in women differed from men in our national cohort and, despite lower troponin levels, women had more frequently reduced LVEF and experienced worse clinical outcomes both during hospitalization and at follow-up.Table 1Figure 1
title: Sex differences in the clinical presentation and outcomes of acute myocarditis: insights from the PREMYO multicenter registry

abstract: Abstract Introduction Myocardial injury has been observed during the acute phase of COVID-19 infection. Whether this persists at long-term follow-up and if there is an association with acute COVID-19 severity is unclear. Aim To investigate the long-term effects of acute COVID-19 infection severity on cardiac structure and function. Method This study included patients with prior confirmed COVID-19 infection who underwent a standardized clinical follow-up approximately 4 years after infection, including transthoracic echocardiography, lung ultrasound (LUS), and symptom questionnaire. Acute COVID-19 severity was categorized as: mild (managed at home), moderate (hospitalised), or severe (intensive care unit (ICU) admission). Associations were examined using linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and comorbidities, with tests for linear trend across increasing severity class. Results A total of 695 patients were included (52.5% female, median age 61 years [51;70]), distributed in the following severity groups: mild (n=468), moderate (n=179), and severe (n=48). Prevalent comorbidities included hypertension (37.3%), dyslipidaemia (36.7%), asthma (17.1%), atrial fibrillation (11.1%), diabetes (7.9%), and ischemic heart disease (7.8%). (Table 1). The prevalence of ≥3 B-lines on LUS and NYHA ≥II was higher with increasing COVID-19 severity (home, hospital, ICU) (6.4%, 14.4%, 25.6%, p &lt;0.05, and 28.2%, 74.1%, 69.2% p &lt;0.001) (Table 1). Increasing COVID-19 severity was associated with a higher prevalence of left ventricular systolic dysfunction; GLS &lt; 16% (9.7%, 18.0%, 33.3%, p &lt;0.05), LVEF (40-49%) (17.8, 27.7, 30.3%, p &lt;0.05) and LVEF (&lt;40%) (5.9%, 11.8%, and 12.1%, p&lt;0.05) (Figure 1). Prevalence of LV diastolic dysfunction (E/e’ ratio &gt;14) was similar across groups (p=0.35) but became significantly different after adjustment (p &lt;0.05). Right ventricular (RV) function was worse in higher severity groups according to RV fractional area change (42.5% (10.4), 38.5% (11.0), 35.2% (9.1), p &lt;0.001), with association persisting after adjustment. Left atrial (LA) parameters were also worse in higher severity groups (peak atrial longitudinal strain (36.2 [30;44], 32.9 [26;41], 27.5 [24;36], p &lt; 0.001), and LA conduit strain (17.9 [13;24], 14.7 [10;20], 11.0 [9;16], p &lt;0.001), however these trends were attenuated after adjustment. Conclusion Increasing severity of acute COVID-19 infection was associated with long-term echocardiographic signs of worse RV, LA, and LV systolic function, and higher number of B-lines on LUS.Figure 1Table 1
title: Long-term prevalence of cardiac dysfunction according to acute COVID-19 infection severity

abstract: Abstract Background Sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have demonstrated clinical benefits in heart failure (HF) across a broad spectrum of ejection fraction and diabetes status. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) remains limited. Purpose We aimed to evaluate the association between SGLT2 inhibitors use and clinical outcomes in a nationwide HCM cohort, including those without diabetes. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Health Insurance Service database. A total of 5,312 patients with HCM (mean age 65 ±14 years; female 39%; diabetes 80%; obstructive type 10%) were identified and matched in a 1:1 ratio by propensity score with 35 baseline variables. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, HF hospitalization, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI). Results Over a median follow-up of 5.1 years, patients on SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with a lower risk of hospitalizations for HF or mortality compared to those not on SGLT2 inhibitors (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.71-0.90, P&lt;0.001, Figure). This reduction was primarily driven by a decrease in HF hospitalization (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.70-0.89; P&lt;0.001). SGLT2 inhibitor use was also associated with a lower risk of stroke (HR 0.51; 95% CI 0.40-0.65; P&lt;0.001), but not of mortality (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.89-2.18; P=0.15) or MI (HR 0.76. 95% CI 0.57-1.01; P=0.063). The reduction in the primary endpoint was consistent irrespective of diabetic status and obstructive phenotype (P for interaction=0.39 for diabetes; 0.18 for obstructive type). Conclusion In a nationwide cohort of patients with HCM, SGLT2 inhibitor was associated with a lower risk of a composite end-point of mortality and HF hospitalization, with consistent effects across diabetic and non-diabetic patients and across HCM subtypes. These findings suggest potential clinical benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in a broader HCM population.KM Curves for Outcomes by SGLT2i in HCM
title: Impact of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary plaque burden and myocardial ischaemia are both recognised markers of risk in patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD). However, their relative impact on cardiovascular outcomes over time remains incompletely understood. Purpose To investigate the time-dependent prognostic value of quantitatively assessed coronary plaque burden and myocardial ischaemia in patients with suspected CAD. Methods We included patients with suspected CAD who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging. Plaque burden was measured on CCTA as percent atheroma volume (PAV) using AI-based analysis. Myocardial perfusion was assessed on PET by regional hyperaemic myocardial blood flow (hMBF). Multivariable Cox regression models including both PAV and hMBF were used to evaluate associations with a composite endpoint of death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or unstable angina at 3, 6, and 9 years. Results Among 1,385 patients, mean age was 62 ± 9 years, 746 (54%) were men, median PAV was 7.9% (IQR: 2.7%–16.4%), and impaired regional perfusion was present in 678 (49.0%). During a median follow-up of 7.1 years, 185 patients (13%) experienced the composite endpoint. Higher PAV was independently associated with greater risk at all assessed time points, with HRs ranging from 1.036 to 1.047 per 1% increase (all p&lt;0.001) (Figure 1). Lower hMBF was independently associated with adverse outcomes at 3 years (HR: 1.050; p=0.004) and 6 years (HR: 1.028; p=0.024), but not at 9 years (HR: 1.020; p=0.063), per 0.1 mL/min/g decrease (Figure 1). After excluding patients who underwent early revascularization, lower hMBF remained associated with outcomes throughout follow-up (Figure 2). Conclusions Coronary plaque burden and myocardial ischaemia provide independent prognostic information in suspected CAD. Plaque burden showed a consistent association with adverse outcomes over time, whereas ischaemia was mainly related to short- and intermediate-term risk, likely influenced by the effects of myocardial revascularization.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Temporal associations of coronary plaque burden and myocardial perfusion with clinical outcomes

abstract: Abstract Introduction Single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) virus–associated myocarditis is driven by innate nucleic-acid sensing and can progress through inflammatory amplification and programmed cell death, resulting in virus myocardial injury. Polyuridylic acid (PolyU) is a synthetic ssRNA mimic and a canonical TLR7/8 agonist, providing a tractable model ssRNA-triggered cardiac inflammation. Purpose To establish a PolyU-induced murine model of ssRNA-driven myocarditis and to delineate a TLR7/NF-κB signaling that couples inflammatory amplification with apoptotic and pyroptotic cell-death programs in cardiac tissue. Methods Five-week-old male BALB/c mice were assigned to Control and PolyU-treated cohorts . At day 3 after PolyU administration, mice were euthanized for serum collection and cardiac tissue harvest. Myocardial pathology was evaluated using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining to assess inflammatory infiltration and tissue injury. Circulating injury and inflammatory burden were quantified by serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and C-reactive protein (CRP), together with pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6). Mechanistic profiling of heart tissue was performed by western blot to quantify TLR7 pathway components (TLR7, MyD88, TRAF6) and NF-κB activation (IκBα/p-IκBα, p65/p-p65). Programmed cell death signaling was assessed by western blot for apoptosis markers (Bad, Bax, Bcl-2, Bcl-xL) and pyroptosis markers (NLRP3, ASC, pro/cleaved caspase-1, GSDMD). Results H&E staining demonstrated myocarditis-like changes in PolyU-treated hearts, characterized by inflammatory cell infiltration and myocardial tissue injury. In parallel, systemic injury/inflammatory burden increased following PolyU exposure, reflected by elevated serum LDH and CRP, along with increased circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines. Mechanistically, western blot analyses of cardiac tissue showed activation of the TLR7 signaling axis with concomitant NF-κB activation which enhanced phosphorylation of IKK, IκBα, and p6. These inflammatory signals were accompanied by coordinated engagement of programmed cell-death pathways, evidenced by pro-apoptotic shifts and induction of pyroptosis-related components including NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1 activation, and GSDMD cleavage, supporting a TLR7-centered linkage between inflammatory amplification and coupled apoptosis/pyroptosis in PolyU-induced myocarditis. Conclusion PolyU induced a robust ssRNA-mimic murine myocarditis phenotype characterized by inflammatory myocardial infiltration and injury, systemic elevation of LDH/CRP and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and activation of the cardiac TLR7/NF-κB axis. This inflammatory cascade is tightly coupled to concurrent engagement of apoptotic and pyroptotic programs, supporting a mechanistic framework in which TLR7/NF-κB signaling links innate immune sensing to programmed cardiomyocyte death in ssRNA-driven viral myocarditis.
title: PolyU triggered viral myocarditis cardiac injury via TLR7/NF-κB activation and programmed cell death

abstract: Abstract Background Recent Guidelines of the European Society of Cardiology have introduced the concept of Inflammatory Myocardial and Pericardial Syndrome (IMPS), a unified entity encompassing both myocarditis and pericarditis (1). This framework reflects the continuum between these conditions in term of anatomy, shared etiologies, and a common diagnostic approach (2,3). This study sought i) to describe factors associated with pericardial involvement; ii) to compare the outcomes of patients hospitalized for proven acute myocarditis (AM) with or without pericardial effusion; iii) to identify the independent correlates of clinical outcome. Methods This is an observational ambispective cohort study based on the AMPHIBIA registry, including patients hospitalized for proven AM between august 2008 and December 2024 at a French hospital. Patients were stratified into two groups based on the presence of pericardial effusion on admission transthoracic echocardiography, ranging from minimal effusions to tamponade. The main composite outcome was defined as the occurrence of all-cause death, temporary mechanical circulatory support, severe ventricular arrhythmia and heart transplantation, at longest follow-up, up to 7 years. Results A total of 581 patients with AM were included (follow-up 3.7 [1.3 – 7.3] years). Among them, 134 (23%) patients presented with pericardial effusion and 447 (77%) patients without. Four independent variables were associated with pericardial effusion at admission: left ventricular (LV) dysfunction, immunological myocarditis, elevated CRP, and fever. The occurrence of the composite event was significantly higher in patients with pericardial effusion compared than in those without (38.1% vs. 15.7%, hazard ratio [HR] 2.69, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.88-3.86, p &lt; 0.001). This difference was observed regardless of pericardial effusion size. After multivariate analysis, pericardial effusion was independently associated with the main composite outcome (HR 1.99 [1.32-3.00], p = 0.001). Conclusion This study characterizes the phenotypes and outcomes of patients hospitalized for an AM, with and without pericardial effusion. Pericardial involvement was associated with LV dysfunction, immunological myocarditis, elevated CRP, and fever; and was linked to a markedly higher risk of the composite outcome, remaining an independent predictor of adverse events. Differentiating these two phenotypes may provide physicians with valuable guidance for managing therapy in these patients.Graphical abstract
title: Prognosis impact of pericardial effusion in patients with acute myocarditis

abstract: Abstract Background Giant cell myocarditis is a rare but highly aggressive inflammatory cardiomyopathy frequently presenting with rapidly progressive heart failure. Despite treatment with intensive combined immunosuppression, many patients progress to advanced heart failure, transplantation, or death. A deeper understanding of the immunological pathways driving myocardial injury is therefore urgently needed to enable more effective and targeted therapeutic strategies. Purpose To characterize the transmural immune and metabolic organization of giant cell myocarditis across the human cardiac wall using whole-transcriptome spatial profiling of explanted heart tissue. Methods Whole-transcriptome spatial RNA sequencing was performed on explanted human cardiac tissue obtained at heart transplantation for fulminant giant cell myocarditis. Twenty tissue sections from twelve predefined ventricular regions were analyzed. Spatial clustering, cell-type deconvolution, and layer-resolved pathway analyses were applied along a continuous epicardial-to-endocardial axis to characterize immune, stromal, and cardiomyocyte programs. Results Layer-resolved pathway analysis revealed marked epicardial enrichment of IL-6/JAK/STAT3 and TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, identifying a dominant pro-inflammatory signaling niche at the outer myocardial layer. Spatial profiling demonstrated cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and immune populations arranged in distinct transmural patterns, with immune cells concentrated in epicardial inflammatory regions dominated by activated myeloid populations. Lymphoid compartments exhibited a continuum from IgM-expressing B cells to IgG4-secreting plasma cells, consistent with sustained humoral immune activation. These spatial immune–metabolic gradients were conserved across ventricular regions despite marked regional heterogeneity. Conclusion First full-heart spatial transcriptomic analysis of giant cell myocarditis identifies dominant epicardial IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling as a central feature of the disease-associated immune landscape. This first spatial multi-region profiling of a human GCM explant reveals a layered immune–metabolic organization linking epicardial inflammatory niches to myocardial injury and highlights potential therapeutic targets.Figure
title: First full-heart spatial transcriptomic analysis of giant cell myocarditis reveals transmural immune - metabolic gradients

abstract: Abstract Background Radiomic analysis of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) enables quantification of myocardial textural features that are not visible to the human eye with potential diagnostic and prognostic value in cardiovascular disease. The aim of this study was to predict myocardial injury, defined by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), in acute myocarditis using artificial intelligence (AI) applied to clinical and CMR radiomic features. Methods The cohort included patients with a clinical diagnosis of acute myocarditis in a large tertiary centre. Left ventricular LGE extent was quantified using the 5SD threshold method and stratified into high (&gt;10%) or low LGE (&lt;10%) categories. Myocardial segmentation of short-axis cine and T1 mapping was performed using a trained nnUNet model (v2). Radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics (v3.1.0). Four feature sets were evaluated: clinical, T1 radiomics, clinical + T1 radiomics, and clinical + T1 + cine radiomics. Clinical variables included age, sex, time to CMR and troponin and cardiovascular risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes and smoking. Recursive feature elimination was utilised for feature selection. Supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms were evaluated across all feature sets including logistic regression, random forest and three boosting methods. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. Feature importance was examined using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). Results 96 patients had short axis cine imaging, T1 mapping and LGE imaging with age 41.2 +/- 16.9 years. 61/96 patients were male and 67/96 were in the high LGE category. The best performing ML algorithms for each feature set are shown in Table 1. The AUROC to predict high LGE for the clinical + T1 feature set was 0.833 ± 0.069 (sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.78) compared with the AUROC for the T1 feature set alone (0.830 ± 0.068 (sensitivity 0.90, specificity 0.79)). Texture-based radiomic descriptors derived from T1 mapping, predominantly from the grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) family appeared to be the most influential features for predicting high LGE (Figure 1). Conclusions CMR radiomics data can be leveraged to predict myocardial injury (LGE burden) in acute myocarditis. Adding clinical features to the T1 radiomic feature set results in minimal predictive improvement. Using an explainable AI approach, provides insight into why predictions are made and the mechanisms underlying myocardial injury in myocarditis. The most impactful radiomic features (GLCM), may reflect myocardial heterogeneity on T1 mapping and influence the prediction of the spatial extent of cardiac injury. Radiomics offers potential novel biomarkers for enhanced diagnosis. Predictive models could be used to guide disease stratification, and follow-up including the timing of repeat CMR study, and/or genetic testing.
title: Beyond the visible: radiomic texture analysis of cardiovascular magnetic resonance for prediction of myocardial injury in acute myocarditis

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocarditis (AM) occurs substantially more frequently in males. In contrast, females tend to present at older ages, and may experience higher risks of complications although results are conflicting (1, 2). Data on sex-specific prospective course of AM are lacking. This study aimed to fill this gap by comparing clinical features, imaging findings, and in-hospital outcomes between men and women, and describing their distinct phenotypes. Methods MyocarditIRM is a multicenter prospective observational study of patients with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-proven AM (3). The main non-inclusion criterion was initial admission to the intensive care unit. Patients were divided into male and female groups. Clinical, biological, electrocardiogram (ECG), and imaging data as well as in-hospital events were systematically collected. CMR features were analyzed centrally by the CoreLab (IHU-ICAN, Paris, 2024/109689.1). In-hospital complications were analyzed by sex using logistic regression adjusted for age and initial severity. Results A total of 788 patients with AM were included (647 men, 141 women). Women were older (34 vs. 30 y, p=0.009) and had higher rates of hypertension and immunological disorders. At presentation, women more frequently presented with dyspnea, whereas men more often had chest pain and infectious prodromes. On CMR, women had higher LVEF and fewer segments with late gadolinium enhancement. Biologically, women had lower troponin and C-reactive protein at admission. Coronary imaging and endomyocardial biopsy were performed in a similar proportion of women and men. The proportion of patients meeting criteria for initial severity – including LVEF &lt;50%, severe arrhythmia, high-degree AV block, or cardiogenic shock – was not statistically different in women and men (18% vs. 12%; p=0.071), despite a trend towards more complicated AM in women. STEMI-like presentations – defined as a chest pain with ST-elevation on admission ECG, without initial severity criteria or in-hospital complications – occurred in 40% overall, more often in men (44% vs. 24%, p&lt;0.001). In logistic regression adjusted for age and initial severity, sex was not associated with in-hospital complications – including death, LVEF &lt;40%, sustained arrhythmia, cardiogenic shock, or need for mechanical or device support – which occurred in 10% of women and 7% of men. Conclusion In the prospective MyocarditIRM study, AM predominantly affected men, whereas women were older, had more comorbidities, were less likely to present with STEMI-like symptoms, and had fewer affected segments on CMR; however, initial severity and in-hospital complications were not statistically between sexes. These sex-specific analyses may have implications for diagnosis and therapeutic strategies.
title: Sex-related differences in characteristics and outcome of patients with acute myocarditis: insights from the Prospective MyocarditIRM Study

abstract: Abstract Introduction Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially fatal pregnancy-associated cardiomyopathy with overlapping pathophysiology with preeclampsia and eclampsia, including shared angiogenic dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and systemic inflammation. Whether concurrent hypertensive disorders of pregnancy modify in-hospital outcomes in PPCM remains unknown. We examined the impact of concurrent preeclampsia/eclampsia on cardiogenic shock and other acute adverse outcomes in patients hospitalized with PPCM. Methods Using 2016-2022 National Inpatient Sample (NIS) databases we identified delivery hospitalizations complicated by PPCM with ICD-10-CM code 090.3.Concurrent preeclampsia/eclampsia was identified through co-documentation of codes 011.x, 014.x, or 015.x. Survey weighted logistic regression was performed adjusting for necessary comorbidities and confounders, taking into account the sampling style of NIS. The primary outcome of our study was cardiogenic shock, secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury (AKI), in-hospital mortality, cardiac arrest, acute respiratory failure, mechanical circulatory support (MCS), venous thromboembolism (VTE), and a composite adverse outcome. Results Among 1,293 unweighted PPCM delivery hospitalizations (≈5,114 nationally weighted), 553 (42.8%) had concurrent preeclampsia/eclampsia. Strikingly, concurrent preeclampsia/eclampsia was associated with significantly lower adjusted odds of cardiogenic shock (6.62% vs. 2.89%; aOR 0.35; 95% CI 0.18–0.67; p=0.002) and VTE (4.19% vs. 1.81%; aOR 0.43; 95% CI 0.20–0.93; p=0.033). Conversely, concurrent preeclampsia/eclampsia independently predicted higher odds of acute respiratory failure (28.92% vs. 40.33%; aOR 1.67; 95% CI 1.29–2.17; p&lt;0.001) and a higher composite adverse outcome rate (38.24% vs. 49.37%; aOR 1.52; 95% CI 1.19–1.96; p=0.001). AKI was more prevalent in the concurrent group (9.73% vs. 14.47%) but the adjusted association was borderline (aOR 1.41; p=0.074). In-hospital mortality, cardiac arrest, and MCS use did not differ significantly. Conclusion In our nationally representative cohort of the United States, coexisting preeclampsia/eclampsia paradoxically conferred protection against cardiogenic shock in PPCM, the most catastrophic inhospital event, yet increased acute respiratory failure and composite morbidity. This challenges the presumption that preeclampsia worsens PPCM outcomes. The findings of our study signal for the potential adjustment of how we identify PPCM risk for hypertensive pregnancies. Our results also identify a need to develop hemodynamic monitoring and pulmonary edema prevention protocols informed by syndrome specific cardio-obstetric stratification.
title: Among delivery hospitalizations complicated by peripartum cardiomyopathy; does co-presence of preeclampsia or eclampsia increase the odds of cardiogenic shock?

abstract: Abstract Background Diabetes mellitus (DM) accelerates coronary atherosclerosis and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Artificial intelligence–guided quantitative CT (AI-QCT) enables comprehensive plaque characterization and quantification, offering potential for refined risk stratification. We evaluated the association between AI-QCT–derived plaque burden and composition and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with and without DM. Purpose To assess AI-QCT–derived plaque burden for MACE risk stratification according to diabetes status. Methods CONFIRM2 is a global, multicenter registry of symptomatic patients with suspected coronary artery disease referred for coronary computed tomography angiography. In this analysis, 4,977 patients were included (750 with DM and 4,227 without DM). AI-QCT was used to quantify plaque burden and characterize plaque composition. Plaque characteristics and clinical outcomes were compared according to DM status. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, myocardial infarction, late revascularization, cerebrovascular events, unstable angina, or heart failure. Results Patients with diabetes were older and exhibited a greater atherosclerotic burden compared with non-DM patients. Total plaque volume (TPV) was higher in DM (median 106.2 [IQR 36.4–288.1] vs. 50.8 [15.3–166.9] mm³), with higher non-calcified plaque (74.0 [26.2–170.7] vs. 38.8 [12.5–105.6] mm³) and calcified plaque volumes (22.0 [0.8–96.6] vs. 5.3 [0–44.4] mm³) (all p&lt;0.001). Percentage atheroma volume was greater (3.8% [1.5–10.2] vs. 1.9% [0.6–5.8], p&lt;0.001), and obstructive and multivessel disease were more prevalent (p&lt;0.001). During follow-up, 234 MACE occurred, with higher events in DM compared with non-DM patients (8.9% vs. 4.0%, p&lt;0.001). Cox regression demonstrated a stepwise increase in risk across TPV stages, with hazard ratios of 1.9, 7.5, and 10.4 in non-DM patients and 2.3, 9.5, and 9.9 in DM patients (p&lt;0.05 for moderate and high TPV). In multivariable models, atheroma burden conferred a higher risk in patients with DM (Pinteraction=0.013). Kaplan–Meier analyses showed low event rates in minimal plaque burden and progressively higher MACE with increasing TPV; within each stage, patients with DM had higher events, most pronounced in moderate plaque burden. Addition of TPV to RF-CL categories improved discrimination for MACE (AUC 0.61 vs. 0.74, p&lt;0.001). Conclusions Atheroma quantification by AI-QCT stratifies risk patients with and without DM. MACE increases with plaque burden, and patients with DM have higher event rates at similar TPV levels, particularly in the moderate stage. These findings support quantitative plaque assessment for improved risk stratification in DM patients.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Risk stratification of major adverse cardiovascular events by AI-guided quantitative coronary CT according to diabetes status: the CONFIRM2 registry

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Mavacamten improves symptoms and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). While favorable changes in left ventricular (LV) diastolic function are also well established, the mechanistic response of left atrial (LA) function remains insufficiently characterized. LA strain may capture distinct stages of atrial adaptation to chronic LV pressure overload and its resolution. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate LA strain adaptation during mavacamten therapy in oHCM patients. Methods We analyzed clinical, biochemical, and echocardiographic data from 38 oHCM patients treated with mavacamten at the University Hospital Zurich. LA strain was assessed at baseline, 6 months and last available follow-up. Results Over a median follow-up of 56 ± 21.7 weeks, mavacamten led to reductions in resting LVOT gradient by 81.3% (from 50.0 ± 33.3 to 9.3 ± 6.2 mmHg) and Valsalva LVOT gradient by 76.7% (from 89.0 ± 38.0 to 20.7 ± 16.2 mmHg), respectively (both p&lt;0.001). LA volume index decreased by 21.2% (from 47.6 ± 12.9 to 37.5 ± 11.7 ml/m2, p&lt;0.001). Diastolic function and atrioventricular coupling improved, including decreases in average E/e′ (-31%, p&lt;0.001), left atrioventricular coupling index (-14%, p=0.023) and LA stiffness index (-20%, p=0.002). In contrast, LA strain values did not improve in the overall cohort. However, patients with baseline left atrial reservoir strain (LARS) below median demonstrated increases in LARS from 15.3 ± 3.5% to 18.2 ± 6.3%, LA pump strain (LAPS) from 6.1 ± 3.4% to 6.6 ± 5.7%, and LA conduit strain (LACS) from 9.1 ± 3.6% to 11.6 ± 4.0%. Conversely, patients with baseline LARS above median exhibited reductions in all LA strain components with significant between-group differences (LARS p=0.006; LAPS p=0.033; LACS p=0.009). Conclusion LA mechanical adaptation to mavacamten therapy in oHCM follows heterogeneous trajectories determined by baseline atrial function. Higher baseline LA strain likely reflects an adaptive state to high LV filling pressure that regresses after LV unloading, whereas lower baseline LA strain identifies advanced atrial dysfunction with partial recovery.
title: Heterogeneous left atrial strain trajectories during mavacamten therapy in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation induces local vascular injury and inflammation, and drug elution may reach surrounding perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT). PVAT inflammation is linked to atherosclerotic activity and can be assessed non-invasively on coronary CT angiography (CCTA) using the fat attenuation index (FAI) and PVAT volume, but the longitudinal impact of DES on peri-stent PVAT remodelling remains unclear. Purpose To assess 1-year changes in peri-stent PVAT FAI and volume after DES implantation, explore distance-to-stent gradients, evaluate drug-related differences, and contextualize peri-stent findings using non-target lesion (NTL) perivascular fat attenuation on serial CCTA. Methods Single-centre retrospective cohort (2015-2022) of patients with baseline CCTA before DES implantation and 1-year follow-up CCTA. Peri-stent PVAT FAI (HU) and volume were quantified along the stent (in-stent) and an extended peri-stent segment (stent+/-5 mm), using two radial definitions: within one vessel diameter and within half a vessel diameter from the stent surface. Change in FAI was compared across DES drugs; multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, LDL and stent length. Lesion-specific perivascular fat attenuation around NTLs was quantified on baseline and follow-up CCTA as an internal comparator of background coronary inflammatory status. Results 576 patients (64.06+/-9.84 years; 72.05% male) had paired CCTA. Peri-stent FAI increased at 1 year for both in-stent and peri-stent segment PVAT across radial definitions (all P&lt;0.0001). The increase was larger closer to the stent: in-stent change in FAI +17.17 HU within half diameter versus +8.13 HU within one diameter; peri-stent segment change in FAI +15.66 versus +7.17 HU, consistent with a proximity-dependent peri-stent gradient. PVAT volume decreased in parallel (e.g., in-stent: 1812+/-1228 to 772+/-571 mm3 within one diameter; P&lt;0.0001). Change in FAI differed by eluted drug (in-stent, half-diameter median change [IQR]: everolimus 19.48 [11.81-27.93] HU, rapamycin 15.83 [7.35-24.98], zotarolimus 12.09 [2.79-21.38]; P&lt;0.0001). After adjustment, everolimus was associated with larger change in FAI (beta 6.46, 95% CI 3.81-9.11; P&lt;0.0001) and zotarolimus with smaller change in FAI (beta -6.11, 95% CI -9.14 to -3.08; P=0.0001). In contrast, NTL perivascular fat attenuation decreased over 1 year on serial CCTA (P&lt;0.0001). Conclusion(s) DES implantation was associated with peri-stent PVAT remodelling characterised by increased FAI and reduced PVAT volume at 1 year. The FAI response showed a spatial gradient and drug dependence, while background NTL perivascular fat attenuation moved in the opposite direction, supporting peri-stent FAI as a marker of a local stent-tissue inflammatory signature rather than a global coronary inflammatory trend.
title: Drug- and distance-dependent peri-stent perivascular adipose tissue changes after implantation of drug-eluting stents

abstract: Abstract Background Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) has traditionally been viewed as a monogenic disease. Increasing evidence, however, suggests that gene-elusive HCM constitutes a distinct subgroup. A clearer understanding of its natural history is essential to support tailored management strategies. Purpose To characterise clinical and epidemiological profile of patients with gene-elusive HCM. Methods Over 10 years, 842 patients with HCM underwent genetic testing according to established referral criteria. Of these, 637 with longitudinal follow-up were included in the Natural History of HCM registry (NatHCM). The present analysis focuses on patients with negative genetic test (HCMG-). Results A total of 322 HCM patients from 302 families were included. Mean age at first assessment was 53.5 ± 13.1 years (IQR 44.5–62). Mean duration of follow-up (FU) from diagnosis to last assessment was 8.1 ± 5.9 years. Overall, 236 patients (73.3%) were men, while women were older at first assessment (58.1 ± 14.4 vs 51.8 ± 12.2 years). Ethnicity was recorded as Caucasian in 151 patients (46.9%), Asian in 69 (21.4%), Black in 59 (18.3%), and other ethnic backgrounds in 43 (13.3%). The most common reason for referral was presence of symptoms (62.4%). At diagnosis, 68% of patients had at least one cardiovascular risk factor (CRF): hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes mellitus, or obesity (BMI&gt;30). By the end of follow-up, 82% of the cohort had at least one CRF, and 52.4% had two or more. During follow-up, 61 patients (19.6%) experienced at least one cardiovascular event, with a median time to first event of 5 years. Symptomatic arrhythmias were the most frequent first event (34.4%), predominantly fast atrial fibrillation (14/21). Cerebrovascular accidents (CVA) accounted for 17 patients (27.9%), heart failure for 10 (16.4%), and acute coronary syndromes for 9 (14.8%). Cardiovascular events prior to first appointment were documented in 48 patients (15%). Patients with cardiovascular events were older (57.1 ± 13.3 vs 52.6 ± 12.9 years) and had a higher prevalence of CRFs, particularly hypertension (28.0% vs 7.2%; p&lt;0.001). They demonstrated a more advanced structural phenotype, with greater maximal wall thickness on CMR (20.3 ± 3.3 vs 17.2 ± 3.5 mm; p=0.001) and larger left atrial diameter (43.2 ± 6.5 vs 41.2 ± 5.9 mm; p=0.024). Interestingly, no events occurred among patients without cardiovascular risk factors (0/43). 26 patients died during follow-up (8%), of whom 30% (8/26) had a cardiovascular cause of death. Conclusions Gene-elusive HCM is associated with a substantial risk of adverse events, driven primarily by cardiovascular risk-factor burden. Patients without risk factors had no events, whereas those with multiple risk factors developed mainly CVA, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure. These findings indicate that standard treatment thresholds may be insufficient, and more intensive risk-factor management is warranted in HCMG-.Cardiovascular risk factor progressionFirst cardiovascular event during FU
title: Risk factor burden drives adverse outcomes in gene-negative hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

abstract: Abstract Background The prognostic significance of plaque burden (PB) derived from coronary CTA is increasingly recognized, yet the incremental value of serial PB monitoring remains unclear. We evaluated the association between baseline PB and its long-term trends with MACCE in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). Methods In a cohort of patients undergoing sequential CCTA evaluations (N=1,212), patients were stratified based on their initial examination results using the optimal plaque burden cut-off point (PB ≥ 15%). Among patients who underwent two sequential CCTA scans (N=1,204), PB status was divided into four groups: persistent low PB, low PB → high PB, high PB → low PB, and persistent high PB. The primary endpoint was MACCE, including unstable angina, myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, and cardiac death. Results Patients with PB ≥ 15% at initial coronary CT angiography demonstrated a significantly higher cumulative incidence of MACCE compared to those with PB &lt; 15% (log-rank test P &lt; 0.001). Compared with the persistently low PB group, the persistently high PB group had the highest risk of MACCE (aHR 3.4, 95% CI 2.13–5.29, P&lt;0.001); The risk of MACCE also increased in the group transitioning from low to high PB (aHR 2.9, 95% CI 1.37–6.10, P=0.01); while the group transitioning from high-risk to low-risk PB (aHR 1.9, 95% CI 0.97–3.47, P=0.06) showed residual risk that was not statistically significant. Conclusions A plaque burden ≥15% can independently identify MACCE in CAD patients. Persistently high PB levels or PB progression can further guide long-term risk stratification. Dynamic monitoring of PB provides more clinically meaningful prognostic information.Plaque Burden
title: Prognostic implications of serial coronary CTA–derived plaque burden in patients with coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a), is a genetically mediated lipid particle independently associated with the development of premature coronary artery disease and ischaemic events. Prior studies have shown that elevated levels promote inflammation and increase plaque volume and vulnerability over long-term follow-up. Here, we examined the short-term impact of Lp(a) on residual atheroma in survivors of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Methods This multicentre, prospective study recruited individuals with an ACS who had undergone invasive coronary angiography and then had their residual atheroma imaged by serial photon-counting coronary computed tomography angiography (PC-CCTA) within 30 days, and 12 months later. Paired scans were analysed by semi-automated software to quantify plaque burden, volume and composition at a per-patient level. Lp(a) was analysed at 12 months using an immunoturbidimetric assay, with a threshold of 125 nmol/L used to define elevated levels. Results 82 participants were included (median age: 61.9 years; female: 22%; STEMI: 50%, NSTEMI: 41%, unstable angina: 9%). Participants received usual clinician-directed care during follow-up, with 96% on statins and median LDL-C reducing from 2.9 mmol/L (112 mg/dL) to 1.4 mmol/L (54 mg/dL). 18% had elevated Lp(a). There were no significant differences between low and high Lp(a) groups for other risk factors, medication use or level of risk factor control over the study duration. Although they also had comparable baseline measurements for plaque volume, burden and composition, high Lp(a) was associated with greater progression of total plaque (TP) volume (34.5 vs 5.0 mm3, P=0.020) and burden (5.9 vs 0.1%, P=0.005), and noncalcified plaque (NCP) volume (28.9 vs -3.8 mm3, P=0.030) and burden (4.9 vs -1.2%, P=0.007) over 12 months. In contrast, changes in calcified plaque (CP) and low-density noncalcified plaque (LD-NCP) were similar between the two groups. Using a threshold of 2% change for total plaque burden to define meaningful plaque progression, 73% of patients with high Lp(a) met progressor status, compared to 34% in those without raised Lp(a) (P=0.01). Conclusion Raised Lp(a) levels &gt;125 nmol/L are present in almost 20% of people presenting with an ACS and associate with at least five-fold greater progression of total and noncalcified plaque over the first year of usual clinician-directed treatment.
title: Raised lipoprotein(a) associates with rapidly progressive coronary atherosclerosis after acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Abstract Dynamic computed tomography perfusion (DynCTP) provides functional information complementary to coronary CT angiography (CCTA), enabling combined anatomical and functional non-invasive assessment of coronary artery disease (CAD). However, standardized cut-off values for grading the extent of perfusion defects and their clinical implications remain poorly defined. Purpose To evaluate clinically relevant cut-off values for grading myocardial perfusion defect extent on DynCTP in symptomatic patients with suspected CAD or prior chronic coronary syndrome (CCS). Methods Prospective single-center observational study including consecutive unselected patients (April 2021–June 2025) who underwent CCTA and DynCTP when CCTA showed CAD-RADS ≥3 or non-diagnostic coronary segments. Perfusion defect extent was quantified using a 16-segment myocardial model: no defect (0 segments), mild-to-moderate (1–4 segments; 1–25%), and extensive (≥5 segments; &gt;25%). Cardiovascular outcomes (CV-MACE) during follow-up included coronary revascularization (percutaneous or surgical), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and cardiovascular death. Results 210 patients were included (mean follow-up 2.2 ± 1.2 years), and we excluded cases with missing perfusion quantification. 203 patients were analyzed and 133 (65.5%) had positive CTP. Mean age was 68 ± 10 years and 82% were male. Hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes were present in 75%, 73%, and 30%, respectively. Half had prior CCS; and pretest CAD probability in those without CCS was 29 ± 13%. Baseline CCTA showed mean CAD-RADS of 3.9 ± 1.1, segment involvement score (SIS) of 8.3 ± 3.1, and segment stenosis score (SSS) of 9 ± 5.6. There was a stepwise increase across perfusion extent categories in coronary revascularization (4,2%, 26,7%, and 63,9% for 0, 1–4, and ≥5 segments, respectively; p&lt;0.001) and ACS (1,4%, 3,3%, and 11,1%; p=0,026). Two cardiovascular deaths occurred, only in patients with ≥5 segments (Table 1). Event-free survival differed significantly among groups (p&lt;0.01) (Figure 1). In multivariable Cox models adjusted for clinical risk factors and CCTA anatomical burden (CAD-RADS stenosis and SIS) perfusion extent remained an independent predictor of CV-MACE. Compared with patients with no hypoperfused segments, adjusted hazard ratios were 5.85 (95%CI 1.64–20.85;p=0.006) for 1–4 segments and 24.90 (95% CI 7.37–84.13;p&lt;0.001) for ≥5 segments. Adding perfusion extent to clinical and anatomical model provided an incremental improvement in model fit (likelihood ratio χ²=62,19,p&lt;0,001). Conclusions In this cohort, Dynamic CTP perfusion defect extent was an independent and incremental predictor of downstream invasive management and CV-MACE beyond clinical and CCTA anatomical variables. A threshold of ≥5 hypoperfused segments identified a high-risk group with increased likelihood of revascularization and ACS. Given the low number of cardiovascular deaths, prognostic value for hard outcomes should be confirmed.MACE in perfusion defect extension categoriesKaplan-Meier survival analysis
title: Prognostic impact of the extent of myocardial perfusion defect assessed by dynamic computed tomography perfusion

abstract: Abstract Background Patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) have a relatively high prevalence prevalence of Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR), yet optimal screening strategies have not been clearly established. Purpose To develop and validate an easily utilized risk score for predicting ATTR in patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI. Methods In the prospective multicentre GRECA-TAVI registry, 500 patients with severe AS scheduled for TAVI were screened for ATTR using technetium-99m–labelled DPD or PYP bone scintigraphy across 12 tertiary hospitals in Greece and Cyprus, between January 1 and December 31, 2024. Systematic collection of clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic data was performed. An integer-based risk score derived from logistic regression was developed in a training cohort (n=350) and subsequently validated in a validation cohort (n=150). Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results ATTR was diagnosed in 38 patients (7.7%). Older age, male sex, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), greater maximal wall thickness (MWT), higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, and increased rates of intracardiac device implantation were more frequent among ATTR-CM patients. Five variables (age, sex, MWT, LVEF, and intracardiac device presence) formed the basis of an 8-point risk score. The score demonstrated good discrimination (AUC=0.75 in the training cohort and 0.76 in the validation cohort; Figure 1A). At a score ≥4, the model identified 8 of 11 ATTR-CM cases in the validation cohort, while flagging 46 patients in total, achieving a sensitivity of 72.7% and a negative predictive value of 97.1% (Figure 1B). Using this threshold, ATTR-CM prevalence was approximately 16% among patients with a score ≥4, compared with 2.4% in those with a score &lt;4. This cutoff captured 73% of ATTR-CM cases while limiting screening to 36% of the overall cohort (Figure 1C). Decision curve analysis demonstrated net clinical benefit across clinically relevant thresholds (5–20%) compared with both a guideline-recommended approach (MWT ≥12 mm) and a screen-all strategy (Figure 1D). Conclusions A simple bedside score derived from routinely available clinical variables can identify patients with severe AS at increased risk of ATTR-CM. Targeted screening based on this tool may improve diagnostic yield while optimizing resource utilization.Figure
title: Targeted screening for transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in severe aortic stenosis: development and validation of a clinical risk score

abstract: Abstract Background Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) frequently coexists with severe aortic stenosis (AS). In this setting, non-contrast cardiac computed tomography (CCT) may reveal a relatively low aortic valve calcium (AVC) burden despite hemodynamically severe AS, potentially reflecting a mixed calcific and non-calcific (including amyloid) valvular substrate. Purpose To evaluate whether low AVC identifies a higher probability of concomitant ATTR-CM and should be considered an imaging red flag in older patients with severe AS. Methods This subanalysis of the prospective, multicenter CAUSATIVE study1 included consecutive patients aged ≥65 years with symptomatic severe degenerative AS (aortic valve area &lt;1.0 cm²), indication for aortic valve replacement, and ≥1 clinical/echocardiographic red flag for amyloidosis. All patients underwent standardized CCT AVC quantification and a systematic diagnostic work-up for ATTR-CM. Patients were stratified by sex-specific tertiles of indexed AVC (Agatston units, AU). Multivariable logistic regression tested the association between indexed AVC and ATTR-CM, with the odds ratio calculated for a 1000-unit change in indexed Agatston units, adjusting for age, sex, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and low-flow low-gradient (LFLG) AS phenotype. Results Among 504 patients, 104 (20.6%) were diagnosed with ATTR-CM. ATTR-CM prevalence decreased across increasing AVC tertiles both in men (38.5%, 33%, and 15.2%; p-trend = 0.001) and women (18.8%, 9.2%, and 4.3%; p-trend = 0.009). In multivariable analysis, indexed AVC was independently and inversely associated with ATTR-CM (odds ratio 0.49 per 1000 AU/m²; 95% CI 0.32–0.73; p=0.001). Adjusted predicted probability curves demonstrated a marked increase in ATTR-CM probability at lower indexed AVC values, particularly in men (Figure 1). Using guideline-referenced CT-AVC likelihood strata, ATTR-CM prevalence was highest in the “unlikely severe” stratum (37.3%; NNT 2.68) and lowest in the “very likely severe” stratum (14.0%; NNT 7.12) (Table 1). Conclusion In older patients with severe AS undergoing aortic valve replacement evaluation, a low aortic valve calcium score is independently associated with concomitant ATTR-CM and should be considered an imaging red flag prompting dedicated amyloidosis assessment. Reliance on calcium score thresholds alone may underestimate the likelihood of severe AS in patients with dual pathology.Figure 1.Table 1.
title: Low aortic valve calcium score as an imaging red flag for concomitant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in severe aortic stenosis: A CAUSATIVE study subanalysis

abstract: Abstract Background Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) exhibits heterogeneous clinical presentations and outcomes. Based on triggering factors, TTS can be classified into primary and secondary forms; however, differences in clinical characteristics and short-term outcomes between these two entities remain incompletely understood. Purpose To compare clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes between patients with primary and secondary TTS. Methods Patients with TTS enrolled in the JapanTAK registry between 2010 and 2021 were retrospectively analyzed. TTS was classified as primary when triggered by emotional stress, physical activities, or no obvious stress, and as secondary when triggered by medical illness, trauma, or injuries. Clinical characteristics and in-hospital events (ventricular arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and in-hospital death) were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with cardiogenic shock. Results A total of 447 patients were included, of whom 238 (53.2%) were classified as secondary TTS. Acute neurological disease and acute infectious disease were the most common triggers of secondary TTS (Figure). Compared with primary TTS, patients with secondary TTS were younger (73.5 ± 11.4 vs. 70.9 ± 13.3 years, p=0.026), less frequently female (88.0% vs. 76.1%, p=0.001), and less likely to present with chest pain (60.8% vs. 12.2%, p&lt;0.001). Primary TTS patients had higher prevalence of hypertension (57.9% vs. 47.5%, p=0.029), dyslipidemia (41.6% vs. 24.4%, p&lt;0.001), and cardiovascular disease (21.5% vs. 14.3%, p=0.048). Secondary TTS patients more frequently had pulmonary disease (11.0% vs. 18.1%, p=0.045), cerebrovascular disease (13.9% vs. 22.7%, p=0.020), and cancer (18.2% vs. 26.5%, p=0.041). Secondary TTS was associated with lower LVEF at diagnosis (45.0 [39.4–55.9] vs. 40.0 [35.0–50.0] %, p&lt;0.001), higher BNP levels (228.5 [65.4–504.0] vs. 378.4 [130.4–973.2] pg/mL, p&lt;0.001), higher CRP levels (0.11 [0.05–0.43] vs. 1.66 [0.32–6.00] mg/dL, p&lt;0.001), and higher white blood cell counts (7,800 [6,400–10,180] vs. 11,250 [7,575–14,800] /μL, p&lt;0.001). There was no significant difference in ventricular arrhythmias (2.4% vs. 6.3%, p=0.065); however, cardiogenic shock (5.3% vs. 18.5%, p&lt;0.001) and in-hospital death (2.4% vs. 11.8%, p&lt;0.001) occurred more frequently in secondary TTS. On multivariable analysis, secondary TTS (odds ratio [OR] 2.8, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.3–6.0, p=0.0084) and lower LVEF (OR 0.97 per 1% increase, 95% CI 0.95–0.99, p=0.012) were independently associated with cardiogenic shock. Conclusions Secondary TTS is associated with significantly worse short-term outcomes, including cardiogenic shock and in-hospital mortality, and represents an independent risk factor for cardiogenic shock. Distinguishing between primary and secondary TTS may be clinically important for early risk stratification and management.figure
title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of primary vs. secondary takotsubo syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) predominantly affects elderly women, with men accounting for approximately 10% of cases in Western registries. Male patients are often reported to present with more severe physical stressors and worse outcomes. While large European registries such as InterTAK have described sex-related differences, comprehensive data in East Asian populations remain limited. Purpose To investigate sex differences in clinical characteristics, in-hospital events, and long-term outcomes in an East Asian TTS cohort. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 447 consecutive patients diagnosed with TTS either at admission or during hospitalization for other conditions. Clinical characteristics, triggers, comorbidities, cardiovascular events (including lethal arrhythmias and cardiogenic shock), in-hospital mortality, and long-term survival were compared between male and female patients. Results Among 447 patients, 82 (22.5%) were male. Mean age was comparable between sexes (74 years in both groups, p=0.83). Males had significantly higher smoking rates (48.6% vs. 16.2%, p&lt;0.001) and lower prevalence of emotional triggers (4.9% vs. 16.7%, p=0.005). Comorbidities were more common in men, including cancer (36.5% vs. 19.5%, p=0.001) and cardiovascular disease (26.8% vs. 15.6%, p=0.024). In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in men (37.8% vs. 19.5%, p=0.001). The incidence of lethal ventricular arrhythmias and cardiogenic shock was also higher in men. Long-term survival was significantly worse in male patients (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.24–0.57, log-rank p&lt;0.001). Conclusions In this East Asian cohort, men accounted for a higher proportion of TTS cases than previously reported in Western registries and exhibited significantly worse short- and long-term outcomes. These findings underscore important sex-related differences in TTS presentation and prognosis in East Asian populations.Fifigure1figure2
title: Sex differences in clinical characteristics and outcomes of Takotsubo syndrome in an east asian population

abstract: Abstract Purpose Cardiac diffusion tensor imaging (cDTI) is a novel technique which allows the non-invasive estimation of the magnitude and direction of water diffusion within the myocardium. Although cDTI is currently a research tool, it is a rapidly emerging technique that allows in vivo assessment of the microstructure of the myocardium without the need for contrast agents. This technique allows us to infer the orientations of cardiomyocytes and sheetlets from the anisotropic diffusion of water molecules within the myocardium. Microstructural changes in the myocardium can be quantified by mean diffusivity (MD), fractional anisotropy (FA), secondary eigenvector angle (E2A) and helix angle gradient (HAg). MD is a measure of the magnitude of diffusion of water molecules and FA is a measure of the preference of diffusion towards a particular direction. E2A is a marker of sheetlet orientation through units of myocytes and HAg describes the angle or twist of the myocytes as they wrap around the heart. Recent studies have demonstrated the ability of cDTI to detect abnormalities in cardiac disease such as acute myocardial injury, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy(1). As cDTI is approaching the transition from a research method to a diagnostic clinical tool, it needs to be integrated into routine clinical protocols, which routinely includes the administration of gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA). To date, studies using cDTI have mostly been performed without prior GBCA administration and it is unknown whether an acquisition following the administration of contrast affects cDTI measurements. Determining the effects of GBCA on cDTI read-outs will be helpful to streamlining clinical protocols and enhance clinical applicability of the method. Aim To investigate the effect of GBCA administration on cDTI markers MD, FA, E2A and HAg. Methods In this single centre study, 17 healthy adult subjects (mean age 60 years, range 24-73 years, M:F= 10:7) underwent free breathing, motion compensated (M2) single shot spin echo (SE) cDTI on a Siemens Prisma 3T scanner as reported previously(2). Each subject underwent pre-GBCA cDTI imaging. Once completed, 0.15ml/kg GBCA was routinely administered through a cannula. A timer was set and exactly 20 mins later, post-GBCA cDTI imaging was performed with scanning parameters copied from the first cDTI imaging. Results Baseline patient characteristics and CMR metrics are given in Table 1 and are within normal ranges as established by the SCMR cDTI consensus document. There were no significant differences between any of the cDTI metrics pre-GBCA and post-GBCA; MD (p=0.970), FA (p=0.162), E2A (p=0.113) and HAg (p=0.171) (Table 2). Conclusion cDTI measurements are not significantly affected by the administration of GBCA contrast agents. This allows for more flexible inclusion of cDTI into clinical protocols, and therefore facilitate the transition of cDTI scanning to clinical practice.Demographics and CMR VariablescDTI pre-GBCA and post-GBCA metrics
title: The effects of a gadolinium-based contrast agent on cardiac diffusion tensor imaging

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Right anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (R-AAOCA) is a rare congenital anomaly potentially associated with adverse events. The growing use of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) in adult patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) has led to increased detection of AAOCA and a noninvasive tool to predict cardiovascular outcomes in AAOCA is needed. Purpose To assess the prognostic value of CCTA-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) in an adult population with R-AAOCA. Methods In this study, consecutive patients with R-AAOCA from two registries were included between 06/1999 and 06/2025. All participants underwent CT-FFR analysis using cFFR software alongside additional CCTA-based quantification of CAD and anatomical features. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were defined as death of all cause, (survived) sudden cardiac death, myocardial infarction and urgent/non-urgent revascularization of the proximal anomalous course. AAOCA-related revascularization at baseline was censored and excluded from the outcome analysis. Follow-up assessments were conducted through telephone interviews and clinical reports. Results A total of 180 patients (28% female; mean age 55±13 years) were included in the final analysis. Of these, 38 patients (21%) underwent AAOCA-related revascularization. After a median follow-up of 33 months (IQR 9-54months), 16 patients (9%, thereof 63% with previous AAOCA-related revascularization) experienced a first MACE, including 8 deaths (1 cardiovascular death, 3 non-cardiovascular deaths and 4 unknown), 1 myocardial infarction, and 7 non-urgent revascularizations. CT-FFR emerged as a significant predictor (odds ratio (OR) 0.011, 95%-CI 0.000-0.257, p=0.005), but this association lost significance after adjusting for CAD within the anomalous vessel (OR 0.046; p=0.072). OR for presence of CAD within the anomalous vessel was 4.508 (95%-CI 1.547-13.136, p=0.006). Length of the intramural course was the only anatomical feature, which could independently predict MACE (OR 1.110, 95%-CI 1.006-1.224, p=0.038). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a significant difference in event-free survival based on the length of the intramural course and the presence of CAD in the anomalous vessel, but not for CT-FFR. Conclusions In adult patients with R-AAOCA, length of the intramural course and CAD in the anomalous vessel, but not CT-FFR, was predictive of adverse outcomes, highlighting the value of the anatomical high-risk feature intramural course as well as the prognostic relevance of atherosclerosis in this population.Kaplan-Meier estimates of MACE
title: Predictive value of CT-FFR in right anomalous aortic origin of coronary artery in an adult population

abstract: Abstract Background The MuSCAT protocol established a pathway for risk stratification and treatment of patients with an anomalous coronary artery from the opposite sinus of Valsalva (AAOCA) (1). It demonstrated a high degree of discrepancy between non-invasive and invasive functional testing, altering the management for 20% of adults with high-risk AAOCA anatomy (2). Data on clinical outcomes of this risk stratification driven management strategy is lacking. Methods Consecutive AAOCA patients aged ≥16 years from five cardiology centers in the Netherlands who underwent non-invasive and invasive functional stress testing as part of the MuSCAT study and completed the two-year follow-up were included for analysis. Invasive assessment comprised of fractional flow reserve (FFR), instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR) or resting full-cycle ratio (RFR); and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) to assess the dynamic compression in rest and under pharmacological stress. The outcome measures were survival, adverse cardiac events (re-intervention, myocardial infarction, arrythmia) and the evolution of symptoms at follow-up. Results A total of 69 patients with two-year follow-up were analysed. The median age at AAOCA diagnosis was 52 years [43–59], and 52% were female. 91% of the patients had AAORCA, the systolic left ventricular function was preserved in 87% of patients. Cardiovascular risk factors were common - hypertension (44%), hypercholesterolemia (29%), and (history of) tobacco use (38%). Thoracic symptoms were reported in 65% of patients: typical angina (22%), atypical angina (23%) and non-specific chest pain (17%). Coronary artery disease (CAD) was present in 25% of patients of which 56% had CAD in the AAOCA. Invasive functional testing was positive in 20% of patients and dynamic compression with IVUS was significant in 14.5%. Sixteen (23% of total cohort) patients underwent surgical correction (93.8% AAORCA and 6.3% AAOLCA). At two-year follow-up, no cardiac deaths occurred in either treatment groups, one operated patient required percutaneous treatment for ostial restenosis and no patients had a myocardial infarction in the effluence territory of the AAOCA. Thoracic symptoms improved in both surgically (81% to 31%) and conservatively (57% to 32%) managed patients; however, surgery was not independently associated with symptom relief (OR 0.5, p=0.4). Conclusions In this cohort, patients with AAOCA demonstrated favourable mid-term prognosis and overall symptom improvement following comprehensive diagnostic evaluation and tailored management. Surgical intervention was not associated with superior symptomatic outcomes, suggesting that operative treatment may be best reserved for patients with documented ischemia or high-risk anatomical features, rather than broadly applied to symptomatic individuals (3). These findings may inform clinical decision-making and patient counselling regarding expected mid-term outcomes.
title: Clinical outcomes of adults with anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery: 2-year data from the multicenter study on coronary anomalies in The Netherlands (MuSCAT)

abstract: Abstract Despite being a significant clinical marker in heart failure, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is not an important predictor of outcome in left ventricular assist device (LVAD) candidates. Based on the Hagen-Poiseuille law, PVR is also influenced by blood viscosity which is mostly determined by hematocrit (HCT); however, it is not taken into account in the clinical practice. Accordingly, we aimed to examine the changes and the prognostic role of HCT-adjusted PVR (aPVR) in a single center cohort of patients before LVAD implantation. Of the 101 LVAD implants, 96 patients prior to surgery (53±10 years old, 84% male) were enrolled. We collected clinical characteristics, preprocedural and early postoperative laboratory and right heart catheterization data. The aPVR was calculated using previous experimental data and PVR was adjusted to a reference HCT of 0.45. Our outcome was 365-day mortality, reached by 20 patients (21%). Adjustment to HCT resulted in a mean 35% relative change of aPVR compared to PVR, with more pronounced relative difference in patients with clinically relevant HCT-abnormality (62% change). Notably, adjustment resulted in frequent reclassification of pulmonary vascular disease severity compared to PVR (Figure 1). PVR was not a predictor of outcome, while aPVR was significantly associated with poor prognosis (HR: 1.183 [1.014-1.379], p=0.03). The prognostic value of aPVR remained significant even when other clinically and statistically significant predictors, such as RVAD support or the HM3 Survival Risk Score were added to the model. Corresponding blood viscosity should not be neglected in the assessment of PVR: aPVR significantly reclassifies the severity of pulmonary vascular disease in LVAD candidates, moreover, aPVR is an independent predictor of survival.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Viscosity-corrected pulmonary vascular resistance: a prognostic marker in left ventricular assist device candidates

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary artery calcifications (CAC) are frequently detected incidentally on chest CT performed for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE). Their prognostic relevance and potential role in refining PE risk stratification remain insufficiently explored. Purpose To assess the prognostic impact of visually graded CAC on CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) in patients with acute PE and to evaluate their contribution to reclassifying risk beyond the simplified PESI (sPESI) score and ESC 2019 guidelines. Methods This single center retrospective study included 475 consecutive patients diagnosed with PE by CTPA between 2016 and 2019. CAC were visually graded (0: none, 1: mild, 2: moderate, 3: severe). The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction (MI), coronary revascularization, stroke, hospitalization for heart failure, and major bleeding. Secondary outcomes included 1- short term outcome: PE related death and all death at 30 days, and 2- Five-year extended MACE including cardiovascular mortality, MI, coronary revascularization, ischemic stroke, peripheral arterial events, and hospitalization for heart failure Results CAC were observed in 70.3% of patients. Moderate-to-severe CAC (grades 2–3) or a history of ischemic heart disease (IHD) were associated with older age and higher comorbidities. Thirty-day all-cause mortality and PE-related death were significantly higher in patients with CAC 2–3 or IHD compared to those without (15.5% vs 6.0%, p=0.0013 and 8.8% vs 2.5%, p=0.0027, respectively). In multivariate Cox analysis adjusted for comorbidities, CAC 2–3 remained an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR=1.43 [1.07–1.91], p=0.015) and extended MACE (HR=3.22 [1.74–5.97], p&lt;0.001). Integrating CAC grading into the clinical risk model refined the risk stratification, reclassifying 22.2% of low- and intermediate-low–risk patients into higher risk categories. Conclusion Visual CAC assessment on routine CTPA is a simple, and independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes after PE. At no additional cost or radiation, integrating CAC assessment provides a valuable "safety net" to identify high-risk patients who are underestimated by clinical scores alone.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Refinement of risk stratification in patients with acute pulmonary embolism by visual assessment of coronary artery calcifications on thoracic computed tomography

abstract: Abstract Background Aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with progressive left ventricular (LV) remodeling and diastolic dysfunction (DD). While cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) enables assessment of myocardial structure, function and tissue characteristics, accurate assessment of DD has remained limited. Recently, CMR-derived mitral annular relaxation velocity (E´) has been introduced as a novel imaging parameter of longitudinal LV relaxation dynamics. However, its role in characterising DD in severe AS remains insufficiently studied. Purpose To characterise DD in patients with severe AS and preserved LV ejection fraction (EF) using CMR-derived E´ and to explore its relationship with left atrial (LA) function and atrio–ventricular functional coupling. Methods Patients with severe AS scheduled for transcatheter aortic valve replacement underwent pre-procedural CMR. CMR-derived E´ was calculated by measuring the distance from LV apex to mitral annulus in end-systole and end-diastole in long-axis views divided by the corresponding time interval, representing a surrogate marker of longitudinal mitral annular relaxation velocity (Figure 1). For exploratory diastolic characterisation, patients were grouped according to median splits of CMR E´ and LA reservoir strain (Es). An atrio-ventricular coupling index (AVCI) integrating E′ and LA Es using Z-Score normalisation was calculated to assess the relative contribution of atrial and ventricular functional components to overall diastolic impairment. Results A total of 95 patients were included (median age 80 [75-83] years; 44.3% women). CMR E´ correlated with markers of diastolic dysfunction, including NT-pro-BNP, LV mass index and LA-Es (all p&lt;0.05), independently of AS subtype. No significant correlations were observed with CMR-based tissue characteristics (late gadolinium enhancement [p=0.09]; extracellular volume fraction [p = 0.74]). Combined assessment of CMR E´ (median 2.88 cm/s) and LA Es (median 15.0%) classified four distinct patterns of atrio–ventricular functional interaction. While three suggest a continuum of progressive LV DD with secondary LA impairment (1: E´↑/LA Es↑; 2: E´↓/LA Es↑; 3: E´↓/ LA Es↓), a fourth group demonstrated disproportionately high LA dysfunction (4: E´↑/LA Es↓) despite preserved CMR E´. Although LA Es was similarly reduced in Groups 3 and 4, Group 4 exhibited significantly lower NT-proBNP, higher LV concentricity index and elevated AVCI compared with Group 3 (all p&lt;0.05). Conclusion CMR-derived E´ provides additional functional information on DD in patients with severe AS and preserved LVEF. Integration of CMR E´ with LA strain enables more refined characterisation of atrio–ventricular functional patterns and identifies a subgroup with disproportionate atrial dysfunction relative to longitudinal LV relaxation. This integrative approach may refine evaluation of DD and atrio-ventricular functional interplay in severe AS.Graphik 1Graphik 2
title: CMR-derived mitral annular relaxation velocity refines characterisation of diastolic functional phenotypes in patients with severe aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary artery aneurysms (PAA) are a potentially severe structural complication of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, data regarding their prevalence, risk factors, natural history and prognostic impact remain limited and mainly derive from small series. Purpose To assess the prevalence, predictors, progression, complications and prognostic impact of PAA in a large PAH cohort. Methods A retrospective observational study of 356 patients with PAH followed at a European reference centre with at least one computed tomography or cardiac magnetic resonance allowing measurement of the main pulmonary artery (MPA) diameter was conducted. PAA was defined as MPA diameter ≥40 mm. Patients were classified according to presence or absence of PAA at first imaging. Demographic, clinical characteristics, and haemodynamics were compared between groups. Multivariable regression analysis identified independent predictors of PAA. In patients with serial imaging (≥6 months apart), progression was defined as incident PAA or diameter growth of PAA from first imaging. PAA-related complications and time-to-event analyses for all-cause mortality and lung transplantation were performed. Results Mean age at PAH diagnosis was 45.9±15.8 years, 112 patients (31.5%) were male. Among the 356 patients, 145 (40.7%) had PAA at first imaging. Median time from PAH diagnosis to first imaging was 25 months (1–88), among the 145 patients with PAA, time to detection was 74 months (7–130.5). Patients with PAA had younger age, more frequently PAH associated with congenital heart disease or toxic rapeseed oil and less commonly with connective tissue or veno-occlusive disease, and worse haemodynamics (Table 1). In multivariable analysis, age at PAH diagnosis and congenital heart disease were independently associated with PAA, whereas connective tissue disease was protective (Table 2). Among 164 patients with serial imaging, PAA progression occurred in 62 (37.8%) during a median follow-up of 91.5 months (28.5–126). At final follow-up, 168 patients had PAA, of whom 25 (14.9%) developed PAA-related complications: 4 (2.4%) dissection, 12 (7.1%) thrombosis, and 11 (6.6%) left main coronary artery compression requiring stenting. During follow-up, 132 patients (37.1%) died and 47 (13.2%) underwent lung transplantation. Median time to death or lung transplantation was not significantly different in patients with versus without PAA (Log-rank p = 0.87). Conclusion In a large quaternary PAH cohort, PAA were frequent and development independently associated with age at diagnosis and disease aetiology. Aneurysm progression was common during follow-up. Although PAA were not associated with increased mortality or lung transplantation, they were linked to severe complications. Further prospective studies are needed to better define clinical and prognostic implications of PAA and to establish optimal surveillance and management strategies.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
