title: Pulmonary artery aneurysms in pulmonary arterial hypertension: prevalence, predictors, progression and clinical impact

abstract: Abstract Background Untreated pulmonary embolism (PE) with right heart failure (RHF) is associated with high mortality. The appropriate treatment for these patients is still a matter of debate. Methods The German InEK data collection system anonymously records all cases and DRG and OPS codes of patients who are hospitalized for PE and their treatment strategies, allowing mortality rates to be analyzed. We therefore analyzed all patients with PE and RHF (I26.0) who also exhibited symptoms of shock (R57.0, .8, .9). Results Of all 63361 patient cases between January 2022 and September 2025, a total of 13,78% died. Patients who went into shock (4104) died at a rate of 57,56%. Of these patient cases, 1829 received systemic lysis (SL, 8-020.8), with an average mortality rate of 55,48 %. 463 patients underwent invasive thrombus aspiration (TA, 8-838.n0), with an average mortality rate of 44,08 %, and a few patients (129) underwent ultrasound-guided regional lysis (URL, 8-83b.j), with a mortality rate of 36,66 %. It should be noted that TA, which was still associated with a 63,89% mortality rate in 2022, has fallen steadily to 35,22 % by 2025. Conclusion Patients with PE combined with shock have a high mortality rate. Classic SL therapy can hardly improve this mortality rate. In contrast, interventional procedures for TA or URL lead to a nearly halving of the mortality rate.Impatient Mortality in PE and shockFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Patients with pulmonary embolism and cardiogenic shock benefit from interventional therapy rather than conventional thrombolytic therapy. A case analysis of all inpatients in Germany 2022 and 2025

abstract: Abstract Background Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USAT) may enhance right ventricular recovery in intermediate–high-risk pulmonary embolism, but evidence is limited. We compared the safety, efficacy, and net benefit of USAT versus standard anticoagulation. Methods We analyzed a propensity-matched prospective cohort of 432 intermediate-high-risk patients (216 USAT vs 216 anticoagulation) from the Italian USAT-HI and OPTIRAPE registries. Outcomes included all- cause, cardiovascular (CV) and PE-related mortality, major bleedings, and a composite net clinical benefit (NCB), with a day-7 landmark analysis distinguishing early (0–7 days) from late (8–30 days) events. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan–Meier estimates and Cox regression with Hazard ratios (HRs) and relative 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Baseline demographics (mean age 64 ± 12 years; 48% female) and comorbidities were balanced between cohorts. USAT was associated with lower all-cause (7.4% vs 13.9%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28–0.85; p=0.01), cardiovascular (3.2% vs 8.3%; HR 0.39; p&lt;0.001), and PE-related mortality (2.3% vs 6.5%; HR 0.34; p=0.02) compared with anticoagulation. Major bleeding was similar (2.7% vs 1.9%; p=0.56). USAT significantly improved net clinical benefit (13.4% vs 25.9%; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30–0.75; p=0.001), mainly driven by reductions in early mortality and clinical deterioration. Landmark analysis indicated that benefits were largely confined to the first 7 days, with favourable but non-significant effects during days 8–30. Conclusions In intermediate–high-risk PE, USAT appears to confer an early survival benefit, improved net clinical outcomes, and a safety profile comparable to standard anticoagulation, supporting its role in rapid right ventricular recovery and early clinical stabilization.Kaplan-meiers curveFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised registry comparison open to residual confounding and selection of patients for catheter therapy.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched registry comparison of ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis with anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, with lower early mortality in the USAT group.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality 7.4% vs 13.9% (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28-0.85); major bleeding 2.7% vs 1.9% (p=0.56); net clinical benefit 13.4% vs 25.9% (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Mortality benefit from catheter-directed therapy in intermediate-high-risk PE remains unproven by randomised data, so a hard-endpoint signal is relevant to ongoing trials.

title: Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis versus anticoagulation alone in intermediate–high risk pulmonary embolism

abstract: Abstract Background Intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism (IHRPE) is associated with worse outcomes. The place of catheter-directed therapy (CDT) is growing but data remains sparse to identify the best patient profile1–7. Purpose To evaluate the efficacy and safety of CDT in routine clinical practice and to identify predictors of a favorable clinical response. Methods Consecutive IHRPE patients defined according to ESC guidelines8 (elevated cardiac biomarkers associated with right ventricular involvement and initial hemodynamic stability) were included between January 2023 to January 2025 from two French university hospitals. Patients were divided into two groups based on the therapy they received, a conventional group (anticoagulation therapy alone) and a CDT group (anticoagulation therapy combined with one of the two percutaneous pulmonary reperfusion techniques available, either the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy system FlowTriever™ or the ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis system EKOS™ Endovascular System). All patients were followed during hospitalization using clinical, imaging and biological variables. The primary endpoint was the achievement of a “favorable therapy response” defined as oxygen therapy weaning, halving of cardiac biomarkers (troponin and/or Nt-ProBNP) and lactate clearance. Results Among the 126 patients included, 75 patients were assigned to the CDT group and 51 to the conventional one. Those in the CDT group appeared to be more severely affected based on baseline clinical, biological and imaging findings. Procedural success was achieved in 96% of patients of the CDT group. With respect to the primary endpoint, 22 patients (76%) in the conventional group, versus 35 (73%) in the CDT group met the criteria for a “favorable therapy response” with no significant difference (p = 0.775, OR 1.17 [0.41 – 3.31]). However, a ≥50% reduction in NT-proBNP occurred more frequently in the CDT group (81% vs 56%, HR 3.44, 95% CI 1.23–9.58; p = 0.015). Normalization of right ventricular function was also more frequent in the CDT group, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (80% vs 56%, p = 0.19). Nevertheless, there was no significant difference in oxygen weaning or time to oxygen weaning, in the reduction of RV diameter, reduction of the RV/LV ratio or MILLER II CT obstruction score9. Regarding safety outcomes, clinically relevant bleeding (BARC10 ≥ 2) was significantly more frequent in the CDT group (24% vs 10% (p = 0.043)), mainly driven by puncture-site hematoma (50%) and blood transfusions (22%). The mortality rate was particularly low with an overall mortality of 5%. Conclusion With a high technical success rate and safe procedure, CDT demonstrated an advantage in halving Nt-proBNP compared to anticoagulation therapy alone at the cost of a higher risk of clinically relevant bleeding. Further data are awaited to try to confirm this effect on hard clinical outcomes.Central illustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Catheter-directed therapy in intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism: which predictive factors for a favorable therapy response?

abstract: Abstract Background Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is an established catheter-based treatment for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Since the safety of refined BPA techniques was reported in 2012, BPA has rapidly disseminated nationwide in Japan, with increasing adoption by centers with less experience. Although BPA is known to involve a learning curve, objective criteria defining institutional expertise based on cumulative procedural experience remain undefined. Purpose This study aimed to clarify institutional expertise in BPA based on cumulative procedural experience. Methods Using the Japanese Cardiovascular Disease All-Case Registry (2012–2022), we retrospectively analyzed 14,468 BPA procedures performed in 3,708 patients. Complications were defined as a composite of the following major adverse events within 30 days after the procedure: death, initiation of mechanical ventilation (including noninvasive positive pressure ventilation), initiation of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, initiation of continuous hemodiafiltration, transfusion, cardiac tamponade, or surgery. Cumulative procedural experience for each procedure was defined as its chronological order number among BPA procedures performed at the same center. Cumulative procedural experience was categorized into tertiles (1–73, 74–324, ≥324 procedures) and evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Nonlinear learning-curve effects were assessed using restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling. A secondary analysis was performed among incident centers that initiated BPA in 2013 or later. Results Complication rates decreased stepwise with increasing cumulative procedural experience (low-experience 9.4%, intermediate-experience 5.4%, high-experience 2.6%; trend P &lt; 0.001). This reduction was primarily driven by a lower incidence of mechanical ventilation, while transfusion also declined with increasing experience (trend P &lt; 0.001 and P = 0.049, respectively). In multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and procedural year, the high-experience group had significantly lower complication risk than the low-experience group (adjusted odds ratio 0.331, 95% CI 0.205–0.535). RCS analysis demonstrated a marked reduction in adjusted complication rate, with an elbow point at approximately 52 cumulative procedures, followed by a plateau around 264 procedures. Among incident centers (9,265 procedures), the elbow point was less distinct, whereas adjusted complication rate stabilized at low levels beyond approximately 250 cumulative procedures, consistent with findings in the overall cohort. Conclusions A cumulative procedural experience threshold of approximately 250 procedures may serve as a practical institutional benchmark for achieving low complication rates with BPA.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Cumulative institutional experience and the learning curve of balloon pulmonary angioplasty for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension

abstract: Abstract Background Catheter-directed reperfusion therapies are increasingly used in patients with intermediate- to high-risk acute pulmonary embolism (PE). However, comparative data between ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) and catheter-directed mechanical thrombectomy (MT) remain limited. Methods This retrospective cohort study compared periprocedural efficacy and safety outcomes between CDT and MT in patients with acute PE. The primary efficacy endpoint was change in right ventricular to left ventricular (RV/LV) ratio from baseline to post-procedure. Secondary endpoints included 90-day all-cause mortality, hemoglobin decline, major bleeding (BARC severe bleeding) and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH). Results Eighty-three patients were included (CDT: n=41; MT: n=42). Baseline characteristics were broadly comparable between groups. Both strategies achieved significant within-group reductions in RV/LV ratio from baseline to post-procedure. In the CDT group, RV/LV ratio decreased from 1.47 ± 0.34 to 0.94 ± 0.27, while in the MT group it decreased from 1.46 ± 0.44 to 0.91 ± 0.27. There were no significant between-group differences in baseline RV/LV, post-procedure RV/LV, absolute RV/LV reduction, relative RV/LV reduction, or the proportion of patients achieving a normalized post-procedural RV/LV ratio (≤0.9). 90-day all-cause mortality was similar between CDT and MT (17.0% vs. 9.5%, P=0.50). Hemoglobin decline was numerically greater with CDT than with MT (2.56 ± 2.18 vs. 1.77 ± 1.62 g/dL), and major bleeding occurred more frequently in the CDT group (20.0% vs. 7.1%), although neither difference reached statistical significance (P=0.07 and P=0.20, respectively). No ICH occurred in the MT group, whereas two ICH events (4.9%) were observed in the CDT group. Conclusions In patients with acute PE, CDT demonstrated efficacy in improving RV/LV ratio comparable to MT but was associated with a non-significant trend toward higher rates of severe bleeding. These findings suggest that both modalities are viable catheter-directed options, and choice of strategy may be guided by institutional expertise and individual patient characteristics.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Periprocedural efficacy and safety comparison between ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis and catheter-directed mechanical thrombectomy for acute pulmonary embolism

abstract: Abstract Background Pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension carries a poor prognosis. Reversed Potts shunt has been proposed as a bridge from medical therapy to lung transplantation, yet evidence supporting its ability to preserve right ventricular function and improve symptoms in this population remains limited. Method Pediatric patients diagnosed with pulmonary artery hypertension (WHO Group I) and underwent the reversed Potts shunt procedure at Fuwai Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. The study thoroughly summarized the baseline, operative, and outcome characteristics of these patients. All-cause mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included echo-evaluated right ventricular function, pulmonary artery pressure, 6-minute walk distance (age over eight), and plasma NT-pro BNP levels. Sensitivity group of patients underwent elective reversed Potts and isolated Potts were beforehand extorted. Results A total of seven pediatric patients classified as intermediate–high or high risk by the ESC simplified risk stratification were included; six underwent elective reversed Potts shunt and one underwent salvage reversed Potts shunt. Two patients had concomitant mitral valve disease and underwent simultaneous mitral valve intervention (repair or mechanical replacement). Most procedures were performed via left thoracotomy, except for two cases via median sternotomy due to concomitant mitral valve surgery. Shunt diameter (median 7.0 mm, IQR 6.5–7.5) was selected according to the descending aortic diameter at the diaphragmatic level (median 12.1 mm, IQR 11.18–12.88). The salvage case, performed after prior mitral valve repair with concomitant valved homograft right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction, resulted in in-hospital mortality. Among the remaining patients, postoperative recovery was uneventful; one late death occurred due to recurrent pulmonary crisis. No consistent improvement was observed in echocardiographic right ventricular function or pulmonary artery pressure. Nevertheless, during a median follow-up of 9.9 months, our data suggested reductions in NT-pro BNP and increases in 6-minute walk distance. Conclusion Our prior study suggest that the reversed Potts shunt may not halt progression of pulmonary arterial hypertension and right heart declination, but may provide symptomatic improvement in selected patients, warranting confirmation in larger cohorts.Figure_flowchart_and_outcomeFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure_change_of_outcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Early outcomes of reversed potts shunt in pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension

abstract: Abstract Background Catheter-based reperfusion strategies, including ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USAT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT), are increasingly used in intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE), yet comparative real-world data remain limited. We compared short-outcomes, echocardiographic recovery, and mortality between USAT and MT. Methods We analysed 286 patients with acute intermediate–high risk PE enrolled in the multicentre USAT IH-PE registry (March 2018–October 2025). Patients underwent USAT (EKOS™, Boston Scientific) or MT (FlowTriever, Inari Medical; Indigo, Penumbra) during index hospitalisation. Primary endpoints were 30-day all-cause, cardiovascular, and PE-related mortality. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced baseline characteristics. Kaplan–Meier analyses with log-rank testing assessed time-to-event outcomes. In-hospital bleeding was classified by BARC criteria. Changes in right ventricular (RV) function and pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) were evaluated. Results After matching (69 patients per group), baseline clinical and hemodynamic variables were well balanced. Both USAT and MT significantly improved RV/LV ratio, tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, and PASP (all p&lt;0.001). Thirty-day all-cause mortality was similar between USAT and MT (13.0% vs. 11.5%; p=0.78), with no differences in cardiovascular or PE-related mortality. Survival curves did not differ at 30 days. Major bleeding was infrequent and observed only in the USAT group (4.3%, p=0.16). Conclusion In this real-world multicentre cohort, USAT and MT showed comparable short-term mortality, safety, and echocardiographic recovery, supporting individualized catheter-based reperfusion strategies for intermediate–high risk PE.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comparative outcomes of ultrasound-assisted thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy in intermediate–high-risk pulmonary embolism

abstract: Abstract Background High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) is characterized by hemodynamic instability, and early mortality remains high under current guidelines that recommend first-line systemic thrombolysis (ST). Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) might improve outcomes of high-risk PE, but comparative data are scarce. Purpose In this combined analysis of two studies that enrolled patients with high-risk PE, the results of LBMT and ST are evaluated in a population that was medically and anatomically eligible to receive either thrombectomy or a lytic-based treatment. Methods The analysis included subjects with high-risk PE from the FLAME study (NCT04795167) and the FLASH study (NCT03761173), including both the US and European cohorts. These prospective, observational studies defined high-risk PE according to European Society of Cardiology guidelines. In this analysis, subjects eligible for LBMT are defined as those with central and/or lobar PE, and subjects eligible for ST are defined as those with no absolute or relative contraindication to lytic agents. In extremis indicates cardiopulmonary resuscitation on arrival for FLASH subjects and SCAI SHOCK Stage E for FLAME subjects. Results In a cohort of 257 high-risk PE subjects, 181 were eligible for both ST and LBMT. Of these, 136 (75.1%) subjects received primary LBMT, and 33 (18.2%) received primary ST. The primary treatment groups demonstrated similar baseline characteristics: The LBMT group was a mean age of 61.0±13.6 years and 50.7% female, and the ST group was a mean age of 59.1±14.4 years and 60.6% female. Body mass index was 33.7±8.2 kg/m2 and 34.6±9.0 kg/m2 in the LBMT and ST groups, respectively. Also, baseline vitals and imaging evidence were clinically similar: heart rates at presentation were 104.9±21.1 bpm (LBMT) and 108.5±28.8 bpm (ST), lowest systolic blood pressures, including subjects on vasopressors, were 100.3±25.7 mmHg (LBMT) and 93.8±32.1 mmHg (ST), and right ventricle/left ventricle ratios were 1.7±0.5 (LBMT) and 1.6±0.5 (ST). After reperfusion therapy, the in-hospital mortality rate was 2.2% (n=3) in the LBMT group and 27.3% (n=9) in the ST group. Comparing LBMT with ST, LBMT was associated with numerically lower rates of major bleeding (6.7% [n=9] vs. 24.2% [n=8]), clinical deterioration (5.9% [n=8] vs. 12.1% [n=4]), and bailout or adjunctive therapy use (3.7% [n=5] vs. 27.3% [n=9]). When excluding the 15 FLASH subjects and 14 FLAME subjects in extremis at baseline, the outcomes remained similar (Figure). Conclusions In this pooled high-risk PE cohort, favorable clinical trends were observed among patients who received LBMT as an alternative to ST. The observed data point toward the potential utility of LBMT as a primary intervention in patients with high-risk PE who can be safely transitioned to the interventional setting.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of the FLAME (NCT04795167) and FLASH (NCT03761173) prospective observational studies; 257 high-risk PE subjects, 181 eligible for both treatments (136 LBMT, 33 ST).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised, industry-linked registries with small ST group, no adjusted estimate and likely selection bias.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of two prospective observational studies of high-risk PE comparing large-bore thrombectomy with systemic thrombolysis in patients eligible for both.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In-hospital mortality was 2.2% (n=3) in the LBMT group and 27.3% (n=9) in the ST group; major bleeding 6.7% vs 24.2%. The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: High-risk PE has high mortality under first-line thrombolysis, and the large mortality difference supports the need for randomised comparison.

title: High-risk pe patients eligible for both large-bore mechanical thrombectomy and systemic thrombolysis: insights from the FLASH and FLAME Studies

abstract: Abstract Background Despite successful reperfusion, early heart failure (HF) remains frequent after STEMI. We assessed whether a multidimensional cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) evaluation at discharge identifies patients at risk for 6-month HF-related events in a real-world cohort. Methods Consecutive STEMI patients undergoing discharge CMR were analyzed. The 6-month composite endpoint included HF hospitalization, HF-related emergency visit, NYHA class ≥ II, or LVEF &lt;50% at follow-up. CMR parameters reflected complementary pathophysiological domains: infarct size (structural injury), global radial strain (mechanical dysfunction), and left atrial biplane ejection fraction (atrial functional reserve). Hierarchical logistic modeling and bootstrap validation were performed. Results Among 115 patients with complete CMR and follow-up data, 21 (18%) experienced the composite HF endpoint at 6 months. In univariable analysis, larger infarct size, lower global radial strain (GRS), and reduced left atrial ejection fraction (LAEF) were all associated with increased HF risk. In the final multivariable model, infarct size remained independently associated with HF events (OR 1.08 per 1% increase; p=0.008), corresponding to an 8% increase in odds per 1% increment. Higher global radial strain was independently protective (OR 0.88 per 1% increase; p=0.023), translating into a 12% reduction in odds per 1% increment. Although left atrial ejection fraction was associated with HF risk in univariable analysis, it did not retain independent significance after adjustment (OR 0.95 per 1% increase; p=0.082), suggesting partial overlap with ventricular injury and mechanical impairment. Hierarchical modeling demonstrated incremental discrimination with the sequential addition of atrial functional reserve and radial mechanics beyond infarct size. The multivariable model showed good explanatory power (Nagelkerke R² = 0.405) and favorable discrimination (AUC 0.862). Conclusions Early post-STEMI HF is not driven by infarct size alone. Structural injury, impaired radial mechanics, and reduced atrial functional reserve represent complementary determinants of early structural–functional HF progression. Patients combining larger infarcts, impaired radial contraction, and reduced atrial functional reserve represent a high-risk phenotype for early heart failure progression after STEMI. Multidimensional discharge CMR may refine post-infarction risk stratification in routine clinical practice.TablesGraphical Abstract
title: Multidimensional CMR profiling at discharge predicts early heart failure–related events after STEMI

abstract: Abstract Background Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) is an established catheter-directed therapy for acute pulmonary embolism (PE). The relationship between aspirated thrombus weight and volume with hemodynamic and echocardiographic outcomes remains unclear. Methods Patients undergoing LBMT for PE using the FlowTriever system between 2021 and 2024 were included. Thrombus weight and volume were quantified, and clot composition was assessed histopathologically. Associations between thrombus characteristics and clinical, invasive hemodynamics, echocardiographic parameters, and biomarkers were evaluated immediately after the procedure, at hospital discharge, and at 3 months follow-up. Results Thrombus material was available in 48 patients (31% women), of which 41 presented with intermediate-risk and 7 with high-risk PE. LBMT resulted in significant reductions in systolic pulmonary artery pressures (sPAP) intraprocedurally (-12.8±8.3 mmHg, p&lt;0.001), with a further invasively measured decrease through 3 months (-9.6±10.6 mmHg, p&lt;0.001). From baseline to discharge, right ventricular coupling improved (+0.24 (IQR 0-0.6), p&lt;0.001), right ventricle (RV)/left ventricle (LV) ratio decreased (-0.28±0.2, p&lt;0.001), driven by a reduction in RV end-diastolic diameter (-8±6.6 mm, p&lt;0.001). NT-proBNP and troponin T declined significantly. Neither thrombus weight nor volume correlated with acute changes in sPAP (rvolume=0.06; rweight=0.10), RV-uncoupling (rvolume=0.47; rweight=0.46), and RV/LV ratio (rvolume=-0.08; rweight=-0.10) (p for all &gt;0.05), nor with outcomes at 3 months. Conclusions Apirated thrombus weight and volume were not associated with hemodynamic or echocardiographic improvements after LBMT, suggesting that, beyond mechanical obstruction, additional mechanisms potentially including paracrine and endocrine effects of thrombus material may contribute to acute and chronic PE-related cardiopulmonary dysfunction. title: Thrombus weight and volume alone do not predict drop in pulmonary artery pressure after large bore mechanical thrombectomy

abstract: Abstract Background Syncope is a severe symptom of acute pulmonary embolism (PE) and is associated with a higher prevalence of hemodynamic instability and increased short-term mortality. The STRIKE-PE study is evaluating safety and effectiveness of computer assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) for the treatment of PE. Purpose This subanalysis of 595 patients from STRIKE-PE compares outcomes of acute PE patients with vs without syncope at presentation. Methods STRIKE-PE is a prospective, international, multicentre study that will enrol up to 1500 patients with acute PE symptoms of ≤14 days and a right-to-left ventricular (RV/LV) ratio of ≥0.9. Patients with (n = 141) vs without (n = 454) syncope at presentation were compared. Results At baseline, the syncope group had higher percentages of patients who were Black (33.7% vs 23.6%, P = .049) and had elevated thrombus burden (modified Miller score ≥12; 91.5% vs 81.7%, P = .006), elevated biomarker (99.3% vs 91.9%, P = .002), and high-risk PE (12.1% vs 6.8%, P = .046). No significant between-group differences were detected for baseline RV/LV ratio (1.42 vs 1.35), thrombectomy time (32 vs 30 min), procedure time (61 vs 61 min), and functional outcomes (Figure 1) and quality of life (QOL; Figure 2) at baseline. The RV/LV ratio improved from baseline to 48 hours postprocedure (primary effectiveness endpoint) for both groups (P &lt; .001); improvement was significantly greater for patients with syncope (−0.47 vs −0.37, P = .004). The RV/LV ratio at 48 hours was similar for both groups (0.95 vs 0.98). No significant difference was observed between the groups for rate of composite major adverse events within 48 hours (primary safety endpoint; 0.7% vs 2.2%). For patients with and without syncope, Borg dyspnoea scale, 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance, and all QOL measures improved out to 90 days (P ≤ .014 for within-group changes over time), with similar magnitudes of improvement over time for each group (Figures 1, 2). Median Borg dyspnoea scale at rest improved by −4.0 vs −4.5 from baseline to discharge and by −4.3 vs −5.0 from baseline to 90 days. Median Borg dyspnoea scale after 6MWT improved by 0.0 vs −1.0 from discharge to 90 days. Mean 6MWT distance improved by +135.9 vs +116.9 metres from discharge to 90 days. From baseline to 90 days, mean EQ visual analog scale improved by +25.0 vs +26.8, mean EQ-5D-5L index value improved by +0.283 vs +0.340, and mean total PEmb-QoL score improved by −19.7 vs −22.8. The NYHA classification distribution was similar between the groups at discharge and 90 days. Conclusion In this STRIKE-PE subanalysis, CAVT improved RV/LV ratio comparably in patients with and without syncope. Clinical and functional outcomes and QOL were similar between groups, and syncope did not affect procedural time or safety. These data demonstrate that intermediate-risk and high-risk patients with syncope can be treated safely and effectively.Figure 1.Functional outcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2.Quality of lifeFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: STRIKE-PE: Impact of syncope on functional outcomes and quality of life to 90 days for acute pulmonary embolism patients treated with computer assisted vacuum thrombectomy

abstract: Abstract Background Catheter-based thrombectomy (CBT) is increasingly used for intermediate–high and high-risk acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but most evidence derives from industry-sponsored trials conducted in selected centres. Purpose To evaluate the clinical characteristics and short-term outcomes of patients treated with large-bore CBT in a multicentre real-world cohort. Methods The Spanish Registry of Catheter Intervention in Pulmonary Embolism prospectively enrols consecutive patients undergoing catheter-based treatment for acute PE across 22 centres (overall registry population n=1002). For this analysis, patients treated with large-bore (≥24 French) thrombectomy devices were selected. The primary outcome was a 7-day composite of recurrent PE, in-hospital resuscitation, or death. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital adverse events. Results A total of 221 patients were analysed. In-hospital PE occurred in 14%, prior PE in 9.5%, and active or recent cancer in 20%. Overall, 32.1% were classified as high risk and 67.9% as intermediate–high risk, with additional markers of clinical severity shown in Figure 1A. The mean shock index was 1.06 ± 0.41 (Figure 1B), mean PESI 123 ± 41.3, and mean lactate 3.29 ± 3.76 mmol/L. Moderate-to-severe right ventricular dysfunction was present in 63%, and bilateral main pulmonary artery involvement in 79%. A formal reperfusion indication was present in 62% of cases; 13% were treated as rescue after failed fibrinolysis and 25% electively according to local protocols or PE response team decisions. Lysis-free mechanical thrombectomy was performed in 91%. In centres reporting paired haemodynamic data (n=177), mean pulmonary artery pressure decreased significantly after the procedure (−7.4 ± 6.2 mmHg; p&lt;0.001) (Figure 1C). Technical success was achieved in 94%. The 7-day composite outcome occurred in 9.9% of patients (Figure 1D); seven-day mortality was 7.0%, recurrent PE 0.9%, and in-hospital cardiac arrest 5.4%. Major bleeding occurred in 10%, respiratory failure in 15%, renal failure in 11%, and infection in 15%. Conclusions In this multicentre real-world cohort, large-bore CBT was associated with significant immediate haemodynamic improvement and high procedural success. The 7-day composite outcome occurred in 9.9%, driven mainly by a 7.0% mortality rate. Early adverse events were more frequent than those reported in industry-sponsored trials, likely reflecting greater clinical severity and broader real-world inclusion criteria.Figure 1.Central IllustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Real-world outcomes of large-bore catheter-based thrombectomy in intermediate-high and high-risk pulmonary embolism

abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate the prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature tracking-derived left ventricular global longitudinal strain (FT-LVGLS) for adverse outcomes in patients with chronic moderate to severe aortic regurgitation (AR), and to further assess its incremental prognostic value beyond the 2025 ESC/EACTS Class I/IIb surgical decision indications among a prespecified subgroup of patients with no or minimal symptoms (NYHA functional class I–II) who were potential candidates for aortic valve replacement. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 707 patients (mean age 54.5 ± 13.5 years; 593 male) with at least moderate chronic AR who underwent CMR between 2010 and 2024. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as all-cause mortality, heart transplantation, rehospitalization for heart failure, or ICD discharge. Results During a median follow-up of 52.6 months, 152 patients experienced MACE. Multivariable Cox regression identified FT-LVGLS as an independent predictor of MACE (adjusted HR: 1.148 per 1% increase, P &lt; .001). Among patients with NYHA class I-II, incorporating FT-LVGLS into models based on each ESC/EACTS Class I/IIb surgical indication significantly improved model discrimination, with higher C-index (from 0.739-0.747 to 0.775) and likelihood ratio χ² values (from 34.00-39.18 to 46.65-47.66). Kaplan-Meier survival curves demonstrated that a cutoff of -12% for FT-LVGLS further refined risk stratification. Conclusion FT-LVGLS independently predicted adverse outcomes in patients with chronic moderate-to-severe AR, providing incremental prognostic value beyond ESC/EACTS surgical indicators and improving risk identification.Graphical Abstract
title: Left ventricular global longitudinal strain improves risk assessment in chronic aortic regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial fibrosis is a key determinant of adverse outcomes in patients with severe aortic stenosis (1); however, its reliable noninvasive detection remains challenging. Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)–derived myocardial strain and tissue characterization parameters for identifying severe myocardial fibrosis using histology as the reference standard. Methods Thirty-one patients with severe aortic stenosis meeting guideline criteria for surgical valve replacement were prospectively enrolled. All patients underwent comprehensive CMR, including feature-tracking–derived global longitudinal (GLS), circumferential (GCS), and radial strain, native T1 mapping, and extracellular volume (ECV) quantification. During surgery, deep needle biopsies were obtained from the basal interventricular septum. Diffuse myocardial fibrosis (Hx-FIB) was quantified on Picrosirius Red–stained sections as collagen volume fraction using digital image analysis. Results Mean age was 64 ± 10 years; 25% of patients were female. Mean transvalvular gradient was 57 ± 19 mmHg, and aortic valve area was 0.80 ± 0.24 cm². Mean GLS was 10 ± 4%, GCS 18 ± 8%, native T1 1007 ± 43 ms, ECV 28.3 ± 6.1%, and Hx-FIB 19.6 ± 5.2% (Table 1). Seven patients (23%) exhibited extensive fibrosis (Hx-FIB &gt; 30%). Heart-rate–adjusted GLS and GCS, as well as left ventricular mass, showed moderate correlations with Hx-FIB (r &gt; 0.43). Native T1 and ECV were also significantly correlated with Hx-FIB (r = 0.38 and r = 0.31, respectively). Combinations of GLS with ECV or native T1 demonstrated good diagnostic performance (AUC 0.851 and 0.839, respectively; both P &lt; 0.001), with sensitivities of 86% and 100% and specificities of 75% and 62% using cutoff values of ≤11% for GLS, &gt;30% for ECV, and &gt;1009 ms for native T1. (Fig 1) Similarly, combinations of GCS (cutoff ≤17%) with ECV or native T1 showed strong diagnostic performance for detecting Hx-FIB &gt; 30% (AUC 0.821 and 0.881, respectively; both P &lt; 0.01), with sensitivities of 86% and 100% and specificities of 75% and 79%.(Fig 1) Conclusions Combined CMR-derived myocardial strain and tissue characterization parameters enable accurate noninvasive identification of histologically confirmed severe myocardial fibrosis in patients with aortic stenosis.Figure 1Table 1
title: Advanced cardiac magnetic resonance techniques for the detection of severe myocardial fibrosis in severe aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Introduction Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common valvular disease and one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality. Progressive valvular narrowing results in chronic pressure overload, compensatory left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), and structural remodelling. Irreversible myocardial injury may develop before overt systolic dysfunction or adverse remodelling becomes evident. In this study, we use cardiac diffusion tensor imaging (cDTI) to investigate the relationship between segmental myocardial fibrosis and microstructural alterations in patients with AS. Purpose To explore whether segmental DTI parameters differ between late gadolinium enhancement positive (LGE+) and LGE-negative (LGE-) myocardium in the AS cohort. Methods Twenty-one patients with moderate/ severe AS underwent 3T CMR, including cine images, free-breathing spin-echo DTI (3 slices, 18 diffusion directions at b-values 100s/mm2, 200s/mm2, and 500s/mm2 using second-order motion-compensated (M2) gradients, resolution of 2.20*2.27*8mm3), tissue mapping pre- and post-contrast, and LGE. Segmental analysis was performed in the basal and mid-ventricular slices using the AHA model. LGE was quantified using a≥5 standard deviation threshold above the remote myocardium. DTI metrics included mean diffusivity (MD) (a measure of the freedom of water diffusion in the myocardium; increase in interstitial fibrosis), fractional anisotropy (FA) (a measure of directionality of water molecules; decrease in cardiomyocyte disorganisation), and secondary eigenvector angle (E2A) (a marker of sheetlet orientation). DTI parameters were compared between LGE+ and LGE- segments. Segmental native T1 and extracellular volume (ECV) were also assessed. Results LGE was present in 15 of 21 patients (71%). After exclusion of apical and artefact-affected segments, 169 segments were included, of which 43 (25%) were LGE +, and 126 (75%) were LGE-. LGE+ segments demonstrated significantly higher MD compared with LGE- segments (1.60±0.11 vs 1.56±0.09, p=0.017). FA was significantly lower in LGE+ compared with LGE- segments (0.29±0.05 vs 0.31±0.04, p=0.0139). There was no significant difference in E2A between the two groups (53±13 vs 52±14, p=0.721). Segmental native T1 and ECV did not differ significantly among them (T1: 1343±60 vs 1336±62 ms, p=0.506; ECV median 26% vs 26%, p=0.113). Within LGE+ segments, ECV correlated with segmental native T1 (r = 0.5152, p = 0.0008). Conclusions cDTI differentiates fibrotic from non-fibrotic segments even when native T1 and ECV were not significantly different at the segmental level. LGE+ segments demonstrate higher diffusivity and lower anisotropy, consistent with microstructural disorganisation in fibrotic myocardium in aortic stenosis. cDTI may provide complementary microstructural information beyond conventional tissue characterisation in pressure-overload remodelling. Larger studies are warranted to confirm clinical utility.Table 1.Demographic, CMR parametersFig 1.MD, FA, E2A in LGE+ and LGE- AS patients
title: Regional myocardial microstructural assessment in aortic stenosis by cardiac diffusion tensor imaging

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) effectively reduces mitral regurgitation (MR) and improves symptoms in patients at high surgical risk. However, the determinants of left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) after TEER and the role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) remain incompletely defined. Purpose identifying predictors of LVVR after mitral TEER1,2. Methods In this single-centre prospective study, 65 patients with degenerative MR who underwent TEER were evaluated with echocardiography and CMR before and six months after the procedure. LVRR was defined as a &gt;10% reduction in LV end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) on follow-up CMR. Changes in MR severity and LV volumes were quantified, and predictors of LVRR were identified through linear and logistic regression analyses. Results TEER induced a significant reduction in MR severity, with concordant decrease in regurgitant volume, regurgitant fraction, and LV volumes on both echocardiography and CMR. CMR LVEDV decreased by an average of 26 ± 39 mL, and 56.9% of patients exhibited significant LVRR. CMR-derived regurgitant volume and fraction correlated strongly with the magnitude of LVEDV reduction (r = 0.59 and r = 0.57, respectively; both p &lt; 0.001). In multivariable analysis, baseline MR regurgitant fraction (OR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.03–1.46, p = 0.003) and the reduction in MR regurgitant volume (OR = 1.31, 95% CI 1.05–1.63, p = 0.002) were independent predictors of LVRR. In figure 1 the scatter plot shows the relationship between LVRR (ΔLV EDV) assessed by CMR and MR RV assessed by CMR (on left panel) and Echo (middle panel). Both modalities demonstrate a positive association between MR severity and the degree of LV volume reduction, with stronger correlation observed for CMR-derived measurements. The shaded area represents the 95% CI of the regression line. The right panel illustrates a Bland–Altman plot comparing MR regurgitant volume derived from CMR and echocardiography. The mean bias was −20.25 mL, indicating that CMR tended to show lower MR volumes than echocardiography, with limits of agreement (LoA) from −61.66 to 21.16 mL. Conclusions Quantitative CMR assessment of MR provides robust markers of LVRR after TEER in degenerative MR. Both baseline MR severity and its reduction post-procedure showed independent association with structural recovery, emphasizing the role of CMR as a reference tool for procedural evaluation and patient selection.Figure 1.Scatter plot and Bland Altman.
title: Reverse cardiac remodeling after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for primary mitral regurgitation: a cardiac magnetic resonance study

abstract: Abstract Background Disproportionate left ventricular remodelling (DLVR) refers to excessive LV dilatation that cannot be explained by mitral regurgitation (MR) severity alone. While DLVR has been described in mitral valve prolapse (MVP) with mild-to-moderate MR, its significance in patients with severe MR remains unclear [1-3]. Purpose To characterise the structural phenotype of DLVR using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with preserved LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and isolated significant MR (grade 3+/4+) due to MVP who were referred for mitral valve repair (MVR). Methods In this prospective pilot study, 66 patients (20% female) undergoing preoperative CMR were analysed. LV volumes were derived from short-axis cine stacks and indexed to body surface area (BSA). MR regurgitant volume (RVol) was calculated as the difference between total LV stroke volume and aortic forward stroke volume. DLVR was defined as LV dilatation exceeding age- and sex-adjusted upper limits after correction for RVol: (LVEDV − RVol)/BSA − ULN(LVEDVi) &gt; 0. Results DLVR was present in 19 patients (29%). MR grade distribution did not differ between groups (p = 0.586). Compared with patients exhibiting proportional remodelling (n = 47), those with DLVR showed significantly greater LV dilatation across all linear and volumetric indices: LVDDi (36±4 vs 31±3 mm/m²), LVESDi (23±4 vs 18±3 mm/m²), LVEDVi (156±30 vs 115±14 mL/m²), and LVESVi (63±18 vs 41±8 mL/m²; all p &lt; 0.001). Eccentric hypertrophy was more prevalent in the DLVR group (95% vs 68%, p = 0.027). Biventricular and biatrial involvement was evident, with higher RVEDVi (94±17 vs 76±16 mL/m², p &lt; 0.001) and larger atrial dimensions (all p ≤ 0.016). Guideline-based surgical thresholds were more frequently met in the DLVR group (LVESD≥40 mm: 58% vs 15%; LVESDi≥20 mm/m²: 84% vs 21%; both p &lt; 0.001), consistent with a higher-risk phenotype. RVol was higher in DLVR (89±30 vs 70±18 mL, p = 0.002) and correlated strongly with LVEDV (r = 0.80, p &lt; 0.001). However, regurgitant fraction (RF) (52±9% vs 48±10%, p = 0.212) was comparable between groups. Multiple linear regression analysis showed that RVol and male sex were significant independent predictors of LVEDVi, whereas age, MVP subtype and EROA (PISA, TTE) were not. Despite preserved LVEF, patients with DLVR had lower LVEF (60±5% vs 64±4%, p &lt; 0.001). This finding, together with comparable systolic blood pressure and larger end-systolic dimensions, suggests reduced LV end-systolic elastance and possible intrinsic myocardial dysfunction. Conclusions Nearly one-third of patients with nonsyndromic MVP and significant MR exhibit DLVR. Although RF appropriately classifies MR severity, it does not adequately capture the extent of LV remodelling. RVol may better reflect the true haemodynamic burden. Whether DLVR represents an intrinsic cardiomyopathy or a time-dependent progression of MV disease warrants further investigation.
title: Disproportionate left ventricular remodelling in nonsyndromic mitral valve prolapse with significant mitral regurgitation: a CMR pilot study

abstract: Abstract Background Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease closely linked to metabolic disorders, yet it is often asymptomatic and underdiagnosed at early stages. The cholesterol–high-density lipoprotein–glucose (CHG) index integrates lipid and glucose metabolism and may capture residual cardiometabolic risk. However, evidence regarding its association with AAA is limited. Objective To investigate the association between the CHG index and the presence of AAA in a Chinese screening population. Methods From June 2019 to June 2021, 10,169 individuals underwent AAA screening at one cardiovascular center and two community sites in China. The CHG index was calculated as ln{[TC × FBG]/[2 × HDL-C]}. AAA was defined as a maximal abdominal aortic diameter ≥30 mm on ultrasound. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were applied to assess potential non-linear associations. Missing covariates were handled using multiple imputation. Prespecified subgroup analyses evaluated effect modification. Results A total of 9,603 participants were included in the final analysis; 213 (2.22%) had AAA. Participants with AAA had a higher CHG index than those without AAA (5.39 ± 0.41 vs 5.33 ± 0.46, P=0.018). In multivariable analyses, a higher CHG index was independently associated with greater odds of AAA. In RCS analysis, the overall association was significant (P-overall &lt;0.001), with no strong evidence of non-linearity (P-non-linear = 0.269). Subgroup analyses showed generally consistent associations across sex, smoking status, diabetes mellitus, statins, and antiplatelet drugs, while a significant interaction was observed for age (P for interaction = 0.004) and hypertension status (P for interaction = 0.022). Conclusion A higher CHG index is independently associated with the presence of AAA our study. This integrated metabolic marker may aid AAA risk stratification, and prospective studies are needed to confirm its predictive value.Table 1.Multivariable analysesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 1.RCS analysis and subgroup analysesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Association of the CHG index with prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm: a cross-sectional study in a chinese screening population

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are first-line devices for endovascular revascularization in peripheral arterial disease (PAD), improving patency and reducing reinterventions compared with plain balloon angioplasty. Evidence is largely based on paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), while data on sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) remain limited. Given the differences in pharmacologic mechanisms, coating technologies and safety profiles, this study compared short- and mid-term outcomes of SCBs versus PCBs in patients with PAD. Methods We retrospectively analyzed endovascular PAD interventions from the multicenter, prospective RECCORD registry using either SCBs or PCBs between 2022 and 2024. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to adjust for baseline differences between groups using demographic variables, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, lesion characteristics and procedural details. After matching, each cohort included 85 patients with standardized mean differences (SMD) &lt; 0.2 for all covariates. Primary endpoints were procedural complications and 12-month clinical outcomes, including major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major adverse limb events (MALE) and functional outcomes. Results A total of 1728 endovascular interventions with DCBs were performed between 2022 and 2024, including 108 interventions with SCBs and 1630 with PCBs. After propensity score matching, 85 patients remained in each group with well-balanced baseline characteristics. All matched interventions showed procedural success with comparable complication rates between the groups. In the follow-up, there were no statistically significant differences between SCBs and PCBs regarding MACE, MALE and functional outcomes. Conclusion In this propensity score matched analysis from the real-world RECCORD registry, the use of SCBs versus PCBs was associated with comparable procedural and one-year clinical outcomes regarding MACE, MALE and functional outcomes. The present findings suggest that both coating technologies offer similar safety and efficacy profiles in real-world practice. Larger, prospective studies with extended follow-up are needed to determine whether patient- or lesion-specific subgroups may benefit preferentially from one DCB type.
title: Sirolimus- vs. paclitaxel-coated balloons in peripheral arterial disease: a propensity score matched analysis from the real-world RECCORD registry

abstract: Abstract Background The physiological determinants of peripheral blood flow after endovascular therapy (EVT) for lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) remain incompletely understood. Below-knee (BK) runoff reflects distal inflow status, whereas vascular flow reserve (VFR) measured at the popliteal artery reflects microcirculatory function. However, the relationship between these parameters and post-EVT tissue perfusion assessed by skin perfusion pressure (SPP) remains unclear. Methods Fifty-seven consecutive patients who underwent EVT of the femoropopliteal artery were prospectively enrolled. Concomitant BK intervention was performed in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). BK runoff was evaluated, and VFR and fractional flow reserve (FFR) were measured in the popliteal artery immediately after EVT. Post-EVT SPP was assessed during hospitalization. Associations between clinical or physiological variables and low post-EVT SPP (&lt;40 mmHg), defined as impaired lower leg tissue perfusion, were evaluated using logistic regression analyses. Results Univariate analysis identified VFR (odds ratio [OR], 0.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.12–0.88; p=0.017), hemoglobin (OR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.26–0.90; p=0.019), absence of BK runoff (OR, 27.5; 95% CI, 4.5–245; p=0.0003), diabetes (p&lt;0.0001), and CLTI (OR, 7.5; 95% CI, 1.41–57.3; p=0.017) as associated with low post-EVT SPP. In multivariate analysis including BK runoff and VFR, absence of BK runoff was an independent predictor of low post-EVT SPP (OR 28.1, 95% CI 3.3–395; p=0.002), whereas VFR was not. Conclusions VFR was associated with impaired tissue perfusion after EVT; however, distal inflow status represented by BK runoff was the dominant determinant. These findings suggest that optimization of distal runoff may be essential to achieve adequate tissue perfusion after femoropopliteal EVT.
title: Impact of vascular flow reserve and below-knee runoff on tissue perfusion after lower extremity endovascular therapy

abstract: Abstract Introduction Stroke is a leading cause of disability with no restorative treatments beyond the acute phase. Secretome-based strategies offer an alternative to cell therapies (1), Betacellulin (BTC), a growth factor from the endothelial secretome, promotes neural stem cell activation, neurogenesis, and angiogenesis in preclinical settings (2). Its defined nature and paracrine action make it a strong candidate for regenerative therapy. Purpose To evaluate the therapeutic potential of betacellulin as a post-ischemic regenerative treatment in preclinical models of ischemic stroke. Methods Adult mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and received recombinant BTC via intranasal or using osmotic minipump for 5–7 days post-stroke (3,4). Outcomes included neural stem/progenitor cell activation, angiogenesis, infarct reduction, and behavioral testing. Mechanistic studies focused on BTC-induced ErbB1/ErbB4 receptor activation. Toxicity assessments included in vitro human cell studies and in vivo monitoring for adverse responses. This study has followed the "Principles of laboratory animal care". Results BTC significantly increased neurogenic markers (BrdU+, Sox2+) in neurogenic niches (SVZ, DG) and enhanced NeuN+ and Olig2+ populations in injured areas (3). Infarct size was reduced, and angiogenesis stimulated. Behavioral recovery was improved in locomotor and sensory-motor tests. Mechanistically, BTC activates ErbB receptors without disrupting niche integrity. Its effects are reproducible across delivery routes and sexes, with no observed toxicity. BTC stands out for its safety, scalability, and defined mechanism, addressing barriers in secretome translation (1). Conclusions BTC enhances neural repair and functional recovery post-stroke through safe, non-invasive administration. Acting via physiological pathways, BTC is highly suitable for translational development as a regenerative, secretome-derived therapy. BTC is the first defined secretome protein to safely restore neural function post-stroke through non-invasive delivery. BTC could redefine post-stroke therapy, prolonging treatment windows and validating secretome-based regenerative medicine.Graphical abstract of BTC therapy: overviewFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Betacellulin promotes post-ischemic brain repair in preclinical stroke models

abstract: Abstract Background Despite improvements in the safety of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), cerebrovascular events (CVE) remain a clinically significant concern. Purpose This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the incidence, associated predictors of CVE, and their impact on major clinical outcomes in patients following TAVI. Methods and results A comprehensive literature search of PubMed, Cochrane, and Embase databases was conducted to identify relevant studies reporting CVE up to 30 days post-procedure. The primary endpoint of the present meta-analysis was the incidence of periprocedural CVE after TAVI. Secondary endpoints included in-hospital, 30-day, and one-year mortality rates in patients who experienced early CVEs after TAVI. We also evaluated patient and procedure-related predictors of CVEs, including history of stroke, atrial fibrillation (AF), peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), type of valve (self-versus balloon-expandable valves), predilatation, transapical approach, and Valve-in-Valve technique. A meta-analysis with odds ratio (OR) and risk ratio (RR) was performed using random effects model, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Results A total of 143 studies encompassing 804,534 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled occurrence of CVE after TAVR was 2.6% (95% CI:2.4%-2.8%). CVE after TAVR were associated with &gt;3 times greater risk of in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR] 3.68, 95% CI: 3.16 - 4.30), &gt;5 times greater risk of 30-day mortality (OR 5.22, 95% CI: 4.25 - 6.41) and 3 times greater risk of 1year mortality (OR 2.99, 95% CI: 2.19 - 4.10). Meta-regression results indicated a significant reduction in stroke incidence based on study publication year (p=0.038). Significant predictors of CVE included prior stroke (RR: 1.61; 95%CI: 1.31 – 1.76), peripheral artery disease (PAD) (RR: 1.24; 95%CI: 1.11 – 1.61), chronic kidney disease (CKD) (RR: 1.27; 95%CI: 1.10 – 1.45), as well as procedural characteristics such as self-expandable valve implantation (RR: 1.63; 95%CI: 1.23 – 1.46). In contrast, no significant risk increase was observed in atrial fibrillation, pre-dilatation, transapical approach, or valve-in-valve procedures Conclusions Post-procedure CVE following TAVI remain a significant and potentially preventable source of patient mortality. These findings serve as an initial step toward guiding preventive strategies, such as the use of embolic protection devices in patients at higher risk.incidence of CVEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.mortality ratesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Periprocedural cerebrovascular events after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral embolic protection devices (CEPD) have been evaluated in multiple randomized trials during transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Methods A systematic literature search including PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane databases was conducted to identify randomized controlled studies (RCTs) comparing CEPDs in patients undergoing TAVI. A random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) was performed within a frequentist framework. The primary outcome was periprocedural stroke up to 30 days. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, disabling stroke, non-disabling stroke, volume and number of ischemic lesions, bleeding, vascular complications and acute kidney injury (AKI). Network diagrams were constructed for each outcome to depict direct comparisons among interventions in the included RCTs. Treatment ranking probabilities for the different CEPDs were estimated using P-scores, which reflect the relative performance of each intervention. Results A total of 9 RCT studies encompassing 23,072 patients (CEPD n=5,813, control n=5,638) were included in the NMA. No cerebral embolic protection device significantly reduced mortality, stroke, acute kidney injury, bleeding, or vascular complications compared with no-CEPD group, except ischemic cerebral lesions. Claret Montage dual filter system significantly reduced both total cerebral lesion volume (mean difference [MD] -370.40 [-500.48; -240.32]) and the number of lesions (MD -4.30, 95% CI -8.31; –0.29) versus no-CEPD group. According to p-scores, the Sentinel device ranked highest among all evaluated treatments for stroke-related outcomes, including overall stroke, disabling and non-disabling stroke, as well as for bleeding and vascular complications. However, Sentinel was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.69–1.12) or mortality (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.53–1.39). Conclusions CEPDs during TAVI were not associated with a significant reduction in periprocedural stroke. The relative efficacy of alternative devices remains uncertain due to the limited data. Future trials should focus on better risk stratification to identify TAVI patients with a higher baseline risk of stroke, as well as on the development of next-generation devices.figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Effect of cerebral embolic protection devices on TAVI outcomes: a network meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Factor XIa inhibitors represent a novel anticoagulant class targeting the intrinsic coagulation pathway, potentially offering stroke prevention with reduced bleeding risk compared to direct oral anticoagulants. Despite promising phase 2 data, comprehensive evaluation across diverse patient populations remains limited. Traditional aggregate meta-analyses cannot adequately address heterogeneity in patient characteristics and comparator regimens. Purpose We performed an individual patient data meta-analysis to evaluate efficacy and safety of Factor XIa inhibitors (milvexian, asundexian, abelacimab) for stroke prevention across multiple clinical settings, using reconstructed pseudo-IPD from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Our objective was to determine pooled treatment effects on ischemic stroke/systemic embolism and major bleeding while accounting for between-trial heterogeneity. Methods We reconstructed pseudo-IPD for 31,681 patients from four phase 2/3 trials (AXIOMATIC-SSP, PACIFIC-STROKE, AZALEA-TIMI 71, OCEANIC-AF) using the Guyot algorithm. Validation against published hazard ratios demonstrated 65% achieved good-to-excellent concordance (mean relative difference 18.4%). We conducted both one-stage (stratified Cox regression) and two-stage (random-effects pooling) IPD meta-analyses. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses excluded trials with poor validation quality. Comprehensive audit of 51 verification checks confirmed 94% pass rate, validating analysis integrity from raw data to final estimates. Results Among high-quality trials (n=8,653 patients, 613 events), Factor XIa inhibitors demonstrated significant 29% relative risk reduction in ischemic stroke/systemic embolism (pooled HR 0.71, 95%CI 0.56-0.90, p=0.005; I²=22.1%) with low heterogeneity. Major bleeding showed neutral effect (HR 1.03, 95%CI 0.67-1.57, p=0.902), though substantial heterogeneity reflected diverse comparators (placebo vs. rivaroxaban). One-stage and two-stage approaches demonstrated excellent agreement in validated trials. The stroke risk reduction translates to approximately 1.5% absolute risk reduction annually in high-risk populations (NNT=68). Conclusion Factor XIa inhibitors demonstrate clinically meaningful stroke prevention efficacy with potentially favorable bleeding profiles. The 29% relative risk reduction represents a significant advancement over standard anticoagulation. However, inter-trial heterogeneity driven by methodological quality differences underscores the critical need for rigorous data validation in reconstructed IPD meta-analyses. Future head-to-head trials comparing Factor XIa inhibitors directly to DOACs in adequately powered atrial fibrillation cohorts are warranted to definitively establish their clinical role.Forest plot showing two stage meta analysisFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Reconstruction summaryFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Efficacy and safety of factor XIa inhibitors for stroke prevention: a reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Introduction The optimal management of patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis remains controversial. Improvements in medical therapy, carotid artery stenting and carotid endarterectomy, call into question the preferred management o asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Whether adding revascularization to intensive medical treatment would provide greater benefit than intensive medical treatment alone is unclear. Purpose To compare the efficacy and safety of optimized medical therapy alone versus carotid revascularization plus intensive medical therapy in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs was performed across four databases. Trials comparing optimized medical therapy with revascularization, either percutaneous or surgical, in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis were included. Hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled for death, any stroke, ipsilateral stroke, ipsilateral ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack and myocardial infarction. Perioperative death or stroke was analyzed using risk ratios (RR). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method, with between-study variance estimated by the Sidik-Jonkman estimator. Heterogeneity was assessed using forest plot inspection and the I² statistic. Results Four randomized controlled trials were included. Revascularization was not associated with a significant reduction in death compared with optimized medical therapy alone (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.61-1.47; I² = 0%). Similarly, no significant reduction was observed for any stroke (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.67-1.19; I² = 0%). No statistically significant differences were found for ipsilateral ischemic stroke (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.19-3.30; I² = 70.7%) or overall ipsilateral stroke (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.37-2.86; I² = 38.6%). Transient ischemic attack was also not significantly reduced with revascularization (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.26-3.67; I² = 26.7%). In contrast, myocardial infarction occurred more frequently in the revascularization group (HR 2.26, 95% CI 1.46-3.50; I² = 0%), indicating a significantly increased risk associated with invasive treatment. Conclusion In patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis, revascularization combined with intensive medical therapy did not reduce death or stroke compared with optimized medical therapy in patients with asymptomatic high-grade carotid stenosis. These findings likely reflect advances in optimal medical treatment. Overall, these results suggest that optimized medical therapy represents a reasonable first-line strategy for these patients in the contemporary era.
title: Optimized medical therapy versus revascularization in high-grade asymptomatic carotid stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure is widely recommended to prevent recurrent cryptogenic stroke in patients with moderate-to-large shunts. However, a substantial proportion of patients have “uncrossable” PFOs in which guidewire passage fails, potentially leading to futile procedures or the need for transseptal puncture. Echocardiographic markers that reliably predict the technical feasibility of PFO closure have not been clearly defined. Methods We retrospectively evaluated patients with cryptogenic stroke or transient ischemic attack who underwent TEE and were referred for catheter-based PFO closure at a tertiary center between April 2010 and March 2022. Patients with concomitant atrial septal defect or transseptal puncture–assisted closure were excluded. Uncrossable PFO was defined as persistent failure of guidewire advancement through the PFO tunnel despite escalation to support sheaths. TEE parameters included shunt grade, PFO height, tunnel length, presence of bubbles at the PFO outlet during the Valsalva maneuver, resting shunt, atrial septal aneurysm or septal hypermobility, Eustachian valve or Chiari network, and the inferior vena cava–PFO (IVC–PFO) angle. Predictors of successful guidewire passage were identified using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. Results Among 240 patients undergoing attempted PFO closure, 90 (37.5%) had uncrossable PFOs. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, including shunt grade, were similar between groups. In contrast, uncrossable PFOs were characterized by smaller PFO height, longer tunnel length, narrower IVC–PFO angle, and markedly lower frequencies of resting shunt and presence of bubbles at the PFO outlet. In multivariable analysis, the presence of bubbles at the PFO outlet emerged as the strongest independent predictor of successful guidewire passage (adjusted OR 7.47), followed by PFO height ≥2 mm (adjusted OR 5.67), larger IVC–PFO angle (per 1° increase; adjusted OR 1.05), and resting shunt (adjusted OR 10.7). Shunt grade alone was not predictive. Sequential incorporation of these anatomical and functional markers resulted in progressive improvement in discrimination, with the highest predictive accuracy achieved when outlet-level bubble presence was included (AUC 0.845). Conclusions Approximately one-third of patients with cryptogenic stroke and moderate-to-large shunts had uncrossable PFOs despite similar shunt grades. TEE-derived functional and anatomical markers—particularly the presence of bubbles at the PFO outlet during the Valsalva maneuver, along with PFO height and IVC–PFO angle—were strongly associated with guidewire passage and substantially enhanced prediction beyond shunt grade alone. Incorporation of these parameters into pre-procedural assessment may refine patient selection, reduce futile closure attempts, and guide consideration of alternative medical therapy.
title: ﻿Anatomical and functional predictors of uncrossable PFO in patients with cryptogenic stroke

abstract: Abstract Background The safety and efficacy of transcatheter patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure for secondary prevention in patients with cryptogenic stroke have been demonstrated in multiple randomized controlled trials. The recently published European guidelines recommend a 21-day course of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following an ischemic stroke, followed by tailored therapy with aspirin or clopidogrel, and DAPT for 3–6 months after PFO closure, followed by individualized antiplatelet therapy. However, the extent to which these recommendations are implemented in contemporary practice remains unclear, and data regarding discontinuation of antithrombotic therapy are limited. Aim This study aimed to investigate prevailing trends in the duration and customization of antithrombotic therapy before and after transcatheter PFO closure, and to assess the safety of antiplatelet therapy discontinuation months after the procedure. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 135 patients who underwent percutaneous PFO closure for secondary stroke prevention at a tertiary center between July 2017 and September 2024. Complete data were available for 102 patients. Baseline demographics, comorbidities, and pharmacological treatments were collected from electronic medical records. The primary endpoint was recurrent ischemic cerebrovascular events. Secondary endpoints included bleeding complications and the occurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) or other arrhythmias. Results The mean age of patients was 45.5 years, and 56.6% were male. Common comorbidities included dyslipidemia (50%), hypertension (30.2%), and diabetes mellitus (10%), while AF and coronary artery disease were present only in one patient. Before the procedure, 72% of patients received single and 28% received dual antiplatelet therapy. The Amplatzer™ Talisman™ PFO Occluder was used in 52% and GORE® CARDIOFORM in 48% of the patients, with sizes ranging from 12 to 35 mm. After the PFO Closure, 99 patients received antiplatelet therapy, with 92% receiving DAPT for a mean duration of 3 months, followed by monotherapy in 61% of cases. Only 5 patients received NOACs. Over a mean follow-up of 913 days, two patients experienced cerebrovascular events (one ischemic stroke and one TIA), and nine patients developed new-onset paroxysmal AF, primarily within the first three months after the procedure. No major bleeding events were observed, and minor bleeding occurred in 4.9% of patients. Conclusions Percutaneous PFO closure is safe in real-world clinical practice. Low rates of recurrent cerebrovascular events, arrhythmias, and bleeding complications are reported under antithrombotic agents and gradual discontinuation of antiplatelet therapy was feasible in most patients without adverse outcomes. These findings provide important insights into contemporary antithrombotic management following PFO closure.
title: Optimizing antithrombotic therapy after PFO closure: insights from real-world practice

abstract: Abstract Background Data regarding the benefit of patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure in patients with PFO-related transient ischemic attack (TIA), as compared with ischemic stroke, remain limited. Purpose To compare clinical outcomes after PFO closure according to the type of index cerebrovascular event (stroke ± TIA vs. isolated TIA). Methods We included patients who underwent PFO closure for secondary prevention of stroke or TIA in the international AIR FORCE registry across 31 centers in France, Italy, and the Netherlands between 2001 and 2025. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of center-reported stroke, TIA, or peripheral arterial embolism during follow-up. Cumulative incidence up to 3 years was estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods, and associations between indication for PFO closure (TIA vs. ischemic stroke) and outcomes were assessed over the entire follow-up using adjusted Cox proportional hazards models. Results A total of 4672 patients were included. Baseline characteristics are presented in Table 1. After a median follow-up of 1.0 years [0.1–2.8], no significant association was observed between the indication for PFO closure and the composite outcome (aHR 1.52, 95% CI 0.83–2.77), with corresponding 3-year risks of 4.12% [2.08–8.08] in patients with only TIA and 1.80% [1.28–2.52] in patients with prior stroke (figure 1). Similarly, no significant association was observed for stroke or peripheral arterial embolism (aHR 0.73, 95% CI 0.26–2.04). In contrast, a significant association was observed for TIA recurrence (aHR 3.49, 95% CI 1.68–7.27), with higher 3-year risks in patients with only TIA (3.62% [1.71–7.59] vs. 0.72% [0.41–1.25]). Conclusion In this large international registry, the risk of stroke, TIA, or peripheral arterial embolism after PFO closure did not differ between patients with a PFO-related TIA versus those with a PFO-related stroke as the index event. However, patients with index TIA had a significantly higher risk of TIA recurrence, suggesting the involvement of other causes.Table 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Patent foramen ovale percutaneous closure for transient ischemic attack versus ischemic stroke

abstract: Abstract Background Stroke-Heart Syndrome (SHS) involves acute cardiac injury and hemodynamic stress following a cerebrovascular event. The differential magnitude of myocardial injury between hemorrhagic and non-hemorrhagic stroke and its impact on in-hospital outcomes, remains incompletely defined. Purpose To compare cardiac biomarker activation and short-term outcomes between hemorrhagic (HS) and ischaemic stroke (IS), and to identify independent predictors of length of stay (LOS) and in-hospital mortality. Methods We analyzed 396 consecutive stroke patients in 2025. We measured NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity troponin I (Hs-TnI) at admission and at peak. We assessed left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), LOS, and in-hospital death. Linear regression modeled LOS; logistic regression modeled in-hospital death (per 1 unit). Results The study comprised patients diagnosed with IS, n=370 (mean age 73.85±13.27, 53.24% female) and HS, n=26 (mean age 74.15±10.53, 38.46% female). Baseline comorbidities including heart failure (27.84%, n=103 vs 34.62%, n=9; p=0.46), diabetes mellitus (27.03%, n=100 vs 42.31%, n=11; p=0.09), hypertension (87.30%, n=323 vs 92.31%, n=24; p=0.45), hyperlipidemia (61.62%, n=228 vs 53.85%, n=14; p=0.43), chronic coronary syndrome (14.05%, n=52 vs 7.69%, n=2; p=0.36), past myocardial infarction (7.3%, n=27 vs 0.0%, n=0; p=0.15), past stroke (9.19%, n=34 vs 15.38%, n=4; p=0.3) did not differ significantly between groups. HS demonstrated markedly grater cardiac biomarker activation: peak NT-proBNP: 10645.6±12707.3 vs 2539.8±3974.0 pg/mL (p&lt;0.001); peak Hs-TnI: 2124.3±9778.0 vs 346.5±2806.3 ng/L (p=0.02); The proportion of patients with elevated Hs-TnI was higher in HS (69.23% vs 41.08%, p=0.005) as was &gt;10xULN Hs-TnI (26.92% vs 10.54%, p=0.012). HS was associated with longer hospitalization (17.58±9.42 vs 7.81±3.90 days, p&lt;0.001) and higher in-hospital mortality (19.23%, n=5 vs 4.32%, n=16, p=0.001). In linear regression, age (β=0.042, 95%CI 0.003–0.081, p=0.03) and LVEF (β=−0.084, 95%CI −0.149 to −0.019, p=0.011) were independent predictors of LOS, while peak cardiac biomarkers were not. In logistic regression for in-hospital death, age (OR 1.047 per 1-year increase, 95%CI 0.034-1.207; p=0.030), peak NT-proBNP (OR+1000pg/mL 1.117 per 1,000 pg/mL increase, 95%CI 1.034-1.207, p=0.005), peak Hs-TnI (OR+1000pg/mL1.078 per 1,000 pg/mL increase, 95%CI 1.015-1.143, p=0.014) and LVEF+5% (OR 0.737, 95% CI 0.580-0.936, p=0.012) were all predictors. Conclusion(s) HS may be associated with substantially stronger SHS activation and higher in-hospital mortality than IS. While age and LVEF predict the duration of stay, cardiac biomarkers (NT-proBNP and Hs-TnI) serve as predictors of mortality. These findings support systematic cardiac screening across stroke subtypes to identify high-risk neurocardiac phenotypes.M Chlabicz graphical abstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Stroke-heart syndrome: biomarkers and in-hospital outcomes—pilot data from the SHS-PARTICLES study

abstract: Abstract Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) causes chronic right ventricular (RV) volume overload, increased myocardial work, impaired RV-pulmonary arterial (RVPA) coupling, and progressive RV dysfunction. Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) acutely reduces RV volume loading, followed by longer-term ventricular remodelling. Right ventricular pressure-volume (PV) loop analysis characterises these changes in RV mechanics. Aims To characterise longitudinal changes in RV mechanics over 12 months following T-TEER using PV loop analysis. Methods RV pressure and volume waveforms were integrated to construct PV loops at baseline, post-T-TEER, and at 12-month follow-up. Stroke work (SW), potential energy (PE; wasted work), and pressure-volume area (total mechanical work (TW) and surrogate of myocardial oxygen demand) were quantified. End systolic elastance (Ees) as a measure of RV contractility, effective arterial elastance (Ea), as a measure of afterload and RVPA coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived.
