Longitudinal analyses were performed in patients with complete 12-month follow-up, with paired comparisons performed between baseline and post-procedure, and post-procedure and 12 months. Results Thirty-three patients had complete 12-month follow-up. Compared with baseline, T-TEER was associated with a significant immediate reduction in right ventricular myocardial work, with decreases in SW (-443 ± 260 mmHg·mL, p &lt;0.001) and total mechanical work (-693 ± 491 mmHg·mL, p &lt; 0.001). RVPA coupling decreased significantly early after intervention (0.91 ± 0.36 vs 0.62 ± 0.28; p &lt; 0.001), while RV contractility increased (Ees: +0.07 ± 0.08 mmHg/mL, p &lt;0.001). From post-procedure to 12 months, further reductions in myocardial work were observed. SW continued to decline (-169 ± 168 mmHg·mL, p = 0.04), as did total work (-439 ± 286 mmHg·mL, p = 0.012). RVPA coupling was stable over time (RVPAc: 0.62 ± 0.28 post-procedure vs 0.62 ± 0.26 at 12 months; p = 0.94), and RV contractility also remained stable (Ees: -0.03 ± 0.12 mmHg/mL, p = 0.37). Conclusion T-TEER produces sustained improvements in RV mechanical efficiency, with early unloading followed by longer-term remodelling reflected in PV loop-derived metrics. Pressure-volume analysis provides mechanistic insight into RV adaptation after T-TEER and may offer a valuable framework for assessing therapeutic response.
title: Longitudinal changes in right ventricular mechanics after tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair

abstract: Abstract Background Diffuse left anterior descending coronary disease often forces long, overlapping stent segments. That solves acute scaffolding but leaves a large permanent metal footprint, which can translate into repeat revascularisation in real-world follow-up. A drug-coated balloon-first approach aims to deliver antiproliferative therapy without an implant, but the practical concern is whether balloon-only treatment can achieve a reliable final result in long lesions and whether any short-term advantage persists beyond the procedure. Purpose To compare a drug-coated balloon-first strategy (bail-out stenting permitted) with a drug-eluting stent strategy for procedural success and 12-month clinical outcomes in de novo diffuse left anterior descending disease. Methods We analysed consecutive adults undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2023 and December 2024 for de novo left anterior descending lesions with angiographic length ≥20 mm. In-stent restenosis and planned hybrid index strategies were excluded to keep treatment attribution clear. Because operators tend to select drug-coated balloons for different anatomy than stents, we chose inverse probability of treatment weighting to reduce confounding while preserving the full cohort, and we checked overlap and balance after weighting. Time-to-event outcomes were assessed using Kaplan–Meier methods and Cox regression; a prespecified strategy-based sensitivity analysis retained bail-out conversions within the attempted drug-coated balloon group. Results Among 520 patients, 262 underwent a drug-coated balloon-first strategy and 258 underwent a drug-eluting stent strategy. Lesion complexity was higher in the drug-coated balloon group (type C: 181/262 [69.1%] vs 145/258 [56.2%]). Procedural success was similar (255/262 [97.3%] vs 248/258 [96.1%]). At 12 months, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred less often with the drug-coated balloon strategy (28/262 [10.7%] vs 43/258 [16.7%]), driven by fewer target lesion revascularisations (12/262 [4.6%] vs 27/258 [10.5%]). Event-free survival was higher with drug-coated balloon-first (hazard ratio for drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon 2.01, 95% confidence interval 1.21–3.42; Cox p=0.008). Here’s the trade-off: these differences are clinically meaningful in a long-lesion setting, but residual confounding remains possible despite weighting and prespecified sensitivity analyses. Conclusion In de novo diffuse left anterior descending disease, a drug-coated balloon-first strategy achieved comparable procedural success and was associated with lower 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events and repeat revascularisation than drug-eluting stenting. These real-world data support a "leave-nothing-behind" option in selected long lesions, while randomised trials with protocolised angiographic follow-up are needed to confirm durability and clarify which anatomical subsets benefit most.Adjusted cox model for time to mACE.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.MACE-free survival and propensity scoreFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Drug-coated balloon-first versus drug-eluting stent strategy for de novo diffuse left anterior descending disease: a propensity-weighted cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can miss stent underexpansion or malapposition that intravascular imaging may detect and correct during the index procedure, potentially reducing downstream ischaemic events and repeat revascularisation. Purpose To quantify the clinical impact of intravascular imaging guidance and assess whether effects are consistent across intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT). Methods Trial composite endpoints are not uniform; to keep the analysis anchored to what each study actually tested, we pooled each trial’s prespecified primary composite outcome (major adverse cardiovascular events, target vessel failure, or target lesion failure) rather than applying post-hoc endpoint harmonisation. Pubmed and ScienceDirect were searched through February 2025 for randomised controlled trials comparing IVUS- or OCT-guided versus angiography-guided PCI. Outcomes were extracted at the longest reported follow-up. Risk ratios were pooled using a Mantel–Haenszel random-effects model; heterogeneity was assessed with I2. We prespecified subgroup analyses by imaging modality (IVUS vs OCT). Secondary outcomes included target lesion revascularisation, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis and all-cause death when reported. Results Ten trials (12,343 patients; 6,174 imaging-guided and 6,169 angiography-guided) were included. Imaging guidance reduced the trial-defined primary composite endpoint (risk ratio 0.60, 95% confidence interval 0.54–0.68; I2=0%). Effects were consistent across modalities: IVUS 0.56 (0.48–0.65) and OCT 0.67 (0.56–0.80). The clearest downstream signal was fewer repeat procedures: in IVUS trials reporting target lesion revascularisation, the pooled risk ratio was 0.52 (0.34–0.80). Estimates for myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis and all-cause death were imprecise with no clear between-group differences, reflecting low event rates and incomplete reporting across trials. Conclusion In contemporary randomised evidence, intravascular imaging guidance during PCI improves trial-defined composite clinical outcomes compared with angiography guidance, with benefit most consistently reflected in fewer repeat revascularisations. The trade-off is uncertainty on hard endpoints, supporting the need for adequately powered, longer-term randomised trials.Forrest Plot by ModalityFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Forest plots of TLRFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention versus angiography guidance: updated meta-analysis of randomised trials

abstract: Abstract Background Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an efficient and emerging calcification modifying technique with a short learning curve and few complications. Methods We analyzed intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) findings in 412 patients in whom has a severe coronary calcification and a clinical indication for vessel preparation with IVL. The efficacy outcome was procedural success (defined as residual area stenosis &lt;30%, without interventional complications or in-hospital MACE). Results The mean age was 67.40 ± 9.37 years, and 71.4% were males. The most common target lesion was the LAD, 19.2% lesions was chronic total occlusion, and 8.7% lesions were in-stent restenosis. Patients underwent IVUS examinations before IVL and after PCI. The average area stenosis was 72.18 ± 7.40 %, and pre-MLD was 1.44 ± 0.19 mm. The average calcification length was 29.84 ± 11.24 mm, 7.5% of lesions has calcified nodule, and calcified plaque burden was 59.93 ± 5.54%. The calcified rings fractured after IVL treatment, with a median of 4 (3, 4) fractured sites. The acute lumen gain was 1.15 ± 0.27mm, the post-MLD was 2.59 ± 0.22 mm, and residual area stenosis was 22.06 ± 9.49 %. The IVUS measurements of pre-IVL and post-PCI were compared. After procedure, the MLD (2.56(2.45, 2.74) mm vs. 1.42(1.30, 1.56) mm, p&lt;0.001) and MLA (5.93(5.41, 6.54) mm2vs. 2.04(1.75, 2.52) mm2, p&lt;0.001) were significantly improved, and area stenosis was significantly reduced (24.00(15.25, 28.00) % vs. 74.00(68.00, 77.00) %, p&lt;0.001). Regarding the plaque burden, compared to pre-IVL, the max plaque thickness (0.68(0.64, 0.72) mm vs, 0.90(0.86, 0.95) mm, p&lt;0.001) and the plaque burden (48.17 (45.48, 50.47) % vs. 59.72(56.06, 63.47) %, p&lt;0.001) of post-PCI was significantly reduced. Regarding the efficacy outcome, 93.4% of patients achieved proceduresuccess, and only 4 patients (1.0%) experienced complications during PCI and 1 patient (0.2%) experienced in-hospital MACE. Conclusions IVL treatment is a safe and effective calcification modifying technique for severe coronary calcified lesions, which can fragment the calcified ring and provide efficient pretreatment for subsequent stent implantation.Lesion Characteristics and PCI Outcomes.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Comparison of Pre-IVL and Post-PCI on IVUS.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Intravascular ultrasound characterisation of intravascular lithoplasty for treatment of coronary calcified lesions

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial fibrosis (MF) is a key determinant of adverse outcomes in severe aortic stenosis and limits the efficacy of valve implantation. Endomyocardial biopsy is the reference standard for diagnosing MF, but its invasiveness limits routine use. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV%) is a non-invasive surrogate but correlates only modestly with biopsy-proven MF. Purpose We investigated whether comprehensive radiomic analysis of CMR images improves the non-invasive identification of increased biopsy-proven MF burden. Methods We prospectively enrolled 56 patients with severe aortic stenosis scheduled for transcatheter aortic valve implantation. All patients underwent pre-procedural 3T CMR and intraprocedural endomyocardial biopsy. Histologic MF was quantified by digital morphometry, with patients classified as high (≥11% collagen area fraction) or low fibrotic burden. CMR mid-ventricular short-axis myocardium was manually segmented on cine, native T1 maps, and late gadolinium enhancement images. Radiomics features were extracted using the PyRadiomics package. Only features with intra-/interobserver correlation ≥0.80 were included, and outcome-blinded principal component analysis was applied for dimensionality reduction. Five machine learning models, each using five-fold cross-validation, were tested to model the association between radiomics PCs and MF. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), compared with an ECV%-only model and a combined ECV% + radiomics PCs model. Radiomics PCs were correlated with clinical and imaging features to contextualise the radiomics signature (Figure 1). Results Median age was 80 [77-83] years, and 30% were female. A total of 29 patients (52%) had a high MF burden. Patients with higher MF had larger LV end-diastolic volumes (92 vs 76mL/m²; p=0.018) and showed a trend towards higher ECV% (28% vs 26%; p=0.072). For detecting an increased MF burden, the ECV%-only model achieved an AUC of 0.62 [0.57–0.67]. The machine learning models based on five cine radiomics PCs outperformed ECV% alone (AUC 0.80 [0.77-0.83] for logistic regression, similar for other models). Adding ECV% to the radiomics model did not provide additional discriminatory benefit (ΔAUC −0.01). Native T1 and late gadolinium enhancement radiomics demonstrated modest discrimination. Radiomics PCs showed associations with markers of cardiac size and remodeling, suggesting that radiomics captures morphologic and functional aspects (Figure 2). Correlations were modest, implying that radiomics are not simple surrogates of single conventional parameters but capture a broader spectrum of myocardial remodeling. Conclusion CMR-derived cine radiomics improved non-invasive detection of biopsy-proven MF in severe aortic stenosis, supporting its potential role in precision phenotyping and personalised management.Figure 1.Study workflowFigure 2.Correlation matrix
title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance radiomics for phenotyping myocardial fibrosis in severe aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Intravascular imaging (IVI)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is associated with improved outcomes in complex coronary disease. However, whether IVI guidance uniformly reduces excess risk across distinct lesion complexity phenotypes remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluate residual risk across predefined lesion complexity phenotypes following real-world IVI-guided PCI and to assess the impact of post-procedural stent optimization. Methods We analyzed a prospective single-center registry of consecutive IVI-guided (intravascular ultrasound or optical coherence tomography) PCI procedures performed between January 2015 and March 2025. Eight predefined phenotypes were evaluated: left main, bifurcation, long lesion, severe calcification, in-stent restenosis, chronic total occlusion, ostial lesion, and multiple stents. The reference group comprised non-complex PCI (no phenotype flags). The primary endpoint was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE: all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). Adjusted hazard ratios (HR) were derived using multivariable Cox proportional-hazards models. A secondary analysis evaluated patients achieving an optimal post-procedural minimum stent area (MSA ≥5.5 mm² for non-left main lesions and ≥8.0 mm² for left main lesions). Results Among 3,664 patients, 3339 (91.1%) had ≥1 complex phenotype. At 1 year, MACE occurred in 380 patients (13.6%, 95% CI 12.4-14.9). After multivariable adjustment, in-stent restenosis (HR 2.66, 95% CI 1.46-4.84, p=0.001), chronic total occlusion (HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.31-4.56, p=0.005), multiple stents (HR 2.23, 95% CI 1.29-3.87, p=0.004), long lesion (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.11-2.95, p=0.017), and bifurcation (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.03-2.72, p=0.037) remained independently associated with higher MACE compared with non-complex PCI. In contrast, left main, severe calcification, and ostial lesions were not independently associated with excess risk after adjustment. Achievement of optimal post-procedural MSA was associated with lower 1-year MACE; however, high-risk phenotypes remained predictive despite achievement of optimal expansion. Conclusions In real-world IVI-guided PCI, lesion complexity confers heterogeneous residual risk. In-stent restenosis, chronic total occlusion, multiple stents, long lesion, and bifurcation PCI remain independently high-risk despite imaging guidance. These findings suggest that IVI use does not fully attenuate risk across complexity phenotypes and support further refinement of structured, phenotype-specific optimization strategies in complex PCI.KM Curves for 1-Year MACEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Adjusted HRs for 1-Year MACEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Residual risk according to lesion complexity phenotypes after intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Management of calcified in-stent restenosis (ISR) with stent underexpansion remains challenging. Calcification within the stent and persistent stent underexpansion often hinder achieving adequate lumen area with conventional balloon angioplasty alone. In recent years, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has demonstrated both efficacy and safety as a lesion preparation strategy for calcified coronary lesions. Accordingly, IVL may represent a promising therapeutic option for recurrent ISR, particularly in cases associated with neoatherosclerosis-related calcification or extrastent calcification contributing to stent underexpansion. In this study, we compared IVL with conventional scoring balloon angioplasty for lesion preparation prior to drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) analysis. Methods Between 2018 and 2025, 227 ISR lesions were identified. Lesions were included as following criteria: (1) final treatment with a DCB; (2) availability of pre- and post-procedural IVUS for quantitative analysis; (3) presence of calcification within the stented segment; and (4) evidence of stent underexpansion. A total of 54 lesions fulfilled these criteria. Patients were divided into 2 groups based on lesion preparation strategy: the IVL group (n=27) received intravascular lithotripsy prior to DCB treatment, while the conventional group (n=27) underwent predilation with a scoring balloon followed by DCB. The primary endpoints were final minimum lesion area (MLA) and minimum stent area (MSA) assessed by IVUS. Additional IVUS parameters included presence of calcium nodules, maximum calcium arc, and degree of neointimal hyperplasia. Results The mean age was 76.6 ± 9.4 years. Diabetes mellitus was present in 56%, chronic kidney disease in 63%, and 30% were on hemodialysis. The mean DCB diameter and length were 3.13 ± 0.30 mm and 27.2 ± 15.8 mm, respectively. Pre-procedural IVUS findings were comparable between the IVL and conventional groups. Pre-PCI MLA was 2.46 ± 0.86 mm² vs. 2.71 ± 0.75 mm² (p = 0.27), and MSA was 6.39 ± 2.82 mm² vs. 6.70 ± 1.91 mm² (p = 0.64). Maximum calcium arc within the stent was also similar (167.2 ± 133.4° vs. 166.4 ± 98.2°, p = 0.98). Post-procedural IVUS demonstrated significantly greater luminal and stent expansion in the IVL group compared with the conventional group. Final MLA was 6.49 ± 1.80 mm² vs. 4.75 ± 1.22 mm² (p = 0.0001), and final MSA was 9.76 ± 3.29 mm² vs. 7.90 ± 2.27 mm² (p = 0.02). Post-PCI IVUS findings stratified by maximum calcium arc are presented in the figure. Conclusions This study assessed the impact of IVL versus scoring balloon angioplasty for lesion preparation in calcified, underexpanded ISR treated with DCB. The results indicate that IVL achieves superior stent expansion and greater luminal gain compared with conventional techniques. Notably, the advantages of IVL are particularly pronounced in lesions with more extensive calcification.Final MLA & MSAFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Intravascular lithotripsy versus scoring balloon for lesion preparation in underexpanded calcified in-stent restenosis treated with drug-coated balloon: an IVUS analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Adequate endothelialization after drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation is crucial for reducing thrombotic risk. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) defines adequate strut coverage (ASC) as neointimal thickness ≥40 μm, a threshold validated by histological studies; however, its functional significance in vivo remains unclear. Moreover, it is uncertain whether the overall percentage of adequate strut coverage (%ASC) contributes to thrombus prevention or plaque stabilization when individual struts already meet the ≥40 μm criterion. Coronary angioscopy (CAS) uniquely enables direct visualization of intrastent thrombus and evaluation of plaque stabilization through yellow plaque grading. This study aimed to assess functionally adequate endothelialization after DES implantation and to identify its contributing factors. Methods We performed post-hoc analyses of the COLLABORATION 1 and 2 studies, which included serial OCT and CAS assessments at 1 and 12 months after DES implantation. Four DES types were evaluated: durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents (DP-EES), sirolimus-eluting stents (SES), polymer-free biolimus-coated stents (PF-BCS), and dual-therapy sirolimus-eluting stents (DTS). The relationship between %ASC assessed by OCT and neointimal function, defined as absence of intrastent thrombus and presence of white plaque on CAS, was analyzed at both time points. PF-BCS and DTS were classified as "ingenious" DES, and DP-EES and SES as "fundamental." The primary endpoint was to determine the optimal %ASC cut-off value on OCT for thrombus absence and plaque stabilization assessed by CAS. The secondary endpoint was to identify clinical and procedural predictors, including ingenious DESs and the fundamental DESs, associated with good chronic adequate endothelialization (CAE) at 12 months. Results A total of 150 patients with 177 lesions were analyzed. At 12 months, intrastent thrombus and yellow plaque grade were inversely correlated with %ASC, whereas no such correlation was observed at 1 month. This discrepancy likely reflects the limited ability of OCT in the subacute phase to reliably differentiate thrombus from neointimal tissue, as confirmed by both OCT and CAS findings, leading to potential overestimation of endothelialization by OCT at 1 month. The optimal %ASC cut-off values at the chronic phase were 67% for thrombus prevention and 90% for plaque stabilization (Figure). Multivariable analysis identified the use of ingenious DESs, prasugrel therapy, and hypertension as independent predictors of CAE at 12 months (Table). Conclusions Assessment of adequate endothelialization after DES implantation using OCT is more reliable at 12 months than at 1 month post-procedure. The optimal %ASC thresholds at 12 months are 67% for thrombus prevention and 90% for plaque stabilization. Use of prasugrel and ingenious DES may favorably influence chronic endothelialization after DES implantation.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.TableFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Assessment and contributing factors of adequate endothelization after drug-eluting stent implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables detailed characterisation of plaque morphology, including features of plaque vulnerability. However, whether anatomical vulnerability is associated with subsequent physiological deterioration remains uncertain. Purpose To investigate the association between baseline OCT-derived plaque vulnerability and subsequent fractional flow reserve (FFR) deterioration in intermediate coronary stenosis. Methods We analysed lesions from a prospective multicentre registry of patients with angiographically intermediate coronary lesions (40–70% diameter stenosis) who underwent baseline OCT and FFR assessment, with repeat FFR evaluation at 2 years. Plaque vulnerability features were defined as thin-cap fibroatheroma, macrophage accumulation, microvessels, and cholesterol crystals. Vulnerability burden was calculated as the number of features present (range 0–4). FFR deterioration was defined as a decrease in FFR ≥0.05 from baseline. Relative minimal lumen area (MLA) was calculated as MLA divided by the mean of proximal and distal reference lumen areas. Multivariable logistic regression using a generalised estimating equation approach was performed to evaluate independent predictors of FFR deterioration, including vulnerability burden, relative MLA and lesion length, with additional adjustment for age, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. Results A total of 151 lesions were analysed. Baseline FFR was 0.917 ± 0.065 and follow-up FFR was 0.913 ± 0.079, corresponding to a mean change of −0.004 ± 0.062. FFR deterioration occurred in 20 lesions (13.2%). Among these lesions, mean change in FFR was −0.114 ± 0.079 compared with 0.013 ± 0.036 in lesions without deterioration. Vulnerability burden was independently associated with FFR deterioration (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 1.64 per 1-feature increase, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04–2.58; p=0.032). Relative MLA (OR 1.14 per 0.1 increase, 95% CI 0.84–1.56; p=0.407) and lesion length (OR 1.03 per 1 mm increase, 95% CI 0.98–1.08; p=0.233) were not independently associated. The predicted probability of FFR deterioration increased progressively from 3.4% in lesions without vulnerable features to 20.2% in lesions with four features. Among individual features, thin-cap fibroatheroma showed the strongest trend (OR 3.46, 95% CI 0.80–15.04; p=0.098). Conclusion In intermediate coronary stenosis, baseline OCT-derived plaque vulnerability was independently associated with subsequent physiological deterioration at 2 years. These findings suggest that OCT-defined plaque vulnerability may provide prognostic information regarding subsequent physiological deterioration.Multivariable predictors of FFR deteriorationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.FFR deterioration by vulnerability burdenFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Plaque vulnerability assessed by optical coherence tomography and longitudinal physiological deterioration in intermediate coronary stenosis

abstract: Abstract Purpose The OCCUPI trial demonstrated the clinical benefit of optical coherence tomography (OCT)–guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with complex coronary lesions. However, whether the effect of OCT guidance differs according to coronary lesion vessel remains unclear. This prespecified substudy evaluated the consistency of clinical outcomes with OCT-guided PCI in left anterior descending (LAD) versus non-LAD coronary vessels. Methods Among 1,375 patients without left main disease enrolled in the OCCUPI trial, 888 had LAD lesions and 487 had non-LAD lesions. Patients were randomized to undergo PCI guided by either OCT or conventional angiography. The primary endpoint was 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Event rates were assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis, and group differences were compared using the log-rank test. Results In the LAD group, 1-year MACE occurred in 4.5% of patients treated with OCT-guided PCI and 5.5% of those treated with angiography-guided PCI, with no statistically significant difference on Kaplan–Meier analysis (overall log-rank p = 0.486). In the non-LAD group, corresponding MACE rates were 4.6% and 7.7%, respectively, also without a significant difference (overall log-rank p = 0.154). There was no significant interaction between lesion location and PCI guidance strategy (p for interaction = 0.351). Ischemia-driven TVR occurred less frequently with OCT-guided PCI in both LAD and non-LAD lesions, without evidence of heterogeneity according to lesion location (p for interaction = 0.872). Conclusions In patients with complex coronary lesions, OCT-guided PCI was associated with fewer repeat revascularizations and a consistent trend toward improved clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI, irrespective of coronary lesion location.MACE for angiography/OCT guided PCIFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Optical coherence tomography–guided PCI in left anterior descending versus non–left anterior descending lesions: a prespecified substudy of the OCCUPI trial

abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Calcified coronary plaques frequently harbor lipid-rich components, yet identifying residual lipid burden within calcification remains challenging. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of optical coherence tomography (OCT) to identify lipidic calcification, utilizing near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound (NIRS-IVUS) as the reference standard. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing PCI for de novo calcified lesions (IVUS arc ≥90°) assessed by both NIRS-IVUS and OCT. Lipidic calcification was defined as a lesion with a maximum lipid core burden index in 4 mm (maxLCBI4mm) ≥400. On OCT, the "attenuated calcium index" was calculated as the mean angle of calcification exhibiting an invisible trailing edge across the 20-mm lesion segment. We compared clinical and imaging characteristics between vessels with and without lipidic calcification. Results Among 102 patients, 38 lesions (37.3%) exhibited lipidic calcification. While clinical demographics were comparable between groups, OCT analysis revealed significantly greater lipid length, attenuated calcium index, and prevalence of cholesterol crystals in the lipidic calcification group. Multivariable analysis identified the attenuated calcium index (OR 1.03; 95% CI 1.01–1.05) and cholesterol crystals (OR 10.5; 95% CI 2.91–37.9) as independent predictors of lipidic calcification. Furthermore, among calcified nodules, eruptive nodules demonstrated a significantly higher maxLCBI4mm than non-eruptive ones (401 vs. 208; p=0.035). Conclusions The OCT-derived attenuated calcium index and cholesterol crystals are distinct markers associated with lipidic calcification. Additionally, eruptive calcified nodules appear to harbor a greater lipid burden. OCT facilitates the identification of high-risk phenotypes even within complex calcified lesions.
title: Identification of near-infrared spectroscopy-defined lipid content within calcified coronary plaques using optical coherence tomography

abstract: Abstract Background Acute coronary syndromes (ACS) result from plaque instability; however, conventional imaging focuses primarily on culprit lesions rather than systemic vulnerability. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables high-resolution plaque characterization but remains time-intensive and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) may allow automated pancoronary vulnerability quantification and improve risk stratification beyond traditional clinical scores. Purpose To evaluate whether an AI-based three-vessel OCT model can automatically quantify pancoronary plaque vulnerability and improve prediction of 1-year clinical outcomes in ACS. Methods This was a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained three-vessel OCT registry including consecutive ACS patients between January and December 2024. A convolutional neural network performed automated lipid-rich plaque segmentation, thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA) classification, fibrous cap thickness (FCT) quantification, and macrophage detection. Model performance was validated against independent core laboratory assessment. Patients were followed for 12 months (through December 2025) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or unplanned revascularization). Multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, LDL-C, and GRACE score. Results Among 312 patients (mean age 59±11 years; 27% female; 38% diabetes; median GRACE 128 [IQR 112–146]), complete follow-up was available in 300 (96%). For TCFA classification, AI achieved AUC 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89–0.95), sensitivity 90% (95% CI: 86–93%), specificity 87% (95% CI: 83–91%), precision 0.88, recall 0.90, and F1-score 0.89. Lipid segmentation showed Dice coefficient 0.88 (95% CI: 0.86–0.90). FCT measurements strongly correlated with manual assessment (r=0.91, 95% CI: 0.88–0.93; mean absolute error 12 μm). Macrophage detection yielded AUC 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82–0.90), sensitivity 82%, specificity 79%, and F1-score 0.81. Pancoronary vulnerability was common: TCFA was present in 72% (95% CI: 66–78%) of culprit and 24% (95% CI: 20–29%) of non-culprit lesions; 42% (95% CI: 36–48%) had ≥1 non-culprit TCFA. Non-culprit TCFA burden independently predicted MACE. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 60 patients (19.2%, 95% CI: 15.0–23.4%). Patients in the highest AI-derived lipid tertile had HR 3.52 (95% CI: 2.10–5.80; p&lt;0.001), with adjusted HR 2.94 (95% CI: 1.76–4.90). Addition of AI-derived OCT metrics improved C-statistic from 0.71 (95% CI: 0.66–0.76) to 0.82 (95% CI: 0.78–0.87; p=0.003), with net reclassification improvement of 0.27 (95% CI: 0.14–0.40). Conclusion Automated pancoronary AI-OCT quantification provides objective assessment of systemic plaque vulnerability and independently predicts 1-year adverse outcomes in ACS, significantly improving risk discrimination beyond traditional clinical scoring.
title: Artificial intelligence–driven three-vessel OCT quantification identifies the vulnerable patient and predicts 1-year outcomes in acute coronary syndromes

abstract: Abstract Background Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides excellent resolution at the cost of shallow penetration depth, limiting its ability for complete assessment of the vessel wall and, consequently, plaque burden (PB). A deep learning (DL) algorithm was therefore developed for fully automated media delineation and PB estimation from OCT. Purpose To perform the first head-to-head comparison of AI-enabled OCT versus intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for quantifying media area and PB, using histopathology as the reference standard. Methods Ten post-mortem human hearts were harvested, yielding 29 major epicardial coronary arteries. The arteries were ligated at the side branches and connected to a coronary perfusion system during OCT and IVUS pullbacks. After imaging, the arteries were subdivided into different coronary segments and serially sectioned at 1-mm intervals and stained with haematoxylin-eosin, Masson trichrome, and Alizarin Red when applicable (Figure 1). The matching between histopathologic and OCT and IVUS cross-sections relied primarily on distance from the barbed connector, supplemented by corresponding luminal configurations and anatomical landmarks including side branches or plaque morphology. The Lumen area, media area and PB from OCT and IVUS was fully automatically derived using DL, and semiautomatically derived using a developed prototype in a blinded fashion and compared to histopathology (Figure 2). Statistical analyses accounted for within-heart clustering. Results A total of 834 paired OCT-IVUS cross-sections were obtained and compared. Using histopathology as the reference standard, the lumen area concordance was high for both modalities (r=0.89 [95% CI: 0.88, 0.91] for OCT versus r=0.90 [95% CI: 0.89, 0.91] for IVUS, p=0.30). For the assessment of IEL area, AI-powered OCT was numerically lower compared to IVUS (r=0.85 [95% CI: 0.83-0.87] for OCT versus r=0.86 [95% CI: 0.84-0.88] for IVUS), but statistically non-significant (p=0.45). AI-powered OCT were non-inferior to IVUS for assessing PB (r= 0.76 [95% CI: 0.73-0.79] for OCT versus r=0.79 [95% CI: 0.76, 0.81] for IVUS, p=0.12) (Figure 1). In identifying histologically significant cross-sections (PB&gt;65%), the AI-powered OCT achieved a non-inferior discrimination compared with IVUS (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve compared [AUC]=0.93 [95% CI: 0.91-0.94] for OCT and 0.93 [95% CI: 0.91-0.94] for IVUS, p= 0.75). Conclusions Validated against histopathology, the DL algorithm enables reliable, fully automated IEL delineation and plaque burden estimation from OCT, with performance non-inferior to co-localised IVUS. AI-empowered OCT demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy and may broaden the quantitative capabilities of OCT in clinical practice.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: AI-empowered OCT is non-inferior to IVUS for media and plaque burden quantification: head-to-head histopathology validation using human coronary arteries

abstract: Abstract Background Intracoronary optical coherence tomography (OCT) can be used to assess stent malapposition and its expansion rates, which are critical measurements of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) success. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have demonstrated the potential to provide automated, rapid, and accurate post-PCI stent evaluation, potentially improving workflow efficiency and diagnostic confidence. Purpose To develop a rapid, automated AI system for stent strut detection and perform subsequent stent expansion and malapposition analysis simultaneously from OCT images after PCI procedures. Methods This study developed a deep learning model consists of two convolutional neural networks. The first neural network was trained (N=8640 frames from 16 pullbacks) to segment individual stent struts within OCT frames, while the second one was trained (N=4300 frames from 290 pullbacks) to delineate the vessel lumen afterwards. The segmented stent struts were then used to calculate frame-wise stent expansion, defined as the difference in spline area between the reference and predicted strut expansion projection. Malapposition was identified by detecting struts in the lumen with a distance larger than 0.2 mm from the vessel wall. Manually annotated stents struts and malappositions combining with spline interpolated stent expansion areas were used as reference. Results The system was evaluated on a held-out test set comprising 2160 OCT frames from 4 patients. The stent strut detection model achieved an overall precision of 0.913 and a recall of 0.828 across all frames, indicating high accuracy in identifying stent struts. The stent expansion area error was 0.019 mm2 [0.007-0.86] (median [Q1-Q3]) across all analysed frames, providing a quantitative measure of stent placement success. Malapposition detection achieved an overall precision of 0.926 and a recall of 0.910 on stent strut level. The entire pipeline, including image preprocessing, strut segmentation, lumen contour delineation, expansion calculation, and malapposition assessment, was completed in under 20 seconds for pullbacks of 540 frames. Conclusion This study demonstrates that AI-based stent detection and evaluation, based on OCT imaging, can be performed rapidly and with high accuracy to identify struts, calculate frame-wise stent expansion and detect malapposition. Unlike commercial OCT analysis software, which is typically specialised to single case online study during the procedure, our system also enables retrospective analysis of large numbers of OCT pullbacks, providing comprehensive research and quality improvement initiatives. While this evaluation was performed on a limited number of patients, the results suggest that AI-based OCT analysis could reduce workload for interventional cardiologists. Future research will focus on expanding this system to larger, diverse patient populations to evaluate its impact on downstream decisionsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Artificial intelligence-based analysis of stent malapposition and expansion from intracoronary optical coherence tomography

abstract: Abstract Background Intravascular imaging enables in vivo characterization of coronary plaque morphology and composition. While several plaque features are known to independently predict adverse outcomes, the underlying pathobiology remains incompletely defined. Plasma proteomic studies may contribute to its elucidation. Purpose We aimed to relate plasma proteomic profiling to plaque characteristics, and to identify clinically relevant coronary artery disease (CAD) subphenotypes. Methods We examined 581 CAD patients who underwent diagnostic coronary angiography/percutaneous coronary intervention. Blood samples were drawn prior to the procedure. Proteins were quantified by Slow Offrate Modified Aptamer assay, yielding relative fluorescence unit measurements for 1500 pre-selected plasma proteins involved in cardiovascular and inflammatory processes. All patients underwent virtual histology intravascular ultrasound, and a subset of 273 patients underwent near-infrared spectroscopy. We assessed associations of individual proteins with plaque characteristics, 5-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and 12-year all-cause mortality. Using the significant proteins, we performed Reactome pathway enrichment analysis. To identify distinct patient subphenotypes, we used principal component analysis, uniform manifold approximation and projection, and then HDBSCAN clustering. Subphenotypes were subsequently related to clinical outcomes and plaque characteristics, using linear/logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models, respectively (subphenotype vs. the remainder of the cohort). Results Median age was 61.5 years, 75% were males and 55% of patients were diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome, while 45% presented with chronic coronary syndrome. Over a median follow-up of 4.3 years 151 MACEs occurred, and over a median of 12.8 years 179 patients died. Figure 1 presents pathway enrichment analyses for proteins associated with plaque components (A-B) and for those linked to MACE and all-cause mortality (C). Overall, inflammatory, hemostatic, and metabolic pathways were overrepresented in relation to plaque vulnerability and adverse outcomes. Figures 2A-B show the results of the clustering algorithm, yielding four distinct subphenotypes. In particular, Cluster 4 displayed significant protective associations with both all-cause mortality (HR=0.55 [95%CI: 0.35–0.88], padj=0.013) and MACE (HR=0.54 [0.33–0.87], padj=0.011) as well as associations with several plaque components: dense calcium percentage, fibrous tissue, and Lipid Core Burden Index. Conclusion This study identified plasma proteins and pathways associated with plaque components and morphological features. Moreover, unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional proteomic data delineated distinct, clinically relevant CAD subphenotypes. Together, these findings motivate future mechanistic studies and may support improved risk stratification and personalized therapeutic strategies.Figure 1.ORA plaque characteristicsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2.Subphenotypes cluster analysisFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Plasma proteomics are linked to intravascular imaging–derived plaque characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients with coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Calcified nodules (CNs) are classified into eruptive and non-eruptive subtypes, which are associated with different clinical outcomes following stenting. However, their distinct pathological and topographical characteristics remain poorly understood. Methods We compared clinical and multimodality imaging characteristics of eruptive and non-eruptive CNs in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The analysis included pre-procedural intracoronary imaging with optical coherence tomography (OCT) and near-infrared spectroscopy–intravascular ultrasound (NIRS-IVUS). NIRS-IVUS was used to measure the maximum 4-mm lipid core burden index (maxLCBI4mm) at the CN site. Results We identified 70 CNs (31 eruptive, 39 non-eruptive) in 64 patients. OCT-derived calcium angle and thickness were greater, calcium length were longer, NIRS-derived maxLCBI4mm were higher in lesions with eruptive CN. Topographically, eruptive CNs clustered in the mid-right coronary artery (RCA) and proximal left anterior descending artery, whereas non-eruptive CNs were distributed homogeneously throughout the coronary tree. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified hemodialysis (odds ratio [OR] 6.19, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28-29.9, P=0.02), RCA-mid segment location (OR 18.5, 95% CI 1.24-275.6, P=0.03), OCT-derived high calcium score (OR 7.46, 95% CI 1.10-50.6, P=0.04) and maxLCBI4mm (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.01, P&lt;0.01) as independent predictors of eruptive CNs. Conclusion Eruptive and non-eruptive CNs exhibit distinct imaging phenotypes and topographical distributions. Eruptive CNs are characterized by a greater calcium burden, a larger adjacent lipid component, and a predilection for specific biomechanically stressed locations. These findings suggest different underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and may enhance risk stratification for complex calcified lesions.
title: Distinct imaging phenotypes and topographical distribution of eruptive versus non-eruptive calcified nodules: a multimodality imaging study

abstract: Abstract Background Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but the relative contributions of its cholesterol and triglyceride content to coronary plaque burden and vulnerability are unknown. Methods In 873 patients with recent acute myocardial infarction from the PROSPECT II cohort, non-culprit coronary segments were imaged with near-infrared spectroscopy-intravascular ultrasound. Lp(a)-associated cholesterol [Lp(a)-C] and triglycerides [Lp(a)-TG] were measured using validated immune-isolation assays. Associations with pan-coronary plaque volume (PPV), pan-coronary lipid burden, maximum 4-mm lipid core burden index (maxLCBI₄mm), and a combined high-risk plaque phenotype (plaque burden ≥70% and maxLCBI₄mm ≥324.7) were assessed by multivariable linear and logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes category, prior PCI, STEMI vs NSTEMI presentation, baseline statin use, and analyzed segment length. Results In multivariable analyses, the highest Lp(a)-C tertile was modestly associated with greater pan-coronary plaque volume compared with the lowest tertile (β = 1.36; 95% CI 0.00 to 2.72; p = 0.050). Continuous or log-transformed Lp(a)-C showed similar directional trends without reaching statistical significance. Neither Lp(a)-C nor Lp(a)-TG was independently associated with pan-coronary lipid burden or isolated maxLCBI₄mm ≥324.7. In contrast, log-transformed Lp(a)-TG was independently associated with the combined high-risk plaque phenotype (adjusted odds ratio 1.13; 95% CI 1.00 to 1.29; p = 0.048), whereas Lp(a)-C showed no association with this endpoint. Conclusions Cholesterol-enriched and triglyceride-enriched Lp(a) particles exhibit differential associations with coronary plaque characteristics in PROSPECT II. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest Lp(a) lipid composition influences plaque phenotype beyond particle concentration alone.
title: Differential associations of lipoprotein(a)-associated cholesterol and triglycerides with coronary plaque burden and vulnerability: a PROSPECT II substudy

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is increasingly recognized as a cause of myocardial ischemia in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Emerging evidence suggests a pathophysiologic link between CMD and atrial fibrillation (AF), potentially mediated by endothelial dysfunction, atrial ischemia, and systemic inflammation. However, data based on invasive assessment of coronary microvascular function remain limited. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from consecutive patients undergoing clinically indicated invasive coronary microvascular assessment between November 2019 and January 2025. All patients underwent coronary angiography with physiological assessment of the left anterior descending artery, including fractional flow reserve, coronary flow reserve (CFR), index of microvascular resistance (IMR), and resistive reserve ratio (RRR). CMD was defined as the presence of at least one abnormal parameter (CFR &lt;2.5, IMR &gt;25, or RRR &lt;3.5). Associations between AF and CMD were evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Results Among 422 patients included (median age 69 years; 55% female), CMD was identified in 219 (52%). AF was more prevalent in patients with CMD compared with those without CMD (13% vs. 6%, p=0.019). In multivariable analysis, AF was independently associated with CMD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.09, 95% CI 1.09–4.33, p=0.029), along with older age and ischemic heart disease. Among patients with CMD, those with AF were older and demonstrated higher left ventricular filling pressures and reduced right ventricular systolic function. A trend toward higher prevalence of persistent or permanent AF was observed in CMD patients with AF compared with those without CMD. Conclusions Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease. These findings support a mechanistic link between CMD and atrial arrhythmogenesis and suggest that patients with CMD may benefit from enhanced rhythm surveillance. Further prospective studies are warranted to clarify causality and clinical implications.Flowchart summarizing the study populationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Atrial fibrillation and coronary microvascular dysfunction - A Clinical Signal

abstract: Abstract Background Fractional flow reserve (FFR) remains the reference standard for invasive physiologic lesion assessment. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) provides a wire-free alternative; however, determinants of clinically relevant discordance remain incompletely defined. Purpose To evaluate agreement between QFR and FFR and determine whether lesion length and grey-zone physiology interact to influence discordance. Methods Seventy-six lesions with available FFR measurements were included in the comparative analysis. Hemodynamic significance was defined as FFR ≤0.80 and QFR ≤0.80. Correlation and categorical agreement were calculated. Discordance was modeled using penalized logistic regression lesion length (per 10 mm), FFR grey-zone status (0.75–0.85), and their interaction. Results QFR correlated with FFR (r=0.57, p= 0.000000094) with 82.9% agreement (κ=0.61). Overall discordance occurred in 17.1% of lesions. Grey-zone lesions demonstrated substantially higher discordance rates. In penalized logistic regression (n=73), grey-zone status was associated with a 4.5-fold higher odds of QFR–FFR discordance (OR 4.50). An interaction between lesion length and grey-zone status was observed, with increasing lesion length amplifying discordance specifically in borderline lesions (interaction OR 1.18 per 10 mm). Conclusions In an expanded real-world cohort, QFR shows moderate agreement with FFR; however, physiologic discordance is strongly influenced by borderline FFR values. Lesion length amplifies discordance predominantly within the grey zone, suggesting that anatomic complexity modulates angiography-based physiologic assessment in intermediate lesions.
title: Grey-zone–dependent discordance between angiography-based quantitative flow ratio and fractional flow reserve: interaction with lesion length in an expanded real-world Cohort

abstract: Abstract Background While fractional flow reserve (FFR) plays a crucial role in determining initial management strategies for patients with intermediate coronary artery stenosis, adverse clinical events can still occur even in patients with negative FFR results, which remains scientifically noteworthy. We hypothesized that coronary angiographic findings may provide a certain answer to identify this unique patient subset. Purpose This retrospective study aimed to explore the prognostic values of angiographic morphology of functionally non-significant coronary stenosis. Methods A total of 209 intermediate lesions (percent stenosis of 50% to 75% on visual estimation) from 195 patients with FFR &gt;0.80 and deferred revascularization were included in this analysis. Patients with a history of prior stent implantation and/or myocardial infarction were excluded. FFR were measured using a pressure wire in a standard manner. Based on coronary angiographic findings, target lesions were classified into focal lesions, defined as a single intermediate stenosis which lesion length of &lt;20 mm, and tandem/diffuse lesions, defined as a sequential lesion with ≥2 focal lesions or a intermediate stenosis with lesion length of ≥20 mm. The angiographic contrast intensity (ACI) was also evaluated by calculating the ratio of mean pixel value of the target lesion site to that of the reference site (Figure). Higher ACI values indicate reduced contrast filling at the target lesion sites. Primary endpoint of this study was target-vessel failure (TVF). Results Median FFR value in the target lesions was 0.87 (interquartile range: 0.84 to 0.91). Patients (mean age was 71±9 years, 76% of patients were men) were followed for a median of 57 months. During this period, TVF occurred in 15 (7%) lesions. Patients with TVF, compared with those without, showed higher rates of diabetes mellitus (60% vs. 31%, p=0.026), dyslipidemia (87% vs. 52%, p=0.005), tandem/diffuse lesions (80% vs. 28%, p&lt;0.001) and lesions with higher ACI (1.56±0.32 vs. 1.31±0.19, p=0.009). In the multivariate regression analysis, tandem/diffuse lesions and higher ACI were statistically associated with subsequent TVF (Table). Receiver operating characteristics curve analysis revealed the optimal cut-off value of ACI to predict TVF was 1.67. When stratified by tandem/diffuse lesions and ACI, subsequent TVF rates were markedly higher in lesions with both tandem/diffuse and ACI ≥1.67 compared with those without (75% vs. 1.5%, p&lt;0.0001). Conclusions Tandem/diffuse intermediate lesions and higher angiographic contrast intensity were both associated with subsequent TVF in lesions with FFR negative. Although further studies need to elucidate the mechanisms of this association, our findings may suggest the need for close follow-up and targeted medical treatments for this patient subsets.figureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.tableFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Prognostic impact of angiographically morphology in functionally non-significant coronary stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Treatment of calcified coronary artery stenosis remains challenging and is associated with worse clinical outcomes. For successful PCI of calcified lesions, it is imperative to achieve sufficient plaque modification before stent implantation. However, the impact of different calcium-modification technique on the coronary microcirculation remains unclear. Aims The aim of this study is to evaluate the influence of plaque modification techniques on coronary microcirculation with severely calcified coronary artery lesions. Methods We retrospectively analyzed physiological measurements and procedural outcomes of 94 patients who underwent PCI for severely calcified coronary stenosis treated with calcium-modification devices from January 2022 to December 2025 at our hospital. Coronary microvascular function was assessed using a temperature-sensor pressure guidewire before and after PCI. The primary endpoint was impairment of coronary microvascular resistance and reserve assessed by the index of microvascular resistance (IMR), resistive reserve ratio (RRR), and microvascular resistance reserve (MRR). Secondary endpoints included periprocedural complications and short-term clinical outcomes. Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) was defined as IMR≧25. Results A total of 48 patients underwent calcium modification with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) and 46 with rotational atherectomy (RA). The mean age was 76 years, 74% were male and the left anterior descending artery was the most frequently treated vessel. Baseline physiological data were comparable between groups. FFR improved significantly after PCI in both groups. In the IVL group, IMR did not significantly change (median 15.0 [IQR 9.0-22.0] to 12.0 [IQR 9.0-19.0], p=0.27), while coronary microvascular reserve improved, with increase in RRR (median 2.5 [IQR1.8-3.65] to 3.0 [IQR 2.12-4.60], p=0.03), and MRR (median 2.33 [IQR 1.65-3.44] to 2.77 [IQR 2.05-4.54], p=0.01). In contrast, in the RA group IMR increased (median 14.0 [IQR 10.75-21.00] to 17.5 [IQR 11.25-36.5], p&lt;0.01) and RRR decreased (median 2.50 [IQR 1.68-3.30] to 1.55 [IQR 1.20-2.35], p=0.04) (Figure1), suggesting post-PCI impairment of the coronary microcirculation. The rate of post-PCI CMD was lower in IVL group than in the RA group (10% vs. 36%, p&lt;0.01). Periprocedural MI and slow flow during PCI were more frequent in the RA group (26% vs 4%, p&lt;0.01; and 20% vs 4%, p=0.03, respectively) (Figure 2). On multivariable logistic regression, RA emerged as an independent predictor of post-PCI CMD (odds ratio 5.41, 95% confidence interval 1.60–18.3; p&lt;0.01). Conclusion IVL and RA are both effective devices to treat severely calcified coronary stenosis . However, IVL was associated with a lower incidence of CMD than RA, suggesting that consideration on device selection would be required in high risk patients with severely calcified coronary disease.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction and short-term outcomes after PCI for severely calcified lesions: a comparison between intravascular lithotripsy and rotational atherectomy

abstract: Abstract Background Wire-free angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) has emerged as an alternative physiological approach for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, direct comparative evidence against established strategies, including angiography-guided, wire-based FFR-guided, and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI, remains limited. Purpose To compare the clinical effectiveness of angiography-derived FFR guidance with other established coronary assessment strategies using a frequentist network meta-analysis. Methods A systematic search identified randomised controlled trials comparing angiography-derived FFR-guided PCI with angiography-, wire-based FFR-, or IVUS-guided strategies. Outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction (MI), and ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation (ID-TVR). A random-effects frequentist network meta-analysis was performed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). P-scores were used to rank treatment strategies. Results Eight randomised trials including 10,532 patients were analysed. In pairwise random-effects analyses, angiography-derived FFR showed no statistically significant differences compared with conventional strategies for MACE (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.54–1.10), cardiovascular death (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.56–1.48), MI (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.55–1.59), or ID-TVR (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.67–1.26). In the network meta-analysis, angiography-guided PCI was associated with a higher risk of MACE (OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.11–2.53) and MI (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.24–2.34) compared with angiography-derived FFR guidance. No significant differences were observed between angiography-derived FFR, wire-based FFR, and IVUS-guided strategies across all outcomes. P-score ranking consistently placed wire-based FFR and IVUS highest, angiography-derived FFR intermediate, and angiography-guided PCI lowest. Conclusions Angiography-derived FFR was associated with superior outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI and demonstrated comparable effectiveness to wire-based FFR and IVUS. These findings position angiography-derived FFR as a clinically meaningful physiological alternative when invasive pressure-wire assessment is not routinely implemented.ESC2026_network_meta_outcomes.jpgFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Clinical outcomes of angiography-derived fractional flow reserve compared with invasive and imaging-guided PCI: a network meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary physiology-guided revascularisation improves outcomes, yet invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) is underused due to complexity and cost. Angiography-based FFR, including Murray law-based QFR (μQFR), allows wire-free assessment without hyperaemia. Whether its diagnostic accuracy varies by coronary stenosis location remains unclear. Purpose To assess μQFR accuracy versus FFR across coronary arteries and lesion segments, and to determine the influence of lesion location. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing coronary angiography with pressure wire-based FFR assessment for at least one intermediate stenosis (30–70% by visual estimation) were analysed. Vessels with left main disease, recent myocardial infarction, in-stent restenosis, or inadequate image quality were excluded. FFR ≤0.80 defined haemodynamic significance. μQFR was computed offline by blinded analysts from single angiographic projections. Per-vessel correlation and agreement with FFR were assessed by Spearman and Bland–Altman analyses. ROC curves were compared with QCA-derived diameter stenosis (QCA-%DS) using the DeLong test. Results 497 vessels from 460 patients were analysed. Haemodynamic significance occurred in 107/335 LAD (32%), 13/79 LCX (16.5%), and 10/83 RCA (12.0%) vessels, and in 66/245 proximal (27.0%), 58/222 middle (26.1%), and 6/30 distal (20.0%) segments. μQFR correlated well with invasive FFR across different arteries (LAD: rho=0.770; LCX: rho=0.759; RCA: rho=0.684; P&lt;0.001 for all) and segments (proximal: rho=0.787; middle: rho=0.761; distal: rho=0.820; P&lt;0.001 for all) (Figure 1), with minimal bias (LAD: 0.010±0.052; LCX: 0.001±0.045; RCA: -0.005±0.061; proximal: 0.008±0.054; middle: 0.004±0.051; distal: 0.004±0.051). Per-vessel analysis showed that μQFR had higher diagnostic accuracy than QCA-%DS in LAD 85.4% (95% confidence interval, 81.1–89.0) vs. 71.6% (66.5–76.4, P&lt;0.001), proximal 86.5% (81.6–90.5) vs. 73.9% (67.9–79.3, P&lt;0.001), and middle segments 86.9% (81.8–91.1) vs. 75.2% (69.0–80.8, P&lt;0.001), a trend toward improvement in LCX 88.6% (79.5–94.7) vs. 84.8% (75.0–91.9, P=0.051), while differences in RCA 89.2% (80.4–94.9) vs. 81.9% (72.0–89.5, P=0.396) and distal segments 83.3% (65.3–94.4) vs. 90.0% (74.5–97.9, P=0.266) were not statistically significant (Figure 2). Conclusions μQFR provides stable, location-independent diagnostic performance across coronary arteries and lesion segments. It outperforms angiographic diameter stenosis assessment in commonly affected vessels and segments, while maintaining reliable accuracy in distal lesions, supporting its use as a consistent, wire-free tool for physiological lesion assessment in routine practice.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of coronary lesion location on the diagnostic performance of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio

abstract: Abstract Background Physiology-guided coronary revascularization using fractional flow reserve (FFR) and instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR) improves outcomes compared with angiography alone. However, FFR–iFR discordance occurs in 15–20% of lesions and is associated with heterogeneous clinical outcomes, yet the underlying hemodynamic mechanisms are not fully captured by conventional pressure tracings. Reservoir–excess pressure analysis (REPA), which decomposes arterial pressure into reservoir pressure (Pr) and excess pressure (Pxs) and quantifies the diastolic rate constant (DRC), offers additional pathophysiological insight into these differences, as chronically elevated DRC and Pxs, together with reduced Pr, may indicate systemic hyperperfusion accompanied by lower aortic compliance. Purpose The objective of this study was to characterize pressure-derived hemodynamics and identify mechanisms underlying FFR–iFR discordance in angiographically intermediate coronary artery stenoses using REPA. Methods The analysis included 249 unique lesions with intermediate coronary artery stenoses (40%–70% severity) from 223 patients enrolled in the prospective, international, multicenter DEFINE–FLOW study. FFR was defined as hyperemic Pd/Pa and iFR as resting Pd/Pa during the wave-free period. Established cutoffs (FFR≤0.80 and iFR≤0.89) were used to define concordant and discordant stenoses. REPA was performed on ensemble-averaged proximal aortic pressure waveforms at rest to derive Pr, Pxs, and related parameters (Figure 1). Results REPA parameters demonstrated distinct hemodynamic profiles across groups. FFR−/iFR+ cases showed significantly higher Pxs (7.53 [4.97, 10.12]) and DRC (3.00 [2.06, 3.52]) and lower IntPr/IntPxs (11.73 [9.57, 17.00]) compared to FFR+/iFR− (Pxs: 5.19 [4.21, 6.89], DRC: 2.28 [1.69, 2.51], IntPr/IntPxs: 17.90 [14.23, 19.87]) and FFR−/iFR− (Pxs: 5.38 [4.03, 7.17], DRC: 2.20 [1.67, 2.91], IntPr/IntPxs: 17.03 [12.76, 21.21]) cases. Notably, both Pxs and DRC values were highest and IntPr/IntPxs was lowest in FFR−/iFR+ cases compared to all other groups. Pxs was an independent predictor of FFR−/iFR+ discordance among cases with FFR&gt;0.80, as increased aortic Pxs was associated with lower iFR values and increased likelihood of positive iFR classification (OR: 1.386; 95% CI: 1.109–1.732; p=0.004). In contrast, higher hAPV (OR: 1.160; 95% CI: 1.070–1.258; p&lt;0.001) and lower bAPV (OR: 0.772; 95% CI: 0.647–0.921; p=0.004), reflecting higher CFR, were independent predictors of FFR+/iFR− discordance. Conclusions Higher aortic Pxs and weaker proximal aortic reservoir function are associated with abnormal iFR in lesions with normal FFR, whereas higher CFR is associated with normal iFR in lesions with abnormal FFR. Systemic hemodynamics, including proximal aortic reservoir behavior, may provide additional mechanistic insight into altered coronary pressure hemodynamics and improve the pathophysiological understanding of FFR–iFR discordance.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Exploring hemodynamic differences in patients with discordant FFR–iFR using reservoir–excess pressure analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the standard treatment for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, angiographic success PCI does not necessarily reflect normalization of coronary physiology, and residual ischemia may persist. Post-PCI fractional flow reserve (FFR) is well-established method for evaluating suboptimal revascularization. We aimed to evaluate impaired culprit lesion revascularization in patients treated with primary PCI. Purpose To evaluate the prevalence and determinants of suboptimal functional revascularization, defined by post-PCI FFR ≤0.89, in STEMI patients treated with primary PCI. Method In this prospective cohort study, STEMI patients underwent planned follow-up coronary angiography approximately 9 months after index PCI to evaluate residual epicardial disease, when acute microvascular dysfunction is expected to have resolved. Invasive physiological assessment included resting full-cycle ratio (RFR), FFR, and hyperaemic pressure pullback recordings with calculation of the pressure pullback gradient (PPG). Suboptimal functional revascularization was defined as post-PCI FFR ≤0.89. Results Of 126 enrolled patients, post-PCI FFR was available in 122. At follow-up, 54 (44%) patients demonstrated suboptimal FFR (≤0.89). In adjusted analyses, increasing age (odds ratio (OR) 1.06 per year increase, 95% CI 1.02–1.11, p=0.009); anterior infarction (OR 11.96, 95% CI 4.84–32.73, p&lt;0.001) and left anterior descending (LAD) as the culprit vessel (OR 13.92, 95% CI 5.50–39.65, p&lt;0.001) were independently associated with higher risk of suboptimal FFR. Higher admission LVEF (OR 0.96 per % increase, 95% CI 0.92–1.00, p=0.038) and larger stent diameter (OR 0.18 per mm increase, 95% CI 0.06–0.46, p&lt;0.001) were associated with lower risk of suboptimal FFR (Figure 1). Traditional cardiovascular risk factors, lesion complexity, intravascular ultrasound use and time from symptom onset to wire were not associated with post-PCI physiological impairment. Conclusion Nearly half of STEMI patients demonstrate incomplete functional revascularization at follow-up despite apparently successful PCI. Suboptimal FFR appears to be mainly related to age, infarct-related territory (LAD) and luminal dimensions (stent diameter), rather than procedural factors.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Determinants of suboptimal functional revascularization after primary PCI in STEMI: a prospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background While fractional flow reserve (FFR) remains the gold standard for hemodynamic assessment of epicardial coronary stenosis, non-hyperemic pressure ratios (NHPRs), such as the resting full-cycle ratio (RFR), have emerged as simplified alternatives. However, recent evidence suggests that NHPR-guided revascularization may be associated with suboptimal clinical outcomes compared to FFR1.2. The physiological underpinnings of the discrepancy between these two metrics remain incompletely understood. Purpose We hypothesized that the numerical difference between RFR and FFR (the RFR-FFR delta) reflects a composite of systemic comorbidity burden and coronary microvascular impairment. This study aimed to elucidate the clinical significance of the RFR-FFR delta in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) and left anterior descending artery (LAD) stenosis, focusing on its association with microvascular function and long-term mortality. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, we evaluated 460 patients with CCS and significant LAD stenosis (FFR ≤ 0.80) who underwent FFR-guided elective PCI. All patients received pre-PCI comprehensive physiological assessment including RFR, FFR, coronary flow reserve (CFR), and microvascular resistance reserve (MRR). Patients were stratified into tertiles based on the RFR-FFR delta. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results Patients in the lowest RFR-FFR tertile exhibited a high-risk clinical phenotype, characterized by advanced age, female sex, increased NT-proBNP levels, and impaired renal function. Notably, a lower RFR-FFR delta was significantly associated with impaired microvascular indices, including lower CFR and MRR. Over a median follow-up of 5.2 years, the lowest tertile demonstrated the highest rate of all-cause mortality (Log-rank P = 0.030). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis identified an RFR-FFR delta &lt; 0.060 (HR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.01–3.45; P = 0.048) and log NT-proBNP as independent predictors of death. Conclusions The RFR-FFR delta serves as a potent integrator of systemic comorbidities and coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing FFR-guided PCI. A lower RFR-FFR gap identifies a high-risk patient subset with unfavorable long-term survival. This novel preprocedural metric facilitates refined risk stratification and supports a personalized approach to the management of complex coronary artery disease.Graphical AbstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Study Flow ChartFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: The RFR-FFR delta: a novel physiological signature of microvascular dysfunction and long-term mortality in patients undergoing LAD PCI

abstract: Abstract Background While intensive lipid-lowering favourably modifies coronary plaque morphology, its effects on angiography-derived coronary physiology and arterial mechanics remain unclear. Radial wall strain (RWS), Murray law based quantitative flow ratio (μFR), and angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR) enable comprehensive wire-free assessment of plaque vulnerability and coronary physiology Purpose We evaluated the impact of intensive lipid-lowering therapy on serial 6-month changes in RWS, μFR, AMR and whether these effects differ between focal and diffuse coronary artery disease (CAD) Methods YELLOW III was a prospective, paired imaging study of patients with stable CAD and lipid-rich, non-obstructive plaques treated with Evolocumab added to high-intensity statin therapy. Coronary angiography and intravascular imaging was performed at baseline and 26 weeks. μFR, RWS, AMR, and virtual pullback pressure gradient (PPG) were analyzed by a blinded core laboratory Results 220 coronary vessels (110 paired baseline and follow-up) were analyzed. Evolocumab therapy was associated with modest but significant improvement in epicardial physiology (both vessel-level µFR and lesion-level ΔµFR improved following maximal lipid lowering therapy [µFRvessel: 0.88 ± 0.084 vs. 0.89 ± 0.088, p &lt; 0.001; ΔµFRlesion: 0.069 ± 0.063 vs. 0.077 ± 0.081, p = 0.028]). and reduction in RWS (16.9 ± 4.2% vs. 14.9 ± 3.5%; p&lt;0.001). AMR did not change (23.2 ± 5.3 vs. 23.8 ± 4.9 mmHg·s/dm; p=0.28). Virtual PPG improved modestly (PPGi: 0.61 ± 0.084 vs. 0.63 ± 0.092, p = 0.038), without systematic reclassification of focal versus diffuse disease. 30% of vessels were reclassified over time; however, overall disease pattern distribution remained unchanged, with a numerically greater transition from diffuse to focal than focal to diffuse disease (17/90, 18.9% vs. 10/90, 11.1%; p = 0.248). While MaxLCBI₄mm was comparable between focal and diffuse disease, diffuse CAD was associated with a higher frequency of LCBI response (82.2% vs. 71.1%, p&lt;0.001). Conclusions Intensive lipid lowering with Evolocumab improves epicardial coronary physiology and reduces RWS without affecting microvascular resistance. Diffuse CAD demonstrates greater lipid responsiveness, suggesting a biologically distinct and therapeutically modifiable disease phenotype.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Serial ai based comprehensive coronary physiological assessment before and after intensive lipid lowering therapy: YELLOW III substudy

abstract: Abstract Introduction Visual estimation of coronary artery disease (CAD) often correlates poorly with functional severity (1). We aimed to evaluate the impact of systematic physiological assessment—incorporating resting full-cycle ratio (RFR), fractional flow reserve (FFR), hydrostatic pressure correction, and pressure predicted microvascular resistance reserve (ppMRR)—on lesion characterization and therapeutic decision-making. Methods We prospectively analyzed 144 intermediate lesions in 114 patients in the Ready registry (2) across three centers. Distal pressure values were refined using individual hydrostatic pressure correction in cases with significant height differences between the catheter tip and the sensor of the pressure wire. Lesions were categorized as non-significant, focal, diffuse, or mixed based on distal RFR and pullback-derived pressure gradients (ΔRFR). Microvascular function was assessed using ppMRR, which integrates visual area stenosis with pressure-derived parameters. Pressure values were defined in most cases, allowing for the investigation of their correlation with resting and hyperemic parameters. Results Therapy recommendations (OMT vs. intervention) based on visual assessment demonstrated poor agreement with both FFR (52.1%, kappa=0.058) and RFR (54.2%, kappa=0.053), frequently overestimating stenosis severity. Reclassification was substantial: diagnostic categorization changed in 65.3% of cases when switching from visual to combined physiological assessment. The application of hydrostatic pressure correction further altered the classification in 25.0% of the total cohort; however, this impact was significantly more pronounced in the LAD (36.2%) compared to non-LAD vessels (4.0%, p &lt; 0.001). Physiological profiles were highly vessel-specific. The LAD exhibited a significantly higher burden of positive physiology (79.8%) compared to the CX (47.8%, p=0.004) and RCA (33.3%, p&lt;0.001). Correspondingly, RFR/FFR discordance was more frequent in the LAD than in non-LAD vessels (33% vs. 16%, p=0.047). Microvascular function differed significantly across phenotypes. The FFR+/RFR- discordant group demonstrated significantly higher ppMRR (3.99 ± 1.81) than both the double-positive (2.96 ± 0.97, p=0.04) and the FFR-/RFR+ groups (2.78 ± 1.02, p=0.01). Overall, microvascular dysfunction (ppMRR &lt; 2.5) was present in 40.6% of cases, with the highest prevalence in the RFR+/FFR- discordant phenotype. Conclusion Visual assessment is frequently inaccurate for defining CAD significance and pattern. Systematic physiological assessment is essential for precise lesion evaluation. Differences in microvascular function (ppMRR) may underlie RFR/FFR discordance. Our findings reinforce that the LAD is a 'different animal' in coronary physiology.Coronary Lesion TypesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.MRR by Discordance PatternFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Vessel specific discrepancies between visual assessment and resting and hyperemic physiological indices

abstract: Abstract Background Impaired flow following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a known predictor of adverse outcomes. The pullback pressure gradient (PPG) is a novel physiological metric that differentiates focal from diffuse disease and enables prediction of post-PCI fractional flow reserve (FFR). This post hoc analysis of the PPG Global (NCT04789317) study aimed to evaluate the prognostic performance of a PPG model for predicting post-PCI FFR and to determine whether the predicted physiological outcome is associated with adverse events following PCI. Methods Prospective and multicenter study including patients with hemodynamically significant coronary artery disease undergoing PCI. A prediction model based on FFR and PPG was used to estimate post-PCI FFR. Based on the predicted values, vessels were classified as having either optimal or suboptimal post-PCI physiology. The primary end point was target vessel failure at 1 year. Target vessel failure was defined as a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, and ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization. Results A total of 855 patients (890 vessels) were analyzed. The mean difference between predicted and measured post-PCI FFR was 0.001 (limits of agreement, –0.10 to 0.10). There was a strong correlation between predicted and measured delta FFR (r=0.92 [95% CI, 0.91–0.93]; P&lt;0.001). Vessels with predicted suboptimal post-PCI physiology had a significantly higher incidence of target vessel failure (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.97 [95% CI, 1.24–3.15]; P=0.004). Predicted suboptimal physiology was independently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Conclusions PPG-predicted post-PCI physiology was associated with target vessel failure at 1 year. These findings extend the role of coronary physiology beyond diagnostic assessment to include risk stratification and outcome prediction following PCI.PPG prediction modelFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
