title: Impact of pullback pressure gradient on clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions

abstract: Abstract Background Heavily Calcified coronary lesions are a challenge for advanced percutaneaous coronary interventions (PCI). While Rotational Atherectomy (RA), Orbital Atherectomy (OA) and Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) are used to modify calcified plaques, their respective impact on microcirculatory function and periprocedural myocardial injury are not fully investigated. Purpose We aimed to compare the physiological and biological safety profiles of RA, OA and IVL. Methods From a monocentric prospective registry, we analyzed 60 consecutive patients (n=20 per group) undergoing PCI for severely calcified lesions using IVL (Shockwave), RA (Rotapro) or OA (Diamonback). Micovascular resistance (AMR) was measured pre- and post-procedure. Periprocedural myocardial injury was assessed by the variation of high-sensitivity troponin (ΔTropo). Statistical analysis for Δtroponin utilized the Kruskal-Wallis test for global comparison and the Dunn test for post-hoc pairwise comparisons due to non-normal distribution. Results Baseline clinical characteristics including age (72.8 ± 8.2 years), LVEF (56.8 ± 10.6 %), and lesion complexity (length &gt;20 mm in 68.3 %), were well-balanced across the groups (p&gt; 0.05). Procedural success (TIMI 3 flow) was achieved in 100% of cases. Significant micocircularoty impairement was observed in mechanical atherectomy groups, with marked increase in AMR for OA (+39.4%, p=0.008) an RA (+14.8 %, p=0.041) whereas AMR remained stable in the AVL group (+14.5 %, p=0.12). Regarding myocardial injury, a significant global difference was found between the three groups (p=0.024). Pairwise comparisons concluded that IVL was associated with significantly lower troponin elevation compared to RA (p=0.018) and OA (p=0.044). No significant difference was observed between OA and RA (p=0.58). Conclusion In patients with severely calcified lesions, IVL preserves microcirculatory function an minimizes periprocedural myocardial injyry more effectively than mechanical atherectomy. While both RA and OA significantly increase micovascular resistance, IVL demonstrates a superior safety profile, with significantly lower troponin release compared to both mechanical techniques.Table1 Baseline Characteristics and OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Exemple of microFR and AMR studyFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comparative impact of intravascular lithotripsy, rotational atherectomy, and orbital atherectomy on microvascular resistance and myocardial injury in complex coronary disease

abstract: Abstract Background Device success is a critical endpoint in PCI, yet its heterogeneous definition limits comparability. The standardized European Association of PCI (EAPCI) device success algorithm was reported in 20201. In this algorithm, device success is evaluated using the following Step1-5: Step1 - attempted to cross lesion with assigned device; Step2 - any device was delivered and implanted to lesion; Step3 - device was implanted at the intended location; Step4 - the first assigned device was successfully implanted; Step5 - final residual % diameter stenosis (%DS) &lt;20% using visual assessment or quantitative coronary angiography (QCA). However, this algorithm has not yet been prospectively applied using core-laboratory adjudication. In addition, the association between device success and lesion-oriented clinical endpoints (LOCE) remains insufficiently investigated. Purpose To prospectively evaluate the EAPCI device success algorithm, incorporating core-lab post-PCI QCA and angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (angio-FFR) into Step 5, and to assess its relationship with 1-year LOCE, in the PIONEER IV trial. Methods PIONEER IV is a multicenter, randomized trial comparing angio-FFR-guided PCI versus usual care using HT Supreme drug-eluting stents. An interim analysis was performed in the first 1270 patients of the total population of 2130. Step 5 of device success was adjudicated using four hierarchical definitions: (1)site-reported (visual residual %DS&lt;20%); (2)core-lab QCA (residual %DS&lt;20%); (3)core-lab angio-FFR (Δangio-FFR across the stent≤0.05); and (4)combined core-lab QCA + angio-FFR. Device success rates as per these definitions were also compared between the angio-FFR (A) and usual care (U) arms. LOCE was the composite of cardiovascular death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, and clinically and physiologically driven target-lesion revascularization. Results Among 1270 patients (1936 lesions), HT Supreme PCI was attempted in 1119 lesions. Site-reported device success rate was 95.2% with no difference between arms (P=0.651). Core-lab QCA reduced success rates to 88.7% (A: 90.3% vs U: 87.0%; P=0.082). Rates using Δangio-FFR≤0.05 were 93.8%, and significantly higher with angio-FFR guidance (A: 96.4% vs U: 91.3%; P&lt;0.001). Combining QCA and angio-FFR reduced success to 84.7%, favoring angio-FFR guidance (A: 88.0% vs U: 81.5%; P=0.003). At 1 year, LOCE was consistently numerically lower in lesions with device success, particularly using the angio-FFR definition (Log-rank P=0.037). Conclusions Operator-reported device success is high, but core-lab QCA and angio-FFR reveal additional abnormalities, favoring angio-FFR-guided PCI. Standardized QCA and post-PCI angio-FFR may support device success as an early trial endpoint. The final patient is expected to complete the 1-year follow-up visit in June 2026. We plan to present device success and LOCE in the 2130-patient full cohort at ESC Congress 2026.Figure AFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure BFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Prospectively applied EAPCI device success algorithm, comparison of angiography-derived FFR guided and usual care, and association with 1-year lesion-oriented clinical endpoints: the PIONEER IV trial

abstract: Abstract Background We sought to quantify the actual proportion of patients who derive clinical benefit from angiography-derived quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-guided PCI and to define the distinct key features that portend potential to optimize procedural decision-making and guidance. Methods In FAVOR III China trial, operators were required to declare all target vessels intended for PCI before randomization based on angiography guidance alone, termed as pre-randomization declared treatment plan. In this study, patients in whom all vessels intended to be treated were physiologically ischemic (offline QFR ≤0.80) and in whom all vessels intended for deferral presented with offline QFR &gt;0.80 were defined as having pre-randomization physiology-concordant plan; otherwise, they were termed as having pre-randomization physiology-nonconcordant plan. The primary outcome of interest for the present study was 2-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Results Among pooled 3,768 patients, it was determined that 1,167 (31.0%) had pre-randomization physiology-nonconcordant plan, including 868 patients (23.0%) with inappropriate treatment, 239 patients (6.3%) had inappropriate deferral, and an additional 60 patients (1.6%) had both inappropriate treatment and deferral. Patients with older age, multivessel disease, LCX or RCA involved, and lower SYNTAX score were found more likely to have pre-randomization physiology-nonconcordant. The primary 2-year MACE rates were 7.6% in patients assigned to QFR-guided group compared to 17.0% in those assigned to angiography-guided group in whom pre-randomization nonconcordant plan was observed (HR 0.43, 95% CI: 0.30-0.61), and in 8.9% vs. 10.4% respectively among patients with a pre-randomization concordant plan (HR 0.85, 95% CI: 0.66-1.09), indicating a significant interaction (interaction P = 0.002). Conclusion Approximately 30% of patients showed a discrepancy between angiography-based treatment plans and physiological ischemia, among whom a substantial prognosis impact for QFR-guided PCI was observed in comparison with standard angiography guidance. Physiology non-concordance of initial treatment plan was a predictable clinical entity by demographic and angiographic characteristics.Central illustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 2-year MACE was 7.6% with QFR guidance versus 17.0% with angiography guidance among patients with a physiology-nonconcordant pre-randomization plan (HR 0.43, 95% CI: 0.30-0.61), and 8.9% versus 10.4% among those with a concordant plan (HR 0.85, 95% CI: 0.66-1.09); interaction P = 0.002.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests that the benefit of QFR-guided PCI is concentrated in the roughly 31.0% of patients whose angiographic plan disagrees with physiology, which bears on targeting wire-free physiology.

title: Who benefits from angiography-derived FFR-guided revascularization? Defining the beneficial population and its key features

abstract: Abstract Introduction Adequate knowledge of the physiological impact and morphological pattern of coronary artery disease (CAD) optimizes therapeutic strategy selection. Hemodynamically significant focal lesions are relatively often effectively treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas diffusely diseased vessels more frequently warrant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or optimal medical therapy (OMT). Clinicians increasingly use pullback measurements to assess disease patterns and improve percutaneous interventions, but the influence on clinical decision-making is relatively unknown. Purpose This ongoing prospective, multicenter registry aims to gain insights on a coronary physiology based treatment strategy by evaluating the relative effectiveness of surgical versus pharmacological treatment strategies for patients with CAD. It also assesses how these three strategies affect the quality of life and angina status up until 1 year of follow-up. Methods This registry recruits patients with hemodynamically significant (Fractional Flow Reserve [FFR} ≤ 0.80, Resting Full-cycle Ratio [RFR] ≤ 0.89) left anterior descending artery (LAD) disease with an involvement of the proximal segment. The COMMIT-LAD group comprises patients with diffuse LAD disease, as proven by a RFR pullback, who had undergone OMT or CABG, and patients with proven focal disease who were treated with Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) guided PCI. The standard group comprises patients who have not undergone such measurements or whose treatment plan deviates from the results of those measurements. During follow-up assessments at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) serve as a primary endpoint, while the quality of life and angina score, serve as secondary endpoints. Results 213 patients have been enrolled in this registry: 64 in the standard group and 149 in the COMMIT-LAD group. Aside from the greater representation of men in the COMMIT-LAD group, the baseline characteristics of the participants are similar across both groups, as is shown in Table 1. To date, 9 MACE events (6.0%) have occurred in the COMMIT-LAD group, compared with 4 events (9.4%) in the standard group. In the standard group, PCI is more frequent, while CABG and OMT are less common (PCI: 82.3% vs 24.2%; CABG: 11.3% vs 39.4%; OMT: 6.5% vs 36.4%; standard vs COMMIT-LAD; p&lt;0.0001). Conclusion Intracoronary functional measurements in stable CAD with hemodynamically significant LAD disease favor CABG and OMT over PCI. This updated interim analysis emphasised the role of plaque burden assessment in treatment decisions. The completed data will provide more insights into it’s impact on clinical outcomes and quality of life.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comprehensive analysis of medical and invasive treatment strategies for patients with significant left anterior descending artery disease (COMMIT-LAD): an interim analysis update

abstract: Abstract Introduction Myocardial bridging (MB) is an acknowledged epicardial structural mechanism of myocardial ischaemia and associated to ischaemia and non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA). Beta-blockers are the most frequently used and recommended drugs for the management of symptomatic MB according to current guidelines and expert consensus. Purpose The aims of this subanalysis are to describe the prevalence of INOCA endotypes among patients with MB and to evaluate their responsiveness to tailored medical therapy in terms of symptoms and quality of life improvement. Materials and methods The analysis was performed on data from the INOCA-IT Registry, which consecutively enrolled patients with angina and/or inducible myocardial ischemia, without obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD), who underwent full invasive coronary functional assessment including acetylcholine provocative testing. This subanalysis investigates the prevalence of INOCA endotypes amongst patients with MB at coronary angiography, and the impact of a stratified therapeutic approach on angina severity and on quality of life via the Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) and EQ-5D-5L questionnaire at baseline and at 12-months clinical follow-up. Results Of 213 patients included in the registry, 38 (17.8%) had a documented MB. Baseline characteristics such as typical cardiovascular risk factors, atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease were comparable to general INOCA patients, as well as the characteristics of angina upon presentation (atypical angina: 7.9% in MB vs 11.4% in no-MB, p=0.525; unstable angina: 5.3% vs 8%, respectively, p=0.562) and the severity assessed via the Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) class (p for overall comparison 0.656). At baseline, 47.3% of MB patients were on beta blockers (BB), whereas 5.3% were taking non-dihydropyridinic calcium channel blockers (NH-CCB). As displayed in Figure 1 the distribution of different INOCA endotypes was significantly different between patients with and without MB. The most frequent endotype amongst patients with MB was the combination of epicardial spasm (ES) and coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), whereas microvascular spasm (MVS) was the rarest (44.7% and 2.6 %, respectively). Therefore, amongst MB patients, 63.2% were treated with first-line NH-CCB, whereas only 23.7% with BB. Tailored medical therapy was effective in improving both the chest pain symptoms in terms of CCS class and SAQ summary score (p&lt;0.001 – Figure 2). Regarding quality of life, the pain and discomfort and usual activity domains of the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire showed improvements, as well as the EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale (EQ VAS). Conclusions MB was detected in 17.8% of patients in the INOCA-IT Registry and the combination of CMD and EP was the most frequent endotype. Tailored medical therapy effectively improved symptoms and quality of life at follow-up.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Endotype distribution and response to tailored medical therapy in patients with myocardial bridging and ischaemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary artery disease (CAD) patients remain at substantial risk of recurrent ischemic symptoms and adverse cardiovascular events even after successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), partly due to persistent endothelial and microvascular dysfunction. Although flow-mediated dilation evaluates conduit artery endothelial function, skin post-occlusive reactive hyperemia (PORH) provides a complementary assessment of systemic microvascular reactivity through multiple vascular pathways. Purpose The purpose of this study was to determine whether impaired skin PORH response is associated with long-term composite cardiovascular outcomes in patients with chronic CAD undergoing PCI. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients with obstructive coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and baseline assessment of skin microvascular function using post-occlusive reactive hyperemia (PORH). Clinical characteristics, laboratory data, and angiographic findings were collected, and participants were followed for long-term cardiovascular outcomes, including cardiac death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, and ischemia-driven revascularization. Patients were stratified according to the median PORH index, and propensity score matching was performed to reduce baseline imbalance. Time-to-event outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with adjustment for relevant clinical covariates. Results Patients with a lower PORH index had a higher burden of cardiovascular risk factors and experienced a significantly greater incidence of long-term composite cardiovascular events compared with those with a higher PORH response. A higher PORH index was independently associated with a reduced risk of composite cardiovascular outcomes in both the overall cohort (adjusted HR 0.422) and the propensity score–matched cohort (adjusted HR 0.331), which was also supported by Kaplan–Meier analyses. Although individual event components and ischemia-driven revascularization showed similar trends, these differences did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions In the present study, a higher PORH index was independently associated with a lower risk of long-term composite CV events in patients with obstructive CAD undergoing PCI, and this inverse association remained robust after PSM. Notably, the composite endpoint incorporated both hard clinical events and ischemic-driven TLR or TVR, reflecting clinically relevant residual ischemic risk after PCI. Patients with a lower PORH index exhibited a higher burden of traditional cardiovascular risk factors, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, prior stroke, and microalbuminuria, consistent with the concept that impaired skin microvascular reactivity reflects a more adverse systemic vascular risk profile.Kaplan–Meier curves of long-term CV outcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Flow chartFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Peripheral microvascular function and long-term cardiovascular outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Background Mechanical LV unloading and coronary revascularization are cornerstone therapies in cardiogenic shock, however, evidence supporting a physiology-guided strategy integrating the extent of revascularization in acute myocardial infarction–related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) is limited Purpose To assess the association between physiology-guided full left ventricular unloading and revascularization strategy, with complete (CR) versus partial (PR), and myocardial recovery and native heart survival (NHS) in patients with AMI-CS Methods We analyzed a registry of patients with AMI-CS treated between January 2022 and June 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of NHS (freedom from death, transplant, or durable LVAD at discharge) and myocardial recovery, defined as left ventricular ejection fraction ≥ 45% at ≥1 year Results Among 179 patients with AMI-CS, 127 required Impella 5.5 for full LV unloading; 65 underwent CR and 62 PR. Despite greater angiographic burden in the PR group, lesion complexity was higher in the CR group (SYNTAX score median 29 [IQR 21–32] vs 25 [IQR 19–28]). Baseline LVEF was comparable between groups (27.6 ± 12.9% vs 25.4 ± 12.1%). The CR group demonstrated significantly higher LVEF at discharge (38.8 ± 13.4% vs 30.5 ± 9.2%) and at 1 year (49.8 ± 15.4% vs 34.7 ± 13.6%), mean difference 15.1% (95% CI 7.8–22.4; p&lt; 0.001). The primary endpoint was achieved in 50.8% of the CR group versus 22.6% of the PR. At 1 year, CR in the setting of full LV unloading was associated with achievement of the primary endpoint. In the adjusted analysis, CR was independently associated with native heart survival and myocardial recovery (OR 3.15, 95% CI 1.62–6.10; p=0.001). Escalation to ECMO and new RRT were similar between groups (15.4% vs 17.7% and 31.0% vs 30.6%, respectively), despite a higher baseline renal risk profile in the CR group. Conclusion In patients with AMI-CS, a physiology-guided strategy integrating full unloading with CR during the index hospitalization was associated with greater NHS and myocardial recovery. These findings support an integrative shock care approach in which mechanical unloading and comprehensive myocardial perfusion are aligned to optimize long-term outcomes.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised single-registry comparison with selection and survivor bias (recovery measured at 1 year or later), and a small sample.
appraisal.one_line: Registry of AMI-related cardiogenic shock treated with Impella 5.5 compares complete with partial revascularisation for native heart survival and myocardial recovery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint was achieved in 50.8% of the complete revascularisation group versus 22.6% of the partial group; adjusted OR 3.15, 95% CI 1.62-6.10; p=0.001. LVEF at 1 year differed by a mean of 15.1% (95% CI 7.8-22.4; p<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Complete revascularisation in shock with full unloading is an open equipoise question; the signal is hypothesis-generating for the extent of revascularisation in AMI-CS.

title: Physiology-guided integration of full left ventricular unloading and coronary revascularization in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Erectile dysfunction (ED) may represent a silent and under-recognised symptom after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), particularly following myocardial infarction (MI). The underlying mechanisms, including the contribution of coronary burden, remain unclear. Purpose To prospectively evaluate determinants of erectile function at 3 months after PCI in MI and non-MI patients and to identify independent predictors of ED. Methods In this prospective observational study (Ethics approval No. 2025.10.39), consecutive male patients undergoing PCI were enrolled. Of 312 screened patients, 186 comprised the 3-month cohort (77 MI; 109 non-MI). Erectile function was assessed using the International Index of Erectile Function-5 at baseline and 3 months. Fear of sexual relations (FSR), demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, laboratory parameters, baseline SYNTAX score and residual SYNTAX score were analysed. Correlation and multivariable regression analyses were performed separately for MI and non-MI patients. Longer-term follow-up is ongoing. Results At 3 months, ED was more prevalent in MI than in non-MI patients (92.2% vs 79.8%). FSR showed a strong inverse correlation with erectile function in MI patients (rho = -0.692, p &lt; 0.001) and a weaker association in non-MI patients (rho = -0.532, p &lt; 0.001). In multivariable analysis including clinical and anatomical variables, FSR independently predicted worse erectile outcomes only in the MI group, whereas coronary anatomical indices were not significant determinants at this time point. Conclusion(s) ED after PCI, particularly following MI, appears to be influenced by fear of sexual relations within a multifactorial framework. Early sexual counselling and structured reassurance regarding safe resumption of physical and sexual activity may facilitate recovery.Baseline caharacteristics of the groupsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Predictors of EDFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Determinants of erectile dysfunction in the early phase after percutaneous coronary intervention: a prospective comparative analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with cancer who develop acute myocardial infarction (AMI) are frequently managed conservatively due to concerns regarding competing mortality risks and bleeding. The long-term benefit of invasive management, particularly percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), in this population remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluated the utilization of invasive strategies and the association of PCI with long-term cardiovascular and cancer-specific outcomes in patients with AMI and cancer. Methods This longitudinal cohort study included 500,876 UK Biobank participants (54.4% women) enrolled between 2006–2010, with follow-up to October 31, 2022 (median 14.0 years). Among 68,873 participants diagnosed with cancer, 3,121 developed AMI (1,529 post-cancer AMI). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). Analyses included propensity score matching (PSM) for PCI/CABG versus no revascularization and competing risk models for cause-specific mortality. Results Patients with post-cancer AMI were significantly less likely to undergo coronary angiography, PCI, or CABG compared with patients without prior cancer (p&lt;0.01, respectively), with the lowest PCI utilization observed in those with metastatic disease (40.1% vs. 72.8% in non-metastatic, p&lt;0.01). After propensity matching, PCI was associated with significant reductions in long-term mortality and MACCE in both STEMI and NSTEMI presentations, irrespective of metastatic status (all p&lt;0.05). In competing-risk analyses, PCI was independently associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56–0.87) and cancer-specific mortality (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.53–0.71). Older age, frailty, smoking, socioeconomic deprivation, and cardiometabolic comorbidities were independent predictors of adverse outcomes, according to multivariable Cox regression analyses. Conclusions Cancer patients with AMI experience markedly worse long-term outcomes and are less likely to receive invasive management, particularly post-cancer AMI with metastasis. PCI is associated with significant long-term reductions in both cardiovascular and cancer-related mortality, including in advanced malignancy. These findings support consideration of an invasive strategy in appropriately selected cancer patients presenting with AMI.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

title: Underutilization of invasive management and its association with long-term outcomes in cancer patients with acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Lipid-rich plaques can cause distal embolization and slow flow/no-reflow (SFNR) during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), leading to adverse clinical outcomes. Perfusion balloons (PB), enabling prolonged dilatation while maintaining distal perfusion, have been reported to reduce distal embolization and SFNR. However, their mechanistic impact on lipid-rich plaques remains incompletely understood. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the impact of PB on lipid core plaques in high-risk lesions using near-infrared spectroscopy–intravascular ultrasound (NIRS-IVUS), assessing changes in maxLCBI4mm, lipid core plaque area, and intraprocedural SFNR. Methods This single-center retrospective study was conducted on consecutive patients who underwent NIRS-IVUS-guided PCI between January 2025 and January 2026. Lesions with a pre-procedural maxLCBI4mm ≥400 were analyzed. We excluded patients with stentless procedures or poor image quality. Patients were categorized into the PB group and the conventional balloon (CB) group based on the balloon type used prior to stent implantation. Transient SFNR was defined as a TIMI flow grade ≤2 occurring during the procedure, followed by recovery to TIMI 3 flow by the end of PCI after adjunctive treatments, including intracoronary vasodilators, whereas final SFNR was defined as a TIMI flow grade ≤2 on the final angiogram. Plaque burden was assessed by IVUS, and lipid core plaque area was quantified pre- and post-procedure at the same location using ImageJ software from longitudinal frames derived from NIRS chemograms. Serial NIRS-IVUS measurements were obtained at matched segments before balloon dilatation, after dilatation, and after stenting using anatomical landmarks and constant-speed pullback. Results Of the 44 patients undergoing NIRS-IVUS-guided PCI during the study period, 29 cases were included in the analysis (PB, n=16; CB, n=13). Balloon length (PB: 20.0 mm vs. CB: 10.0 mm, p&lt;0.001) and inflation time (PB: 180 s vs. CB: 20 s, p&lt;0.001) differed between groups, whereas other baseline characteristics were comparable. Transient SFNR occurred in 1 patient (6.3%) in the PB group and 5 patients (38.5%) in the CB group (p=0.064). No statistically significant differences were observed in reductions of maxLCBI4mm or lipid core plaque area. However, the PB group showed a tendency toward a smaller reduction in lipid core plaque area after balloon dilatation (PB: −7.4% vs. CB: −35.2%, p=0.159). Conclusion(s) Prolonged dilatation using a PB may potentially reduce distal embolization by preventing rapid dispersion of lipid-rich plaque components during PCI. Although no statistically significant difference was observed in this small cohort, the PB demonstrated a tendency toward reduced SFNR incidence and decreased lipid-rich plaque disruption, suggesting a potential mechanism for microvascular protection.NIRS-IVUS chemograms pre- and post-ballooningFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.PB vs CB: Baseline, imaging and outcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Perfusion balloon prolonged inflation in lipid-rich coronary lesions and slow flow/no-reflow: NIRS-IVUS insights

abstract: Abstract Background Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) is an important component in the management of cardiogenic shock and high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, contemporary descriptive data on tMCS use in these settings are limited, despite the recent publications of potentially practice-changing randomised controlled trials, including DANGER-SHOCK and ECLS-SHOCK (1,2). Purpose To describe current patient characteristics and clinical outcomes associated with the use of tMCS, including intra-aortic balloon pumps (IABP), microaxial flow pumps, and veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), in patients undergoing PCI, without performing any comparative analysis between devices. Methods We included the first-time event of patients recorded in the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry (SCAAR) undergoing PCI with support from IABP, VA-ECMO or microaxial flow pump between September 2019 and 27 August 2025. For patients admitted to a cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) during the admission, data were linked to the Register of Information and Knowledge about Swedish Heart Intensive Care Admissions (RIKS-HIA). Patient characteristics, procedural indications, timing of procedure, antithrombotic treatment, and outcomes were assessed separately for each tMCS. Results A total of 401 patients were included: 153 treated with IABP, 128 with VA-ECMO, and 120 with a microaxial flow pump. Median ages were 67, 62, and 70 years, respectively. ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) was the most common indication for PCI across groups (65% for IABP, 59% for VA-ECMO, and 44% for microaxial flow pump. Presentation with Killip class III or IV occurred in 63%, 71%, and 43% of patients in the respective groups. In the catheterisation laboratory, cangrelor was administered in 56% of IABP cases, 64% of VA-ECMO cases, and 32% of microaxial flow pump cases. Thirty-day mortality was 45% for IABP, 50% for VA-ECMO, and 24% for microaxial flow pump recipients, increasing to 58%, 63%, and 31% at one year. Among patients discharged alive from the CICU, one-year mortality was 7.4%, 7.0%, and 2.5%, respectively. Three procedure-related deaths were recorded: two in the IABP group and one in the microaxial flow pump group. Conclusion Use of tMCS in patients undergoing coronary PCI varied by device type and clinical presentation. tMCS were most frequently used in STEMI and commonly used in patients with cardiogenic shock (Killip class III or IV). VA-ECMO was regularly used in cardiac arrest. Despite high overall mortality, outcomes among surviving patients discharged from CICU were favourable.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Contemporary use and outcomes of temporary mechanical circulatory support in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Remnant cholesterol (RC), reflecting the cholesterol content of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, has been implicated in residual atherosclerotic risk. However, data regarding its prognostic significance in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain limited, particularly concerning the differentiation between ischaemic and fatal outcomes over the long term. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the association between baseline RC and 10-year clinical outcomes in a large Chinese PCI cohort and to assess its incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors. Methods This retrospective cohort study analysed 9,095 consecutive patients undergoing PCI at the Hospital in 2013. Individuals with extreme lipid outliers were excluded. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), repeat revascularisation, and stroke. Results During a median follow-up of 10.4 years, 3,450 (37.9%) MACCE occurred. Multivariable Cox regression analysis demonstrated that the highest RC quartile was associated with a significantly elevated risk of MACCE compared with the lowest quartile (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10–1.34; P &lt; 0.001). Notably, elevated RC was strongly associated with recurrent ischaemic events, including incident MI (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.11–1.69) and repeat revascularisation (HR 1.19, 95% CI 1.05–1.36). Conversely, no significant independent association was identified between RC and all-cause mortality (P = 0.060) or cardiac death (P = 0.390) in the fully adjusted model. Subgroup analyses indicated a robust risk association, particularly in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome. Furthermore, adding RC to the conventional risk model significantly improved risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement: 0.042, P = 0.010). Conclusion(s) In this large cohort of PCI patients with extended follow-up, elevated baseline RC levels were independently associated with long-term ischaemic events, specifically MI and revascularisation, but not with fatal outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of RC as a distinct marker for residual ischaemic risk and suggest that it provides incremental prognostic value beyond established risk factors.Kaplan-Meier curves of incidence for MACCEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Remnant cholesterol and residual ischemic risk after percutaneous coronary intervention: a 10-year real-world cohort study

abstract: Abstract Introduction Drug coated balloons (DCB) in de novo large vessel disease and in acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain under scrutiny with a paucity of data. Purpose This study reports on outcomes of a DCB only strategy compared to a drug eluting stent (DES) only strategy in large epicardial coronary arteries in an ACS population. Methods Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data on all ACS patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) from January 2021 to June 2025. The primary outcome was medium to long term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Results There were 247 patients in the DCB arm with treated large epicardial vessels &gt;3mm) and they were matched with 247 patients treated with DES. The median age was 64 (58-74) in the DCB group and 64 (57-73) in the DES group. No significant difference in MACE at median 21-month follow-up between the DCB and DES groups (10.1% vs 11.7%, p=0.94, all-cause mortality (5.3% vs 8.1%, p=0.44) or repeat revascularisation (4.9% vs 4.5%, p=0.49) in the DCB group compared to the DES group. Conclusion The medium-term clinical outcome following the use of a DCB only strategy in large vessel in ACS patient population was comparable to a DES only strategy.KM Graph of MACE after DCB and DES strategiesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Outcomes following percutaneous coronary revascularisation in acute coronary syndromes: a comparison of drug coated balloon versus drug eluting stent strategies in de novo large epicardial vessels

abstract: Abstract Background In percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) lesions with plaque continuity to the ostium, the optimal revascularization strategy remains controversial. Previous studies have suggested that left main (LM)–to–LAD crossover stenting may reduce repeat revascularization compared with focal ostial stenting1, although acceptable outcomes have also been reported with ostium-only stenting when lesion coverage is appropriate. With the increasing use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) under intravascular imaging guidance, whether outcomes differ according to the final treatment strategy remains unclear2. Methods Between April 2023 and March 2025, 146 consecutive patients undergoing PCI for LAD lesions with angiographically and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-confirmed ostial plaque continuity were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were classified into three groups according to the final strategy: DCB-only (n=28), crossover stenting from the left main trunk (n=65), and ostium stenting (n=53). LAD ostial plaque burden was assessed by IVUS as percentage plaque area (plaque area/vessel area). Clinical endpoints included major adverse cardiac events (MACE: target lesion revascularization [TLR], cardiac death, or myocardial infarction) and target vessel revascularization (TVR). Results Crossover stenting was more frequently selected in lesions extending from the left main trunk (p=0.011), whereas debulking devices were more commonly used in the DCB group (p&lt;0.001). Baseline and post-preparation plaque burden differed among groups (DCB vs. crossover vs. ostium stenting: 42.7±19.6% vs. 53.4±17.8% vs. 44.2±15.7%; p=0.026), with the highest burden observed in the crossover stent group. However, at final IVUS assessment, plaque burden became significantly smaller in the crossover stent group (p=0.048). Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated no significant differences among the three strategies in MACE (p=0.24), TLR (p=0.25), or TVR (p=0.97). Among 13 patients in the ostium stenting group with residual uncovered plaque, additional DCB angioplasty did not affect clinical outcomes. Conclusion When lesion attachment and plaque burden are appropriately assessed, finalization with DCB or ostium stenting achieves clinical outcomes comparable to crossover stenting for LAD lesions extending to the ostium, without compromising mid-term results.
title: Outcomes of drug-coated balloon, crossover stenting, and ostium stenting for LAD lesions with ostial plaque continuity: an IVUS-guided comparative study

abstract: Abstract Background and aims Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) and transcatheter-based valve therapies are performed with increasing frequency. However, the amount of waste generated during these procedures and the associated environmental burden remain largely unknown. Methods This prospective lifecycle assessment and modelling study was conducted at a tertiary center. Waste generated during ten cases of the five most common procedure types (diagnostic coronary angiography, PCI, complex PCI, transcatheter aortic valve implantation [TAVI], and transcatheter edge-to-edge repair [TEER]) was assessed. Procedural waste was classified into incinerable waste, paper/cardboard, recyclable plastics, hazardous medical waste, and sharps waste. A partial lifecycle assessment was performed focusing exclusively on the waste disposal phase to isolate the environmental burden attributable to waste treatment. Environmental footprint analysis was conducted using openLCA software with the ecoinvent database and the EF v3.1 method, integrating 16 environmental impact categories into a single normalized score (micropoints, µPt). Study endpoints were (1) total waste per procedure and distribution across waste categories, and (2) ecological footprint under three disposal models: waste separation (model 1), full municipal incineration (model 2), and full hazardous incineration (model 3). Results Across all procedures, median waste per case was 7.68 kg (IQR 4.72–14.37), ranging from 3.54 kg (IQR 3.42–3.88) for diagnostic coronary angiography to 17.51 kg (IQR 15.15–18.56) for TEER. Overall waste composition consisted predominantly of incinerable waste (70.8%). The environmental burden ranged from 246 µPt for diagnostic angiography to 724 µPt for TEER. Based on procedure volumes at the study center, the five analyzed procedure types generate an estimated total of 15.24 tons of waste annually. Scenario modelling demonstrated a strong association between disposal strategy and environmental burden. The ecological footprint per average procedure ranged from 477.95 µPt (15.85 kg CO₂-eq) to 506.76 µPt (16.59 kg CO₂-eq) and reached 1272.11 µPt (22.98 kg CO₂-eq) for models 1, 2, and 3, respectively. These values correspond to gasoline-vehicle travel equivalents of approximately 25.3 km, 26.9 km, and 67.4 km for models 1–3, respectively. Economic modelling showed similar trends (costs hazardous-only disposal vs. waste separation +422%). Extrapolation to Germany indicates that these procedure types generate approximately 4,022 tons of waste annually, and, even under waste separation, an environmental burden equivalent to driving nearly 22 million kilometres per year (≈544 Earth circumferences). Conclusion Interventional cardiology procedures generate substantial amounts of waste, and its disposal alone results in a measurable environmental footprint and CO₂ burden. Simple waste separation strategies can reduce environmental impact and costs.Grapical_AbstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure_1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Waste production and environmental impact in interventional cardiology: a lifecycle assessment and modelling study

abstract: Abstract Background In-hospital mortality and causes of death after elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are not well elucidated in contemporary practice. Purpose To investigate causes of in-hospital death in patients undergoing elective PCI. Methods Data were derived from the Beijing PCI (BJ-PCI) registry between 2010 and 2022. Across 60 hospitals in Beijing, patients who underwent elective coronary procedures were screened. Information of in-hospital deaths were submitted to the Beijing Quality Control and Improvement Center for Cardiovascular Intervention every month. The causes of death were judged and finally confirmed by a review board quarterly, and were classified as procedure-related or disease-related. Results Among 1,907,498 patients who underwent elective coronary procedures from 2010 to 2022, 644,577 patients receiving elective PCI were included. A total of 720 in-hospital deaths were reported, with a overall in-hospital mortality of 0.11% (ranging from 0.08% to 0.15% across years). There were 389 (53.89%) deaths were procedure-related, with mechanical complications of 22.36% , stent thrombosis of 13.47%, and acute coronary occlusion of 12.22%, aortic dissection of 2.78%, PCI-related bleeding of 2.08%, and anaphylactic shock of 1.11%. In 331 (46.11%) patients with disease-related deaths, heart failure was the first cause of death contributing to 18.47%, followed by multiple organ failure of 9.31%. Ischemic stroke of 7.64% , severe infection of 6.81%, and pulmonary embolism of 2.08%. Compared with disease-related deaths, patients with procedure-related deaths were younger (68.20±10.52 vs 72.34±10.70 years, p&lt;0.001) and more often died within 72 hours after PCI (59.38% vs 22.36%, p&lt;0.001). Hospitals with annual PCI volumes above the median (&gt;327 cases/year) had lower mortality than those below the median (0.067% vs 0.538%, p &lt; 0.001). Tertiary hospitals demonstrated a lower mortality than non-tertiary hospitals (0.074% vs 0.288%, p &lt; 0.001). Conclusion In-hospital mortality after elective PCI persistently at a low level in Beijing from 2010 to 2022, more than half of deaths were attributable to procedure-related complications. Mortality differed substantially by hospital PCI volume and hospital level.
title: 2010–2022 in-hospital mortality and causes of death after elective PCI in China: a multicenter real-world study

abstract: Abstract Background Sex differences after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are well recognized1; however, women undergoing PCI are typically older and have greater comorbidity burden2, making it uncertain whether outcome disparities persist within an elderly population. As contemporary PCI populations are increasingly aged ≥65 years, understanding sex-specific risks in this group is clinically important for treatment planning and follow-up strategies. Purpose We aimed to evaluate sex-specific clinical outcomes after PCI among elderly patients and to determine whether men and women demonstrate distinct post-procedural risk profiles after adjustment for baseline characteristics. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global collaborative network. Patients aged ≥65 years diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome, undergoing PCI were identified and stratified by sex. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed, adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), cardiovascular comorbidities, and medications. Outcomes at 1 year included major bleeding (primary outcome), all-cause mortality, repeat revascularization, new onset of atrial fibrillation (AF), and all-cause hospitalization. Hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Results A total of 142,885 patients were identified before matching. After propensity score matching, 50,547 matched pairs were included in the analysis. At 1 year, women had a higher risk of major bleeding compared with men (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.068 – 1.196, p-value &lt; 0.0001), and higher all-cause hospitalization (HR 1.061, 95% CI 1.042 – 1.081, p-value &lt; 0.0001). All-cause mortality was similar between groups (HR 1.014, 95% CI 0.976 – 1.054, p-value = 0.4807). Men had higher risks of repeat revascularization (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.833 – 0.887, p-value &lt; 0.0001) and new-onset AF (HR 0.907, 95% CI 0.859 – 0.958, p-value = 0.0004). Conclusion In elderly PCI patients, sex differences were more pronounced for safety than survival: women experienced higher bleeding risk, whereas men had higher repeat revascularization. These findings support sex-aware risk assessment when tailoring post-PCI antithrombotic and follow-up strategies.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2.Major BleedingFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Gender matters more for safety than survival after PCI in elderly patients

abstract: Abstract Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with increased ischemic and bleeding risk in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk (ARC-HBR) classifies severe CKD as a major and moderate CKD as a minor criterion; however, the performance of modified ARC-HBR criteria within a CKD population remains uncertain. Purpose This study aimed to validate a modified version of the Academic Research Consortium High Bleeding Risk (ARC-HBR) criteria in PCI patients with CKD and to evaluate its prognostic performance according to CKD severity and HBR burden. Methods This retrospective study included consecutive PCI patients with baseline CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] &lt;60 mL/min/1.73m²) treated at a large tertiary care academic center in the United States between 2012 and 2022. Patients with cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, or missing follow-up data were excluded. HBR status was defined according to ARC-HBR criteria, excluding moderate and severe CKD to avoid circular risk attribution. The primary endpoint was 1-year bleeding (in-hospital or post-discharge). The key secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all-cause death, myocardial infarction (MI), or stroke. Associations between HBR status and outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline variables showing significant imbalance between groups. Stratified analyses of endpoints were performed according to CKD severity based on eGFR (moderate CKD [30–59 mL/min/1.73m²] and severe CKD [&lt;30 mL/min/1.73m²]). Results Among 7,388 CKD patients undergoing PCI, 4,320 (58.5%) met the modified ARC-HBR definition. Moderate-to-severe anemia was the most prevalent major criterion, while age &gt;75 years was the most common minor criterion. Compared with non-HBR patients, those classified as HBR were older, more frequently female, and had a greater burden of comorbidities. At 1 year, HBR status was associated with a significantly higher risk of bleeding (10.5% vs. 4.5%; HR 2.21, 95% CI 1.83–2.67; p&lt;0.001), predominantly driven by in-hospital events, as well as a 2.15-fold increased risk of MACE, largely due to all-cause mortality and spontaneous MI. Stratified analyses according to CKD severity demonstrated differential prognostic patterns: in moderate CKD, modified HBR criteria preserved strong discrimination for both bleeding and ischemic outcomes; conversely, in severe CKD, bleeding risk remained elevated, whereas incremental discrimination for ischemic outcomes was attenuated (Figure). Conclusion In PCI patients with CKD, a modified ARC-HBR definition excluding renal impairment provides effective risk stratification. Importantly, its stage-specific performance supports the classification of severe CKD as a major and moderate CKD as a minor ARC-HBR criterion.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: CKD severity and high bleeding risk in patients undergoing PCI: stage-specific validation of modified ARC-HBR criteria

abstract: Abstract Background Optical coherence tomography (OCT) influences decision-making during metallic drug-eluting stent implantation, but its procedural impact during bioresorbable scaffold (BRS) implantation is less well defined. Because polymeric BRS are radiolucent, have thick struts, and have limited overexpansion tolerance, an OCT-based, BRS-specific workflow may be particularly valuable. Purpose To quantify OCT-driven intraprocedural strategy changes and acute post-procedural OCT imaging outcomes after OCT-guided BRS implantation. Methods In a single-center prospective observational cohort (March 2021–March 2024), angiography–OCT co-registration was used to guide BRS implantation during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in 172 lesions (170 patients) using a prespecified STOP-HEAD algorithm (STOP: sizing, taper assessment, overlap avoidance, preparation; HEAD: high-pressure post-dilatation and OCT assessment of scaffold expansion, apposition, and edge dissections). Treatment plans based on angiography alone were recorded and compared with plans after pre-PCI OCT; post-PCI OCT findings and any additional optimisation were documented. Post-procedural OCT metrics included scaffold expansion index (SEI) and minimum scaffold eccentricity index (SEC). Results Most lesions were in the left anterior descending artery (71.2%), and a single scaffold was implanted in 95.9%. OCT changed operator decision-making in 79% of lesions (136/172). Pre-PCI OCT altered the procedural plan in 76% (131/172), including changes in lesion preparation (unplanned cutting/scoring balloon use in 33%), scaffold diameter selection (35%), and scaffold length selection (52%). Post-PCI OCT prompted further optimisation in 15% (26/172) due to scaffold malapposition (8%) and/or scaffold underexpansion (12%) not detected by angiography. Final SEI was 0.83±0.11 and minimum SEC was 0.72±0.08; both indices were lowest in calcified lesions. Final TIMI 3 flow was achieved in all treated vessels. Conclusion Even in angiographically selected lesions considered suitable for BRS implantation, systematic OCT guidance within a prespecified STOP-HEAD workflow frequently changes procedural planning and identifies residual deployment issues requiring further optimisation, supporting routine pre- and post-implantation OCT to refine preparation, sizing, and scaffold optimisation.Figure 1 BRS-specific STOP workflowFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2 BRS-speific HEAD WorkflowFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Optical coherence tomography guidance during bioresorbable scaffold implantation: intraprocedural decision-making and post-procedural imaging outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background Routine angiographic follow-up (RAF) after drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation generally does not improve clinical outcomes and may increase revascularization rates. However, patients with multivessel disease (MVD) may require closer monitoring due to worse clinical outcomes compared with those with single-vessel disease. We evaluated the impact of RAF on long-term clinical outcomes in patients with MVD treated with DES. Methods This study included 1,774 patients with MVD treated with DES between January 2004 and June 2021. Patients who experienced unexpected death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or revascularization within 6 months post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were excluded. RAF was defined as scheduled angiography performed at the physician's discretion. Patients were categorized into two groups: the clinical follow-up (CF) group (n = 1,024) and the RAF group (n = 750). We compared 5-year major clinical outcomes between the groups using propensity score matching (PSM) to adjust for baseline confounders. Results After PSM, 624 matched pairs were generated, with well-balanced baseline characteristics between the CF and RAF groups. Up to 5 years, the RAF group had significantly higher rates of target lesion revascularization (HR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.29–3.01) and target vessel revascularization (HR: 1.75, 95% CI: 1.25–2.46), but showed a trend toward lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.37–1.01, P = 0.055). In a landmark analysis beyond 1 year, the RAF group showed no significant difference in repeat PCI, but demonstrated significantly lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.31–0.94), as well as lower risks of major adverse cardiac events (MACE; HR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.48–0.95) and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE; HR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.50–0.95) compared with the CF group. Conclusions In patients with MVD treated with DES, RAF was associated with higher revascularization rates compared to CF. However, RAF may be associated with improved survival and better long-term composite clinical outcomes.RAF_MVD_PCI -Rha.pngFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of routine angiographic follow-up on long-term clinical outcomes in patients with multivessel disease underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) are novel metabolic biomarkers in coronary heart disease, both of which have shown certain value in risk stratification and prognosis evaluation. However, the prognostic value of their combination in predicting adverse outcomes in the special population of elderly patients aged≥65 years with coronary artery disease(CAD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has not been fully investigated. Purpose This study,based on a cohort of elderly patients aged≥65 years with CAD undergoing PCI,aims to explore the clinical value of the combination of TyG index and SHR in predicting adverse prognosis in this high-risk population. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 1202 CAD elderly patients aged≥65 years undergoing PCI from December 2017 to January 2024. Patients were divided into 4 groups (G1 to G4) based on the median TyG index (T1: TyG&lt;8.87; T2: TyG≥8.87) and median SHR index (Q1: SHR&lt;0.84; Q2: SHR≥0.84). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs) at the 12-month follow-up, which included all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, unplanned repeat revascularization, and stroke. Cox proportional hazards model, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and subgroup analysis were employed to access associations between the combined TyG index and SHR with MACCEs.A nomogram was developed using multivariable logistic regression models, incorporating SHR, TyG index, and variables identified by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to further elucidate the predictive performance of each individual factor. Result The cohort had a median age of 75.1±5.5 years(69.6–80.6 years), with 62.4% male (750/1202). Fully adjusted Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated that, compared with the reference group (TyG&lt;8.72 and SHR&lt;0.84), patients with both TyG≥8.72 and SHR≥0.84 had the highest risk of MACCEs (HR 2.66, 95% CI 1.66–4.27,p&lt;0.001). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis confirmed a linear positive correlation between the TyG index and MACCEs (P for overall: 0.004, P for non−linearity: 0.118). SHR exhibited a J-shaped relationship with MACCEs (P for overall: 0.019, P for non−linearity: 0.048), with an ideal SHR of 0.84. Following feature selection via LASSO regression,the key predictors identified and incorporated into the predictive nomogram model, which includes SHR, TyG index, previous PCI,Barthel, hypersensitive C-reactive protein,weight, white blood cell and 7 other variables.SHAP analysis revealed that SHR and TyG index were the most influential predictors. Conclusion This study find that the combined assessment of the TyG index and SHR provides a robust basis for prognostic stratification in elderly CAD patients undergoing PCI.RCS analysis of SHR and the TyG indexFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.nomogram & SHAP analysisFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Predictive value of combined Triglyceride glucose index and stress hyperglycemia ratio for adverse prognosis in elderly patients with coronary artery disease after percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Current international guidelines strongly recommend Heart Team–based decision-making using integrated anatomical and clinical risk scores, including SYNTAX II and EuroSCORE II, to guide selection between percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in patients with multivessel coronary artery disease. However, real-world adherence to these recommendations in centers without on-site cardiac surgery remains insufficiently studied. Objectives To retrospectively evaluate real-world concordance between SYNTAX II– and EuroSCORE II–derived revascularization recommendations and actual treatment decisions in a tertiary hospital without on-site cardiac surgery, and to identify predictors of guideline discordance. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center analysis of 270 consecutive patients evaluated for coronary revascularization between 2023 and 2024. SYNTAX II and EuroSCORE II were calculated retrospectively by two experienced interventional cardiologists blinded to treatment decisions. Guideline-based recommendations (PCI, CABG, or either) were compared with the revascularization strategy performed in practice. Predictors of discordance were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Results Overall concordance between guideline-derived recommendations and real-world management was highly asymmetric. Concordance was high when SYNTAX II favored PCI (81%), but markedly low when CABG was recommended (16%). A CABG recommendation was the sole independent predictor of discordance, conferring a &gt;20-fold increased likelihood of deviation from guideline-based management (OR ≈23, p&lt;0.001). Notably, age, frailty score, left ventricular function, renal function, EuroSCORE II, and major cardiovascular risk factors were not associated with discordance. Conclusions In hospitals without on-site cardiac surgery, guideline-recommended CABG strategies are frequently not implemented, independent of patient risk or anatomical complexity. This systematic deviation reflects institutional and structural constraints rather than patient-level clinical judgment, revealing a critical implementation gap in contemporary revascularization care. These findings highlight the urgent need for adaptive Heart Team models, inter-institutional pathways, or guideline frameworks that explicitly account for institutional capabilities.
title: Guideline–Practice Mismatch in Coronary Revascularization at Hospitals Without On-Site Cardiac Surgery: A SYNTAX II and EuroSCORE II–Based Real-World Analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Evidence regarding the prognostic impact of optical coherence tomography (OCT) guidance in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), particularly those without complex angiographic lesions, remains limited. Purpose To determine the impact of OCT-guided versus angiography-guided stent implantation on clinical outcomes in ACS patients. Methods Between January 2023 and October 2023, 1668 ACS patients who underwent coronary stent implantation were retrospectively enrolled. Patients were divided into the OCT-guided group (n=998) and the angiography-guided group (n=670) based on whether OCT imaging alone was used during PCI. The primary endpoint was 2-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiac death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and ischemia-driven revascularization. Subgroup analysis was performed based on the presence of complex coronary lesions (as defined in the RENOVATE-COMPLEX-PCI study). Results The mean age of all patients was 62.4±10.4 years, with 67.1% were male. Compared with the angiography-guided group, the OCT-guided group had fewer stents implanted, larger stent and post-dilation balloon diameters, and higher post-dilation rates (all P&lt;0.05). The OCT-guided group had a significantly lower incidence of 2-year MACE than the angiography-guided group (6.6% vs. 13.0%, P&lt;0.001), primarily attributed to a significantly lower incidence of cardiac death (1.5% vs. 7.5%, P&lt;0.001) and non-fatal myocardial infarction (0.5% vs. 2.4%, P=0.001) in the OCT-guided group. After adjustment for clinical and angiographic characteristics, multivariate Cox regression analyses showed that OCT guidance was independently associated with a reduced risk of 2-year MACE (HR=0.53, 95%CI: 0.37-0.76), non-fatal myocardial infarction (HR=0.23, 95%CI: 0.08-0.62), cardiac death (HR=0.35, 95%CI: 0.17-0.71), and all-cause death (HR=0.49, 95%CI: 0.28-0.84) compared to angiography guidance. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that OCT guidance, compared with angiography guidance, significantly reduced the incidence of 2-year MACE in both the complex lesion group (8.2% vs. 17.5%, P&lt;0.001) and the non-complex lesion group (5.4% vs. 10.1%, P=0.003), with P for interaction=0.526. After adjustment for clinical and other angiographic characteristics, the results remained consistent. Conclusion Compared with angiography guidance, OCT-guided stent implantation significantly reduced the risk of 2-year MACE in ACS patients, regardless of the presence of complex lesions.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: The impact of OCT-guided coronary stent implantation on clinical outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background In chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) patients undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography (CAG), angiographic findings guide the decision to perform an ad-hoc percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). In contemporary practice, clopidogrel is initiated either several days before CAG (outpatient preloading) or administered as a loading dose in the catheterization laboratory directly before PCI. Currently, no clear consensus exists regarding the optimal timing for clopidogrel initiation for CCS patients undergoing a diagnostic CAG. Purpose To evaluate whether in-laboratory clopidogrel loading is noninferior to outpatient preloading of clopidogrel at -3 days in CCS patients who are planned to undergo diagnostic CAG with optional ad-hoc PCI. Methods In this prospective monthly cluster randomization trial, the rates of net adverse clinical events (NACE, a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, definite/probable stent thrombosis, stroke and bleeding academic research consortium type 2, 3 or 5 bleeding) within 30 days were compared between patients with an outpatient preloading strategy vs an in-laboratory loading strategy. In-laboratory loading consisted of a 600mg clopidogrel loading dose in the catheterization laboratory in case of an ad-hoc PCI. Preloading was defined as a 300mg clopidogrel loading dose on day -3, followed by 75mg clopidogrel daily until the day of CAG (day 0). Secondary endpoints included NACE at 30 days in the overall cohort and a pre-specified interaction analysis for high bleeding risk (HBR), as defined as an Academic Research Consortium HBR score ≥2. We determined that inclusion of 1462 patients would be needed to demonstrate noninferiority (80% power, margin 4%). The study was prematurely terminated after 2.5 years and the inclusion of 768 patients due to slow recruitment. Results Of 768 patients included (in-laboratory loading n=408, preloading n=360, mean age 66 years, 32% female), 98% completed the 30-day follow-up. HBR was observed in 17% (in-laboratory 19% vs preloading 15%). Rates of performed PCI were similar (in-laboratory 36% vs preloading 34%, p=0.53). At 30-day follow-up, the incidence of NACE was comparable between the in-hospital and the preloading group in patients who underwent PCI (Fig A). Similarly, NACE, as well as its individual endpoint rates did not differ significantly in the overall cohort undergoing diagnostic CAG (in-laboratory 7% vs preloading 10%, OR 0.69 [0.40–1.16 95% CI], p=0.16). No significant interaction was observed between HBR status and clopidogrel loading strategy (p-interaction 0.74). Conclusions Among CCS patients undergoing diagnostic CAG with potential ad-hoc PCI, in-laboratory loading was not associated with an increased incidence of NACE, as compared to outpatient preloading of clopidogrel. These findings suggest that in-laboratory loading of clopidogrel may represent a safe and more selective alternative to routine outpatient preloading.Figure BFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure AFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective monthly cluster randomisation trial; 768 patients included (in-laboratory loading n=408, preloading n=360) against a planned 1462, terminated after 2.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Terminated at 768 of 1462 planned patients, so non-inferiority (4% margin) was not formally tested at the planned power; cluster allocation by month.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective monthly cluster-randomised trial comparing in-laboratory clopidogrel loading with outpatient preloading in chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing angiography with possible ad-hoc PCI; stopped early for slow recruitment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the overall cohort NACE at 30 days was 7% with in-laboratory loading versus 10% with preloading (OR 0.69 [0.40-1.16 95% CI], p=0.16); no significant interaction with HBR status (p-interaction 0.74).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs pre-treatment practice in chronic coronary syndrome, where guideline advice on clopidogrel timing before angiography is unsettled; results are compatible with a selective in-laboratory strategy.

title: Clopidogrel in-laboratory versus outpatient preloading in chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography with potential ad-hoc percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Radial access is the default strategy for coronary angiography (CAG) and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Traditionally, sheath insertion is performed by the interventional cardiologist. Previous nurse-led interventions in cardiovascular care, such as venous sheath removal and post-procedural monitoring, have been shown to be safe and effective. Optimising cath lab workflow and patient-centred care is increasingly important in high-volume centres. We investigated whether task-shifted radial sheath insertion performed by trained cath lab nurses is safe and associated with improved patient experience and procedural efficiency compared with conventional physician-led insertion. Methods In this single-centre, randomised controlled trial, 1,188 patients undergoing CAG and/or PCI were allocated 1:1 to radial sheath insertion performed by trained cath lab nurses or physicians. Co-primary endpoints were patient-reported pain (Numeric Rating Scale [NRS], 0–10) and patient-reported comfort/safety (Comfort Rating Scale [CRS], 0–10). Secondary endpoints included sheath insertion time (from sterile preparation to sheath placement), radial artery occlusion (RAO) before discharge, ultrasound use, and procedural success. Results A total of 1,188 patients were included (73% male; median age 68 years [IQR 61–75]). Baseline characteristics were balanced between the groups (Table 1). Nurse-led sheath insertion was associated with significantly lower patient-reported pain compared with physician-led insertion (mean NRS 1.46 (SD 1.67) vs 2.82 (SD 2.45); mean difference -1.37 (95% CI -1.61 to -1.12), p&lt;0.001). Patient-reported comfort was modestly but significantly higher (mean CRS 9.78 (SD 0.75) vs 9.38 (SD 1.25); mean difference 0.39 (95% CI 0.26 to 0.52), p&lt;0.001). Nurse-led insertion markedly reduced mean sheath insertion time (4.65 (SD 4.63) vs 11.55 (SD 6.68) minutes; mean difference -6.90 minutes (95% CI -7.57 to -6.23), p&lt;0.001), representing a substantial improvement in procedural efficiency (Figure 1). Procedural success was high and similar between groups (99.6% vs 98.9%, p=0.131). RAO rates were low with no significant difference (0.38% vs 0.35%, p=0.296). Ultrasound guidance was more frequently used in the nurse-led group (8.5% vs 4.2%; p=0.003). Conclusions In a large randomised trial, task-shifted radial sheath insertion performed by trained cath lab nurses improved patient-reported pain and comfort and substantially reduced insertion time without compromising procedural success or early vascular safety outcomes. These findings support structured task-shifting strategies as a potential approach to enhance patient-centred care and cath lab efficiency in contemporary radial practice.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Randomized trial of task-shifted radial sheath insertion in coronary angiography and PCI: impact on patient experience and procedural efficiency

abstract: Abstract Introduction Routine functional testing after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains widely practiced in high-risk patients despite uncertainty in guideline recommendations. Its impact on clinical outcomes compared with a selective, symptom-driven approach is unclear. Objectives To evaluate whether routine functional testing reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in high-risk post-PCI patients compared to selective functional testing and to assess its impact on rates of invasive angiography and repeat revascularization. Methods We systematically searched MEDLINE, HERDIN, and reference lists for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing routine versus selective functional testing after PCI. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), hospitalization for unstable angina (UA), invasive angiography, and repeat revascularization (PCI or CABG). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using fixed- and random-effects models. Results Three RCTs comprising 1,851 patients (925 routine; 926 selective) were included. Routine functional testing significantly increased repeat PCI (RR 1.48, 95% CI 1.03–2.11; p=0.03) without reducing all-cause mortality, cardiac death, MI, or hospitalization for UA. Rates of invasive angiography and CABG were similar between groups. Conclusion In high-risk post-PCI patients, routine functional testing increased repeat PCI without improving survival or reducing adverse cardiovascular outcomes. A selective, symptom-driven testing strategy may avoid unnecessary procedures, optimize care, and align follow-up care with patient-centered outcomes.Repeat PCIFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Myocardial InfarctionFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
