title: Routine functional testing versus selective functional testing among high-risk patients post-percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Severely calcified coronary lesions are associated with increased procedural complications, stent underexpansion, and higher restenosis rates. While atherectomy prepares vessels for treatment, drug-eluting stents (DES) are usually preferred over drug-coated balloons (DCB). DCBs offer a stent-free alternative that may improve vessel remodeling and require shorter antiplatelet therapy. However, for severely calcified lesions, it remains unclear whether DCB or DES is more effective, as evidence is limited and studies yield conflicting results. Purpose To evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of drug-coated balloons versus drug-eluting stents following atherectomy in patients with severely calcified coronary lesions, regarding target lesion revascularization, and major adverse cardiac events. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane Central databases in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, identifying randomized controlled trials and adjusted observational studies comparing drug-coated balloons versus drug-eluting stents following atherectomy in patients with severely calcified coronary lesions. We assessed major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause death, myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, and major bleeding defined by BARC criteria. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and 95% prediction intervals (PIs). Heterogeneity was evaluated using the I² statistic. All analyses were performed using R software (version 4.5.2). Results After screening 2,594 records, seven studies were included, comprising 1,497 patients, with 596 treated with DCB and 901 with DES. Drug-coated balloons were not associated with MACE compared with DES (RR 1.12; 95% CI 0.85–1.47; I²=0%), and no significant difference was observed for myocardial infarction (RR 0.94; 95% CI 0.32–2.80; I²=2.1%). Target lesion revascularization (RR 1.29; 95% CI 0.88–1.88; I²=34.6%) and all-cause mortality (RR 1.18; 95% CI 0.78–1.79; I²=0.0%) showed non-significant trends favoring DES, whereas cardiac death showed a non-significant trend favoring DCB (RR 0.65; 95% CI 0.28–1.46; I²=0%). Major bleeding was similar between groups (RR 1.11; 95% CI 0.36–3.37; I²=0%). Prediction intervals were wide for most endpoints, reflecting between-study variability. Conclusion In patients with severely calcified coronary lesions undergoing atherectomy, drug-coated balloons (DCBs) and drug-eluting stents (DES) were similar in MACE, myocardial infarction, or major bleeding. Although trends favored DES for target lesion revascularization and all-cause mortality, and favored DCBs for cardiac death, these differences were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that both strategies may be acceptable, but larger trials are needed to identify which patients benefit most from each approach.
title: Drug-coated balloons versus drug-eluting stents following coronary atherectomy in severely calcified lesions: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background In STEMI, primary PCI restores epicardial patency but does not consistently achieve myocardial reperfusion because distal thrombus embolization and microvascular obstruction remain common. Adjunctive low-dose intracoronary thrombolysis may improve tissue-level perfusion, but randomised evidence remains inconsistent. We performed an updated meta-analysis of randomised trials to compare intracoronary thrombolysis versus placebo during primary PCI and assess clinical and major adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Purpose To evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intracoronary thrombolytic therapy during primary PCI in STEMI. Methods PubMed and Embase were searched through February 20 2026, thirteen randomised controlled trials (RCT), including 2,151 patients (1,179 with thrombolytic therapy and 972 with placebo) with STEMI and who underwent PCI, were analysed. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Safety outcomes included all-cause mortality, target vessel revascularisation (TVR), stent thrombosis, myocardial infarction (MI), minor and major bleeding. Mechanistic outcomes included TIMI myocardial blush grade (MBG), corrected TIMI frame count (CTFC), cTnl peak, wall motion score index (WMSI), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Risk ratios (RR) and Mean Differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Chi-squared test and I² statistic. Prespecified subgroup analyses according to fibrin-specific (tPA based) vs non-fibrin-specific agents (non-tPA). Results In overall analysis, adjunctive thrombolytic therapy did not significantly reduce MACE compared with placebo (RR 0.83 [0.62–1.10]). However, in subgroup analysis, non-tPA showed a reduction in MACE (RR 0.65 [0.44-0.95]). No significant differences were observed for all-cause mortality, TVR, stent thrombosis, minor and major bleeding. Non-fibrin-specific therapy was associated with a high reduction of CTFC (MD -4.10 [-5.53 to -2.66]), WMSI (MD -0.09 [-0.14 to -0.05]), cTnl peak value (MD -5.20 [-8.34 to -2.06]) and a marked elevation of the LVEF (MD 2.46 [1.33 to 3.59]). Conclusion(s) Adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolytic therapy during primary PCI in STEMI did not significantly reduce overall major adverse cardiovascular events versus placebo. However, prespecified subgroup analysis suggested a potential class-dependent benefit, with non-fibrin-specific agents showing favourable effects on MACE, markers of myocardial reperfusion, and left ventricular function, without an apparent increase in bleeding. These findings support a possible mechanistic and clinical advantage of selected intracoronary fibrinolytic strategies, but larger adequately powered trials are needed to confirm whether these subgroup effects translate into consistent clinical benefit.Central IllustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Adjunctive low-dose intracoronary thrombolysis during primary PCI in STEMI: an updated meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background Selecting the optimal pharmacotherapy after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is critical for long-term survival. Although renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASI) are standard of care, individual responses vary. We aimed to develop a machine learning (ML)-based decision support model to predict 3-year mortality and guide personalized RASI selection using a large-scale nationwide registry. Methods We analyzed 12,598 patients with AMI who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and were discharged alive from the KAMIR-NIH (Korea AMI Registry) between 2011 and 2015. Three ML algorithms—Logistic Regression (LR), AdaBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—were implemented to predict 3-year all-cause mortality. The models incorporated 25 clinical variables, including age, LV function, diabetes mellitus (DM), and medication profiles. Results The overall 3-year mortality rate was significantly lower in patients receiving RASI (ACE inhibitors or ARBs) compared to those who did not (8.2% vs. 25.0%, p &lt; 0.001). Patients with DM exhibited a nearly two-fold higher risk of 3-year mortality compared to non-diabetic patients (18.0% vs. 9.8%, p &lt; 0.001). The ML models successfully predicted 3-year mortality with high precision (LR-based probability outputs showed distinct risk stratification). By simulating different RASI strategies (No RASI vs. ACEI vs. ARB), the ML model identified that specific subgroups—particularly those with DM or impaired LV function—derived varying degrees of survival benefit from different RASI classes, suggesting that a one-size-fits-all approach may be suboptimal. Conclusions Machine learning algorithms can effectively predict long-term mortality and provide personalized drug recommendations for AMI patients. Implementation of such ML-driven decision support systems may optimize post-AMI pharmacotherapy and significantly improve 3-year survival outcomes by identifying the most beneficial treatment for individual patient profiles.
title: Machine learning-based personalisation of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors to reduce 3-year mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction: insights from the KAMIR-NIH Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Distal radial access (DRA) has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional transradial access (TRA), potentially reducing vascular complications and enhancing patient comfort. However, evidence on operator radiation exposure during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is currently limited. This study aimed to compare operator radiation exposure between left DRA and right TRA in patients undergoing PCI. Methods In this pre-specified subgroup analysis of the prospective, multicenter, randomized DOSE trial (N=1,101) (1), we evaluated 256 patients who underwent PCI, with 139 in the left DRA group and 117 in the TRA group. The primary endpoint was operator radiation exposure (µSv) at the left wrist, head, and chest using real-time dosimeters. Secondary endpoints included access site crossover rate, fluoroscopy time, procedure time, and contrast volume. Results Baseline clinical characteristics and PCI complexity were comparable between the two groups, with complex PCI performed in 37.4% of the Left DRA group and 41.9% of the right TRA group. No significant differences were observed in operator radiation exposure to the left wrist (9.28 µSv vs 11.53 µSv, P=0.113), head (4.76 µSv vs 4.65 µSv, P=0.856), and chest (2.38 µSv vs 2.41 µSv, P=0.945) between the left DRA and right TRA groups (Figure 1). The incidence of crossover (5.0% vs. 6.0%, P=0.955), fluoroscopy time (16.3 minutes vs 15.5 minutes, P=0.681), procedure time (50.0 minutes vs 47.0 minutes, P=0.739), and contrast volume (210.0 mL vs 196.0 mL, P=0.245) were not significantly different between the two groups (Figure 2). Conclusions In patients undergoing PCI, operator radiation exposure at the left wrist, head, and chest was not significantly different between left DRA and right TRA.Figure1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Operator radiation exposure between left distal and right conventional radial access in patients undergoing PCI

abstract: Abstract Background Despite advancements, ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of mortality, requiring early risk assessment. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) provides parameters like infarct size (IS) or ejection fraction (LVEF) to predict remodeling. However, the role of myocardial metabolites in human remodeling after STEMI remains unknown, representing a gap between functional and structural characterisation. 1H-magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) allows non-invasive assessment of triglycerides (TG) and total creatine (CR), a key marker of energy metabolism. Previous studies showed the prognostic value of TG in acute heart failure, but 1H-MRS was primarily limited to whole-septum measurements, restricting precise quantification in infarcted regions. Purpose The objective was to implement myocardial metabolite characterisation using 1H-MRS in both infarct and non-infarct regions in a cohort of patients after left anterior descending (LAD) or right coronary artery (RCA) STEMI Methods Navigator-free, metabolite-cycled 1H-MRS was performed on a 1.5T system in 22 patients with LAD or RCA STEMI (18 males, 59.9 ± 8.2 years). Spectra from infarct (identified by T2-weighted imaging) and adjacent non-infarct zones in the interventricular septum were acquired using an ECG-triggered PRESS sequence. Post-processing used a customised reconstruction pipeline. Ratios of TG-to-water (TG/W) and CR-to-water (CR/W) were calculated. CMR was repeated six months post-STEMI to assess LVEF, end-diastolic volume, and IS. Results Patients undergoing CMR measurements were less severely affected (lower Killip class and IS by enzyme levels) compared to the entire cohort. Spectra showed high quality in both regions with no significant difference in water linewidth. Across all patients, CR/W showed a near-significant decrease (p=0.061) in the infarct zone, while TG/W was non-significantly decreased. In RCA infarctions (n=8), the TG/W decreased significantly (p=0.066). CR/W did not reach significance in subgroups, likely due to sample size, though trends were visible in both territories. Acute TG/W and CR/W did not correlate with baseline LVEDV, LVEF, or IS. However, at six months, patients with an LVEF increase of &gt;=15% had higher acute infarct TG/W levels compared to those without improvement. This effect was most evident in LAD infarctions (p = 0.067 for TG/W in the infarct zone). CR/W showed no correlation with follow-up functional parameters or remodeling. Conclusions Regional 1H-MRS distinguishes metabolic alterations between infarct and non-infarct zones. Lower TG/W and CR/W characterise infarcted tissue. Higher acute infarct TG/W is associated with 6-month LVEF recovery, suggesting 1H-MRS provides incremental prognostic value post-STEMI.
title: Cardiovascular proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy to distinguish between infarct and non-infarct region after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Transradial access has revolutionized interventional cardiology by reducing vascular complications compared to femoral approaches. However, as novel techniques emerge, comprehensive quantitative synthesis comparing these methodologies remains limited, creating uncertainty regarding the optimal procedural strategy. Introduction This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the comparative efficacy and safety of distal radial access versus proximal radial access in patients undergoing diagnostic or interventional percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods We conducted a random-effects meta-analysis using the DerSimonian-Laird method, synthesizing data from seven randomized controlled trials. Clinical outcomes evaluated included radial artery occlusion, hematoma formation, time to hemostasis, puncture time, vascular complications, and post-procedural bleeding, as well as sheath insertion time. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics and τ² values. Results The meta-analysis revealed clinically significant advantages for distal radial access. Hematoma formation demonstrated a 48% risk reduction (RR=0.52, 95% CI: 0.26-0.78, I²=0.0%). Time to hemostasis decreased dramatically by 137.84 minutes (95% CI: -219.55 to -56.13), despite high heterogeneity (I²=97.6%). Post-procedural bleeding showed a 67% risk reduction (RR=0.33, 95% CI: -0.05-0.71). Radial artery occlusion trended toward 25% reduction (RR=0.75, 95% CI: 0.49-1.01). Trade-offs included modestly increased puncture time (MD=20.03 seconds, 95% CI: 2.80-37.26) and sheath insertion time (MD=12.81 seconds, 95% CI: 8.76-16.86). Conclusion Distal radial access significantly reduces major complications, including hematoma formation and post-procedural bleeding, while dramatically accelerating hemostasis compared to standard proximal access in patients undergoing PCI. The minimal procedural time increases are clinically negligible compared to these substantial safety benefits. These findings support adopting distal radial access protocols as a preferred standard practice in contemporary interventional cardiology.visual abstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.forest plot hematoma formationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Distal radial access dramatically reduces hemostasis time and bleeding in coronary interventions: a meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials

abstract: Abstract Background In patients with radial artery occlusion (RAO), upper-limb access options are limited. Ipsilateral transulnar access (TUA) represents a potential alternative; however, prospective data regarding procedural feasibility, vascular safety, and objective early neurofunctional impact remain limited. We evaluated procedural performance, vascular complications, and quantitative hand-function outcomes following ipsilateral TUA. Methods ULNART is a prospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or PCI via ipsilateral TUA. RAO was assessed by baseline color duplex ultrasonography (CDUS) and confirmed fluoroscopically through retrograde radial angiography after ulnar cannulation; CDUS was repeated within 24 hours to assess vessel patency and access-related changes. Grip strength, pinch strength, and sensory function (WEST) were assessed at baseline and at 24 hours, with within-patient comparison between access and contralateral hands. Vascular and neuromuscular complications were prospectively recorded. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. Results Forty-two patients were analyzed (65.5 ± 10.2 years; 71% male). Diabetes and hypertension were present in 71% and 86%, respectively; prior PCI in 79%. Patients had undergone 2.05 ± 1.15 prior catheterizations (range 1–5). Right-sided TUA was performed in 71% (ultrasound-guided in 64%). CAG was performed in 90%; 50% underwent PCI, including 17% CTO PCI. Technical success was 97.6%, with one crossover (2.4%). One major vascular complication occurred (EASY III hematoma, 2.4%). At 24 hours, hematomas were distributed as follows: none 59%, EASY I 24%, EASY II 14%, EASY III 2%, with no EASY IV–V events. Bleeding events were: none 86%, BARC 1 10%, BARC 2 2%, and BARC 3c 2% (adjudicated unrelated to the access technique). No arterial occlusion, pseudoaneurysm, arteriovenous fistula, hand ischemia, compartment syndrome, or need for surgical or endovascular intervention was detected clinically or by CDUS. Baseline grip strength was symmetrical (33.4 ± 10.6 vs 32.4 ± 11.3 kg). At 24 hours, access-side grip declined modestly but significantly (−5.4 ± 7.5 vs −1.4 ± 2.9 kg; mean paired difference −3.9 kg; p = 0.002); pinch showed a similar pattern (p = 0.002), whereas sensory changes were not significant (p = 0.318). In bilateral CTO procedures (n = 6), no significant asymmetry between TUA and contralateral TRA limbs was observed for grip (p = 0.249), pinch (p = 0.463), or sensory change (p = 0.317). Conclusions TUA ipsilateral to RAO demonstrated high procedural feasibility and low major vascular complication rates. Although a modest early reduction in access-side strength was observed, no objective sensory deficit or major neurovascular complication occurred. Controlled within-patient analyses support ipsilateral TUA as a safe and strategically valuable upper-limb alternative.
title: Transulnar access in patients with ipsilateral radial artery occlusion undergoing coronary angiography or angioplasty: 24-hour clinical and quantitative outcomes from the ULNART study

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal stenting strategies for bifurcation lesions in Complex and High-risk Indicated Patients (CHIP) remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to compare long-term clinical outcomes between 1- and 2-stent strategies for bifurcation lesions in a well-defined CHIP cohort. Methods We performed a propensity score–matched cohort analysis using two large prospective bifurcation PCI registries (Coronary Bifurcation Stenting [COBIS] II and COBIS III), including those who fulfilled strict CHIP criteria with both patient- and lesion-level high-risk features beyond bifurcation anatomy. Among 2,273 matched patients, 1,788 underwent a 1-stent strategy, and 485 received a 2-stent strategy. The primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Results At 5 years, the incidence of TLF was significantly lower in the 1-stent strategy group compared with the 2-stent group (7.9% versus 13.8%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.61; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48–0.78; P &lt; 0.001). Clinically driven TLR was significantly reduced in the 1-stent group (5.0% versus 10.1%; HR 0.47; 95% CI, 0.32–0.67; P &lt; 0.001). Rates of cardiac death (2.1% versus 2.4%; HR 0.83; 95% CI, 0.53–1.30; P = 0.42) and MI (1.8% versus 2.7%; HR 0.77; 95% CI, 0.44–1.37; P = 0.38) were similar between groups. Conclusions In CHIP patients with bifurcation lesions, the 1-stent strategy was associated with significantly lower 5-year TLF compared to a 2-stent strategy, without increasing the risk of cardiac death or MI (COBIS II; NCT01642992; COBIS III; NCT03068494).FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

title: Comparison of 1- versus 2-stent strategy for bifurcation lesions in complex and high-risk indicated patients

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) have emerged as a promising strategy for stent-free percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Nevertheless, despite the growing evidence supporting DCB-based approaches, data remain limited regarding optimal lesion pre-dilatation strategies required to maximize procedural success and clinical outcomes. Purpose To compare the clinical outcomes of using standard balloons including semi-compliant and non-compliant (NC) versus specialized balloons including cutting and scoring balloons prior to DCB application to the target lesion in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 274 consecutive ACS patients treated with DCB between January 2022 and January 2025. Patients were grouped by lesion preparation strategy: standard balloon pre-dilatation (n = 147) and specialized balloon pre-dilatation (n = 127).Cases requiring bail-out drug-eluting stents for flow-limiting dissections were excluded. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), composite of all-cause mortality, cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), and target-vessel revascularization (TVR), assessed during hospitalization and at one-year follow-up Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Standard balloons were more frequently used in distal lesion compared with specialized balloons (26% vs. 11.8%, P = 0.003). There was no significant difference in balloon type use across different vessel calibres, native, or in-stent lesions. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was employed in approximately 59.4% of cases to ensure the absence of flow-limiting dissection and adequate lumen gain. Regarding the primary outcome, MACE was significantly higher in the standard balloon group compared with the specialized balloon group, both during hospitalization (16.3% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.03) and at 1-year follow-up (19.7% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.003). Compared with specialized balloons, the regular balloon pre-dilatation group had a significantly higher rate of in-hospital TV-MI (8.2% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.016) and a significantly greater incidence of TVR at 1-year follow-up (15.7% vs. 6.4%, P = 0.017). Kaplan–Meier survival analysis showed that one-year post-PCI cumulative MACE rates were lower with specialized balloons compared to standard balloons (P = 0.03). Subgroup analysis showed numerically lower event rates in terms of MACE, mortality, TV-MI, or TVR for non-compliant balloons compared with semi-compliant balloons; however, these differences did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion In ACS patients undergoing DCB treatment, specialized balloon pre-dilatation was associated with lower in-hospital and 1-year MACE compared with standard balloons. In contrast, standard balloons, predominantly semi-complaint, were linked to higher rates of in-hospital TV-MI and 1-year TVR and therefore should be discouraged for routine use before DCB.Clinical outcomes comparisonFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Kaplan–Meier CurveFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Does pre-dilatation balloon choice matter? standard versus specialized balloons prior to drug-coated balloon therapy in acute coronary syndrome patients

abstract: Abstract Background Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an efficient and emerging calcification modifying technique with a short learning curve and few complications. The poor lesion crossing ability of catheters is the main challenges in clinical practice. This study aimed to analyze the safety and effectiveness of IVL therapy using catheters size selected based on the calcification segment diameter measured by intravascular ultrasound (IVUS). Methods This is a prospective observational multicenter study enrolled patients with severe coronary calcification and a clinical indication for vessel preparation with IVL. Patients underwent IVUS examinations before IVL and after PCI. Based on the diameter of the shockwave catheters and IVUS measurements, patients were divided into the RVD group (the ratio of the catheter diameter to RVD was 1:1) and the CAC group (the ratio of the catheter diameter to the maximum diameter of calcification segment was 1:1). The primary outcome was procedural success (defined as residual area stenosis &lt;30%, without interventional complications or in-hospital MACE), and the secondary outcome was pretreatment with other calcification modifying techniques. Results Between September 2024 to December 2025, 412 patients were enrolled, including 187 patients in the RVD group and 225 patients in the CAC group. The mean age was 67.40 ± 9.37 years, and 71.4% were males. The most common target lesion was the LAD, and 19.2% lesions were chronic total occlusion. The calcified plaque burden was 59.93 ± 5.54 %, the acute lumen gain was 1.15 ± 0.27 mm, and residual area stenosis was 22.06 ± 9.49 %. The IVUS measurements of pre-IVL and post-PCI were compared. After procedure, the MLA and MLD were significantly improved (p&lt;0.001), and the area stenosis and plaque burden was significantly reduced (p&lt;0.001). Regarding the primary outcomes, 93.4% of patients achieved procedure success, with no significant difference between the two groups (p=0.272). Regarding the secondary outcomes, only 18.0% of patients received direct IVL treatment. Compared with the RVD group, patients in the CAC group had significantly lower demands for pretreatment (73.3% vs 92.5%, p&lt;0.001). Compared to the RVD group, more patients in the CAC group receiving direct IVL treatment (26.7% vs 7.5%) or ordinary balloon pretreatment (52.0% vs 49.2%), while fewer patients received special balloon (18.2% vs 27.8%) or other special calcification modifying technique pretreatment (3.1% vs 15.0%), and the differences between the groups were statistically significant (p&lt;0.001). Conclusions IVL therapy is a safe and effective calcification modifying technique. The selection of the shockwave catheters size guided by maximum calcification segment diameter on IVUS is expected to improve the lesion crossing ability while ensuring the safety and efficacy of the procedure, and reduce the need for pretreatment with other calcification modifying techniques.Measurements of Calcified Lesions on IVUS.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Study outcomes and IVUS images.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Intravascular lithotripsy for severe coronary calcification: superior lesion crossability and comparable safety and efficacy in catheter size selection based on IVUS-guided calcified segment diameter

abstract: Abstract Background Complex de novo left main coronary bifurcation lesions are among the most challenging scenarios in contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention, involving a large myocardial territory and high procedural risk. Two stent techniques remain conventional but increase metal burden, complexity and restenosis risk. A hybrid strategy using a drug eluting stent in the main vessel and a drug coated balloon in the side branch has emerged as an alternative, yet no prior systematic synthesis has focused on this approach in left main bifurcation lesions. Purpose To provide the first systematic comparative evaluation of a hybrid drug eluting stent plus drug coated balloon strategy versus two stent techniques in complex de novo left main bifurcation intervention. Methods A systematic search through 1 January 2026 identified studies exclusively evaluating de novo left main coronary bifurcation lesions and reporting target lesion revascularisation, target vessel myocardial infarction or post procedural luminal stenosis. Comparative and single arm studies were analysed separately and not combined in pooled models. Comparative cohorts were synthesised using random effects models, while single arm hybrid studies were analysed independently to estimate pooled mid term event rates. Results Of 1 045 screened records, five cohort studies including 269 patients met inclusion criteria. Two propensity matched cohorts (n=160) showed numerically lower target lesion revascularisation with the hybrid strategy compared with two stent techniques (RR 0.45 [95% CI 0.14 to 1.40]; p=0.17) and a similar directional reduction in target vessel myocardial infarction (RR 0.63 [95% CI 0.08 to 4.97]; p=0.66). Main branch residual stenosis favoured the hybrid approach (−0.91% [95% CI −1.83 to −0.00]; p=0.05), whereas side branch residual stenosis was higher (8.38% [95% CI 6.99 to 9.77]; p&lt;0.00001). Three additional hybrid cohorts (n=109), analysed separately, showed low mid term event rates, with pooled target lesion revascularisation of 1% (95% CI [0.00 to 0.05]) and target vessel myocardial infarction of 0% (95% CI [0.00 to 0.01]), consistent with the direction observed in comparative analyses. Conclusion(s) In complex de novo left main coronary bifurcation lesions, a hybrid drug eluting stent and drug coated balloon strategy was associated with numerically lower repeat revascularisation and myocardial infarction compared with two stent techniques and improved main branch angiographic results, with higher residual stenosis in the side branch. While evidence remains limited and predominantly observational, this synthesis provides a structured clinical framework for future prospective and randomised investigations.Post-PCI side branch stenosis (%)For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.TLR: hybrid vs two-stentFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Redefining PCI for complex de novo left main coronary bifurcation lesions: first systematic review and meta-analysis of a hybrid drug-eluting stent and drug-coated balloon strategy

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-coated balloons (DCB) have emerged as a compelling stent-free alternative in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), combining the mechanical benefits of balloon angioplasty with targeted, localized antiproliferative drug delivery. While established for in-stent restenosis, there is growing clinical interest in their application for de-novo coronary lesions. However, large-scale, real-world data regarding DCB-only PCI remains limited. Purpose This study sought to evaluate the five-year temporal trends and clinical characteristics of DCB use in de novo lesions within a contemporary PCI cohort. Methods We analyzed data from the ORPKI Registry, a large-scale national registry of PCI in Poland. A total of 535,989 PCIs entered the registry between January 2020, and December 2024. After exclusion in-stent restenosis, only plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) and CTO procedures the final analysis included 417,689 PCIs for de-novo lesions. DCB procedures were compared with stent PCI. Results The utilization of DCB for de novo lesions PCI demonstrated a significant upward trend, increasing from 0.5% in 2020 to 2.8% in 2024 (p&lt;0.001) (Figure). Of the 6,231 procedures involving DCB, 5,015 (80.5%) were performed as a definitive treatment, while 1,216 involved a hybrid approach with stenting. Patients treated with DCB-only were more likely to have diabetes, chronic kidney disease, previous myocardial infarction and previous PCI. DCB use was significantly higher in chronic coronary syndrome compared with acute coronary syndromes (ACS), whereas stents were predominantly used in ACS. DCB were frequently employed in smaller vessels, including diagonal and marginal branches, as well as distal segments of main vessels. FFR, IVUS and OCT were more frequently used with DCB compared with stent group (Table). In multivariable analysis diabetes, chronic kidney disease, previous myocardial infarction, previous PCI, previous CABG and IVUS and OCT usage were independently associated with DCB strategy selection. Conclusion The utilization of DCB for de novo coronary lesions has increased more than fivefold over the past five years. Current clinical practice favors DCB use in patients with higher baseline complexity and frequently employing adjunctive physiological assessment and intravascular imaging lesion assessment. Notably, DCB are predominantly utilized in specific anatomical location, with a preference for distal segments and side-branch vessels.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.TableFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Temporal trends and clinical characteristics of drug-coated balloon angioplasty for de dovo coronary lesions: A five-year analysis from the ORPKI Registry

abstract: Abstract Drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty has emerged as a promising alternative to drug eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly in small-vessel coronary disease (defined as target vessels with a reference diameter ≤2.75 mm). Nevertheless, multicenter real-world data focusing exclusively on de novo lesions remain limited. To evaluate procedural success, safety profile, and effectiveness of DCB angioplasty in de novo coronary lesions with 6-month clinical follow-up. This prospective observational registry included 156 consecutive patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with DCB for de novo coronary lesions between June 2024 and August 2025 across three tertiary cardiac centers. Clinical follow-up was performed at 1, 3, and 6 months post-procedure to record major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as cardiac death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularisation. Procedural success was defined as fulfillment of all the following: device success and freedom from in-hospital cardiovascular death or target lesion revascularization or peri-procedural myocardial infarction (MI) or any stroke or BARC 3–5 bleeding, or the need for bailout stenting. Optimal lesion preparation was defined as full balloon expansion (1:1 ratio), ≤30% residual stenosis, TIMI 3 flow and absence of flow-limiting dissection. The mean age was 67.9 ± 10.8 years; 86.1% were men and 32% had diabetes mellitus. 8% presented with acute coronary syndrome. Target vessels included LAD (31.8%), LCx (21.6%), RCA (17.0%), D1 (12.5%) and others (17.1%). A total of 36 DCBs (18.4%) were implanted in side branches of bifurcation lesions, predominantly involving the left anterior descending (LAD)–diagonal and left circumflex–obtuse marginal (OM) branches. DCB diameters ranged from 2.0 mm to 2.75 mm (most commonly 2.5 mm [53%]) and lengths were 15 mm (49%), 25mm (22%), 30mm (14%), 20 mm (9%) and 10mm (6%). Sirolimus-coated balloons were used in 23.1% and paclitaxel-coated in 76.9%. Residual dissections occurred in all DCB-treated segments (n = 11/156), 3 of which were flow-limiting and required bailout stenting, while on the other hand 8 were non–flow-limiting and left untreated. Overall procedural success was 98%. At 6-month follow-up, the MACE rate was 5.7% (n = 9). DCB-based PCI achieved high procedural success and excellent in-hospital and mid-term safety across 3 tertiary centers. This strategy proved effective even in complex-and bifurcation-lesions while minimizing metal implantation. These findings reinforce the feasibility and growing adoption of a "leave-nothing-behind" approach in contemporary coronary intervention. Moreover, DCB-only angioplasty may allow shortening of dual antiplatelet therapy duration and represent a valuable alternative for patients at high bleeding risk.Central IllustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Safety and effectiveness of drug-coated balloon angioplasty in de novo coronary lesions: 6-month outcomes from a multicenter registry

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty is currently recommended by the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) as a Class I, Level A-therapy for the treatment of in-stent restenosis (ISR). Its role in de novo coronary lesions remains under investigation, particularly in real-world clinical practice. Despite their expanding use, multi-center data evaluating both procedural and clinical outcomes are still limited. Purpose To assess procedural success and 12-month clinical outcomes of DCB angioplasty in a real-world, multicenter setting. Methods This prospective, observational registry included 244 consecutive patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with DCB between January 2024 and January 2025 across 3 tertiary, Greek cardiac centers. Clinical, angiographic and procedural data were prospectively collected. Procedural success was defined as achievement of TIMI 3 flow without procedural failure or bailout stenting. Clinical follow-up was performed at 1,3,6 and 12 months via structured telephone interviews. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were defined as the composite of cardiac death, target lesion failure, target vessel re-vascularization or unplanned re-hospitalization. Results The mean age was 67.4 ± 10.8 years and 88.5% were men. Clinical presentation included stable coronary artery disease (≈85%) and acute coronary syndromes (≈15%). DCB angioplasty was performed in de novo lesions (80.8%) and ISR (19.2%). Target vessels included LAD (50.3%), RCA (18.5%), and LCx (13.9%). DCB diameters were mainly 2.5 mm (36.8%), 2.0 mm (29%) and 3.0 mm (25%), while lengths were predominantly 15 mm (42.4%) and 25 mm (26.3%). A hybrid DCB–DES approach was used in 51.4%, while DCB-only PCI accounted for 48.6%. Procedural success was 96%. At 12-month follow-up (no contact 11,8%), 10 (4%) target lesion failure, 12 (5%) target lesion re-vascularization and 1 cardiac death (0.045%) were recorded. The overall 12-month MACE rate was 9.7%, with 3.7% in de novo lesions and 4.2% in ISR lesions, respectively. Conclusions In this multicenter real-world registry, DCB angioplasty demonstrated high procedural success (96%) and 12-month MACE (7.9%) across both de novo and ISR lesions. These findings reinforce the safety and efficacy of a DCB-based strategy, supporting its evolving role into contemporary PCI practice, so long as adequate lesion preparation is preceded.Drug coated balloons PCI: 12 months follow upFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Procedural success and 12-month clinical outcomes of drug-coated balloon angioplasty: results from a multicenter prospective registry

abstract: Abstract Background Left main (LM) disease is a life-threatening pathology. Current guidelines, supported by meta-analyses of large randomized trials, endorse PCI for LM disease as an alternative to CABG in patients with lower anatomic complexity when PCI can achieve equivalent revascularization to CABG. However, in contemporary PCI, comparative outcome data for patients requiring LM stent implantation between newer-generation ultra-thin-strut and thin-strut drug-eluting stents are scarce. Purpose To evaluate 1-year clinical outcomes of patients, undergoing PCI for de novo three-vessel disease (3VD), that nevertheless underwent LM stent implantation and to compare ultra-thin-strut Supraflex Cruz™(60μm) and thin-strut SYNERGY™(74-81μm) in the Multivessel TALENT trial (NCT04390672). Methods This is a post-hoc sub-analysis of the Multivessel TALENT trial, a multicentre randomized trial (in 54 European sites) that randomized and treated 1533 patients with de novo 3VD with protocolar exclusion of LM disease. Patients were randomized 1:1 to Supraflex Cruz or SYNERGY and treated with contemporary PCI practice, including corelab-analysed angiography-derived FFR, post-PCI intravascular imaging-guided optimization, and 1-month DAPT followed by prasugrel monotherapy. The treatment of LM stenosis (n=20) or both ostial LAD and LCX stenoses (n=3) were exclusion criteria and protocol deviation, but single ostial LAD or LCX lesion treatment with extension of stent in LM (n=90) was allowed by protocol. The primary outcome in this sub-analysis was 1-year patient-oriented composite endpoint (POCE): composite of all-cause death, any MI, any stroke, and any revascularization. The patients with stent implantation to LM were compared with those without LM stent. The comparison between study stents (Supraflex Cruz and SYNERGY) was also performed within each group. Results Among 1533 patients that underwent PCI, 126 (8.2%) received stent(s) in LM. Compared with those without LM stenting, the LM stent group had significantly higher SYNTAX scores, larger total number of stents, and longer total stent length. Of 126 LM stent cases, LM bifurcations were present in 107 cases(10 true[Medina 1,1,1; 1,0,1; 0,1,1] and 97 non-true[Medina 1,1,0; 1,0,0; 0,1,0; 0,0,1]). For treatment of LM bifurcations, 1-stent and 2-stent strategies were used in 93 and 27 cases. The 1-year POCE was numerically higher with LM stenting but not statistically significant (17.7% vs 14.4%,HR 1.26, 95%CI 0.81-1.95, P=0.309). All-cause mortality tended to be higher in LM stent group (5.7% vs 2.7%,HR 2.09, 95%CI 0.93-4.67, P=0.074). However, 1-year POCE was comparable between ultra-thin Supraflex Cruz and thin SYNERGY (LM subset: 17.9% vs 17.4%, HR 1.08, 95%CI 0.46-2.49; non-LM subset: 14.8% vs 13.9%, HR 1.07, 95%CI 0.81-1.41; P for interaction=0.978). Conclusions In this underpowered post-hoc analysis, outcomes after LM stenting were comparable between ultra-thin Supraflex Cruz and thin SYNERGY.Figure AFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure BFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Outcome of left main stent implantation: a randomized comparison between ultra-thin strut (Suprafex Cruz) and thin strut (SYNERGY) stent, a post-hoc sub-analysis of the Multivessel TALENT trial

abstract: Abstract Background Imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), including intravascular ultrasonography (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT), has emerged as an alternative to standard coronary angiography (CAG)-guided PCI. However, evidence regarding the safety of low-dose imaging-guided PCI in reducing contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the safety and efficacy of low-contrast IVUS-guided PCI (IVUS-low), low-contrast OCT-guided PCI (OCT-low), standard-contrast IVUS-guided PCI (IVUS-std), and standard-contrast OCT-guided PCI (OCT-std), compared with conventional CAG-guided PCI (CAG-std). Method A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from their inception through January 2026. Patients with CKD undergoing PCI were included. The primary endpoint was the incidence of CA-AKI. The secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac events (MACE), myocardial infarction (MI), cardiovascular (CV) mortality, and all-cause mortality. Results A total of 6 studies comprising 7,182 patients (4,621females [64.3%]; mean age 68.1 ± 10.6 years) were included. The IVUS-low group demonstrated a significant reduction in CA-AKI incidence compared with the IVUS-std group (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.05–0.92, p = 0.039) and the CAG-std group (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.07–0.87, p = 0.030), with the highest P-score of 0.89. Although the IVUS-low group showed significantly higher all-cause mortality than the OCT-std group (OR 2.98, 95% CI 1.10–8.10, p = 0.032), its efficacy in reducing MACE, MI, and CV mortality was comparable to that of the IVUS-std, OCT-std, and CAG-std groups. Compared with the CAG-std group, both the IVUS-std and OCT-std groups demonstrated significant reductions in MACE, CV mortality, and all-cause mortality, with more favorable P-scores. Conclusions Low-contrast IVUS-guided PCI may help reduce the incidence of CA-AKI in patients with CKD, with comparable rates of MACE, MI, and CV mortality to standard-contrast imaging-guided PCI (either IVUS or OCT) and conventional CAG-guided PCI.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Low-contrast intravascular ultrasonography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention for contrast-associated acute kidney injury prevention in chronic kidney disease: a meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Atherectomy using rotational (RA) or orbital (OA) devices facilitates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in severely calcified lesions. However, the optimal revascularization strategy following plaque modification remains uncertain. Purpose We aimed to compare one-year clinical outcomes between stent and non-stent strategies after atherectomy under intravascular imaging guidance. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 425 severely calcified lesions treated with RA or OA between October 2019 and June 2024. Intravascular ultrasound or optical coherence tomography was used in all cases for lesion assessment and procedural optimization. Patients were categorized into a stent strategy group or a non-stent strategy group. Procedural success was defined as ≤30% residual stenosis with TIMI 3 flow and dissection grade A–C. The primary endpoint was one-year target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary endpoints included target vessel revascularization (TVR), major adverse cardiac events (MACE: cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or heart failure hospitalization), and all-cause mortality. Kaplan–Meier analysis and log-rank testing were performed. Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to adjust for baseline differences. Results Before PSM, the stent strategy was associated with lower one-year TLR (5.8% vs 12.6%, p&lt;0.001) and TVR (8.0% vs 14.0%, p=0.003), with no significant differences in MACE (p=0.133) or all-cause mortality (p=0.151). After PSM (125 matched pairs), the stent strategy remained associated with reduced TLR (8.0% vs 13.8%, p=0.011) and TVR (8.8% vs 13.8%, p=0.021), whereas MACE (p=0.809) and all-cause mortality (p=0.488) were comparable between groups. Conclusion In severely calcified lesions treated with atherectomy under intravascular imaging guidance, stent implantation was associated with fewer repeat revascularizations but did not improve survival or reduce major adverse cardiac events at one year.TLR Rate After PSMFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comparative evaluation of one-year outcomes between stent and non-stent strategies following atherectomy for severely calcified coronary lesions

abstract: Abstract Background Transradial access has evolved as the preferred approach for coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention. Radial artery occlusion (RAO) is the most common complication of transradial coronary catheterization. Purpose To evaluate the incidence of RAO and its predisposing factors. Methods Prospective, multicenter, open-label study involving 1,357 patients (mean age: 64.8±11.7 years, females: 24.9%) who underwent cardiac catheterization via the transradial route for angiography and/or a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). RAO was diagnosed with radial artery ultrasound in the first 24 hours after successful hemostasis. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify potential predictors of RAO occurrence. Results The incidence of RAO was 9.5% overall, 10.6% in the angiography-only group and 6.2% in the PCI group. Independent predictors of RAO were as follows: (i) the female gender [aOR = 1.72 (1.05–2.83)], (ii) access site cross-over [aOR = 4.33 (1.02–18.39)], (iii) increased total time of the sheath in the artery [(aOR = 1.01 (1.00–1.02)], (iv) radial artery spasm [aOR = 2.47 (1.40–4.36)], (v) presence of hematoma [aOR = 2.28 (1.28–4.06)], (vi) post-catheterization dabigatran use [aOR = 5.15 (1.29–20.55)], (vii) manual hemostasis [aOR = 1.94 (1.01–3.72)] and (viii) numbness [aOR = 8.25 (1.70–40)]. Contrariwise, two variables were independently associated with increased odds for radial artery patency (RAP): (i) PCI performance [aOR = 0.19 (0.06–0.63)], and (ii) a higher dosage of intravenous heparin per patient weight [aOR = 0.98 (0.96–0.99)], particularly, a dosage of &gt;50 IU/kg [aOR = 0.56 (0.31–1.00)]. Conclusion The incidence of RAO in an unselected, all-comers European population after transradial coronary catheterization for angiography and/or PCIs is similar to that reported in the international literature. Several RAO prognostic factors have been confirmed, and new ones are described. The female gender, radial artery trauma and manual hemostasis are the strongest predictors of RAO. Our results could help in the future identification of patients at higher risk of RAO, for whom less invasive diagnostic procedures may be preferred, if possible.
title: Radial artery occlusion in transradial coronary catheterization: incidence and prognostic factors

abstract: Abstract Background Transradial access has become the preferred approach for coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention due to its safety profile. However, the influence of sex on upper limb vascular complications remains under investigation. Purpose To evaluate whether sex is associated with differences in early upper limb vascular complications following transradial cardiac catheterization. Methods A total of 769 consecutive adult patients (mean age 65±12 years, 22% females), undergoing transradial coronary angiography and/or percutaneous coronary intervention that were screened for the LOW-RAO study were analyzed. Upper limb vascular complications within 24 hours were systematically recorded and compared between males and females. Results Of the total cohort, 600 patients (78%) were male and 169 (22%) females. Forearm bleeding was significantly more frequent in females compared with males (10.5% vs 3.8%, p=0.0015). No statistically significant differences were observed between sexes for RAO (p=0.296), hematoma (p=0.404), pain (p=0.073), paresthesia (p=0.409), non-palpable radial pulse (p=0.680), negative reverse Allen (p=0.988), negative reverse Barbeau (p=1.000), or other limb complications. Conclusion Female sex was associated with a higher incidence of early hemorrhagic complications following transradial access, whereas thrombotic and ischemic complications did not differ significantly between sexes. These findings suggest that bleeding risk mitigation strategies may be particularly relevant in female patients undergoing transradial procedures.RESULTS TABLEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Sex differences in upper limb vascular complications following transradial cardiac catheterization. A sub-study of the LOW-RAO study

abstract: Abstract Background Although transradial access is considered safe across age groups, elderly patients may present increased vascular vulnerability. The effect of age on upper limb vascular complications remains unclear. Purpose To assess whether age ≥70 years is associated with increased early upper limb vascular complications following transradial cardiac catheterization. Methods A total of 769 consecutive adult patients (mean age 65±12 years, 22% females), undergoing transradial coronary angiography and/or percutaneous coronary intervention that were screened for the LOW-RAO study were analyzed. Upper limb vascular complications within 24 hours were systematically recorded and compared between older (age ≥70 years) and younger patients (age &lt;70 years). Results Radial artery spasm was significantly more frequent in patients aged ≥70 years compared with younger patients (p=0.012). No significant differences were observed between age groups for radial artery occlusion (p=0.477), haematoma (p=0.368), bleeding (p=0.254), pain (p=0.665), non-palpable radial pulse (p=0.580), negative reverse Allen (p=0.305), negative reverse Barbeau (p=0.181), or other vascular complications. Conclusion Advanced age was associated with a higher incidence of radial artery spasm but not with increased thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications. These findings support the overall safety of transradial access in elderly patients while highlighting the need for careful management of vasospasm in this population.RESULTS TABLEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of age on early upper limb vascular complications after transradial cardiac catheterization. A sub-study of the LOW-RAO study

abstract: Abstract Background Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is an established revascularization strategy for selected patients with left main coronary artery disease (LMCAD). However, outcomes differ depending on whether the left coronary system is protected by prior CABG. While unprotected PCI is clinically recognized to carry a higher risk, the extent of this risk difference has not been comprehensively quantified. Purpose This study aimed to quantify the difference in all-cause mortality and adverse cardiovascular outcomes between unprotected and protected left main PCI. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through April 2025. Eligible studies included patients with LMCAD undergoing PCI, stratified by prior CABG status. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We calculated pooled odds ratios using a random-effects model with Paule–Mandel variance estimation. For studies reporting Kaplan–Meier curves on all-cause mortality, individual patient data (IPD) were reconstructed to derive a pooled hazard ratio using Cox regression. Results Individual patient data reconstructed from Kaplan–Meier curves involving 3,022 patients showed a significantly higher risk of all-cause mortality in unprotected patients (HR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.55–2.23), with 1-year survival rates of 88% in the protected group versus 71% in the unprotected group. The proportional hazards assumption was not violated. Meta-analysis of 11 studies comprising 4,786 patients further demonstrated increased all-cause mortality in the unprotected group (OR: 5.56; 95% CI: 2.56–12.50; I² = 57.3%), including in-hospital mortality (OR: 5.88; 95% CI: 1.79–20.00) and 1-year mortality (OR: 6.25; 95% CI: 1.85–20.00). Major adverse cardiovascular events were also more frequent in unprotected patients (OR: 2.08; 95% CI: 1.32–3.23; I² = 48.5%), particularly at 1 year (OR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.27–3.33). Revascularization rates were similar overall (OR: 1.22; 95% CI: 0.64–2.33), although in-hospital revascularization was significantly more common in the unprotected group (OR: 10.00; 95% CI: 1.27–100.00). Conclusion Unprotected left main PCI is associated with significantly worse outcomes compared to protected PCI, including a 17% absolute reduction in 1-year survival and a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular events.Graphical AbstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Unprotected vs. protected left main PCI outcomes: a meta-analysis of reconstructed time-to-event data

abstract: Abstract Background Nonagenarians with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are frequently underrepresented in clinical trials, leading to uncertainty regarding the optimal management strategy. While invasive management is guideline-recommended for ACS, concerns regarding frailty, comorbidities, and procedural risk often lead to a conservative approach in this very elderly population. Purpose To evaluate the impact of an invasive strategy compared with a conservative strategy on in-hospital and long-term mortality among nonagenarians presenting with ACS. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in 3 databases (Pubmed, Scopus, Web of Science) assessing studies that compared an invasive strategy that included percutaneous coronary intervention versus conservative management in patients aged ≥90 years with ACS. The primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and long-term mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Results Database search yielded 1289 studies. After removal of duplicates and title/abstract screening, the full text of 74 manuscripts was assessed. Ultimately, 12 studies were included for data extraction. Nine studies comprising 1,902 nonagenarians (881 invasive, 1,021 conservative) were assessed in-hospital mortality. An invasive strategy was associated with a significant reduction in in-hospital mortality compared with conservative management (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.43–0.75; p = 0.0016), with considerable heterogeneity (I² = 73.9%). Ten studies including 1,138,508 patients (98,829 invasive, 1,039,679 conservative) contributed to the long-term mortality analysis. Invasive management was associated with significantly lower long-term mortality (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49–0.77; p = 0.0009), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 93.8%). Conclusion Among nonagenarians with ACS, an invasive strategy is associated with significantly lower in-hospital and long-term mortality compared with conservative management. Despite substantial heterogeneity, these findings suggest that advanced age alone should not preclude consideration of invasive management in carefully selected nonagenarian patients.In-Hospital Mortality in NonagenariansFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Long-Term Mortality in NonagenariansFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

title: Invasive vs. conservative management in nonagenarians with acute coronary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the principal revascularisation strategy in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Although haemodynamic instability is a recognised determinant of adverse outcome, early post-procedural major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) continue to occur in patients who present clinically stable. The predictors and long-term prognostic implications of these early complications remain insufficiently characterised. Purpose To determine the incidence, independent predictors, and long-term survival impact of immediate post-PCI MACE in haemodynamically stable ACS patients. Methods We analysed 16,312 consecutive adults undergoing PCI between 2012 and 2024 from a prospective institutional registry. Patients with cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, mechanical ventilation, or vasopressor requirement were excluded. Immediate MACE comprised in-hospital cardiovascular and major bleeding events. Baseline demographic, clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and angiographic characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Long-term survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis with log-rank testing. Results Immediate post-PCI MACE occurred in approximately 6% of haemodynamically stable patients. Patients experiencing MACE were older, more frequently female, and had higher prevalence of renal dysfunction, anaemia, impaired left ventricular systolic function, multivessel coronary artery disease, and impaired baseline TIMI flow (all p&lt;0.001). On multivariable analysis, the strongest independent predictors were severe left ventricular dysfunction (aOR 3.6, 95% CI 2.5–5.2), impaired coronary flow (TIMI &lt;3; aOR 2.6, 1.8–3.7), elevated creatinine (aOR 2.6, 2.2–3.1), moderate anaemia (aOR 2.7, 1.8–4.1), and three-vessel disease (aOR 2.1, 1.7–2.6) (all p&lt;0.001). Female sex (aOR 1.9, 1.6–2.4) and age 71–80 years (aOR 1.6, 1.3–2.0) also remained significant. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated early and sustained separation of survival curves. Cumulative mortality exceeded 30% among patients with immediate MACE compared with approximately 15% among those without MACE (log-rank χ² 348.6, p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Among haemodynamically stable ACS patients undergoing PCI, immediate post-procedural MACE occurs in a substantial minority and is independently driven by ventricular dysfunction, renal impairment, anaemia, impaired coronary flow, and multivessel disease. Importantly, early complications confer a persistent and clinically meaningful excess risk of long-term mortality. Immediate post-PCI MACE should therefore be regarded as a powerful marker of systemic vulnerability warranting intensified follow-up and optimisation of secondary prevention.Predictors of Immediate Post-PCI MACEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Kaplan Meier CurveFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Early Post-PCI MACE in haemodynamically stable ACS confers a twofold long-term mortality risk: a 16,312-patient contemporary analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-coated balloon (DCB) has emerged as potential alternative to drug-eluting stents (DES) in specific lesion subsets for de novo coronary lesions. However, evidence supporting DCB in severely calcified lesions remains limited. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) is a noninvasive quantitative tool for evaluating post-procedural results following PCI. Purpose This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes between DCB angioplasty and DES implantation in heavily calcified coronary lesions after rotational atherectomy (RA). Methods We retrospectively collected data from three hundred and fourteen consecutive patients with heavily calcified lesions who underwent DCB angioplasty (n=37) or DES implantation (n=277) after RA between Jan 2022 and June 2024 in our center. Patients with prior DES implantation in the target vessel or treated with both DCB and DES in the target vessel were excluded from the study. Results The baseline clinical characteristics showed that compared with DES group, patients in DCB group had a lower LVEF (56.3±10.8% vs 61.3±7.8%, p=0.01). Regarding RA, no significant differences were observed between the two groups in terms of initial or final burr size, or the total number of burrs used. However, the RA speed was significantly higher in the DCB group (19.5±1.5 vs 18.7±1.7×105 RPM, p=0.003). Furthermore, device diameter and length were significantly smaller and shorter in the DCB group compared to the DES group (2.6 ±0.3 mm vs 3.0 ± 0.4 mm, p &lt; 0.001; and 38.1 ±18.8 mm vs 53.2 ± 22.6 mm, p&lt; 0.001, respectively). Post-procedural target vessel QFR (PPQFRV) was higher in DES group as compared with DCB group(0.88±0.11 vs 0.78±0.12, p&lt;0.001). During the median follow-up of 571 days, no significant differences were observed between the DES and DCB groups regarding the rates of clinically driven target vessel revascularization (10.1% vs. 8.1%), target vessel myocardial infarction (3.6% vs. 5.4%), or cardiac death (1.8% vs. 2.7%). The long-term rates of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were also comparable between the two groups (14.4% in DES group vs 16.2% in DCB group, p=0.816)(Figure 1). Multivariate analysis revealed that PPQFRV lacked independent prognostic value for MACE in the entire cohort and the DES subgroup. In contrast, PPQFRV remained independently associated with MACE risk among patients treated with DCB (p=0.029). The cut-off value for PPQFRV in the DCB group to predict MACEs during follow-up was 0.715 (AUC=0.758; sensitivity, 0.667; specificity, 0.806; P=0.048)(Figure2). Conclusion For highly calcified coronary lesions, relative to DES, treatment with DCB after RA could provide clinically favorable results despite lower PPQFRV. Lower PPQFRV (0.72-0.80) may be acceptable after DCB treatment in such lesions.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Long term clinical outcomes of drug-coated balloon angioplasty in comparison to drug eluting stents following rotational atherectomy for calcified coronary lesions: a single center retrospective study

abstract: Abstract Background Perfusion balloon, which enables long-time pre-dilation by maintaining coronary blood flow, is expected to enhance thrombus/plaque compression and promote lesion dilation during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). On the other hand, direct stenting without pre-dilation aims to avoid unnecessary manipulation of the target lesion and improve epicardial and myocardial reperfusion as well as clinical outcomes. Purpose We sought to investigate the efficacy and safety of long-time pre-dilation with perfusion balloon prior to stent implantation as compared to direct stenting in primary PCI for acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Methods We studied 279 AMI patients who underwent primary PCI with long-time (180 sec) pre-dilation using a perfusion balloon prior to stent implantation (n = 105) or direct stenting (n = 174). The findings of angiography and intravascular imaging at post-PCI, as well as major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or clinically-driven target lesion failure) at one-year follow-up, were compared between the two groups. Results Patient and lesion characteristics at baseline were not different between the perfusion balloon pre-dilation group and the direct stenting group. The diameter of perfusion balloon for pre-dilation was 3.0 mm (interquartile range [IQR]: 3.0–3.0 mm). Stent diameter was similar between the two groups. The frequency of post-dilation balloon use was comparable between the two groups. At post-PCI, minimum stent area was numerically larger in the perfusion balloon pre-dilation group than the direct stenting group (7.16 mm2 [IQR: 5.77–8.20 mm2] vs. 6.88 mm2 [IQR: 5.38–8.06 mm2], p = 0.172). Stent expansion index (83 % [IQR: 75–92 %] vs. 78 % [IQR: 69–88 %], p = 0.001) and minimum intra-stent lumen area (6.57 mm2 [IQR: 5.55–8.12 mm2] vs. 5.98 mm2 [IQR: 4.92–7.42 mm2], p = 0.003) were significantly larger in the perfusion balloon pre-dilation group than the direct stenting group. The frequency of irregular thrombus/plaque protrusion was significantly lower in the perfusion balloon pre-dilation group than the direct stenting group (14 % vs. 48 %, p &lt; 0.001). Maximum thrombus/plaque protrusion area was significantly smaller in the perfusion balloon pre-dilation group than the direct stenting group (0.31 mm2 [IQR: 0.00–0.59 mm2] vs. 0.66 mm2 [IQR: 0.00–1.31 mm2], p &lt; 0.001). There was no significant difference between the two groups in the frequency of slow flow/no reflow and distal embolization during PCI, nor in the frequency of MACE at one-year follow-up. Conclusion In primary PCI for AMI, the long-time pre-dilation with a perfusion balloon prior to stent implantation, compared to direct stenting, resulted in a larger intra-stent lumen area by reducing irregular thrombus/plaque protrusion without increasing slow flow/no reflow and distal embolization.ESC2026image1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.ESC2026image2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Efficacy and safety of long-time pre-dilation with perfusion balloon prior to stent implantation in acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-eluting balloon (DEB) angioplasty is increasingly used across the spectrum of chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) and acute coronary syndromes (ACS), but comparative lesion-level data for ACS versus CCS procedures are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-centre analysis of 398 consecutive patients (mean age 67.1±12.6 years, 83.2% male) treated with DEB, yielding 518 DEB-treated lesions. Hypertension, dyslipidaemia and diabetes were present in 77.4%, 78.4% and 38.2% of patients, respectively. Baseline presentation was STEMI in 21.4%, NSTEMI 29.1%, unstable angina 4.3% and chronic coronary syndrome 45.0%. ACS (STEMI/NSTEMI/UA for 271 lesions (52.3%), whereas 247 lesions (47.7%) were CCS. Lesion complexity was frequent (bifurcation 40.9%, de novo 75.5%, in-stent restenosis 24.9%). The primary endpoint was lesion-level TLF (composite of TLR and non-TLR events including MI/CV death); secondary endpoints were TLR and TLF components. Univariate comparisons (Fisher’s exact test) and penalised multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results Over follow-up, TLF occurred in 12/271 ACS lesions (4.43%) versus 2/247 CCS lesions (0.81%; odds ratio [OR] 5.68, p=0.013). In contrast, TLR rates were low and similar (0.74% ACS vs 0.81% CCS, OR 0.91, p=1.000). Subanalysis of TLF components and secondary outcomes showed increased cardiovascular death (2.95% vs 0.81%, p=0.110) and all-cause death (4.43% vs 2.04%, p=0.146), while follow-up MI rates were comparable (2.58% vs 2.02%, p=0.775), as well as numerically higher non-TLR events in ACS lesions (18.1% vs 12.6%, p=0.089). In multivariable analysis, ACS presentation remained an independent predictor of TLF (adjusted OR 6.15, 95% CI 1.66–22.82; p=0.007), and bifurcation lesions were also associated with higher TLF risk (adjusted OR 4.48, 95% CI 1.30–15.44; p=0.018); other lesion characteristics, AHA class and segment location were not significant. Conclusion In this analysis, ACS presentation was independently associated with a six-fold higher risk of target lesion failure after DEB PCI compared with CCS, driven predominantly by cardiac death and target-vessel MI rather than repeat revascularisation. Importantly, TLR rates remained very low and comparable between ACS and CCS lesions, suggesting preserved local anti-restenotic efficacy of the DEB platform. This pattern contrasts with contemporary drug-eluting stent (DES) data, where excess adverse events in ACS are typically driven by both thrombotic complications and restenosis-related TLR. The absence of increased TLR in ACS lesions suggests that biological instability of ACS—rather than insufficient antiproliferative effect—may account for the higher event rates. These findings highlight that, similar to DES in ACS, overall outcomes remain influenced by clinical presentation; however, DEBs appear to maintain local lesion control comparable to CCS when adequate lesion preparation is achieved.Multivariable Logistic Regression for TLFFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Baseline CharacteristicsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Acute coronary syndrome vs chronic coronary syndrome drug-eluting balloon PCI: a lesion-level analysis of predictors and outcomes of target lesion failure

abstract: Abstract Background Bioresorbable polymer drug eluding stents in coronary interventions have shown promising, yet mixed results in terms of outcome. The long-term results in case of bifurcation interventions remains largely unknown. Purpose The goal of this study is to elucidate the long-term outcome of usage of bioresorbable polymer stents versus durable stents in a large volume center. Methods We investigated 3991 patients in a large registry undergoing percutaneous coronary bifurcation intervention with a follow up time of three years. 17.9% of patients received bioresorbable polymer and 82.1% received durable polymer stents respectively. Primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE) consisting of death, myocardial infarction, or target lesion re-intervention. Survival was analysed with Kaplan-Meier curves and proportional hazard models. Results MACE occurred in 20.7% of patients, which received bioresorbable polymer and in 24.5% of patients which received durable polymer stents respectively. Survival analysis has shown no statistical difference between the types of stents (log rank=0.013, P=0.909). Conclusions Stenting of bioresorbable versus durable polymers in bifurcation lesions have shown no statistical difference after three years.Survival bio versus durable stentsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comparison of long term results after percutanous coronary intervention in coronary bifurcation lesions using drug-eluding stents with durable or resorbable polymer

abstract: Abstract Background Randomized trials have demonstrated similar long-term mortality with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in unprotected left main coronary artery disease (ULMCAD). However, contemporary real-world outcomes remain unclear. Purpose To compare in-hospital mortality (IHM) and 5-year mortality (5-yr) between PCI and CABG in a contemporary ULMCAD cohort, including patients with ejection fraction ≤35% (HFrEF), diabetes, and surgical turndown status, and to evaluate outcomes among PCI patients treated with IVUS guidance or Impella support, as well as temporal trends in revascularization. Methods We performed a retrospective study of patients with ULMCAD treated at our clinic from 2009–2024. Baseline demographic, comorbidity, laboratory, procedural, and outcome data were collected. Primary outcomes were IHM and 5-yr mortality. Univariate analyses compared PCI and CABG overall and among patients with HFrEF or diabetes. Exploratory subgroup analyses assessed 5-yr by surgical candidacy (PCI despite surgical acceptance, surgical turndown, and CABG). Additional univariate analyses evaluated PCI patients with HFrEF treated with versus without Impella and PCI with versus without IVUS guidance. Temporal trends were assessed using annual PCI and CABG utilization rates (per 100 patients) and the Mann–Kendall test. Results A total of 4,366 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 727 (16.7%) underwent PCI and 3,639 (83.3%) underwent CABG. Compared to CABG, PCI showed lower IHM (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.27–0.97; p=0.04) but a significant increase in 5-yr mortality (OR 2.94, 2.45–3.53; p&lt;0.01; Pic. 1A). 5-yr was higher in the PCI subgroup compared with CABG among patients with HFrEF (OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.89–3.89, p&lt;0.001) and diabetes (OR 3.06, 95% CI 2.31–4.06, p&lt;0.001). Among PCI patients, 489 (56.3%) underwent surgical evaluation; 29.3% underwent PCI despite CABG recommendation, while 70.7% were turned down for surgery. Picture 1B demonstrates 5-yr mortality in these subgroups compared with CABG (p&lt;0.0001). In the PCI subset, IVUS demonstrated a trend toward reduced 5-yr (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54–1.04; p=0.079; Pic. 1C), whereas no significant difference was observed with Impella use among patients with HFrEF (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.36–1.56; p=0.432; Pic. 1D). Over the study period, PCI utilization increased from 0.45 to 7.51 per 100 patients (p=0.022), while CABG declined from 50.0 to 17.5 per 100 patients (p&lt;0.001; Pic. 2). Conclusions In this retrospective cohort, PCI utilization increased while CABG declined. Although CABG was associated with improved 5-yr overall, IHM was lower with PCI. Among PCI patients who underwent surgical evaluation, exclusion of those deemed unsuitable for surgery (70.7%) resulted in similar outcomes through three years, with late separation favoring CABG. A trend toward reduced 5-yr was observed with IVUS, with no significant difference seen with Impella.Picture 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Picture 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Management of unprotected left main coronary disease with PCI versus CABG: a single-center retrospective study

abstract: Abstract Background The optimal revascularization strategy in patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction (MI) complicated by cardiogenic shock (CS) remains uncertain. Prior studies comparing multivessel (MV) and culprit-vessel–only (CV-only) revascularization have shown inconsistent findings. Purpose This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the differences in outcomes following MV versus CV-only revascularization in patients with acute MI complicated by CS. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library was conducted through January 2026 to identify studies comparing MV versus CV-only percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute MI complicated by CS. Meta-analysis inclusion criteria followed Cochrane guidelines. Three reviewers independently extracted data and assessed study quality. Risk of bias was determined using the ROBINS-I and ROB-2 tools. We pooled dichotomous data using odds ratios (OR) to describe effect sizes, employing a Mantel-Haenszel procedure in a random-effects model, with a 95% confidence interval. Results We included a total of 31 studies (29 observational and 2 RCTs) comprising 220,306 patients (69.7% CV-only; 30.3% MV). Among patients with acute MI complicated by CS, no significant differences were observed between MV and CV-only PCI for: short-term mortality (OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.95–1.20; p=0.30; I²=90%); late-term mortality (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.75–1.11; p=0.34; I²=83%); cardiac death (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.60–1.16; p=0.29; I²=69%); MACE (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.94–1.29; p=0.22; I²=80%); major bleeding (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.94–1.36; p=0.20; I²=83%); reinfarction (OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.89–1.26; p=0.53; I²=0%); and heart failure rehospitalization (OR 1.40, 95% CI 0.94–2.09; p=0.10; I²=39%). However, MV-PCI was associated with a lower risk of repeat revascularization (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.46–0.98; p=0.04; I²=78%) but a higher risk of new renal replacement therapy (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.32–1.49; p&lt;0.00001; I²=0%) and stroke (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.08–1.28; p&lt;0.0001; I²=0%). Conclusions Despite the limitations of predominantly observational data, this updated meta-analysis shows that MV PCI in acute MI complicating CS does not improve short- or long-term mortality compared with a CV-only strategy. Randomized trial data are needed to further clarify the safety and optimal use of complete revascularization in this high-risk population.FIGCS11For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.FIGCSMI2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Culprit-only versus multivessel percutaneous coronary intervention in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis
