abstract: Abstract Aim Resistant angina despite optimal medical treatment (OMT) is a common condition in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) that reduces their quality of life. In these patients, the presence of chronic total occlusion (CTO) is a strong predictor of incomplete revascularization. A better understanding of the burden of angina in these patients and the improvement in quality of life after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is critical in determining treatment management. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between successful CTO-PCI and health status variability in patients with angina or equivalent symptoms. Materials and Methods Between 2020 and 2025, 109 patients who presented to our clinic with a diagnosis of CCS and were found to have CTO were included in the study. Patients were divided into two groups: those who underwent successful PCI and those who only received OMT. Patients were evaluated at baseline and 12 months later using the "Seattle Angina Questionnaire," "Rose Dyspnea Score," and "Canadian Cardiovascular Society Angina Score." Results Demographic data, laboratory variables, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were similar among the patients included in the study. Except for a history of cerebrovascular accident (CVA), no statistically significant clinical features were observed. The number of patients with LAD CTO was 7 (13.7%) in the OMT group and 33 (56.9%) in the PCI group, and was statistically significant (p &lt;0.001). The median J-CTO score was 2 (2.0-3.0) in the OMT group and 1 (0.0-2.0) in the PCI group, and was found to be significantly higher in the OMT group (P&lt;0.001). In both the OMT and PCI groups, CCS and RDS scores showed a significant decrease compared to baseline at the end of 12 months (p&lt;0.001). However, when comparing the change in improvement values in CCS and RDS scores, this difference was found to be statistically more pronounced in patients in the PCI group (p=0.001, p=0.029, respectively). When the baseline and 12-month values of the SAQ parameters were analyzed, patients in both groups showed a statistically significant improvement in all five parameters and the summary score compared to baseline values. When comparing the improvement change values of the groups, it was found that this difference was significantly greater in patients in the PCI group compared to the OMT group in all parameters (p&lt;0.001). Conclusion Significant improvement was observed in all SAQ parameters, CCS Angina Score, and Rose Dyspnea Score in patients in both groups. However, when the amount of change after one year was examined, the improvement in the PCI group was found to be significantly higher than in the OMT group. To improve the success of CTO interventions, careful patient selection focusing on symptomatic patients and determining the risk category of the lesion are important.SAQ scoreFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.CCS Angina Score and Rose Dyspnea ScoreFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comparison of the effects of percutaneous coronary intervention and medical treatment on quality of life in patients with chronic total occlusion

abstract: Abstract Background There are no definitive randomized trials demonstrating prognostic benefit of chronic total occlusion percutaneous intervention (CTO-PCI) and prior studies have been neutral due to lack of power and high cross-over rates. The main anticipated gain is therefore symptomatic relief and better quality of life. Given the complexity of CTO-PCI more data is needed. Purpose To evaluate the impact of CTO-PCI on quality of life and major adverse cerebrovascular and cardiac events (MACCE). Methods The NOrdic-Baltic Randomized Registry Study for Evaluation of PCI in Chronic Total Coronary Occlusion (NOBLE-CTO, NCT03392415), multicenter, multinational randomized trial, ran from June 2018 to August 2025. Patients eligible for CTO-PCI with a vessel diameter ≥ 3.0 mm were offered enrollment. Main exclusion criteria were life expectancy &lt;1 year, dialysis and inability to undergo cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Patients were randomly assigned to optimal medical therapy (OMT) or PCI. Following inclusion, Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) was recorded at baseline and at 6 months. Subsequently, the OMT group was offered cross-over. Endpoints were change in SAQ and MACCE (all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, revascularization, stroke and transitory cerebral ischemia). Premature ending of the trial due to slow inclusion gave power to evaluate SAQ only. Results Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Of 247 patients included for analysis, 123 received PCI, and 124 OMT. Mean age was 66.8 years (±8.9), 205 (83.0%) were male, 180 (72.9%) were smokers, 207 (83.8%) had hypercholesterolemia, 184 (71.0%) hypertension and 20 (22.7%) diabetes mellitus. 122 (49.4%) patients had a history of PCI, and 11 (4.5%) coronary artery bypass grafting. 143 (57.9%) had multivessel disease. In 147 (60.7%) the index lesion was RCA, 52 (21.5%) LAD and 43 (17.8%) CX. Mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 50.8% (±14.6%). Mean follow-up at time of analyses (30-09-2025) was 4.35 years with a combined 1073.94 patient years of follow-up. 17 (13.7%) of OMT patients chose PCI after 6 months. In both arms SAQ increased significantly during follow-up, without any difference between arms. In patients with an initial Quality of Life Score &lt;60, a larger increase in Angina Frequency Score (PCIΔ25.76 vs OMTΔ20.62, p=0.008), Quality of Life Score (PCIΔ39.41 vs OMTΔ28.76, p=0.01) and Treatment Satisfaction Score (PCIΔ2.48 vs OMTΔ0.89, p=0.026) was found among patients who underwent PCI (Figure 1). In patients with a CCS &gt;1 at enrolment a larger increase in Quality of Life Score (PCIΔ22.8 vs OMTΔ14.68, p=0.007) and Treatment Satisfaction Score (PCIΔ2.74 vs OMTΔ1.88, p=0.043) among patients who underwent PCI, was observed (Figure 2). Conclusion This randomized trial showed that both CTO-PCI and OMT have equally good effect on quality of life. In patients with poor baseline quality of life, CTO-PCI was superior. There was no difference in MACCE between groups.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of PCI versus optimal medical therapy on quality of life in patients with chronic total occlusions: NOBLE-CTO randomized controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background Severe coronary calcification remains a major determinant of procedural difficulty and failure in chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO-PCI). Among calcification patterns, “full moon”–like calcification on cardiac computed tomography (CT) has been considered particularly unfavourable; however, its assessment is susceptible to calcium blooming artefacts, and prior evaluations have largely relied on limited cross-sectional analysis. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the impact of more accurately classified CT-derived full moon–like calcification on procedural characteristics and clinical outcomes of CTO-PCI. Methods This registry was a retrospective, multicentre observational study conducted at 42 centres in Japan. Patients who underwent CTO-PCI between April 2022 and August 2024 and had pre-procedural contrast-enhanced cardiac CT within 1 year were screened. Calcification morphology was reassessed using window level/window width adjustment (400/1500) to minimise blooming artefacts, combined with three-dimensional CT analysis. “True full moon” calcification was defined as circumferential luminal occupation persisting even after window adjustment (Figure 1A). The primary endpoint was guidewire crossing success. Results A total of 91 CTO lesions were included. Guidewire crossing success was significantly lower in lesions with “True full moon” calcification compared to “Pseudo full moon” calcification (47.8% vs 83.8%; p=0.002) (Figure 1B). Multivariable logistic regression identified “true full moon” morphology and calcification length ≥15 mm as strong predictors of guidewire crossing failure. When both factors were present, guidewire crossing success was markedly reduced. Incorporation of these CT-based parameters significantly improved the prediction of procedural failure beyond the performance of established CTO complexity scores, including J-CTO (Multicentre CTO Registry of Japan), KCCT (Korean Multicentre CTO CT Registry), and CT-RECTOR (Computed Tomography Registry of Chronic Total Occlusion Revascularisation) scores (Figure 2). Conclusion PCI for CTO lesions with “True full moon” calcification is associated with a significantly lower guidewire crossing success rate. CT-derived true full moon morphology and longitudinal calcification extent provide incremental prognostic value and may enhance pre-procedural risk stratification and procedural planning for CTO-PCI.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of “Full Moon” calcification assessed by preprocedural cardiac computed tomography on guidewire crossing in percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion: FULL MOON registry

abstract: Abstract Background In coronary chronic total occlusion (CTO), revascularization is often guided by angiographic collaterals and relative perfusion. However, whether these indices reflect actual hemodynamic reserve remains unclear. Purpose We aimed to investigate the relationship between morphological supply and dynamic reserve, with the latter defined by an O2 pulse plateau during cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) as a marker of global hemodynamic limitation. Methods We prospectively included 38 CTO patients (33 men; median age, 71.0 [IQR, 62.8–77.3] years) scheduled for PCI. Patients underwent CPET, dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), and adenosine myocardial perfusion SPECT (MPS). O2 pulse, defined as VO2 divided by heart rate, represents the oxygen volume extracted per heartbeat; a plateau in this parameter reflects a stroke volume limitation induced by extensive ischemia. Contractile response in the CTO territory during DSE was categorized into five patterns: normal, sustained improvement, worsening, biphasic, or no change. Patients were stratified by O2 pulse plateau status: the ischemia (+) group (n=12) vs. the (-) group (n=26). Results Resting LVEF was preserved and comparable between groups (p=0.22). The incidence of a biphasic wall motion pattern on DSE, induced by high-dose dobutamine and indicating local mechanical limitation, was significantly more frequent in the O2 pulse plateau (+) group than in the (-) group (83.3% vs. 46.2%, p=0.03); this finding was consistent with global hemodynamic limitation. Conversely, morphological and relative perfusion parameters showed possible discordance; neither Rentrop collateral grade (p=0.47) nor SPECT-ischemia (58.3% vs. 73.1%, p=0.37) differed significantly between groups. Conclusion While angiographic and pharmacological perfusion metrics primarily provide anatomical information on the supply side, dynamic stress testing (CPET and DSE) may provide clinically relevant insights into hemodynamic and contractile limitations under high-demand conditions in CTO; these parameters do not necessarily coincide.Functional Reserve vs. Supply in CTOFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Patient Characteristics and Imaging FindingsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Morphological supply and dynamic reserve mismatch in coronary chronic total occlusion: a multimodality imaging study

abstract: Abstract Introduction Chronic total occlusion(CTO)lesions are commonly encountered in patients with coronary artery disease and associated with major adverse cardiovascular outcomes and mortalities.With emerging technical success, percutaneous coronary intervention(PCI) of CTO lesions is considered safe and feasible,and its comparative procedural outcomes and survival benefits against optimal medical therapy(OMT) remain controversial1,2 Objective Our primary aim was to evaluate the benefit of PCI compared with OMT in patients with CTO over extended medium-term follow-up of a dedicated CTO registry. Further objectives were to compare a 5-year all-cause cardiovascular mortality among patients undergoing CTO-PCI compared with optimal medical therapy (OMT) alone. Methods and Results From January 2015 to December 2018 , a total of 125 patients with CTO lesions were enrolled into a large single-centre registry and followed for 5 years. We included patients who had true native vessel CTO , viable myocardium ,and had confirmed J-CTO score &gt;3 .We excluded patients whose data were incomplete, whom had non-viable myocardium , whom not on optimised medical therapy(OMT )or non-compliance with OMT. We classified patients into the CTO-PCI group (n=47) or OMT group (n=44). Patients with multivessel disease received PCI for obstructive non-CTO and with previous coronary artery bypass graft(CABG)included in both groups. Baseline characteristics include cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, etc), procedural complexity(J-CTO, access, technical approach), and 5-year survival benefits in both arms. In the CTO-PCI group, 40 patients (85%) underwent successful revascularization. Average J-CTO score was 3 suggestive of highly complex anatomy. Antegrade approach was used 90%with experienced operator achieving higher procedural success rate of 94%. One patient died within procedure and one died due to covid infection post-operatively. 90% of patients with CTO-PCI were discharged asymptomatically and on optimised anti-anginal therapy whereas all of them continued maximal one anti-anginal medication. On extended follow-up of five years, the majority of CTO-PCI group(96%) had higher survival rates compared to 72% of patients in medical therapy arm. This difference was statistically significance in chi-squared of 9.24 ,with p value of 0.02. Odds ratio after adjustment for baseline factors (OR for mortality with medical therapy compared to successful CTO-PCI) was 8.42 [95% CI , 1.77-40.32]; p= 0.008). Conclusion Successful CTO-PCI in a complex anatomical subset (J-CTO 3 or above) confers a medium-term survival benefit compared to medical therapy alone in addition to better symtom reliefand quality of life. It remains to be seen that if the results can be replicated in large scale multi-centred studies for prognostic significance. If proven, these findings will help us in decision making at Heart MDT for symptomatic patients with complex CTO.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Medium-term survival benefits and vessel CTOsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Medium-term mortality and safety of complex antegrade CTO-PCI in stable angina: a real world registry- observational comparison with optimised medical therapy

abstract: Abstract Background High bleeding risk (HBR) is common among elderly patients presenting with myocardial infarction (MI) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). In the FIRE trial, HBR status defined according to the Academic Research Consortium–HBR (ARC-HBR) criteria was highly prevalent and associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse events at 1 year. Data on the long-term prognostic implications of HBR and on the performance of newer bleeding risk stratification tools in this population remain limited. The PRECISE-HBR score is a novel risk model developed to provide comprehensive bleeding risk assessment across the spectrum of patients undergoing PCI, demonstrating improved discrimination for bleeding events compared with previous scores, including ARC-HBR and PRECISE-DAPT. Its role in elderly MI patients with multivessel disease and its long-term prognostic impact have not been investigated. Purpose To assess whether the long-term benefits of complete revascularization are consistent across bleeding risk strata defined by the PRECISE-HBR score in older MI patients enrolled in the FIRE trial. Methods In the FIRE trial, 1,445 patients aged ≥75 years with MI and multivessel disease were randomized to complete or culprit-only revascularization. Patients were stratified according to PRECISE-HBR score into three categories: ≤22 (no HBR), 23–26 (HBR), and ≥27 (very HBR). The primary endpoint was a 3-year composite of death, MI, stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularization. The key secondary endpoint was cardiovascular death or MI at 3 years. The safety endpoint was a composite of contrast-associated acute kidney injury, stroke, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3–5 bleeding. Results 682 patients were classified as no HBR, 197 as HBR, and 566 as very HBR. Compared with no HBR, HBR and very HBR patients had a higher risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.27–2.33; HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.53–2.39) and of the secondary endpoint (HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.23–2.85; HR 2.23, 95% CI 1.63–3.04). Very HBR patients were also at increased risk of the safety endpoint (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.10–1.88). No significant differences in bleeding events were observed across PRECISE-HBR strata at 3 years. Complete revascularization reduced the primary outcome in no HBR, HBR and very HBR patients, with negative interaction testing (p for interactions 0.739). No heterogeneity according to bleeding risk was observed for secondary or safety endpoints. Conclusions In elderly MI patients, complete revascularization provided sustained ischemic and safety benefit at 3 years irrespective of PRECISE-HBR–defined bleeding risk. These findings support the use of physiology-guided complete revascularization regardless HBR status. The absence of long-term bleeding differences may be explained by discontinuation of dual antiplatelet therapy beyond 12 months, attenuating late bleeding risk.Outcomes PRECISE HBR FIREFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.KM PRECISE HBR FIREFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Complete revascularization across PRECISE-HBR bleeding risk strata in older patients with myocardial infarction and multivessel coronary artery disease: a FIRE trial subanalysis

abstract: Abstract Background Frailty is a multidimensional geriatric syndrome that may amplify procedural risk and attenuate recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention, yet reported prevalence and prognostic magnitude vary across frailty instruments and clinical settings. Purpose To quantify (1) frailty prevalence by assessment instrument, (2) associations between frailty and mortality and bleeding after percutaneous coronary intervention, and (3) the dose–response relationship across frailty severity. Methods PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to 30 September 2025 for observational studies enrolling adults undergoing contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention with outcomes reported by frailty status using a defined instrument. Random-effects meta-analysis (inverse-variance) pooled adjusted relative risks; subgroup analyses were prespecified by instrument type (bedside phenotype/functional tools, Clinical Frailty Scale, and administrative/deficit scores). Dose–response analyses compared robust, pre-frail/vulnerable, and frail strata when available. Results Fifteen cohort studies comprising 14,716,621 patients were included. In bedside-assessed cohorts, the pooled frailty prevalence was 19.4% (range 7.7%–32.6%), whereas administrative coding algorithms identified high-risk frailty in 0.03%. Frailty was consistently associated with higher all-cause mortality. In studies using the Clinical Frailty Scale, frailty conferred a threefold higher mortality risk (hazard ratio 3.40, 95% confidence interval 2.23–5.16); phenotype/functional instruments showed a similar direction of effect (hazard ratio 2.18, 95% confidence interval 1.52–3.11), while administrative/deficit scores produced larger estimates (hazard ratio &gt;7). Eight studies provided severity strata, demonstrating a graded relationship: pre-frail/vulnerable patients had intermediate risk (adjusted hazard ratios 1.70–3.82 vs robust), with further escalation in frail patients (2.37–7.81). Frailty was also associated with major bleeding after percutaneous coronary intervention (hazard ratio 3.14, 95% confidence interval 2.00–4.94). Conclusion(s) Frailty is common when measured at the bedside and is a strong, graded predictor of mortality and bleeding after percutaneous coronary intervention. Routine pre-procedure frailty assessment may improve risk stratification, shared decision-making, and tailoring of peri-procedural and post-discharge care.Forest Plot of Frail vs Non-Frail PatientsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Subgroup Analysis by Frailty InstrumentsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Frailty and outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and dose–response meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Patients undergoing PCI are clinically heterogeneous, and single-variable stratification often fails to capture distinct risk trajectories. Data-driven unsupervised phenotyping in real-world cohorts may identify clinically interpretable subgroups to support refined risk assessment and follow-up. Purpose To identify clinical phenotypes among PCI-treated patients using unsupervised clustering and to evaluate phenotype-specific differences in ischaemic, bleeding, and mortality-related outcomes. Methods Data were derived from a real-world coronary artery disease specialty database of PCI-treated patients from 82 hospitals, with an independent single-center PCI cohort for external validation. We performed unsupervised phenotyping using the k-prototypes algorithm. Kaplan–Meier curves were used to compare cumulative event risks across phenotypes. For the primary outcome, multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were fitted to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), using Cluster 2 as the reference. The primary endpoint was the composite NACE, defined as the occurrence of any of the following: cardiovascular death (CD), myocardial infarction (MI), intracranial haemorrhage, ischaemic stroke, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 bleeding (BARC3). Secondary endpoints were the individual components of these composites. Results A total of 197,387 PCI-treated patients were classified into three clinically interpretable phenotypes: Cluster 1 (n=7,002), Cluster 2 (n=107,054), and Cluster 3 (n=83,331). Cluster 1 was an acute high-risk, event-driven phenotype with a high STEMI prevalence (45.4%). Cluster 3 was an older, female-predominant chronic-burden phenotype (age 63.62±9.79 years; female 57.1%), distinct from Cluster 2 (STEMI 12.9%; female 34.5%) (all P&lt;0.001).Over 1-year follow-up, NACE Kaplan–Meier curves differed significantly among phenotypes (P&lt;0.001). In multivariable Cox models, both Cluster 1 and Cluster 3 had higher risk of NACE compared with Cluster 2 (Cluster 1: HR 1.138, 95% CI 1.042–1.242, P=0.004; Cluster 3: HR 1.122, 95% CI 1.079–1.167, P&lt;0.001). Cluster 3 also had increased risk of BARC type 3 bleeding (HR 1.269, 95% CI 1.172–1.375, P&lt;0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly higher in Cluster 1 and Cluster 3 (Cluster 1: HR 1.371, 95% CI 1.265–1.485; Cluster 3: HR 1.270, 95% CI 1.217–1.325; both P&lt;0.001). In contrast, MACCE was lower in Cluster 3 (HR 0.894, 95% CI 0.867–0.923, P&lt;0.001), suggesting that composite endpoints may be influenced by differences in event composition across phenotypes. External validation showed consistent directions of phenotype–outcome associations. Conclusion(s) Unsupervised clustering identified three PCI phenotypes with distinct ischaemia–bleeding–mortality profiles, enabling finer risk stratification and underscoring the need to interpret composite endpoints alongside key individual outcomes.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.1-Year Clinical OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Not all pci patients share the same risk trajectory: unsupervised clustering identifies three clinical phenotypes with divergent ischaemia–bleeding–mortality profiles

abstract: Abstract Background Microaxial flow pump-supported high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (pHRPCI) has emerged as a revascularization strategy for patients with complex coronary artery disease who are not suitable candidates for surgery. However, the prognostic impact of baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in contemporary pHRPCI practice remains uncertain. Purpose To investigate the association between baseline LVEF, procedural complexity, and clinical outcomes in a large multicenter real-world pHRPCI cohort. Methods This multicenter observational study included patients undergoing pHRPCI at 22 Polish centers and one major German center (n=467). Patients were stratified by baseline LVEF ≤40% (n=324) and &gt;40% (n=143). Baseline characteristics, procedural parameters, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Multivariable Cox regression analyses identified independent predictors of 30-day and 1-year mortality. Results The cohort represented a highly complex pHRPCI population with extensive coronary disease and high clinical risk. Patients with LVEF ≤40% had a significantly higher baseline risk profile despite being younger, including higher EuroScore II (median 5.8% vs. 3.6%, p&lt;0.001), higher rate of chronic kidney disease (49.1% vs. 34.3%, p=0.003), and more advanced heart failure symptoms (NYHA III/IV: 65.0% vs. 35.2%, p&lt;0.001). Overall, coronary complexity was substantial, with a median SYNTAX score of 36 (IQR 25–46) and left main disease in 78.4%. Procedurally, extensive multivessel PCI was performed with a median of 3 treated vessels (IQR 2–3). A residual SYNTAX score ≤8 was achieved in 54.9% without differences between LVEF groups. Procedure-related complications reflected the high-risk nature of the population, with BARC 3–5 bleeding in 23.8% (20.9% vs. 30.2%, p=0.033) and access-site complications in 25.8% (22.6% vs. 32.9%, p=0.019), both significantly lower in patients with LVEF &lt;40%. LVEF &lt;40% was associated with higher early mortality (30-day mortality: 13.0% vs. 4.9%, p=0.009) and independently predicted early death in multivariable analysis (HR 3.11, 95% CI 1.35–7.18, p=0.008). In contrast, 1-year mortality was primarily driven by comorbidities including atrial fibrillation (HR 1.79, 95% CI 1.18–2.72, p=0.006), diabetes mellitus (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.16–2.63, p=0.007), dialysis dependency (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.01–4.52, p=0.048), and surgical risk assessed by EuroScore II (HR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00–1.04, p=0.039). In contrast, baseline LVEF was not independently associated with mid-term outcomes. Conclusion In a large contemporary multicenter real-world pHRPCI cohort, LVEF &lt;40% identifies patients at increased early procedural risk but does not independently determine mid-term prognosis. These findings suggest that the comorbidity burden, rather than ventricular function alone, drives outcomes after pHRPCI and may inform patient selection and risk stratification in complex high-risk PCI.30-day and 1-year survivalFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Predictors of early and mid-term mortality after microaxial flow pump–supported high-risk pci: the role of baseline LVEF in a large multicenter real-world cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Mechanical circulatory support with percutaneous ventricular assist devices (pVADs) has progressively expanded its role in the management of complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary interventions (CHIP). Among pVADs, Impella provides active left ventricular unloading and hemodynamic stabilization, potentially allowing safer and more complete revascularization in patients with advanced coronary artery disease and impaired cardiac function. However, robust long-term outcome data in this setting remain limited. Objectives To evaluate long-term clinical outcomes, procedural safety, and predictors of mortality in patients undergoing Impella-protected CHIP, using data from the international IMMERGE registry Methods IMMERGE was an international, multicenter, observational registry including patients treated with Impella CP, 5.0, or 5.5 for cardiogenic shock or high-risk PCI among 19 centers across the world between 2013 and 2025. The present analysis focused on 570 consecutive patients who underwent Impella-supported CHIP, with follow-up censored at 2 years. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary endpoints included in-hospital complications and long-term adverse events. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of mortality. Results The study population was predominantly male (82.3%), with a mean age of 71.7 ± 10.5 years and a high burden of cardiovascular comorbidities. Impella CP was used in 99.1% of cases, with device implantation performed before PCI in 81.0%. The most common PCI target was left anterior descending artery (LAD), accounting for 81.7% of cases; a bifurcation PCI was carried out in 367 patients, of whom 179 (48.8%) were treated with provisional stenting. Intracoronary imaging was performed in 52.5% of patients, mostly IVUS (48.4%). At 2-years censored follow-up, all-cause mortality was 19.8%, with an in-hospital mortality of 3.6% and 30-day mortality of 8.7%. Acute kidney injury (15.1%), vascular complications (14.5%), and major bleeding (13.8%) were the most frequent in-hospital adverse events. Independent predictors of long-term mortality included STEMI presentation, advanced age, diabetes mellitus and major bleeding (BARC 3–5). Conclusions In a large real-world, international cohort, Impella-protected CHIP was associated with acceptable early mortality and meaningful long-term survival. Although periprocedural complication rates remain non-negligible, these were lower than reported in the historical cohorts due to the increased operators’ expertise and ICU management.

appraisal.design_and_n: IMMERGE international multicentre observational registry (19 centres, 2013 to 2025); 570 consecutive patients with Impella-supported CHIP, follow-up censored at 2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry with no comparator group, so the contribution of mechanical support to outcomes cannot be judged.
appraisal.one_line: International multicentre registry reporting two-year outcomes after Impella-protected complex high-risk indicated PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2-years censored follow-up, all-cause mortality was 19.8%, with an in-hospital mortality of 3.6% and 30-day mortality of 8.7%; acute kidney injury (15.1%), vascular complications (14.5%) and major bleeding (13.8%) were the most frequent in-hospital events.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides some of the longest follow-up for Impella-supported high-risk PCI, a setting where randomised evidence on benefit versus unsupported PCI is lacking.

title: Long term outcomes in patients undergoing Impella protected high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention: insights from the international IMMERGE registry

abstract: Abstract Background Severely calcified coronary lesions often require plaque modification using atherectomy devices such as Rotablator™ or Diamondback®. However, even after adequate lesion preparation, stent underexpansion may occur. In such situations, particularly in lesions with calcified nodules, a stentless strategy using a drug-coated balloon (DCB) has recently been adopted. Nevertheless, the clinical outcomes of this approach remain unclear. Purpose We aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of DCB versus drug-eluting stent (DES) following atherectomy in severely calcified coronary lesions, further stratified into calcified sheet and calcified nodule based on intravascular imaging findings. Methods All consecutive severely calcified lesions requiring atherectomy at our institution between 2017 and 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Atherectomy devices included Rotablator™ and Diamondback®. The choice of final device (DCB or DES) was left to the operator’s discretion. Lesions were evaluated using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) and categorized as calcified sheet or calcified nodule. The primary endpoint was device-oriented cardiovascular events (DoCE), defined as ischemia-driven target lesion revascularization, myocardial infarction, or cardiac death. DoCE rates were compared between DCB and DES groups overall and within each calcification subtype. Results A total of 148 lesions were included as shown in figure 1 (DCB: n=56; DES: n=92). Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups (table). A representative case is shown in figure 2. Overall, DoCE rates were not significantly different between DCB and DES in severely calcified lesions (Figure 3A, P=0.14). When stratified by lesion morphology, DoCE rates were comparable between the two strategies in calcified sheet lesions (Figure 3 B, P=0.98). In contrast, in calcified nodules, DCB showed a trend toward lower DoCE compared with DES (Figure 3C, P=0.07). Conclusion A stentless strategy using DCB after atherectomy may be a feasible alternative to DES, particularly in lesions with calcified nodules.ESC slideFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Drug-coated balloon versus drug-eluting stent after atherectomy in severely calcified coronary lesions including calcified nodules

abstract: Abstract Background Patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for in-stent restenosis (ISR) lesions have been reported to experience worse outcomes than those treated for de novo lesions. However, no study has yet directly compared these two lesion types when treated in the same patient during the same procedure. Purpose To compare the risk of restenosis between ISR and de novo lesions treated during the same PCI procedure. Methods This retrospective, observational, single-centre cohort study included 1,493 patients who underwent PCI for at least one ISR lesion and one de novo lesion during the same procedure at a tertiary cardiac centre, between 2006 and 2015. Patients with cardiogenic shock and lesions located in close proximity were excluded. The primary endpoint was clinical restenosis, as assessed by the need for target lesion revascularisation (TLR), and the secondary endpoint was definite stent thrombosis. Both were evaluated at 1 and 3 years. Results A total of 1,493 patients were included, contributing 3,794 lesions, of which 1,766 were ISR lesions and 2,028 were de novo lesions. Clinical restenosis rates were significantly higher in ISR than in de novo lesions at 1 year (16.1% vs. 10.3%; HR=1.62, 95% CI 1.35–1.94; p &lt;0.001) and 3 years (22.4% vs. 15.3%; HR=1.55, 95% CI 1.33–1.80; p &lt;0.001). However, definite stent thrombosis rates were low and did not differ significantly between ISR and de novo lesions at 1 year (0.3% vs. 0.5%, HR=0.64, 95% CI 0.21–1.90; p = 0.416) or 3 years (0.5% vs. 0.6%; HR=0.76, 95% CI 0.31–1.86; p = 0.548). Conclusions In patients undergoing PCI for both ISR and de novo lesions, ISR lesions were associated with a significantly higher risk of clinical restenosis at 1 and 3 years than de novo lesions, whereas definite stent thrombosis did not differ between lesion types.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Risk of restenosis for in-stent restenosis and de novo lesions treated during the same percutaneous coronary intervention procedure

abstract: Abstract Background Patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for in-stent restenosis (ISR) with multiple stent layers represent a complex subgroup. However, the prognostic impact of multiple stent layers on long-term procedural and clinical outcomes remains unclear. Objectives To evaluate the association of multilayer versus single-layer lesions with long-term clinical outcomes and recurrent TLR in patients undergoing PCI for ISR. Methods This post hoc analysis of a randomised trial included 402 patients who underwent PCI in 500 ISR lesions. Lesions were classified into two groups according to the number of stent layers present at baseline: multilayer (≥2 layers) vs. single-layer (1 layer). Ten-year clinical outcomes included cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), and target lesion revascularisation (TLR). Recurrent TLR during follow-up was assessed by counting first and all subsequent TLR procedures. Results Overall 112 lesions (80 patients) were classified as multilayer and 388 lesions (322 patients) as single-layer. At 10 years, rates of cardiac death (32.0% vs. 29.6%; HR=1.14; 95% CI 0.73–1.78; p = 0.55) and MI (10.1% vs. 5.4%; HR=1.98; 95% CI 0.85–4.63; p = 0.11) were not different in patients with multilayer versus single-layer ISR, rates of TLR were significantly higher in the multilayer group as compared to single-layer ISR (54.1% vs. 40.5%; HR=1.45; 95% CI 1.05–2.02; p = 0.03). Overall, ≥1 repeat PCI was performed in 204 of 500 lesions (40.8%). Compared with single-layer lesions, multilayer lesions were associated with a higher risk of both first TLR (54.1% vs. 39.0%; hazard ratio (HR) 1.53, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.10–2.13; p = 0.01) and total number of recurrent TLR (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.03–1.93; p = 0.033). Conclusions In patients undergoing PCI for ISR, lesions with 2 or more stent layers were associated with a higher risk of recurrent revascularisation than single-layer lesions. However, patients in the multilayer group did not have a higher risk of cardiac death or myocardial infarction.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: The impact of multiple stent layers on the 10-year outcomes of patients treated with percutaneous coronary intervention for in-stent restenosis

abstract: Abstract Background The long-term outcomes of patients with in-stent restenosis (ISR) presenting with Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) are not well studied. This study aims at investigating the outcomes of patients with drug-eluting stents (DES)-ISR presenting with ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with DCB or thin strut-DES. Methods Consecutive patients from the Dragon-Register with DES-ISR who underwent PCI with thin-DES or paclitaxel-DCB were enrolled [Figure 1]. Primary outcome was target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary outcomes were target vessel revascularization (TVR) and device-oriented composite endpoint [DOCE, cardiac death, TLR, and target vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI)]. Propensity-score matching was used to adjust for baseline differences. Results A total of 1,317 patients were included in the pooled analysis of whom 585 (44.4%) were treated with a thin-DES and 732 (55,6%) with drug-coated balloons. In the crude analysis of patients with ACS (N = 697) undergoing PCI for ISR, thin-DES vs. DCB showed similar outcomes for TLR (HR = 1.21, 95% CI 0.78–1.86; P = 0.400), TVR (HR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.62–1.34; P = 0.641), MI (HR = 1.25, 95% CI 0.82–1.86; P = 0.281), TV-MI (HR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.43–1.90; P = 0.793), CV death (HR = 0.76, 95% CI 0.27–2.09; P = 0.589), and DOCE (HR = 1.04, 95% CI 0.70–1.54; P = 0.840). After propensity score matching (N = 606), the HRs remained non-significant for TLR (1.08, 95% CI 0.69–1.69; P = 0.731 [Figure 2]), TVR (0.88, 95% CI 0.59–1.31; P = 0.523), MI (1.24, 95% CI 0.80–1.91; P = 0.336), TV-MI (0.93, 95% CI 0.43–2.05; P = 0.865), CV death (0.75, 95% CI 0.26–2.18; P = 0.602), and DOCE (0.98, 95% CI 0.65–1.46; P = 0.904). Conclusions In patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for in-stent restenosis, treatment with thin-DES was associated with a numerical reduction in the rates of TLR and DOCE compared with DCB. However, these differences did not achieve statistical significance in either the crude or propensity score–matched analyses.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Long-term outcomes following DCB versus thin-strut DES for treatment of in-stent restenosis in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Despite the widespread clinical application of second-generation stent balloons, recurrent in-stent restenosis (RISR) remains one of the major adverse events following percutaneous coronary intervention. Pericoronary epicardial adipose tissue (PCAT) surrounds the coronary arteries without any anatomic barrier. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms between PCAT and recurrent restenosis in coronary arteries still remains unclear. Method We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing on PCAT samples collected from 3 groups: 1) controls (patients with valvular disease requiring surgery, n=4), 2) stable coronary artery disease (CCS, patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting, CABG, n=5), and 3) recurrent in-stent restenosis (RISR, n=5) Comparative analyses were performed including cellular compositional analysis, cell-type resolved transcriptomic changes, gene coexpression network analysis, and intercellular communication analysis. Results Clustering of 165,329 nuclei revealed 12 distinct clusters, with adipocytes, monocytes/macrophages, preadipocytes, and T cells as the predominant cell types across all groups. BCL11Bhigh T cells were significantly expanded in the RISR group. Subpopulation analysis of smooth muscle cell (SMC) identified a SKAP1high SMC subset.Gene Ontology (GO) analysis indicated that this subset is involved in immune regulation and T cell activation, while KEGG pathway analysis suggested its role in signaling pathways related to T cell differentiation. Conclusion This study presents the first comprehensive transcriptomics map of PCAT in patients. SKAP1high VSMCs within PCAT may play an immunoregulatory role in modulating T cell activation and expansion. Targeting these cells might present promising novel strategies for RISR.Transcriptomic landscape in RISRFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of human pericoronary epicardial adipose tissue across different stages of coronary artery disease: a study on recurrent in-stent restenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Paclitaxel-coated balloon (PCB) is an established treatment for coronary in-stent restenosis (ISR), yet the optimal lesion preparation strategy before PCB remains unclear. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate association between lesion preparation strategy and long-term clinical outcomes after PCB treatment for ISR. Methods This is a post-hoc analysis from the prospective, multicenter, real-world PEPCAD China registry which was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of PCB in the treatment of real world Chinese patients with coronary ISR. Patients were classified according to lesion preparation strategy: plain balloon angioplasty (PBA), scoring balloon angioplasty (SBA), or cutting balloon angioplasty (CBA). The primary endpoint was a device-oriented composite endpoint of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target lesion revascularization at 5 years. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate HR and 95% CI for composite endpoint, , adjusting for confounding factors. Results Among 465 patients enrolled, 246 patients (52.9%), 54 patients (11.6%), and 165 patients (35.5%) were in PBA, SBA, and CBA groups, respectively. The mean age was more than 60 years and about one fifth of the patients were female in all three groups. The prevalence of diabetes mellitus was 36.2% in the PBA group, compared with 42.6% in the SBA group and 40.0% in the CBA group. At 5 years, the primary composite endpoint occurred in 11.0% of PBA group, 16.7% of SBA group, and 23.6% of CBA group (log-rank p=0.003). After adjustment, CBA group was associated with a significantly higher risk of composite endpoint compared to PBA (adjusted HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.05–1.81, p=0.020). However, no significant differences were observed between the other groups (SBA group vs. PBA group adjusted HR: 1.33, 95%CI: 0.55-3.25, p=0.525; CBA group vs. SBA group adjusted HR: 1.33, 95%CI: 0.60-2.92, p=0.483)). Conclusion In this real-world ISR registry, lesion preparation with CBA before PCB was associated with increased long-term adverse cardiac events compared to PBA, whereas SBA showed similar outcomes to PBA or CBA. These findings call into question the use of CBA for lesion modification prior to PCB in ISR.
title: Lesion preparation strategy before paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty for in-stent restenosis: a multicenter real-world study

abstract: Abstract Background Drug-coated balloons (DCB) are established therapy for coronary in-stent restenosis and are increasingly used in small-vessel disease, where they showed non-inferiority to DES in randomized trials such as BASKET-SMALL 2. Current ESC and international consensus documents primarily frame DCB as a strategy for ISR and de novo small vessels (&lt;2.75–3.0 mm), with much less evidence in larger reference diameters. Concerns persist that using large-diameter DCBs may lead to suboptimal drug transfer and higher bailout DES rates. We therefore evaluated the safety of DCB ≥3.0 mm in routine practice. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-centre analysis of 398 consecutive patients (mean age 67.1±12.6 years, 83.2% male) treated with DEB, yielding 518 DEB-treated lesions. Lesions were stratified by mean DCB diameter: &lt;3.0 mm (n=358) vs ≥3.0 mm (n=160). The primary endpoint was bailout DES during the index procedure (Rescue DES). Secondary endpoints were lesion-level TLF, TLR, non-TLR revascularization and all-cause death. Univariate comparisons were followed by penalized multivariable logistic regression including vessel territory, de novo vs ISR, bifurcation, lesion preparation (NC, cutting, scoring, IVL balloons), intravascular imaging and procedural complications (dissection, perforation, rupture, no-reflow). Results Rescue DES occurred in 35 lesions (6.8% overall): 22/358 (6.1%) with DCB &lt;3.0 mm vs 13/160 (8.1%) with DCB ≥3.0 mm (crude OR 1.35; p=0.45). Rates of TLF, TLR, non-TLR and mortality were low in both groups (e.g. TLF 2.5% vs 3.1%; all-cause death 3.1% vs 3.8%; all p&gt;0.7). In the multivariable ridge model, use of DCB ≥3.0 mm was not independently associated with Rescue DES (adjusted OR 0.92; 95% CI 0.15–5.58; p=0.93), whereas procedural complications remained the main driver of bailout. Conclusions In this real-world lesion-level cohort, larger-diameter DCBs (≥3.0 mm) were not associated with higher bailout DES rates or worse lesion-level outcomes compared with DCBs &lt;3.0 mm. Although DCB therapy is traditionally considered a small-vessel strategy, our data suggest that, with meticulous lesion preparation and careful case selection, extending DCB use to larger epicardial vessels appears procedurally and clinically safe. These findings complement existing RCT and consensus data and support further prospective evaluation of DCB-only strategies beyond classic small-vessel indicationsBaseline CharacteristicsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Safety and efficacy of drug-eluting balloons in large coronary vessels: a lesion-level analysis of real-world PCI practice

abstract: Abstract Background In STEMI with high thrombus burden, immediate stenting increases distal embolization, potentially impairing myocardial recovery. Deferred stenting might improve outcomes, but the optimal adjunctive therapy remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluate the effects of deferred stenting with dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and triple therapy (including Apixaban) on myocardial recovery and microvascular perfusion in high thrombus burden STEMI. Methods In this randomized trial, 150 STEMI patients with high thrombus burden were assigned to three groups: immediate stenting, deferred stenting with DAPT, or deferred stenting with triple therapy including Apixaban. The primary endpoints were TIMI flow and myocardial blush grade (MBG) at 6 months. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), reinfarction, stroke, mortality, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) assessed by 3D speckle-tracking echocardiography. Results Deferred stenting with Apixaban led to superior angiographic and functional outcomes. TIMI III flow was achieved in 94% of patients in the Apixaban group compared to 76% in the DAPT group (p=0.03). MBG 3 was observed in 82.9% of patients in the Apixaban group, compared to 70.9% in DAPT and 30% in the immediate stenting group (p&lt;0.01). Apixaban significantly reduced no-reflow (p&lt;0.01) and improved LVEF (+14.5% vs. +12.9%, p=0.0067). No significant differences were noted in MACE and mortality at 6 months (p=0.45 and p=0.52, respectively). Conclusion Deferred stenting with triple therapy, including Apixaban, improves myocardial recovery and microvascular perfusion in high thrombus burden STEMI without reducing short-term MACE. Larger studies are needed to assess long-term survival and benefits.Figure 1-3D measurements of LV volumes and EFFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2-6 months FU of 3D LV volumes and EFFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Randomized trial of deferred stenting with apixaban in high thrombus burden stemi using 3d echocardiography

abstract: Abstract Background Cangrelor is recommended for the prevention of periprocedural thrombotic events in P2Y12 inhibitor-naïve patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Bleeding risk scores have not been definitely validated in cangrelor-treated patients. Aim We assessed the performance of the PRECISE-HBR score in PCI patients receiving cangrelor. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing PCI with cangrelor enrolled in the ICARUS registry were analyzed to assess the ability of the PRECISE-HBR score in predicting Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type 2-5 bleeding within 48 hours. The associations between the PRECISE-HBR score and 48-hour BARC 2-5 bleeding and net adverse clinical events (NACE) were also assessed. Results Among 1,067 patients undergoing PCI with cangrelor, the PRECISE-HBR score demonstrated modest discrimination (c-statistic 0.66, 95% CI 0.58-0.73) in predicting BARC 2-5 bleeding at 48 hours. The score classified 442 patients (41.4%) at high bleeding risk (HBR) (score ≥23). At 48 hours, BARC 2-5 bleeding (7.9% vs. 2.9%; odds ratio [OR] 2.91, 95% CI 1.63-5.21, p&lt;0.001) and NACE (9.8% vs. 3.8%; OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.62-4.53, p&lt;0.001) were more frequent in HBR than in non-HBR patients. Natural spline analyses showed a consistent, graded association between the PRECISE-HBR score and the risk of BARC 2-5 bleeding and NACE at 48 hours. Conclusions Among patients undergoing PCI treated with cangrelor, the PRECISE-HBR score identified 41% of patients at HBR and showed modest ability in predicting early bleeding. The PRECISE-HBR score was associated with BARC 2-5 bleeding and NACE at 48 hours, which supports its role for early risk stratification in this setting.AUC PRECISE-HBR scoreFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Spline functionFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Early bleeding risk prediction with the PRECISE-HBR score in PCI patients treated with cangrelor: the ICARUS registry

abstract: Abstract Background The introduction of drug-eluting stents (DES) has substantially improved safety and outcome after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), resulting in lower rates of procedure related complications such as target lesion revascularization (TLR) and stent thrombosis (ST). Previous studies have demonstrated associations between TLR and various stent-related characteristics, however, the prognostic performance of these individual parameters remains modest. Purpose This study evaluates the predictive performance of basic stent characteristics and introduces a novel length-to-diameter ratio (L/D-Ratio) as a composite metric for the prediction of TLR. Methods Patients who underwent PCI with second-generation DES implantation between 2010 and 2021 at a tertiary care centre were included in this study. L/D-Ratio was defined as the quotient of maximal stent length and minimal stent diameter. The primary endpoint was defined as TLR within a year after the index procedure and the secondary endpoint as 30-day ST. Results The total study population comprised of 11910 patients with a median age of 65 (IQR: 55-75) years and 73.8% (n = 8790) of patients being male. Within one year, TLR occurred in 589 (4.9 %) patients. These patients more frequently underwent elective index PCI (p &lt; 0.001) and had a higher prevalence of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes and chronic kidney disease (p for all &lt; 0.001). Compared to patients without, those with TLR showed significantly higher mortality rates (p = 0.024). Patients with TLR had a higher L/D-Ratio (7.5 vs. 7.2, p = 0.001), greater maximal stent length (23 vs. 22 mm, p = 0.007), greater total stent length (38.00 vs. 30.00 mm, p &lt; 0.001) and higher number of stents (2 vs. 1, p &lt; 0.001) than the ones without. Patients with a higher L/D-Ratio showed increased rates of TLR (log-rank p &lt; 0.001). In multivariable regression analysis for various clinical and interventional variables the L/D-Ratio demonstrated the strongest association with TLR (HR per 1-SD 1.15 [CI: 1.06 - 1.24], p &lt; 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) demonstrated superior discriminatory performance of the L/D-Ratio for TLR compared to stent diameter (AUC 0.539 vs. 0.465, p = 0.001) and comparable discriminatory performance to maximal stent length (AUC 0.539 vs. 0.533, p = 0.139). In secondary analysis, 30-day ST occurred in a total of 35 patients (0.29 %). Patients with higher L/D-Ratios had increased rates of ST (log-rank p = 0.002). In multivariable logistic regression only L/D-Ratio (adj. HR per 1-SD 1.41 [1.04 – 1.91], p = 0.026) and stent length (adj. HR per 1-SD 1.40 [1.01 – 1.92], p = 0.042) were associated with a higher risk of 30-day ST. Conclusion The L/D-Ratio is a suitable predictor of 1-year TLR and 30-day ST after second-generation DES implantation. Its predictive value seems to be mainly driven by stent length rather than diameter, highlighting the importance of optimal stent sizing.KM-Curves TLR and STFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.HR-Plot TLR and STFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Length-to-diameter ratio predicts target lesion revascularization in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Patients underwent complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are at higher ischemic and bleeding risk. Extended dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is usually recommended in this population to prevent future ischemic events in exchange with risk of bleeding. Purpose We aimed to investigate efficacy and safety of short-term DAPT after complex PCI. Method A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library up until January 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included if they compared at least two different antiplatelet strategies following complex PCI using 2nd generation or newer drug-eluting stents. Complex PCI was defined as the treatment of three vessels or ≥3 lesions, implantation of ≥3 stents, bifurcation treatment with a two-stent technique, total stent length ≥60 mm, or intervention for a chronic total occlusion as the target lesion. The primary outcomes were cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and any myocardial infarction. The secondary endpoint was major bleeding, defined as Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type 3 or 5 bleeding. Results A total of 10 RCTs comprising 21,790 patients were included (female 20.9%; mean age 66.2±11.4 years). Compared with standard 12-month DAPT, 3–6 months of DAPT followed by SAPT ranked highest for reducing cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.67, 95% CrI 0.56–0.78; SUCRA=0.73), myocardial infarction (HR 0.57, 95% CrI 0.50–0.63; SUCRA=0.86), and stroke (HR 0.58, 95% CrI 0.49–0.68; SUCRA=0.91), followed by 12 months of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy, 3 months of DAPT followed by 9 months of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy, and aspirin monotherapy. For major bleeding, 1 month of DAPT followed by 23 months of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy ranked best (HR 0.77, 95% CrI 0.67–0.89; SUCRA=0.77), followed by 3–6 months of DAPT followed by SAPT (HR 0.86, 95% CrI 0.72–1.04; SUCRA=0.38), whereas 1 month of DAPT followed by SAPT ranked last (SUCRA=0.29). Conclusions Patients underwent complex PCI with newer generation of drug-eluting stents, 3-to-6 months DAPT followed by SAPT and P2Y12i monotherapy after index procedures lowered risk of CV mortality, MI, stroke and major bleeding compared to standard 12 months of DAPT.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Optimal antiplatelet strategies after complex percutaneous coronary intervention in newer drug-eluting stent era: a bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background Current guidelines recommend deferring percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for angiographically intermediate coronary lesions without functional ischemia (FFR &gt;0.80). However, the long-term safety of this strategy and the potential role of preventive PCI in high-risk anatomical subsets remain uncertain. Objectives This study aimed to compare long-term vessel-level outcomes between PCI and medical therapy (MT) for functionally non-ischemic intermediate lesions, identify anatomical predictors of events under MT, and evaluate the net clinical benefit of preventive PCI. Methods In this single-center, retrospective cohort study, we analyzed 550 functionally non-ischemic intermediate lesions from 410 patients with chronic coronary syndrome. Lesions were managed by either PCI plus MT or MT alone based on clinician preference, and angiography-derived FFR was computed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was the vessel-oriented composite endpoint (VOCE), a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction and ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization. Results During a median follow-up of 9 years, PCI did not reduce the risk of VOCE in the overall cohort compared with MT (9.1% vs. 13.3%; HR 0.635, 95% CI 0.379-1.057, P=0.081). However, significant heterogeneity was observed. Among lesions with high-risk anatomical features (stenosis ≥70%, multivessel disease, and left anterior descending artery involvement), PCI was associated with a significantly lower risk of VOCE (9.4% vs. 28.2%; HR 0.297, 95% CI 0.164-0.535, P&lt;0.0001). The number needed to treat to prevent one VOCE event in this high-risk subgroup was 4 at 9 years, with a favorable number needed to harm of 9, indicating a positive net clinical benefit. Conclusions A uniform strategy of deferring PCI for all functionally non-ischemic intermediate lesions may not be optimal in the long term, and lesions with high-risk anatomic features may still benefit from PCI.Kaplan-Meier curves for clinical outcomeFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Benefits and harms of PCIFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Selective PCI for high-risk non-ischemic lesions: a viable strategy with long-term benefit

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Graft failure following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is a common clinical problem associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Although percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for bypass graft lesions is frequently performed in clinical practice, the optimal device strategy remains debated. Recently, drug-coated balloon (DCB) has emerged as a potential stentless alternative. Purpose This study aimed to compare one-year clinical outcomes between DCB and drug-eluting stent (DES) in patients undergoing PCI for bypass graft lesions. Methods Data were analysed from a nationwide PCI registry in Japan between 2017 and 2020. Patients who underwent PCI with DES or DCB for bypass graft lesions were included in the analysis. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which were defined as a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke within one year after PCI. The secondary endpoints included the individual components of MACE, major bleeding, and planned repeat revascularisation. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to compare outcomes, with subgroup analyses performed according to graft type (saphenous vein graft [SVG] or arterial graft [AG]). Results Of the 165,266 patients who underwent PCI during the study period, 780 patients underwent PCI for bypass graft lesions. After excluding 141 PCIs performed without DES or DCB, and 29 PCIs in which both DES and DCB were used, 610 PCIs were included in the final study cohort: 426 (69.8%) with DES and 184 (30.2%) with DCB alone. At one year after PCI, the incidence of MACE did not differ significantly between the DES and DCB groups (10.3% vs. 8.6%; P=0.69; Figure 1). Additionally, no significant differences were observed when outcomes were stratified by SVG or AG PCI (P=0.72 and P=0.91, respectively; Figure 1). Similarly, there were no significant differences in all-cause death (P=0.57), cardiovascular death (P=0.71), non-fatal ACS (P=0.73), non-fatal stroke (P=0.22), non-fatal major bleeding (P=0.19), and planned repeat revascularisation (P=0.33) between the DES and DCB groups (Figure 2). After multivariable adjustment, the risk of MACE was comparable for DCB and DES (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.01; 95% confidence interval, 0.58-1.76; P=0.96). Conclusion(s) Stentless PCI with DCB was frequently employed and demonstrated comparable one-year clinical outcomes to DES implantation for bypass graft lesions.Fig. 1.KM curves for MACE incidenceFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Fig. 2.KM curves for secondary outcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Drug-coated balloons angioplasty versus drug-eluting stents for coronary artery bypass graft

abstract: Abstract Background Periprocedural myocardial infarction (PMI) is a standard yet controversial component of composite endpoints in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) trials. Despite its widespread inclusion in primary outcomes, the clinical and prognostic significance of PMI remains uncertain. Data regarding contemporary PMI definitions and reporting practices are lacking. Methods We systematically reviewed PCI randomised controlled trials published in six high-impact journals (New England Journal of Medicine, Lancet, JAMA, European Heart Journal, Circulation, JACC) between 2019 and 2023. We assessed PMI reporting frequency, definitions, and contribution to composite outcomes. For trials reporting PMI separately, we performed sensitivity analyses on cumulative event counts excluding PMI to determine whether primary endpoint statistical significance was altered. Results Forty-nine trials met inclusion criteria. Only 24 (49%) separately reported PMI. Definitional heterogeneity was substantial: 12 trials (50%) used the Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, 5 (21%) SCAI criteria, 4 (17%) ARC-2 definitions, and 3 (13%) protocol-specific criteria. As seen in the figure, PMI comprised a median of 19% (range 4–54%) of composite endpoint events and 41% (range 9–91%) of all reported MIs. Excluding PMI reversed primary endpoint significance in 2 of 24 trials (8%): in ISCHEMIA, the result changed from non-significant to significant (p=0.34 to p&lt;0.001), while in OCTOBER, significance was lost (p=0.035 to p=0.073). Both trials with reversals reported PMI exclusively in supplementary materials. Conclusions PMI reporting in contemporary PCI trials is inconsistent and definitionally heterogeneous. PMI events constituted a substantial proportion of composite endpoints and, in some trials, materially altered primary conclusions. Standardised, separate PMI reporting with prespecified sensitivity analyses would enhance trial interpretability and reduce concerns about selective outcome reporting.Contribution of PMI to composite endpointsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review of PCI randomised controlled trials in six high-impact journals, 2019 to 2023; 49 trials met inclusion criteria, 24 (49%) separately reported PMI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Restricted to six journals and 24 trials reporting PMI separately; the sensitivity analyses use cumulative event counts rather than patient-level data.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review of how periprocedural MI is defined and reported in PCI randomised trials, and whether excluding it changes primary endpoint conclusions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PMI comprised a median of 19% (range 4-54%) of composite endpoint events; excluding PMI reversed primary endpoint significance in 2 of 24 trials (8%): ISCHEMIA changed from p=0.34 to p<0.001 and OCTOBER from p=0.035 to p=0.073.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that heterogeneous PMI definitions can alter trial conclusions, which bears on endpoint design and on interpretation of trials such as ISCHEMIA and OCTOBER.

title: Reporting of periprocedural myocardial infarctions in coronary intervention trials: a systematic review

abstract: Abstract Background / Introduction The Global Thrombosis Test (GTT) simultaneously assesses thrombotic status (Occlusion Time, OT) and fibrinolytic capacity (Lysis Time, LT) using native blood under physiological shear. While prolonged LT (≥3,000 s) is an established marker of impaired fibrinolysis, the prognostic role of markedly prolonged OT—reflecting bleeding tendency—and its combination with prolonged LT (dual impairment) remain unexplored in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Purpose To evaluate the prognostic significance of dual impairment of thrombotic and fibrinolytic pathways (OT ≥750 s and LT ≥3,000 s) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and revascularisation), all-cause mortality, and bleeding in patients undergoing PCI. Methods We prospectively enrolled 2,000 consecutive PCI patients (41.5% acute coronary syndrome) at two centres. GTT was performed prior to or within 24 hours of the index procedure. Dual impairment was defined as OT ≥750 and LT ≥3,000 s. The primary endpoints were MACE (all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and revascularisation), all-cause death, and bleeding (BARC ≥2) over a median 42-month follow-up. Multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, hypertension, diabetes, haemoglobin, smoking, and ACS presentation. Results Among 2,000 patients (mean age 66.8 years, 70.3% male), 289 (14.5%) had dual impairment. They were older (69.3 vs. 66.4 years, p&lt;0.001), had more diabetes (47.7% vs. 35.0%, p&lt;0.001), lower haemoglobin (13.2 vs. 14.0 g/dL, p&lt;0.001), higher fibrinogen (337 vs. 309 mg/dL, p&lt;0.001), elevated D-dimer (0.52 vs. 0.37 µg/mL, p&lt;0.001), and prolonged aPTT (35.4 vs. 33.7 s, p&lt;0.001). On multivariable analysis, dual impairment independently predicted all-cause death (HR 2.39, 95% CI 1.45–3.94, p&lt;0.001) and MACE (HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.18–2.53, p=0.005), with a trend for bleeding (HR 1.48, 95% CI 0.93–2.36, p=0.095). Single-pathway impairment showed no significant risk increase, indicating a synergistic effect (Figure). Conclusion(s) Concurrent impairment of both thrombotic and fibrinolytic pathways by GTT identifies a high-risk subgroup with a 2.4-fold increase in mortality and 1.7-fold increase in MACE after PCI. This synergistic dual impairment phenotype provides unique prognostic information by capturing both ischaemic and haemorrhagic vulnerability in a single bedside test.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Dual impairment of thrombotic and fibrinolytic pathways assessed by the global thrombosis test predicts adverse clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Accumulating evidence suggests that DCB may achieve clinical outcomes comparable to DES, even in large coronary arteries and selected complex lesion subsets. However, the definition of “complex PCI” remains heterogeneous, and direct long-term comparisons between DCB-only strategies and newer-generation DES in anatomically complex large-vessel lesions are limited. Purpose To compare 3-year clinical outcomes between a DCB-only strategy and newer-generation DES in patients with large (≥3.0 mm) coronary arteries and complex lesions defined as ACC/AHA type B2/C. Methods We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients undergoing PCI between January 2018 and December 2023. Inclusion criteria were: large coronary vessels (≥3.0 mm), and complex lesions (ACC/AHA type B2 or C). Patients with in-stent restenosis or acute coronary syndrome were excluded. After propensity score matching, 113 patients treated with DCB were compared with 113 patients treated with newer-generation DES. The primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or target lesion revascularization at 3 years. Secondary endpoints included all-cause death, cardiac death, target vessel revascularization (TVR), and target lesion revascularization (TLR). Procedural characteristics were also assessed. Results Median follow-up duration was 1223 ± 690 days. At 3 years, cumulative TLF was numerically lower in the DCB group compared with the DES group (6.0% vs. 11.3%), but the difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank p=0.159). The cumulative incidences of all-cause death, cardiac death, TVR, and TLR were comparable between groups. Procedural parameters, including contrast volume, procedure time, and fluoroscopy time, were similar between strategies, suggesting no procedural simplification advantage with DCB-only treatment. Conclusions In patients with large coronary vessels and ACC/AHA type B2/C complex lesions, a DCB-only strategy demonstrated comparable but not superior 3-year outcomes compared with newer-generation DES. Lesion complexity alone may not be sufficient to guide device selection. Instead, patient-specific factors—such as bleeding risk or the desire to avoid permanent metallic implantation—may play a more decisive role when considering a DCB-only strategy. A more patient-centered approach, rather than lesion morphology alone, may better inform optimal device selection in complex PCI.
title: Drug-coated balloon–only strategy versus drug-eluting stents in large-vessel complex PCI: a propensity-matched 3-year outcome analysis

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) are increasingly performed in complex settings, influenced by lesion characteristics, procedural strategies, and patient-related factors. The impact of sex differences on PCI risk and outcomes remains uncertain. Prior evidence indicates that women more frequently present with higher bleeding risk (HBR), which may influence procedural strategy and outcomes. Purpose The NAGOMI COMPLEX study evaluates the safety and effectiveness of a new-generation sirolimus-eluting stent in complex PCI. This analysis assesses the impact of sex-based differences in clinical outcomes at one-year follow-up. Methods NAGOMI COMPLEX is a prospective, multicentre, observational study enrolling more than 3000 patients undergoing complex PCI across 52 European sites. Patients were eligible if they met at least one of the predefined procedural complexity criteria. Following completion of enrolment, this analysis includes patients with available one-year follow-up data, in which clinical outcomes were assessed by sex. The primary endpoint is one-year target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR). Results Among 3031 patients, 72.9% had chronic coronary syndrome and 20.9% were women (n=633). Women were older (71.1 ± 9.66 vs 68.6 ± 10.29 years; p&lt;0.0001) and more frequently HBR patients (51.1% vs 41.6%; p&lt;0.0001). Prior PCI (32.2% vs 37.0%; p=0.0264) and CABG (6.0% vs 8.3%; p=0.0595) were less frequent in women. Complex procedural features such as left main stenting (20.6%), complex bifurcations (15.4%), chronic total occlusion (22.3%), and multivessel PCI (41.3%) did not differ between genders, nor did the number of implanted stents per lesions. Women had lower use of radial access (75.0% vs 84.0%; p&lt;0.0001) and intravascular imaging (24.1% vs 29.5%; p=0.0006, at lesion level). At one year, TLF was comparable (7.4% vs 8.9%; p=0.3104), including cardiovascular death (3.0% vs 2.0%), TVMI (4.0% vs 5.6%), and CDTLR (2.8% vs 3.6%). Access site bleeding (BARC 1–5) (5.8% vs 2.0%; p&lt;0.0001) and major bleeding (BARC 3–5) (5.0% vs 2.5%; p=0.0085) were both higher in women, without differences in all-cause mortality (4.2% vs 4.5%; p=0.821). Rates of MI were 5.2% in men and 6.5% in women (p=0.2766), TLR 3.9% vs 5.6% (p=0.1447), stent thrombosis 1.2% vs 1.8% (p=0.3783), and stroke 1.1% vs 2.3% (p=0.0664). Conclusion(s) In this large multicentre cohort of patients undergoing complex PCI with new-generation sirolimus-eluting stents, female patients more frequently presented with HBR features and had higher postprocedural bleeding events, while overall procedural performance was similar between sexes. These results highlight the need for sex-specific approaches to bleeding risk minimization in complex PCI.
title: Female vs male complex PCI by sirolimus-eluting stenting: one-year NAGOMI COMPLEX study outcome

abstract: Abstract Introduction PCI has been established as a suitable treatment approach for LMS disease. There is a lack of data regarding the safety and efficacy of PCI in LMS trifurcation lesions. Purpose We assessed the long-term outcomes of patients with LMS trifurcation PCI compared to bifurcation PCI. Methods Retrospective analysis of all patients treated with PCI for LMS disease from January 2012 to March 2023. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, secondary outcomes were target vessel failure, MI and angina. Results A total of 543 patients with LMS trifurcation lesions were matched with 418 patients with LMS bifurcation lesions. The median age was 71 (63-78) years in the trifurcation group and 70 (62-77) years in the bifurcation group. The primary outcome of all-cause mortality at median follow-up of 5.8 (3.5-8.9) years was significantly greater in the trifurcation group compared to the bifurcation group (40.7% vs 34%, p=0.027). Cox regression analysis demonstrated that trifurcations are associated with increased mortality (HR 1.267, 1.026 to 1.565). There were more perforations in the bifurcation group compared to the trifurcation group (2.4% vs 0.6%, p=0.014). Conclusion PCI in LMS trifurcation lesions is associated with higher longer-term mortality compared to LMS bifurcation lesions.Kaplan Meier Graph of all-cause mortalityFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Long term outcomes of left main stem trifurcation PCI compared to left main stem bifurcation anatomy

abstract: Abstract Background Permanent metallic drug-eluting stents (DES) provide effective coronary scaffolding but may impair long-term vessel physiology due to chronic metallic caging. Bioadaptor technology has been developed to allow early mechanical support followed by adaptive vessel restoration. We performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing bioadaptor devices with contemporary DES in patients undergoing PCI. Methods A systematic meta-analysis of RCTs comparing bioadaptor versus DES was conducted. The primary endpoints were target lesion failure (TLF) and target vessel failure (TVF). Secondary endpoints included target lesion revascularization (TLR), myocardial infarction (MI), cardiovascular death, all-cause death, and definite/probable device or stent thrombosis. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Results Three randomized controlled trials with a total of 2886 patients were included. Overall risk of bias was low in the large multicenter RCTs, with some concerns in the small mechanistic trial. Bioadaptor was associated with a numerically lower risk of target lesion failure (RR 0.70, 95% CI 0.40–1.20; I²=9.8%) and target vessel failure (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.23–1.53; I²=64.2%) compared with DES; however, these differences did not reach statistical significance.Target lesion revascularization showed a favorable trend (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.31–1.03; I²=0%). There were no significant differences in target-vessel myocardial infarction (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.41–1.46; I²=0%) or any myocardial infarction (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.79–2.22; I²=0%). Cardiovascular death (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.06–4.66; I²=54%) and all-cause death (RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.72–2.56; I²=0%) were similar between groups. Definite or probable device/stent thrombosis was not increased with bioadaptor (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.43–3.16; I²=0%). Conclusion In randomized evidence, bioadaptor technology demonstrates similar safety and efficacy profiles compared with contemporary DES. Although statistical significance was not reached, consistent numerical trends toward reduced lesion-related events were observed without an increased risk of thrombosis. Larger trials with extended follow-up are warranted to determine whether adaptive vessel restoration translates into meaningful long-term clinical benefit.Risk of biasFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Random-Effects Meta-AnalysisFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Bioadaptor versus contemporary drug-eluting stents: Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has been established as a widely available procedure for managing patients with and without acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While age is a strong predictor of outcomes after PCI, contemporary data in patients with very advanced age are limited.
