Purpose To delineate the current practice patterns and clinical outcomes of PCI, with a specific focus on septuagenarians, octogenarians, and nonagenarians with AMI and non-AMI in Japan, a country at the forefront of the global aging crisis. Methods The Japanese PCI (J-PCI) is a nationwide registry covering most of the PCI procedures performed within the country. PCI procedures between 2019 and2024 were included. Patients were divided into four age categories: 20–69, 70–79, 80–89, and 90–99 years, and further grouped according to the indications (AMI versus non-AMI). The trends and patterns of PCI procedures, in-hospital mortality, and complications across the age groups were assessed. Results A total of 1,454,940 PCI procedures, with 387,454 (26.6%) and 1,067,486 (73.4%) for AMI and non-AMI, were analyzed. During the study period, the mean age has consistently increased from 71.0 to 72.1 years in the entire study population. Nonagenarians accounted for 3.9% and 1.7% in the AMI and non-AMI cohorts in 2019 and 5.0% and 2.4% in 2024. In both cohorts, the higher age categories were associated with increased risks of in-hospital mortality and complications (Figure). Conclusions Our nationwide study demonstrated a consistent year-on-year increase in the age of patients undergoing PCI, despite a modest annual increase of 0.2–0.3 years, without reaching a plateau. Advanced age was strongly associated with poor outcomes, particularly in nonagenarians, reinforcing the need for shared decision-making in PCI in the oldest-old population.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Temporal trends and outcomes of superelderly patients undergoing coronary intervention with and without acute myocardial infarction: Insights from the Japanese nationwide registry

abstract: Abstract Background Each of fibrinogen and platelet–fibrin clot strength (PFCS) is independently associated with the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Objective The association between fibrinogen and PFCS and their prognostic implications remains uncertain in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods A total of 2,526 patients undergoing PCI, with on-admission fibrinogen and PFCS measured by thromboelastography (TEG®) was analyzed. Patients were classified according to fibrinogen (Fibrinogenhigh, defined fibrinogen &gt; 350 mg/dL) and PFCS (PFCShigh, defined TEG®-maximal amplitude ≥ 68 mm) levels. Patients were stratified into four groups: (1) Fibrinogenlow-PFCSlow (46.0%), (2) Fibrinogenlow-PFCShigh (21.3%), (3) Fibrinogenhigh-PFCSlow (14.7%), and (4) Fibrinogenhigh-PFCShigh (17.9%). MACE was defined as composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or stroke during 4-year follow-up. Results Serum fibrinogen and PFCS showed a moderate correlation (r = 0.333, P &lt; 0.001). Fibrinogen and PFCS phenotypes had an additive prognostic implication. The Fibrinogenhigh-PFCShigh group showed significantly higher risks of MACE compared with the Fibrinogenlow-PFCShigh (adjusted hazard ratio [HRadj], 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04-2.20; P=0.031) and Fibrinogenhigh-PFCSlow groups (HRadj, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.01-2.27; P=0.044). Similar results were observed for all-cause death. The risk of major bleeding was significantly associated with the fibrinogen phenotype. Compared with the Fibrinogenlow-PFCSlow group, the Fibrinogenhigh-PFCSlow (HRadj, 2.89; 95% CI, 1.33-6.29; P=0.008) and Fibrinogenhigh-PFCShigh groups (HRadj, 2.40; 95% CI, 1.12-5.14; P=0.025) had significantly higher rates of major bleeding. Conclusions In PCI-treated patients, fibrinogen and P-FCS showed important prognostic associations. Their combined assessment may enhance post-PCI risk stratification and support more personalized cardiovascular therapy.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Association between fibrinogen and clot strength and their prognostic implications after percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Periprocedural myocardial infarction (PPMI) is associated with increased mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Although diagnostic biomarkers for PPMI have evolved from creatine kinase-myocardial band (CK-MB) to high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn), the current troponin thresholds have not been updated, and the relationship between post-PCI CK-MB and hs-cTn not re-evaluated. Consequently, the diagnosis and prognostic stratification of PPMI needs reassessment. Purpose We evaluated the relationship between post-PCI hs-cTn and CK-MB, and compare the frequency and clinical impact of PPMI across different definitions in patients with de novo three-vessel disease in a randomized PCI trial (Multivessel TALENT: NCT04390672). Methods This post-hoc sub-analysis from the Multivessel TALENT trial included patients with paired post-procedural CK-MB and hs-cTn measurements. Peak post-PCI CK-MB and hs-cTn values were used and expressed as ratios of the assay-specific upper limit of normal (ULN). PPMI rates were compared across three definitions: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI), Academic Research Consortium-2 (ARC-2), and Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (4th UDMI). Analyses using the SCAI definition were performed separately with CK-MB alone or hs-cTn alone. 1-year all-cause mortality was compared according to the presence of PPMI for each definition. Results Among 969 procedures (657 patients), paired post-PCI CK-MB and hs-cTnI or hs-cTnT measurements were available in 32.9% (288 procedures in 216 patients) and 67.1% (681 procedures in 441 patients), respectively. Post-PCI hs-cTn showed significant correlations with CK-MB on a log10-transformed scale, with a steeper slope for hs-cTnI than hs-cTnT (hs-cTnI: β=1.404 vs hs-cTnT: β=1.007, P&lt;0.001). CK-MB thresholds of 5× and 10× ULN corresponded to hs-cTnT thresholds of 29× and 59×ULN, and to hs-cTnI thresholds of 101× and 266×ULN, respectively. Using the SCAI definitions, the incidence of PPMI was higher using hs-cTnI compared with CK-MB (15.6% vs. 1.7%, p&lt;0.001), but not when using hs-cTnT compared with CK-MB (1.9% vs 1.0%, p=0.114). Using either hs-cTn did not affect the incidences of ARC-2 PPMI (hs-cTnI: CK-MB-based SCAI 1.7% vs ARC-2 3.8%, P=0.149; hs-cTnT: CK-MB-based SCAI 1.0% vs ARC-2 1.8%, P=0.267). However, the incidence of 4th UDMI PPMI was higher in both hs-cTn groups (hs-cTnI: CK-MB-based SCAI 1.7% vs 4th UDMI 12.5%, P&lt;0.001; hs-cTnT: CK-MB-based SCAI 1.0% vs 4th UDMI 9.3%, P&lt;0.001). Irrespective of the definition, PPMI was not associated with a significantly increased risk of all-cause mortality at 1 year. Conclusions Using hs-cTnI instead of CK-MB may overdiagnose PPMI by the purely biomarker-based SCAI definition. Refining the PPMI definition to incorporate differences between hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT is warranted.Figure AFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure BFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Relationship between CK-MB and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin after PCI and the impact on the diagnosis of periprocedural myocardial infarction: insights from Multivessel TALENT trial

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial perfusion abnormalities detected by stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) are established markers of adverse prognosis in patients with chest pain and non-obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease. However, the prognostic significance of CMR-detected perfusion abnormalities in patients without chest pain, particularly when significant epicardial coronary stenosis is carefully excluded, remains unclear. Purpose To investigate the long-term prognostic impact of stress perfusion CMR-detected perfusion abnormalities in patients without significant epicardial coronary artery disease, focusing on differences according to chest pain status. Methods This single-center retrospective study screened 3,301 consecutive patients who underwent stress perfusion CMR between May 2008 and July 2023. The main exclusion criteria were ischemic heart disease, defined as a history of myocardial infarction or prior treatment for coronary artery disease, and significant epicardial coronary disease (&gt;50% stenosis or fractional flow reserve &lt;0.80). We also excluded patients with unavailable coronary evaluation, late gadolinium enhancement on CMR, major cardiac comorbidities, and follow-up shorter than 90 days. After these exclusions, 597 patients were included and followed through September 2024. Patients were stratified by the presence or absence of chest pain. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared according to the presence or absence of myocardial perfusion abnormality. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoints were major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and hard cardiac events. MACCE comprised cardiac death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, unplanned revascularization, heart failure hospitalization, new-onset arrhythmia, or stroke, while hard cardiac events comprised cardiac death or non-fatal myocardial infarction. Results During a median follow-up of 8.6 years, perfusion abnormality was not associated with higher mortality in patients without chest pain (p=0.57) (Figure 1A) In contrast, perfusion abnormality was associated with higher all-cause mortality among those with chest pain (p&lt;0.01) (Figure 1B). In multivariable Cox analysis, perfusion abnormality independently predicted all-cause mortality in patients with chest pain (Hazard ratio:2.44, 95%CI:1.03-5.74), whereas in patients without chest pain it was not associated with mortality. Perfusion abnormality was not associated with MACCE or hard cardiac events regardless of chest pain. Conclusion In patients without significant epicardial coronary disease, stress perfusion CMR-detected perfusion abnormalities were associated with higher long-term all-cause mortality only in those with chest pain. These findings suggest that chest pain status should be considered when interpreting stress perfusion CMR perfusion abnormalities in patients without significant epicardial coronary disease.Figure 1
title: Impact of stress perfusion abnormalities by cardiac magnetic resonance on long-term prognosis in patients without significant epicardial coronary artery stenosis: a comparative study by chest pain

abstract: Abstract Background Premature coronary artery disease (CAD) affects patients at a young age and places a significant burden on patients’ quality of life and societal productivity. Contemporary real-world data on PCI outcomes in this population are scarce. Purpose This study sought to evaluate the prevalence, clinical profile, and 1-year outcomes of patients with premature CAD undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods We analysed data from the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), an ongoing, multicentre PCI registry. Premature CAD was defined as PCI at age &lt;50 years in men and &lt;55 years in women. Baseline characteristics were compared between premature CAD and older patients. The primary endpoint was 1-year major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as a composite of myocardial infarction, unplanned revascularisation, ischemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or cardiovascular mortality. Cox proportional hazards modelling was performed to assess the independent association between premature CAD and 1-year MACCE. Results Among 8,767 patients undergoing PCI, 584 (6.7%) met criteria for premature CAD (mean age of 46 years). Compared with older patients, those with premature CAD more frequently presented with acute coronary syndrome or out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and had lower baseline socioeconomic status. They had higher body mass index (28.8 vs 27.6 kg/m2) and LDL-cholesterol (3.3 vs 2.7 mmol/L), and were more often active smokers (56% vs 22%). In contrast, hypertension, diabetes, peripheral artery disease, or multivessel disease were less prevalent. Unadjusted 1-year MACCE rates were similar between groups. However, after multivariable adjustment, premature CAD was independently associated with a higher risk of MACCE (HR 1.95, 95% CI 1.17-3.25, p=0.011). Conclusion In this registry, premature CAD accounted for almost 7% of patients undergoing PCI. Despite a lower burden of traditional comorbidities, these patients had an increased adjusted risk of 1-year MACCE. These findings underscore the need for intensified secondary prevention and attention to both clinical and socioeconomic risk factors in this high-risk subgroup.Risk of 1-year MACCE premature CADFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Premature coronary artery disease and 1-year outcomes after PCI

abstract: Abstract Background Severe coronary calcification remains a major challenge in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Data on outcomes of rotational atherectomy (RA) in left main (LM) lesions are limited and inconsistent. Purpose To assess procedural and 2-year clinical outcomes after LM PCI with RA based on the largest published single-center European registry to date. Methods Among 1060 patients with severe coronary calcification treated with PCI using RA between 2008 and 2022, LM was target vessel in 178 cases. The primary endpoint was procedural success (lesion modification with RA with stent placement with ≤20% residual stenosis) and and clinical success (achievement of procedural success in the absence of major in-hospital complications). The secondary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE: cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, stroke) and all-cause mortality at 24 months. Outcome rates were calculated for LM PCI alone and for comparison with non-LM patients. Results In final LM PCI cohort median age was 77 (69-82), 26% (46) were female, median SYNTAX score was 35 (28-43), EuroSCORE II 4.9% (2.02-9.8%) and ejection fraction (EF) 45% (30-52%). Majority of patients had true bifurcation lesion (defined as medina 1-1-1; 83 [47%]) and intravascular imaging (IVI) was used in 56 patients (32%). Technical and clinical success rates were 98% and 81%, respectively. Both uni- and multivariate analysis including age, IVI and EF revealed SYNTAX score as the only factor associated with higher risk of clinical failure (OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.01-1.97, P=0.043 per 10-point increase). In-hospital MACCE occurred in 19 patients (11%). In two-year observation there were 71 MACCE [cumulative incidence estimated by Kaplan-Meier method was 40.8% (95% CI 33.9-48.5%)]. Univariable Cox analysis recognized clinical success as the only factor significantly associated with reduction of MACCE (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.14-0.37, P&lt;0.001). In 2-year observation there were 42 all-cause deaths [mortality rate 23.2% (95% CI 17.6–30.1%)]. In multivariable analysis, EF remained the only independent predictor of all-cause mortality (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.93-0.98, P&lt;0.001 per 1% increase), whereas renal dysfunction, atrial fibrillation, anemia and age had no significant impact. Compared with non-LM PCI, LM PCI was associated with similar rate of procedural success (unadjusted OR 1.11, 95% CI 0.38-3.27) but lower clinical success (unadjusted OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40–0.94; P=0.03). 2-year MACCE (unadjusted HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.86–1.43; P=0.45) and all-cause mortality (unadjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 0.92–1.83; P=0.13) were similar between two groups. Conclusion LM PCI with RA achieved high clinical success despite complex anatomy. Worse clinical outcomes were driven by anatomical complexity, whereas mid-term prognosis was primarily determined by baseline myocardial function rather than lesion characteristics.Predictors of clinical success and MACCEFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Comparison of LM vs non-LM PCI with RAFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Clinical outcomes of left main percutaneous coronary intervention with rotational atherectomy: results from the RA-BIA cohort

abstract: Abstract Background The coronary bifurcation lesion remains a unique challenge for the modern interventionalist. Current outcome data in treatment of bifurcation lesions have shown varying results. Additionally, long-term outcomes remain largely unexplored. Purpose The main objective of this study is to investigate and compare the long-term outcome of patients after percutaneous coronary interventions in bifurcation lesions in single versus double stenting strategies in a large volume center. Methods We analyzed 3991 patients from a large registry undergoing percutaneous coronary interventions for bifurcation lesions for over 3 years. Primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE) consisting of all cause death, myocardial infarction, or target lesion revascularization. Survival analysis with weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazard models were constructed. Results Double stenting was associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE at three years with a hazard ratio of 1.27 (95% CI 1.08–1.50). Survival analysis has shown a superior outcome in terms of occurrence of MACE in single stenting versus double stenting (P&lt;0.01). Subgroup analysis has shown an amplified risk in higher degree of calcification (hazard ratio 1.42; 95% CI 1.12–1.79) and side branch ostial involvement (hazard ratio HR 1.30; 95% CI 1.08–1.56). Conclusions Our large cohort has shown that single stenting strategies was associated with significantly better outcome than double stenting strategies.Single versus double stenting survivalFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Long term results after percutanous coronary intervention in large cohort of coronary bifurcation lesions in large volume center in single versus double stenting

abstract: Abstract Background The optimal revascularisation strategy for complex coronary artery disease (CAD) remains debated, particularly in the context of rapidly evolving stent technology, intravascular imaging, physiologic assessment and pharmacotherapy. Randomised trials comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) span multiple technological eras, limiting direct interpretation of long-term outcomes across generations of stents. Purpose To evaluate long-term survival after PCI versus CABG across stent generations using a large-scale reconstructed individual patient data (IPD) approach derived from eight published randomised trials. Methods Kaplan-Meier survival curves from landmark randomised trials (FREEDOM, SYNTAX, VA-CARDS, PRECOMBAT, BEST, EXCEL, NOBLE and FAME3) comparing PCI and CABG were digitised directly from published figures using image-based analytical reconstruction. Time-to-event data and numbers at risk were extracted to generate pseudo-IPD, enabling pooled survival analyses with long-term follow-up (Figure). Cox proportional hazards models stratified by trial were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for PCI versus CABG in the total cohort as well as according to stent generation (first-generation versus second-generation or later stents) and degree of CAD. Results The reconstructed database represents the largest aggregated long-term survival dataset comparing PCI and CABG derived from randomised evidence, including 9,967 patients with complex CAD with follow-up extending to 10 years. In the total cohort, PCI was associated with higher mortality compared with CABG (HR 1.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-1.36; p&lt;0.001). When stratified by technological era, first-generation stents demonstrated worse outcomes compared to CABG (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.09-1.44; p=0.002). In contrast, outcomes with second- and later-generation stents showed equipoise to CABG, with no significant difference in long-term mortality (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.93-1.33; p=0.26) (Figure). When stratified by coronary anatomy, PCI was associated with higher long-term mortality compared with CABG in patients with three-vessel disease (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.09-1.38; p=0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed in left main disease (HR 1.18, 95% CI 0.91-1.53; p=0.21). Conclusion This study provides the largest long-term comparative randomised assessment of PCI and CABG across technological eras. While early-generation stents were associated with inferior survival compared with CABG, contemporary PCI demonstrates neutral long-term outcomes, suggesting technological evolution has fundamentally narrowed the historical survival gap. RCTs are urgently required to compare state-of-the-art PCI including imaging and physiologic assessment to CABG to potentially redefine guidelines.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Ultra long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention versus coronary artery bypass grafting in complex coronary artery disease: a reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background The clinical relevance of prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains controversial. The aim of this study was to compare the frequency of PPM after TAVI using a self-expanding or a balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve and to investigate the impact of PPM on clinical outcomes and health-related quality of life measures throughout three years. Methods Patients treated in the SCOPE I trial were stratified according to PPM, which was determined by the indexed effective orifice area (EOAi). All patients were stratified according to the EOAi: moderate PPM was defined as 0.66-0.85 cm2/m2 and severe PPM as ≤0.65 cm2/m2. Outcomes of interest included a composite endpoint integrating both vital status and patient-reported, disease-specific health status, as well as clinical endpoints defined according to VARC-3 criteria. Results A total of 701 patients were included. The frequency of any PPM was 41.9% (moderate 29.7% [208/701]; severe 12.3% [86/701]). Any PPM was more frequent with balloon-expandable prosthesis compared with self-expandable prosthesis (53.5% versus 29.9%, p &lt;0.01). Patients with any PPM had less improvement in patient-reported health status after TAVI throughout three years compared to patients with no PPM (improvement of Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire 12 Overall Summary score: +14.6 [3.1-32.3] vs. +21.4 [8.3-38.0], p=0.04). The rate of VARC-3 unfavorable outcome was comparable in patients with any and no PPM (16.5% vs. 18.4%, p=0.53). All-cause mortality at three years was not significantly increased in patients with any PPM (24.8% vs. 21.1%, Hazard Ratio 1.14, p=0.13). Conclusions PPM was frequently observed, especially in TAVI patients treated with balloon expandable valves. Patients with any PPM after TAVI had less improvement in patient-reported health status, without impact on all-cause mortality rates during extended follow-up.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Mid-term impact of prosthesis-patient mismatch after transcatheter aortic valve implantation using a self-expanding or balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve

abstract: Abstract Background Hypoattenuating leaflet thickening (HALT) has been associated with the eccentricity of implanted transcatheter aortic valve (TAV). However, its relationship with valve type (balloon-expandable vs. self-expandable) or valve design (supra-annular vs. intra-annular) remains unclear. The purpose of our study was to investigate the incidence of HALT and valve eccentricity among TAV series (Sapien, Evolut, and Navitor). Methods We retrospectively evaluated 125 consecutive patients (Sapien: n = 54, Evolut: n = 39, Navitor: n = 32) who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement from December 2022 to April 2024. HALT and eccentricity of the implanted TAV were analyzed with 30-day postprocedural computed tomography. HALT was defined as involvement of more than 25% from the leaflet base in at least one leaflet, based on the Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. Results The overall incidence of HALT was 30.4%, with a significantly higher incidence in Navitor than in Sapien or Evolut (56.2% vs. 22.2% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.001). In all three groups (Sapien, Evolut, and Navitor), eccentricity at the leaflet inflow level was significantly greater in patients with HALT compared to without HALT (median 0.38 [IQR 0.36-0.45] vs. 0.34 [0.29-0.39]; p = 0.040, 0.59 [0.39-0.67] vs 0.36 [0.32-0.41]; p &lt; 0.001, 0.64 [0.57-0.77] vs 0.44 [0.40-0.51]; p &lt; 0.001). Eccentricity at the native annulus level was significantly lower in Sapien compared with Evolut and Navitor (0.36 [0.33-0.42] vs. 0.60 [0.48-0.67] and 0.59 [0.49-0.70], respectively; p &lt; 0.001). Eccentricity at the leaflet inflow level was significantly greater in Navitor compared with Sapien and Evolut (0.36 [0.31-0.39] and 0.36 [0.33-0.44] vs. 0.57 [0.45-0.67], respectively; p &lt; 0.001). Conclusion The self-expandable, intra-annular design is more affected by the device landing zone and results in leaflet level deformation, leading to increased incidence of HALT.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Association between HALT incidence and deformation of transcatheter aortic valve prostheses: Sapien vs. Evolut vs. Navitor

abstract: Abstract Background Valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is the preferred therapy for degenerated surgical bioprostheses, yet residual gradients, patient–prosthesis mismatch (PPM), and coronary obstruction remain major concerns. Purpose This study aims to assess procedural safety and mid-to-long term outcomes in a prospective ViV TAVI cohort. Methods This is a prospective single-center cohort of consecutive patients with symptomatic structural valve degeneration (NYHA III–IV) undergoing transfemoral ViV TAVI between July 2022 and June 2025. Outcomes followed VARC-3 definitions with echocardiography at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. Exploratory modeling examined predictors of elevated 1-year gradients and PPM. Results Sixty-eight patients (51% female; mean age 77 ± 7 years; EuroSCORE II 7.3 ± 1.8%) were treated. Failure mechanism was stenosis in 50%, regurgitation 22%, mixed 28%; mean true ID 22 ± 3 mm, with 35% ≤21 mm. Valve fracture was performed in 24% (n=16). Commissural alignment was successful in 98.5%. Coronary protection was used in 11.8% (n=8); chimney stenting in 5.9% (n=4), all preserving flow. Technical success was 100%. Thirty-day outcomes: mortality 0%, stroke 0%, MI 0%, new pacemaker 2.9%, major vascular complication 1.5%. Mean transvalvular gradient decreased from 38.0 ± 9.5 mmHg to 6.6 ± 2.0 mmHg post-procedure (p&lt;0.001), was 7.4 ± 2.3 mmHg at 30 days, and 8.2 ± 2.4 mmHg at 1 year. Aortic valve area increased from 0.80 ± 0.23 cm² to 2.00 ± 0.18 cm² (p&lt;0.001), measuring 1.92 ± 0.20 cm² at 30 days and 1.88 ± 0.22 cm² at 1 year. At 1 year, 23.5% (16/68) had gradients ≥10 mmHg. Each 1 mm decrease in true ID increased odds of a 1-year gradient ≥10 mmHg (adjusted OR 1.31; 95% CI 1.04–1.76; p=0.03). In small valves (≤21 mm), gradients were higher (9.0 ± 2.5 vs 7.6 ± 2.2 mmHg; p=0.01) and ≥10 mmHg more frequent (38% vs 14%; p=0.01); valve fracture reduced this risk (21% vs 50%; p=0.04). Moderate/severe PPM at 1 year occurred in 7.4% overall. At median follow-up of 12.8 months, survival was 95.6%, HF hospitalization 4.4%, and no endocarditis, valve thrombosis, or reintervention. NYHA I–II was achieved in 94.1% (0% at baseline). Post-ViV coronary angiography/PCI was feasible in all attempted cases (20/20). Conclusions In this prospective single-center study, a standardized ViV TAVI strategy achieved high technical success, favorable safety, and durable hemodynamics. Smaller true ID was the main predictor of elevated 1-year gradients, while surgical valve fracture mitigated this risk in small valves. Universal coronary access preservation and marked functional improvement reinforce the value of anatomy-driven planning and contemporary device selection in the modern ViV TAVI era.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Surgical bioprosthesis true ID and fracture impact on gradients after valve-in-valve TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the most common aortic valve replacement method for aortic stenosis. A known complication after valve replacement is paravalvular leakage (PVL). Severe PVL has been shown to increase mortality, but the significance of minor PVL remains uncertain. The aim of this retrospective observational cohort study was to investigate the clinical significance of mild and moderate PVL on mortality. Methods This study was based on data from the Swedish transcatheter cardiac intervention registry (SWENTRY) and included 14 296 patients undergoing TAVI during the years 2008–2025. SWENTRY was combined with the Swedish population registry to obtain survival data. Multivariate cox proportional hazards regression was used to analyse survival, where patients with mild and moderate PVL after TAVI were compared to patients with no PVL after TAVI. Landmark analyses from 30 days, 1 year and 5 years were performed to verify the effect of PVL on survival across varying post-surgical time-periods. Results Moderate PVL was associated with a significant higher hazard of mortality (HR 1.21, 95% CI [1.07–1.38], p=0.003). The results were consistent in the 30-day-landmark analysis (HR 1.16, 95% CI [1.02–1.32], p=0.027), but not in the other landmark analyses. Mild PVL was not associated with a statistically significantly higher hazard of mortality in any of the analyses (HR 1.05, 95% CI [0.99–1.11], p=0.107). Conclusions The results indicate that mild PVL does not have a statistically significant adverse effect on mortality. However, moderate PVL seems to have a more pronounced negative impact on survival, which should not be disregarded. This adverse effect seems to occur mainly during the first years after TAVI. These results indicate that mild PVL is presumably not associated with increased mortality, as well as highlight the clinical relevance of moderate PVL and imply that further attention to its management might be needed.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective observational cohort study of 14 296 patients undergoing TAVI during the years 2008–2025 in the Swedish transcatheter cardiac intervention registry (SWENTRY), linked to the population registry.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry design with residual confounding; PVL grading by echocardiography without core laboratory is not described in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: In a Swedish national TAVI registry, moderate but not mild paravalvular leakage was associated with higher mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Moderate PVL was associated with a significant higher hazard of mortality (HR 1.21, 95% CI [1.07–1.38], p=0.003). Mild PVL was not associated with a statistically significantly higher hazard of mortality in any of the analyses (HR 1.05, 95% CI [0.99–1.11], p=0.107).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs how much residual mild leak should be traded against conduction risk when choosing valve and post-dilatation strategy.

title: Mortality in patients with mild and moderate paravalvular leakage after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is widely performed in patients with severe degenerative aortic stenosis (AS). Although TAVI generally improves stroke volume by reducing left ventricular afterload, a subset of patients develop left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) after the procedure. Post-TAVI LVOTO is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication associated with acute haemodynamic instability. We previously developed a deep learning-derived index for predicting LVOTO in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy using only parasternal long-axis (PLAX) transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) images. Purpose To evaluate the clinical utility of a deep learning-based LVOTO index derived from pre-procedural TTE for predicting post-TAVI LVOTO. Methods We retrospectively analysed 301 consecutive patients who underwent TAVI at a tertiary referral centre between 2017 and 2025. A pre-trained deep learning model was applied to PLAX views extracted from pre-procedure TTE to capture morphological and dynamic motion features of the left ventricle, generating a deep learning index for LVOTO (DLi-LVOTO; range 0–100). Discriminative performance for post-TAVI LVOTO was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Independent association with post-TAVI LVOTO was assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for established clinical and echocardiographic risk factors. Results DLi-LVOTO was positively correlated with baseline LVOTO severity on pre-procedural TTE. Post-TAVI LVOTO occurred in 42 patients (14.0%). Patients who developed post-TAVI LVOTO had significantly higher DLi-LVOTO scores than those who did not (median 54 vs. 17; P&lt;0.001). DLi-LVOTO demonstrated good discriminative performance for predicting any post-TAVI LVOTO (AUROC 0.782) and moderate-or-greater LVOTO (AUROC 0.736) (Figure 1). After adjustment for conventional risk factors, including small left ventricular cavity size and baseline LVOTO, DLi-LVOTO remained independently associated with post-TAVI LVOTO (adjusted OR 1.31 per 10-point increase; 95% CI 1.08–1.58; P=0.005). Consistent associations were observed in patients without baseline LVOTO on pre-procedure TTE. Conclusions A deep learning-derived index obtained from a single PLAX echocardiographic view is associated with post-TAVI LVOTO and demonstrates good discriminative performance. DLi-LVOTO may serve as a complementary tool for identifying patients at risk of post-TAVI LVOTO during pre-procedural evaluation.ROC curves for post-TAVR LVOTOFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: A deep learning-based single-view echocardiographic analysis for prediction of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) can be utilized to increase vessel compliance and diameter and allow for safe transfemoral access during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Purpose The aim of our study is to systematically evaluate the safety and efficacy of IVL-facilitated transfemoral access in patients undergoing TAVR implantation. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted for studies including patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR implantation with IVL-facilitated femoral access from inception through December 2025. The primary outcomes of interest included 30-day mortality, successful IVL-facilitated transfemoral access, and successful TAVR implantation. Secondary outcomes included perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm, need for covered stent, major vascular complication, stroke, and acute kidney injury. Proportion-based meta-analyses were conducted using random-effects models in R. Results Nine studies encompassing 546 patients with IVL-facilitated TAVR were included in our analysis. The mean age was 80 years with 59% males and a median STS score of 3.9. The pooled 30-day all-cause mortality rate was 2.3% (95% CI 1.01-5.27; I2 0%). Successful IVL-facilitated transfemoral access was 95.2% (95% CI 84.4-100; I2 82%) and successful TAVR implantation was achieved in 100% of patients (95% CI 99-100; I2 0%). Rates of vessel perforation (0%), dissection (4.5%), pseudoaneurysm (3.9%), need for covered stent (5.6%), major vascular complication (5%), stroke (0.1%), and acute kidney injury (4.4%) were low. The primary outcomes are depicted further in Figure 1. Conclusion(s) IVL-facilitated transfemoral access during TAVR is associated with low 30-day all-cause mortality and high procedural success. Major procedural complications were infrequent. Larger prospective studies are warranted to further define patient selection and optimize outcomes.figure--1--primary--outcomes.pngFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Safety and efficacy of intravascular lithotripsy-facilitated transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Rapid ventricular pacing is mandatory during transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Conventional right ventricular (RV) temporary pacing requires transvenous lead placement and introduces a potentially preventable mechanism of myocardial perforation and cardiac tamponade. Left ventricular (LV) guidewire pacing avoids RV instrumentation, but its impact on clinically relevant outcomes has not been systematically evaluated. Purpose To assess whether LV guidewire pacing improves procedural safety compared with conventional RV temporary pacing during TAVI. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis of MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and Web of Science was performed through February 2026. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Comparative studies of LV versus RV pacing during TAVI were included. The primary endpoint was cardiac tamponade. A pre-specified mechanistic analysis differentiated pacing lead–related from annular rupture–related tamponade. Random-effects models were applied. Results Five studies (1 randomised trial and 4 observational cohorts) including 2,840 patients (1,910 LV; 930 RV) were analysed. Global cardiac tamponade occurred in 1.1% with LV pacing versus 2.5% with RV pacing (OR 0.45; 95% CI 0.18–1.16; p=0.08; I²=0%). LV pacing significantly reduced pacing lead–related tamponade (OR 0.09; 95% CI 0.02–0.56; p=0.03; I²=0%), while annular rupture–related events were similar between strategies. All-cause mortality was lower in pooled analyses (OR 0.45; 95% CI 0.36–0.57; p&lt;0.001), predominantly driven by observational data. Stroke, major vascular complications, bleeding and permanent pacemaker implantation did not differ. LV pacing shortened procedural duration by 5.8 minutes (p=0.0002). Conclusion Elimination of transvenous RV lead instrumentation markedly reduces pacing lead–related cardiac tamponade without increasing major adverse events and improves procedural efficiency. LV guidewire pacing represents a mechanistically rational and immediately implementable strategy aligned with contemporary minimalist TAVI practice.Forest plotFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.PRISMAFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Eliminating transvenous right ventricular leads reduces pacing-related cardiac tamponade during TAVI: a mechanistic meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation remains a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The long-term clinical implications of pacemaker dependency following TAVI remain a subject of ongoing debate and investigation. In a previous single-center study from our group, examining the relationship between TAVI implantation depth and subsequent pacing burden, we found that approximately one-third of patients with initially low PPM stimulation rates experienced a clinically relevant increase to &gt;20% ventricular pacing within the first three months following TAVI. This temporal evolution suggests progressive conduction system injury and raises concerns about potential delayed adverse effects on cardiac function and clinical outcomes. Purpose This multicenter study investigated long-term changes in ventricular pacing burden and their association with mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods Patients receiving PPM after TAVI between 2009 and 2024 at two tertiary centers were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were categorized by ventricular pacing burden (&gt;20% defined as high) at baseline and follow-up: high/high (n=309), high/low (n=103), low/high (n=143), and low/low (n=216). Both self-expanding and balloon-expandable valves were included. Pacemaker burden was assessed at discharge and three months, and five-year outcomes, including mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events, were recorded. Results A total of 771 patients who underwent TAVI followed by PPM implantation were analyzed (median age 82 years; 49.5% female). Patients were categorized by ventricular pacing burden at baseline and follow-up: high/high (n=309), high/low (n=103), low/high (n=143), and low/low (n=216). At 5 years, all-cause mortality did not differ significantly among groups (log-rank p=0.310). In contrast, the composite MACE endpoint differed significantly (p=0.038). Compared with the low/low group, hazard ratios for 5-year MACE were 0.74 (95% CI 0.52–1.06) for low/high, 0.61 (95% CI 0.40–0.93) for high/low, and 0.97 (95% CI 0.69–1.35) for high/high, with the high/low group exhibiting the lowest cumulative MACE incidence. Conclusions Approximately 30% of patients experienced changes in ventricular pacing burden over time. While neither initial nor temporal pacing patterns affected overall mortality, a decreasing pacing rate (high/low) was significantly associated with a lower risk of MACE. These findings indicate that patients with persistently high pacing burden should may benefit from structured cardiological follow-up, including optimization of pacing parameter.
title: Long-term changes in pacemaker stimulation burden and its influence on clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a multicenter study

abstract: Abstract Background Patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) frequently present with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and metabolic comorbidities, complicating risk stratification. Right ventricular–pulmonary artery (RV–PA) coupling, assessed by the tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to systolic pulmonary artery pressure ratio (TAPSE/sPAP), has emerged as a potential prognostic marker. However, its prognostic relevance across distinct cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) phenotypes remains unclear. Methods We analysed 886 consecutive TAVI patients stratified into four CKM phenotypes (no burden, metabolic-only, kidney-only, combined). Baseline TAPSE/sPAP was measured by echocardiography. The primary endpoints were 36-month cardiovascular (CV) mortality, all-cause mortality, and heart failure (HF) hospitalisation. Cox regression and classification and regression tree (CART) analysis were performed to assess prognostic impact and derive optimal cut-points. Results Baseline TAPSE/sPAP differed significantly across CKM phenotypes (overall p&lt;0.001; Figure 1). Mean values were 0.599±0.295 in the no-burden group (n=229), 0.557±0.258 in the metabolic-only group (n=125), 0.489±0.231 in the kidney-only group (n=346), and 0.525±0.285 in the combined group (n=186). TAPSE/sPAP was lowest in the kidney-only phenotype (p&lt;0.001 vs no burden; p=0.048 vs metabolic-only). Using data-driven cut-points (≤0.318, 0.319–0.623, &gt;0.623), Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated stepwise increases in 36-month event rates across decreasing TAPSE/sPAP categories (Figure 2). All-cause mortality was 18.4% for &gt;0.623, 25.9% for 0.319–0.623, and 35.2% for ≤0.318 (log-rank p=0.003). Similar graded associations were observed for CV mortality (log-rank p=0.003) and HF hospitalisation (log-rank p&lt;0.001). In multivariable analysis, higher TAPSE/sPAP was independently associated with lower risk of CV death, all-cause mortality, and HF hospitalisation (all p&lt;0.01). The prognostic impact was most pronounced in patients with CKD. In the kidney-only phenotype, each unit increase in TAPSE/sPAP was associated with reduced CV death (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07–0.76; p=0.016) and HF hospitalisation (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.12–0.83; p=0.019). Conclusion TAPSE/sPAP provides incremental prognostic information beyond CKM burden in TAVI patients. Lower TAPSE/sPAP identifies progressively higher mortality and HF risk, particularly in the kidney-only phenotype, supporting integration of RV–PA coupling into post-TAVI risk assessment.Figure 1 For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Prognostic value of TAPSE/sPAP ratio across cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic phenotypes after TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Transfemoral approach has become the standard primary access for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) due to low complication rates. An additional femoral secondary access (FSCA) is often used for angiographic guidance of the procedure. Recently, small single-center studies demonstrated feasibility of transfemoral TAVI through a single access (SA). However, comparative and large-scale data are missing. We assessed vascular and bleeding complications of FSCA and SA approaches in a large multicenter registry to evaluate both strategies. Methods The PULSE registry (Plug or sUture based vascuLar cloSurE after TAVI) retrospectively evaluated data of 7,819 patients who underwent transfemoral TAVI at 10 high-volume German heart centers from 2016 to 2021. FSCA and SA were performed in 7071 (90%) and 748 (10%) patients, respectively. A propensity score was used to match 375 patients who received FSCA with 375 patients who received SA. Outcomes were evaluated in accordance with the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC-3) definitions. In contrast to prior abstracts derived from the same registry, the present study examines a single access compared to a bi-femoral approach and includes extensive propensity-score matching as well as novel results all differing to previous analyses. Results Mean age was 81.7±3.6 years and 46.7% of patients were female (mean logistic EuroSCORE II &gt;4: 35.3%). Groups were comparable regarding available baseline comorbidities, echo, computed tomography and procedural variables. Secondary access-related vascular complications occurred in 4.0% of patients with FSCA (major 1.6%; minor 2.4%) vs. none in SA. These were mainly characterized as pseudoaneurysms (2.9%) and bleeding (0.8%) mostly treated conservatively (2.4%), yet in some cases surgical repair was required (0.8%). Complications at the TAVI access did not differ significantly (8.0 vs. 6.4%, p=0.48). SA was associated with lower rates of stage III/IV acute kidney injury (5.1 vs. 2.1%, p=0.05). No significant difference was observed regarding type III/IV bleeding (2.7% vs. 4.3%, p=0.32), stroke rate (1.6% vs. 3.2%, p=0.23), procedural results, or all-cause 30-day mortality (2.9% and 4.8%, p=0.26) for FSCA and SA groups. Conclusion In patients treated with transfemoral TAVI, a single access approach was associated with lower rates of major and minor access-related vascular complications related to the secondary access, without compromising the procedure, suggesting potential benefits of a streamlined TAVI approach with the omission of additional vascular access.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentre PULSE registry of 7,819 transfemoral TAVI patients at 10 German centres (2016 to 2021); single access 748 versus secondary access 7071; propensity matching of 375 with 375.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective, non-randomised comparison in which single access was used in only 10% of patients, so operator selection may have influenced results.
appraisal.one_line: Single femoral access for transfemoral TAVI was associated with fewer secondary-access vascular complications without worse 30-day outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Secondary access-related vascular complications occurred in 4.0% of patients with FSCA (major 1.6%; minor 2.4%) vs. none in SA. Complications at the TAVI access did not differ significantly (8.0 vs. 6.4%, p=0.48). No significant difference was observed regarding type III/IV bleeding (2.7% vs. 4.3%, p=0.32), stroke rate (1.6% vs. 3.2%, p=0.23), or all-cause 30-day mortality (2.9% and 4.8%, p=0.26) for FSCA and SA groups.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a minimalist TAVI access strategy that could be tested in a randomised or registry-based trial.

title: Rethinking access in TAVI: large multicenter cohort-based evaluation of a single access approach compared with standard bi-femoral strategy

abstract: Abstract Background The recent 2025 ESC guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease emphasize the role of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for the treatment of severe aortic stenosis. Despite extensive scientific evidence for TAVI, many steps of the procedure or periprocedural management ultimately remain at the discretion of the operator due to a paucity of recommendations. Aims To assess the routine procedural and periprocedural management of patients undergoing TAVI for the treatment of aortic stenosis in Germany. Methods The working group for interventional cardiology (AGIK) of the German Cardiac Society (DGK) designed an online survey that was distributed to all German TAVI centers to obtain a representative assessment of clinical practice. The questionnaire comprised a total of 68 questions covering pre-procedural planning, procedural strategies, the post-procedural course and structural aspects. Data were collected from October 2023 to June 2024. Results The survey was completed by 56/85 centers (66%), representing a cumulative volume of approximately 20.000 procedures annually. Most centers (70%) performed 200-600 TAVI procedures per year. Preprocedural workup and procedural aspects differed: Coronary angiography remained routine in 76% of centers while transesophageal echocardiography was restricted to specific indications (86%). Analgosedation was the preferred anesthesia strategy (56%) followed by local anesthesia (24%). Transfemoral access was first-choice (93.4%), transaxillary (2.9%) and transapical (2.7%) approaches were selectively employed. US-guided puncture was performed in 54% of cases with subsequent suture-based preclosure (67%). The preferred secondary access was femoral (57%). Cerebral embolic protection (&lt;5% in 87% of centers), and direct LV-pacing (9%) were limited to selected cases. Transcatheter heart valve selection was related to various factors, including calcification patterns (66%), annular dimensions (59%) and preservation of coronary access (51%). Final aortography (93%) and invasive hemodynamic assessment (71%) were considered standard by most respondents. Heparin was antagonized after conclusion of the procedure in most centers partially (42%) or completely (32%). Only 16% regularly transferred patients after uneventful TAVI to ICU the remainder to intermediate care or normal wards. Routine rhythm monitoring was performed for 1-2 days in 60% of centers. Aspirin was the standard antithrombotic drug after TAVI (93%) and DOAC monotherapy was preferred in patients with an indication for anticoagulation. Conclusions With the recent guideline-supported expansion of TAVI, this nationwide survey offers important insights into the current clinical routine and detailed (peri-)procedural steps of TAVI. These findings suggest a heterogenous approach to TAVI and may stimulate further discussions on workflow optimization to improve outcomes for patients with severe aortic stenosis.
title: The current state of TAVI in Germany – a nationwide assessment

abstract: Abstract Background Paravalvular leak (PVL) and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) remain clinically important complications after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Procedural strategies aimed at reducing PVL, including valve oversizing and post-dilatation, may increase the risk of conduction disturbances and PPI. Conversely, strategies intended to minimize conduction disturbances and avoid PPI, such as selecting a smaller valve size and avoiding post-dilatation, may increase the risk of residual PVL. However, the relative prognostic impact of PVL versus PPI after TAVI remains unclear. Purpose The purpose of the present study was to compare the prognostic impact of mild-or-greater PVL and new-onset PPI after TAVI in a multicenter registry. Methods We analyzed data from a prospective, multicenter registry in Japan that enrolled 3,129 consecutive patients undergoing TAVI at seven centers between April 2010 and June 2022. After excluding patients with prior PPI, missing post-procedural PVL data, preprocedural left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) &lt;40%, a history of surgical or transcatheter aortic valve replacement, or unsuccessful transcatheter valve implantation, 2,673 patients were included in the present analysis. PVL(+) was defined as mild or greater PVL on post-procedural transthoracic echocardiography, and PPI(+) as new-onset PPI during the index hospitalization. Patients were categorized into four groups: PVL(–)/PPI(–) (n=1,864), PVL(+)/PPI(–) (n=614), PVL(–)/PPI(+) (n=135), and PVL(+)/PPI(+) (n=60). The primary endpoint was three-year all-cause mortality and the secondary endpoint was three-year heart failure hospitalization (HFH). Results For all-cause mortality, Kaplan–Meier analysis across the four groups showed the highest mortality in the PVL(+)/PPI(+) group, and PVL(+)/PPI(–) patients had significantly higher three-year all-cause mortality than PVL(–)/PPI(+) patients (21.9% vs. 12.9%, P=0.02) (Figure 1A). However, in multivariable analysis, neither PVL(+) nor PPI(+) was an independent prognostic factor for all-cause mortality. In a subgroup analysis restricted to PVL(+)/PPI(–) and PVL(–)/PPI(+) patients, PVL(+) showed a consistent trend toward worse all-cause mortality than PPI(+) across most subgroups (Figure 2). For HFH, Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated that HFH rates were comparable between PVL(+)/PPI(–) and PVL(–)/PPI(+) patients (10.1% vs. 10.6%, P=0.95) (Figure 1B). However, in multivariable analysis, PVL(+) was an independent predictor of HFH (HR 1.38, P=0.03), whereas PPI(+) was not (HR 1.52, P=0.07). Conclusion In patients undergoing TAVI with LVEF ≥40%, mild-or-greater PVL was associated with a stronger adverse prognostic factor than new-onset PPI. When a trade-off between PVL reduction and conduction safety is unavoidable, prioritizing PVL reduction may be reasonable, while individualized decision-making remains essential.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Comparative prognostic impact of paravalvular leak versus permanent pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation without reduced ejection fraction patients

abstract: Abstract Background Permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) occurs in 10–25% of patients after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and adversely affects long-term outcomes. As TAVR expands to younger, lower-risk populations, accurate preprocedural risk stratification becomes critical. Current prediction models rely on limited clinical or single-modality imaging variables and demonstrate modest discriminatory performance (c-statistics 0.65–0.75). No preprocedural score integrating multimodal CT geometry, aortic valve calcification burden, echocardiographic diastolic function, and baseline conduction status has been developed. Purpose To derive and temporally validate a preprocedural multimodal imaging-based Conduction Risk Index (CRI) for predicting 30-day PPI after TAVR and to compare its performance against existing risk scores and machine learning algorithms. Methods This single-centre retrospective study analysed 1,226 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR between June 2019 and December 2024. We derived the CRI, a dimensionless composite index incorporating standardised CT-derived annular geometry, device-landing-zone calcium volume, and echocardiographic diastolic function parameters. Internal-external cross-validation was conducted across three non-overlapping temporal blocks (2019–2020, 2021–2022, 2023–2024). Model discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI) were compared against a preprocedural modified Maeno score, clinical variables alone, and a gradient boosting machine. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed in a stratified random subsample. Results Among 1,226 patients (mean age 71 ± 8 years; 47.8% male), 151 (12.3%) required PPI within 30 days. The final model combining CRI, age, and baseline right bundle branch block achieved a pooled area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89 (95% CI 0.86–0.91) with excellent calibration (slope 1.02; Brier score 0.09). It outperformed the modified Maeno score (AUC 0.71; ΔAUC 0.18, p &lt; 0.001), clinical variables alone (ΔAUC 0.21, p &lt; 0.001), and performed comparably to a gradient boosting machine (AUC 0.87). Continuous NRI versus the modified Maeno score was 0.58 (95% CI 0.44–0.72, p &lt; 0.001). Performance remained stable across all pre-specified subgroups (all interaction p &gt; 0.20). Interobserver agreement for CT measurements was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient &gt; 0.94). Conclusions A dimensionless multimodal imaging index integrating CT-derived geometric and calcific parameters with echocardiographic diastolic function and baseline conduction status provides robust preprocedural PPI risk stratification after TAVR. External validation in independent multicentre cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.Multimodal Imaging Score for PredictingFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Multimodal CT-echocardiographic score for preprocedural prediction of permanent pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Reliable estimation of long-term survival after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains challenging, and commonly used surgical scores, including the EuroScore II, show limited prognostic accuracy in this setting. We aimed to identify simple clinical predictors of 3-year mortality and to develop an intuitive, bedside-applicable risk score. Methods In this single-center cohort study, 585 consecutive TAVI patients (follow-up of at least 3.8 years) were analyzed. LASSO-Cox regression was used to select predictors of 3-year all-cause mortality, followed by multivariable Cox modeling. A point-based score was constructed by scaling regression coefficients, and its discriminative performance was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analyses and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. The EuroScore II served as comparator. Results Six routinely available clinical variables—age &gt; 80 years, male sex, eGFR &lt; 60 ml/min, atrial fibrillation, anemia, and diabetes mellitus—were identified as independent predictors and incorporated into the SALZBURG score (range 0–11 points). Increasing score levels showed a stepwise rise in 3-year mortality, with clear separation of low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (log-rank p &lt; 0.001). The SALZBURG score demonstrated good discriminative performance (AUC 0.662; 95% CI 0.611–0.714), significantly (p = 0.002) outperforming the EuroScore II (AUC 0.564;95% CI 0.508–0.620). The score requires no imaging parameters or specialized assessments and can be calculated within seconds using standard pre-TAVI data. Conclusion The SALZBURG score provides simple, robust, and clinically meaningful prediction of 3-year mortality after TAVI and outperforms the EuroScore II while relying on fewer and more readily available variables. Its ease of use supports integration into routine evaluation, and external validation is warranted to confirm its generalizability.SALZBURG ScoreFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Kaplan-Meier Curve SALZBURG ScoreFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: The SALZBURG score: a comorbidity-focused model for long-term survival stratification following TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background The progressive expansion of indications for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) towards lower-risk and younger populations has raised concerns about potential outcome attenuation with increasing procedural volumes. Real-world evidence addressing this concern is limited. Objective To assess longitudinal trends and changes in patient characteristics and procedural outcomes in a large nationwide TAVI cohort. Methods The SwissTAVI Registry prospectively enrolled consecutive patients undergoing TAVI in Switzerland. Baseline characteristics, procedural complications and outcomes were compared across three periods: 2011-2015, 2016-2020 and 2021-2024. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke) at one year. The secondary endpoint was 30-day MACE. Results Among 19’452 patients, TAVI volume increased 27% annually. Patient age (82 years) and comorbidity burden remained stable, while the proportion of women increased (51% to 58%) and the median STS score decreased (4.5% to 3.3%). Considering the expansion to lower-risk patients, 1-year MACE declined significantly from 16% to 14% to 9.1% across periods (adjusted HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.62-0.78, p&lt;0.001). Similarly, 30-day MACE decreased from 6.9% to 5.2% to 4.0% (adjusted HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.55-0.78, p&lt;0.001). Procedural mortality declined from 2.9% to 1.2%, periprocedural myocardial infarction from 0.4% to 0.2% and stroke from 3.2% to 2.0% (all p&lt;0.001). (Figure 1). Conclusion Risk-adjusted TAVI outcomes improved continuously despite a significant volume increase, with improvements exceeding those expected from lower-risk patients risk profiles alone.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective national SwissTAVI Registry; 19’452 patients compared across three periods: 2011-2015, 2016-2020 and 2021-2024.
appraisal.main_limitation: Temporal comparison within a registry is open to era effects and unmeasured changes in case selection and reporting.
appraisal.one_line: In the Swiss national TAVI registry, risk-adjusted one-year MACE fell across three eras despite rising volume and lower-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 1-year MACE declined significantly from 16% to 14% to 9.1% across periods (adjusted HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.62-0.78). 30-day MACE decreased from 6.9% to 5.2% to 4.0% (adjusted HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.55-0.78).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the concern that expansion of TAVI to lower-risk patients and higher volumes dilutes outcomes.

title: Longitudinal trends and outcomes in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a report from the Swiss TAVI registry

abstract: Abstract Background Approximately 10–20% of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) require permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). As the conduction system is located close to the aortic root, mechanical interaction during valve implantation is the main cause of new conduction disturbances. While pre-procedural right bundle branch block is an established risk factor for PPI after TAVI, the association with left bundle branch block (LBBB) is less understood. Identifying patients at high risk of PPI may help to better anticipate these post-procedural complications and prevent readmissions. The aim of this study was to evaluate whether pre-existing or new-onset LBBB (occurring after TAVI) is associated with higher odds of PPI within 30 days after TAVI. Methods This study included participants from the SwissTAVI cohort study (NCT01368250) who underwent TAVI between January 2017 and December 2024, and had an available baseline electrocardiogram (ECG) showing either no intraventricular conduction delay or LBBB. Participants with prior pacemaker implantation or valve-in-valve procedures were excluded. The association between LBBB status (no LBBB, pre-procedural LBBB, and new-onset LBBB after TAVI) and PPI within 30 days was assessed using logistic regression, adjusting for age, comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, renal function), baseline ECG rhythm, baseline atrioventricular block, and prosthetic valve size. Secondary analyses assessed sex-specific associations and 30-day mortality. Results A total of 10,319 patients (48% women) undergoing TAVI were included in the study. A new PPI was required in 1,322 (12.8%). Among the participants, 71.8% (n=7,404) had no LBBB, 11.3% (n=1,166) had pre-procedural LBBB, and 16.9% (n=1,749) developed new-onset LBBB. After adjustment, both pre-procedural LBBB (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.07–1.53) and new-onset LBBB (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.29–1.75) were associated with higher odds of 30-day PPI. These associations were largely consistent in both women and men. Pre-procedural (adjusted OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.62–1.48) or new-onset LBBB (adjusted OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.57–1.26) were not significantly associated with higher 30-day mortality. Conclusions Both pre-procedural and new-onset LBBB were significantly associated with increased odds of PPI within 30 days after TAVI. The highest odds were observed in patients with new-onset LBBB. These findings suggest that LBBB, and not only RBBB, should be included in pre-procedural risk stratification.OR for PPI within 30 days post-TAVIFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Left bundle branch block and risk for pacemaker implantation after TAVI: insights from the SwissTAVI Cohort Study

abstract: Abstract Background although assessment of inducible myocardial ischemia in patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of the Coronary Arteries (AAOCA) is generally recommended, there is no clear consensus regarding the most appropriate stress test. In a previous study from our centre, we demonstrated that, in a cohort of 100 AAOCA patients, 14% exhibited perfusion abnormalities during dobutamine stress cardiac magnetic resonance (dsCMR) consistent with inducible myocardial ischemia. Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery (p &lt; 0.001) and the presence of an intramural course (IM) (p = 0.049) were significantly associated with inducible ischemia. In 9% of cases LGE with an ischemic pattern was found in the AAOCA territory; these patients were older [p = 0.001] and had a history of acute coronary syndrome (p &lt; 0.001). However, no computed tomography (CT) parameters have been studied in relation to inducible myocardial ischemia on dsCMR to better identify patients who require further investigation, particularly within the high-risk subgroup of right AAOCA (R-AAOCA) with an intramural course (IM). Purpose a) To determine which CT characteristics are associated with reduced fractional flow reserve (FFR) during hyperaemia in patients with R-AAOCA and IM; b) To evaluate whether these parameters are associated with inducible myocardial ischemia. Methods This single-centre study included two cohorts of patients, both with R-AAOCA and IM. In the first cohort, all patients underwent CT and invasive coronary angiography with evaluation of FFR during hyperaemia. In the second cohort, all patients underwent dsCMR and CT according to the internal AAOCA evaluation protocol for risk stratification. CT analysis was performed using convolutional neural networks. Results The cohort of R-AAOCA patients with IM included 42 individuals, of whom 17% exhibited hyperaemic FFR &lt; 0.80. Among the CT parameters, only the minimum diameter measured was found to be associated with positive FFR (1.37 ± 0.17 vs. 1.64 ± 0.35 mm; p = 0.020). For the minimum area measured, a trend toward significance was observed (2.26 ± 0.42 vs. 4.5 ± 2.2 mm²; p = 0.053). ROC curve analysis of the minimum diameter yielded an AUC of 0.752 [0.583–0.921] (p = 0.038). The best cut-off identified using the Youden index was 1.59 mm. In a larger cohort of R-AAOCA patients with IM including 61 patients, 15% exhibited perfusion abnormalities on dsCMR consistent with inducible myocardial ischemia. In this cohort, a minimum diameter measured at CT &lt; 1.59 mm was associated with inducible myocardial ischemia on dsCMR (27% vs. 6%; p = 0.044). Conclusions In the high-risk subgroup of patients with R-AAOCA and IM, a minimal intramural diameter &lt; 1.59 mm was associated with hyperaemic FFR &lt; 0.80. Notably, this anatomical parameter was also associated with inducible myocardial ischemia on dsCMR, supporting its potential role in identifying patients at higher functional risk.ROC CURVE
title: Imaging-based identification of high-risk anomalous aortic origin of coronary arteries (AAOCA) patients

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve intervention (TAVI) has become an established treatment for patients with severe aortic stenosis. Although nearly half of the patients are female, women remain underrepresented in clinical research. The clinical profile differs from that of men, with a higher prevalence of small aortic annulus and increased risk of bleeding complications. Large scale real-world data comparing sex- differences in TAVI remain scarce. Purpose This study aims to describe sex-differences in characteristics and clinical outcomes of patients receiving TAVI from a large, contemporary, nationwide cohort. Methods We included data from the Netherlands Heart Registration between 2019-2024. We described differences between women and men in terms of patient- and procedural characteristics as well as VARC-3 adverse-events using the Mann-Whitney U test and chi-squared test. We calculated odds-ratios using logistic regression. We described differences in all-cause mortality using unadjusted cox-regressions and Kaplan-Meier mortality curves. Results Of 6866 patients undergoing TAVI in the Netherlands between 2019-2024, 3070 (44.7%) were female. Female patients were older and had a higher EuroSCOREII. Valve-sizes in women were significantly smaller compared to men’s. More women received a self-expanding valve. Major vascular complications at 30 days occurred more often in women, while men more often had a new permanent pacemaker-implantation at 30 days. Median follow-up was 501 days. While there was no difference in 30-day unadjusted all-cause mortality risk, men had a higher one-year unadjusted all-cause mortality risk compared to women. Patient characteristics and clinical outcomes per sex are presented in Table 1 and Figure 1. Conclusions 44.7% of the patients undergoing TAVI in the Netherlands is female. In a purely descriptive manner, unadjusted one-year mortality risk was higher for men compared to women. Women more often had major vascular complications, whereas men more often required new permanent pacemaker implantation. These findings underscore the need for more research regarding factors impacting sex-based differences in clinical outcomes in TAVI.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Differences between women and men undergoing transcatheter aortic valve intervention: a nationwide cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with end-stage kidney disease requiring dialysis represent a particularly high-risk population among those undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for aortic stenosis. Prior studies have suggested poorer outcomes for dialysis patients, with higher rates of mortality and complications including structural valve deterioration. Purpose Valve durability is a key consideration for all TAVI patients and this study aims to evaluate the incidence and progression of SVD in dialysis patients and examine its association with clinical outcomes. Method An initial cohort of 22,447 eligible patients was identified on the Australasian Cardiac Outcomes Registry (ACOR), with 428 receiving dialysis. A 1:2 propensity score matching model was constructed using baseline demographic and clinical variables to balance covariates between groups. SVD was defined according to VARC-3 criteria as an increase in transvalvular gradient and/or worsening aortic regurgitation relative to post-procedural baseline. Echocardiographic assessment windows were predefined as 14-60 days (30-day analysis) and 9-15 months (12-month analysis). Conditional logistic regression was then used to evaluate the association between dialysis and SVD at 30 days and 12 months. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards modelling were performed to assess 12-month mortality. Results After propensity matching, 760 patients were included in the 30-day SVD analysis. 17 SVD events occurred within 30 days. Dialysis was associated with significantly increased odds of early SVD (OR 3.50, 95% CI ~1.1–11.4, p=0.03). At 12 months, 406 patients had eligible echocardiographic follow-up, with 14 SVD events observed. Dialysis was associated with a numerically increased risk of SVD (OR 3.24, 95% CI 0.29–36.63; p=0.34), although this did not reach statistical significance. Interpretation is limited by low event rates and significant follow-up attrition. For 12-month mortality, 816 matched patients were analysed and 80 deaths observed. One-year survival was 96.4% (95% CI 94.8–98.0%) in non-dialysis patients compared with 91.7% (95% CI 88.4–95.1%) in dialysis patients. Dialysis was associated with a significantly increased hazard of death at 12 months (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.56–3.76, p&lt;0.001). Conclusion In this propensity-matched cohort, dialysis was independently associated with increased early SVD and significantly higher 12-month mortality following TAVI. Although a similar magnitude of association between dialysis and SVD was observed at 12 months, statistical significance was not achieved due to limited event rates and incomplete follow-up These findings suggest that dialysis-related pathophysiologic mechanisms may exert their greatest impact early after valve implantation, though further studies with comprehensive longitudinal follow-up are warranted to clarify long-term structural durability in this population.12-Month Survival post TAVIFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of dialysis on structural valve deterioration post TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) remains a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), yet its long-term prognostic impact remains debated. Purpose To determine the association between new PPI after TAVI and long-term mortality and heart failure (HF) rehospitalization using reconstructed individual patient time-to-event data. Methods We systematically identified studies reporting Kaplan–Meier curves with numbers at risk after TAVI. Individual patient time-to-event data were reconstructed using validated methodology. Patients who died within 30 days were excluded to reduce survivorship bias. Hazard ratios (HR) were derived using Cox regression and pooled with random-effects models. Time-dependent effects were assessed using flexible parametric mixed-effects modeling. Results Twenty-two studies including 92’296 patients were analyzed (68’037 no PPI; 15’625 new PPI; 8’634 previous PPI). After excluding early mortality, 87’107 patients remained for time-to-event analysis. New PPI after TAVI was associated with significantly higher long-term mortality compared with no PPI (pooled HR 1.25 [95% CI 1.15–1.36]; pooled Kaplan–Meier HR 1.26 [1.21–1.31]; p&lt;0.0001). Patients with previous PPI exhibited the highest mortality risk (HR 1.38 [1.32–1.45] vs no PPI; HR 1.09 [1.03–1.16] vs new PPI). New PPI was also associated with increased HF-related rehospitalisation (HR 1.28 [1.06–1.55]). Time-dependent modelling demonstrated that excess mortality risk in PPI patients is greatest early after TAVI but remains elevated for up to 5 years. Conclusion In this large meta-analysis using reconstructed time-to-event data, PPI after TAVI is associated with a sustained increase in mortality and HF rehospitalization. These findings underscore the clinical importance of procedural strategies aimed at minimizing conduction injury and avoiding unnecessary PPI.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of permanent pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an updated systematic review with meta-analysis of reconstructed time-to-event data

abstract: Abstract Background Suboptimal haemodynamic performance following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) poses significant risks to valve durability and patient outcomes1,2. Invasive haemodynamic measurements during TAVI help identify patients at risk. Recently, a TAVI guidewire equipped with integrated fibre-optic pressure sensor was developed to guide valve delivery and enable real-time invasive haemodynamic monitoring3. While previous studies have demonstrated its safety profile and pacing efficacy, comprehensive data on the construct validity of its haemodynamic measurements are limited. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the construct validity of haemodynamic measurements obtained with a fibre-optic pressure sensor TAVI guidewire compared to conventional fluid-filled pigtail catheters. Methods This investigator-initiated, prospective registry, included patients undergoing TAVI for severe aortic stenosis. Complete haemodynamic assessment was performed pre- and post-TAVI with both the fibre-optic TAVI guidewire and conventional fluid-filled pigtail catheters. Primary endpoint was the construct validity of fibre-optic guidewire-derived post-TAVI mean pressure gradient (PG) compared to fluid-filled pigtail catheter measurements. Secondary endpoints included construct validity of the fibre-optic guidewire for isolated pressure measurements and assessment of paravalvular regurgitation (PVR). Finally, in-depth signal analysis was conducted using previously validated automated algorithm4, which allowed direct comparison of continuous pressure signals by correcting for discrepancies between software packages with different calculation algorithms. Results This study included 150 patients (mean age 79.7±5.8 years; 46.7% female). Comparison of invasive pressure measurements yielded moderate to excellent agreement (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]-range:0.65-0.95). Bias was observed in left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP), with the fibre-optic guidewire measuring higher LVEDPs (+3.5 mmHg). Post-TAVI mean PG showed a mean absolute difference of 2.7±2.1 mmHg (ICC:0.67), minimal bias (-0.45mmHg), and 87% concordance with a discrete cut-off (10 mmHg). Good overall agreement was observed for most indices of PVR [ICC-range:0.81-0.87]. Automated algorithm assessment revealed fewer artefacts and calibration errors for the fibre-optic guidewire (p=0.048). Repeat analysis using algorithm-derived parameters improved agreement between fibre-optic and pigtail catheter measurements of mean PG (ICC:0.85). Conclusions The fibre-optic guidewire effectively classifies clinically relevant transvalvular gradients with limited bias post-TAVI.
