The fibre-optic guidewire produced higher LVEDPs, possibly resulting from wire-induced leaflet interaction. Algorithm-derived assessment revealed the fibre-optic guidewire producing measurements with fewer artefacts and calibration errors, thereby potentially challenging current measurement standards.Figure 1 Central IllustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2 Primary EndpointFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Construct validity of a fibre-optic pressure sensor integrated TAVI guidewire for invasive pressure measurements in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a prospective registry

abstract: Abstract Background As transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) expands towards younger patients, valve selection has become increasingly important for lifetime management and durability. Randomized trials demonstrated comparable mortality rates between balloon-expandable and self-expanding valves but differences in outcomes such as stroke and permanent pacemaker implantation. However, strict inclusion criteria limit their generalizability. Contemporary large-scale real-world data are therefore needed to assess patient selection and outcomes with different valve types in routine practice. Purpose The aim of this study was to characterize patients and compare clinical outcomes among those undergoing TAVI with balloon-expandable versus self-expanding valves in a large, nationwide, contemporary cohort. Methods Netherlands Heart Registration data identified patients undergoing TAVI between 2019 and 2024, excluding patients with an unknown implanted valve type and with prior aortic valve intervention. Time-to-event analysis for mortality was performed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusting for baseline characteristics and medical history variables associated with mortality in univariable analyses. Results A total of 6,922 patients underwent TAVI in the Netherlands between 2019 and 2024. Mean age was 79.9 ± 6.3 years, and 44.9% was female. Median Euroscore II was 3.07% (interquartile range 1.95%–4.87%). Of these, 3,522 (50.9%) patients received a self-expanding valve, while 3,400 (49.1%) received a balloon-expandable valve. Patients who received self-expanding valves were more often female, frail, and more frequently had poor mobility and dyspnea. In contrast, patients who received balloon-expandable valves more often had extracardiac arteriopathy and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. Patients receiving balloon-expandable valves experienced stroke with neurological dysfunction during hospitalization less often than those receiving self-expanding valves (1.5% vs. 2.5%; OR 0.60; 95%CI 0.42-0.85; p=0.004). Major vascular complications within 30 days after TAVI were more frequent in patients receiving balloon-expandable valves (2.4% vs. 1.7%; OR 1.45; 95%CI 1.01-2.08; p=0.04). Need for permanent implantation at 30 days was comparable between both groups (9.9% vs. 11.3%; OR 0.86; 95%CI 0.74-1.00; p=0.05). Adjusted mortality up to 4-year follow-up was comparable between patients receiving balloon-expandable and self-expanding valves (37.6% vs. 34.7%; HRadj 1.10; 95%CI 0.99-1.23; p=0.07; Fig. 1). Conclusion In this nationwide cohort, balloon-expandable valves were more often implanted in males and patients with extracardiac arteriopathy. Major vascular complications occured more often in patients receiving balloon-expandable valves. In contrast, strokes occurred more often in patients receiving self-expanding valves. The 4-year mortality rate and need for pacemaker implantation was comparable between both groups.Kaplan Meier plot for mortalityFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Nationwide comparison of patients treated with self-expanding versus balloon-expandable valves for TAVI: insights from the netherlands heart registration

abstract: Abstract Background The latest generation supra-annular self-expandable transcatheter heart valve (Evolut FX+) features three apertures positioned 120 degrees apart designed to facilitate coronary cannulation after implantation. However, it is unknown whether the coronary artery ostia align with these apertures in the Asian population, and the optimal implantation depth of Evolut FX+ is also unclear. Purpose We aimed to clarify the optimal implantation depth by evaluating the positional relationship between the coronary artery ostium and the Evolut FX+ apertures in the Asian population, as predicted from preoperative computed tomography (CT). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 496 patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) at our hospital between October 2015 and June 2025. We excluded cases in which contrast-enhanced CT were unavailable and a total of 470 cases were included in the present analysis. A 26-mm Evolut FX+ valve was virtually implanted at depths of 0, 3, and 6 mm below the annular plane, and we assessed whether the coronary artery ostium matched the inside of the apertures, and if it did not, we defined it as a coronary misalignment. Results The median age of the entire cohort was 84 years, and 61.9 % of patients were female. The mean annulus perimeter was 73.0 mm and the average sinus of valsalva (SOV) diameter was 30.5 mm. The mean coronary height was 16.9 mm in the right coronary artery (RCA) and 13.2 mm in the left coronary artery (LCA). The relationship between the coronary ostium of LCA and RCA and the flame apertures at implantation depth of 0, 3, and 6 mm is shown in Figure 1. For the RCA, the coronary ostium and apertures were most closely matched at an implanted position of 3 mm. On the other hand, for LCA, the best match was observed at the 6 mm position. For both LCA and RCA, the coronary ostium and aperture locations matched in 44 % of cases at the 3mm position and in 54 % of cases at the 6mm position (Figure 2). At the 3 mm implantation depth, the coronary artery ostium was statistically more likely to be aligned with the apertures in men (p&lt; 0.001), and in those with a larger annulus perimeter (p&lt; 0.001), a larger right coronary cusp SOV (p&lt; 0.001) and a larger non-coronary cusp SOV (p&lt; 0.001), a higher RCA ostium (p&lt; 0.001), a higher LCA ostium (p&lt; 0.001). Conclusions In the Asian populations, the implantation depth most likely to align the RCA ostium with the Evolut FX + valve was 3 mm, whereas a depth of 6 mm was most likely to match the LCA ostium.Figure1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Underlying coronary misalignment after latest generation supra-annular self-expandable transcatheter heart valves in the asian population

abstract: Abstract Background Permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). While procedural and electro-anatomic factors are well established, patient-related susceptibility markers remain unclear.We aimed to evaluate whether the preprocedural C-reactive protein–albumin–lymphocyte (CALLY) index independently predicts and aids in risk stratification for 30-day PPI after TAVR. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 812 consecutive TAVR patients with complete baseline labs (2010–2025). The CALLY index was calculated as (albumin × lymphocytes ÷ CRP) ×10, and patients were stratified into quartiles (Q1–Q4). The primary endpoint was new PPI within 30 days. Kaplan–Meier curves and Cox regression assessed the association between CALLY quartiles and PPI risk. Multivariable models adjusted for prespecified clinical, anatomic, and procedural factors. Subgroup analyses evaluated consistency across age, sex, hypertension, and valve type. Results Median time to PPI was 4 days (IQR 2–9), and 145 patients (17.9%) required implantation. Higher CALLY quartiles were associated with a progressively lower PPI risk compared with Q1: Q2 HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.42–0.99), Q3 HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.41–0.98), and Q4 HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.31–0.79). After multivariable adjustment, Q4 remained independently protective (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35–0.94). The protective effect of Q4 was consistent across subgroups, including age ≥80 years, males, females, hypertensive patients, and recipients of self-expanding valves. No significant effect modification was observed. Conclusions A higher preprocedural CALLY index was independently linked to a lower 30-day pacemaker requirement after TAVR. As a simple, inexpensive marker, CALLY may improve pre-TAVR risk stratification and guide peri-procedural planningFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Preprocedural CALLY index as a novel predictor of pacemaker requirement after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Pacemaker dependency and the impact of ventricular pacing burden after Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) in patients with pre-existing pacemakers remain poorly defined. Objectives To assess changes in pacemaker dependency after TAVR, identify predictors of 1-month dependency, and evaluate whether Ventricular Pacing (VP) % ≥40% predicts 1-year clinical outcomes. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis and a preexisting permanent pacemaker who underwent TAVR at a single center between 2010 and 2024. Pacemaker interrogation was performed before TAVR, at 1 month, and at 6–12 months. Pacemaker dependency was defined as ventricular pacing percentage (VP%) &gt;80% with a programmed lower rate of 60 bpm in VVI or DDD mode. Predictors of 1-month dependency were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression. For 1year outcomes (stroke, heart failure hospitalization, allcause mortality, and newonset atrial fibrillation), patients were stratified by VP% ≥40% at 1 month, and timetoevent analyses were performed using Royston–Parmar flexible parametric models or Cox regression. Results Among 102 patients analyzed, 53% were pacemakerdependent before TAVR, increasing to 75% at 1 month and 69% at 6–12 months. In multivariable analysis, preprocedural QRS duration was the only strong independent predictor of 1month dependency (odds ratio [OR] 1.07 per 1ms increase; 95% CI 1.02–1.11; p=0.001), whereas baseline dependency, QTc interval, and annulus perimeter were not significant. A ventricular pacing burden ≥40% at 1 month was not significantly associated with 1year stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or allcause mortality. There was a association with newonset atrial fibrillation (adjusted hazard ratio 7.29; 95% CI 1.98–9.16; p=0.043). Conclusions Pacemaker dependency is common and increases after TAVR. Baseline QRS duration predicts 1-month dependency. VP% ≥40% at 1 month was not associated with 1-year mortality, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization but may relate to higher atrial fibrillation risk.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of TAVR on pacemaker dependency in patients with pre-existing devices: predictors and one-year outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background With the expansion of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) to younger and lower-risk patients, long-term bioprosthetic valve durability has become a major clinical concern. While some procedural and anatomical contributors to valve deterioration have been explored, the overall landscape of durability predictors—including host-related mechanisms—remains incompletely understood, and the role of systemic inflammation remains largely unclear Objectives To investigate whether baseline systemic inflammation, early post-procedural valve hemodynamics, and anatomical characteristics are independently associated with long-term hemodynamic valve deterioration (HVD) after TAVR. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study including 755 patients who underwent TAVR between 2015 and 2025 with echocardiographic follow-up for up to 10 years. HVD was defined according to VARC-3 criteria. Baseline systemic inflammation index (SII) was calculated from pre-procedural blood counts. Associations with HVD were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and a time-dependent matched (risk-set) analysis. Results During follow-up, 102 patients (13.5%) developed HVD. Patients with HVD had significantly higher baseline SII and higher early post-TAVR mean transprosthetic gradients. In multivariable analysis, SII (hazard ratio [HR] 1.58 per 10³ increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.44–1.73), post-TAVR mean gradient (HR 1.46 per 5 mmHg; 95% CI 1.35–1.57), diabetes mellitus, female sex, and left ventricular outflow tract calcification were independently associated with HVD. In time-dependent matched analyses, elevated SII (HR 3.75; 95% CI 1.91–7.37) and higher post-TAVR mean gradient (HR 3.23; 95% CI 1.54–6.77) remained strong predictors of valve deterioration. Conclusions Baseline systemic inflammation and early post-procedural valve hemodynamics are independently associated with long-term hemodynamic valve deterioration after TAVR. Incorporating inflammatory biomarkers may improve risk stratification and surveillance strategies in contemporary TAVR practice.Geographical abstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Novel clinical, procedural, and imaging predictors of long-term durability after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Contemporary risk assessment before transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) increasingly recognizes the limitations of traditional surgical risk scores. While the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score remains an established tool for peri-procedural risk estimation, it does not incorporate objective measures of frailty, such as sarcopenia or skeletal muscle quality, which are important determinants of outcome in TAVI populations [1-3]. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate whether automated artificial-intelligence (AI)-derived body composition (BC) parameters obtained from routine pre-procedural computed tomography (CT) provide incremental prognostic value beyond the STS score in TAVI patients. Methods Consecutive TAVI patients at a German tertiary center (2019-2023) with available pre-procedural CT imaging were included. Automated three-dimensional (3D) body and organ analysis (BOA) software quantified skeletal muscle and adipose tissue compartments. Incremental prognostic value of BC parameters beyond STS score for 30-day and 3-year mortality was assessed using Cox regression and likelihood ratio tests (LRT). Predicted survival across BC deciles within STS risk strata was estimated using multivariable regression. Results A total of 1,418 TAVI patients were included in the analysis. Median age was 82 years (interquartile range [IQR] 78-85), and 42.3% were female. Median effective orifice area was 0.8cm² (IQR 0.6–0.9), and median transvalvular gradient was 41.0mmHg (IQR 30.0–56.0). Coronary artery disease was present in 64.3% and median STS score was 2.5% (IQR 1.7-4.0). The STS score was significantly associated with mortality across all follow-up periods. Among pre-procedural BC parameters, lower psoas muscle volume was associated with increased 30-day mortality beyond STS (hazard ratio [HR]=0.57, 95%CI 0.36–0.89; p=0.013) and significantly improved model fit (χ²(1)=6.26, p=0.012). Total skeletal muscle volume showed a similar association (HR=0.62, 95%CI 0.40–0.98; p=0.040; χ²(1)=4.49, p=0.034). Higher intramuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) was independently associated with 3-year mortality beyond STS (HR=1.19, 95%CI 1.05–1.35; p=0.006) and significantly improved model performance (χ²(1)=6.85, p=0.009), whereas psoas and total skeletal muscle volume were not. Predicted 3-year survival declined progressively across increasing IMAT deciles within comparable STS risk categories (Figure 1). Conclusion AI-based CT-derived BC analysis provides incremental prognostic information beyond established clinical risk scores such as STS in TAVI patients. Lower skeletal and psoas muscle volume were primarily associated with early mortality, whereas higher IMAT, reflecting impaired muscle quality, predicted mid-term mortality. Assessment of sarcopenia and muscle quality may therefore serve as a complementary component of contemporary risk stratification and support individualized Heart Team decision-making.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Artificial intelligence-based computed tomography quantification of sarcopenia markers enhances risk stratification in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (Tf-TAVI) requires large-bore femoral arterial access. Although the incidence of access-site complications has declined over time, vascular complications remain a clinically relevant challenge and are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Reliable vascular closure devices (VCDs) are essential for safe large-bore access management. VCDs include plug-based and suture-based systems; however, comparative data—particularly for latest-generation devices—remain limited and partially conflicting. Purpose To compare the efficacy and safety of the latest-generation suture-based ProStyle device with the collagen plug–based MANTA device for large-bore femoral arteriotomy closure following transfemoral TAVI. Methods This multicenter retrospective registry included 900 consecutive transfemoral TAVI patients treated at three high-volume university hospitals between 2017 and 2023: 450 patients underwent closure with the MANTA device and 450 with the ProStyle device. All participating centers transitioned from MANTA to ProStyle as their primary vascular closure strategy during the study period. Each center contributed data on the last 150 consecutive patients treated with MANTA and the first 150 consecutive patients treated after adoption of ProStyle. All patients underwent systematic preprocedural computed tomography–based vascular assessment. The primary endpoint was modified vascular closure device failure, defined as the need for additional intervention to achieve hemostasis, device embolization, or hemodynamically significant stenosis attributable to the VCD. Manual compression and adjunctive Angio-Seal use was not considered VCD failure. Secondary endpoints included VARC-3–defined major and minor vascular access-site complications, VARC-3 bleeding, need for endovascular or surgical bailout, and length of hospital stay. Results Mean age was 79.6 ± 6.3 years; 45.8% were women. The primary endpoint occurred in 7.2% overall and was significantly more frequent with MANTA compared with ProStyle (11.3% vs. 3.1%; p&lt;0.001). Both major (6.4% vs. 3.1%; p=0.018), and minor (8.7% vs. 3.5%; p=0.001) vascular complications were more frequent with MANTA. Endovascular bailout procedures were markedly more common in the MANTA group, including balloon angioplasty (32 vs. 1; p&lt;0.01) and covered stent implantation (10 vs. 0; p&lt;0.01). VARC-3 bleeding—particularly grade 3 bleeding—was also higher with MANTA (18 vs. 5 events). Median length of hospital stay was similar in both groups (3 [2–4] days). Conclusions In this large retrospective multicenter cohort, the ProStyle closure strategy was associated with significantly lower VCD failure rates and fewer major and minor vascular complications compared with MANTA following transfemoral TAVI. These findings suggest that a suture-based closure strategy may provide superior safety for large-bore femoral access management.
title: Prostyle versus MANTA for large-bore femoral closure in transfemoral TAVI: a multicenter comparative study

abstract: Abstract Backround Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) induces a thromboinflammatory response characterized by hypercoagulability and dynamic platelet alterations. The integrated mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely defined. Purpose To comprehensively characterize periprocedural hemostatic and inflammatory changes after TAVR across systemic, cellular, and transcriptomic levels. Methods In this prospective single-center study, patients undergoing TAVR were enrolled between September 2022 and July 2024. Blood samples were obtained on the day of the procedure (T0; prior to valve implantation) and at hospital discharge (T1; median 3.5 days, IQR 2–4 days). At both time points, soluble biomarkers were assessed by routine laboratory testing, cellular phenotype by flow cytometry (FACS), and isolated platelets underwent RNA sequencing. Results Soluble biomarkers were assessed in 102 consecutive TAVR patients, with FACS and transcriptomic analysis in a sub-cohort of 32. TAVR induced a pronounced systemic increase in markers of coagulation and inflammation. The most relevant changes were observed for D-dimers (medianΔ 0.67 mg/L [IQRΔ 0.44–1.07]; p = 0.001), von Willebrand factor activity (medianΔ 87% p &lt; 0.0001), fibrinogen (medianΔ 125 mg/dL; p &lt; 0.0001), Il-6 (medianΔ 19.70 ng/l [IQRΔ 10.80–35.25]; p &lt; 0.0001 and Troponin T medianΔ 43.20 ng/l;p &lt; 0.0001, consistent with acute coagulation and inflammatory activation with myocardial injury. At cellular level, platelet count declined (medianΔ −27 × 10³/µL [−54.5 to −5.5]; p &lt; 0.0001), accompanied by reduced GPIIb/IIIa (ΔgeoMFI −275 a.u.; p &lt; 0.0001) and CD62P expression (ΔgeoMFI −98 a.u.; p =0.003), and increased platelet–neutrophil aggregates (CD42a+CD15+, ΔgeoMFI 377.0 a.u. p = 0.036), reflecting platelet phenotypic alteration and enhanced platelet–immune interaction. At the transcriptomic level, RNA sequencing identified 188 upregulated and 508 downregulated differentially expressed transcripts.Gene set enrichment analysis demonstrated upregulation of platelet activation, aggregation, and hemostasis pathways. Over-representation analysis confirmed enrichment of platelet activation–associated genes, including DMTN, FCER1G, MMRN1, SELP, and FUNDC2. Conclusion TAVR induces a coordinated thromboinflammatory response across systemic, cellular, and transcriptomic levels, characterized by systemic coagulation and inflammatory activation, platelet phenotypic alterations, and transcriptional enrichment of platelet activation pathways. Together, these findings provide mechanistic insight into the acute thromboinflammatory milieu associated with the procedure.Periprocedural changes of systemic parametersFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Periprocedural changes of cell based markersFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Multi-level thromboinflammatory activation after TAVR: systemic, cellular, and platelet transcriptomic changes

abstract: Abstract Background Previous studies have suggested the relative relationship between membranous septum (MS) length and device implantation depth is associated with conduction disturbances following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, no study has evaluated the actual anatomical relationship between the implanted transcatheter valve and the MS using postprocedural imaging modalities, nor its association with new conduction disturbances. Purpose The aim of this study was to determine whether the transcatheter valve position relative to the MS assessed by postprocedural contrast-enhanced cardiac computed tomography (CCT) is associated with the incidence of conduction disturbances. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study included consecutive patients who underwent TAVR at our institution and had postprocedural CCT available between March 2018 and December 2024. A total of 235 patients were analyzed (age 83 ± 5 years; 156 women ［66%］; self-expanding valves in 145 patients ［62%］). The transcatheter valve position relative to the MS was evaluated at the commissural plane between the non-coronary and right-coronary cusps. Patients were classified into the Within-MS group which is the transcatheter valve edge located within the MS region, and the Outside-MS group which is the transcatheter valve position below the MS as shown in Figure. The primary outcome measure was the incidence of new permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) within 1 month following TAVR. Results Valves were positioned within the MS in 167 patients (71%), including 70 balloon-expandable valves (78%) and 97 self-expanding valves (67%) cases. New-onset complete left bundle branch block (LBBB) immediately after TAVR occurred in 87 patients (37.0%). The incidence decreased to 29 patients (12.3%) at 48 hours and only 14 patients (6.0%) had persistent complete LBBB at 1 month. There were no significant differences between the Within-MS (n=167) and the Outside-MS (n=68) groups at any time point. New PPI within 1 month was required in 4 patients (2.4%) in the Within-MS, whereas it was in 7 patients (10.3%) in the Outside-MS groups (P=0.03). Conclusion(s) The current study firstly confirmed that implantation of the transcatheter valve beyond the MS was associated with a significantly higher incidence of new PPI using postprocedural CCT, further supporting the practice of preprocedural assessment of MS length and individualized planning of valve implantation depth for minimizing conduction complications.The valve position relative to the MSFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Is the anatomical relationship between the membranous septum and transcatheter valve truly associated with conduction disturbances after TAVR? a postprocedural CT-based analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter heart valve (THV) underexpansion is associated with hemodynamic valve deterioration. Double-inflation of balloon-expandable valves using the delivery balloon with unchanged volume (double-tap) may improve THV expansion, whilst minimising the risk of complications. Aim To evaluate the efficacy of double-tap after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with SAPIEN-3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR) valves. Methods This observational study included consecutive patients who underwent TAVR for severe native aortic stenosis and had same-volume double-tap. Patients were included from a single high-volume centre from November 2024 to September 2025. We excluded patients with prior TAVR or surgical aortic valve replacement, severe left ventricular outflow tract or annular calcium, or aortic regurgitation as the indication for TAVR. THV expansion and deformation were assessed fluoroscopically before and after double-tap (after appropriate calibration). Expansion (%) = ((Pi x [THV diameter divided by 2]2) divided by nominal THV area) x 100. Deformation index = (area at THV inflow + outflow) divided by (2 x area at narrowest). Thirty-day clinical outcomes were reported. Results Of 113 patients who underwent TAVR with same-volume double-tap (mean age: 79.3±7.3 years, 26.5% female, 13.3% bicuspid anatomy), the median THV expansion before double-tap, at the inflow, mid-portion and outflow was 88.6% (IQR: 86.4-90.4%), 80.1% (IQR: 77.3-82.3%) and 90.1% (IQR: 88.4-90.0%) respectively, and after double-tap increased to 96.4% (IQR: 94.6-98.4%), 90.8% (IQR: 88.6-92.0%) and 97.6% (IQR: 96.2-99.0%) (all P&lt;0.001). The largest increase in expansion following double-tap occurred in the THV mid-portion (median: 10.6% [IQR: 9.9–11.6%]) (Figures). Multivariable predictors of the extent of minimum expansion improvement following double-tap were bicuspid anatomy (median increase with bicuspid vs. tricuspid: 11.7% [IQR: 11.2-12.8%] vs. 10.6% [9.7-11.4%], coefficient 0.27 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.08-0.45] P=0.005) and aortic valve calcium volume &gt;median (385mm3) (median increase with calcium volume &gt;385mm3 vs. &lt;/= 385mm3: 11.1% [IQR: 10.0-12.1%] vs 10.4% [IQR: 9.8-11.2%], coefficient 0.19 [95% CI: 0.00-0.38] P=0.046). Even though pre-dilatation was undertaken in 60% of patients, this did not mitigate the benefit of double tap on THV expansion (median increase in minimum expansion with vs. without pre-dilatation: 11.1% [IQR: 10.0-12.1%] vs. 10.3% [IQR: 9.4-11.0%], coefficient 0.11 [95% CI: -0.09 to 0.30] P=0.278). The median THV deformation index decreased from 1.05 (IQR: 1.04-1.07) to 1.03 (IQR: 1.02-1.04) after double-tap (P&lt;0.001). Thirty-day mortality rate was 0.9%. Conclusion Routine double-tap post-dilatation of balloon-expandable valves appears safe, and improves THV expansion and frame deformation. Bicuspid anatomy and aortic valve calcium burden were associated with the extent of expansion improvement after double-tap.Figure case exampleFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure change in expansionFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Post-dilatation using the balloon-expandable valve delivery balloon with same volume (double-tap) to optimise transcatheter aortic valve expansion

abstract: Abstract Background High-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) improves intraprocedural oxygenation during transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) under conscious sedation. Early results from the HIGH-OXY-TAVR randomized trial suggested improved postoperative renal function, but longterm effects remain uncertain. 1 Purpose To assess one-year changes in renal and cardiac biomarkers and postoperative clinical outcomes following TAVI with HFNO versus standard oxygen therapy. Methods This predefined longitudinal follow-up included all 125 patients enrolled in the single-centre HIGH-OXY-TAVR RCT comparing HFNO (60 L/min, FiO₂ 60%) with low-flow oxygen (5 L/min) during TAVI. Serum creatinine, glomerular filtration rate (GFR), and NT-proBNP were evaluated at baseline, 1 month, and 1 year. Clinical outcomes included allcause mortality, stroke, heart failure rehospitalisation, acute kidney injury (AKI) defined according to VARC-2, and a composite major adverse events (MAE) endpoint. Results One year follow-up was complete for all patients (HFNO n=64; control n=61). Decline in GFR was significantly attenuated with HFNO at 1 month (−0.53 vs −3.93 mL/min/1.73m2 ; p&lt;0.05) and 1 year (−1.0 vs −4.9 mL/min/1.73m2; p&lt;0.05). Similarly, the median increase in serum creatinine was significantly lower with HFNO at 1 month [0.01 mg/dL (IQR −0.12 to 0.08) vs 0.09 mg/dL (IQR −0.05 to 0.21); p&lt;0.05] and at 1 year [0.02 mg/dL (IQR −0.10 to 0.12) vs 0.095 mg/dL (IQR 0.02 to 0.22); p&lt;0.05]. AKI incidence was lower with HFNO at 1 month (0% vs 14.8%; p&lt;0.05) and numerically reduced at 1 year (7.8% vs 19.7%; p=0.053). NT-proBNP evolution was similar between groups. MAE occurred less frequently with HFNO at 1 month (7.8% vs 19.7%; p=0.053) and was significantly lower at 1 year (26.5% vs 44.3%; p&lt;0.05). See table 1 Conclusions During TAVI under sedation, HFNO was associated with sustained renal function preservation and a consistent reduction in clinically relevant complications, reaching significance for the composite endpoint at one year. These findings support a potential role for optimised periprocedural oxygenation in longterm organ protection and warrant validation in larger multicentre trials.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: High-flow nasal oxygen during transcatheter aortic valve implantation under sedation: one-year follow-up of the HIGH-OXY-TAVR randomised controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal valve size selection for balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valves (BEVs) in borderline annulus cases remains uncertain. We hypothesized that self-expanding valves (SEVs) may provide more favorable hemodynamic and clinical outcomes in patients with borderline annulus dimensions for BEV sizing. This study aimed to compare the hemodynamic performance and clinical outcomes of BEVs and SEVs in this population. Methods From the multicenter TAVI registry, we analyzed patients who underwent TAVI between 2010 and 2025 (n = 5,797). Borderline annulus for BEVs was defined as an estimated BEV oversizing rate ≤–5% or ≥30%. Propensity score matching was performed between BEV and SEV cohorts, adjusting for age, sex, body surface area, annulus area, annulus perimeter, and STS score. Outcomes were compared between the BEV group (SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA, S3UR) and the SEV group (Evolut Pro/Pro+/FX/FX+). Results Among eligible patients, 964 (36.4%) met the borderline criteria and were treated with either BEV (41.1%) or SEV (58.8%). Mean age was 84 years, and 40% were male. At baseline, the SEV group had a smaller pre-procedural aortic valve area and higher mean gradient, suggesting more advanced disease severity. Device success (90.7% vs. 83.7%, p = 0.008) and early safety (94.9% vs. 89.2%, p=0.012) were significantly higher in the BEV group (figure). Post-procedural mean pressure gradient was significantly lower in the SEV group (8.8 vs. 7.3 mmHg, &lt;0.001), whereas ≥mild paravalvular leak was more frequent. Permanent pacemaker implantation was also more common in the SEV group (1.9% vs. 5.4%, p=0.016). Rates of vascular complications, bleeding, and annular rupture were comparable between groups. Two-year mortality and heart failure hospitalization were similar (17.0% vs. 16.8%, log-rank p = 0.37). In the small annulus subgroup (annulus area 312–345 mm²), the SEV group demonstrated a lower incidence of mean gradient ≥20 mmHg (3.1% vs. 9.9%, p=0.007) and Vmax ≥3.0 m/s (3.6% vs. 10.6%, p=0.009), with a trend toward higher device success (92.3% vs. 86.6%, p=0.10). Conclusions In patients with borderline annulus dimensions for BEV sizing, SEVs were associated with superior hemodynamic performance but higher rates of paravalvular leak and pacemaker implantation, without differences in mid-term clinical outcomes. Selection bias due to preferential use of SEVs in anatomically or clinically more complex cases may have influenced these findings.Study flowchartFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure2For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of self-expanding valve selection on hemodynamics and clinical outcomes in patients with borderline annular dimensions for balloon-expandable valve: insights from the multicenter-TAVI registry

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction The incidence and hemodynamic impact of hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) in new-generation transcatheter heart valves (THVs) have not been fully elucidated. Purposes The purpose of this study is to investigate the hemodynamic impact of HALT. Methods We enrolled 306 cases of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) performed between July 2023 and October 2025. Balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) included Sapien3 Ultra RESILIA, while self-expanding valves (SEVs) included Evolut FX, Evolut FX+, and Navitor. A total of 212 patients with both one-month follow-up computed tomography and echocardiography were analyzed. Results BEV and SEV were implanted in 106 patients each. The incidence of HALT was significantly lower in the BEV group compared with the SEV group (21% vs. 36%, p=0.01). In the SEV group, the presence of HALT did not significantly affect the mean transprosthetic pressure gradient (PG) (8.5 mmHg vs. 8.8 mmHg, p=0.65). In contrast, HALT was associated with a significantly higher mean PG in the BEV group (12.5 mmHg vs. 9.8 mmHg, p=0.02). Notably, this effect was evident only in patients receiving 20mm (25.7 mmHg vs. 14.8 mmHg, p=0.053) and 23mm BEVs (11.9 mmHg vs. 9.8mmHg, p=0.044). Conclusion Among new-generation THVs, HALT was less frequent in BEVs compared with SEVs. However, HALT at one month after TAVI was associated with an increased mean PG in BEVs, particularly in smaller THVs.
title: Early hemodynamic impact of hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in new-generation transcatheter heart valves

abstract: Abstract Background A comprehensive understanding of the incidence, mechanisms, and clinical consequences of bioprosthetic valve dysfunction after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is increasingly needed given the expansion of indications toward younger and lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy. The Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 (VARC-3) has introduced the concept of bioprosthetic valve failure (BVF) as a patient-oriented clinical endpoint that integrates the downstream consequences of bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, irrespective of its underlying mechanism. However, data on the long-term incidence and clinical impact of BVF after TAVR remain limited. Purpose To assess the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of BVF following TAVR. Methods We analyzed the data of an international, multicenter registry including patients undergoing TAVR at 13 centers. The primary outcome was BVF according to VARC-3 criteria. The cumulative incidence of BVF was estimated using a competing risk approach. The association between BVF and clinical outcomes was assessed using multivariable Cox models with BVF as a time-dependent covariate. Results Among 7,501 patients, BVF occurred in 380 patients (5.1%) over a median follow-up of 4 (IQR 2-5) years. The cumulative incidence of BVF increased over time, reaching 1.4% at 1 year, 4.5% at 5 years, and 8.0% at 10 years. Independent predictors of BVF included younger age, balloon-expandable valve, prosthesis size &lt;26 mm, valve-in-valve procedure, mean gradient at discharge ≥15 mmHg, moderate or severe AR at discharge, and early hemodynamic valve deterioration (Table 1). BVF was independently associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.72 [95% CI, 1.48-2.01], p&lt;0.001), cardiovascular mortality (aHR 2.68 [95% CI, 2.15-3.34], p&lt;0.001), stroke (aHR 1.88 [95% CI, 1.12-3.14], p=0.016) and heart failure hospitalization (aHR 1.74 [95% CI, 1.20-2.51], p=0.003) (Figure 1). Consistent findings were observed in different sensitivity analyses. Conclusions In this study, the 10-year cumulative incidence of BVF following TAVR was 8.0%. BVF was associated with adverse clinical outcomes during follow-up, including increased risks of death, stroke and heart failure hospitalization. These findings underscore that BVF is not merely a structural or hemodynamic endpoint, but a clinically meaningful event with important implications for patient prognosis. These results support the implementation of tailored surveillance and preventive strategies to mitigate BVF-related risk.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

appraisal.design_and_n: International multicentre registry of 13 centres; 7,501 patients undergoing TAVR; competing-risk cumulative incidence and time-dependent Cox models.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with echocardiographic surveillance that differed between centres and few patients followed to 10 years.
appraisal.one_line: Bioprosthetic valve failure by VARC-3 criteria occurred in 5.1% of TAVR patients and was associated with higher mortality, stroke and heart failure hospitalisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BVF occurred in 380 patients (5.1%) over a median follow-up of 4 (IQR 2-5) years. The cumulative incidence of BVF increased over time, reaching 1.4% at 1 year, 4.5% at 5 years, and 8.0% at 10 years. BVF was associated with all-cause mortality (aHR 1.72 [95% CI, 1.48-2.01]), cardiovascular mortality (aHR 2.68 [95% CI, 2.15-3.34]), stroke (aHR 1.88 [95% CI, 1.12-3.14]) and heart failure hospitalization (aHR 1.74 [95% CI, 1.20-2.51]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides a large patient-oriented durability estimate and predictors (younger age, balloon-expandable valve, small prosthesis, valve-in-valve) relevant to lifetime management planning.

title: Bioprosthetic valve failure after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Coronary obstruction (CO) is an uncommon but critical complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). In anatomically high-risk patients, two commonly used preventive approaches are coronary stent-based protection via chimney stenting, and leaflet modification via Bioprosthetic or Native Aortic Scallop Intentional Laceration to Prevent Iatrogenic Coronary Artery Obstruction (BASILICA). Contemporary observational data comparing these strategies remains inconsistent. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to consolidate the existing evidence, comparing outcomes between BASILICA and chimney stenting in high-risk TAVI. Methods This study was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched until February 20, 2026 for all studies enrolling TAVI patients undergoing preventive BASILICA or chimney stenting. Technical success was defined as procedure completion without clinically significant ostial CO. The primary endpoint was early all-cause mortality (in-hospital and at 30 days). The secondary outcome was the composite 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or unplanned target lesion revascularisation. Odds ratios (OR) were pooled using a random-effects model. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses explored heterogeneity. Results A total of 13 studies were included (424 patients undergoing BASILICA and 389 chimney stenting). Patients undergoing BASILICA had higher baseline preprocedural risk of CO, as indicated by smaller sinus of Valsalva height (14.9 ± 3.1 mm vs 19.3 ± 3.0 mm ; P &lt; 0.001) and diameter (26.7 ± 3.0 mm vs 28.0 ± 5.1 mm ; P &lt; 0.001), smaller left main coronary height (7.1 ± 2.3 mm vs 9.2 ± 3.9 mm ; P &lt; 0.001), more valve-in-valve procedures (277/356 (77.8%) vs 142/249 (57.0%), p&lt;0.001) and shorter virtual transcatheter distance (3.6 ± 1.0 mm vs 4.0 ± 1.9 mm ; P &lt; 0.001). Technical success was 97.4% and 87.9% in chimney and BASILICA groups, respectively (p &lt; 0.001). Planned BASILICA was converted to bailout coronary stenting in 20/424 (4.7%) of cases. In the pooled analysis, there was no statistically significant difference in MACE at 1-year between the chimney and BASILICA strategies (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.42–2.01), despite a trend towards increased early all-cause mortality (8.3% vs 4.8%, p = 0.07), major bleeding (9.3% vs 6.3%, p = 0.56), paravalvular leak and acute kidney injury (8.2% vs 4.9%, p = 0.36) in the chimney group. Conclusion Chimney stenting and BASILICA demonstrate comparable 1-year efficacy in preventing clinically significant CO in high-risk TAVI. Despite trend towards increased mortality, AKI and paravalvular leak in the chimney stenting group, there was insufficient evidence to demonstrate superiority of either strategy. Procedural risk profile, operator expertise, and long-term coronary access considerations may guide selection.30-Day Mortality: BASILICA vs ChimneyFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Chimney Stenting versus BASILICA for prevention of coronary obstruction in high-risk transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in patients with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and severe aortic stenosis remain uncertain, largely because this population was excluded from major clinical trials. Purpose This meta-analysis aims to compare major clinical outcomes of TAVI in BAV and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients. Methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases to identify relevant studies. Our primary endpoints were 30-day and one year all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included 30-day Stroke, major or life-threatening bleeding events, periprocedural vascular complications, and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM) up to 30 days, as well as aortic root injury, conversion to cardiac surgery, coronary obstruction, paravalvular leakage (pvl), and prosthesis-patient mismatch. Statistical analysis included Risk Ratio (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) using the random-effects model (Mantel-Haenszel). Results A total of 38 studies, involving 219,071 patients, were included in the meta-analysis. There was no significant difference regarding 30-day Mortality (Risk Ratio (RR): 1.34, 95% Confidence Intervals (CI): 0.88-2.04) and one-year mortality (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.73-1.00) were similar between the two groups. However, the risk of 30-day stroke (RR: 1.35, 95% CI: 1.10-1.43), conversion to cardiac surgery (RR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.12-1.87), and pvl (RR: 1.37, 95% CI: 1.22-1.53) were higher in the BAV group compared with TAV group. No differences were observed in the remaining secondary endpoints. Conclusion TAVI in BAV demonstrates acceptable short-term safety compared with TAV. However, the incidence of certain procedural complications is higher in BAV patients than in those with TAV and should be considered during the decision-making process. Further randomized studies are required to establish long-term clinical outcomes and durability.figure 1 For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Clinical outcomes of TAVI in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valve anatomy: an updated meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Echocardiography at discharge frequently estimates higher transvalvular mean pressure gradients (MG) compared to intraoperative invasive measurements following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). This discordance is incompletely understood and may lead to misinterpretation of valve performance and unwarranted invasive procedures and re-interventions. Purpose To assess the extent of discordance between invasive intraoperative pressure gradients and echocardiography-derived pressure gradients. Furthermore, to test the hypothesis that procedural interventions such as conscious sedation and rapid pacing may reduce transvalvular flow during the TAVI-procedure and hence explain the discordance. Methods In this prospective study, 34 patients underwent simultaneous invasive and transthoracic echocardiographic pressure gradient measurements. Assessment of simultaneous gradients was performed immediately after TAVI, both at baseline and during pharmacologically increased flow using dobutamine. Echocardiography was repeated the following day (discharge). Results Echocardiographic MG at discharge was significantly higher than invasive MG measured immediately post-TAVI (12 ± 4 mmHg vs. 4 ± 3 mmHg, p &lt; 0.001; mean difference 8 ± 5 mmHg). In contrast, simultaneous measurements immediately post-TAVI reduced, but did not eliminate the discordance (mean difference 3 ± 4 mmHg, p &lt; 0.001). Dobutamine infusion increased both echocardiographic and invasive MG (8 ± 5 to 13 ± 4 mmHg and 4 ± 3 to 8 ± 5 mmHg, respectively, both p &lt; 0.001). Echocardiographic MG was similar during dobutamine infusion and at discharge (13 ± 4 vs. 12 ± 4, p = 0.24). A representative patient example is shown in the Figure. Conclusion Echocardiography systematically overestimates transvalvular mean pressure gradients compared with invasive measurements after TAVI, but simultaneous assessment substantially reduced the discordance. This may be explained by differences in transvalvular flow.FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Towards understanding the discordance between invasive and echocardiographic pressure gradients after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction New-onset conduction disturbance (CD) is a common complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Recently, basal septal bulge (BSB) has been reported as a predictor of new-onset CD. However, the impact of BSB on new-onset CD according to the position of deployed valve remains unclear. Purpose This study investigated the impact of BSB on new-onset CD after TAVR according to the implantation depth (ID) relative to membranous septum (MS) length. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 2375 patients who underwent TAVR. New-onset CD was defined as 30-day new permanent pacemaker implantation or new left bundle branch block lasting until discharge. The study endpoints were the predictors of new-onset CD and the impact of BSB on new-onset CD. Results The incidence of new-onset CD was 14.2%. Multivariate analysis showed that complete right bundle branch block (OR: 1.85; 95% CI: 1.36–2.51), MS length &lt;2 mm (OR: 1.48; 95% CI: 1.17–1.87), and BSB ≥3 mm (OR: 1.30; 95% CI: 1.03–1.64) were independent baseline predictors of new-onset CD. Use of self-expanding valve (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 1.26–2.16), ID &gt;MS length (OR: 2.57; 95% CI: 1.97–3.35), and post-dilatation (OR: 1.61; 95% CI: 1.03–2.53) were the independent procedural predictors. In the group of ID &gt;MS length, BSB ≥3 mm was the significant predictor of new-onset CD (OR: 1.38; 95% CI: 1.04–1.82). Conclusions BSB was significantly associated with new-onset CD especially in the group of low deployment. These findings might be beneficial for peri-procedural management and TAVR strategy.
title: Impact of basal septal bulge on conduction disturbance relative to valve position after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Introduction Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a proven effective treatment for severe aortic valve disease in inoperable patients. In those patients, concurrent mitral regurgitation (MR) remains common. Although MR improvement following TAVI is expected, the timeframe, predictors, and potential clinical implications remain unclear. Purpose To evaluate changes in MR severity post-TAVI at pre-defined timepoints, determine potential predictive factors and assess the impact on all-cause mortality. Methods A registry of consecutive patients (n=924) undergoing successful TAVI at a tertiary cardiac centre between 2020 and 2024 was retrospectively reviewed to identify those with pre-existing MR. MR severity was assessed by BSE-accredited practitioners using transthoracic echocardiography and a multimetric semi-quantitative approach, categorised as none, mild, moderate, or severe. Data was analysed at baseline, immediately post-TAVI, and at 3-6 months follow-up. MR severity changes were analysed using paired non-parametric testing while univariable comparative statistics was used to assess MR improvement predictors and mortality impact. Results 124 patients were included with baseline MR - mild in 16.3%(n=20), moderate in 67.4%(n=84) and severe in 16.3%(n=20). Mean age was 81.2±8.0 years, 59 were male(47.7%) and 65 female(52.4%). Self-expanding prosthesis was used in 45%(n=56) and balloon-expandable in 55%(n=68). Post-procedural echocardiographic data was available for 120 patients (96.8%) immediately post-TAVI and 83 patients (66.9%) at follow-up. MR improved by at least one grade in 45% (n=54) (p&lt;0.05) immediately post-TAVI and in 71.1% (n=59) (p&lt;0.05) at outpatient follow-up. Where MR severity remained static immediately post-TAVI, a delayed improvement was noted at outpatient echocardiography in 26.6%. Immediately post-TAVI, female gender was significantly correlated with MR improvement (54.0% vs 35.1%; Fisher's exact p=0.045). MR severity changes were independent of operator(p=0.711), valve platform(p=0.133) and size(p=0.698) used, MR aetiology(p=0.672), baseline tricuspid regurgitation (TR) severity (p=0.801) or LV function (p=0.738). At outpatient follow-up, there was no baseline or procedural variables significantly associated with MR improvement (all p&gt;0.05). This was also independent of TAVI indication and baseline moderate or severe AR at both timepoints (p=0.223 and p=0.214). We have observed, however, a non-significant trend towards higher late MR improvement with increasing baseline TR severity (linear-by-linear association p=0.072). Mortality was lower among patients with MR improvement(death OR 0.37, 95% CI 0.15–0.94; p=0.036). Conclusion Baseline MR severity significantly improved following TAVI, both immediately and at outpatient follow-up. Female sex predicted early improvement, while no predictors of late improvement were identified. MR improvement was associated with reduced all-cause mortality.Predictors of MR improvement post TAVIFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation effects on pre-existing mitral regurgitation: improvement timing, predictive factors and mortality impact

abstract: Abstract Background Although transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) effectively relieves valvular obstruction, clinical outcomes remain heterogeneous. The prognostic role of early physiologic recovery and integrated post-procedural remodeling remains incompletely defined. Objectives To characterize temporal changes in myocardial mechanics after TAVR and determine whether early remodeling parameters independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods In 150 patients undergoing TAVR, speckle-tracking echocardiography was performed at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months to assess left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr). The prognostic cohort with complete clinical and imaging data at 6 months. Ventriculo-arterial coupling (VAC) was calculated non-invasively using echocardiographic volumes as the ratio of end-systolic volume to stroke volume (ESV/SV), reflecting ventricular–vascular interaction. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to identify independent predictors of MACE, incorporating electrical substrate, residual afterload, myocardial recovery, and atrial reverse remodeling. Results The mean age was 80 ± 5 years, 54% were male, 12% had atrial fibrillation, and 68% had coronary artery disease. During a median follow-up of 3 years, 30 patients experienced MACE. Significant structural reverse remodeling occurred within 6 months, with left atrial volume index decreasing from 48 to 42 mL/m² (p &lt; 0.001) and left ventricular mass index decreasing from 149 to 134 g/m² (p = 0.002). Both atrial and ventricular mechanics improved significantly after TAVR. LASr increased at 3 months (+1.92%, p = 0.031), 6 months (+4.44%, p &lt; 0.001), and 12 months (+2.96%, p = 0.001). LVGLS improved at 3 months (+2.32%, p &lt; 0.001), 6 months (+3.04%, p &lt; 0.001), and 12 months (+3.28%, p &lt; 0.001), with most recovery occurring within 6 months and subsequent plateau. Independent predictors of MACE included atrial fibrillation (HR 3.76, p = 0.0021), higher post-procedural VAC (HR 1.89, p = 0.0055), impaired LVGLS at 6 months (HR 0.84 per unit improvement, p = 0.0029), and absence of ≥10% reduction in left atrial volume (HR 2.69, p = 0.012). Conclusions Myocardial recovery after TAVR follows a time-dependent trajectory characterized by early structural and functional improvement with plateau after six months. Long-term outcomes are determined not only by procedural success but also by early physiologic recovery integrating electrical substrate, ventricular–vascular interaction, myocardial mechanics, and atrial reverse remodeling. Early remodeling parameters may improve post-TAVR risk stratification and guide individualized follow-up strategies.Remodeling GraphicFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Integrated remodeling dynamics and early physiologic recovery predict outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Up to 20% of transcatheter aortic valve implantations (TAVIs) are followed by post-procedural conduction disturbances. As next-day discharge is becoming standard of care, predictors of permanent high-degree conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation (PPMI) are of increasing clinical relevance. Purpose This study was set out to study ECG characteristics associated with post-discharge PPMI. Post-TAVI, pre-discharge ECGs were compared between patients subjected to PPMI before and after TAVI-discharge, and patients not subjected to PPMI. Methods The target population was patients undergoing TAVI without pre-existing PPM. All patients undergoing TAVI from 4th of Nov. 2016 through 28th of April 2023 in Eastern Denmark, were retrospectively included. Patients with prior aortic valve replacement were excluded. To characterise patients requiring PPMI after TAVI-discharge, post-TAVI, pre-discharge ECGs were identified and considered abnormal if heart rate &lt; 50 (bradycardia), PR-interval &gt; 240 ms (AV-block), or QRS-duration &gt; 120 ms (BBB). BBB configuration was further described as LBBB, RBBB, or unspecified. Next, patients were classified according to timing of PPMI. “Late” included patients subjected to PPMI within 1 to 30 days after TAVI-discharge. “Early” and “None” included patients subjected to PPMI before TAVI-discharge and patients not requiring PPMI within the first 30 days after TAVI-discharge, respectively. The association between post-TAVI ECG abnormality and patient classification was assessed by means of a χ2-test. Significance level was set to 0,05. Results A total of 2055 patients (57,3% males) were included. Mean age at TAVI was 79,3 years. We identified 217 patients (11,0%) and 28 patients (1,4%) classified as “Early” and “Late”, respectively. Among patients classified as “Late”, 46,4% (n = 13) had an abnormal ECG with the most prevalent ECG abnormality being BBB. It was identified in 92,3% of patients with an abnormal ECG (n = 12). LBBB was the most common configuration and was observed in 50% of patients with BBB (n = 6). RBBB was observed in 2 patients (16,7%), whereas the BBB configuration was unspecified in 4 patients (33,3%). Bradycardia and AV-block were equally prevalent among patients classified as “Late” with prevalences of 7,1% (n = 2). For patients classified as “Early” and “None”, prevalences of abnormal ECGs were 55,1% (n = 114) and 33,1% (n = 583), respectively (Figure 1). Patients classified as "Late" were more likely to have an abnormal post-TAVI, pre-discharge ECG compared to patients classified as “Early” and less likely in comparison to patients classified as “None” (p-value &lt; 0,001). Conclusion In this study of 2055 patients subjected to TAVI between years 2016 and 2023, the incidence of PPMI within 1 to 30 days after TAVI discharge was 1,4%. Roughly half of these patients had an abnormal ECG at discharge with BBB being the most prevalent abnormality.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation and need for post-discharge pacemaker implantation in the modern era of fast discharge

abstract: Abstract Background Relief of symptoms is a key goal of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe, symptomatic aortic stenosis. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) are at higher risk of residual symptoms after TAVI, but whether the myocardial response after TAVI is associated with symptomatic relief remains unclear. We hypothesized that symptomatic relief relates to improvement in cardiac structure and function. Purpose To determine whether symptomatic response measured by New York Heart Association (NYHA) class is associated with longitudinal changes in echocardiographic measures. In patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥ 50%), we evaluated whether HFpEF is associated with an unfavourable echocardiographic response post-TAVI. Methods TAVI patients underwent NYHA assessment at baseline and at 30 days. Symptomatic relief was defined as NYHA class I at 30 days. Echocardiograms at baseline, before discharge and beyond 3 months post-TAVI were collected and analysed using an automated, validated, deep-learning workflow (Us2.ai, Singapore). HFpEF was defined as an H2FPEF score ≥ 6. Trajectories of echocardiographic parameters over time were modelled using linear mixed-effects models using a spline term for time to allow for non-linear trajectories. Differences were compared at 1 month before TAVI, and 6 and 12 months after TAVI using contrast analysis. Results Among 1,334 patients undergoing TAVI (median age 81 years [IQR: 76 – 84 years], 51% women), 933 (70%) achieved symptomatic relief at 30 days. Patients with persistent symptoms had lower peak aortic jet velocity before TAVI (3.86 vs. 4.08 m/s, p &lt; 0.001). Symptomatic relief was significantly associated with improvement in left ventricular (LV) systolic function, measured by LVEF and global longitudinal strain (-16.0% in NYHA I vs. -14.9% in NYHA II-IV at 12 months, p = 0.017; Figure). In addition, improvement in RV systolic function (TAPSE) was associated with symptomatic relief. In contrast, change in diastolic function was not associated with symptomatic response. Also, no differences were observed in the hemodynamic effect of TAVI on the aortic valve parameters. Patients with persistent symptoms had higher NT-proBNP levels at 6 and 12 months post-TAVI. In patients with preserved LVEF (n = 707), 18% (n = 125) had HFpEF. Despite similar LVEF at baseline, patients with HFpEF had significantly worse LV systolic function post-TAVI. Conclusion In patients undergoing TAVI, symptomatic relief is associated with improvement in LV and RV systolic function. Persistent dyspnoea may be related to underlying HFpEF, which was also associated with worse LV systolic function post-TAVI. Trials targeting HFpEF therapy post-TAVI are warranted.Trajectories by symptomatic responseFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Trajectories by HFpEF vs. no HFpEFFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Relief of dyspnoea after TAVI is associated with improvement in left ventricular systolic function

abstract: Abstract Introduction Ventriculo–arterial coupling (VAC) reflects the interaction between left ventricular (LV) contractility and afterload and can be non-invasively estimated as the ratio of arterial elastance (Ea) to LV end-systolic elastance (Ees). In aortic stenosis (AS) elevated VAC at discharge after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has been linked to adverse midterm outcomes. Data regarding factors related to an increased VAC in patients with structural heart disease interventions are still scarce. Purpose To evaluate the correlates of post-procedural VAC and its relationship with functional status improvement after TAVI. Methods We enrolled 250 patients with severe AS who underwent TAVI between 2017 and 2024 (76.2±7.1 years, 54.8%men), evaluated right before and one month post-procedure. Comprehensive echocardiography included LV myocardial work (MW) parameters: Global Work Index (GWI), Global Constructive Work (GCW), Global Wasted Work (GWW), and Global Work Efficiency (GWE). Ea and Ees were calculated as ESP/SV and ESP/ESV, respectively (ESP-end-systolic pressure; SV-stroke volume; ESV-end-systolic volume). Results Indexed LV mass decreased after TAVI (147.9±38.4 vs 167.4±46.4 g/m², p&lt;0.001), accompanied by improved systolic function, with higher LVEF (55.2±9.4 vs 51.4±11.8%, p&lt;0.001) and better GLS (-14.3±3.7 vs -12.5±4.1%, p&lt;0.001). MW parameters changed significantly after TAVI, with lower GWI (1622.1±464 vs 1828.8±686.1 mmHg%, p=0.003) and GWW (214.5±159.7 vs 251.2±122 mmHg, p=0.01), while GWE increased (89.7±5.8 vs 88.6±5.9%, p=0.06). Patients with patient–prosthesis mismatch had higher VAC compared with those without mismatch (0.81±0.61 vs 0.48±0.32, p&lt;0.001). Similarly, patients with persistent NYHA III–IV symptoms exhibited higher post-TAVI VAC than those with functional improvement (0.76±0.66 vs 0.49±0.29, p=0.03).On univariate analysis, post-TAVI VAC correlated inversely with age, baseline LV functional and MW parameters (GWI,GCW,GWE,LVEF) and with post-procedural indexed aortic valve area and decrease of mean transvalvular gradient. Positive associations were found with baseline indexed LV mass, indexed LA volume and E/e′. In multivariable analysis, age (β −0.36, p&lt;0.001), GWI (β −0.27, p 0.03), and decrease of mean transvalvular gradient (β −0.29, p 0.01) were independent correlates of post-procedural VAC. Conclusions Higher post-TAVI VAC values were associated with persistent NYHA class III–IV symptoms, suggesting that Ea/Ees index may identify patients with incomplete functional recovery. By contrast, lower VAC values were associated with better LV systolic performance, larger effective valve area and greater gradient reduction, suggesting that optimized valve hemodynamics translate into more favorable ventriculo–arterial interaction and improved energetic efficiency. These findings support the potential role of VAC as an integrated marker of both mechanical and clinical response after TAVI.
title: Ventriculo–arterial coupling after TAVI: a mechanistic link between residual hemodynamic burden and persistent symptoms

abstract: Abstract Introduction GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1a) are a novel class of cardiometabolic drugs that have been shown to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiovascular mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes, overweight, or obesity. Improved outcomes have also been reported in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) treated with the SGLT2 inhibitor dapagliflozin in the recent DAPA-TAVI trial. Whether GLP-1a could provide similar benefits in patients with valvular heart disease, such as aortic stenosis, remains unknown. Methods We retrospectively analyzed TAVI patients enrolled in the monocentric MOTIVE registry at a hospital, between 2015 and 2025. Patients were stratified according to whether they were prescribed GLP-1a at discharge. Outcomes were compared between groups using both propensity score matching (PSM) and inverse probability weighting (IPW). Cox regression was applied to assess the following endpoints: the composite of all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), all-cause death, cardiovascular death, HHF, and stroke. Results A total of 803 TAVI patients were included, of whom 45 (5.6%) received GLP-1a at discharge. The mean age was 81.1 ± 6.2 years, with a slight female predominance (403, 50.2%). Mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 56.5 ± 11.3%, and mean transvalvular gradient was 42.1 ± 12.3 mmHg. A self-expandable valve was implanted in 509 patients (63.4%), most commonly the Evolut R/PRO/PRO+ (362, 45.0%). Baseline, echocardiographic, and procedural characteristics were balanced between groups, except for diabetes, which was markedly more prevalent in the GLP-1a group (43/45, 95.5%). After a median follow-up of 363.5 days (IQR 224–592), in the IPW-adjusted cohort, GLP-1a prescription at discharge was associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint of all-cause death or HHF (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17–0.68, p = 0.01), primarily driven by a reduction in HHF (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.15–0.56, p = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or stroke during long-term follow-up. Conclusions In this contemporary cohort of TAVI patients, GLP-1a prescription at discharge was associated with a marked reduction in the composite of all-cause death and HHF, mainly due to fewer heart failure hospitalizations. Given the observational and monocentric nature of this study, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger multicenter registries and randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these preliminary results.
