title: Role of GLP1a drugs after TAVI: insights from the MOTIVE registry

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) with third generation devices has become the standard of care for many patients with severe aortic stenosis. Stroke is a non-negligible complication after TAVI that may affect post-procedural and long-term outcomes, leading to disability. However, comparative data on neurological outcomes across different transcatheter heart valve (THV) models are limited. Methods A Network Meta Analysis was performed including all randomized controlled trials comparing third-generation THV, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) and clinical surveillance, with available data on neurological outcomes. The primary endpoint was stroke; major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were the secondary ones. Results A total of seven randomized trials encompassing 5,232 patients were analysed. The mean age of the study population was 80.2 years, with a slight prevalence (54%) of females. Hypertension (84.8%), dyslipidemia (63.1%), and coronary artery disease (47%) were the most prevalent comorbidities. Procedural success was achieved in 96.6% of cases, with transfemoral access used in 95%. The majority of patients received the Edwards Sapien bioprosthetic valve (40.2%), followed by Evolut R/PRO (20.7%), Acurate NEO (14.7%), and Portico (7.1%). A small subset of patients (8.7%) underwent SAVR, while 446 patients (8.6%) received clinical surveillance alone. No significant differences in the risk of stroke or MACCE were observed across the different THV types (stroke incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.56, 95% CI 0.21–1.52; MACCE IRR 0.59, 95% CI 0.30–1.17). In contrast, clinical surveillance was associated with significantly worse outcomes for both endpoints, while SAVR was linked to an increased risk of MACCE and showed a non-significant trend toward higher stroke rates. At SUCRA analysis, PORTICO valve resulted the device with the highest probability of preventing strokes. A Sensitivity analysis restricted to THV comparisons confirmed the absence of between-device differences. Conclusions In this comprehensive network meta-analysis encompassing different strategies of severe aortic stenosis management no device demonstrated superiority in reducing the risk of stroke or MACCE. Among THV models, PORTICO was the highest ranking in terms of stroke prevention. Conversely, both conservative management and SAVR were associated with less favorable outcomes compared to TAVI.
title: Incidence of stroke after severe aortic stenosis treatment: a network meta-analysis comparing several strategies of intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement (VIV TAVR) for failed tissue valves in high risk patients can lead to suboptimal expansion in smaller valves with reported one year mortality up to 25% [1]. Bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) which uses high-pressure balloon inflation to fracture the surgical valve ring is used to allow for further expansion [2]. Whilst early data suggests improved haemodynamics, concerns have been raised regarding efficacy and safety outcomes. Aim This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesise short and long term haemodynamic and safety outcomes following BVF in comparison to non-BVF. A rigorous synthesis was warranted to inform procedural planning and guidelines. Methods A comprehensive systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL). The primary haemodynamic endpoints were short and long-term mean transvalvular gradient and aortic valve area. The primary safety endpoints were 30 day and 1 year all cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular mortality, stroke, new pacemaker implantation, major bleeding and annular rupture. Adjusted comparative effect estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Results The search identified 499 studies with 16 studies meeting inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis revealed significant heterogeneity (I² = 63.84%) but demonstrated a reduction in the short term and a sustained reduction in the long term for mean gradient. The short-term pooled mean gradient was 29.12 (95% CI: 26.45-31.78) with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 63.84%), whilst the non-BVF cohort had a smaller reduction of 20.51 (95% CI: 19.24-21.78; I² = 52%). In the long term, the reduction in mean gradient was 26.49 (95% CI: 21.19-28.78). In the short term, the pooled mean difference in aortic valve area (AVA) was 0.59 (95% CI: 0.28–0.90; I² = 96.1%), while the non-BVF cohort had a similar change of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.50–0.63; I² = 79%). In this meta-analysis, the pooled incidence of 30-day all-cause mortality was 3% (95% CI 2%–4%) compared to 2.38% (95% CI 2%-3%) in the non-BVF cohort and 1 year mortality was 8% (95% CI 5-14%). Secondary outcomes included a pooled incidence of cardiovascular mortality 1% (95% CI 1-3%), stroke was 1% (95% CI 1%-3%), new pacemaker implantation was 2% (95% CI 2%-4%), major bleeding 3% (95% CI 2%-5%), annular rupture 1% (95% CI 1%-3%), with no observed heterogeneity across studies for any outcome (all I² = 0%, p = 1.00). Conclusion This study demonstrates that BVF significantly reduces transvalvular gradients and improves aortic valve area, with sustained haemodynamic benefit at longer-term follow-up. These findings support BVF as an effective adjunct to optimise valve expansion, with clinical outcomes suggesting an acceptable safety profile in appropriately selected patients.Mean gradient outcomes with BVF in short termFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.AVA outcomes with BVF in short termFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Haemodynamic and safety outcomes of bioprosthetic valve fracture in VIV-TAVI: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Few prospective studies have explored the long-term prognostic value and warranty period of functional imaging in patients with stable chest pain. The CE-MARC trial recruited 752 patients with suspected angina and demonstrated the high diagnostic accuracy of stress CMR against SPECT against a reference of invasive coronary angiography. Objectives To assess the comparative long-term prognostic value of stress CMR and SPECT and to establish operational warranty periods for normal test results. Methods Participants in CE-MARC were followed up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and unplanned coronary revascularization. The warranty period identified the time interval where patients with a normal test result remained 97.5% free of MACE. Multivariable regression analysis identified key warranty period modifiers. Results Of 752 recruited patients, 652(86.9%) with CMR and SPECT with follow-up available formed the study cohort. At 15.5 years (IQR12.4–16.6), 40(6.1%) cardiovascular deaths occurred, 29(4.4%) patients experienced a myocardial infarction and 47(7.2%) unplanned revascularization. After adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, an abnormal CMR remained a strong independent MACE predictor (HR 2.74,_95%CI 1.70–4.42,p&lt;0.001). Patients with a normal test result had a warranty period of 6.8 years for stress CMR and 5.1 years for SPECT. Age, smoking, and diabetes identified high-risk patients in which the warranty period for a normal result was reduced. Conclusions In a long-term prospective study of patients with stable chest pain, stress CMR remained a strong, independent predictor of hard cardiovascular events, with a warranty period of almost 7 years for a normal scan.MACE KM curvesGraphical abstract
title: Long-term warranty period of stress CMR and SPECT in stable angina: implications for repeat testing

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Stroke remains a feared complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Administrative databases have characterized stroke epidemiology, but lack clinical granularity including stroke subtype, precise timing, hemodynamic data, and cerebral protection device (CPD) details. Purpose To characterize the incidence, predictors, and outcomes of stroke/TIA after TAVR using granular clinical data from a single-centre TVT Registry, and to evaluate the real-world impact of Sentinel CPD use. Methods We analysed 1,039 consecutive TAVR patients (January 2021–June 2025) from the TVT/NCDR Registry. Stroke/TIA was identified through standardised follow-up and classified by subtype (ischaemic, haemorrhagic, undetermined, TIA) and timing (≤30 vs &gt;30 days). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified predictors. Model discrimination was assessed by C-statistic. Sentinel CPD effect was evaluated after multivariable adjustment. Results Over median 354-day follow-up (746.7 person-years), 17 patients (1.6%) experienced stroke/TIA (incidence 2.28/100 person-years): 9 ischaemic strokes (52.9%), 5 TIAs (29.4%), 2 undetermined (11.8%), and 1 haemorrhagic (5.9%). Sixty-five percent occurred within 30 days, with nearly all ischaemic strokes within 18 days. On multivariable analysis (C-statistic 0.741), atrial fibrillation was the only independent predictor (aOR 2.86, 95% CI 1.03–7.93, p=0.043). Univariable signals included STS-PROM (OR 1.07/1%, p=0.012) and low stroke volume index &lt;35 mL/m² (OR 2.26, p=0.043). Sentinel CPD (used in 17.9%) showed no stroke reduction (1.9% vs 1.9%, aOR 1.12, p=0.865). Stroke/TIA patients had markedly higher readmission rates (64.7% vs 27.1%, p&lt;0.001) and numerically higher mortality (17.6% vs 7.8%, p=0.148). Conclusion(s) In this single-centre analysis with granular clinical data, stroke/TIA after TAVR was predominantly ischaemic and periprocedural. Atrial fibrillation was the sole independent predictor. Sentinel CPD showed no real-world stroke reduction. These findings reinforce AF management as the primary target for post-TAVR stroke prevention.
title: Outcomes and predictors of stroke after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in the cerebral protection device era: a single-centre TVT registry analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV-TAVI) in degenerated surgical bioprostheses may achieve suboptimal hemodynamic results, particularly in patients with small surgical valves (valve size23 mm, stent inner diameter 21 mm). These patients are at increased risk of residual patient–prosthesis mismatch and elevated transvalvular pressure gradients. Bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) may facilitate optimal valve expansion and improve hemodynamic performance after ViV-TAVI. We compared clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of ViV-TAVI with and without adjunctive BVF in patients with small surgical aortic bioprostheses. Methods We retrospectively analyzed ViV-TAVI procedures from our institutional TAVI registry. Adjunctive BVF was performed when considered feasible in patients with significant residual gradients following ViV-TAVI. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and prior to hospital discharge. Outcomes were compared between patients with small surgical aortic bioprostheses treated with and without BVF. Optimal hemodynamic outcome was defined as a final echocardiographic mean transvalvular gradient 20 mmHg. Results Between 2010 and 2025, 1,469 TAVI procedures were performed at our institute, including 44 ViV-TAVI cases. Of these, 37 patients had small surgical aortic bioprostheses. BVF was performed in 13 patients (35%) with small surgical bioprostheses, while the others underwent standard ViV-TAVI alone. At discharge, patients undergoing adjunctive BVF achieved lower final echocardiographic mean transvalvular gradients compared with those treated without BVF (15.9±4.9 vs. 20.0±9.3 mmHg) (Figure 1). A final mean transvalvular gradient 20 mmHg was achieved in 11 of 13 patients (84.6%) in the BVF group, compared with 13 of 24 patients (54.2%) treated with standard ViV-TAVI alone. No BVF-related procedural complications were observed. Conclusions In patients with small surgical aortic bioprostheses undergoing ViV-TAVI, adjunctive BVF was safe and associated with significantly improved valve hemodynamics compared with standard ViV-TAVI alone.These findings support BVF as an effective targeted adjunctive strategy when surgical valve size limits optimal ViV-TAVI outcomes.FIGURE 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Outcome of bioprosthetic valve fracture in small-valve ViV-TAVI procedures

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) has emerged as a standard procedure for treatment of severe mitral regurgitation (MR). Procedural success is often defined by residual MR. However, predictors that affect course of residual MR after M-TEER remain poorly understood. Purpose To assess course of residual MR after M-TEER and to identify clinical and procedural determinates that may affect residual MR after 6 months of follow-up (FU). Methods We retrospectively analysed 386 patients undergoing M-TEER at a tertiary heart centre. MR severity was assessed immediately after the procedure and after a median of 6 months of FU. Deterioration of MR was defined as an increase in MR grade ≥ 0.5. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify predictors of MR deterioration. Results Within 6 months after M-TEER, MR deterioration occurred in 233 patients (60.4%). Residual MR remained unchanged in 33.2% and improved in 6.5%. Transition patterns differed significantly across all post-procedural MR groups (x2= 104.5, p&lt;0.001). Patients with residual MR &lt; I showed the highest rate (93.2%) of MR deterioration at FU. In multivariable analysis, residual MR was the strongest independent predictor of early deterioration (OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.09-0.33; p&lt;0.001). Independent associations were also observed for higher EuroScore II (OR 1.07 per point, 95% CI 1.01-1.12; p=0.011), secondary vs primary MR (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.28-0.96; p=0.036), smoking status (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.78; p=0.008), coronary artery disease (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.95; p=0.034) and arterial hypertension (OR 2.40, 95% CI 1.01-5.69; p=0.048). Conclusion Early deterioration of residual MR after M-TEER is frequent. Residual MR represents the dominant determinate of early MR worsening, while baseline risk profile and MR aetiology further modulate risk. These findings underscore that residual MR on its own does not fully capture procedural success and highlight the need for early FU strategies.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: 6 months follow-up after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: clinical and procedural determinates that may affect residual mitral regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is an established treatment for symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR) in patients at high surgical risk. This study aimed to develop a risk stratification tool to predict one year-mortality and to investigate how baseline risk modifies the prognostic impact of procedural success. Purpose To (1) develop the CHAMPIONS risk score for predicting one-year mortality after M-TEER and (2) evaluate the interaction between baseline risk and residual MR. Methods Score development followed a machine learning-guided approach. A random forest classifier was trained on 80% of the overall cohort (n=939). The remaining 20% served as an internal validation subset. The top 20 variables were selected for logistic regression. Regression coefficients were translated into a point-based score (0-14 points), with higher beta-coefficients corresponding to higher point allocations. The score incorporates nine routinely available parameters. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate and high-risk groups based on their total score. Results The CHAMPIONS score demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.67) and excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test: x2 = 0.41, p=0.995). One-year mortality rates increased stepwise across risk categories: low (7.6%), intermediate (16.7%) and high risk (30.9%) (log-rank p&lt;0.001). A significant interaction was found between baseline risk and residual MR. Achieving residual MR ≤ 1 was associated with survival benefits primarily in the intermediate-risk group (mortality 10.4% vs 25.1%, p&lt;0.001). Residual MR did not significantly change survival for patients in the low- or high-risk categories. Conclusion The CHAMPIONS score is a simple tool for pre-procedural risk stratification in M-TEER patients. It identifies intermediate-risk patients as the primary group were achieving residual MR ≤ 1 leads to a significant survival benefit. External validation is needed to confirm its generalizability and refine its predictive performance.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Pre-procedural risk stratification for percutaneous mitral valve repair: a mortality score integrating baseline risk and procedural success

abstract: Abstract Background Valve-in-valve (ViV) Transcatheter Mitral Valve replacement (TMVR) is an alternative to redo surgery in failed surgical bioprosthesis. The impact of sex on clinical outcomes of patients undergoing ViV TMVR remains unclear. Objective The aim of this study was to investigate sex differences in clinical characteristics and outcomes in patients undergoing ViV TMVR. Methods We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients who underwent transseptal valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement (ViV TMVR) using a SAPIEN prosthesis between 2011 and 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, hospitalization for heart failure, or mitral bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. Bioprosthetic valve dysfunction was defined as a composite of: (1) structural or non-structural valve deterioration resulting in a mean mitral transvalvular gradient ≥10 mmHg, moderate or severe mitral regurgitation, or the need for repeat mitral intervention; (2) valve thrombosis, defined as at least one thickened leaflet with restricted motion or a mass suggestive of thrombus confirmed by transesophageal echocardiography or cardiac computed tomography; or (3) infective endocarditis, defined according to modified Duke criteria, or confirmed by histopathology/microbiology at reoperation or autopsy. Sex-related differences in outcomes were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Results Among the 138 patients included, 92 were women (66.7%). The mean age was 66.6 ± 15.9 years for men versus 61.5 ± 21.8 years for women (p = 0.12). The mean EuroSCORE II was 11.2% ± 15.6 in men and 11.7% ± 11.3 in women (p = 0.84). Females were more likely to receive smaller prostheses, with a significant difference in size distribution between sexes (80.4% vs. 56.0% Size 29 in men and women respectively, p = 0.01). Male patients were more frequently required prosthesis post-dilation (43.5% vs. 20.0%, p &lt; 0.01). There was no difference in technical success between sexes with 100% of men and 95.4% experienced technical success (p = 0.35). At one year, female sex was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome (26.1% in women vs. 43.5% in men; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.28–0.99, p = 0.04) (Figure 1) and experienced lower rates of heart failure rehospitalization (3.9% vs. 23.6%; aHR: 0.22, 95% CI: 0.05–0.86, p = 0.03) and valve thrombosis (2.5% vs. 17.2%; aHR: 0.12, 95% CI: 0.02–0.70, p = 0.02). Conclusions In patients undergoing ViV TMVR, female sex was associated with a lower rate of the composite of death, rehospitalization for heart, mitral valve dysfunction or structural valve disease at one year. Sex does not appear to impact procedural or haemodynamic outcomes.Kaplan Meier estimates of the primary outcomeFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Sex-related differences in clinical outcomes after valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) has emerged as a therapeutic option for patients within funcional mitral regurgitation (FMR) and Advanced heart failure (AdHF) as a potential bridge therapy to heart transplantation (HTx), but mortality remains high, highlighting the need to better define which patients may truly benefit from this therapy. Purpose To analyse futility and to identify predictors of futility following M-TEER in patients with AdHF and significant FMR, evaluated for HTx listing. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted using data obtained from a prospective, multicenter, observational registry of all patients treated with M-TEER in two tertiary european hospitals. Futility was defined as all-cause mortality, urgent HTx or left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation within 12 months, or failure to reduce heart failure (HF) hospitalization rate. The primary endpoint was the rate and predictors of futility. Secundary endpoints included survival free from the composite of all-cause mortality, HTx or LVAD implantation, first rehospitalization for HF, predictors of the combined endpoint, and changes in HF hospitalization rate after the procedure. Results A total of 100 patients (median age 61- IQR 54-66 years-, 84% male) were included. At least one criterium of futility was observed in 30 patients (30%) within the first year (5 LVAD implantations, 9 urgent HTx, 19 deaths). 99% of the patients had technical success with moderate or less mitral regurgitacion (MR) in 87% at discharge. The results in univariate analysis are in Table; in multivariate analysis, the anteroposterior mitral annulus diameter was the only independent predictor of futility (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.98; p=0.023), with a cut-off value of 36.5 mm (Figure), AUC 0.70(95%CI 0.57-0.83), p=0.007. Survival free from the combined endpoint was 51%, 34% and 26% at 1, 3 and 5 years, respectively (Figure). Independent predictors of the composite event were INTERMACS class 1–4, alanine aminotransferase, NT-proBNP, and lower left ventricular ejection fraction. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 63% of patients, with symptomatic improvement (NYHA III–IV) in 56% at last follow-up. Hospitalization rates decreased from 176 to 20 per 100 patient-years after M-TEER (rate ratio 0.11, 95% CI 0.09–0.15; p &lt;0.005). Conclusions In a cohort of AdHF patients with FMR evaluated for HTx, nearly one third of patients presented futility following M-TEER and a smaller mitral annulus was identified as an independent predictor of futility. M-TEER appears to be safe and effective, significantly reducing symptoms and HF hospitalizations. However, patient selection remains crucial.Table 1 MTEERFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 1 Futility MTEERFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Futility and event-free survival predictors of mitral valve edge-to-edge repair in patients with advanced heart failure evaluated for heart transplantation

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a well-established therapeutic intervention for mitral regurgitation in elderly patients who are considered unsuitable for surgical procedures. Although procedural success is typically evaluated through echocardiography, the hemodynamic changes occurring shortly after the intervention are not well characterized. Continuous noninvasive monitoring may offer novel insights into the early cardiovascular adaptations following M-TEER. Purpose The objective is to assess early hemodynamic changes following M-TEER by utilizing a continuous, wearable, noninvasive chest-patch device designed for multiparameter hemodynamic evaluation. Methods This single-center prospective study involved the enrollment of 40 patients undergoing M-TEER procedures between April 2024 and January 2025. Hemodynamic parameters were recorded at 15-minute intervals using wearable, noninvasive, photoplethysmography-based chest patch sensors for a minimum of 12 hours prior to and more than 24 hours following the intervention. The hemodynamic features recorded included cardiac output (CO), cardiac index (CI), stroke volume (SV), and systemic vascular resistance (SVR). Results Continuous monitoring was technically feasible in all 40 patients included in the study. The mean age of the participants was 79.1±10.3 years, with 21 patients (53%) being female. Following the M-TEER procedure, significant increases were observed in cardiac output (5.5±0.7 vs. 5.8±0.9 L/min, p=0.011), cardiac index (3.0±0.5 vs. 3.2±0.6 L/min/m², p=0.002), and stroke volume (77.0±13.8 vs. 78.0±14.3 ml, p=0.005), alongside a significant reduction in systemic vascular resistance (1398.7±332.1 vs. 1333.3±356.3 dynsec/cm5, p=0.004). Within the entire M-TEER cohort, the early increase in cardiac output varied according to the etiology of mitral regurgitation (p=0.026), with atrial secondary mitral regurgitation (90%) being more frequently observed among cardiac output responders compared to ventricular secondary mitral regurgitation (10%). Conclusions Continuous noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring following M-TEER is both feasible and indicative of procedure-specific early cardiovascular adaptations. The M-TEER procedure has been shown to elicit a beneficial hemodynamic effect, characterized by an enhancement in cardiac output and a reduction in systemic vascular resistance. Further extensive studies are required to ascertain the prognostic significance of the early hemodynamic response after M-TEER.
title: Monitoring of early hemodynamic changes after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair using a wearable, non-invasive device

abstract: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation and mitral regurgitation frequently coexist, creating a bidirectional cycle that accelerates atrial remodelling. This volume overload and arrhythmia burden readily extend to the right heart, driving tricuspid annular enlargement and functional tricuspid regurgitation. Purpose We evaluated a single-session strategy combining pulsed-field ablation and transcatheter edge-to-edge repair. We compared a dual intervention (ablation and mitral repair) against a triple intervention (adding tricuspid repair) to define invasive haemodynamic and structural outcomes in this complex patient population. Methods We prospectively enrolled ten consecutive high-surgical-risk patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation and severe regurgitation. We performed all procedures via a single transseptal puncture. We compared the dual intervention (eight patients) and triple intervention (two patients) strategy groups, measuring procedure time, invasive left atrial pressures (measured in triplicate before and after repair), and echocardiographic parameters through six-month follow-up. Results We achieved procedural success in all ten cases. In the dual intervention group, mean left atrial pressure dropped from 13.8 to 12.1 millimetres of mercury, while peak v-waves fell from 22.0 to 18.8 millimetres of mercury. Acute mitral regurgitation reduction to moderate or less occurred in 88% of these cases. At six months, mean mitral regurgitation grade improved from 3.75 to 1.75, and functional class (New York Heart Association) improved from 2.88 to 1.75. The triple intervention group exhibited a distinct advanced atrial phenotype. Despite severe regurgitation, these patients presented with lower baseline v-waves (mean 15.5 millimetres of mercury) than the dual group, reflecting extreme atrial compliance. In these patients, mean left atrial pressure shifted only from 12.5 to 10.5 millimetres of mercury. Massive geometric distortion (mean left atrial diameter 59.0 millimetres) prevented optimal mitral reduction; neither patient achieved moderate or less residual regurgitation. At six months, their mitral regurgitation grade remained largely unchanged (4.0 to 3.5), while functional class improved marginally from 2.5 to 2.0. Conclusion(s) A single-session strategy combining pulsed-field ablation and transcatheter edge-to-edge repair offers a feasible approach for early rhythm control and functional improvement. Our data suggest that the atrial fibrillation, mitral, and tricuspid regurgitation triad represents a late-stage phenotype driven by profound atrial remodelling. While dual interventions yield high structural success, massive baseline atrial dilatation—often masked by high atrial compliance and lower-than-expected v-waves—severely limits the efficacy of the clip and necessitates refined anatomical selection criteria.baseline characteristicsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Defining the limits of transcatheter valve repair: a prospective comparison of multivalvular interventions in the atrial fibrillation triad

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (TEER) has become an established treatment for patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR) at high surgical risk. Given its low procedural risk, TEER is frequently offered even to the highest-risk patients, raising concerns about the lack of meaningful clinical benefit. The rate and determinants of mortality after TEER remain incompletely understood; identifying these factors could optimize patient stratification. Purpose To assess the incidence and the clinical and procedural predictors of 1-year mortality after TEER. Methods The MAVERICK registry is an international observational cohort including consecutive patients undergoing TEER across 5 centers. The primary endpoint was all-cause death at 1-year follow-up. Univariable Cox regression was performed to identify predictors of mortality. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was built using variables with a p-value &lt;0.10 in the univariable analysis. Sensitivity analyses were performed according to MR etiology (organic vs. functional, with mixed mechanisms classified as functional). Results Among 824 patients that underwent TEER, 100 (12%) had died within the first year. Independent predictors of death were NYHA class III/IV (aHR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3–4.2; p=0.003), and implantation of than 3 clips (aHR 3.10, 95% CI 1.75–5.51; p&lt;0.001). In the functional MR subgroup early mortality was 11% (59/519). NYHA class III/IV, baseline tricuspid regurgitation at least moderate, and peripheral artery disease were independent predictors of early death in this subgroup. In the organic MR subgroup, mortality was 12% (37/305); NYHA class III/IV and post-TEER MR ≥ moderate were independent predictors of early death. Conclusions Mortality at one-year post-TEER is primarily driven by baseline clinical status and procedural complexity. Advanced heart failure symptoms consistently predict mortality across all MR etiologies. Concomitant significant tricuspid regurgitation portends a worse prognosis in functional MR, and procedural success is a key driver of early survival in organic MR. These findings highlight the critical importance of optimized patient selection and procedural efficacy to improve survival following TEER.Predictors of early death after mitral TEERFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Sensitivity analysis according to type of MRFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Predictors of early death after transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair: results from the MAVERICK registry

abstract: Abstract Introduction Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction is a serious complication of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Current guidelines suggest a predicted neo-LVOT area &lt; 200 mm² as a threshold to reconsider the procedure. However, this cut-off is largely derived from TMVR in native valves or rings, and its applicability to valve-in-valve (ViV) TMVR remains debated. Purpose To evaluate the post-procedural neo-LVOT area using computed tomography (CT) and to assess the clinical and hemodynamic impact of a small neo-LVOT following ViV TMVR. Methods We included patients who underwent successful ViV TMVR at a high-volume tertiary center between 2014 and 2025 and had a post-procedural CT. Neo-LVOT was defined as the smallest area in the LVOT between the stent frame and the interventricular septum, measured at end-systole. Patients were dichotomized by neo-LVOT size (&lt; 200 mm² vs. ≥ 200 mm²). The primary outcome was significant hemodynamic LVOT obstruction, defined as a maximal LVOT gradient ≥ 30 mmHg on the first post-procedural transthoracic echocardiogram. Secondary outcomes included 30-day functional status and a composite of all-cause mortality or mitral re-intervention at the end of follow-up. A sensitivity analysis was performed for patients with a neo-LVOT &lt; 100 mm². Results A total of 97 patients were analyzed. Following ViV TMVR, the median neo-LVOT area was 170 (IQR: 105–305) mm², with 57 patients (58.8%) presenting a neo-LVOT &lt; 200 mm². Patients with a reduced neo-LVOT were more likely to be female (82.5% vs. 45.0%, p &lt; 0.001) with a higher left ventricular ejection fraction (59.3 ± 9.2% vs. 55.1 ± 10.4%, p = 0.04). Two cases of LVOT obstruction occurred, both in patients with a neo-LVOT &lt; 200 mm² (169 mm² and 87 mm²), but neither had clinical consequences. One of these cases occurred in a woman who had undergone alcohol septal ablation prior to ViV TMVR, with complete regression of the LVOT gradient at 3 months. A neo-LVOT &lt; 200 mm² was not associated with worse 30-day functional outcomes (73.7% in NYHA class I/II vs. 60.0% in the ≥ 200 mm² group, p = 0.42). Over a mean follow-up of 2.7 ± 2.4 years, 22 (22.7%) composite events (death or mitral re-intervention) occurred, with no significant difference between groups (HR 1.74, 95% CI 0.69–4.38, p = 0.24). Results were similar in the 23 (23.7%) patients with a neo-LVOT &lt; 100 mm². Conclusion Post-procedural neo-LVOT areas &lt; 200 mm² are common after ViV TMVR, occurring in nearly 60% of patients. However, this finding is infrequently associated with significant hemodynamic LVOT obstruction and does not negatively impact long-term clinical outcomes. Even a neo-LVOT &lt; 100 mm² (present in a quarter of patients) showed no adverse impact on long-term outcomes. These findings suggest the conventional 200 mm² threshold may be overly restrictive for ViV TMVR candidates.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-centre retrospective analysis of 97 patients with successful ViV TMVR (2014 to 2025) and post-procedural CT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small single-centre cohort with only two obstruction events and post-procedural rather than predicted neo-LVOT measurement.
appraisal.one_line: Small post-procedural neo-LVOT areas were common after valve-in-valve TMVR yet rarely caused obstruction or worse outcomes, questioning the 200 mm² threshold.

Two cases of LVOT obstruction occurred, both in patients with a reduced neo-LVOT, but neither had clinical consequences. Composite of death or mitral re-intervention: 22 (22.7%) events, with no significant difference between groups (HR 1.74, 95% CI 0.69–4.38, p = 0.24).

title: Favorable outcomes despite small neo-left ventricular outflow tract area in valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Introduction Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is common among patients undergoing transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). However, its evolution after intervention and the prognostic impact of residual TR remain uncertain. Purpose We aimed to assess the evolution of TR after TMVR, evaluate the impact of residual TR on mortality, and identify predictors of TR improvement. Methods Patients undergoing TMVR with a balloon-expandable prosthesis in 2 centers were included. Those undergoing concomitant tricuspid percutaneous intervention were excluded. Follow-up was performed at 1, 6, and 12 months, and annually thereafter. At each time point, TR severity was classified as ≤ mild, moderate, or severe. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality according to residual TR at 30 days. Secondary endpoints were TR evolution at 30 days and 1 year, as well as changes in tricuspid annular diameter, pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), right ventricular dilatation and dysfunction at 30 days. Results A total of 268 patients were included. At baseline, 170 (63%) had ≤ mild TR, 51 (19%) had moderate TR, and 47 (18%) had severe TR. The median age was 71 [56-80] years, with 63% women. Most patients (92%) had prior cardiac surgery, and 34% had previous tricuspid intervention. Among them, 185 (69%) underwent valve-in-valve, 49 (18%) valve-in-ring, and 34 (13%) valve-in-mitral annulus calcification procedures. TMVR was associated with a non-significant trend toward TR improvement at 30 days (15% of residual severe TR and 16% of residual moderate TR versus 18% and 19% respectively, at baseline; p = 0.14) with no change at 1 year (p = 0.47). Tricuspid annular diameter remained unchanged (p = 0.60), whereas PASP significantly decreased (53 [42-65] mmHg to 42 [35-50] mmHg; p &lt; 0.01). There were no changes in right ventricular dilatation (p = 0.73) and dysfunction (p = 0.23). After a median follow-up of 2.1 [0.5-4.9] years, 103 deaths occurred, 56% of cardiovascular cause. One- and 5-year survival rates were 93 [89-97]% and 65 [56-75]% in patients with ≤ mild residual TR at 30 days, compared with 84 [71-97]% and 34 [15-53]% in those with moderate TR (p &lt; 0.01 at each time point), and 79 [65-93]% and 35 [14-55]% in those with severe TR (p &lt; 0.01 at each time point). After adjustment for confounders, both moderate and severe residual TR remained independently associated with increased mortality (aHR = 2.05 [1.05-4.02]; p = 0.04 and 2.40 [1.29-4.48]; p &lt; 0.01, respectively). Smaller baseline tricuspid annular diameter was the only predictor of TR improvement at 30 days (aOR = 0.91 [0.84-0.99] per mm; p = 0.03). Conclusions Despite a trend toward early improvement, TMVR was not associated with significant reduction in TR severity at 30 days and 1 year. Residual moderate and severe TR at 30 days after TMVR were independently associated with increased mortality during follow-up.TR evolution at 30 days and 1 year after TVMRFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Survival according to residual TR at 30 daysFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Evolution and prognostic impact of residual tricuspid regurgitation after transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR)

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral annular calcification (MAC) represents a growing challenge in patients with mitral valve disease (MVD), as complex anatomy and advanced age often limit surgical options. Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is an established therapy for mitral regurgitation (MR), but extensive MAC may impair procedural outcomes. Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) has emerged as an alternative providing predictable MR reduction. Purpose To characterize treatment pathways and compare procedural outcomes in patients with significant MAC and MVD. Methods Consecutive patients with significant MAC referred for TMVR screening were prospectively enrolled in a single-center registry. MAC severity was assessed using contrast-enhanced multi-slice computed tomography (MSCT). Patients were stratified by treatment strategy: TMVR with dedicated devices, M-TEER, or conservative management. Patients undergoing mitral valve surgery (n=2) were excluded. Baseline clinical, echocardiographic, and MSCT characteristics were analyzed. Short-term outcomes included technical success, post-procedural transmitral gradient, residual MR at discharge, and in-hospital mortality. Results Among 230 screened patients, 48 (21%) with significant MAC were included. TMVR was performed in 25% (n=12) and M-TEER in 23% (n=11), while 52% (n=25) received conservative management. TMVR patients were younger (median 75 years [IQR 66–80]) than those treated with M-TEER (81 years [80–84]) or conservatively (79 years [76–81]). Secondary MR predominated in the TMVR group (67%), whereas primary MR was more common in the M-TEER and conservative groups (55–60%). Baseline transmitral gradients were similar (median 4 mmHg). Left ventricular ejection fraction was lower in TMVR patients (mean 42.5%) compared with M-TEER (58%) and conservative management (55%). Moderate or greater mitral stenosis (52%) and severe circumferential MAC (60%) were most prevalent in conservatively managed patients. Both interventions achieved substantial MR reduction, with residual MR ≤ I+ at discharge in 92% after TMVR and 82% after M-TEER. In contrast, 92% of conservatively treated patients had persistent severe MR (IV+). Median post-procedural transmitral gradient was 3 mmHg after both interventions. Technical success was high (TMVR 91.7%, M-TEER 90.9%). One in-hospital death occurred after TMVR (8.3%); none after M-TEER or conservative management. Conclusion Patients with significant MAC and MVD represent a heterogeneous high-risk population with limited treatment options. Both TMVR and M-TEER showed high procedural success and effective MR reduction. However, over half remained unsuitable for intervention, particularly those with severe circumferential MAC and concomitant mitral stenosis. These findings underscore the need for alternative strategies and prospective studies with long-term follow-up to optimize treatment selection in this challenging population.Study Flowchart and Treatment TrajectoriesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Treatment trajectories and procedural outcomes of patients with significant mitral annular calcification and mitral valve disease

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) adoption is limited by high screening failure rates, mainly due to anatomical constraints such as neo-left ventricular outflow tract (neo-LVOT) obstruction risk. A novel transseptal TMVR system with left atrial (LA) fixation may expand anatomical eligibility while avoiding LVOT compromise. Purpose To assess anatomical eligibility for a transseptal TMVR system with LA fixation in patients with relevant mitral regurgitation (MR) previously screened for TMVR and to evaluate its potential impact on overall TMVR eligibility. Methods All consecutive patients with relevant MR referred for TMVR evaluation were prospectively enrolled in a single-center registry. Patients screened for dedicated TMVR devices with full cardiac cycle CT imaging were included. Retrospective eligibility for the LA fixation system was assessed using manufacturer-recommended CT thresholds. Patients were classified as Screen Pass or Screen Failure. Reasons for ineligibility were analyzed, and clinical, echocardiographic, and CT parameters compared. Overall impact was determined by comparing real-world acceptance rates (sub-valvular TMVR devices only) with the expected screen pass rate using the LA fixation system. A subgroup analysis included patients with prior screening failure due to high neo-LVOT obstruction risk. Results Among 211 screened patients, 24 were excluded due to incomplete CT imaging; 187 were analyzed (mean age 76.3 years [IQR 73–81], 55.6% male, ejection fraction 45.8% [IQR 34–57], 48.9% primary MR). CT-based evaluation showed that 112 patients (59.9%) fulfilled eligibility criteria (Screen Pass), whereas 75 (40.1%) did not (Screen Failure). Main reasons for screening failure were high LA volume change (N=36, 48.0%), mitral annular size (N=22, 29.3%), LA width (N=19, 25.3%; 17 too small, 2 too large), unfavorable LA tilt (N=16, 21.3%), excessive LA height (N=15, 20.0%), and small left ventricular volume (N=4, 5.3%). Screen Pass patients were more often male (57.1% vs. 53.3%) and had higher atrial fibrillation prevalence (82.14% vs. 57.33%). Secondary MR predominated in the Screen Pass group (N=72, 66.06%), whereas primary MR was more frequent in Screen Failure patients (N=43, 58.90%). Comparing real-world acceptance for sub-valvular TMVR devices (33.6%) with the expected screen pass rate for the LA fixation system (59.9%) suggested a potential overall eligibility increase of 26.3%. In patients with prior screening failure due to high neo-LVOT obstruction risk, screen pass and failure rates were 42.9% and 57.1%, respectively. Conclusion Integrating a transseptal TMVR system with LA fixation into the screening portfolio may substantially expand TMVR eligibility, particularly in patients at high risk of neo-LVOT obstruction, as the device spares the LVOT. Further studies should evaluate whether treatment improves prognosis in severe MR.Figure 1.Study Flow ChartFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2.Reasons for Screening FailureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Expanding TMVR Suitability with a Transseptal Left Atrial Fixation Device: A CT-based Eligibility Analysis

abstract: Abstract Introduction The MitraScore is a recently developed risk stratification tool designed to predict mortality after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER). It integrates eight easily obtainable clinical parameters into a single score, allowing for rapid bedside assessment. However, its external validation in real-world populations remains limited. Aim To evaluate the prognostic performance of the MitraScore in predicting all-cause mortality among patients undergoing M-TEER at our centre. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-centre study including all consecutive patients who underwent M-TEER between 2013 and October 2025. Clinical and laboratory data were obtained from electronic medical records. The MitraScore was calculated by assigning one point for each of the following: age ≥75 years, anemia, eGFR &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m², left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) &lt;40%, peripheral artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, high-dose diuretics, and absence of renin–angiotensin system inhibitor therapy. Survival was analysed using Kaplan–Meier curves and Cox regression. Diagnostic accuracy of the MitraScore for all-cause mortality was assessed using ROC analysis. Results A total of 95 procedures were performed, with 86 patients included in the final analysis (mean age 74 ± 11 years, 63% male). Underlying heart disease was primary mitral regurgitation in 43%, ischemic cardiomyopathy in 29%, non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy in 27%, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 1%. Mean LVEF was 44 ± 15%, hemoglobin 12.6 ± 1.8 g/dL, and eGFR 50 ± 22 mL/min/1.73 m². Peripheral artery disease and COPD were present in 11% and 15% of patients, respectively. Over a median follow-up of 42 months, all-cause mortality was 22%, 35%, and 59% at 12, 24, and 60 months, respectively. Mean MitraScore was 3 ± 1. The score demonstrated good discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.686), with each 1-point increase associated with a 50% higher risk of mortality (HR 1.50; 95% CI 1.21–1.86; p &lt; 0.001). The optimal cut-off for mortality prediction was ≥3 (70% sensitivity, 68% specificity). Conclusion The MitraScore showed good performance in predicting all-cause mortality after M-TEER in our real-world cohort, confirming its validity as a simple and practical risk stratification tool in this population.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: MitraScore: a simple, powerful tool to predict mortality after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair

abstract: Abstract Introduction Assessment of procedural success following transcatheter mitral edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), including non-invasive parameters, remains challenging. Purpose The association between iatrogenic atrial septal defect (iASD) gradient and post-procedural three-dimensional vena contracta area (3D-VCA) as a marker of residual mitral regurgitation severity has not been clearly defined. Methods In this prospective study, 26 patients who underwent M-TEER at a tertiary cardiovascular center were analyzed over the past year. Median age was 78 years (IQR 74–81.2), and 80.7% were male. Secondary mitral regurgitation was present in 50%, primary in 34.6%, and mixed etiology in 15.3%. The median post-procedural transmitral valve gradient was 2 mmHg (IQR 2–3), assessed by transesophageal echocardiography. Continuous-wave Doppler recordings across the iASD were obtained intraoperatively immediately after catheter withdrawal from the left atrium. The largest systolic 3D-VCA was quantified by direct planimetry from en face short-axis views using multiplanar reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to post-procedural 3D-VCA (≤0.2 vs &gt;0.2, cm2). Diagnostic accuracy of the iASD gradient for identifying 3D-VCA &gt;0.2cm2 was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with optimal cutoff determined by the Youden index. Results Patients with post-procedural 3D-VCA &gt;0.2 cm² demonstrated significantly higher iASD gradients than those with 3D-VCA ≤0.2 cm² (5.64±2.84 vs 3.07±1.10 mmHg, p=0.007). ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory ability for identifying 3D-VCA &gt;0.2cm2 (AUC 0.81, 95% CI 0.61–0.97). An optimal iASD cutoff gradient ≥5 mmHg yielded a sensitivity of 63.6% and specificity of 93.3% for predicting 3D-VCA &gt;0.2 cm². Conclusion The iASD gradient is associated with residual mitral regurgitation severity and shows good diagnostic accuracy for detecting 3D-VCA &gt;0.2 cm². An iASD gradient ≥5 mmHg may serve as a simple and highly specific marker for immediate post-procedural assessment after M-TEER; however, validation in larger cohorts is required.Violin PlotFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.ROC curveFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Iatrogenic ASD gradient as a marker of residual mitral regurgitation severity after M-TEER procedure

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) has emerged as a treatment option for patients with mitral regurgitation (MR), ineligible for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair. Anatomical conditions and clinical risk profiles differ substantially between women and men. Evidence on sex-specific differences and outcomes after TMVR remains limited. Purpose To evaluate sex-specific differences in clinical and anatomical phenotypes, procedural, and mid-term clinical outcomes following TMVR using data from an international multicentre registry. Methods The CHOICE-MI registry included patients with symptomatic MR treated with dedicated TMVR devices at 41 international centres. Clinical, echocardiographic, and CT parameters were compared between sexes. Kaplan-Meier analyses assessed all-cause and cardiovascular (CV) mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization up to 36 months. Multivariable Cox regression identified independent predictors of outcomes stratified by sex. Results A total of 545 patients (median age 77 years [IQR 71–81], EuroSCORE II 5.6% [3.6–10.6]) undergoing TMVR were included and stratified by sex. TMVR was performed in 236 women (43%), using transapical devices in 73.7% (n=174) and transfemoral in 26.3% (n=62). Women more frequently had arterial hypertension, but less coronary artery disease and fewer prior PCI, CABG, and SAVR. The prevalence of primary MR (female vs. male: 36.3% vs. 36.0%, p=0.99) and secondary MR (47.0% vs. 45.5%, p=0.80) was similar between sexes. Atrial secondary MR was more common in women (27.0% vs. 13.2%, p=0.002), whereas ischemic MR was more frequent in men (24.7% vs. 41.6%, p=0.001). Women had smaller LV volumes (LVEDV 125 vs. 166 mL; LVESV 63 vs. 95 mL; both p&lt;0.001) and annular dimensions (annulus area 10.5 vs. 11.5 cm², p=0.001). Technical success (94.5% vs. 92.6%, p=0.47) and MR reduction to ≤1+ (96.4% vs. 95.5%, p=0.96) were comparable. NYHA class improved significantly from baseline to 1 year and remained stable at 2 years (both p&lt;0.001), without sex differences. At 3 years, no significant differences were observed between women and men regarding all-cause mortality (47.1% vs. 52.6%, p=0.55), CV mortality (31.4% vs. 25.5%, p=0.37), or HF hospitalization (35.2% vs. 44.3%, p=0.19). In multivariable analysis restricted to women, renal function assessed by eGFR predicted 3-year survival (HR 0.99 [95% CI 0.97–1.00], p=0.012). Conclusions Despite marked sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and cardiac geometry, TMVR showed comparable procedural efficacy, sustained symptomatic improvement, and similar mid-term outcomes in women and men. Women more often had atrial functional MR, indicating a distinct phenotype warranting further study. These findings indicate that sex-specific anatomical and remodeling differences do not translate into differential clinical benefit, supporting TMVR as an effective therapeutic strategy across sexes.Graphical Abstract TMVR in WomenFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Outcomes of TMVR in WomenFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Sex-specific differences and outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve replacement in women

abstract: Abstract Background Concomitant transcatheter mitral (M-TEER) and tricuspid (T-TEER) edge-to-edge repair has emerged as a valuable therapeutic strategy for patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR). The use of a single TriClip® steerable guide catheter (SGC) for both valves may streamline the procedure and reduce invasiveness. Purpose This study evaluated the safety, efficacy, and clinical outcomes of combined M-TEER and T-TEER performed with a single TriClip® SGC. Methods From January 2022 to December 2024, 47 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe (3+) degenerative or functional MR and severe TR in NYHA class III–IV underwent combined M-TEER and T-TEER using a single TriClip® SGC at our center. Propensity score matching was applied to adjust for baseline differences in subgroup analyses. Echocardiographic and clinical data were collected at baseline, 30 days, and 1 year. Primary endpoints included procedural success, MR and TR severity reduction, and NYHA class improvement. Results The cohort consisted of 47 patients (20 matched pairs; 64% female; median age 77 years [IQR: 9]). Procedural success was achieved in all cases, with mean device and procedure times of 39.4 ± 6.8 minutes and 71.5 ± 9.4 minutes, respectively. No in-hospital or 30-day major adverse events occurred, except for one atrial septal defect closure (2.1%). During a median follow-up of 0.82 years, heart failure hospitalization occurred in 4 patients (8.5%), with no deaths reported. At 30 days and 1 year, MR ≤2+ was maintained in all patients, with 72.3% having only mild MR at 1 year. MR severity reduction over time was significant (p&lt;0.001), with post hoc testing confirming improvement from baseline to 30 days (p&lt;0.001) and to 1 year (p&lt;0.001), consistent across age (p=0.66) and MR etiology subgroups (p=0.08). TR severity also improved markedly, with 75% achieving trivial TR and 21% mild TR at 1 year (p&lt;0.001), with sustained reduction from baseline to follow-up (p&lt;0.001), unaffected by age (p=0.68) or MR etiology (p=0.87). Functional status improved significantly, with all patients in NYHA class I–II at 1 year; 32% remained fully asymptomatic from 30 days onwards. NYHA class improvement over time was significant (p&lt;0.001), with no interaction with age (p=0.54) or MR etiology (p=0.77). Conclusions Combined M-TEER and T-TEER using a single TriClip® SGC is safe, achieves durable MR and TR reduction, and improves functional status across patient subgroups, supporting its role in managing advanced bi-valvular regurgitation.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Concomitant mitral and tricuspid TEER with a single steerable guide catheter

abstract: Abstract Background In patients undergoing tricuspid valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class is central to patient selection and follow-up assessment. However, real-world data on its prognostic value and determinants of symptomatic response remain limited. Purpose To assess the prognostic impact of baseline NYHA class and to identify correlates of NYHA class improvement and deterioration after T-TEER. Methods We analysed patients undergoing T-TEER for symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in the multicentre, real-world EuroTR registry (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation). Baseline NYHA class was related to survival and heart failure hospitalisation using Kaplan-Meier analyses. In patients with paired NYHA assessments, changes from baseline to follow-up were evaluated, and predictors of NYHA class improvement and worsening were identified using multivariable logistic regression, including pre-specified covariates: age, sex, body mass index (BMI), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), TR severity, estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure (PAPs), log(NT-proBNP), and baseline NYHA class. Results In the overall cohort (n=3,434), Kaplan-Meier curves demonstrated stepwise separation by baseline NYHA class for both overall and event-free survival, indicating progressively higher risk with advancing baseline functional limitation (log-rank χ²=121.14 and 98.48, respectively; both p&lt;0.001). In adjusted Cox regression with administrative censoring at 2 years, higher baseline NYHA class independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR 1.78 per 1-class increase; 95% CI 1.50-2.10; p&lt;0.001). Among patients with paired NYHA data (n=1,974), baseline NYHA class was predominantly advanced, with NYHA I/II in 323 patients (16.4%) and NYHA III/IV in 1,651 patients (83.6%). At follow-up, functional status improved substantially, with NYHA I/II observed in 1,173 patients (59.4%) and NYHA III/IV in 801 patients (40.6%). In multivariable analysis of improvement, higher baseline NYHA class was the strongest correlate of improvement (OR 4.76 per NYHA class; 95% CI 3.70-6.12; p&lt;0.001), alongside lower BMI (per 1 kg/m² decrease; OR 1.04; 95% CI 1.02-1.06; p&lt;0.001), higher TAPSE (OR 1.03 per mm; 95% CI 1.00-1.06; p=0.030), and lower log(NT-proBNP) (per 1-log decrease; OR 1.27; 95% CI 1.14-1.43; p&lt;0.001). Worsening was infrequent (n=104) and was associated with higher PAPs (OR 1.03 per mmHg; 95% CI 1.01-1.04; p&lt;0.001) and lower baseline NYHA class (OR 0.17 per class; 95% CI 0.11-0.25; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion In the large EuroTR real-world T-TEER cohort, baseline NYHA class is a strong independent predictor of 2-year mortality. While improvement is common, particularly in patients with advanced baseline limitation, worsening is rare and mainly related to higher pulmonary pressures.Kaplan-Meier curvesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Alluvial for NYHA class shiftFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Baseline New York Heart Association class as a prognostic marker and determinant of symptomatic response after tricuspid valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: insights from the EuroTR registry

abstract: Abstract Background Interventional therapies for tricuspid regurgitation (TR) are rapidly advancing; however, identifying patients who derive a survival benefit remains difficult. The TRI-Score has become the most established clinical risk score for mortality prediction after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI), outperforming alternative scoring systems. Although it integrates key clinical and echocardiographic markers of systemic congestion and end-organ dysfunction, invasive right-heart hemodynamics are not included. Parameters such as pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) may better capture right-sided circulatory burden and thereby refine risk stratification. This study investigated whether adding invasively assessed PVR to the TRI-Score improves prediction of 12-month mortality following TTVI. Methods In this single-center prospective cohort, 118 patients with severe TR (≥3 according to Hahn) underwent either edge-to-edge repair (81,3%) or minimally invasive tricuspid valve replacement (18,7 %). Both the TRI-Score and PVR were obtained prior to intervention. Patients were followed for 12 months after the procedure. The results of the TRI-score were sorted into low-risk and medium-risk versus high-risk categories according to the calculator. A Kaplan–Meier analysis was performed to illustrate survival rates between TRI-Score risk categories. Receiver-operating-characteristic analyses (ROC) with area-under-the-curve (AUC) calculation were conducted to assess their separate and combined predictive performance for all-cause mortality at 12 months. Results Baseline characteristics are summarized in Table 1. Mean age was 81 ± 6.6 years, and 44.9% of patients were male. Twelve-month all-cause mortality was 18.6%. The TRI-Score demonstrated good prognostic discrimination for 12-months mortality (AUC = 0.76, 95% CI 0.65–0.88, p &lt; 0.001), Figure 1.A. The Kaplan–Meier analysis revealed significantly better survival for patients in the low- and intermediate-risk TRI categories compared with high-risk TRI-Score categories (log rank p &lt; 0.001), Figure 2. Among right-heart hemodynamic parameters, both RA and RV pressure showed prognostic relevance for 12-months mortality (Figure 1.B). In contrast, PVR alone demonstrated limited and statistically non-significant discriminatory ability (AUC 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.76; p = 0.140). However, the combination of the TRI-Score and PVR yielded the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.81, 95% CI 0.69–0.93, p &lt; 0.001), Figure 1.C. Conclusion The TRI-Score provides reliable risk stratification for 12-month all-cause mortality after TTVI. Its prognostic performance is enhanced by the addition of PVR.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figures 1.A), 1. B), 1. title: Combined TRI-Score and pulmonary vascular resistance enhance 12-month mortality prediction after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation is associated with adverse outcomes and increasing interest in transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions. Accurate anatomical characterisation of the tricuspid valve is essential for patient selection and procedural planning. Transesophageal echocardiography provides an en face view and represents the reference standard; however, its invasive nature limits widespread use. A modified transthoracic subcostal approach may allow non-invasive en face visualisation, although its diagnostic performance has not been systematically validated. Purpose To evaluate the feasibility, reproducibility, and diagnostic concordance of a transthoracic en face view of the tricuspid valve compared with transesophageal echocardiography. Methods In this observational cross-sectional study, consecutive adult patients referred for transesophageal echocardiography underwent prior two- and three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. An en face view of the tricuspid valve was obtained using a modified subcostal approach. Valve morphology was classified according to contemporary echocardiographic criteria. Feasibility was graded using a five-point scale. Diagnostic concordance and interobserver agreement were assessed using the kappa statistic. Results A total of 124 patients were included. Adequate en face visualisation was achieved in 71% of cases using two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. The most frequent morphological pattern was a three-leaflet configuration (72%), followed by a four-leaflet configuration with posterior leaflet segmentation (20%). Overall concordance between transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography was substantial for both two- and three-dimensional imaging (kappa 0.68 and 0.69, respectively; p&lt;0.005). In patients with good or fair image quality, concordance increased to almost perfect (kappa 0.82 and 0.84). Interobserver reproducibility was substantial (kappa 0.67). Conclusion A modified transthoracic subcostal en face view provides reliable and reproducible anatomical characterisation of the tricuspid valve. When image quality is adequate, this non-invasive approach shows high diagnostic concordance with transesophageal echocardiography and enables identification of anatomical variants. This technique may represent a valuable and widely accessible tool for routine assessment and preprocedural planning in patients undergoing transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions.Tricuspid valve morphology (Hahn).For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.TTE–TEE concordance by image qualityFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Feasibility and diagnostic concordance of a transthoracic en face view for tricuspid valve morphological assessment

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Despite increasing attention to the management of tricuspid regurgitation (TR), a substantial unmet clinical need persists for safe and effective transcatheter therapies in high-risk patients with severe TR. A novel transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) system has been specifically developed for the tricuspid position. Its innovative dual-stent design allows accommodation of a wide range of anatomical configurations while preserving optimal valve geometry and functional performance. Purpose The objective of this First-in-Human study is to assess the safety and feasibility of the TTVR system in patients with clinically significant tricuspid regurgitation. Methods This prospective, multicentre, single-arm, nonrandomized First-in-Human clinical investigation is conducted across eight sites in France, Belgium, and Switzerland. A total of 20 adult patients with severe, symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation who were considered unsuitable for open-heart surgery were enrolled. The primary safety endpoint is a composite endpoint measure that includes all-cause mortality, rehospitalization for heart failure, and reintervention for failed tricuspid intervention at 30 days. The primary performance endpoint is device success, defined as reduction of tricuspid regurgitation by at least 1 grade between the baseline and post-intervention evaluation (as assessed by the echo core laboratory), and no more than moderate tricuspid regurgitation. The study is closely monitored by an independent Data Safety Monitoring Committee (DMC) and an independent Clinical Events Committee (CEC), which adjudicates all adverse events. Additionally, all echocardiographic and computed tomography (CT) imaging are evaluated by independent core laboratories to ensure objective and consistent data assessment. Results In the TRICURE FIH a total of 20 patients (mean age 77 ± 6.6 years, 90 % female, TRI-SCORE 4.6 ± 2.5) were enrolled. All patients were symptomatic with NYHA ≥ II and had severe (grade ≥ 3) TR at baseline. The procedure time was 35 ± 16 minutes. At 30 days, the primary safety endpoint, a composite of major adverse events, was observed in 7 patients (35 %), including three all-cause deaths, three re-interventions (thereof two elective), and one hospitalization for heart failure. The primary performance endpoint was successfully achieved in all patients (100%), with all patients having a TR reduction of at least 3 grades, and none of the patients having more than mild TR post-procedure. No device-related pacemaker implant was reported. Conclusion(s) The primary endpoint results of the TRICURE FIH study provide convincing evidence of the feasibility and safety of this novel TTVR system. Additional outcomes will be assessed in the ongoing TRICURE EU PIVOTAL study.
title: The TRICURE FIH study results and future trials update

abstract: Abstract Background and aims Transcatheter tricuspid valve repair (T-TEER) is increasingly used in patients deemed unfit for surgery. Large-scale real-world data on long-term survival predictors and health economic implications within the German health system are limited. We sought to identify mortality predictors—frailty and comorbidity burden—and to assess costs before and after T-TEER using a national health-insurance database. Purpose To evaluate long-term survival determinants (age, frailty, and comorbidities) and to quantify one-year post-procedural cost changes in a large German real-world T-TEER cohort. Methods Observational analysis of all T-TEER patients (01/2018–12/2023) in the BARMER database (~10% of the German population). Frailty was assessed via care levels (“Pflegegrad”). Cox proportional hazards models quantified associations with survival. Costs were compared 12 months before vs. after T-TEER. Results Among 1,712 patients, age groups (50–69, 70–79, 80–99) showed no significant survival differences; female sex was protective (HR 0.51). Frailty strongly predicted mortality: care levels 3–5 vs 0–2 had HR 2.30 (p&lt;0.001). Non-cardiac comorbidities increased mortality risk: ≥3 comorbidities HR 1.85 (p&lt;0.001). Right-heart failure was the primary cardiac predictor for increased mortality after T-TEER (HR 1.96, p&lt;0.001). One-year costs decreased substantially after T-TEER: median costs fell from €14,843 to €11,573 (p&lt;0.00001). Interestingly, even among patients with a high burden of cardiac and non-cardiac comorbidities—such as baseline right heart failure and chronic kidney disease—the center’s volume did not demonstrate a volume–outcome relationship. Conclusion In this real-world German cohort, frailty and non-cardiac comorbidity burden, rather than age, were the dominant predictors of long-term mortality after T-TEER. The procedure was associated with a meaningful reduction in subsequent medical costs at one year. These findings support prioritizing frailty and multimorbidity assessment in patient selection and health-economic planning for T-TEER.
title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve repair: long-term survival and economic implications in a German real-world cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation was long considered a benign or secondary condition and was therefore often left untreated. This dogma has been abandoned in recent years. Tricuspid valve disease is now recognised as an independent predictor of morbidity and mortality and has become a field of extensive research activity, particularly in transcatheter therapies. Yet surgical tricuspid valve interventions, historically associated with high perioperative mortality, continue to play a crucial role in the treatment of tricuspid valve disease. Contemporary nationwide data on surgical practice and outcomes in the era of transcatheter therapies remain limited. Purpose The aim of this study was to evaluate national trends in comorbidities, surgical management and in-hospital outcomes of patients undergoing tricuspid valve surgery in Germany from 2011 to 2023. Methods This study is based on data from the German Diagnosis-Related Groups database. All inpatient cases undergoing tricuspid valve surgery between 2011 and 2023 were identified. Using ICD-10-GM and OPS codes, data on procedures, comorbidities and outcomes were obtained and statistically analysed. Results Between 2011 and 2023, 47,297 patients (46% female; median age 71 years) underwent tricuspid valve surgery in Germany. Annual surgical volumes remained stable over the study period (p=0.10). Over time, the mean age declined significantly (p&lt;0.001). Most patients had severe comorbidities, particularly cardiovascular conditions (65.5% hypertension, 65.6% congestive heart failure, 73.2% atrial fibrillation or flutter). The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (28.9%) and liver disease (2.3%), both markers of end-organ damage, decreased significantly over time (p&lt;0.001). The most common documented aetiology was non-rheumatic tricuspid regurgitation (58.5%). Rheumatic tricuspid regurgitation was less frequent (13.7%) but significantly increasing over time (p=0.004). Infective endocarditis accounted for 2.8% of cases. The predominant procedure was tricuspid valve annuloplasty (83%). Valve replacement was performed in 8% of patients. Overall, in-hospital mortality was 12%. Mortality and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events declined significantly over time. Mortality in complex procedures including tricuspid valve surgery, left-sided valve surgery and coronary artery bypass grafting was significantly higher (20%) than in isolated tricuspid valve surgery (6%). Conclusions In Germany, surgical tricuspid valve volumes remained stable from 2011 to 2023 despite the rapid expansion of transcatheter therapies. Most patients present with severe comorbidities. The prevalence of infective endocarditis was substantially lower than previously reported. Although perioperative outcomes improved, in-hospital mortality remains considerable, particularly in complex combined procedures. These findings highlight the need for careful timing, patient selection and risk stratification.
title: National trends and in-hospital outcomes of tricuspid valve surgery in Germany from 2011 to 2023

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with torrential tricuspid regurgitation (TR; grade V of V) represent a particularly high-risk subgroup with advanced right-sided heart disease and pronounced structural remodeling. Despite growing experience with transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER), the clinical phenotype, procedural complexity, and outcome determinants in this subgroup remain insufficiently characterized. Large-scale real-world registries provide an opportunity to better define these features. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing T-TEER enrolled in the multicenter EuroTR registry (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06307262) were analyzed. Tricuspid regurgitation severity was graded using a five-grade scheme, with torrential TR defined as grade V of V. Baseline clinical, echocardiographic, procedural, and invasive hemodynamic characteristics, as well as outcomes, were compared between patients with torrential versus non-torrential TR (grades III–IV of V). Clinical outcomes included functional status, heart failure rehospitalization, and all-cause mortality during follow-up. Results Among 2,846 patients undergoing T-TEER, 580 (20.4%) presented with torrential TR. Baseline age, BMI, and overall comorbidity burden were comparable; however, patients with torrential TR more frequently had right ventricular pacemaker leads (32.4 vs. 26.8%, p=0.008) and atrial fibrillation (93.2 vs. 89.4%, p=0.008). Echocardiography demonstrated more advanced right heart remodeling, including larger right ventricular end-systolic area (18.0 [13.5–22.4] vs. 15.0 [11.4–20.0] cm², p&lt;0.001) and tricuspid annular diameter (46.0 [41.0–50.0] vs. 43.0 [38.0–48.0] mm, p&lt;0.001), while TAPSE was similar. Invasive hemodynamics showed higher right atrial pressures and v-waves (both p&lt;0.001), accompanied by laboratory signs of more advanced hepatic congestion. Procedural complexity was higher in patients with torrential TR, reflected by a greater number of implanted devices and longer procedure times (both p&lt;0.001). Acute echocardiographic outcomes were less favorable, with lower rates of TR ≤ mild (22.0 vs. 52.8%) and higher residual TR≥3+ at discharge (39.3 vs. 11.6%; p&lt;0.001). Despite comparable functional improvement and heart failure rehospitalization rates, torrential TR was associated with higher 2-year all-cause mortality (p=0.032). Conclusion In this large real-world registry, torrential TR was associated with more advanced right-sided remodeling, greater procedural complexity, and higher long-term mortality after T-TEER. While symptomatic benefit can be achieved, these findings underscore the importance of careful patient selection and expectation management in this challenging population.
