title: Torrential tricuspid regurgitation and outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair: Insights from the EuroTR registry

abstract: Abstract Background Randomized trials of transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) show marked symptomatic improvement in severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), yet the relationship between early patient-reported benefit and subsequent clinical outcomes remains unclear. Purpose To characterize the trajectory of health-status improvement after T-TEER and determine whether early change predicts long-term heart-failure hospitalization (HFH) and major events. Methods TRI-FR randomized 300 patients with severe symptomatic TR to T-TEER plus optimized medical therapy (OMT) or OMT alone. Health status was assessed by Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ), Minnesota Living with Heart Failure (MLHF), and Patient Global Assessment (PGA) at baseline through extended follow-up (mean 40 months). Mixed-effects models evaluated between-group differences over time. Associations between 6-week KCCQ change and subsequent clinical outcomes (HFH, tricuspid surgery, cardiovascular death) were tested using Cox and Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying recurrent-event models. Results T-TEER produced rapid and sustained health-status improvement versus OMT. At 12 months, KCCQ-OS was higher with T-TEER (66.2 vs 56.8; Δ +9.5 points, p &lt; 0.001) and MLHF lower (27.5 vs 36.0; Δ −8.5, p = 0.001). Benefits persisted through 3 years (ΔKCCQ +8.5, p = 0.014). PGA favored T-TEER (probability of better status &gt; 0.70). Early KCCQ improvement predicted outcomes only in the T-TEER arm: each 10-point increase at 6 weeks reduced risk of first HFH/surgery/CV death (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.73–1.00) and recurrent HFH burden (rate ratio 0.85, 95% CI 0.73–0.99; interaction p = 0.005). Overall, T-TEER reduced recurrent HFHs versus OMT (28 vs 45 events).(fig1) Conclusions In severe TR, T-TEER induces early and durable improvement in patient-reported health status. Early KCCQ gain identifies patients with subsequent reduction in HF hospitalizations, linking symptomatic benefit to modification of clinical trajectory. These findings support health-status response as an early surrogate of long-term benefit after tricuspid intervention.fig 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Early health-status improvement after transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair predicts long-term reduction in heart-failure hospitalizations: insights from theTRI-FR randomized trial

abstract: Abstract Background Secondary tricuspid regurgitation (STR) comprises two distinct phenotypes: atrial STR (ASTR), driven by right atrial dilatation with preserved RV function, and ventricular STR (VSTR), characterised by RV remodeling and leaflet tethering. Whether STR phenotype influences outcomes following T-TEER remains incompletely defined, limiting the ability to tailor patient selection and optimize intervention timing. Aim To compare baseline characteristics, procedural outcomes, and short-term clinical results of patients with ASTR versus VSTR undergoing T-TEER in a real-world, two-centre European cohort. Methods Consecutive patients with severe STR undergoing T-TEER at two tertiary referral centers - were retrospectively analyzed. ASTR was defined as severe STR with preserved LVEF (≥50%), normal RV function, absence of significant left-sided valvular disease, and low pulmonary pressures (sPAP ≤50 mmHg), consistent with a predominantly atrial and annular mechanism. All remaining patients were classified as VSTR. Exclusion criteria were primary (organic) TR and TR attributable to a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) lead. The primary endpoint was procedural success (TR reduction to ≤2+) and clinical success at 1 month (TVARC criteria). The secondary endpoint was mortality and HF hospitalization at 3 months. Results A total of 71 patients were included (ASTR n=17, 23.9%; VSTR n=54, 76.1%). Baseline characteristics are summarized in Table 1. Mean age was 75.3±10.7 years; 35.2% were male and 84.5% had atrial fibrillation. ASTR patients exhibited significantly higher LVEF (67.2±9.6% vs 58.0±9.5%, p=0.001), better TAPSE (20.8±3.9 vs 18.0±4.2 mm, p=0.020), and lower sPAP (39.2±6.9 vs 51.4±17.5 mmHg, p&lt;0.0005), with no differences in age, TRI-SCORE, EuroSCORE II, or renal function. The most frequently used device was PASCAL (88.2% in ASTR vs 68.5% in VSTR), followed by Triclip (11.8% vs 31.5%). Procedural success at 24h was comparable between groups (88.2% vs 92.6%, p=0.625), as was 1-month clinical success (88.2% vs 87.0%, p=1.000). ASTR achieved a higher rate of in-hospital TR reduction to ≤1+ (82.4% vs 55.7%, p=0.042). At 3 months, diuretic dose reduction was numerically more frequent in ASTR (44.4% vs 18.8%, p=0.165). Mortality (0% vs 15%, p=0.177) and HF hospitalization (9.1% vs 35.0%, p=0.115) trended favorably in ASTR. Conclusions T-TEER demonstrated comparable procedural success across both phenotypes, confirming suitability regardless of etiology. ASTR patients achieved a significantly higher rate of TR reduction to ≤1+ at discharge (82.4% vs 55.7%, p=0.042). No significant differences were observed in mortality or HF hospitalization. Routine STR phenotyping before T-TEER is strongly encouraged, and prospective validation in larger phenotype-stratified cohorts is warranted.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Atrial versus ventricular secondary tricuspid regurgitation in patients undergoing tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: a two-centre european cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently coexist, and renal function improvement has been observed following treatment with tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER). However, the prognostic relevance of such improvement remains unclear and large-scale data are scarce. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the incidence and prognostic impact of renal function improvement in patients with CKD undergoing T-TEER. Methods We analysed patients undergoing T-TEER for symptomatic TR in the multicentre, real-world EuroTR registry (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation). Only patients with prevalent CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] &lt;60ml/min/1.73m2) with available eGFR at baseline and discharge were included. Patients were stratified according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO)-CKD stages (G3a: eGFR 45-59, G3b: 30-44, G4: 15-29, G5: &lt;15 ml/min/1.73m2). Renal function improvement was defined as a ≥1 stage improvement from baseline to discharge. Associations between renal function improvement and 2-year outcomes (all-cause mortality and the composite of mortality or heart failure hospitalization [HFH]) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazard models. Predictors of renal function improvement were evaluated using logistic regression. Results A total of 903 patients with CKD undergoing T-TEER were included (G3a: n=287, G3b: n=386, G4: n=184, G5: n=46). Renal function improvement occurred in 35.5% (n=321), whereas 64.5% (n=582) showed no improvement (Figure 1). Improvement rates were numerically higher among patients achieving a 3-grade TR reduction (44.7%) compared with those with 2- or 1-grade reduction (34.9% and 36.2%, respectively, p=0.35). In Kaplan-Meier analysis, 2-year all-cause mortality was 26.4% in patients with vs. 35.6% in those without renal function improvement (p=0.060, Figure 1). Corresponding rates for the composite endpoint were 44.2% and 53.7%, respectively (p = 0.12). In multivariable Cox regression, renal function improvement was independently associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.52-0.97, p=0.030) and the composite endpoint (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59-0.96, p=0.020) at 2 years. Lower body mass index was independently associated with renal function improvement (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.94-1.00, p=0.027). Conclusions Renal function improvement occurs in more than one third of patients with TR and CKD undergoing T-TEER and is associated with more favourable clinical outcomes at 2-years. These findings emphasize the potential impact of TR treatment in patients with advanced CKD, warranting further investigation into renal function as a therapeutic target and prognostic surrogate after T-TEER.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Prognostic impact of renal function improvement following tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: Insights from the EuroTR Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a relatively frequent and under-treated condition, particularly in elderly and high-risk patients, whom this condition significantly decrease life expectancy and QoL on, considering the heavy consequences of surgical treatment and the high rate of procedure-related adverse events. Recently transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) has emerged as a promising alternative for patients unsuitable for traditional surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) due to high risk of complications. However, comprehensive data on its efficacy and safety remain limited. Aim To evaluate the clinical outcomes, echocardiographic impact and complication rates in a large contemporary cohort of patients undergoing orthotopic TTVR. Searching methods This metanalysis was conducted according to Cochrane Collaborations and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statements. Searches were conducted up to 3 April 2025 in PubMed Central, Ovid EMBASE and Scopus databases, focusing on observational studies and RCTs that evaluated clinical and echocardiography impact on patients undergoing TTVR, as well as incidence of procedure-related adverse events. Results 13 studies published between 2020 and 2025 were analysed, including 12 observational study and 1 RCT, encompassing a total number of 827 patients. Primary outcomes included procedural success and incidence of all-cause mortality at the latest follow-up. Secondary outcomes were divided in safety outcomes, focusing on incidence of adverse events selected according to TVARC criteria, and efficacy outcomes, including TR reduction, as long as echocardiographic remodelling, and symptom improvement. Data were pooled using random-effects models. The average procedural success rate was 92.5%, with an all-cause mortality rate of 13.2% at a median 12-month follow-up (IQR 4.2-12.0). TTVR significantly improved NYHA class (RR 0.38), 6-minute walk distance (MD +99 m), and KCCQ score (MD +24.4). A marked reduction in severe or greater TR, RV dimensions, and pulmonary artery pressure was observed, without impact on LV and RV function but with significative impact on RV dimension. The most common adverse events were permanent pacemaker implantation (14.9%) and major bleeding (13.6%), while stroke, myocardial infarction, and device-related embolism were rare. Conclusions TTVR is a feasible and effective option for symptomatic TR patients at high surgical risk and unsuitable for T-TEER basing on anatomical or imaging limitations. It achieves significant symptomatic and hemodynamic improvement with an acceptable safety profile, being a useful tool to improve QoL and foavouring RV remodelling in a population not eligible for any other effective treatment.

title: Clinical, echocardiographic outcomes and complications after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR): a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) causes systemic venous and liver congestion promoting extracellular matrix expansion. Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV) quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is a non-invasive assessment of hepatic extracellular matrix remodeling and a prognostic marker of congestion which was recently shown to be associated with adverse outcomes in TR patients. The clinical impact of tricuspid intervention and the subsequent changes in TR severity following treatment with tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) on L-ECV has not been previously described. Methods TRILUMINATE Pivotal is the first randomized (1:1) trial evaluating T-TEER (TriClip) vs guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) alone in symptomatic, severe TR patients. A concurrent single-arm cohort enrolled patients with complex anatomy for T-TEER. A pre-specified, prospective multicentric imaging substudy was conducted at 10 sites, which included CMR and 4D-CT evaluation of cardiac anatomy and function at baseline and 30 days post-treatment, and a final 4D-CT at 1 year. L-ECV was assessed by identifying liver parenchyma on short-axis cardiac T1 mapping pre- and post-contrast carefully excluding artifacts and blood pool/vessels. Imaging was randomly analyzed by an independent core lab without knowledge of TR reduction. Results Forty-five patients with evaluable baseline L-ECV (mean age 78 years; 69% female; hypertension 78%; renal disease 31%; MELD-XI score 12 pts) were included (T-TEER=28, GDMT alone=17). Right-sided adverse cardiac remodeling was observed, with a right ventricular (RV) end-diastolic volume of 210 ± 81 mL, a right atrial (RA) end-diastolic volume of 176 ± 98 mL, and a mean tricuspid valve anatomic regurgitant orifice area of 83 ± 60 mm². Median (Q1, Q3) baseline L-ECV was 34% (31, 39). L-ECV was positively correlated with TR volume (r=0.50, p=0.0005), RV and RA end-diastolic volumes (r=0.54, p=0.0001 and r=0.35, p=0.02, respectively), and MELD-XI score (r=0.51, p=0.0004) at baseline. At 30 days, L-ECV decreased significantly in T-TEER treated patients (-2% on average, p=0.046), whereas in GDMT patients a significant increase was observed (+3% on average, p=0.007). Between-group difference favored T-TEER after adjusting for baseline L-ECV (p=0.0005). A greater proportion of T-TEER patients experienced L-ECV reduction (61% vs 25%), while most GDMT patients experienced an increase (63% vs 30%). Of note, traditional liver biomarkers including ALT, AST and bilirubin showed no significant changes over time in either treatment group. Conclusions In the TRILUMINATE Pivotal imaging substudy, most patients with severe TR who received T-TEER with TriClip had demonstrable improvement of L-ECV within 30-days. L-ECV improvement associated with TR reduction and RV reverse remodeling provides additional objective evidence supporting the clinical benefit of T-TEER in these patients.
title: Liver extracellular volume improves after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention: seminal insights from TRILUMINATE Pivotal imaging substudy

abstract: Abstract Background Risk stratification after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) remains challenging, as prognosis is driven by systemic congestion and multiorgan dysfunction rather than residual regurgitation alone. Biomarkers reflecting systemic stress (GDF-15), hepatorenal dysfunction (MELD-XI), and right-sided hemodynamics (right atrial [RA] pressure) have individually shown prognostic relevance, but have not been integrated into a unified model. Purpose To derive and assess the discriminatory performance of the TRIO Score integrating RA pressure, MELD-XI, and GDF-15 for prediction of 12-month mortality after TTVI. Methods In a prospective single-centre cohort, 131 consecutive patients undergoing TTVI were included. Baseline assessment comprised invasive right heart catheterisation and laboratory testing. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 12 months. The TRIO Score was derived from a multivariable logistic regression model integrating RA pressure, MELD-XI, and GDF-15. Discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis (AUC with 95% confidence intervals). Survival was additionally analysed using Kaplan–Meier estimates across TRIO tertiles. Results Median age was 82 years; 44% were female, and PASCAL was the predominant device used, Table 1. During 12-month follow-up, 22 patients (16.8%) died. The TRIO model demonstrated strong discrimination for 12-month mortality (AUC 0.829, 95% CI 0.726–0.931; p&lt;0.001), Figure 1. Discriminatory performance of the individual components was lower: GDF-15 AUC 0.789 (0.670–0.909; p&lt;0.001), RA pressure AUC 0.708 (0.588–0.828; p=0.005), and MELD-XI AUC 0.665 (0.512–0.819; p=0.021). Mortality increased stepwise across TRIO tertiles, with highest risk observed in the upper tertile (log-rank p&lt;0.001). Conclusion The TRIO Score demonstrated strong discrimination and clinically meaningful risk stratification for 12-month mortality after TTVI, integrating right-sided hemodynamics, organ dysfunction, and systemic stress signalling.table1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: TRIO score for risk stratification of 12-month mortality after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention

abstract: Abstract Background In severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension (PH) drive adverse outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid valve edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER). RV-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling is a key prognostic marker; however, pulmonary arterial compliance (PAC) reflects pulsatile RV afterload and integrates pulmonary vascular load with RV–PA interaction and may therefore provide additional prognostic value. Purpose To define the clinical and hemodynamic profile associated with reduced PAC and to evaluate the prognostic value of PAC ≤2.0 mL/mmHg in patients undergoing T-TEER. Methods This retrospective two-center study included 389 patients with significant TR undergoing T-TEER. PAC was invasively calculated as stroke volume divided by pulmonary artery pulse pressure. Patients were stratified according to PAC &gt;2.0 versus ≤2.0 mL/mmHg. Two-year survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier estimates and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, comorbidities, procedural success, and RV-PA coupling expressed as the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure (TAPSE/PASP). Results Reduced PAC was present in 191 patients (49%). These patients were older, more frequently female, and had higher NT-proBNP levels. Echocardiography showed higher pulmonary pressures and impaired RV-PA coupling (TAPSE/PASP 0.34 vs. 0.42 mm/mmHg; p&lt;0.001), while left-ventricular function and TR severity were similar. Invasive hemodynamics revealed a distinct adverse profile with higher pulmonary artery pressures, pulmonary vascular resistance (3.3 vs. 1.9 WU), and transpulmonary gradient, together with lower stroke volume (46 vs. 61 mL) and cardiac index (1.9 vs. 2.2 L/min/m²; all p&lt;0.001). Procedural success and residual TR did not differ between groups. During follow-up, 99 deaths occurred; PAC ≤2.0 mL/mmHg was associated with reduced survival (log-rank p=0.001) and predicted mortality (HR 1.69; 95% CI 1.06–2.68; p=0.026), independent of other prognostically relevant covariates, including TAPSE/PASP. Conclusions In patients undergoing T-TEER, reduced PAC identifies a high-risk hemodynamic phenotype characterized by increased pulmonary vascular load and impaired RV-PA interaction. Procedural success after T-TEER is comparable between patients with and without impaired PAC. PAC provides incremental prognostic information beyond RV-PA coupling and may refine risk stratification in this high-risk population.Kaplan–Meier estimator plotFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Pulmonary arterial compliance independently predicts mortality after transcatheter tricuspid valve edge-to-edge repair

abstract: Abstract Background Biomarker trajectories following transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) remain insufficiently characterized. Interpretation of natriuretic peptides in this population is challenging due to frequent renal dysfunction and cardiorenal syndrome. Soluble ST2 (sST2) provides prognostic information independent of renal function and natriuretic peptides. Complementary biomarkers reflecting systemic stress, inflammation, and myocardial injury were assessed in parallel to contextualize biological response after TTVI. Purpose To characterize serial changes of sST2 and compare its longitudinal dynamics with other stress and inflammation biomarkers after TTVI. Methods In a prospective single-centre cohort, 135 patients undergoing TTVI were included. sST2, GDF-15, suPAR, H-FABP, and NT-proANP were measured at baseline, discharge, 3 months, and 12 months. Longitudinal changes were analysed using paired non-parametric comparisons. Results The cohort was elderly (median age 82 years), with high prevalence of atrial fibrillation and advanced right heart failure. sST2 exhibited a distinct biphasic trajectory, with significant increase from baseline to discharge (n=135; p=0.004), followed by significant reduction at 3 months (n=124; p=0.003) and sustained decline at 12 months (n=82; p&lt;0.0001).GDF-15 showed no significant longitudinal change. suPAR demonstrated early reduction at discharge (p&lt;0.001) and 3 months (p=0.004), without sustained decline at 12 months (p=0.895). H-FABP decreased only at 12 months (p=0.007), whereas NT-proANP showed no consistent dynamic pattern. Conclusion Among the biomarkers assessed, sST2 exhibited the most consistent longitudinal trajectory following TTVI. This dynamic pattern suggests potential utility for monitoring biological response in this population and warrants further validation in independent cohorts.Table1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Soluble ST2 as a dynamic biomarker of biological response after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention

abstract: Abstract Objectives Right atrial–right ventricular (RA–RV) coupling may represent the central mechanism linking atrial remodeling, ventricular adaptation, and systemic congestion in severe functional tricuspid regurgitation (TR). We investigated the longitudinal behavior and clinical significance of RA–RV coupling after transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER). Background Clinical recovery after T-TEER is heterogeneous and incompletely explained by residual TR severity or right ventricular–pulmonary arterial (RV–PA) coupling, suggesting that post-repair physiology extends beyond ventriculo-arterial interaction alone. Methods In 131 consecutive patients undergoing T-TEER (median age 77 years; 61% women), comprehensive echocardiography was obtained at baseline, pre-discharge, 6 months, and 12 months. RA–RV coupling was quantified by RV systolic function normalized to right-atrial size (primary: RV strain/RAVImax). RV–PA coupling served as comparator. Longitudinal mixed-effects models, ordinal regression for residual TR, and decongestion phenotyping were applied. Results RA–RV coupling exhibited a biphasic trajectory with early deterioration after repair followed by partial recovery, whereas RV–PA coupling showed weaker and less consistent dynamics. RA–RV indices demonstrated greater patient-level stability than RV–PA metrics. In multivariable longitudinal models, RA strain and RA–RV coupling independently tracked NT-proBNP trajectories, whereas RV–PA coupling did not. Impaired baseline RA–RV coupling predicted higher residual TR at 6 months and lower probability of combined biological and symptomatic decongestion. At 12 months, RA strain emerged as the dominant correlate of residual TR severity, consistent with progressive atrial substrate influence. Conclusions After T-TEER, recovery is governed predominantly by atrioventricular mechanical efficiency rather than ventriculo-arterial interaction alone. RA–RV coupling integrates atrial remodeling, ventricular adaptation, and systemic congestion, providing a mechanistic framework for phenotyping and risk stratification beyond TR reduction.Determinants of Residual TR After T-TEERFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Central IllustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Right atrial–right ventricular coupling drives decongestion and residual regurgitation after transcatheter tricuspid repair

abstract: Abstract Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions (TTVI) are commonly employed in severe tricuspid valvulopathy in patients with high surgical risk. Up to a third of patients undergoing TTVI will also have a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED), which may increase the risk of both developing TR and the complications of TTVI. However, there have been no meta-analyses conducted assessing the influence of CIEDs on TTVI outcomes. Purpose To compare the clinical safety and efficacy of TTVI in patients with CIED versus without CIEDs. Methods PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Embase were systematically searched for randomised and non-randomised studies on the topic. Studies reporting data on TTVI outcomes stratified by CIED status were included. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted, using the Mantel-Haenszel method and a random-effects model, reporting risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for all dichotomous outcomes. The primary outcome was in-hospital procedural mortality. Results 10 studies (n=6,664) were included in the systematic review, with data from 7 studies (n=5,427) included in the meta-analysis, with a focus on in-hospital and 30 day follow-up data. 3 studies were not included in the meta-analysis due to a lack of compatible data. Procedural mortality was not significantly different (RR 1.17; 95% CI 0.48-2.86). Residual TR moderate or worse (RR 1.12; 95% CI 0.97-1.30), successful device implantation (RR 1.00; 95% CI 0.95-1.06), major bleeding (RR 0.81; 95% CI 0.51-1.29), re-intervention (RR 1.20; 95% CI 0.67-2.13), stroke (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.16-3.61), heart failure hospitalization (RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.71-1.48), patients ≤NYHA Class 2 (RR 1.00; 95% CI 0.91-1.09), and 1-year all-cause mortality (RR 1.23; 95% CI 0.86-1.74) were not significantly different. Residual TR severe or worse was more frequent in the CIED group (RR 1.38; 95% CI 1.03-1.84). Conclusion CIED status is not associated with a significantly higher early or late mortality, reduced procedural success, or major adverse events after TTVI. The increased risk of severe or worse residual TR suggests possible decreased efficacy of TR attenuation in patients with CIED.Successful Dev. title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are common in patients with cardiovascular disease, particularly heart failure, and are associated with impaired functional status and adverse outcomes. Patients undergoing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) represent a high-risk population with heterogeneous clinical trajectories. However, the prognostic relevance of anemia and ID in patients treated with T-TEER remains poorly defined. Purpose This study evaluated the association of baseline anemia and ID with clinical outcomes after T-TEER using data from a large, multicenter registry. Methods The Euro-TR (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation) registry includes 3,048 patients undergoing T-TEER between 2016 and 2022. For this analysis, 2945 patients with available hemoglobin status were included. Anemia was defined according to World Health Organization criteria (hemoglobin &lt;12g/L in women and &lt;13g/L in men). In a subgroup of 476 patients with available ferritin and transferrin measurements, iron deficiency (ID) was defined according to guideline-recommended threshold. The primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure rehospitalization (HFH). Kaplan–Meier analyses and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between anemia, ID, and outcomes. Results Among 2945 patients (median age: 80 [IQR 76-83] years; 45.7% male; median EuroSCORE II: 4.5% [IQR 2.6-7.7], anemia was highly prevalent (57.2%). Patients with anemia had worse baseline functional status and showed less functional improvement following T-TEER (NYHA improvement ≥ 1 stage 61.1% vs. 54.0%, p = 0.004). Anemia was independently associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR = 2.11; 95%-CI [1.69-2.63], p &lt; 0.001 and with the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or HFH (HR = 2.01; 95%-CI [1.68-2.39, p &lt; 0.001) at 3 years follow-up even after adjustment for relevant comorbidities (sex, BMI, LVEF, CKD, AFib). Although ID was highly prevalent in the subgroup with available ferritin and transferrin saturation measurements (318/476 patients, 66.8%), it was not associated with either endpoint. Conclusion Baseline anemia, but not iron deficiency, identifies patients undergoing T-TEER at higher risk of adverse events. As an easily available and routinely measured parameter, hemoglobin may support risk stratification and complex clinical decision-making, while these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective evaluation.Kaplan Meier EstimatesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Anemia but not iron deficiency predicts outcomes after tricuspid edge-to-edge repair: insights from the Euro-TR registry

abstract: Abstract Background Right ventricular (RV) adaptation after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains poorly characterized, particularly following complete tricuspid regurgitation (TR) elimination. Purpose To characterize the acute and early RV functional response following orthotopic TTVR with two of the most widely adopted systems (EVOQUE and LuX-Valve Plus), and evaluate its prognostic implications. Methods multicenter cohort of consecutive patients undergoing TTVR with EVOQUE (n=49) or LuX-Valve Plus (n=18) systems from 2019 to 2025. Intraprocedural and pre-discharge changes in RV size and function were assessed by core-lab echocardiography.Load-independent metrics of RV contractility (end-systolic elastance, Ees), afterload (arterial elastance, Ea) and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive pressure–volume loop analysis. Predictors of all-cause mortality at follow-up were analyzed. Results Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years [IQR: 73-84], 72% female, 76% NYHA ≥III) achieved near-complete TR reduction (grade 5 [IQR 4–5] to 1 [IQR 0–1], p&lt;0.001) with both devices. Baseline RV contractility (Ees) and afterload (Ea) were comparable among both cohorts. Parameters of longitudinal (RV free-wall longitudinal strain, RV-FWLS: -10.8% [95% confidence interval, CI: −8.5 to −12.2], RV global longitudinal strain by −8.7% [95% CI: −6.5 to −10.8] and radial function (RV-fractional area change [RV-FAC]:−13.6% [95% CI: −11.4 to −15.8]) declined intraprocedurally, irrespective of TTVR design. The reduction in RV-FAC was primarily driven by a significant increase in RV-end systolic area (mean absolute increase: 3.6 cm2 [95%CI: 2.4 to 4.8]), consistent with an acute increase in afterload. At discharge, decline in RV function metrics persisted (Figure 1) and 39 (58%) patients fulfilled criteria for severe RV dysfunction according to the criteria proposed in the 2025 ESC/EACTS Guidelines for the Management of Valvular Heart Disease. At a median follow-up of 13.9 months (IQR 7.8–21.9), all-cause mortality was 20.6% and was not associated with device design, early RV functional changes, or load-independent metrics. Patients with baseline global impairment of longitudinal (TAPSE &lt;17 mm and/or RV-FWLS &lt; 23%) and radial (RV-FAC&lt;35%) function exhibited higher mortality (log-rank P=0.001; Figure 2). Conclusions TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function metrics, regardless of device anchoring mechanisms. Although common, early RV deterioration does not predict mid-term mortality. Figure 1. Changes in right ventricular longitudinal function assessed by TAPSE (A), RV-FWLS (B), RV-GLS (C). Panel D illustrate changes in RV radial function (RV-FAC). Figure 2. Kaplan–Meier curves showing all-cause mortality stratified by (A) TTVR device; (B) baseline RV-Ees (dichotomized at the median value), (C) baseline Ees/Ea (dichotomized at the median value) and (D) baseline RV contraction pattern.Figure 1.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Figure 2.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Acute impact on right ventricular function following orthotopic transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement. Insights from deformation imaging and non-invasive pressure–volume analysis

abstract: Abstract Background The Cardioband System enables direct annuloplasty as a minimally invasive technique to reduce the annular diameter and tricuspid regurgitation. Purpose The aim of this study was to analyse the patterns in the utilisation of the Cardioband System in Germany and compare them to the use of TEER. Methods The data used in this study were derived from the Diagnosis Related Groups (DRG) statistics (2021-2023) and accessed through the Research Data Center of the Federal Statistical Office of Germany. All German in-hospital cases coded for transvenous tricuspid annuloplasty were retrospectively analysed and compared with patients treated by TEER of the tricuspid valve. Results In Germany, 697 patients underwent the Cardioband procedure; 64.1% were female. Patients treated by TEER were also predominantly female, at a rate of 58.7%, in a total of 9,274. In both treatment groups, most patients were between 80 and 85 years old, representing 267 (38.3%) in the Cardioband group and 3,618 (39.0%) in the TEER group. No differences were observed in mortality rates (1.7% vs 1.7%). However, Cardioband patients subsequently received more intensive care: 23.5% compared to 17.6% treated by TEER. The use of the Cardioband device was highest in Berlin (2.4 per 100,000) and North Rhine-Westphalia (1.7 per 100,000), while TEER procedures were most frequent in Hamburg (30.8 per 100,000) and Thuringia (21 per 100,000). In 2023, a total of 40 hospitals performed Cardioband procedures, 37 of which treated fewer than 12 patients during that year. In contrast, TEER interventions were carried out in 174 hospitals, ranging from 1–12 procedures in 75 centres to more than 52 in 16 centres. Conclusions Significant differences in baseline characteristics and in-hospital outcomes were observed between patients undergoing Cardioband and TEER procedures for tricuspid valve repair, which may provide a better understanding of the target group of the Cardioband procedure. In addition, differences were found in the utilisation across the federal states of Germany and in the number of centres performing the procedures.
title: The cardioband system: utilisation and treatment trends in Germany based on national in-hospital data

abstract: Abstract Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation causes disabling symptoms and predicts adverse outcomes independently of left-sided disease. Transcatheter tricuspid interventions have emerged as minimally invasive therapies; however, their benefit compared with optimized medical therapy remains uncertain. Conventional meta-analyses provide dichotomous statistical conclusions, which may limit clinical interpretability. Purpose To perform a Bayesian meta-analysis of randomized trials comparing transcatheter tricuspid interventions versus optimized medical therapy to quantify the probability of benefit and harm and better inform clinical decision-making. Methods A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases for studies evaluating transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) compared with optimized medical therapy (OMT). Primary outcomes included NYHA functional class improvement and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) score. Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses were performed in R (version 4.5.1) using the bayesmeta package, applying a weakly informative normal prior for the overall effect and a half-normal prior for heterogeneity. Posterior probabilities of benefit were calculated as P(RR &gt; 1) for binary outcomes and P(MD &gt; 0) for continuous outcomes. Results Four randomized controlled trials, encompassing 1,292 patients (710 TTVI vs 582 OMT), with a mean age of 78.6 years (78.6 TTVI vs 78.5 OMT), were analyzed. Atrial fibrillation and hypertension were the most prevalent comorbidities and 57.7% of patients were in NYHA III/IV (59.2% TTVI and 56.0% OMT). At one year, TTVI significantly improved health-related quality of life (KCCQ) compared with OMT (MD 13.28 points; 95% CrI 9.89–16.62; P(MD &gt; 0) 100%; I²=69.4%) and increased the likelihood of NYHA functional class improvement (RR 2.07; 95% CrI 1.09–3.89; P(RR &gt; 1): 98.9%; I²=76.6%). Although heterogeneity was high for both outcomes, prior sensitivity analyses did not demonstrate any meaningful impact on the results. TTVI also reduced tricuspid regurgitation severity (RR 7.71; 95% CrI 4.76–12.42; P(RR &gt; 1): 100%; I²=11%). No evident differences were observed in heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.89; 95% CrI 0.53–1.47; P(RR &lt; 1): 68.1%; I²=0%), all-cause mortality (RR 1.21; 95% CrI 0.78–1.87; P(RR &lt; 1): 19.5%; I²=0%), or cardiovascular mortality (RR 1.07; 95% CrI 0.62–1.83; P(RR &lt; 1): 40.1%; I²=0%). Conclusion Transcatheter tricuspid intervention provides clear symptomatic benefit, but current randomized evidence shows no reduction in mortality or heart failure hospitalization compared with medical therapy, likely due to small sample sizes and short follow-up duration. These findings support intervention for quality-of-life improvement in symptomatic patients, while highlighting that survival benefit may require longer follow-up to emerge.FIGURE 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.FIGURE 2.Secondary OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention versus medical therapy in severe tricuspid regurgitation: a systematic review and bayesian meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is associated with high morbidity and mortality, yet surgical treatment is often deferred due to elevated operative risk. Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has emerged as a less invasive therapeutic alternative. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate clinical, echocardiographic, and safety outcomes after T-TEER. Methods Following PRISMA and Cochrane recommendations, PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus were searched through June 10, 2025. Randomized and observational studies including ≥20 patients undergoing T-TEER were eligible. Primary endpoints were procedural success and all-cause mortality at latest follow-up. Secondary endpoints included T-VARC-defined safety outcomes, functional status, quality of life, and echocardiographic parameters. Random-effects models were applied. Results Thirty-two studies (3 RCTs, 29 observational) including 7,563 patients were analyzed. Patients were elderly (median age 78 years), predominantly female (57%), and highly symptomatic (87.5% NYHA III–IV; 97.6% ≥ severe TR; median LVEF 56%). Procedural success was achieved in 87.0% of cases. T-TEER significantly reduced severe TR (RR 0.39, 95% CI 0.30–0.51; p&lt;0.001) and TR effective regurgitant orifice area (MD –0.37 cm²; p&lt;0.001), with concomitant reductions in right ventricular dimensions and inferior vena cava diameter, suggesting reverse right heart remodeling. A modest but significant decline in TAPSE and FAC was observed, while LVEF and sPAP remained unchanged. Functional status improved markedly, with fewer patients in NYHA III–IV (RR 0.44; p&lt;0.001), increased 6-minute walk distance (MD +42.4 m; p&lt;0.001), and higher KCCQ scores (MD +15.3 points; p&lt;0.001). At latest follow-up, all-cause mortality was 10.1% and cardiovascular mortality 6.9%. Stroke (1.5%), major vascular complications (0.8%), and need for tricuspid surgery (0.9%) were infrequent, whereas major bleeding occurred in 6.3%. Conclusions In a high-risk, predominantly symptomatic population with advanced TR, T-TEER provides high procedural success, significant reduction in regurgitation severity, reverse right heart remodeling, and meaningful improvements in functional capacity and quality of life, with acceptable safety outcomes. These findings support T-TEER as an effective therapeutic option in appropriately selected patients, although longer-term randomized evidence is needed.
title: Functional, echocardiographic outcomes and complications after Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair (T-TEER): a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Introduction Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) has emerged as a promising option for severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR), but real-world data outside pivotal trials are still limited. Purpose To evaluate procedural and 30-day outcomes of TTVR in a real-world Portuguese cohort. Methods Retrospective, single-center study including consecutive patients undergoing TTVR, between October 2024 and October 2025. Baseline characteristics, procedural metrics, and early clinical outcomes were collected. Results Eighteen patients were included (median age 79.5 [IQR 10.0] years; 44.4% male). TR was severe in 27.8%, massive in 16.7%, and torrential in 55.6%. TR etiology was mixed primary/functional in 44.4%, followed by atrial/ventricular functional TR in 38.9%. Degenerative disease (5 cases), valve prolapse (2), and electrocatheter impingement (2) were the most frequent primary causes. Mean TRISCORE was 3.3±1.9, and 94.4% were in NYHA II–III. Median NT-proBNP was 1801.5 pg/mL (IQR 3084.8). Atrial fibrillation was present in 94.5%, and 16.7% had a previous pacemaker. Baseline right ventricle (RV) function included mean fractional area change (FAC) 39.8±7.0%, TAPSE 17.8±4.1mm, RV strain −19.3±3.5%, and TAPSE/sPAP 0.44±0.12. Right heart catheterization was performed in 94.4%, revealing pulmonary hypertension in 12 patients (27.8% precapillary, 22.2% postcapillary, 16.7% combined). Mean pulmonary artery pressure was 23.6±6.3mmHg and PCWP 15.6±5.7mmHg. Median procedural duration was 112.5 minutes (IQR 33.8). The 52-mm valve was the most used (38.9%). TR reduction was achieved in all patients: none/trace in 33.3%, mild in 55.6%, and moderate in 11.1%. Mean transprosthetic gradient was 3.2±1.1mmHg. Post-operative worsening of RV function was observed: RV strain −12.4±3.7% (p&lt;0.001), TAPSE 10.9±3.9mm (p&lt;0.001), and FAC 25.4±7.6% (p&lt;0.001). Procedural complications included one cardiac tamponade and one acute heart failure requiring inotropes. No in-hospital mortality occurred. Median hospitalization was 4.5 days (IQR 2.3). At 30 days, two patients required pacemaker implantation for complete heart block (2/15 patients, 13.3%), two were rehospitalized for heart failure (11.1%), one had a transient ischemic attack, and one was hospitalized for access-site hematoma. Conclusions Our center experience aligns with TRISCEND-II, supporting the safety and efficacy of TTVR in real-world practice. Notably, the pacemaker implantation rate was substantially lower than the 24.7% reported in TRISCEND-II. These findings reinforce the expanding role of TTVR as a viable therapeutic option for severe symptomatic TR.TR reductionFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Early portuguese experience with TTVR: procedural and early outcomes

abstract: Abstract Introduction Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement (TTVR) is a minimally invasive treatment for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). While significant improvement in quality-of-life post-intervention has been demonstrated, the post-procedural changes in right ventricular (RV) morphology and physiology are poorly understood. Purpose To determine RV morphological changes post-intervention and their association with changes in cardiac function and pulmonary pressures. Secondary aim was to explore associations between changes in the latter 2. Methods This is a single-centre observational analysis of patients who underwent TTVR for symptomatic ≥ severe TR at a specialist referral centre from June 2024 to September 2025. Routine 2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) at timepoints: pre-procedure, &lt;48hrs, 1-3 and 5-9 months was used. Associations in TTE-measured RV size, function, PASP and cardiac output (CO) were analysed using univariate Pearson’s or Kendall’s Tau correlation coefficient as appropriate, and temporal changes in parameters with paired t-tests. Results 19 patients underwent TTVR: 12 (63%) female, mean age 82 years (IQR 79-84). Pre-intervention, 26% had severe, 26% massive and 47% torrential TR. Post-intervention all patients had ≤mild-moderate TR, with 100% procedural success and no conversion to surgery. Significant RV reverse remodelling was seen by 5-9 months (Fig. 1). Decrease in RV base diameter trended towards significance at 1-3 months (p=0.114). RV mid diameter significantly declined from baseline by 5-9 months (p=0.002). Similarly, a significant decline in RV end diastolic area (EDA) at 1–3 months was seen (p=0.036). RV end systolic area (ESA) increased significantly at 1-3 months (p=0.034), later decreasing; however, baseline to 5-9 months slightly increased without significance (p=0.143). RV length shows similar trends. A significant decline in RV function was seen by 5-9 months: TAPSE (p&lt;0.001), RV S’ (p=0.005), FAC (p&lt;0.001) and global RV function (p=0.005). Forward CO significantly increased from baseline (p=0.023). PASP saw a significant decline (p=0.05). Baseline PASP and RV-PA coupling (TAPSE/PASP) correlated with early RV reverse remodelling at 1-3 months (Tables 1 and 2), but not at 5-9 months. Curiously, there was no clear relationship between measures of RV function and output, and between RV output and RV-PA coupling. Conclusion This study shows significant changes in RV structure and function, forward CO and PASP post-TTVR. The changes in RV morphology, especially RV ESA and length, along with the corresponding changes in RV function, forward output and PASP, suggest two phases of reverse remodelling: initial unloading of the RV overload, followed by a later phase – perhaps myocardial muscle fibre shortening. A continuous decline in metrics of RV function was observed, while forward CO increased. Baseline PASP correlated with the extent of early reverse remodelling.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Right ventricular reverse remodelling and pulmonary pressure changes post-TTVR for tricuspid regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is present in about one-third of the population, and percutaneous PFO closure is recommended for the secondary prevention of cryptogenic stroke. Evidence suggests that patients with PFOs exhibit a prothrombotic phenotype, which is thought to be associated with an increased incidence of migraines and early-onset dementia. Percutaneous PFO closure has indeed been associated with improvements in migraine symptoms. However, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Aim The study aimed to investigate whether platelets are activated at the site of PFO due to a left-to-right shunt, and if so, whether this activation ceases after PFO closure. Methods This prospective, single-centre, observational study included patients undergoing percutaneous PFO closure between February 2024 and January 2026. Blood samples were collected from the right atrium before and immediately after closure. We assessed platelet activation by quantifying adenosine diphosphate (ADP)-stimulated CD62P (P-selectin) expression using flow cytometry. Migraine was classified according to the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) criteria, and severity was assessed using the Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS) questionnaire and the Headache Impact Test (HIT-6). Results A total of 125 patients were included in the study. Mean age was 51.2 years (± SD 11.9) and 76 patients (60.8%) were male. Of those, 21 patients had migraines (16.8%), 15 (71.4%) of whom were female and six (28.6%) of whom were male. ADP stimulation revealed significantly higher CD62P+ count in samples from the right atrium before device closure, compared to samples collected immediately after closure (p&lt;0.001), with a mean reduction of 6.2% (± SD 5.9; Figure 1). Further, multivariable linear regression analysis revealed a significant interaction between sex and migraine, indicating that female patients with migraines experienced a greater reduction in platelet activation following PFO closure (estimated effect size β=7.54, 95% CI 1.58–13.49, p = 0.014). Conclusion Left-to-right shunt, as occurs in PFO, leads to measurable changes in platelet activation that decrease significantly immediately after PFO closure. These findings are particularly relevant for female patients with migraines, because our data support a sex-specific mechanism in which women with migraines appear to have a greater biological benefit from PFO closure.Figure 1:Comparison of platelet activationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Shunt-related platelet activation in patients with patent foramen ovale

abstract: Abstract Background The optimal duration of antiplatelet therapy (APT) after patent foramen ovale (PFO) device closure remains uncertain. Objectives To evaluate the impact of APT duration on long-term outcomes after PFO closure. Methods This analysis of the PROLONG (PFO Transcatheter Occlusion Long-Term Outcomes National Group) registry included patients with successful PFO closure, no significant residual shunt, and no other indication for long-term antithrombotic therapy. Patients were categorized according to APT duration after PFO closure into a short-term (≤12 months) or long-term (&gt;12 months) strategy. The primary outcome was net adverse clinical events (NACE), defined as the composite of ischemic events (ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism) and major bleeding (BARC ≥3). A propensity score was developed, then inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied in HR estimation to account for confounders. Results Among 940 patients (mean age 47 ± 12 years; 55% women) followed for 14.0 ± 3.1 years, NACE occurred in 3.7% of those managed with a short-term and 6.3% with a long-term strategy (aHR 0.71; 95% CI 0.38–1.37; p=0.311). In subgroup analysis, short-term APT was associated with significantly lower NACE in patients with RoPE score ≥7 (aHR 0.32; 95% CI 0.11–0.90; p=0.039), but not in those with RoPE &lt;7 (aHR 1.07; 95% CI 0.49–2.35; p=0.891; p for interaction=0.089). Conclusions In patients with a RoPE score ≥7, early discontinuation of APT (within 12 months) after effective PFO closure was associated with a lower incidence of net adverse clinical events at long-term follow-up.AlgorithmFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.KM high ropeFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

title: Tailoring antiplatelet therapy duration after PFO closure: insights from the PROLONG registry

abstract: Abstract Aims Transcatheter patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure is an established treatment for patients with PFO and cryptogenic embolism. However, main randomized trials investigating PFO closure for secondary stroke prevention excluded patients older than 60 years. As a result, limited evidence is available for population. This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and long-term outcomes of elderly patients undergoing transcatheter PFO closure. Methods and results This retrospective multicenter registry included patients who underwent transcatheter PFO closure between between 1999 and 2013 at 13 high-volume Centers, ensuring a minimum of 10 years of follow-up. Patients receiving closure for secondary prevention of cryptogenic embolism were identified and stratified by age (&lt;60 vs. ≥60 years). Among 1,245 included patients, 216 (17.3%) were aged ≥60 years. Elderly patients exhibited higher rates of cardiovascular risk factors and a lower Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE) score (3.9±1.0 vs. 6.7±1.4, p&lt;0.001). In contrast, a history of migraine was more common in younger patients (33.7% vs. 21.8%, p&lt;0.001). Procedural success rates were high and comparable across age groups (98.6% vs. 99.2%, p=0.39). Rates of in-hospital atrial fibrillation (2.8% vs. 2.0%, p=0.50) and significant residual shunt at discharge (1.3% vs. 1.7%, p=0.75) were similarly low in both groups. At a median follow-up of 14.5 ± 2.4 years, the incidence of the composite endpoint (stroke, transient ischemic attack, and systemic embolism) was low among elderly patients (0.28 per 100 patient-years, 95% CI 0.12–0.55) and did not differ significantly from younger patients (IRR 1.58, 95% CI 0.75–3.50, p=0.25). However, older patients exhibited a higher incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (0.83 vs. 0.20 per 100 patient-years, IRR 4.10, 95% CI 2.37–7.01, p&lt;0.001) and bleeding events (0.30 vs. 0.06 per 100 patient-years, IRR 5.28, 95% CI 1.53–18.25, p=0.01). Conclusions In this large multicenter registry with extended follow-up, transcatheter PFO closure in older patients was safe and comparably effective to younger counterparts. Prospective data are warranted to confirm these observations and guide optimal management in this cohort.K-M curveFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.TableFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Long term outcomes of patent foramen ovale closure in elderly patients

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure is the gold-standard treatment for patients with cryptogenic embolism and PFO. While current guidelines recommend the use of intraprocedural echocardiography, there is no consensus on the optimal imaging strategy. Objectives To compare the procedural and clinical outcomes of fluoroscopy-only guidance versus echocardiographic guidance—transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or intracardiac echocardiography (ICE)—during transcatheter PFO closure. Methods The multicenter, retrospective PROLONG registry included 1,302 patients who underwent PFO closure between 1999 and 2013 with available data on intraprocedural guidance. Of these, 714 patients (55%) underwent TEE-guided procedures, 416 (32%) received ICE, and 172 (13%) were treated under fluoroscopy-only guidance. All patients in the fluoroscopy-only group had undergone preprocedural TEE to assess PFO anatomy. Results Baseline characteristics were similar across groups, including atrial septal aneurysm (34%, 33%, and 37% in the TEE, ICE, and fluoroscopy-only groups, respectively; p=0.685) and baseline severe right-to-left shunt (58%, 58%, and 49%, respectively; p=0.143). Procedural success was high across all groups (99.0% for TEE, 99.7% for ICE, and 98.2% for fluoroscopy-only; p=0.163). Echocardiographic guidance was associated with significantly shorter procedure duration (33, 28, and 48 minutes for TEE, ICE, and fluoroscopy-only; p&lt;0.001), lower fluoroscopy time, reduced radiation exposure (11, 7.1, and 31 Gy·cm²; p&lt;0.001), and less frequent contrast use (28%, 17%, and 94%; p&lt;0.001). In-hospital and long-term complication rates, including new-onset atrial fibrillation, residual shunt, and recurrent embolic events, were low and comparable across groups. Conclusions All intraprocedural imaging strategies for PFO closure were safe and effective. However, echocardiographic guidance was associated with significant procedural advantages and may offer added value even in anatomically straightforward cases. A tailored imaging approach based on patient anatomy, operator expertise, and resource availability is recommended.Central illustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Effectiveness of intraprocedural guidance modalities on PFO closure outcomes: insights from the PROLONG registry

abstract: Abstract Background Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is associated with paradoxical embolism, cryptogenic stroke, and migraine with aura. The biomechanical mechanisms underlying these associations remain poorly defined. We previously reported that patients with PFO display reduced erythrocyte count, hemoglobin, and hematocrit, all of which normalize after PFO closure. These findings suggest a possible role for chronic mechanical and oxidative stress in erythrocyte dysfunction. Purposes To investigate erythrocyte morphology, deformability, and aggregability in patients with PFO before and six months after PFO closure. Methods Sixty-seven patients with PFO were evaluated before and six months after transcatheter PFO closure and compared with 28 healthy subjects (HS). Erythrocyte count and red blood cell distribution width (RDW-CV) were assessed by automated blood count. Erythrocyte morphology was analyzed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Erythrocyte deformability under increasing shear stress and aggregability were assessed using laser-assisted optical rotational cell analyzer (LoRRca). Results Patients with PFO showed significantly higher RDW-CV compared with HS (13.43% ± 1.36 vs 12.44% ± 0.53; p = 0.0011), a parameter that remained elevated six months after PFO closure (13.82% ± 1.75), consistent with the long lifespan of erythrocytes. TEM analysis revealed, in addition to normal biconcave erythrocytes, a previously undescribed “shield-shaped” erythrocyte morphology observed exclusively in PFO patients (Figure). Functionally, erythrocytes from PFO patients showed reduced deformability under prolonged shear stress compared with post-closure values (elongation index 0.18 ± 0.03 vs 0.20 ± 0.04; p=0.019). Moreover, erythrocyte aggregability was significantly increased before PFO closure and decreased at six-month follow-up (amplitude 36.45 ± 3.66 vs 34.07 ± 3.36; p=0.0002). Conclusions Patients with PFO exhibit a distinct erythrocyte phenotype characterized by altered morphology, reduced deformability, and increased aggregability. While erythrocyte mechanical function partially recovers after PFO closure, morphological alterations persist, suggesting chronic erythrocyte remodeling. These findings support a role for PFO-related mechanical stress in erythrocyte dysfunction, potentially contributing to the prothrombotic and vasoactive milieu associated with PFO. Figure. Ultrastructural analysis of erythrocytes in patients with patent foramen ovale. Transmission electron microscopy reveals heterogeneous erythrocyte morphology in patients with patent foramen ovale, including normal biconcave “disc-shaped” cells and a previously undescribed shield-shaped phenotype. This abnormal morphology was observed exclusively in PFO patients and was not detected in healthy subjects. Scale bar: 10 μm.Ultrastructural analysis of erythrocytesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Chronic hemodynamic stress drives erythrocyte remodeling in patent foramen ovale

abstract: Abstract Introduction Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is a recognized potential source of paradoxical embolism and has been implicated in cryptogenic stroke and transient ischemic attack (TIA). Percutaneous PFO closure reduces recurrent events in carefully selected patients; however, the degree of benefit may vary with individual clinical and anatomical characteristics. In routine practice, treatment decisions are increasingly guided by risk evaluation tools, such as the Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (ROPE) score, which estimates the likelihood of a causal PFO–stroke relationship. Aim To assess the long-term effectiveness of percutaneous PFO closure and explore outcomes across varying levels of PFO–stroke causal probability as defined by the ROPE score. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent percutaneous PFO closure between 2011 and 2023. Baseline characteristics and follow-up data on recurrent TIA or stroke were extracted from medical records. To illustrate expected recurrence, a simulated dataset was created using actual follow-up times truncated at 2 years, assigning each patient a 2-year recurrence probability based on published estimates. Kaplan–Meier and Cox analysis compared time to TIA / stroke recurrence between the simulated and study groups. Results A total of 271 patients were included (mean age 50 years, 51% female). Hypertension, diabetes and smoking history were present in 35%, 7% and 7% of patients, respectively; cortical infarct was detected in 64%. The mean ROPE score was 6. Recurrent TIA / stroke occurred in 4 patients, compared with 24 expected. The study group demonstrated a significantly longer time-to-event than the simulation group [HR 0.155 CI 0.054-0.047, p&lt;0.001]. Interestingly, when stratified by ROPE score, patients with higher scores (≥7) had recurrence rates comparable to expected values, whereas those with lower scores (&lt;7) had only one event [HR 0.051 CI 0.007-0.382, p=0.004). Conclusion Recurrent stroke or TIA after PFO closure was markedly lower than expected, particularly among patients with lower ROPE scores. These findings support the effectiveness of PFO closure across the whole cohort and suggest benefit even in patients with lower causal probability, provided treatment is individualized within the broader clinical context. More robust, prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.Figure 1For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: PFO closure and recurrent stroke - beyond the ROPE score

abstract: Abstract Purpose Contrast transthoracic echocardiography (cTTE) is used to assess the presence and size of a shunt in patients suspected of a patent foramen ovale (PFO), both during normal breathing and the Valsalva manoeuvre. The shunt pattern on cTTE, shunt at rest or shunt only during Valsalva, may reflect anatomical complexity and thereby influence the risk of residual shunting. This study aimed to determine whether pre-procedural shunt characteristics are associated with the presence of residual shunting at 6 months after percutaneous PFO closure. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing percutaneous PFO closure between 2005 and 2024 were included. Patients were divided in two groups based on the initial, pre-procedural cTTE, with group A consisting of patients with a spontaneous shunt and group B consisting of patients with a shunt that was only present during the Valsalva manoeuvre. The presence of any residual shunting between group A and B was compared using the Χ2-test. A multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between shunt pattern and residual shunting at 6 months, correcting for pre-procedural shunt size (graded as small/medium/large based on cTTE) and size of the closure device. Results Of the included patients, 443 patients had available data of the pre-procedural cTTE and the primary outcome of residual shunting at 6 months. A residual shunt was present at 6 months in 37.7% of the patients in group A and 33.3% of the patients in group B (P = 0.41). In the multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for pre-procedural shunt size and device size, no association was observed between pre-procedural spontaneous shunting and residual shunting at 6 months (OR 1.22, 95% CI; 0.77-1.98). The pre-procedural shunt size was not associated with residual shunting, whereas a larger device size was independently associated (OR 1.17, 95% CI; 1.10-1.26). Conclusion In this study the pre-procedural shunt pattern and size were not associated with residual shunting at 6 months. The size of the closure device emerged as an independent predictor of residual shunting, suggesting the features of the closure device in relation to the surrounding structures may play a more prominent role in residual shunting than initial shunt characteristics.Figure 1.Shunt pattern and residual shuntingFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Pre-procedural shunt characteristics and residual shunting at 6 months after percutaneous PFO closure

abstract: Abstract Background Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. However, conventional manual LAAO exposes operators to radiation and physical strain, while being subject to operator-dependent variability. Objectives This study aimed to conduct a comprehensive preclinical evaluation of a novel robotic-assisted system for LAAO, comparing its efficacy and safety against the conventional manual approach. Methods In a prospective, randomized controlled trial, 20 canines were assigned to undergo LAAO via robotic assistance (n=10) or manual technique (n=10). The robotic system featured a bedside unit with manipulators for sheath and delivery cable control, operated remotely from a console. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success, defined as successful device implantation with satisfactory position, stability, complete LAA seal (peri-device leak &lt; 5 mm). Safety endpoints included adverse events and pathological findings. Results The final procedural success rate was 100% (10/10) in the robotic group and 90% (9/10) in the manual group (P=1.000). First-attempt success rates were 80% (8/10) and 70% (7/10), respectively (P=0.605). There were no statistically significant differences between groups in the number of anchor attempts or the degree of final residual leak. No procedure-related adverse events occurred in the robotic group, compared to two events in the manual group (0% vs. 20%, P=0.474). However, robotic procedures were associated with longer fluoroscopy times (77.5 vs. 55.5 min, P=0.028) and higher radiation exposure doses, which were attributed to the initial learning curve and a protocol emphasizing precision. Conclusion In this preclinical study, the novel robotic LAAO system demonstrated non-inferior effectiveness and a favorable safety profile compared to the manual approach. It offered enhanced procedural standardization, albeit with initial trade-offs in efficiency. These findings support the system's feasibility and justify further development and larger-scale studies to establish its clinical role.graphic abstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Robotic-assisted left atrial appendage occlusion: feasibility and safety in a preclinical randomized study in a canine model

abstract: Abstract Background Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an effective option for patients with atrial fibrillation at high risk of stroke who are unsuitable for long-term anticoagulation. Preprocedural planning with transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac CT is routinely performed to assess anatomy and rule out thrombus before LAAC, although the supporting evidence remains limited.¹ As the number of LAAC procedures increases and newer devices facilitate implantation, the value of routine preprocedural imaging in a resource-limited healthcare environment is uncertain. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-centre study of patients evaluated for LAAC between 2023 and 2025 who underwent preprocedural transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Patients were excluded if the procedure was cancelled for clinical reasons unrelated to TEE evaluation. The Heart Team determined the device recommendation (Watchman FLX Pro vs Amulet). The primary objective was to assess the clinical relevance of preprocedural TEE, defined as cancellation due to TEE findings, detection of thrombus, the need for additional imaging, and guidance on device selection. Secondary objectives included new intraprocedural TEE findings leading to cancellation, procedural success, and the final device implanted. Results A total of 122 patients were included. Four (3.3%) procedures were cancelled due to TEE findings. LAA thrombus was detected in three patients (2.5%), and additional imaging with CT or repeat TEE was recommended for 17 patients (13.9%) to further assess the LAA. Of the patients who underwent additional imaging, only one had the procedure cancelled. LAAC was deemed feasible in 118 patients (96.7%), and an Amulet device was recommended for only four patients (3.3%). Among patients with thrombus, two had a previous history of persistent thrombus despite anticoagulation therapy, and one had discontinued anticoagulation due to recurrent intracranial bleeding. The procedural success rate was 94.1%, with failures occurring due to technical challenges rather than TEE findings. Of the eight Amulet implants (7.2%), five were initially considered suitable for a Watchman device, while one patient planned for an Amulet received a Watchman device. Among the 64 patients with a device size recommendation, 37 (57.8%) received a size consistent with preprocedural planning, highlighting discrepancies between preprocedural planning and final device selection. Conclusion In LAAC programs where periprocedural TEE guidance is standard, systematic preprocedural TEE appears to provide limited additional value and may lead to unnecessary testing. A more appropriate approach may be to reserve preprocedural imaging for selected patients who are off anticoagulation or at very high thromboembolic risk. However, larger prospective studies are needed.Primary and Secondary OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Table 1:Characteristics of PatientsFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Impact of pre-procedural TEE on left atrial appendage closure strategy

abstract: Abstract Background Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. LAAC is increasingly considered for recurrent embolic events despite oral anticoagulation (OAC), yet data on long-term outcomes in this emerging indication remain limited. Purpose To assess the embolic event rate after LAAC for recurrent embolic events despite adequate OAC compared to estimated event rates in patients managed with OAC alone and to other indications for LAAC. Methods We conducted a retrospective bi-center study (2012–2025) of patients undergoing successful LAAC. The primary endpoint was a composite of ischaemic stroke and systemic embolism. Secondary endpoints included all-cause death, major bleeding, device-related thrombosis (DRT), and ischaemic stroke. Patients were matched using propensity score matching (PSM) on age, CHA2DS2-VASc, HAS-BLED, diabetes, and peripheral artery disease. Survival analysis was adjusted for CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scores in the overall population. Theoretical event rates were extracted from large literature cohorts. Results Of 814 patients, 66 underwent LAAC for recurrent embolic events and 748 for other indications (92.4% for bleeding under OAC). The recurrent embolic events group was younger (74.5 vs. 78 years, p=0.018), had lower HAS-BLED scores (3 vs. 4, p&lt;0.001), and more peripheral artery disease (42.4% vs. 26.1%). At discharge, 92.4% received anticoagulant therapy versus 28.8% in patients with other LAAC indications (p&lt;0.001). After a median follow-up of 20 [7-43] months, 52 embolic events occurred: 10 (15.2%) in the LAAC for recurrent embolic events group versus 42 (5.6%) for other indication (aHR 2.88, 95% CI [1.39-5.97], p=0.005), driven by a higher rate of stroke (aHR 3.92, 95% CI [1.86–8.26], p&lt;0.001). All-cause mortality was lower in the recurrent embolic events group (aHR 0.46, 95% CI [0.26–0.82], p=0.008). No differences were found for major bleeding (p=0.16) or DRT (p=0.72). After PSM, results were unchanged (aHR 3.65, 95% CI [1.31–10.15], p=0.013 for the primary outcome). Compared to estimated annualized event rate in patients with recurrent stroke despite OAC, patients who underwent LAAC had lower annualized event rates (5.2% per patient-year vs 9.7% in RENO-EXTEND and 8.9% in the STR-OAC LAAO control group). Conclusion Patients undergoing LAAC for recurrent embolic events despite anticoagulation had a nearly 3-fold increased risk of embolic recurrence compared with other LAAC indications, consistent after PSM, highlighting the heterogeneity of patients undergoing LAAC for bleeding versus ischaemic indications. While the annualized event rate in this high-risk ischaemic subset appears lower than historical rates for patients maintained on OAC alone, it remains higher than rates reported in other LAAC registries. This variability suggests substantial clinical heterogeneity in this high-risk subset of patients.Embolic event KM curvesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Annualized event ratesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: Embolic events after left atrial appendage closure for recurrent embolic events despite anticoagulation

abstract: Abstract Background Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is increasingly performed in patients with atrial fibrillation at high thromboembolic risk and contraindicated to long-term oral anticoagulation due to major bleeding risk. However, the incidence, determinants, and prognostic impact of in-hospital complications remain incompletely characterized in this high bleeding risk population. Purpose To assess the incidence and predictors of in-hospital major adverse events (IHMAE) following LAAO and their impact on long-term mortality. Methods We conducted a multicenter observational study including 1085 consecutive patients undergoing LAAO between 2012 and 2025 in three tertiary French centers. Baseline, procedural, and follow-up data were collected. IHMAE were defined as a composite of death, stroke/systemic embolism, pericardial effusion/tamponade, device embolization, major bleeding, or vascular complications. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of IHMAE. The association between IHMAE and all-cause mortality was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression, restricted to patients discharged alive. Results Patients were mostly males (63.3%) with a mean age of 77.2±10 years and had high thromboembolic and bleeding risks (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4.7±1.5; HAS-BLED 3.6±1.0). Procedural success was high (99.5%). Median length of stay was 3 days [IQR 2–3]. IHMAE occurred in 6.3% of patients. The most frequent complications were pericardial effusion/tamponade (2.9%) and major bleeding (2.6%), followed by vascular complications (1.2%). Periprocedural or in-hospital death occurred in 0.6%, stroke/systemic embolism in 0.4%, and device embolization in 0.1%. No baseline characteristic independently predicted IHMAE in multivariable analysis. During a median follow-up of 702 days [IQR 211–1437], all-cause mortality occurred in 37.8%, recurrent thromboembolic events in 8.8%, recurrent bleeding events in 18.5%, and rehospitalization in 62.3%. IHMAE were associated with higher post-discharge mortality in the unadjusted analysis (9.1% vs 4.6%, p=0.004). However, after exclusion of in-hospital deaths, this association was not significant in time-to-event analysis (log-rank p=0.704) or after adjustment for age and sex (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.64–1.36, p=0.728). Conclusion In this large multicenter cohort, LAAO was associated with a low rate of in-hospital complications, mainly driven by manageable bleeding and pericardial events. IHMAE did not independently predict long-term mortality after time adjustment. Our findings suggest that most complications are managed appropriately during hospitalization and have limited impact on long-term prognosis. Mortality of these high-risk patients remains high at relatively short term follow-up.Abstract FigureFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Abstract TableFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
title: In-hospital complications after left atrial appendage occlusion and their impact on long-term mortality: a multicenter study

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal antiplatelet therapy after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains uncertain. While aspirin remains the standard of care, intensified platelet inhibition with ticagrelor plus aspirin has been proposed to improve saphenous vein graft (SVG) patency. However, whether this benefit outweighs the increased risk of major bleeding and translates into improved clinical outcomes remains uncertain. Purpose To assess whether the graft patency benefit of ticagrelor plus aspirin after CABG outweighs the risk of major bleeding, and to evaluate its effects on mortality and ischaemic outcomes Methods PubMed and Embase were systematically searched from inception through December 30, 2025, for randomized and observational studies comparing ticagrelor-based DAPT versus aspirin monotherapy after CABG. Primary outcomes included major bleeding, all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and SVG occlusion at 1 year. Secondary outcomes were myocardial infarction, stroke, and repeat revascularization. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Chi-squared test and I² statistic. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed according to study design. Results Five studies, including 9,659 patients (3,369 patients with ticagrelor and aspirin, and 6,290 with aspirin alone) were analyzed. DAPT with Ticagrelor and aspirin was associated with a lower risk of SVG occlusion (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47–0.85; p=0.002; I²=2%) but increased major bleeding risk (RR 1.69, 95% CI 1.06–2.72; p=0.03; I²=42%). No significant differences were observed for stroke, myocardial infarction, cardiovascular mortality and new revascularization. Conclusion After CABG, ticagrelor plus aspirin improves SVG patency but increases major bleeding compared with aspirin alone, without clear benefits in other clinical outcomes. These findings support selective use of ticagrelor-based DAPT in patients with a higher graft-failure risk profile and low bleeding risk, whereas aspirin alone may be favoured in patients with elevated bleeding risk.. Further adequately powered RTCs are needed to identify patient subgroups most likely to derive a net clinical benefit.Primary OutcomesFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.Central IllustrationFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.
