Inclusion of physical activity significantly improved model discrimination (AUC 0.701 vs. 0.861; p&lt;0.001). Conclusions Lower habitual physical activity is independently associated with more extensive angiographic CAD in patients with MI, providing incremental predictive value beyond traditional risk factors. These findings support systematic assessment of physical activity in risk stratification and reinforce its central role in cardiovascular prevention strategies.Figure 2
title: Age, sex and habitual physical activity as determinants of multi-vessel coronary disease in acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Physical inactivity is associated with adverse cardiac remodelling and increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Left atrial and ventricular structure and function are established predictors of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. The Activity quotient (AQ) is a heart rate-based weekly score that quantifies the health impact of endurance-type physical activity, providing an objective measure of habitual activity, with low scores reflecting physical inactivity. We aimed to investigate whether lower AQ score are associated with unfavourable left atrial and ventricular structure and function, and with higher incidence of MACE in middle-aged adults from the general population. Methods We included 3610 participants from the general population, all born in 1950, and examined between 2012 and 2015. Weekly AQ scores were calculated from self-reported physical activity and categorized into four categories: AQ = 0, AQ ≤50, AQ 51–99, and AQ ≥100. Participants with AQ = 0 were classified as physically inactive and served as the reference group. Follow-up continued until 31 December 2022 (median 8.3 years), and MACE was defined as first occurrence of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal ischemic stroke, non-fatal heart failure, myocardial revascularization (coronary artery bypass grafting or percutaneous revascularization), or cardiovascular death. We used multivariable linear regression models to examine associations between AQ and echocardiographic measures of cardiac structure and function, and Cox proportional hazard models to assess associations between AQ categories and incident MACE. All models were adjusted for age, sex, site, current smoking, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, diabetes, C-reactive protein and atrial fibrillation. Association between physical activity and MACE was presented by Kaplan-Meier plot and we used log-rank test to assess differences between the groups. Results Participants had a mean age of 63.9 years (range 62.1–65.7) and 51.2% were male. Inactive participants had significantly smaller left atrial and left ventricular volumes and lower left ventricular mass compared to active participants (Table). Lower AQ scores were significantly associated with higher incidence of MACE during follow-up (log-rank p = 0.001), and physical inactivity (AQ = 0) remained independently associated with MACE after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio 1.38, CI 1.03-1.84), p=0.03. Conclusion In this cohort of middle-aged adults from the general population, physical inactivity as reflected by AQ score of 0, was associated with smaller left atrial and ventricular volumes and lower left ventricular mass compared with higher AQ levels. Inactive individuals also experienced more MACE during follow-up, and this association remained significant after adjustment for established cardiovascular risk factors, highlighting the importance of regular physical activity in midlife.Kaplan Meier Survival CurveTable
title: Physical inactivity measured by activity quotient score is associated with low cardiac volumes and mass and clinical events in middle-aged subjects from the general population

abstract: Abstract Background The cardiovascular protective effects of regular exercise have been well established. Viral infection can lead to myocardial injury, and current research on the impact of exercise on post-viral myocardial injury has primarily focused on competitive athletes, while imaging evidence regarding the effect of daily exercise on myocardial injury in the general population following viral infection remains limited. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameters, including myocardial native T1 values for quantifying myocardial tissue characteristics and left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) for assessing myocardial motion function, can non-invasively and sensitively detect viral-induced myocardial changes. Purpose To investigate the association between daily exercise habits in the general population and changes in myocardial tissue and function following viral infection. Methods We prospectively enrolled patients during the convalescent phase of Omicron infection (defined as ≥1 month after symptom resolution or negative viral test) who underwent CMR examination. Patients were grouped according to pre-infection exercise habits and levels of physical activity energy expenditure (PAEE). Myocardial native T1 values and LV GLS were compared between groups. Results A total of 54 patients (36 men, 66.7%; mean age 54 ± 12 years) were included, undergoing CMR at 54 ± 12 days after positive viral testing. Myocardial native T1 values were negatively correlated with years of exercise (non-exercise: 1286.1 ± 55.5 msec; ≤5 years: 1244 ± 43.5 msec; &gt;5 years: 1225.7 ± 57.4 msec, P-trend = 0.002) and pre-infection total PAEE (low: 1318.1 ± 39.9 msec; moderate: 1248.1 ± 47.6 msec; high: 1235.9 ± 50.6 msec, P-trend &lt; 0.001). Extracellular volume fraction was also negatively correlated with years of exercise (non-exercise: 35.9 ± 3.8%; ≤5 years: 34.1 ± 5.6%; &gt;5 years: 30.8 ± 4.6%, P-trend = 0.005). The absolute value of LV GLS was significantly higher in the exercise group than in the non-exercise group (-18.1 ± 2.3% vs. -15.8 ± 2.1%, P = 0.004). Multivariable linear regression analysis demonstrated that myocardial native T1 values were independently and negatively associated with pre-infection total PAEE (B coefficient [95% CI]: -25.28 [-41.413, -9.147]; P = 0.003). LVGLS was independently and negatively associated with years of exercise (B coefficient [95% CI]: -2.179 [-3.689, -0.668]; P = 0.006). Conclusion(s) Pre-viral infection daily exercise habits are associated with more favorable myocardial tissue characteristics and systolic function following infection, suggesting a cardioprotective role in the general population that may attenuate viral-induced myocardial injury.
title: Impact of daily exercise on myocardial injury and adaptive changes following viral infection: a prospective observational cardiac magnetic resonance study in patients recovered from Omicron

abstract: Abstract Background Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) exhibits substantial phenotypic heterogeneity in sleep clinic populations; however, its prognostic relevance in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) undergoing revascularization remains uncertain. Methods We pooled two prospective cohorts of patients with CAD (total n = 2318) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (n = 1311) or coronary artery bypass grafting (n = 1001). All patients underwent baseline overnight sleep studies and detailed phenotyping. Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE: cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and unplanned revascularization) were recorded over a mean follow-up of 1.9 ± 1.1 years. Latent class analysis using nine demographic and clinical variables (age, sex, body mass index [BMI], ethnicity, diabetes, prior myocardial infarction, excessive daytime sleepiness, left ventricular ejection fraction, and revascularization type) was performed to identify phenogroups. Cox regression models were used to evaluate associations between OSA (apnea–hypopnea index ≥15 events/h) and MACCE overall and within each phenogroup. Results Phenogroup 1 (42.2%) comprised younger, symptomatic individuals (mean age 54 years; ESS &gt;10 in 15.8%). Phenogroup 2 (30.9%) was characterized by a high burden of cardiometabolic comorbidities (diabetes 68.7%, prior myocardial infarction 67.5%). Phenogroup 3 (26.9%) consisted predominantly of older, lean Chinese patients (mean age 67 years; BMI 24 kg/m²). The prevalence of OSA was similar across phenogroups (45.5%, 50.7%, and 47.8%, respectively). During follow-up, 11.4% of patients experienced MACCE. The crude incidence of MACCE was higher in patients with OSA than in those without OSA in phenogroup 1 (2-year estimate: 13.5% vs. 6.4%; P = 0.028) and phenogroup 2 (15.9% vs. 9.3%; P = 0.003), but not in phenogroup 3 (12.7% vs. 10.1%; P = 0.171). Overall, OSA was associated with an increased risk of MACCE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.34–2.19; P &lt; 0.001). However, associations differed by phenogroup: significant in phenogroup 1 (adjusted HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.06–2.50; P = 0.027) and phenogroup 2 (adjusted HR 1.83, 95% CI 1.19–2.83; P = 0.006), but not in phenogroup 3 (adjusted HR 1.44, 95% CI 0.88–1.94; P = 0.151). Conclusions In revascularized patients with CAD, OSA is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, and this association varies by phenogroup. Younger, sleepy patients and those with cardiometabolic comorbidities appear to be at highest risk, whereas risk is attenuated in older, lean, predominantly Chinese patients. Phenogroup-based approaches may enhance risk stratification and inform targeted OSA management in CAD populations.Central illustrationlca--fig--3.png
title: Phenogroup-based stratification of cardiovascular risk in obstructive sleep apnea

abstract: Abstract Background Whether glycemic status modifies the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains largely unknown. Objectives To examine whether glycemic status, including prediabetes and glycemic control in diabetes, modifies the association between OSA and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ACS. Methods In this prospective cohort study, we recruited 2160 ACS patients undergoing portable sleep monitoring between June 2015 and January 2020. Glycemic status was classified as normoglycemia, prediabetes, or diabetes according to hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) levels, and patients with diabetes were further stratified into controlled and uncontrolled diabetes. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, ischemia-driven revascularization or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. Results A total of 1,848 ACS patients were included in the final analysis, 371 with normoglycemia (20.1%), 681 with prediabetes (36.9%), and 796 with diabetes, of whom 354 had controlled diabetes (19.2%) and 442 (23.9%) had uncontrolled diabetes. The median follow-up duration was 4.9 years (3.7–6.2 years). OSA was associated with a significantly higher risk of MACCE not only in patients with diabetes (aHR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.02–1.72; P=0.04) but also in those with prediabetes compared with non-OSA (aHR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00–1.86; P=0.05), whereas no significant association was observed in normoglycemia. Among patients with diabetes, OSA was associated with increased MACCE risk only in those with uncontrolled diabetes (aHR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04–2.10; P=0.02), whereas no significant association was observed in controlled diabetes. Conclusions In patients with ACS, the prognostic impact of OSA varies according to glycemic status. The prognostic impact of OSA in ACS extends beyond established diabetes to individuals with prediabetes and varies according to glycemic control in diabetes. These findings highlight the importance of considering glycemic status when assessing cardiovascular risk related to OSA.Central Illustration
title: Glycemic status modifies the association between obstructive sleep apnea and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Chronotropic incompetence (CI), a frequent sequela after myocardial infarction (MI), can negatively affect exercise capacity and quality of life (QoL). Targeted deprescription of negative chronotropic therapy (NCT) may be beneficial in selected patients with CI. Purpose We aimed to analyse the incidence and evolution of CI in relation to NCT during follow-up in our local post-MI Phase 2 Cardiac Rehabilitation Program (CRP). Methods Patients with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) or occlusion MI (OMI) between November 2021 and November 2024 who completed our Phase 2 CRP were included in a prospective registry. Exercise testing (ExECG) was performed before and after Phase 2. Peak VO2 (estimated or measured), predicted functional capacity (as % of FRIEND equation), and chronotropic reserve index (CRI) [(maximum heart rate – resting heart rate) / ([220-age] – resting heart rate)] were assessed. CI was defined as &lt;80% CRI (≤62% in patients receiving NCT). NCT was recorded in absolute and equivalent doses standardized to bisoprolol 2.5mg units (B2.5EU). QoL was evaluated using the Short-Form 36-item (SF-36) questionnaire before and after Phase 2. Results Our cohort comprised 251 patients (mean age 61.84±10.7 years, 83.7% men, 50.2% previous smokers, and 22.7% with diabetes mellitus), most presenting with anterior and inferior STEMI (n=107, 42.6% for each). The mean LVEF was 52.25±10.2%, with 89 patients (35.5%) showing LVEF&lt;50%. Most patients received NCT before Phase 2 CRP (n=216, 86.1%). On initial ExECG, 107 (42.6%) patients demonstrated CI. NCT use was associated with lower CRI (66.48±19.29 vs. 76.06±23.03%, p=0.02). Patients with CI had worse initial peak VO2 (21.77±8.34 vs. 29.13±8.57 mL/kg/min, p&lt;0.001), lower predicted functional capacity (73.33±29.58 vs. 92.18±26.62%, p&lt;0.001), and poorer baseline QoL scores. NCT deprescription was performed in 58 patients (23.1%), including 32 of 107 patients with CI (29.9%), which increased the proportion of patients not receiving NCT from 13.9% to 19.1% (p&lt;0.05). This subgroup had lower initial CRI (60.26 vs. 70.09%, p=0.001), with no differences on final ExECG (CRI 67.02 vs. 68.82%, p=0.62). Among patients with initial CI who received NCT deprescription, we observed the largest improvement in CRI on final ExECG (+15.84%, ANOVA p&lt;0.001). A similar absolute increase in peak VO2 was observed across initial CI and NCT deprescription categories (mean +3.62mL/kg/min, ANOVA p=0.83). A weak correlation was found between CRI and peak VO2 both before (R2 0.249) and after (R2 0.309) Phase 2 CRP. Conclusion A substantial proportion of patients exhibit CI after MI, which adversely affects functional capacity and QoL. Deprescription of NCT is associated with the most pronounced improvement in chronotropic response after Phase 2 CRP. The role of this strategy in post-MI patients with CI and no clear indication for NCT warrants further investigation.Chronotropic incompetence and NCTChronotropic response and VO2 peak
title: Chronotropic incompetence and negative chronotropic therapy in myocardial infarction patients during Phase 2 Cardiac Rehabilitation

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) enables the assessment of cardiorespiratory fitness. Previously, sex-specific clustering models were trained on time series from cycle ergometry in a Belgian cohort. Those models provided a promising artificial intelligence-based integrative tool for cardiovascular (CV) risk stratification, warranting external validation before its implementation in clinical practice. Purpose To evaluate the performance of the CPET time series clustering models in an external cohort from the United States tested on a treadmill. Methods The external cohort consisted of individuals who achieved a respiratory exchange ratio (RER)≥1.0 during CPET at a university medical center between 2014 and 2020. We included individuals without a diagnosis of heart failure or congenital heart disease that were referred to CPET mainly due to symptoms or for cardiopulmonary disease evaluation. The previously developed models, derived using dynamic time warping with k-medoids (unsupervised machine learning), were applied to time series of oxygen uptake, heart rate, RER, and end-tidal partial pressure of oxygen and carbon dioxide of the external cohort. The resulting clusters were evaluated regarding clinical characteristics and health outcomes. Events included stroke, atrial fibrillation, cardiac arrest, acute coronary syndrome, acute heart failure, heart or lung transplants, cardiac and valve surgeries, cardiogenic shock, shockable rhythm or arrythmia surgery. The median follow-up time was 2.5 years with maximum time set to 4 years. Results Among the 751 patients, 277 (36.9%) were females; the mean age was 47±16 years, body mass index was 27±5 kg/m2, and 447 (59.5%) had a history of CV disease. Cluster 1 represented the most favorable CV proﬁle whereas cluster 5 represented the worst profile, consistent with the observations in the training data. Compared to the other clusters, cluster 5 had significantly higher values for age and hypertension, and lower peak VO2 values (Table 1). In 1841 person-years (py) of follow-up, 183 individuals experienced at least one CV event (99.4/1000 py) and the event rates increased gradually across the clusters: 52.5/1000 py in cluster 1 (35 events), 67.5/1000 py in cluster 2 (31 events), 113.3/1000 py in cluster 3 (45 events), 207.6/1000 py in cluster 4 (42 events) and 259.4/1000 py in cluster 5 (30 events). In line, the Kaplan-Meier curves showed differences in cumulative incidence of events between clusters (Figure 1A). After adjustments for traditional risk factors, clusters 4 and 5 presented signiﬁcantly higher CV risks compared to cluster 1 (Figure 1B). Conclusion The previously developed CPET-based clustering models were able to stratify CV risk and event rates in an external cohort, tested in a different country and CPET modality. These findings increase the confidence of using those models as a decision support tool for CV-risk assessment based on CPET time series.
title: External validation of clustering models for cardiovascular risk stratiﬁcation based on cardiopulmonary exercise testing

abstract: Abstract Background Early vascular aging (EVA) contributes to elevated cardiovascular risk and impaired hemodynamics in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). While cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves functional capacity, targeted therapeutic strategies to improve vascular function during CR remain limited. Intermittent hypoxic-hyperoxic training (IHHT) induces cellular adaptions that may promote vascular remodeling and improve vascular function. Purpose To investigate the effects of IHHT on markers of EVA in CAD patients undergoing CR. Methods 36 CAD patients after myocardial infarction and/or percutaneous coronary intervention referred to 3-4 weeks of inpatient CR were randomized into an IHHT (N=18; 31% female; 53.9±9.2 years) or control group (CG, N=18; 37% female; 58.4±8.0 years). Clinical assessment included pulse wave analysis (PWA), as well as cardiopulmonary exercise testing, functional tests (6-MWT and Chair-Rise Test) and disease perception questionnaires at admission and before discharge. In addition to standard CR, IHHT patients received three weekly sessions (30-40 min/session) consisting of six to eight individually adjusted cycles alternating between hypoxic (10-12% O2, 3-5 min) and hyperoxic breathing (30-35% O2). CG patients received standard care with matched breathing exercises (3 sessions/week, 30 min/session). Results Patients completed 24.8±3.6 days of CR and no adverse events were reported. IHHT patients received 6.9±1.2 sessions corresponding to 26±6 min of hypoxic breathing. Pulse Pressure Amplification (PPA) increased in IHHT but decreased in CG (+0.05±0.11 vs. −0.06±0.06; p=0.002), indicating reduced central cardiac load (decreased PPA is a key indicator of EVA). Total vascular resistance (−0.11±0.22 vs. +0.06±0.21 s/mmHg/ml; p=0.031), Augmentation Pressure (−5.27±8.88 vs. +1.38±3.86 mmHg; p=0.038) and Augmentation Index (−9.6±14.4 vs. +4.1±11.6%; p=0.004) improved significantly in IHHT compared to CG, reflecting reduced arterial stiffness and improved central hemodynamics. Peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak) increased more in IHHT (+1.9±1.7 ml/min/kg) compared to CG (+0.8±2.3 ml/min/kg), but missed statistical significance (p=0.098). However, respiratory minute ventilation at peak exercise showed a greater improvement in IHHT (+9.3±10.6 l/min) than in CG (+2.4±9.8 l/min; p=0.049), with strong correlation between changes in ventilation and VO₂peak (r=0.83; p&lt;0.001). Conclusion IHHT in addition to guideline-based CR significantly improves markers of EVA, particularly pulse pressure amplification and indices of arterial stiffness, suggesting favorable effects on central vascular function and cardiac afterload in CAD patients. Improvements in ventilatory efficiency and a trend toward greater VO₂peak enhancement further support potential physiological benefits of IHHT during CR.
title: Intermittent hypoxic-hyperoxic training improves markers of vascular aging in coronary artery disease patients – a randomized controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a multidisciplinary intervention recommended for patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). While the benefits of exercise-based rehabilitation on cardiorespiratory fitness and health-related quality of life are well documented, its metabolic effects are less well explored. Purpose This study investigated fat oxidation (FatOx) and carbohydrate oxidation (ChOx) during exercise as an indirect measure of mitochondrial oxidative capacity during CR and evaluated dependent changes in lipid profiles in CAD patients. Methods 458 CAD patients (23% women, 55.3±7.3 years) after myocardial infarction and/or percutaneous coronary intervention referred to 3–4 weeks of inpatient CR underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing at admission and before discharge. Breath-by-breath spiroergometric data were used to stoichiometrically determine substrate oxidation rates. Data were expressed relative to peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak). Mean area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence interval as well as linear regression slopes from start to peak were calculated. Responder analyses were conducted for submaximal and peak exercise capacity based on VO₂ at ventilatory threshold 1 (VT1) and VO₂peak, as well as for maximal fat oxidation (MFO), using the typical-error method. Results FatOx was impaired in CAD patients (MFOpre: 0.32±0.15 g/min; AUCpre: 9.7[9.2–10.2]) compared to healthy controls (MFO: 0.46±0.17 g/min; p&lt;0.001), while ChOx was largely unaffected. CR induced significant improvements in FatOx (+14.3%; AUCpost: 11.1[10.6–11.7]; p&lt;0.001) and MFO (MFOpost: 0.34±0.15 g/min; p&lt;0.0001). Improvements were smaller in women, older patients, and patients with reduced ejection fraction (+8.0%, +7.6%, and +8.7%) compared to their respective counterparts (+15.9%, +20.8%, and +15.6%). Responder analyses revealed that 37% of patients showed a response in VO2@VT1, 41% in VO2peak and 31% improved in MFO. However, a subgroup of metabolic responders (“metabolic phenotype”; ~10%) was identified that improved significantly in metabolic endpoints (+0.14±0.06 g/min in MFO, +90.4% in FatOx, +15.4% in ChOx) but showed no changes in VO2-based outcomes. Patients with the metabolic phenotype exhibited significantly larger reductions in blood lipid profiles, including total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and triglycerides (all p≤0.031) compared to VO2-based responders. The lipid-lowering effect was independent of medication. Conclusion CAD patients exhibited improved FatOx capacity in response to CR indicating enhanced mitochondrial oxidative capacity. Adaptations were less-pronounced in women, older patients, and those with reduced EF suggesting subgroup-specific differences in metabolic responsiveness. In addition to traditional outcome assessments based on VO₂ uptake, MFO may identify CR responders in terms of beneficial metabolic adaptations accompanied by larger reductions in blood lipid levels.
title: The lipid-lowering effect of metabolic adaptations during cardiac rehabilitation in coronary artery disease patients

abstract: Abstract Background The Managed Care after Acute Myocardial Infarction (MC-AMI) program, providing one year of coordinated post-infarction care, was launched in Poland. Hybrid cardiac telerehabilitation (TELEREHAB) is one of its key and innovative components. Purpose The objective of the MC-AMI-TELEREHAB registry was to evaluate the implementation of TELEREHAB within the MC-AMI framework and to assess its feasibility, safety, and patient adherence. Methods All centers in Poland offering TELEREHAB within the MC-AMI program from 2022 to 2025 were invited to participate in the registry. The TELEREHAB program consisted of 3–5 educational on-site training sessions and 24 telemonitored home-based exercise sessions (one session per day, two to five times per week), including endurance training (walking, Nordic walking, or cycle ergometer), resistance and respiratory exercises, combined with pro-health behavior education and consultations with a dietitian and a psychologist. Each training session was telemonitored using a device capable of ECG recording and data transmission via mobile phone to a central monitoring center. The impact on physical capacity was evaluated by comparing exercise test duration and functional capacity at the beginning and at the end of TELEREHAB. Results Ten centers participated in the MC-AMI-TELEREHAB registry, enrolling 580 patients with a mean age of 60.2 ± 9.9 years; 79.5% were men (n = 461), after AMI (NSTEMI - 56.3%; STEMI - 43.7%), with a mean LVEF of 52.25 ± 8.5%. TELEREHAB led to a significant improvement in physical capacity (Table). No deaths or major adverse events occurred during the program. The drop-out rate from TELEREHAB was 3.3% (n = 19). Conclusion Hybrid cardiac telerehabilitation delivered as part of the MC-AMI program is a feasible and safe form of rehabilitation, with high patient adherence.
title: Feasibility of hybrid cardiac telerehabilitation within the managed care after acute myocardial infarction program: insights from the multicenter polish MC-AMI-TELEREHAB Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) lowers resting systolic blood pressure (SBP) and increases peak exercise SBP and peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak), a surrogate of cardiac output and cardiorespiratory fitness. Because exercise SBP is strongly determined by exercise capacity, higher peak SBP and its increase after CR may reflect physiological training adaptations rather than an adverse haemodynamic response. Indexing SBP to VO₂peak accounts for fitness and may better distinguish benign increases related to improved cardiac output from pathological exercise blood pressure responses. The effect of CR on peak SBP/VO₂peak has not previously been investigated. Purpose To assess the impact of outpatient CR on changes in exercise blood pressure response, particularly peak SBP/VO₂peak. Methods This analysis included adults who underwent outpatient phase II exercise-based CR between September 2016 and December 2025 and agreed to be included in the registry. The 12-week programme comprised three supervised exercise sessions per week and structured education on the underlying disease, risk factor management, secondary prevention, medication adherence, psychosocial support, lifestyle modification, and nutrition. All patients underwent ergometer-based cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) at CR admission and discharge. Results A total of 2,560 adults (median age 63 years; 23% women) were included. Most patients were referred to CR after acute coronary syndromes (39% STEMI, 36% NSTEMI) and heart failure (19%). From CR admission to discharge, peak workload (0.26 W/kg; 95% CI, 0.25 to 0.28), METs (0.65; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.70), and VO₂peak (2.33 ml·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹; 95% CI, 2.16 to 2.5) improved (all p&lt;0.001). Resting and peak SBP at admission were 125 mmHg (IQR 111-139) and 180 mmHg (IQR 158-201). From CR admission to discharge, resting SBP rose slightly by 1.0 mmHg (95% CI, 0.5 to 2; p&lt;0.001) and peak SBP increased by 8.5 mmHg (95% CI: 7 to 9.5; p&lt;0.001). In contrast, peak SBP/VO₂peak decreased by −0.65 mmHg per ml·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹ (95% CI, −0.74 to −0.56; p&lt;0.001), and this remained significant after adjustment for number of antihypertensive medication and intake of a beta-blocker at admission and discharge (p&lt;0.001). The reduction in peak SBP/VO₂peak did not differ in patients with and without heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (p for interaction=0.86) but greater in those with than without hypertension at admission (p for interaction=0.043). Conclusions In a large real-world cohort undergoing outpatient phase II CR, cardiorespiratory fitness and peak SBP increased, whereas peak SBP/VO₂peak decreased. Thus, higher peak SBP after CR likely primarily reflects physiological increases in cardiac output rather than an adverse haemodynamic response. Therefore, peak SBP/VO₂peak should be considered when interpreting exercise blood pressure, and its relationship with cardiovascular outcomes should be evaluated prospectively.Figure 1.Change in VO2-adjusted SBP
title: Cardiorespiratory fitness-normalized peak exercise systolic blood pressure decreases after cardiac rehabilitation

abstract: Abstract Background / Introduction Risk stratification for ventricular arrhythmias in ischemic heart disease (IHD) traditionally relies on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and exercise-derived variables such as blood pressure response, Duke treadmill score, Veterans score, and rate–pressure product. However, these static parameters may not adequately capture beat-to-beat electrical instability. Dynamic T-wave angle variation, reflecting periodic repolarization instability, may provide superior predictive value. Purpose To determine whether dynamic T-wave angle variation during cardiac rehabilitation is superior to conventional pre-rehabilitation risk markers in predicting ventricular arrhythmias. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study including 78 patients with IHD (31 women). LVEF was &lt;35% in 27 patients, 35–49% in 15, and &gt;50% in the remainder. Fifty-two underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and the rest coronary bypass surgery, with no difference in arrhythmic outcomes between revascularization strategies. All patients completed a 12-session cardiac rehabilitation program with continuous 12-lead telemetry. Beat-to-beat T-wave angle was analyzed in real time. A sudden change &gt;10° was predefined as abnormal. The primary endpoint was ventricular arrhythmias (paired premature ventricular complexes, ventricular bigeminy, or non-sustained ventricular tachycardia). Predictive performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and comparative diagnostic accuracy analysis. Between-method comparisons were performed using chi-square testing, with p&lt;0.05 considered significant. Results A T-wave angle change &gt;10° predicted ventricular arrhythmias with sensitivity 89% and specificity 96% (p&lt;0.001 vs no angle change). False-negative cases were attributable to supraventricular arrhythmias (17 atrial tachycardia, 4 atrial flutter), in which T-wave angle variation was not statistically significant. Among conventional predictors, only LVEF &lt;35% (sensitivity 77%, specificity 94%; p=0.01) and exercise-induced hypotension (sensitivity 78%, specificity 97%; p=0.008) were significant, but both showed lower sensitivity compared with T-wave angle variation (p&lt;0.05 for sensitivity comparison). Other markers demonstrated inferior diagnostic performance: Duke score (44%/86%), Veterans score (47%/89%), flat and hypertensive blood pressure responses (28%/74% and 35%/68%), and rate–pressure product (56%/87%), none reaching comparable discriminative capacity. Conclusion(s) Dynamic T-wave angle variation &gt;10° during supervised cardiac rehabilitation showed superior sensitivity and high specificity for predicting ventricular arrhythmias compared with conventional pre-rehabilitation risk markers. Beat-to-beat repolarization monitoring may enhance electrical risk detection beyond traditional stratification strategies in patients with ischemic heart disease.Comparative ROC CurvesForest Plot – Diagnostic Accuracy
title: Superior diagnostic performance of beat-to-beat T-wave angle monitoring for ventricular arrhythmia prediction during cardiac rehabilitation

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) focuses on improving exercise capacity, that could be assessed as oxygen uptake at peak exercise (peak VO2). Despite CR being performed according to the recommended program, patients achieve different degrees of improvement in peak VO2. A change in peak VO2 (Δ peak VO2) from baseline to post-CR of at least 2 ml/min/kg is associated with better long-term prognosis. Aim The aim of this study was to identify predictors of improvement in VO2 ≥2 ml/min/kg in patients undergoing CR. Methods A single-center, retrospective registry of 518 patients who underwent CR was conducted. Exclusion criteria included history of cardiac surgery, inpatient rehabilitation, and the absence of cardiopulmonary exercise testing performed twice during CR. The clinical reasons for CR, demographic data, comorbidities, and hemodynamic parameters at rest (assessed via impedance cardiography (ICG)) were analyzed. The analysis included 271 patients who were divided into two subgroups according to Δ peak VO2: Δ peak VO2 ≥ 2ml/min/kg (95 patients, 76 men, median age 60 years) and Δ peak VO2 &lt; 2ml/min/kg (176 patients, 133 men, median age 63 years). Variables that significantly differed between the two subgroups with a p-value &lt; 0.1 were selected for the logistic regression analysis. Results In the univariate logistic regression, the following parameters were identified as predictors of Δ peak VO2 ≥ 2ml/min/kg: age (OR 0.96, p=0.007), number of previous percutaneous coronary intervention (OR 1.25, p=0.039), total fluid content (TFC) (OR 1.08, p=0.032), and Karvonen upper training heart rate range (OR 1.02, p=0.042). In multivariate regression analysis as independent predictors revealed: baseline predicted value of peak VO2 (baseline peak VO2 % pred. - OR 0.91, p&lt;0.001) and Karvonen upper training heart rate range (OR 1.03, p=0.004). Other variables, including comorbidities, left ventricular ejection fraction, reason of CR, other than TFC parameters via ICG were not associated with improvement in peak VO2 during CR. Conclusions The improvement of Δ peak VO2 ≥ 2ml/min/kg after CR has complex background. Lower exercise capacity before CR and higher training intensity revealed independent predictors of this positive effect. Individual comprehensive assessment is crucial for the qualification to CR, planning of intervention and prediction of the effects regarding exercise performance.
title: Predictors of improved physical performance during cardiac rehabilitation

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiovascular disease (CVD) continues to be the foremost cause of death in developed nations. Although there have been significant advancements in the acute management of myocardial infarction (MI), the implementation of secondary prevention strategies remains substantially underutilized. Comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation (CCR) is recognized as a critical component in improving outcomes for post-MI patients. This study was designed to rigorously evaluate the impact of CCR participation on survival rates. Methods Hungary has systematically recorded ACS cases since 2014 through the National Myocardial Infarction Register. For this retrospective cohort study, ACS outcomes were examined over a ten-year period, from 2014 to 2024. The study population included all individuals with a documented ACS event, and specific attention was paid to those surviving at least 30 days post-index event to mitigate the influence of early mortality and focus on those eligible for rehabilitation interventions. To ensure comparability between groups, a 1:1 propensity score-matching (PSM) analysis was conducted. Results A total of 158,599 ACS cases were identified during the study period. Of these, only 17.4% of eligible individuals enrolled in a CCR program. The subgroup analysis revealed that patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) who did not undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) exhibited both the lowest rates of CCR participation and the highest mortality rates. Factors independently associated with reduced CCR engagement included advanced age, male sex, NSTEMI diagnosis, and lack of PCI. To address potential confounding, a PSM analysis was conducted using age, sex, diabetes mellitus diagnosis, ACS type, and PCI status as fixed covariates. The procedure established a highly balanced cohort of 27,640 pairs (Mean Bias: 2.6%, Rubin’s B: 7.4%), effectively neutralizing baseline clinical disparities. This rigorous statistical approach demonstrated that CCR participation was associated with a 12.9% reduction in all-cause mortality (ATT = -0.1288; t = -25.84; p &lt; 0.001), compared to non-participants (24.8% vs. 37.7% in the matched groups). These findings were validated using the Rosenbaum-sensitivity test, which confirmed the robustness of the observed effect (p &lt; 0.001) even at a Gamma level of 2.0, indicating the results are insensitive to potential unmeasured confounding. Conclusion The results of this nationwide, retrospective cohort study provide compelling evidence that early survivors of ACS who participate in CCR programs experience significant improvements in survival. Despite the well-documented effectiveness and cost-efficiency of CCR, enrollment rates remain suboptimal at only 17.4%. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted interventions to increase CCR uptake, particularly among high-risk subgroups such as elderly NSTEMI patients without revascularization.
title: Participating in a comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation program enhances both mid- and long-term outcomes for early survivors of an acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a recognised cause of acute coronary syndrome in younger women. Beyond acute angiographic diagnosis and predominantly conservative management, many patients report persistent chest pain, reduced confidence to exercise, impaired functional capacity, and psychological distress. Optimal secondary prevention remains uncertain, and current recommendations rely largely on limited evidence for SCAD-specific interventions. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) may offer a structured pathway to restore exercise capacity and support psychosocial recovery beyond coronary healing. Purpose To quantify the association of CR with patient-centred recovery outcomes and to summarise available comparative evidence on clinical events after SCAD. Methods PubMed and Embase were searched through 15 February 2026 for studies reporting quantitative outcomes in SCAD patients participating in CR programmes. Outcomes included treadmill performance (METs), peak VO2, depression (PHQ-9), generalised anxiety (GAD-7), recurrent chest pain, revascularisation, MACE, angina hospitalisations, and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MD) and dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RR) using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Chi-squared test and the I2 statistic. Results Five observational studies, including 953 patients (459 CR; 494 no CR), were included. CR was associated with improved exercise capacity: pooled treadmill performance increased by 1.06 METs (MD 1.06 CI 0.48 to 1.64; p=0.0004), and pooled peak VO2 increased by 2.89 mL/kg/min (MD 2.89 CI 0.71 to 5.06; p=0.009). Chest pain prevalence decreased during CR, with study-level relative reductions ranging from 41% to 80%. Psychological outcomes improved where reported: PHQ-9 decreased by 2.33 points (MD -2.33 CI -5.58 to 0.92), and GAD-7 decreased by 4.4 points (MD -4.4 CI -6.44 to -2.36). Across pooled dichotomous clinical endpoints (revascularisation, MACE, angina hospitalisations, and recurrent MI), no significant differences were observed between CR participants and non-participants with short follow-up across studies. Conclusion(s) In patients with SCAD, CR is associated with clinically meaningful improvements in exercise capacity and patient-centred recovery outcomes, including reduced chest pain burden and improved anxiety and depressive symptoms, supporting CR as a key step beyond angiography to optimise recovery and return to function. However, available comparative data are underpowered for clinical events and cannot exclude benefit or harm. Larger prospective studies with standardised CR protocols and longer follow-up are required to define the impact of CR on recurrent events, health-care utilisation, and long-term quality of life, particularly given the prognostic relevance of cardiorespiratory fitness.Central IllustrationForest Plot of ETT and Peak VO
title: Beyond angiography: cardiac rehabilitation after spontaneous coronary artery dissection — a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background and objectives Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is an established component of secondary cardiovascular prevention. The extent to which it benefits postoperative patients remains clinically important. Accordingly, we evaluated the association between CR and clinical outcomes among patients undergoing cardiac valve interventions. Methods The TriNetX global federated research network was used to identify patients undergoing cardiac valve interventions (transcatheter aortic, pulmonary, mitral, and tricuspid valve implantation or replacement) and to compare those who subsequently received CR within 2 months with those without documented CR. The primary outcomes were 2-year composite events (death, myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction). Secondary outcomes were heart failure (HF), incident atrial fibrillation, valve prosthesis complications and dementia. The analyses were conducted with a 1-month landmark period to minimise the influence of early events. Results Before propensity-score matching (PSM), cardiac intervention patients who underwent CR (N=3,158, age:77.2 ± 8.8, 58.4% male) were more often male and had a higher prevalence of comorbidities, including hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, and diabetes mellitus, when compared with those who did not undergo CR (N=56,600, age: 76.7 ± 11.8, 56.6% male). After PSM (matched N=2,886), CR was associated with significantly lower 2-year risk of composite events (HR: 0.73, 95% CI: 0.65-0.82). In analyses restricted to aortic valve interventions, CR was associated with a lower 2-year risk of composite events (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.69-0.87) and heart failure (HR: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.47-0.87). Subgroup analyses stratified by age, sex, BMI and prior myocardial infarction, as well as sensitivity analysis of aortic valve interventions performed after 2020, were in line with the primary findings for composite events. Conclusion Among patients undergoing cardiac valve interventions, initiation of CR within 2 months was associated with significantly lower 2-year risks of composite events. These findings extend prior evidence supporting the effectiveness of CR in cardiovascular diseases.Main resultsSubgroups
title: Cardiovascular outcomes of cardiac rehabilitation in cardiac valve interventions: a TriNetX global federated network study

abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are among the leading causes of death globally. CVD is the most common comorbidity in patients with COPD, affecting up to 70% of patients. COPD is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular and pulmonary events, yet contemporary nationwide information about the magnitude of this risk is limited. We used a nationwide database of linked primary care, secondary care and death registry records from a representative sample in England to describe the incidence and timing of cardiopulmonary (CP) events in patients with COPD. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients with an incident diagnosis of COPD in the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) and Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) linked dataset. Patients aged ≥40 years with a first diagnosis of COPD between 01 Jan 2014 and 31 Dec 2019 were included. The primary outcome was CP events defined as any moderate or severe acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD), or hospitalisation for heart failure, myocardial infarction, revascularisation, stroke or arrythmia (including atrial fibrillation and flutter, tachycardia and other arrythmias). Hospitalisation spells for cardiovascular events were counted using either the primary-diagnosis only, or diagnosis in any position. Results Of 79,567 patients with COPD, mean age was 68 years, 54.0% were male, 28.0% had a cardiovascular event during baseline, 27.0% were prescribed an antiplatelet and 44.5% prescribed a statin. Median follow up was 3.2 years; 40.2% experienced a CP event within 1 year and 62.2% within 5 years of COPD diagnosis. After 5 years of follow up, cardiovascular hospitalisations affected 10.7% of patients when restricted to primary-diagnosis events and 27.4% when including primary and other diagnoses. Event-specific proportions (shown as primary versus any-listed diagnoses) were: heart failure 4.1% vs 14.3%, arrhythmia 3.1% vs 16.9%, myocardial infarction 2.2% vs 3.0%, and stroke 2.6% vs 7.7%. All-cause mortality was 22.6% and severe AECOPD hospitalisation occurred in 25.7%. Conclusions Following diagnosis of COPD, our results suggest that between 1–3 in 10 people with COPD will have experienced a cardiovascular event and 2 in 3 will have experienced a CP event within 5 years, with cardiovascular morbidity emerging early after COPD diagnosis. COPD should be considered a high cardiovascular risk condition, and emphasis placed on both the initiation and optimisation of guideline-directed cardiovascular and COPD therapies to comprehensively address cardiopulmonary risk and reduce overall cardiovascular burden.Figure 1:Cumulative incidence plots
title: Burden of cardiopulmonary events following diagnosis of COPD; a nationwide linked primary care, secondary care and death registry study

abstract: Abstract Background Evidence regarding the benefits and harms of intensive blood pressure control in patients with different stages of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains limited. Methods From the ESPRIT trial (Effects of intensive Systolic blood Pressure lowering treatment in reducing RIsk of vascular evenTs), participants with complete data were categorized by CKM staging followed AHA guidelines. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, revascularisation, hospitalization for heart failure, stroke or death from cardiovascular causes. We used Cox proportional hazards models to evaluate the effects of intensive treatment on primary outcome, MACE (a composite of myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, stroke, or death from cardiovascular diseases) all-cause death, and safety outcomes (kidney outcomes, and other serious adverse events of special interest [hypotension, syncope, electrolyte abnormality, injurious fall, or acute kidney injury]. Results We included 11,255 participants whose average age was 64.6 ± 7.1 years. Of the total participants, 2,542 (22.6%) were stage 2 CKM, 2,836 (25.2%) were stage 3 CKM, and 5,877 (52.2%) were stage 4 CKM. The effect of intensive treatment on primary and secondary outcomes did not differ significantly on the relative scale (Pinteraction &gt; 0.05). Furthermore, no significant interaction (except for kidney outcome; Pinteraction = 0.008]) was observed between CKM stages and the risk of serious adverse events associated with intensive treatment (Pinteraction &gt; 0.05). Conclusion Hypertensive patients with high cardiovascular risk benefit from the treatment strategy of targeting systolic BP &lt;120 mm Hg, regardless of their CKM stage status. In addition, the effects of intensive treatment on experiencing adverse events did not differ by CKM status except for kidney outcome.Forest plot
title: Effects of intensive blood pressure control in patients with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome:a post hoc analysis from ESPRIT

abstract: Abstract Background It is unknown whether homocysteine is associated with cardiovascular risk in controlled hypertensive patients, and whether it modifies the benefit of intensive blood pressure (BP) control. Methods ESPRIT was a multicenter, open-label, blinded-outcome, randomized controlled trial assigned participants with high cardiovascular risk 1:1 to intensive treatment (targeting systolic BP [SBP] below 120 mm Hg) or standard treatment (targeting SBP below 140 mm Hg). Participants were stratified into tertiles (T1: &lt;11.7μmol/L; T2: 11.7-15.2μmol/L; T3: ≥15.2μmol/L) by baseline homocysteine. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, revascularisation, hospitalization for heart failure, stroke or death from cardiovascular causes. We used Cox proportional hazards models to evaluate the association between homocysteine and cardiovascular events and effects of intensive treatment on cardiovascular outcomes, kidney outcome and safety outcomes. Results A total of 11220 patients (mean age, 64.6±7.1 years) were included in current study. Compared with participants in T1, participants in T3 had a significantly higher risk of primary outcome in the intensive and standard blood pressure control arms (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.21-1.95] and 1.33 [95% CI, 1.06-1.67], respectively). The effect of intensive treatment on primary outcome was not modified by homocysteine tertiles, with adjusted hazard ratios of 0.84 (95%CI, 0.66–1.06), 0.87 (95%CI, 0.71–1.06) and 0.91 (95% CI, 0.77-1.09) respectively (P for interaction=0.71). There’s no significant difference of kidney outcome and safety outcomes by intensive intervention across homocysteine tertiles (all P for interaction&gt;0.05). Conclusion Elevated homocysteine was associated with higher cardiovascular risk in well-controlled hypertensive patients, regardless of the targeting SBP level. Homocysteine did not modify the effect of intensive BP control.Effect of homocysteine on primary outcome
title: Effect of homocysteine on the outcomes of intensive blood pressure control: a post hoc analysis of the ESPRIT trial

abstract: Abstract Introduction Patients presenting with acute chest pain, dynamic cardiac biomarkers elevation and non-obstructive coronary arteries require additional testing to establish the underlying diagnosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is the reference standard but has limited availability and contraindications. Novel spectral computed tomography (CT) offers non-invasive assessment of coronary anatomy and pericoronary inflammatory status, as well as quantitative, advanced myocardial tissue characterization within a single examination. Purpose To assess whether myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) and late iodine enhancement (LIE) assessment by spectral CT can detect acute myocardial damage and differentiate among underlying aetiologies. Methods in this multicentre study, patients with acute chest pain and troponin cardiac rise referred for CMR were enrolled. Exclusion criteria included ≥ 50% coronary stenosis, prior diagnosis of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy or ischemic heart disease, or contraindications to contrast CMR or CT. Patients were also scheduled to undergo a spectral CT scan during admission. A control cohort consisted of patients without structural heart disease or epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent spectral CT for unrelated clinical indications. Automated myocardial segmentation (17-segment AHA model) using TotalSegmentator enabled extraction of median iodine density values from first-pass and LIE acquisitions, global extracellular volume (ECV), apex-to-base gradients. Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation was also analysed using a semi-automated software. A machine-learning model (XGBoost) integrating quantitative spectral CT parameters was trained for multiclass diagnosis using 10-fold cross-validation, with CMR as ground truth. Results among 154 consecutive patients admitted with acute myocardial damage, CMR diagnosis were myocarditis (n=66), MINOCA (n=33), stress cardiomyopathy (n=37), and undetermined aetiology (n=18). The control group included 169 individuals. Patients with stress cardiomyopathy (Table 1) had higher values of first-pass iodine density (2.34±0.44 mg/mL, p&lt;0.001) and global ECV (38.2±3.8%, p&lt;0.001), negative first perfusion apex-to-base gradient (-0.06 ± 0.29, p&lt;0.05) and a apex-to-base ECV gradient (3.7±5.1, p&lt;0.001). PCAT did not differ between groups (p=0.176). The XGBoost model achieved significant multiclass discrimination among the aetiologies, with highest performance for stress cardiomyopathy versus myocarditis (area under the curve: 0.88; Figure 2). Conclusions Quantitative spectral CT enables automated myocardial tissue characterization with meaningful diagnostic performance in this clinical scenario. This comprehensive single-test imaging strategy may expand access to tissue characterization beyond CMR and represents a comprehensive alternative when CMR is unavailable or in patients with low pretest probability of coronary disease.Figure 2.
title: Diagnostic utility of spectral computed tomography in acute myocardial damage without obstructive coronary disease: the CADAMI-SPECTRAL study

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) frequently remain at high residual risk due to suboptimal lipid control and clustering of cardiometabolic comorbidities. Scalable, implementation-ready approaches to systematically identify and prioritise these individuals in UK primary care remain elusive(1). We evaluated a digitally enabled phenotyping strategy, combined with a pragmatic additive cardiovascular risk management (CVRM) care-gap score, to quantify modifiable residual burden. Methods Within a primary care population of 10,306 adults, a standardised electronic search (CVDPL2F) identified patients with established ASCVD (CHD, PCI/stent, PAD, stroke/TIA), excluding familial hypercholesterolaemia and those using inclisiran, with LDL-C &gt;1.8 mmol/L or non-HDL &gt;2.5 mmol/L (2). Structured EHR data were extracted cross-sectionally. A CVRM care-gap score was defined as: baseline 2 (ASCVD + LDL above target) plus 1 point each for diabetes (HbA1c &gt;53 mmol/mol), hypertension (SBP &gt;140 mmHg), CKD (eGFR &lt;60), and obesity (BMI &gt;30 kg/m²). Risk modifiers (smoker, COPD, heart failure, AF, fatty liver) were flagged but not scored. Primary analysis quantified multimorbidity burden and treatment gaps. Results Of 10,306 patients, n=173 (1.7%) met criteria. Mean age 71.1±12.2 years; 57.2% male. Mean LDL-C 2.7mmol/L; 44.5% &gt;2.6 mmol/L. SBP &gt;140 mmHg in 7.5%; diabetes in 24.9% (HbA1c &gt;53: 11.6%); CKD in 26.0%; BMI &gt;30 in 24.9%. Mean CVRM score 3.2±0.7; 33.5% scored 4 or more. Two or more risk modifiers were present in 34.7% of cases. Conclusion Digital phenotyping identified a concentrated, very-high-risk ASCVD cohort with substantial multimorbidity and modifiable care gaps. The CVRM score provides a scalable prioritisation framework for structured community-based secondary prevention. A prospective longitudinal evaluation is underway to quantify intervention intensity (pharmacological and lifestyle) and the associated change in mean CVRM score, providing an objective measure of individualised care-gap modification within primary care.Figure 1
title: Digital phenotyping and additive multimorbidity scoring to operationalise very-high-risk secondary prevention in primary care

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction In coronary artery disease, stenosis burden and prognosis vary across patients, but in routine practice clinicians often have to act on incomplete risk stratification. We wanted an analysis that stays close to "what we actually see in the cath lab": angiographic stenosis severity in key segments, and survival differences by sex and common metabolic comorbidities. Purpose To quantify how gender, age, and hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidaemia relate to coronary stenosis severity and survival in a large angiography cohort. Methods We analysed a retrospective cohort of 19,890 patients with angiographically diagnosed coronary artery disease who underwent coronary angiography between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024 at a single tertiary cardiac centre. Percent stenosis was extracted for the left main coronary artery and the left anterior descending artery (LAD) (proximal and mid–distal segments). Because our main decision question was "does stenosis location/severity and diabetes add prognostic information beyond age?", we used Kaplan–Meier curves for unadjusted survival comparisons and multivariable Cox regression to adjust for age and comorbidities. Sex comparisons of stenosis severity used independent t-tests. Statistical significance was set at p &lt; 0.05, with hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals reported. Results Stenosis severity showed a location-specific sex pattern rather than a uniform difference. Men had higher stenosis in the proximal LAD (80.1% vs 77.4%; p &lt; 0.0001) and mid–distal LAD (78.9% vs 77.4%; p = 0.0245), while women had higher stenosis in the left main (66.6% vs 62.0%; p = 0.0127). Survival curves separated modestly but significantly: men had lower survival probability than women (log-rank p = 0.027). Comorbidity clustering marked a higher stenosis burden; for example, diabetes plus hypertension was associated with higher stenosis (proximal LAD 84.5%; p &lt; 0.001). In the adjusted model, proximal LAD stenosis (hazard ratio 1.15, 95% confidence interval 1.08–1.23; p &lt; 0.01) and diabetes (hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.10–1.35; p &lt; 0.05) independently predicted mortality. Here’s the trade-off: these associations are clinically usable for risk stratification, but the retrospective design means residual confounding cannot be fully excluded. Conclusion In a large angiography cohort, gender differences in stenosis were segment-specific (higher LAD stenosis in men, higher left main stenosis in women), and survival differed by sex. Diabetes and hypertension tracked with greater stenosis burden, and proximal LAD stenosis and diabetes independently predicted mortality after adjustment. These findings support personalised risk assessment that explicitly integrates stenosis location with comorbidity profile, while prospective studies with standardised follow-up should validate causality and refine risk thresholds.Stenosis Severity by artery and genderKaplan-Meier Curve for Male vs.female
title: Gender differences, age trends, and comorbidities impact on coronary artery stenosis severity and survival outcomes: a retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Pregnancy complications and female-specific conditions are recognised cardiovascular risk modifiers, yet their link with ischaemic heart disease is unclear. Purpose To determine associations between female-specific cardiovascular risk modifiers and ischaemic heart disease. Methods This cross-sectional study included 1,000 women with cardiac symptoms. The diagnosis of Ischaemic heart disease (IHD) comprised acute coronary syndromes, myocardial infarction, angina, and coronary artery disease. Exposures were gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus, pre-eclampsia, pre-term delivery, and polycystic ovary syndrome. Associations were analysed and adjusted for age, hypertension, and diabetes. The study was approved by an ethics committee and conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. Results IHD occurred in 272 women (27.2%). Hypertension and diabetes were more common (p &lt; 0.001). Adjusted odds ratios (OR) were 3.51 (95% CI 2.04–6.03) for gestational hypertension, 2.82 (1.62–4.89) for gestational diabetes, 5.22 (2.58–10.55) for pre-eclampsia, 1.98 (1.21–3.24) for pre-term delivery, and 2.52 (1.46–4.38) for polycystic ovary syndrome. Conclusion(s) Female-specific cardiovascular risk modifiers are independently associated with ischaemic heart disease in women. Recording pregnancy and hormonal history may improve early identification of women at high cardiovascular risk.Figure1_ForestPlot_AdjustedORsFigure2_ Comparison of IHD vs Non IHD_pv
title: Female specific cardiovascular risk modifiers associated with ischaemic heart disease in women: cross sectional analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in adults aged 18–55 years presents ongoing challenges, with evidence indicating worse outcomes for young women compared to men. This study investigates sex differences in AMI outcomes, treatment, and comorbidity burden to explore the “ischaemic paradox” where women experience higher mortality despite similar or lower risk profiles. Methods A national inpatient cohort of young AMI discharges from 2018 to 2022 (N=602,565) was analyzed using survey weights to generate national estimates. Comparisons between men and women were made on in-hospital mortality, revascularisation rates (PCI and CABG), and comorbidity burden. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for patient demographics, hospital characteristics, and Elixhauser comorbidities. Results Young AMI discharges were more frequent in men (2.12 million) than in women (0.89 million). Crude in-hospital mortality was similar by sex (men 2.04%, women 2.02%), but women had lower rates of PCI (42.12% vs 53.17%) and CABG (5.52% vs 7.94%). Adjusted analyses revealed female sex was associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality (OR 1.134), slightly higher odds of PCI (OR 1.075), and lower odds of CABG (OR 0.817). Mortality peaked in 2020 for both sexes, with persistent lower revascularisation use in women. Conclusions Despite similar crude mortality, adjusted analyses confirm higher in-hospital mortality for young women with AMI, supporting the persistence of the ischaemic paradox. Differences in treatment utilization suggest sex-specific variations in case-mix and treatment selection. Further research incorporating detailed AMI phenotyping and treatment timing is needed to address sex disparities in outcomes.
title: Sex differences in in-hospital mortality and revascularisation among young adults with acute myocardial infarction: evidence of an ischaemic paradox from a national cohort (2018–2022)

abstract: Abstract Background Ischemic heart disease disproportionately affects Eastern Europe and is the leading cause of death in Romania. Despite this, sex-specific outcomes after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remain underreported in the region. Purpose To explore sex differences in clinical care, ventricular remodeling, and clinical outcomes among Romanian patients with STEMI. Methods We examined the characteristics of 777 men and 308 women prospectively enrolled in the Romanian Registry for Post-myocardial Infarction Left Ventricular Remodeling and Heart Failure Prevention (REDEFINE-HF) from 2020 to 2023. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) was performed in 130 patients at baseline and 6-month follow-up. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Results Women had a higher prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors, longer total ischemic time, and larger infarctions than men (p&lt;0.05). Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) restored TIMI 3 flow in 78% of women vs 86% of men, and 23% of women vs 15% of men developed significant ischemic mitral regurgitation (p&lt;0.01). Female sex, diabetes, and the extent of acute myocardial injury were associated with larger 6-month scars on CMR (p&lt;0.01). In Kaplan-Meier analysis, the 3-year mortality was 27% in women vs 17% in men (Figure, p&lt;0.001). In Cox regression analysis, women and men had comparable survival after adjustment for age, diabetes, hypertension, smoking, baseline troponin T, kidney function and glycemia, and restored epicardial flow at PCI (p=0.28). Conclusions Substantial sex gaps in risk factor management and STEMI care contribute to excess mortality among Romanian women after STEMI. These findings underscore the need for targeted population interventions and sex-specific follow-up for patients at risk of, or with established, ischemic heart disease in the region.Figure
title: Sex gaps in clinical care, left ventricular remodeling, and mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction in an Eastern European cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Preserved ejection fraction (EF) can mask subclinical dysfunction in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS). Global longitudinal strain (GLS), B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and the E/e′ ratio (E/E′) provide prognostic information before aortic valve replacement (AVR), but uniform cut offs may overlook sex differences. Building on our previous study that for the first time defined cut off values for these parameters in asymptomatic severe AS with preserved EF, we now investigate sex specific thresholds within an integrated risk model. Purpose To explore sex specific thresholds for GLS, BNP and E/E′ and validate their predictive value in a longitudinal risk model for adverse left ventricular (LV) remodeling and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after AVR. Methods This substudy expands our previously published cohort of 96 patients by including additional female patients, resulting in 116 patients with severe asymptomatic AS and preserved EF (&gt;50%) who underwent AVR (60% men, 40% women). Echocardiography (GLS, EF, LV mass index [LVMI], interventricular septal diameter [IVSd], LV internal diameter in diastole [LVIDd], E/E′), BNP and clinical outcomes were assessed at baseline and 1, 3 and 6 months. Primary endpoint was LV remodeling; secondary endpoint MACE. Results Women had smaller LV dimensions but higher relative wall thickness. Impaired GLS (&lt;15) was frequent in both sexes (74% men vs. 80% women). At 6 months, negative remodeling persisted more in men (68% vs. 57%), while GLS &gt;15 predicted favorable remodeling, stronger in women (OR 7.2, p=0.018). For MACE, E/E′ was predictive in men (OR 3.45, p=0.003), BNP in women (OR 1.01 per 10 pg/ml, p=0.041). ROC analysis confirmed prognostic value of GLS, BNP and E/E for adverse remodeling and MACE in both sexes, with sex related differences in optimal thresholds. GLS showed strong discrimination in women (AUC 0.85, optimal cut off ≤14) and men (AUC 0.80, optimal cut off ≤15). BNP remained predictive in men (AUC 0.70, cut off 200 pg/ml) and in women at lower thresholds (150 pg/ml). E/E′ demonstrated strong discrimination in men (AUC 0.84, cut off 13) and moderate but significant discrimination in women (AUC 0.72, cut off 15). MACE occurred more frequently in men (27%) than in women (15%), but at higher (more impaired) GLS thresholds, lower BNP thresholds, and higher E/E′ thresholds in women. Conclusion Women with asymptomatic severe AS exhibit negative remodeling and increased risk of MACE at more impaired GLS thresholds, higher E/E′ thresholds, and lower BNP thresholds compared with men as identified within our integrated model. Sex-specific thresholds refine risk stratification and guide individualized timing of AVR. These findings, supported by our sex- specific integrated GLS–BNP–E/E′ model, warrant multicenter validation.
title: Uniform cut offs underestimate women: sex specific thresholds for GLS, BNP and E/E′ model in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis

abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) predominantly affects women with limited traditional atherosclerotic risk burden and is frequently accompanied by persistent extra-cardiac symptoms suggestive of autonomic involvement. However, systematic autonomic phenotyping in SCAD is lacking. We quantified autonomic symptom burden and examined its association with antecedent dysautonomic features in SCAD survivors. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 227 adults with angiographically confirmed SCAD completed the Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31 (COMPASS-31) and EuroQol-5Dimension-5L (EQ-5D-5L). A 10-item Composite Historical Autonomic Predisposition Score (CHAPS) assessed adolescent and early adult autonomic features. Internal consistency (Cronbach’s α=0.76) and known-groups validity were evaluated. Hierarchical linear regression examined independent predictors of autonomic burden with prespecified blocks including demographics (age, body mass index, smoking), SCAD characteristics (recurrence, time since event), and biological phenotype variables (historical predisposition, hypotension, migraine). Results Participants were 97.8% female with median age 53 [47–58] years, assessed a median 3.0 [1.0–5.0] years post-index event; 21.6% reported recurrence. Moderate autonomic burden (COMPASS-31 ≥20) was present in 56.4%, with 16.3% severe (≥40). Cardiovascular (orthostatic intolerance) and gastrointestinal domains contributed most to overall severity. Historical autonomic predisposition correlated with contemporary COMPASS-31 (ρ=0.559; 95%CI 0.459–0.644; p&lt;0.001). In hierarchical modelling, CHAPS was the strongest independent predictor of autonomic burden (β=0.514; p&lt;0.001), with the final model explaining 36.0% of variance; younger age and smoking were also independently associated (both p≤0.01). Migraine was more frequent among those with COMPASS-31 ≥20 (p=0.043). (Table 1.) Participants with COMPASS-31 ≥20 more frequently reported impairment in mobility and pain/discomfort domains of the EQ-5D (all p≤0.03), with lower health utility (0.903 [0.793–0.956] vs 0.924 [0.890–0.968]; p&lt;0.001). Autonomic burden independently predicted reduced health utility in multivariable analysis (β=−0.150; p=0.029). Hypertension (26.0%) and dyslipidaemia (17.6%) were modest, with current smoking uncommon (2.2%), and traditional cardiovascular risk factors were not independently associated with autonomic severity. Autonomic measures were not associated with SCAD recurrence. Conclusion Autonomic symptom burden is common and clinically meaningful in SCAD. The strong and independent association with antecedent dysautonomic features supports a pre-existing autonomic vulnerability rather than a purely reactive consequence of a cardiac event. These findings suggest altered autonomic regulation may represent an under-recognised component of the SCAD phenotype warranting prospective mechanistic investigation.
title: Autonomic phenotype and antecedent autonomic symptoms in spontaneous coronary artery dissection

abstract: Abstract Background Women with coronary artery disease (CAD) often report worse health-related quality of life (HRQoL) compared to men. However, the longitudinal effect of elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) on HRQoL between women and men is less studied. Purpose The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of elective PCI on patients’ health status measured by HRQoL instruments, and to determine whether there are differences in improvement of symptoms and HRQoL between women and men. Methods A total of 88 women (29.3%) and 212 (70.7%) men undergoing elective PCI self-assessed their HRQoL using both the disease-specific seven-item Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) and the generic HRQoL 15D instrument at baseline and at one and 12 months after PCI. We used unadjusted and adjusted linear mixed models to compare the groups. Results Women were almost three years older, had lower glomerulus filtration rate, and had less severe CAD compared to men. At baseline, women reported more angina-related physical limitations (SAQ-PL) (p=0.003). Otherwise, both instrument scores (SAQ-7 and 15D) were comparable between the sexes. At one month, both sexes improved their SAQ-7 and 15D scores, with statistically significant and clinically important improvements. Excellent health status (SAQ-7 score) was more common among men (62.8% vs. 75.5%). Both groups improved their SAQ-AF clinically importantly, whereas women were less often angina-free (32.2% vs. 52.4%, p=0.017) (Figure 1). At 12 months, both instrument scores remained improved in women and men. Fair health status (SAQ-7) was more common among women (11.9% vs. 6.8%), while men reported their health status more often as excellent (58.3% vs. 75.2%, respectively) (p=0.027). Moreover, women had worse SAQ-PL (p=0.013), and they were less often free of angina (38.8% vs. 48.6%, p=0.020). In both groups, the 15D score started to decline but remained improved (Figure 2). There was no difference in 12-month improvement in 15D between sexes (p=0.852). In addition, there were no differences between sexes in major adverse cardiac or cerebrovascular events during the 12-month follow-up. Conclusions Both women and men reported significant improvements in disease-specific and generic HRQoL following elective PCI. However, at 12 months, women showed less improvement in the SAQ-7, SAQ-PL, and SAQ-AF scores than men.
title: Sex differences in health status after elective percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background and Aim Sex-related disparities in the presentation, management, and outcome of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) persist globally. However, evidence from transitional healthcare systems remains limited. We aimed to investigate sex-based differences in clinical characteristics, invasive management, and in-hospital outcomes among patients hospitalized with AMI in Kosovo over an 11-year period. Methods In this observational cohort study, 13,099 consecutive patients admitted with AMI between 2014 and 2024 were analyzed. Demographic, clinical, and procedural data were compared by sex. Trends were evaluated using polynomial regression, and predictors of in-hospital mortality were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Results Women comprised 29% of the cohort (n = 3,759) and were older than men (67.7 ± 11.0 vs. 62.2 ± 11.3 years; p &lt; 0.001). Hypertension and diabetes were more prevalent in women (78 vs. 62% and 48 vs.31%, respectively; p &lt; 0.001 for both), while smoking was more prevalent in men (58 vs. 26%; p &lt; 0.001). Women underwent coronary angiography and primary PCI less often (64 vs. 73% and 47 vs. 55%; p &lt; 0.001 for both) and had higher in-hospital mortality (14 vs. 6.2%; p &lt; 0.001). After adjustment, increasing age and diabetes mellitus independently predicted mortality in both sexes. Conclusions In this national cohort from a transitional health care system, women with AMI presented at older age, carried greater comorbidity burden, received less invasive management, and experienced higher in-hospital mortality. These findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to ensure equitable access to reperfusion therapy and sex-specific cardiovascular prevention.Figure 1.Adjusted odds ratios of outcomes
title: Persistent sex disparities in presentation, invasive management, and in-hospital mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction: an 11-year national cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Women with angina and no obstructive coronary artery disease (ANOCA) remain at increased cardiovascular risk, likely in part driven by systemic inflammation and coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD). Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a key inflammatory mediator associated with cardiovascular events in the general population and with CMD in women with ANOCA. We aimed to investigate whether IL-6 identifies a cardiometabolic high-risk phenotype and whether IL-6 predicts long-term cardiovascular prognosis in women with ANOCA, more on whether its prognostic value is influenced by CMD. Methods We studied 1,636 women with stable angina and &lt;50% coronary stenosis from the iPOWER (Improving Diagnosis and Treatment of Women with Angina Pectoris and Microvascular Disease) cohort. Key exclusion criteria in the iPOWER cohort were suspected non-ischemic chest pain, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (&lt;45%), prior myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization and severe comorbidity. Plasma IL-6 was measured at baseline. The primary outcomes was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, revascularization, ischemic stroke, and heart failure. Associations with outcome were assessed using Fine-Gray sub distribution hazard model including non-cardiovascular death as a competing risk adjusted for age and cardiovascular risk factors. Prespecified subgroup analyses included assessment of potential effect modification by CMD defined as coronary flow velocity reserve (CFVR) &lt;2.0. Results Higher IL-6 was associated with a cardiometabolically shifted phenotype characterized by adiposity, diabetes, a high triglyceride–low HDL-C lipid profile and reduced CFVR. During a median follow-up of 10.8 years, 250 women (15.3%) experienced major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Doubling in IL-6 was associated with increased risk of MACE (subdistribution hazard ratio (SHR) 1.19, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.03-1.37). The association was independent of CMD (unadjusted SHR: 1.30 vs 1.27). Conclusion IL-6 identified an inflammation-driven cardiometabolic high-risk phenotype in women with ANOCA and independently predicted major adverse cardiovascular events. Its prognostic value was not explained by CMD, underscoring IL-6 as a clinically relevant marker of long-term cardiovascular risk.HeatMap Inflammatory Profiling Women wANOCASmooth HR and density IL-6 and risk of MACE
title: Inflammatory profiling in ANOCA: IL-6 predicts cardiovascular events independent of coronary microvascular dysfunction

abstract: Abstract Background In women presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) without high-risk features, the underlying pathophysiology often differs from that observed in men. Women are less likely to exhibit obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) and more frequently present with alternative mechanisms of myocardial injury, including spontaneous coronary artery dissection, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, and coronary microvascular dysfunction. In this context, coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) offers a valuable non-invasive approach, given its high sensitivity and negative predictive value for the exclusion of obstructive coronary artery disease. Purpose To analyze the role of CCTA in ACS in low and intermediate risk female patients. Methods 436 female patients were evaluated with a protocol that includes the use of CCTA in ACS, among a total cohort of 1,001 patients. Women over 18 years of age with a diagnosis of ACS without ST elevation who did not meet high-risk criteria (hemodynamic instability, dynamic changes in the ST segment or T wave, ventricular arrhythmia, GRACE score &gt;140, refractory angina, heart failure or cardiorespiratory arrest) and consulted the emergency department were included. Data collection was carried out between May 2022 and February 2026. Results 436 female patients were included, with a mean age of 58 years.
