However, elderly patients, particularly those aged 75 years or older with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), have a higher risk of both thrombotic events and bleeding complications. The optimal choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in this vulnerable population remains a subject of debate, with a lack of large-scale, real-world evidence to guide clinical decision-making. Purpose This study aimed to compare the association of ticagrelor versus clopidogrel with the risks of ischemic and hemorrhagic events in patients aged ≥75 years with STEMI. Methods We conducted a retrospective, multicenter, target trial emulation study. The study included 13,884 consecutive patients aged ≥75 years diagnosed with STEMI who were treated with dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) consisting of aspirin plus either clopidogrel or ticagrelor. All patients were followed for at least one year. To minimize confounding, a propensity score weighting approach using overlap weights was employed. The primary endpoint was net adverse events (NACE) at one year, including ischemic events (cardiac death, recurrent myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke), hemorrhagic events (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) classification≥3 or intracerebral hemorrhage), and cardiac death. Secondary outcomes were major adverse cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events (MACCE) including ischemic events (cardiac death, recurrent myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke) and all-cause death at one year. Results Among 13,884 eligible STEMI patients aged ≥75 years, 12,078 (87.0%) received clopidogrel and 1,806 (13.0%) received ticagrelor. In the overlap-weighted cohort, the risk of one-year NACE was significantly lower in the ticagrelor group compared with the clopidogrel group (HR: 0.852, 95% CI: 0.746-0.969, P = 0.015). The risk of one-year MACCE was also significantly lower in the ticagrelor group (HR: 0.845, 95% CI: 0.739-0.967, P = 0.014). However, there was no statistically significant difference in the risk of all-cause death at 1 year between the two groups (HR: 0.903, 95% CI: 0.772-1.055, P = 0.199). Conclusion In this target trial emulation study of patients aged ≥75 years with STEMI, the use of ticagrelor, compared with clopidogrel, was associated with a significant reduction in both NACE and MACCE at one-year follow-up, without a significant increase in all-cause mortality.Kaplan–Meier curveBaseline characteristics and SMD plot
title: Comparative effectiveness of ticagrelor versus clopidogrel in older adults (≥75 years) with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a target trial emulation study

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Despite advances in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk assessments by standardised risk calculators for primary prevention, cardiovascular events and complications remain difficult to predict, particularly in old age and for secondary prevention. DNA methylation (DNAm) age calculated from epigenetic clocks strongly correlates with chronological age but whether epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has relevance to acute cardiovascular events has been unexplored. Purpose To determine the capacity of EAA to predict incident acute cardiovascular events. Methods Community-living older adults aged &gt;/=60y were profiled for blood DNAm using Infinium MethylationEPIC v1 arrays (Illumina). Five epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge and GrimAge2 were analysed. EAA was calculated from regression residuals where positive and negative values indicated acceleration and deceleration of biological age, respectively. ASCVD and comorbidities were documented at baseline. Prospective outcomes of mortality and hospitalisation were collected. 1H-nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (Nightingale) was used to quantify blood concentrations of glycosylated acetyls (GlycA) as a composite marker of inflammation. p&lt;0.05 was considered significant. The study was approved by institutional ethics committee and all participants provided written informed consent. Results DNAm at baseline was analysed in 535 older adults (median age 78y, IQR 69–85, range 60–99). DNAm age independently calculated from five epigenetic clocks were all positively correlated with chronological age and frailty (all p&lt;0.0001), with no sex differentiated effects. Of five EAA estimates, only PhenoAge (PhenoAA), GrimAge (GrimAA) and GrimAge2 (Grim2AA) were associated with GlycA (p&lt;0.01, p&lt;0.0001 and p&lt;0.0001, respectively). By logistic regression, only GrimAA and Grim2AA remained significantly associated with baseline ASCVD risk factors and comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, p&lt;0.05 to p&lt;0.01; angina pectoris, both p&lt;0.05; history of ischaemic heart disease, both p&lt;0.05; history of myocardial infarction, both p&lt;0.05). During a median follow-up of 4.68y (IQR 3.91–6.44), 30 individuals were lost to follow-up, 55 (10.9%) died, while 178 (35.2%) and 101 (20.0%) experienced first all-cause and cardiovascular hospitalisations, respectively. In all analyses performed, Grim2AA was superior to GrimAA. Of note, the median Grim2AA in persons hospitalised for ASCVD predominantly secondary to ACS (not including stroke) was +0.73y (IQR -1.36 to +4.39, n=42). For every 1-year increase in Grim2AA, the hazard of future cardiovascular hospitalisation was increased by 5.7–6.1% (all p&lt;0.05), and the hazard of ASCVD hospitalisation predominantly secondary to acute coronary syndrome (ACS) was increased by 11% (p&lt;0.01). Conclusion(s) GrimAge2 can predict incident cardiovascular and ASCVD hospitalisation predominantly secondary to ACS.
title: Acceleration of DNA methylation (epigenetic) clocks especially GrimAge2 can predict incident acute coronary syndrome in older adults

abstract: Abstract Introduction The growing proportion of very elderly patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) raises uncertainty regarding the benefit of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), particularly in those aged ≥85 years, who often exhibit increased frailty and multiorgan impairment. Purpose To compare clinical characteristics, management strategies and predictors of in-hospital mortality between patients aged 75–84 years and those aged ≥85 years hospitalised with ACS, focusing on the impact of PCI. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of consecutive patients aged ≥75 years admitted with ACS. Patients were stratified into two groups: 75–84 years and ≥85 years. Categorical variables were analysed using χ² or Fisher’s exact test and continuous variables using Student’s t-test or Mann–Whitney U test, as appropriate. Univariate logistic regression was performed separately in each group to identify predictors of in-hospital mortality. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was used to assess renal function. Results PCI was performed more frequently in patients aged 75–84 years than in those aged ≥85 years (34.8% vs 17.4%, p&lt;0.001). In-hospital mortality was similar between groups (16.2% vs 19.9%, p=0.178). Patients aged ≥85 years had lower systolic blood pressure, lower haemoglobin, higher urea, lower eGFR, lower albumin and a higher prevalence of chronic kidney disease (all p&lt;0.05), indicating reduced physiological reserve. In patients aged 75–84 years, PCI was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (p&lt;0.001); absence of PCI was associated with increased risk of death (odds ratio 2.678; 95% confidence interval 1.673–4.258). In contrast, PCI was not associated with mortality reduction in patients aged ≥85 years (p=0.943). In both groups, mortality was associated with higher Killip class, cardiac arrest at admission, lower systolic blood pressure, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, hyperglycaemia, elevated urea and creatinine, and lower eGFR. Conclusion Patients aged 75–84 years appear to benefit from invasive management, whereas in those aged ≥85 years short-term mortality is predominantly driven by systemic factors, and PCI does not significantly influence in-hospital outcome. These findings support age- and frailty-oriented individualised decision-making in elderly patients with ACS.
title: Impact of percutaneous coronary intervention on in-hospital mortality in elderly patients with acute coronary syndrome: an age-stratified analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Long-term prognosis after Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) is increasingly influenced by non-cardiovascular deaths, with cancer emerging as the leading contributor. Nevertheless, comprehensive real-world evidence on cancer-specific mortality across ACS subtypes and their temporal trajectories remains limited. Purpose To investigate the spectrum of cancer-related mortality after ACS and to compare temporal cancer mortality risks between Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) and Unstable Angina (UA). Methods In this nationwide, multicentre, individual-based cohort study, ACS patients discharged from the Chinese Cardiovascular Association database - Chest Pain Centers (2018–2021) were initially involved. Outcome data were obtained by linking their national identification numbers to the Chinese CDC - Cause of Death Reporting System. In-hospital deaths and cases with missing discharge data were excluded. Causes of death were categorised according to ICD-10 codes. Competing risks analysis was used to compare cancer mortality between AMI and UA by employing the Fine-Gray model, with cardiovascular death treated as a competing event. Temporal patterns were assessed in two phases: within 12 months and beyond 12 months post-discharge. Results Among 1,562,956 ACS patients (mean age 63.8±12.3 years; AMI: 60.95%, UA: 39.05%), 11,172 cancer deaths (72.2% male) occurred over 4 years. Lung cancer accounted for 34.7% of cases, followed by gastric (12.6%), liver (12.4%), oesophageal (5.6%), and pancreatic cancers (4.1%). Lung cancer was the leading cause across ACS subtypes (Table 1). After multivariable adjustment, UA patients had a lower survival probability compared with AMI patients (adjusted sHR 1.44, 95% CI 1.39–1.50, p&lt;0.01) (Figure 1A and B). Within the first year post-discharge, cancer-specific mortality risk was similar across ACS subtypes; however, a significantly elevated risk was observed in UA patients beyond 12 months (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08–1.19, p&lt;0.05) (Figure 1C). Conclusion Among Chinese ACS-discharged patients, lung cancer was the predominant cause of cancer mortality. Patients presenting with UA exhibited a significantly elevated long-term cancer mortality burden compared to those with AMI. These findings highlight the importance of long-term cancer risk monitoring after ACS, in particular for the follow-up care of UA patients.Table1Figure1
title: Cancer-specific mortality after acute coronary syndrome: insights from a nationwide real-world cohort

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is established in patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR) and high operative risk. Cancer patients with severe MR are frequently considered at increased risk for surgical mitral valve repair due to tumor burden, comorbidities, and potential cardiotoxic effects of oncologic therapies. Despite the growing overlap between oncology and structural heart disease, evidence on procedural safety and outcomes of M-TEER in cancer patients remains limited. Purpose To evaluate and compare procedural success and post-procedural MR reduction in patients with active cancer (AC), stable cancer (SC), and no cancer undergoing M-TEER. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 400 consecutive patients (age 77.3 ± 10.0 years; 58.3% male) who underwent M-TEER using the PASCAL system between 2019 and 2024. Patients were stratified into three groups: no cancer (n=293), SC (n=71), and AC (n=36). We compared residual MR at discharge and follow-up, as well as procedure time, in-hospital major adverse events (MAE) defined according to the Mitral Valve Academic Research Consortium (MVARC) criteria and 1-year mortality between groups. Results At baseline 310 patients (77.5%) had severe MR, while the rest of the patients had moderate to severe MR. This did not differ between patients with AC, SC or no cancer (figure 1). Likewise, residual MR post procedure was comparable between groups with overall 360 patients (90%) reaching residual MR ≤ I° (figure 2). Reduction in MR remained stable upon 90 days and 1 year, again with no differences between groups (figure 3 and 4). Procedure time tended to be shorter in AC patients (75.9 ± 34.5 minutes) compared with controls (91.4 ± 48.3 minutes; p = 0.06). In-hospital MAE were infrequent in all groups (4.1% in controls, 9.9% in SC, and 2.8% in AC; p = 0.70 for AC vs. controls), and no intraprocedural mortality was observed. No significant differences in mortality were observed between the control, SC, and AC sub-groups during the first 30 days after M-TEER (1% vs. 0% vs. 0%; p = 0.58; for AC, SC and controls, respectively) and at 1 year (7.5% vs. 14.1% vs. 5.6%; p = 0.57; for AC, SC and controls, respectively). Conclusions M-TEER achieves high procedural success and effective MR reduction in patients with and without cancer. Cancer status, including active malignancy, does not impair immediate procedural outcomes, safety, or long-term MR reduction. These findings support M-TEER as a feasible and effective therapeutic option in cancer patients with severe MR.
title: Procedural success after M-TEER in cancer patients: a single-center study

abstract: Abstract Background Inherited arrhythmogenic and structural cardiomyopathies represent the leading cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests (OHCAs) in the young. Previous studies focusing exclusively on OHCA survivors have identified inherited cardiovascular diseases (CVD) in 11–40% of cases. Purpose to assess the prevalence of genetic variants in genes associated with CVD among young patients experiencing OHCA due to medical causes in Lombardy Region, Italy. Methods This is a prospective study including all OHCA occurring in individuals ≤50 years of age due to medical causes in Pavia province from 5/2021 to 12/2025. Following this initial phase, enrollment was extended to the entire Lombardy Region in 1/2026. Blood samples were collected, and Next Generation Sequencing was performed using a multigene panel targeting genes associated with CVD. Genetic variants were classified according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines. Family-based genetic and clinical screening was offered when a pathogenic (P) or likely pathogenic (LP) variant was identified. An additional evaluation of "hot" variants of uncertain significance (VUS) was conducted based on the geneticist’s recommendation. Results In the pilot study, 2457 OHCA cases were recorded; 118 met the inclusion criteria, and 68 underwent genetic testing (4 tests are still ongoing). At least 1 genetic variant was detected in 29 patients (43%), and 8 (13%) carried at least 1 LP/P variant. Family genetic and clinical screening has been completed in 5 cases: in 2 patients, autopsy demonstrated acute coronary syndrome as the cause of death, unrelated to the identified variants (TTN and LAMA2, respectively); in 1 case, two LP/P variants in trans in the GAA gene were identified, although no clinical signs were observed in the victim; family screening revealed heterozygous variants consistent with autosomal recessive late-onset Pompe Disease; in another case, the post-resuscitation imaging showed cerebellar hemorrhage, which was not consistent with the identified LP variant in MYH7; in the last patient, a P variant in GAA and two VUS in DSP were detected, compatible with post-OHCA diagnosis of non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy. Family segregation analysis is currently ongoing and may lead to variant reclassification. The extended analysis started in 2026 across the entire region has so far enrolled 22 new subjects (44% of the 50 new patients eligible for enrolment), whose genetic analyses are currently underway. Conclusions GenetiCA study is currently the largest real-world assessment of inherited CVD among young OHCA patients within an entire geographical area of 10 million inhabitants. Preliminary results highlight the importance of genetic testing correlating with clinical autopsy to establish the causality of death. The study aims to clarify the genetic bases of OHCA with potential impact on epidemiology and preventive medicine.
title: Feasibility and preliminary results of the GenetiCA study: evaluation of genetic-molecular causes of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest - from patients to families

abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) associated myocarditis (ICIAM) is a lethal complication caused mainly by cytotoxic CD8(+) T cells. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation (NETosis), albeit an innate immune-mechanism, has also been implicated in various autoimmune diseases, yet its contribution to ICIAM remains unexplored. Objective This study aims to examine the role of NET/NETosis in the latent or overt ICIAM (OICIAM/LICIAM) induced by anti-programmed cell death protein-1 antibody (αPD1), and to explore the potential values of NET/NETosis in early detection and treatment targets of ICIAM. Methods The study first performed scRNA-seq of PBMCs from LICIAM patients and RNA-seq of myocardial tissues from melanoma-bearing mice with LICIAM and OICIAM to identify the differential expression genes (DEGs) and enrich potential pathway related to ICIAM. Then further assess the transcriptional and expression alterations of NET/NETosis axis in LICIAM mice, LICIAM mice treated with PF-1355 alone or in combination with PMA, with RT-qPCR, western blotting, and histopathological studies. Patients with LICIAM/OICIAM were recruited to essay serum biomarkers related to NET/NETosis and pyroptosis. Results Transcriptomic enrichment results from cancer patients and tumor-bearing mice with LICIAM identified the DEGs including CXCR1, GZMB, and CAPZB in humans, as well as Ly6g and Padi4 in mice, with pathway analyses consistently implicating neutrophils activation and NET/NETosis. Myocardial tissues from LICIAM mice demonstrated significantly increased fluorescence intensities of MPO and CitH3, accompanied by elevated mRNA levels of NETosis-related genes (Mpo, Ly6g, Padi4) and neutrophil-related chemokines (Cxcl2, Il17, Ifnγ) (all P&lt;0.0001). Concurrently, the transcriptional and expressional level of NLRP3 inflammasome-pyroptosis pathway was activated. Treatment with the MPO inhibitor PF-1355 effectively reduced these changes, which could be totally reversed by PMA co-treatment, thereby confirming mechanistic involvement. In the clinical cohort with control (n=20), LICIAM (n=20), and OICIAM (n=20) groups, NETosis biomarkers (CitH3 and cfDNA) were strongly correlated with ICIAM patients, especially in LICIAM group (all R&gt;0.80), while the conventional myocardial injury marker hs-cTnT showed only a moderate-to-strong association (all R≤0.75), suggesting that NETosis-related biomarkers may offer additional value to hs-cTnT for the early detection of LICIAM. Conclusion This study demonstrates that NET/NETosis contributes to ICIAM, particularly LICIAM, blocking NET/NETosis may be promising for ICIAM treatment, and assessing NETosis-related biomarkers may provide additional values to cardiac troponins for LICIAM detection. However, these findings based on animal experiments warrant further clinical verifications.central graphical abstract
title: Neutrophils contribute to αPD1-induced latent myocardial injury via NET/NETosis axis: exploration of potential patho-mechanism, diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets in ICIs-associated myocard

abstract: Abstract Background Doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity is driven by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress and inflammatory activation. In pathological conditions, the heart undergoes metabolic remodelling, increasing its reliance on ketone bodies (KB) as an auxiliary energy substrate. Although exogenous KB have demonstrated cardioprotective effects in models of cardiac remodelling, their impact on the DOX-induced cardiac injury remains undefined. Purpose To determine whether exogenous ketosis modulates mitochondrial regulatory pathways, redox balance and inflammatory signalling in acute DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. Methods Male Wistar rats (n = 64) were allocated to six groups: Control, DOX, KB1 (1,3-butanediol 5 g/kg), KB2 (1,3-butanediol 10 g/kg), DOX+KB1 and DOX+KB2. 1,3-Butanediol was administered by oral gavage once a day, for two weeks, to induce ketosis. Acute cardiotoxicity was triggered by a single intraperitoneal DOX injection (20 mg/kg). Forty-eight hours post-DOX injection, cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography and invasive left ventricular haemodynamics. Myocardial oxidative stress markers were quantified spectrophotometrically, and protein expression of mitochondrial dynamics, metabolic regulators and inflammatory mediators was analysed by Western blotting. Statistical analysis: Two-way ANOVA. Results Rats receiving KB exhibited reduced food and water intake, accompanied by a decrease in body weight. Blood ketone levels increased at 4 and 8 hours following KB administration, with a more pronounced rise at 8 hours in animals receiving 10 g/kg (Figure 1A). DOX-treated animals showed a higher E/E′ ratio and reduced S′ on echocardiography, together with decreased +dP/dt and –dP/dt during left ventricular pressure assessment, indicating both systolic and diastolic dysfunction (Figure 1B). Myocardial troponin T levels were reduced following DOX administration, suggesting myocardial injury. DOX treatment decreased myocardial expression of the mitochondrial fusion protein mitofusin 2 and increased protein levels of TNF-α, Keap1 and NF-κB, which are associated with inflammatory signalling and oxidative stress regulation (Figure 2). Catalase activity was increased in rats that received DOX, without effects of KB (C: 2.41 ± 0.73; D: 3.71 ± 2.02; KB1: 2.62 ± 1.45; KB2: 4.35 ± 1.40; DKB1: 3.65 ± 1.07; DKB2: 1.81 ± 0.53 U/mg protein; p_DOX &lt; 0.001; p_KB = 0.358; p_interaction = 0.790). No significant differences were observed in superoxide dismutase activity, malondialdehyde levels, carbonylated proteins, or myocardial expression of AMPK, SIRT3, DRP1, IL-10, PGC-1α and PPAR-γ. Conclusions Acute DOX cardiotoxicity is characterised by early disruption of mitochondrial fusion machinery and activation of pro-inflammatory and redox-sensitive pathways. Despite inducing systemic ketosis, exogenous KB supplementation failed to modulate these molecular perturbations or preserve cardiac function.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Exogenous ketosis fails to mitigate cardiac dysfunction, mitochondrial and inflammatory dysregulation in acute doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity

abstract: Abstract Background The Heart Failure Association–International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) risk tool is recommended by guidelines to stratify baseline cardiovascular risk before cardiotoxic cancer therapy. Whether HFA-ICOS risk classification differentiates subclinical myocardial injury, predicts cancer therapy–related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), or modifies cardioprotective treatment response in randomized settings remains uncertain. Purpose To assess longitudinal changes in myocardial function across HFA-ICOS risk categories and determine whether the cardioprotective effect of sacubitril/valsartan varies by baseline cardiovascular risk in a randomized placebo-controlled trial of adjuvant breast cancer therapy. Methods In this predefined substudy, 138 breast cancer patients (placebo n = 69, sacubitril-valsartan n = 69) receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy underwent echocardiography at baseline, post-anthracycline therapy, and at 18 months. Patients were categorized as low, moderate, high or very high risk by HFA-ICOS. The primary endpoint was change in left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS). Secondary endpoints included 2D left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), right ventricular function, diastolic echocardiographic parameters, and cardiac biomarkers. Mild CTRCD was defined as &gt; 15% relative GLS decline and/or biomarker increase. Linear mixed-effects models estimated longitudinal trajectories and treatment effects within each risk category. Results Most patients were low (n=59) or moderate (n=59) risk; 20 were high risk and none very high risk. Mild CTRCD increased numerically across categories at 18 months, Table 1. No consistent risk-dependent differences were observed in GLS, LVEF, right ventricular function, or diastolic changes. The effect of sacubitril/valsartan on GLS was similar across risk groups, with between-group differences from baseline to 18 months of −1.26% (95% CI −2.62 to 0.09) in low, −1.48% (95% CI −2.89 to −0.07) in moderate, and −1.72% (95% CI −4.26 to 0.81) in high risk (Figure 1). No significant interaction by risk category was observed. Overall, GLS remained stable with sacubitril–valsartan but deteriorated with placebo (between-group difference −1.26%, 95% CI −2.19 to −0.33; p = 0.008). Conclusion Mild CTRCD occurred across all risk categories, increasing numerically with higher risk. Sacubitril/valsartan attenuated GLS deterioration, with broadly similar effects across baseline risk categories. Findings should be interpreted cautiously, given the limited number of high-risk participants and the exploratory nature of subgroup analyses.Figure 1
title: Cardioprotective effects of sacubitril/valsartan according to baseline cardiovascular risk during adjuvant breast cancer therapy: a randomized placebo-controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an important complication of cancer treatment that may lead to interruption of treatment. Anthracyclines and anti-HER2 therapies are highly effective but carry risk of myocardial injury, ranging from subclinical changes to overt heart failure. Clinical trials data evaluating cardioprotective strategies remain heterogeneous and lacking direct comparisons between drug classes. Consequently, the optimal pharmacologic approach to cardioprotection remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomised trials evaluating pharmacologic strategies for primary prevention of CTRCD. Methods MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to Feb 2026. We included randomised controlled trials enrolling adults receiving anthracycline- and/or anti-HER2–based chemotherapy that evaluated primary prevention of CTRCD. Interventions included beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA), statins, angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI), and combination regimens. The primary outcome was incidence of clinically meaningful CTRCD (LVEF &lt;50%). Secondary outcomes were study-defined cardiotoxicity (which have changed in definition over time) and absolute change in LVEF. Where LVEF &lt;50% was not reported, proportions were derived assuming normal distribution of follow-up LVEF values. Results Forty-two trials (94 treatment arms) were included. For incident LVEF &lt;50%, MRAs demonstrated the largest effect (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01–0.44), followed by dual therapy [beta blocker + ACEi/ARB] (OR 0.26, 0.10–0.66) and ACE inhibitors (OR 0.29, 0.10–0.85). Beta-blockers (OR 0.55, 0.33–0.91) and statins (OR 0.52, 0.29–0.94) were also associated with reduced risk, while ARBs and ARNIs were not significant.Secondary analyses suggested divergence across endpoints. Using contemporary, study-defined cardiotoxicity criteria, statins and ARNIs performed best, whereas ACE inhibitors did not demonstrate consistent benefit. ARBs showed no signal of efficacy across outcomes. Conclusions Cardioprotective therapy was associated with reduced CTRCD, with effects varying by drug class and outcome definition. Therapies traditionally targeting neurohormonal pathways were most consistently associated with preservation of LVEF, whereas statins and ARNIs showed greater benefit when broader, study-defined cardiotoxicity criteria were applied. In contrast, ARBs demonstrated no consistent signal of efficacy across analyses. Treatment benefit is sensitive to outcome definition, which may partly explain heterogeneity across trials. These findings may have important clinical implications for the choice of cardioprotective therapies in cancer patients undergoing anthracycline or anti-HER2 based therapy.Table 1Figure 1
title: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of cardio-protective therapies in cancer patients

abstract: Abstract Background&Objective Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICIAM),through occurring in only 1%-1.4% of patients, carries a mortality rate of up to 60%. Despite this high lethality, its pathogenesis remains poorly understood. While T cell-driven inflammation is a known feature of ICIAM, the key transcriptional regulators and downstream effector mechanisms responsible for cardiomyocyte death have not been identified.This study aimed to identify pivotal molecular drivers of ICIAM and elucidate the mechanisms by which they induce myocardial injury. Methods Transcriptomic profiling was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from ICIAM patients and matched controls to identify differentially expressed genes. In vitro, human CD3⁺ T cells were transduced with a FOXA1-overexpressing adeno-associated virus (AAV) or a control AAV, then co-cultured with AC16 cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte injury and pyroptosis were assessed using Western blot, qRT-PCR, caspase-1 activity assays, LDH release assays, ELISA, and Calcein-AM/PI staining. To investigate underlying mechanisms, co-cultures were treated with disulfiram or DAPT. Chromatin immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to validate the transcriptional regulation of DLL1 by FOXA1. In vivo, we established an experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM) mouse model. FOXA1-overexpressing CD3⁺ T cells were adoptively transferred into EAM mice, which were subsequently treated with disulfiram or DAPT. Cardiac function, myocardial inflammation, pyroptosis, and structural damage were evaluated by echocardiography, Western blot, qRT-PCR, ELISA, H&E staining, immunohistochemistry, and transmission electron microscopy. Results Transcriptomic analysis identified FOXA1 as a key gene significantly upregulated in PBMCs from ICIAM patients, a finding that was recapitulated in T cells from EAM mice. In vitro, FOXA1-overexpressing CD3⁺ T cells exacerbated myocardial injury and inflammation, characterized by elevated cTnI, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-18, and IL-1β. This effect was mediated by NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis and was abrogated by treatment with disulfiram and DAPT. Mechanistically, FOXA1 promoted DLL1 transcription, leading to activation of the Notch1 signaling pathway in cardiomyocytes. Inhibition of Notch1 signaling with DAPT significantly attenuated pyroptosis and subsequent cardiomyocyte injury. In vivo, adoptive transfer of FOXA1⁺ T cells into EAM mice exacerbated cardiac dysfunction, myocardial inflammation, and pyroptosis. These pathological effects were significantly mitigated by treatment with either disulfiram or DAPT. Conclusion FOXA1⁺CD3⁺ T cells exacerbate myocardial injury by directly binding the DLL1 promoter to activate the Notch1 signaling pathway, which in turn induces NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated cardiomyocyte pyroptosis.Targeting this FOXA1/DLL1/Notch1 axis may provide a promising therapeutic strategy for ICIAM.
title: FOXA1+CD3+T lymphocytes exacerbate myocardial injury in immune checkpoint inhibitor associated myocarditis via the DLL1/Notch1/GSDMD signaling pathway

abstract: Abstract Background 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is an antimetabolite chemotherapy agent used to treat gastrointestinal and other solid organ malignancies. Despite its therapeutic benefits, it has known adverse effects, including severe cardiotoxicity, but most notably an association with coronary vasospasm. There are limited studies that define the incidence, risk factors, and outcomes for these patients. Purpose The objective of this project is to determine the local incidence of 5-FU-associated coronary vasospasm in patients with gastrointestinal cancers treated within our local Australian health district and explore key patient demographics, clinical characteristics and treatment-related factors that are associated with increased risk of cardiotoxicity in this cohort. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of all adult patients, aged 18 years and above, who were diagnosed with gastrointestinal malignancies within our local health district between 1st January 2020 to 31st December 2024 and received at least one cycle of 5-FU chemotherapy or its oral prodrug formulations. Two electronic medical records were screened manually for clinical presentations for chest pain, heart failure, acute coronary syndromes and the diagnosis of coronary vasospasm was verified with documented cardiologist opinion, along with biochemical or electrocardiographic evidence for confirmation. Results A total of 1,016 patients across four cancer centres within the district were included in the analysis. The cohort comprised of 611 males (60.1%) and 405 females (39.9%), with 41.5% patients born in Australia, 21.7% born in Asia and 16% born in Europe. Colorectal cancer constituted 65.8% of the tumour groups, while upper gastrointestinal cancers made up 34.2%. At the time of treatment, 426 patients (41.9%) had Stage III disease and 422 (41.5%) had Stage IV disease. The most frequently prescribed chemotherapy regimens were FOLFOX in 478 patients (47%) and CAPOX in 307 (30.2%) patients. Prior use of calcium channel blockers was documented in 12.7% of patients. Cardiovascular risk factors such as hypertension were documented in 42.5%, hypercholesterolemia 35.8%, diabetes in 25%, prior myocardial infarction in 7.8% and smoking history in 33.7% of patients. The incidence of 5-FU–associated coronary vasospasm was low, occurring in 5 patients (0.5%). During follow-up, the overall mortality rate was 39.4% over 5 years. The incidence of new acute coronary syndrome occurred in 2.4%, new persistent arrhythmia in 4.1% and new congestive cardiac failure in 2.4% of patients. Conclusion In this large retrospective cohort across four cancer centres, the incidence of 5-FU-associated coronary vasospasm was low (0.5%) despite a substantial burden of cardiovascular risk factors. These findings suggest that while vasospasm is an uncommon complication, ongoing cardiovascular vigilance remains important in patients receiving 5-FU–based chemotherapy.
title: Retrospective cohort study exploring the incidence of 5-Flurouracil associated coronary vasospasm in patients with gastrointestinal cancers

abstract: Abstract Improved prognostic models are needed to guide personalized prevention and treatment decisions for breast cancer patients to reduce the risk of myocardial injury after anti-cancer therapy. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic nomogram to predict early myocardial injury after treatment. Breast cancer patients with at least three hypersensitive troponin T (hs-cTnT) measurements between January 2014 and December 2021 were included. Patients with hs-cTnT &gt;14 pg/mL during 6-month follow-up were considered to have early myocardial injury. Participants were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 366) and a validation cohort (n = 185). Univariate Cox regression and LASSO analysis were used to identify candidate predictors, followed by multivariable Cox regression to construct the nomogram. A total of 551 patients were included. Independent predictors included hs-cTnT level, HDL-C level, thoracic aortic calcification score, and anti-HER2 therapy. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.901, 95% CI 0.832–0.971) and calibration (C-index 0.908, 95% CI 0.883–0.933) in the validation cohort. Decision curve analysis indicated clinical usefulness, and patients were effectively stratified into high- and low-risk groups (p &lt; 0.001). This nomogram accurately predicts the 6-month risk of myocardial injury after anti-cancer treatment and may assist in risk stratification and clinical decision-making for breast cancer patients.Abstract_Figure1.jpegAbstract_Figure2.jpg
title: Construction and validation of a nomogram prediction model for myocardial injury in breast cancer patients after treatment

abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (irAE-MC) is a rare but potentially fatal complication with limited diagnostic specificity using conventional biomarkers. Glycosylation is a crucial post-translational modification that modulates IgG effector functions and reflects systemic inflammatory status. However, whether specific IgG N-glycosylation patterns can serve as biomarkers to distinguish irAE-MC from patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment remains unexplored. Purpose To investigate the association between specific IgG N-glycosylation patterns and the development of irAE-MC, and to evaluate the diagnostic potential of these glycan signatures in distinguishing irAE-MC from patients prior to ICI (Pre-ICI) and ICI-treated patients without irAEs (Non-irAE) patient group. Methods We analyzed IgG N-glycosylation in three age- and sex-matched cohorts: patients with irAE-MC (n=38), Pre-ICI (n=46) and Non-irAE (n=44). Profiling was conducted using high-resolution mass spectrometry. Group differences between cohorts were assessed in R Studio using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s post-hoc test for normally distributed variables, and the Mann–Whitney U test for non-normally distributed variables. Results The three cohorts were comparable in age and sex [median 65.5–68.5 years; 63.1%–71.7% male; all P &gt; 0.05]. Heatmap and profiling analyses revealed that IgG N-glycosylation patterns in irAE-MC were distinct from those in pre-ICI and non-irAE groups. Specifically, H3N4F1was significantly decreased, while H5N4F1 and H5N4F1E1 were significantly elevated in irAE-MC compared with both pre-ICI and non-irAE groups (all P &lt; 0.05). Among derived glycan traits, galactosylation-related features, including CG, A2FG, and A2S0G, were significantly elevated in the irAE-MC group compared with pre-ICI and non-irAE group (all P &lt; 0.05). In contrast, the bisecting N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc)-related trait A2FSB was significantly reduced in irAE-MC compared with both pre-ICI and non-irAE groups (all P &lt; 0.05). No significant differences were observed between the pre-ICI and non-irAE groups for these traits (Figure 2). Conclusion These distinct IgG N-glycosylation patterns reflect the unique systemic inflammatory milieu of ICI induced myocardial injury. Our findings suggest that specific glycan signatures serve as novel non-invasive biomarkers for the early diagnosis of irAE-MC in patients receiving ICI therapy.
title: IgG N-glycosylation as a novel biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a comparative glycomic study

abstract: Abstract Background Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has established itself as a cornerstone therapeutic intervention for a broad spectrum of hematologic malignancies. However, despite improvements in procedural safety, cardiovascular (CV) adverse events remain a substantial concern, contributing significantly to both treatment-related morbidity and overall mortality in this population. This regional registry was established to quantify the incidence of such cardiovascular complications and to evaluate their specific influence on patient survival during the follow-up period. Methods This prospective, regional observational cohort study consecutively enrolled adult patients undergoing either autologous or allogeneic HSCT between 2019 and 2025. Each participant was subjected to a standardized cardiac screening protocol designed for early detection of toxicity, including 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography, and the longitudinal assessment of cardiac biomarkers. These evaluations were performed at the baseline prior to transplantation, and subsequently at the 2-month, 6-month, and semi-annual intervals throughout the post-transplant period. The primary clinical outcomes included new-onset systolic dysfunction, venous thromboembolic events (encompassing both deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism), cerebrovascular accidents (stroke), various cardiac arrhythmias, pericarditis, and acute hypertensive crises. Results 147 patients, with a mean age of 56±13 years, were followed for a median of 2.6 years (1.1-5.1 years). The prevalence of significant cardiovascular risk factors was relatively low, with only 17% of the participants having a documented history of prior cardiovascular events. Nevertheless, 39% of the entire cohort experienced at least one cardiovascular-related adverse event during the study's duration. Detailed clinical monitoring identified 12 cases of VTE/PE, 8 instances of atrial fibrillation, 7 cases of heart failure or cardiogenic shock, and 5 cases each of peripheral vascular disease and hypertensive crises (Figure 1). Notably, a majority of these complications (68%) manifested within the first six months following the transplant. The occurrence of any cardiovascular adverse event was linked to a more than twofold increase in all-cause mortality, which rose from 12% in unaffected patients to 29% in those with complications (Figure 2; p=0.003). Conclusions Cardiovascular complications are remarkably prevalent among recipients of HSCT and can affect a wide range of patients, including those who are young and lack baseline comorbidities. The development of a cardiovascular event is a negative prognostic indicator for overall survival. Because two thirds of these events occurs within the initial six months post-transplantation, it is critical to improve early cardiac surveillance to improve long-term patient outcomes.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Long-term prognostic significance of cardiovascular complications following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a prospective regional cohort analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Anthracycline therapy induces dose-dependent cardiotoxicity and systemic adverse effects, including functional disability. While sacubitril/valsartan attenuates early subclinical myocardial injury during breast cancer therapy, its impact on functional capacity and skeletal muscle injury remains unknown. Purpose To evaluate whether sacubitril/valsartan attenuates anthracycline-induced decline in functional capacity and skeletal muscle injury compared to placebo. Methods PRADA II was a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicentre trial including 138 women with early breast cancer receiving (neo)adjuvant anthracycline therapy±trastuzumab. Participants were randomised prior to anthracycline initiation to sacubitril/valsartan or placebo for 18 months. The predefined primary outcome of this substudy was change in maximal handgrip strength from baseline to 18 months. Secondary outcomes included changes in 6-minute walk distance and circulating creatine kinase (CK) and myoglobin concentrations. Assessments were performed at baseline, post-anthracycline (Visit 2), and at 18 months (Visit 3). Changes were analysed using generalised linear mixed models, and a two-sided alpha level of 0.05 was applied to the primary outcome. Results Maximal handgrip strength declined in both groups from baseline to Visit 2, with partial recovery at Visit 3 in the sacubitril/valsartan group and continued decline in the placebo group. No significant between-group difference was observed in handgrip strength (between-group change from baseline to Visit 3: -0.3 kg, 95% CI -1.5 to 0.8, p=0.57). However, a greater decline from baseline to Visit 2 was observed with sacubitril/valsartan than placebo, corresponding to a between-group difference of -1.8 kg, 95% CI -3.0 to -0.6. 6-minute walk distance increased from baseline to both follow-up timepoints in the sacubitril/valsartan group, and a transient reduction was observed in the placebo group from baseline to Visit 2. Between-group changes did not differ at Visit 2 (8.8 m, 95% CI -19.3 to 36.9) or Visit 3 (13.6 m, 95% CI -13.3 to 40.5). CK and myoglobin were numerically higher in the placebo group from baseline to Visit 3, however, the confidence intervals for between-group differences included the null value (CK geometric mean ratio 1.17, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.45; myoglobin 1.10, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.23). Temporal changes by randomisation group are shown in Figure 1. Conclusions Sacubitril/valsartan did not significantly attenuate anthracycline-related decline in functional capacity assessed by maximal handgrip strength and 6-minute walk distance or changes in biomarkers of skeletal muscle injury. These findings suggest a neutral effect of sacubitril/valsartan on functional capacity, without challenging its potential cardioprotective role during anthracycline therapy.
title: The effect of sacubitril/valsartan on functional disability and skeletal muscle injury during breast cancer therapy: insights from the PRADA II trial

abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but prior observational studies reported large relative increases in atherosclerotic cardiovascular events post-exposure. These estimates may be confounded by differences in treatment line and cumulative prior therapy. Purpose To evaluate the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in cancer patients treated with ICIs compared to matched patients treated with targeted regimens or epirubicin. Methods Using linked administrative databases, we conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study of adults initiating upfront systemic treatment for melanoma, lung, or breast cancer (2012–2024). The exposure group (ICIs) was matched 1:1 with controls receiving targeted regimens (Melanoma: BRAF/MEK; Lung: EGFR/ALK/ROS1/RET/MET) or epirubicin (Breast). Matching was based on sex, cancer site, and stage. The primary outcome (MACE) was a composite of acute myocardial infarction, stroke, or coronary revascularization (CABG/PCI), with death as a competing risk. Patients were followed from date of initiation of systemic treatment until the earliest of 5 years thereafter, death, loss of insurance eligibility (+7 days), or March 31, 2025. Crude mortality was assessed via Kaplan-Meier curves, and the Aalen-Johansen estimate was used for MACE incidence. Cause-specific hazards regression adjusting for age, hypertension, diabetes (DM), ischemic heart disease (IHD), heart failure (HF), atrial fibrillation (AF), stroke, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was used to estimate the adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of the composite outcome in the ICI group relative to controls. Results Among 9,478 patients (4,739 matched pairs; 66.8% female; 76.1% lung, 17.2% breast, 6.7% melanoma), ICI recipients were slightly younger (median 67 vs. 69 years) with a higher baseline prevalence of IHD, PAD, and HF, but similar rates of HTN, DM, and stroke. Over mean follow-up of 463 days, there were 5,624 (59.3%) deaths and 3,514 (37.1%) MACE events. The median survival at 3 years was 31.4% (95% CI 29.8%-33.1%) in the ICI group and 40.2% (95% CI 38.7%-41.7%) for controls. The crude 3-year incidence of MACE was similar between groups (4.0%, 95% CI 3.4%-4.7% vs. 3.2%, 95% CI 2.7%-3.8%, p= 0.34). After multivariable adjustment, the cause-specific HR for MACE for the ICI group relative to controls was 1.34, 95% CI 1.07-1.67, p= 0.01). Conclusion After adjustment, ICI therapy was associated with a 34% higher hazard of MACE compared to controls. Notably, this hazard ratio is lower than estimates from earlier observational studies that did not restrict to upfront treatment. These findings support proactive cardiovascular risk assessment and optimization in long-term survivors while reinforcing that the excess risk is modest and should not deter use of these life-prolonging therapies.HR for ICI-treated individuals vs. controls
title: Upfront immune checkpoint inhibitors and long-term risk of major adverse cardiovascular events: a population-based propensity-matched cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloHSCT) recipients face substantial cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Traditional risk stratification tools may not adequately capture the heterogeneity of cardiovascular risk in this population. Phenotypic clustering using unsupervised machine learning (ML) approaches may identify distinct patient subgroups with differential cardiovascular risk profiles. Purpose To identify distinct phenotypic clusters among alloHSCT recipients and assess their association with cardiovascular events (CE). Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,381 consecutive patients who underwent alloHSCT at Saint-Louis Hospital (Paris, France) between July 2011 and July 2023. We applied a Latent Class Model, a probabilistic unsupervised ML approach, to baseline demographic, clinical, biological, echocardiographic, and transplant-related variables. Final clustering was selected based on statistical robustness and clinical relevance. A decision tree classifier was developed to predict cluster membership. The primary outcome was a composite of CE including cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation/flutter, ventricular tachycardia, and conductive disorders resulting in pacemaker implantation, and acute arterial events (acute coronary syndrome, ischaemic stroke). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the prognostic significance of each phenotypic cluster to predict the primary outcome. Results Four distinct phenotypic clusters were identified: Cluster 1 (28%) comprised young patients with non-malignant hematologic diseases; Cluster 2 (38%) included young patients with malignancies and high cardiotoxic therapy exposure; Cluster 3 (35%) consisted of older patients with myeloproliferative/myelodysplastic syndromes; and Cluster 4 (6%) represented patients with the highest cardiovascular risk burden. During a median follow-up of 3 (1-6) years, 247 patients (18%) experienced CE. Kaplan-Meier survival curves demonstrated significant differences in CE-free survival across clusters (log-rank test p&lt;0.001) (Figure 1). Compared to Cluster 1, Cluster 3 (adjusted HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.07-3.03, p=0.026) and Cluster 4 (adjusted HR: 2.00, 95% CI: 1.08-3.71, p=0.027) were independently associated with higher risk of CE. A decision tree classifier achieved 87% accuracy using five readily available variables (Figure 2). Phenotypic clustering significantly improved cardiovascular risk prediction beyond the hematopoietic stem cell transplantation-comorbidity index (C-statistic improvement: 0.08, integrative discrimination index: 0.050, net reclassification index: 0.640, all p&lt;0.001). Conclusion ML-derived phenotypic clustering identifies distinct patient subgroups with differential cardiovascular risk among alloHSCT recipients. This approach may enhance risk stratification and guide personalized cardiovascular surveillance and prevention strategies.Figure 1.Kaplan Meier survival curvesInterpretable decision tree
title: Phenotypic clustering of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients associated with cardiovascular events

abstract: Abstract Background Both immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and platinum-based doublet chemotherapy carry cardiovascular risk in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet existing comparative data are conflicting,¹,² derived largely from heterogeneous trial meta-analyses. Platinum agents cause direct endothelial injury and vascular toxicity; taxanes are associated with myocardial ischemia and arrhythmia.³ Whether ICIs confer net greater or lesser cardiovascular harm in direct clinical practice comparison is unknown. Methods Retrospective active-comparator cohort study using Epic Cosmos, a de-identified real-world EHR network of 300,262,705 patients (diagram). Among 1,405,504 patients receiving systemic cancer therapy (2018–2023), 148,743 carried an NSCLC diagnosis; 84,097 initiated either a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor (pembrolizumab or nivolumab; n=53,833) or platinum-based doublet chemotherapy (carboplatin/cisplatin + taxane or pemetrexed within ±28 days; n=30,264). Index date was the first qualifying dose. Patients were censored at last encounter or cross-over to the alternate treatment class to prevent exposure misclassification. Propensity scores were estimated by logistic regression; stabilized IPTW truncated at the 1st/99th percentiles was applied, with balance verified by standardized mean differences (all post-IPTW SMDs &lt;0.10). The primary analysis used an IPTW-weighted Cox proportional hazards model with robust variance. IPTW-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and competing-risk cumulative incidence functions (death) were generated as complementary analyses. Results 11,825 incident heart failure (HF) events occurred (12.4%). ICI was associated with a 24% lower hazard of HF compared with platinum-based chemotherapy (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.72–0.80; p&lt;0.001, see Fig.), with consistent reductions in both HFpEF (HR 0.68, 0.63–0.74) and HFrEF (HR 0.76, 0.70–0.83). Among pre-specified secondary outcomes, ICI was associated with lower rates of atrial fibrillation (HR 0.65, 0.62–0.68), coronary artery disease (HR 0.70, 0.66–0.73), and unstable angina (HR 0.70, 0.56–0.87). In contrast, ICI carried significantly higher risk of myocarditis (HR 2.03, 1.01–4.09; p=0.047) and stroke (HR 1.27, 1.15–1.39; p&lt;0.001). Conclusions In this large real-world active comparator analysis, ICI therapy was associated with substantially lower risk of heart failure, arrhythmia, and ischemic cardiovascular events compared with platinum-based chemotherapy, consistent with the intrinsic vascular and cardiodepressant burden of platinum and taxane agents. The trade-off of elevated immune-mediated myocarditis and stroke risk with ICIs reinforces the need for vigilant cardio-oncology monitoring, particularly early in the treatment course4. These findings challenge the framing of ICIs as categorically more cardiotoxic and provide actionable real-world evidence for cardiovascular risk stratification in NSCLC treatment planning.Consort DiagramFig.HF KM
title: Divergent cardiovascular risk profiles of immune checkpoint inhibitors versus platinum-based chemotherapy in NSCLC: a real-world study of 84,097 patients

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with a history of cancer represent a growing subset of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) survivors and may harbor a high residual cardiovascular risk. NT-proBNP is a well-established biomarker of cardiac stress, but its prognostic value at 1-year follow-up specifically in oncologic ACS patients remains unclear. Purpose To assess whether persistently elevated NT-proBNP at 1 year identifies oncologic ACS patients at higher risk of net adverse clinical events (NACE). Methods Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients admitted to four Swiss University Hospitals and enrolled in the multicenter SPUM registry between 2009 and 2017 were followed prospectively for 1 year. NT-proBNP was measured at baseline and at 1-year follow-up in survivors and persistently elevated NT-proBNP at 1 year was defined among patients alive at 1 year. The primary endpoint was a composite of net adverse clinical event (NACE), i.e. death, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial and major bleedings at 1 year. Multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazard regression models were fit to estimate NACE risk. Results Out of 4,787 ACS patients, 372 (7.8%) had a history of cancer. Compared to non-oncologic patients, these patients were older (70.3 ± 10.4 vs 63.1 ± 12.4 years, p &lt; 0.001), more frequently female (25.0% vs 20.0%, p = 0.018), and had a higher prevalence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors (all p &lt; 0.001), except for dyslipidemia. They also had a higher rate of prior percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI; 19.6% vs 14.5%, p = 0.006). NSTEMI was more common at presentation (50.5% vs 42.7%, p = 0.003). Baseline renal function was slightly lower (eGFR 74.0 ± 22.8 vs 84.7 ± 20.7 mL/min/1.73 m², p = 0.021), and these patients exhibited higher inflammatory activity as reflected by hs-CRP (17.1 ± 40.3 vs 11.1 ± 27.7 mg/L, p &lt; 0.001). At 1 year, ACS patients with a history of cancer had a higher incidence of NACE compared to non-oncologic patients (19.6% vs 11.1%, p &lt; 0.001), which remained significant after adjustment for baseline confounders (adjusted HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.07–2.07, p = 0.018; Figure 1, Panel A). Among oncologic patients, those with persistently elevated NT-proBNP at 1 year exhibited an even higher risk of NACE compared to patients with low or normalized NT-proBNP (adjusted HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.02–1.81, p = 0.036; Figure 1, Panel B). Conclusions In ACS patients with a history of cancer, persistently elevated NT-proBNP at 1 year identifies a high-risk biological phenotype. Serial NT-proBNP measurements provide incremental prognostic information beyond baseline clinical characteristics and may support long-term risk stratification in this vulnerable population.KM event rate in oncologic ACS patients.
title: Residual cardiovascular risk after ACS in oncologic patients: the prognostic role of persistently elevated NT proBNP

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cancer patients frequently present with complex coronary disease and elevated ischemic and bleeding risks. The ARC-HBR criteria were developed to identify patients at high bleeding risk, but their performance in cardio-oncology populations remains insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the ability of ARC-HBR to predict major bleeding in cancer patients with severe coronary disease treated across different revascularization strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 150 consecutive cancer patients from 2017 to 2023 with severe coronary disease who underwent PCI, CABG, or, when revascularization was not feasible, were treated with DAPT or single antiplatelet therapy plus anticoagulation for at least 6 months. ARC-HBR status was determined according to the original definition. Baseline characteristics, angiographic data, and clinical outcomes were compared between ARC-HBR and non–ARC-HBR patients. Major bleeding was defined as BARC type 3 or 5. Logistic regression assessed associations with major bleeding and mortality. Mean follow-up was 3.4 years. Results Ninety-nine patients (66%) met ARC-HBR criteria and 51 (34%) were classified as non–ARC-HBR. Baseline cardiovascular risk factors and angiographic characteristics were generally comparable between groups. Age tended to be higher in ARC-HBR patients, and chronic kidney disease was markedly more prevalent (62% vs 26%, p&lt;0.001). Hemoglobin and platelet levels were lower in ARC-HBR patients, though without statistical significance. As expected, active malignancy occurred exclusively in the ARC-HBR group, as it constitutes a major criterion. Major bleeding occurred in 15 patients (10%), with substantially higher rates in ARC-HBR compared with non–ARC-HBR patients (14% vs 2%, p=0.018). In ARC-HBR patients, the 3.4-year mean follow-up corresponds to an annualized major bleeding rate of 4.1 events per 100 patient-years, closely matching the ≥4% 1-year risk threshold that defines ARC-HBR. ARC-HBR status was associated with an eight-fold increase in major bleeding risk (OR 8.24, p=0.045) and a significant rise in mortality (OR 5.08, p&lt;0.001). Conclusion In cancer patients with severe coronary disease, ARC-HBR status effectively identified individuals at substantially higher risk of major bleeding and mortality, supporting its applicability and internal validity in this cardio-oncology population.ACR-HBR
title: Refining risk in cancer patients with coronary artery disease: do ARC-HBR criteria deliver?

abstract: Abstract Introduction While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have redefined cancer management, however their clinical utility is severely capped by fatal cardiovascular complications. Current consensus attributes this cardiotoxicity exclusively to the dysregulation of peripheral T-cells. We challenge this view by proposing an upstream etiology: the thymus. We propose that anti-PD-1 therapy compromises central tolerance mechanisms, effectively priming the immune system for myocardial injury. Purpose We have investigated whether a functional thymus is required for the development of ICI-mediated cardiac dysfunction. Furthermore, we evaluated whether inducing thymic involution through either naturally with biological aging or pharmacologically via 5-Azacytidine (AZA), confers cardioprotection against immunotherapy-induced injury. Methods We employed a comparative murine model involving young (12-week) and aged (16-month) C57BL/6J cohorts subjected to anti-PD-1 treatment. To isolate the role of thymic output, we induced pharmacological atrophy in young mice using AZA. Cardiac performance was assessed via high-resolution echocardiography, complemented by myocardial gene expression analysis and deep analysis of thymic and splenic microenvironments via RNAseq, flow cytometry and RNAscope. Results Administration of anti-PD-1 precipitated significant systolic impairment in young mice, a cardiotoxic effect that was notably absent in the aged cohort. Mechanistically, young thymuses exhibited profound transcriptional alterations indicative of impaired T-cell selection and regulatory T-cell reduction. In the heart, this resulted in a pro-inflammatory milieu characterized by upregulated Cxcl9, Cxcl10, and Ifng, occurring even in the absence of fulminant myocarditis. Moreover, pharmacological suppression of thymic activity with AZA successfully preserved systolic function and dampened myocardial inflammatory signaling, effectively replicating the protective phenotype observed in aging. Conclusion These findings expand the peripheral-centric model of immunotherapy complications, identifying the thymus as a key driver of ICI-induced cardiotoxicity. We demonstrate that anti-PD-1 lowers tolerance thresholds centrally, fueling a heart-specific inflammatory loop. Consequently, thymic activity represents a novel biomarker for cardiovascular risk stratification, and its therapeutic modulation offers a promising new way to decouple potent anti-tumor immunity from life-threatening cardiotoxicity.Graphical abstract
title: Suppressing thymic output prevents systolic impairment in anti-PD-1 therapy

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiovascular (CV) diseases are a leading cause of mortality among prostate cancer (PC) survivors. (1) Although diabetes is a well-established risk factor for CV complications, its impact on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) in this population is not fully characterized. We aimed to assess whether diabetes control, defined by an HbA1c of 6.5%, is associated with MACE (myocardial infarction, CABG/PCI, stroke, heart failure, unstable angina, and CV death). Methods A retrospective cohort of 4,561 PC patients (median age: 72; IQR: 67–76) was evaluated using Fine-Gray competing risk models, comparing MACE development and non-CV death. Baseline HbA1c was defined as the measurement closest to the cancer diagnosis; the follow-up value was the final measurement recorded after diagnosis but prior to any MACE event or censoring. Patients were categorized into four groups: Optimal Control (reference: &lt;6.5% and stable/decreasing), New Onset Diabetes (&lt;6.5% and increasing), Controlled Diabetes (&gt;6.5% and decreasing), and Uncontrolled Diabetes (&gt;6.5% and stable/increasing). Models were adjusted for age (years), BMI (kg/m²) and hormone therapy. Cumulative incidence curves were plotted to visualize the temporal distribution of events across cohorts. Results A total of 1,179 patients experienced MACE over the study period. In multivariable-adjusted models, uncontrolled diabetes was independently associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE (HR: 1.24; 95% CI: 1.07–1.43; p = 0.004) compared to the optimal control group. Conversely, neither new-onset diabetes (HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.90–1.20; p = 0.611) nor controlled diabetes (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.95–1.36; p = 0.150) reached statistical significance. Age (HR: 1.07 per year; 95% CI: 1.06–1.07; p &lt; 0.001) and BMI (HR: 1.01 per kg/m²; 95% CI: 1.00–1.02; p = 0.041) remained significant predictors, while hormone therapy was not associated with the outcome (HR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.84–1.08; p = 0.491) (Table 1). Cumulative incidence curves demonstrate a clear separation, where optimal control (red) displayed a sustained lower MACE probability compared to the other cohorts. Notably, beyond the 10-year mark, both controlled (yellow) and uncontrolled (green) diabetes groups exhibited similar event probabilities (Figure 1). Conclusions In PC survivors, uncontrolled diabetes is independently associated with MACE. These findings highlight the importance of achieving and maintaining glycemic control in patients with PC.Cumulative incidence of 5point MACECharacteristics of PC patients
title: Uncontrolled diabetes as an independent predictor of mayor adverse cardiovascular events in prostate cancer survivors

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction In cancer survivors, severe mitral regurgitation (MR) can be a direct consequence of therapy-related cardiotoxicity (such as functional MR due to anthracycline-induced dysfunction or degenerative MR following left-sided chest radiotherapy) or an incidental overlap. The prognostic implications of the MR etiology in this high-risk population undergoing percutaneous treatment remain underexplored. Purpose To evaluate whether the cardiotoxic etiology of MR impacts the clinical outcomes of patients with a prior cancer diagnosis undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER). Methods We conducted a multicenter observational sub-study from the Spanish M-TEER registry, including 155 cancer survivors treated with M-TEER. Patients were stratified into two groups based on MR etiology: MR attributable to cardiotoxicity (MR-CTOX) and MR not attributable to cardiotoxicity (MR-NCTOX). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or unplanned heart failure (HF) hospitalization at mid-term follow-up. Results Among the 155 patients, 60 (38.7%) had MR-CTOX and 95 (61.3%) had MR-NCTOX. Baseline characteristics differed significantly: MR-CTOX patients were younger (71.8 vs. 75.5 years, p=0.035), more frequently female (56.7% vs. 26.3%, p&lt;0.001), had a higher prevalence of hematological malignancies (35.0% vs. 10.5%, p&lt;0.001), and presented a lower EuroSCORE II (4.6 vs. 6.5, p=0.012). They also had lower rates of comorbidities such as diabetes, hypertension, and anemia (all p&lt;0.05). During follow-up, the primary composite endpoint occurred at similar rates between groups: 29 (48.3%) in MR-CTOX and 47 (49.5%) in MR-NCTOX (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.66-1.67, p=0.824). There were no significant differences in all-cause mortality (36.7% vs. 32.6%, p=0.498) or HF hospitalization (33.3% vs. 33.7%, p=0.840) (Figure 1). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, a cardiotoxic etiology of MR was not an independent predictor of the primary endpoint (HR 1.41, 95% CI 0.83-2.39, p=0.203). Independent predictors of adverse outcomes were diabetes, anemia, EuroSCORE II, and hematological malignancies (Figure 2). Conclusion(s) MR attributable to cancer-therapy cardiotoxicity is common among cancer survivors undergoing M-TEER. Despite differences in baseline clinical profiles, the origin of MR (cardiotoxic vs overlap) does not significantly impact mid-term mortality or HF hospitalizations, suggesting that M-TEER is a safe and equally effective therapeutic option regardless of MR etiology in this population.
title: Clinical outcomes of transcatheter mitral edge-to-edge repair in cancer survivors according to MR etiology

abstract: Abstract Background Globally, maternal mortality remains disproportionately high in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). While obstetric hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, peripartum cardiomyopathy and infections are the leading causes of maternal mortality, undiagnosed or untreated rheumatic and congenital heart diseases pose a significant risk of maternal mortality and morbidity in young pregnant women in SSA. In addition, there are limited structured programs to provide care to women with cardiovascular diseases in pregnancy. Purpose Assess feasibility of implementing Cardio-Obstetric programs in SSA. Methods Between 2024 -2025 two teaching institutions, one in Ethiopia and one in Tanzania were selected. To ensure sustainability, a three-phase approach was undertaken. Phase 1: Initial discussions with institutional leadership and department heads (Obstetrics, Cardiology, Anesthesiology, Pediatric Cardiology, and Nursing) secured program support, with unanimous agreement on its clinical and strategic importance. Phase 2: A small equipment grant enabled launch of a dedicated weekly multidisciplinary clinic, supported by referral outreach within the institution and surrounding community. Phase 3: With a functioning clinic, regular case discussions were held to formulate a patient treatment plan. Computer based patient registries and data collection were started. Results Several key barriers were identified during implementation of the program 1.Limited availability of Maternal–Fetal Medicine (MFM) specialists: Tanzania faces a shortage of MFM specialists; one obstetrician was sponsored for a two-year MFM fellowship to build local expertise. 2.Restricted use of epidural anesthesia for high-risk deliveries: Limited catheter supply and inadequate training constrained epidural use; targeted training and equipment procurement later strengthened anesthesia capacity and improved care quality. 3.Inconsistent International Normalized Ratio monitoring: Inconsistently available in the clinic, but this gap was later resolved, improving anticoagulation management. 4.Limited access to advanced diagnostic equipment: Dedicated echocardiography services were initially unavailable; acquiring an echocardiography unit later improved onsite diagnostic capacity. 5.Restricted access to advanced cardiac interventions: Patients needing specialized care were referred to higher-level centers, often requiring travel to distant facilities. 6.Lack of maternal cardiovascular disease registries: Local data collection to influence national maternal health policy was encouraged. Conclusion Both programs remain operational with steady gains in service delivery, capacity building, and patient outcomes. Although resource limitations in SSA constrain Cardio-Obstetric program growth, coordinated strategies, mentorship, and targeted support can overcome many barriers while generated data can guide health-system planning.
title: Barriers to implementing cardio-obstetrics programs in sub-saharan Africa

abstract: Abstract Introduction Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) face elevated risks of cardiovascular (CV) complications during delivery hospitalizations.Rates of PCOS and obesity have risen in parallel among childbearing women, yet the extent to which obesity mediated PCOS associated peripartum CV remains unclear. Our study aimed to address this by quantifying the proportion of excess CV risk attributable to PCOS that is explained by obesity. Methods Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016–2022), we identified delivery hospitalizations among women aged 12–55 years via ICD-10-CM codes. PCOS was identified by code E28.2 and obesity by E66.x/O99.21x. The primary outcome was a composite acute CV event (preeclampsia, eclampsia, peripartum cardiomyopathy, heart failure, pulmonary oedema, venous thromboembolism, acute myocardial infarction, stroke, arrhythmia, cardiogenic shock, and cardiac arrest). Survey-weighted logistic regression employed a change-in-estimate mediation approach: Model 1 (unadjusted), Model 2 (adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and hospital characteristics without obesity, showcasing total effect), and Model 3 (additionally adjusted for obesity, showcasing direct effect). Percent attenuation was calculated as (β-total − β-direct) / β-total × 100. Results Among 26,659,071 weighted delivery hospitalizations, 208,620 (0.78%) had PCOS. Women with PCOS were older (mean 30.9 vs 29.0 years, p&lt;0.01) and had higher prevalence of obesity (34.8% vs 12.2%), diabetes (5.6% vs 2.0%), gestational diabetes (17.9% vs 8.3%), chronic hypertension (3.4% vs 1.2%), and dyslipidemia (2.5% vs 0.4%; all p&lt;0.01). Composite acute CV events were more frequent with PCOS (10.1% vs 6.2%, p&lt;0.01). PCOS was associated with 70% higher unadjusted odds of composite CV events (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.65–1.76). After multivariable adjustment excluding obesity, PCOS remained independently associated (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.34–1.44). Upon further adjustment for obesity, the PCOS effect was attenuated but persisted (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.19–1.28). Obesity was a strong independent predictor (aOR 1.77, 95% CI 1.75–1.79). The percent attenuation attributable to obesity was 35.7%, indicating that approximately one-third of PCOS-associated excess CV risk is mediated through obesity. Conclusion In this analysis of over 26 million delivery hospitalisations, PCOS was independently associated with significantly elevated peripartum CV risk. Obesity mediated approximately 36% of this excess risk, yet a substantial direct PCOS effect persisted. These findings underscore the dual importance of targeting both PCOS-specific pathophysiology and obesity-related cardiometabolic burden to improve maternal CV outcomes.
title: Obesity as a mediator of peripartum cardiovascular complications in polycystic ovary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Advanced maternal age (AMA) refers to pregnancy ≥ 35 years at delivery, and is subcategorized as very AMA (VAMA, ≥ 40 years) and extremely AMA (EAMA, ≥ 45 years). While AMA is associated with obstetric and peripartum cardiovascular complications, its long-term implications for coronary risk remain incompletely characterised. With rising maternal age across Europe (EU mean 31.2 years (Eurostat)) clarifying if delayed childbearing confers sustained vulnerability to long-term adverse cardiovascular (CV) events has implications for risk assessment tools. Aim To evaluate whether AMA at first delivery is independently associated with long-term coronary or CV outcomes and if it may represent a female-specific CV risk modifier. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched, on February 16th 2026, for original articles in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, EBSCOhost, and Cochrane from January 2006 onwards, using terms: ‘Advanced maternal age’ (OR ‘maternal age at first delivery’ OR ‘maternal age at first birth’ OR ‘delayed childbearing’ OR (‘maternal age’ AND ‘first birth’) AND (‘acute coronary syndrome’ OR ‘myocardial infarction’ OR ‘STEMI’ OR ‘NSTEMI’ OR ‘coronary artery disease’ OR ‘coronary heart disease’ OR ‘ischemic heart disease’ OR ‘cardiovascular mortality’). After screening 100 studies, 15 abstracts were reviewed, and 4 were included; quality was appraised with the LEGEND tool. Results Four studies met inclusion criteria, including three prospective cohort studies and one large cross-sectional analysis comprising &gt;150,000 women across Japan and the United States. Two Japanese prospective cohorts demonstrated a significant association between AMA at first delivery and increased long-term CV mortality (adjusted HRs 1.22–1.33), which persisted after adjustment for demographic, lifestyle, and reproductive factors. In contrast, a large U.S. cohort found no independent association between AMA and incident CV disease after multivariable adjustment, suggesting socioeconomic confounding. A U.S. cross-sectional study reported a U-shaped association between age at first birth and CV disease, with both early and later maternal age associated with increased odds of CV disease. Conclusion AMA at first delivery demonstrates a modest but population-dependent association with long-term CV mortality, with consistent trends observed in Asian cohorts and attenuated association in U.S. populations after socioeconomic adjustment. Although most available data relate to composite CV outcomes rather than coronary-specific events, the observed heterogeneity suggests delayed childbearing may function as a context-dependent female-specific CV risk modifier rather than a direct causal determinant. These findings support further evaluation of reproductive timing within population-specific CV risk stratification frameworks. European cohort validation is warranted in view of this critical gap in coronary risk stratification for women of AMA in Europe.PRISMA Diagram for AMA and Coronary Outcome
title: Advanced maternal age at first delivery as a female-specific cardiovascular risk modifier: a systematic review of long-term coronary and cardiovascular outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac disease complicating pregnancy remains a major contributor to maternal morbidity in low- and middle-income countries, largely driven by rheumatic valvular lesions. However, real-world multicentre data on the indications and outcomes of cardiac interventions during pregnancy are limited. Purpose To evaluate the indications, procedural profile, and outcomes of cardiac interventions during pregnancy in the ongoing NPAC-India prospective registry. Methods NPAC-India is an ongoing multicentre prospective registry across 56 sites in India enrolling pregnant women with structural or acquired heart disease. We analysed participants who underwent cardiac intervention during pregnancy between August 2024 and January 2026. Indications included severe symptoms despite optimal medical therapy or severe disease with anticipated clinical deterioration during pregnancy. Functional class, gestational age at intervention, procedural success, and pregnancy outcomes were assessed. Results Among 5,200 enrolled participants, cardiac intervention during pregnancy was performed in 102 women (1.9%) across 21 participating sites. The mean age was 27.2 ± 4.8 years, and the mean gestational age at intervention was 25.4 ± 6.0 weeks. Most women were significantly symptomatic antenatally, with 53.9% (55/102) in NYHA class III or IV. Balloon mitral valvotomy was the predominant intervention (83/102, 82.4%), followed by balloon pulmonary valvotomy and permanent pacemaker implantation (5 each, 4.9%). Other procedures included percutaneous coronary intervention with stenting (3/102, 2.9%), aortic coarctation intervention (2/102, 2.0%), and miscellaneous procedures (3/102, 2.9%). Most procedures were performed as emergency (33/102, 32.4%) or urgent (33/102, 32.4%), while 36/102 (35.3%) were planned. Complete procedural success was achieved in 91 (89.2%), with partial success in 9 (8.8%) and failure in 2 (1.9%). There were 2 maternal deaths (1.9%). Of the 102 pregnancies, 22 are yet to deliver, 5 underwent medical termination, and 1 had a spontaneous abortion. Among the remaining 74 pregnancies, there were 72 live births and 2 stillbirths. Conclusion In this large prospective multicentre Indian registry, cardiac interventions during pregnancy were required in a small but high-risk subset.
