Interventions were most often performed in the second trimester and were associated with high procedural success and favourable perinatal outcomes despite significant baseline maternal symptom burden. These findings support the feasibility and relative safety of carefully selected, timely cardiac interventions during pregnancy in experienced centres, underscoring the importance of multidisciplinary evaluation and early referral in symptomatic women.
title: Indications, procedural profile, and outcomes of cardiac interventions during pregnancy: interim insights from the NPAC-India study registry

abstract: Abstract Background Women with HIV comprise over half the global HIV population and face a disproportionately high myocardial infarction (MI) risk compared to women without HIV. Yet research on MI presentation and management in this population remains limited, with most studies concluding several years ago or confined to single countries. Purpose To address potential disparities in equitable cardiovascular (CV) care, this study utilised a large, geographically diverse cohort to characterise MI in women and men with HIV. Method RESPOND is a multinational cohort collaboration with rigorous validation of MI events and systematic CV risk factor ascertainment. We followed adults with HIV in RESPOND from baseline (latest of 1 Jan 2012 or local cohort enrolment) until first type I MI, death, last follow-up, or 31 Dec 2023. MI presentation (symptoms, type of ECG changes), risk factors at MI and MI management (invasive CV procedures, secondary prevention medication) in women and men were summarised using descriptive statistics. Results At baseline, a higher proportion of women (n=9345) than men (n=28585) had acquired HIV through intravenous drugs (26.9% vs 12.8%) and presented with prior AIDS (37.3% vs 25.9%), chronic kidney disease (6.0% vs 3.3%) and unsuppressed HIV viral load (&gt;200 copies/mL; 26.9% vs 17.2%). During follow-up, MI occurred in 0.5% of women and 1.0% of men (total n=334 MIs with detailed clinical data available). Median age at MI was similar between women and men (58 [IQR 51-63] vs 57 [IQR 51-65] years). ST-elevation MI (STEMI) occurred in 18 women (39.1%) and 132 men (45.8%); non-ST-elevation MIs (NSTEMI) or MI with unknown/no ECG in 28 women (60.9%) and 156 men (54.2%). Across types of ECG changes, a higher proportion of women than men experienced atypical symptoms at MI event (atypical pain, acute heart failure, shock, syncope, dyspnoea without chest pain or cardiac disease except ischaemic heart disease) while fewer women tended to receive an invasive CV procedure within 72 hours (Table). A lower proportion of women than men with NSTEMI or MI with unknown/no ECG used antihypertensive, or lipid-lowering drugs while a higher proportion of women with STEMI used secondary prevention medication at or within 31 days of the MI. Among STEMIs, a higher proportion of women than men were obese (16.7% vs 11.4%) but a lower proportion were current smokers (38.9% vs 48.5%). Among NSTEMI or MI with unknown/no ECG, more women than men were obese (17.9% vs 5.6%) and smokers (50.0% vs 40.4%). HIV markers were similar across groups and by sex. Conclusion In this large cohort of individuals with HIV in Europe and Australia, a higher crude proportion of women presented with atypical symptoms and a lower proportion received invasive or guideline-recommended medical therapies for NSTEMI. Whilst these findings require further exploration in adjusted models, they could suggest potential sex-based treatment gap requiring greater awareness.Abstract_Table_MI_sex_HIV
title: Sex disparities of myocardial infarction in individuals with HIV across Europe and Australia: a multinational cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Despite viral suppression, people with HIV (PWH) experience residual cardiovascular and mortality risk not explained by traditional risk factors. Age-related clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is an independent predictor of mortality and cardiovascular disease (CVD) in people without HIV (PWoH) and is reportedly more prevalent among PWH, suggesting its possible role in residual risk. Purpose To assess baseline CHIP prevalence and its association with incident clinical events in US veterans with and without HIV in the Veterans Aging Cohort Study Biomarker Cohort. Methods We assayed baseline CHIP driver mutations using high-coverage targeted sequencing, defining presence of CHIP as variant allele frequency (VAF) &gt;2%. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, race, and smoking status were used to assess cross-sectional associations of HIV with CHIP (logistic regression) and individual and interactive effects of CHIP and HIV on mortality and incident CVD events, including acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina, revascularization, heart failure, or ischemic stroke (Cox models). We report odds ratios (OR), hazard ratios (HR), and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results Among 1524 PWH and 852 PWoH, 66% of participants were Black. At baseline, 316 (13%) had CHIP, with no difference by HIV status (191 [14.7%] PWH, 125 [12.5%] PWoH). PWH and PWoH with CHIP were older than those without CHIP, and 57% of those with CHIP reported current smoking (Table 1). DNMT3A was the most common driver mutation among PWH and PWoH, followed by TET2 and PPMD1 (Figure 1A). In multivariable-adjusted models, older age (OR 1.08 [95% CI 1.06-1.10]; p &lt;0.001) and current smoking (OR 1.51 [1.11-2.08]; p &lt;0.01) were associated with CHIP, whereas HIV was not (OR 0.99 [0.77-1.29]). Over a median follow-up of 17.5 years, baseline CHIP showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher mortality risk (adjusted HR 1.15 [0.99-1.35]; p = 0.073), whereas HIV was significantly associated with mortality (HR 1.26 [1.11-1.43]; p &lt;0.001). The concomitant presence of CHIP and HIV was associated with nearly 50% higher incident mortality compared with absence of both (HR 1.48 [1.20-1.83]; p&lt; 0.001; Figure 1B). Among participants free of baseline CVD, CHIP was not associated with incident CVD overall but was associated with lower risk among PWoH (HR 0.55 [0.35-0.86], p = 0.009) over 12.5 years of median follow-up, which was robust in stratified analyses. CHIP did not modify the association between HIV and mortality; however, a significant CHIP-HIV interaction was observed for incident CVD, with more than twofold higher risk among PWH than PWoH (pinteraction = 0.006). Conclusions In contrast to prior reports, HIV was not associated with the presence of CHIP in this older cohort of US veterans. The observed interaction between CHIP and HIV warrants further investigation to clarify potential synergistic effects on cardiovascular risk.
title: Clonal hematopoiesis and risk of mortality and cardiovascular disease in older adults with and without HIV

abstract: Abstract Background and Aims People living with HIV (PWH) are at higher risk of coronary heart disease (CHD). There is a need for improved cardiovascular (CV) risk stratification. We assessed the long-term prognostic value of silent myocardial ischaemia (SMI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in asymptomatic PWH without known CHD. Methods Between 2003 and 2016, consecutive asymptomatic PWH without known CHD underwent systematic CV evaluation, including non-invasive screening for CHD. Clinical events were collected up to 2023. The primary endpoint was 4-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or coronary revascularisation). Secondary endpoints were 3-point MACE, coronary events, and all atherothrombotic events. Predicted risk using SCORE2 and ASCVD risk scores was compared with observed risk. Results Among 810 eligible PWH, overall loss to follow-up was exceptionally low at 0.6% (5/810). The final analysis included 756 participants (mean age 51.1 ± 8.3 years; 85.3% men) with long-standing, well-controlled HIV (median known duration 19.8 years; 15.9 years on ART; 89% virologically suppressed). Median SCORE2 and ASCVD risk scores were 3.7 (IQR 2.5–5.5) and 6.0 (IQR 3.0–11.0), respectively. Among 756 participants, 29 (3.8%) had a positive ischaemia test at baseline. Over a median follow-up of 11.0 years, the 10-year cumulative incidence of CV events was 18.4%. These events were significantly more frequent in patients with a positive vs negative test (39.3% vs 17.5%; P = 0.004). The primary endpoint (4-point MACE) occurred in 8.5% of the cohort (incidence 9.7/1,000 person-years), with significantly lower 10-year event-free survival in the positive test group (log-rank P = 0.009).This difference was consistent across all secondary endpoints (all log-rank P ≤ 0.03). Sudden cardiac death accounted for 57.7% of CV deaths. In multivariable analysis, a positive baseline stress test was independently associated with 4-point MACE (adjusted HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.03–5.68; P = 0.043). HIV-specific variables (including HIV seropositivity duration and cumulative ART exposure) were not associated with outcomes. Risk prediction using SCORE2 and ASCVD was modest (C-statistics 0.64 and 0.63, respectively) with discordant calibration patterns. Specifically, SCORE2 underestimated risk in low-to-moderate categories, while ASCVD overestimated it. Conclusions In asymptomatic PWH without known CHD, SMI was infrequent (3.8%) but independently associated with a 2.4-fold higher risk of 4-point MACE over long-term follow-up, identifying a high-risk cardiovascular phenotype. Conventional risk scores showed modest discrimination and imperfect calibration. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of cardiovascular risk in asymptomatic PWH and support targeted non-invasive ischaemia testing for risk refinement.Kaplan–Meier survival curves for 4-P MACEAdjusted/unadjusted Cox regression for 4PMACE
title: Long term prognostic value of silent myocardial ischaemia in asymptomatic people with HIV

abstract: Abstract Background and Aims The use of iodinated contrast agents during cardiovascular procedures carries the risk of kidney injury. Although contrast-induced nephropathy is well recognized in the acute setting, the potential impact of contrast volume on medium- to long-term renal function remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the association between cumulative contrast volume and subsequent medium- to long-term changes in renal function in patients with repeated percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI). Methods This retrospective single-center study included all patients who underwent repeated PCIs between 2003 and 2023, with intervals of ≥7 days and ≤365 days between procedures. Volume of contrast agent administered during the initial intervention as well as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) values at the time of the initial PCI and at readmission were extracted from hospital records. Renal function was classified using the “Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes” (KDIGO) staging system. The primary endpoint was progression to a higher KDIGO stage at readmission, excluding patients initially at stage G5, as further deterioration was not possible. Secondary endpoint was association with eGFR, analyzed in relation to the contrast volume and potential confounders. Results A total of 6,714 patients were included in the study. The mean age was 67.2 ± 10.4; 80.2% were male. KDIGO stage analysis was available for 6,611 patients. Baseline mean eGFR was 74.4 ± 21.5 mL/min/1.73 m². The median interval between procedures was 127 days. The median contrast volume administered was 220 mL. At readmission, mean eGFR was 72.2 ± 21.6 mL/min/1.73 m². 1,700 patients (25.7%) had KDIGO stage progression. In univariable analyses, contrast volume was not significantly associated with KDIGO stage progression (HR: 1.08; 95% CI: 0.98-1.19) or reduced eGFR (Estimate: 0.31, 95% CI: -0.64-1.25). Multivariable analyses confirmed these findings. In contrast, diabetes mellitus (KDIGO: HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.07-1.32, eGFR: Estimate -3.17; 95% CI: -4.15- -2.18), arterial hypertension (KDIGO: HR: 1.25; 95% CI: 1.11-1.40, eGFR: Estimate -2.92; 95% CI: -3.94- -1.89), and age (KDIGO: HR: 1.03; 95% CI: 1.02-1.03, eGFR: Estimate -0.13; 95% CI: -0.18- -0.08) were significantly associated with worse renal outcomes. Conclusion No association was observed between the cumulative contrast volume administered during PCI and medium- to long-term deterioration of renal function in patients undergoing repeated procedures. Instead, diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, and age emerged as the main predictors of renal impairment at readmission.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Impact of cumulative contrast volume on medium- to long-term renal function in patients undergoing repeated percutaneous coronary interventions

abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Contrast-induced nephropathy remains a challenge in cardiovascular procedures. Minimization of contrast volume and the use of a transradial vascular access whenever feasible are considered key modifiable risk factors for acute kidney injury. Contemporary approaches emphasize individualized assessment, such as the maximum allowable contrast dose (MACD), which accounts for body weight and baseline renal function. However, whether these factors also contribute to a decline in medium- to long-term renal function remains unclear. Therefore, the aim of this analysis was to investigate this association in patients undergoing repeated percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI). Methods In this subgroup analysis of a retrospective single-center study, patients with repeated PCI between 2003 and 2023 with an interval of ≥7 and ≤365 days between procedures were included. All data, including the chosen vascular access for the initial PCI, were extracted from hospital records. The individual MACD was calculated for each patient according to the original formula (5 × body weight [kg] / serum creatinine [mg/dL]), with a maximum dose of 300 mL. Renal function was classified according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) staging system. The primary endpoint was the risk of KDIGO stage progression at readmission, excluding patients initially classified as stage G5. Secondary endpoints were associations with eGFR at readmission. Results In 1,814 (27%) of the 6,714 patients included, the contrast volume administered during PCI exceeded the individual MACD. The median MACD was 300 mL in both groups. The median contrast volume administered was substantially higher in the exceedance group (400 mL vs. 200 mL in the non-exceedance group). These patients had lower mean eGFR (68.5 ± 26.1 vs. 76.6 ± 19.0 mL/min/1.73 m²) at baseline. Other baseline characteristics were similar between groups. At readmission, mean eGFR was 69.25 ± 24.3 mL/min/1.73 m² in the exceedance group and 73.24 ± 20.4 mL/min/1.73 m² in the non-exceedance group. Univariable analyses showed no statistically significant association between MACD exceedance and increased risk of KDIGO stage progression (HR 0.93; 95% CI: 0.83-1.04) or eGFR (Estimate: 0.22; 95% CI: -0.79-1.24) at follow-up, which was confirmed in multivariable analyses. In 2,500 patients (37.2%) the initial PCI was performed via radial access. While there was a trend towards lower risk for renal impairment at readmission, ultimately no statistically significant association was found (KDIGO: HR 0.91; 95% CI: 0.82-1.01; eGFR: Estimate 0.79; 95% CI: -0.17-1.75). Conclusion Neither the chosen vascular access route nor exceeding the individual MACD during PCI were associated with a decline in medium- to long-term renal function in patients with repeated interventions within one year.Figure1
title: Association between vascular access route and exceedance of the maximum allowable contrast dose with medium- to long-term renal function decline in patients undergoing repeated PCI

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a systemic chronic disease state characterized by metabolic dysfunction as the core pathology, culminating in cardiovascular and kidney target organ damage [1]. Stage 4 CKM syndrome is defined by the presence of clinical cardiovascular disease (CVD). Patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) are already at this highest-risk stage (Stage 4), yet they frequently harbor multiple additional CKM risk conditions, including hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease (CKD), hypertriglyceridemia (HTG), and obesity [2]. The incremental prognostic impact of this CKM multimorbidity burden in the NSTEMI population remains inadequately defined. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the association between the burden of core CKM components—hypertension, diabetes, CKD, HTG, and obesity—and the risk of all-cause mortality in patients presenting with NSTEMI, and to delineate the differential contributions of these individual components to mortality risk. Methods This multi-cohort study included patients with a confirmed diagnosis of NSTEMI from two independent cohorts: the TAMI cohort (n=14,880) and the MIMIC-IV cohort (n=1,707). Patients were stratified into six groups based on the total number of coexisting CKM conditions at baseline, ranging from 0 to 5. The primary endpoint was 10-Year all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were employed to assess the association between CKM burden groups and mortality risk, and to analyze the independent contribution of each CKM component. Results In the TAMI cohort, 1,432 (9.6%) deaths occurred. In the MIMIC-IV cohort, 571 (28.5%) deaths occurred. Kaplan-Meier curves demonstrated a significant graded increase in all-cause mortality risk with escalating CKM multimorbidity burden in both cohorts (log-rank P &lt; 0.001). In adjusted Cox regression models, compared to patients with NSTEMI alone (0 condition), those with a burden of 5 exhibited a substantially higher risk of death in both the TAMI cohort (HR: 2.010; 95% CI: 1.363–2.898; P &lt; 0.001) and the MIMIC-IV cohort (HR: 3.206; 95% CI: 1.245–8.254; P = 0.016). Among the individual components, CKD was associated with the highest mortality risk in both cohorts (TAMI cohort HR: 1.466; MIMIC-IV cohort HR: 1.495), whereas obesity did not demonstrate a statistically significant independent risk effect in either cohort. Conclusions In patients with NSTEMI overlapping with CKM stage 4, a higher burden of concomitant CKM conditions is associated with a significant and dose-dependent increase in all-cause mortality. CKD emerges as the predominant driver of this risk. These findings underscore the importance of comprehensive CKM risk assessment and stratified management strategies to improve outcomes in NSTEMI patients, with particular attention to those with CKD.
title: Prognostic impact of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic overlap among patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a multi-cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Increased urinary albumin/creatinine ratio (uACR) is independently associated with renal disease progression, and all-cause mortality. uACR reduction improves cardiorenal prognosis. Data on the effect of renal denervation (RDN) on uACR in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and albuminuria is scarce. Methods The Global SYMPLICITY Registry DEFINE is a RDN registry of real-world patients undergoing radiofrequency (RF) RDN with Symplicity RDN system (Medtronic, Plc). Two groups of patients with either microalbuminuria (uACR 30-299 mg/g) or macroalbuminuria (uACR ≥300mg/g) at baseline were analysed. UACR, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), office systolic BP (OSBP) and prescribed number of antihypertensive medication classes (AH med classes) were assessed at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months after RDN. UACR values were log-transformed to compare changes from baseline using paired t-tests. Percentage change in geometric mean of uACR from baseline to follow-up was calculated. To evaluate the correlation between uACR and BP changes, a multivariable linear regression analysis with repeated measures was performed on uACR changes through 2 years with independent variables including OSBP changes. Results Five hundred-fifty-five patients had uACR spot measurements evaluable at baseline. Among these, 125 (23%) patients had microalbuminuria (median uACR 69 [IQR: 46-128] mg/g) with mean eGFR 77 mL/min/1.73 m², and 56 (10%) patients had macroalbuminuria (median uACR 829 [IQR: 437 - 1966] mg/g) with mean eGFR 56 mL/min/1.73 m². In the microalbuminuria group, OSBP was 168±23 mmHg, with 4.8±1.3 prescribed AH med classes, 42% had diabetes, and 45% had renal disease history. In the macroalbuminuria group, OSBP was 166±26 mmHg, with 5.1±0.9 prescribed AH med classes, 63% had diabetes, and 73% had renal disease history. 2 years after RDN, the uACR was significantly reduced by 50% (95% CI: -68%, -23%) and 66% (95% CI: -82%, -33%) in the micro- and macroalbuminuria groups, respectively (Figure). Log-transformed uACR showed significant reductions from baseline at all timepoints (p&lt;0.05). OSBP reduced by 21.9 ± 26.6 mmHg and 16.0 ± 24.4 mmHg at 2 years in the micro- and macroalbuminuria groups, respectively. There were no major changes to AH med classes. Multivariable linear regression showed a significant association between OSBP and uACR changes with a 10mmHg reduction in OSBP being associated with a 14% reduction in uACR (p&lt;0.0001). Conclusion RF RDN was associated with significant uACR reductions in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and albuminuria. The magnitude of the UACR reduction was more pronounced than expected from the BP lowering effect per se, indicative of a potential additional nephroprotective effects of RF RDN. Further prospective study is warranted.Figure
title: Effects on albuminuria and blood pressure after radiofrequency renal denervation: two-year results from the Global SYMPLICITY Registry DEFINE

abstract: Abstract Background The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKM) is a multisystem disorder increasingly recognized for its association with adverse outcomes. The incidence and prognostic relevance of CKM in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has not been investigated. Methods A double center, retrospective analysis of patients undergoing TAVI from 2011 to 2024 was performed. CKM syndrome was diagnosed and quantified using a simplified definition based on the presence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (ASCVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetes mellitus (DM). The prevalence of CKM and its association with procedural success, bleeding events, permanent pacemaker implantation and 1-year mortality was evaluated. Results Among 5,834 TAVI patients, 5,280 (90%) fulfilled criteria for CKM. The overall prevalence remained stable. Procedural success was highest in patients with no CKM conditions, followed by patients with 1 and 2 CKM conditions. Patients with 3 CKM conditions had the worst procedural success (p=0.002). Patients with 2 and 3 CKM conditions had higher probability of death within 1 year as compared to patients with no CKM conditions and 1 CKM condition (HR for 2 CKM conditions 1.40, p=0.030, HR for 3 CKM conditions 1.88, p&lt;0.001). Patients with 3 CKM conditions had higher rates of permanent pacemaker implantation (OR 1.45, p=0.02), but not of major bleeding (HR 1.24, p=0.328). After adjustment for baseline differences in comorbidities and patient characteristics, 3/3 CKM conditions remained associated with increased all-cause mortality at 1, 2 and 5 years. Conclusion CKM is highly prevalent in patients undergoing TAVI. Higher CKM condition burden appeared to be associated with adverse outcomes.
