title: Prevalence and influence of cardiovascular kidney metabolic syndrome on outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Bioprosthetic surgical AVR (bioSAVR) often requires reintervention once structural valve degeneration occurs1. In dialysis, accelerated calcification leads to markedly earlier bioprosthesis failure2. No study has ever focused on the optimal management of failed bioprosthetic aortic valves in dialysis, and current ESC/EACTS and ACC/AHA guidelines do not provide procedure-specific recommendations on redo AVR in dialysis. Purpose To address this knowledge gap by comparing outcomes of redo SAVR vs Valve-in-Valve TAVR in dialysis patients in a nationwide, real-world cohort. Methods All patients on dialysis in the USA with prior bioSAVR undergoing isolated second-time AVR over 10 years (2011-2020) were included from the United States Renal Data System (USRDS) national database and categorized by procedure: redo SAVR (RS) or ViV TAVR (TI). Exclusion criteria: infective endocarditis and any concomitant or planned cardiac interventions. Follow-up data was 100% complete until either death or kidney transplant. Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimates assessed all-cause mortality by procedure and logistic regression identified factors associated with in-Hospital (In-H) mortality. Analyses were repeated after propensity score matching (PSM) by 16 baseline characteristics. Results 729 patients were included (median age 67y; 64% male): 330 RS and 399 TI. Before PSM, the cohorts differed significantly in several characteristics: age (p&lt;0.01), CKD aetiology (p=0.04), dyslipidaemia (p&lt;0.01), COPD (p=0.03) and a-fib/flutter (p=0.02). After PSM (Figure 1), 269 patient pairs were created with excellent balance across all demographics (all p&gt;0.05 and SMD&lt;0.1). TI patients had lower In-H all-cause mortality both before (13% RS vs 5% TI,p&lt;0.01) and after (15% RS vs 3% TI,p&lt;0.01) matching. Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that TI was independently associated with lower odds of In-H mortality compared to RS (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.16–0.52; p&lt;0.01). However, no difference in 1-year mortality was observed (unmatched 28% RS vs 34% TI,p=0.12; matched 29% RS vs 31% TI,p=0.71). No differences in In-H stroke, ECMO or major bleeding were recorded; RS patients had greater ICU stays (median days 5.0 RS vs 1.0 TI,p&lt;0.01) and &gt;96h ventilation (13% RS vs 4% TI,p&lt;0.01). 18 (5.5%) RS and 12 (3.0%) TI patients (p=0.14) underwent kidney transplant during follow-up. The statistical significance of all findings remained consistent after PSM (Figure 1). Both unadjusted and matched KM curves demonstrated higher 5-year mortality in TI compared with RS patients (p&lt;0.01;Figure 2). Conclusions In dialysis patients with degenerated bioprosthetic aortic valves, ViV TAVR is independently associated with fewer short-term adverse events, but higher long-term mortality, compared with redo SAVR. ViV TAVR may be preferred in dialysis patients with limited life expectancy or prohibitive surgical risk, whereas redo SAVR may be favoured in younger, surgically eligible patients.Figure 11816 10MB finalFigure 21818 10MB final

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective USRDS cohort, 2011-2020; 729 patients (330 redo SAVR, 399 ViV TAVR); 269 matched pairs after propensity matching
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective administrative registry with residual confounding and selection of operative candidates; no durability or reintervention data in this extract.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide registry comparison of redo surgical AVR with valve-in-valve TAVR in 729 dialysis patients with failed bioprosthetic SAVR; ViV TAVR was associated with lower in-hospital mortality but not 1-year mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Multivariable logistic regression showed ViV TAVR was independently associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality compared with redo SAVR (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.16-0.52; p<0.01). No difference in 1-year mortality was observed (unmatched 28% RS vs 34% TI, p=0.12; matched 29% RS vs 31% TI, p=0.71).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a population absent from trials and without procedure-specific guideline recommendations (D3, CKD), and could seed a transportability or target trial emulation question.

title: Nationwide 5-year outcomes in U.S. dialysis patients with failed bioprosthetic surgical AVR: valve-in-valve TAVR versus redo surgery

abstract: Abstract Introduction Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a frequent and lethal comorbidity in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This study aimed to quantify the clinical impact of CKD on post-MI outcomes and investigate the molecular mechanisms of cardiorenal crosstalk involving FKBP5. Methods We analyzed MI populations from two large-scale cohorts: the CIN-II (n=27,103 MI patients) and the UK Biobank (n=10,809 MI patients). Experimental CKD+MI models were established in mice using 5/6 nephrectomy followed by LAD ligation. Comprehensive flow cytometry was performed across multiple tissues (heart, bone marrow, spleen, peripheral blood) to profile diverse immune cells. Furthermore, transcriptomic sequencing of CKD mouse hearts, cross-referenced with public databases, was utilized to screen for differentially expressed genes. Protein expression and localization were validated via Western blot, PCR, and immunofluorescence (IF). Mechanistically, protein-protein interactions were confirmed using Co-Immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). The in vivo role of FKBP5 in cardiomyocyte apoptosis and remodeling was evaluated using TUNEL staining and the specific inhibitor SAFit2. Results In the CIN-II cohort, 21.03% of AMI patients had comorbid CKD. Compared to those without CKD, CKD+AMI patients showed a 90% increased risk of all-cause mortality and a 139% increased risk of cardiovascular death (validated in UKB). Clinically, CKD was associated with adverse cardiac remodeling. Systematic flow cytometric screening revealed no significant differences in most immune cell types across tissues, except for a specific expansion of CCR2+ macrophages exclusively in CKD+MI hearts. Transcriptomics and protein validation identified FKBP5 as a key upregulated factor, primarily co-localizing with CCR2+ macrophages. Co-IP confirmed that FKBP5 directly interacts with HSP90 in cardiomyocytes, negatively regulating the protective HIF-1α pathway and promoting hypoxia-induced apoptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of FKBP5 by SAFit2 significantly reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis (via TUNEL assay), decreased infarct size, and improved cardiac function. Conclusion CKD aggravates post-MI cardiac damage by inducing CCR2+ macrophage-derived FKBP5, which suppresses the HSP90/HIF-1α protective axis. Targeting the FKBP5/HSP90 interaction represents a novel therapeutic strategy for cardiorenal syndrome.central illustration
title: Macrophage-derived FKBP5 exacerbates myocardial injury post-infarction in chronic kidney disease via the HSP90/HIF-1α signaling pathway

abstract: Abstract Background Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) patients with renal dysfunction exemplify the "risk-treatment paradox": they face the highest mortality yet receive the least invasive therapy. It remains debated whether this poor prognosis is a consequence of uremic pathology or undertreatment. Purpose To evaluate the utilization of invasive coronary angiography and clinical outcomes in NSTEMI patients across the full spectrum of renal function, specifically comparing Stage 5 Non-Dialysis (5ND) versus Stage 5 Dialysis (5D) patients, and to quantify the mediating role of angiography underuse on 1-year mortality. Methods We analyzed 45,098 NSTEMI patients from multicenter cohort Patients were stratified into five groups based on admission estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and dialysis status: Normal/Mild (Reference, eGFR ≥60 ml/min/1.73 m2), chronic kidney disease (CKD) Stage 3, Stage 4, Stage 5ND, and Stage 5D. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. We performed multivariable Cox regression and causal mediation analysis to estimate the proportion of excess mortality risk attributable specifically to the non-performance of coronary angiography. Results Despite a progressive accumulation of comorbidities with worsening renal function (Ptrend&lt;0.001) (Table 1), angiography utilization followed a striking U-shaped paradox: plummeting from 58.3% (Reference) to a nadir of 8.2% (Stage 5ND), but rebounding to 22.0% in Stage 5D. Mirroring this, 1-year mortality peaked in Stage 5ND (47.8%), significantly exceeding both Reference (10.4%) and Stage 5D groups (36.0%) (Figure 1A). Adjusted mediation analysis identified angiography underuse as a key driver, mediating 22.8% and 25.8% of the excess mortality risk in Stage 5ND and 5D patients, respectively (Figure 1B). Conclusion The excess mortality in advanced CKD is not purely intrinsic but is significantly driven by the withholding of angiography—accounting for one-quarter of preventable deaths. Overcoming this diagnostic inertia to ensure equitable invasive management is imperative to improve survival, particularly for the neglected pre-dialysis population.Table 1.BaselineFigure 1A and B

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre cohort; 45,098 NSTEMI patients stratified by eGFR and dialysis status; causal mediation analysis
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational mediation analysis is vulnerable to confounding by indication and unmeasured frailty; conference abstract without confidence intervals.
appraisal.one_line: In 45,098 patients with NSTEMI, angiography underuse was associated with a quarter of the excess 1-year mortality in advanced CKD in a mediation analysis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Angiography use fell from 58.3% (Reference) to 8.2% (Stage 5ND) and rebounded to 22.0% in Stage 5D; 1-year mortality was 10.4% (Reference), 47.8% (Stage 5ND) and 36.0% (Stage 5D). Mediation analysis estimated that angiography underuse mediated 22.8% and 25.8% of the excess mortality risk in Stage 5ND and 5D patients, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the risk-treatment paradox in advanced CKD with NSTEMI, a population excluded from most invasive-strategy trials (D6), supporting a target trial emulation question.

title: The withholding of invasive assessment mediates one-quarter of excess mortality in NSTEMI patients with advanced chronic kidney disease: a large-scale multicenter analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiovascular complications are a major cause of morbidity after liver transplantation; however, the predominant phenotype of early post-transplant events remains incompletely characterised. This study aimed to evaluate whether early post-transplant cardiovascular events are predominantly arrhythmic rather than ischaemic in nature. Purpose To define the clinical phenotype of one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after liver transplantation and determine the relative contribution of arrhythmic versus ischaemic complications. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-centre cohort study of 637 consecutive adult patients undergoing orthotopic liver transplantation between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2024. The primary endpoint was MACE occurring within one year of transplantation. MACE was defined as a composite of myocardial infarction, new or decompensated heart failure, new or worsening pulmonary hypertension, cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, clinically significant arrhythmia, cardiovascular death, or cerebrovascular accident. Time to first event was calculated from the date of transplantation. All suspected cardiovascular events were adjudicated by structured chart review and categorised according to predefined clinical subtypes. Results Within one year, 89 patients (14.0%) experienced MACE. Arrhythmias were the predominant event type, accounting for 48 of 89 events (53.9%). Cardiac arrest occurred in 14 patients (15.7%), and new or decompensated heart failure in 13 (14.6%). Cerebrovascular accident was observed in 5 cases (5.6%), while myocardial infarction occurred in 2 patients (2.2%). Arrhythmic events occurred early after transplantation, with a median time to event of 2.5 days (interquartile range 0.0–11.5 days), and 83.3% occurring within 30 days. Among arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation was most frequent (31/48, 64.6%), followed by supraventricular tachycardia (6/48, 12.5%). Bradyarrhythmias and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia each accounted for 6.2% of arrhythmic events. Sustained ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation were infrequent. Conclusion In this cohort, early post-transplant cardiovascular events were predominantly arrhythmic rather than ischaemic, with atrial fibrillation representing the most common MACE phenotype. These findings suggest that early cardiovascular risk after liver transplantation may be driven more by perioperative electrophysiologic and haemodynamic instability, including autonomic dysregulation, altered loading conditions, and cirrhotic cardiomyopathy, than by obstructive coronary disease. This pattern highlights the importance of early rhythm surveillance and haemodynamic optimisation in this high-risk population.Figure 1:A/BFigure: 2
title: Arrhythmias as the dominant phenotype of early cardiovascular events after liver transplantation

abstract: Abstract Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a high-risk phenotype characterized by impaired renal reserve and chronic inflammation. In patients undergoing Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair (M-TEER), these vulnerabilities may predispose to cardiorenal instability and adverse outcomes. This study aims to quantify the magnitude of CKD-associated risk to improve early identification and renal-protective strategies in this population. Purpose To determine the association between CKD and mortality and major in-hospital complications, with particular emphasis on acute kidney injury (AKI), in patients undergoing M-TEER. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases identified observational studies comparing outcomes in patients with CKD versus without CKD. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included AKI, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, vascular complications, bleeding, and stroke. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using fixed-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using $I^2$ statistics, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Seven studies comprising 23,831 patients (6,078 with CKD; 17,753 without CKD) were included. CKD was associated with a nearly threefold increased risk of AKI (RR 2.99, 95% CI 2.82–3.17; I2=90%), representing the most pronounced adverse association observed. CKD was also associated with higher mortality (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.56–2.07; I2=62%), cardiogenic shock (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.50–1.96; I2=32%), respiratory failure (RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.31–1.58; I2=36%), and vascular complications (RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.25–1.90; I2=85%). No significant association was observed for stroke (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.65–1.15; I2=92%). Findings remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. Conclusion CKD markedly amplifies vulnerability to AKI and significantly increases mortality and multiple in-hospital complications in patients undergoing M-TEER. These findings reinforce CKD as a powerful cardiorenal risk phenotype and support the need for early renal-protective and risk-adapted management strategies in this high-risk population.
title: Chronic kidney disease as a potent amplifier of acute kidney injury and mortality following mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER): a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Current clinical guidelines for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) advocate for an aggressive LDL-c target of &lt;1.4 mmol/L. However, the safety and efficacy of this "lower-is-better" strategy remain controversial in "vulnerable" populations, particularly those with combined renal insufficiency and malnutrition. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the impact of follow-up LDL-c levels on clinical outcomes in AMI patients with renal impairment, stratified by nutritional status. Methods In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, AMI patients with renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] &lt;90 mL/min/1.73m²) were enrolled from 82 hospitals in China, between 2010 and 2024. Patients were categorized by follow-up LDL-c levels at 3-6 months and nutritional status using the Nutritional Risk Index (NRI). To eliminate baseline confounding in the malnourished subgroup (NRI &lt; 100), Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting (IPTW) was applied to balance age, sex, Killip class, comorbidities, and eGFR. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and Restricted Cubic Splines (RCS) were used to evaluate adjusted Hazard Ratios (aHRs) for all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE, a composite of all-cause death, cardiac death, myocardial infarction, revascularization, and cerebral infarction), and bleeding events, using LDL-c &lt;1.4 mmol/L as the reference. Results Among 5,387 included patients, 1,689 (31.4%) were identified as malnourished (NRI &lt; 100). In the malnourished cohort, restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant U-shaped relationship between LDL-c levels and all-cause mortality, whereas a linear association was observed in well-nourished patients. After IPTW adjustment, ultra-low LDL-c (&lt;1.4 mmol/L) did not confer a survival benefit compared with the reference group in malnourished individuals. Notably, malnourished patients with LDL-c &lt;1.4 mmol/L exhibited a significantly elevated risk of BARC 3–5 bleeding events relative to those with moderate LDL-c levels (adjusted hazard ratios [aHRs] for 1.4–1.8 mmol/L and 1.8–2.6 mmol/L were 0.53 [95% CI 0.33–0.83] and 0.55 [0.37–0.81], respectively; all P &lt; 0.05). In contrast, well-nourished patients demonstrated a monotonically increasing risk profile, while ultra-low LDL-c levels were associated with protective effects. Conclusions Nutritional status significantly modulates the prognostic value of LDL-c in acute myocardial infarction patients with renal insufficiency. Although intensive lipid-lowering therapy remains beneficial in well-nourished individuals, ultra-low LDL-c levels in the setting of malnutrition are associated with an elevated risk of major bleeding and do not improve ischemic outcomes or all-cause mortality.
title: The prognostic paradox of LDL cholesterol modulated by nutritional status in acute myocardial infarction patients with renal impairment: a multicenter retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Both cardiovascular diseases and cognitive impairment (CI) are major public health problems in ageing societies. Growing evidence indicates shared mechanisms between ischaemic heart disease, including myocardial infarction (MI), and CI; however, cognitive assessment is not routinely implemented in cardiology care. Purpose To evaluate the prevalence and dynamics of CI in patients hospitalised for MI and to develop a prototype AI-based digital screening tool to classify CI after MI, focusing on attention- the cognitive function most frequently impaired in this patient population. Methods A total of 468 patients with MI treated with percutaneous coronary intervention were prospectively assessed during hospitalisation (days 2–3) and at 6-month follow-up. Cognitive function was evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and the Clock Drawing Test (CDT). CI was defined as MMSE &lt;27 points and/or ≥1 CDT error. Clinical and psychological data were collected. Based on these data, an AI-assisted screening tool was developed using automated analysis of CDT drawings combined with selected MMSE items assessing attention and recall. Results Previously undiagnosed CI was identified in 37% of patients during hospitalisation and in 25% at follow-up. CI both during MI and at 6 months was present in 8.9–12.5% of patients, CI limited to the peri-infarction period in 16.3–18.1%, and CI emerging at follow-up in 7.7–9.8%, depending on the test used. Attention deficits were present in all cases of CI and closely correlated with changes in global cognitive status; improvement or deterioration in cognition during follow-up was accompanied by corresponding changes in attention in 81% and 100% of patients, respectively. Compared with patients without CI, those with CI were older (60.4 ± 10.2 vs. 58.3 ± 9.3 years; p = 0.03) and demonstrated more severe myocardial injury, reflected by higher B-type natriuretic peptide levels (p = 0.01) and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (p = 0.05). They also had more advanced coronary atherosclerosis and higher LDL cholesterol levels (both p = 0.05). Depressive symptoms and sleep disturbances were more pronounced in patients with CI. These findings formed the basis for development of a prototype AI-based screening tool aimed at early identification of CI in patients after MI. The tool integrated two CDT tasks (free placement of numbers on the clock face and setting the clock hands to a specific time, 11:10) with MMSE attention and recall items. The combined feature set achieved the highest performance, with an accuracy of 0.93, precision of 0.97, and AUROC of 0.95. Conclusion CI is common after MI and often remains unrecognised. Attention deficits represent the predominant cognitive domain affected. An AI-based screening approach focused on attention may support early identification of post-MI patients with CI in cardiology practice while minimising the burden on medical staff.Proposed AI-based screening tool.
title: Attention deficits as a target for AI-based screening of cognitive impairment after myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) promotes thrombogenicity through antiphospholipid antibodies, leading to thrombotic events in both venous and arterial systems. Although uncommon, acute coronary syndrome (ACS) can occur as a thrombotic manifestation of APS. However, the prevalence of antiphospholipid antibodies among patients with ACS and their association with clinical outcomes remain unclear. Purpose We aimed to assess the prevalence and prognostic impact of antiphospholipid antibodies in patients with ACS. Methods ACS patients (N=184) who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and blood testing for antiphospholipid antibodies at hospitalization were retrospectively enrolled between October 2022 and September 2024. Antiphospholipid antibodies included lupus anticoagulant (LA), anti-cardiolipin IgG (aCL-IgG), anti-cardiolipin IgM (aCL-IgM), and beta-2-glycoprotein I (β2GPI). Depending on whether at least one antibody was present, patients were divided into a ≥1 positive group (n=49) or a negative group (n=135), and clinical characteristics were compared. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularization. Results Overall, LA, aCL-IgG, aCL-IgM, and β2GPI antibodies were positive in 23.4%, 3.3%, 1.1%, and 0% of patients, respectively. At least one antiphospholipid antibody was positive (≥1 positive) in 26.6% of patients. Clinical characteristics are shown in Table 1. Patients with ≥1 positive antibodies had a lower prevalence of hyperlipidemia and higher eGFR values, while there were no differences in ACS characteristics. Kaplan–Meier survival curves for MACE are shown in Figure 1. Patients with ≥1 positive antibodies showed significantly worse event-free survival than those with negative antibodies (HR 3.04, 95% CI:1.27-7.63, P=0.01). Conclusion The presence of antiphospholipid antibodies is associated with worse clinical outcomes in patients with ACS, beyond conventional coronary risk factors.Figure and table
title: Prognostic impact of antiphospholipid antibodies in acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background Immune-mediated inflammation plays a central role in atherosclerosis and clinical progression of ischemic heart disease (IHD). The balance between pro-inflammatory and regulatory immune pathways remains incompletely characterized in different coronary syndromes. This study investigated circulating interleukin-35 (IL-35), interleukin-17A (IL-17A), and FOXP3 in patients with varying IHD presentations. Methods A case–control observational study included 100 participants aged 25–85 years. Sixty patients with IHD were classified as stable angina (n=30), unstable angina (n=15), or myocardial infarction (n=15), and compared with 40 controls (with and without cardiovascular risk factors). Diagnosis was established according to guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology. Serum IL-35, IL-17A, FOXP3, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) were quantified using ELISA. Statistical comparisons were performed using SPSS. Results hs-CRP levels were significantly elevated in IHD patients and showed a stepwise increase from stable angina to myocardial infarction (p&lt;0.00001). IL-17A concentrations were markedly higher in myocardial infarction and unstable angina compared with stable angina and controls (p&lt;0.00001). FOXP3 levels were significantly increased in unstable angina and myocardial infarction (p&lt;0.001), indicating enhanced regulatory T-cell activation in advanced disease. In contrast, IL-35 concentrations were significantly reduced in IHD patients and in individuals with cardiovascular risk factors compared with healthy controls (p&lt;0.00001). Combined biomarker profiles correlated with disease severity and inflammatory burden. Conclusions IHD is characterized by dysregulated immune homeostasis with reduced anti-inflammatory IL-35 and increased IL-17A, FOXP3, and hs-CRP. These biomarkers reflect disease severity across the spectrum of coronary syndromes and may represent complementary tools for risk stratification. Clinical Implications Immunological profiling may support inflammatory risk assessment and identify novel therapeutic targets aimed at restoring immune balance in IHD.Figure 1
title: Immunoregulatory cytokine profile in ischemic heart disease: association of IL-35, IL-17A and FOXP3 with clinical severity

abstract: Abstract Background The mortality rate in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has been estimated to be increased by approximately 50% compared with general population, and cardiovascular diseases are the most frequent cause of death in RA patients. However, it is unclear whether the changes in RA treatment strategies over the past two decades have altered cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in this population. Purpose To examine long-term outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in RA. Methods We used data from Silesian Cardiovascular Database (SILCARD) which is based on the data from the Regional Department of the National Health Fund (NHF) in Poland. We included in the analysis consecutive adult patients who presented with ACS, admitted between January 2010 and December 2022 to participating hospitals, who were identified using ICD-10 codes for primary discharge diagnosis. Patients with prevalent RA were recognized from the registry database using ICD-10 codes. Baseline characteristics, co-morbidities, and outcomes during index hospitalization, within 12 months and 3 years from hospital discharge were obtained from hospital records and NHF. The primary endpoint was the time to the first MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event including all-cause death, recurrent non-fatal acute myocardial infarction (MI), unstable angina (UA), stroke). Cox proportional hazard ratio (HR) was calculated to estimate associations and adjusted for confounding (age, sex, comorbidities, revascularization for index ACS). Results A total of 196 588 patients with ACS (mean age 67.3±11 years, 38.2% women), including 9 232 patients with prevalent RA were enrolled. Patients with RA were older, more often female and had a higher burden of comorbidities than individuals without rheumatoid arthritis, with the exception of stroke (Table). Revascularization by percutaneous coronary intervention was performed in a comparable proportion of patients in both groups (61.3% in RA vs. 62.1% in non-RA group, P=0.122), and coronary artery bypass graft surgery was performed less frequently in RA than in non-RA patients (8.6% vs.9.6%; P=0.002). During 12 months and 3 years after discharge for index ACS both groups experienced similar rates of MI, stroke and all-cause mortality, patients with RA had higher rates of hospitalization. In the Cox regression model, the relative rate of MACE during follow-up after discharge for index ACS was 3.4% higher among participants with RA compared to patients without RA (adjusted HR 1.034; 95% Confidence Interval 1.003 – 1.066; P =0.032). Conclusion Our findings suggests that, during 3 years following ACS, patients with RA experience a modestly elevated risk of MACE compared with individuals without RA. These results underscore the importance of early risk stratification, rigorous management of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, and optimal control of systemic inflammation in this population.
title: Long-term outcomes after acute coronary syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis

abstract: Abstract Introduction and Aim Myocarditis presents with high clinical heterogeneity, and predicting long-term symptom recurrence remains a challenge despite current diagnostic standards. The INFLA-SCORE, a multidimensional systemic inflammation index, may better characterize this inflammatory burden. We evaluated the utility of the INFLA-SCORE in predicting clinical management and 1-year outcomes within a large, prospective, nationwide myocarditis cohort. Methods Patients with confirmed myocarditis and complete baseline data were selected from the Pre-MYO registry (76 centers, Spain). The INFLA-SCORE, a composite index of systemic inflammation (CRP, leukocyte count, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio), was calculated at admission. Patients were stratified into quartiles (Q1–Q4) to assess the score's discriminative capacity. The primary endpoint was 1-year MACE (cardiovascular death, heart failure hospitalization, or life-threatening arrhythmias). Secondary endpoints included 1-year symptom recurrence and LVEF recovery. Results The cohort included 658 patients (mean age 40.6±18.8 years; 79.2% male). Baseline LVEF was preserved (54.4%±10.6), and CMR findings, including late gadolinium enhancement, were evenly distributed across the inflammatory spectrum (p=0.887). Markers of acute myocardial injury, such as peak troponin and NT-proBNP levels, showed no significant differences between groups, confirming the INFLA-SCORE successfully stratified the population into quartiles, from Q1 (median -8) to Q4 (median 9). Clinical management at discharge varied by inflammatory baseline: Q4 patients were significantly more likely to receive corticosteroids than Q1 (15.9% vs. 5.9%; p=0.020). Other treatments, such as colchicine (51.7%) and NSAIDs (34.8%), were used homogeneously (Table 1). At 1-year, MACE incidence was low (1.5%) and did not differ across quartiles (p=0.298; Figure 1). However, a notable clinical trend appeared in symptom recurrence: Q4 patients exhibited the lowest rate (30.7%) vs. Q1 (44.7%; p=0.069), primarily driven by lower recurrent chest pain in the most inflamed group (28.0% vs. 41.6%; p=0.090). Readmission and LVEF recovery were similar across quartiles, suggesting the score correlates with therapeutic decisions and the subsequent symptomatic course rather than hard endpoints. Conclusions The INFLA-SCORE effectively identifies myocarditis patients with a higher systemic inflammatory burden who are more frequently targeted for corticosteroid therapy in real-world practice. This high-score phenotype showed a more favorable symptomatic course with lower recurrence of chest pain at 1 year, suggesting that early, personalized anti-inflammatory interventions guided by this score could reduce the long-term symptomatic burden.Table 1.Myocarditis outcomes by INFLA-SCOREFigure 1.Clinical outcomes by INFLA-SCORE
title: Predictive value of the INFLA-SCORE in patients with myocarditis: insights from the nationwide prospective pre-MYO registry

abstract: Abstract Introduction Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), driven by age-related somatic mutations in hematopoietic stem cells, has emerged as a novel modulator of cardiovascular risk. Objectives This study investigates the prognostic interplay between TET2-CHIP mutations, systemic inflammation quantified by high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) by bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) to elucidate causal relationships among ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients. Patients and methods A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study was performed using genetic instruments for TET2-CHIP from the UK Biobank (2,041 cases; 173,918 controls) and hs-CRP data from the European Bioinformatics Institute consortium (353,466 cases and 34,594,039 controls) to assess causality. Results Bidirectional MR studies indicated that the increased value of hs-CRP improves the propensity for CHIP.265 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with P &lt; 10−8 were pruned as 10 Mb apart and in linkage disequilibrium with each SNP exhibiting an F-statistic exceeding the threshold of 10 (p＜5*10-8, r2＜0.001, window size=1000kb). Inverse variance weighted estimates suggested that hs-CRP had a risk causal relationship effect on TET2-CHIP mutations (odds ratio = 1.0024, 95% confidence interval: 1.0005-1.0043, P = 0.0153) . MR-Egger (Q = 215.2087, Q value = 0.2817；IVW，Q = 215.871, Q value = 0.2876) and MR-PRESSO (p value=0.564) intercept did not identify any pleiotropic SNPs. We found no evidence supporting significant horizontal pleiotropy (Egger intercept = 0.00004, P = 0.4291) . Forest plot has shown the beta estimates and 95% confidence intervals of MR. No significant heterogeneity of instrumental variables or horizontal pleiotropy was found. The findings of scatter plots indicated that the trajectories of various algorithms exhibit an overall upward trend, suggesting that the risk of TET2-CHIP mutations escalates with increasing concentrations of hs-CRP. The positive potential causal effect of TET2-CHIP on hs-CRP was not shown in the conventional two-sample MR approach [inverse variance weighted method; Estimate = 0.6296, 95% CI: 0.3262–1.2154, P = 0.1680]. According to the results of reverse MR analysis, no significant causal effect of CHIP was found on hs-CRP. We next evaluated the relationship of PCSK9 with the occurrence of CHIP acquired genome-wide singleton single nucleotide polymorphism. However, MR analyses did not supported a causal relationship between PCSK9 and increased somatic mutations in two-sample MR study. Conclusion Mendelian randomization establishes a unidirectional causal relationship where genetically determined hs-CRP elevation predisposes to TET2-CHIP acquisition. These findings align with emerging paradigms of somatic mutation-driven inflammation while providing novel insights into risk stratification and therapeutic targeting in post-MI populations.Mendelian randomization of CRP on CHIPScatter plots
title: Bidirectional mendelian randomzation study of TET2-clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential-mutations with hs-CRP in patients with STEMI

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac remodeling post-myocardial infarction (MI) can occur even after successful coronary reperfusion, particularly in anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). This remodeling process may lead to a decline in left ventricular (LV) fuction, cardiac output and exercise capacity thereby increasing the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events. Finerenone, a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, exerts anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects that may attenuate post-infarction remodeling. Studies evaluating the effects of finerenone on cardiac remodeling and exercise capacity in post MI patients are still very limited. Purpose to evaluate the effect of Finerenone on LV function, cardiac output (CO) and exercise capacity in patients with anterior STEMI who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI). Methods This was a double-blind randomized controlled clinical trial involving patients with anterior STEMI and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) &gt;40% who successfully underwent primary PCI. Participants received either Finerenone 10 mg daily (n = 27) or placebo (n = 25) for 60 days, in addition to standard medical therapy. LVEF and global longitudinal strain (GLS) as parameters of LV function and cardiac output was measured using echocardiography at predischarge and after 60 days of treatment. Exercise capacity was assessed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Results Baseline clinical characteristics were comparable between the two groups. After 60 days follow up, improvement of LVEF and GLS was greater in finerenone group compared with control group (Δ LVEF pre→post 4,62 ± 3,11% vs 2,16 ± 3,23%; p = 0.007; Δ GLS pre→post -3,22 ± 2,68% vs -1,60 ± 2,29; p = 0.024). The mean change in CO (Δ pre→post) was greater in the Finerenone group (+0.32 ± 1.03 vs −0.07 ± 1.17; p = 0.203), though not statistically significant. Exercise capacity parameters were also higher in the Finerenone group but did not reach statistical significance (peak VO2 23.6 ± 3.8 vs 21.6 ± 3.9 mL·kg−1·min−1, p = 0.084; oxygen pulse 12.5 ± 2.3 vs 11.6 ± 2.7 mL/beat, p = 0.216; METs 6.66 ± 1.24 vs 6.17 ± 1.10, p = 0.139). No clinically relevant adverse events related to Finerenone 10 mg were observed during the follow up. Conclusions Administration of Finerenone 10 mg for 60 days improve of LV function, while did not result in significant differences in cardiac output or exercise capacity compared with placebo in patients with anterior STEMI following primary PCI.Picture and diagram
title: Effect of finerenone on cardiac remodeling and exercise capacity in patients with anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Oral anticoagulation (OAC) monotherapy is recommended for patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) requiring long-term anticoagulation. Recent trials suggest a mortality benefit not demonstrated previously. We conducted a Bayesian meta-analysis to quantify probabilities of benefit. Methods PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched to January 2026 for randomised controlled trials comparing OAC monotherapy with dual antithrombotic therapy (DATT) in CCS patients requiring long-term anticoagulation. Bayesian random-effects models used weakly informative priors for treatment effects and outcome-specific heterogeneity priors; robustness was assessed with sensitivity analyses using non-informative priors. Primary outcomes were all-cause death and major bleeding. Secondary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction (MI), ischaemic stroke, all stroke, major or clinically relevant non major bleeding, and net adverse clinical events (NACE). Results are reported as risk ratios (RR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI) and probabilities of superiority. Results Six trials (5924 participants) were included. OAC monotherapy was associated with likely reduced all-cause death (RR 0.77, 95% CrI 0.58–1.07; 94.6% probability of superiority) and significantly reduced major bleeding (RR 0.51, 95% CrI 0.36–0.69; 100%). Cardiovascular death favoured OAC monotherapy (RR 0.73; 95% CrI 0.53 - 1.06; 95.4%), as did major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (RR 0.50; 95% CrI 0.37–0.65; 100%) and net adverse clinical events (RR 0.64; 95% CrI 0.49–0.82; 99.8%). There was inconclusive evidence for MACE (RR 0.88, 95% CrI 0.68–1.14; 86.0%), MI (RR 1.03, CrI 0.62–1.70; 45.9%), ischaemic stroke (RR 1.07, 95% CrI 0.71–1.68; 36.8%), and all stroke (RR 1.12; 95% CrI 0.68–1.86; 33.1%). Between-study heterogeneity was low to moderate; findings were robust in sensitivity analyses.CRD420260533373 Conclusions In CCS patients requiring long-term anticoagulation, OAC monotherapy significantly reduces bleeding and demonstrates high probability of mortality benefit compared with DATT, without increased ischaemic risk, supporting its use as the preferred antithrombotic strategy. Registration: PROSPERO CRD420260533373mainplotabstract.jpegfig2abstract.jpeg
title: Oral anticoagulation monotherapy versus dual antithrombotic therapy in chronic coronary syndrome patients requiring long-term anticoagulation: a bayesian meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), oral anticoagulation is indicated, yet concomitant antiplatelet therapy (APT) is frequently prescribed for concurrent ischaemic prevention indications. It remains unknown whether the risk-benefit profile of concomitant APT differs by sex in this patient population. Purpose To determine if the risk-benefit profile of oral anticoagulation with concomitant APT differs by sex in patients with AF undergoing TAVI. Methods This post hoc analysis used the ENVISAGE-TAVI AF safety analysis set (N = 1377), in which patients received edoxaban or vitamin K antagonist therapy after successful TAVI. In this analysis, patients were stratified by sex and by any APT exposure during the full study period. Primary outcomes included net adverse clinical events (NACE), a composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, systemic thromboembolism, valve thrombosis, or major bleeding. Secondary outcomes included individual components of the primary outcome. Results Among 1377 anticoagulated patients, 719 were men (52.2%) and 658 were women (47.8%). Concomitant APT was used in 436 (60.6%) men and 388 (59.0%) women. Among patients receiving concomitant APT, both female and male patients had a higher prevalence of prior myocardial infarction and percutaneous coronary intervention, although these characteristics were observed more frequently in male patients than female patients (Table). Male patients with vs without APT were also more likely to have a higher prevalence of history of stroke/transient ischaemic attack, peripheral arterial disease, hypercholesterolaemia, and diabetes (Table). One hundred ninety-seven (50.8%) female patients and 214 (49.1%) male patients on APT were randomised to edoxaban. Risk of NACE was higher with APT in both males and females (Figure). The risk increase of major bleeding with APT was attenuated in males (hazard ratio [HR], 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], [0.84–2.15]) compared with females (HR 2.22 [1.36–3.63], P = 0.1 for interaction). Similarly, APT was associated with a higher risk of major gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding in females (HR, 3.61; 95% CI, 1.60–8.12) but not in males (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 0.59–2.10; P = 0.03 for interaction). No statistically significant differences were noted for secondary outcomes (Figure). Conclusions Among anticoagulated TAVI patients with AF, concomitant APT was associated with a higher risk of NACE. Bleeding risk, particularly major GI bleeding, was higher in females compared with males. APT should be avoided in the absence of a strong indication in anticoagulated patients with AF after TAVI; sex-specific bleeding vulnerability may warrant greater caution.
title: Concomitant antiplatelet therapy in anticoagulated TAVI patients with atrial fibrillation: impact of sex on bleeding and ischaemic events in ENVISAGE-TAVI AF

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) who present with High Bleeding Risk (HBR) criteria are often underrepresented in randomized trials. The optimal antithrombotic strategy post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) in this vulnerable population remains a clinical dilemma, balancing ischemic protection against bleeding complications. Real-world data regarding the use of Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH) in this specific subset is limited. Purpose To evaluate the association between the use of post-PCI LMWH and 30-day clinical outcomes in AMI patients with HBR undergoing PCI. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing a large-scale institutional database. From an initial cohort of 163,472 AMI patients, we consecutively enrolled those meeting HBR criteria (defined as age &gt;65 years, anemia, prior stroke, prior intracranial hemorrhage, CKD, or thrombocytopenia) who underwent PCI. Key exclusion criteria included malignancy, specific high-risk arrhythmias (ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation, sinus arrest), Killip class III-IV, use of alternative anticoagulants (bivalirudin, fondaparinux), or oral anticoagulants.The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. The secondary endpoint was 30-day BARC type 3 bleeding. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to adjust for potential confounders and estimate treatment effects. Results A total of 33,686 patients met the inclusion criteria, of whom 30,294 (89.9%) received post-PCI LMWH and 3,392 (10.1%) did not. The 30-day all-cause mortality was significantly lower in the LMWH group compared to the no-LMWH group (0.7% vs. 1.7%, p &lt; 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, LMWH use was independently associated with a significant reduction in 30-day mortality (Adjusted HR: 0.565; 95% CI: 0.400–0.797; p=0.001). The incidence of BARC type 3 bleeding was numerically similar between groups (LMWH: 31 [0.10%] vs. no-LMWH: 4 [0.12%]; p=1.0), with no significant difference in the adjusted analysis (HR: 0.845; 95% CI: 0.273–2.617; p=0.771).Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed a significant reduction in 30-day all-cause mortality in the LMWH group (log-rank p&lt;0.001, Figure 1). Subgroup analyses consistently demonstrated a protective effect of LMWH across various HBR categories(Figure 2). Conclusion In this real-world cohort of AMI patients with HBR undergoing PCI, the use of post-procedural LMWH was associated with a significantly lower risk of 30-day all-cause mortality without a significant increase in major bleeding events. These findings suggest a favorable net clinical benefit for LMWH in this high-risk population, warranting further validation in prospective randomized trials.Kaplan-Meier curves
title: Prognostic impact of post-procedural low-molecular-weight heparin in high-bleeding risk patients undergoing pci for acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background The management of antithrombotic therapy in patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) requiring long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC), primarily for atrial fibrillation, poses a significant clinical challenge due to the need to balance thrombotic and bleeding risks. Aim This Bayesian meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of OAC monotherapy versus combination therapy (OAC plus single antiplatelet therapy [SAPT]) in patients with stable CAD requiring long-term OAC. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase up to September 2025 for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing OAC monotherapy with combination therapy in the target population. Data on primary outcomes (major adverse cardiovascular events [MACE], net adverse clinical events [NACE], and major bleeding) were extracted. A Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis was performed with vague priors specified for the pooled effect (normal(mean=0, sd=2)) and between-study heterogeneity (half-normal(scale=0.5)). Results are presented as posterior mean risk ratios (RR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI), and the probability of benefit was calculated as the posterior probability of benefit (PPoB) that RR &lt;1. Results Six studies (5,924 patients) were included. OAC monotherapy demonstrated a high probability of benefit for safety outcomes, with strong evidence for reducing ISTH major bleeding (RR 0.48, 95% CrI 0.31–0.72; PPoB: 99.8%) and major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CrI 0.28–0.66; PPoB: 99.8%). For composite efficacy-safety outcomes, OAC monotherapy reduced trial-defined NACE (RR 0.64, 95% CrI 0.46–0.88; PPoB: 99.3%) and showed a high probability of benefit for MACE (RR 0.85, 95% CrI 0.66–1.09; PPoB: 89.4%). Mortality outcomes, including all-cause death (RR 0.80, 95% CrI 0.53–1.28; PPoB: 86.9%) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.75, 95% CrI 0.50–1.21; PPoB: 91.1%), favoured OAC monotherapy. Ischaemic stroke and myocardial infarction demonstrated neutral effects. Conclusion In patients with stable CAD requiring long-term OAC, OAC monotherapy demonstrates superior net clinical benefit and should be considered the standard of care, as combination therapy provides no additional protection against ischaemic events while substantially increasing the risk of bleeding.Forest Plot For all Outcomes
title: Single vs. dual antithrombotic therapy in patients with stabilized coronary artery disease requiring long-term oral anticoagulation: A Bayesian meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain, as therapy must balance ischemic protection against bleeding risk. While prolonged DAPT may enhance antithrombotic efficacy, shorter regimens have been proposed to improve safety. Purpose To compare the efficacy and safety of short (≤6 months) versus prolonged (&gt;6 months) DAPT following PCI. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through November 27, 2025. Randomized controlled trials and observational cohort studies comparing short versus prolonged DAPT were included. Efficacy outcomes were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). The primary safety outcome was bleeding. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) were calculated using random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed by the I² statistic. Results Thirty-three studies (24 RCTs and 9 cohorts), including 86,676 patients, were analyzed. Short DAPT showed comparable efficacy to prolonged DAPT, with no significant differences in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, MACE, or TVR. Short DAPT significantly reduced bleeding events (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.76–0.98; p=0.02) with no heterogeneity (I²=0%). Conclusions In patients undergoing PCI, ≤6 months of DAPT provides similar protection against ischemic events as &gt;6 months, while significantly reducing bleeding. These findings support guideline-aligned strategies favoring shorter DAPT in appropriately selected patients, particularly those at higher bleeding risk, without compromising cardiovascular outcomes.OutcomesINFOGRAPHIC
title: Efficacy and safety of short (≤6 months) versus prolonged (&gt;6 months) dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Extended clopidogrel monotherapy following dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) has demonstrated potential efficacy in patients receiving drug-eluting stents (DES). Purpose This prespecified subgroup analysis of the OPT-BIRISK trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of extended clopidogrel monotherapy versus continued DAPT in acute coronary syndromes (ACS) patients with coexisting high ischemic and bleeding risks, stratified by troponin status. Methods In the OPT-BIRISK study, 7,758 ACS patients with both high ischemic and bleeding risks who completed 9-12 months DAPT after DES implantation were randomized to receive clopidogrel monotherapy or clopidogrel plus aspirin for 9 months. The primary endpoint was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 2, 3, or 5 bleeding at 9 months. Primary and key secondary endpoints included Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 2, 3, or 5 bleeding and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), respectively. Results Clopidogrel monotherapy demonstrated a consistent 25% non-significant reduction in BARC 2, 3, or 5 bleeding risk across troponin strata (troponin-negative: 2.8% vs. 3.7%, HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54 - 1.06, P = 0.101; troponin-positive: 2.0% vs. 2.7%, HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.49 - 1.15, P = 0.181). Any bleeding risk was significantly lower with monotherapy in both subgroups (troponin-negative: 16.3% vs. 20.3%, HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.68-0.91, P = 0.001; troponin-positive: 12.4% vs. 15.5%, HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66-0.94, P = 0.008). MACCE rates were comparable between treatment arms (troponin-negative: 2.3% vs. 3.2%, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.48 - 1.01, P = 0.060; troponin-positive: 3.0% vs. 3.8%, HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.55 - 1.12, P = 0.175). No significant interaction was observed for all endpoints. Conclusions In bi-risk ACS patients completing 9-12 months of DAPT post-DES, extended clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with a lower risk of any bleeding without increasing the risk of MACCE compared to DAPT, irrespective of troponin status.
title: Troponin-stratified outcomes of extended clopidogrel monotherapy versus dual antiplatelet therapy in acute coronary syndrome: insights from the OPT-BIRISK randomized trial

abstract: Abstract Background the clinical benefit of genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy compared with standard treatment in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the impact of a genetic testing–guided strategy on ischaemic and safety outcomes after PCI. Methods electronic databases were systematically searched to identify randomised controlled trials comparing genotype-guided versus standard antiplatelet therapy in patients undergoing PCI. After screening the retrieved records, eligible trials were included in a meta-analysis. Pooled effect estimates were calculated as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models. Analyses were performed in the overall population and according to clinical presentation (acute versus chronic coronary syndromes). Results our analysis included 8 randomised controlled trials with data for 10,850 patients. Compared with standard therapy, genotype-guided antiplatelet selection was associated with a significant reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (IRR 0.63, 95% CI 0.43–0.94) and stent thrombosis (IRR 0.64, 95% CI 0.43–0.95). Stroke showed a borderline reduction in the overall population (IRR 0.65, 95% CI 0.41–1.01), reaching statistical significance in the acute coronary syndrome cohort (IRR 0.56, 95% CI 0.33–0.97). No significant differences were observed for all-cause mortality (IRR 0.65, 95% CI 0.31–1.38) or cardiovascular mortality (IRR 0.70, 95% CI 0.40–1.21). Similarly, major bleeding (IRR 0.86, 95% CI 0.63–1.16) and minor bleeding (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56–1.09) did not differ significantly between strategies. Subgroup analyses according to acute or chronic clinical presentation did not reveal significant interactions; however, these analyses were limited by the small number of patients within each subgroup and wide confidence intervals. Conclusions in patients undergoing PCI, a genotype-guided antiplatelet strategy is associated with improved ischaemic outcomes, particularly through reductions in MACE and stent thrombosis, without an excess of bleeding. However, no significant reduction in all-cause or cardiovascular mortality was observed. These findings support a selective role for genetic testing in tailoring antiplatelet therapy, while highlighting the need for adequately powered studies to clarify effects on hard mortality endpoints.Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE)ACM and CVM outcomes
title: Genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

abstract: Abstract Background The PRECISE-DAPT score has demonstrated utility in predicting hemorrhagic events associated with dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and in guiding therapy duration in patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS). However, its predictive accuracy in older adults, a population characterized by increasing ACS prevalence and elevated baseline bleeding risk, remains uncertain. Objective To assess the predictive performance of the PRECISE-DAPT score for clinically significant bleeding in patients aged &gt;75 years receiving DAPT after ACS. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted including patients aged ≥75 years admitted with ACS between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients with prior DAPT exposure or discharged on oral anticoagulation were excluded. Clinical and laboratory variables required for PRECISE-DAPT calculation—history of prior bleeding, baseline hemoglobin, leukocyte count, and estimated glomerular filtration rate—were collected at discharge. The primary endpoint was BARC (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium) grade ≥ 2 bleeding, defined as requiring at least medical intervention, occurring during the course of DAPT. Discriminatory performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results A total of 402 patients (74% male; mean age 80 ± 4 years) were included. Most (92%) received aspirin plus clopidogrel. During a mean follow-up of 9 ± 4 months, 61 patients (18.7%) experienced BARC ≥2 bleeding. PRECISE-DAPT scores were similar in patients with and without bleeding (34 ± 10 vs 32 ± 7; p = 0.54). The proportion classified as high risk (score &gt; 25) was comparably high in both groups and even within this high-risk category the score displayed no discriminative ability (81% vs. 76%; p = 0.48). No significant differences were observed in any individual score components. Overall, the score demonstrated poor discriminatory performance, with an AUC of 0.519. Conclusions Among patients aged ≥ 75 years with ACS, the PRECISE-DAPT score demonstrated minimal ability to predict clinically relevant bleeding during DAPT. Accordingly, the score should not be used in isolation to guide DAPT duration in this population but rather integrated with individualized clinical judgment and geriatric-specific bleeding risk stratification tools
title: PRECISE-DAPT Score fails to predict clinically relevant bleeding in elderly patients with ACS

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with diabetes are at an increased risk of ischaemic events following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and may benefit from more intensive antiplatelet therapy. While prasugrel has been shown to inhibit platelets more effectively than ticagrelor in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) who are managed invasively, it is unclear whether diabetes affects this differential effect. Purpose To evaluate platelet reactivity in patients with and without diabetes treated with prasugrel or ticagrelor. Methods The ISAR-REACT 5 was a randomized controlled trial of prasugrel- versus ticagrelor-based strategy with a pre-specified analysis according to the presence or absence of diabetes mellitus. Eligible for the platelet function sub-study were patients who were P2Y12 inhibitor-naïve and underwent PCI in 2 study centres. Patients who received glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors were excluded. The platelet function test (PFT) was assessed by Multiplate analyzer within 24 hours after receipt of the loading dose (LD) of the assigned treatment. The primary endpoint was adenosine diphosphate (ADP)-induced platelet aggregation expressed in aggregation units [AU] x min. Secondary endpoints included ischemic events (composite of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) and bleeding events (BARC type 3-5) at 12 months. Results A total of 597 patients were included, of whom 129 with and 468 without diabetes. Patients with diabetes exhibited an overall higher cardiovascular risk profile compared with those without diabetes, characterized by a higher prevalence of hypertension and prior PCI, more frequent use of aspirin, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, and statins, but a lower likelihood of current smoking. The ADP-induced platelet aggregation at baseline did not differ between patients with and without diabetes (880 [25th; 75th percentiles, 565;1097] vs. 826 [608;1110] AU x min, respectively, p = 0.92). The presence of diabetes did not affect inhibition of platelet aggregation by prasugrel (102 [57.8;142] vs. 106 [58.8;183] AU x min for no diabetes, p = 0.34) by ticagrelor (130 [75.0;213] vs. 138 [78.5;207] AU x min for no diabetes, p = 0.61), p for interaction = 0.68. The 12-month rate of ischemic events was 14.9% among patients with diabetes and 13.1% among those without diabetes treated with prasugrel, and 13.1% and 14.2%, respectively, among patients treated with ticagrelor (p for interaction = 0.14). Bleeding rates among patients with and without diabetes were 13.4% and 5.5% with prasugrel, and 11.5% and 8.9% with ticagrelor, respectively (p for interaction = 0.31). Conclusions Among patients with ACS undergoing PCI, the presence of diabetes did not affect the inhibition of platelet aggregation achieved through randomised treatment with prasugrel or ticagrelor.Figure 1
title: Influence of diabetes on platelet inhibition in patients with acute coronary syndrome treated with prasugrel or ticagrelor

abstract: Abstract Background High platelet reactivity (HPR) is significantly associated with recurrent ischemic events in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). However, the combined prognostic implications of HPR to aspirin and to a P2Y12 inhibitor—and their differential impact on early vs. late clinical events after drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation—remain uncertain. Purpose To investigate the prognostic impact of HPR to aspirin and P2Y12 inhibitors on early and late clinical outcomes after DES implantation in patients with ACS. Methods From the nationwide PTRG-DES consortium, we analyzed 3,848 patients with ACS who were discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and underwent platelet function testing (VerifyNow®) for aspirin and clopidogrel. HPR on aspirin (HAPR) was defined as ≥ 414 ARU (aspirin reaction unit), and HPR on clopidogrel (HCPR) as ≥ 252 PRU (P2Y12 reaction unit), according to prior reports. Patients were stratified into four phenotypes: NAPR–NCPR (37.8%), NAPR–HCPR (8.8%), HAPR–NCPR (28.5%), and HAPR–HCPR (24.9%). Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE; composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, or stroke) and major bleeding (BARC type 3–5) were assessed through 1 year. Multivariable Cox regression and 90-day landmark analyses were performed. Results ARU and PRU showed a moderate correlation (r = 0.318, P &lt; 0.001). Higher PRU (per 10-unit increase) was independently associated with HAPR (adjusted OR [ORadj], 1.09; 95% CI, 1.08–1.10; P &lt; 0.001), and higher ARU (per 10-unit increase) was independently associated with HCPR (ORadj, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.04–1.07; P &lt; 0.001). At 1-year, HAPR-HCPR demonstrated an additive association with MACCE (log-rank P = 0.006), but not with major bleeding (log-rank P = 0.122). The HAPR–HCPR group had the highest MACCE risk compared with both the NAPR–NCPR (adjusted HR [HRadj], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.14–2.91; P = 0.013) and HAPR–NCPR (HRadj, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.03–2.70; P = 0.040). In landmark analysis, the prognostic impact of the HAPR–HCPR phenotype was more pronounced for thrombotic events within the first 90 days after PCI (HRadj of 2.44, 3.01, and 6.06 for MACCE, myocardial infarction, and stent thrombosis, respectively, vs. NAPR–NCPR), whereas these associations were substantially attenuated beyond 90 days. Conclusions In patients with ACS undergoing DES implantation, responsiveness to aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor demonstrated an additive association with thrombotic risk, particularly during the early post-PCI period. These findings support a time-dependent effect of dual platelet hyporesponsiveness on ischemic outcomes.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Prognostic implications of responsiveness to aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor after drug-eluting stent implantation in patients with acute coronary syndrome

abstract: Abstract Background High bleeding risk (HBR) patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face competing ischaemic and bleeding hazards during antiplatelet therapy. Both CYP2C19 phenotype and on-treatment platelet reactivity are used to estimate clopidogrel response; however, their relative prognostic value in patients fulfilling Academic Research Consortium (ARC-HBR) criteria remains uncertain. Methods Among 13,160 patients in the PTRG-DES registry, 2,939 fulfilled ARC-HBR criteria. The analytic cohort comprised 1,530 HBR patients with available VerifyNow P2Y12 reaction units (PRU), CYP2C19 phenotype, and complete covariate data. High platelet reactivity (HPR) was defined as PRU ≥252. The primary ischaemic endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as the composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or definite/probable stent thrombosis at 1 year. The primary analysis stratified patients into four groups by CYP2C19 phenotype (RM/NM vs. IM/PM) crossed with HPR status, comparing outcomes using Kaplan–Meier estimates and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for 21 pre-specified covariates. Results Mean age was 72.8±9.3 years; 54.6% were male. CYP2C19 distribution: RM/NM 37.5%, IM 47.0%, PM 15.6%; HPR was present in 48.1%. One-year MACCE rates differed significantly across four groups: 3.4% (RM/NM & Non-HPR), 9.4% (RM/NM & HPR), 6.2% (IM/PM & Non-HPR), and 7.6% (IM/PM & HPR) (log-rank p=0.021); major bleeding did not differ (p=0.655). On multivariable Cox regression, both RM/NM & HPR (HR 3.07, 95% CI 1.48–6.38; p=0.003) and IM/PM & HPR (HR 2.33, 95% CI 1.21–4.48; p=0.011) were independently associated with higher MACCE risk versus the reference group. In secondary models, HPR remained independently associated with MACCE (HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.07–2.52; p=0.024), whereas CYP2C19 phenotype categories were not. Conclusions In ARC-HBR patients treated with clopidogrel after PCI, on-treatment platelet reactivity provided more direct prognostic information for 1-year ischaemic events than CYP2C19 phenotype categorisation. Phenotype-guided risk stratification combining genotype with platelet function identifies clinically meaningful heterogeneity in ischaemic risk without an apparent increase in major bleeding.Clinical outcomes
title: Differential prognostic value of platelet reactivity and CYP2C19 phenotype in high bleeding risk patients undergoing PCI: insights from the PTRG-DES Registry

abstract: Abstract Background The safety of intravenous alteplase, the standard thrombolytic therapy for acute ischemic stroke, in Asian patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) prior to stroke remains uncertain, particularly with respect to bleeding and mortality risks. Purpose To evaluate bleeding and mortality risks following alteplase treatment for acute ischemic stroke among patients in Taiwan receiving DAPT prior to stroke compared with those receiving single or no antiplatelet therapy. Methods We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database (2011–2022). Adult patients hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke and treated with intravenous alteplase were identified. Antiplatelet exposure within 7 days before stroke was classified as DAPT, single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT), or no antiplatelet therapy. Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline characteristics and reduce potential confounding. The primary outcome was intracranial hemorrhage during the index hospitalization following stroke and alteplase treatment. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding and in-hospital mortality. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Results Among 9,264 alteplase-treated stroke patients, 280 (3.0%) had DAPT exposure prior to stroke, 2,239 (24.2%) had SAPT, and 6,745 (72.8%) had no antiplatelet therapy. In propensity score–matched analyses, DAPT prior to stroke was not associated with increased risks of intracranial hemorrhage (OR 0.69; 95% CI, 0.38–1.26), major bleeding (OR 0.75; 95% CI, 0.42–1.32), or in-hospital mortality (OR 1.06; 95% CI, 0.54–2.11) compared with no antiplatelet therapy. Risks were also similarly comparable between DAPT and SAPT groups. Findings were consistent across stratified analyses by age, sex, and stroke severity, and sensitivity analyses using multivariable adjustment and inverse probability of treatment weighting. Conclusions In this nationwide Taiwanese cohort of alteplase-treated stroke patients, DAPT exposure prior to stroke was not associated with increased bleeding or in-hospital mortality compared with single or no antiplatelet therapy. These findings suggest that bleeding and mortality outcomes following alteplase treatment may not differ by prior antiplatelet exposure and may inform clinical decision-making in Asian populations.
title: Bleeding and mortality risks after intravenous alteplase in stroke patients with prior dual antiplatelet therapy: a nationwide cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation (AFib) and coronary artery disease frequently coexist: around 10% of patients with AFib require percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Although randomized trials demonstrated direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and a P2Y12 inhibitor are the best antithrombotic combination in this setting, important gaps in knowledge remain, limiting certainty and generalizability of these findings. Purpose To conduct a patient-level meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with AFib undergoing PCI: 6 trials (10,634 patients) comparing 1.DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor (4,083), 2.vitamin K antagonist (VKA) plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT, 1,247), 3.VKA plus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT, 3,715), and 4.DOAC plus DAPT (1,589) were included (Figure 1). Methods The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke. The primary safety outcome was TIMI major or minor bleeding. Results At 1-year follow-up no differences were found in the risk of the primary efficacy outcome among the strategies. DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor reduced the risk of the primary safety outcome compared with VKA plus DAPT (HR, 0.59, 95%CI, 0.50 – 0.70) or DOAC plus DAPT (HR 0.73, 95%CI 0.57 – 0.95), while the risk was similar compared to VKA plus SAPT. Consistent findings were observed using BARC and ISTH bleeding definitions. The risk of intracranial bleeding was reduced with DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor compared with VKA plus DAPT. The risk of stent thrombosis did not differ among the antithrombotic strategies (Figure 2). Subgroup analyses showed consistent findings, except for enhanced reduction of bleeding in patients younger than 65 years old with DOAC plus P2Y12 (pinteraction: 0.042). When assessing the impact of aspirin cessation timing on the risk of MI and definite or probable ST, no significant interaction between randomized antithrombotic strategy and timing of aspirin cessation was observed (pinteraction MI = 0.59, definite or probable ST =0.084). Consistently, when the duration of aspirin therapy was analyzed as a continuous variable, the risk of MI (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.01) and definite or probable ST (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02) was not affected in patients randomized to DOAC or VKA plus P2Y12 inhibitor, while the risk of definite or probable ST was marginally reduced for each additional day of aspirin therapy in patients randomized to triple antithrombotic therapy (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.98-1.00). Conclusion In patients with AFib undergoing PCI, the risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke was similar regardless of whether patients received DOAC or VKA, or SAPT versus DAPT. Omission of a second antiplatelet agent reduced the risk of bleeding across all severity grades, including intracranial haemorrhage. These findings were consistent across subgroups assessed and independent of the duration of aspirin therapy.Figure 1Figure 2
