abstract: Abstract Background Currently, the diagnostic criteria for left bundle branch block (LBBB) are based on recommendations from the American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/Heart Rhythm Society (HRS) and the criteria proposed by Strauss. The left bundle branch is highly vulnerable to damage during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), increasing the risk of periprocedural complications. This study evaluated whether a new Time-to-Notch criterion combined with the ACC/AHA/HRS guidelines outperforms the Strauss criteria. The goal of this study is to validate the new criterion using a Chinese cohort of patients with new-onset LBBB following TAVR. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, the subjects were patients who underwent TAVR between September 2017 and March 2025. Postprocedural electrocardiograms (ECGs) were analyzed to identify patients with new-onset LBBB after TAVR. Among them, a subset of patients had preprocedural ECGs exhibiting QRS widening fulfilling the standard ECG criteria for LBBB. Given the significant increase in QRS width observed in their postprocedural ECGs compared to their preprocedural ECGs, we reclassified their preprocedural ECGs as pseudo-left bundle branch block (pseudo-LBBB). Their preprocedural ECGs were categorized into the presence or absence of pseudo-LBBB. We additionally selected patients with preprocedural ECGs that met the above criteria as the pseudo-LBBB group, and the remaining patients whose preprocedural ECGs lacked pseudo-LBBB were classified into the LBBB group. The ECGs were analyzed using the Time-to-Notch and Strauss criteria. Results The 351 ECGs obtained from 157 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR were analyzed. A total of 52 patients with new-onset LBBB after TAVR were included in the study. Of these, 7 patients with preprocedural ECGs meeting the LBBB criterion and significant postprocedural prolongation of the QRS duration were assigned to the pseudo-LBBB group, and the remaining 45 patients were assigned to the LBBB group. Two professionally trained ECG doctors independently analyzed the ECGs of both groups. Combining the Time-to-Notch and the ACC/AHA/HRS criteria had a sensitivity of 73.3% and specificity of 85.7%, while the Strauss criteria had a sensitivity of 91.1% and specificity of 71.4%. Conclusions Our results indicate that the combined Time-to-Notch ACC/AHA/HRS criteria, with a notch time &gt; 75 ms in lead I, demonstrate higher specificity compared to the Strauss criteria. Therefore, the Time-to-Notch criterion may offer significant value for diagnosing true LBBB in clinical practice.Figure
title: Validation of the 'Time to Notch' criterion in patients with left bundle branch block following transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Background PCSK9 inhibition with evolocumab reduced the risk of a first major cardiovascular event in high-risk patients with no prior MI or stroke in the VESALIUS-CV trial. Recurrent major cardiovascular events are common and important to patients, clinicians, and healthcare systems as they provide additional information regarding overall health status and total costs. Purpose To evaluate the effect of evolocumab on not only first, but also recurrent and total cardiovascular events. Methods The VESALIUS-CV trial randomized patients with qualifying atherosclerosis or high-risk diabetes, no prior MI or stroke, and an LDL-C ≥ 90mg/dL on optimized lipid-lowering therapy to evolocumab or placebo. The dual primary endpoints (PEP) were a composite of coronary heart disease death (CHD death), MI or ischemic stroke (3-P MACE) and 3-P MACE with the addition of ischemia-driven arterial revascularization (IDR)(4-P MACE).In this prespecified analysis, total dual PEP events (ie, first and subsequent) were analyzed using a negative binomial regression model. Results Among 12,257 patients followed for a median of 4.6 years, there were 779 first 3-P MACE and 146 subsequent events (19% more) for 925 total events. For 4-P MACE, there were 1654 first events and 1107 subsequent events (67% more) for 2,761 total events.Evolocumab reduced the risk of first 3-P MACE by 25% (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.65-0.86), recurrent events by 37% (incidence-rate ratio [IRR] 0.63, 95% CI 0.42-0.94) and total events by 27% (IRR 0.73, 95% CI 0.63-0.86; p&lt;0.001)(Figure). Likewise for 4-P MACE, evolocumab reduced the risk of first events by 19% (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.89), recurrent events by 25% (incidence-rate ratio [IRR] 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.91), and total events by 20% (IRR 0.80, 95% CI 0.71-0.90; p&lt;0.001)(Figure). For every 1000 patients treated for 5 years, evolocumab prevented 20 first 3-P MACE events, 5 subsequent events and 25 total events. Similarly, for every 1000 patients treated for 5 years, evolocumab prevented 31 first 4-P MACE events, 24 subsequent events and 55 total events. Results were consistent across key subgroups, including by qualifying atherosclerosis and high-risk diabetes without atherosclerosis, age, sex, and statin intensity. Conclusions The addition of the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab to statin therapy significantly reduced the rate of total MACE. For 4-P MACE, close to double the number of events were prevented with evolocumab vs placebo as compared with the analysis of only first events. These data provide further support for the role of intensive LDL-C lowering to reduce the first and subsequent MACE in patients with atherosclerosis or high-risk diabetes and no prior MI or stroke.

title: Reduction in total cardiovascular events with evolocumab in patients with no prior myocardial infarction or stroke: a pre-specified analysis of VESALIUS-CV

abstract: Abstract Background Hypercholesterolemia is a primary driver of cardiovascular disease, affecting approximately 39% of the global population. In developed nations, over 50 million individuals receive lipid-lowering treatments, yet many fail to reach targets. The advent of PCSK9-targeted therapies, including monoclonal antibodies (PCSK9i) and small interfering RNA (inclisiran), has enabled LDL cholesterol reductions of over 50% when added to standard care. However, the introduction of these potent injectables may inadvertently lead to reduced adherence to concomitant oral medications. This multicenter, retrospective study evaluates how changes in background therapy (BT) and statin/ezetimibe adherence influence the real-world LDL-c lowering efficacy of PCSK9-targeted treatments. Methods This regional observational registry included consecutive patients from nine referral centers initiated on PCSK9i or siRNA therapy according to clinical guidelines. The primary objective was to assess LDL-c reduction variability based on BT modifications and patient adherence. Adherence was quantified using the Adherence in Chronic Diseases Scale (ACDS), classifying patients into high (≥27), intermediate (21–26), or low (≤20) groups. Patients were also categorized by BT trajectory: those who reduced or stopped background drugs (BT-), those who maintained stable doses (BT=), and those who intensified oral therapy (BT+). Statistical analyses were performed using R software, with significance defined as p&lt;0.05 (two-tailed). Results The study cohort comprised 403 patients (70% male, mean age 65 ± 11 years) followed for a median of 15 months. Reported adherence was high in 38%, moderate in 43%, and low in 19% of the population. Secondary prevention was the indication for 71% of patients (65% previous myocardial infarction, 6% previous stroke/TIA), while 27% met the criteria for statin intolerance. While the average LDL-c reduction was -48% across the entire cohort, results differed widely according to adherence (Figure 1 depicts the waterfall plot of all patients). Patients who decreased or discontinued their background therapy (BT-) experienced a significantly lower LDL-c drop (-28%) compared to those with stable (BT=, -58%) or intensified (BT+, -65%) background regimens (p&lt;0.001, Figure 2). Conclusions The clinical effectiveness of PCSK9i and siRNA therapy is strictly dependent on the maintenance of background statin and ezetimibe adherence. Although highly adherent patients achieve LDL-c reductions consistent with phase III clinical trials, the perceived benefit of these advanced therapies is significantly diminished in the real world when oral background therapy is scaled back. These findings underscore the necessity of patient education to ensure that new injectable therapies supplement, rather than replace, established oral lipid-lowering regimens.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Perceived effectiveness of PCSK9i-SiRNA therapy and adherence to background statin therapy: real-world analysis of the DAMAGE registry

abstract: Abstract Background The 2025 ESC/EAS Focused Update on the Management of Dyslipidaemias recommends initiating combination therapy with a high-intensity statin plus ezetimibe during the index hospitalization for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in lipid-lowering therapy (LLT)-naive patients unlikely to achieve LDL-C goals with monotherapy. This Class IIa recommendation upgrades the previous IIb advice, targeting patients with high baseline LDL-C levels. Purpose This study aims to identify the proportion of ACS patients eligible for this upfront strategy specifically based on high admission LDL-C, and to evaluate its real-world efficacy in achieving the therapeutic target (&lt;55 mg/dL). Methods This is a prospective, observational, single-centre study of consecutive ACS patients from the CARTACS registry. We analyzed 923 patients admitted for ACS with confirmed coronary disease and Friedewald-calculated in-hospital LDL-C measurements between July 2023 and August 2025. "LDL-driven Predicted Monotherapy Failure" (LDL-PMF) was defined as an admission LDL-C &gt;110 mg/dL in LLT-naive patients, representing the threshold where the expected ≈50% reduction from high-intensity statin monotherapy fails to reach the &lt;55 mg/dL target. A binary logistic regression model was used to identify independent predictors of achieving the LDL-C target after 3 months of follow-up. Results A total of 444 patients (48%) were LLT-naive. Within this naive cohort, 211 (48%) met the criteria for LDL-PMF (LDL-C &gt;110 mg/dL). In this specific subgroup, 85 (40%) received statin monotherapy, 124 (59%) received combination therapy (high-intensity statin + ezetimibe) at discharge, and 2 (1%) received alternative LLT regimens. Patients on combination therapy achieved significantly lower follow-up LDL-C levels (47 [39–62] vs. 65 [55–86] mg/dL; p &lt; 0.001) and a higher rate of target achievement (65% vs. 27%; p &lt; 0.001) than those on monotherapy. In the multivariable analysis (Table), ezetimibe use was the strongest independent predictor of reaching the target (OR 6.17, 95% CI: 2.78–13.71; p &lt; 0.001). Conclusions Nearly half of LLT-naive ACS patients are at high risk of monotherapy failure based on their high admission LDL-C levels. Our findings strongly support the 2025 ESC/EAS Guidelines update: in patients with LDL-PMF, adding ezetimibe to high-intensity statins at discharge significantly increases the likelihood of achieving the &lt;55 mg/dL target compared to monotherapy.TableFigure
title: Upfront combination lipid-lowering therapy in statin-naive acute coronary syndrome patients with high admission LDL-C: real-world support for the 2025 ESC dyslipidaemias guidelines

abstract: Abstract Background Effective lipid management is a fundamental pillar of secondary prevention following acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Over the past decade, the field has evolved rapidly, with the introduction of novel lipid-lowering therapies, now widely available to the UK population. This therapeutic expansion has been accompanied by increasingly stringent low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol targets in European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines, reflecting the growing recognition of intensive lipid reduction in improving cardiovascular outcomes. However, despite clear and robust recommendations, adherence and achievement of guideline-directed LDL targets remain inconsistent. Purpose To compare trends in lipid testing and LDL-C target attainment over a 10-year period in patients admitted with ACS at a UK tertiary centre. Methods This retrospective observational comparative study included two ACS cohorts (2015/16, n = 284; 2025/26, n = 200). Within each cohort, patients were stratified into pre- and post-intervention groups to assess the impact of targeted quality improvement strategies. In 2015/16, the intervention involved the development of local lipid management guidelines for post-ACS follow-up and structured referral pathways to specialist lipid clinics. In 2025/26, guidelines were updated to incorporate newer agents (bempedoic acid and icosapent ethyl), pathology request forms were posted directly to patients to facilitate follow-up testing, and an Inclisiran service was established. We evaluated rates of inpatient lipid profiling, repeat lipid measurement at three months, and attainment of guideline-recommended LDL-C targets before and after intervention. Results The mean age for the 2015/16 cohort was 62.2 ± 12.3 years, compared to 67.1 ± 12.4 years in the 2025/26 cohort. Inpatient lipid testing improved from 80% to 93% in 2015/16 and from 77% to 96% in 2025/26 following intervention. Follow-up lipid testing increased from 31% to 37% in 2015/6 and reached 83% in the 2025/26 cohort. In 2015/16, 62% of patients were deemed to have met lipid targets then of LDL-C &lt;1.8 mmol/L. When compared with current lipid targets of LDL-C &lt;1.4mmol/L, only 26% met targets. In the 2025/26 cohort, 32% achieved LDL-C &lt;1.4mmol/L. 2% of eligible patients with hypertriglyceridemia received Icosapent Ethyl. Conclusion(s) Over the past decade, structured interventions have improved inpatient and follow-up lipid testing following ACS. While incorporation of newer therapies has modestly increased attainment of contemporary LDL-C targets, a substantial gap persists. Continued systematic, protocol-driven approaches are required to align clinical practice with evolving guideline standards.Lipid Management Poster
title: Lipid assessment and target attainment in acute coronary syndrome: a 10-year comparative review in a UK tertiary centre

abstract: Abstract Background Despite effective and innovative contemporary therapies, survivors of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remain at high risk for recurrent events and death. In Poland, two distinct nationwide pathways address this risk: KOS-Zawał, a multidisciplinary programme combining early cardiac rehabilitation, lifestyle counselling, and systematic follow-up, which has already demonstrated substantial efficacy, and the drug program B.101, a pharmacotherapy-centred pathway providing intensive combination lipid-lowering therapy with PCSK9 modulators for MI patients. Robust head-to-head data comparing these two effective strategies are lacking. Purpose To assess whether participation in the B.101 drug program favourably affects endpoints in post-MI patients compared to those participating in the KOS-Zawał program and not included in the drug program. Methods Patients who participated in the KOS-Zawał program between 2021-2024 and experienced an AMI during their program care period (within 30 days) were included. Similarly, patients who began the B.101 program under the "very high cardiovascular risk" branch between 2021–2024 were selected. Those who appeared in both investigated groups simultaneously were excluded from the defined population. Both groups were matched using propensity score matching (PSM) that was conducted in a 4:1 ratio (KOS-Zawał:B.101). The groups were compared in terms of endpoints: all-cause mortality, and the composite of death or AMI occurrence. Results The final dataset included 1,760 patients (n=352 in the B.101 group and n=1,408 in the KOS-Zawał group), comprising 1,200 men (68.2%) and 560 women, with a mean age of 60.6 years. Diabetes was diagnosed in 28% of patients, obesity in 6.5%, chronic kidney disease in 5.7%, and stroke or TIA in 4%. Based on logistic regression analysis over a follow-up of 2 years, there were no statistically significant differences for all-cause mortality or the composite endpoint (KOS-Zawał vs. B.101 program; OR=1.83, p=0.287, and OR=1.28, p=0.506). Based on the Cox proportional hazards model with a longer follow-up of 4.4 years, the KOS-Zawał comprehensive program, compared to the treatment of patients with PCSK9 modulators in the B101 program, was associated with a significantly higher risk of death (HR=3.28; 95%CI: 1.52–7.07) (Figure 1A) and the composite of death or recurrent acute myocardial infarction (HR=1.70; 95%CI: 1.10–2.63) (Figure 1B). Conclusions The B101 drug program, where patients are treated with intensive combination LLT including statins, ezetimibe, and PCSK9 inhibitors or inclisiran, is associated with a significant 70% lower risk of all-cause mortality and a 41% lower risk of death or recurrent AMI compared to patients included in the coordinated comprehensive post-MI care program. These findings suggest that, for optimal healthcare outcomes, the B.101 drug program should be made available to all patients enrolled in KOS-Zawał.Figure
title: Coordinated post-myocardial infarction care versus the PCSK9 modulator drug program: a comparative outcomes study

abstract: Abstract Background Intensive LDL-cholesterol lowering with the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab reduces the risk of major adverse cardiovascular (CV) events, but a detailed characterization of the effects on myocardial infarction (MI) in patients at high CV risk but without a prior MI or stroke has not been performed. Purpose To characterize the effect of evolocumab on the incidence of a first MI by type, ECG phenotype, and infarct size, in the VESALIUS-CV trial. Methods VESALIUS-CV randomized 12,257 patients with qualifying atherosclerosis or high-risk diabetes, without a prior MI or stroke, and an LDL-C ≥ 90 mg/dL to evolocumab or placebo on background optimized lipid-lowering therapy. MI was adjudicated and classified according to the Universal Definition (UDMI Types 1–5), ECG phenotype (STEMI/NSTEMI) and infarct size (peak troponin [Tn]) by a blinded clinical events committee. This prespecified analysis evaluated the first MI of a given type in the intention-to-treat population with stratified Cox proportional hazards models in the overall study population and in key subgroups. Results During a median follow-up of 4.6 years (interquartile range, 4.0-5.2), 378 patients experienced MI (3.1%). Type 1 MI was the predominant mechanism (79% of all MIs), followed by Type 2 MI (12%). NSTEMI (69%) was more frequent than STEMI (26%) and unknown ECG phenotype (6%). Patients with MI were more likely to have met inclusion for qualifying coronary disease and to have had a prior coronary revascularization and less likely to be on a high-intensity lipid regimen at baseline. Evolocumab significantly reduced the risk of any MI by 36% compared with placebo (149 [5-Yr Kaplan-Meier, 2.7%] vs 229 [5-Yr Kaplan-Meier, 4.1%]; HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.52–0.79; p&lt;0.0001) (Fig 1). The cumulative incidence curves separated early such that the risk of MI was already significantly lower by 6 months (p&lt;0.01), and the benefit persisted over time. Risk reductions were consistent across UDMI type (Type 1: HR 0.61, 0.48–0.77; Type 2: HR 0.70, 0.39-1.26), ECG phenotype (NSTEMI: HR 0.63, 0.49–0.81; STEMI: HR 0.64, 0.43–0.96), and MI size (Tn≥10x ULN: HR 0.60, 0.46–0.78; Tn&lt;10x ULN: HR 0.77, 0.50–1.20). Results were consistent for the endpoint of first MI across the key subgroups defined according to the baseline variables of LDL-C quartile, statin intensity, presence of diabetes, and presence of qualifying atherosclerosis. Conclusions Among patients without a history of a prior MI or stroke, evolocumab reduced the incidence of a first MI, with a robust early benefit that was maintained over time. These favourable results were observed across subtypes of MI, including for spontaneous Type 1 events, large MIs and both NSTEMI and STEMI. These findings strongly support intensive LDL-C lowering with evolocumab for prevention of a first MI in high-risk patients.Abstract Figure

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial; 378 patients experienced MI (3.1%) during a median follow-up of 4.6 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Congress abstract; subgroup estimates for type 2 MI have wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified VESALIUS-CV analysis of evolocumab and first myocardial infarction, by MI type and ECG phenotype.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Evolocumab significantly reduced the risk of any MI by 36% compared with placebo (149 [5-Yr Kaplan-Meier, 2.7%] vs 229 [5-Yr Kaplan-Meier, 4.1%]; HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.52-0.79; p<0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Characterises the MI phenotypes prevented by intensive LDL-cholesterol lowering, informing secondary prevention after MI.

title: Evolocumab and risk of a first myocardial infarction: a prespecified analysis of the VESALIUS-CV trial

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) and prior myocardial infarction are at extremely high cardiovascular risk. Despite maximally tolerated statin therapy, many fail to achieve guideline-recommended LDL-C targets. Inclisiran, a small interfering RNA targeting PCSK9, provides potent, durable LDL-C reduction and may also lower atherogenic lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], potentially mitigating residual cardiovascular risk. Objectives To assess the long-term efficacy and safety of inclisiran added to statin therapy in reducing LDL-C and Lp(a) in high-risk FH patients over two years. Methods In this prospective, multicenter study, 172 adults (mean age 62 ± 10 years; 68% male) with FH diagnosed ≥5 years, prior myocardial infarction, and on stable statin therapy were enrolled. Inclisiran 300 mg was administered subcutaneously at baseline, 3 months, and every 6 months thereafter for 24 months. Primary endpoints were percent change in LDL-C and Lp(a). Safety endpoints included hepatic enzyme and creatine kinase elevations, adverse events, and the incidence of acute cardiovascular events. Results Inclisiran plus statin therapy resulted in a mean LDL-C reduction of 51% (baseline 4.8 ± 0.5 → 2.3 ± 0.4 mmol/L, p&lt;0.001) and Lp(a) reduction of 27% (baseline 70 ± 15 → 51 ± 12 mg/dL, p&lt;0.001). At 24 months, 78% of patients achieved LDL-C &lt;1.8 mmol/L and 42% reached &lt;1.4 mmol/L. No patient experienced an acute cardiovascular event during follow-up. The regimen was well tolerated; mild transient liver enzyme elevations occurred in 6% of patients, CK remained stable, and no discontinuations due to adverse events were reported. Conclusions In high-risk patients with familial hypercholesterolemia and prior myocardial infarction, inclisiran added to statin therapy provides robust, durable LDL-C and clinically meaningful Lp(a) reductions. The absence of acute cardiovascular events over two years underscores the potential of mechanism-based combination therapy to reduce residual atherogenic risk. These findings support early implementation of inclisiran in statin-treated FH patients inadequately controlled with conventional therapy, highlighting its clinical and prognostic relevance.
title: Inclisiran in combination with statin therapy achieves profound LDL-C and lipoprotein(a) reduction without acute cardiovascular events in high-risk patients with familial hypercholesterolemia

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Bempedoic acid (BA), alone or combined with ezetimibe (E), is an oral lipid-lowering therapy option for patients who do not achieve LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) targets or have limited statin tolerance. Real-world evidence on its efficacy across different background lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) regimens remains limited. Purpose BEMPENET is an Italian multicenter observational registry designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BA-based therapeutic strategies in routine clinical practice. This analysis assessed LDL-C percentage reduction at first follow-up according to concomitant LLT. Methods Consecutive patients initiating BA alone or in combination with E according to standard clinical practice were enrolled in the registry. The primary endpoint was median percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to follow-up. Results A total of 283 patients initiated a BA-based strategy (54.8% male, mean age 66.6±10.4 years) and were followed for a median time of 6.5 months. Of these patients, 68.2% had hypertension, 22.6% had type 2 diabetes mellitus, 32.5% had a previous acute coronary syndrome, 42% had chronic coronary syndrome, and 20.8% had peripheral atherosclerotic artery disease. Among enrolled patients, 132 started BA+E and 108 BA alone, on top of stable background LLT. Median LDL-C reduction was significantly higher in patients starting BA+E (34.5%, IQR 13.2; 47.1), compared to those on BA alone (20.1%, IQR 0.0; 39.4) (p=0.003). When stratifying by cardiovascular (CV) risk class, 85.4% of patients were at high or very high risk; in this cohort, BA+E achieved a significantly higher LDL-C reduction compared to BA alone (31.5% [IQR 8.7; 47.2] vs 19.6% [IQR 0; 38.6]; p=0.029). Among patients starting BA+E, LDL-C reduction was 30.8% (IQR 8.7; 43.5) in patients taking statins (n=68), compared to 40.4% (IQR 20.4; 49.5) in patients who did not (n=64). Among patients starting BA alone, LDL-C reduction was 18.3% (IQR -3.3; 38.3) in patients taking statins (n=69), compared to 32.3% (IQR 11.4; 44.8) in patients who did not (n=39). Additional 43 patients started BA+E (n=33) or BA (n=10) alone, concomitantly adding anti-Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type-9 (PCSK9) therapy on top of stable background LLT. In this cohort, median LDL-C reduction was 58.7% (IQR 49; 69.3). Adherence was high in 95.1% of patients, partial in 1.4%, and poor in 3.5%. Conclusion(s) In this real-world experience, BA effectively reduced LDL-C, especially in patients not taking background statins and when associated with E and anti-PCSK9 therapy.
title: Real-world efficacy of bempedoic acid: early insights from the BEMPENET Italian Registry

abstract: Abstract Background Left bundle branch block (LBBB) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), altering ventricular activation and challenging ECG interpretation. This study sought to establish novel electrocardiographic criteria to define the electrical position of the heart (EPH) before and after LBBB post-TAVR. Methods In this single-center, retrospective study, 439 TAVR patients (2018–2023) were screened; 74 developed new LBBB. Patients with pre- and post-TAVR ECGs, without pacemaker, infiltrative disease, or baseline conduction disorders, were included. ECGs were analyzed for QRS duration, electrical axes (AQRS, AT), and patterns of concordance/discordance in leads II/III and aVL/aVF. EPH was categorized as intermediate (IEP), horizontal (HEP), or vertical (VEP) by AQRS. Morphology in leads I, aVL, V5, and V6 was also assessed. Results Among 74 patients with LBBB, 36 (48.6%) had IEP, 32 (43.2%) HEP, and 6 (8.1%) VEP. In patients without LBBB, AQRS averaged 50°±15° in IEP and –10°±20° in HEP (p&lt;0.0001). With LBBB, AQRS shifted to –20°±25° in IEP and –60°±30° in HEP (p&lt;0.0001). Positive concordance in II/III and aVL/aVF identified IEP, whereas positive discordance indicated HEP. In LBBB, negative concordance in II/III with positive discordance in aVL/aVF defined HEP, while positive discordance in II/III with positive concordance in aVL/aVF characterized IEP. Conclusion Novel ECG criteria enable reliable classification of cardiac electrical position in both baseline and post-TAVR LBBB. Leftward axis deviation with LBBB often reflects intrinsic EPH rather than new pathology, enhancing interpretation and clinical decision-making.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Heart position by ECG: baseline and post-TAVR LBBB

abstract: Abstract Background Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) yields high cardiovascular morbidity, resulting in overwhelming healthcare costs. Purpose We investigated whether the combined administration of the cardioprotective agent Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1-RA) liraglutide and Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor (SGLT2i) empagliflozin reduces the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events and results in improved economic outcomes. Methods We prospectively enrolled (n=336) consecutive participants with T2DM, of which (n=94) received Insulin, (n=72) GLP1-RA, (n=82) SGLT2i and (n=78) their combination (GLP1-RA+SGLT2i). We obtained a comprehensive medical history and performed a clinical examination. Participants were strictly followed-up for six years. We recorded the occurrence of the adverse events the composite outcome of the non-fatal cardiac events: hospitalization for heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization For cost effectiveness analysis of hospitalization for non fatal CV events we calculated the cost of treatment and the cost of hospitalization Results The median follow-up period was 69 [60 – 75] months, 252/336(75%) were males and were 60±10 years old. 134/336 (40%) had Coronary Artery Disease (CAD), 225/336 (67%) hypertension and 336/336(100%) hyperlipidemia. At follow-up, n=92 non-fatal events were documented, of which (n=22) myocardial infarctions, (n=23) heart failure hospitalizations, (n=7) strokes and (n=39) coronary revascularizations. Individuals under the combination displayed the lowest incidence of the composite outcome, heart failure hospitalization and revascularization (p&lt;0.05) (Table). The combination group displayed the lowest risk for developing the composite outcome of non-fatal cardiovascular events after adjusting for age, sex, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking and CAD (Insulin vs Combination group: Hazard ration (HR)=4.36, 95%CI:2.04-9.33, p&lt;0.001;GLP1-RA vs Combination group: HR=2.45, 95%CI: 1.06-5.64, p=0.035; SGLT2i vs Combination group: HR=3.07, 95%CI: 1.38-6.81, p=0.006). The cost estimation of hospitalization for non-fatal CV events revealed that participants in the combination group displayed the lowest total Cost per patient per month through 80 months (Insulin: 562€, 95%CI: 344-781; GLP1-RA: 216€, 95%CI:36-396; SGLT2i:253€, 95%CI: 72-434; Combination:133 €, 95%CI: 0-266). Conclusion The combined administration of liraglutide and empagliflozin led to lower risk for non-fatal cardiovascular events in conjunction with better economic outcomes.TABLEGRAPH
title: Cardiovascular and economic outcomes of combined liraglutide and empagliflozin therapy in type 2 diabetes: a 6-year study

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction In SURPASS-CVOT, tirzepatide (TZP) was non-inferior to dulaglutide (dula) in reducing the first occurrence of 3-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-3) including myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death, while superior in reducing MACE-5 (additionally including hospitalization for unstable angina and coronary revascularization) among patients with type 2 diabetes and established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This pre-specified analysis assessed total (first and recurrent) cardiovascular events for MACE-5 and MACE-3. Methods SURPASS-CVOT was an active-comparator-controlled, double-blind, trial in which patients with type 2 diabetes and established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive a weekly TZP up to 15 mg or dula 1.5 mg, an agent previously shown to reduce the incidence of cardiovascular events versus placebo. The rate ratio was estimated from the semi-parametric proportional rates model with treatment and SGLT-2i use at baseline as fixed effects. Results A total of 13,165 patients (29% female, mean age [SD]: 64.1 [8.8] yrs, BMI: 32.6kg/m2 [5.5], HbA1c: 8.4% [0.9]) were included in the modified intent to treat population (TZP 6586, dula 6579). CV history included coronary artery disease (65.0%), myocardial infarction (47.2%), stroke (19.2%), peripheral artery disease (25.3%), heart failure (20.3%), and coronary revascularization (57.2%). For MACE-5, TZP treatment was associated with a significantly lower total event burden, with 1,489 total events (1,112 first and 377 recurrent) compared with 1,696 total events in the dula group (1,240 first and 456 recurrent), rate ratio 0.87 (95% CI 0.80–0.95; p=0.002) Figure. For MACE-3, patients treated with TZP experienced fewer total events than those receiving dula, with 925 total events (801 first and 124 recurrent) versus 1,005 total events (862 first and 143 recurrent), respectively, rate ratio 0.91 (95% CI 0.82–1.01; p=0.070) Table. Fewer patients in the TZP group experienced multiple expanded MACE events compared with dula, with 835 patients experiencing a single event and 277 experiencing two or more events, versus 921 patients with a single event and 319 with two or more events in the dula group. Conclusions In patients with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease, TZP reduced the total burden of cardiovascular events compared with dula, with consistent benefits observed for first and recurrent MACE-5.
title: First plus recurrent major adverse cardiovascular events with tirzepatide in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk from SURPASS CVOT

abstract: Abstract Background A substantial number of patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) experience adverse events after TAVI, with health care expenditure. Purpose We aimed to investigate cardiac remodeling and long-term outcomes in diabetic patients with severe AS and extra-valvular cardiac damage (EVCD) undergoing TAVI treated with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) versus other glucose-lowering strategies (no-SGLT2i users). Methods Multicenter international registry of consecutive diabetic patients with severe AS, LVEF&lt;50%, and EVCD undergoing TAVI. Based on glucose-lowering therapy at hospital discharge, patients were stratified in SGLT2i versus no-SGLT2i users. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure (HF)-hospitalization (major adverse cardiovascular events, MACE) at 2-year follow-up. Secondary outcomes included all-cause death, cardiovascular death, and HF hospitalization. Results The study population included 311 patients, among which 24% were SGLT2i users. Within 1-year after TAVI, SGLT2i users experienced a higher rate of LV recovery (p=0.032), especially those with baseline LVEF£30% (p=0.026), despite the lower baseline LVEF. Patients not treated with SGLT2i were more likely to progress to a worse EVCD stage over time (p=0.018). At 2-year follow-up, SGLT2i use was associated with a lower rate of MACE, all-cause death, and HF hospitalization (p&lt;0.01 for all). After adjusting for confounding factors, the use of SGLT2i emerged as an independent predictor of reduced MACE (HR=0.45; 95%CI 0.17-0.75; p=0.007), all-cause death (HR=0.51; 95%CI 0.25-0.98; p=0.042) and HF-hospitalization (HR=0.40; 95%CI 0.27-0.62; p=0.004). Conclusions In diabetic patients with severe AS, LVEF&lt;50%, and EVCD undergoing TAVI, the use of SGLT2i was associated with a more favorable cardiac remodeling and a reduced risk of MACE at 2-year follow-up.Summary of the main findings of the study.
title: SGLT2-inhibitors in diabetic patients with severe aortic stenosis and extra-valvular cardiac damage undergoing TAVI

abstract: Abstract Background Although SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and metformin are first-line treatments for T2DM, evidence comparing their cardiovascular outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains limited. Purpose This study aimed to compare the major clinical outcomes after acute myocardial infarction between diabetic patients treated with SGLT2i and those treated with metformin. Methods Data were derived from a multicenter retrospective study across 82 hospitals in China. We enrolled patients with a confirmed diagnosis of T2DM who were hospitalized for AMI between January 2010 and March 2024, and were treated with either SGLT2i or metformin. Patients who received both medications, had severe renal disease, malignancy, severe heart failure (Killip class≥3), or were under 18 years of age were excluded. The main outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), including cardiac death, cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction, and revascularization, and net adverse clinical events (NACE), which is a composite of all-cause death, cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction, revascularization, and bleeding events. Secondary outcomes included individual components of MACCE and NACE. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for differences in clinical characteristics between the two groups. Multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed before and after weighting to evaluate the prognostic impact of different hypoglycemic agents. Results The final study population comprised 12,950 patients, of whom 7,641 were treated with metformin (Table 1). The metformin group had a higher proportion of female patients (37.7% vs. 32.1%), a slightly older mean age (64.53 ± 15.27 vs. 63.14 ± 11.90 years), and higher prevalences of cerebrovascular comorbidity. Before adjustment, the SGLT2i group had significantly lower rates of one-year MACCE and NACE than the metformin group. All baseline variables achieved balance after IPTW (all SMD &lt; 0.1). Following adjustment, compared with the metformin group, the SGLT2i group had a reduced risk of one-year MACCE (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72–0.85, p &lt; 0.001) and NACE (aHR 0.81, 95% CI 0.75–0.87, p &lt; 0.001). However, there was no significant difference in bleeding risk between the two hypoglycemic agents (p &gt; 0.05, Table 2). Conclusions In patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and acute myocardial infarction, the use of SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) within a broader glucose-lowering regimen was associated with a lower risk of one-year MACCE and NACE, without a higher bleeding risk, when compared with the use of metformin. These findings suggest that SGLT2i may offer superior cardiovascular and survival benefits in this clinical setting.
title: Prognostic outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors versus metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes and acute myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Melatonin is commonly used for the treatment of insomnia. It is considered harmless despite a lack of robust safety studies. Recent data raises concern over a potential risk of heart failure (HF) associated with long-term use(1). We sought to assess the cardiovascular safety associated with melatonin treatment using the nationwide Danish registries. Methods We identified all new users of melatonin from 2015-2023 aged &gt;18 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease (CVD) at baseline. They were matched in a 1:1 ratio on age, date, and sex with non-user controls without prevalent CVD. Time zero was the date of first melatonin prescription and the corresponding matched date for controls. The outcomes were HF, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), arrythmia, and ischemic stroke (IS). Cause-specific Cox regression models accounting for the competing risk of death adjusted for comorbidities (including diabetes, mental illness) and concomitant pharmacotherapy (including antidepressants, opioids) were used to calculate 5-year standardized risks, risk differences, and risk ratios (sRR) for melatonin vs. controls overall and in subgroups. In addition, we performed active comparator (zopiclone and zolpidem, Z-drugs) and landmark cumulative daily defined dose (cDDD) sensitivity analyses. Importantly, in Denmark, melatonin and other hypnotics require a prescription and are not sold over the counter. Results In the main analyses, 273,167 new users of melatonin were matched with the same number of controls (median age 45 years, 62% female). Melatonin users had more comorbidities, including cancer (4.7% vs. 3.0%) and COPD (1.3% vs. 0.8%), and took more antidepressants (28.4% vs. 6.9%), opioids (13.5% vs. 5.6%), and benzodiazepines (8.1% vs 1.8%) at baseline. They also had a higher prevalence of risk factors for CVD (diabetes, 5.2% vs. 4.1%; hypertension, 8.6% vs. 7.6%). Melatonin use was not associated with an increased 5-year risk of HF (0.56% vs. 0.55%, sRR 1.01 [0.93-1.10]), ACS (0.55% vs. 0.56%, sRR 0.98 [0.89-1.06]), or IS (1.00% vs. 0.99%, sRR 1.01 [0.94-1.07]), Figure 1. However, melatonin users had a significantly higher 5-year risk of arrythmia compared with controls (0.80% vs. 0.71%, sRR 1.14 [1.06-1.22]). Subgroup analyses showed similar risks across subgroups, except for a slightly higher risk of arrythmia in those aged &gt;45 vs. &lt;45 years, Figure 2. Melatonin users had lower or similar 5-year risks of HF (sRR 0.50), ACS (sRR 0.88), arrythmia (sRR 0.66), IS (sRR 1.03) compared to Z-drug users. In the 1-year landmark analysis, a cDDD of &gt;180 vs. 0 was not associated with HF (sRR 1.08), ACS (sRR 0.97), arrytmia (sRR 1.03), or IS (sRR 1.07). Conclusion Melatonin was not associated with increased long-term risks of ACS, HF, and IS. However, melatonin may be associated with slightly higher long-term risks of arrythmia. Further research is needed to elucidate whether this signal is a genuine safety concern or is driven by residual confounding.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Cardiovascular safety of melatonin: insights from nationwide Danish registries

abstract: Abstract Background Chemotherapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is a major limitation of cardiotoxic cancer therapies. Although global longitudinal strain (GLS) allows early detection of myocardial injury, preventive strategies remain scarce. Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) may offer cardioprotection, but current evidence is limited. Purpose To evaluate the efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan in preventing chemotherapy-related cardiac dysfunction, given the clinical need for early cardioprotection. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating sacubitril/valsartan versus control in patients undergoing chemotherapy. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs were computed for binary and continuous outcomes. Results Four RCTs comprising 412 participants were included; 42.7% received ARNI therapy, with follow-up ranging from 6 to 18 months. Compared with control, ARNI significantly preserved left ventricular systolic function (MD 1.47%, 95% CI 0.59 to 2.34; Figure 1A) and attenuated GLS deterioration (MD -0.93%, 95% CI -1.49 to -0.38; Figure 1B). However, ARNI did not significantly reduce the incidence of CTRCD (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.08-1.97) or all-cause mortality (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.08-5.0). ARNI increased the risk of hypotension but had no significant effects on NT-proBNP or dyspnea. Conclusions ARNI therapy improves GLS and LVEF during chemotherapy but has not yet demonstrated reductions in CTRCD or mortality. Hypotension remains a key safety consideration.Graphical AbstractFigure 1
title: Sacubitril/valsartan and prevention of chemotherapy-induced cardiac dysfunction: meta-analysis of randomized trials

abstract: Abstract Background Sequential administration of anthracyclines and HER2-targeted agents represents a highly effective therapeutic strategy in breast cancer but is frequently complicated by cumulative cardiotoxicity, limiting treatment durability and long-term cardiovascular outcomes. Inflammation-driven myocardial injury and multi-organ stress responses are increasingly recognised as central mechanisms in cancer therapy–related cardiac dysfunction. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) exert pleiotropic cardiovascular and anti-inflammatory effects independent of glucose lowering, yet their role in preventing chemotherapy-induced cardiac injury in non-diabetic settings remains largely unexplored. Methods Non-diabetic murine models were exposed to sequential doxorubicin followed by trastuzumab over a 10-day protocol. Animals were randomised to receive the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide or vehicle. Cardiac function was serially assessed by echocardiography, including left ventricular ejection fraction and myocardial strain parameters. Histopathological analyses evaluated myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Immunohistochemical profiling was performed in cardiac, hepatic, and renal tissues. Circulating biomarkers of myocardial injury and systemic inflammation, including troponins, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, CCL12, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, were quantified. Results Sequential anthracycline and HER2 blockade induced marked cardiac dysfunction, characterised by significant impairment of systolic performance and myocardial deformation, accompanied by increased myocardial fibrosis, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and elevated circulating markers of cardiac injury and inflammation. Semaglutide administration significantly preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and strain parameters and substantially attenuated structural myocardial remodelling. These functional benefits were paralleled by a robust reduction in circulating troponins and pro-inflammatory cytokines. In addition, semaglutide mitigated inflammatory signalling across cardiac, hepatic, and renal tissues, indicating a broader cardio-renal protective profile. Conclusions GLP-1 receptor agonism confers significant protection against chemotherapy-induced cardiac dysfunction and systemic inflammatory injury in non-diabetic preclinical models exposed to anthracycline and HER2-targeted therapy. These findings support a novel, glucose-independent role for GLP-1RAs in cardio-oncology, with potential implications for integrated strategies aimed at preserving cardiovascular and multi-organ health during intensive anticancer treatment. Further translational studies are warranted to define their clinical relevance in patients at high risk of cancer therapy–related cardiac dysfunction.
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist reduces anthracycline– and trastuzumab–induced cardiac dysfunction and systemic hs-CRP, IL-1β and IL-6 in non-diabetic preclinical models

abstract: Abstract Background Cancer therapy-related cardiotoxicity (CTRCD) remains a major complication of breast cancer treatment. Circulating microRNAs (miRs) regulate pathways involved in myocardial injury, fibrosis, and remodeling and may serve as early biomarkers of cardiotoxicity. However, longitudinal data linking miR alterations to CTRCD are limited. Purpose To investigate longitudinal changes in circulating miRs during cancer therapy and identify miRs differentially modulated in patients who develop cardiotoxicity. Methods We prospectively enrolled women with breast cancer undergoing cancer therapy. Circulating miRs were quantified at baseline and after completion of therapy. Cardiotoxicity was defined according to standard echocardiographic criteria. Fold-change analysis assessed overall therapy-induced modulation. Repeated-measures analysis evaluated interaction between time and cardiotoxicity status to identify miRs with differential longitudinal trajectories. Results A total of 47 patients with breast cancer were included, of whom 14 (29.8%) developed CTRCD. Cancer therapy induced alterations in several circulating miRs, including significant downregulation of miR-30c-5p (-4.07-fold, p&lt;0.001), miR-31-5p (-2.98-fold, p&lt;0.001), miR-423-3p (-1.99-fold, p&lt;0.001), miR-124-3p (-1.89-fold, p=0.005), and miR-29b-3p (-1.52-fold, p=0.03), as well as upregulation of miR-23a-3p (2.27-fold, p=0.001) and miR-144-3p (2.46-fold, p=0.01). In repeated-measures interaction analysis, three miRs demonstrated cardiotoxicity-specific longitudinal patterns. miR-124-3p showed a relative increase in patients who developed CTRCD compared with a decrease in those without cardiotoxicity (Figure 1, Panel A). miR-29b-3p exhibited a more pronounced downregulation in the cardiotoxicity group (Figure 1, Panel B). In contrast, miR-423-3p displayed a considerable increase in patients with CTRCD compared with non-cardiotoxic patients (Figure 1, Panel C). Conclusions Cancer therapy induces significant alterations in circulating microRNA profiles. Importantly, miR-124-3p, miR-29b-3p, and miR-423-3p demonstrate cardiotoxicity-specific longitudinal modulation, identifying a potential early molecular signature of CTRCD. These findings support further evaluation of circulating miRs as dynamic biomarkers for early detection and risk stratification of cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction.Figure 1
title: Dynamic circulating microRNA signatures associated with cancer therapy-related cardiotoxicity in breast cancer patients

abstract: Abstract Background Patients’ medication beliefs influence medication adherence. The “Beliefs about Medicine Questionnaire Specific” (BMQ-S) identifies four attitudinal profiles (accepting, ambivalent, indifferent, sceptical), based on the balance between perceived necessity of treatment against concerns about medication. Whether clinical characteristics are associated with these profiles among patients hospitalised for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or elective coronary revascularisation remains unclear. Purpose To investigate the prevalence of medication belief profiles in patients hospitalised for ACS or elective coronary revascularisation and to assess their association with clinical characteristics. Methods We enrolled patients from 26 Dutch medical centres during hospitalisation for ACS or elective coronary revascularisation (percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass graft). Clinical data were collected from electronic health records. During admission, patients received an email survey on demographics, BMQ-S with an additional item on side-effects, and prior medication adherence (1-100 visual analogue scale). Surveys completed ≤ 14 days after discharge were included. Based on BMQ-S necessity and concern scores, patients were classified into beliefs profiles (accepting, ambivalent, indifferent, or sceptical) using the scale midpoint. Multinomial regression was performed to assess associations between characteristics and these profiles, with ´accepting´ as reference category. Results Between June 2024 and February 2026, 1013 patients (24% women; median age 68 years) completed the survey (response rate 50%) a median of 3 days after discharge (IQR 1-7). Based on BMQ-S scores, 59% of patients were accepting, 22% ambivalent, 14% indifferent, and 6% sceptical. Self-reported medication adherence was high across all profiles. High-concern patients (ambivalent or sceptical) more often reported that their medication causes side effects than accepting and indifferent patients. Older age was associated with lower odds of being sceptical than accepting (OR 0.97 per year; [0.94-1.00]). Non-smokers, patients with prior medication use, or a history of cardiovascular disease (CVD) were less likely to be indifferent than accepting (OR 0.47 [0.25-0.90], 0.35 [0.22-0.54], and 0.63 [0.42-0.93], respectively). No significant associations were observed between attitudinal profiles and sex or reason for admission. Conclusions Nearly 30% of patients report ambivalent or sceptical medication beliefs during or shortly after hospitalisation for ACS or elective coronary revascularisation. These high-concern profiles showed limited associations with measured clinical characteristics. Non-smokers, patients with a history of CVD, or those who used medication prior to admission were more likely to be accepting. Long-term follow-up is needed to assess how medication beliefs evolve over time.Table 1.Characteristics
title: More than one in four patients hospitalised for coronary artery disease report high medication concerns: findings from a multicentre observational cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal long-term medication adherence is a crucial part of secondary prevention in patients after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to achieve guideline-based treatment goals. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) provides an objective method of assessing adherence to prescribed medications. Although patients generally respond positively to TDM when it is delivered within a supportive and autonomy-respecting clinician–patient relationship, the extent of non-adherence that persists is underexplored. Purpose To quantify adherence to prescribed cardiovascular medications using TDM 12 months after PCI. Methods A sub-sample of 500 patients from the prospective multicentre cohort CONCARDPCI were invited to undergo TDM of a range of cardiovascular medications 12 months after hospital discharge. The panel comprised 21 antihypertensive agents or metabolites, 3 direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), and 2 statins. Serum samples were analysed utilizing ultra-high performance liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry. Sampling was done at the time of inclusion, permitting spontaneous sampling irrespective of timing of drug intake. Medication adherence was dichotomized as either full or suboptimal adherence. Results from the TDM analyses were compared to self-reported medication adherence utilizing the Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5). To assess representativeness of the sample, it was compared with the full CONCARDPCI data (n=1970) on selected background variables (e.g. age, sex, polypharmacy, number of comorbidities, and education). Results In all, 167 patients consented to TDM and provided spontaneous blood samples and an updated medication list. The TDM sample was similar to the CONCARDPCI cohort except for age (median age 65.5 vs 67.2 for CONCARDPCI and TDM sample respectively, p=0.043). The number of concomitant measurable medications ranged from 1 to 5 (median 2). Non-adherence to one or more prescribed medications was identified in 19 patients (12%). Of these, 13 had MARS-5 scores of ≥24, indicating high medication adherence. In 15 patients (9%), cardiovascular medications not documented in the patients’ medication lists were detected. Adherence to DOACs, calcium channel blockers, and doxazosin was 100%. For beta-blockers, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers, and diuretics, adherence ranged from 90% to 100%. Non-adherence to atorvastatin however was 12%. Conclusions Long-term adherence to prescribed cardiovascular medications, especially statins, was suboptimal. Non-adherence and the presence of undocumented medications persisted even among patients who consented to TDM, indicating that TDM is superior to self-reported medication adherence. This supports the clinical value of TDM in identifying discrepancies in medication use and supporting patient-centred adherence-improvement strategies.
title: Long term adherence to prescribed cardiovascular medications in patients after percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Smoking cessation constitutes a fundamental secondary prevention intervention after ST elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI). Purpose We investigated at 12 months after STEMI the association between smoking status with mood disorder and their interrelation with arterial stiffness and integrity of endothelial glycocalyx. Methods We included smokers hospitalized for STEMI. We also included a matched group (for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia) of STEMI non-smokers as a control group. All smokers had attended the smoking cessation clinic after their discharge for their index event. We evaluated at baseline, at 6 and at 12 months: a) smoking status and nicotine dependence via Fagerström Test, b) levels of depressive symptoms via Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale, c) arterial stiffness via carotid-to-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV), central systolic blood pressure (cSBP) and d) thickness of endothelial glycocalyx through measurement of perfused boundary region of the sublingual microvessels with diameter range 4-25 μm. Results We totally included 190 STEMI patients, aged 59±8 years, 133/190 (70%) were males, of which 150 were active smokers and 40 non-smokers (control group). At 6-month follow-up, 91/150 (60,6%) smokers had quitted smoking and managed to abstain from smoking at 12-month follow-up. Out of 91 quitters, 70 (77%) quitted smoking on their own , 10 (11%) received Nicotine replacement therapy and 11 (12%) cytisinicline. Fageström score was reduced significantly during follow-up assessments (from 4.68±1.13 to 1.75±0.36 to 1.26±0.23 respectively, p&lt;0.05), whereas Zung score remained unchanged (p&gt;0.05). Baseline Fageström score was associated with baseline Zung score (r=0.218, p=0.036) and this association was not overt at follow-up. During 12-month follow-up, smoking AMI quitters and non smokers displayed a significant decrease of PBR4-25, PWV, cSBP compared to AMI patients who continued smoking (for PBR4-25: -5.65% and -6.57% vs -0.95% respectively, p&lt;0.05;for PWV: -18.39% and -13.74% vs -3.41% respectively, p&lt;0.05; for cSBP: -9.30% and -7.25% vs 11.92%, p&lt;0.05). Among those who continued smoking those who further increasedFagerström score at 1 year showed greater increase of PWV (r=0.364, p=0.04) Conclusions One year after the after the index event, STEMI smokers who quit smoking one showed a similar amelioration of arterial stiffness and integrity of endothelial glycocalyx to non smoker AMI patients while those who continued smoking showed no improvement in vascular functionTable
title: Smoking habit and changes of endothelial glycocalyx and arterial stiffness in AMI patients after one year follow up

abstract: Abstract Background Appropriate strategies to improve the medical care quality in transapical transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TA-TAVR) are urgently warranted. Recent evidence suggests that pre-operative physiotherapy is associated with better outcomes in patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery. To investigate the feasibility and effectiveness of the modified I COUGH care bundle (I COUGH-WCH). Methods and Results A single-blinded controlled trial was conducted from 2023 to 2025. Participants who eligible for TA-TAVR were recruited and randomly assigned to either I COUGH-WCH care bundle group (IG) or standard ERAS group (CG) in a 1:1 ratio. Of 144 participants, 52.08% were male, the mean age was 70.79 years. The postoperative respiratory complications were present in 16 of 72 participants in the IG (22.22%) and 30 of 72 in the CG (41.67%) (RR: 0.533, 95% CI: 0.320-0.889, P=0.012). The respiratory function and exercise capacity of the IG were consistently better than those of the CG before discharge, 1-month after discharge, and 3-month after discharge (P&lt;0.05). Conclusion Implementation of I COUGH-WCH care bundle effectively reduces the incidence of PPCs, enhances postoperative functional capacity, and improves quality of life in patients undergoing TA-TAVR. These findings support its adoption as a standardized perioperative management protocol in this patient population.Graphical abstract
title: The effect of I COUGH-WCH Perioperative care bundle in patients undergoing transapical transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a randomized controlled trial

abstract: Abstract Background Frailty is associated with increased mortality following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). It is not clear how the level of preoperative frailty is associated with the risk of unplanned readmission. Therefore, we examined the risk of mortality and unplanned readmission the first year after TAVI, in relation to preoperative frailty level. Methods All patients, aged &gt;65 years, who were treated with TAVI at a Swedish University Hospital from November 2019 to December 2023 were included in the study. To estimate preoperative frailty, we used Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), divided in three frailty groups. To compare the proportions of mortality and unplanned readmission, Chi2 and Fischer’s exact test were used. Cumulative survival analysis was performed. The risk of mortality and unplanned readmission was estimated by using relative risk estimate calculation. Results In total, 460 TAVI patients were included (mean age 81.8 years, SD 5.4), 50.7% women. Preoperatively, 19% of the patients were assessed as not frail (CFS 2–3), 58% with very mild frailty (CFS 4) and 23% with mild to moderate frailty (CFS 5–6). Within the first year after TAVI, there was a significant difference in cumulative survival between patients in CFS groups 2–4 and 5–6, favouring CFS groups 2–4 (p=0.001). The mortality rates within the first year after TAVI were 5.9% in CFS group 2–3, 3.0% in CFS group 4, and 12.3% in CFS groups 5–6 (p = 0.02). Overall, 28.9% of the patients had unplanned readmission by any reason the first year after TAVI. The proportion of patients with an unplanned readmission within the first year was 22.1% in CFS groups 2–3, 26.5% in CFS group 4, and 37.7% in CFS groups 5–6 (p=0.04). Patients in CFS group 5–6 had a significantly higher cumulative rate of unplanned readmission compared with patients in CFS groups 2–4 (p=0.01). The relative risk (RR) of unplanned readmission was 1.48 (95% CI: 1.10–2.01) in patients with mild to moderate frailty (CFS 5–6) compared with those with no to very mild frailty (CFS 2–4) (p = 0.02). Overall, readmission occurred in 13.0% for cardiovascular, 1.2% for neurological, and 16.0% for other reasons. In total, 9.9% of the patients had &gt;1 unplanned hospitalizations, 7.1% in CFS 2–3, 8.6% in CFS 4 and 14.4%in CFS 5–6 (p=0.12). Conclusions Patients with mild to moderate frailty had a significantly higher risk of both mortality and unplanned readmission the first year following TAVI than patients with no or very mild frailty. These results emphasize the importance of evaluate level of frailty preoperatively, in order to facilitate a careful patient selection to TAVI. Furthermore, patients who are mildly or moderate frail before TAVI need to receive effective approaches to mitigate the negative consequences of frailty.KM-curves mortalityKM- curves unplanned readmission
title: Preoperative frailty and risk of unplanned readmission and mortality within the first year after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), an increasingly recognized cause of acute coronary syndrome that predominantly affects women, is associated with persistent psychological distress and difficulties in life adjustment. Illness identity, the extent to which a health condition becomes integrated into one’s sense of self, predicts mental health outcomes in other chronic illness populations but has not been studied in SCAD. Purpose This study examined whether illness identity is associated with symptoms of anxiety and depression in SCAD patient-samples from Canada and Australia. Methods Data were drawn from the Canadian MINDSET study and the Australian ACHH psychosocial sub-study of the VCCRI Arteriopathies and SCAD Cohort (VASC), both assessing psychological outcomes post SCAD. Adults diagnosed with SCAD within 3 years were included. Participants completed sociodemographic questionnaires and validated measures, including the Illness Identity Questionnaire (IIQ, engulfment, rejection, acceptance, enrichment, see Figure 1), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) for anxiety symptoms, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) for depressive symptoms. Between-country differences were assessed with chi-square tests, independent-samples t-tests, and ANCOVA for anxiety and depression, controlling for time since diagnosis. Multiple linear regression examined associations between illness identity dimensions, anxiety and depression, adjusting for age, sex, time since diagnosis, and country. Results Participants included 323 individuals from Canada and 126 from Australia (N=449, 93% female; mean age = 54 years; 47% within one year of SCAD, see Table 1). Clinically significant symptoms were observed in 19% for generalized anxiety and 23% for depression. Canadian and Australian patients did not differ significantly in anxiety, depression, or any of the four illness identity subscales. In adjusted models, higher engulfment (B=2.64, p&lt;.001) and rejection (B=0.76, p=.011) were significantly associated with anxiety symptoms. Similarly, higher engulfment (B=2.57, p&lt;.001), rejection (B=1.14, p&lt;.001), and lower enrichment (B=-1.33, p&lt;.001) were significantly associated with depressive symptoms. Younger age was associated with both anxiety and depression, while female sex was associated with depression only. Conclusions Illness identity dimensions, particularly engulfment and rejection are key correlates of anxiety and depression in SCAD, consistent across the international cohorts. These findings underscore the importance of assessing and addressing illness identity in SCAD psychological care and support global efforts to improve mental health interventions for this population.Picture 1.
