Genetically modified immunocompromised pigs (LEA29Y) allow investigation of remodelling mechanisms. To account for strong regional immune responses, we performed a detailed whole-heart examination of I/R injury and remodelling, combining functional and molecular data with comprehensive immunohistochemical assessment of differently affected regions. Methods Using a catheter-based approach, 45–60 minutes of ischemia were induced in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) of LEA29Y pigs and WT controls, followed by permanent reperfusion. I/R-treated and control animals were functionally assessed and sacrificed after 3, 9, 14, & 26 days. Each heart was sectioned into 36 locally assigned left ventricular samples, classified as remote zone, area at risk, or infarct zone, and separated for fixation and cryoconservation. All fixed samples were stained with HE and Sirius Red. Immunohistochemistry for IBA1, CD3 T-cells, and neutrophils was performed on every fourth systematically selected sample per region. Whole-slide scans were analysed using QuPath for global high-resolution quantification by creating pixel classifiers and complemented by cluster analysis in ImageJ. Statistical comparisons were performed using t tests. Results LEA29Y and WT animals displayed similar infarct sizes. LV angiography revealed a tendency of greater early loss of ejection fraction in transgenic pigs up to day 14, but less aggravated impairment after 26 days (-18.96%) compared to WT (-27.34%, p=0.0016). Collagen analysis demonstrated an earlier, lower peak at day 9 in LEA29Y versus day 14 in WT animals. Global IBA1-stained macrophages were significantly reduced in transgenic pigs (p=0.000751) with rapid post-MI recovery to WT-comparable levels after 3 days. In infarct areas, macrophage levels were initially higher in LEA29Y pigs but declined rapidly, whereas WT levels peaked at day 9, resulting in higher WT levels at this timepoint and similar levels at day 26. Cluster analysis of IBA1-stained infarcted areas showed homogeneous macrophage clustering at day 3, followed by increased clustering in LEA29Y and decreased clustering in WT, which later reversed; by day 26 WT animals exhibited greater clustering. Quantitative measurements of stained CD3 T-cells showed significantly lower levels in LEA29Y pigs at baseline and they remained reduced in infarct areas through day 26. Conclusion Histological findings in post-I/R hearts align with functional data indicating slower but more sustained recovery of ejection fraction in LEA29Y pigs. Proteomics and snRNAseq support the suggestion of a delayed and reduced remodelling under immunosuppression, co-inciding with a more pronounced clustering of macrophages in infarcted areas. Early cardiac remodelling thus depends on precise immune orchestration.
title: Immunosuppression modulates post-ischemic myocardial scar formation and remodelling in LEA29Y pigs

abstract: Abstract Background Ferroptosis plays a central role in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury. M1 macrophage-derived small extracellular vesicles (M1-sEVs) deliver protein cargo that promote lipid peroxidation. Epicardial adipose tissue browning reduces local inflammatory response and remodels lipid metabolism, gowever, whether it modulates cardiomyocyte ferroptosis via the ACSL1 cargo loading in M1-sEVs remains unclear. Purpose To investigate how EAT browning attenuates cardiomyocyte ferroptosis and alleviates MI/R injury by suppressing M1 macrophage polarization and ACSL1 cargo loading in M1-sEVs. Methods Peripheral sEVs were collected from patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS, n=150), chronic coronary syndrome (CCS, n=150) and healthy controls (HC, n=50) for sEVs extraction. ACSL1 expression in sEVs was measured by western blotting (WB) and ELISA, and correlated with cardiac injury markers. M1-sEVs were isolated from LPS-stimulated BMDMs and identified. LFQ proteomics was used to analyze differentially expressed proteins. Brown adipocyte markers and macrophage polarization markers were measured. Mouse MI/R and cardiomyocyte hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) models were constructed. Cardiac function/infarct size were assessed by echocardiography/TTC. Ferroptosis was assessed by lipid peroxidation, ROS, iron, MDA/GSH and GPX4. An ACSL1 knockdown model in M1 macrophages was established using siRNA and ferroptosis was inhibited by Fer-1. Results Elevated ACSL1 expression in sEVs was higher in ACS group than CCS and HC groups and positively correlated with cTnI, CK-MB and BNP. LFQ proteomics identified ACSL1 as an enriched ferroptosis-related cargo protein in M1-sEVs. In vitro, M1-sEVs were efficiently taken up by cardiomyocytes and exacerbated ferroptosis under H/R, as evidenced by decreased cell viability, elevated lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress, iron accumulation, and reduced GPX4 levels. These changes were significantly reversed by Fer-1. In vivo, the MI/R+ M1-sEVs group exhibited severe myocardial injury compared to the group, evidenced by worsened cardiac function, increased infarct size, reduced GPX4 levels, and elevated lipid peroxidation. EAT browning upregulated UCP1expression, reduced M1 polarization, and decreased ACSL1 cargo loading in M1-sEVs, accompanied by reduced ferroptosis-related signals, improved cardiac function, and reduced infarct size after MI/R. siACSL1 in M1 macrophages inhibited cardiomyocyte ferroptosis, protected the injured myocardium, and promoted cardiac function recovery. Conclusion EAT browning attenuates cardiomyocyte ferroptosis and MI/R injury by suppressing ACSL1 enrichment in M1-sEVs. ACSL1 appears to be a pivotal mediator of ferroptosis in MI/R injury, suggesting potential therapeutic approaches of promoting EAT browning and targeting ACSL1 cargo loading in M1-sEVs.Graphical Abstract
title: Epicardial adipose tissue browning attenuates cardiomyocyte ferroptosis in ischemia/reperfusion injury by suppressing ACSL1 cargo loading in M1 macrophage-derived small extracellular vesicles

abstract: Abstract Background Myocardial microvascular dysfunction and endothelial cell injury are important risk factor for poor prognosis in patients with coronary heart disease. There is a communication relationship between macrophages and endothelial cells, which regulates inflammatory injury and programmed cell death of endothelial cells, which is a key mechanism to regulate microvascular dysfunction. However, the mechanism of the role of myocardial microvascular injury is still not clear. Previous studies found that ischemia-reperfusion injury induced macrophage phenotype transformation, and promoted macrophage-endothelial cell communication, regulating the endothelial cell ferroptosis. Purpose This study aims to elucidate the mechanism of MsrB1 in circulating macrophages and the protection of reparative cell communication in myocardial microvascular ferroptosis. Method I/R injury in C57bl/6 mice and Macrophage-specific MsrB1 knockout mice were established by ligating the left anterior descending artery. The immunofluorescence, FACS, scRNA-seq and proteomics analysis were performed to explore the underlying mechanisms of macrophage recruitment and polarization after IR. The benefits of microvascular perfusion and vascular no-reflow phenomenon were assessed by FITC-lectin perfusion assay and Thioflavin S staining assay. Result By analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and proteomics data of cardiac I/R injury, we found that MsrB1 expression was significantly upregulated in circulating reparative macrophages, which enhanced the macrophage endothelial communication. MsrB1 knockout further promotes immune cell inflammation and microvascular ischemia injury, aggravated cardiac remodeling, cardiac dysfunction, and fibrosis after IR and vice versa. Consistently, ELISA assays demonstrated that MsrB1 overexpression attenuated macrophage pro-inflammatory factors secretion and promoted anti-inflammatory factors. Furthermore, we discovered that MsrB1 over-expressed macrophages significantly promoted the transcription of anti-ferroptosis proteins, which alleviated ferroptosis and improved endothelial cell function. MsrB1 activated anti-ferroptosis secretion by reducing the transcription factor methionine oxidation (MetO) and promoting the transcription of CP in macrophages. Macrophage-specific knockout of MsrB1 in mice can induce the pro-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, aggravate the ferroptosis of endothelial cells, and aggravate myocardial microvascular ischemia-perfusion injury. Conclusion In conclusion, MsrB1 reduces the oxidized methionine residues in macrophage transcription factors, induces the reprogramming of macrophage secreted proteins, attenuates endothelial ferroptosis by secreting anti-ferroptosis proteins, and finally protects myocardial microvascular I/R injury. The results of this study will provide a new theoretical basis for the strategies targeting MsrB1-centered intervention of myocardial microvascular reperfusion injury.I/R injury activates reparative macrophages.MsrB1 reduces transcription factor MetO
title: The mechanism of MsrB1 mediating the macrophage-endothelial reparative communication in myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction After myocardial infarction (MI), an inadequate resolution of inflammation and failure to activate reparative macrophage programs contribute to infarct expansion and adverse left ventricular remodelling. Cell therapy is increasingly thought to confer cardiac repair primarily via paracrine immunomodulation. However, it remains unclear whether a cell donor’s MI history enhances the cell secretome’s potency to induce a macrophage phenotype shift that supports tissue repair. Purpose To: determine whether MI-primed donor Bone Marrow cells (BMC) produce a distinct secretome that promotes macrophage reparative polarisation and assess if this translates into improved post-MI cardiac repair in vivo. Methods MI was induced in rats by left coronary ligation. BMCs from healthy donors (hBMC) or from donors 2 weeks post-MI (iBMC) were harvested and expanded ex vivo for 2 weeks. The conditioned media (secretomes) were analyzed by LC–MS/MS proteomics. Bone-marrow–derived macrophages were cultured with BMC-conditioned media for 48 h and then assessed by flow cytometry and gene expression profiling of polarization markers. For in vivo, rats 2 weeks post-MI received an epicardial fibrin patch delivering BMCs at the infarct. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography before BMC delivery and 4 weeks after, with change in ejection fraction as the primary outcome. Infarct size was assessed by Masson–Goldner trichrome staining, and immunofluorescence was performed Results In vitro, iBMC cultures contained a higher proportion of hematopoietic/myeloid cells (CD45⁺, CD68⁺) and less CD90⁺ cells compared to hBMC, along with greater expression of M2-associated markers (CD206, CD163) and no increase in M1 markers (Fig 1). Proteomic analysis revealed that the iBMC secretome was distinct from hBMC, enriched in myeloid-related, pro-angiogenic and matrix-remodelling factors. Functionally, macrophages exposed to iBMC-conditioned media showed enhanced growth and a shift to a reparative (M2-like) gene expression profile, with upregulation of Arg1, CD163, IL-10 and downregulation of iNOS, CD80, IL-1β. In vivo, rats treated with iBMCs exhibited superior improvement in EF (Fig2) and attenuated adverse remodelling compared to hBMC-treated or untreated controls. Consistently, immunofluorescence of iBMC-treated hearts showed an infarct-zone immune shift with reduced persistence of inflammatory macrophages and an enrichment of CD206⁺ reparative macrophages, indicating that the MI-primed secretome effectively “educates” macrophages toward a healing phenotype in the infarct. Conclusion(s) Donor MI history primes BMC composition and secretory profile toward an immunoreparative program that drives reparative macrophage polarization by effectively instructing macrophages towards a pro-healing phenotype, in line with improved post-MI cardiac repair in vivo.
title: Post-MI bone marrow cell secretome reprograms macrophages to a reparative M2 phenotype, enhancing cardiac repair

abstract: Abstract Background High levels of neuropeptide Y (NPY), a molecule co-released from cardiac sympathetic neurons, are associated with poor outcomes in myocardial infarction and heart failure. One possible reason for this might be cardiac remodelling triggered by NPY-induced changes in calcium handling—a mechanism which has not yet been explored in human models. Purpose To explore the link between NPY exposure and cardiac hypertrophy as well as the underlying cellular mechanisms in humans. Methods The relationship between peripheral venous NPY concentration and left ventricular (LV) mass was investigated in 35 patients recruited to the Oxford Acute Myocardial Infarction (OxAMI) study following ST-elevated myocardial infarction (STEMI). To isolate the effects of NPY on cardiomyocytes, human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CM) were incubated with NPY for 48 hours. Some cells were additionally incubated with antagonists of the Y1 (1 μM BIBO3004), Y2 (1 μM BIIE0246) or Y5 (1 μM CGP71683) NPY receptors, or with inhibitors of CAMKII (1 μM KN93) or calcineurin (1 μM FK506). Cell size was assessed using confocal microscopy and pathological relevance by brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) immunoblotting. Optical mapping with Rhod-2 fluorescent dye was used to visualise hiPSC-CM calcium transients in response to NPY. Results In patients with STEMI, peripheral venous NPY levels were significantly correlated with the percentage increase in LV mass between 2 days and 6 months post-infarct (r = 0.35, p = 0.04) and with the absolute LV mass at 6 months, independent of age, sex, blood pressure and infarct size on multiple linear regression (p &lt; 0.05). In vitro, NPY exposure produced a significant increase in hiPSC-CM size (at 1, 10 and 100 nM, p &lt; 0.0001) as well as BNP expression, a marker of cardiac hypertrophy. This could be prevented by antagonists of NPY receptors. Inhibition of both CAMKII and calcineurin prevented hiPSC-CM enlargement in response to NPY (100 nM). A direct effect of NPY (100 nM) on calcium transient kinetics was observed in optical mapping experiments. Calcium entry and extrusion time—quantified by rise time, CTD-30 and CTD-90 (calcium transient duration at 30% and 90% decay of peak amplitude)—were significantly shortened (p &lt; 0.01) which, again, could be reversed by antagonists of NPY receptors. Conclusions This study is the first to demonstrate an association between venous NPY levels and left ventricular hypertrophy after myocardial infarction independent of infarct size. Elevated intracellular calcium and subsequent activation of CAMKII and calcineurin might be driving cardiomyocyte enlargement secondary to NPY receptor activation. NPY receptor antagonists may therefore be potential targets to treat cardiac remodelling in patients after MI.Graphical Abstract
title: The Role of Neuropeptide Y in Human Cardiac Hypertrophy after Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Abstract Background High-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels are linked to cardiovascular outcomes; however, clinical trials aiming to reduce cardiovascular risk by increasing HDL concentrations have largely been unsuccessful. This suggests that HDL functionality, rather than its quantity, plays a pivotal role in cardiovascular protection. In this study, we investigated whether HDL from patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) exhibits impaired lipoprotective function and explored potential strategies to restore HDL functionality. Methods We investigated HDL properties by transfer experiments. Human HDL from CAD patients and healthy individuals were applied to mice undergoing acute myocardial infarction (AMI) via transient open-chest LAD ligation. Furthermore, HDL composition was measured using targeted LC/MS analyses. Results HDL from healthy individuals substantially reduced infarct size and improved ejection fraction after murine AMI (IS: 42.8±7.1% vs. 33.3±4.7%; EF: 33.7±4.9% vs. 41.1±4.5%). In contrast, HDL from CAD patients did not (IS: 40.4±5.2%; EF: 32.3±7.8%; n vehicle = 36, n healthy HDL = 21, n CAD-HDL = 12). The cardioprotective effect of healthy HDL was also evident in analyses conducted 21 days after AMI (scar size: 29.7±8.3% vs. 14.6±7.8%; n vehicle = 4, n healthy HDL = 5, p=0.0269). BSA-loaded sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) also provided cardioprotection. This was not surprising, as S1P administration enhances HDL-S1P content withing minutes. However, in animals with HDL receptor SRBI deficiency, the cardioprotective effects of HDL and BSA-S1P were absent. Comprehensive LC/MS analyses provided a detailed characterization of HDL composition. We found that S1P content was significantly reduced in CAD-HDL as compared to healthy individuals (HDL-S1P: 209.3±33.8pmol/mg vs. 158.2±47.31pmol/mg; n healthy HDL = 21, n CAD-HDL = 13, p=0.0009). ApoM-HDL content was similar in both groups. Hence, the ability to bind S1P is still present in CAD-HDL. Next, we aimed to restore HDL dysfunction by S1P-loading. Indeed, applying this S1P-loaded HDL from CAD patients in AMI mice, led to similar lipoprotection as compared to healthy-HDL. Conclusion In conclusion, we here found that HDL of CAD patients lack S1P, leading to blunted HDL cardioprotection. We found an option to restore that by loading diseased CAD-HDL with S1P.
title: Restoring cardioprotection via S1P-Enriched HDL in coronary artery disease

abstract: Abstract Introduction Cancer is a major comorbidity that may worsen outcomes after myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury. Cancer-associated cachexia (CAC) is an anabolic wasting syndrome characterized by muscle atrophy and systemic metabolic alterations, but its stage-dependent impact on IR remains unclear, particularly across different stages of cachexia progression. Methods Male Balb/c mice were injected subcutaneously with 1×10^6 C26 colon carcinoma cells or C26-shIL-6 cells to induce and distinguish either early (day 8–9) or advanced (day 18–20) stages of CAC. And non–tumor-bearing mice served as controls. Myocardial IR injury was induced (n=16) by left anterior descending coronary artery ligation for 40 minutes followed by 72 hours reperfusion. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography, and the extent of myocardial injury assessed by plasma troponin levels. Cardiac tissue proteomics was assessed using unbiased mass spectrometry–based analysis, while pSTAT3 expression was examined by western blotting and mitochondrial respiration was additionally assessed prior to IR insult. Results Cachexia was confirmed a significant fat and lean mass loss (p &lt; 0.0001) in our model. Interestingly, the expression of pSTAT3 was markedly increased in cardiac tissue from advanced stage of CAC mice. In addition, gene ontology analysis was identified a massive deregulation of oxidative phosphorylation proteins expression in CAC mice heart tissue. In line with, the capacity of FA metabolism was declined in the same group in compared to non-tumor or C26-shIL-6 group. Furthermore, the markers for autophagy was significantly and exclusively upregulated in heart tissue from CAC (advanced-stage) mice. Functionally, LVEF was moderately reduced in CAC vs. non–tumor mice before IR, but post-IR decline was attenuated in CAC mice, accompanied by lower cTnI and infarct size. In advanced CAC, LVEF decreased from baseline to pre-IR (p = 0.0019) and post-IR (p = 0.0197). While PBS controls showed significant pre- vs. post-IR reduction (p = 0.0009). For cTnI, PBS (p = 0.0313) and advanced CAC (p = 0.0349) showed significant increases post-IR. Conclusion Our findings highlight a stage-dependent effects of CAC in respect to myocardial IR injury. While early cachexia may contribute to systemic frailty, advanced CAC appears to induce adaptive mechanisms, including enhanced pTAT3 levels, metabolic rewiring (shifting to glicolyis), and activation of autophagy, which collectively and synergistic manner render to myocardium paradoxically more resistant to IR-injury. Ongoing proteomic and mechanistic studies will further clarify molecular pathways and may identify novel therapeutic targets for cardioprotection in setting of acute IR-injury.cardiac function resultspSTAT3 results
title: Stage-dependent effects of cancer cachexia on myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Viral myocarditis is an inflammatory heart disease caused by viral infections such as coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3), often affecting young adults and contributing to sudden cardiac death. Stimulator of interferon genes (STING), a central component of innate immunity, is increasingly implicated in cardiovascular inflammation. However, its precise role and downstream mechanisms in CVB3-induced myocarditis remain unclear. Purpose To investigate the role of STING in CVB3-induced viral myocarditis and identify its downstream molecular mechanisms. Methods CVB3-induced myocarditis was modeled in mice. Transcriptomic and multi-omics analyses were performed to identify potential downstream effectors of STING. Pharmacological inhibition studies in vivo and mtDNA-stimulated THP-1 macrophages in vitro were used to validate the STING–SPHK1 axis through molecular and functional assays. Results STING signaling was markedly activated in CVB3-induced myocarditis and macrophages, and its inhibition reduced cardiac inflammation and improved cardiac function. CVB3-induced cardiomyocyte injury led to mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release, activating STING mainly in macrophages. Multi-omics analysis revealed sphingosine kinase 1 (SPHK1) as a downstream STING target, transcriptionally upregulated by the STAT1::STAT2 transcriptional complex. In vivo SPHK1 inhibition similarly attenuated myocardial inflammation and dysfunction. SPHK1 knockdown in mtDNA-stimulated macrophages decreased reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial damage, and mtDNA release, suppressing STING activation and cytokine production. Conclusion(s) STING promotes CVB3-induced viral myocarditis by upregulating SPHK1 via STAT1::STAT2. This signalling axis amplifies macrophage-mediated inflammation and myocardial injury. Targeting STING or SPHK1 alleviates disease severity, highlighting a previously unrecognized proinflammatory amplification loop and suggesting potential therapeutic strategies for viral myocarditis.Figure 1
title: STING promotes CVB3-induced acute viral myocarditis via regulation of SPHK1

abstract: Abstract Introduction In adult mammals, myocardial injury (ΜΙ) results in a permanent loss of cardiomyocytes due to their limited proliferative capacity. However, organisms like amphibians and neonatal rodents exhibit cardiac regenerative potential, suggesting that mammalian heart may retain reparative programs, silenced with maturation. Evidence implicates the transcription factor Tbx5 as a critical mediator of injury-induced regenerative responses. Similarly, acute high-dose administration of triiodothyronine (T3) has been shown to modulate cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity and enhance aspects of cardiac repair. These findings raise the possibility that thyroid hormone (TH) signalling may intersect with Tbx5-dependent pathways to influence myocardial regeneration. Purpose Our aim was to determine whether T3 treatment modulates Tbx5 function during cardiac repair process following ΜΙ. Methods A well-defined tamoxifen-induced Tbx5Cre;Rosa26ReYFP/eYFP transgenic mouse model was used. Animals (3-4 months old) were subjected to pharmacological ΜΙ via isoproterenol (ISO) administration (3 doses of 10mg/Kg/day) (n=18). Another group was treated with T3 (50μg/kg/day) for 2 days following ISO administration (n=17). Animals treated with vehicle were used as control (n=10). Echocardiography was performed, while nuclear and cytoplasmic protein expression as well as kinase activation was assessed in the left ventricle by immunoblotting and immunohistochemistry on days 6 and 28. Results T3 improved cardiac function, as assessed by echocardiographic analysis, and restored SERCA/Phospholamban ratio. Immunohistochemistry showed reduced fibrotic tissue deposition, upon T3 treatment, after 28 days. Western blot analysis revealed differential nuclear localisation between Tbx5 (5-fold decrease) and TRα1 (3-fold increase) within the early reparative stage (day 6). Regarding kinase signalling, activation of Akt did not change, whereas T3 treatment significantly reduced p38 MAPK activation at day 6. Interestingly, in the late reparative stage (day 28), T3 treatment resulted in increased nuclear localisation of both Tbx5 and TRα1 in ISO+T3 hearts. More importantly, T3 augmented YFPTbx5 signal in cardiac tissue indicating increased transcriptional activity of Tbx5. Our in silico analysis based on recent literature indicated a possible Tbx5 feedback loop and cooperative binding of Tbx5 and TRα1 in adult mammalian cardiomyocytes. Conclusions These findings indicate that TH signalling exerts stage-specific regulatory effects on key transcriptional and signalling pathways involved in adult cardiac repair. T3 facilitates a coordinated transition from early injury-induced plasticity toward later redifferentiation and functional restoration, potentially through a Tbx5–TRα1 regulatory axis. This work positions TH signalling as a modulatory mechanism capable of re-engaging latent Tbx5-dependent regenerative pathways in the adult mammalian heart.
title: Involvement of Tbx5 in triiodothyronine’s reparative effect after pharmacological myocardial injury

abstract: Abstract Background Mitral valve replacement (MVR) alters left ventricular hemodynamics, potentially leading to thrombosis, hemolysis, and ventricular remodeling. While prior studies have assessed prosthetic valve flows, a direct in vitro comparison of vortex evolution and blood transport efficiency among native, bioprosthetic, and mechanical valves remains limited. Purpose This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate the impact of different mitral valve types on LV vortex structures and blood transport, focusing on residence time and apical washout. Methods We constructed a left heart simulator using a 3D-printed silicone LV and native porcine mitral apparatus. Three valve conditions were tested: native, bioprosthetic and bileaflet mechanical (Figure 1). Time-resolved tomographic particle image velocimetry (Tomo-PIV) was applied to capture three-dimensional velocity fields, and then the Q-criterion was adopted to identify the intraventricular vortex patterns. Lagrangian particle tracking was performed to compute blood residence time (τ, in cardiac cycles) and the apical-transit ratio (percentage of particles passing through the apical region of the LV) (Figure 1). Results Prosthetic valves fundamentally altered diastolic vortex morphology and transport dynamics (Figure 2). The native valve formed a saddle-shaped diastolic vortex ring with optimal apical convection, resulting in the shortest residence time (46.0 ± 1.1% residual blood after 3 cycles) and highest apical-transit ratio (74.8 ± 2.2%). The bioprosthetic valve produced a near-circular vortex ring with intermediate transport efficiency (52.7 ± 1.6% residual blood; 72.7 ± 1.5% apical transit). The mechanical valve generated fragmented crescent-shaped vortices confined to the basal LV, resulting in the longest residence time (64.7 ± 7.0% residual blood) and the lowest apical-transit ratio (50.7 ± 11.2%). These findings indicate that mechanical valves are associated with significantly prolonged blood stasis and reduced apical washout. Conclusions This study demonstrates that native mitral valve hemodynamics optimize apical washout and minimize intraventricular stasis through organized vortex convection. Both bioprosthetic and mechanical valves disrupt this physiological flow, with mechanical valves exhibiting the most pronounced deficits in transport efficiency. These results highlight the importance of vortex-driven apical washout in LV hemodynamics and suggest that future valve designs should aim to restore physiological vortex-driven apical washout.Figure 1.Experimental Process and MethodsFigure 2.Results Presentation
title: Hemodynamic evaluation for mitral valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Introduction Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is a serious complication and a leading cause of death in patients undergoing heart valve surgery. The main aim of the present study was to assess the predictive capacity of selected perioperative parameters, including Troponin T levels, to predict the occurrence of postoperative MODS and 30-day mortality in patients undergoing heart valve surgery. Purpose The main aim of the present study was to assess the predictive capacity of selected perioperative parameters in terms of their ability to predict the occurrence of postoperative MODS and 30-day mortality in patients undergoing heart valve surgery. Methods This prospective study included a group of patients with hemodynamically severe symptomatic valvular heart disease who underwent valve surgery. The primary endpoint was postoperative multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), defined as the dysfunction of at least two organs/systems, including cardiogenic shock, perioperative stroke, respiratory failure requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation, and/or postoperative acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy. The secondary endpoint was death during the 30-day follow-up. Logistic regression was used to assess the relationships between the variables. Results In total, 739 patients undergoing valvular heart surgery were included in this study. The primary end point was observed in 45 patients. Preoperative hemoglobin level (P = 0.01) and red cell distribution width (RDW) (P = 0.001) as well as troponin T level measured on the first day after surgery (TnT II) (P &lt; 0.001) were independent predictors of the primary endpoint. EuroSCORE II (P = 0.002) and TnT II (P &lt; 0.001) were independent predictors of 30-day mortality. The area under the receiver operator characteristic curve for 30-day mortality for EuroSCORE II is 0.699 (95% CI 0.664-0.732) and for TnT II is 0.766 (0.733-0.797). Conclusions MODS is a clinical condition that is associated with a high risk of death. Troponin T levels measured within the first 24 h postoperatively may be useful in predicting postoperative MODS and 30-day mortality in patients undergoing heart valve surgery as a complement to commonly used risk calculators.
title: The role of markers of myocardial damage in predicting post-operative multiple organ dysfunction syndrome and 30-day mortality in patients undergoing heart valve surgery

abstract: Abstract Introduction Low-grade inflammation is a major contributor to the development and progression of calcified aortic stenosis (AS). Inflammatory activity within calcified valves is heterogeneous, with high-grade inflammation involving activation of the AT1R/NADPH oxidase/SGLT1/2 axis that drives pro-inflammatory, pro-calcific, pro-remodeling, and fibrotic responses. Although angiotensin and aldosterone pathways are closely interconnected, the role of aldosterone synthase (AS) in mediating inflammatory and oxidative processes within human calcified aortic valves remains insufficiently understood. Aim To evaluate aldosterone-mediated pro-oxidant responses in the calcified aortic valve and in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of patients with aortic stenosis. Methods Pathological aortic valves and PBMCs were collected from patients undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement at the University Hospital of Strasbourg. Protein expression was assessed by Western blot, and in situ localization within valve tissue was examined by immunofluorescence staining. ROS production was measured using dihydroethidium (DHE) staining. In PBMCs, glucose uptake was quantified using 2-NBDG, and aldosterone release by ELISA. Results ROS levels were increased 1.7-fold in calcified aortic valve regions compared with non-calcified areas, and this augmented oxidative activity was significantly attenuated by NAC, losartan, VAS-2870, empagliflozin, eplerenone, and FAD286. Exogenous aldosterone markedly enhanced ROS production in non-calcified valves, an effect fully reversed by the same inhibitors, whereas calcified valves were unresponsive to aldosterone stimulation. Calcified valves demonstrated a pronounced upregulation of aldosterone synthase (AS), with immunofluorescence analyses localizing AS predominantly to CD68-positive macrophages. PBMCs from aortic stenosis patients exhibited elevated ROS generation and increased glucose uptake, both of which were significantly reduced by NAC, losartan, VAS-2870, empagliflozin, eplerenone, and FAD286. Combined inhibition with FAD286 (1 nM) and empagliflozin (10 nM) produced a synergistic suppression of ROS and glucose uptake, as confirmed by synergy analysis. AS expression in PBMCs from aortic stenosis patients was higher than in healthy controls, and was downregulated by VAS-2870, empagliflozin, and FAD286, and slightly by losartan. ELISA quantification showed aldosterone release was elevated in PBMCs from aortic stenosis patients relative to healthy subjects, markedly reduced by FAD286 whereas empagliflozin and eplerenone had minor effects. Conclusion Aldosterone synthase is upregulated in calcified aortic valves, particularly within infiltrating macrophages, and promotes pro-oxidant and metabolic dysregulation in both valve tissue and PBMCs. These findings suggest that aldosterone signaling contributes to the progression of calcified aortic stenosis and represents a potential therapeutic target.
title: Inflammation of the calcified aortic valve in cardiac patients is associated with activation of the local aldosterone system, promoting oxidative stress–driven pathological responses

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Atrial fibrillation (AF) and its underlying atrial myopathy increase the left atrial thrombotic risk, as calculated by the CHA2DS2-VA score, which correlates well with the presence of atrial myopathy. However, the risk prediction of this score is modest (C-statistic=0.6). Other factors, such as mitral valve regurgitation (MR), may influence thrombotic risk. In nonrheumatic AF, the effect of MR on left atrial thrombotic risk remains controversial. Furthermore, the thrombotic effect of AF itself, without atrial myopathy, is not well studied. Purpose To assess the effect of MR (high flow) and lone AF (low flow) on left atrial thrombotic risk. Methods A total of 20 Piétrain pigs (with equal sex distribution) were randomized to severe MR, induced by selective cutting of the chordae tendineae (n=14), or the sham procedure (n=6). High-frequency atrial tachypacing was performed to induce paroxysmal AF (15 min.). Left atrial blood samples were collected before and after AF-induction. After four weeks, blood sampling was repeated in all pigs, and the sham group underwent a longer AF-tachypacing session (60 min.). To explore left atrial thrombotic risk, platelet aggregation, intrinsic, extrinsic, and common coagulation pathways, fibrinolysis, and von Willebrand factor (vWF) assays were measured. Results Echocardiography showed MR severity grade 3.5-4/4 in all pigs of the intervention group. Severe MR led to left atrial dilation, with a greater increase in mean left atrial volume compared to the sham group (+28.1 ± 5.4 ml vs. +6.7 ± 2.1 ml; p=0.01), and more left atrial fibrosis (25.8 ± 5.2% vs. 13.0 ± 2.9%; p&lt;0.001). There was a significantly divergent effect of MR vs. AF on left atrial thrombotic risk (P-values for all interactions &lt;0.05, Figure 1). MR was associated with increases in mean platelet volume (MPV, +9.1%), APTT (+9.6%), PT (+8.5%), and D-dimers (+54.0%), and decreases in platelet aggregation (-9.7%), fibrinogen (-23.1%), and vWF antigen (-18.1%) and activity (-31.1%), indicating an antithrombotic effect. The opposite effect was observed for AF, with decreases in MPV (-2.2%), APTT (-1.1%), and PT (-1.9%), and increases in platelet aggregation (+1.4%), fibrinogen (+2.2%), and vWF antigen (+3.4%) and activity (+4.1%), indicating a prothrombotic effect. Conclusion Our data show a prothrombotic effect of lone AF and an antithrombotic effect of MR on left atrial thrombotic risk. The antithrombotic effect of MR was observed despite the development of significant atrial myopathy. This implies that MR could be a modifying protective factor in thrombotic risk assessment of AF patients and could help individualize anticoagulant treatment. The data of our AF model, without underlying atrial myopathy, emphasizes the importance of rhythm control in AF patients to minimize left atrial thrombogenicity and challenges safety of withholding anticoagulation in patients with low CHA2DS2-VA scores and persistent AF.Effect of MR and AF on thrombotic risk
title: The effect of mitral valve regurgitation and lone atrial fibrillation on left atrial thrombotic risk: a porcine model of alternating left atrial flow conditions

abstract: Abstract Background Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO) is associated with migraine with aura and a systemic prothrombotic milieu. Beyond previously described platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction may contribute to this phenotype. Endothelial colony-forming cells (ECFCs) provide a patient-specific model to investigate endothelial thromboinflammatory properties and their modulation after PFO closure. Purposes To characterize the procoagulant phenotype, shear-stress response, and transcriptomic profile of ECFCs from PFO patients before and after closure compared with healthy subjects (HS). Methods ECFCs were obtained from 35 PFO patients at baseline (T0) and 6 months after closure (T1), and from 25 HS. Intracellular Tissue Factor (TF) and Tissue Factor Pathway Inhibitor (TFPI) were measured by flow cytometry and ELISA, and thrombin generation by calibrated automated thrombography. ECFCs were exposed to high laminar shear stress to assess expression of genes involved in endothelial homeostasis, inflammation, vascular tone, and coagulation (including KLF2, KLF4, NOS3, EDN1, HMGB1, TF). Whole-transcriptome analysis compared T0 and T1 profiles. Results ECFCs from PFO patients showed a procoagulant phenotype. A higher proportion of patient-derived ECFC lines generated measurable thrombin compared with HS (29% vs 11%), persisting at T1 (33%). The TF/TFPI ratio was higher in patients than HS (0.18 ± 0.17 vs 0.065 ± 0.043) and remained elevated after closure. TF protein levels were also higher in patients (466.7 ± 233.5 vs 388.3 ± 208.0 pg/mg), whereas TFPI tended to be lower (60.8 ± 49.1 vs 77.5 ± 41.7 ng/mg). Under high laminar shear stress, patient ECFCs showed reduced activation of shear-protective pathways, including lower KLF4 expression, along with persistence of pro-inflammatory/procoagulant signals such as TF and HMGB1. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment at T0 of pathways related to platelet activation, leukocyte adhesion, and cell–matrix interaction, whereas T1 cells showed relative upregulation of immunoregulatory (e.g., IL-10–associated) and vascular repair pathways, including wound-healing and tissue remodeling programs. Conclusions ECFCs from PFO patients exhibit a sustained prothrombotic and thromboinflammatory phenotype characterized by enhanced TF-driven activity and altered shear-stress responses. PFO closure is associated with partial transcriptional reprogramming toward immunoregulation and endothelial repair, although the procoagulant imbalance is not fully normalized, identifying the endothelium as an active contributor to the thromboinflammatory milieu associated with PFO.
title: Residual endothelial prothrombotic imbalance after patent foramen ovale closure

abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but can induce severe immune-related adverse effects, including myocarditis. However, the pathogenesis and risk factors of ICI-related myocarditis remain poorly understood and would benefit from improved preclinical pharmacological models. Purpose We hypothesized that ICI-related myocarditis in mice involves a “dual-hit” mechanism with an ischemic index event priming the immune system, followed by loss of tolerance during ICI therapy. Methods We subjected A/J mice to a single isoprenaline injection (160 mg/kg IP) or saline (w1). Three weeks later, both groups received 5 injections of either anti-PD-1 (25 mg/kg IP, q3 days) or saline. Analysis of myocardial injury (plasma troponin I) and systemic inflammation (serum amyloid A, SAA) was performed in 4 groups: isoprenaline+anti-PD-1 (n=11), isoprenaline+saline (n=10), saline+anti-PD-1 (n=11), and saline+saline (n=10) at baseline, 1h after isoprenaline or saline injection, before anti-PD-1 or saline injection, and at w8. Cardiac magnetic resonance-based measurements (7T Brucker Biospec 70/30) of LV systolic function and T2-relaxation times were performed at baseline, prior to anti-PD-1, and at w8. We semi-quantitatively measured inflammation (CD45 positive cell count) and fibrosis (CSA, cross sectional area on Sirius red-stained sections) on 13 randomly selected high-power fields at midventricular level. Results Troponin I levels significantly increased 1h after isoprenaline (p&lt;0.0001 vs saline) with no further rise after anti-PD1 treatment in contrast to SAA, which peaked after anti-PD-1 (p&lt;0.0001 vs saline). Administration of isoprenaline, anti-PD1 or combination did not affect global LV systolic function as evidenced by stable EDVi, ESVi or LVEF measurements after 8w. However, at 8w mean T2 relaxation times, reflecting myocardial edema, were significantly higher compared to baseline in mice exposed to isoprenaline+anti-PD-1 (p&lt;0.0001 vs saline). Consistent with SAA levels, cardiac CD45-positive leukocyte cell count was significantly higher in mice receiving anti-PD1 alone (p&lt;0.01 vs saline) and in double-hit mice (p&lt;0.0001 vs saline) in whom prior isoprenaline-induced injury was associated with a further rise in CD45+ cells [58.5 (30.4 – 104.7) cells/mm² vs 36.5 (27.2 – 41.8) median (IQR) in anti-PD-1 alone]. Consequently, mice in the double hit group had significant more fibrosis (7.8±4.7%, mean±SD) compared to mice who received saline (1.5±0.5%, p&lt;0.0001) or either challenge alone (anti-PD1 1.1±0.4%, p&lt;0.0001 or isoprenaline 3.2±1.9%, &lt;0.001). Conclusion We successfully characterized a dual-hit mouse model for ICI-related myocarditis based on an initial ischemic myocardial injury and sequential anti-PD1 administration. Our data highlight the intricate interplay between ischemia and PD1-mediated immune activation and will facilitate future studies on targeted interventions for ICI-myocarditis.
title: Dual-hit with sequential isoprenaline and PD-1 blockade in A/J Mice to model immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis

abstract: Abstract Background Pathological cardiac fibrosis following myocardial infarction (MI) is primarily driven by the activation and differentiation of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) into myofibroblasts—a process critically dependent on enhanced aerobic glycolysis. Nevertheless, the epigenetic mechanisms that couple metabolic reprogramming with pro-fibrotic gene expression in CFs remain largely elusive. Objective This study sought to delineate the role of the RNA helicase DDX21 in post-MI fibrosis and to uncover its non-canonical function in orchestrating histone methylation, lactate metabolism, and CF activation. Methods DDX21 expression was assessed in activated CFs isolated from murine post-MI hearts and in TGF-β-stimulated human CFs using qRT-PCR and immunoblotting. To dissect the underlying molecular mechanisms, we employed an integrative approach combining RNA-sequencing, CUT&Tag assay, and co-immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry. The functional relevance of DDX21 was further interrogated in vivo through cardiac-specific knockdown of DDX21 via adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery in a mouse model of MI, followed by comprehensive evaluation of cardiac function, fibrotic remodeling, and molecular alterations. Results DDX21 expression was markedly upregulated in activated CFs from both murine infarcted hearts and TGF-β-treated human CFs. Mechanistically, nuclear DDX21 leveraged its protein-interaction domain to competitively engage the PHD1 domain of the histone demethylase KDM5A, thereby displacing histone H3 binding. This competitive interaction attenuated KDM5A enzymatic activity, resulting in global enrichment of H3K4me3. Notably, this epigenetic shift led to promoter hypermethylation and increased chromatin accessibility at the SLC16A3 locus, which encodes the lactate transporter MCT4. The consequent upregulation of MCT4 facilitated lactate efflux from CFs, sustaining the elevated glycolytic flux required for persistent myofibroblast activation and collagen deposition. Conversely, AAV-mediated cardiac-specific silencing of DDX21 in post-MI mice disrupted the DDX21-KDM5A interaction, reinstated KDM5A demethylase activity, diminished H3K4me3 occupancy at the SLC16A3 promoter, normalized MCT4 expression, and suppressed glycolytic activity in CFs. These interventions markedly attenuated myocardial fibrosis, preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, and reduced infarct size. Conclusion We identify a novel DDX21-KDM5A regulatory axis linking epigenetic control to metabolic reprogramming in fibrosis. By maintaining SLC16A3 promoter methylation, DDX21 drives MCT4-mediated lactate export, fueling CF glycolytic capacity and differentiation. Targeting DDX21 or its interaction with KDM5A represents a promising therapeutic strategy for heart failure.Schematic diagram
title: DDX21-mediated epigenetic remodeling drives cardiac fibroblast activation and fibrosis post-myocardial infarction by stabilizing SLC16A3 expression

abstract: Abstract Background Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor inhibitors(VEGFRI), as drugs targeting angiogenesis, are widely used in the treatment of various malignant tumors with remarkable therapeutic effects. However, due to its off-target effect, it may cause cardiovascular side effects, which has also become one of the main causes of death for cancer patients. Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction(CTRCD) is associated with the use of VEGFRI. Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) is a major factor in cardiovascular disease. Elevated PARP1 expression and poly (ADP-ribose) ylation were observed in cardiac remodeling. The increase in PARP1 activity leads to extreme energy consumption by myocardial cells. Meanwhile, in cardiac injury caused by anti-tumor treatment, the application of PARP inhibitors can improve LVEF and CO in model mice. PARP1 can modify and regulate multiple signaling pathways through PARylatyion, and participate in various activities of cells such as proliferation, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and autophagy. Purpose This study explored whether the PARP inhibitor Olaparib could improve cardiac insufficiency caused by VEGFRI, and demonstrated that PARP1 could mediate the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway through PARylylation dependence, thereby improving CTRCD Methods All mice were randomly divided into the control group, Cediranib group, Cediranib + Olaparib group, and Olaparib group. They were adaptively raised for one week and were respectively given 2ml/kg/day of normal saline, 6mg/kg/d of Cediranib, 6mg/kg/d of Cediranib + 50mg/kg/d of Olaparib. After continuous administration for 35 days, The mice were anesthetized by inhaling 1.0-2.5% isoflurane to collect blood, and the tissues were immediately frozen in liquid nitrogen. Results Proteomics detection revealed the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was significantly altered. Small animal ultrasound indicated that the ejection fraction of mice decreased. HE staining showed that the myocardial tissue was disordered and myocardial cells were damaged. Masson staining showed that collagen fibers in the myocardial interstitium were deposited and myocardial fibrosis occurred. Further Western Blot showed that compared with the control group, the oxidative stress markers SOD1 and OGG1 were significantly increased, and the expression of PARP1 was increased, while the ratios of P-PI3K/PI3K and P-AKT/AKT decreased. Further experiments demonstrated that after treatment with Cediranib combined with the Olaparib, the LVEFof mice did not show a significant decrease. Pathological staining indicated that myocardial damage improved and the degree of fibrosis was reduced, and oxidative stress markers did not show a significant increase. the expression of PARP1 was decreased compared with Cediranib group, while the ratios of P-PI3K/PI3K and P-AKT/AKT increased. Conclusions PARP1 mediates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway through PARylation-dependent to alleviate the myocardial injury.FIG 1
title: PARP1 mediates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway through PARylation-dependent to alleviate the myocardial injury caused by Cediranib

abstract: Abstract Introduction Several studies suggest that cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs) may improve cardiac function by increasing viable myocardial tissue and limiting adverse ventricular remodeling. On the other hand, evidence indicates that the delivery route may modulate the effect of cell therapy. The aim of this study was to comparatively evaluate the efficacy of CDC administration through either the intracoronary (IC) or intrapericardial (IP) route in a porcine model of reperfused myocardial infarction (MI). Methods This blinded, randomized study was approved by the institutional animal care and use committee. Twenty-six female Large White pigs were used to establish a reperfused myocardial infarction via transient occlusion (90 minutes) of the LAD immediately distal to the first diagonal branch. Surviving animals were randomized into three groups: control (n = 8), IC (n = 8), and IP (n = 8). At a mean of 4 days after MI induction, 30 × 10⁶ CDCs were administered via the IC or IP route in the treated groups. Control animals received saline IC (n=4) or IP (n=4). IP administration was performed through a left lateral mini-thoracotomy, and IC delivery via percutaneous femoral artery access. Cardiac function was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), including late gadolinium enhancement, immediately before therapy administration and at 10 weeks. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), indexed end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes (EDVi and ESVi), infarct size, and treatment effects (defined as the change in these parameters from baseline to 10 weeks) were calculated. Values are expressed as mean (S.E.M). Results were compared using Kruskal–Wallis ANOVA and the Mann–Whitney test. Results All animals received therapy or placebo in absence of complications or electrocardiographic abnormalities regardless of the delivery route. The measured CMR parameters are summarized in the table. As no significant differences were observed between control subgroups, control animals were pooled for analysis. At the end of follow-up (10 weeks), LVEF was significantly higher in both treated groups compared with controls (p = 0.04). Similarly, the treatment effect on LVEF (ΔLVEF) differed among the three groups (p = 0.04), due to a significant difference between the control and IP groups. No other significant differences were found among groups in either ventricular volumes or IS, nor were there any additional differences related to the delivery route. Conclusions Administration of 30 × 10⁶ CDCs via either the IP or IC route in a porcine model of reperfused MI may slightly but significantly improve cardiac function compared to placebo, regardless of the delivery route, which suggests that the approach could be tailored to the specific clinical circumstances with equal efficacy.Abstract table
title: Effect of cardiosphere-derived cell administration on cardiac function after myocardial infarction: influence of the delivery route in a relevant porcine model

abstract: Abstract Background Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) is the primary predictor of cardiovascular disease (CVD); nevertheless, several studies in specific populations have indicated that lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) and galectin-3 possess predictive capabilities for CVD. No direct comparative data on LDL, Lp(a), and Galectin-3 in Indonesians exists under specific circumstances. Objective Hence, the study analyses plasma levels of galectin-3, Lp(a), and LDL in secondary prevention patients post percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) to forecast cardiac events. Methods A multicenter prospective cohort conducted in 7 centers in Indonesia. The participants were individuals who had previously undergone an elective PTCA within the past 6 - 24 months. Participants were monitored for 12 months; also, the patients who experienced re-hospitalization and mortality related to CVD during the follow-up period were counted as cardiac events. The values of all predictors are classified into a binary variable with cut-off thresholds of 23.5 ng/mL and 21.95 mg/dL for galectin-3 and Lp(a), respectively, based on the Youden index calculation. Also, the cut-off 55 mg/dL for LDL is based on recent guidelines. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazard regression were employed to estimate the hazard ratio (HR) of the predictors and 13 covariates. The prognostic value between galectin-3 and Lp(a) towards cardiac events was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results Cox proportional hazards regression analysis involving 145 post-PTCA patients across 7 centers in Indonesia indicates that galectin-3 is a considerably superior predictor for assessing the prognosis of cardiac events (HR: 6.70; p: 0.005; 95% CI: 1.8 - 25.2) followed by Lp(a) (HR: 4.72; p:0.022; 95% CI: 1.2 - 17.8). Incongruously, the ability of LDL in assessing a cardiac event in post-PTCA patients is deemed insignificant (HR: 0.68; p:0.56; 95% CI: 0.18 - 2.55). Moreover, the ROC curve showed that galectin-3 had the highest area under the curve (AUC) compared to Lp(a), and LDL with 0.733 (p: 0.004), 0.692 (p: 0.019), and 0.461 (p: 0.675), respectively. Conclusion Galectin-3 and Lp(a) showed a superiority in predicting cardiac events compared to LDL in post-PTCA patients who are undergoing a secondary prevention program in Indonesia.Graphycal Abstract
title: Beyond conventional markers: Navigating the complex prognostic landscape of galectin-3 and Lp(a) in predicting MACE in post-PTCA procedure

abstract: Abstract Introduction Current biomarkers for coronary artery disease (CAD) fail to adequately predict disease progression or recurrent cardiovascular events. The asialoglycoprotein receptor 1 (ASGR1), which clears circulating glycans (sugars), is emerging as a novel regulator of atherosclerosis. The relationship between ASGR1, the glycome and CAD progression remains unexplored. Aim To investigate associations between ASGR1, the N-glycome, and related proteome with coronary atherosclerosis progression in a human cohort with symptomatic CAD. Methods One-hundred CAD patients with residual atheroma were prospectively recruited for simultaneous serial blood biobanking and coronary plaque imaging with serial photon-counting coronary computed tomography angiography (PC-CCTA) and quantitative plaque burden analysis, at baseline and 12-months follow-up. Isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were assessed for: (1) ASGR1 protein by ELISA, (2) their N-glycome and (3) proteome by mass spectrometry. Healthy Control participants (N= 31) were free from atheroma. Plaque progression was defined as a ≥2% in total plaque burden. Results In this high-risk cohort, with median age 62 years, 76% male, 85% recent acute coronary syndrome, 95% on statins at follow-up, serial PC-CCTA revealed dynamic responsiveness of residual coronary atheroma one-year after invasive angiography (Figure 1). 39% of patients were plaque Progressors, 32% had Stable disease and 29% were Regressors. Clinical risk factors and baseline or achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels did not differ between Regressors or Progressors. However, higher ASGR1 protein levels demonstrated a positive trend with CAD progression (median in Healthy 0.096 ng/mL, Regressors 0.091 ng/mL, Stable 0.098 ng/mL, Progressors 0.138 ng/mL; P-trend = 0.031) (Figure 2). A doubly-sialylated N-glycan (S2F1.a) was overexpressed in CAD versus Healthy Control PBMCs, which remained elevated in Progressors (Figure 3). Two oligomannose N-glycans were also lower in the Progressors compared to Healthy Controls (Figure 3). Accompanying proteomics revealed 363 differentially regulated proteins between Healthy Controls versus CAD (Figure 4) with metabolic and inflammatory patterns with mechanistic links to CAD pathobiology (Figure 5). Amongst the individual significant proteins in CAD patients, a protein phosphatase-regulator and autophagy-promoter, Immunoglobulin Binding Protein 1, was downregulated relative to Healthy Controls (Figure 6). In another comparison Thymosin beta-4 was upregulated in Regressors, relative to Progressors, at baseline. Conclusions Although clinical factors did not differentiate coronary atheroma progression status on quantitative PC-CCTA, differences were identified in PBMC ASGR1, their N-glycome and proteome. Our multi-omics findings implicate ASGR1 and the glycome as new biomarkers of CAD progression, and highlights known proteins as ready therapeutic targets.Picture 1Picture 2
title: The asialoglycoprotein receptor 1, the glycome, and proteome associate with coronary atherosclerosis progression on serial photon-counting coronary computed tomography angiography

abstract: Abstract The aftermath that acute myocardial infarction patients have to face is one that includes significant clinical repercussions that affect their quality of life. Our objetive was to identify circulating proteomic biomarkers that characterize and improve the prognosis of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), using a profiled panel of molecules with special focus on the advanced glycation end-products and their receptor (AGE/RAGE axis) and Galectin-3. 108 consecutive STEMI patients were classified according to relevant clinical variables. Blood samples were obtained within the first 24 hours post-AMI, and plasma proteins were quantified using SWATH mass spectrometry following trypsin digestion. Data analysis aimed to identify proteins differentially expressed between groups and the metabolic pathways involved, using open-source tools. Plasma sRAGE and Galectin-3 levels were measured by ELISA. Our results provide a molecular description of the patient, indicating which metabolic pathways gain greater relevance and which proteins emerge as potential biomarkers. The groups of worse clinical profile showed an increase in proteins related to the AGE/RAGE axis, particularly reflected in plasma sRAGE concentrations, which rose in parallel with Killip class. sRAGE and Galectin-3 measurements allowed stratification into quartiles, with the highest quartiles associated with a proteomic profile indicative of greater oxidative stress and cellular damage. Moreover, sRAGE and Galectin-3 correlated with validated clinical variables: GRACE (Galectin-3: r=0.288, p=0.017; sRAGE: r=0.354, p=0.004), troponin peak (Galectin-3: r=0.295, p=0.008; sRAGE: r=0.239, p=0.036) and NT-proBNP (Galectin-3: r=0.282, p=0.012; sRAGE: r=0.237, p=0.039). The findings align with previous knowledge regarding the AGE/RAGE axis and Galectin-3 and their roles in the pathophysiology of the post-STEMI setting, and they lay the groundwork for future studies aimed at validating and expanding their potential as prognostic and therapeutic tools at the AMI onset.Flowchart abstract
title: Profiling STEMI: improving prognosis through proteomic analysis

abstract: Abstract Background Patients at high bleeding risk (HBR, approximately 30% of the PCI population) continue to pose the challenge of achieving an optimal balance between ischemic and bleeding events. Safely reducing the duration or even the need for dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) has therefore emerged as a critical unmet need. A CD31 endothelial-mimetic coating, utilizing SP1072,—a 16-amino-acid peptide replicating a key motif in CD31 domain mediating trans-homophilic interactions essential for blood homeostasis—creates a biomimetic surface that potentially restores anti-thrombo-inflammatory signaling . Purpose Mechanical, morphometric and physiological performances of the SP1072-coated cobalt-chromium stent CD31 stent was compared with a contemporary everolimus-eluting stent and a bare metal stent (BMS, L605 cobalt chromium) in a healthy porcine coronary model, using both angiography and optical coherence tomography (OCT) post procedure and at 28 days. Methods Fifteen CD31-coated stents ,4 DES and 5BMS were implanted in the left anterior descending (LAD,n=9), left circumflex (LCX,n=6), and right coronary artery (RCA,n=9) of nine pigs. At implantation balloon artery ratio (BAR) as a surrogate for baro-trauma and acute mechanical recoil were computed from Quantitative coronary angiography (QCA). Post implantation and at 28 days. Quantitative Flow Ratio (QFR) and QCA (Diameter Stenosis, DS and Minimal Lumen Diameter, MLD) derived from angiography as well as Minimal Luminal Area (MLA)derived from OCT were analyzed at an independent Corelab ( CORRIB lab of the University of Galway ,Ireland ) Results At implantation, BAR averaged 1.16 (SD, 0.09) for BMS, 1.14 (0.06) for CD31, and 1.19 (0.08) for DES (ANOVA, p = 0.34). Acute recoil was similar amongst groups (BMS: 4.00 [4.33] %, CD31: 5.47[1.95] %) and DES: 6.03 [1.96] %, p = 0.48). At 28 days, minimal luminal area on OCT was comparable (BMS: 4.21 [0.60], CD31: 4.49 [1.33], DES: 4.78 [1.05], p=0.66). DS, MLD, QFR and the correlation between DS and QFR is presented are presented in figure 1. Conclusion In this study of healthy porcine coronary arteries, CD31-coated stents ,DES and BMS were exposed to similar baro-trauma and exhibited comparable acute recoil. At 28 days in this small exploratory pilot study the 3 stents showed comparable minimal luminal area with OCT,did not exhibit binary restenosis (DS&gt;50%) or flow limitation below the threshold of QFR&lt;0.80.These preliminary results mandated further experimentation in restenotic and atherosclerotic porcine model.figure 1
title: Coronary porcine studies of mechanical, morphometric, and physiological performance based on OCT /angiography of CD31-endothelial-mimetic coating stent, drug-eluting stent and bare metal stent

abstract: Abstract Background The Variable Loop Circular Catheter (VLCC) is a pulsed-field ablation (PFA) device for treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF) that has demonstrated a favorable safety and efficacy profile in clinical use. A novel pulse protocol, Sequence 2, which shortens ablation delivery from the ~20.6 second pulse delivery of Sequence 1 to ~3.8 seconds, is untested for its ability to be safe under excessive use conditions. Because the shorter delivery time increases instantaneous pulse density, it is pertinent to assess if Sequence 2 creates a risk of focal electrode heating or energy stacking during repeated applications. Purpose The objective of this study was to assess the safety and efficacy of the new VLCC Sequence 2 pulse recipe, when used outside the bounds of the recommended clinical workflow. Methods A total of eight porcine subjects were randomized into two test groups: 2X nominal dose and 4X nominal dose, corresponding to two or four consecutive PFA applications per site, respectively. PFA was performed with intentional lesion stacking and nominal electrode irrigation (30ml/min). Subsequent coronary angiography, blood chemistry panels, and evaluation of VLCC electrode charring was also performed. Animals were survived for 30±3 days post ablation to undergo follow-up remapping procedures before being euthanized to allow for gross necropsy and histopathology. Results For all animals, 100% acute and chronic effectiveness was observed for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). Safety metrics were met, no incidence of phrenic nerve injury, esophageal injury, or catheter charring were observed. Transient asymptomatic coronary spasm could be induced and was detected following cavotricuspid ablation in both the 2X and 4X dose groups, whereas spasm following mitral isthmus ablation only occurred in the 2X group. All coronary spasms resolved following administration of a nitroglycerin dose and no hemodynamic compromise was observed. The 4X group exhibited greater transient increases in hemolysis (e.g., plasma-free hemoglobin, LDH) and myocardial injury markers (e.g., CK/troponins) compared with the 2X group, with all values returning to or near baseline by the survival endpoint. The 4X treatment group showed more marked changes in hemolysis and myocardial injury markers than the 2X treatment group, with all markers returning to or near baseline by the survival endpoint (Figure 1). Conclusion In this study, Sequence 2 maintained a favorable safety profile even when applied at 2X and 4X nominal dosing with no evidence of charring or excessive electrode heating at nominal irrigation and only transient elevations in hemolysis and myocardial injury markers. PFA applications near coronary arteries, under these excessive use conditions, resulted in self-limiting spasm. These findings suggest that the accelerated pulse protocol preserves PFA’s non-thermal safety characteristics and remains well-tolerated even during excessive use conditions.Figure 1
title: A faster, optimized pulsed field timing sequence demonstrates safety under aggressive lesion stacking without evidence of electrode heating

abstract: Abstract Background Inter-individual variability in LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains incompletely explained. Although pharmacogenetic variation has been proposed as a determinant of atorvastatin response, the role of acute inflammatory burden in the setting of STEMI is less well defined. Purpose To evaluate clinical and genetic determinants of LDL-C reduction 6 months after STEMI. Methods We studied 93 consecutive STEMI patients with lipid assessment at baseline and 6 months. Absolute LDL-C reduction (ΔLDL = LDL₆M − LDL_baseline) and achievement of ESC guideline targets were analysed. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models included baseline LDL-C, age, sex, smoking status, statin intensity, and preprocedural white blood cell count (WBC). Comprehensive genetic profiling (&gt;300 lipid- and pharmacokinetic-related variants) was assessed using candidate gene scores, genetic burden models, unsupervised clustering, and penalized regression (Elastic Net with nested cross-validation). Results Median LDL-C reduction was −1.49 mmol/L (range −4.09 to −0.01). However, 33% of patients failed to achieve ≥30% LDL reduction, 19% showed an absolute reduction of &lt;1.0 mmol/L, and 44% remained above 1.4 mmol/L at 6 months. Baseline LDL-C was the strongest predictor of LDL reduction (β = −0.511, p &lt; 0.001). Importantly, preprocedural WBC independently predicted an attenuated LDL response (β = +0.069 per 1×10⁹/L increase, p &lt; 0.001), with the model explaining 42.6% of the variability in ΔLDL (R² = 0.426). WBC consistently predicted poor response across all definitions (e.g., OR 1.16 for &lt;30% reduction, p = 0.004). In contrast, none of the genetic approaches improved prediction beyond that provided by clinical variables (all p &gt; 0.60). No stable genetic signature of impaired statin response was identified. Conclusion In STEMI patients, systemic inflammatory burden at presentation independently predicts attenuated LDL-C reduction at 6 months, whereas extensive genetic variation does not. These findings support a state-dependent, inflammation-modulated model of lipid-lowering response in acute coronary disease.
title: Inflammatory burden, but not genetic variation, predicts attenuated LDL cholesterol reduction after ST-elevation myocardial infarction

abstract: Abstract Background Permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and preoperative identification of high-risk patients is crucial for clinical decision-making. Most existing PPI prediction models after TAVR focus on clinical, echocardiographic and procedural factors, while the value of electrocardiographic (ECG) indicators remains under-explored. This study aimed to establish and validate a clinical prediction scoring model for PPI after TAVR integrating ECG indicators. Methods A total of 157 TAVR patients were enrolled and stratified by PPI status (No PPI, n=136; PPI, n=21). Univariate analysis (P&lt;0.1) screened variables, and multivariate Logistic regression identified independent PPI predictors. A clinical prediction scoring system was built based on the regression coefficients of these predictors, with patients stratified into low-, medium-, and high-risk groups by total score. The model was evaluated using ROC and calibration curves. Results Univariate analysis identified 15 variables with P&lt;0.05. Multivariate Logistic regression showed that valve implantation depth (OR=1.430, 95%CI:1.092–1.915, P=0.011), aortic valve peak velocity (OR=0.994, 95%CI:0.989–0.998, P=0.003), DIIISA (an ECG parameter, OR=4.055, 95%CI:1.375–12.870, P=0.011), moderate/severe aortic regurgitation (AR) (OR=6.215, 95%CI:1.463–39.193, P=0.025), and prosthetic valve size (OR=0.616, 95%CI:0.432–0.830, P=0.003) were independent predictors of PPI. Height (OR=0.938, 95%CI:0.866–1.010, P=0.099) was retained due to its clinical relevance despite marginal significance. The clinical prediction scoring model was constructed by converting regression coefficients into integer weights: valve implantation depth (+2 points/SD increase), DIIISA (an ECG parameter, +8 points/SD increase), moderate/severe AR (+10 points if present), prosthetic valve size (-3 points/SD increase), while aortic valve peak velocity and height had no contribution (scoring weight=0). Patients were stratified into three risk groups based on the total score (-3 to 20 points, calculated after continuous variable standardization): low-risk (≤5 points, PPI risk &lt;20%), medium-risk (6–12 points, PPI risk 20%–50%), and high-risk (≥13 points, PPI risk &gt;50%). The model showed good discrimination (AUC=0.8697, sensitivity=76.19%, specificity=86.03%) and calibration (mean absolute error=0.023). Conclusions The constructed clinical prediction scoring model for PPI after TAVR, which innovatively integrates ECG indicators (mainly DIIISA) with valve implantation depth, moderate/severe AR, and prosthetic valve size, has good discrimination and calibration. Stratifying patients into low-, medium-, and high-risk groups by total score, it facilitates preoperative PPI risk stratification clinically, helps clinicians formulate individual prevention strategies, and fills the gap of insufficient ECG application in existing PPI prediction models.Figure
title: Development of a risk stratification model for permanent pacemaker implantation after Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR)

abstract: Abstract Background Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is frequent after cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse outcomes 1. After surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) for aortic stenosis, POAF may be particularly common, potentially reflecting an aortic stenosis-related atrial substrate beyond perioperative triggers alone 2. We compared the incidence, predictors, and prognostic implications of new-onset POAF after SAVR versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Purpose To (i) quantify the incidence and independent predictors of new-onset POAF after SAVR ±CABG using isolated CABG as comparator, and (ii) evaluate the association between POAF and long-term survival after each surgery. Methods In this prospective cohort study, consecutive adults undergoing cardiac surgery at a tertiary center (2013-2021) were screened (n=6,181). Patients with preoperative atrial fibrillation ([AF]; n=898), severe aortic regurgitation (n=281), or concomitant non-SAVR/non-CABG procedures (n=714) were excluded. The final cohort included 4,288 patients: SAVR group (n=1,830; isolated SAVR n=821; SAVR+CABG n=1,009) and isolated CABG (n=2,458). POAF was defined as new-onset AF or flutter within 30 days post intervention. Predictors were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Long-term survival was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier and surgery-specific Cox proportional hazards model. Results Median age was 72 (66-77) years in the SAVR group (28% women) and 68 (61-64) years in the CABG group (22% women). POAF occurred in 1,881 (44%) patients and was more frequent after isolated SAVR (47.7%) and SAVR+CABG (52.7%) than isolated CABG (38.9%; p&lt;0.001. Compared with CABG, SAVR remained independently associated with higher POAF risk (isolated SAVR: odds ratio [OR] 1.28, 95% CI 1.04-1.57, p=0.01; SAVR+CABG: OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53, p=0.02). Additional predictors included age (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.04-1.06, p&lt;0.001), female sex (OR 0.80; 95% CI 0.68-0.93, p=0.003), and red blood cell (RBC) transfusion (OR 1.05 per unit, 95% CI 1.00-1.09, p=0.03). POAF was associated with an increased risk of mortality in all groups (p&lt;0.01). After adjustment for age, sex, EuroSCORE II, CHA2DS2-VA and perioperative RBC transfusion, POAF remained significantly associated with mortality in SAVR (isolated SAVR: hazards ratio [HR] 1.58; 95% CI 1.04-2.40, p=0.03 ; AVR+CABG: HR 1.46; 95% CI 1.10-1.94, p=0.008), but not after isolated CABG (HR 1.27, 95% CI 0.96-1.47; p=0.07). Conclusions In this study, SAVR conferred higher risk of new-onset POAF compared to isolated CABG, consistent with an intrinsic atrial susceptibility beyond shared perioperative stressors. POAF was independently associated with mortality after SAVR while not after isolated CABG. These findings support POAF as a marker for aortic stenosis-related atrial myopathy and suggest that intensified prevention and long-term surveillance, particularly after SAVR.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Postoperative atrial fibrillation as a marker of atrial myopathy in aortic stenosis: a prospective surgical cohort analysis

abstract: Abstract Introduction Reported new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) incidence following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) varies widely, likely reflecting disease severity and differences in monitoring intensity. Robust data on post-STEMI AF burden is needed to guide therapeutic decisions, such as initiation of anticoagulants. Purpose We therefore aimed to assess the incidence, timing, and burden of NOAF after STEMI using systematic 14-day continuous ECG patch monitoring. Methods Consecutive patients presenting with STEMI at a Swiss tertiary center were prospectively enrolled and prescribed a 14-day single-lead ECG patch. Patients with known AF prior to STEMI or implanted cardiac devices with an atrial lead were excluded. Results Among 265 STEMI admissions, 182 patients (69%; median age 66 years; 26% female) underwent patch monitoring. Median analyzable monitoring duration was 13.6 days [IQR 13.2–13.8]. NOAF was detected in 11/182 patients (6.0%; median age 76 years; 27% female). Ten patients (91%) had paroxysmal AF and one (9%) persistent AF. Median AF burden was 2.72% [0.79–10.86], corresponding to a mean AF duration of 39 minutes per day. First AF detection occurred after a median of 44 hours [1.4 - 95] of monitoring. Patients with NOAF were older than those without AF (76 vs 65 years; p=0.004). Median CHA₂DS₂-VA score in NOAF patients was 4 [4–5]. Oral anticoagulation in addition to antiplatelet therapy was initiated in 9 of 11 patients (82%). Conclusion In this prospective cohort of STEMI patients, 14-day ECG patch monitoring identified NOAF in 6.0% of patients, mainly within the first two days. Despite a high thromboembolic risk profile, AF burden was generally low, highlighting the unresolved question of whether oral anticoagulation benefits outweigh bleeding risk in low-burden NOAF detected after STEMI. Further studies are warranted to define burden-informed anticoagulation strategies in this population.Graphical Abstract
title: Incidence and burden of new-onset atrial fibrillation after STEMI detected by 14-day ECG patch monitoring

abstract: Abstract Background Ambulatory long term ECG monitoring after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) enables detection of arrhythmias that may otherwise remain underdiagnosed. While post-procedural conduction disturbances have been extensively studied, less attention has been directed toward the occurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmias after hospital discharge. Purpose The precise incidence and temporal distribution of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) during the in-hospital phase and after discharge remain insufficiently characterized. Methods Adult patients undergoing TAVI at a Swiss tertiary centre were prospectively monitored using a 14-days ambulatory ECG patch applied prior to discharge. Patients were instructed to report any cardiac symptoms using the patch-reporting-system. NOAF was defined as AF episodes ≥ 30 seconds in patients without documented AF. Results A total of 307 patients underwent 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring after TAVI (median age 82 years [78–86], 57% male). The median analyzable monitoring time was 13.3 days [11.5–13.8]. Atrial fibrillation was detected in 82 patients (27%), of whom 15 patients (5%) had NOAF. Among patients with NOAF, 12 (80%) were diagnosed exclusively through ambulatory patch monitoring after discharge, whereas 3 patients (20%) were diagnosed during in-hospital telemetry monitoring. In those diagnosed by ambulatory monitoring, the first AF episode occurred at a median of 6 days [2–10] after initiation of monitoring. Thirteen patients (87%) had paroxysmal AF and two (13%) had persistent AF. The median AF burden was 3% [1–12]. Only five patients (33%) reported symptoms temporally associated with AF episodes. The CHA₂DS₂-VA score was ≥2 in 14 patients (93%). Detection of NOAF led to a change from antiplatelet therapy to oral anticoagulation in four patients (27%) and initiation or adjustment of antiarrhythmic therapy in seven patients (47%). Conclusions NOAF occurs in a small but clinically relevant proportion of patients undergoing TAVI, with the majority of cases remaining undetected during hospitalization. These findings underscore the importance of structured post-discharge rhythm surveillance to identify clinically actionable AF in this high-risk population.Graphical Abstract
title: Time to new-onset atrial fibrillation after transaortic valve implantation using 14-days ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring

abstract: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) in younger adults is a highly heterogeneous condition, encompassing a broad clinical spectrum and associated with markedly different cardiovascular outcomes. Purpose We aimed to identify distinct clinical–echocardiographic phenotypes of AF in patients aged &lt;65 years and to evaluate their associations with adverse outcomes across large European and Asian cohorts. Methods We analysed patients aged &lt;65 years enrolled in the European (EORP-AF) and Asian (APHRS-AF) registries.
