Latent Class Analysis (LCA) integrating demographic, cardiovascular, and echocardiographic variables was performed to identify clinical phenotypes. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and thromboembolic events (TEE). Associations between phenotype membership and outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional-hazards models, with the low-risk class serving as the reference group. Results Among 2,547 patients, LCA identified three distinct phenotypes: Class 1 – Cardiometabolic–Early Remodelling (40%) included middle-aged, overweight patients (median age 60 years, BMI 27 kg/m²) with a high prevalence of hypertension (77%), dyslipidaemia (44%), and diabetes (19%), but largely preserved systolic function (LVEF 60%) and normal chamber dimensions. Class 2 – Low-Risk Normal Structure (28%) comprised the youngest participants (median age 52 years, 79% male) with minimal comorbidities (hypertension 5%, diabetes &lt;1%), normal LV and LA size, and the lowest CHA₂DS₂-VASc and HAS-BLED scores; this phenotype was more common among Asian patients (53%). Class 3 – High-Risk Cardiomyopathic (32%) included predominantly European patients (80%) with advanced structural remodelling, enlarged LV and LA (LVEDD 56 mm; LA 48 mm), reduced systolic function (LVEF 45%), and frequent heart failure (70%) or coronary artery disease (33%), representing an overtly remodelled and high-risk phenotype. Compared with the Low-Risk Normal Structure, High-Risk Cardiomyopathic showed markedly higher risk for the composite outcome (HR 4.49, 95% CI 2.37–8.52), MACE (HR 3.76, 95% CI 1.90–7.44), all-cause death (HR 14.23, 95% CI 3.43–59.12), and ACS (HR 2.56, 95% CI 1.03–6.39). Cardiometabolic–Early Remodelling exhibited intermediate risk across all endpoints. Conclusions Three reproducible AF phenotypes emerged, spanning from idiopathic to cardiometabolic and cardiomyopathic forms associated with worsening outcomes. These findings emphasize the clinical heterogeneity of AF and the value of phenotype-driven risk stratification.Baseline characteristics across LCAKaplan–Meier curves for the composite outcome
title: Clinical phenotypes and echocardiographic profiles in young patients with atrial fibrillation: insights from european and asian cohorts

abstract: Abstract Background New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is a frequent complication following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and is associated with prolonged hospitalisation and adverse outcomes. Existing clinical risk scores have shown variable performance in surgical populations. Improved pre-operative risk stratification may facilitate targeted preventive strategies. Purpose To develop and externally validate a transportable pre-operative prediction model for NOAF after CABG. As a secondary objective, we assessed whether adding intraoperative variables improved predictive performance. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing isolated CABG were identified from a Polish CABG cohort (development set). Patients with prior atrial fibrillation, active endocarditis during index hospitalisation, or concomitant mitral valve repair/replacement were excluded. The primary outcome was NOAF, defined by documented atrial fibrillation during postoperative monitoring during index hospitalisation. Candidate predictors included routinely available pre-operative demographic, clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables. Model discrimination was assessed using cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and compared with established clinical risk scores (POAF score and CHA₂DS₂-VASc). The final model was refitted on the full development cohort and externally validated in an independent external CABG cohort. In a secondary analysis, intraoperative variables(off-pump CABG status, extracorporeal circulation time, and aortic clamping time) were added to assess incremental predictive value. Results The development cohort included 4,810 patients (mean age 65.2 ± 8.6 years; 26.1% female), of whom 17.8% developed NOAF. A penalised logistic regression model with 10 pre-operative predictors demonstrated the highest cross-validated discrimination (AUC 0.651 ± 0.030), outperforming the POAF score (AUC 0.61) and CHA₂DS₂-VASc score (AUC 0.59). In the final model, increasing age (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.05–1.08), left atrial dimension (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.25–1.77), heart failure (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.08–1.91), and male sex (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.08–1.55) were independently associated with POAF. External validation demonstrated preserved discrimination (AUC 0.692). In secondary analysis, adding intraoperative variables provided modest incremental improvement (internal AUC 0.655±0.029; external AUC 0.697). Conclusion A pre-operative prediction model for NOAF after CABG outperformed established clinical risk scores. Discrimination was preserved in external validation. The addition of intraoperative variables provided only modest incremental improvement, supporting the clinical utility of pre-operative risk stratification.Forest Plot for NOAFPerformance and Clinical Utility
title: Development and external validation of a pre-operative prediction model for new-onset atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting

abstract: Abstract Introduction Since atrial fibrillation (AF) is strongly associated with ischemic stroke, the CHA2DS2-VASc score is the commonly used scale for stroke risk stratification. However, the conventional angiographic threshold of ≥50% stenosis may not reliably represent meaningful coronary artery disease (CAD), as intermediate stenosis is often discordant with hemodynamic significance. Given that the CHA2DS2-VASc score was derived from a Danish cohort, the definition of CAD used for the vascular component should account for regional variation, particularly in East Asia; in the context of the East Asian Paradox. Purpose This study aimed to validate whether this predictive association is optimal in East Asian population. Methods We identified 27,964 patients who underwent cardiac computed tomography or invasive coronary angiography between 2006 and 2025. From this cohort, a total of 2,898 patients were included who had AF without history of myocardial infarction, angina and previous percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary endpoint was the ischemic stroke incidence within 3 years after the baseline, classified by coronary artery stenosis (CAS) severity: None (0%), mild (1–49%), moderate (50–69%), and severe (≥70%). To reduce confounding, inverse probability weighting was applied, and the risks were estimated using Cox hazards models. Results The 3-year ischemic stroke incidence demonstrated a significant increasing trend across stenosis grades: None 5.6%, mild 4.3%, moderate 7.9%, severe 9.7% (trend p &lt; 0.001). The stroke incidence curves among non-severe groups did not differ significantly (minimum log-rank p = 0.292), whereas the severe group curve diverged significantly (moderate vs. severe: log-rank p &lt; 0.001). Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for the primary endpoint were: mild 0.90 (95% CI 0.68-1.18; p = 0.431); moderate 1.16 (95% CI 0.89-1.50; p = 0.275); severe 1.48 (95% CI 1.12-1.95; p = 0.005). Modifying the CAS threshold from ≥50% to ≥70% within the CHA2DS2-VASc framework improved specificity by +4.93 percentage points (from 0.137 to 0.187, a 35.9% relative increase; 95% CI +4.29 to +5.57 pp; p &lt; 0.001), while the sensitivity slightly declined by -2.03 percentage points (from 0.923 to 0.902; 95% CI -3.51 to -0.55 pp; p = 0.013), for the oral anticoagulation recommendation. Conclusion The non-severe CAS (&lt;70%) did not significantly increase the ischemic stroke risk in East Asian patients with AF. Aligning with the East Asian Paradox, where higher bleeding risks emphasizes greater diagnostic specificity, raising the CAS threshold to ≥70% may refine anticoagulation strategies. Further investigation into the net clinical benefit of this modification, explicitly considering bleeding risk, is warranted.CAD_figure
title: Association between ischemic stroke and coronary artery disease severity in patients with atrial fibrillation: big data evidence supporting a regional paradox

abstract: Abstract Background Major bleeding (MB) is a serious complication in anticoagulated patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The prognostic implications of bleeding occurrence and anatomical location in this high-risk population remain insufficiently characterised. Purpose To investigate clinical outcomes after MB in anticoagulated patients with AF after TAVI. Methods ENVISAGE-TAVI AF (NCT02943785) was a randomised trial comparing edoxaban with vitamin K antagonist therapy in patients with AF following successful TAVI. This post hoc analysis included 1377 patients from the trial safety population who received at least one dose of the study drug. Patients were stratified by the occurrence of on-treatment MB and bleeding location (gastrointestinal [GI], intracranial, or non-GI/non-intracranial), as defined by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis. Outcomes included all-cause death, net adverse clinical events, major adverse cardiovascular events, cardiovascular death, ischaemic stroke/systemic embolic events, intracranial haemorrhage (ICH), and recurrent MB. Results Of 1377 patients, 138 (10.0%) had at least one on-treatment MB event. Patients with MB more frequently presented with a history of recent percutaneous coronary intervention (9.4% vs 4.0%, P = 0.008), abnormal renal function (4.3% vs 1.5%, P = 0.03), higher mean HAS-BLED scores (1.9 vs 1.5, P &lt;0.001), edoxaban assignment (60.9% vs 49.1%, P = 0.009), and hypercholesterolaemia (80.4% vs 68.4%, P = 0.003) at randomisation than those without MB. Fatal outcomes of MB events were most frequent with ICH and uncommon with GI or non-GI/non-ICH bleeding, with no meaningful differences between treatment arms (Figure 1A). Annualised all-cause mortality was markedly higher in patients with vs without on-treatment MB (40.29%/year vs 6.60%/year; hazard ratio [HR], 5.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.00–8.13), with similar higher risk for cardiovascular death (HR, 6.68; 95% CI, 4.18–10.68). Similar patterns were observed with the other clinical outcomes (Figure 2). Within one year of a first on-treatment MB event, recurrent MB was most frequent after GI bleeding, intermediate after non-GI/non-ICH bleeding, and rare after non-fatal ICH, with similar patterns across treatment arms (Figure 1B). Conclusions In anticoagulated patients with AF after TAVI, MB was associated with a worse prognosis. GI bleeding identified patients at high risk for recurrence, while ICH conferred the greatest early mortality risk.
title: Prognostic associations of major bleeding in anticoagulated patients with atrial fibrillation after TAVI: a post hoc analysis of the ENVISAGE-TAVI AF trial

abstract: Abstract Background Data on the benefit of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who experience stroke despite chronic oral anticoagulation (OAC) are limited and not always consistent. Aim To evaluate the association between LAAO and recurrent stroke or mortality using a pre-post LAAO study design accounting for recurrent events, comparing event rates before and after LAAO, each patient serving as their own control. Methods In this retrospective cohort study from two tertiary French centers, only patients undergoing LAAO for AF-related stroke despite well conducted OAC were included. The primary outcome was incidence of the composite of recurrent ischemic stroke and/or all-cause death during follow-up. Ischemic stroke rates during the 5-year pre-procedure period were compared with primary outcome after LAAO until last follow-up using a quasi-Poisson regression model. This model analyzed the number of events over time while accounting for potential overdispersion (variance not equal to the incidence rate) and adjusting for individual exposure time through a patient-level offset. Results Between 2012 and 2024, 60 patients were included (median age 75 [71-83], male 61.7%]). Prior to LAAO, patients experienced 104 AF-related strokes (mean annualized incidence 0.37 [0.26-0.39] per patient). After LAAO and over a follow-up of 3.5[0.9-6.5] years, 18 recurrences of stroke and 17 deaths occurred (primary outcome mean annualized incidence 0.15[0.10-0.20] per patient). Using a quasi-Poisson regression model, LAAO was associated with a reduction of recurrent stroke or death (RR 0.46 (95% CI 0.24–0.85), p=0.01). Conclusion In this observational cohort of patients with AF-related stroke despite OAC, LAAO was associated with a marked reduction in recurrent stroke or death comparing pre and post-LAAO periods. Dedicated randomized controlled trials are warranted in this population.Graphical abstract
title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for atrial fibrillation–related stroke despite chronic oral anticoagulation

abstract: Abstract Background The temporal sequence of heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) onset may represent different pathophysiological trajectories. Whether this chronology is associated with multi-organ outcomes has not been well defined. Methods Using a large federated electronic health record network (TriNetX), patients with both HF and non-valvular AF were categorized according to onset sequence (HF→AF or AF→HF). Two temporal cohorts were constructed requiring ≥1-month separation between HF and AF diagnoses to minimize misclassification of concurrent events. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for demographics and major comorbidities. Five-year outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. Landmark sensitivity analyses (3 months–5 years and 1–5 years) were conducted to account for early competing risk. Stratified analyses were performed by anticoagulant class (direct oral anticoagulant [DOAC] vs vitamin K antagonist [VKA]).The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major adverse kidney events (MAKE), stroke, and overall dementia (including Alzheimer’s disease, vascular dementia, and unspecified dementia). Results Before PSM, 111,254 patients were HF-first (72.9 ±12.7 years; 42.5% female) and 222,938 were AF-first (75.8 ± 11.2 years; 57.3% female). After PSM, in the primary 0–5-year analysis, the HF→AF trajectory was associated with higher risks of all-cause death (aHR 1.180, 95% CI 1.161-1.200), MACE (1.080, 1.049-1.111), and MAKE (1.198, 1.130-1.270), whereas the association with overall dementia was modest (1.026, 0.984-1.069). Estimates remained consistent after exclusion of early deaths and landmark restriction [Figure1]. In anticoagulant-stratified analyses, chronology-associated risk gradients for stroke, vascular dementia, and MAKE were attenuated among DOAC users (vascular dementia aHR 0.929, 95% CI 0.796-1.085) but more pronounced among VKA users (1.747, 1.351-2.258) [Figure 2]. Conclusion The clinical chronology of HF and AF onset is associated with distinct multi-organ risk profiles. These trajectory-associated gradients appear attenuated among DOAC users but more pronounced among VKA users, indicating differential modification of trajectory-associated risk by anticoagulant class.HF_AF_Chronology_MultiOrgan_RiskHF_AF_Chronology_Anticoagulant_modification
title: Clinical trajectories of heart failure and atrial fibrillation onset influence multi-organ risks: an analysis from a global federated research network

abstract: Abstract Introduction Catheter ablation treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF) induces controlled myocardial injury to the pulmonary veins. This targeted injury initiates a wound-healing response involving fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling. Remodelling of collagen type III and VI may indicate a persistent wound-healing response rather than physiological scar formation. Purpose In this study, we investigated changes in circulating biomarkers of collagen III and collagen VI formation in individuals with AF that underwent ablation to characterize the ECM remodelling response and explore their potential as indicators of post-procedural fibrosis. Methods Levels of collagen type III formation (PRO-C3) and collagen type VI turnover (PRO-C6) were quantified with enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays in serum samples of 276 individuals diagnosed with AF that underwent catheter ablation. Differences in serum levels of the biomarkers preoperative and 12 months post-ablation between paroxysmal and persistent AF and in individuals with and without heart failure, ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and diabetes were assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Biomarker changes from baseline to follow-up were compared between individuals with and without AF recurrence using linear mixed models. To assess the biomarker associations with AF recurrence during the first year after ablation unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression models were used. Results Levels of circulating PRO-C3 and PRO-C6 increased significantly post-ablation (p&lt;0.001, for both markers). Individuals who experienced AF recurrence had higher increase in post-ablation PRO-C3 and PRO-C6 levels from baseline compared to those without AF recurrence (p=0.003 and p=0.008, respectively). PRO-C3 levels were more elevated in individuals with persistent AF (p=0.018). PRO-C6 levels were more elevated in individuals with hypertension (p=0.04) and diabetes mellitus (p=0.03). Baseline levels of the markers were not associated with risk of AF recurrence, while post-ablation levels of PRO-C3 and PRO-C6 were associated to AF recurrence (OR 3.0, [1.4-6.7], p=0.006 and OR 2.6 [1.1-6.0], p=0.026, respectively). After adjustment for age and sex, only PRO-C3 levels remained associated to AF recurrence (OR 2.8 [1.3-6.4], p=0.012). Conclusion The association between AF recurrence and higher levels of circulating PRO-C3 and PRO-C6 12 months post-ablation, and the greater post-ablation increase from baseline of these biomarkers in individuals who suffered AF recurrence, suggest that these biomarkers may reflect excessive activation of fibroblasts following the ablation scarring procedure. Although physiological scarring is necessary for successful ablation procedure, AF recurrence might be driven by overactive fibrosis. Measuring PRO-C3 and PRO-C6 may help identify patients who develop excessive scarring and could benefit from antifibrotic treatment after ablation.
title: Elevated formation of collagen type III and VI after ablation reflects recurrence of atrial fibrillation

abstract: Abstract Background New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is associated with poor outcomes, including death and stroke (1, 2). It would therefore be useful to risk stratify patients before TAVI to guide post-TAVI surveillance and clinical care. We have recently shown the FIND-AF machine learning algorithm can accurately predict short-term AF from primary care electronic health records (EHR) but its utility in the setting of post-TAVI NOAF is yet to be evaluated (3). Purpose To explore whether it is feasible and beneficial to use the FIND-AF machine learning algorithm to predict NOAF and all-cause mortality in the one year following TAVI using pre-TAVI patient characteristics. Methods We retrospectively analysed the electronic health record (EHR) data at a single tertiary cardiology centre to identify patients ≥ 18 years old without prior AF who underwent TAVI between 3rd January 2023 and 27th December 2023. Risk scores were assigned to patients using the FIND-AF machine learning algorithm. Scores &gt; 90th centile were deemed high-risk. The primary outcome was NOAF, which was defined as a new AF diagnosis coded on hospital or primary care electronic health records at one year following TAVI. The exploratory outcome was all-cause mortality within one year of TAVI. Mantel-Haenszel tests were used to compare outcomes between the low-risk and high-risk groups with the former being the reference group. The negative predictive value (NPV) and positive predictive value (PPV) of a high FIND-AF risk category for NOAF after TAVI was also calculated. Results There were 247 patients identified (223 [90.3%] low-risk and 24 [9.7%] high-risk). Compared to the low-risk group, the high-risk group were older with a higher prevalence of multiple valve disease and heart failure (Table 1). Baseline AS severity was similar between groups. The primary outcome occurred in ten (4.5%) low-risk patients and one (4.2%) high-risk patient (HR 0.932; 95% CI: 0.127 to 6.855; p = 0.707). Twelve (5.4%) low-risk and two (8.3%) high-risk patients experienced the exploratory outcome (HR 1.711; 95% CI: 0.289 to 10.120; p = 0.554) (Figure 1). NPV and PPV of FIND-AF risk categorisation for NOAF at one year post-TAVI was 95.5% and 4.2% respectively. Conclusion After TAVI, AF detection in routine care was not associated with a risk score that includes common predictors of AF. AF after TAVI may be under-detected through routine practice and/or originate from different biopathology.
title: Predicting new-onset atrial fibrillation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation using the FIND-AF machine learning algorithm

abstract: Abstract Background and objectives New onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is common in critically ill patients and is associated with increased adverse outcomes such as death, stroke, and myocardial infarction. While beta-blockers and amiodarone are both commonly used in the management of NOAF, there remains a need to determine whether these treatment strategies differ in terms of clinical benefits. Methods The TriNetX Global Collaborative Network was used to define two cohorts of patients who developed NOAF within 2 weeks of receiving critical care services and were treated with either beta-blockers or amiodarone, excluding patients with concomitant calcium channel blocker or digoxin treatment and prior beta-blocker use in the past 3 months. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 and 90 days. Analyses were performed before and after propensity score matching (PSM). Results Before PSM, the beta-blocker group (N=2841, age=71.9 ± 13.1) was older with fewer comorbidities, including hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and heart failure, when compared to the amiodarone group (N=610, age=69.8 ± 12.5). After PSM (matched N=577), patients in the beta-blocker group had a lower risk of 30-day (HR: 0.47, 95% CI: 0.32, 0.69) and 90-day all-cause mortality (HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.43, 0.83). Subgroup analyses were mainly consistent with the primary findings. Conclusion Beta-blocker therapy was associated with significantly lower 30-day and 90-day mortality compared with amiodarone in patients receiving critical care services who subsequently developed NOAF. However, the lack of a surrogate for acute disease severity limits interpretation of observed associations. Prospective randomised controlled trials are warranted to better define the optimal therapeutic strategy for patients who develop NOAF in the critical care setting.Main resultsSubgroups
title: Beta-blockers vs amiodarone in management of new onset atrial fibrillation in patients receiving critical care services: an analysis from a global federated research network

abstract: Abstract Background Early rhythm control improves cardiovascular outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients at risk, but its benefits in patients with cancer remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of early rhythm control in patients with AF and history of cancer. Methods This secondary analysis of EAST-AFNET 4 compared patients with and without a history of cancer. The analysis included the primary outcome, a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, or hospitalization for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome; the safety outcome, a composite of all-cause death, stroke, and prespecified serious adverse events of special interest related to rhythm-control therapy; and rhythm at 24 months. Results Cancer history was available in 2779/2789 patients (99.6%). Cancer history was present in 216/2779 (7.8%, mean age 73 years, 95 (44%) women, mean CHA2DS2-VASc score 3.5). There was no evidence of heterogeneity for the efficacy outcome of the trial (pinteraction=0.232). Rates of sinus rhythm at 24 months were not different (cancer: 84.9%, without cancer 81.8%; pinteraction=0.601). In patients with a cancer history, the safety outcome occurred more often with early rhythm control than with usual care, with more strokes and more adverse events of rhythm control therapy. Conclusion These hypothesis-generating data suggest that early rhythm control therapy is effective in patients with a cancer history and atrial fibrillation but may be less safe than in patients without a cancer history. More research is needed to understand the mechanisms of stroke and the safety of rhythm control in patients with a history of cancer.
title: Early rhythm control in patients with atrial fibrillation and cancer: a subgroup analysis of the EAST-AFNET 4 trial

abstract: Abstract Background In the ALONE-AF trial, discontinuation of oral anticoagulation (OAC) reduced the risk of the primary outcome (a composite of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding) in patients without atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF). Purpose This post-hoc analysis aimed to identify risk factors for atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation and to evaluate whether the effect of OAC discontinuation varied according to recurrence risk. Methods We randomized patients with AF to continue or discontinue OAC and followed them for ≥2 years. The risk factors associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence at 2 years were identified using Cox regression models based on backward elimination. We evaluated the 2-year cumulative incidence of the primary outcome using the Kaplan–Meier method and assessed the interaction between recurrence risk and OAC strategy. Results Overall, 840 patients (mean age 64.1±8.1 years, 24.9% female) were included. Atrial arrhythmia recurrence was documented in 77 patients and was independently associated with female sex (HR, 2.31 [95% CI, 1.37–3.91]), heart failure (HR, 2.37 [95% CI, 1.35–4.17]), and left atrial enlargement (HR, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.08–3.05]). Among the 231 patients without risk factors, the risk of the primary outcome was significantly higher in patients who continued OAC than in those who discontinued OAC (absolute difference, 5.5% points [95% CI, 1.2–9.7]). Among the 568 patients with ≥1 risk factors, the differences were not prominent (absolute difference, 0.4% points [95% CI, −1.0–1.9]; p for interaction=0.028). Conclusions Female sex, heart failure, and left atrial enlargement were identified as risk factors for atrial arrhythmia recurrence. The significant interaction between recurrence-risk strata and OAC strategy supports tailored anticoagulation strategies guided by an individual’s recurrence risk profile.Graphical abstractStudy population
title: Risk factors of atrial arrhythmia recurrence and impact on the benefit of oral anticoagulation discontinuation: insights from the ALONE-AF trial

abstract: Abstract Background Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) has emerged as a safer modality than conventional thermal ablation. Concurrently, cerebral infarctions (CIs) after PFA have been sporadically reported, most of which are asymptomatic. Although their mechanisms remain unclear, air embolism is considered as a main cause due to air-trapping by the sheaths with larger diameter and the various structure shapes of the PFA. Meanwhile, these procedural characteristics may also become potential risks for thrombus formation. Purpose We investigated the occurrence and predictors of CIs following PFA. Methods A total of 56 patients with AF referred for PFA were enrolled (FARAPULSE, n=32; PulseSelect, n=24). Preoperative anticoagulation was managed with dabigatran bridging or warfarin continuation, and the absence of left atrial appendage thrombus was confirmed within one week by contrast-enhanced computed tomography or transesophageal echocardiography in all patients. The left atrium mapping was performed before and after PFA using high density mapping catheter. Concerning brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on the following day, CIs were defined as high-signal-intensity lesions on diffusion-weighted imaging and air embolism as low-signal-intensity lesions on T2*-weighted imaging(T2*WI) or susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). Results CIs were detected in total 22 patients (39.3%) {10 patients(31.3%) in FARAPULSE and 12 patients (50.0%) in PulseSelect). No patients exhibited neurological symptoms. The median lesion number of CIs per patient was 1(1-3) in FARAPULSE and 1(1-2) in PulseSelect. Regarding MRI findings, no CI lesions showed low intensity on T2*WI or SWI (figure1). In univariate analysis, CI occurrence related to higher brain natriuretic peptide before the PFA (143.4[38.1-302.7] vs. 58.7[28.6-108.2]pg/mL, p=0.019), the use of EnSite mapping system (77% vs. 47%, p=0.03) and lower minimum activated clotting time (ACT) during the procedure (364[352-390] vs. 396[363-423] seconds, p=0.029). Multivariate analysis revealed lower minimum ACT (odds ratio[OR]: 0.981, p=0.048) as the only predictors of CI occurrence. The cut-off value of minimum ACT was 420 seconds with 100% sensitivity and 29.4% specificity (figure2). Conclusion In PFA using FARAPULSE and PulseSelect, CIs were likely to occur under insufficient ACT control. Additionally, no patients showed typical air embolism by MRI findings, and which also support the result of ACT. It might be better to keep ACT level above 420 seconds during the PFA procedure for preventing silent CIs.
title: Silent cerebral infarctions following pulsed-field ablation using FARAPULSE and PulseSelect

abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone therapy for atrial fibrillation (AF) and may modulate cardiac autonomic function (CAF) due to the close anatomical relationship between the PV antra and atrial ganglionated plexi. Thermal PVI using radiofrequency (RF) or cryoballoon energy (CB) has been associated with acute reductions in heart rate variability (HRV) and increases in resting heart rate, consistent with transient parasympathetic withdrawal (1,2). In some studies, greater post-ablation HRV reduction was linked to lower AF recurrence, suggesting that autonomic modification may contribute to procedural efficacy (3,4). Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a non-thermal alternative for PVI. Data suggest relative preservation of perivascular autonomic structures after PFA, potentially resulting in less pronounced autonomic modulation (5). Purpose We aimed to investigate immediate effects of PVI on CAF in a real-world cohort from the Swiss-AF PVI registry (University Hospital, Switzerland). Methods Consecutive patients undergoing first-time PVI were prospectively included. Five-minute high-resolution digital ECG recordings were obtained immediately before PVI and prior to discharge. CAF was assessed using periodic repolarization dynamics (PRD), deceleration capacity (DC), standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN), root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), mean heart rate (MHR), and HRV triangular index (HRVI). Primary endpoint was the acute change of CAF between baseline and post-ablation assessment. Results 281 patients (age 68 [61–75] years; 31% female) were analyzed. Median CHA2DS2-VA score was 2 (IQR 1–3; mean 2.3±1.6). EHRA class III–IV symptoms were present in 15%, hypertension in 54.7%, diabetes in 11.6%, coronary artery disease in 12.9%, prior MI in 7.4%, prior PCI in 9.8%, prior stroke or TIA in 6.2%, heart failure in 14.3%, and renal insufficiency in 9.2%. Oral anticoagulation was used in 92.2% and beta-blockers in 67.2%. Energy sources were predominantly PFA (90.6%), followed by dual energy (RF + PFA) in 6.3%, RF alone in 1.8%, and CB in 1.3%. At baseline, the median CAF was PRD 5.97°, DC 4.99 ms, SDNN 58.8 ms, RMSSD 32.5 ms and HRVI 14.6. After PVI, PRD increased to 7.02°, while DC, SDNN, RMSSD, and HRVI decreased to 3.47 ms, 40.6 ms, 22.1 ms, and 11, respectively (p&lt;0.001, Figure). MHR showed a modest, non-significant rise from 66.1 to 67.6 bpm. Conclusions In this cohort with predominantly PFA-based PVI, significant acute alterations in CAF were observed two days after ablation. Despite the non-thermal nature of PFA, autonomic parameters showed a pattern consistent with parasympathetic withdrawal and sympathetic predominance. These findings suggest that even contemporary PVI strategies are associated with early autonomic modulation. Further studies are warranted to determine the persistence of these changes and their relationship with outcomes.Autonomic function before and after PVI
title: Acute autonomic modulation after pulmonary vein isolation: real-world evidence from the Swiss-AF PVI Registry

abstract: Abstract Background and Aim Atrial fibrillation (AF) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) frequently coexist and are linked through shared mechanisms of atrial and ventricular remodeling. Both catheter ablation and transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (M-TEER) improve clinical status, yet the optimal sequence of these interventions remains unclear. This study evaluates real-world outcomes in patients with AF and FMR, comparing catheter ablation and M-TEER as initial strategies, with focus on MR severity, symptom stability, mortality, and hospitalization. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective analysis of patients with AF and moderate to moderate-to-severe FMR. Patients were grouped according to the initial treatment strategy: AF ablation or M-TEER. Clinical and echocardiographic data were reviewed at baseline and follow-up. A retrospective two-year follow-up was performed to evaluate changes in mitral regurgitation severity, symptom stability, mortality, and hospitalization. Results A total of 281 patients were included (129 M-TEER, 152 AF ablation). MR severity improved more frequently following M-TEER (p &lt; 0.001). However, AF ablation was associated with better symptom stability (69% vs. 44%, p &lt; 0.001), markedly lower all-cause mortality (3% vs. 14%, p= 0.002), less all-cause cardiac hospitalizations (p = 0.021), and significant improvment in left ventricular ejection fraction at follow-up (53 ± 11.1%vs. 47 ± 13.9%, p &lt; 0.001). Conclusion In functional MR, M-TEER reduced regurgitation degree more effectively, whereas AF ablation was associated with better survival, fewer hospitalizations, improved ventricular function, and greater symptom stability, supporting rhythm control as a preferred initial strategy in selected AF-related functional MR patientsKaplan–Meier of all-cause mortalityKaplan–Meier of time to first hospitalisation
title: Atrial fibrillation ablation versus transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair as first-line therapy in atrial fibrillation with functional mitral regurgitation

abstract: Abstract Background Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) offers a nonthermal and tissue-selective alternative with promising safety data; however, evidence in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is limited. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of PFA for atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with CKD. Methods Patients with AF who underwent their initial catheter ablation with PFA were enrolled. Patients on dialysis were excluded. Biomarkers for hemolysis (haptoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase), myocardial injury (creatine kinase [CK], CK-MB, troponin I [TnI]), and renal function (creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR]) were assessed before and 24 hours after procedure. Renal function and N-terminal prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels were assessed before and at one-month post procedure. CKD was defined as eGFR &lt; 60 mL/min/1.73m² before procedure. Results A total of 187 patients (72.0 [65.0, 77.0] years old, 122 [65.2%] male, 112 [59.9%] paroxysmal AF) were included; 100 (53.5%) patients in the non-CKD group, 87 (46.5%) patients in the CKD group. The CKD group was significantly older, had a lower body mass index, and showed a higher prevalence of heart failure. CHA2DS2-VASC score and baseline NT-proBNP levels were significantly higher, and left ventricular ejection fraction was lower in the CKD group than in the non-CKD group. After procedure, the increase in TnI level was significantly higher (16288 [11056, 26621] vs. 13162 [9857, 19496] pg/mL, p = 0.026) and eGFR improved (0.93 [-3.16, 4.83] vs. -1.16 [-6.76, 3.29], p = 0.031) in the CKD group. However, no significant differences were observed in the changes in other biomarkers. Procedure-related complications and acute kidney injury (AKI) were observed in 12 (6.4%) and 4 patients (2.1%), respectively. No significant differences were identified between the CKD and non-CKD groups, with 6 (6.9%) vs. 6 (6.0%) cases (p = 1) and 2 (2.3%) vs. 2 (2.0%) cases (p = 1), respectively. All patients in the CKD group who experienced complications underwent additional procedures other than pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) (6 [14.6%] vs. 0 [0.0%], p &lt; 0.01). However, in the non-CKD group, there was no association between additional procedures other than PVI and complications. At one-month follow-up, eGFR significantly improved in the CKD group, with no difference in the non-CKD group (3.59 [0.18, 5.67] vs. 1.13 [-3.07, 6.41], p = 0.012). While NT-proBNP levels decreased in both groups, the reduction was more pronounced in the CKD group (235.4 [-16.6, 851.9] vs. 23.8 [-31.9, 376.9] pg/mL, p &lt; 0.01). Conclusions PFA for AF can be safely performed even in patients with CKD, and improvements in eGFR and reductions in NTproBNP levels were observed, indicating that PFA is an effective treatment. However, when additional treatments other than PVI are performed in patients with CKD, careful attention to complications is necessary.
title: Pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation in patients with chronic kidney disease: acute safety and efficacy

abstract: Abstract Introduction Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is an established rhythm control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF). Different energy sources may induce variable peri-procedural inflammatory responses, the clinical relevance of which remains insufficiently defined. Purpose This study aimed to compare peri-procedural inflammatory response between pulsed field ablation (PFA) and cryoballoon ablation (CBA) using validated inflammatory indices. Methods In this single-center registry, patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time PVI between July 2022 and January 2025 were included. Venous blood samples were collected at admission and on the morning after the procedure. The following biomarkers were assessed pre- and post-procedure: systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and inflammation score (INFLA). High-sensitivity troponin I (hsTnI) was measured as a marker of myocardial injury. Results A total of 175 patients were included (median age 64 years, IQR 56–69; 63% male; 64% paroxysmal AF). PFA was performed in 103 patients and CBA in 72. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for a higher prevalence of paroxysmal AF in the CBA group (p=0.001), and more frequent history of heart failure and beta-blocker therapy in the PFA group (p=0.001). Post-procedural analysis showed a significant rise in inflammatory biomarkers in the CBA group: SII (p&lt;0.001), SIRI (p=0.022), AISI (p=0.011), NLR (p&lt;0.001), PLR (p=0.009), and INFLA score (p=0.009), while MLR did not reach statistical significance (p=0.168). After adjustment for baseline values, SII and NLR remained significantly higher in the CBA group (SII: PFA median 592.3 [IQR 451–895] vs. CBA median 797.2 [IQR 619.5–1099], p=0.001; NLR: PFA 3.30 [IQR 2.5–4.6] vs. CBA 3.9 [IQR 3.1–5.1], p=0.001). SIRI and AISI showed a trend toward lower values with PFA, whereas PLR, MLR, and INFLA score showed no consistent differences. Post-procedural hsTnI levels differed significantly between groups, being higher in the PFA group (PFA 5673 ng/L [IQR 3798–8672] vs. CBA 5385 ng/L [IQR 3962–6729], p=0.042). No significant differences in inflammatory indices or hsTnI were observed among different PFA systems. Conclusion The acute systemic inflammatory response appears more pronounced after CBA compared with PFA, particularly reflected by SII and NLR changes. Further studies are needed to determine whether these differences translate into clinically meaningful outcomes, including long-term AF recurrence.Study population baseline characteristics
title: Cooling down or moving on - acute systemic inflammatory response across contemporary catheter ablation procedures for atrial fibrillation

abstract: Abstract Background The comparative long-term clinical outcomes of catheter ablation versus pacemaker implantation in patients with atrial fibrillation(AF) and sick sinus syndrome(SSS) remain controversial. Purpose This study aims to evaluate the long-term clinical outcomes between catheter ablation and permanent pacemaker implantation in patients with AF and SSS utilizing real-world evidence. Methods This population-based cohort study included 1,727 patients with AF and SSS who underwent catheter ablation or permanent pacemaker implantation. After 1:2 propensity score matching (PSM), the final matched cohort comprised 910 patients. The primary clinical outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, hospitalization for worsening heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and revascularization. Secondary endpoints comprised all-cause mortality, stroke, and hospitalization for worsening heart failure. Multivariable Cox regression was used to adjust for confounders, combined with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis to systematically evaluate the robustness of treatment effects. Results The final cohort included 350 patients who received catheter ablation and 560 who received permanent pacemaker implantation. During a mean follow-up of 1,852 days,patients in the catheter ablation group were younger, had higher CHA2DS2-VASc scores, and had a higher prevalence of dyslipidemia compared with the permanent pacemaker group. They were also more likely to be prescribed oral anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs, statins, and anti-arrhythmic drugs. After PSM, the catheter ablation group was associated with a significantly decreased risk of MACE compared with the permanent pacemaker implantation group (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39–0.70; P &lt; 0.001). Catheter ablation also significantly reduced the risks of all-cause stroke (HR = 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37–0.90; P = 0.014) and hospitalization for worsening heart failure (HR = 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37–0.90; P = 0.014). However, there was no significant difference in the risk of all-cause mortality between the two groups (HR = 0.60; 95% CI, 0.27–1.34; P = 0.20). These findings remained consistent after adjustment in multivariable Cox regression models. Conclusion In this real-world cohort, catheter ablation was associated with a lower risk of MACE, stroke, and hospitalization for worsening heart failure, but a similar risk of all-cause mortality compared with permanent pacemaker implantation. Given the observational nature of this study, further prospective research is warranted to validate the efficacy of catheter ablation in patients with AF and SSS.Characteristics of the Patients at BaselineCox regression and Kaplan–Meier curves
title: Long-term clinical outcomes of catheter ablation versus pacemaker implantation in patients with atrial fibrillation and sick sinus syndrome: a multicenter real-world cohort study

abstract: Abstract Backgrounds Left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) is reported to associate with the atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after ablation. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is known to cause less collateral damage compared with thermal ablation; however, its impact on adipose tissue remains unclear. Purpose To compare changes in left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) after pulsed-field ablation (PFA) with those observed after conventional thermal ablation using a cryoballoon. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing a first atrial fibrillation ablation at our institution who had both pre-procedural and post-procedural left atrial CT imaging within 6 months and next-day troponin measurements. Seventy-five PFA and 145 cryoballoon. cases were screened. To adjust for baseline LA fat volume and post-procedural changes, propensity-score matching was performed using age, AF type, CHADS2 score, dyslipidemia, pre-procedural LA-EAT volume, AF recurrence at the time of CT, and the interval between CT scans. Changes in hs-troponin I and LA-EAT were compared between matched PFA and cryoballoon. cohorts. Results A total of 70 patients (35 per group) were included in the matched analysis (mean age 66.1±9.7 years; 48 men; LAD 39.3±5.7 mm; paroxysmal AF 63 patients; CHADS2 1.1±1.0). In the PFA group, 24 procedures used circular catheter and 11 used pentaspline catheter. Baseline LA-EAT volume was similar between groups (PFA 15.8±9.2 mL vs cryoballoon 15.7±7.3 mL; p=0.098; SMD 0.006). Baseline CT attenuation was also comparable (PFA 75.6±4.7 HU vs cryoballoon 74.9±5.1 HU; p=0.52). The mean interval between CT scans was 153.1±60.2 days. Eight patients in the PFA group and six in the cryoballoon group had AF recurrence, including blanking-period recurrences, at the time of the post-procedural CT scan. The mean number of cryoballoon applications was 4.9±1.6 per case, whereas PFA required 51.7±13.2 applications per case; posterior wall isolation was performed in 18 PFA cases with a mean of 9.4±10.3 applications. Hs-troponin I value were significantly higher after PFA (22,411.2±10,145.1 ng/L vs 12,546.2±4,881.0 ng/L; p&lt;0.001) (Figure 1). Post-procedural LA-EAT volume was 14.3±8.8 mL in the PFA group and 12.3±6.3 mL in the cryoballoon. group (p=0.26). The reduction in LA-EAT was significantly smaller after PFA (1.43±2.62 mL vs 3.46±3.96 mL; p=0.014) (Figure 2). Conclusions Although PFA resulted in greater myocardial injury as reflected by higher troponin release, its impact on LA-EAT reduction was smaller compared with cryoballoon ablation.Figure 1Figure 2
title: Impact of pulsed field ablation on left atrial epicardial adipose tissue: a comparative study with cryoballoon ablation

abstract: Abstract Background Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is a novel non-thermal energy modality that delivers high-voltage, ultra-short electrical pulses (microseconds to nanoseconds) to induce myocardial-selective irreversible electroporation. Nanosecond PFA ablation system represents a next-generation technology utilizing nanosecond-duration high-voltage electrical pulses (nsPFA™), inducing regulated cell death while sparing non-cellular components. Real-world data comparing workflow performance between ns and ms-based PFA remain limited. Aim To compare workflow characteristics between a nsPFA system and a conventional msPFA during atrial fibrillation ablation. Methods This is a retrospective, two-centre, comparative study including consecutive patients undergoing first-time catheter ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Exclusion criteria included prior atrial fibrillation ablation, persistent atrial fibrillation, left ventricular ejection fraction &lt;40% and contraindications to anticoagulation. This study evaluated 348 patients undergoing AF ablation using PFA system. A total of 43 patients for the nsPFA group and 43 patients for the msPFA group were generated by propensity matching, based on calculated risk factor scores, using a logistic model. All cases followed a standardised workflow including three-dimensional electroanatomical mapping and pulmonary vein isolation with confirmation of entrance and exit block. Additional left atrial target lesions were performed at the operator’s discretion. Workflow endpoints were fluoroscopy time, left atrial dwell time (from transseptal access to final catheter exit), and total procedure duration (skin-to-skin, from groin puncture to sheath removal). Additional procedural metrics included number of applications per vein and per patient. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups (nsPFA group: 58.1 ± 9.6 years, 27.9% female; msPFA group: 62.4 ± 8.7 years, 33.8% female). Pulmonary vein isolation was successfully achieved in all patients of both groups (100%). Adjunctive left atrial ablation was performed in 100% of patients in the ns group and 87% in the ms group. In the nsPFA cohort, the mean number of applications required to achieve pulmonary vein isolation was 2,7 ± 0.2 per vein, corresponding to 18,4 ± 4,6 applications per patient. In the msPFA cohort, the mean number of applications per vein was 18.0 ± 4.4, with 70 ± 18.1 applications per patient (p &lt;0.001) With respect to predefined workflow endpoints, the ns group demonstrated shorter total procedure duration (35.7 ± 8.57 minutes vs 84.8 ± 11.8 minutes, p &lt;0.001), comparable fluoroscopy time (17.0 ± 3.15 vs 16.97 ± 2.6; p=0.91), and shorter left atrial dwell time (10 ± 4.0 vs 59.4 ± 18.3 minutes; p &lt;0.001) compared with the ms group. Conclusion NsPFA was associated with improved procedural workflow compared with msPFA, showing comparable fluoroscopy exposure, a reduction in LA dwell time and total procedure duration.
title: Workflow efficiency of nanosecond versus microsecond pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation

abstract: Abstract Background Conventional thermal atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation (radiofrequency or cryoballoon) induces immediate coagulation necrosis and can augment early postoperative inflammatory responses. Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal modality based on irreversible electroporation; experimental and histopathological studies suggest a distinct injury profile that may influence the timing of biomarker release and the early inflammatory footprint after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). 1,2 Purpose To compare early postoperative inflammation and myocardial injury after first-time PVI performed with PFA, cryoballoon ablation (CBA), or radiofrequency ablation (RFA). Methods Single-centre retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first-time AF ablation with PVI only (no additional substrate modification) between April 2024 and April 2025. We collected venous blood samples to assess high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) at three time points (baseline, 30 minutes post-procedure, and the next morning [Day 1]) and creatine kinase (CK) and creatine kinase MB isoform (CK-MB) at four time points (baseline, 30 minutes post-procedure, 6 hours post-procedure, and the next morning [Day 1]). The hs-CRP levels were considered as a surrogate for systemic inflammation, whereas the CK-MB levels served as a marker of myocardial injury. Data are presented as median [IQR]. Overall group differences were evaluated using Kruskal–Wallis tests. Results We retrospectively analysed 130 consecutive patients (PFA n=61; CBA n=15; RFA n=54). Baseline characteristics were similar among the three groups. CK-MB dynamics revealed different temporal patterns among the three energy sources. In the CBA group, the CK-MB levels increased 30 minutes after the ablation procedure. Conversely, in the PFA group, the peak values were observed at 6 hours post-ablation. The CK-MB levels at 30 minutes were significantly lower in the PFA group than in the CBA group (PFA group vs. CBA group, 25.0 [16.5-41.0] vs. 64.0 [41.0-95.0] U/L, p &lt; 0.001). However, the CK-MB levels remained elevated and were similar between the groups on Day 1. The CK-MB levels remained consistently lower in the RFA group across all measured time points. The hs-CRP levels on Day 1 were significantly lower in the PFA group than in the CBA group (PFA group vs. CBA group, 0.47[0.23-0.58] vs. 0.83[0.55-1.21] mg/dL, p=0.05). Conclusion These findings support the hypothesis that PFA causes delayed myocardial injury and less acute systemic inflammation than CBA, consistent with the apoptosis-based mechanism. 1,2 In RFA, the lesion set is typically more linear than in CBA or PFA, which may partly explain the lower levels of myocardial enzyme release observed in the RFA group.Time course of CK, CKMB and CRP
title: Delayed myocardial injury and reduced inflammation after pulsed-field vs. cryoballoon vs. radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation

abstract: Abstract Background Very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) carry high predicted thromboembolic risk yet are underrepresented in randomised trials of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). Evidence on real-world stroke protection at extreme age and the performance of bleeding risk scores in this setting remains limited. Purpose To evaluate thromboembolic and major bleeding outcomes in DOAC-treated AF patients aged ≥90 years, contextualise observed 1-year event rates against CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED–based expected risks, and assess HAS-BLED discrimination for major bleeding. Methods Retrospective single-centre cohort study at Meir Medical Center (Israel) including consecutive AF patients aged ≥90 years treated with DOACs between 2016–2021. Follow-up started at DOAC initiation and continued until end of follow-up or death. Outcomes were stroke/transient ischaemic attack (TIA) and major bleeding. Event rates were reported as incidence per 100 person-years and cumulative 1-year rates. HAS-BLED performance was assessed by AUC for 1-year bleeding and Harrell’s C-index; association with bleeding was tested using Cox regression. Results The cohort included 480 patients (mean age 93.0±2.6 years; 63.5% women), mean CHA2DS2-VASc 4.7±1.2 and mean HAS-BLED 2.6±0.7. Over 1556 person-years (median follow-up 2.9 years), stroke/TIA occurred in 31 patients (2.0 per 100 person-years) with a 1-year rate ~1.3%, markedly lower than the ~5–6% annual risk expected without anticoagulation. Major bleeding occurred in 49 patients (3.15 per 100 person-years) with a 1-year rate 4.4%, consistent with the ~4–6% annual risk expected from HAS-BLED. HAS-BLED showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.49; 95% CI 0.38–0.60; C-index 0.47) and was not associated with major bleeding (HR per point 0.80; 95% CI 0.54–1.19; p=0.29). All-cause mortality was high (85.0%). Conclusion In AF patients aged ≥90 years, DOAC therapy was associated with substantially lower observed thromboembolic risk than predicted by CHA2DS2-VASc, while major bleeding remained clinically relevant. HAS-BLED demonstrated limited ability to discriminate individual bleeding risk at extreme age, supporting the need for geriatric-informed risk assessment to guide anticoagulation decisions.
title: Direct oral anticoagulants in very elderly (≥90 years) patients with atrial fibrillation: observed versus predicted thromboembolism and bleeding risk, and HAS-BLED performance

abstract: Abstract Background - Renal dysfunction commonly coexists with clinical atrial fibrillation and is associated with thromboembolism and bleeding. In a prespecified analysis of the Apixaban for the Reduction of Thrombo-Embolism in Patients with Device-Detected Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation (ARTESiA) trial, we investigated associations between renal function and prognosis in patients with subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF). Methods - In ARTESiA, participants with SCAF were randomised within a double-blind, double-dummy design to receive either guideline-indicated doses of apixaban or aspirin 81 mg daily. The primary efficacy endpoint was the composite of stroke or systemic embolism (SE); the primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was conducted to explore the association of baseline creatinine clearance (CrCl) with outcomes and restricted cubic splines were fitted to capture non-linear associations. Treatment effect modification by renal function was assessed with interaction tests. Analyses were by intention-to-treat. Results - All 4012 trial participants had pre-randomisation creatinine measurements and were included. On average, those with lower CrCl were older, female, at lower body weight, had higher CHA2DS2-VASc scores and were more likely to meet apixaban dose reduction criteria. There were non-linear, inverse associations between declining renal function, and both major bleeding and death (Figure 1A). Below a CrCl of 60 mL/min, declining renal function was associated with higher risk of major bleeding (adjusted HR per 10 mL/min decrease 1.31, 95%CI 1.01–1.71; P=0.04), with no association above this threshold. Below a CrCl of 60 mL/min there was an increase in death from any cause (adjusted HR per 10 mL/min decrease 1.39, 95%CI 1.27–1.52, P&lt;0.0001) and cardiovascular death (adjusted HR per 10 mL/min decrease 1.45, 95%CI 1.28–1.65, P&lt;0.0001). Lower CrCl was not associated with increased risk of stroke or SE, nor did it modify treatment effects of apixaban versus aspirin with respect to reducing stroke/SE (Pinteraction=0.78) or increasing major bleeding (Pinteraction=0.73) (Figure 1B). Conclusion - In patients with SCAF, renal dysfunction is associated with increased major bleeding and death below a CrCl of 60 mL/min but does not influence stroke risk. Renal function did not modify the treatment effects of apixaban versus aspirin for any trial outcomes.Figure 1AFigure 1B
title: Renal function and outcomes in subclinical atrial fibrillation: a prespecified analysis of the ARTESIA trial

abstract: Abstract Background Oral anticoagulants (OAC) are the cornerstone for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but long-term adherence and bleeding risk remain major limitations. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) provides a non-pharmacological alternative; however, comparative outcome data across study designs are inconsistent. We assessed the efficacy and safety of LAAC versus OAC in AF. Methods We performed a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science up to 30 September 2025 for randomized trials and propensity score–matched studies comparing LAAC with OAC in AF. Random-effects models were used to pool relative risks (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Prespecified outcomes included a composite endpoint, stroke outcomes, mortality, and major bleeding. Results Fifteen studies (4 randomized trials and 11 propensity-matched studies) comprising 17,116 patients were included. Compared with OAC, LAAC significantly reduced the composite endpoint (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66–0.95; p=0.010) and was associated with marked reductions in all-cause mortality (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.49–0.69; p&lt;0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.44–0.67; p&lt;0.001). Rates of any stroke (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.86–1.31), ischemic stroke (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85–1.17) and hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.54–1.70) were comparable between strategies. Major bleeding showed a non-significant trend favoring LAAC (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.67–1.04; p=0.112). Conclusion Across randomized and propensity-matched evidence, LAAC is associated with significant reductions in mortality and composite clinical outcomes compared with OAC, while maintaining similar stroke risk. LAAC may represent a favorable alternative for selected AF patients, particularly when long-term anticoagulation is challenging.LAAC vs OAC: Composite Clinical EndpointLAAC vs OAC: All-Cause and CV Mortality
title: Left atrial appendage closure versus oral anticoagulants in atrial fibrillation: updated evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis

abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is a non-pharmacological alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF). However, randomised trials span different therapeutic eras-comparing LAAC to warfarin or direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and distinct clinical contexts, making a single composite interpretation of "net clinical benefit" challenging. Purpose To synthesise randomised evidence using a domain-specific framework that separately evaluates efficacy and safety across different therapeutic eras and clinical settings. Methods We conducted a systematic review and two-part meta-analysis of four randomised controlled trials (PROTECT AF, PREVAIL, PRAGUE-17, and OPTION) totalling 3,116 patients. Part 1 utilised conventional random-effects pooling of relative risks (RRs). Part 2 applied a hierarchical Bayesian synthesis to separate the efficacy domain (thromboembolism/death) from the safety domain (clinically significant bleeding). Results Pooled efficacy outcomes showed no significant difference between LAAC and OAC (RR 0.79; 95% CI 0.58–1.08; I2=6%). Directional heterogeneity was noted across trials based on comparator era. In the safety domain, the primary pooled estimate was imprecise (RR 0.74; 95% CI 0.37–1.47; I2=86%), reflecting non-exchangeable bleeding definitions. However, in the contemporary post-ablation/DOAC-era setting (OPTION trial), LAAC significantly reduced non-procedural major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding at 36 months (RR 0.47; 95% CI 0.36–0.62). Early device-related events occurred in 2.2% of patients within 7 days in the PREVAIL trial. Conclusion LAAC provides stroke prevention comparable to OAC. Safety advantages are context-dependent, with significant bleeding reductions observed in contemporary DOAC-era and post-ablation populations, though these are offset by early procedural risks. A domain-specific interpretation better reflects net clinical benefit than a single pooled composite across heterogeneous trials.Forest plot 2.1: Efficacy endpointsForest plot 3.1: Safety endpoints
title: Efficacy and safety of left atrial appendage closure versus oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: a two-part randomised-trial synthesis and a pooled analysis

abstract: Abstract Background/introduction Patients with cardiac amyloidosis (CA) frequently develop atrial fibrillation (AF) due to atrial infiltration and remodeling. both conditions increase thromboembolic risk, while amyloid-related vascular fragility and anticoagulation increase bleeding risk, complicating long-term therapy. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to anticoagulation in selected AF populations; however, patients with CA were underrepresented in major trials, and outcome data remain limited. We present the first meta-analysis of outcomes of LAAO for AF in CA patients. Purpose To systematically evaluate the safety and efficacy of LAAO in patients with CA and AF compared with non-CA patients undergoing LAAO. Methods Pubmed, embase, cochrane databases, and clinicaltrials.gov were searched from january 2000 to january 2026 for studies reporting outcomes of LAAO in adult patients with CA and AF with a non-CA comparator. Studies with ≥180 days follow-up were included. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and ischemic stroke; secondary outcomes were major bleeding and hospitalization. Pooled analyses were performed using the inverse variance method within a random-effects model to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). IRR was used as it accounts for differences in follow-up duration across different studies. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment was applied to account for the small number of included studies. Sensitivity analyses included subgroup analysis and leave-one-out sensitivity analysis to assess robustness. Results Four observational studies comprising 67,302 patients (852 CA and 66,450 non-CA) met inclusion criteria. compared with non-CA patients, CA patients undergoing LAAO had no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (IRR 1.65, 95% CI 0.62–4.39), ischemic stroke (IRR 2.15, 95% CI 0.82–5.65), major bleeding (IRR 1.14, 95% CI 0.42–3.13), or hospitalization (IRR 0.91, 95% CI 0.65–1.28). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. Sensitivity analyses showed pooled estimates were influenced by large datasets, with heterogeneity for selected outcomes indicating limited robustness and highlighting the hypothesis-generating nature of these findings. Conclusion In pooled observational data, LAAO in patients with CA and AF appears feasible, with outcomes comparable to non-CA populations despite elevated baseline risk. These findings support consideration of LAAO in carefully selected CA patients unsuitable for long-term anticoagulation. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized antithrombotic strategies and amyloid subtype–specific analyses (AL vs ATTR) are needed to better define patient selection and long-term efficacy.Forest Plots of Outcomes
title: Outcomes of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion in patients with cardiac amyloidosis and atrial fibrillation

abstract: Abstract Introduction Antithrombotic therapy is used after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) to prevent device-related thrombosis (DRT) that could lead to stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). Ageing in atrial fibrillation (AF) as well as many age-associated comorbidities are known risk factor for stroke. Moreover, bleeding risk is high in elderly patients on oral anticoagulation (OAC). Therefore, balancing the risk of bleeding and thromboembolic events is critical in older AF patients. Objective We aimed to assess the efficacy of half-dose of the direct oral anticoagulant (HD-DOAC) in preventing DRT and stroke while keeping the bleeding risk low in patients aged ≥75 years with vs without comorbidities such as diabetes, uncontrolled hypertension and heart failure. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing LAAO procedure were screened for those aged ≥75 years and these elderly patients were divided into two groups based on their comorbidity status. Group 1: No hypertension, diabetes or heart failure and Group 2: presence of ≥1 of the 3 above-mentioned conditions. All received HD-DOAC for 6 months after the LAAO procedure along with aspirin 81 mg followed by long-term HD-DOAC monotherapy. These patients were monitored for 1-year for DRT, Stroke/TIA and bleeding events. A total of 3 trans-esophageal echocardiography was performed at 1.5, 3 and 12-months post-procedure, to assess DRT. Results Of the 1636 AF patients undergoing LAAO procedure, 779 (47.6%) aged ≥75 years were included in this analysis (Group 1: 322 and Group 2: 457). In group 2, 214 (46.8%), 288 (63%) and 98 (21.4%) patients had diabetes, hypertension and heart failure respectively. HD-DOAC included apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily (n=568, 72.9%) or rivaroxaban 10 mg once a day (n=211, 27.1%). The median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 3 (IQR 2-4) and 4 (IQR: 3-6) in group 1 and 2 respectively. At 1 year, stroke/TIA were reported in 3 (0.93%) and 5 (1.09) patients in group 1 and 2 respectively (p=0.82). Major bleeding events were comparable across groups (Group 1: 2 (0.62%); Group 2: 4 (0.87%); p=0.69). No DRT was detected in either group. Conclusion After successful Watchman implantation, long-term HD-DOAC is safe and effective in reducing the risk of DRT, stroke/TIA and bleeding events in elderly patients regardless of their comorbidity status.
title: Oral anticoagulation regimen after left atrial appendage occlusion in elderly atrial fibrillation patients with versus without cardiovascular comorbidities

abstract: Abstract Background Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains uncertain. Reduced-dose direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used in clinical practice as alternatives to antiplatelet-based strategies, but comparative outcome data are limited. We aimed to compare clinical outcomes associated with low-dose DOAC therapy versus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and versus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) after LAAO. Methods This study was conducted using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, a federated research platform aggregating de-identified electronic health records from 169 healthcare organizations worldwide, comprising more than 150 million patients. We identified adult patients with AF undergoing percutaneous LAAO between 2010 and 2025. Three parallel propensity score–matched analyses were conducted: reduced-dose DOAC versus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) versus DAPT, and reduced-dose DOAC versus SAPT. Outcomes included all-cause death, thromboembolic events, device-related thrombosis, bleeding events, and net clinical benefit (NCB). Results After matching, 1,773 patients were included in each group for the reduced-dose DOAC versus DAPT comparison (mean follow-up 1.4±1.0 years). Reduced-dose DOAC was associated with lower risks of all-cause death (hazard ratio [HR] 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65–0.96) and major bleeding (HR 0.87, 95%CI 0.77–0.98), with no significant differences in ischemic stroke, thromboembolism, or device-related thrombosis. NCB favored reduced-dose DOAC (HR 0.87, 95%CI 0.78–0.96). SAPT was also associated with fewer bleeding events and favorable outcomes compared with DAPT (Figure). In the reduced-dose DOAC versus SAPT comparison (1,582 matched patients per group), reduced-dose DOAC showed a borderline higher risk of major bleeding (HR 1.14, 95%CI 1.00–1.30; p=0.06), while mortality, thromboembolic outcomes, and NCB did not differ significantly. Clinical outcomes did not differ significantly in an additional matched analysis between reduced-dose apixaban and rivaroxaban after LAAO, although a numerical trend toward lower event rates with rivaroxaban was observed. In sensitivity analyses limited to early post-implant period (follow-up beginning 1 day after the index date and administratively censored at 90 days), findings were directionally consistent with the primary analyses. Conclusions In contemporary practice after LAAO, reduced-dose DOAC therapy was associated with more favorable outcomes than DAPT but showed no clear advantage over SAPT, supporting simplified and individualized post-implant antithrombotic strategies.Figure
title: Reduced-dose direct oral anticoagulation vs antiplatelet strategies after left atrial appendage occlusion in atrial fibrillation. a triple target trial emulation from a federated research network

abstract: Abstract Background Transcatheter left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation in patients with contraindications. However, optimal long-term imaging follow-up strategy after the procedure remains uncertain. Purpose This study sought to assess the clinical relevance of systematic long-term follow-up imaging using transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at 1 year after LAAC. Methods This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients who underwent LAAC and had systematic TEE follow-up at 45 days and 1 year post-procedure. Clinical and echocardiographic outcomes were assessed at early (45-day) and late (1-year) follow-up. Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between patients with early or late device-related thrombosis (DRT) and those without DRT. Results Between 2013 and 2023, 191 patients underwent LAAC with systematic long-term TEE follow-up at our institution. Early DRT was detected in 10 patients (5.2%) at a mean of 51.4 ± 14.3 days after LAAC, whereas late DRT was identified in 6 patients (3.1%) at a mean of 403.4 ± 62.4 days after LAAC. Among patients with late DRT, 2 had a prior early DRT that had resolved on interim imaging before recurrence at 1 year. Patients with early or late DRT tended to be older than those without DRT (79 ± 5.7 and 81 ± 4.0 vs. 74 ± 7.6 years, respectively; p = 0.09 and p = 0.06), while other baseline and procedural characteristics were similar across groups. At early TEE, 20 patients (10.8%) had a residual leak. Among them, 8 persisted at late TEE and 3 increased in size. Late TEE also identified 6 new residual leaks not present at early follow-up, all measuring &gt; 5mm. Conclusion Systematic TEE imaging at 1 year after LAAC identifies a non-negligible proportion of late residual leaks and late device-related thrombosis, including recurrent DRT after apparent early resolution. These findings support the clinical relevance of long-term echocardiographic surveillance following LAAC.Figure 1.Timeline of patients with DRTFollow-up transesophageal echocardiographies
title: Clinical utility of one-year transesophageal echocardiography after left atrial appendage closure: a tertiary care center experience

abstract: Abstract Background Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) for non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) is approved in Japan. The standard postprocedural regimen consists of oral anticoagulation plus an antiplatelet agent for the first 45 days, followed by dual antiplatelet therapy up to 6 months. However, in real-world clinical practice, modification of antithrombotic therapy is frequently required due to bleeding concerns. Aim To evaluate the safety and efficacy of two monotherapy strategies after LAAC in Japanese patients with NVAF, with a particular focus on modification of the antithrombotic protocol during follow-up. Methods The Safety and Efficacy of Two Monotherapies after LAAC in Patients with NVAF (SAPT-LAA) study is a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, interventional, non-randomized study. We planned to enroll NVAF patients eligible for WATCHMAN FLX Pro implantation according to the Japanese Circulation Society guidelines. After device implantation, patients received either single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) or low-dose direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) for 3 months, followed by SAPT alone for an additional 3 months. For this analysis, the primary endpoint was modification of the antithrombotic protocol within 6 months after LAAC. Device-related thrombus (DRT) was assessed using cardiac computed tomography or transesophageal echocardiography at 45 days and 6 months. Results A total of 106 patients were enrolled (SAPT group: 60; DOAC group: 46). The mean age was 76.1 ± 5.5 years, and 38 (36%) were women. Non-paroxysmal AF was present in 57 (54%) patients. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.7 ± 1.3, and the mean HAS-BLED score was 3.0 ± 0.3, indicating a cohort with high thromboembolic and bleeding risks. No procedural major complications occurred. One patient in the DOAC group and one patient in the SAPT group died of heart failure, both considered unrelated to the procedure. Excluding these two patients, 6-month follow-up was completed in all remaining patients. In the SAPT group, antithrombotic protocol modification occurred in four patients (6.7%). Two patients developed asymptomatic pulmonary embolism, one developed left atrial thrombus, and one developed right atrial thrombus; in all four cases, DOAC therapy was initiated. In the DOAC group, protocol modification occurred in two patients (4.3%). One patient developed asymptomatic pulmonary embolism and required dose escalation from a reduced to a standard DOAC dose. Another patient developed device-related thrombus and was switched to an alternative DOAC. During follow-up, no stroke,or systemic embolism were observed. Conclusions This sub-analysis of the SAPT-LAA study suggests that both monotherapy strategies appear safe and effective during early follow-up after LAAC. Although antithrombotic protocol modification was required in a small proportion of patients in both groups due to thrombotic events, no stroke, or systemic embolism was observed.
title: Two monotherapies after left atrial appendage closure in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation: an analysis of antithrombotic protocol modification from the SAPT-LAA study

abstract: Abstract Background The concept for left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is appealing, as it potentially mitigates the stroke risk while reducing the bleeding risk compared to long-term anticoagulation. In Germany, favorable reimbursement of the procedure led to the common use of LAAC. However, the CLOSURE-AF trial, as an industry-independent randomized controlled multicenter trial showed that LAAC was not non-inferior as compared to best medical care in elderly high-risk patients. The trial was conducted in 46 high volume centers with substantial expertise in LAAC in Germany. Purpose To investigate the representativeness of the CLOSURE-AF trial population compared with patients undergoing LAAC in clinical routine using real-world data from the German healthcare system. Methodology We compared the characteristics and outcomes of patients enrolled in the the CLOSURE-AF trial with those of patients treated in clinical routine in Germany using data from the German DRG-Registry. Further we explored the centre volume and the associated patient characteristics and outcomes. Results and Discussion Key patient demographics of the CLOSURE-AF trial were similar to those treated in the German health care system (Table 1). Differences in CHA2DS2VASC score could be explained by an underreporting in secondary use data as ICD-Codes used for calculation are not relevant for reimbursement. Reported complications were lower in the Closure-AF LAAC intervention arm (Table 1). In Germany, the number of centers performing LAAC rises (2016: N = 311, 2022; N = 419) and the yearly cases/centers decreases (2016 centers with less than 12 implantations/year: N = 159, 2022; N = 263). In 2022, there were 1608 LAAC-devices in hospitals implanted that were doing just one or less LAAC-cases per week. 105 centers (the lowest quartile) implant less than 4 devices per year (equals 290 patients receiving a device in centres of the lowest quartile). However, patient characteristics and outcome measurements were comparable in all size categories (Table 2). Conclusion Our report did not provide evidence that patient characteristics and outcomes in routine practice differ substantially to the data and patient characteristics reported from CLOSURE-AF. Furthermore there is a high number of low volume centres. From a healthcare system perspective LAAC may represent an area in which more selective use could enable a meaningful reallocation of resources.
title: Closure of the left atrial appendage: CLOSURE-AF vs. nationwide routine care in Germany

abstract: Abstract Background Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices reduce stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation unsuitable for long-term anticoagulation. While randomized trials demonstrate similar efficacy, real-world complication patterns may differ. Objective We analyzed the FDA MAUDE database to compare adverse event profiles of current-generation LAAO devices. Methods We queried MAUDE adverse event reports (2021–2025) for Watchman FLX family (FLX and FLX Pro) and Amplatzer Amulet. After excluding literature reports, non-manufacturer submissions, and delivery system-only events, we compared complications using chi-square tests.
