Deaths were limited to procedural events (≤30 days). Rates (%) are the proportion of reports. Results The analysis included 8,406 reports: Watchman FLX (n=6,135) and Amulet (n=2,271). A total of 8,406 reports were included (Watchman FLX 6,135; Amulet 2,271). Amulet had substantially higher rates of pericardial complications (40.6% vs 20.0%), driven by higher tamponade (16.1% vs 7.5%) and lower perforation (0.8% vs 2.5%). Thromboembolic events were more frequent with Amulet (16.4% vs 5.9%; OR 2.83), including higher stroke/CVA (5.3% vs 11.2%) and device thrombosis (11.1% vs 24.6%). Device embolization was similar. Procedural deaths ≤30 days were nearly twice as common with Amulet (6.3% vs 3.3%). Key findings are summarized in Table 1. Conclusion While true incidence is unknown, MAUDE analysis suggests there are clinically distinct complication profiles for contemporary Watchman and Amulet LAAO devices in real-world use.
title: Real-world complication profiles of left atrial appendage occlusion devices: a MAUDE database analysis of 8,406 adverse events

abstract: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia and is associated with increased risk of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that AF may also contribute to cognitive decline and dementia, even in the absence of overt cerebrovascular events, but this relationship remains incompletely characterized. Purpose To evaluate the association between atrial fibrillation and cognitive impairment in older adults, and to assess the impact of oral anticoagulation on dementia risk. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2018 to 2023. Patients aged ≥65 years with a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation were included. Individuals with prior ischemic stroke or mechanical valves were excluded. Patients were stratified into three groups: AF without cognitive impairment, AF with cognitive impairment/dementia, and cognitive impairment without AF (control). Multivariable analyses were performed adjusting for age, sex, comorbidities, and anticoagulation use. Results A total of 187,452 hospitalised patients with AF were identified, of whom 36,215 (19.3%) had cognitive impairment or dementia. Compared with patients without AF, AF was independently associated with cognitive decline (adjusted OR 1.48; 95% CI 1.36–1.61). This association remained significant after excluding patients with prior stroke (OR 1.41; 95% CI 1.28–1.56). Patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) had a lower prevalence of cognitive impairment compared with those on vitamin K antagonists (14.9% vs 18.5%; p=0.008), suggesting a potential protective effect. Conclusion Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with cognitive impairment and may represent a preclinical marker of neurocognitive decline. The observed association persists even in the absence of overt stroke, supporting alternative mechanisms such as microembolism, hypoperfusion, and systemic inflammation. Anticoagulation, particularly with DOACs, may confer a protective effect. These findings highlight AF as a systemic condition with important neurocognitive implications and support early, comprehensive management strategies aimed at both cardiovascular and neurological outcomes.
title: Atrial fibrillation as an independent predictor of cognitive decline: a national inpatient sample analysis

abstract: Abstract Background The MIRACLE-AF (a Novel Model of Integrated Care of Older Patients with Atrial Fibrillation in Rural China) cluster-randomised trialdemonstrated that a telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care model significantly reduced the risk of a composite cardiovascular outcome among older patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) in rural China. Multimorbidity is highly prevalent in older patients with AF and is associated with worse clinical outcomes but the impact of telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care on patients with multimorbidity is uncertain. Purpose To evaluate whether the MIRACLE-AF integrated care intervention reduced adverse clinical events in patients with multimorbidity. Methods This post-hoc subgroup analysis included patients with multimorbidity from the MIRACLE-AF trial. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 comorbid conditions, including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, coronary artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathy, peripheral arterial disease, prior stroke or systemic embolism, or liver or kidney dysfunction. In the MIRACLE-AF trial, 30 village clinics (clusters) were randomly assigned (1:1) to the intervention group (telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care) or the control group (usual care). The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, all strokes, hospitalisation due to worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and emergency visits due to AF. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary composite, all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and clinically relevant non-major bleeding. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate treatment effects, adjusting for cluster effects and baseline risk factors. Results Among the 1,039 patients in the primary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% women), 586 patients with multimorbidity were analysed, including 301 in the intervention group and 285 in the control group. Over a median follow-up of 34 months, the annualised rate of the primary composite outcome was significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (7.1% vs. 12.0% per year; rate difference -4.88 percentage points, 95% CI -7.45 to -2.31,P&lt;0.001; adjusted HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.83, P&lt;0.001). Hospitalisation due to worsening heart failure or ACS was significantly reduced with the intervention (3.3% vs. 5.8% per year; rate difference -2.51% percentage points, 95% CI -4.76% to 0.26%, P = 0.0301; adjusted HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.96, P=0.030). Other secondary outcome did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusions In patients with AF and multimorbidity, the telemedicine-based, village doctor-led MIRACLE-AF integrated care intervention was associated with a significant reduction in the composite primary outcome, when compared with usual care.Annualised rates of clinical outcomesCumulative incidence of the primary outcome
title: Integrated care improves outcomes in multimorbid patients with atrial fibrillation: insights from the MIRACLE-AF trial

abstract: Abstract Background Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a non-thermal modality with high tissue selectivity and favorable acute safety in the treatment of atypical atrial flutter (AAF). Although PFA is hypothesized to improve acute procedural outcomes due to its rapid and homogeneous lesion formation, its long-term performance compared with radiofrequency (RF) ablation remains uncertain. Experimental and clinical observations suggest that reduced acute collateral and myocardial injury with PFA may paradoxically lead to incomplete substrate modification and higher arrhythmic recurrence over time. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 98 consecutive patients who underwent catheter ablation for AAF between January 2023 and September 2025. Baseline characteristics included age, sex, CHA2DS2-VASc score, LVEF, CT-derived left atrial volume index (LAVI), and history of prior AF ablation. Patients were treated with RF (n=60, 61%), PFA (n=35, 36%), or a combination of both (n=3, 3%). Acute success was defined as termination of the clinical flutter during ablation and non-inducibility of atrial arrhythmias at the end of the procedure. Long-term recurrence was defined as documented AAF or AF on ECG or Holter monitoring during follow-up. Median follow-up was 13 (6-21) months. Results Mean age was 69 ± 13 years, 47% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 3 ± 1, and the CT-LAVI was 67 ± 20 mL/m². Regarding ablation lesion sets, 33% of lines were delivered for pulmonary vein isolation, 24% targeted the posterior wall, 27% corresponded to a mitral isthmus line, and 16% were performed at other atrial sites. Acute procedural success was numerically higher with PFA compared with RF (90% vs 83%), although this difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.397). Of the total procedures, 24 (24,5%) were redo radiofrequency ablations. During follow-up, the outcome of interest occurred in 34 (34,7%) patients. In the mid-term, PFA was independently associated with a significantly higher risk of arrhythmia recurrence compared with RF (HR 2.62, 95% CI 1.31–5.26, p = 0.007). Conclusions In this contemporary cohort of AAF, approximately one-third of patients experienced arrhythmia recurrence. Although acute success was numerically higher with PFA, mid-term recurrence rates were greater in this group. This pattern may reflect the reversible or retractile characteristics of acute PFA lesions, which could limit long-term substrate modification. These results highlight the need to refine PFA lesion strategies in complex atrial arrhythmias and underscore the importance of prospective evaluation of long-term lesion durability.PFA vs RF
title: Is PFA ready for atypical atrial flutter?

abstract: Abstract Background Conduction disturbances are common after transcatheter aortic valve implantation(TAVI) and may evolve dynamically in the post-procedural period. Brief or single ECG recordings may fail to capture transient or unstable conduction abnormalities. Purpose To prospectively evaluate conduction changes within 48 hours after TAVI using continuous 12-lead Holter monitoring and to identify patients requiring permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation within 30 days. Methods In this prospective observational study, 52 consecutive TAVI patients were enrolled between Feb 2025—Jan 2026. Two patients who died in-hospital from non-arrhythmic causes were excluded, leaving 50 patients for analysis. All patients underwent 24-hour pre-procedural and continuous 48-hour post-procedural 12-lead rhythm Holter monitoring. Conduction patterns within 48 hours were classified as high-grade AV block, new-onset LBBB (± intermittent), isolated PR prolongation (≥50 ms), alternating bundle branch block (BBB), or no major conduction change. Patients with persistent LBBB underwent electrophysiological study (EPS) to measure AH and HV intervals. The study aim was descriptive assessment of rhythm changes and documentation of PPM implantation within 30 days. Results High-grade AV block occurred in 4 patients, all of whom underwent in-hospital PPM implantation. New-onset LBBB was observed in 12 patients, of whom 4 required in-hospital PPM due to prolonged HV interval &gt; 70 ms. Isolated PR prolongation was identified in 2 patients, with 1 requiring PPM. Alternating BBB was detected in 2 patients; one remained stable, whereas the other developed ventricular tachycardia followed by complete AV block during the first week, requiring PPM implantation. Patients without major conduction change (n=30) demonstrated a predominantly stable course; however, even in this group, 2 required PPM in hospital and 2 additional patients underwent PPM within 30 days, presenting with complete AV block on day 5 and day 13, respectively. Overall, 11 patients underwent in-hospital PPM implantation and 3 additional patients required PPM within 30 days(14/50, 28%). Among the 14 patients who underwent PPM implantation, one patient was lost to follow-up and three had not yet completed one-month device evaluation. Device interrogation data were therefore available in 10 patients.During follow-up, seven patients were pacing-dependent, two demonstrated lower pacing burden(2%), and one had 0% ventricular pacing. Based on Holter-defined phenotypes, the pacing-dependent group comprised four patients with high-grade AV block, two with new-onset LBBB, and one with alternating BBB. Conclusion Continuous 12-lead Holter monitoring allows detailed characterization of conduction changes after TAVI. Standard ECG recordings may miss transient conduction abnormalities such as alternating or intermittent BBB, whereas 12-lead Holter monitoring provides a more comprehensive assessment of post-procedural rhythm.Study Design and Pacemaker OutcomesHolter-Defined Conduction Phenotypes
title: Silent conduction disturbances after TAVI: insights from 12-lead holter monitoring

abstract: Abstract Introduction High degree AV block occurs in a proportion of patients after TAVR leading to pacemaker implantation. The rate and clinical predictors of pacemaker dependency are not well established. Objectives The objective of this study was to determine the percentage of patients who remain pacemaker dependent at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after TAVR implantation. Secondary endpoints included patient and procedural predictors of long-term dependency. Methods Consecutive patients from May 2024 to October 2025 who underwent pacemaker placement at a single center within 30 days before or after TAVR were retrospectively included. Pacemaker dependency was defined as &gt;90% ventricular pacing burden on device interrogation at follow-up. Patient comorbidity and procedural data were used to analyze predictors of long-term dependency by Chi-Square testing and Pearson correlation. Results Of 430 patients undergoing TAVR, 37 patients (8.6%) received pacemakers within 30 days. 45.9% of those patients (17/37) remained pacemaker dependent at 6 weeks. Dependency rates decreased to 29.7% (11/37 patients) at 6 months. At 12 months only 16.2% of patients (6/37) remained pacemaker dependent. Pre-procedural conduction abnormalities (left bundle branch block and bifascicular block) and atrial arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation and flutter) were significant predictors of pacemaker dependency. Patients with LBBB pre-TAVR who received pacemakers post-TAVR had a 30% rate of dependency compared to 11% for patients without LBBB (p&lt;0.01). Similar rates were observed in 33% of patients with pre-existing bifascicular block compared to 13% without (p&lt;0.01). Patients with atrial fibrillation and/or flutter had a 25% dependency rate compared to 12% without (p&lt;0.01). Other factors (RBBB, sex, CAD, and LVEF) had no statistically significant association with dependency. The Self-expanding supra-annular valves (n=6) resulted in the highest rate of dependency at 33%, followed by Balloon-expandable intra-annular valves (n=22) at 14%, and Self-expanding intra-annular valves (n=9) at 11%. Analysis of valve size indicates a strong positive relationship (r=0.928) between valve width and 12-month dependency. Conclusion In this single center experience, the rate of periprocedural pacemaker placement was modest at 8.6%. The pacemaker dependency rate was high at 6 weeks (45.9%), but decreased to only 16.2% at 12 months, predicted by pre-existing conduction abnormalities, atrial arrhythmias, and valve type/width. These findings can help guide pacemaker choices and programming.
title: Pacemaker dependency rates decrease within the first year of post-TAVR implantation

abstract: Abstract Background Biological age (BA) is a composite indicator integrating multiple clinical and biochemical biomarkers to quantify physiological aging and reflects overall health status more accurately than chronological age (CA). Objective This study aimed to evaluate the associations between three biological age algorithms and 10-year mortality risk after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), to identify the most clinically applicable aging metric. Methods In this large prospective cohort study, 9,234 patients with coronary artery disease undergoing PCI were included. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (n = 1,122), and the secondary endpoint was cardiac mortality (n = 366), with a median follow-up of 10 years. Established algorithms, including PhenoAge, KDMAge, and a novel simplified LightBioAge, were used to calculate biological age. Biological age acceleration was defined as a regression residual of biological age over chronological age &gt;0, while residuals ≤0 were classified as non-accelerated aging. Cox proportional hazards models were applied to assess the associations between biological age acceleration and 10-year mortality risk after PCI. Discrimination and reclassification metrics were used to evaluate the incremental predictive value of different biological age measures for mortality outcomes. Additionally, life expectancy analyses were conducted to quantify the impact of accelerated biological aging on expected survival. Results After multivariable adjustment, acceleration of all three biological age measures was independently associated with increased risks of 10-year all-cause and cardiac mortality after PCI, with PhenoAge acceleration showing the strongest risk effect. For 10-year all-cause mortality, each one standard deviation increase in LightBioAge, KDMAge, and PhenoAge acceleration was associated with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.23, 1.27, and 1.31, respectively. As the degree of aging acceleration increased (from Q1 to Q4), the risks of all-cause and cardiac mortality rose progressively. PhenoAge acceleration provided greater improvements in discrimination and reclassification (IDI ≈1.6%; NRI 12.2–14.4%) than LightBioAge or KDMAge acceleration. Life expectancy analyses revealed that patients with accelerated biological aging experienced a significant reduction in expected lifespan, with a graded increase in life-years lost as aging acceleration worsened. For example, a 45-year-old patient with accelerated aging exhibited a marked reduction in life expectancy, most prominently under the PhenoAge model, with a loss of up to 3.91 years (95% CI, 2.78–4.89). Conclusions Accelerated biological aging, particularly as measured by PhenoAge, is an independent predictor of 10-year all-cause and cardiac mortality after PCI in patients with coronary artery disease and is associated with shortened life expectancy.Graphical AbstractLife expectancy and biological ageing
title: Accelerated biological aging increases the 10-year mortality risk in patients with coronary artery disease after percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has high mortality, mainly from hypoxic–ischemic brain injury. In patients hemodynamically unstable after return of spontaneous circulation, escalation to advanced therapies such as renal replacement therapy or, less commonly, mechanical circulatory support may be considered. However, these decisions are often made while patients are deeply sedated and mechanically ventilated, before reliable neurological assessment is feasible. Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a sensitive biomarker of hypoxic–ischemic neuronal injury and measurement of NfL at 24 hours may provide an early, quantitative estimate of cerebral injury severity prior to clinical awakening. Purpose To determine if 24-hour NfL discriminates neurological from non-neurological death following OHCA and to define a clinically actionable threshold to support early escalation decision-making. Methods This post-hoc exploratory analysis was conducted within the BOX trial (NEJM 2022), which included comatose adults resuscitated from OHCA. Plasma NfL was measured 24 hours after return of spontaneous circulation, and results were blinded to treating clinicians. Cardiac index (CI)and pulmonary wedge pressure were recorded by a pulmonary artery catheter (PCWP) at 24 hours. One-year mortality was classified as neurological or non-neurological by assessors blinded to NfL concentrations. Discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis with AUC and 95% confidence intervals. A high-specificity threshold (≥95%) for neurological death was prespecified. Results Of 789 patients, 523 patients had a 24-hour NfL measurement and for these patients neurological death occurred in 127 (24.3%), non-neurological death in 38 (7.3%), and 358 (68.5%) survived to one year. Twenty-four–hour NfL showed excellent discrimination for neurological death versus all other outcomes (AUC 0.97, 95% CI 0.95–0.99), see Figure 1. A prespecified high-specificity threshold (lowest cutoff achieving ≥95% specificity) was NfL ≥875 pg/mL, yielding sensitivity 94.5% and specificity 95.2% (PPV 86.3%, NPV 98.2%; accuracy 95.0%). Among non-survivors alive at 24 hours (n=165), NfL discriminated neurological from non-neurological death (AUC 0.86, 95% CI 0.78–0.95); applying the same 875 pg/mL threshold, 71.1% (27/38) of non-neurological deaths had NfL below the cutoff (Figure 2). CI and PCWP did not discriminate all-cause mortality vs survivors; among non-survivors CI modestly discriminated neurological vs non-neurological death (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.63–0.83 Conclusion Twenty-four–hour NfL differentiates neurological from non-neurological death with good accuracy and provides early quantification of hypoxic–ischemic brain injury before clinical awakening. This ability to distinguish neurological irreversibility from potentially reversible causes may help inform the clinician on escalation decisions in patients with salvageable neurological prognosis.Figure 1.Figure 2.
title: Early neurofilament light chain supports escala-tion decision-making in comatose cardiac arrest patients

abstract: Abstract Background Patients suffering implantable cardiac defibrillator (ICD) shocks for Ventricular Tachycardia (VT) despite anti-arrhythmic drugs (AADs) remain at high risk of further shocks and death without ablative therapy. Purpose To determine safety and efficacy outcomes in all patients receiving stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) in our centre with a minimum of six months follow-up. Methods We performed STAR using multimodal imaging and non-invasive mapping to target a single fraction of 25 Gy delivered as an out-patient. Patients referred to the STAR programme were at high-risk of recurrent shocks, had VT recurrence despite prior catheter ablation (CA), or were unable to receive CA (e.g. LV thrombus). All patients were taking anti-arrhythmic drugs (AADs) (amiodarone: 92%, beta blockers: 86%). No patients were declined STAR for any reason, and all were entered into a prospective registry. We describe outcomes in all patients with a minimum of six months follow up. No blanking period was observed. Results 50 patients underwent STAR and followed for a minimum of six months. Mean age of all patients was 69 years, 84% were male, and the aetiology was Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy (ICM) in 64% (Table 1). All patients suffered VT despite AADs with elevated PAINESD (17 IQR 14-21) and Charlson Index (6 IQR 5-8), predicting patients were at high risk of recurrent VT and death (Table 1). CTCAE grade ≥2 events were observed in 4 patients (8%) post-STAR. There were two cases of CTCAE grade 3 pneumonitis at 6 months, requiring steroid therapy. There were 2 cases of pericarditis: one CTCAE grade 2 at 6 months, self-resolving, and one CTCAE 3 at 22 months, requiring elective pericardiocentesis. No clinically significant deleterious effects on LV ejection fraction, valve function or ICD performance were observed. Following STAR therapy, ATP events decreased from 54 to 15 per-patient-year (95% CI 0.259–0.298; p&lt;0.001) and shocks decreased from 8 to 2 per-patient-year (95% CI 0.152–0.232; p&lt;0.001) at up to 6 years follow up. Of all 50 patients, 40% (n=20) died during follow up after a median of 10 months (IQR 5-14). 70% (n=14) of those who died were free from VT, with 75% (n=15) dying of non-cardiovascular causes. Of 35 patients who completed 12-month follow-up, 68% (n=24) were free from shock and death. We compared the number of VT events pre and post STAR (12 months). 27 patients (77%) saw a reduction in ATP events with a median burden reduction of 100% (IQR 91-100%). Furthermore, 30 patients (86%) saw a reduction in shocks at 12-months, with a median burden reduction of 100% (IQR 80-100%). Conclusion STAR appears to be safe and effective for patients with VT at high risk of recurrent shocks or death at up to 6 years of follow up. Randomised multicentre studies of RA are needed to confirm these results.STAR ESC Table 1
title: Stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR): safety and efficacy in first 50 patients

abstract: Abstract Background Millimeter-scale pacemakers integrated into transcatheter aortic valve (TAVR) platforms are emerging as a potential solution for post-valve conduction disease. Their development, however, is limited by the lack of in vivo human data defining where reliable myocardial capture can be achieved from the paravalvular aortic root and at what electrical cost. Objective To compare the feasibility and electrophysiologic characteristics of transaortic pacing from the right coronary cusp (RCC), left coronary cusp (LCC), non-coronary cusp (NCC), and the left-sided His bundle (LV His) region, and to translate these findings into design constraints for valve-integrated and ultra-miniaturized pacing systems. Methods In 25 consecutive patients undergoing clinically indicated left-sided electrophysiology procedures, sequential bipolar pacing was performed via a retrograde transaortic approach at the RCC, LCC, NCC, and LV His region following completion of the index procedure. Pacing sites were localized using 3D electroanatomic mapping, biplane fluoroscopy, and intracardiac echocardiography. Capture thresholds (1 ms pulse width), local electrogram amplitudes, and paced QRS duration and morphology were quantified. Results Ventricular capture was universal at the LV His region (25/25, 100%), frequent at the RCC (23/25, 92%) and LCC (19/25, 76%), and absent at the NCC (0/25, 0%), where atrial capture occurred in 8/25 (32%). LV His pacing demonstrated markedly lower capture thresholds (4.6 ± 2.1 mA) and the narrowest paced QRS duration (137.5 ± 15.6 ms), most often with an RBBB-like morphology in V1. In contrast, coronary cusp pacing required significantly higher outputs (RCC 13.3 ± 5.1 mA; LCC 14.2 ± 4.7 mA) and produced wider QRS complexes (≈165 ms). Conclusions Among paravalvular aortic root sites, pacing adjacent to the left-sided His bundle uniquely combined universal ventricular capture, lower capture thresholds, and narrower paced QRS duration, distinguishing it from coronary cusp pacing, which was feasible but required higher outputs and produced less synchronous ventricular activation. The non-coronary cusp demonstrated no ventricular capture but showed atrial excitability, suggesting a distinct dual-chamber electrophysiologic niche.
title: Comparative electrophysiology of aortic root pacing in humans

abstract: Abstract Background Studies comparing conduction system pacing (CSP) with conventional pacemaker (PM) implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remain scarce. Aim To evaluate the 1-year outcomes of patients undergoing CSP versus conventional PM after TAVI. Methods In this prospective, observational, multicentric cohort study, the outcomes of patients undergoing permanent PM implantation were investigated. Patients were enrolled from three centers across Switzerland between February 2011 and June 2022. Results Among 778 patients receiving PM implantation within 30 days after TAVI (mean age 83±7 years, 40% female, self-expanding valves 54%), 85 (11%) underwent CSP. Patients that received CSP had lower prevalence of coronary artery disease (36, 42% vs. 377, 54%, p = 0.04), received more often balloon-valvuloplasty (36, 42% vs 376, 54%, p=0.04). At one year after PM implant, a composite of all-cause death, a LVEF decline ≥ 10%, and worsening of NYHA class III/IV occurred less often in CSP (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43-0.88, p = 0.007) but was not significant after adjusting for age, sex, year of TAVI implant as well as several baseline and procedural parameters (aHR 0.72, 95% CI 0.49- 1.05, p = 0.09). A LVEF decline ≥10% occurred numerically less often, yet not statistically different in CSP compared to right ventricular pacing (3, 8% vs. 78, 18%, HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.15-1.35, p=0.16). Conclusions In this prospective multicentric study, patients receiving CSP within 30 days after TAVI had a lower occurrence of a combined endpoint of death, LVEF decline of ≥ 10% or a worsening in NYHA class III/IV at one year compared to conventional right ventricular pacing but not significantly after multivariable adjustment. The findings are subject to potential time-related confounding despite multivariable adjustment.Graphical Abstract
title: 1-year outcomes after conduction system pacing after transcatheter aortic valve implantation

abstract: Abstract Background The ALLEVIATE-HF trial found high rates of arrhythmia detection and arrhythmia-directed interventions after insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) insertion in patients with heart failure (HF). However, real-world generalizability, the share of interventions attributable to ICM use, and impact on HF outcomes remain uncertain. Methods We emulated a target trial using United States Medicare claims comparing ICM insertion vs no ICM within 6 months after first HF exacerbation (index). A marginal structural model with inverse-probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) used demographic, comorbidity, and utilization data to address baseline and time-varying confounding during the 6-month initiation period. ICM status was time-varying during the initiation period and fixed thereafter; patients receiving ICM after the initiation period were censored at insertion. Outcomes included arrhythmia-directed intervention (pacemaker, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, cardiac ablation, cardioversion, or left atrial appendage occlusion/exclusion), HF exacerbation or death, and HF exacerbation rates. Weighted Fine-Gray, Cox, and negative binomial regression models were used. Prespecified falsification endpoints (cataract extraction, urinary tract infection [UTI], community-acquired pneumonia [CAP]) assessed residual confounding. To assess trial generalizability, cumulative incidence of arrhythmia-directed interventions in real-world ICM recipients was compared with linked an ALLEVIATE-HF subset with Medicare enrollment. Results In the target trial, 1,040,258 patients met inclusion criteria; 2,818 initiated ICM within 6 months and 1,037,440 did not. While ICM recipients were younger and had more atrial fibrillation, IPTW achieved robust covariate balance (all standardized mean differences &lt; 0.10). ICM was associated with higher arrhythmia-directed intervention (weighted HR: 2.7; 95% CI: 2.5-3.1; Figure 1a), with increases for all intervention types (Figure 1b-c). ICM was also associated with lower weighted risk of HF exacerbation or death (HR: 0.82; 95% CI; 0.77–0.88, Figure 2a) and lower HF exacerbation rates (IRR: 0.84, 95% CI: 0.75-0.94), driven by fewer inpatient events (IRR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.72-0.91; Figure 2b). No association was observed with falsification endpoints: cataract extraction (HR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.84-1.19); UTI (HR: 1.21; 95% CI: 0.87-1.67); CAP (HR: 0.99; 95% CI: 0.79-1.24). Among ICM recipients, cumulative incidence of arrhythmia-directed intervention was similar in real-world and trial cohorts at 3, 12, and 24 months (real-world: 15.9%, 30.1%, 37.3%; trial: 15.7%, 31.7%, 36.3%; HR=0.97; 95% CI: 0.78-1.37). Conclusion In real-world target-trial emulation, ICM insertion after HF exacerbation was associated with substantially higher arrhythmia-directed interventions and improved HF outcomes. Similar intervention rates between trial and real-world cohorts support generalizability of ALLEVIATE-HF to routine practice.
title: Insertable cardiac monitors after hf exacerbation: a target-trial emulation study

abstract: Abstract Background Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and left bundle branch–optimized CRT (LOT-CRT) improve electrical resynchronization; however, a subset of patients remain non-responders or present technical failure of coronary sinus lead implantation. Fully endocardial LV pacing using standard conduction system pacing tools has not been systematically studied. Importantly, interventricular septal (IVS) lead passage implies intentional septal perforation, raising procedural safety concerns. Purpose To evaluate feasibility, safety, and clinical efficacy of LV endocardial pacing via controlled IVS lead passage using standard conduction system pacing tools (“LOT endo CRT”) as bailout therapy after ineffective LOT-CRT. Methods Between 2019–2025, 636 LBBAP procedures were performed for CRT indications. LBBAP was ineffective in 35 patients (5.5%). After additional coronary sinus lead implantation, 12 patients had ineffective or technically impossible LOT-CRT and underwent LOT endo CRT. Using a Selectra 3D delivery sheath (Biotronik) and stylet-driven active fixation lead (Solea 60 cm, 5.6F), the lead was advanced through the mid-septal IVS under continuous transthoracic echocardiographic guidance into the LV cavity and positioned at the lateral LV wall. The LV endocardial lead was connected to the LV port; the LBBAP lead to the RV port. All patients received uninterrupted therapeutic oral anticoagulants consistently with anticoagulation strategies recommended for transseptal left-sided interventions. Results Procedural success was achieved in 10/12 patients (83.3%). IVS thickness &gt;15 mm predicted failure. Mean number of septal screwing attempts: 3.2 ± 1.7. QRS duration decreased from 171 ± 19 ms (failed LOT-CRT) to 130 ± 14 ms (LOT endo CRT), p&lt;0.001. No acute or long-term complications—including hemopericardium, cardiac tamponade, stroke, systemic embolism, thromboembolic or device-related events, or lead dislodgement—were observed during the extended follow-up of 3.3 ± 1.6 years. LVEF improved from 26.4 ± 9.0% to 37.8 ± 7.1% at 6 months (p&lt;0.001). Clinical response (≥5% absolute LVEF increase) occurred in 9/10 patients (90%). Conclusion In selected patients with ineffective LOT-CRT, LV endocardial pacing via controlled IVS perforation using standard LBBAP equipment is feasible and appears relatively safe under uninterrupted anticoagulation and imaging guidance. Septal thickness may predict technical success. Larger studies are warranted to define procedural safety boundaries and thromboembolic risk.
title: Left ventricular endocardial pacing via controlled interventricular septal lead passage as bailout after failed left bundle branch area pacing optimized CRT

abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients with chronic mitral regurgitation (MR) and advanced left-sided heart failure (HF) undergoing transcatheter mitral valve edge-to-edge repair (mTEER). While mTEER effectively reduces left atrial (LA) pressure and MR severity, a substantial subset of patients exhibit persistent PH and remain at elevated risk for adverse outcomes. The contribution of pulmonary vascular remodeling, reflected by pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) and pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), to this residual risk remains uncertain Objectives To evaluate whether echocardiographically-derived markers of pulmonary vascular disease, including right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) as a surrogate for PASP, and noninvasively estimated PVR, can identify patients at increased risk of heart failure (HF) hospitalization and death following mTEER Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing mTEER between January 2021 and August 2024. PH was defined as RVSP ≥50 mmHg. Additionally, PVR was estimated noninvasively using peak tricuspid regurgitation (TR) velocity and right ventricular outflow tract velocity time integral (RVOT-VTI) measurements from echocardiography. Elevated PVR was defined as ≥2 WU. We examined the prognostic impact of baseline and post-procedural metrics on a composite endpoint of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization at 1 year Results Among 184 patients undergoing mTEER, PH was present in 167 patients (91%). Baseline PH was not independently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, residual post-procedural PH was associated with a significantly increased risk of the composite endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 2.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06–6.17; log-rank p = 0.031). Similarly, persistently elevated echocardiographically-derived PVR was strongly associated with elevated risk of the primary endpoint (HR 2.41, 95% CI 1.13–5.12; log-rank p = 0.021). Patients with residual PH demonstrated higher rates of HF hospitalization (31.9% vs 18%). Impaired right ventricular–pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling, defined by TAPSE/RVSP &lt;0.36, was additionally associated with a numerically higher risk of the composite endpoint compared with preserved coupling (42.5% vs 32%) Conclusions Residual PH and persistently elevated Doppler echocardiographically-derived PVR following mTEER were independently associated with increased risk of HF hospitalization and mortality at 1 year. These findings suggest that pulmonary vascular remodeling phenotype, rather than isolated post-capillary pressure overload, contributes to residual risk after MR correction. Echocardiography provides a practical, noninvasive approach to post-mTEER risk stratification and longitudinal assessment. Prospective studies are needed to assess whether echocardiography-guided identification of residual pulmonary vascular disease may inform post-mTEER management and clinical outcomes.Figure 1
title: Echocardiographic markers of residual pulmonary vascular disease and clinical risk after transcatheter mitral valve edge-to-edge repair

abstract: Abstract Background Anthracycline cardiotoxicity affects up to one third of patients at long-term follow-up, yet current risk stratification tools cannot predict individual susceptibility. Some patients develop severe heart failure whilst others tolerate high exposures without dysfunction, suggesting that resilience mechanisms, rather than cumulative dose, determine individual response. Purpose To identify molecular determinants distinguishing resilient from susceptible phenotypes using patient-derived cardiomyocytes representing clinical extremes. Methods We recruited patients from opposite ends of the cardiotoxicity spectrum: three resilient patients (RES) tolerated high doxorubicin doses (490±46 mg/m²) without cardiac dysfunction for over 30 years, whilst two cardiotoxic patients (TOX) developed severe heart failure requiring mechanical circulatory support after lower exposures (303±85 mg/m²). Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells were differentiated into cardiomyocytes and assembled into three-dimensional dynamic engineered heart tissues (dyn-EHT). We performed chronic low-dose doxorubicin exposure (four 48-hour cycles at 0.1 µmol/L), mitochondrial DNA sequencing, bioenergetic profiling, and antioxidant analysis. Results After chronic doxorubicin exposure, TOX-dyn-EHT exhibited progressive tissue dilatation (11.4±0.3 versus 7.9±0.3 mm in RES, p&lt;0.001), increased fibrosis, and severe contractile dysfunction with a 56% decline in contractile force in TOX, whilst RES maintained contractile function (p=0.007). Metabolically, TOX cells exhibited 51% decline in ATP-linked respiration whilst RES maintained function (3% decline, p&lt;0.001) and 31% reduction in glycolytic capacity versus 13% in RES (p=0.007). Adaptive uncoupling increased 98% in RES (p&lt;0.001) versus 31% in TOX (p=0.048). Mechanistically, mitochondrial DNA sequencing revealed two key findings replicated across independent differentiations. First, total indel burden was elevated in TOX versus RES cardiomyocytes (5.28 versus 3.43 per 1,000 reads, p=0.0026) and patient-matched fibroblasts (p=0.0499), with similar elevation observed in independent validation cohort. Second, TOX cardiomyocytes exhibited insertion-biased mutagenesis (76% versus 54% insertions, p&lt;0.001), a cardiomyocyte-specific pattern, representing the first demonstration of cell-type-specific mutagenic signatures in anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Additionally, RES cardiomyocytes exhibited elevated antioxidant protein levels, most notably 3.14-fold higher glutathione S-transferase activity (0.597 versus 0.190 nmol/min/µg protein, p=0.011). Conclusions Patient iPSC-derived 3D models recapitulated both phenotypes, with RES maintaining function whilst TOX exhibited progressive failure. Pre-existing mitochondrial genome integrity and antioxidant capacity distinguish resilient from susceptible phenotypes, providing constitutional biomarkers for pre-treatment risk stratification and personalized cardioprotection.Figure 1Feed forwar model of AIC
title: Mitochondrial DNA integrity and antioxidant determinants of resilience to anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity

abstract: Abstract Objective Conventional resting hemodynamic variables often show poor concordance with outcomes in advanced heart failure (HF). This study investigated whether the left ventricular transmural pressure difference ΔPTM, which accounts for external constraint by the pericardium and right ventricle (RV), provides superior prognostic value compared to traditional filling pressures. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 420 patients with advanced systolic HF (LVEF&lt;25%) undergoing heart transplantation (HTx) evaluation. ΔPTM was calculated as the difference between left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and right atrial pressure (RAP) obtained via invasive right-heart catheterization. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, or HTx over a median follow-up of 871 days. Results Patients in the lowest ΔPTM tertile (≤ 9 mmHg) exhibited significantly higher event rates for the composite endpoint compared to the highest tertile (≥ 16 mmHg; log-rank p&lt;0.01). After adjustment for confounders, each 1-mmHg increase in ΔPTM was associated with a 4% risk reduction for the composite outcome (HR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.93–0.99; p=0.006). Notably, ΔPTM was primarily associated with markers of disease progression—specifically LVAD implantation (p=0.012)—rather than isolated all-cause mortality (p&gt;0.05). Discrimination metrics showed that ΔPTM -based models outperformed models incorporating RAP or LVEDP alone. Conclusions In advanced HF, the transmural pressure gradient is an independent predictor of long-term outcomes, particularly disease progression necessitating mechanical circulatory support. By integrating left- and right-sided filling pressures, ΔPTM provides a physiologically grounded index of effective preload that captures clinical deterioration more effectively than conventional pressure-based measures.Figure1Figure2
title: Beyond filling pressures: transmural pressure gradient and disease progression in advanced heart failure

abstract: Abstract Background Despite treatment advances, residual cardiovascular risk persists after ST-Elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), with heart failure representing a major driver of adverse outcomes. The parsimonious ACEF (Age, Creatinine, Ejection Fraction) score is a widely used risk model that relies primarily on systolic function. Whether incorporating diastolic dysfunction into ACEF improves risk discrimination in a contemporary STEMI cohort remains uncertain. Purpose To develop and externally validate an enhanced ACEF score incorporating guideline-based echocardiographic markers of diastolic dysfunction (ACEF-3) for the prediction of heart failure–related outcomes after STEMI. Methods We studied patients with STEMI from the GIPS-III trial (2011–2013; derivation cohort) and the CardioLines Coronary Biobank (2015–2021; validation cohort). ACEF score was calculated as age divided by left ventricular ejection fraction plus one point for elevated creatinine. Diastolic burden was defined by echocardiographic markers (E/e ratio′ ≥14 and Left atrial Volume Index ≥34 mL/m²) yielding a 0–2 point scale that was incorporated into ACEF to derive ACEF-3. The primary outcome was time to a heart failure–related composite of cardiovascular death, new-onset heart failure, or heart failure hospitalization evaluated at three and five years post-STEMI. Associations were evaluated using Cox regression, discrimination using Harrell’s C-index and incremental discrimination using bootstrap estimation of ΔC. Results In the derivation cohort (n=380; mean age 59 ± 12 years; 25% female), ACEF was associated with the 3-year heart failure composite in multivariable analysis (HR 2.88 per point; 95% CI 1.28–6.49; p=0.011), with a C-index of 0.78 (95% CI 0.63–0.92). The incorporation of diastolic burden improved model discrimination (C-index 0.89; 95% CI 0.84–0.95). Similar improvement was observed at 5 years, with discrimination increasing from 0.77 (95% CI 0.63–0.91) for ACEF to 0.87 (95% CI 0.80–0.94) for ACEF-3. In the validation cohort (n=416; mean age 63 ± 12 years; 26% female), ACEF demonstrated good discrimination for the 3-year heart failure composite (C-index 0.735). ACEF-3 showed comparable performance (C-index 0.743; ΔC=0.008; 95% CI −0.054 to 0.080). At 5 years, ACEF achieved a C-index of 0.728, compared with 0.710 for ACEF-3 (ΔC=−0.018; 95% CI −0.073 to 0.045). Incremental discrimination was not statistically significant (p &gt; 0.05). Conclusion In a contemporary cohort of STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, adding diastolic dysfunction markers to ACEF improved prediction of heart-failure–related outcomes in the development cohort but did not consistently enhance discrimination in external validation. These findings suggest that ACEF already captures much of the prognostic signal conveyed by diastolic burden, and that the value of diastolic parameters for risk stratification may be phenotype-specific, warranting further investigation.ACEF-3 Model Discrimination
title: Prognostic value of diastolic dysfunction markers for heart failure–related outcomes after ST-elevation myocardial infarction: development and external validation of ACEF-3

abstract: Abstract Background Functional recovery leading to successful LVAD explantation occurs in only 1–2% of cases globally. While the severity of the underlying disease is a primary limitation, myocardial atrophy and fibrosis induced by mechanical unloading are considered significant biological barriers that hinder potential recovery. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this "unloading-induced maladaptation" remain poorly understood, and effective preventive strategies are yet to be established. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the effects of unloading through unbiased transcriptomic and proteomic analyses in a rat model of heterotopic heart and lung transplantation. Methods We established an LV unloading model by performing heterotopic heart-lung transplantation from 9-week-old male inbred LEW rats into the abdominal aorta of syngeneic recipients (n=5). Untransplanted hearts served as controls (n=6). The LV function was assessed by ex-vivo Langendorff perfusion system under constant LV loading conditions after 2 weeks of unloading. Cardiomyocyte area and fibrosis were assessed using hematoxylin-eosin and Masson's trichrome staining. Unpaired t test was used for the comparison and the difference between means was indicated with 95% CI. Transcriptomic (RNA sequencing) and proteomic analyses were performed using LV tissue. Differentially expressed genes and proteins shared between both datasets were subjected to Gene Ontology (GO) pathway analysis. Subsequently, protein-protein interaction analysis and hub gene identification were performed using STRING and the Cytoscape cytoHubba plugin, respectively. Results After 2 weeks of LV unloading, significant functional deterioration (difference in rate pressure product: RPP, −6,641; 95%CI [−11,776, −1,506] bpm·mmHg), myocardial atrophy (difference in myocyte size, −91; 95%CI [−109, −73] μm2), and fibrosis (difference in percent area, ＋3.9%; 95%CI [2.1, 5.7]) were observed. Multiomics integration identified 30 commonly upregulated factors, with the collagen-containing extracellular matrix (ECM) pathway showing the highest enrichment. Top 3 hub genes were Thbs1 (Thrombospondin-1), Col3a1 (Collagen Type III Alpha 1), and Postn (Periostin) —frequently appear together as a signature of an activated ECM. Conversely, 11 commonly downregulated factors were identified, with Tfrc (Transferrin Receptor) emerging as the top hub gene related to iron/heme homeostasis. Conclusions LV unloading induced significant LV dysfunction accompanied by myocardial atrophy and fibrosis. Our multiomics approach identified ECM turnover and iron/heme homeostasis as critical biological signatures of this process. We considered that if unloading exerts maladaptive effects even in structurally normal hearts, such effects are likely to be more pronounced in diseased myocardium subjected to LVAD support. This study presents potential targets for overcoming barriers to functional recovery in LVAD therapy.Cardiac function and remodelingCommonly up- and downregulated factors
title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of unloaded normal hearts in rats: insights into barriers to bridge to recovery in LVAD therapy

abstract: Background: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a growing public health concern in Yemen, yet detailed data from local healthcare facilities remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and outcomes of CVDs in a military cardiac center.. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Military Cardiac Center in Sanaa, including all patients admitted to the Coronary Care Unit (CCU) in 2019. Clinical data were extracted from both electronic and archived paper records, including prior medical histories dating back to 2008 or 2010 when available. Variables included demographics, clinical presentations, diagnoses, prior cardiac history, and outcomes. Statistical analyses were performed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, ANOVA, and univariate logistic regression to identify predictors of in-hospital and 5-year mortality. Results: A total of 446 patients were included (mean age: 53.0 (+/- 13.6) years), 84% male. The most common diagnoses were acute coronary syndrome (ACS, 60.9%), acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF, 13%), valvular heart disease (VHD, 9%), and cardiogenic shock (5%). Risk factors included khat use (76%), smoking (61%), hypertension (41%), diabetes (31%), and dyslipidemia (4.9%). Younger patients had higher rates of smoking, khat use, and prior myocardial infarction or PCI, while older patients had more diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Significant predictors of in-hospital mortality included diabetes (OR=2.6), rheumatic heart disease (RHD, OR=2.4), cardiogenic shock (OR=11.3), heart failure (OR=9.2), sepsis (OR=31.1), and cardiac arrest (OR=74.0). For 5-year mortality, key predictors were unstable angina (OR=8.7), ACS (OR=4.0), elective PCI (OR=2.9), and khat use (OR=2.0). Conclusion: CVDs in Yemen affect relatively young patients and are driven by modifiable, region-specific risk factors. Limited access to emergency interventions and late hospital presentation contribute to poor outcomes. Public awareness, preventive measures, and improved cardiac care infrastructure are urgently needed. Keywords: cardiovascular diseases; Acute coronary syndrome; STEMI; NSTEMI; Risk factors; Mortality predictors; Non-communicable disease; Communicable disease; Yemen; Coronary Care Unit
title: Clinical Presentation, Risk Factors, and Outcomes of Cardiovascular Disease in a Military Cardiac Center in Yemen

abstract: BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

appraisal.design_and_n: Safety population analysis of a randomised trial; 12 254 participants (asundexian n=6124, placebo n=6130).
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary bleeding analysis in a stroke population rather than an interventional cardiology population.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified bleeding analysis of OCEANIC-STROKE showing asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy did not significantly increase major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (csHR, 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; P =0.46). Lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]).

title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial

abstract: Background: The association between smoking and clopidogrel response has been stated in numerous studies, so the nature of this relationship remains undefined and may be confounded by methodological, hematological, and clinical factors. This study was designed to examine the relationship between smoking status and clopidogrel response between patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods In this observational analytical study, smoking status was assessed as the primary exposure variable, and responsiveness of clopidogrel was defined according to a predefined area-under-the-curve (AUC) threshold found using the Multiplate platelet function test. Patients were first classified according to smoking status (smokers vs non-smokers). Inside these groups, patients were further categorized as clopidogrel responder’s or non-responders. Baseline laboratory and clinical and features were compared between smokers and non-smokers, and a multivariable logistic regression model was tested to measure whether smoking status was independently related with responsiveness of clopidogrel after modification for main cardiovascular risk factors and hemoglobin level. Results Smokers confirmed a higher percentage of clopidogrel responders compared with non-smokers. Related to multivariable analysis, smoking status remained independently related with an increased likelihood of clopidogrel responsiveness, and level of hemoglobin similarly exhibited a significant positive relation with treatment responsiveness, whereas hypertension, age, BMI, and diabetes were not significant predicters. Conclusions Between patients undergoing PCI; smoking status was independently related with clopidogrel responsiveness; though, this result represents an observational association rather than sign of clinical benefit. The findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and justified further mechanistic and longitudinal study to explain the underlying elucidations for this design.
title: The impact of smoking status on clopidogrel responsiveness in patients with coronary artery disease who undergo percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Background: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a severe manifestation of acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Although several studies have investigated factors associated with OHCA, the findings have been inconsistent. This study evaluates the clinical and angiographic factors associated with OHCA in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This retrospective study included consecutive STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI at Rambam Health Care Campus between 2010 and 2024. Patients were categorized by the presence of pre-hospital OHCA. Clinical and angiographic characteristics were compared, and logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of OHCA. Results: Among 2,176 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, 135 (6.2%) experienced pre-hospital OHCA. OHCA patients were younger and had higher serum creatinine levels. The distribution of the IRA differed significantly (p=0.005): LMCA and LAD were more frequently the infarct-related arteries, whereas RCA involvement was less common. Independent predictors of OHCA were LMCA (OR 6.03), LAD (OR 1.81), and higher creatinine (OR 1.44). Age and smoking were inversely associated with OHCA (OR 0.97 per additional year, and OR 0.62, respectively). Lesion location, initial TIMI flow, and extent of coronary artery disease were not associated with OHCA. Conclusions: Patients with OHCA in the setting of STEMI are younger, have higher creatinine levels, and more often have culprit lesions in the LMCA or LAD. These findings suggest that specific anatomic and metabolic factors, rather than overall coronary disease burden, are associated with pre-hospital cardiac arrest.
title: Clinical and Anatomical Correlates of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Patients With ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) remains an established imaging modality for guiding percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), providing real-time visualization during transseptal puncture, device deployment and procedural assessment. However, esophageal instrumentation and prolonged probe manipulation may result in gastrointestinal injury, particularly in patients with pre-existing esophageal abnormalities or increased bleeding risk. This narrative review summarizes the available evidence regarding the mechanisms, risk factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, management and prevention of TEE-associated esophageal injury during LAAO while examining alternative imaging strategies. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by targeted searches of broader structural heart intervention literature. Although clinically recognized TEE-associated gastrointestinal complications are uncommon, studies employing systematic endoscopic surveillance have identified substantially higher rates of subclinical mucosal injury. Reported manifestations range from transient dysphagia and superficial mucosal lesions to gastrointestinal bleeding, intramural esophageal hematoma, perforation and fistula formation. Nevertheless, limited LAAO-specific evidence, heterogeneous outcome definitions and differences in surveillance strategies preclude reliable estimation of procedure-specific esophageal injury incidence. Intracardiac echocardiography eliminates esophageal instrumentation but carries a distinct procedural risk profile, whereas cardiac computed tomography (CCT) provides complementary opportunities for preprocedural planning and postprocedural surveillance. Careful preprocedural assessment, judicious probe manipulation, early recognition of complications and individualized imaging selection are important considerations. Prospective studies incorporating standardized esophageal injury endpoints are needed to establish the true clinical burden and guide preventive strategies.
title: Esophageal Injury During Transesophageal Echocardiography-Guided Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Narrative Review

abstract: Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) causes increased sleep systemic systolic blood pressure (SBP) and cardiovascular (CV) risk. Methods: This secondary analysis encompassed data of 2,065 Spanish polysomnography-confirmed OSA hypertensives (61±11.9 years, 79.5% male) and 32,471 Spanish non-OSA hypertensives (60.2±14.0 years, 51% male) from the Hygia Project. Annually throughout the 5.1-year median follow-up, they underwent comprehensive clinical evaluation and 48-h ambulatory blood pressure (BP) monitoring, with bed and wake-up times diary-recorded to calculate individualized awake and sleep BP means and sleep-time relative declines. Results: OSA subjects experienced higher CV event rates (p<0.001), including a 1.79-fold higher rate of the primary composite study outcome: myocardial infarction, surgical coronary revascularization, heart failure, stroke, and CV death. Cox survival analyses revealed the baseline asleep SBP mean most strongly predicted the primary composite study outcome [HRadjusted =1.37 (1.23, 1.52); p<0.001], while baseline enhanced sleep-time relative SBP decline most strongly predicted protection against it (HRadjusted=0.75 (0.67, 0.83); p<0.001]. Furthermore, when the Cox statistical model included adjustment for the sleep SBP mean, office BP was not predictive of risk. Conclusion: The sleep SBP mean and decline were the BP parameters most predictive of CV events in OSA subjects, constituting major targets of clinical management.
title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Is Associated with Adverse Cardiovascular Events Related to Sleep Blood Pressure

abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular revascularization is an established treatment for symptomatic femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease. Drug-coated balloon angioplasty allows antiproliferative drug delivery without permanent metallic implantation, while atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation in calcified and occlusive disease. This study evaluated the procedural safety and one-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty, with additional assessment of dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and continued smoking. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included 107 patients with Rutherford category 4–5 femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease who underwent JETSTREAM atherectomy exclusively through retrograde popliteal access followed by Ranger paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty. No distal embolic protection device was used. Aspirin 100 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily were prescribed for 12 months. The primary procedural safety endpoint was clinically evident distal embolization within 24 hours. Longitudinal outcomes included tibialis posterior artery and dorsalis pedis artery Doppler waveform scores, Rutherford category, and ankle-brachial index. Outcomes were compared according to dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and smoking status. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed for factors associated with treatment non-adherence. RESULTS: Mean age was 67.0±6.9 years, and 69.2% of patients were male. Total occlusions were present in 45.8%, PACSS grade 4 calcification in 83.2%, and adjunctive stenting was required in 21.5%. No clinically evident distal embolization occurred within 24 hours (0/107; upper two-sided 95% exact confidence limit, approximately 3.4%). At one year, mean tibialis posterior artery and dorsalis pedis artery waveform scores improved from 1.05±0.42 to 2.42±0.71 and from 1.07±0.60 to 2.28±0.74, respectively; mean Rutherford category decreased from 4.16±0.37 to 1.64±1.17, and median ankle-brachial index increased from 0.59 to 1.20 (all P< .001). Seventy-seven patients (72.0%) were adherent to dual antiplatelet therapy. At one year, adherent patients had better tibialis posterior artery (2.69 vs 1.73), dorsalis pedis artery (2.56 vs 1.57), Rutherford category (1.13 vs 2.93), and ankle-brachial index (1.218 vs 0.873; all P< .001). Forty-six patients continued smoking. Compared with patients not smoking during follow-up, continued smokers had poorer one-year tibialis posterior artery (2.24 vs 2.56; P=.036), dorsalis pedis artery (2.04 vs 2.46; P=.004), Rutherford category (2.02 vs 1.34; P=.002), and ankle-brachial index (1.044 vs 1.179; P=.004). Continued smoking was independently associated with dual antiplatelet therapy non-adherence (adjusted odds ratio, 3.43; 95% confidence interval, 1.27–9.29; P=.015). CONCLUSIONS: Filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with substantial one-year clinical and hemodynamic improvement and no clinically evident distal embolization in this cohort. Dual antiplatelet therapy adherence was associated with better one-year outcomes, whereas continued smoking was associated with poorer outcomes and greater non-adherence.
title: Filter-Free Retrograde Popliteal JETSTREAM Atherectomy Followed by Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty: Procedural Safety and One-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes

abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), often called “broken heart syndrome,” is an acute and usually reversible form of left ventricular dysfunction that mimics acute coronary syndrome but is not explained by an obstructive coronary lesion [1,2]. It is preceded by an emotional or physical trigger in many, but not all, patients and predominantly affects postmenopausal women [2]. This narrative review synthesizes current understanding of the epidemiology, proposed cellular and systemic mechanisms, brain–heart interactions, diagnosis, clinical course, and management of TTS. Particular emphasis is placed on the catecholamine surge and sympathetic activation thought to link stress to myocardial dysfunction, and on the contributions of receptor-level signaling, microvascular dysfunction, inflammation, and altered limbic and autonomic brain networks. Seven tables and four figures summarize registry data, proposed mechanisms, neuroimaging findings, diagnostic tools, management, and practical nursing considerations. Many mechanistic details remain hypotheses rather than established facts, no treatment has been proven to improve outcomes in randomized trials, and the evidence for psychological interventions is limited. The review is non-systematic and is intended as an accessible synthesis for students and early-career clinicians.
title: The Neuro-Cardiac Axis: Cellular and Systemic Consequences of Acute Stress in Takotsubo Syndrome

abstract: Background: Severe COVID-19 is driven by a complex interplay between systemic hyperinﬂammation, cellular immune dysregulation, and activation of coagulation cascades. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 52-year-old man with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis managed with chronic etanercept therapy, who was hospitalized with rapidly progressive COVID-19. Longitudinal monitoring of C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), D-dimer, and ﬁbrinogen demonstrated a transient suppression of select acute-phase reactants followed by profound cellular immune dysregulation and escalating thrombo-inﬂammatory activity. Despite multimodal management—including remdesivir, convalescent plasma, invasive mechanical ventilation, and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)—the patient suﬀered fatal cardiac arrest. Conclusions: This case highlights the clinical utility of longitudinal, multiparametric biomarker proﬁling in severe COVID-19 and underscores the critical importance of timely immunomodulatory interventions prior to irreversible immunothrombotic damage.
title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Inflammatory, Immune, and Coagulation Biomarkers in Critical COVID-19 Under Chronic Etanercept Therapy: A Case Report

abstract: Background: Mechanical circulatory support significantly improved survival in end-stage heart failure patients. However, this treatment associated with a wide range of complications, including infections, stroke and bleeding. Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is often underreported gynecological disorder in female patients following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. Case Presentation: A 15-year-old female patient with dilated cardiomyopathy and chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction underwent implantation of “Heart Mate 3” as a “bridge” to transplant. After LVAD implantation she had recurrent nosebleeds and AUB complicated with moderate anemia. She frequently admitted to the hospital and then managed with antifibrinolytic medication (Tranexamic acid: 500 mg was administered once a day for 3 days) and blood transfusions. By heart team it was decided to reduce antithrombotic therapy: antiplatelets were discontinued and her INR level was maintained 1.4-1.8. For 2 years prior to HTx LVAD function kept fine on minimized antithrombotic therapy without thromboembolic complications. It was made a multidisciplinary team decision to avoid combined oral contraceptives due to the high risk of thromboembolic complications outweighing the benefits. Twice she underwent urgent laparoscopic surgeries but after all her fertile function remained preserved. Conclusions: LVAD patients should be managed with a multidisciplinary heart team. In case of recurrent bleeding and low-risk of thromboembolic complications reduction of antithrombotic therapy should be considered. A personalized approach is essential to determine whether conservative or surgical management is superior, as it balances evidence-based medicine with individual patient needs, reducing the risks of futile or overly aggressive care. Taking into account the reproductive function, an organ-preserving operation was performed for the subsequent preservation of fertile function. Surgical interventions for gynecological disorders can be safely performed in patients “bridged” with LVAD.
title: Management of Abnormal Uterine Bleeding in a Patient “Bridged” with LVAD

abstract: Coronary artery calcification is common in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); it impairs device delivery and stent expansion and predicts stent failure. Balloon-based techniques (non-compliant, super high-pressure, cutting and scoring balloons, intravascular lithotripsy), rotational and orbital atherectomy, and excimer laser coronary atherectomy are now widely available. This narrative review describes the mechanism of each technique, the calcium morphology it suits on intravascular imaging, and its advantages and limitations, and synthesizes the randomized trials published between 2018 and 2026, including their longer-term follow-up. Dedicated calcium modification improves procedural success compared with balloon-only strategies in selected calcified lesions, but no trial has shown fewer deaths or myocardial infarctions; the only trial powered for a clinical endpoint comparing preparation strategies found no benefit from routine orbital atherectomy. Head-to-head comparisons were powered for imaging surrogates and mostly found the techniques non-inferior to one another. Intravascular imaging guidance is associated with larger stent areas and fewer adverse events. We also review technique-specific complications and their percutaneous management, and the evidence on performing these procedures in centers without on-site cardiac surgery. Finally, we propose a lesion-based, imaging-guided approach to technique selection and outline the trials still needed.
title: Calcium Modification Techniques in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Evidence, Mechanics, Complications and Device Selection

abstract: Abstract Background Implantation of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) artificial chordae is an established approach for mitral valve repair, but current transapical systems are typically limited to single-thread implantation per delivery and remain procedurally complex. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and mid-term efficacy of the HaloChord® system, which delivers up to two sets (four threads) of ePTFE chordae per sequence, in a porcine model of acute mitral regurgitation (MR). Methods Five adult Large White pigs (60–80 kg) underwent transapical induction of acute moderate to moderately severe MR via surgical blunt disconnection of the primary chordae tendineae attached to the P2 segment. Under beating-heart transesophageal echocardiographic (TEE) guidance, one or two suturing devices per animal were deployed with the HaloChord® system and anchored at the left ventricular apex. Animals followed a staged terminal-endpoint design (n = 1 at 30 days, n = 1 at 90 days, n = 3 at 180 days). Evaluations included serial echocardiography, clinical pathology, gross examination, and histopathological scoring per GB/T 16886.6–2022 Annex E. Results Implantation succeeded in all 5 animals; two received one suturing device (4 equivalent chordae) and three received two suturing devices (8 equivalent chordae). Suturing-device operation time was 10.5 ± 5.10 min per device; fixation-device operation time was 5.2 ± 6.14 min per cycle, with the wide fixation-time variability reflecting iterative echocardiographic length titration. MR grade was reduced from 2 + to 3 + post-modeling to ≤ 1 + immediately post-procedure and remained stable through each terminal endpoint. Vena contracta width decreased substantially and remained stable at follow-up. Gross examination confirmed stable anchoring with no detachment, rupture, or thrombus. Histopathological scoring showed a more pronounced tissue response at 30 days that moderated to predominantly moderate scores at 90 and 180 days, driven primarily by fibrosis and neovascularization rather than active inflammation. Conclusions In this porcine acute MR model, the HaloChord® system demonstrated procedural feasibility on the beating heart, effective acute MR reduction, and acceptable mid-term device stability and biocompatibility. The dual-set delivery design simplifies transapical chordal implantation, providing a foundation for clinical evaluation.
title: Preclinical Animal Study of a Dual-Set Artificial Chordae Mitral Valve Repair System in a Porcine Model
